        nonce: attribute_or_empty(attribute_name!("nonce")),
        integrity: attribute_or_empty(attribute_name!("integrity")),
        integrity_present: attribute(attribute_name!("integrity")).is_some(),
        referrer_policy: attribute_or_empty(attribute_name!("referrerpolicy")),
        fetch_priority: attribute_or_empty(attribute_name!("fetchpriority")),
        media: attribute_or_empty(attribute_name!("media")),
    };
    callback(&entry)
}

fn attribute_value(attributes: &[Attribute], name: KnownName) -> Option<Utf16View<'_>> {
    attributes
        .iter()
        .find(|attribute| attribute.local_name == name)
        .map(|attribute| attribute.value.as_slice())
}

/// The code units of an attribute value as bytes, to look for ASCII keywords in. A code unit that doesn't fit in a
/// byte becomes one that is in no keyword and isn't whitespace.
fn keyword_bytes(value: Utf16View<'_>) -> Cow<'_, [u8]> {
    match value {
        Utf16View::Latin1(code_units) => Cow::Borrowed(code_units),
        Utf16View::Utf16(code_units) => Cow::Owned(
            code_units
                .iter()
                .map(|&code_unit| u8::try_from(code_unit).unwrap_or(0xFF))
                .collect(),
        ),
    }
}

fn rel_contains_keyword(rel: &[u8], keyword: &[u8]) -> bool {
    rel.split(|byte| byte.is_ascii_whitespace())
        .any(|token| token.eq_ignore_ascii_case(keyword))
}

fn translate_preload_destination(destination: Option<Utf16View<'_>>) -> Option<RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination> {
    Some(match &*keyword_bytes(destination?) {
        b"fetch" => RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::None,
        b"font" => RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Font,
        b"image" => RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Image,
        b"script" => RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Script,
        b"style" => RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Style,
        b"track" => RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Track,
        _ => return None,
    })
}

fn translate_modulepreload_destination(destination: Option<Utf16View<'_>>) -> Option<RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination> {
    let Some(destination) = destination else {
        return Some(RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Script);
    };

    let destination = &*keyword_bytes(destination);

    // A module preload destination is "json", "style", "text", or a script-like destination.
    if destination.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"audioworklet") {
        return Some(RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::AudioWorklet);
    }
    if destination.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"json") {
        return Some(RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::JSON);
    }
    if destination.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"paintworklet") {
        return Some(RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::PaintWorklet);
    }
    if destination.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"script") {
        return Some(RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Script);
    }
    if destination.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"serviceworker") {
        return Some(RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::ServiceWorker);
    }
    if destination.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"sharedworker") {
        return Some(RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::SharedWorker);
    }
    if destination.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"style") {
        return Some(RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Style);
    }
    if destination.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"text") {
        return Some(RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Text);
    }
    if destination.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"worker") {
        return Some(RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Worker);
    }

    const NON_MODULE_DESTINATIONS: [&[u8]; 15] = [
        b"audio",
        b"document",
        b"embed",
        b"fetch",
        b"font",
        b"frame",
        b"iframe",
        b"image",
        b"manifest",
        b"object",
        b"report",
        b"track",
        b"video",
        b"webidentity",
        b"xslt",
    ];
    if NON_MODULE_DESTINATIONS
        .iter()
        .any(|candidate| destination.eq_ignore_ascii_case(candidate))
    {
        return None;
    }

    // NB: Invalid and empty values put the enumerated as attribute in no state, so step 2 uses "script".
    Some(RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Script)
}

fn cors_setting_from_attribute(attributes: &[Attribute]) -> RustFfiPreloadScannerCorsSetting {
    let Some(crossorigin) = attribute_value(attributes, attribute_name!("crossorigin")) else {
        return RustFfiPreloadScannerCorsSetting::NoCors;
    };

    if crossorigin.eq_ignore_ascii_case("use-credentials") {
        RustFfiPreloadScannerCorsSetting::UseCredentials
    } else {
        RustFfiPreloadScannerCorsSetting::Anonymous
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    struct ScannedEntry {
        action: RustFfiPreloadScannerAction,
        url: String,
        destination: RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination,
        cors_setting: RustFfiPreloadScannerCorsSetting,
    }

    fn collect(input: &str) -> Vec<ScannedEntry> {
        collect_with_scripting(input, true)
    }

    fn collect_with_scripting(input: &str, scripting_enabled: bool) -> Vec<ScannedEntry> {
        let mut entries = Vec::new();
        scan(input.as_bytes(), scripting_enabled, |entry| {
            entries.push(ScannedEntry {
                action: entry.action,
                url: entry.url.to_test_string(),
                destination: entry.destination,
                cors_setting: entry.cors_setting,
            });
            true
        });
        entries
    }

    fn collect_utf16(input: &str) -> Vec<ScannedEntry> {
        let input = input.encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let mut entries = Vec::new();
        scan_utf16(&input, true, |entry| {
            entries.push(ScannedEntry {
                action: entry.action,
                url: entry.url.to_test_string(),
                destination: entry.destination,
                cors_setting: entry.cors_setting,
            });
            true
        });
        entries
    }

    #[test]
    fn scans_utf16_input() {
        let entries = collect_utf16(r#"<base href="/base/😀"><img src="./photo.png">"#);

        assert_eq!(

                ScannedEntry {
                    action: RustFfiPreloadScannerAction::Base,
                    url: "/base/😀".to_string(),

                    cors_setting: RustFfiPreloadScannerCorsSetting::NoCors,

                    url: "./photo.png".to_string(),
                    destination: RustFfiPreloadScannerDestination::Image,
                    cors_setting: RustFfiPreloadScannerCorsSetting::NoCors,
                },
            ]
        );
    }

    fn code_units(input: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        input.encode_utf16().collect()
    }

    fn scan_urls(scanner: &mut RustFfiPreloadScanner) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut urls = Vec::new();
        scanner.scan(&mut |entry| {
            urls.push(entry.url.to_test_string());
            true
        });
        urls
    }

    #[test]
    fn goes_on_from_where_it_stopped() {
        let mut scanner = RustFfiPreloadScanner::new(true);

        // The input runs out inside a tag, and then inside the text of a script.
        scanner.append_input(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units(r#"<img src="./a.png"><img sr"#)));
        assert_eq!(scan_urls(&mut scanner), vec!["./a.png"]);

        scanner.append_input(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units(
            r#"c="./b.png"><script>var trap = '<img src="./tr"#,
        )));
        assert_eq!(scan_urls(&mut scanner), vec!["./b.png"]);

        scanner.append_input(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units(
            r#"ap.png">';</script><img src="./c.png">"#,
        )));
        assert_eq!(scan_urls(&mut scanner), vec!["./c.png"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn hands_on_only_input_not_scanned_yet() {
        let mut parser_tokenizer = HtmlTokenizer::new(code_units("<img src=a>"));
        parser_tokenizer.set_input_stream_closed(false);

        let (input, continues) = parser_tokenizer.input_for_speculative_scan();
        assert_eq!(input.to_utf16(), code_units("<img src=a>"));
        assert!(!continues);

        parser_tokenizer.append_input(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units("<img src=b>")));
        let (input, continues) = parser_tokenizer.input_for_speculative_scan();
        assert_eq!(input.to_utf16(), code_units("<img src=b>"));
        assert!(continues);

        // Once the parser gets past the scanned input, the scan starts over where the parser is.
        while parser_tokenizer.next_token(false, false).is_some() {}
        parser_tokenizer.append_input(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units("<img src=c>")));
        let (input, continues) = parser_tokenizer.input_for_speculative_scan();
        assert_eq!(input.to_utf16(), code_units("<img src=c>"));
        assert!(continues);
        parser_tokenizer.append_input(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units("<img src=d><img src=e>")));
        while parser_tokenizer.next_token(false, false).is_some() {}
        parser_tokenizer.parser_did_run();
        parser_tokenizer.append_input(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units("<img src=f>")));
        let (input, continues) = parser_tokenizer.input_for_speculative_scan();
        assert_eq!(input.to_utf16(), code_units("<img src=f>"));
        assert!(!continues);
    }

    #[test]
    fn starts_over_after_input_is_inserted_before_the_scanned_input() {
        let mut parser_tokenizer = HtmlTokenizer::new(code_units("<script></script><img src=a>"));
        parser_tokenizer.set_input_stream_closed(false);
        parser_tokenizer.next_token(false, false);
        parser_tokenizer.next_token(false, false);
        parser_tokenizer.update_insertion_point();

        let (input, _) = parser_tokenizer.input_for_speculative_scan();
        assert_eq!(input.to_utf16(), code_units("<img src=a>"));

        // Input that document.write() inserts at the insertion point comes before the scanned input, so the scan has
        // to take it in too.
        parser_tokenizer.insert_input_at_insertion_point(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units("<img src=w>")));
        let (input, continues) = parser_tokenizer.input_for_speculative_scan();
        assert_eq!(input.to_utf16(), code_units("<img src=w><img src=a>"));
        assert!(!continues);
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Scans over runs of input code units.
//!
//! A scan for the end of a run looks at a block of 16 code units at a time: it asks of all of them at once which ones
//! end the run, and gets a bit for each. Most runs in markup are over within a block or two, so a scan has nothing to
//! set up and its first block is as cheap as any other.
//!
//! The scans that only count look at a fixed-size chunk of code units at a time with no early exits inside a chunk,
//! which is the shape the compiler turns into vector instructions for whatever the target CPU has.

use crate::token::Position;
use ak::Utf16View;

/// A code unit of the input stream, in either of the forms it is stored in.
pub trait CodeUnit: Copy + Default + Eq + Into<u16> + From<u8> {
    /// Loads a block of code units as bytes, with every code unit above U+00FE as 0xFF.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// `BLOCK_SIZE` code units must be readable at `code_units`.
    unsafe fn load_block(code_units: *const Self) -> block::Block;

    /// One bit for each code unit of a block: whether it is a surrogate.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// `BLOCK_SIZE` code units must be readable at `code_units`.
    unsafe fn surrogates_in_block(code_units: *const Self) -> u32;

    fn view(code_units: &[Self]) -> Utf16View<'_>;
}

impl CodeUnit for u8 {
    #[inline(always)]
    unsafe fn load_block(code_units: *const u8) -> block::Block {
        unsafe { block::load_narrow(code_units) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    unsafe fn surrogates_in_block(_: *const u8) -> u32 {
        0
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn view(code_units: &[u8]) -> Utf16View<'_> {
        Utf16View::Latin1(code_units)
    }
}

impl CodeUnit for u16 {
    #[inline(always)]
    unsafe fn load_block(code_units: *const u16) -> block::Block {
        unsafe { block::load_wide(code_units) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    unsafe fn surrogates_in_block(code_units: *const u16) -> u32 {
        unsafe { block::surrogates(code_units) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn view(code_units: &[u16]) -> Utf16View<'_> {
        Utf16View::Utf16(code_units)
    }
}

use block::BLOCK_SIZE;

#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
mod block {
    use core::arch::x86_64::*;

    pub(super) const BLOCK_SIZE: usize = 16;
    pub type Block = __m128i;

    #[inline(always)]
    pub unsafe fn load_narrow(code_units: *const u8) -> Block {
        unsafe { _mm_loadu_si128(code_units.cast()) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub unsafe fn load_wide(code_units: *const u16) -> Block {
        unsafe {
            // NB: x - saturating_sub(x, 0xFF) is min(x, 0xFF), with nothing that every x86-64 CPU doesn't have.
            let limit = _mm_set1_epi16(0xFF);
            let low = _mm_loadu_si128(code_units.cast());
            let high = _mm_loadu_si128(code_units.add(8).cast());
            let low = _mm_sub_epi16(low, _mm_subs_epu16(low, limit));
            let high = _mm_sub_epi16(high, _mm_subs_epu16(high, limit));
            _mm_packus_epi16(low, high)
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub unsafe fn surrogates(code_units: *const u16) -> u32 {
        unsafe {
            let top_bits = _mm_set1_epi16(0xF800u16 as i16);
            let surrogate = _mm_set1_epi16(0xD800u16 as i16);
            let low = _mm_loadu_si128(code_units.cast());
            let high = _mm_loadu_si128(code_units.add(8).cast());
            let low = _mm_cmpeq_epi16(_mm_and_si128(low, top_bits), surrogate);
            let high = _mm_cmpeq_epi16(_mm_and_si128(high, top_bits), surrogate);
            _mm_movemask_epi8(_mm_packs_epi16(low, high)) as u32
        }
    }

    /// One bit for each code unit of a block: whether it is `byte`.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn equal_to(block: Block, byte: u8) -> u32 {
        unsafe { _mm_movemask_epi8(_mm_cmpeq_epi8(block, _mm_set1_epi8(byte as i8))) as u32 }
    }

    /// One bit for each code unit of a block: whether it is above U+007F.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn non_ascii(block: Block) -> u32 {
        unsafe { _mm_movemask_epi8(block) as u32 }
    }
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
mod block {
    use core::arch::aarch64::*;

    pub(super) const BLOCK_SIZE: usize = 16;
    pub type Block = uint8x16_t;

    #[inline(always)]
    pub unsafe fn load_narrow(code_units: *const u8) -> Block {
        unsafe { vld1q_u8(code_units) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub unsafe fn load_wide(code_units: *const u16) -> Block {
        unsafe {
            vcombine_u8(
                vqmovn_u16(vld1q_u16(code_units)),
                vqmovn_u16(vld1q_u16(code_units.add(8))),
            )
        }
    }

    /// One bit per byte, from a vector whose bytes are all ones or all zeros.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn bits_of(bytes: Block) -> u32 {
        const BITS: [u8; 16] = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128];
        unsafe {
            let masked = vandq_u8(bytes, vld1q_u8(BITS.as_ptr()));
            vaddv_u8(vget_low_u8(masked)) as u32 | (vaddv_u8(vget_high_u8(masked)) as u32) << 8
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub unsafe fn surrogates(code_units: *const u16) -> u32 {
        unsafe {
            let top_bits = vdupq_n_u16(0xF800);
            let surrogate = vdupq_n_u16(0xD800);
            let low = vceqq_u16(vandq_u16(vld1q_u16(code_units), top_bits), surrogate);
            let high = vceqq_u16(vandq_u16(vld1q_u16(code_units.add(8)), top_bits), surrogate);
            bits_of(vcombine_u8(vmovn_u16(low), vmovn_u16(high)))
        }
    }

    /// One bit for each code unit of a block: whether it is `byte`.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn equal_to(block: Block, byte: u8) -> u32 {
        unsafe { bits_of(vceqq_u8(block, vdupq_n_u8(byte))) }
    }

    /// One bit for each code unit of a block: whether it is above U+007F.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn non_ascii(block: Block) -> u32 {
        unsafe { bits_of(vcgeq_u8(block, vdupq_n_u8(0x80))) }
    }
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]
mod block {
    pub(super) const BLOCK_SIZE: usize = 16;
    pub type Block = [u8; BLOCK_SIZE];

    #[inline(always)]
    pub unsafe fn load_narrow(code_units: *const u8) -> Block {
        unsafe { core::ptr::read_unaligned(code_units.cast()) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub unsafe fn load_wide(code_units: *const u16) -> Block {
        core::array::from_fn(|i| unsafe { core::ptr::read_unaligned(code_units.add(i)) }.min(0xFF) as u8)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub unsafe fn surrogates(code_units: *const u16) -> u32 {
        (0..BLOCK_SIZE).fold(0, |bits, i| {
            let code_unit = unsafe { core::ptr::read_unaligned(code_units.add(i)) };
            bits | u32::from(code_unit & 0xF800 == 0xD800) << i
        })
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn bits_of(block: Block, test: impl Fn(u8) -> bool) -> u32 {
        block
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .fold(0, |bits, (i, &byte)| bits | u32::from(test(byte)) << i)
    }

    /// One bit for each code unit of a block: whether it is `byte`.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn equal_to(block: Block, byte: u8) -> u32 {
        bits_of(block, |code_unit| code_unit == byte)
    }

    /// One bit for each code unit of a block: whether it is above U+007F.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn non_ascii(block: Block) -> u32 {
        bits_of(block, |code_unit| code_unit >= 0x80)
    }
}

const CHUNK_SIZE: usize = 32;

/// The offset of the first code unit that is one of `stops` or a surrogate, or the length of `code_units` if there is
/// none. `seen_non_ascii` is set if a code unit before it is above U+007F.
#[inline(always)]
fn find_first<T: CodeUnit, const N: usize>(code_units: &[T], stops: [u8; N], seen_non_ascii: &mut bool) -> usize {
    // One bit for each code unit of the block at `block`: whether it ends the scan, and whether it isn't ASCII.
    let scan_block = |block: *const T| {
        // SAFETY: Both callers pass a pointer to `BLOCK_SIZE` code units.
        let (bytes, surrogates) = unsafe { (T::load_block(block), T::surrogates_in_block(block)) };
        let stops = stops
            .iter()
            .fold(surrogates, |bits, &stop| bits | block::equal_to(bytes, stop));
        (stops, block::non_ascii(bytes))
    };

    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset + BLOCK_SIZE <= code_units.len() {
        let (stops, non_ascii) = scan_block(code_units[offset..].as_ptr());
        if stops != 0 {
            let stop = stops.trailing_zeros();
            *seen_non_ascii |= non_ascii & ((1 << stop) - 1) != 0;
            return offset + stop as usize;
        }
        *seen_non_ascii |= non_ascii != 0;
        offset += BLOCK_SIZE;
    }

    // NB: What is left is less than a block, and is looked at as the start of one that ends the scan after it.
    let remaining = code_units.len() - offset;
    let mut last_block = [T::default(); BLOCK_SIZE];
    last_block[..remaining].copy_from_slice(&code_units[offset..]);
    let (stops, non_ascii) = scan_block(last_block.as_ptr());
    let stop = (stops | 1 << remaining).trailing_zeros();
    *seen_non_ascii |= non_ascii & ((1 << stop) - 1) != 0;
    offset + stop as usize
}

/// The bytes of `name`, which has to be ASCII, if they fit in `buffer`.
#[inline(always)]
pub fn ascii_name_bytes<'a, T: CodeUnit, const N: usize>(name: &[T], buffer: &'a mut [u8; N]) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
    let bytes = buffer.get_mut(..name.len())?;
    for (byte, &code_unit) in bytes.iter_mut().zip(name) {
        *byte = code_unit.into() as u8;
    }
    Some(bytes)
}

/// A run of code units at the start of some input.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct Run {
    pub length: usize,
    pub is_ascii: bool,
}

/// The run of code units at the start of `code_units` that the data and RCDATA states emit as they are: everything
/// up to the first U+003C (<), U+0026 (&), U+0000 NULL, U+000D CR, or surrogate that isn't half of a pair.
pub fn data_run<T: CodeUnit>(code_units: &[T]) -> Run {
    text_run(code_units, [b'<', b'&', 0, b'\r'])
}

/// The run of code units at the start of `code_units` that the RAWTEXT and script data states emit as they are:
/// everything up to the first U+003C (<), U+0000 NULL, U+000D CR, or surrogate that isn't half of a pair.
pub fn raw_text_run<T: CodeUnit>(code_units: &[T]) -> Run {
    text_run(code_units, [b'<', 0, b'\r'])
}

/// The number of code units at the start of `code_units` that a quoted attribute value takes as they are, and whether
/// they are all ASCII: everything up to the first `quote`, U+0026 (&), U+0000 NULL, U+000D CR, or surrogate that isn't
/// half of a pair.
pub fn quoted_attribute_value_run<T: CodeUnit>(code_units: &[T], quote: u8) -> Run {
    text_run(code_units, [quote, b'&', 0, b'\r'])
}

#[inline(always)]
fn text_run<T: CodeUnit, const N: usize>(code_units: &[T], stops: [u8; N]) -> Run {
    let mut length = 0;
    let mut seen_non_ascii = false;
    loop {
        length += find_first(&code_units[length..], stops, &mut seen_non_ascii);
        let Some(&[high, low]) = code_units.get(length..length + 2) else {
            break;
        };
        if !is_surrogate_pair(high.into(), low.into()) {
            break;
        }
        seen_non_ascii = true;
        length += 2;
    }
    Run {
        length,
        is_ascii: !seen_non_ascii,
    }
}

/// The number of code units at the start of `code_units` that a quoted attribute value takes as they are: everything
/// up to the first `quote`, U+0026 (&), U+0000 NULL, U+000D CR, or surrogate.
pub fn attribute_value_run<T: CodeUnit>(code_units: &[T], quote: u8) -> usize {
    find_first(code_units, [quote, b'&', 0, b'\r'], &mut false)
}

/// Whether any code unit is something other than the ASCII whitespace the tree builder ignores for "frameset-ok".
pub fn contains_non_whitespace<T: CodeUnit>(code_units: &[T]) -> bool {
    code_units
        .iter()
        .any(|&code_unit| !matches!(code_unit.into(), 0x09 | 0x0A | 0x0C | 0x0D | 0x20))
}

/// The number of U+000A LF and of U+000D CR code units.
fn count_line_feeds_and_carriage_returns<T: CodeUnit>(code_units: &[T]) -> (usize, usize) {
    let mut line_feeds = 0;
    let mut carriage_returns = 0;
    let (chunks, remainder) = code_units.as_chunks::<CHUNK_SIZE>();
    for chunk in chunks {
        // NB: A chunk has fewer than 256 code units, so the narrow counters the vector loop wants can't overflow.
        let mut line_feeds_in_chunk = 0u8;
        let mut carriage_returns_in_chunk = 0u8;
        for &code_unit in chunk {
            line_feeds_in_chunk += u8::from(code_unit == T::from(b'\n'));
            carriage_returns_in_chunk += u8::from(code_unit == T::from(b'\r'));
        }
        line_feeds += usize::from(line_feeds_in_chunk);
        carriage_returns += usize::from(carriage_returns_in_chunk);
    }
    for &code_unit in remainder {
        line_feeds += usize::from(code_unit == T::from(b'\n'));
        carriage_returns += usize::from(code_unit == T::from(b'\r'));
    }
    (line_feeds, carriage_returns)
}

#[inline(always)]
fn is_surrogate_pair(high: u16, low: u16) -> bool {
    (0xD800..=0xDBFF).contains(&high) && (0xDC00..=0xDFFF).contains(&low)
}

/// The source position the tokenizer is at after it consumes `code_units` from `position`.
///
/// A line ends at a U+000A LF, a U+000D CR, or the two together, and a column is a code point. `code_units` must
/// start and end between code points, and not between a CR and the LF it belongs with.
pub fn position_after<T: CodeUnit>(position: Position, code_units: &[T]) -> Position {
    let is_line_end = |code_unit: T| code_unit == T::from(b'\n') || code_unit == T::from(b'\r');
    let Some(last_line_end) = code_units.iter().rposition(|&code_unit| is_line_end(code_unit)) else {
        return Position {
            line: position.line,
            column: position.column + code_point_count(code_units) as u64,
        };
    };
    let lines = &code_units[..=last_line_end];
    let (line_feeds, carriage_returns) = count_line_feeds_and_carriage_returns(lines);
    let line_ends = if carriage_returns == 0 {
        line_feeds
    } else {
        // NB: A CR that is followed by an LF ends the same line the LF does.
        let pairs = lines
            .windows(2)
            .filter(|pair| pair[0] == T::from(b'\r') && pair[1] == T::from(b'\n'))
            .count();
        line_feeds + carriage_returns - pairs
    };
    Position {
        line: position.line + line_ends as u64,
        column: code_point_count(&code_units[last_line_end + 1..]) as u64,
    }
}

fn code_point_count<T: CodeUnit>(code_units: &[T]) -> usize {
    let surrogate_pairs = code_units
        .windows(2)
        .filter(|pair| is_surrogate_pair(pair[0].into(), pair[1].into()))
        .count();
    code_units.len() - surrogate_pairs
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn code_units(input: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        input.encode_utf16().collect()
    }

    fn run(length: usize, is_ascii: bool) -> Run {
        Run { length, is_ascii }
    }

    #[test]
    fn data_runs_stop_at_markup_and_characters_the_tokenizer_changes() {
        assert_eq!(data_run(b"plain text" as &[u8]), run(10, true));
        assert_eq!(data_run(b"" as &[u8]), run(0, true));
        assert_eq!(data_run(b"a<b" as &[u8]), run(1, true));
        assert_eq!(data_run(b"a&b" as &[u8]), run(1, true));
        assert_eq!(data_run(b"a\0b" as &[u8]), run(1, true));
        assert_eq!(data_run(b"a\r\nb" as &[u8]), run(1, true));
        assert_eq!(data_run(b"caf\xe9\n<" as &[u8]), run(5, false));
        assert_eq!(data_run(b"caf<\xe9" as &[u8]), run(3, true));
    }

    #[test]
    fn raw_text_runs_go_on_past_ampersands() {
        assert_eq!(raw_text_run(b"a && b < c" as &[u8]), run(7, true));
        assert_eq!(raw_text_run(b"a && b\0" as &[u8]), run(6, true));
        assert_eq!(raw_text_run(b"a\r\n" as &[u8]), run(1, true));
        assert_eq!(raw_text_run(&code_units("a&\u{1f600}</")), run(4, false));
        assert_eq!(raw_text_run::<u16>(&[0x61, 0x26, 0xD83D]), run(2, true));
    }

    #[test]
    fn data_runs_find_stops_and_non_ascii_at_every_offset() {
        // Long enough to put a stop in every place of a block, in the part that is less than a block, and on the
        // seams.
        let length = BLOCK_SIZE * 5 + 7;
        for offset in 0..length {
            let mut input = vec![b'x'; length];
            input[offset] = b'<';
            assert_eq!(data_run(&input), run(offset, true));
            let mut wide: Vec<u16> = input.iter().copied().map(u16::from).collect();
            assert_eq!(data_run(&wide), run(offset, true));

            input[offset] = 0xe9;
            assert_eq!(data_run(&input), run(length, false));
            wide[offset] = 0x2014;
            assert_eq!(data_run(&wide), run(length, false));
        }
        assert_eq!(data_run(&vec![b'x'; length]), run(length, true));
    }

    #[test]
    fn data_runs_take_surrogate_pairs_but_not_lone_surrogates() {
        assert_eq!(data_run(&code_units("a\u{1f600}b\u{1f600}<")), run(6, false));
        assert_eq!(data_run::<u16>(&[0x61, 0xD83D]), run(1, true));
        assert_eq!(data_run::<u16>(&[0x61, 0xD83D, 0x62]), run(1, true));
        assert_eq!(data_run::<u16>(&[0x61, 0xDE00, 0xD83D]), run(1, true));
        assert_eq!(data_run::<u16>(&[0x61, 0xD83D, 0xDE00]), run(3, false));
    }

    #[test]
    fn attribute_value_runs_stop_at_the_quote_and_characters_the_tokenizer_changes() {
        assert_eq!(attribute_value_run(b"a b<c>'d\" e" as &[u8], b'"'), 8);
        assert_eq!(attribute_value_run(b"a b<c>'d\" e" as &[u8], b'\''), 6);
        assert_eq!(attribute_value_run(b"caf\xe9&amp;" as &[u8], b'"'), 4);
        assert_eq!(attribute_value_run(b"a\0" as &[u8], b'"'), 1);
        assert_eq!(attribute_value_run(b"a\r\n" as &[u8], b'"'), 1);
        assert_eq!(attribute_value_run(&code_units("a\u{2014}b\u{1f600}\""), b'"'), 3);
        let length = BLOCK_SIZE * 5 + 7;
        for offset in 0..length {
            let mut input = vec![b'x'; length];
            input[offset] = b'"';
            assert_eq!(attribute_value_run(&input, b'"'), offset);
            assert_eq!(attribute_value_run(&input, b'\''), length);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn finds_non_whitespace() {
        assert!(!contains_non_whitespace(b" \t\n\x0c" as &[u8]));
        assert!(contains_non_whitespace(b" \t\n\x0c." as &[u8]));
        assert!(contains_non_whitespace(&code_units(" \u{a0}")));
    }

    fn position_after_all<T: CodeUnit>(code_units: &[T]) -> (u64, u64) {
        let position = position_after(Position { line: 3, column: 5 }, code_units);
        (position.line, position.column)
    }

    #[test]
    fn columns_count_code_points() {
        assert_eq!(position_after_all(b"" as &[u8]), (3, 5));
        assert_eq!(position_after_all(b"one" as &[u8]), (3, 8));
        assert_eq!(position_after_all(b"caf\xe9" as &[u8]), (3, 9));
        assert_eq!(position_after_all(&code_units("a\u{1f600}\u{e9}")), (3, 8));
        // A surrogate without its other half is a code point of its own.
        assert_eq!(position_after_all::<u16>(&[0xD83D, 0x61, 0xDE00]), (3, 8));
    }

    #[test]
    fn lines_end_at_line_feeds_and_carriage_returns() {
        assert_eq!(position_after_all(b"one\ntwo\nth" as &[u8]), (5, 2));
        assert_eq!(position_after_all(b"one\n" as &[u8]), (4, 0));
        assert_eq!(position_after_all(b"one\r\ntwo\rthree\n\rfour" as &[u8]), (7, 4));
        assert_eq!(position_after_all(b"\r\r\n\n" as &[u8]), (6, 0));
        assert_eq!(position_after_all(&code_units("\u{1f600}\na\u{1f600}\u{e9}")), (4, 3));
        let long = vec![b'\n'; CHUNK_SIZE * 9 + 5];
        assert_eq!(position_after_all(&long), (3 + (CHUNK_SIZE * 9 + 5) as u64, 0));
    }
}

use crate::code_units::CodeUnits;
#[cfg(not(test))]
use ak::Utf16StringUnits;
use ak::Utf16View;
use std::cell::RefCell;

/// Source position in the input.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Position {
    pub line: u64,
    pub column: u64,
}

/// Where in the tokenizer's input something starts or ends, as an offset in code units, or nowhere at all.
///
/// The tokenizer only works out which line and column an offset is at when it is asked to.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct SourceOffset(usize);

impl SourceOffset {
    pub const NONE: Self = Self(usize::MAX);

    pub fn new(offset: usize) -> Self {
        debug_assert!(offset != usize::MAX);
        Self(offset)
    }

    pub fn get(self) -> Option<usize> {
        (self != Self::NONE).then_some(self.0)
    }
}

impl Default for SourceOffset {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::NONE
    }
}

/// A small number that stands for a known tag name, so that the tree builder can tell which of them a token has
/// without comparing names. Every other name has the id `UNKNOWN`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct TagId(u16);

impl TagId {
    pub const UNKNOWN: Self = Self(0);

    pub const fn from_index(index: u16) -> Self {
        Self(index)
    }

    pub const fn index(self) -> usize {
        self.0 as usize
    }

    pub fn for_name(name: &str) -> Self {
        crate::known_names::tag_id_for_name(name.as_bytes())
    }

    pub fn for_code_units(name: Utf16View<'_>) -> Self {
        // NB: Every known tag name is ASCII, so a name with other code units in it is found to be none of them.
        match name {
            Utf16View::Latin1(name) => crate::known_names::tag_id_for_name(name),
            Utf16View::Utf16(_) => Self::UNKNOWN,
        }
    }
}

/// A set of known tag names.
pub struct TagSet([u64; crate::known_names::TAG_SET_WORD_COUNT]);

impl TagSet {
    pub const fn new(ids: &[TagId]) -> Self {
        let mut words = [0; crate::known_names::TAG_SET_WORD_COUNT];
        let mut i = 0;
        while i < ids.len() {
            let index = ids[i].0 as usize;
            assert!(index != 0, "a tag set can only have known tag names in it");
            words[index / 64] |= 1 << (index % 64);
            i += 1;
        }
        Self(words)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub const fn contains(&self, id: TagId) -> bool {
        let index = id.0 as usize;
        (self.0[index / 64] >> (index % 64)) & 1 != 0
    }
}

/// A set of the known tag names it is given, worked out when the parser is compiled.
macro_rules! tag_set {
    ($($name:tt),+ $(,)?) => {
        const { &$crate::token::TagSet::new(&[$($crate::known_names::tag_id!($name)),+]) }
    };
}
pub(crate) use tag_set;

/// A single attribute on a start or end tag token.
///
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Attribute {
    pub local_name: HtmlName,
    pub value: CodeUnits,
    pub name_start_offset: SourceOffset,
    pub name_end_offset: SourceOffset,
    pub value_start_offset: SourceOffset,
    pub value_end_offset: SourceOffset,
}

const MAX_SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_LISTS: usize = 4;
const MAX_SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUES: usize = 64;
// Buffers grown past these sizes by an unusually large tag are freed rather than kept, so the spare
// set retains at most a few hundred KiB after the parser that filled it is gone.
const MAX_SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_LIST_CAPACITY: usize = 64;
const MAX_SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_CAPACITY: usize = 4096;

thread_local! {
    // Dropped tag tokens leave their attribute lists and value buffers here for the next tag.
    static SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_LISTS: RefCell<Vec<Vec<Attribute>>> = const { RefCell::new(Vec::new()) };
    static SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUES: RefCell<Vec<CodeUnits>> = const { RefCell::new(Vec::new()) };
}

/// The attributes of a tag token, backed by a spare buffer when there is one and the tag has attributes.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct AttributeList(Vec<Attribute>);

impl AttributeList {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self(Vec::new())
    }

    /// Adds an empty attribute, with a spare value buffer when a dropped tag token left one.
    pub fn start_new_attribute(&mut self) {
        // NB: Most tags have no attributes, so a list only takes a spare buffer once it has an attribute to hold.
        if self.0.capacity() == 0 {
            self.0 = SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_LISTS.with_borrow_mut(Vec::pop).unwrap_or_default();
        }
        self.0.push(Attribute {
            value: SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUES.with_borrow_mut(Vec::pop).unwrap_or_default(),
            ..Default::default()
        });
    }
}

impl Default for AttributeList {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl Clone for AttributeList {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self(self.0.clone())
    }
}

impl std::ops::Deref for AttributeList {
    type Target = Vec<Attribute>;

    fn deref(&self) -> &Vec<Attribute> {
        &self.0
    }
}

impl std::ops::DerefMut for AttributeList {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Vec<Attribute> {
        &mut self.0
    }
}

impl IntoIterator for AttributeList {
    type Item = Attribute;
    type IntoIter = std::vec::IntoIter<Attribute>;

    fn into_iter(mut self) -> Self::IntoIter {
        std::mem::take(&mut self.0).into_iter()
    }
}

impl<'a> IntoIterator for &'a AttributeList {
    type Item = &'a Attribute;
    type IntoIter = std::slice::Iter<'a, Attribute>;

    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
        self.0.iter()
    }
}

impl Drop for AttributeList {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if self.0.capacity() == 0 {
            return;
        }
        SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUES.with_borrow_mut(|spare_values| {
            for attribute in self.0.drain(..) {
                if spare_values.len() == MAX_SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUES {
                    break;
                }
                let mut value = attribute.value;
                value.clear();
                let capacity = value.capacity();
                if capacity == 0 || capacity > MAX_SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_CAPACITY {
                    continue;
                }
                spare_values.push(value);
            }
        });
        if self.0.capacity() > MAX_SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_LIST_CAPACITY {
            return;
        }
        SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_LISTS.with_borrow_mut(|spare_lists| {
            if spare_lists.len() < MAX_SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_LISTS {
                spare_lists.push(std::mem::take(&mut self.0));
            }
        });
    }
}

#[cfg(not(test))]
#[derive(Clone, Default, Eq)]
pub struct HtmlName(ak::Utf16FlyString);

// Standalone Rust test binaries have no C++ fly-string table to own these names.
#[cfg(test)]
#[derive(Clone, Default, Eq)]
pub struct HtmlName(String);

#[cfg(not(test))]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct KnownName(usize);

#[cfg(test)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum KnownName {
    Raw(usize),
    Literal(&'static str),
}

impl KnownName {
    pub const fn from_raw(raw: usize) -> Self {
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        {
            Self(raw)
        }
        #[cfg(test)]
        {
            Self::Raw(raw)
        }
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    pub const fn from_literal(name: &'static str) -> Self {
        Self::Literal(name)
    }

    /// The identity of the C++ `Utf16FlyString` that holds this name.
    #[cfg(not(test))]
    pub const fn raw_identity(self) -> usize {
        self.0
    }
}

impl HtmlName {
    pub fn from_code_units(name: Utf16View<'_>) -> Self {
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        {
            match name.as_ascii() {
                // SAFETY: ASCII is valid UTF-8.
                Some(name) => Self(ak::Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(unsafe { str::from_utf8_unchecked(name) })),
                None => Self(ak::Utf16FlyString::from_utf16(&name.to_utf16())),
            }
        }
        #[cfg(test)]
        {
            Self(String::from_utf16_lossy(&name.to_utf16()))
        }
    }

    pub fn from_utf8(name: &str) -> Self {
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        {
            Self(ak::Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(name))
        }
        #[cfg(test)]
        {
            Self(name.to_string())
        }
    }

    /// Borrow an existing C++ `Utf16FlyString` identity.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// `raw` must identify a live `Utf16FlyString` for the duration of this call.
    pub unsafe fn from_borrowed_raw(raw: usize) -> Self {
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        {
            unsafe { ak::reference_utf16_string(raw) };
            Self(unsafe { ak::Utf16FlyString::from_raw_owned(raw) })
        }
        #[cfg(test)]
        {
            let _ = raw;
            unreachable!("C++ string identities are unavailable in standalone Rust tests")
        }
    }

    pub fn raw_identity(&self) -> usize {
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        {
            self.0.raw_identity()
        }
        #[cfg(test)]
        {
            0
        }
    }

    pub fn equals(&self, other: &str) -> bool {
        #[cfg(test)]
        return self.0 == other;

        #[cfg(not(test))]
        {
            if let Some(raw) = ak::utf16_short_string_raw(other) {
                return self.raw_identity() == raw;
            }
            match self.0.as_units() {
                Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(units) => units == other.as_bytes(),
                Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(units) => units.iter().map(|&unit| u16::from(unit)).eq(other.encode_utf16()),
                Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => units.iter().copied().eq(other.encode_utf16()),
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn is_one_of(&self, names: &[KnownName]) -> bool {
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        {
            names.contains(&KnownName::from_raw(self.raw_identity()))
        }
        #[cfg(test)]
        {
            names.iter().any(|name| self == name)
        }
    }

    pub fn eq_ignore_ascii_case(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        #[cfg(test)]
        return self.0.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&other.0);

        #[cfg(not(test))]
        {
            match (self.0.as_units(), other.0.as_units()) {
                (
                    Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(left) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(left),
                    Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(right) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(right),
                ) => left.eq_ignore_ascii_case(right),
                (Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(left), Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(right)) => {
                    left.len() == right.len()
                        && left.iter().zip(right).all(|(left, right)| {
                            left == right
                                || (*left <= 0x7f
                                    && *right <= 0x7f
                                    && (*left as u8).eq_ignore_ascii_case(&(*right as u8)))
                        })
                }
                (Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(left) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(left), Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(right))
                | (Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(right), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(left) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(left)) => {
                    left.len() == right.len()
                        && left.iter().zip(right).all(|(left, right)| {
                            u16::from(*left) == *right || (*right <= 0x7f && left.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&(*right as u8)))
                        })
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

impl PartialEq<KnownName> for HtmlName {
    fn eq(&self, other: &KnownName) -> bool {
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        {
            self.raw_identity() == other.0
        }
        #[cfg(test)]
        {
            match other {
                KnownName::Raw(raw) => self.raw_identity() == *raw,
                KnownName::Literal(name) => self.0 == *name,
            }
        }
    }
}

impl PartialEq<HtmlName> for KnownName {
    fn eq(&self, other: &HtmlName) -> bool {
        other == self
    }
}

impl PartialEq for HtmlName {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.0 == other.0
    }
}

impl PartialEq<str> for HtmlName {
    fn eq(&self, other: &str) -> bool {
        self.equals(other)
    }
}

impl PartialEq<&str> for HtmlName {
    fn eq(&self, other: &&str) -> bool {
        self.equals(other)
    }
}

impl PartialEq<&HtmlName> for HtmlName {
    fn eq(&self, other: &&HtmlName) -> bool {
        self == *other
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for HtmlName {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        {
            formatter.debug_tuple("HtmlName").field(&self.0.raw_identity()).finish()
        }
        #[cfg(test)]
        {
            formatter.debug_tuple("HtmlName").field(&self.0).finish()
        }
    }
}

/// Data specific to DOCTYPE tokens.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct DoctypeData {
    pub name: CodeUnits,
    pub public_identifier: CodeUnits,
    pub system_identifier: CodeUnits,
    pub missing_name: bool,
    pub missing_public_identifier: bool,
    pub missing_system_identifier: bool,
    pub force_quirks: bool,
}

/// The type of an HTML token.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum TokenType {
    #[default]
    Invalid = 0,
    Doctype = 1,
    StartTag = 2,
    EndTag = 3,
    Comment = 4,
    Character = 5,
    EndOfFile = 6,
}

/// Type-specific data for an HTML token.
///
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub enum TokenPayload {
    #[default]
    None,
    Tag {
        tag_name: HtmlName,
        tag_id: TagId,
        self_closing: bool,
        // AD-HOC: See AD-HOC comment on Element.m_had_duplicate_attribute_during_tokenization about why this is tracked.
        had_duplicate_attribute: bool,
        attributes: AttributeList,
    },
    Comment(CodeUnits),
    Doctype(Box<DoctypeData>),
}

/// An HTML token produced by the tokenizer.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Token {
    pub token_type: TokenType,
    pub code_point: u32,
    pub payload: TokenPayload,
    pub start_offset: SourceOffset,
    pub end_offset: SourceOffset,
}

impl Token {
    pub fn new_character(code_point: u32) -> Self {
        Token {
            token_type: TokenType::Character,
            code_point,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    pub fn new_eof() -> Self {
        Token {
            token_type: TokenType::EndOfFile,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn tag_name(&self) -> &HtmlName {
        match &self.payload {
            TokenPayload::Tag { tag_name, .. } => tag_name,
            _ => panic!("tag_name called on non-tag token"),
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn tag_id(&self) -> TagId {
        match &self.payload {
            TokenPayload::Tag { tag_id, .. } => *tag_id,
            _ => panic!("tag_id called on non-tag token"),
        }
    }

    pub fn set_tag_name(&mut self, name: Utf16View<'_>) {
        match &mut self.payload {
            TokenPayload::Tag { tag_name, tag_id, .. } => {
                *tag_name = HtmlName::from_code_units(name);
                *tag_id = TagId::for_code_units(name);
            }
            _ => panic!("set_tag_name called on non-tag token"),
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn set_self_closing(&mut self, value: bool) {
        match &mut self.payload {
            TokenPayload::Tag { self_closing, .. } => *self_closing = value,
            _ => panic!("set_self_closing called on non-tag token"),
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn is_self_closing(&self) -> bool {
        match &self.payload {
            TokenPayload::Tag { self_closing, .. } => *self_closing,
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn had_duplicate_attribute(&self) -> bool {
        match &self.payload {
            TokenPayload::Tag {
                had_duplicate_attribute,
                ..
            } => *had_duplicate_attribute,
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn start_new_attribute(&mut self) {
        match &mut self.payload {
            TokenPayload::Tag { attributes, .. } => attributes.start_new_attribute(),
            _ => panic!("start_new_attribute called on non-tag token"),
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn attributes_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Vec<Attribute> {
        match &mut self.payload {
            TokenPayload::Tag { attributes, .. } => &mut attributes.0,
            _ => panic!("attributes_mut called on non-tag token"),
        }
    }

    pub fn normalize_attributes(&mut self) {
        let TokenPayload::Tag {
            attributes,
            had_duplicate_attribute,
            ..
        } = &mut self.payload
        else {
            return;
        };

        let mut i = 0;
        while i < attributes.len() {
            let is_duplicate = (0..i).any(|seen_index| attributes[seen_index].local_name == attributes[i].local_name);
            if is_duplicate {
                *had_duplicate_attribute = true;
                attributes.remove(i);
            } else {
                i += 1;
            }
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn set_comment_data(&mut self, data: CodeUnits) {
        match &mut self.payload {
            TokenPayload::Comment(s) => *s = data,
            _ => panic!("set_comment_data called on non-comment token"),
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn doctype_data_mut(&mut self) -> &mut DoctypeData {
        match &mut self.payload {
            TokenPayload::Doctype(dd) => dd,
            _ => panic!("doctype_data_mut called on non-doctype token"),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod spare_buffer_tests {
    use super::*;

    fn clear_spare_buffers() {
        SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_LISTS.with_borrow_mut(Vec::clear);
        SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUES.with_borrow_mut(Vec::clear);
    }

    fn spare_value_capacities() -> Vec<usize> {
        SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUES.with_borrow(|values| values.iter().map(CodeUnits::capacity).collect())
    }

    fn spare_list_capacities() -> Vec<usize> {
        SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_LISTS.with_borrow(|lists| lists.iter().map(Vec::capacity).collect())
    }

    fn attribute_with_value_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Attribute {
        Attribute {
            value: CodeUnits::Latin1(Vec::with_capacity(capacity)),
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn dropped_lists_keep_small_buffers_for_the_next_tag() {
        clear_spare_buffers();
        let mut list = AttributeList::new();
        list.push(attribute_with_value_capacity(16));
        list.push(attribute_with_value_capacity(MAX_SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_CAPACITY));
        drop(list);
        assert_eq!(spare_value_capacities().len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(spare_list_capacities().len(), 1);
        let mut list = AttributeList::new();
        assert_eq!(list.capacity(), 0);
        assert_eq!(spare_list_capacities().len(), 1);
        list.start_new_attribute();
        assert!(list.capacity() >= 2);
        assert!(list[0].value.capacity() >= 16);
        assert!(spare_list_capacities().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn oversized_value_buffers_are_freed() {
        clear_spare_buffers();
        let mut list = AttributeList::new();
        list.push(attribute_with_value_capacity(MAX_SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_CAPACITY + 1));
        list.push(attribute_with_value_capacity(1 << 20));
        drop(list);
        assert!(spare_value_capacities().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn oversized_lists_are_freed() {
        clear_spare_buffers();
        let mut list = AttributeList::new();
        list.reserve(MAX_SPARE_ATTRIBUTE_LIST_CAPACITY + 1);
        list.push(attribute_with_value_capacity(16));
        drop(list);
        assert!(spare_list_capacities().is_empty());
        assert_eq!(spare_value_capacities().len(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_value_buffers_are_not_retained() {
        clear_spare_buffers();
        let mut list = AttributeList::new();
        list.push(Attribute::default());
        drop(list);
        assert!(spare_value_capacities().is_empty());
    }
}

            }
            value if value == Self::AfterDOCTYPESystemKeyword as u8 => Self::AfterDOCTYPESystemKeyword,
            value if value == Self::BeforeDOCTYPESystemIdentifier as u8 => Self::BeforeDOCTYPESystemIdentifier,
            value if value == Self::DOCTYPESystemIdentifierDoubleQuoted as u8 => {
                Self::DOCTYPESystemIdentifierDoubleQuoted
            }
            value if value == Self::DOCTYPESystemIdentifierSingleQuoted as u8 => {
                Self::DOCTYPESystemIdentifierSingleQuoted
            }
            value if value == Self::AfterDOCTYPESystemIdentifier as u8 => Self::AfterDOCTYPESystemIdentifier,
            value if value == Self::BogusDOCTYPE as u8 => Self::BogusDOCTYPE,
            value if value == Self::CDATASection as u8 => Self::CDATASection,
            value if value == Self::CDATASectionBracket as u8 => Self::CDATASectionBracket,
            value if value == Self::CDATASectionEnd as u8 => Self::CDATASectionEnd,
            value if value == Self::CharacterReference as u8 => Self::CharacterReference,
            value if value == Self::NamedCharacterReference as u8 => Self::NamedCharacterReference,
            value if value == Self::AmbiguousAmpersand as u8 => Self::AmbiguousAmpersand,
            value if value == Self::NumericCharacterReference as u8 => Self::NumericCharacterReference,
            value if value == Self::HexadecimalCharacterReferenceStart as u8 => {
                Self::HexadecimalCharacterReferenceStart
            }
            value if value == Self::DecimalCharacterReferenceStart as u8 => Self::DecimalCharacterReferenceStart,
            value if value == Self::HexadecimalCharacterReference as u8 => Self::HexadecimalCharacterReference,
            value if value == Self::DecimalCharacterReference as u8 => Self::DecimalCharacterReference,
            value if value == Self::NumericCharacterReferenceEnd as u8 => Self::NumericCharacterReferenceEnd,
            _ => return None,
        })
    }
}

/// The lines and columns of offsets into the input, which are only worked out when something asks for them.
#[derive(Default)]
struct SourcePositions {
    /// The position of the start of the input buffer, which stops being the start of the input once consumed input
    /// is discarded.
    start: Position,
    /// The last offset a position was worked out for, and that position. Offsets are mostly asked about in
    /// increasing order, so the next one is usually found by going on from here.
    known_offset: usize,
    known_position: Position,
}

/// The HTML tokenizer state machine.
///
/// Implements the WHATWG HTML tokenizer specification (section 13.2.5).
pub struct HtmlTokenizer {
    pub state: State,
    return_state: State,
    pub input: CodeUnits,
    pub current_offset: usize,
    prev_offset: usize,
    current_token: Token,
    current_builder: CodeUnits,
    pub queued_tokens: VecDeque<Token>,
    temporary_buffer: Vec<u32>,
    character_reference_code: u32,
    last_emitted_start_tag_name: Option<HtmlName>,
    source_positions: SourcePositions,
    has_emitted_eof: bool,
    aborted: bool,
    insertion_point: Option<usize>,
    old_insertion_points: Vec<Option<usize>>,
    input_stream_closed: bool,
    stop_at_insertion_point: bool,
    cdata_allowed: bool,
    entity_matcher: NamedCharacterReferenceMatcher,
    // Where the input that a speculative HTML parser's preload scanner has been given ends, while it's still a place
    // the scanner can go on from.
    speculative_scan_end: Option<usize>,
}

#[inline]
fn is_ascii_alpha(c: u32) -> bool {
    matches!(c, 0x41..=0x5A | 0x61..=0x7A)
}

#[inline]
fn is_ascii_upper_alpha(c: u32) -> bool {
    matches!(c, 0x41..=0x5A)
}

#[inline]
fn is_ascii_digit(c: u32) -> bool {
    matches!(c, 0x30..=0x39)
}

#[inline]
fn is_ascii_hex_digit(c: u32) -> bool {
    matches!(c, 0x30..=0x39 | 0x41..=0x46 | 0x61..=0x66)
}

#[inline]
fn is_ascii_alphanumeric(c: u32) -> bool {
    is_ascii_alpha(c) || is_ascii_digit(c)
}

#[inline]
fn to_ascii_lowercase(c: u32) -> u32 {
    if is_ascii_upper_alpha(c) { c + 0x20 } else { c }
}

/// Reads the tag whose "<" ends right before `offset` into `token`, and returns the offset after its ">", if the tag
/// is as plain as `HtmlTokenizer::try_scan_tag` describes and all of it is in `input`.
fn scan_tag<T: scan::CodeUnit>(input: &[T], mut offset: usize, token: &mut Token) -> Option<usize> {
    // NB: U+0000 NULL, which nothing here takes, stands in for the end of the input.
    let at = |offset: usize| -> u16 { input.get(offset).map_or(0, |&code_unit| code_unit.into()) };
    let is_tag_whitespace = |code_unit: u16| matches!(code_unit, 0x09 | 0x0A | 0x0C | 0x20);
    let is_tag_end = |code_unit: u16| matches!(code_unit, 0x09 | 0x0A | 0x0C | 0x20 | 0x2F | 0x3E);

    let is_end_tag = at(offset) == 0x2F;
    if is_end_tag {
        offset += 1;
    }

    let name_start = offset;
    if !matches!(at(offset), 0x61..=0x7A) {
        return None;
    }
    offset += 1;
    while matches!(at(offset), 0x61..=0x7A | 0x30..=0x39 | 0x2D) {
        offset += 1;
    }
    if !is_tag_end(at(offset)) {
        return None;
    }
    let mut name_buffer = [0; 64];
    let name = Utf16View::Latin1(scan::ascii_name_bytes(&input[name_start..offset], &mut name_buffer)?);
    *token = Token {
        token_type: if is_end_tag {
            TokenType::EndTag
        } else {
            TokenType::StartTag
        },
        code_point: 0,
        payload: TokenPayload::Tag {
            tag_name: HtmlName::from_code_units(name),
            tag_id: crate::token::TagId::for_code_units(name),
            self_closing: false,
            had_duplicate_attribute: false,
            attributes: crate::token::AttributeList::new(),
        },
        start_offset: SourceOffset::new(name_start),
        end_offset: SourceOffset::NONE,
    };
    let TokenPayload::Tag {
        attributes,
        self_closing,
        ..
    } = &mut token.payload
    else {
        unreachable!();
    };

    loop {
        let after_whitespace = offset;
        while is_tag_whitespace(at(offset)) {
            offset += 1;
        }
        match at(offset) {
            0x3E => return Some(offset + 1),
            0x2F if !is_end_tag && at(offset + 1) == 0x3E => {
                *self_closing = true;
                return Some(offset + 2);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        // NB: An attribute comes after whitespace, and an end tag with attributes is a parse error.
        if is_end_tag || offset == after_whitespace {
            return None;
        }

        let name_start = offset;
        while matches!(at(offset), 0x61..=0x7A | 0x30..=0x39 | 0x2D | 0x2E | 0x3A | 0x5F) {
            offset += 1;
        }
        if offset == name_start || !(is_tag_end(at(offset)) || at(offset) == 0x3D) {
            return None;
        }
        let name = Utf16View::Latin1(scan::ascii_name_bytes(&input[name_start..offset], &mut name_buffer)?);
        attributes.start_new_attribute();
        let attribute = attributes.last_mut().unwrap();
        attribute.local_name = HtmlName::from_code_units(name);
        attribute.name_start_offset = SourceOffset::new(name_start);
        attribute.name_end_offset = SourceOffset::new(offset);

        let mut after_name = offset;
        while is_tag_whitespace(at(after_name)) {
            after_name += 1;
        }
        if at(after_name) != 0x3D {
            // NB: The attribute has no value, and the whitespace after it is that before what comes next.
            continue;
        }
        offset = after_name + 1;
        while is_tag_whitespace(at(offset)) {
            offset += 1;
        }

        let quote = at(offset);
        attribute.value_start_offset = SourceOffset::new(offset);
        if quote == 0x22 || quote == 0x27 {
            offset += 1;
            let length = scan::attribute_value_run(&input[offset..], quote as u8);
            if at(offset + length) != quote {
                return None;
            }
            attribute.value.push_slice(T::view(&input[offset..offset + length]));
            offset += length + 1;
            if !is_tag_end(at(offset)) {
                return None;
            }
        } else {
            let value_start = offset;
            loop {
                match at(offset) {
                    0x09 | 0x0A | 0x0C | 0x20 | 0x3E => break,
                    0x00 | 0x0D | 0x22 | 0x26 | 0x27 | 0x3C | 0x3D | 0x60 | 0xD800..=0xDFFF => return None,
                    _ => offset += 1,
                }
            }
            if offset == value_start {
                return None;
            }
            attribute.value.push_slice(T::view(&input[value_start..offset]));
        }
        attribute.value_end_offset = SourceOffset::new(offset);
    }
}

#[inline]
fn is_whitespace(c: u32) -> bool {
    matches!(c, 0x09 | 0x0A | 0x0C | 0x20)
}

/// Numeric character reference replacement table.
/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#table-charref-overrides
fn numeric_char_ref_replacement(code: u32) -> Option<u32> {
    match code {
        0x80 => Some(0x20AC),
        0x82 => Some(0x201A),
        0x83 => Some(0x0192),
        0x84 => Some(0x201E),
        0x85 => Some(0x2026),
        0x86 => Some(0x2020),
        0x87 => Some(0x2021),
        0x88 => Some(0x02C6),
        0x89 => Some(0x2030),
        0x8A => Some(0x0160),
        0x8B => Some(0x2039),
        0x8C => Some(0x0152),
        0x8E => Some(0x017D),
        0x91 => Some(0x2018),
        0x92 => Some(0x2019),
        0x93 => Some(0x201C),
        0x94 => Some(0x201D),
        0x95 => Some(0x2022),
        0x96 => Some(0x2013),
        0x97 => Some(0x2014),
        0x98 => Some(0x02DC),
        0x99 => Some(0x2122),
        0x9A => Some(0x0161),
        0x9B => Some(0x203A),
        0x9C => Some(0x0153),
        0x9E => Some(0x017E),
        0x9F => Some(0x0178),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Check if a code point is a Unicode surrogate.
fn is_surrogate(c: u32) -> bool {
    (0xD800..=0xDFFF).contains(&c)
}

#[inline]
fn is_high_surrogate(code_unit: u16) -> bool {
    (0xD800..=0xDBFF).contains(&code_unit)
}

/// Check if a code point is a Unicode noncharacter.
fn is_noncharacter(c: u32) -> bool {
    (0xFDD0..=0xFDEF).contains(&c) || matches!(c & 0xFFFF, 0xFFFE | 0xFFFF)
}

#[inline]
fn is_ascii_lower_alpha(c: u32) -> bool {
    matches!(c, 0x61..=0x7A)
}

/// What ends a run of text that a state emits as it is, besides U+0000 NULL, U+000D CR and lone surrogates.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq)]
enum TextRunStops {
    /// U+003C (<).
    Markup,
    /// U+003C (<) and U+0026 (&).
    MarkupAndCharacterReferences,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum CharacterReferenceContext {
    Data,
    Attribute,
}

/// Decode references in text supplied by another tokenizer. Only an ampersand enters the HTML state machine;
/// literal code units, including line endings and unpaired surrogates, belong to the caller's input.
pub fn decode_character_references(input: &[u16], context: CharacterReferenceContext) -> Cow<'_, [u16]> {
    let ampersand = u16::from(b'&');
    let Some(mut start) = input.iter().position(|&unit| unit == ampersand) else {
        return Cow::Borrowed(input);
    };
    let mut tokenizer = HtmlTokenizer::new(input.to_vec());
    tokenizer.return_state = match context {
        CharacterReferenceContext::Data => State::Data,
        CharacterReferenceContext::Attribute => State::AttributeValueUnquoted,
    };
    let mut output = Vec::with_capacity(input.len());
    output.extend_from_slice(&input[..start]);
    loop {
        tokenizer.current_offset = start + 1;
        tokenizer.state = State::CharacterReference;
        let mut token = Token::default();
        let first = tokenizer
            .next_token_into_impl::<true>(&mut token, false, false)
            .then_some(token);
        for token in first.into_iter().chain(tokenizer.queued_tokens.drain(..)) {
            debug_assert_eq!(token.token_type, TokenType::Character);
            let character = char::from_u32(token.code_point).expect("a character reference emits scalar values");
            output.extend_from_slice(character.encode_utf16(&mut [0; 2]));
        }
        output.extend(tokenizer.current_builder.as_slice().code_units());
        tokenizer.current_builder.clear();

        let remaining = &input[tokenizer.current_offset..];
        let Some(next) = remaining.iter().position(|&unit| unit == ampersand) else {
            output.extend_from_slice(remaining);
            return Cow::Owned(output);
        };
        output.extend_from_slice(&remaining[..next]);
        start = tokenizer.current_offset + next;
    }
}

impl HtmlTokenizer {
    /// Create a new tokenizer for the given input.
    pub fn new(input: impl Into<CodeUnits>) -> Self {
        HtmlTokenizer {
            state: State::Data,
            return_state: State::Data,
            input: input.into(),
            current_offset: 0,
            prev_offset: 0,
            current_token: Token::default(),
            current_builder: CodeUnits::new(),
            queued_tokens: VecDeque::new(),
            temporary_buffer: Vec::new(),
            character_reference_code: 0,
            last_emitted_start_tag_name: None,
            source_positions: SourcePositions::default(),
            has_emitted_eof: false,
            aborted: false,
            insertion_point: None,
            old_insertion_points: Vec::new(),
            input_stream_closed: true,
            stop_at_insertion_point: false,
            cdata_allowed: false,
            entity_matcher: NamedCharacterReferenceMatcher::new(),
            speculative_scan_end: None,
        }
    }

    /// Set the tokenizer state.
    pub fn switch_to(&mut self, state: State) {
        self.state = state;
    }

    // -- Insertion point management --

    pub fn store_insertion_point(&mut self) {
        self.old_insertion_points.push(self.insertion_point);
    }

    pub fn restore_insertion_point(&mut self) {
        self.insertion_point = self.old_insertion_points.pop().unwrap_or(None);
    }

    pub fn update_insertion_point(&mut self) {
        self.insertion_point = Some(self.current_offset);
    }

    pub fn undefine_insertion_point(&mut self) {
        self.insertion_point = None;
    }

    /// Undefine the insertion point along with every old insertion point that is waiting to be restored.
    pub fn discard_insertion_points(&mut self) {
        self.insertion_point = None;
        self.old_insertion_points.fill(None);
    }

    pub fn is_insertion_point_defined(&self) -> bool {
        self.insertion_point.is_some()
    }

    pub fn is_insertion_point_reached(&self) -> bool {
        self.insertion_point
            .is_some_and(|insertion_point| self.current_offset >= insertion_point)
    }

    pub fn append_input(&mut self, code_units: Utf16View<'_>) {
        self.input.append(code_units);
    }

    pub fn insert_input_at_insertion_point(&mut self, code_units: Utf16View<'_>) {
        if let Some(ip) = self.insertion_point {
            let ip = ip.min(self.input.len());
            self.input.insert(ip, code_units);
            self.insertion_point = Some(ip + code_units.len());
            self.forget_speculative_scan_end_before(ip);
            // NB: A line feed inserted right after a carriage return becomes part of its line end.
            if ip <= self.source_positions.known_offset {
                self.source_positions.known_offset = 0;
                self.source_positions.known_position = self.source_positions.start;
            }
            for old_insertion_point in &mut self.old_insertion_points {
                if let Some(old_ip) = old_insertion_point
                    && ip <= *old_ip
                {
                    *old_ip += code_units.len();
                }
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn unparsed_input(&self) -> Utf16View<'_> {
        self.input.slice_from(self.current_offset)
    }

    /// The input a speculative HTML parser's preload scanner hasn't been given yet, and whether the scanner can go on
    /// from where it stopped. It can't once this tokenizer has got past that point, or input was inserted before it;
    /// the input then runs from the current position, and the scanner has to start over there.
    pub fn input_for_speculative_scan(&mut self) -> (Utf16View<'_>, bool) {
        let (start, continues) = match self.speculative_scan_end {
            Some(end) if end >= self.current_offset => (end, true),
            _ => (self.current_offset, false),
        };
        self.speculative_scan_end = Some(self.input.len());
        (self.input.slice_from(start), continues)
    }

    /// Makes the next speculative scan start over at the current position.
    pub fn forget_speculative_scan_end(&mut self) {
        self.speculative_scan_end = None;
    }

    fn forget_speculative_scan_end_before(&mut self, offset: usize) {
        if self.speculative_scan_end.is_some_and(|end| offset < end) {
            self.speculative_scan_end = None;
        }
    }

    fn can_discard_consumed_input(&self) -> bool {
        if self.current_offset == 0 || self.current_offset != self.input.len() {
            return false;
        }

        // Tokens say where they are with offsets into the input.
        if !self.queued_tokens.is_empty() {
            return false;
        }

        // A token that isn't finished has such offsets too, and the states that lead up to one work out where it
        // starts from where they are, so the input stays until the tokenizer is back between tokens.
        let is_between_tokens = matches!(
            self.state,
            State::Data
                | State::RCDATA
                | State::RAWTEXT
                | State::ScriptData
                | State::PLAINTEXT
                | State::ScriptDataEscaped
                | State::ScriptDataDoubleEscaped
                | State::CDATASection
        );
        if !is_between_tokens {
            return false;
        }

        if self.insertion_point.is_some_and(|insertion_point| insertion_point != 0)
            || !self.old_insertion_points.is_empty()
        {
            return false;
        }

        true
    }

    pub fn parser_did_run(&mut self) {
        if !self.can_discard_consumed_input() {
            return;
        }

        // All of the input is consumed, so a preload scanner that has been given all of it can still go on from there.
        self.speculative_scan_end = self
            .speculative_scan_end
            .filter(|end| *end == self.input.len())
            .map(|_| 0);
        let end_position = self.position_at(SourceOffset::new(self.input.len()));
        self.source_positions = SourcePositions {
            start: end_position,
            known_offset: 0,
            known_position: end_position,
        };
        self.input = CodeUnits::default();
        self.current_offset = 0;
        self.prev_offset = 0;
    }

    pub fn insert_eof(&mut self) {
        self.input_stream_closed = true;
    }

    pub fn set_input_stream_closed(&mut self, closed: bool) {
        self.input_stream_closed = closed;
    }

    pub fn abort(&mut self) {
        self.aborted = true;
    }

    // -- Input helpers --

    #[inline]
    fn peek_code_point(&self, offset: isize) -> Option<u32> {
        let idx = self.current_offset as isize + offset;
        if idx < 0 || idx as usize >= self.input.len() {
            return None;
        }
        if self.stop_at_insertion_point
            && let Some(ip) = self.insertion_point
            && idx as usize >= ip
        {
            return None;
        }
        self.code_point_at(idx as usize).map(|(code_point, _)| code_point)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn code_point_at(&self, offset: usize) -> Option<(u32, usize)> {
        let limit = self.fast_scan_limit();
        let first = self.input.get(offset)?;
        if is_high_surrogate(first) {
            if offset + 1 < limit {
                let second = self.input.code_unit_at(offset + 1);
                if (0xDC00..=0xDFFF).contains(&second) {
                    let code_point = 0x10000 + ((u32::from(first) - 0xD800) << 10) + (u32::from(second) - 0xDC00);
                    return Some((code_point, 2));
                }
            }
            return Some((0xFFFD, 1));
        }
        if (0xDC00..=0xDFFF).contains(&first) {
            return Some((0xFFFD, 1));
        }
        Some((u32::from(first), 1))
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn advance(&mut self, code_unit_count: usize) {
        self.prev_offset = self.current_offset;
        self.current_offset += code_unit_count;
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn skip_ascii(&mut self, count: usize) {
        debug_assert!(
            (self.current_offset..self.current_offset + count).all(|offset| self.input.code_unit_at(offset) < 0x80)
        );
        self.current_offset += count;
        self.prev_offset = self.current_offset - 1;
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn next_code_point(&mut self) -> Option<u32> {
        if self.current_offset >= self.input.len() {
            self.prev_offset = self.current_offset;
            return None;
        }
        let (cp, code_unit_count) = self.code_point_at(self.current_offset)?;
        if cp != 0x0D {
            self.advance(code_unit_count);
            return Some(cp);
        }
        // Slow path: CR normalization
        let next = self.peek_code_point(1).unwrap_or(0);
        if next == 0x0A {
            self.advance(2);
        } else {
            self.advance(1);
        }
        Some(0x0A)
    }

    /// Where the code point that was consumed last starts.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn offset_before_last_code_point(&self) -> SourceOffset {
        let offset = self.current_offset;
        if offset < 2 {
            return SourceOffset::new(0);
        }
        let last = self.input.code_unit_at(offset - 1);
        let second_to_last = self.input.code_unit_at(offset - 2);
        // NB: A CR and the LF after it are consumed as one line feed, and a surrogate pair is one code point.
        let is_one_code_point = (second_to_last == 0x0D && last == 0x0A)
            || (is_high_surrogate(second_to_last) && (0xDC00..=0xDFFF).contains(&last));
        SourceOffset::new(offset - if is_one_code_point { 2 } else { 1 })
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn offset(&self) -> SourceOffset {
        SourceOffset::new(self.current_offset)
    }

    /// The line and column of an offset into the input, which must not be in the middle of a code point.
    pub fn position_at(&mut self, offset: SourceOffset) -> Position {
        let Some(offset) = offset.get() else {
            return Position::default();
        };
        let offset = offset.min(self.input.len());
        let positions = &mut self.source_positions;
        if offset < positions.known_offset {
            positions.known_offset = 0;
            positions.known_position = positions.start;
        }
        let range = positions.known_offset..offset;
        positions.known_position = match &self.input {
            CodeUnits::Latin1(code_units) => scan::position_after(positions.known_position, &code_units[range]),
            CodeUnits::Utf16(code_units) => scan::position_after(positions.known_position, &code_units[range]),
        };
        positions.known_offset = offset;
        positions.known_position
    }

    /// Fast-path character emission from the Data state: if the tokenizer
    /// is positioned at a plain-text code point (not `<`, `&`, NUL, CR,
    /// or any non-ASCII character) and the queue is empty, advance one
    /// code point and return it, skipping the
    /// full `next_token` state-machine dispatch and Token construction.
    /// Returns None if the slow path is required.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn try_fast_data_char(&mut self) -> Option<u32> {
        if self.aborted {
            return None;
        }
        if self.state as u8 != State::Data as u8 {
            return None;
        }
        if !self.queued_tokens.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        if self.current_offset >= self.input.len() {
            return None;
        }
        let cp = u32::from(self.input.code_unit_at(self.current_offset));
        if cp == 0x3C || cp == 0x26 || cp == 0x00 || cp == 0x0D || cp >= 0x80 {
            return None;
        }
        self.prev_offset = self.current_offset;
        self.current_offset += 1;
        Some(cp)
    }

    /// Consume the run of input at the current position that the Data state would emit unchanged, one character
    /// token per code point, and return where in the input it is. The caller can take the text straight from the
    /// input instead of having a `Token` constructed and dispatched for each code point.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn try_fast_data_run(&mut self) -> Option<InputRun> {
        if !self.has_fast_data_run() {
            return None;
        }
        Some(self.take_text_run(TextRunStops::MarkupAndCharacterReferences))
    }

    /// Whether `try_fast_data_run()` would return a run.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn has_fast_data_run(&self) -> bool {
        self.state == State::Data && self.has_text_run(TextRunStops::MarkupAndCharacterReferences)
    }

    /// Like `try_fast_data_run()`, for the text of an element whose content isn't markup: what the RCDATA, RAWTEXT
    /// and script data states would emit unchanged.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn try_fast_element_text_run(&mut self) -> Option<InputRun> {
        let stops = self.element_text_run_stops()?;
        if !self.has_text_run(stops) {
            return None;
        }
        Some(self.take_text_run(stops))
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn element_text_run_stops(&self) -> Option<TextRunStops> {
        match self.state {
            State::RCDATA => Some(TextRunStops::MarkupAndCharacterReferences),
            State::RAWTEXT | State::ScriptData => Some(TextRunStops::Markup),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn has_text_run(&self, stops: TextRunStops) -> bool {
        if self.aborted || !self.queued_tokens.is_empty() {
            return false;
        }
        if self.current_offset >= self.fast_scan_limit() {
            return false;
        }
        // NB: A surrogate pair can be inside a run, but a run that starts with one is left to the slow path, which
        //     knows what to do when the surrogate turns out not to have its other half.
        match self.input.code_unit_at(self.current_offset) {
            0x3C | 0x00 | 0x0D | 0xD800..=0xDFFF => false,
            0x26 => stops == TextRunStops::Markup,
            _ => true,
        }
    }

    fn take_text_run(&mut self, stops: TextRunStops) -> InputRun {
        let start_offset = self.current_offset;
        let limit = self.fast_scan_limit();
        let scan::Run { length, is_ascii } = match (&self.input, stops) {
            (CodeUnits::Latin1(code_units), TextRunStops::MarkupAndCharacterReferences) => {
                scan::data_run(&code_units[start_offset..limit])
            }
            (CodeUnits::Utf16(code_units), TextRunStops::MarkupAndCharacterReferences) => {
                scan::data_run(&code_units[start_offset..limit])
            }
            (CodeUnits::Latin1(code_units), TextRunStops::Markup) => {
                scan::raw_text_run(&code_units[start_offset..limit])
            }
            (CodeUnits::Utf16(code_units), TextRunStops::Markup) => {
                scan::raw_text_run(&code_units[start_offset..limit])
            }
        };
        debug_assert!(length > 0);
        let end_offset = start_offset + length;
        let ends_with_surrogate_pair = (0xDC00..=0xDFFF).contains(&self.input.code_unit_at(end_offset - 1));
        self.prev_offset = end_offset - if ends_with_surrogate_pair { 2 } else { 1 };
        self.current_offset = end_offset;
        InputRun {
            range: start_offset..end_offset,
            is_ascii,
        }
    }

    /// Appends the code units that come next to the attribute value being read, as far as a value in quotes takes
    /// them as they are. This is what the attribute value states do with them one at a time.
    fn append_attribute_value_run(&mut self, quote: u8) {
        let start_offset = self.current_offset;
        let limit = self.fast_scan_limit();
        if start_offset >= limit {
            return;
        }
        let length = match &self.input {
            CodeUnits::Latin1(code_units) => scan::attribute_value_run(&code_units[start_offset..limit], quote),
            CodeUnits::Utf16(code_units) => scan::attribute_value_run(&code_units[start_offset..limit], quote),
        };
        if length == 0 {
            return;
        }
        let end_offset = start_offset + length;
        self.current_builder
            .push_slice(self.input.slice(start_offset..end_offset));
        self.prev_offset = end_offset - 1;
        self.current_offset = end_offset;
    }

    fn restore_to(&mut self, offset: usize) {
        self.current_offset = offset;
    }

    /// OPTIMIZATION: Most tags are written the same plain way: a lowercase name, attributes with lowercase names and
    ///               values that hold no character references, and nothing out of place. Such a tag is read here in
    ///               one go, right after its "<" in the data state, into the token that the tag open state and the
    ///               states after it would have made of it one code point at a time. Any other tag is left to them,
    ///               with nothing consumed.
    fn try_scan_tag(&mut self) -> bool {
        let limit = self.fast_scan_limit();
