namespace Web::PaintTiming {

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html#image-request
// NB: What paint timing needs to know about an image request.
struct ImageRequestInfo {
    Utf16String url;

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html#img-req-data
    // NB: The natural dimensions of the image data, which an image request has once it is available.
    Optional<CSSPixelSize> natural_size;
};

// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#pending-image-record
struct PendingImageRecord {
    // element, an Element
    GC::Ref<DOM::Element> element;

    // request, an image request
    ImageRequestInfo request;

    // loadTime, a DOMHighResTimeStamp
    HighResolutionTime::DOMHighResTimeStamp load_time { 0 };

    void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor&) const;
};

// https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#largest-contentful-paint-candidate
struct LargestContentfulPaintCandidate {
    // element, an element
    // NB: Held weakly, as only the size of the current candidate is read once its element is removed.
    GC::Weak<DOM::Element> element;

    // size, a number
    double size { 0 };

    // width, a number
    double width { 0 };

    // height, a number
    double height { 0 };

    // request, a Request or null
    Optional<ImageRequestInfo> request;

    // loadTime, a number
    HighResolutionTime::DOMHighResTimeStamp load_time { 0 };
};

// NB: The elements that get a text node in their set of owned text nodes for the first time as a frame is painted,
//     with those text nodes.
using PaintedTextNodes = GC::OrderedRootHashMap<GC::Ref<DOM::Element>, GC::RootVector<GC::Ref<DOM::Text>>>;

struct DocumentPaintTimingState {
    // https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#set-of-previously-reported-paints
    // Each Document has a set of previously reported paints, which is an ordered set of strings, initially empty.
    OrderedHashTable<Utf16String> set_of_previously_reported_paints;

    // https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#images-pending-rendering
    // Each Document has an images pending rendering, which is a list of pending image records, initially empty.
    Vector<PendingImageRecord> images_pending_rendering;

    // https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#set-of-elements-with-rendered-text
    // NB: Only whether an element is in the document's set of elements with rendered text is ever asked, so each
    //     element knows whether it is in it. See Element::is_in_set_of_elements_with_rendered_text().

    // NB: The user agent learns that it paints a Text node for the first time from the layout nodes of text nodes: the
    //     layout node arena notes each text layout node that was given new rendered text, as one made for an inserted
    //     text node or one whose text changed is, and the notes are taken as each frame is painted. These are the
    //     taken text layout nodes that were not paintable yet but may be once their style or layout changes, by slot.
    //     A slot whose layout node is gone is dropped the next time the list is looked at, so the list holds nothing of
    //     a removed node.
    Vector<Compositing::RustFFI::NodeSlotId> text_boxes_pending_first_paint;

    // NB: Whether the layout node arena was told to stop noting text layout nodes, once nothing reports them.
    bool stopped_noting_text_boxes { false };

    // https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#current-largest-contentful-paint-candidate
    // A current largest contentful paint candidate, a largest contentful paint candidate or null, initially null.
    Optional<LargestContentfulPaintCandidate> current_largest_contentful_paint_candidate;

    void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor&);
};

}

{
    visitor.visit(element);

static Utf16String const& first_paint_name()
{
    static NeverDestroyed<Utf16String> name { "first-paint"_utf16 };
    return *name;
}

{
    static NeverDestroyed<Utf16String> name { "first-contentful-paint"_utf16 };
    return *name;

// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#non-empty
static bool is_non_empty(Utf16View const& string)
{
    // A DOMString is non-empty if it contains at least one character excluding document white space characters.
    for (auto code_unit : string) {
        if (code_unit != ' ' && code_unit != '\t' && code_unit != '\n' && code_unit != '\r' && code_unit != '\f')
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

static RefPtr<CSS::StyleValue const> style_value_of(CSS::ComputedValuesFFI::ComputedStyleValueHandle const& handle)
{
    if (!handle.pointer)
        return nullptr;
    return CSS::StyleValue::adopt_rust_style_value_data(CSS::StyleValueFFI::rust_style_value_retain(static_cast<CSS::StyleValueFFI::StyleValueData const*>(handle.pointer)));
}

static bool is_zero_length_or_percentage(CSS::StyleValue const& value)
{
    if (value.is_length())
        return value.as_length().raw_value() == 0;
    if (value.is_percentage())
        return value.as_percentage().raw_value() == 0;
    return false;
}

// Whether the used background-size of the given background layer has a zero width or height.
static bool background_size_is_empty(Layout::NodeWithStyle const& node, size_t layer_index)
{
    auto background_size = style_value_of(node.style_group<CSS::ComputedValues::BackgroundValues>().background_size);
    if (!background_size)
        return false;
    if (background_size->is_value_list()) {
        auto const& list = background_size->as_value_list();
        if (list.size() == 0)
            return false;
        background_size = list.value_at(layer_index, true);
    }
    if (!background_size->is_background_size())
        return false;
    auto const& size = background_size->as_background_size();
    return is_zero_length_or_percentage(size.size_x()) || is_zero_length_or_percentage(size.size_y());
}

// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#contentful-image
static bool is_contentful_image(Layout::NodeWithStyle::ImageObserver const* observer)
{
    // A CSS image img is a contentful image when all of the following apply:
    // - img is url valued.
    // - img is available.
    // NB: Only url-valued images have an observer, which holds the decoded image data once it is available.
    return observer && observer->decoded_image_data();
}

static bool svg_has_rendered_descendants(Layout::Node const& svg_box)
{
    bool has_rendered_descendants = false;
    svg_box.for_each_in_inclusive_subtree([&](Layout::Node const& node) {
        if (&node == &svg_box)
            return TraversalDecision::Continue;
        switch (node.kind()) {
        case Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::SVGGeometryBox:
        case Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::SVGImageBox:
        case Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::SVGTextBox:
        case Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::SVGTextPathBox:
        case Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::SVGForeignObjectBox:
            has_rendered_descendants = true;
            return TraversalDecision::Break;
        default:
            return TraversalDecision::Continue;
        }
    });
    return has_rendered_descendants;
}

// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#contentful
// NB: This answers the question for the box of an element, or for a text node's box, which stands for the element
//     the text node is a child of. Generated content has boxes of its own, so a pseudo-element's content is found
//     the same way as an element's.
// NB: A box this can answer yes for must also make layout_rows_may_be_contentful() answer yes.
static bool is_contentful(Layout::Node const& node)
{
    // An element target is contentful when one or more of the following apply:

    // - target has a text node child, representing non-empty text, and the node's used opacity is greater than zero.
    // NB: The opacity of the text node's ancestors is checked as part of whether it is paintable.
    if (auto const* text_node = as_if<Layout::TextNode>(node)) {
        if (auto const* dom_text = text_node->dom_text())
            return is_non_empty(dom_text->data().utf16_view());
        // NB: Generated text has no DOM node, so its rendered text is looked at instead.
        auto rendered_text = text_node->rendered_text_for_dom();
        return is_non_empty(rendered_text.utf16_view());
    }

    auto const* node_with_style = as_if<Layout::NodeWithStyle>(node);
    if (!node_with_style)
        return false;

    switch (node.kind()) {
    // - target is a replaced element representing an available image.
    case Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::ImageBox:
    case Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::SVGImageBox: {
        auto const* image_provider = as<Layout::Box>(node).image_provider_if_any();
        if (image_provider && image_provider->is_image_available())
            return true;
        break;
    }
    // - target is a canvas with its context mode set to any value other than none.
    case Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::CanvasBox:
        if (auto const* canvas = as_if<HTML::HTMLCanvasElement>(node.dom_node()); canvas && !canvas->context().has<Empty>())
            return true;
        break;
    // - target is a video element that represents its poster frame or the first video frame and the frame is
    //   available.
    case Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::VideoBox:
        if (auto const* video = as_if<HTML::HTMLVideoElement>(node.dom_node())) {
            auto representation = video->current_representation();
            if (representation == HTML::HTMLVideoElement::Representation::PosterFrame && video->poster_frame().has_value())
                return true;
            if (representation == HTML::HTMLVideoElement::Representation::VideoFrame || representation == HTML::HTMLVideoElement::Representation::FirstVideoFrame)
                return true;
        }
        break;
    // - target is an svg element with rendered descendants.
    case Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::SVGSVGBox:
        if (svg_has_rendered_descendants(node))
            return true;
        break;
    // - target is an input element with a non-empty value attribute.
    // NB: The value is what the control renders, which the value attribute only provides the default for.
    case Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::TextInputBox:
        if (auto const* input = as_if<HTML::HTMLInputElement>(node.dom_node())) {
            auto value = input->value();
            if (is_non_empty(value.utf16_view()))
                return true;
        }
        break;
    default:
        break;
    }

    // - target has a background-image which is a contentful image, and its used background-size has non-zero width
    //   and height values.
    auto background_layer_count = node_with_style->background_images().size();
    for (size_t layer_index = 0; layer_index < background_layer_count; ++layer_index) {
        if (is_contentful_image(node_with_style->background_image_observer(layer_index)) && !background_size_is_empty(*node_with_style, layer_index))
            return true;
    }

    // - target has a border-image-source which is a contentful image, and its used border-image-width has non-zero
    //   value.
    // FIXME: Check the used border-image-width.
    if (is_contentful_image(node_with_style->border_image_source_observer()))
        return true;

    // - target is an originating element for a paintable pseudo-element that represents a contentful image or
    //   non-empty text.
    // NB: The boxes of a pseudo-element's generated content are checked like those of any element.

    return false;
}

// AD-HOC: Whether the box paints something other than the default background, which is what first paint is about.
static bool paints_non_default_content(Layout::Node const& node)
{
    if (is_contentful(node))
        return true;

    auto const* node_with_style = as_if<Layout::NodeWithStyle>(node);
    if (!node_with_style)
        return false;

    // NB: The enclosing box of a paintable iframe counts towards first paint.
    if (node.kind() == Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::NavigableContainerViewport)
        return true;

    if (node_with_style->background_color().alpha() > 0)
        return true;

    for (auto const& background_image : node_with_style->background_images()) {
        if (background_image)
            return true;
    }

    auto border_is_painted = [](CSS::BorderData const& border) {
        return border.width > 0 && border.line_style != CSS::LineStyle::None && border.line_style != CSS::LineStyle::Hidden && border.color.alpha() > 0;
    };
    return border_is_painted(node_with_style->border_left()) || border_is_painted(node_with_style->border_top()) || border_is_painted(node_with_style->border_right()) || border_is_painted(node_with_style->border_bottom());
}

CSSPixelRect client_rect_of_box(Layout::Node const& node, Layout::RustFFI::FfiViewportMapping const& viewport_mapping)
{
    if (!node.is_text_node())
        return Painting::bounding_client_rect(node, viewport_mapping);

    // NB: The client rect of a text box is the union of the rects of its fragments.
    CSSPixelRect united_rect;
    Layout::RustFFI::layout_script_text_range_rects(
        node.document_host(), Layout::Node::slot_id(&node),
        to_underlying(Painting::SelectionState::Full), 0, 0, 0, NumericLimits<size_t>::max(),
        viewport_mapping, &united_rect, [](void* context, CSSPixelRect rect) {
            auto& united_rect = *static_cast<CSSPixelRect*>(context);
            if (rect.is_empty())
                return;
            united_rect = united_rect.is_empty() ? rect : united_rect.united(rect);
        });
    return united_rect;
}

// NB: This answers whether boxes of the document are paintable, from the state the document has after layout.
class PaintableChecker {
public:
    explicit PaintableChecker(DOM::Document& document)
        : m_read(document)
    {
        auto navigable = document.navigable();
        if (!navigable)
            return;
        m_viewport = document.layout_node(m_read);
        if (!m_viewport || !Painting::has_committed_box(*m_viewport)) {
            m_viewport = nullptr;
            return;
        }

        // NB: The scrolling area is in the coordinate space of the document, while client rects are relative to the
        //     viewport, so client rects are offset by the viewport's scroll offset before they are compared with it.
        m_scrolling_area = Painting::scrollable_overflow_rect(*m_viewport);
        m_scroll_offset = navigable->viewport_scroll_offset();

        m_viewport_mapping = Painting::viewport_mapping(document);
    }

    Layout::BegunRead const& read() const { return m_read; }
    Layout::Viewport const* viewport() const { return m_scrolling_area.has_value() ? m_viewport : nullptr; }

    enum class CheckAncestorOpacity {
        No,
        Yes,
    };

    // https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#paintable
    bool is_paintable(Layout::Node const& node, CheckAncestorOpacity check_ancestor_opacity) const
    {
        if (!viewport())
            return false;

        // An element el is paintable when all of the following apply:
        // - el is being rendered.
        // NB: Only boxes are looked at.

        // - el's used visibility is visible.
        auto const* node_with_style = as_if<Layout::NodeWithStyle>(node);
        if (!node_with_style)
            node_with_style = as_if<Layout::NodeWithStyle>(node.parent_ptr());
        if (!node_with_style || node_with_style->visibility() != CSS::Visibility::Visible)
            return false;

        // - el and all of its ancestors' used opacity is greater than zero.
        if (check_ancestor_opacity == CheckAncestorOpacity::Yes) {
            for (auto const* ancestor = &node; ancestor; ancestor = ancestor->parent_ptr()) {
                if (auto const* ancestor_with_style = as_if<Layout::NodeWithStyle>(*ancestor); ancestor_with_style && ancestor_with_style->opacity() <= 0)
                    return false;
            }
        }

        // - el's paintable bounding rect intersects with the scrolling area of the document.
        // https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#paintable-bounding-rect
        // 1. Let boundingRect be the result of running the getBoundingClientRect() on target.
        auto bounding_rect = client_rect_of_box(node, m_viewport_mapping).translated(m_scroll_offset);

        // 2. Clip boundingRect with the document's scrolling area.
        // 3. Return boundingRect.
        // NB: The clipped rect is not empty only if the rect intersects with the scrolling area.
        return bounding_rect.intersects(*m_scrolling_area);
    }

private:
    Layout::ForcedReadScope m_read;
    Layout::Viewport const* m_viewport { nullptr };
    Optional<CSSPixelRect> m_scrolling_area;
    CSSPixelPoint m_scroll_offset;
    Layout::RustFFI::FfiViewportMapping m_viewport_mapping {};
};

struct PaintedContent {
    bool has_non_default_content { false };
    bool has_contentful_content { false };
};

// NB: This finds whether the document has an element that is both paintable and contentful, and whether it paints
//     anything other than the default background, from the boxes it has after layout. Only boxes are looked at, so
//     elements that are not being rendered are skipped, and a box with an opacity of zero hides its whole subtree.
static PaintedContent find_painted_content(PaintableChecker const& checker, PaintedContent const& already_found)
{
    PaintedContent result = already_found;

    auto const* viewport = checker.viewport();
    if (!viewport)
        return result;

    // OPTIMIZATION: This runs every frame until first contentful paint is reported, which a document with nothing that
    //               can be contentful never does, so its boxes are not walked.
    if (result.has_non_default_content && !Layout::RustFFI::layout_rows_may_be_contentful(viewport->document_host(), &checker.read()))
        return result;

    viewport->for_each_in_inclusive_subtree([&](Layout::Node const& node) {
        if (auto const* node_with_style = as_if<Layout::NodeWithStyle>(node); node_with_style && node_with_style->opacity() <= 0)
            return TraversalDecision::SkipChildrenAndContinue;

        if (!result.has_non_default_content && paints_non_default_content(node) && checker.is_paintable(node, PaintableChecker::CheckAncestorOpacity::No))
            result.has_non_default_content = true;

        if (is_contentful(node) && checker.is_paintable(node, PaintableChecker::CheckAncestorOpacity::No)) {
            result.has_non_default_content = true;
            result.has_contentful_content = true;
            return TraversalDecision::Break;
        }

        // NB: The rendered descendants of an svg element make the svg element contentful, so they are not looked
        //     at by themselves.
        if (node.kind() == Layout::RustFFI::NodeKind::SVGSVGBox)
            return TraversalDecision::SkipChildrenAndContinue;

        return TraversalDecision::Continue;
    });

    return result;
}

// NB: Largest contentful paint is the only user of the images pending rendering and of the text nodes that are
//     painted, and it reports nothing once the window has dispatched a scroll event or an input event.
// FIXME: Keep tracking these for element timing, once it is implemented.
static bool tracks_painted_images_and_text(DOM::Document& document)
{
    if (!document.browsing_context())
        return false;
    auto window = document.window();
    if (!window)
        return false;
    return !window->has_dispatched_scroll_event() && !EventTiming::has_dispatched_input_event(*window);
}

// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#process-an-image-that-finished-loading
void process_an_image_that_finished_loading(DOM::Element& element, ImageRequestInfo image_request)
{
    // 1. Let root be element's root.
    // 2. If root is not a Document, return.
    auto* root = as_if<DOM::Document>(element.root());
    if (!root)
        return;

    // OPTIMIZATION: An image that nothing would report once it is painted is not recorded.
    if (!tracks_painted_images_and_text(*root))
        return;

    // 3. Let now be the current high resolution time given element's relevant global object.
    auto now = HighResolutionTime::current_high_resolution_time(HTML::relevant_global_object(element));

    // 4. Let record be a pending image record with element element, request imageRequest and loadTime now.
    // 5. Add record to root's images pending rendering.
    root->paint_timing_state().images_pending_rendering.append({
        .element = element,
        .request = move(image_request),
        .load_time = now,
    });
}

// NB: The element whose box is the containing block of the given text box.
static GC::Ptr<DOM::Element> element_which_determines_the_containing_block_of(Layout::Node const& text_box)
{
    for (auto const* box = static_cast<Layout::Node const*>(text_box.containing_block()); box; box = box->parent_ptr()) {
        if (auto const* element = as_if<DOM::Element>(box->dom_node()))
            return const_cast<DOM::Element*>(element);
        if (box->is_generated_for_pseudo_element()) {
            if (auto generator = box->pseudo_element_generator())
                return const_cast<DOM::Element*>(generator.ptr());
        }
    }
    return nullptr;
}

// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#mark-paint-timing
void mark_paint_timing(DOM::Document& document)
{
    // 1. If the document's browsing context is not paint-timing eligible, return.
    // NB: We configure every nested browsing context to report paint timing, so every browsing context is eligible.
    if (!document.browsing_context())
        return;

    auto& state = document.paint_timing_state();
    auto& reported_paints = state.set_of_previously_reported_paints;

    auto* host = document.layout_node_arena().host();

    // OPTIMIZATION: Nothing reports the images and text nodes that are painted from now on.
    auto tracks_images_and_text = tracks_painted_images_and_text(document);
    if (!tracks_images_and_text) {
        state.images_pending_rendering.clear();
        state.text_boxes_pending_first_paint.clear();
        if (!state.stopped_noting_text_boxes) {
            Layout::ForcedReadScope read { document };
            Layout::RustFFI::layout_stop_noting_text_rows_for_first_paint(host, read);
            state.stopped_noting_text_boxes = true;
        }
    }

    // OPTIMIZATION: The layout node arena knows without being asked whether it noted any text layout node since the
    //               last frame, so a frame that made none and changed no text asks nothing about text.
    auto may_have_noted_text_boxes = tracks_images_and_text && Layout::RustFFI::layout_text_rows_may_await_first_paint(host);

    // OPTIMIZATION: Nothing below reports anything once first paint and first contentful paint have been reported,
    //               unless an image or a text node may be painted for the first time.
    if (reported_paints.contains(first_paint_name()) && reported_paints.contains(first_contentful_paint_name())
        && state.images_pending_rendering.is_empty() && state.text_boxes_pending_first_paint.is_empty() && !may_have_noted_text_boxes)
        return;

    // AD-HOC: Nothing is painted for a document whose initial paint is deferred until its fonts load.
    if (document.font_computer().should_defer_initial_paint())
        return;

    PaintableChecker checker { document };

    // 2. Let paintTimingInfo be a new paint timing info, whose rendering update end time is the current high
    //    resolution time given document's relevant global object.
    PaintTimingInfo paint_timing_info {
        .rendering_update_end_time = HighResolutionTime::current_high_resolution_time(HTML::relevant_global_object(document)),
        .implementation_defined_presentation_time = {},
    };

    // 3. Let paintedImages be a new ordered set
    GC::RootVector<PendingImageRecord> painted_images;

    // 4. Let paintedTextNodes be a new ordered set
    PaintedTextNodes painted_text_nodes;

    // 5. For each record in doc's images pending rendering list:
    state.images_pending_rendering.remove_all_matching([&](PendingImageRecord& record) {
        // AD-HOC: An image whose element left the document is never painted.
        if (!record.element->is_connected() || &record.element->document() != &document)
            return true;

        // 1. If record's request is available and ready to be painted, then run the following steps:
        // NB: The request is available, as the record was made once it was. The image is ready to be painted once its
        //     element is paintable.
        auto const* layout_node = record.element->layout_node(checker.read());
        if (!layout_node || !checker.is_paintable(*layout_node, PaintableChecker::CheckAncestorOpacity::Yes))
            return false;

        // 1. Append record to paintedImages.
        painted_images.append(record);

        // 2. Remove record from doc's images pending rendering list.
        return true;
    });

    // NB: The text layout nodes the layout node arena noted since the last frame join the ones that were not paintable
    //     yet. The arena hands each one out once, so a slot is in the list twice only if it was pending already.
    auto& text_boxes = state.text_boxes_pending_first_paint;
    if (may_have_noted_text_boxes) {
        auto pending_count = text_boxes.size();
        Layout::RustFFI::layout_take_text_rows_for_first_paint(host, &checker.read(), &text_boxes, [](void* context, Compositing::RustFFI::NodeSlotId slot) {
            static_cast<Vector<Compositing::RustFFI::NodeSlotId>*>(context)->append(slot);
        });
        if (pending_count != 0 && text_boxes.size() != pending_count) {
            quick_sort(text_boxes, [](auto a, auto b) { return a.index < b.index; });
            size_t unique_count = 0;
            for (size_t i = 0; i < text_boxes.size(); ++i) {
                if (unique_count == 0 || text_boxes[unique_count - 1].index != text_boxes[i].index)
                    text_boxes[unique_count++] = text_boxes[i];
            }
            text_boxes.shrink(unique_count);
        }
    }

    // NB: This is when the user agent paints a Text node for the first time.
    text_boxes.remove_all_matching([&](Compositing::RustFFI::NodeSlotId slot) {
        // NB: A text node whose layout node is gone has its new layout node noted once it gets one.
        auto const* text_box = document.layout_node_arena().node_if_live(checker.read(), slot);
        if (!text_box)
            return true;
        auto* text = as_if<DOM::Text>(const_cast<DOM::Node*>(text_box->dom_node()));
        if (!text || !text->is_connected() || &text->document() != &document)
            return true;

        // OPTIMIZATION: Once an element is in the set of elements with rendered text, the text nodes it owns are never
        //               read, so a text node whose element is in it already is not looked at again. Its layout node
        //               is noted again if its text changes, or if it is rebuilt, as it is when the node moves.
        auto element = element_which_determines_the_containing_block_of(*text_box);
        if (!element || element->is_in_set_of_elements_with_rendered_text())
            return true;

        if (!checker.is_paintable(*text_box, PaintableChecker::CheckAncestorOpacity::Yes)) {
            // OPTIMIZATION: Text that is all white space and paints nothing, often in a box without fragments, is not
            //               looked at again until its data changes to something else.
            return !is_non_empty(text->data().utf16_view());
        }

        // https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#sec-modifications-dom
        // When the user agent paints a Text node text for the first time, it should execute the following steps:
        // FIXME: - If text will not be painted due to the font face being in its font block period, then return.

        // - Let element be the Element which determines the containing block of text.
        // NB: The element was found above.

        // - Append text to element's set of owned text nodes.
        // NB: The set of owned text nodes is only read for the elements that are appended to paintedTextNodes below,
        //     in this frame, so only their text nodes are kept.
        painted_text_nodes.ensure(*element).append(*text);
        return true;
    });

    // 6. For each Element element in doc's descendants:
    // OPTIMIZATION: Only the elements that got their first owned text nodes in this frame can be appended below.
    for (auto& it : painted_text_nodes) {
        auto& element = it.key;

        // 1. If element is contained in doc's set of elements with rendered text, continue.
        // 2. If element's set of owned text nodes is empty, continue.
        // NB: Both were checked as the text nodes were appended.

        // 3. Append element to doc's set of elements with rendered text.
        element->append_to_set_of_elements_with_rendered_text();

        // 4. Append element to paintedTextNodes.
        // NB: The element is in paintedTextNodes already.
    }

    // 7. Let reportedPaints be the document's set of previously reported paints.
    // FIXME: 8. Let frameTimingInfo be document's current frame timing info.
    // FIXME: 9. Set document's current frame timing info to null.

    // 10. Let flushPaintTimings be the following steps:
    auto flush_paint_timings = [&] {
        // NB: The boxes are looked at once for both first paint and first contentful paint, and not at all once both
        //     have been reported.
        PaintedContent already_found {
            .has_non_default_content = reported_paints.contains(first_paint_name()),
            .has_contentful_content = reported_paints.contains(first_contentful_paint_name()),
        };
        auto painted_content = already_found.has_non_default_content && already_found.has_contentful_content
            ? already_found
            : find_painted_content(checker, already_found);

        // 1. If reportedPaints does not contain "first-paint", and the user agent is configured to mark first paint,
        //    then report paint timing given document, "first-paint", and paintTimingInfo.
        // NOTE: First paint excludes the default background paint, but includes non-default background paint.
        if (!reported_paints.contains(first_paint_name()) && painted_content.has_non_default_content)
            report_paint_timing(document, first_paint_name(), paint_timing_info);

        // 2. If document should report first contentful paint, then:
        // https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#should-report-first-contentful-paint
        //   1. If document's set of previously reported paints contains "first-contentful-paint", then return false.
        //   2. If document contains at least one element that is both paintable and contentful, then return true.
        //   3. Otherwise, return false.
        if (!reported_paints.contains(first_contentful_paint_name()) && painted_content.has_contentful_content) {
            // 1. Report paint timing given document, "first-contentful-paint", and paintTimingInfo.
            report_paint_timing(document, first_contentful_paint_name(), paint_timing_info);
        }

        // 3. Report largest contentful paint given document, paintTimingInfo, paintedImages and paintedTextNodes.
        if (!painted_images.is_empty() || !painted_text_nodes.is_empty())
            LargestContentfulPaint::report_largest_contentful_paint(document, paint_timing_info, painted_images, painted_text_nodes);

        // FIXME: 4. Report element timing given document, paintTimingInfo, paintedImages and paintedTextNodes.
        // FIXME: 5. If frameTimingInfo is not null, then queue a long animation frame entry given document,
        //           frameTimingInfo, and paintTimingInfo.
    };

    // 11. If the user-agent does not support implementation-defined presentation times, call flushPaintTimings and
    //     return.
    // NB: The frame is presented by another process, which does not report back when it was presented.
    flush_paint_timings();
}

ImageRequestInfo image_request_info(Utf16String url, GC::Ptr<HTML::DecodedImageData const> image_data)
{
    ImageRequestInfo info { .url = move(url), .natural_size = {} };
    if (image_data) {
        auto width = image_data->intrinsic_width();
        auto height = image_data->intrinsic_height();
        if (width.has_value() && height.has_value())
            info.natural_size = CSSPixelSize { *width, *height };
    }
    return info;
}

// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#report-paint-timing
void report_paint_timing(DOM::Document& document, Utf16String const& paint_type, PaintTimingInfo const& paint_timing_info)
{
    // 1. Create a new PerformancePaintTiming object newEntry with document's relevant realm and set its attributes as
    //    follows:
    //    1. Set newEntry's name attribute to paintType.
    //    2. Set newEntry's entryType attribute to "paint".
    //    3. Set newEntry's startTime attribute to the default paint timestamp given paintTimingInfo.
    //    4. Set newEntry's duration attribute to 0.
    // 2. Set newEntry's paint timing info to paintTimingInfo.
    auto new_entry = PerformancePaintTiming::create(paint_type, paint_timing_info);

    // 3. Queue newEntry in document's relevant realm.
    auto& window = HTML::relevant_window(document);
    window.queue_performance_entry(new_entry);
    window.add_performance_entry(new_entry);

    // 4. Append paintType to document's set of previously reported paints.
    document.paint_timing_state().set_of_previously_reported_paints.set(paint_type);
}

// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#exposed-for-paint-timing
bool is_exposed_for_paint_timing(DOM::Element const& element, GC::Ptr<DOM::Document const> document)
{
    // 1. If element is not connected, return false.
    if (!element.is_connected())
        return false;

    // 2. If document is null, let document be element's relevant settings object's relevant global object's
    //    associated document.
    if (!document)
        document = HTML::relevant_window(element).associated_document();

    // 3. If document is not fully active, return false.
    if (!document->is_fully_active())
        return false;

    // 4. If element's root is not equal to document, return false.
    if (&element.root() != document.ptr())
        return false;

    // 5. Return true.
    return true;
}

void DocumentPaintTimingState::visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    for (auto& record : images_pending_rendering)
        visitor.visit(record.element);
}

extern "C" {

bool web_paint_timing_is_exposed_for_paint_timing(DOM::Node const* node)
{
    auto const* element = as_if<DOM::Element>(node);
    return element && is_exposed_for_paint_timing(*element, nullptr);
}
}

#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibJS/HostClassBuilder.h>
#include <LibJS/Runtime/VM.h>

namespace Web::PermissionsAPI {

Optional<Web::Permissions::PermissionName> permission_name_from(Utf16View name)
{
    if (name == "geolocation"_utf16)
        return Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Geolocation;
    if (name == "microphone"_utf16)
        return Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Microphone;
    if (name == "notifications"_utf16)
        return Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Notifications;
    return {};
}

static Optional<PermissionsPolicy::PolicyControlledFeature> policy_controlled_feature_for(Web::Permissions::PermissionName name)
{
    switch (name) {
    case Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Geolocation:
        return PermissionsPolicy::PolicyControlledFeature::Geolocation;
    case Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Microphone:
        return PermissionsPolicy::PolicyControlledFeature::Microphone;
    case Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Notifications:
        // Notifications is a powerful feature, but not a policy-controlled one.
        return {};
    }
    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

static PermissionState permission_state_from(Web::Permissions::EffectiveState state)
{
    switch (state) {
    case Web::Permissions::EffectiveState::Granted:
        return PermissionState::Granted;
    case Web::Permissions::EffectiveState::Denied:
        return PermissionState::Denied;
    case Web::Permissions::EffectiveState::Prompt:
        return PermissionState::Prompt;
    }
    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

// Steps 6 and 7 of https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-request-permission-to-use
static void store_permission_decision(Web::Permissions::PermissionName name, HTML::EnvironmentSettingsObject& settings, PermissionState current_state)
{
    // 6. Let key be the result of generating a permission key for descriptor with settings's top-level origin and settings's origin.
    VERIFY(settings.top_level_origin.has_value());
    auto key = permission_key_generation_algorithm(settings.top_level_origin.value(), settings.origin());

    // AD-HOC: Our permission state is backed by PermissionStore, so update it before returning to make the new current
    //         state observable to callers that continue synchronously.
    PermissionStore::the().set_permission_store_entry(name, key, current_state);

    // 7. Queue a task on the current settings object's responsible event loop to set a permission store entry with descriptor, key, and current state.
    HTML::queue_global_task(HTML::Task::Source::Permissions, settings.global_object(), GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(name, key, current_state), [](auto& name, auto& key, auto& current_state) {
        PermissionStore::the().set_permission_store_entry(name, key, current_state);
    }));
}

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-request-permission-to-use
void request_permission_with_user_prompt(Web::Permissions::PermissionName name, HTML::EnvironmentSettingsObject& settings, PermissionDecisionCallback on_decided)
{
    // 1. Let current state be the descriptor's permission state.
    auto current_state = permission_state(name, settings);

    // 2. If current state is not "prompt", return current state and abort these steps.
    if (current_state != PermissionState::Prompt) {
        on_decided->function()(current_state);
        return;
    }

    // 3. Ask the user for express permission for the calling algorithm to use the powerful feature described by descriptor.
    // NB: Only windows have a page to ask through; a worker's request is denied.
    auto* window = HTML::window_from_global_object(settings.global_object());
    if (!window) {
        on_decided->function()(PermissionState::Denied);
        return;
    }

    auto settle = GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(name, GC::Ref(settings), on_decided), [](auto& name, auto& settings, auto& on_decided, Web::Permissions::EffectiveState answer) {
        // 4. If the user gives express permission to use the powerful feature, set current state to "granted"; otherwise to "denied".
        //    The user's interaction may provide new information about the user's intent for the origin.
        // AD-HOC: A prompt the user dismisses or ignores leaves the permission at "prompt", rather than storing "denied";
        //         only the calling algorithm sees "denied" then, so the site may ask again.
        auto current_state = answer == Web::Permissions::EffectiveState::Granted ? PermissionState::Granted : PermissionState::Denied;

        // 5. Let settings be the current settings object.
        // NB: The user's answer arrives outside any script, so the requester's settings object was captured instead.
        // 6. Let key be the result of generating a permission key for descriptor with settings's top-level origin and settings's origin.
        // 7. Queue a task on the current settings object's responsible event loop to set a permission store entry with descriptor, key, and current state.
        // NB: The UI process stores the user's answer, and sends the snapshot that reflects it ahead of the answer itself.
        //     It can't key an answer for an opaque top-level origin (a file: page's), so that answer is kept here, for
        //     as long as the origin lives.
        if (settings->top_level_origin->is_opaque() && answer != Web::Permissions::EffectiveState::Prompt)
            store_permission_decision(name, settings, current_state);

        // 8. Return current state.
        on_decided->function()(current_state);
    });

    window->page().request_permission(window->associated_document().id(), Utf16String::from_utf8(Web::Permissions::to_string(name)), settle);
}

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-permission-state
PermissionState permission_state(Web::Permissions::PermissionName name, Optional<HTML::EnvironmentSettingsObject&> settings)
{
    // 1. If settings wasn't passed, set it to the current settings object.
    auto& settings_object = settings.has_value() ? settings.value() : HTML::current_settings_object();

    // 2. If settings is a non-secure context, return "denied".
    if (!HTML::is_secure_context(settings_object))
        return PermissionState::Denied;

    // 3. Let feature be descriptor's name.
    auto feature = name;

    // 4. If there exists a policy-controlled feature for feature and settings' relevant global object has an associated Document run the following step:
    auto policy_controlled_feature = policy_controlled_feature_for(feature);
    if (auto* window = HTML::window_from_global_object(settings_object.global_object()); policy_controlled_feature.has_value() && window) {
        // 1. Let document be settings' relevant global object's associated Document.
        auto& document = window->associated_document();

        // 2. If document is not allowed to use feature, return "denied".
        if (!document.is_allowed_to_use_feature(*policy_controlled_feature))
            return PermissionState::Denied;
    }

    // 5. Let key be the result of generating a permission key for descriptor with settings's top-level origin and settings's origin.
    VERIFY(settings_object.top_level_origin.has_value());
    auto key = permission_key_generation_algorithm(settings_object.top_level_origin.value(), settings_object.origin());

    // 6. Let entry be the result of getting a permission store entry with descriptor and key.
    auto entry = PermissionStore::the().get_permission_store_entry(feature, key);

    // 7. If entry is not null, return a PermissionState enum value from entry's state.
    if (entry.has_value())
        return entry.release_value().state;

    // 8. Return the PermissionState enum value that represents the permission state of feature, taking into account any permission state constraints for descriptor's name.
    auto& page = Bindings::principal_host_defined_page(settings_object.realm());
    return permission_state_from(PermissionStore::the().state_for(feature, key, page));
}

extern "C" {
Permissions* web_rust_permissions_api_create_permissions(JSVM*);
u8 web_permissions_api_permission_state(HTML::EnvironmentSettingsObject*, u8 name);
void web_permissions_api_request_permission_to_use(HTML::EnvironmentSettingsObject*, u8 name, GC::Cell* cell, void (*steps)(JSVM*, void*, u8));
}

static_assert(to_underlying(Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Geolocation) == 0);
static_assert(to_underlying(Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Microphone) == 1);
static_assert(to_underlying(Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Notifications) == 2);
static_assert(to_underlying(PermissionState::Granted) == 0);
static_assert(to_underlying(PermissionState::Denied) == 1);
static_assert(to_underlying(PermissionState::Prompt) == 2);

GC::Ref<Permissions> Permissions::create()
{
    return *web_rust_permissions_api_create_permissions(JS::HostABI::vm_to_abi(JS::VM::the()));
}

u8 web_permissions_api_permission_state(HTML::EnvironmentSettingsObject* settings, u8 name)
{
    return to_underlying(permission_state(static_cast<Web::Permissions::PermissionName>(name), *settings));
}

void web_permissions_api_request_permission_to_use(HTML::EnvironmentSettingsObject* settings, u8 name, GC::Cell* cell, void (*steps)(JSVM*, void*, u8))
{
    request_permission_with_user_prompt(static_cast<Web::Permissions::PermissionName>(name), *settings, GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(GC::Ref { *cell }, steps), [](auto& cell, auto& steps, PermissionState state) {
        steps(JS::HostABI::vm_to_abi(JS::VM::the()), cell.ptr(), to_underlying(state));
    }));
}

#include <LibJS/HostClassBuilder.h>

namespace Web::PermissionsAPI {

bool permission_key_is_equal_to(Web::Permissions::PermissionName, URL::Origin const& key1, URL::Origin const& key2)
{
    // FIXME: 1. If key1 is not of descriptor's permission key type or key2 is not of descriptor's permission key type, return false.

    // 2. Return the result of running the permission key comparison algorithm for the feature named by descriptor's name, passing key1 and key2.
    return permission_key_comparison_algorithm(key1, key2);
}

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-permission-key-comparison-algorithm
bool permission_key_comparison_algorithm(URL::Origin const& key1, URL::Origin const& key2)
{
    // 1. Return key1 is same origin with key2.
    return key1.is_same_origin(key2);
}

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-permission-key-generation-algorithm
URL::Origin permission_key_generation_algorithm(URL::Origin const& origin, URL::Origin const&)
{
    // Takes an origin origin and an origin embedded origin, and returns a new permission key.
    // If unspecified, this defaults to the default permission key generation algorithm.
    // A feature that specifies a custom permission key generation algorithm MUST also specify a permission key comparison algorithm.

    // 1. Return origin.
    return origin;

    // Note: Permission Delegation
    // Most powerful features grant permission to the top-level origin and delegate access to the requesting document via Permissions Policy.
    // This is known as permission delegation.
}

// FIXME: This should be store at the user-agent level (IPC to the browser process)
PermissionStore& PermissionStore::the()
{
    static auto& s_the = *new PermissionStore;
    return s_the;
}

extern "C" {
// Defined in Bindings/Rust/src/permissions_api/exports.rs.
bool web_rust_permissions_api_update_statuses_of_this_agent(JSVM*, u64 revision, bool store_changed);
}

Optional<PermissionStoreEntry> PermissionStore::get_permission_store_entry(Web::Permissions::PermissionName name, URL::Origin const& key)
{
    MutexLocker locker(m_mutex);

    // 1. If the user agent's permission store contains an entry whose descriptor is descriptor, and whose key is equal to key given descriptor, return that entry.
    for (auto const& entry : m_entries) {
        if (entry.name == name && permission_key_is_equal_to(name, entry.permission_key, key))
            return entry;
    }

    // 2. Return null.
    return {};
}

void PermissionStore::set_permission_store_entry(Web::Permissions::PermissionName name, URL::Origin const& key, PermissionState state)
{
    MutexLocker locker(m_mutex);

    // 1. Let newEntry be a new permission store entry whose descriptor is descriptor, and whose key is key, and whose state is state.
    PermissionStoreEntry new_entry { name, key, state };

    // 2. If the user agent's permission store contains an entry whose descriptor is descriptor, and whose key is equal to key given descriptor, replace that entry with newEntry and abort these steps.
    for (auto& entry : m_entries) {
        if (entry.name == name && permission_key_is_equal_to(name, entry.permission_key, key)) {
            entry = new_entry;
            return;
        }
    }

    // 3. Append newEntry to the user agent's permission store.
    m_entries.append(move(new_entry));
}

bool PermissionStore::store_snapshot(Web::Permissions::PermissionSnapshot const& snapshot)
{
    MutexLocker locker(m_mutex);
    auto changed = false;

    if (!m_defaults_revision.has_value() || snapshot.revision > *m_defaults_revision) {
        m_defaults_revision = snapshot.revision;
        m_geolocation_default = snapshot.geolocation_default;
        m_microphone_default = snapshot.microphone_default;
        m_notifications_default = snapshot.notifications_default;
        changed = true;
    }

    for (auto const& origin : snapshot.origins) {
        auto key = origin.serialize();
        if (auto cached = m_sites.get(key); cached.has_value() && snapshot.revision <= cached->revision)
            continue;

        CachedSite site { .revision = snapshot.revision, .entries = {} };
        for (auto const& entry : snapshot.entries) {
            if (entry.top_level_origin.is_same_origin(origin))
                site.entries.append(entry);
        }
        m_sites.set(key, move(site));
        changed = true;
    }

    return changed;
}

void PermissionStore::apply_snapshot(Web::Permissions::PermissionSnapshot snapshot, Notify notify)
{
    auto changed = store_snapshot(snapshot);
    if (notify == Notify::No)
        return;

    if (!web_rust_permissions_api_update_statuses_of_this_agent(JS::HostABI::vm_to_abi(JS::VM::the()), snapshot.revision, changed))
        return;

    // Only a window agent has documents.
    if (!HTML::surrounding_agent().is_similar_origin_window_agent())
        return;

    // A document whose microphone permission went away loses its live microphone tracks.
    for (auto& navigable : HTML::all_local_navigables()) {
        auto document = navigable.active_document();
        if (!document || !document->window())
            continue;
        if (auto navigator = document->window()->navigator_if_created(); navigator) {
            if (auto media_devices = navigator->media_devices_if_created())
                media_devices->end_tracks_without_permission();
        }
    }
}

Web::Permissions::EffectiveState PermissionStore::state_for(Web::Permissions::PermissionName name, URL::Origin const& key, Page& page)
{
    // NB: The caller holds the lock.
    auto default_state = [&] {
        switch (name) {
        case Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Geolocation:
            return m_geolocation_default;
        case Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Microphone:
            return m_microphone_default;
        case Web::Permissions::PermissionName::Notifications:
            return m_notifications_default;
        }
        VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
    };

    if (key.is_opaque()) {
        MutexLocker locker(m_mutex);
        return default_state();
    }

    auto serialized_key = key.serialize();
    auto is_cached = [&] {
        MutexLocker locker(m_mutex);
        return m_sites.contains(serialized_key);
    }();
    if (!is_cached) {
        // No status has seen this site's state yet, so there's nothing to tell them about.
        if (auto snapshot = page.client().page_did_request_permission_snapshot(key); snapshot.has_value())
            apply_snapshot(snapshot.release_value(), Notify::No);
    }

    MutexLocker locker(m_mutex);
    if (auto site = m_sites.get(serialized_key); site.has_value()) {
        for (auto const& entry : site->entries) {
            if (entry.name == name)
                return entry.state;
        }
    }
    return default_state();
}

Vector<String> PermissionStore::cached_origins_for_testing() const
{
    MutexLocker locker(m_mutex);
    Vector<String> origins;
    for (auto const& it : m_sites) {
        if (!it.value.entries.is_empty())
            origins.append(it.key);
    }
    return origins;
}

}

namespace Web::PermissionsAPI {

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-permission-store-entry
struct PermissionStoreEntry {
    Web::Permissions::PermissionName name;
    URL::Origin permission_key; // https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-permission-key
    PermissionState state;
};

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-permission-store
// NB: The decisions are the process's and any thread may read them. The statuses that show them are cells, so each agent
//     keeps its own.
class WEB_API PermissionStore {
public:
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    static PermissionStore& the();

    // https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-get-a-permission-store-entry
    Optional<PermissionStoreEntry> get_permission_store_entry(Web::Permissions::PermissionName, URL::Origin const& key);

    // https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-set-a-permission-store-entry
    void set_permission_store_entry(Web::Permissions::PermissionName, URL::Origin const& key, PermissionState state);

    // The UI process owns the user agent's permission decisions. It tells this process the states of the sites it
    // shows: the first time the process reads one, through the page reading it, and again whenever one changes. Of
    // each site, the newest state wins.
    enum class Notify : bool {
        No,
        Yes,
    };
    // With Notify::Yes this updates the statuses of the calling agent. Another agent gets the same snapshot from its own
    // connection to the UI process, and the revision tells it that it has more to do than this store.
    void apply_snapshot(Web::Permissions::PermissionSnapshot, Notify = Notify::Yes);
    Web::Permissions::EffectiveState state_for(Web::Permissions::PermissionName, URL::Origin const& key, Page&);

    // The sites this process holds decisions for.
    Vector<String> cached_origins_for_testing() const;

private:
    PermissionStore() = default;

    bool store_snapshot(Web::Permissions::PermissionSnapshot const&);

    mutable Mutex m_mutex;

    Vector<PermissionStoreEntry> m_entries;

    struct CachedSite {
        u64 revision { 0 };
        Vector<Web::Permissions::PermissionSnapshotEntry> entries;
    };
    HashMap<String, CachedSite> m_sites;
    Optional<u64> m_defaults_revision;
    Web::Permissions::EffectiveState m_geolocation_default { Web::Permissions::EffectiveState::Prompt };
    Web::Permissions::EffectiveState m_microphone_default { Web::Permissions::EffectiveState::Prompt };
    Web::Permissions::EffectiveState m_notifications_default { Web::Permissions::EffectiveState::Prompt };
};

bool permission_key_is_equal_to(Web::Permissions::PermissionName, URL::Origin const& key1, URL::Origin const& key2);

bool permission_key_comparison_algorithm(URL::Origin const& key1, URL::Origin const& key2);

URL::Origin permission_key_generation_algorithm(URL::Origin const& origin, URL::Origin const&);

}

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(PictureInPictureController);

PictureInPictureController::PictureInPictureController(Page& page)
    : m_page(page)
{
}

void PictureInPictureController::visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_page);
    visitor.visit(m_pending_operations);
    visitor.visit(m_window_awaiting_open);
    visitor.visit(m_open_window);
}

void PictureInPictureController::WindowAwaitingOpen::visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    request.visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(traversable);
}

static void resolve_promise(WebIDL::Promise& promise, GC::Ptr<PictureInPictureWindow> window = nullptr)
{
    auto& realm = WebIDL::promise_realm(promise);
    HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext execution_context { realm, HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext::CallbacksEnabled::Yes };
    if (window)
        WebIDL::resolve_promise(promise, Bindings::wrap(Bindings::host_defined_wrapper_world(realm), realm, GC::Ref { *window }));
    else
        WebIDL::resolve_promise(promise);
}

static void reject_promise_with_invalid_state_error(WebIDL::Promise& promise, Utf16String const& message)
{
    auto& realm = WebIDL::promise_realm(promise);
    HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext execution_context { realm, HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext::CallbacksEnabled::Yes };
    WebIDL::reject_promise(promise, WebIDL::InvalidStateError::create(message));
}

static void fire_picture_in_picture_event(DOM::Element& element, Utf16FlyString const& event_name, PictureInPictureWindow& window)
{
    auto event = create_picture_in_picture_event(HTML::relevant_realm(element), event_name, { .bubbles = true }, window);
    element.dispatch_event(event);
}

void PictureInPictureController::enqueue_request(HTML::HTMLVideoElement& video, WebIDL::Promise& promise)
{
    enqueue(Request { video, promise });
}

void PictureInPictureController::enqueue_exit(DOM::Document& document, GC::Ptr<WebIDL::Promise> promise)
{
    enqueue(Exit { document, promise });
}

void PictureInPictureController::enqueue_close_window(PictureInPictureWindow& window)
{
    enqueue(CloseWindow { window });
}

void PictureInPictureController::enqueue(Operation operation)
{
    m_pending_operations.append(move(operation));
    process_pending_operations();
}

void PictureInPictureController::process_pending_operations()
{
    // A request suspends the queue until the UI process has opened the window for it.
    while (!m_window_awaiting_open.has_value() && !m_pending_operations.is_empty()) {
        auto operation = m_pending_operations.take_first();
        operation.visit(
            [&](Request const& request) {
                run_request_steps(request);
            },
            [&](Exit const& exit) {
                // https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#dom-document-exitpictureinpicture
                // AD-HOC: These are the parallel steps of exitPictureInPicture() in the overhaul proposed in
                //         https://github.com/w3c/picture-in-picture/pull/260.
                // 1. If this's Picture-in-Picture element is null:
                if (!exit.document->picture_in_picture_element()) {
                    // 1. Queue a global task on the media element event task source given this's relevant global
                    //    object to resolve p.
                    // AD-HOC: There is no media element to take the task source from, so this uses the DOM
                    //         manipulation task source. The promise is rejected, as the overhaul's reviewers asked.
                    if (exit.promise) {
                        HTML::queue_global_task(HTML::Task::Source::DOMManipulation, HTML::relevant_global_object(*exit.document), GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(GC::Ref { *exit.promise }), [](auto& promise) {
                            reject_promise_with_invalid_state_error(promise, "There is no Picture-in-Picture element to exit"_utf16);
                        }));
                    }

                    // 2. Return.
                    return;
                }

                // 2. Run the exit Picture-in-Picture algorithm given this and p.
                run_exit_steps(exit.document, exit.promise, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface::Yes);
            },
            [&](CloseWindow const& close_window) {
                // https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#unloading-steps
                // 1. Run the close window algorithm with window.
                this->close_window(close_window.window, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface::Yes);
            },
            [&](UserInterfaceClosedWindow const& closed_window) {
                auto& window = *closed_window.window;
                if (!window.is_open())
                    return;

                // AD-HOC: The spec leaves closing the window to the user agent. When the user closes it, or the UI
                //         process gives it to another page, run the exit algorithm for the document it belongs to.
                auto& video = window.video();
                auto& document = video.document();
                if (video.is_picture_in_picture_element())
                    run_exit_steps(document, nullptr, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface::No);
                else
                    this->close_window(window, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface::No);
            });
    }
}

// The window's page is a player whose video shows the frames of the video in Picture-in-Picture, and plays it
// through its controls.
static void create_player(DOM::Document& document, HTML::HTMLVideoElement& source)
{
    PictureInPicturePlayerDOM player { document, *document.body() };
    as<HTML::HTMLVideoElement>(*player.video).set_visual_source(source);
}

// https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#request-picture-in-picture
void PictureInPictureController::run_request_steps(Request const& request)
{
    auto& video = *request.video;

    // NB: Nothing is left to do for a request whose promise the disable Picture-in-Picture steps rejected.
    if (!video.has_pending_picture_in_picture_promise(request.promise))
        return;

    // 1. If this is doc's Picture-in-Picture element:
    if (video.is_picture_in_picture_element()) {
        // 1. Queue a global task on the media element event task source given global to resolve p with the
        //    Picture-in-Picture window associated with this.
        HTML::queue_global_task(video.media_element_event_task_source(), HTML::relevant_global_object(video), GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(request.video, request.promise), [](auto& video, auto& promise) {
            if (video->take_pending_picture_in_picture_promise(promise))
                resolve_promise(promise, video->picture_in_picture_window());
        }));

        // 2. Abort these steps.
        return;
    }

    // 2. Attempt to associate a Picture-in-Picture window with this.
    // NB: The window shows a page of its own, which the UI process creates along with the window. The UI process lets a
    //     document replace its open window without user activation, as step 7 does, so it is told doc's navigable.
    PageClient::NewWebViewResult new_web_view;
    if (auto navigable = video.document().navigable()) {
        HTML::WebViewHints hints;
        hints.picture_in_picture_window = HTML::PictureInPictureWindowHints {
            .navigable_id = navigable->id(),
            .video_size = Gfx::Size<u32> { video.video_width(), video.video_height() }.to_type<int>(),
        };
        new_web_view = m_page->client().page_did_request_new_web_view(HTML::ActivateTab::No, hints, navigable->id(), {}, HTML::TokenizedFeature::NoOpener::Yes, {});
    }

    // 3. If the previous step failed:
    if (!new_web_view.page) {
        // 1. Queue a global task on the media element event task source given global to reject p with
        //    InvalidStateError DOMException.
        HTML::queue_global_task(video.media_element_event_task_source(), HTML::relevant_global_object(video), GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(request.video, request.promise), [](auto& video, auto& promise) {
            if (video->take_pending_picture_in_picture_promise(promise))
                reject_promise_with_invalid_state_error(promise, "Unable to open a Picture-in-Picture window"_utf16);
        }));

        // 2. Abort these steps.
        return;
    }

    auto traversable = HTML::LocalTraversableNavigable::create_for_new_web_view(move(new_web_view), nullptr);
    create_player(*traversable->active_document(), video);
    m_window_awaiting_open = WindowAwaitingOpen { request, traversable };
}

void PictureInPictureController::did_open_window(Gfx::IntSize window_size)
{
    if (!m_window_awaiting_open.has_value())
        return;

    // https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#request-picture-in-picture
    auto [request, traversable] = m_window_awaiting_open.release_value();
    auto& video = *request.video;
    auto& document = video.document();
    auto& global = HTML::relevant_global_object(video);

    // 4. Let pipWindow be a new instance of PictureInPictureWindow that represents this's associated
    //    Picture-in-Picture window.
    auto picture_in_picture_window = PictureInPictureWindow::create(video, window_size, traversable);

    // NB: The UI process opened the new window in place of any window this page had open. When that window belongs
    //     to doc's Picture-in-Picture element, the next step exits it.
    if (m_open_window) {
        auto& previous_video = m_open_window->video();
        auto& previous_document = previous_video.document();

        // AD-HOC: The spec assumes that each document has its own window. When another document's
        //         Picture-in-Picture element loses its window, run the exit algorithm for that document too.
        if (&previous_document != &document && previous_video.is_picture_in_picture_element())
            run_exit_steps(previous_document, nullptr, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface::No);
        else
            close_window(*m_open_window, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface::No);
    }

    // AD-HOC: This follows the overhaul proposed in https://github.com/w3c/picture-in-picture/pull/260, which runs
    //         the exit algorithm here rather than in the task below, so that leavepictureinpicture fires first.
    // 5. If doc's Picture-in-Picture element is not null, run the exit Picture-in-Picture algorithm given doc and
    //    null.
    if (document.picture_in_picture_element())
        run_exit_steps(document, nullptr, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface::No);

    video.set_picture_in_picture_window(picture_in_picture_window);
    m_open_window = picture_in_picture_window;

    // NB: A document that stopped being fully active while the window opened, such as by unloading, never runs the
    //     task below, so the window would stay open without entering Picture-in-Picture. It is closed again instead.
    if (!document.is_fully_active()) {
        close_window(picture_in_picture_window, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface::Yes);
        process_pending_operations();
        return;
    }

    // 6. Queue a global task on the media element event task source given global, to perform the following steps:
    HTML::queue_global_task(video.media_element_event_task_source(), global, GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(*this, request.video, request.promise, picture_in_picture_window), [](auto& self, auto& video, auto& promise, auto& picture_in_picture_window) {
        auto& document = video->document();

        // NB: When the disable Picture-in-Picture steps rejected p while the window opened, it is closed again
        //     rather than entered.
        if (!video->take_pending_picture_in_picture_promise(promise)) {
            self.close_window(picture_in_picture_window, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface::Yes);
            return;
        }

        // 1. Set doc's Picture-in-Picture element to this.
        document.set_picture_in_picture_element(video);

        // 2. Append relevant settings object's origin to initiators of active Picture-in-Picture sessions.
        // NB: Nothing reads this list, and https://github.com/w3c/picture-in-picture/issues/263 proposes its removal.

        // 3. If this is fullscreenElement, then exit fullscreen.
        // NB: The spec links "exit fullscreen" to the fully exit fullscreen algorithm. The fullscreen element is
        //     compared before it is retargeted, so that a video in a shadow tree leaves fullscreen as well.
        if (document.fullscreen_element().ptr() == video.ptr())
            document.fully_exit_fullscreen();

        // 4. Fire an event named enterpictureinpicture using PictureInPictureEvent at this with its bubbles attribute
        //    initialized to true and its pictureInPictureWindow attribute initialized to Picture-in-Picture window.
        fire_picture_in_picture_event(video, HTML::EventNames::enterpictureinpicture, picture_in_picture_window);

        // 5. Resolve p with pipWindow.
        resolve_promise(promise, picture_in_picture_window);
    }));

    process_pending_operations();
}

// https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#exit-picture-in-picture-algorithm
// AD-HOC: This follows the overhaul proposed in https://github.com/w3c/picture-in-picture/pull/260. The current text
//         fires leavepictureinpicture from a separately queued task, and does not say which document to exit. See
//         https://github.com/w3c/picture-in-picture/issues/252.
void PictureInPictureController::run_exit_steps(DOM::Document& document, GC::Ptr<WebIDL::Promise> promise, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface window_is_open_in_user_interface)
{
    // 1. Assert that these steps are running on the picture-in-picture parallel queue.

    // 2. Let global be doc's relevant global object.
    auto& global = HTML::relevant_global_object(document);

    // 3. Run the close window algorithm with the Picture-in-Picture window associated with doc's Picture-in-Picture
    //    element.
    auto& video = as<HTML::HTMLVideoElement>(*document.picture_in_picture_element());
    close_window(*video.picture_in_picture_window(), window_is_open_in_user_interface);

    // 4. Queue a global task on the media element event task source given global, to perform the following steps:
    HTML::queue_global_task(video.media_element_event_task_source(), global, GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(GC::Ref { document }, promise), [](auto& document, auto& promise) {
        // 1. If doc is not fully active or doc's Picture-in-Picture element is null:
        if (!document->is_fully_active() || !document->picture_in_picture_element()) {
            // 1. If p is not null, resolve p with undefined.
            // AD-HOC: Reject p instead, as the overhaul's reviewers asked.
            if (promise)
                reject_promise_with_invalid_state_error(*promise, "There is no Picture-in-Picture element to exit"_utf16);

            // 2. Return.
            return;
        }

        // 2. Let element be doc's Picture-in-Picture element.
        auto& element = as<HTML::HTMLVideoElement>(*document->picture_in_picture_element());

        // 3. Set doc's Picture-in-Picture element to null.
        document->set_picture_in_picture_element(nullptr);

        // 4. Fire an event named leavepictureinpicture using PictureInPictureEvent at the element with its bubbles
        //    attribute initialized to true and its pictureInPictureWindow attribute initialized to Picture-in-Picture
        //    window associated with element.
        fire_picture_in_picture_event(element, HTML::EventNames::leavepictureinpicture, *element.picture_in_picture_window());

        // 5. Remove one item matching relevant settings object's origin from initiators of active Picture-in-Picture
        //    sessions.
        // NB: Nothing reads this list, and https://github.com/w3c/picture-in-picture/issues/263 proposes its removal.

        // 6. If p is not null, resolve p with undefined.
        if (promise)
            resolve_promise(*promise);
    }));
}

// https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#close-window-algorithm
void PictureInPictureController::close_window(PictureInPictureWindow& window, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface window_is_open_in_user_interface)
{
    if (window.is_open()) {
        window.close();
        window.video().clear_visual_clones();
        window.traversable().close_top_level_traversable(HTML::LocalTraversableNavigable::PromptToUnload::No);
    }

    if (m_open_window.ptr() != &window)
        return;
    m_open_window = nullptr;
    if (window_is_open_in_user_interface == WindowIsOpenInUserInterface::Yes)
        m_page->client().page_did_exit_picture_in_picture();
}

void PictureInPictureController::window_did_resize(Gfx::IntSize window_size)
{
    if (!m_open_window)
        return;
    m_open_window->set_size(window_size);

    // https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#interface-picture-in-picture-window
    // When the size of a Picture-in-Picture window pipWindow changes, the user agent MUST queue a task to fire an
    // event named resize at pipWindow.
    auto& video = m_open_window->video();
    HTML::queue_global_task(video.media_element_event_task_source(), HTML::relevant_global_object(video), GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(GC::Ref { *m_open_window }), [](auto& window) {
        window->dispatch_event(DOM::Event::create(HTML::relevant_global_object(window->video()), HTML::EventNames::resize));
    }));
}

// The window keeps the aspect ratio of its video, including while it opens.
void PictureInPictureController::video_size_did_change(HTML::HTMLVideoElement& video, Gfx::IntSize video_size)
{
    auto is_open_window_video = m_open_window && &m_open_window->video() == &video;
    auto is_opening_window_video = m_window_awaiting_open.has_value() && m_window_awaiting_open->request.video.ptr() == &video;
    if (!is_open_window_video && !is_opening_window_video)
        return;
    m_page->client().page_did_change_picture_in_picture_video_size(video_size);
}

void PictureInPictureController::window_did_close(bool pause_video)
{
    if (!m_open_window)
        return;
    // The user closed the window to stop watching its video, rather than to go back to its tab and watch it there.
    if (pause_video)
        m_open_window->video().pause();
    enqueue(UserInterfaceClosedWindow { *m_open_window });
}

// https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#unloading-steps
// AD-HOC: These are the unloading steps from the overhaul proposed in
//         https://github.com/w3c/picture-in-picture/pull/260. The current text runs the exit algorithm, which throws
//         when there is no Picture-in-Picture element.
void run_unloading_cleanup_steps(DOM::Document& document)
{
    // 1. If doc's Picture-in-Picture element is null, return.
    auto element = document.picture_in_picture_element();
    if (!element)
        return;

    // 2. Let window be the Picture-in-Picture window associated with doc's Picture-in-Picture element.
    auto window = as<HTML::HTMLVideoElement>(*element).picture_in_picture_window();

    // 3. Set doc's Picture-in-Picture element to null.
    document.set_picture_in_picture_element(nullptr);

    // 4. Remove one item matching relevant settings object's origin from initiators of active Picture-in-Picture
    //    sessions.
    // NB: Nothing reads this list, and https://github.com/w3c/picture-in-picture/issues/263 proposes its removal.

    // 5. Enqueue the following steps to doc's picture-in-picture parallel queue:
    document.page().picture_in_picture_controller().enqueue_close_window(*window);
}

}

#include <LibWeb/Export.h>
#include <LibWeb/Forward.h>
#include <LibWeb/PictureInPicture/PictureInPictureWindow.h>

namespace Web::PictureInPicture {

// Runs the steps that the spec enqueues to a traversable navigable's picture-in-picture parallel queue, and tracks
// the window that the UI process shows for this page. The UI shows a single window, so a page has at most one open.
class WEB_API PictureInPictureController final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(PictureInPictureController, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(PictureInPictureController);

public:
    bool has_picture_in_picture_support() const { return m_has_picture_in_picture_support; }
    void set_has_picture_in_picture_support(bool has_support) { m_has_picture_in_picture_support = has_support; }

    void enqueue_request(HTML::HTMLVideoElement&, WebIDL::Promise&);
    void enqueue_exit(DOM::Document&, GC::Ptr<WebIDL::Promise>);
    void enqueue_close_window(PictureInPictureWindow&);

    void did_open_window(Gfx::IntSize window_size);
    void window_did_resize(Gfx::IntSize);
    void video_size_did_change(HTML::HTMLVideoElement&, Gfx::IntSize);
    void window_did_close(bool pause_video);

    bool is_waiting_for_window_to_open() const { return m_window_awaiting_open.has_value(); }
    bool has_open_window() const { return m_open_window != nullptr; }
    GC::Ptr<PictureInPictureWindow> open_window() const { return m_open_window; }

private:
    explicit PictureInPictureController(Page&);

    virtual void visit_edges(Cell::Visitor&) override;

    struct Request {
        GC::Ref<HTML::HTMLVideoElement> video;
        GC::Ref<WebIDL::Promise> promise;

        void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
        {
            visitor.visit(video);
            visitor.visit(promise);
        }
    };

    struct Exit {
        GC::Ref<DOM::Document> document;
        GC::Ptr<WebIDL::Promise> promise;

        void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
        {
            visitor.visit(document);
            visitor.visit(promise);
        }
    };

    struct CloseWindow {
        GC::Ref<PictureInPictureWindow> window;

        void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor) { visitor.visit(window); }
    };

    struct UserInterfaceClosedWindow {
        GC::Ref<PictureInPictureWindow> window;

        void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor) { visitor.visit(window); }
    };

    using Operation = Variant<Request, Exit, CloseWindow, UserInterfaceClosedWindow>;

    struct WindowAwaitingOpen {
        Request request;
        GC::Ref<HTML::LocalTraversableNavigable> traversable;

        void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor&);
    };

    enum class WindowIsOpenInUserInterface : bool {
        No,
        Yes,
    };

    void enqueue(Operation);
    void process_pending_operations();

    void run_request_steps(Request const&);
    void run_exit_steps(DOM::Document&, GC::Ptr<WebIDL::Promise>, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface);
    void close_window(PictureInPictureWindow&, WindowIsOpenInUserInterface);

    GC::Ref<Page> m_page;
    bool m_has_picture_in_picture_support { false };

    Vector<Operation> m_pending_operations;
    Optional<WindowAwaitingOpen> m_window_awaiting_open;

    GC::Ptr<PictureInPictureWindow> m_open_window;
};

void run_unloading_cleanup_steps(DOM::Document&);

}

#include <LibGC/Heap.h>

namespace Web::PictureInPicture {

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(PictureInPictureWindow);

GC::Ref<PictureInPictureWindow> PictureInPictureWindow::create(HTML::HTMLVideoElement& video, Gfx::IntSize size, HTML::LocalTraversableNavigable& traversable)
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<PictureInPictureWindow>(video, size, traversable);
}

// When instantiated, an instance of PictureInPictureWindow has its state set to opened.
PictureInPictureWindow::PictureInPictureWindow(HTML::HTMLVideoElement& video, Gfx::IntSize size, HTML::LocalTraversableNavigable& traversable)
    : m_video(video)
    , m_traversable(traversable)
    , m_size(size)
{
}

PictureInPictureWindow::~PictureInPictureWindow() = default;

void PictureInPictureWindow::visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_video);
    visitor.visit(m_traversable);
}

GC::Ptr<Bindings::Wrappable> PictureInPictureWindow::relevant_global_impl() const
{
    return m_video->document().window();
}

// https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#dom-pictureinpicturewindow-width
WebIDL::Long PictureInPictureWindow::width() const
{
    // The width attribute MUST return the width in CSS pixels of the Picture-in-Picture window associated with
    // pictureInPictureElement if the state is opened. Otherwise, it MUST return 0.
    return is_open() ? m_size.width() : 0;
}

// https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#dom-pictureinpicturewindow-height
WebIDL::Long PictureInPictureWindow::height() const
{
    // The height attribute MUST return the height in CSS pixels of the Picture-in-Picture window associated with
    // pictureInPictureElement if the state is opened. Otherwise, it MUST return 0.
    return is_open() ? m_size.height() : 0;
}

// https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#close-window-algorithm
void PictureInPictureWindow::close()
{
    // When the close window algorithm with an instance of PictureInPictureWindow is invoked, its state is set to
    // closed.
    m_state = State::Closed;
}

void PictureInPictureWindow::set_onresize(WebIDL::CallbackType* event_handler)
{
    set_event_handler_attribute(HTML::EventNames::resize, event_handler);
}

WebIDL::CallbackType* PictureInPictureWindow::onresize()
{
    return event_handler_attribute(HTML::EventNames::resize);
}

}

#pragma once

#include <LibGfx/Size.h>
