/// Begins the outermost style stabilization epoch of a document.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_document_animations_begin_style_stabilization_epoch(animations: &mut DocumentAnimations) {
    animations.begin_style_stabilization_epoch();
}

/// Commits the events a document queued during its outermost style stabilization epoch to its pending animation event
/// queue as the epoch commits, answering how many it committed.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_document_animations_commit_provisional_events(
    animations: &mut DocumentAnimations,
) -> usize {
    animations.commit_provisional_events()
}

/// Appends `event` of `animation` to the pending animation event queue of a document, or, where `provisional`, to the
/// events it queues during its style stabilization epoch.
/// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#pending-animation-event-queue
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_document_animations_append_event(
    animations: &mut DocumentAnimations,
    animation: RcRef<'_, AnimationCell>,
    event: &FfiPendingAnimationEvent,
    provisional: bool,
) {
    let animation = AnimationHandle::retained_from_lent(animation);
    let mut event = *event;
    // NB: A time event is scheduled at the origin-relative time of the current time of a document timeline.
    if event.kind == PendingAnimationEventKind::Time {
        let timeline = animation.borrow().timeline().cloned();
        event.scheduled_event_time = timeline
            .filter(|timeline| matches!(timeline.borrow().kind, TimelineKind::Document { .. }))
            .and_then(|timeline| timeline.convert_a_timeline_time_to_an_origin_relative_time(timeline.current_time()))
            .into();
    }
    animations
        .pending_events
        .append(PendingAnimationEvent { animation, event }, provisional);
}

/// What queueing the events of the animations of a document an animation frame established asks of the host, which
/// hands each function `context`.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiQueueAnimationEventsHost {
    pub context: *mut c_void,
    pub keep_alive: FfiKeepAlive,
    /// The time stamp of an event queued for the host's `DOM::Element` `element` now.
    pub time_stamp: unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, element: NonNull<c_void>) -> f64,
    /// Queues the time events of the host's `SVGAnimationElement` `animation_element` the animation frame established.
    pub queue_time_events: unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, animation_element: NonNull<c_void>),
    pub perform: HostEffectPerformer,
}

/// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#update-animations-and-send-events
/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-transitions-2/#event-dispatch
/// https://www.w3.org/TR/css-animations-2/#event-dispatch
/// For each animation associated with a document whose animations `animations` are, whether or not it has a timeline,
/// appends the events the animation frame established for a CSS animation or transition to the pending animation event
/// queue of the document, or, where `provisional`, to the events it queues during its style stabilization epoch, has
/// the host queue those of the animation of an SVG animation element, and disassociates the animation from the target
/// of its associated effect where it is inert, as a procedure scheduled. Answers how many CSS events it queued.
///
/// # Safety
/// `animations` must be what a live document knows of animations, which the host may reach as it performs.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn animations_document_animations_queue_events(
    animations: *mut DocumentAnimations,
    provisional: bool,
    host: &FfiQueueAnimationEventsHost,
) -> usize {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller, and the borrow ends before the host performs anything.
    let associated = unsafe { &mut *animations }
        .set_mut(DocumentAnimationSetKind::Associated)
        .alive();
    for animation in &associated {
        // SAFETY: The host keeps alive an animation it is handed for as long as this call lasts.
        unsafe { (host.keep_alive)(host.context, animation) };
    }
    let mut queued_count = 0;
    for animation in &associated {
        let events = animation.borrow_mut().take_css_events();
        if let AnimationKind::Smil { animation_element, .. } = *animation.borrow().kind() {
            // SAFETY: The animation keeps its animation element alive.
            unsafe { (host.queue_time_events)(host.context, animation_element) };
        } else if !events.as_slice().is_empty() {
            let owner = animation
                .borrow()
                .owning_element()
                .expect("a CSS animation or transition with events has an owning element");
            // NB: Each event takes the time stamp of when it is queued.
            // SAFETY: The animation keeps its owning element alive.
            let time_stamp = unsafe { (host.time_stamp)(host.context, owner.element) };
            for css_event in events.as_slice() {
                let event = FfiPendingAnimationEvent {
                    kind: PendingAnimationEventKind::Css,
                    css_event_type: css_event.r#type,
                    playback_event_type: PlaybackEventType::Finish,
                    time_event_type: TimeEventType::Begin,
                    detail: 0,
                    elapsed_time: css_event.elapsed_time,
                    current_time: OptionalTimeValue::UNRESOLVED,
                    timeline_time: OptionalTimeValue::UNRESOLVED,
                    scheduled_event_time: events.scheduled_event_time,
                    time_stamp,
                };
                // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller; the borrow ends before the host performs anything.
                unsafe { &mut *animations }.pending_events.append(
                    PendingAnimationEvent {
                        animation: animation.clone(),
                        event,
                    },
                    provisional,
                );
            }
            queued_count += events.as_slice().len();
        }
        if animation.borrow().disassociation_from_target_pending {
            run_procedure(animation, host.perform, |procedures| {
                procedures.disassociate_from_target_if_inert();
            });
        }
    }
    queued_count
}

/// Calls `visit` with `context` and each GC cell of the host that keeps alive the elements the records of the events a
/// document queued name, and the timelines associated with the document, which the document visits as the GC traces
/// it.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_document_animations_visit_edges(
    animations: &DocumentAnimations,
    context: *mut c_void,
    visit: unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, cell: *mut c_void, kind: HostCellKind),
) {
    animations.pending_events.for_each_host_cell(|cell, kind| {
        // SAFETY: The host visits a cell of an animation it queued an event of.
        unsafe { visit(context, cell.as_ptr(), kind) }
    });
    // NB: The document keeps alive the elements and transitions its provisional transition actions decide over.
    animations.provisional_transitions.for_each_host_cell(|cell, kind| {
        // SAFETY: The host visits a cell the document's provisional transition actions keep alive.
        unsafe { visit(context, cell.as_ptr(), kind) }
    });
    // NB: The document keeps the timelines associated with it alive, and the objects script sees of them.
    for timeline in &animations.timelines {
        timeline.for_each_holder_cell(|cell, kind| {
            // SAFETY: The host visits a cell of a timeline associated with the document.
            unsafe { visit(context, cell.as_ptr(), kind) }
        });
    }
}

/// Adds `effect` to the set `kind` of the effects a document knows of, answering whether the set did not hold it yet.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_document_effect_set_insert(
    animations: &mut DocumentAnimations,
    kind: DocumentEffectSetKind,
    effect: RcRef<'_, AnimationEffectCell>,
) -> bool {
    let effect = EffectHandle::retained_from_lent(effect);
    animations.effect_set_mut(kind).insert(&effect)
}

/// Drops the entries of the animations in `set` that died, as the host begins to enumerate it.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_weak_animation_set_prune(set: &mut WeakAnimationSet) {
    set.prune();
}

/// The number of entries of `set`, live or dead, which the host enumerates by index.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_weak_animation_set_entry_count(set: &WeakAnimationSet) -> usize {
    set.entry_count()
}

/// A reference, handed to the host, to the animation of the entry at `index` of `set`, or null where it died.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_weak_animation_set_get(set: &WeakAnimationSet, index: usize) -> *const AnimationCell {
    set.get(index).map_or(std::ptr::null(), AnimationHandle::into_raw)
}

/// Whether `set` holds `animation`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_weak_animation_set_contains(set: &WeakAnimationSet, animation: &AnimationCell) -> bool {
    set.contains(animation)
}

/// New empty lists of the animations of an element, which the element owns.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_create() -> *mut ElementAnimations {
    Box::into_raw(Box::default())
}

/// Destroys the lists of the animations of an element, giving up the references they hold.
///
/// # Safety
/// `animations` must be lists `animations_element_animations_create` handed out, which the host gives up, and
/// `element` null or the element whose lists they are.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_destroy(
    animations: *mut ElementAnimations,
    element: *mut c_void,
) {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let mut animations = unsafe { Box::from_raw(animations) };
    if let Some(element) = NonNull::new(element) {
        animations.forget_element_as_target_of_disassociated(element);
    }
    drop(animations);
}

/// Calls `visit` with `context` and each GC cell of the host that keeps alive what an animation the lists hold names.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_for_each_host_cell(
    animations: &ElementAnimations,
    context: *mut c_void,
    visit: unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, cell: *mut c_void, kind: HostCellKind),
) {
    animations.for_each_host_cell(|cell, kind| {
        // SAFETY: The host visits a cell of an animation it holds.
        unsafe { visit(context, cell.as_ptr(), kind) }
    });
}

/// Associates `animation` with the element, and, where it was not associated yet, with its document, whose animations
/// `document` are, as one created during its style stabilization epoch where `in_style_stabilization_epoch`, answering
/// whether it was not associated yet.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_associate(
    animations: &mut ElementAnimations,
    document: &mut DocumentAnimations,
    animation: RcRef<'_, AnimationCell>,
    in_style_stabilization_epoch: bool,
) -> bool {
    let animation = AnimationHandle::retained_from_lent(animation);
    if !animations.associate(animation.clone()) {
        return false;
    }
    animation.borrow_mut().did_associate_with_target();
    document.associate(&animation, in_style_stabilization_epoch);
    true
}

/// Disassociates `animation`, whose associated effect `effect` was, if any, from the element, whose lists `animations`
/// are where it has any, and from its document, whose animations `document` are, answering whether it was associated
/// with the element.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_disassociate(
    animations: Option<&mut ElementAnimations>,
    document: &mut DocumentAnimations,
    animation: &AnimationCell,
    effect: Option<&AnimationEffectCell>,
) -> bool {
    let was_associated = animations.is_some_and(|animations| animations.disassociate(animation));
    document.disassociate(animation, effect);
    was_associated
}

/// Moves the animations associated with an element, whose lists `animations` are, from the document whose animations
/// `old_document` are to the one whose animations `new_document` are, as ones created during its style stabilization
/// epoch where `in_style_stabilization_epoch`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_move_to_document(
    animations: &ElementAnimations,
    old_document: &mut DocumentAnimations,
    new_document: &mut DocumentAnimations,
    in_style_stabilization_epoch: bool,
) {
    for animation in animations.associated() {
        let effect = animation.borrow().effect().cloned();
        old_document.disassociate(animation, effect.as_deref());
        new_document.associate(animation, in_style_stabilization_epoch);
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_invalidate_composite_order(animations: &mut ElementAnimations) {
    animations.invalidate_composite_order();
}

/// Sorts the animations associated with the element in composite order, with `tree_order` comparing elements in tree
/// order.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_sort_in_composite_order(
    animations: &mut ElementAnimations,
    tree_order: FfiTreeOrder,
) {
    animations.sort_in_composite_order(&mut host_tree_order(tree_order));
}

/// One of the lists of the animations of an element.
#[expect(dead_code, reason = "C++ constructs the variants")]
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum ElementAnimationListKind {
    /// The animations associated with the element.
    Associated,
    /// The CSS animations of one owner.
    CssAnimations,
    /// The CSS transitions of one owner.
    Transitions,
}

fn element_animation_list(
    animations: &ElementAnimations,
    kind: ElementAnimationListKind,
    slot: AnimationOwnerSlot,
) -> &[AnimationHandle] {
    match kind {
        ElementAnimationListKind::Associated => animations.associated(),
        ElementAnimationListKind::CssAnimations => animations.css_animations(slot),
        ElementAnimationListKind::Transitions => animations.transitions(slot),
    }
}

/// The number of animations in the list `kind`, of the owner at `slot` where it is one of an owner's.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_count(
    animations: &ElementAnimations,
    kind: ElementAnimationListKind,
    slot: AnimationOwnerSlot,
) -> usize {
    element_animation_list(animations, kind, slot).len()
}

/// The animation at `index` in the list `kind`, of the owner at `slot` where it is one of an owner's, which it borrows
/// for as long as the list holds it.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_get(
    animations: &ElementAnimations,
    kind: ElementAnimationListKind,
    slot: AnimationOwnerSlot,
    index: usize,
) -> *const AnimationCell {
    std::ptr::from_ref::<AnimationCell>(&element_animation_list(animations, kind, slot)[index])
}

/// The style engine of `host`, or none where it is null, which knows the element as `node`, or not at all where it is
/// zero.
///
/// # Safety
/// A non-null `host` must be live for the call.
unsafe fn style_engine_target<'a>(host: *const DocumentHost, node: u32) -> Option<StyleEngineTarget<'a>> {
    Some(StyleEngineTarget {
        // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
        host: unsafe { host.as_ref() }?,
        node: StyleNodeID::from_raw(node)?,
    })
}

/// Whether the element has had CSS animations since it last canceled them, or has transitions.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_has_css_animations_or_transitions(
    animations: &ElementAnimations,
) -> bool {
    animations.has_css_animations_or_transitions()
}

/// The host's function that runs `run` with `run_context` in an execution context it opens for `animation`, as its
/// caller, which hands it `context`, asks.
pub type FfiInExecutionContext = unsafe extern "C" fn(
    context: *mut c_void,
    animation: &AnimationCell,
    run: unsafe extern "C" fn(run_context: *mut c_void),
    run_context: *mut c_void,
);

/// Runs `run` in the execution context the host opens for `animation` through `in_execution_context` with `context`.
fn in_host_execution_context<F: FnOnce()>(
    in_execution_context: FfiInExecutionContext,
    context: *mut c_void,
    animation: &AnimationCell,
    run: F,
) {
    unsafe extern "C" fn run_once<F: FnOnce()>(run_context: *mut c_void) {
        // SAFETY: `run_context` is the `Option<F>` below, which outlives the host's call.
        let run = unsafe { &mut *run_context.cast::<Option<F>>() };
        (run.take().expect("the host runs the procedure once"))();
    }
    let mut run = Some(run);
    // SAFETY: The host runs `run_once` with `run_context` before it returns.
    unsafe { in_execution_context(context, animation, run_once::<F>, (&raw mut run).cast()) };
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-animations-2/#owning-element-section
/// Updating display to a value other than none will start all animations applied to the element by the animation-name
/// property.
/// Plays or pauses each CSS animation the element and its pseudo-elements own as its `animation-play-state` last
/// computed, the element's first and then each pseudo-element's in the order of the host's `PseudoElement`, each in an
/// execution context the host opens through `in_execution_context` with `context`. The host keeps each animation alive
/// through `keep_alive` with `context`, and performs what that asks of it through `perform`.
///
/// # Safety
/// `animations` must be the lists of an element, which live for the call, and which the host may change as it performs.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_play_or_pause_css_animations(
    animations: *const ElementAnimations,
    keep_alive: FfiKeepAlive,
    in_execution_context: FfiInExecutionContext,
    context: *mut c_void,
    perform: HostEffectPerformer,
) {
    let mut previous_slot = None;
    // NB: What the host performs can change the lists, which are read anew for each owner and no borrow of which
    //     outlives the read.
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    while let Some((slot, css_animations)) = unsafe { &*animations }.css_animations_after(previous_slot) {
        previous_slot = Some(slot);
        for animation in &css_animations {
            // SAFETY: The host keeps alive an animation it is handed for as long as this call lasts.
            unsafe { keep_alive(context, animation) };
        }
        for animation in &css_animations {
            let play_state = animation.borrow().css_animation().last_css_play_state;
            let plays = match play_state {
                Some(CSS_ANIMATION_PLAY_STATE_RUNNING) => true,
                Some(CSS_ANIMATION_PLAY_STATE_PAUSED) => false,
                _ => unreachable!("a CSS-defined animation has the play state animation-play-state computed for it"),
            };
            in_host_execution_context(in_execution_context, context, animation, || {
                run_procedure_on(animation, perform, |procedures| {
                    if plays {
                        procedures.play_from_css()
                    } else {
                        procedures.pause_from_css()
                    }
                })
                .expect("playing or pausing an animation from CSS does not throw");
            });
        }
    }
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-animations-2/#owning-element-section
/// If the display property of an element is set to none and its display value would compute to none when ignoring the
/// Transitions and Animations cascade origins, then terminate running animations with this owning element.
/// Takes the CSS animations and transitions of the element and its pseudo-elements, publishes that the element and its
/// pseudo-elements own no CSS animations to the style engine of `host`, which knows the element as `node`, where the
/// host names one, and cancels each, in an execution context the host opens through `in_execution_context` with
/// `context` where it is not idle. The host keeps each animation alive through `keep_alive` with `context`, and
/// performs what that asks of it through `perform`.
///
/// # Safety
/// `animations` must be the lists of an element, which live for the call, and a non-null `host` must be live for the
/// call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_cancel_css_animations_and_transitions(
    animations: *mut ElementAnimations,
    host: *const DocumentHost,
    node: u32,
    keep_alive: FfiKeepAlive,
    in_execution_context: FfiInExecutionContext,
    context: *mut c_void,
    perform: HostEffectPerformer,
) {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller, and the borrow of the lists ends before the host performs anything.
    let taken = unsafe { &mut *animations }
        .take_css_animations_and_transitions(None, unsafe { style_engine_target(host, node) });
    cancel_taken_animations(&taken, keep_alive, in_execution_context, context, perform);
}

/// As [`animations_element_animations_cancel_css_animations_and_transitions`], of the owner at `slot` alone: a
/// pseudo-element that is no longer rendered, while its element is.
///
/// # Safety
/// As for [`animations_element_animations_cancel_css_animations_and_transitions`].
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_cancel_css_animations_and_transitions_of_owner(
    animations: *mut ElementAnimations,
    slot: AnimationOwnerSlot,
    host: *const DocumentHost,
    node: u32,
    keep_alive: FfiKeepAlive,
    in_execution_context: FfiInExecutionContext,
    context: *mut c_void,
    perform: HostEffectPerformer,
) {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller, and the borrow of the lists ends before the host performs anything.
    let taken = unsafe { &mut *animations }
        .take_css_animations_and_transitions(Some(slot), unsafe { style_engine_target(host, node) });
    cancel_taken_animations(&taken, keep_alive, in_execution_context, context, perform);
}

/// Cancels the CSS animations and transitions taken from their owners, each kept alive by the host for the call.
fn cancel_taken_animations(
    taken: &[AnimationHandle],
    keep_alive: FfiKeepAlive,
    in_execution_context: FfiInExecutionContext,
    context: *mut c_void,
    perform: HostEffectPerformer,
) {
    for animation in taken {
        // SAFETY: The host keeps alive an animation it is handed for as long as this call lasts.
        unsafe { keep_alive(context, animation) };
    }
    for animation in taken {
        cancel_animation(animation, Invalidate::No, in_execution_context, context, perform);
    }
}

/// The bytes the lists of the animations of an element hold, with the records of the animations associated with it and
/// of their effects, and the keyframe sets those run that `first_counted` with `context` answers are counted here first.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_record_memory_size(
    animations: &ElementAnimations,
    first_counted: unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, set: *const KeyframeSet) -> bool,
    context: *mut c_void,
) -> usize {
    let mut bytes = animations.memory_size();
    for animation in animations.associated() {
        bytes += animation.memory_size();
        let Some(effect) = animation.borrow().effect().cloned() else {
            continue;
        };
        bytes += effect.memory_size();
        let keyframes = effect.borrow().keyframes().cloned();
        // SAFETY: The host only notes the address of the set.
        if let Some(keyframes) = keyframes
            && unsafe { first_counted(context, Arc::as_ptr(&keyframes)) }
        {
            bytes += crate::heap_size::ARC_HEADER_BYTES + size_of::<KeyframeSet>() + keyframes.heap_size();
        }
    }
    bytes
}

/// Forgets the descriptions of the effects of the element `animations` belongs to that the host published to the style
/// engine, as the element's identity in the engine changes.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_element_animations_forget_published_effect_descriptions(
    animations: &mut ElementAnimations,
) {
    animations.forget_published_effect_descriptions();
}

/// One effect the host samples on an element, by its record, with the record of its associated animation, or null
/// where it has none, which the host describes but does not sample.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiSampledEffect {
    pub effect: *const AnimationEffectCell,
    pub animation: *const AnimationCell,
}

/// What the host samples of one element's effects: the description of each effect, in composite order, and the
/// effects it samples, each with the timing it samples it with.
pub(crate) struct SampledEffectDescriptions {
    pub(crate) descriptions: smallvec::SmallVec<[Arc<crate::css::style::effect_descriptions::EffectDescription>; 4]>,
    pub(crate) sampled: crate::css::style_compute::HostSampledEffects,
}

/// The descriptions of `effects` and the timing the host samples each with an animation with.
///
/// # Safety
/// Each effect and non-null animation `effects` names must be one the host holds a reference to.
pub(crate) unsafe fn describe_sampled_effects(effects: &[FfiSampledEffect]) -> SampledEffectDescriptions {
    let mut described = SampledEffectDescriptions {
        descriptions: smallvec::SmallVec::with_capacity(effects.len()),
        sampled: smallvec::SmallVec::with_capacity(effects.len()),
    };
    for sampled in effects {
        // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
        let (effect, animation) = unsafe { (&*sampled.effect, sampled.animation.as_ref()) };
        let effect = effect.borrow();
        let description = effect.description().clone();
        described.descriptions.push(description.clone());
        let Some(animation) = animation else {
            continue;
        };
        // NB: The style engine samples the animation's timeline as the timing model reads it now, with what moves it
        //     as a clock tick samples it.
        let animation = animation.borrow();
        let timeline = animation.timeline();
        let timing = super::snapshot::EffectTimingSnapshot {
            effect: effect.timing(),
            playback: *animation.playback(),
            timeline: timeline.map(|timeline| timeline.sample()).unwrap_or_default(),
            has_timeline: timeline.is_some(),
            clock: timeline.map(|timeline| timeline.clock()).unwrap_or_default(),
        };
        described.sampled.push(crate::css::style_compute::HostSampledEffect {
            description,
            timing: (&timing).into(),
        });
    }
    described
}

/// What kind of timeline the host makes.
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FfiTimelineKind {
    Document,
    Scroll,
    View,
    Internal,
}

/// One side of the view progress visibility range of a view timeline, as `ViewTimelineInsetEdge` describes it, whose
/// calculation, if any, is a style value or null.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FfiViewTimelineInsetEdge {
    pub is_auto: bool,
    pub px: f64,
    pub percentage: f64,
    pub calculated: *const c_void,
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/scroll-animations-1/#view-timeline-inset
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FfiViewTimelineInset {
    pub start: FfiViewTimelineInsetEdge,
    pub end: FfiViewTimelineInsetEdge,
}

impl FfiViewTimelineInset {
    /// # Safety
    /// The calculations must be null or live style values.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn retained(&self) -> ViewTimelineInset {
        let edge = |edge: &FfiViewTimelineInsetEdge| ViewTimelineInsetEdge {
            is_auto: edge.is_auto,
            px: edge.px,
            percentage: edge.percentage,
            // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
            calculated: unsafe { retained_optional_value(edge.calculated) },
        };
        ViewTimelineInset {
            start: edge(&self.start),
            end: edge(&self.end),
        }
    }
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/scroll-animations-1/#dom-scrolltimeline-source
/// The host's `DOM::Element` that is the source of a scroll timeline, or null, or, where `is_anonymous`, the host's
/// `CSS::Scroller` that an anonymous timeline finds from `target`, the host's `DOM::Element`, or from its
/// pseudo-element, the host's `PseudoElement`, where `has_pseudo_element`.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FfiScrollTimelineSource {
    pub element: *mut c_void,
    pub is_anonymous: bool,
    pub scroller: u8,
    pub target: *mut c_void,
    pub pseudo_element: u8,
    pub has_pseudo_element: bool,
}

impl FfiScrollTimelineSource {
    pub(crate) fn get(&self) -> ScrollTimelineSource {
        if !self.is_anonymous {
            return ScrollTimelineSource::Element(NonNull::new(self.element));
        }
        ScrollTimelineSource::Anonymous {
            scroller: self.scroller,
            target: NonNull::new(self.target).expect("an anonymous timeline has a target"),
            pseudo_element: self.has_pseudo_element.then_some(self.pseudo_element),
        }
    }
}

impl From<ScrollTimelineSource> for FfiScrollTimelineSource {
    fn from(source: ScrollTimelineSource) -> Self {
        let mut ffi = Self {
            element: std::ptr::null_mut(),
            is_anonymous: false,
            scroller: 0,
            target: std::ptr::null_mut(),
            pseudo_element: 0,
            has_pseudo_element: false,
        };
        match source {
            ScrollTimelineSource::Element(element) => {
                ffi.element = element.map_or(std::ptr::null_mut(), NonNull::as_ptr);
            }
            ScrollTimelineSource::Anonymous {
                scroller,
                target,
                pseudo_element,
            } => {
                ffi.is_anonymous = true;
                ffi.scroller = scroller;
                ffi.target = target.as_ptr();
                ffi.pseudo_element = pseudo_element.unwrap_or(0);
                ffi.has_pseudo_element = pseudo_element.is_some();
            }
        }
        ffi
    }
}

/// What the host makes a timeline of: a document timeline's origin time, a scroll timeline's source and axis, and a
/// view timeline's inset besides.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiTimelineDescription {
    pub kind: FfiTimelineKind,
    pub origin_time: f64,
    pub source: FfiScrollTimelineSource,
    /// The host's `ScrollAxis`.
    pub axis: u8,
    pub inset: FfiViewTimelineInset,
}

/// A new timeline associated with the host's `DOM::Document` `document`, as `description` describes it, which has no
/// object script sees of it yet.
///
/// # Safety
/// The calculations of a view timeline's inset must be null or live style values.
pub(crate) unsafe fn timeline_of_description(
    document: NonNull<c_void>,
    description: &FfiTimelineDescription,
) -> TimelineHandle {
    let scroll = |view| {
        TimelineKind::Scroll(Box::new(ScrollTimelineState {
            source: description.source.get(),
            axis: description.axis,
            last_max_scroll_offset: None,
            followed_scroller: None,
            view,
        }))
    };
    let kind = match description.kind {
        FfiTimelineKind::Document => TimelineKind::Document {
            origin_time: description.origin_time,
        },
        FfiTimelineKind::Scroll => scroll(None),
        FfiTimelineKind::View => scroll(Some(ViewTimelineState {
            // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
            inset: unsafe { description.inset.retained() },
            last_metrics: None,
            subject_style_node: None,
        })),
        FfiTimelineKind::Internal => TimelineKind::Internal {
            time_for_observation: None,
        },
    };
    TimelineHandle::new(document, kind)
}

/// What the host reads of a timeline: its kind and its current time, which is unresolved where the timeline is
/// inactive.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiTimeline {
    pub kind: FfiTimelineKind,
    pub current_time: OptionalTimeValue,
}

/// What the host reads of `timeline`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_timeline_read(timeline: &TimelineCell) -> FfiTimeline {
    let current_time = timeline.sample().current_time;
    let kind = match &timeline.borrow().kind {
        TimelineKind::Document { .. } => FfiTimelineKind::Document,
        TimelineKind::Scroll(scroll) if scroll.view.is_some() => FfiTimelineKind::View,
        TimelineKind::Scroll(_) => FfiTimelineKind::Scroll,
        TimelineKind::Internal { .. } => FfiTimelineKind::Internal,
    };
    FfiTimeline { kind, current_time }
}

/// The animations associated with `timeline`, which lives as long as the timeline.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_timeline_associated_animations(timeline: &TimelineCell) -> *mut WeakAnimationSet {
    timeline.associated_animations().as_ptr()
}

/// The animations associated with `timeline` that an update of its current time may change, which lives as long as the
/// timeline. The others have finished on a monotonically increasing timeline and have no pending task.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_timeline_animations_needing_update(timeline: &TimelineCell) -> *mut WeakAnimationSet {
    timeline.animations_needing_update().as_ptr()
}

/// The animations associated with the elements of a document whose animations are `animations`, which lives as long as
/// the document.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn animations_document_associated_animations(
    animations: &mut DocumentAnimations,
) -> *mut WeakAnimationSet {
    animations.set_mut(DocumentAnimationSetKind::Associated)
}

//! What the procedures of animations ask the host to do: settle promises, queue tasks and events, and invalidate
//! style. A procedure only records these, in the order its steps take them, and the host performs them once the
//! procedure has returned, holding no borrow of any record.

use super::animation::AnimationHandle;
use super::effect::EffectHandle;
use super::timing::TimeValue;
use smallvec::SmallVec;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::ptr::NonNull;

/// The type of an `AnimationPlaybackEvent` a procedure queues.
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PlaybackEventType {
    Finish,
    Cancel,
    Remove,
}

/// One thing a procedure asks the host to do for an animation.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) enum HostEffectKind {
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#current-ready-promise
    /// Let the current ready promise be a new promise in the relevant Realm of the animation.
    ReplaceReadyPromise,
    /// Resolve the current ready promise with the animation.
    ResolveReadyPromise,
    /// Reject the current ready promise with a DOMException named "AbortError", set its [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal
    /// slot to true, and let the current ready promise be a new resolved promise with the animation.
    RejectReadyPromise,
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#current-finished-promise
    /// Let the current finished promise be a new promise in the relevant Realm of the animation.
    ReplaceFinishedPromise,
    /// Resolve the current finished promise with the animation.
    ResolveFinishedPromise,
    /// Reject the current finished promise with a DOMException named "AbortError", set its [[PromiseIsHandled]]
    /// internal slot to true, and let the current finished promise be a new promise.
    RejectFinishedPromise,
    /// Queue a task to run the finish notification steps of the animation, unless there is one queued already.
    QueueFinishNotificationTask,
    /// Cancel the queued task to run the finish notification steps of the animation, if any.
    CancelFinishNotificationTask,
    /// Create an `AnimationPlaybackEvent` and append it to the pending animation event queue of the animation's
    /// document for timing, or queue a task to dispatch it at the animation without one. Its scheduled event time is
    /// `scheduled_timeline_time` converted to an origin-relative time, where the timeline can convert it.
    QueuePlaybackEvent {
        r#type: PlaybackEventType,
        current_time: Option<TimeValue>,
        timeline_time: Option<TimeValue>,
        scheduled_timeline_time: Option<TimeValue>,
    },
    /// Invalidate the style the associated effect produces. `changes_plan` is whether this changes the animation as
    /// the last rendering update planned it for the render clock, rather than move it on in time, as a rendering
    /// update does.
    InvalidateEffect { changes_plan: bool },
    /// Unless the style the associated effect produces can skip its update for this frame, which the host notes
    /// then, invalidate it as `InvalidateEffect` does without changing the plan, where `invalidate`.
    InvalidateUnlessThrottled { invalidate: bool },
    /// Associate the animation with `element`, the host's `DOM::Element` the animation's associated effect targets.
    AssociateWithTarget { element: NonNull<c_void> },
    /// Disassociate the animation from `element`, the host's `DOM::Element` that `effect`, the animation's associated
    /// effect, targeted.
    DisassociateFromTarget {
        element: NonNull<c_void>,
        effect: EffectHandle,
    },
    /// Recompute the style of the target of `effect`, which no longer applies as it did.
    RecomputeEffectStyle { effect: EffectHandle },
    /// Ask for a repaint of the target of the associated effect.
    RequestRepaint,
    /// Ask the document of the target of the associated effect for a rendering update in `delay` milliseconds, as
    /// the effect begins.
    ScheduleWakeup { delay: f64 },
}

/// What one procedure asks the host to do, in order. Most procedures ask for little or nothing, which needs no
/// allocation.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct HostEffects(SmallVec<[(AnimationHandle, HostEffectKind); 4]>);

impl HostEffects {
    pub(crate) fn push(&mut self, animation: &AnimationHandle, kind: HostEffectKind) {
        self.0.push((animation.clone(), kind));
    }

    /// Appends what another procedure asks the host to do after this.
    pub(crate) fn extend(&mut self, other: HostEffects) {
        self.0.extend(other.0);
    }

    /// What the procedures asked for, in order.
    pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &(AnimationHandle, HostEffectKind)> {
        self.0.iter()
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn kinds(&self) -> Vec<HostEffectKind> {
        self.0.iter().map(|(_, kind)| kind.clone()).collect()
    }
}

impl IntoIterator for HostEffects {
    type Item = (AnimationHandle, HostEffectKind);
    type IntoIter = smallvec::IntoIter<[(AnimationHandle, HostEffectKind); 4]>;

    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
        self.0.into_iter()
    }
}

//! What the host's per-frame decisions read of an animation and its associated effect: the throttling of its style
//! updates and ticks, the wakeups it arms, and what the compositor update hands the compositor. The record resolves
//! all of it from one current time, and decides what follows from its timing alone.

use super::animation::{AnimationKind, AnimationRecord, TransitionPhase};
use super::timeline_state::time_unit_of;
use super::timing::{
    self, AnimationEffectPhase, AnimationEffectTiming, AnimationPlayState, AnimationPlayback, OptionalNumber,
    OptionalTimeValue, TimeValue, TimeValueType,
};
use crate::css::animation::FfiCompositeOperation;

/// What made an animation.
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FfiAnimationKind {
    Script,
    CssAnimation,
    CssTransition,
    Smil,
}

/// The instant a compositor animation of an effect is anchored at, as far as the record decides it.
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FfiCompositorAnchorKind {
    /// The timing of the animation keeps the compositor from running it.
    None,
    /// The animation is anchored at the timestamp of the document's last animation frame.
    LastAnimationFrame,
    /// The animation is anchored at an origin-relative time.
    OriginRelativeTime,
}

/// What the host's per-frame decisions read of an animation and its associated effect, all of it at the current time
/// of the animation.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FfiAnimationTimingState {
    pub kind: FfiAnimationKind,
    pub playback: AnimationPlayback,
    pub play_state: AnimationPlayState,
    pub has_monotonically_increasing_timeline: bool,
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#animation-current-time
    pub current_time: OptionalTimeValue,
    /// The current time of the animation at the timestamp the host asked about, where it asked about one.
    pub current_time_at_timestamp: OptionalTimeValue,
    /// Whether the animation has an associated effect, which the rest describe.
    pub has_effect: bool,
    pub effect: AnimationEffectTiming,
    pub composite: FfiCompositeOperation,
    pub phase: AnimationEffectPhase,
    pub is_in_effect: bool,
    pub end_time: TimeValue,
    pub previous_current_iteration: f64,
    /// Whether the animation is a CSS transition that has not started yet, whose play is pending until the next
    /// animation update.
    pub is_initial_pending_css_transition: bool,
    /// Where the compositor may run the effect as far as its timing goes, the instant it is anchored at, and the local
    /// time it has there.
    pub compositor_anchor: FfiCompositorAnchorKind,
    pub compositor_anchor_origin_relative_time: f64,
    pub compositor_anchor_local_time: f64,
    /// Whether the timing of the effect lets a paint-only effect that nothing on screen shows skip its updates.
    pub can_throttle_offscreen_effect: bool,
    /// Whether the timing of the effect lets an effect that the winners of all its properties replace skip its
    /// updates.
    pub can_throttle_replaced_effect: bool,
    /// The time until the effect next changes phase, where it is ahead.
    pub next_phase_boundary_delay: OptionalNumber,
    /// The local time of the next iteration event of a CSS animation whose ticks are throttled, as far as its timing
    /// decides.
    pub next_throttled_iteration_event_time: OptionalNumber,
}

fn is_milliseconds(time: TimeValue) -> bool {
    time.r#type == TimeValueType::Milliseconds
}

impl AnimationRecord {
    /// What made the animation.
    pub(crate) fn ffi_kind(&self) -> FfiAnimationKind {
        match self.kind() {
            AnimationKind::Script => FfiAnimationKind::Script,
            AnimationKind::CssAnimation(_) => FfiAnimationKind::CssAnimation,
            AnimationKind::CssTransition(_) => FfiAnimationKind::CssTransition,
            AnimationKind::Smil { .. } => FfiAnimationKind::Smil,
        }
    }

    /// A zero time in the unit of the times of the timeline of the animation.
    pub(crate) fn zero_time(&self) -> TimeValue {
        let progress_based = self
            .timeline()
            .is_some_and(|timeline| timeline.borrow().is_progress_based());
        TimeValue::zero(time_unit_of(progress_based))
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#associated-effect-end
    pub(crate) fn associated_effect_end(&self) -> TimeValue {
        // The associated effect end of an animation is equal to the end time of the animation’s associated effect. If
        // the animation has no associated effect, the associated effect end is zero.
        match self.effect() {
            Some(effect) => timing::end_time(&effect.borrow().timing()),
            None => self.zero_time(),
        }
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#animation-current-time
    pub(crate) fn current_time(&self) -> Option<TimeValue> {
        let timeline_time = self.timeline().and_then(|timeline| timeline.current_time());
        timing::current_time_at(self.playback(), timeline_time)
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#play-states
    pub(crate) fn play_state(&self) -> AnimationPlayState {
        self.play_state_at(self.current_time())
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#play-states
    /// At `current_time`, the current time of the animation.
    pub(crate) fn play_state_at(&self, current_time: Option<TimeValue>) -> AnimationPlayState {
        timing::play_state_at(self.playback(), current_time, self.associated_effect_end())
    }

    /// Whether the animation has a monotonically increasing timeline.
    pub(crate) fn has_monotonically_increasing_timeline(&self) -> bool {
        self.timeline()
            .is_some_and(|timeline| timeline.borrow().is_monotonically_increasing())
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#animation-effect-phases-and-states
    /// The phase of the associated effect of the animation at the current time of the animation, idle without one.
    pub(crate) fn effect_phase(&self) -> AnimationEffectPhase {
        let Some(effect) = self.effect() else {
            return AnimationEffectPhase::Idle;
        };
        let sample = self.timeline().map(|timeline| timeline.sample());
        let timeline_time = sample.as_ref().and_then(|sample| sample.current_time.get());
        let current_time = timing::current_time_at(self.playback(), timeline_time);
        timing::resolve_timing(
            &effect.borrow().timing(),
            current_time,
            Some(self.playback()),
            sample.as_ref(),
        )
        .phase
    }

    /// What the host's per-frame decisions read of the animation now, with its current time at `timestamp`, where the
    /// host asks about one.
    pub(crate) fn timing_state(&self, timestamp: Option<f64>) -> FfiAnimationTimingState {
        let playback = *self.playback();
        let timeline = self.timeline();
        let sample = timeline.map(|timeline| timeline.sample());
        let current_time =
            timing::current_time_at(&playback, sample.as_ref().and_then(|sample| sample.current_time.get()));
        let current_time_at_timestamp = timestamp.and_then(|timestamp| {
            let timeline_time = timeline.and_then(|timeline| timeline.current_time_at_timestamp(timestamp, None));
            timing::current_time_at(&playback, timeline_time)
        });
        let has_monotonically_increasing_timeline = sample.is_some_and(|sample| sample.is_monotonically_increasing);

        let effect = self.effect().map(|effect| effect.borrow());
        let effect_timing = effect.as_ref().map(|effect| effect.timing());
        let resolved = effect_timing
            .as_ref()
            .map(|effect_timing| timing::resolve_timing(effect_timing, current_time, Some(&playback), sample.as_ref()));
        let associated_effect_end = self.associated_effect_end();
        let mut state = FfiAnimationTimingState {
            kind: self.ffi_kind(),
            playback,
            play_state: timing::play_state_at(&playback, current_time, associated_effect_end),
            has_monotonically_increasing_timeline,
            current_time: current_time.into(),
            current_time_at_timestamp: current_time_at_timestamp.into(),
            has_effect: effect.is_some(),
            effect: effect_timing.unwrap_or_default(),
            composite: effect
                .as_ref()
                .map_or(FfiCompositeOperation::Replace, |effect| effect.composite()),
            phase: resolved
                .as_ref()
                .map_or(AnimationEffectPhase::Idle, |resolved| resolved.phase),
            is_in_effect: resolved.as_ref().is_some_and(timing::is_in_effect),
            end_time: associated_effect_end,
            previous_current_iteration: effect.as_ref().map_or(0.0, |effect| effect.previous_current_iteration),
            is_initial_pending_css_transition: playback.pending()
                && playback.has_pending_play_task
                && matches!(self.kind(), AnimationKind::CssTransition(state) if state.previous_phase == TransitionPhase::Idle),
            compositor_anchor: FfiCompositorAnchorKind::None,
            compositor_anchor_origin_relative_time: 0.0,
            compositor_anchor_local_time: 0.0,
            can_throttle_offscreen_effect: false,
            can_throttle_replaced_effect: false,
            next_phase_boundary_delay: None.into(),
            next_throttled_iteration_event_time: None.into(),
        };
        drop(effect);
        if !state.has_effect {
            return state;
        }

        // NB: A compositor animation runs from an anchor on the monotonic clock, at the playback rate, through one
        //     iteration or an infinite number of them.
        let timing = state.effect;
        let rate = playback.effective_playback_rate();
        let runs_forward = rate > 0.0 && rate.is_finite();
        let runs_on_a_monotonic_clock = state.play_state == AnimationPlayState::Running
            && !playback.pending()
            && rate > 0.0
            && has_monotonically_increasing_timeline;
        let runs_one_or_infinite_iterations = timing.iteration_count.is_infinite() || timing.iteration_count == 1.0;
        let times_in_milliseconds = is_milliseconds(timing.start_delay) && is_milliseconds(timing.iteration_duration);
        let has_finite_positive_duration =
            timing.iteration_duration.value > 0.0 && timing.iteration_duration.value.is_finite();

        let compositor_may_run_it = state.play_state == AnimationPlayState::Running
            && (!playback.pending() || state.is_initial_pending_css_transition)
            && has_monotonically_increasing_timeline
            && matches!(state.phase, AnimationEffectPhase::Before | AnimationEffectPhase::Active)
            && runs_one_or_infinite_iterations
            && state.composite == FfiCompositeOperation::Replace
            && runs_forward
            && times_in_milliseconds
            && timing.iteration_duration.value > 0.0
            && (state.phase != AnimationEffectPhase::Before
                || timing::before_active_boundary_time(&timing) == timing.start_delay);
        if let Some(local_time) = current_time.filter(|time| compositor_may_run_it && is_milliseconds(*time)) {
            state.compositor_anchor_local_time = local_time.value;
            if !state.is_initial_pending_css_transition {
                state.compositor_anchor = FfiCompositorAnchorKind::LastAnimationFrame;
            } else if let Some(origin_relative_time) =
                timeline
                    .zip(self.css_transition_initial_ready_time())
                    .and_then(|(timeline, ready_time)| {
                        // OPTIMIZATION: A new CSS transition is play-pending until the next animation update. Start its
                        //               compositor animation at the time its play becomes ready without resolving its
                        //               pending task.
                        timeline.convert_a_timeline_time_to_an_origin_relative_time(Some(TimeValue::milliseconds(
                            ready_time,
                        )))
                    })
            {
                state.compositor_anchor = FfiCompositorAnchorKind::OriginRelativeTime;
                state.compositor_anchor_origin_relative_time = origin_relative_time;
            }
        }

        state.can_throttle_offscreen_effect = runs_on_a_monotonic_clock
            && rate.is_finite()
            && state.phase == AnimationEffectPhase::Active
            && times_in_milliseconds
            && has_finite_positive_duration
            && timing.end_delay.value == 0.0;
        state.can_throttle_replaced_effect = runs_on_a_monotonic_clock
            && state.phase == AnimationEffectPhase::Active
            && runs_one_or_infinite_iterations
            && times_in_milliseconds;

        if let Some(current_time) =
            current_time.filter(|time| times_in_milliseconds && is_milliseconds(*time) && rate > 0.0)
        {
            let mut next_phase_boundary = timing.start_delay.value;
            let ahead = if current_time.value < next_phase_boundary {
                true
            } else {
                next_phase_boundary += timing.iteration_duration.value * timing.iteration_count;
                !timing.iteration_count.is_infinite()
            };
            let delay = (next_phase_boundary - current_time.value) / rate;
            if ahead && delay > 0.0 {
                state.next_phase_boundary_delay = Some(delay).into();
            }
        }

        // NB: Observable throttled animations need a rendering update at the next iteration boundary, not at every
        //     display refresh. Seeking and cancellation already request their own updates.
        if state.kind == FfiAnimationKind::CssAnimation
            && !playback.pending()
            && state.play_state == AnimationPlayState::Running
            && runs_forward
            && has_monotonically_increasing_timeline
            && times_in_milliseconds
            && has_finite_positive_duration
        {
            state.next_throttled_iteration_event_time = Some(
                timing.start_delay.value
                    + (state.previous_current_iteration + 1.0 - timing.iteration_start)
                        * timing.iteration_duration.value,
            )
            .into();
        }
        state
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::animations::animation::AnimationHandle;
    use crate::animations::effect::EffectHandle;
    use timing::{SpecifiedEffectTiming, SpecifiedIterationDuration};

    /// A script animation of an effect with an iteration duration of a second, `iterations` times, held at
    /// `current_time`.
    fn animation_held_at(current_time: f64, iterations: f64) -> AnimationHandle {
        let effect = EffectHandle::new();
        effect.borrow_mut().set_specified_timing(SpecifiedEffectTiming {
            iteration_duration: SpecifiedIterationDuration {
                is_auto: false,
                milliseconds: 1000.0,
            },
            start_delay: 100.0,
            iteration_count: iterations,
            ..SpecifiedEffectTiming::default()
        });
        effect.borrow_mut().normalize_specified_timing(None);
        let animation = AnimationHandle::new(AnimationKind::Script);
        animation.borrow_mut().set_effect(Some(effect));
        animation.borrow_mut().playback_mut().hold_time = Some(TimeValue::milliseconds(current_time)).into();
        animation
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_next_phase_boundary_is_the_start_delay_and_then_the_active_end() {
        let state = animation_held_at(50.0, 2.0).borrow().timing_state(None);
        assert_eq!(state.phase, AnimationEffectPhase::Before);
        assert_eq!(state.next_phase_boundary_delay.get(), Some(50.0));

        let state = animation_held_at(600.0, 2.0).borrow().timing_state(None);
        assert_eq!(state.next_phase_boundary_delay.get(), Some(1500.0));

        let state = animation_held_at(600.0, f64::INFINITY).borrow().timing_state(None);
        assert_eq!(state.next_phase_boundary_delay.get(), None);
    }
}

/*

//! The keyframes script reads of an effect whose keyframes come from CSS, a `@keyframes` rule or a CSS transition,
//! and those a copy of such an effect takes.
//! https://drafts.csswg.org/css-animations-2/#keyframes

use super::animation::AnimationKind;
use super::bindings_api::ParsedEasing;
use super::effect::AnimationEffectRecord;
use super::keyframes::{
    CompositeOperationOrAuto, KeyframeOrigin, KeyframeProperty, KeyframeSet, ResourceContext, offset_of_key,
};
use crate::css::style_compute::{FfiReflectedKeyframeProperty, FfiStyleSheetResourceContext};
use crate::css::style_value::{RetainedStyleValueData, StyleValueData, retain_style_value};
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::ptr::NonNull;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// A keyframe of CSS as script reads it.
pub(crate) struct CssKeyframe {
    pub(crate) offset: f64,
    pub(crate) easing: ParsedEasing,
    pub(crate) composite: CompositeOperationOrAuto,
    pub(crate) properties: Vec<(KeyframeProperty, RetainedStyleValueData)>,
}

impl CssKeyframe {
    /// Sets the value the keyframe gives `property`, in place of what it gave it before.
    fn set(&mut self, property: KeyframeProperty, value: RetainedStyleValueData) {
        match self.properties.iter_mut().find(|(declared, _)| *declared == property) {
            Some((_, declared_value)) => *declared_value = value,
            None => self.properties.push((property, value)),
        }
    }
}

/// What reading the keyframes of CSS of an effect reads of it, which holds no borrow of its record.
pub(crate) struct ReflectedEffect {
    keyframes: Option<Arc<KeyframeSet>>,
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-animations-2/#keyframes
    /// The easing a keyframe of the effect that declares none of its own runs: the `animation-timing-function` of its
    /// CSS animation, and `linear` for any other.
    default_easing: ParsedEasing,
    target: Option<NonNull<c_void>>,
    /// The host's `PseudoElement` of the target pseudo-selector, if any.
    pseudo_element: Option<u8>,
}

impl ReflectedEffect {
    pub(crate) fn of(effect: &AnimationEffectRecord) -> Self {
        let default_easing = effect
            .associated_animation()
            .map_or_else(ParsedEasing::linear, |animation| {
                let animation = animation.borrow();
                let AnimationKind::CssAnimation(state) = animation.kind() else {
                    return ParsedEasing::linear();
                };
                state
                    .applied_definition
                    .as_ref()
                    .and_then(|definition| ParsedEasing::of_timing_function(definition.timing_function()))
                    .unwrap_or_else(ParsedEasing::ease)
            });
        Self {
            keyframes: effect.keyframes().cloned(),
            default_easing,
            target: effect.target_element(),
            pseudo_element: effect.pseudo_element().map(|pseudo_element| pseudo_element.kind),
        }
    }
}

/// The keyframes of CSS the effect runs as they are declared: those of each block of its `@keyframes` rule, or those
/// of its CSS transition, with the blocks of one offset, easing and composite operation merged.
fn declared_css_keyframes(effect: &ReflectedEffect) -> Vec<CssKeyframe> {
    let mut frames: Vec<CssKeyframe> = Vec::new();
    let Some(set) = effect.keyframes.as_deref() else {
        return frames;
    };

    let default_easing = &effect.default_easing;
    let mut append_frame =
        |key: u64,
         easing: Option<&RetainedStyleValueData>,
         composite: CompositeOperationOrAuto,
         declarations: &mut dyn Iterator<Item = (KeyframeProperty, &RetainedStyleValueData)>| {
            let offset = offset_of_key(key as f64);
            // AD-HOC: Step 2.2 uses the computed timing function. Substitution-dependent keyframe easings use the
            //         animation-wide easing for web compatibility.
            let easing = easing
                .and_then(ParsedEasing::of_timing_function)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| default_easing.clone());
            let index = match frames.iter().position(|frame| {
                frame.offset == offset
                    && frame.easing.serialization() == easing.serialization()
                    && frame.composite == composite
            }) {
                Some(index) => index,
                None => {
                    frames.push(CssKeyframe {
                        offset,
                        easing,
                        composite,
                        properties: Vec::new(),
                    });
                    frames.len() - 1
                }
            };
            for (property, value) in declarations {
                frames[index].set(property, value.clone_retained());
            }
        };
    match set.declared_keyframes() {
        // 2.3.1. Cascade together all of its declaration blocks such that for each CSS property (except those that are
        //        "not animatable", which must be ignored) the last declaration among all its <keyframe-block>
        //        declarations takes precedence.
        Some(declared) => {
            for keyframe in declared.keyframes() {
                append_frame(
                    keyframe.key,
                    keyframe.easing.as_ref(),
                    keyframe.composite,
                    &mut declared
                        .declarations_of(keyframe)
                        .iter()
                        .map(|(property, value)| (property.clone(), value)),
                );
            }
        }
        None => {
            for keyframe in set.keyframes() {
                let declarations = set.declarations_of(keyframe).iter().filter_map(|declaration| {
                    Some((
                        KeyframeProperty::Id(declaration.property_id),
                        declaration.value.declared()?,
                    ))
                });
                let custom_declarations = set.custom_declarations_of(keyframe).iter().filter_map(|declaration| {
                    Some((
                        KeyframeProperty::Custom(declaration.name.clone()),
                        declaration.value.declared()?,
                    ))
                });
                append_frame(
                    keyframe.key,
                    None,
                    keyframe.composite,
                    &mut declarations.chain(custom_declarations),
                );
            }
        }
    }
    frames
}

/// The keyframes of CSS a copy of the effect takes: those it declares, by their offsets, with the values of a CSS
/// transition unscaled by the effective zoom they were computed at.
pub(crate) fn css_keyframes_of_copy(effect: &ReflectedEffect) -> Vec<CssKeyframe> {
    let mut frames = declared_css_keyframes(effect);
    frames.sort_by(|first, second| first.offset.total_cmp(&second.offset));
    if let Some(set) = effect.keyframes.as_deref()
        && set.origin() == KeyframeOrigin::Transition
    {
        unscale_by_zoom(&mut frames, f64::from(set.computed_value_zoom()));
    }
    frames
}

/// The style sheet the keyframes of the effect come from, which a copy of it resolves URLs against.
pub(crate) fn resource_context(effect: &AnimationEffectRecord) -> Option<ResourceContext> {
    effect.keyframes()?.resource_context().cloned()
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-animations-2/#keyframes
/// The keyframes of CSS the effect runs as `getKeyframes()` returns them: the values a `@keyframes` rule declares
/// computed against the target, with its implicit endpoints taking the target's own values, and those of a CSS
/// transition, each by its offset, and unscaled by the effective zoom they were computed at.
pub(crate) fn computed_css_keyframes(effect: &ReflectedEffect) -> Vec<CssKeyframe> {
    let mut frames = declared_css_keyframes(effect);
    let Some(set) = effect.keyframes.as_deref() else {
        return frames;
    };
    if set.origin() == KeyframeOrigin::Transition {
        unscale_by_zoom(&mut frames, f64::from(set.computed_value_zoom()));
        return frames;
    }
    if set.declared_keyframes().is_none() {
        return frames;
    }
    let mut has_custom_properties = false;
    for frame in &mut frames {
        frame.properties.retain(|(property, _)| {
            let is_custom = matches!(property, KeyframeProperty::Custom(_));
            has_custom_properties |= is_custom;
            !is_custom
        });
    }
    let default_easing = &effect.default_easing;
    if !has_custom_properties && frames.iter().all(|frame| frame.properties.is_empty()) {
        return Vec::new();
    }

    let (target, pseudo_element) = (effect.target, effect.pseudo_element);
    if let Some(target) = target
        && let Some(underlying_values) =
            compute_css_keyframe_values(target, pseudo_element, &mut frames, set.resource_context())
    {
        for offset in [0.0, 1.0] {
            let mut present: Vec<u16> = Vec::new();
            let mut destination = None;
            for (index, frame) in frames.iter().enumerate() {
                if frame.offset != offset {
                    continue;
                }
                present.extend(frame.properties.iter().filter_map(|(property, _)| match property {
                    KeyframeProperty::Id(property_id) => Some(*property_id),
                    KeyframeProperty::Custom(_) => None,
                }));
                // AD-HOC: Step 3.1 uses the default composite. Underlying-value endpoints use "replace", even for an
                //         additive effect, so their values aren't added to themselves.
                if destination.is_none()
                    && frame.easing.serialization() == default_easing.serialization()
                    && matches!(
                        frame.composite,
                        CompositeOperationOrAuto::Auto | CompositeOperationOrAuto::Replace
                    )
                {
                    destination = Some(index);
                }
            }
            let missing: Vec<_> = underlying_values
                .iter()
                .filter(|(property_id, _)| !present.contains(property_id))
                .map(|(property_id, value)| (KeyframeProperty::Id(*property_id), value.clone_retained()))
                .collect();
            // AD-HOC: Custom properties contribute keyframe offsets and implicit endpoints, but their values are
            //         omitted from CSS keyframe reflection for web compatibility.
            if missing.is_empty() && !has_custom_properties {
                continue;
            }
            // 3.2. For any property in animated properties that is not otherwise present in a keyframe with an offset
            //      of 0% or one that would be positioned earlier in the used keyframe order, add the computed value of
            //      that property on element to initial keyframe's keyframe values.
            match destination {
                Some(destination) => {
                    for (property, value) in missing {
                        frames[destination].set(property, value);
                    }
                }
                None => {
                    // AD-HOC: Step 3.3 prepends the initial keyframe. For web compatibility, reflected synthetic
                    //         endpoints follow explicitly declared frames at the same offset.
                    frames.push(CssKeyframe {
                        offset,
                        easing: default_easing.clone(),
                        composite: CompositeOperationOrAuto::Replace,
                        properties: missing,
                    });
                }
            }
        }
    }
    // 4. The computed order of keyframes—which is the order returned by getKeyframes()—is found by shifting any
    //    keyframes whose offset was specified as a <percentage>, from keyword, or to keyword to the front of the list
    //    (after the generated initial keyframe, if any), and performing a stable sort on these keyframes by their
    //    keyframe offsets.
    frames.sort_by(|first, second| first.offset.total_cmp(&second.offset));
    let zoom = target.map_or(1.0, |target| {
        // SAFETY: The effect keeps its target alive.
        unsafe { web_animation_effective_zoom_of_target(target, pseudo_element.is_some(), pseudo_element.unwrap_or(0)) }
    });
    unscale_by_zoom(&mut frames, zoom);
    frames
}

/// Unscales the values of the longhands `frames` give by the effective zoom `zoom`.
/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-viewport/#zoom-om
fn unscale_by_zoom(frames: &mut [CssKeyframe], zoom: f64) {
    use crate::css::property_metadata::property_id;
    for frame in frames {
        for (property, value) in &mut frame.properties {
            if matches!(
                property,
                KeyframeProperty::Id(property_id::ZOOM) | KeyframeProperty::Custom(_)
            ) {
                continue;
            }
            let unscaled = crate::css::style_value::rust_style_value_unscaled_by_zoom(value.data(), zoom);
            if !unscaled.is_null() {
                // SAFETY: The unscaled value is retained for the caller.
                *value = unsafe { RetainedStyleValueData::from_retained_pointer(unscaled) };
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Computes over the style of the host's `DOM::Element` `target`, or its pseudo-element of the host's
/// `PseudoElement` `pseudo_element`, what the longhands `frames` declare compute to, replacing each frame's
/// declarations with those, by their physical longhands, and answers the target's values of each of them, or none
/// where the target has no style to compute them over.
fn compute_css_keyframe_values(
    target: NonNull<c_void>,
    pseudo_element: Option<u8>,
    frames: &mut [CssKeyframe],
    resource_context: Option<&ResourceContext>,
) -> Option<Vec<(u16, RetainedStyleValueData)>> {
    let properties: Vec<FfiReflectedKeyframeProperty> = frames
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .flat_map(|(keyframe_index, frame)| {
            frame
                .properties
                .iter()
                .filter_map(move |(property, value)| match property {
                    KeyframeProperty::Id(property_id) => Some(FfiReflectedKeyframeProperty {
                        keyframe_index,
                        property_id: *property_id,
                        value: value.pointer(),
                    }),
                    KeyframeProperty::Custom(_) => None,
                })
        })
        .collect();
    let resource_context = resource_context.map_or(
        FfiStyleSheetResourceContext {
            base_url: std::ptr::null(),
            base_url_length: 0,
            has_value: false,
            origin_clean: false,
        },
        |context| FfiStyleSheetResourceContext {
            base_url: context.base_url.as_ptr(),
            base_url_length: context.base_url.len(),
            has_value: true,
            origin_clean: context.origin_clean,
        },
    );

    struct Computed {
        frames: Vec<Vec<(u16, RetainedStyleValueData)>>,
        underlying: Vec<(u16, RetainedStyleValueData)>,
    }
    unsafe extern "C" fn emit(context: *mut c_void, index: usize, property_id: u16, value: *const StyleValueData) {
        // SAFETY: The context is the computation below, and the value is live for the call.
        let (computed, value) = unsafe {
            (
                &mut *context.cast::<Computed>(),
                RetainedStyleValueData::from_retained_pointer(retain_style_value(value)),
            )
        };
        let values = computed.frames.get_mut(index).unwrap_or(&mut computed.underlying);
        match values.iter_mut().find(|(held, _)| *held == property_id) {
            Some((_, held)) => *held = value,
            None => values.push((property_id, value)),
        }
    }
    let mut computed = Computed {
        frames: frames.iter().map(|_| Vec::new()).collect(),
        underlying: Vec::new(),
    };
    // SAFETY: The effect keeps its target alive, and the declarations and resource context are live for the call.
    let computed_over_style = unsafe {
        web_animation_compute_css_keyframe_values(
            target,
            pseudo_element.is_some(),
            pseudo_element.unwrap_or(0),
            properties.as_ptr().cast(),
            properties.len(),
            frames.len(),
            &resource_context,
            (&raw mut computed).cast(),
            emit,
        )
    };
    if !computed_over_style {
        return None;
    }
    for (frame, values) in frames.iter_mut().zip(computed.frames) {
        frame.properties = values
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(property_id, value)| (KeyframeProperty::Id(property_id), value))
            .collect();
    }
    Some(computed.underlying)
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    /// Computes over the style of the target what the declarations `properties` of `keyframe_count` keyframes, from a
    /// style sheet with `resource_context`, compute to, emitting each computed value with the index of its keyframe and
    /// each value of the target with `keyframe_count`, or answers false where the target has no style. `properties`
    /// points at `property_count` `FfiReflectedKeyframeProperty`s.
    fn web_animation_compute_css_keyframe_values(
        target: NonNull<c_void>,
        has_pseudo_element: bool,
        pseudo_element: u8,
        properties: *const c_void,
        property_count: usize,
        keyframe_count: usize,
        resource_context: &FfiStyleSheetResourceContext,
        context: *mut c_void,
        emit: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, usize, u16, *const StyleValueData),
    ) -> bool;

    /// The effective zoom of the computed style of the target, one where it has none.
    fn web_animation_effective_zoom_of_target(
        target: NonNull<c_void>,
        has_pseudo_element: bool,
        pseudo_element: u8,
    ) -> f64;
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod ffi_test_stubs {
    use super::*;

    #[unsafe(no_mangle)]
    extern "C" fn web_animation_compute_css_keyframe_values(
        _target: NonNull<c_void>,

    }
}

/*
