//! Keyframe sets: the keyframes an effect runs, resolved from a `@keyframes` rule, from the keyframes script gave a
//! `KeyframeEffect`, or for a CSS transition.
//!
//! A set is immutable once built and shared by everything that runs it: every effect of one `@keyframes` rule holds
//! the rule's set. What depends on the effect running it, its composite operation and the easing a keyframe that
//! declares none runs, stays with the effect.

use crate::css::easing::Easing;
use crate::css::retained_fly_string::RetainedUtf16FlyString;
use crate::css::style_value::{RetainedStyleValueData, StyleValueData};
use std::ops::Range;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// What keyframe offsets, as percentages, are scaled by to key a keyframe, which keys an offset of 100% at 100000.
pub(crate) const KEY_SCALE_FACTOR: f64 = 1000.0;

/// The key of a keyframe at an offset of 0%.
pub(crate) const INITIAL_KEY: u64 = 0;

/// The key of a keyframe at an offset of 100%.
pub(crate) const FINAL_KEY: u64 = 100 * KEY_SCALE_FACTOR as u64;

/// The offset `offset`, a fraction of an iteration, scaled as a key, before it is truncated to one.
pub(crate) fn scaled_offset(offset: f64) -> f64 {
    offset * 100.0 * KEY_SCALE_FACTOR
}

/// The key of a keyframe at the offset `offset`, a fraction of an iteration.
pub(crate) fn key_of_offset(offset: f64) -> u64 {
    #[expect(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss)]
    let key = scaled_offset(offset) as u64;
    key
}

/// The offset, a fraction of an iteration, that `key` scales.
pub(crate) fn offset_of_key(key: f64) -> f64 {
    #[expect(clippy::cast_precision_loss)]
    let final_key = FINAL_KEY as f64;
    key / final_key
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#enumdef-compositeoperationorauto
/// In the order of the host's `Bindings::CompositeOperationOrAuto`.
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CompositeOperationOrAuto {
    Replace,
    Add,
    Accumulate,
    Auto,
}

/// The easing a keyframe runs to the next one.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) enum KeyframeEasing {
    /// The keyframe declares none, and runs its effect's.
    None,
    Easing(Easing),
    /// An easing still to be substituted against the element the effect is sampled on.
    Value(RetainedStyleValueData),
}

/// What a keyframe declares for a property.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) enum KeyframeValue {
    /// The element's own value, held by a keyframe the initial and final keyframes were generated as, which is not
    /// known until the element is sampled.
    ElementValue,
    Declared(RetainedStyleValueData),
}

impl KeyframeValue {
    /// The declared value, or `None` for the element's own value.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn declared(&self) -> Option<&RetainedStyleValueData> {
        match self {
            Self::ElementValue => None,
            Self::Declared(value) => Some(value),
        }
    }
}

/// A property a keyframe declares, which may be a shorthand.
pub(crate) struct KeyframeDeclaration {
    pub(crate) property_id: u16,
    pub(crate) value: KeyframeValue,
}

/// A custom property a keyframe declares.
pub(crate) struct KeyframeCustomDeclaration {
    pub(crate) name: RetainedUtf16FlyString,
    pub(crate) value: KeyframeValue,
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#keyframe
pub(crate) struct Keyframe {
    /// The keyframe's offset, scaled by [`KEY_SCALE_FACTOR`].
    pub(crate) key: u64,
    pub(crate) composite: CompositeOperationOrAuto,
    pub(crate) easing: KeyframeEasing,
    declarations: Range<u32>,
    custom_declarations: Range<u32>,
}

/// The style sheet the keyframes of a `@keyframes` rule come from, which their URLs resolve against.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct ResourceContext {
    /// Shared with every resolution of the keyframes' declarations that points into it.
    pub(crate) base_url: Arc<[u8]>,
    pub(crate) origin_clean: bool,
}

/// A property an effect animates: a longhand or shorthand by its id, or a custom property by its name.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) enum KeyframeProperty {
    Id(u16),
    Custom(RetainedUtf16FlyString),
}

impl PartialEq for KeyframeProperty {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        match (self, other) {
            (Self::Id(first), Self::Id(second)) => first == second,
            // NB: Fly strings are interned, so equal names share their raw representation.
            (Self::Custom(first), Self::Custom(second)) => first.raw() == second.raw(),
            _ => false,
        }
    }
}

/// What the keyframes of a set were made from.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum KeyframeOrigin {
    /// Keyframes script gave a `KeyframeEffect`, or anything else that is not CSS.
    Script,
    /// A `@keyframes` rule.
    KeyframesRule,
    /// A CSS transition.
    Transition,
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-animations-2/#keyframes
/// A keyframe block of a `@keyframes` rule as the rule declares it, once for each of the block's keys.
pub(crate) struct DeclaredKeyframe {
    /// The keyframe's offset, scaled by [`KEY_SCALE_FACTOR`].
    pub(crate) key: u64,
    pub(crate) composite: CompositeOperationOrAuto,
    /// The `animation-timing-function` the block declares where it names an easing without substituting anything;
    /// a block that declares none, or one that substitutes, runs its animation's.
    pub(crate) easing: Option<RetainedStyleValueData>,
    declarations: Range<u32>,
}

/// The keyframe blocks of a `@keyframes` rule in the order the rule declares them, before the keyframes of one key are
/// cascaded together, which script reads of the keyframes of a CSS animation.
pub(crate) struct DeclaredKeyframes {
    keyframes: Box<[DeclaredKeyframe]>,
    declarations: Box<[(KeyframeProperty, RetainedStyleValueData)]>,
}

impl DeclaredKeyframes {
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn keyframes(&self) -> &[DeclaredKeyframe] {
        &self.keyframes
    }

    /// The properties the keyframe block declares, longhands and custom properties, in the order it declares them.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn declarations_of(&self, keyframe: &DeclaredKeyframe) -> &[(KeyframeProperty, RetainedStyleValueData)] {
        &self.declarations[keyframe.declarations.start as usize..keyframe.declarations.end as usize]
    }

    fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        size_of_val::<[DeclaredKeyframe]>(&self.keyframes)
            + size_of_val::<[(KeyframeProperty, RetainedStyleValueData)]>(&self.declarations)
    }
}

/// Where in a style sheet the keyframes of a set come from, which few sets have and none of a CSS transition does.
#[derive(Default)]
struct StyleSheetSource {
    resource_context: Option<ResourceContext>,
    declared_keyframes: Option<DeclaredKeyframes>,
}

impl StyleSheetSource {
    fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        size_of::<Self>()
            + self
                .resource_context
                .as_ref()
                .map_or(0, |context| crate::heap_size::ARC_HEADER_BYTES + context.base_url.len())
            + self.declared_keyframes.as_ref().map_or(0, DeclaredKeyframes::heap_size)
    }
}

/// The keyframes an effect runs, in the order they are used, with what follows from them alone.
pub struct KeyframeSet {
    keyframes: Box<[Keyframe]>,
    declarations: Box<[KeyframeDeclaration]>,
    custom_declarations: Box<[KeyframeCustomDeclaration]>,
    /// The style sheet the keyframes come from, which their URLs resolve against, and the keyframe blocks of the
    /// `@keyframes` rule they were made from, if they were.
    style_sheet_source: Option<Box<StyleSheetSource>>,
    /// The longhands the keyframes animate, sorted: what any shorthand they declare expands to.
    target_properties: Box<[u16]>,
    /// The custom properties the keyframes animate.
    target_custom_properties: Box<[RetainedUtf16FlyString]>,
    /// Whether a keyframe declares a custom property, or one that changes the layout tree's shape or what the main
    /// thread observes of an element's box, which a clock tick cannot sample.
    animates_what_a_tick_cannot: bool,
    /// Whether a keyframe declares a custom property or one the children of the target inherit.
    animates_an_inherited_property: bool,
    /// Whether a keyframe adds to or accumulates onto the value beneath it, whatever its effect does.
    has_additive_keyframe: bool,
    origin: KeyframeOrigin,
    /// The effective zoom the values of a CSS transition's keyframes were computed at, which script reads them
    /// unscaled by.
    computed_value_zoom: f32,
}

/// A keyframe a unit test gives a set: its key, composite operation, easing and declarations.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) type KeyframeAsGiven = (
    u64,
    CompositeOperationOrAuto,
    KeyframeEasing,
    Vec<(KeyframeProperty, KeyframeValue)>,
);

/// A keyframe as a builder collects it, before the set lays its declarations out.
struct PendingKeyframe {
    key: u64,
    composite: CompositeOperationOrAuto,
    easing: KeyframeEasing,
    declarations: Vec<(KeyframeProperty, KeyframeValue)>,
}

impl PendingKeyframe {
    fn new(key: u64) -> Self {
        Self {
            key,
            composite: CompositeOperationOrAuto::Auto,
            easing: KeyframeEasing::None,
            declarations: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Sets what the keyframe declares for `property`, in place of what it declared before.
    fn set(&mut self, property: KeyframeProperty, value: KeyframeValue) {
        match self.declarations.iter_mut().find(|(declared, _)| *declared == property) {
            Some((_, declared_value)) => *declared_value = value,
            None => self.declarations.push((property, value)),
        }
    }

    /// Whether the keyframe declares `property`, or a shorthand of it.
    fn declares(&self, property: &KeyframeProperty) -> bool {
        use crate::css::property_metadata::{expanded_longhands_for_shorthand, property_is_shorthand};
        self.declarations
            .iter()
            .any(|(declared, _)| match (declared, property) {
                (KeyframeProperty::Id(shorthand), KeyframeProperty::Id(longhand))
                    if property_is_shorthand(*shorthand) =>
                {
                    expanded_longhands_for_shorthand(*shorthand).contains(longhand)
                }
                (declared, property) => declared == property,
            })
    }
}

/// The scaled key of a keyframe offset given as a percentage.
fn key_of_percentage(percentage: f64) -> u64 {
    #[expect(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss)]
    let key = (percentage * KEY_SCALE_FACTOR) as u64;
    key
}

/// Whether a property, by its id, can be animated: a longhand whose animation type is not `none`, or a shorthand
/// with such a longhand.
pub fn is_animatable_property(property_id: u16) -> bool {
    use crate::css::property_metadata::{longhands_for_shorthand, property_animation_type, property_is_shorthand};
    if property_is_shorthand(property_id) {
        return longhands_for_shorthand(property_id)
            .iter()
            .any(|&longhand| is_animatable_property(longhand));
    }
    property_animation_type(property_id) != crate::css::animation::ANIMATION_TYPE_NONE
}

/// The animated properties of a declaration of `property_id` with `value`: the longhands it expands to.
fn expanded_longhands(
    property_id: u16,
    value: &RetainedStyleValueData,
    mut sink: impl FnMut(u16, &RetainedStyleValueData),
) {
    crate::css::style_compute::expand_shorthands_with(property_id, value, false, &mut |longhand, longhand_value, _| {
        sink(longhand, longhand_value);
    });
}

/// The animated properties a builder collected, without duplicates, in the order it found them.
#[derive(Default)]
struct AnimatedProperties(Vec<KeyframeProperty>);

impl AnimatedProperties {
    fn insert(&mut self, property: KeyframeProperty) {
        if !self.0.contains(&property) {
            self.0.push(property);
        }
    }
}

impl KeyframeSet {
    /// The keyframes of a `@keyframes` rule, given as each keyframe block's keys, which are percentages, and its
    /// declarations, from a style sheet with `resource_context`.
    ///
    /// Loosely based on https://drafts.csswg.org/css-animations-2/#keyframe-processing
    pub(crate) fn from_keyframes_rule<'a>(
        blocks: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'a [f64], &'a crate::css::declaration_block::DeclarationBlockHeader)>,
        resource_context: Option<ResourceContext>,
    ) -> Self {
        use crate::css::css_enums::keyword;
        use crate::css::property_metadata::property_id;

        let mut keyframes: Vec<PendingKeyframe> = Vec::new();
        let mut animated_properties = AnimatedProperties::default();
        let mut declared_keyframes = Vec::new();
        let mut declared_declarations = Vec::new();

        // NB: Forwards pass, resolve all the user-specified keyframe properties.
        for (keys, block) in blocks {
            let mut resolved_keyframe = PendingKeyframe::new(0);
            let mut declared_easing = None;
            for declaration in block.properties() {
                let value = RetainedStyleValueData::from_arc(declaration.value.clone());
                match declaration.property_id {
                    property_id::ANIMATION_TIMING_FUNCTION => {
                        // NB: animation-timing-function is a list property, but inside @keyframes only a single value
                        //     is meaningful.
                        let value = match value.data() {
                            StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. } => match values.as_slice().first() {
                                Some(first) => first.clone_retained(),
                                None => continue,
                            },
                            _ => value,
                        };
                        if crate::css::style_compute::value_is_css_wide_keyword(value.data()) {
                            continue;
                        }
                        resolved_keyframe.easing = match value.data() {
                            StyleValueData::Easing(_) | StyleValueData::Keyword { .. } => {
                                declared_easing = Some(value.clone_retained());
                                KeyframeEasing::Easing(
                                    crate::css::style::effect_descriptions::easing_from_computed_timing_function(
                                        value.data(),
                                    )
                                    .expect("an easing or keyword timing function describes an easing"),
                                )
                            }
                            _ => {
                                declared_easing = None;
                                KeyframeEasing::Value(value)
                            }
                        };
                    }
                    property_id::ANIMATION_COMPOSITION => {
                        let value = match value.data() {
                            StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. } if values.len() == 1 => {
                                values.as_slice()[0].clone_retained()
                            }
                            _ => value,
                        };
                        resolved_keyframe.composite = match value.data() {
                            StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword: keyword::ADD } => CompositeOperationOrAuto::Add,
                            StyleValueData::Keyword {
                                keyword: keyword::ACCUMULATE,
                            } => CompositeOperationOrAuto::Accumulate,
                            _ => CompositeOperationOrAuto::Replace,
                        };
                    }
                    property if !is_animatable_property(property) => {}
                    property => {
                        // NB: Unresolved properties are resolved when the effect is sampled.
                        expanded_longhands(property, &value, |longhand, longhand_value| {
                            animated_properties.insert(KeyframeProperty::Id(longhand));
                            resolved_keyframe.set(
                                KeyframeProperty::Id(longhand),
                                KeyframeValue::Declared(longhand_value.clone_retained()),
                            );
                        });
                    }
                }
            }
            for custom_property in block.custom_properties().iter() {
                let name = RetainedUtf16FlyString::from_utf16(custom_property.name.units());
                animated_properties.insert(KeyframeProperty::Custom(name.clone()));
                resolved_keyframe.set(
                    KeyframeProperty::Custom(name),
                    KeyframeValue::Declared(RetainedStyleValueData::from_arc(
                        custom_property.declaration.value.clone(),
                    )),
                );
            }

            let first_declaration = declaration_index(declared_declarations.len());
            declared_declarations.extend(
                resolved_keyframe
                    .declarations
                    .iter()
                    .filter_map(|(property, value)| Some((property.clone(), value.declared()?.clone_retained()))),
            );
            let declarations = first_declaration..declaration_index(declared_declarations.len());
            for &key in keys {
                let key = key_of_percentage(key);
                declared_keyframes.push(DeclaredKeyframe {
                    key,
                    composite: resolved_keyframe.composite,
                    easing: declared_easing.as_ref().map(RetainedStyleValueData::clone_retained),
                    declarations: declarations.clone(),
                });
                match keyframes.iter_mut().find(|keyframe| keyframe.key == key) {
                    Some(existing_keyframe) => {
                        for (property, value) in &resolved_keyframe.declarations {
                            existing_keyframe.set(property.clone(), value.clone());
                        }
                        if resolved_keyframe.composite != CompositeOperationOrAuto::Auto {
                            existing_keyframe.composite = resolved_keyframe.composite;
                        }
                        if !matches!(resolved_keyframe.easing, KeyframeEasing::None) {
                            existing_keyframe.easing = resolved_keyframe.easing.clone();
                        }
                    }
                    None => keyframes.push(PendingKeyframe {
                        key,
                        composite: resolved_keyframe.composite,
                        easing: resolved_keyframe.easing.clone(),
                        declarations: resolved_keyframe.declarations.clone(),
                    }),
                }
            }
        }

        let mut set = Self::with_initial_and_final_frames(keyframes, &animated_properties, resource_context);
        set.origin = KeyframeOrigin::KeyframesRule;
        set.style_sheet_source.get_or_insert_default().declared_keyframes = Some(DeclaredKeyframes {
            keyframes: declared_keyframes.into(),
            declarations: declared_declarations.into(),
        });
        set
    }

    /// The keyframes script gave a `KeyframeEffect`, each with its computed offset already scaled to a key, in the
    /// order they were given, from a style sheet with `resource_context` where they were copied from keyframes of CSS.
    pub(crate) fn from_processed_keyframes(
        keyframes: Vec<ProcessedKeyframe>,
        resource_context: Option<ResourceContext>,
    ) -> Self {
        let mut animated_properties = AnimatedProperties::default();
        let keyframes = keyframes
            .into_iter()
            .map(|keyframe| {
                let mut resolved_keyframe = PendingKeyframe::new(keyframe.key);
                resolved_keyframe.composite = keyframe.composite;
                resolved_keyframe.easing = keyframe.easing.map_or(KeyframeEasing::None, KeyframeEasing::Easing);
                for (property, value) in keyframe.declarations {
                    match &property {
                        KeyframeProperty::Custom(_) => animated_properties.insert(property.clone()),
                        &KeyframeProperty::Id(property_id) => expanded_longhands(property_id, &value, |longhand, _| {
                            animated_properties.insert(KeyframeProperty::Id(longhand));
                        }),
                    }
                    resolved_keyframe.set(property, KeyframeValue::Declared(value));
                }
                resolved_keyframe
            })
            .collect();
        Self::with_initial_and_final_frames(keyframes, &animated_properties, resource_context)
    }

    /// The keyframes of a computation of the values `frames` declare over an element, each property by its id, keyed
    /// by their position, replacing the value beneath them, from a style sheet with `resource_context`. No initial or
    /// final keyframe is made of what they leave out.
    pub(crate) fn for_value_computation(
        frames: Vec<Vec<(u16, RetainedStyleValueData)>>,
        resource_context: Option<ResourceContext>,
    ) -> Self {
        let mut animated_properties = AnimatedProperties::default();
        let keyframes = frames
            .into_iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(index, declarations)| {
                let mut keyframe = PendingKeyframe::new(index as u64);
                keyframe.composite = CompositeOperationOrAuto::Replace;
                for (property_id, value) in declarations {
                    animated_properties.insert(KeyframeProperty::Id(property_id));
                    keyframe.set(KeyframeProperty::Id(property_id), KeyframeValue::Declared(value));
                }
                keyframe
            })
            .collect();
        Self::laid_out(keyframes, &animated_properties, resource_context)
    }

    /// The keyframes of a CSS transition of `property` from `start` to `end`, values computed at the effective zoom
    /// `computed_value_zoom`.
    pub(crate) fn for_transition(
        property: KeyframeProperty,
        start: RetainedStyleValueData,
        end: RetainedStyleValueData,
        computed_value_zoom: f32,
    ) -> Self {
        let keyframe = |key, value| {
            let mut keyframe = PendingKeyframe::new(key);
            keyframe.set(property.clone(), KeyframeValue::Declared(value));
            keyframe
        };
        let mut animated_properties = AnimatedProperties::default();
        animated_properties.insert(property.clone());
        let mut set = Self::laid_out(
            vec![keyframe(INITIAL_KEY, start), keyframe(FINAL_KEY, end)],
            &animated_properties,
            None,
        );
        set.origin = KeyframeOrigin::Transition;
        set.computed_value_zoom = computed_value_zoom;
        set
    }

    /// The set of `keyframes`, each given as its key, composite operation, easing and declarations, exactly as given,
    /// for a unit test.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn from_keyframes_as_given(keyframes: Vec<KeyframeAsGiven>) -> Self {
        let mut animated_properties = AnimatedProperties::default();
        let keyframes = keyframes
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(key, composite, easing, declarations)| {
                for (property, _) in &declarations {
                    animated_properties.insert(property.clone());
                }
                PendingKeyframe {
                    key,
                    composite,
                    easing,
                    declarations,
                }
            })
            .collect();
        Self::laid_out(keyframes, &animated_properties, None)
    }

    /// The set of `keyframes`, once the initial and final keyframes are generated for `animated_properties`.
    fn with_initial_and_final_frames(
        mut keyframes: Vec<PendingKeyframe>,
        animated_properties: &AnimatedProperties,
        resource_context: Option<ResourceContext>,
    ) -> Self {
        // NB: The keyframes are used in the order of their keys, and those of one key in the order they were given.
        keyframes.sort_by_key(|keyframe| keyframe.key);
        generate_initial_and_final_frames(&mut keyframes, animated_properties);
        Self::laid_out(keyframes, animated_properties, resource_context)
    }

    fn laid_out(
        keyframes: Vec<PendingKeyframe>,
        animated_properties: &AnimatedProperties,
        resource_context: Option<ResourceContext>,
    ) -> Self {
        use crate::css::property_metadata::{property_id, property_is_inherited};

        let mut declarations = Vec::new();
        let mut custom_declarations = Vec::new();
        let mut animates_what_a_tick_cannot = false;
        let mut animates_an_inherited_property = false;
        let mut has_additive_keyframe = false;
        let index = declaration_index;
        let keyframes = keyframes
            .into_iter()
            .map(|keyframe| {
                has_additive_keyframe |= matches!(
                    keyframe.composite,
                    CompositeOperationOrAuto::Add | CompositeOperationOrAuto::Accumulate
                );
                let first_declaration = index(declarations.len());
                let first_custom_declaration = index(custom_declarations.len());
                for (property, value) in keyframe.declarations {
                    match property {
                        KeyframeProperty::Id(property_id) => {
                            animates_what_a_tick_cannot |= matches!(
                                property_id,
                                property_id::DISPLAY | property_id::VISIBILITY | property_id::CONTENT_VISIBILITY
                            );
                            animates_an_inherited_property |= property_is_inherited(property_id);
                            declarations.push(KeyframeDeclaration { property_id, value });
                        }
                        KeyframeProperty::Custom(name) => {
                            animates_what_a_tick_cannot = true;
                            animates_an_inherited_property = true;
                            custom_declarations.push(KeyframeCustomDeclaration { name, value });
                        }
                    }
                }
                Keyframe {
                    key: keyframe.key,
                    composite: keyframe.composite,
                    easing: keyframe.easing,
                    declarations: first_declaration..index(declarations.len()),
                    custom_declarations: first_custom_declaration..index(custom_declarations.len()),
                }
            })
            .collect();

        let mut target_properties: Vec<u16> = Vec::new();
        let mut target_custom_properties = Vec::new();
        for property in &animated_properties.0 {
            match property {
                KeyframeProperty::Id(property_id) => target_properties.push(*property_id),
                KeyframeProperty::Custom(name) => target_custom_properties.push(name.clone()),
            }
        }
        target_properties.sort_unstable();
        target_properties.dedup();

        Self {
            keyframes,
            declarations: declarations.into(),
            custom_declarations: custom_declarations.into(),
            style_sheet_source: resource_context.map(|resource_context| {
                Box::new(StyleSheetSource {
                    resource_context: Some(resource_context),
                    declared_keyframes: None,
                })
            }),
            target_properties: target_properties.into(),
            target_custom_properties: target_custom_properties.into(),
            animates_what_a_tick_cannot,
            animates_an_inherited_property,
            has_additive_keyframe,
            origin: KeyframeOrigin::Script,
            computed_value_zoom: 1.0,
        }
    }

    /// Another reference to the set `set` names.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// `set` must be a keyframe set the host holds a reference to.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) unsafe fn retained_from_host(set: *const Self) -> Arc<Self> {
        // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
        unsafe {
            Arc::increment_strong_count(set);
            Arc::from_raw(set)
        }
    }

    /// The keyframes, in the order they are used.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn keyframes(&self) -> &[Keyframe] {
        &self.keyframes
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn declarations_of(&self, keyframe: &Keyframe) -> &[KeyframeDeclaration] {
        &self.declarations[keyframe.declarations.start as usize..keyframe.declarations.end as usize]
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn custom_declarations_of(&self, keyframe: &Keyframe) -> &[KeyframeCustomDeclaration] {
        &self.custom_declarations
            [keyframe.custom_declarations.start as usize..keyframe.custom_declarations.end as usize]
    }

    /// The custom properties all the keyframes declare, in the order they are used.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn custom_declarations(&self) -> &[KeyframeCustomDeclaration] {
        &self.custom_declarations
    }

    /// The style sheet the keyframes come from, which their URLs resolve against.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn resource_context(&self) -> Option<&ResourceContext> {
        self.style_sheet_source.as_ref()?.resource_context.as_ref()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn origin(&self) -> KeyframeOrigin {
        self.origin
    }

    /// The keyframe blocks of the `@keyframes` rule the keyframes were made from, if they were.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn declared_keyframes(&self) -> Option<&DeclaredKeyframes> {
        self.style_sheet_source.as_ref()?.declared_keyframes.as_ref()
    }

    /// The effective zoom the values of a CSS transition's keyframes were computed at.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn computed_value_zoom(&self) -> f32 {
        self.computed_value_zoom
    }

    /// The longhands the keyframes animate, sorted.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn target_properties(&self) -> &[u16] {
        &self.target_properties
    }

    /// The custom properties the keyframes animate.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn target_custom_properties(&self) -> &[RetainedUtf16FlyString] {
        &self.target_custom_properties
    }

    /// Whether the compositor may run all the keyframes animate.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn may_run_on_the_compositor(&self) -> bool {
        use crate::css::property_metadata::property_id;
        self.target_custom_properties.is_empty()
            && self.target_properties.iter().all(|property| {
                matches!(
                    *property,
                    property_id::OPACITY
                        | property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR
                        | property_id::FILTER
                        | property_id::TRANSLATE
                        | property_id::ROTATE
                        | property_id::SCALE
                        | property_id::TRANSFORM
                )
            })
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn animates_what_a_tick_cannot(&self) -> bool {
        self.animates_what_a_tick_cannot
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn animates_an_inherited_property(&self) -> bool {
        self.animates_an_inherited_property
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn has_additive_keyframe(&self) -> bool {
        self.has_additive_keyframe
    }

    /// Every value the keyframes declare or run their easing by.
    pub(crate) fn declared_values(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &StyleValueData> {
        let declared = self
            .declarations
            .iter()
            .map(|declaration| &declaration.value)
            .chain(self.custom_declarations.iter().map(|declaration| &declaration.value))
            .filter_map(KeyframeValue::declared);
        let easings = self.keyframes.iter().filter_map(|keyframe| match &keyframe.easing {
            KeyframeEasing::Value(value) => Some(value),
            KeyframeEasing::None | KeyframeEasing::Easing(_) => None,
        });
        declared
            .chain(easings)
            .filter_map(RetainedStyleValueData::optional_data)
    }

    /// The bytes the set holds on the heap, beside itself. The values it declares are their rules'.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.style_sheet_source.as_ref().map_or(0, |source| source.heap_size())
            + size_of_val::<[Keyframe]>(&self.keyframes)
            + self
                .keyframes
                .iter()
                .map(|keyframe| match &keyframe.easing {
                    KeyframeEasing::Easing(Easing::Linear(points)) => crate::heap_size::vec_bytes(points),
                    _ => 0,
                })
                .sum::<usize>()
            + size_of_val::<[KeyframeDeclaration]>(&self.declarations)
            + size_of_val::<[KeyframeCustomDeclaration]>(&self.custom_declarations)
            + size_of_val::<[u16]>(&self.target_properties)
            + size_of_val::<[RetainedUtf16FlyString]>(&self.target_custom_properties)
    }
}

/// The index of the next of a set's declarations, where it holds `length` of them.
fn declaration_index(length: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::try_from(length).expect("a keyframe set holds fewer than 2^32 declarations")
}

/// A keyframe script gave a `KeyframeEffect`, as processing the keyframes argument made it.
pub(crate) struct ProcessedKeyframe {
    /// The computed keyframe offset, scaled by [`KEY_SCALE_FACTOR`] as a percentage.
    pub(crate) key: u64,
    pub(crate) composite: CompositeOperationOrAuto,
    pub(crate) easing: Option<Easing>,
    pub(crate) declarations: Vec<(KeyframeProperty, RetainedStyleValueData)>,
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-animations-2/#keyframe-processing
fn generate_initial_and_final_frames(keyframes: &mut Vec<PendingKeyframe>, animated_properties: &AnimatedProperties) {
    // 1. Find or create the initial keyframe, a keyframe with a keyframe offset of 0%, default timing function
    //    as its keyframe timing function, and default composite as its keyframe composite.
    if keyframes.first().is_none_or(|keyframe| keyframe.key != INITIAL_KEY) {
        keyframes.insert(0, PendingKeyframe::new(INITIAL_KEY));
    }

    // 2. For any property in animated properties that is not otherwise present in a keyframe with an offset of
    //    0% or one that would be positioned earlier in the used keyframe order, add the computed value of that
    //    property on element to initial keyframe’s keyframe values.
    let initial_keyframes = keyframes
        .iter()
        .take_while(|keyframe| keyframe.key == INITIAL_KEY)
        .count();
    let missing: Vec<_> = animated_properties
        .0
        .iter()
        .filter(|property| {
            !keyframes[..initial_keyframes]
                .iter()
                .any(|keyframe| keyframe.declares(property))
        })
        .cloned()
        .collect();
    for property in missing {
        keyframes[0].set(property, KeyframeValue::ElementValue);
    }

    // 3. If initial keyframe’s keyframe values is not empty, prepend initial keyframe to keyframes.

    // 4. Repeat for final keyframe, using an offset of 100%, considering keyframes positioned later in the used
    //    keyframe order, and appending to keyframes.
    if keyframes.last().is_none_or(|keyframe| keyframe.key != FINAL_KEY) {
        keyframes.push(PendingKeyframe::new(FINAL_KEY));
    }
    let final_keyframes = keyframes
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .take_while(|keyframe| keyframe.key == FINAL_KEY)
        .count();
    let first_final_keyframe = keyframes.len() - final_keyframes;
    let missing: Vec<_> = animated_properties
        .0
        .iter()
        .filter(|property| {
            !keyframes[first_final_keyframe..]
                .iter()
                .any(|keyframe| keyframe.declares(property))
        })
        .cloned()
        .collect();
    let final_keyframe = keyframes.last_mut().expect("the final keyframe was found or created");
    for property in missing {
        final_keyframe.set(property, KeyframeValue::ElementValue);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn value(keyword: u16) -> RetainedStyleValueData {
        RetainedStyleValueData::from_owned(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword })
    }

    fn declared_properties(set: &KeyframeSet, keyframe: &Keyframe) -> Vec<(u16, bool)> {
        set.declarations_of(keyframe)
            .iter()
            .map(|declaration| (declaration.property_id, declaration.value.declared().is_some()))
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn script_keyframes_gain_initial_and_final_keyframes_for_what_they_leave_out() {
        use crate::css::css_enums::keyword;
        use crate::css::property_metadata::property_id;
        let keyframe = |key, property| ProcessedKeyframe {
            key,
            composite: CompositeOperationOrAuto::Auto,
            easing: None,
            declarations: vec![(KeyframeProperty::Id(property), value(keyword::AUTO))],
        };
        let set = KeyframeSet::from_processed_keyframes(
            vec![
                keyframe(50_000, property_id::OPACITY),
                keyframe(FINAL_KEY, property_id::COLOR),
            ],
            None,
        );
        let keys: Vec<_> = set.keyframes().iter().map(|keyframe| keyframe.key).collect();
        assert_eq!(keys, [INITIAL_KEY, 50_000, FINAL_KEY]);
        let mut initial = declared_properties(&set, &set.keyframes()[0]);
        initial.sort_unstable();
        let mut expected = vec![(property_id::OPACITY, false), (property_id::COLOR, false)];
        expected.sort_unstable();
        assert_eq!(initial, expected);
        let mut last = declared_properties(&set, &set.keyframes()[2]);
        last.sort_unstable();
        let mut expected = vec![(property_id::COLOR, true), (property_id::OPACITY, false)];
        expected.sort_unstable();
        assert_eq!(last, expected);
        let mut target_properties = vec![property_id::OPACITY, property_id::COLOR];
        target_properties.sort_unstable();
        assert_eq!(set.target_properties(), target_properties);
    }

    #[test]
    fn keyframes_of_one_offset_keep_their_order() {
        use crate::css::css_enums::keyword;
        use crate::css::property_metadata::property_id;
        let keyframe = |key, composite| ProcessedKeyframe {
            key,
            composite,
            easing: None,
            declarations: vec![(KeyframeProperty::Id(property_id::OPACITY), value(keyword::AUTO))],
        };
        let set = KeyframeSet::from_processed_keyframes(
            vec![
                keyframe(FINAL_KEY, CompositeOperationOrAuto::Add),
                keyframe(INITIAL_KEY, CompositeOperationOrAuto::Replace),
                keyframe(FINAL_KEY, CompositeOperationOrAuto::Accumulate),
            ],
            None,
        );
        let composites: Vec<_> = set.keyframes().iter().map(|keyframe| keyframe.composite).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            composites,
            [
                CompositeOperationOrAuto::Replace,
                CompositeOperationOrAuto::Add,
                CompositeOperationOrAuto::Accumulate
            ]
        );
        assert!(set.has_additive_keyframe());
    }
}

//! The pending animation event queue of a document, which holds what each event is, not the event: the host creates
//! each event as it dispatches it.
//! https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#pending-animation-event-queue

use super::animation::{AnimationCell, AnimationHandle, HostCellKind};
use super::composite_order::{TreeOrder, composite_order};
use super::css_events::FfiCssEventType;
use super::host_effects::PlaybackEventType;
use super::timing::{OptionalNumber, OptionalTimeValue};
use std::cmp::Ordering;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::ptr::NonNull;

/// The type of a `TimeEvent` an SVG animation element dispatches.
/// https://svgwg.org/specs/animations/#InterfaceTimeEvent
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TimeEventType {
    Begin,
    End,
    Repeat,
}

/// Which interface an event of the pending animation event queue is of.
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PendingAnimationEventKind {
    /// An `AnimationEvent` or a `TransitionEvent` of a CSS animation or transition, dispatched at its owning element.
    Css,
    /// An `AnimationPlaybackEvent`, dispatched at the animation.
    Playback,
    /// A `TimeEvent` of the animation of an SVG animation element, dispatched at the animation element.
    Time,
}

/// An event of the pending animation event queue, as the host creates it as it dispatches it, the fields of its kind
/// set.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct FfiPendingAnimationEvent {
    pub kind: PendingAnimationEventKind,
    /// For `Css`.
    pub css_event_type: FfiCssEventType,
    /// For `Playback`.
    pub playback_event_type: PlaybackEventType,
    /// For `Time`.
    pub time_event_type: TimeEventType,
    /// For `Time`, the iteration a repeat event is of.
    pub detail: i32,
    /// For `Css`, in seconds.
    pub elapsed_time: f64,
    /// For `Playback`.
    pub current_time: OptionalTimeValue,
    pub timeline_time: OptionalTimeValue,
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#scheduled-event-time
    pub scheduled_event_time: OptionalNumber,
    /// The time the event was queued at, which is its time stamp.
    pub time_stamp: f64,
}

/// An event of the queue and the animation it is of, which the queue holds.
pub(crate) struct PendingAnimationEvent {
    pub(crate) animation: AnimationHandle,
    pub(crate) event: FfiPendingAnimationEvent,
}

/// The pending animation event queue of a document, and the events queued while style and layout feedback is
/// provisional, which join it only as the outermost style stabilization epoch commits.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct PendingAnimationEvents {
    pending: Vec<PendingAnimationEvent>,
    provisional: Vec<PendingAnimationEvent>,
}

impl PendingAnimationEvents {
    /// Appends an event to the pending animation event queue, or, where `provisional`, to the provisional events.
    pub(crate) fn append(&mut self, event: PendingAnimationEvent, provisional: bool) {
        if provisional {
            self.provisional.push(event);
        } else {
            self.pending.push(event);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn has_provisional_events(&self) -> bool {
        !self.provisional.is_empty()
    }

    /// Appends the provisional events to the pending animation event queue but those `drops` says to drop, answering how
    /// many it appended.
    pub(crate) fn commit_provisional_events(&mut self, mut drops: impl FnMut(&AnimationCell) -> bool) -> usize {
        let before = self.pending.len();
        for event in std::mem::take(&mut self.provisional) {
            if !drops(&event.animation) {
                self.pending.push(event);
            }
        }
        self.pending.len() - before
    }

    /// Takes the events of the pending animation event queue in the order to dispatch them in.
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#update-animations-and-send-events
    pub(crate) fn take_events_to_dispatch(&mut self, tree_order: &mut impl TreeOrder) -> Vec<PendingAnimationEvent> {
        // 4. Let events to dispatch be a copy of doc’s pending animation event queue.
        // 5. Clear doc’s pending animation event queue.
        let mut events_to_dispatch = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending);

        // 6. Perform a stable sort of the animation events in events to dispatch as follows:
        //    1. Sort the events by their scheduled event time such that events that were scheduled to occur earlier
        //       sort before events scheduled to occur later, and events whose scheduled event time is unresolved sort
        //       before events with a resolved scheduled event time.
        //    2. Within events with equal scheduled event times, sort by their composite order.
        // NB: An event of an animation without an associated effect sorts before those of animations with one.
        events_to_dispatch.sort_by(|a, b| {
            let (a_time, b_time) = (a.event.scheduled_event_time, b.event.scheduled_event_time);
            match (a_time.has_value, b_time.has_value) {
                (false, true) => return Ordering::Less,
                (true, false) => return Ordering::Greater,
                (true, true) => {
                    // NB: A total order keeps the sort well defined should a time be NaN, and adding zero makes
                    //     -0 and +0 equal times, as they compare.
                    let ordering = (a_time.value + 0.0).total_cmp(&(b_time.value + 0.0));
                    if ordering != Ordering::Equal {
                        return ordering;
                    }
                }
                (false, false) => {}
            }
            let (a, b) = (a.animation.borrow(), b.animation.borrow());
            match (a.effect().is_some(), b.effect().is_some()) {
                (true, true) => composite_order(&a, &b, tree_order),
                (a_has_effect, b_has_effect) => a_has_effect.cmp(&b_has_effect),
            }
        });
        events_to_dispatch
    }

    /// Calls `visit` with each GC cell of the host that keeps alive the elements the records of the queued events
    /// name.
    pub(crate) fn for_each_host_cell(&self, mut visit: impl FnMut(NonNull<c_void>, HostCellKind)) {
        for event in self.pending.iter().chain(&self.provisional) {
            event.animation.for_each_host_cell(&mut visit);
        }
    }
}

//! The procedures of the Web Animations timing model that run on an animation.
//! https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#animations
//!
//! A procedure changes the records it runs on and records what it asks the host to do as `HostEffects`, in the order
//! its steps ask for them, which the host performs once it has returned.

use super::animation::{AnimationCell, AnimationHandle, AnimationKind, AnimationRecord, CssAnimationFlag};
use super::composite_order::{TreeOrder, composite_order};
use super::effect::{EffectFlag, EffectHandle};
use super::host_effects::{HostEffectKind, HostEffects, PlaybackEventType};
use super::timeline::{TimelineCell, TimelineHandle};
use super::timeline_state::{TimelineState, zero_time};
use super::timing::{
    self, AnimationEffectPhase, AnimationEffectTiming, AnimationPlayState, AnimationPlayback, AnimationReplaceState,
    FillMode, TimeValue, TimeValueType, time_value,
};
use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::ptr::NonNull;

/// An exception a procedure throws, as the host throws it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum AnimationError {
    /// An "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
    InvalidState(&'static str),
    TypeError(&'static str),
}

/// Whether a procedure updates the finished state of an animation after seeking it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum DidSeek {
    No,
    Yes,
}

/// Whether the finish notification steps of an animation run right away rather than in a task.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum SynchronouslyNotify {
    No,
    Yes,
}

/// Whether a procedure invalidates the style its animation's effect produces.
/// NB: Script always wants this. The style computation does not, as it runs a procedure before it computes the effect
///     stack it would invalidate.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Invalidate {
    No,
    Yes,
}

/// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#playing-an-animation-section
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum AutoRewind {
    No,
    Yes,
}

/// Runs `procedure` on `animation` and hands back what it asks the host to do.
pub(crate) fn run<T>(
    animation: &AnimationHandle,
    procedure: impl FnOnce(&mut Procedures<'_>) -> Result<T, AnimationError>,
) -> Result<(T, HostEffects), AnimationError> {
    let timeline = animation.borrow().timeline_state();
    run_on(animation, timeline, procedure)
}

/// Answers what `procedure`, which only reads, finds of `animation`. Unlike `run`, this does not note that the
/// animation may need updates.
pub(crate) fn query<T>(animation: &AnimationHandle, procedure: impl FnOnce(&Procedures<'_>) -> T) -> T {
    let timeline = animation.borrow().timeline_state();
    let mut effects = HostEffects::default();
    procedure(&Procedures {
        animation,
        timeline,
        effects: &mut effects,
    })
}

/// Runs `procedure` on `animation`, whose timeline reads `timeline` now, if it has one, and hands back what it asks
/// the host to do.
fn run_on<T>(
    animation: &AnimationHandle,
    timeline: Option<TimelineState>,
    procedure: impl FnOnce(&mut Procedures<'_>) -> Result<T, AnimationError>,
) -> Result<(T, HostEffects), AnimationError> {
    let mut effects = HostEffects::default();
    let value = procedure(&mut Procedures {
        animation,
        timeline,
        effects: &mut effects,
    });
    note_animation_may_need_update(animation);
    Ok((value?, effects))
}

/// OPTIMIZATION: Notes that an update of the current time of the timeline of `animation`, if any, may change it, as a
///               procedure ran on it. The timeline updates only those of its animations.
pub(crate) fn note_animation_may_need_update(animation: &AnimationHandle) {
    let timeline = animation.borrow().timeline().cloned();
    if let Some(timeline) = timeline {
        timeline.animations_needing_update().borrow_mut().insert(animation);
    }
}

/// Whether an update of the current time of its timeline leaves `animation` as it is until a procedure runs on it: it
/// has finished on a monotonically increasing timeline that is not progress-based, and has no pending task, which is
/// what the update of an animation as its timeline updates skips.
pub(crate) fn update_leaves_animation_as_it_is(animation: &AnimationCell) -> bool {
    let record = animation.borrow();
    let playback = record.playback();
    if !playback.is_finished || playback.pending() {
        return false;
    }
    record
        .timeline_state()
        .is_some_and(|timeline| timeline.sample.is_monotonically_increasing && !timeline.is_progress_based)
        && record.play_state() == AnimationPlayState::Finished
}

/// An animation and its timeline as it is now, on which the procedures run, and what they ask the host to do so far.
pub(crate) struct Procedures<'a> {
    animation: &'a AnimationHandle,
    /// The animation's timeline as the animation reads it as the procedures begin, if it has one.
    timeline: Option<TimelineState>,
    effects: &'a mut HostEffects,
}

impl Procedures<'_> {
    /// The animation the procedures run on.
    pub(crate) fn animation(&self) -> &AnimationHandle {
        self.animation
    }

    fn emit(&mut self, kind: HostEffectKind) {
        self.effects.push(self.animation, kind);
    }

    fn playback(&self) -> AnimationPlayback {
        *self.animation.borrow().playback()
    }

    fn update_playback(&self, update: impl FnOnce(&mut AnimationPlayback)) {
        update(self.animation.borrow_mut().playback_mut());
    }

    fn start_time(&self) -> Option<TimeValue> {
        self.playback().start_time.get()
    }

    fn hold_time(&self) -> Option<TimeValue> {
        self.playback().hold_time.get()
    }

    fn playback_rate(&self) -> f64 {
        self.playback().playback_rate
    }

    fn pending_playback_rate(&self) -> Option<f64> {
        self.playback().pending_playback_rate.get()
    }

    fn pending(&self) -> bool {
        self.playback().pending()
    }

    fn set_start_time(&self, time: Option<TimeValue>) {
        self.update_playback(|playback| playback.start_time = time.into());
    }

    fn set_hold_time(&self, time: Option<TimeValue>) {
        self.update_playback(|playback| playback.hold_time = time.into());
    }

    fn set_pending_playback_rate(&self, playback_rate: Option<f64>) {
        self.update_playback(|playback| playback.pending_playback_rate = playback_rate.into());
    }

    fn set_has_pending_play_task(&self, value: bool) {
        self.update_playback(|playback| playback.has_pending_play_task = value);
        // The play that started a CSS transition ends with its pending play task, whether the task runs or not.
        if !value {
            self.end_initial_transition_play();
        }
    }

    fn set_has_pending_pause_task(&self, value: bool) {
        self.update_playback(|playback| playback.has_pending_pause_task = value);
    }

    fn set_auto_align_start_time(&self, value: bool) {
        self.animation.borrow_mut().auto_align_start_time = value;
    }

    /// The current time of the timeline, which is unresolved without one or where it is inactive.
    fn timeline_time(&self) -> Option<TimeValue> {
        self.timeline.as_ref().and_then(TimelineState::current_time)
    }

    /// Whether the animation is associated with an active timeline.
    fn has_active_timeline(&self) -> bool {
        self.timeline.as_ref().is_some_and(|timeline| !timeline.is_inactive())
    }

    /// Whether the animation has an associated timeline that is not monotonically increasing.
    fn has_finite_timeline(&self) -> bool {
        self.timeline
            .as_ref()
            .is_some_and(|timeline| !timeline.sample.is_monotonically_increasing)
    }

    /// Whether the animation is associated with a monotonically increasing timeline.
    fn has_monotonically_increasing_timeline(&self) -> bool {
        self.timeline
            .as_ref()
            .is_some_and(|timeline| timeline.sample.is_monotonically_increasing)
    }

    fn zero(&self) -> TimeValue {
        zero_time(self.timeline.as_ref())
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#animation-current-time
    fn current_time(&self) -> Option<TimeValue> {
        timing::current_time_at(&self.playback(), self.timeline_time())
    }

    /// The current time of the animation, substituting an unresolved time value for the hold time.
    fn current_time_without_hold_time(&self) -> Option<TimeValue> {
        let playback = AnimationPlayback {
            hold_time: None.into(),
            ..self.playback()
        };
        timing::current_time_at(&playback, self.timeline_time())
    }

    /// The normalized timing of the associated effect, if any.
    fn effect_timing(&self) -> Option<AnimationEffectTiming> {
        self.animation.borrow().effect().map(|effect| effect.borrow().timing())
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#associated-effect-end
    fn associated_effect_end(&self) -> TimeValue {
        // The associated effect end of an animation is equal to the end time of the animation’s associated effect. If
        // the animation has no associated effect, the associated effect end is zero.
        match self.effect_timing() {
            Some(timing) => timing::end_time(&timing),
            None => self.zero(),
        }
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#play-states
    pub(crate) fn play_state(&self) -> AnimationPlayState {
        timing::play_state_at(&self.playback(), self.current_time(), self.associated_effect_end())
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#animation-relevant
    pub(crate) fn is_relevant(&self) -> bool {
        let effect_timing = self.effect_timing();
        timing::is_relevant(
            &self.playback(),
            self.timeline.as_ref().map(|timeline| &timeline.sample),
            effect_timing.as_ref(),
            self.current_time(),
        )
    }

    /// The phase of the associated effect, if any, at its local time, the current time of the animation.
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#animation-effect-phases-and-states
    fn effect_phase(&self) -> Option<AnimationEffectPhase> {
        let timing = self.effect_timing()?;
        let playback = self.playback();
        let resolved = timing::resolve_timing(
            &timing,
            self.current_time(),
            Some(&playback),
            self.timeline.as_ref().map(|timeline| &timeline.sample),
        );
        Some(resolved.phase)
    }

    /// The host's `DOM::Element` the associated effect targets, if any.
    fn effect_target(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.animation
            .borrow()
            .effect()
            .and_then(|effect| effect.borrow().target_element())
    }

    /// Whether the associated effect has a target.
    fn effect_has_target(&self) -> bool {
        self.effect_target().is_some()
    }

    fn invalidate_effect(&mut self) {
        if self.animation.borrow().effect().is_some() {
            self.emit(HostEffectKind::InvalidateEffect { changes_plan: true });
        }
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#apply-any-pending-playback-rate
    fn apply_any_pending_playback_rate(&self) {
        self.update_playback(|playback| {
            // 1. If animation does not have a pending playback rate, abort these steps.
            let Some(pending_playback_rate) = playback.pending_playback_rate.get() else {
                return;
            };

            // 2. Set animation’s playback rate to its pending playback rate.
            playback.playback_rate = pending_playback_rate;

            // 3. Clear animation’s pending playback rate.
            playback.pending_playback_rate = None.into();
        });
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#animation-silently-set-the-current-time
    /// NB: The host validates seek time as a CSSNumberish time before it runs this procedure.
    fn silently_set_current_time(&self, valid_seek_time: Option<TimeValue>) -> Result<(), AnimationError> {
        // 1. If seek time is an unresolved time value, then perform the following steps.
        let Some(valid_seek_time) = valid_seek_time else {
            // 1. If the current time is resolved, then throw a TypeError.
            if self.current_time().is_some() {
                return Err(AnimationError::TypeError(
                    "Cannot change an animation's current time from a resolve value to an unresolved value",
                ));
            }

            // 2. Abort these steps.
            return Ok(());
        };

        // 2. Let valid seek time be the result of running the validate a CSSNumberish time procedure with seek time as
        //    the input.
        // 3. If valid seek time is false, abort this procedure.
        // AD-HOC: The host has already validated seek time.

        // 4. Set auto align start time to false.
        self.set_auto_align_start_time(false);

        // 5. Update either animation’s hold time or start time as follows:
        let playback = self.playback();

        // -> If any of the following conditions are true:
        //    - animation’s hold time is resolved, or
        //    - animation’s start time is unresolved, or
        //    - animation has no associated timeline or the associated timeline is inactive, or
        //    - animation’s playback rate is 0,
        match self.timeline_time() {
            Some(timeline_time)
                if playback.hold_time.get().is_none()
                    && playback.start_time.get().is_some()
                    && playback.playback_rate != 0.0 =>
            {
                // -> Otherwise,
                //    Set animation’s start time to the result of evaluating timeline time - (seek time / playback
                //    rate) where timeline time is the current time value of timeline associated with animation.
                self.set_start_time(Some(timeline_time - (valid_seek_time / playback.playback_rate)));
            }
            _ => {
                // Set animation’s hold time to seek time.
                self.set_hold_time(Some(valid_seek_time));
            }
        }

        // 6. If animation has no associated timeline or the associated timeline is inactive, make animation’s start
        //    time unresolved.
        if !self.has_active_timeline() {
            self.set_start_time(None);
        }

        // 7. Make animation’s previous current time unresolved.
        self.animation.borrow_mut().previous_current_time = None;

        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#animation-set-the-current-time
    /// NB: The host validates seek time as a CSSNumberish time before it runs this procedure.
    fn set_current_time(&mut self, seek_time: Option<TimeValue>) -> Result<(), AnimationError> {
        // 1. Run the steps to silently set the current time of animation to seek time.
        self.silently_set_current_time(seek_time)?;

        // 2. If animation has a pending pause task, synchronously complete the pause operation by performing the
        //    following steps:
        if self.playback().has_pending_pause_task {
            // 1. Set animation’s hold time to seek time.
            self.set_hold_time(seek_time);

            // 2. Apply any pending playback rate to animation.
            self.apply_any_pending_playback_rate();

            // 3. Make animation’s start time unresolved.
            self.set_start_time(None);

            // 4. Cancel the pending pause task.
            self.set_has_pending_pause_task(false);

            // 5. Resolve animation’s current ready promise with animation.
            self.emit(HostEffectKind::ResolveReadyPromise);
        }

        // 3. Run the procedure to update an animation’s finished state for animation with the did seek flag set to
        //    true, and the synchronously notify flag set to false.
        self.update_finished_state(DidSeek::Yes, SynchronouslyNotify::No, Invalidate::Yes, None);

        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#set-the-start-time
    /// NB: The host validates new start time as a CSSNumberish time before it runs this procedure.
    fn set_the_start_time(&mut self, new_start_time: Option<TimeValue>) {
        // 1. Let valid start time be the result of running the validate a CSSNumberish time procedure with new start
        //    time as the input.
        // 2. If valid start time is false, abort this procedure.
        // AD-HOC: The host has already validated new start time.

        // 3. Set auto align start time to false.
        self.set_auto_align_start_time(false);

        // 4. Let timeline time be the current time value of the timeline that animation is associated with. If there
        //    is no timeline associated with animation or the associated timeline is inactive, let the timeline time be
        //    unresolved.
        let timeline_time = self.timeline_time();

        // 5. If timeline time is unresolved and new start time is resolved, make animation’s hold time unresolved.
        if timeline_time.is_none() && new_start_time.is_some() {
            self.set_hold_time(None);
        }

        // 6. Let previous current time be animation’s current time.
        let previous_current_time = self.current_time();

        // 7. Apply any pending playback rate on animation.
        self.apply_any_pending_playback_rate();

        // 8. Set animation’s start time to new start time.
        self.set_start_time(new_start_time);

        // 9. Update animation’s hold time based on the first matching condition from the following,

        // -> If new start time is resolved,
        if new_start_time.is_some() {
            // If animation’s playback rate is not zero, make animation’s hold time unresolved.
            if self.playback_rate() != 0.0 {
                self.set_hold_time(None);
            }
        }
        // -> Otherwise (new start time is unresolved),
        else {
            // Set animation’s hold time to previous current time even if previous current time is unresolved.
            self.set_hold_time(previous_current_time);
        }

        // 10. If animation has a pending play task or a pending pause task, cancel that task and resolve animation’s
        //     current ready promise with animation.
        if self.pending() {
            self.set_has_pending_play_task(false);
            self.set_has_pending_pause_task(false);
            self.emit(HostEffectKind::ResolveReadyPromise);
        }

        // 11. Run the procedure to update an animation’s finished state for animation with the did seek flag set to
        //     true, and the synchronously notify flag set to false.
        self.update_finished_state(DidSeek::Yes, SynchronouslyNotify::No, Invalidate::Yes, None);
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#set-the-playback-rate
    pub(crate) fn set_playback_rate(&mut self, new_playback_rate: f64) -> Result<(), AnimationError> {
        // 1. Clear any pending playback rate on animation.
        self.set_pending_playback_rate(None);

        // 2. Let previous time be the value of the current time of animation before changing the playback rate.
        let previous_time = self.current_time();

        // 3. Let previous playback rate be the current effective playback rate of animation.
        let previous_playback_rate = self.playback_rate();

        // 4. Set the playback rate to new playback rate.
        self.update_playback(|playback| playback.playback_rate = new_playback_rate);

        // 5. Perform the steps corresponding to the first matching condition from the following, if any:

        // -> If animation is associated with a monotonically increasing timeline and the previous time is resolved,
        if self.has_monotonically_increasing_timeline()
            && let Some(previous_time) = previous_time
        {
            // set the current time of animation to previous time.
            self.as_script_changing_the_play_state(|procedures| procedures.set_current_time(Some(previous_time)))?;
        }
        // -> If animation is associated with a non-null timeline that is not monotonically increasing, the start time
        //    of animation is resolved, associated effect end is not infinity, and either:
        //    - the previous playback rate < 0 and the new playback rate ≥ 0, or
        //    - the previous playback rate ≥ 0 and the new playback rate < 0,
        else if self.has_finite_timeline()
            && let Some(start_time) = self.start_time()
            && !self.associated_effect_end().value.is_infinite()
            && ((previous_playback_rate < 0.0 && new_playback_rate >= 0.0)
                || (previous_playback_rate >= 0.0 && new_playback_rate < 0.0))
        {
            // Set animation’s start time to the result of evaluating associated effect end - start time for animation.
            self.set_start_time(Some(self.associated_effect_end() - start_time));
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#update-an-animations-finished-state
    /// `observed_current_time`, where given, is the unconstrained current time.
    pub(crate) fn update_finished_state(
        &mut self,
        did_seek: DidSeek,
        synchronously_notify: SynchronouslyNotify,
        invalidate: Invalidate,
        observed_current_time: Option<TimeValue>,
    ) {
        // 1. Let the unconstrained current time be the result of calculating the current time substituting an
        //    unresolved time value for the hold time if did seek is false. If did seek is true, the unconstrained
        //    current time is equal to the current time.
        //
        // Note: This is required to accommodate timelines that can change direction. Without this definition, a once-
        //       finished animation would remain finished even when its timeline progresses in the opposite direction.
        let unconstrained_current_time = observed_current_time.or_else(|| match did_seek {
            DidSeek::No => self.current_time_without_hold_time(),
            DidSeek::Yes => self.current_time(),
        });

        // 2. If all three of the following conditions are true,
        //    - the unconstrained current time is resolved, and
        //    - animation’s start time is resolved, and
        //    - animation does not have a pending play task or a pending pause task,
        if let Some(unconstrained_current_time) = unconstrained_current_time
            && self.start_time().is_some()
            && !self.pending()
        {
            // then update animation’s hold time based on the first matching condition for animation from below, if any:
            self.update_hold_time_for_finished_state(did_seek, unconstrained_current_time);
        }

        // 3. Set the previous current time of animation to be the result of calculating its current time.
        let current_time = self.current_time();
        self.animation.borrow_mut().previous_current_time = current_time;

        // 4. Let current finished state be true if the play state of animation is finished. Otherwise, let it be false.
        let current_finished_state = self.play_state() == AnimationPlayState::Finished;

        // 5. If current finished state is true and the current finished promise is not yet resolved, perform the
        //    following steps:
        if current_finished_state && !self.playback().is_finished {
            // 1. Let finish notification steps refer to the following procedure:
            // NB: See finish_notification_steps().

            // 2. If synchronously notify is true, cancel any queued microtask to run the finish notification steps for
            //    this animation, and run the finish notification steps immediately.
            if synchronously_notify == SynchronouslyNotify::Yes {
                self.emit(HostEffectKind::CancelFinishNotificationTask);
                self.finish_notification_steps();
            }
            //    Otherwise, if synchronously notify is false, queue a microtask to run finish notification steps for
            //    animation unless there is already a microtask queued to run those steps for animation.
            else {
                self.emit(HostEffectKind::QueueFinishNotificationTask);
            }
        }

        // 6. If current finished state is false and animation’s current finished promise is already resolved, set
        //    animation’s current finished promise to a new promise in the relevant Realm of animation.
        if !current_finished_state && self.playback().is_finished {
            self.emit(HostEffectKind::ReplaceFinishedPromise);
            self.update_playback(|playback| playback.is_finished = false);
        }

        // AD-HOC: An animation disassociated from its target while inert can only be revived through here.
        if let Some(play_state_when_disassociated) = self.animation.borrow().play_state_when_disassociated_from_target
            && (self.pending() || self.is_relevant() || self.play_state() != play_state_when_disassociated)
            && let Some(element) = self.effect_target()
        {
            self.emit(HostEffectKind::AssociateWithTarget { element });
        }

        // AD-HOC: An animation that has finished without filling produces nothing more, so it leaves its target's list.
        if current_finished_state && !self.pending() && !self.is_relevant() {
            self.animation.borrow_mut().disassociation_from_target_pending = true;
        }

        if invalidate == Invalidate::Yes {
            self.invalidate_effect();
        }
    }

    /// Step 2 of https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#update-an-animations-finished-state
    fn update_hold_time_for_finished_state(&self, did_seek: DidSeek, unconstrained_current_time: TimeValue) {
        let playback_rate = self.playback_rate();
        let previous_current_time = self.animation.borrow().previous_current_time;

        // -> If playback rate > 0 and unconstrained current time is greater than or equal to associated effect end,
        let associated_effect_end = self.associated_effect_end();
        if playback_rate > 0.0 && unconstrained_current_time >= associated_effect_end {
            // If did seek is true, let the hold time be the value of unconstrained current time.
            if did_seek == DidSeek::Yes {
                self.set_hold_time(Some(unconstrained_current_time));
            }
            // If did seek is false, let the hold time be the maximum value of previous current time and associated
            // effect end. If the previous current time is unresolved, let the hold time be associated effect end.
            else if let Some(previous_current_time) = previous_current_time {
                self.set_hold_time(Some(time_value::max(previous_current_time, associated_effect_end)));
            } else {
                self.set_hold_time(Some(associated_effect_end));
            }
        }
        // -> If playback rate < 0 and unconstrained current time is less than or equal to 0,
        else if playback_rate < 0.0 && unconstrained_current_time.value <= 0.0 {
            // If did seek is true, let the hold time be the value of unconstrained current time.
            if did_seek == DidSeek::Yes {
                self.set_hold_time(Some(unconstrained_current_time));
            }
            // If did seek is false, let the hold time be the minimum value of previous current time and zero. If the
            // previous current time is unresolved, let the hold time be zero.
            else if let Some(previous_current_time) = previous_current_time {
                self.set_hold_time(Some(time_value::min(previous_current_time, self.zero())));
            } else {
                self.set_hold_time(Some(self.zero()));
            }
        }
        // -> If playback rate ≠ 0, and animation is associated with an active timeline,
        else if playback_rate != 0.0
            && let Some(timeline_time) = self.timeline_time()
        {
            // Perform the following steps:

            // 1. If did seek is true and the hold time is resolved, let animation’s start time be equal to the result
            //    of evaluating timeline time - (hold time / playback rate) where timeline time is the current time
            //    value of the timeline associated with animation.
            if did_seek == DidSeek::Yes
                && let Some(hold_time) = self.hold_time()
            {
                self.set_start_time(Some(timeline_time - (hold_time / playback_rate)));
            }

            // 2. Let the hold time be unresolved.
            self.set_hold_time(None);
        }
    }

    /// The finish notification steps of step 5 of
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#update-an-animations-finished-state
    pub(crate) fn finish_notification_steps(&mut self) {
        // 1. If animation’s play state is not equal to finished, abort these steps.
        if self.play_state() != AnimationPlayState::Finished {
            return;
        }

        // 2. Resolve animation’s current finished promise object with animation.
        self.emit(HostEffectKind::ResolveFinishedPromise);
        self.update_playback(|playback| playback.is_finished = true);

        // 3. Create an AnimationPlaybackEvent, finishEvent.
        // 4. Set finishEvent’s type attribute to finish.
        // 5. Set finishEvent’s currentTime attribute to the current time of animation.
        // 6. Set finishEvent’s timelineTime attribute to the current time of the timeline with which animation is
        //    associated. If animation is not associated with a timeline, or the timeline is inactive, let timelineTime
        //    be null.
        // 7. If animation has a document for timing, then append finishEvent to its document for timing's pending
        //    animation event queue along with its target, animation. For the scheduled event time, use the result of
        //    converting animation’s associated effect end to an origin-relative time.
        //    Otherwise, queue a task to dispatch finishEvent at animation. The task source for this task is the DOM
        //    manipulation task source.
        // NB: The host creates and queues the event. The conversion of the associated effect end to an origin-relative
        //     time starts here, from the animation as it is now, by converting it to a timeline time.
        let current_time = self.current_time();
        let timeline_time = self.timeline_time();
        let scheduled_timeline_time =
            self.convert_an_animation_time_to_timeline_time(Some(self.associated_effect_end()));
        self.emit(HostEffectKind::QueuePlaybackEvent {
            r#type: PlaybackEventType::Finish,
            current_time,
            timeline_time,
            scheduled_timeline_time,
        });
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#animation-time-to-timeline-time
    fn convert_an_animation_time_to_timeline_time(&self, time: Option<TimeValue>) -> Option<TimeValue> {
        // 1. If time is unresolved, return time.
        let time = time?;

        // 2. If time is infinity, return an unresolved time value.
        if time.value.is_infinite() {
            return None;
        }

        // 3. If animation’s playback rate is zero, return an unresolved time value.
        let playback_rate = self.playback_rate();
        if playback_rate == 0.0 {
            return None;
        }

        // 4. If animation’s start time is unresolved, return an unresolved time value.
        let start_time = self.start_time()?;

        // 5. Return the result of calculating: time × (1 / playback rate) + start time (where playback rate and start
        //    time are the playback rate and start time of animation, respectively).
        Some((time * (1.0 / playback_rate)) + start_time)
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#animation-reset-an-animations-pending-tasks
    fn reset_an_animations_pending_tasks(&mut self) {
        // 1. If animation does not have a pending play task or a pending pause task, abort this procedure.
        if !self.pending() {
            return;
        }

        // 2. If animation has a pending play task, cancel that task.
        self.set_has_pending_play_task(false);

        // 3. If animation has a pending pause task, cancel that task.
        self.set_has_pending_pause_task(false);

        // 4. Apply any pending playback rate on animation.
        self.apply_any_pending_playback_rate();

        // 5. Reject animation’s current ready promise with a DOMException named "AbortError".
        // 6. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot of animation’s current ready promise to true.
        // 7. Let animation’s current ready promise be the result of creating a new resolved Promise object with value
        //    animation in the relevant Realm of animation.
        self.emit(HostEffectKind::RejectReadyPromise);
    }

    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#cancel-an-animation
    fn cancel_an_animation(&mut self, invalidate: Invalidate) {
        // 1. If animation’s play state is not idle, perform the following steps:
        if self.play_state() != AnimationPlayState::Idle {
            // 1. Run the procedure to reset an animation’s pending tasks on animation.
            self.reset_an_animations_pending_tasks();

            // 2. Reject the current finished promise with a DOMException named "AbortError".
            // 3. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot of the current finished promise to true.
            // 4. Let current finished promise be a new promise in the relevant Realm of animation.
