//! Sets of animation records that do not keep them alive.

use std::hash::BuildHasher;
use std::rc::{Rc, Weak};

use hashbrown::HashTable;

/// A set of records, by identity, that keeps none of them alive.
///
/// A record is alive to the set while something keeps it alive and the set's liveness test accepts it. A record that
/// dies stays in the set as a dead entry, which no lookup or enumeration yields, until the set is next
/// pruned. Dropping a record therefore never reaches into a set that holds it. A dead entry still holds its record's
/// allocation, so the address of a record identifies it for as long as the set has an entry for it.
///
/// The entries are kept in insertion order, except that removing one moves the last entry into its place.
pub(crate) struct WeakRecordSet<T> {
    entries: Vec<Weak<T>>,
    /// The index of each entry in `entries`, by the hash of its record's address.
    indices: HashTable<u32>,
    is_alive: fn(&T) -> bool,
}

fn hash_of<T>(record: *const T) -> u64 {
    foldhash::fast::FixedState::default().hash_one(record as usize)
}

impl<T> WeakRecordSet<T> {
    /// A new empty set, to which a record that something keeps alive is alive while `is_alive` accepts it.
    pub(crate) fn new(is_alive: fn(&T) -> bool) -> Self {
        Self {
            entries: Vec::new(),
            indices: HashTable::new(),
            is_alive,
        }
    }

    fn live_record(&self, entry: &Weak<T>) -> Option<Rc<T>> {
        entry.upgrade().filter(|record| (self.is_alive)(record))
    }

    fn find(&self, record: *const T) -> Option<u32> {
        let entries = &self.entries;
        self.indices
            .find(hash_of(record), |&index| entries[index as usize].as_ptr() == record)
            .copied()
    }

    /// The index of the entry of `record` in the set's order, if the set holds it.
    pub(crate) fn position(&self, record: *const T) -> Option<u32> {
        self.find(record)
    }

    /// Whether the set holds `record`.
    pub(crate) fn contains(&self, record: *const T) -> bool {
        self.find(record).is_some()
    }

    /// Adds `record` to the set, answering whether the set did not hold it yet.
    pub(crate) fn insert(&mut self, record: &Rc<T>) -> bool {
        let pointer = Rc::as_ptr(record);
        if self.contains(pointer) {
            return false;
        }
        if self.entries.len() == self.entries.capacity() {
            self.prune();
        }
        let index = u32::try_from(self.entries.len()).expect("a set of records holds fewer than 2^32 entries");
        self.entries.push(Rc::downgrade(record));
        let entries = &self.entries;
        self.indices.insert_unique(hash_of(pointer), index, |&index| {
            hash_of(entries[index as usize].as_ptr())
        });
        true
    }

    /// Removes `record` from the set, answering whether the set held it.
    pub(crate) fn remove(&mut self, record: *const T) -> bool {
        let entries = &self.entries;
        let Ok(slot) = self
            .indices
            .find_entry(hash_of(record), |&index| entries[index as usize].as_ptr() == record)
        else {
            return false;
        };
        let (index, _) = slot.remove();
        let last = u32::try_from(self.entries.len() - 1).expect("a set of records holds fewer than 2^32 entries");
        if index != last {
            let moved = self.entries[last as usize].as_ptr();
            let entries = &self.entries;
            let slot = self
                .indices
                .find_mut(hash_of(moved), |&candidate| {
                    candidate == last && entries[candidate as usize].as_ptr() == moved
                })
                .expect("every entry of a set of records has an index");
            *slot = index;
        }
        self.entries.swap_remove(index as usize);
        true
    }

    /// Drops the entries of records that are no longer alive to the set.
    pub(crate) fn prune(&mut self) {
        let is_alive = self.is_alive;
        let entry_is_alive = |entry: &Weak<T>| entry.upgrade().is_some_and(|record| is_alive(&record));
        if self.entries.iter().all(entry_is_alive) {
            return;
        }
        self.entries.retain(entry_is_alive);
        self.indices.clear();
        for (index, entry) in self.entries.iter().enumerate() {
            let index = u32::try_from(index).expect("a set of records holds fewer than 2^32 entries");
            let entries = &self.entries;
            self.indices.insert_unique(hash_of(entry.as_ptr()), index, |&index| {
                hash_of(entries[index as usize].as_ptr())
            });
        }
    }

    /// The number of entries, live or dead, which enumeration runs over.
    pub(crate) fn entry_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.entries.len()
    }

    /// The record of the entry at `index`, where it is alive to the set.
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<Rc<T>> {
        self.live_record(&self.entries[index])
    }

    /// Empties the set, calling `callback` with each record alive to it, in insertion order.
    pub(crate) fn take_each(&mut self, mut callback: impl FnMut(Rc<T>)) {
        for entry in &self.entries {
            if let Some(record) = self.live_record(entry) {
                callback(record);
            }
        }
        self.clear();
    }

    /// Removes every entry.
    pub(crate) fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.entries.clear();
        self.indices.clear();
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn live(set: &WeakRecordSet<u32>) -> Vec<u32> {
        (0..set.entry_count())
            .filter_map(|index| set.get(index))
            .map(|record| *record)
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn insert_and_remove_track_membership_by_identity() {
        let mut set = WeakRecordSet::new(|_| true);
        let first = Rc::new(1);
        let second = Rc::new(1);
        assert!(set.insert(&first));
        assert!(!set.insert(&first));
        assert!(set.insert(&second));
        assert!(set.contains(Rc::as_ptr(&first)));
        assert!(set.remove(Rc::as_ptr(&first)));
        assert!(!set.remove(Rc::as_ptr(&first)));
        assert!(!set.contains(Rc::as_ptr(&first)));
        assert!(set.contains(Rc::as_ptr(&second)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn taking_each_record_yields_the_live_ones_and_empties_the_set() {
        let mut set = WeakRecordSet::new(|&record| record != 2);
        let records: Vec<_> = (0..4).map(Rc::new).collect();
        for record in &records {
            set.insert(record);
        }
        let mut taken = Vec::new();
        set.take_each(|record| taken.push(*record));
        assert_eq!(taken, [0, 1, 3]);
        assert_eq!(set.entry_count(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_dead_record_is_not_yielded_and_is_pruned() {
        let mut set = WeakRecordSet::new(|_| true);
        let kept = Rc::new(1);
        let dropped = Rc::new(2);
        set.insert(&kept);
        set.insert(&dropped);
        drop(dropped);
        assert_eq!(live(&set), [1]);
        assert_eq!(set.entry_count(), 2);
        set.prune();
        assert_eq!(set.entry_count(), 1);
        assert!(set.contains(Rc::as_ptr(&kept)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_record_the_set_does_not_consider_alive_is_not_yielded_and_is_pruned() {
        let mut set = WeakRecordSet::new(|&record| record != 2);
        let kept = Rc::new(1);
        let retired = Rc::new(2);
        set.insert(&kept);
        set.insert(&retired);
        assert_eq!(set.get(1), None);
        set.prune();
        assert_eq!(live(&set), [1]);
        assert!(!set.contains(Rc::as_ptr(&retired)));
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Columns whose published generations share storage with the column that goes on changing.
//!
//! A [`CowColumn`] keeps its rows in fixed-size chunks behind [`Arc`]s, and its chunks in groups
//! behind [`Arc`]s, under a spine behind an [`Arc`]. A column holds whole chunks, and a row it was
//! never asked to hold reads as the default. Publishing shares the spine, so a [`ColumnSnapshot`]
//! costs one reference count however large the rows are, and so does dropping it. A write copies
//! the spine, the row's group and the row's chunk only where a snapshot still shares them, so the
//! cost of a generation follows the chunks written after it was published rather than the size of
//! the column. Neither is deep-copied: a snapshot's clone shares its spine, and so does a column's
//! clone, its fork. Publishing and forking take the same time however many rows the column holds:
//! nothing in them walks the chunks. Both are `Send` and `Sync` when the row type is: the column is
//! written through `&mut`, and a snapshot never changes.
//!
//! A column is written only through [`CowColumn::set`] and [`RowMut`], and both compare the row
//! they write with the row a snapshot shares before copying the chunk. So a write that leaves a row
//! as it was never copies a chunk, whichever caller makes it.

use std::ops::{Deref, DerefMut};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

/// A chunk starts on a cache line of its own, so rows do not share a line with the reference
/// counts or with another chunk.
#[derive(Clone)]
#[repr(align(64))]
struct Chunk<T, const CHUNK: usize>([T; CHUNK]);

/// How many chunks a group holds: a write after a publication copies this many chunk pointers.
const GROUP: usize = 64;

/// The chunks of a group, the column's last group holding fewer than it has room for.
struct Group<T, const CHUNK: usize> {
    chunks: [Option<Arc<Chunk<T, CHUNK>>>; GROUP],
    /// The edit token of the column that last made each chunk its own. See [`CowColumn::edit_token`].
    owners: [u64; GROUP],
}

impl<T, const CHUNK: usize> Group<T, CHUNK> {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            chunks: std::array::from_fn(|_| None),
            owners: [0; GROUP],
        }
    }
}

impl<T, const CHUNK: usize> Clone for Group<T, CHUNK> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            chunks: self.chunks.clone(),
            owners: self.owners,
        }
    }
}

/// An edit token no column held before, and no chunk names yet.
pub(crate) fn new_edit_token() -> u64 {
    static NEXT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(1);
    NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
}

type Spine<T, const CHUNK: usize> = Arc<[Arc<Group<T, CHUNK>>]>;

#[inline]
fn chunk_of<T, const CHUNK: usize>(spine: &Spine<T, CHUNK>, chunk_index: usize) -> Option<&Arc<Chunk<T, CHUNK>>> {
    spine.get(chunk_index / GROUP)?.chunks[chunk_index % GROUP].as_ref()
}

#[inline]
fn row_of<T, const CHUNK: usize>(spine: &Spine<T, CHUNK>, index: usize) -> Option<&T> {
    Some(&chunk_of(spine, index / CHUNK)?.0[index % CHUNK])
}

/// The group of the chunk at `chunk_index` of `spine`, made the spine's own, for the caller to make the chunk its own.
fn group_mut<T, const CHUNK: usize>(spine: &mut Spine<T, CHUNK>, chunk_index: usize) -> &mut Group<T, CHUNK> {
    Arc::make_mut(&mut Arc::make_mut(spine)[chunk_index / GROUP])
}

pub(crate) struct CowColumn<T, const CHUNK: usize> {
    spine: Spine<T, CHUNK>,
    /// How many chunks the column holds.
    chunk_count: usize,
    /// The chunk the spine holds at each index, so that reaching a row does not walk the spine and the chunk's group. The
    /// spine keeps each alive, and whatever puts another chunk in a slot of the spine updates it. A fork starts without
    /// the table, which would make forking cost a pointer per chunk, and walks the spine instead: only the column a fork
    /// was made from reads at full speed.
    chunks: Vec<*const Chunk<T, CHUNK>>,
    /// What a chunk's group names it by once the column made it its own. A chunk that names this token is unshared, with
    /// its group and the spine, as only sharing the column shares them, and sharing it takes a new token. So what the
    /// column owns is forgotten at once, however many chunks it holds. Atomic because a fork takes `&self`.
    edit_token: AtomicU64,
    /// Advanced as the column is written. See [`Self::version`].
    version: u64,
}

// SAFETY: `chunks` points only into what `spine` holds, and the column hands out its rows only through `&self` and
// `&mut self`, as the spine alone would.
unsafe impl<T: Send + Sync, const CHUNK: usize> Send for CowColumn<T, CHUNK> {}
// SAFETY: As above.
unsafe impl<T: Send + Sync, const CHUNK: usize> Sync for CowColumn<T, CHUNK> {}

/// A generation of a [`CowColumn`], as it was when published. It does not see later writes.
pub(crate) struct ColumnSnapshot<T, const CHUNK: usize> {
    spine: Spine<T, CHUNK>,
}

impl<T, const CHUNK: usize> Default for CowColumn<T, CHUNK> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            spine: Arc::new([]),
            chunk_count: 0,
            chunks: Vec::new(),
            edit_token: AtomicU64::new(new_edit_token()),
            version: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl<T, const CHUNK: usize> Default for ColumnSnapshot<T, CHUNK> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { spine: Arc::new([]) }
    }
}

impl<T, const CHUNK: usize> Clone for ColumnSnapshot<T, CHUNK> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            spine: Arc::clone(&self.spine),
        }
    }
}

/// The bytes of the spine, groups and chunks of `spine` that `sizer` reaches for the first time,
/// with what `row_heap` says each row of such a chunk holds.
fn spine_heap_size<T, const CHUNK: usize>(
    spine: &Spine<T, CHUNK>,
    sizer: &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer,
    row_heap: &mut impl FnMut(&T, &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer) -> usize,
) -> usize {
    use crate::heap_size::ARC_HEADER_BYTES;
    if !sizer.first_sight(Arc::as_ptr(spine)) {
        return 0;
    }
    let mut bytes = ARC_HEADER_BYTES + size_of_val::<[Arc<Group<T, CHUNK>>]>(spine);
    for group in spine.iter() {
        if !sizer.first_sight(Arc::as_ptr(group)) {
            continue;
        }
        bytes += ARC_HEADER_BYTES + size_of::<Group<T, CHUNK>>();
        for chunk in group.chunks.iter().flatten() {
            if !sizer.first_sight(Arc::as_ptr(chunk)) {
                continue;
            }
            // NB: The chunk's alignment pads the reference counts in front of it to a cache line.
            bytes += size_of::<Chunk<T, CHUNK>>().max(ARC_HEADER_BYTES)
                + align_of::<Chunk<T, CHUNK>>()
                + chunk.0.iter().map(|row| row_heap(row, sizer)).sum::<usize>();
        }
    }
    bytes
}

impl<T: Clone + Default, const CHUNK: usize> CowColumn<T, CHUNK> {
    /// The bytes the column holds that `sizer` reaches for the first time, with what `row_heap`
    /// says each row holds.
    pub(crate) fn heap_size(
        &self,
        sizer: &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer,
        mut row_heap: impl FnMut(&T, &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer) -> usize,
    ) -> usize {
        crate::heap_size::vec_bytes(&self.chunks) + spine_heap_size(&self.spine, sizer, &mut row_heap)
    }

    const CHUNK_IS_NOT_EMPTY: () = assert!(CHUNK > 0);

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&T> {
        match self.chunks.get(index / CHUNK) {
            // SAFETY: The spine holds the chunk, and nothing writes it while `&self` is borrowed.
            Some(&chunk) => Some(unsafe { &(*chunk).0[index % CHUNK] }),
            None => row_of(&self.spine, index),
        }
    }

    /// Whether the chunk is known to be unshared, with its group and the spine.
    #[inline]
    fn names_chunk(&self, chunk_index: usize) -> bool {
        self.spine[chunk_index / GROUP].owners[chunk_index % GROUP] == self.edit_token.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    /// The row at `index` in a chunk made the column's own, copying the spine, the chunk's group
    /// and the chunk where a snapshot shares them.
    #[inline]
    fn owned_row(&mut self, index: usize) -> Option<&mut T> {
        let chunk = self.owned_chunk(index / CHUNK)?;
        // SAFETY: See `owned_chunk`. `&mut self` keeps any other reference into the column from being live.
        Some(unsafe { &mut (*chunk).0[index % CHUNK] })
    }

    /// The chunk at `chunk_index`, made the column's own as [`Self::owned_row`] makes a row's. It stays unshared and
    /// in place until the column is shared or a chunk is put in its place, neither of which happens through `&self`.
    #[inline]
    fn owned_chunk(&mut self, chunk_index: usize) -> Option<*mut Chunk<T, CHUNK>> {
        if chunk_index >= self.chunk_count {
            return None;
        }
        self.version += 1;
        if !self.names_chunk(chunk_index) {
            self.make_chunk_own(chunk_index)?;
        }
        let chunk = self.spine[chunk_index / GROUP].chunks[chunk_index % GROUP].as_ref()?;
        // NB: The chunk, its group and the spine have not been shared since they were made unique: the chunk names the
        //     column's token, and sharing the column takes a new one.
        Some(Arc::as_ptr(chunk).cast_mut())
    }

    /// Makes the chunk the column's own, copying the spine, its group and the chunk where a snapshot shares them.
    #[cold]
    fn make_chunk_own(&mut self, chunk_index: usize) -> Option<()> {
        let edit_token = *self.edit_token.get_mut();
        let group = group_mut(&mut self.spine, chunk_index);
        let chunk = group.chunks[chunk_index % GROUP].as_mut()?;
        Arc::make_mut(chunk);
        let chunk = Arc::as_ptr(chunk);
        group.owners[chunk_index % GROUP] = edit_token;
        if let Some(entry) = self.chunks.get_mut(chunk_index) {
            *entry = chunk;
        }
        Some(())
    }

    /// Whether the row at `index` is in a chunk no snapshot shares, marking the chunk so if it is.
    fn owns_chunk_of(&mut self, index: usize) -> bool {
        let chunk_index = index / CHUNK;
        if self.names_chunk(chunk_index) {
            return true;
        }
        let edit_token = *self.edit_token.get_mut();
        let owned = Arc::get_mut(&mut self.spine)
            .and_then(|spine| Arc::get_mut(&mut spine[chunk_index / GROUP]))
            .is_some_and(|group| {
                let unique = group.chunks[chunk_index % GROUP]
                    .as_mut()
                    .is_some_and(|chunk| Arc::get_mut(chunk).is_some());
                if unique {
                    group.owners[chunk_index % GROUP] = edit_token;
                }
                unique
            });
        if owned {
            self.version += 1;
        }
        owned
    }

    /// Grows the column to hold at least `len` rows, the new ones default. A column never
    /// shrinks: rows are reset in place instead.
    pub(crate) fn grow_to(&mut self, len: usize) {
        let () = Self::CHUNK_IS_NOT_EMPTY;
        let edit_token = *self.edit_token.get_mut();
        while self.chunk_count * CHUNK < len {
            let chunk_index = self.chunk_count;
            if chunk_index.is_multiple_of(GROUP) {
                let group = Arc::new(Group::new());
                self.spine = self.spine.iter().cloned().chain([group]).collect();
            }
            let chunk = Arc::new(Chunk(std::array::from_fn(|_| T::default())));
            if self.chunks.len() == chunk_index {
                self.chunks.push(Arc::as_ptr(&chunk));
            }
            let group = group_mut(&mut self.spine, chunk_index);
            group.chunks[chunk_index % GROUP] = Some(chunk);
            group.owners[chunk_index % GROUP] = edit_token;
            self.chunk_count += 1;
            self.version += 1;
        }
    }

    /// How many rows the column holds: whole chunks, the rows it was never asked for reading as the default.
    pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.chunk_count * CHUNK
    }

    /// How far the column has been written. A snapshot reads as the column does for as long as the version stays what
    /// it was when the snapshot was published, whoever published since: every write advances it, except one to a chunk
    /// the column already made its own after it last published, whose first write did.
    pub(crate) fn version(&self) -> u64 {
        self.version
    }

    /// This generation of the column, sharing all of it with the column until the column writes.
    pub(crate) fn publish(&mut self) -> ColumnSnapshot<T, CHUNK> {
        *self.edit_token.get_mut() = new_edit_token();
        ColumnSnapshot {
            spine: Arc::clone(&self.spine),
        }
    }
}

/// A fork of a column shares all of it with the column until either writes, as a snapshot does: it costs one
/// reference count, and each side copies a chunk the other shares the first time it writes there.
impl<T: Clone + Default, const CHUNK: usize> Clone for CowColumn<T, CHUNK> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        self.edit_token.store(new_edit_token(), Ordering::Relaxed);
        Self {
            spine: Arc::clone(&self.spine),
            chunk_count: self.chunk_count,
            chunks: Vec::new(),
            edit_token: AtomicU64::new(new_edit_token()),
            version: self.version,
        }
    }
}

impl<T: Clone + Default + PartialEq, const CHUNK: usize> CowColumn<T, CHUNK> {
    /// Sets the row at `index`: in place in a chunk the column owns, and in a chunk a snapshot
    /// shares only if the row changes, copying the chunk then. `None` if the column does not hold
    /// the row.
    pub(crate) fn set(&mut self, index: usize, value: T) -> Option<()> {
        self.get(index)?;
        if self.owns_chunk_of(index) || *self.get(index)? != value {
            *self.owned_row(index)? = value;
        }
        Some(())
    }

    /// Sets the row at `index` as [`Self::set`] does, answering what the row held. `None` if the column does not hold
    /// the row.
    pub(crate) fn replace(&mut self, index: usize, value: T) -> Option<T> {
        self.get(index)?;
        if self.owns_chunk_of(index) || *self.get(index)? != value {
            return Some(std::mem::replace(self.owned_row(index)?, value));
        }
        Some(value)
    }

    /// The row at `index`, for writing. See [`RowMut`].
    pub(crate) fn row_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> Option<RowMut<&mut Self, T, CHUNK>> {
        RowMut::new(self, index)
    }

    /// A writer of many rows, for a caller that writes rows that change, many of them in the same chunk: it grows the
    /// column to hold each row it is asked for and makes each chunk the column's own once, not once per row.
    pub(crate) fn writer(&mut self) -> ColumnWriter<'_, T, CHUNK> {
        ColumnWriter {
            column: self,
            chunk_index: usize::MAX,
            chunk: std::ptr::null_mut(),
        }
    }
}

/// Writes rows of a [`CowColumn`], keeping the chunk it wrote last at hand. See [`CowColumn::writer`].
pub(crate) struct ColumnWriter<'a, T, const CHUNK: usize> {
    column: &'a mut CowColumn<T, CHUNK>,
    chunk_index: usize,
    /// The rows of the chunk at `chunk_index`, which the column owns, or null before the first write.
    chunk: *mut Chunk<T, CHUNK>,
}

impl<T: Clone + Default + PartialEq, const CHUNK: usize> ColumnWriter<'_, T, CHUNK> {
    /// The row at `index`, as the column holds it, if it holds it.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&T> {
        self.column.get(index)
    }

    /// Sets the row at `index`, growing the column to hold it.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn set(&mut self, index: usize, value: T) {
        let chunk_index = index / CHUNK;
        if chunk_index != self.chunk_index {
            self.column.grow_to(index + 1);
            // NB: Making the row's chunk the column's own advances the version, as a write to it does.
            self.chunk = self.column.owned_chunk(chunk_index).expect("the column was grown");
            self.chunk_index = chunk_index;
        }
        // SAFETY: The chunk is the column's own, and stays unshared and in place while the writer borrows the column
        //         as `&mut`: nothing but the writer can share it or put another chunk in its place.
        unsafe { (*self.chunk).0[index % CHUNK] = value };
    }
}

/// A row of a [`CowColumn`], for writing. While a snapshot shares the row's chunk, the writes go
/// to a copy of the row, and the row is set from it when the guard drops, copying the chunk only if
/// the row changed. In a chunk the column owns, they go to the row in place. `C` is how the guard
/// holds the column: `&mut` it, or a `RefMut` of it.
pub(crate) struct RowMut<C, T, const CHUNK: usize>
where
    C: DerefMut<Target = CowColumn<T, CHUNK>>,
    T: Clone + Default + PartialEq,
{
    column: C,
    index: usize,
    staged: Option<T>,
}

impl<C, T, const CHUNK: usize> RowMut<C, T, CHUNK>
where
    C: DerefMut<Target = CowColumn<T, CHUNK>>,
    T: Clone + Default + PartialEq,
{
    /// The row at `index` of the column `column` holds. `None` if the column does not hold it.
    pub(crate) fn new(mut column: C, index: usize) -> Option<Self> {
        column.get(index)?;
        let staged = if column.owns_chunk_of(index) {
            None
        } else {
            column.get(index).cloned()
        };
        Some(Self { column, index, staged })
    }
}

impl<C, T, const CHUNK: usize> Deref for RowMut<C, T, CHUNK>
where
    C: DerefMut<Target = CowColumn<T, CHUNK>>,
    T: Clone + Default + PartialEq,
{
    type Target = T;

    #[inline]
    fn deref(&self) -> &T {
        match &self.staged {
            Some(row) => row,
            None => self.column.get(self.index).expect("the guard's row is in the column"),
        }
    }
}

impl<C, T, const CHUNK: usize> DerefMut for RowMut<C, T, CHUNK>
where
    C: DerefMut<Target = CowColumn<T, CHUNK>>,
    T: Clone + Default + PartialEq,
{
    #[inline]
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut T {
        match &mut self.staged {
            Some(row) => row,
            None => self
                .column
                .owned_row(self.index)
                .expect("the guard's row is in the column"),
        }
    }
}

impl<C, T, const CHUNK: usize> Drop for RowMut<C, T, CHUNK>
where
    C: DerefMut<Target = CowColumn<T, CHUNK>>,
    T: Clone + Default + PartialEq,
{
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(row) = self.staged.take() {
            self.column.set(self.index, row);
        }
    }
}

impl<T, const CHUNK: usize> ColumnSnapshot<T, CHUNK> {
    /// Whether `other` is this very generation of the column: one no write came between.
    pub(crate) fn is_same_generation_as(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        Arc::ptr_eq(&self.spine, &other.spine)
    }

    /// The bytes of the snapshot's chunks that `sizer` reaches for the first time, with what
    /// `row_heap` says each row holds.
    pub(crate) fn heap_size(
        &self,
        sizer: &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer,
        mut row_heap: impl FnMut(&T, &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer) -> usize,
    ) -> usize {
        spine_heap_size(&self.spine, sizer, &mut row_heap)
    }

    /// How many rows the snapshot has room for: every row index below it may be read.
    pub(crate) fn slot_capacity(&self) -> usize {
        self.spine.last().map_or(0, |last| {
            let in_last = last.chunks.iter().take_while(|chunk| chunk.is_some()).count();
            ((self.spine.len() - 1) * GROUP + in_last) * CHUNK
        })
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&T> {
        row_of(&self.spine, index)
    }
}

/// Whether two rows hold the same shared payload: the same allocation, or two that `same_value`
/// says are equal.
pub(crate) fn same_payload<T: ?Sized>(
    a: Option<&Arc<T>>,
    b: Option<&Arc<T>>,
    same_value: impl FnOnce(&T, &T) -> bool,
) -> bool {
    match (a, b) {
        (Some(a), Some(b)) => Arc::ptr_eq(a, b) || same_value(a, b),
        (None, None) => true,
        _ => false,
    }
}

const _: () = {
    const fn assert_send_and_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
    assert_send_and_sync::<CowColumn<u64, 64>>();
    assert_send_and_sync::<ColumnSnapshot<u64, 64>>();
};

/// A vector whose fork shares its storage, as a [`CowColumn`]'s does: cloning it costs one reference count, and each
/// side copies a chunk the other shares the first time it writes there. Rows past `len` read as the default
/// and are reset to it before the vector grows over them again.
pub(crate) struct CowVec<T, const CHUNK: usize> {
    column: CowColumn<T, CHUNK>,
    len: usize,
}

impl<T, const CHUNK: usize> Default for CowVec<T, CHUNK> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            column: CowColumn::default(),
            len: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl<T: Clone + Default, const CHUNK: usize> Clone for CowVec<T, CHUNK> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            column: self.column.clone(),
            len: self.len,
        }
    }
}

impl<T: Clone + Default, const CHUNK: usize> CowVec<T, CHUNK> {
    pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.len
    }

    /// The bytes the vector holds that `sizer` reaches for the first time, with what `row_heap` says each row holds.
    pub(crate) fn heap_size(
        &self,
        sizer: &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer,
        row_heap: impl FnMut(&T, &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer) -> usize,
    ) -> usize {
        self.column.heap_size(sizer, row_heap)
    }

    /// The bytes of the rows themselves, without what they hold on the heap.
    pub(crate) fn row_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        self.column.len() * size_of::<T>()
    }

    /// Every row, in order.
    pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &T> {
        (0..self.len).filter_map(|index| self.column.get(index))
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&T> {
        if index >= self.len {
            return None;
        }
        self.column.get(index)
    }

    /// The row at `index`, for writing, copying its chunk where a fork shares it.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn get_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> Option<&mut T> {
        if index >= self.len {
            return None;
        }
        self.column.owned_row(index)
    }

    pub(crate) fn push(&mut self, value: T) {
        let index = self.len;
        self.resize_with_default(index + 1);
        self[index] = value;
    }

    /// Empties the vector, answering its rows in order.
    pub(crate) fn take_rows(&mut self) -> Vec<T> {
        let rows = self.iter().cloned().collect();
        *self = Self::default();
        rows
    }

    /// Grows the vector to `len` rows, the new ones default, or truncates it to them.
    pub(crate) fn resize_with_default(&mut self, len: usize) {
        if len < self.len {
            for index in len..self.len {
                if self.column.get(index).is_some() {
                    *self.column.owned_row(index).expect("the row is in the column") = T::default();
                }
            }
        }
        self.column.grow_to(len);
        self.len = len;
    }
}

impl<T: Clone + Default, const CHUNK: usize> FromIterator<T> for CowVec<T, CHUNK> {
    fn from_iter<I: IntoIterator<Item = T>>(rows: I) -> Self {
        let mut vector = Self::default();
        for row in rows {
            vector.push(row);
        }
        vector
    }
}

impl<T: Clone + Default, const CHUNK: usize> std::ops::Index<usize> for CowVec<T, CHUNK> {
    type Output = T;

    #[inline]
    fn index(&self, index: usize) -> &T {
        self.get(index).expect("index within the vector")
    }
}

impl<T: Clone + Default, const CHUNK: usize> std::ops::IndexMut<usize> for CowVec<T, CHUNK> {
    #[inline]
    fn index_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> &mut T {
        self.get_mut(index).expect("index within the vector")
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    type Column = CowColumn<u32, 4>;

    fn column_of(values: &[u32]) -> Column {
        let mut column = Column::default();
        column.grow_to(values.len());
        for (index, &value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
            column.set(index, value).unwrap();
        }
        column
    }

    fn rows(snapshot: &ColumnSnapshot<u32, 4>, count: usize) -> Vec<u32> {
        (0..count).map(|index| *snapshot.get(index).unwrap()).collect()
    }

    fn set(column: &mut Column, index: usize, value: u32) {
        column.set(index, value).unwrap();
    }

    fn chunk(spine: &Spine<u32, 4>, chunk_index: usize) -> &Arc<Chunk<u32, 4>> {
        chunk_of(spine, chunk_index).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_column_reads_back_what_was_written() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
        set(&mut column, 4, 50);
        assert_eq!(
            (0..6).map(|index| *column.get(index).unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            [1, 2, 3, 4, 50, 6]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_column_holds_whole_chunks() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1, 2, 3]);
        assert_eq!(column.get(3), Some(&0));
        assert_eq!(column.get(4), None);
        assert_eq!(column.set(4, 1), None);
        assert!(column.row_mut(4).is_none());
        assert_eq!(column.publish().get(4), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn growing_fills_with_defaults() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[7]);
        column.grow_to(9);
        assert_eq!(column.get(0), Some(&7));
        assert_eq!(column.get(11), Some(&0));
        assert_eq!(column.get(12), None);
        column.grow_to(3);
        assert_eq!(column.get(11), Some(&0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_snapshot_keeps_its_generation_while_the_column_changes() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
        let first = column.publish();
        set(&mut column, 1, 20);
        column.grow_to(7);
        set(&mut column, 6, 7);
        let second = column.publish();
        set(&mut column, 5, 60);
        assert_eq!(rows(&first, 6), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
        assert_eq!(rows(&second, 7), [1, 20, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]);
        assert_eq!(rows(&column.publish(), 7), [1, 20, 3, 4, 5, 60, 7]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_write_copies_only_the_chunk_a_snapshot_shares_and_only_once() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]);
        let snapshot = column.publish();
        set(&mut column, 5, 60);
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(chunk(&column.spine, 0), chunk(&snapshot.spine, 0)));
        assert!(!Arc::ptr_eq(chunk(&column.spine, 1), chunk(&snapshot.spine, 1)));
        let copied = Arc::as_ptr(chunk(&column.spine, 1));
        set(&mut column, 6, 70);
        assert_eq!(Arc::as_ptr(chunk(&column.spine, 1)), copied);
        assert_eq!(rows(&snapshot, 8), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_snapshot_shares_the_column_and_a_write_copies_only_its_group() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1; 4 * GROUP + 4]);
        let snapshot = column.publish();
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&column.spine, &snapshot.spine));
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&snapshot.clone().spine, &snapshot.spine));
        set(&mut column, 4 * GROUP, 2);
        assert!(!Arc::ptr_eq(&column.spine, &snapshot.spine));
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&column.spine[0], &snapshot.spine[0]));
        assert!(!Arc::ptr_eq(&column.spine[1], &snapshot.spine[1]));
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(chunk(&column.spine, 1), chunk(&snapshot.spine, 1)));
        assert_eq!(snapshot.slot_capacity(), 4 * GROUP + 4);
        assert_eq!(snapshot.get(4 * GROUP), Some(&1));
        assert_eq!(column.publish().get(4 * GROUP), Some(&2));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_fork_shares_the_spine_and_each_side_copies_what_it_writes() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1; 4 * GROUP + 4]);
        let mut fork = column.clone();
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&column.spine, &fork.spine));
        assert_eq!(fork.len(), column.len());
        set(&mut fork, 0, 2);
        set(&mut column, 1, 3);
        assert_eq!((column.get(0), column.get(1)), (Some(&1), Some(&3)));
        assert_eq!((fork.get(0), fork.get(1)), (Some(&2), Some(&1)));
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(chunk(&column.spine, 1), chunk(&fork.spine, 1)));
        assert!(!Arc::ptr_eq(chunk(&column.spine, 0), chunk(&fork.spine, 0)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_fork_reads_and_grows_without_the_chunk_table() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
        let mut fork = column.clone();
        assert!(fork.chunks.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(fork.get(5), Some(&6));
        fork.grow_to(12);
        assert!(fork.chunks.is_empty());
        set(&mut fork, 9, 10);
        set(&mut column, 5, 60);
        assert_eq!((fork.get(5), fork.get(9)), (Some(&6), Some(&10)));
        assert_eq!((column.get(5), column.get(9)), (Some(&60), None));
    }

    #[test]
    fn publishing_takes_back_what_the_column_owned() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1, 2, 3, 4]);
        set(&mut column, 0, 10);
        let first = column.publish();
        set(&mut column, 0, 20);
        let second = column.publish();
        set(&mut column, 0, 30);
        assert_eq!(first.get(0), Some(&10));
        assert_eq!(second.get(0), Some(&20));
        assert_eq!(column.get(0), Some(&30));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_write_that_changes_nothing_copies_no_chunk() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]);
        let snapshot = column.publish();
        set(&mut column, 5, 6);
        *column.row_mut(6).unwrap() = 7;
        {
            let mut row = column.row_mut(4).unwrap();
            *row = 50;
            *row = 5;
        }
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(chunk(&column.spine, 1), chunk(&snapshot.spine, 1)));
        *column.row_mut(6).unwrap() += 1;
        assert!(!Arc::ptr_eq(chunk(&column.spine, 1), chunk(&snapshot.spine, 1)));
        assert_eq!(rows(&snapshot, 8), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]);
        assert_eq!(rows(&column.publish(), 8), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 8]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_row_guard_writes_in_place_once_the_column_owns_the_chunk() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1, 2, 3, 4]);
        let snapshot = column.publish();
        set(&mut column, 0, 10);
        let copied = Arc::as_ptr(chunk(&column.spine, 0));
        {
            let mut row = column.row_mut(1).unwrap();
            assert!(row.staged.is_none());
            *row = 20;
        }
        assert_eq!(Arc::as_ptr(chunk(&column.spine, 0)), copied);
        assert_eq!(rows(&snapshot, 4), [1, 2, 3, 4]);
        assert_eq!(rows(&column.publish(), 4), [10, 20, 3, 4]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_chunk_whose_snapshot_is_gone_is_written_in_place() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1, 2, 3, 4]);
        drop(column.publish());
        let in_place = Arc::as_ptr(chunk(&column.spine, 0));
        set(&mut column, 2, 30);
        assert_eq!(Arc::as_ptr(chunk(&column.spine, 0)), in_place);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_snapshot_can_be_read_on_another_thread() {
        let mut column = column_of(&[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);
        let snapshot = column.publish();
        let reader = std::thread::spawn(move || rows(&snapshot, 5));
        set(&mut column, 0, 10);
        assert_eq!(reader.join().unwrap(), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);
    }
}

/*

//! Maps and sets whose fork shares their storage.
//!
//! A [`CowMap`] keeps its entries in a hash trie behind [`Arc`]s, so cloning it costs one reference count however many
//! entries it holds. A write copies only the nodes on the way to its key that a fork still shares: at most one small node
//! a level, of which a 64-bit hash has 13. Leaves hold a few entries each, so what a node costs is spread over them. Keys
//! hash with a fixed seed, so a map and its forks agree on where a key lives.

use smallvec::SmallVec;
use std::borrow::Borrow;
use std::hash::{BuildHasher, Hash};
use std::sync::Arc;

/// How many bits of a key's hash pick a child at each level of the trie.
const BITS_PER_LEVEL: u32 = 5;
const LEVEL_MASK: u64 = (1 << BITS_PER_LEVEL) - 1;

/// How many entries a leaf holds before it splits, which is also how many a write to it copies.
const ENTRIES_PER_LEAF: usize = 8;

#[derive(Clone)]
enum Node<K, V> {
    Leaf(Vec<(K, V)>),
    /// The children of the slots set in `occupied`, in slot order.
    Branch {
        occupied: u32,
        children: Vec<Arc<Self>>,
    },
}

fn hash_of<Q: Hash + ?Sized>(key: &Q) -> u64 {
    foldhash::fast::FixedState::default().hash_one(key)
}

fn slot_of(hash: u64, shift: u32) -> u32 {
    ((hash >> shift) & LEVEL_MASK) as u32
}

fn position_of(occupied: u32, slot: u32) -> usize {
    (occupied & ((1 << slot) - 1)).count_ones() as usize
}

impl<K: Clone + Eq + Hash, V: Clone> Node<K, V> {
    /// Replaces the leaf `node` with a branch over `entries`, which were the leaf's.
    fn split_into_branch(node: &mut Arc<Self>, entries: Vec<(K, V)>, shift: u32) {
        *node = Arc::new(Self::Branch {
            occupied: 0,
            children: Vec::new(),
        });
        for (key, value) in entries {
            Self::insert(node, hash_of(&key), shift, key, value);
        }
    }

    fn insert(node: &mut Arc<Self>, hash: u64, shift: u32, key: K, value: V) -> Option<V> {
        match Arc::make_mut(node) {
            Self::Leaf(entries) => {
                if let Some((_, existing)) = entries.iter_mut().find(|(existing, _)| *existing == key) {
                    return Some(std::mem::replace(existing, value));
                }
                entries.push((key, value));
                // NB: Keys that share what is left of their hash stay together.
                if entries.len() > ENTRIES_PER_LEAF && shift + BITS_PER_LEVEL < u64::BITS {
                    let entries = std::mem::take(entries);
                    Self::split_into_branch(node, entries, shift);
                }
                None
            }
            Self::Branch { occupied, children } => {
                let slot = slot_of(hash, shift);
                let position = position_of(*occupied, slot);
                if *occupied & (1 << slot) != 0 {
                    return Self::insert(&mut children[position], hash, shift + BITS_PER_LEVEL, key, value);
                }
                *occupied |= 1 << slot;
                children.insert(position, Arc::new(Self::Leaf(vec![(key, value)])));
                None
            }
        }
    }

    fn get<'a, Q>(mut node: &'a Self, hash: u64, key: &Q) -> Option<&'a V>
    where
        K: Borrow<Q>,
        Q: Eq + ?Sized,
    {
        let mut shift = 0;
        loop {
            match node {
                Self::Leaf(entries) => {
                    return entries
                        .iter()
                        .find(|(existing, _)| existing.borrow() == key)
                        .map(|(_, value)| value);
                }
                Self::Branch { occupied, children } => {
                    let slot = slot_of(hash, shift);
                    if *occupied & (1 << slot) == 0 {
                        return None;
                    }
                    node = &children[position_of(*occupied, slot)];
                    shift += BITS_PER_LEVEL;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The value of `key`, for writing. Nodes on the way to a key the node does not hold are copied as for one it does.
    fn get_mut<'a, Q>(node: &'a mut Arc<Self>, hash: u64, shift: u32, key: &Q) -> Option<&'a mut V>
    where
        K: Borrow<Q>,
        Q: Eq + ?Sized,
    {
        match Arc::make_mut(node) {
            Self::Leaf(entries) => entries
                .iter_mut()
                .find(|(existing, _)| (*existing).borrow() == key)
                .map(|(_, value)| value),
            Self::Branch { occupied, children } => {
                let slot = slot_of(hash, shift);
                if *occupied & (1 << slot) == 0 {
                    return None;
                }
                let position = position_of(*occupied, slot);
                Self::get_mut(&mut children[position], hash, shift + BITS_PER_LEVEL, key)
            }
        }
    }

    /// The value of `key`, inserting what `make` answers where the node holds none, and whether it did.
    fn get_or_insert_with(
        node: &mut Arc<Self>,
        hash: u64,
        shift: u32,
        key: K,
        make: impl FnOnce() -> V,
    ) -> (&mut V, bool) {
        let splits = matches!(&**node, Self::Leaf(entries)
            if entries.len() >= ENTRIES_PER_LEAF
                && shift + BITS_PER_LEVEL < u64::BITS
                && !entries.iter().any(|(existing, _)| *existing == key));
        if splits {
            let Self::Leaf(entries) = Arc::make_mut(node) else {
                unreachable!("the node was just found to be a leaf");
            };
            let entries = std::mem::take(entries);
            Self::split_into_branch(node, entries, shift);
        }
        match Arc::make_mut(node) {
            Self::Leaf(entries) => match entries.iter().position(|(existing, _)| *existing == key) {
                Some(index) => (&mut entries[index].1, false),
                None => {
                    entries.push((key, make()));
                    (&mut entries.last_mut().expect("an entry was just pushed").1, true)
                }
            },
            Self::Branch { occupied, children } => {
                let slot = slot_of(hash, shift);
                let position = position_of(*occupied, slot);
                if *occupied & (1 << slot) == 0 {
                    *occupied |= 1 << slot;
                    children.insert(position, Arc::new(Self::Leaf(Vec::new())));
                }
                Self::get_or_insert_with(&mut children[position], hash, shift + BITS_PER_LEVEL, key, make)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Removes `key`, which the node must hold, answering its value.
    fn remove<Q>(node: &mut Arc<Self>, hash: u64, shift: u32, key: &Q) -> Option<V>
    where
        K: Borrow<Q>,
        Q: Eq + ?Sized,
    {
        match Arc::make_mut(node) {
            Self::Leaf(entries) => {
                let index = entries.iter().position(|(existing, _)| existing.borrow() == key)?;
                Some(entries.remove(index).1)
            }
            Self::Branch { occupied, children } => {
                let slot = slot_of(hash, shift);
                let position = position_of(*occupied, slot);
                let removed = Self::remove(&mut children[position], hash, shift + BITS_PER_LEVEL, key);
                if children[position].is_empty() {
                    children.remove(position);
                    *occupied &= !(1 << slot);
                }
                removed
            }
        }
    }

    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::Leaf(entries) => entries.is_empty(),
            Self::Branch { children, .. } => children.is_empty(),
        }
    }

    fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        crate::heap_size::ARC_HEADER_BYTES
            + size_of::<Self>()
            + match self {
                Self::Leaf(entries) => entries.capacity() * size_of::<(K, V)>(),
                Self::Branch { children, .. } => {
                    children.capacity() * size_of::<Arc<Self>>()
                        + children.iter().map(|child| child.heap_size()).sum::<usize>()
                }
            }
    }
}

/// A hash map whose clone shares its storage. See the [module documentation](self).
pub(crate) struct CowMap<K, V> {
    root: Option<Arc<Node<K, V>>>,
    len: usize,
}

impl<K, V> Default for CowMap<K, V> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { root: None, len: 0 }
    }
}

impl<K, V> Clone for CowMap<K, V> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            root: self.root.clone(),
            len: self.len,
        }
    }
}

impl<K: Clone + Eq + Hash, V: Clone> CowMap<K, V> {
    pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.len
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.len == 0
    }

    /// The bytes of the trie, whose entries hold nothing else on the heap.
    pub(crate) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.root.as_ref().map_or(0, |root| root.heap_size())
    }

    pub(crate) fn clear(&mut self) {
        *self = Self::default();
    }

    pub(crate) fn get<Q>(&self, key: &Q) -> Option<&V>
    where
        K: Borrow<Q>,
        Q: Eq + Hash + ?Sized,
    {
        Node::get(self.root.as_deref()?, hash_of(key), key)
    }

    pub(crate) fn contains_key<Q>(&self, key: &Q) -> bool
    where
        K: Borrow<Q>,
        Q: Eq + Hash + ?Sized,
    {
        self.get(key).is_some()
    }

    /// The value of `key`, for writing, copying what a fork shares on the way to it.
    pub(crate) fn get_mut<Q>(&mut self, key: &Q) -> Option<&mut V>
    where
        K: Borrow<Q>,
        Q: Eq + Hash + ?Sized,
    {
        Node::get_mut(self.root.as_mut()?, hash_of(key), 0, key)
    }

    pub(crate) fn insert(&mut self, key: K, value: V) -> Option<V> {
        let hash = hash_of(&key);
        let Some(root) = &mut self.root else {
            self.root = Some(Arc::new(Node::Leaf(vec![(key, value)])));
            self.len = 1;
            return None;
        };
        let previous = Node::insert(root, hash, 0, key, value);
        self.len += usize::from(previous.is_none());
        previous
    }

    pub(crate) fn remove<Q>(&mut self, key: &Q) -> Option<V>
    where
        K: Borrow<Q>,
        Q: Eq + Hash + ?Sized,
    {
        let hash = hash_of(key);
        let root = self.root.as_mut()?;
        Node::get(root.as_ref(), hash, key)?;
        let removed = Node::remove(root, hash, 0, key);
        self.len -= 1;
        if root.is_empty() {
            self.root = None;
        }
        removed
    }

    /// The value of `key`, inserting what `make` answers where the map holds none.
    pub(crate) fn get_or_insert_with(&mut self, key: K, make: impl FnOnce() -> V) -> &mut V {
        let hash = hash_of(&key);
        let root = self.root.get_or_insert_with(|| Arc::new(Node::Leaf(Vec::new())));
        let (value, inserted) = Node::get_or_insert_with(root, hash, 0, key, make);
        self.len += usize::from(inserted);
        value
    }

    pub(crate) fn entry(&mut self, key: K) -> Entry<'_, K, V> {
        Entry { map: self, key }
    }

    /// Every entry, in no particular order.
    pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&K, &V)> {
        let mut stack: SmallVec<[&Node<K, V>; 16]> = self.root.as_deref().into_iter().collect();
        let mut entries: std::slice::Iter<'_, (K, V)> = [].iter();
        std::iter::from_fn(move || {
            loop {
                if let Some((key, value)) = entries.next() {
                    return Some((key, value));
                }
                match stack.pop()? {
                    Node::Leaf(leaf) => entries = leaf.iter(),
                    Node::Branch { children, .. } => stack.extend(children.iter().map(|child| &**child)),
                }
            }
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn keys(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &K> {
        self.iter().map(|(key, _)| key)
    }

    pub(crate) fn values(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &V> {
        self.iter().map(|(_, value)| value)
    }

    /// Keeps the entries `keep` answers true for.
    pub(crate) fn retain(&mut self, mut keep: impl FnMut(&K, &V) -> bool) {
        let gone: Vec<K> = self
            .iter()
            .filter(|(key, value)| !keep(key, value))
            .map(|(key, _)| key.clone())
            .collect();
        for key in &gone {
            self.remove(key);
        }
    }
}

/// A key of a [`CowMap`], and what it holds, for writing.
pub(crate) struct Entry<'a, K, V> {
    map: &'a mut CowMap<K, V>,
    key: K,
}

impl<'a, K: Clone + Eq + Hash, V: Clone> Entry<'a, K, V> {
    pub(crate) fn or_insert_with(self, make: impl FnOnce() -> V) -> &'a mut V {
        self.map.get_or_insert_with(self.key, make)
    }

    pub(crate) fn or_default(self) -> &'a mut V
    where
        V: Default,
    {
        self.or_insert_with(V::default)
    }
}

impl<K: Clone + Eq + Hash, V: Clone> std::ops::Index<&K> for CowMap<K, V> {
    type Output = V;

    fn index(&self, key: &K) -> &V {
        self.get(key).expect("the map holds the key")
    }
}

impl<K: Clone + Eq + Hash, V: Clone> Extend<(K, V)> for CowMap<K, V> {
    fn extend<I: IntoIterator<Item = (K, V)>>(&mut self, entries: I) {
        for (key, value) in entries {
            self.insert(key, value);
        }
    }
}

/// A hash set whose clone shares its storage. See the [module documentation](self).
pub(crate) struct CowSet<T>(CowMap<T, ()>);

impl<T> Default for CowSet<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self(CowMap::default())
    }
}

impl<T> Clone for CowSet<T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self(self.0.clone())
    }
}

impl<T: Clone + Eq + Hash> CowSet<T> {
    /// The bytes of the trie, whose values hold nothing else on the heap.
    pub(crate) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.0.heap_size()
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.0.is_empty()
    }

    pub(crate) fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.0.clear();
    }

    pub(crate) fn contains<Q>(&self, value: &Q) -> bool
    where
        T: Borrow<Q>,
        Q: Eq + Hash + ?Sized,
    {
        self.0.contains_key(value)
    }

    /// Answers whether the set did not hold `value` yet.
    pub(crate) fn insert(&mut self, value: T) -> bool {
        self.0.insert(value, ()).is_none()
    }

    /// Answers whether the set held `value`.
    pub(crate) fn remove<Q>(&mut self, value: &Q) -> bool
    where
        T: Borrow<Q>,
        Q: Eq + Hash + ?Sized,
    {
        self.0.remove(value).is_some()
    }

    /// Every value, in no particular order.
    pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &T> {
        self.0.keys()
    }
}

const _: () = {
    const fn assert_send_and_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
    assert_send_and_sync::<CowMap<u64, u64>>();
    assert_send_and_sync::<CowSet<u64>>();
};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    /// A key whose hash is always the same, so that every entry lands in one leaf.
    #[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    struct Colliding(u32);

    impl Hash for Colliding {
        fn hash<H: std::hash::Hasher>(&self, state: &mut H) {
            0u32.hash(state);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_map_acts_as_a_hash_map_through_many_writes() {
        let mut map = CowMap::default();
        let mut expected = HashMap::new();
        let mut state = 1u64;
        for _ in 0..50_000 {
            state = state
                .wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005)
                .wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);
            let key = (state >> 40) % 3000;
            match state >> 62 {
                0 => assert_eq!(map.remove(&key), expected.remove(&key)),
                1 => assert_eq!(map.get(&key), expected.get(&key)),
                _ => assert_eq!(map.insert(key, state), expected.insert(key, state)),
            }
            assert_eq!(map.len(), expected.len());
        }
        let mut entries: Vec<_> = map.iter().map(|(&key, &value)| (key, value)).collect();
        let mut expected: Vec<_> = expected.into_iter().collect();
        entries.sort_unstable();
        expected.sort_unstable();
        assert_eq!(entries, expected);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_fork_shares_the_root_and_neither_side_sees_the_others_writes() {
        let mut map = CowMap::default();
        for key in 0..1000u32 {
            map.insert(key, key);
        }
        let mut fork = map.clone();
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(map.root.as_ref().unwrap(), fork.root.as_ref().unwrap()));
        *fork.get_mut(&1).unwrap() = 100;
        fork.remove(&2);
        map.insert(1000, 1000);
        map.remove(&3);
        assert_eq!(
            (map.get(&1), map.get(&2), map.get(&3), map.get(&1000)),
            (Some(&1), Some(&2), None, Some(&1000))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            (fork.get(&1), fork.get(&2), fork.get(&3), fork.get(&1000)),
            (Some(&100), None, Some(&3), None)
        );
        assert_eq!((map.len(), fork.len()), (1000, 999));
    }

    #[test]
    fn keys_of_one_hash_share_a_leaf() {
        let mut map = CowMap::default();
        for key in 0..2 * ENTRIES_PER_LEAF as u32 {
            map.insert(Colliding(key), key);
        }
        assert_eq!(map.get(&Colliding(5)), Some(&5));
        assert_eq!(map.remove(&Colliding(5)), Some(5));
        assert_eq!(map.get(&Colliding(5)), None);
        assert_eq!(map.iter().count(), 2 * ENTRIES_PER_LEAF - 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn removing_every_entry_empties_the_map() {
        let mut map = CowMap::default();
        for key in 0..100u32 {
            map.insert(key, ());
        }
        for key in 0..100u32 {
            map.remove(&key);
        }
        assert!(map.is_empty());
        assert!(map.root.is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_set_answers_as_a_hash_set_does() {
        let mut set = CowSet::default();
        assert!(set.insert(1));
        assert!(!set.insert(1));
        assert!(set.contains(&1));
        assert!(set.remove(&1));
        assert!(!set.remove(&1));
        assert_eq!(set.iter().count(), 0);
    }
}

//! Native absolutization of style values.
//!
//! Mirrors the C++ `StyleValue::absolutized(ComputationContext const&)` dispatch: structural
//! values recurse into their children and rebuild only when a child changed, dimensions convert
//! to their canonical units, and lengths resolve through the shared length-resolution context.
//! Preserving identity for unchanged values is a real contract: the store batch reuses wrappers
//! and shared allocations based on pointer equality.

// Style value data allocations are thread-confined, like style_value.rs.

use crate::css::style_value::{
    BackgroundSizePayload, BorderImageSlicePayload, BorderRadiusPayload, BorderRadiusRectPayload, ColorFunctionPayload,
    ColorMixPayload, ConicGradientPayload, ContentPayload, CounterDefinitionsPayload, CounterStyleSystemPayload,
    CursorPayload, EasingPayload, FunctionPayload, GridTrackPlacementPayload, GridTrackSizeListPayload, ImagePayload,
    ImageSetPayload, LightDarkPayload, LinearGradientPayload, OpenTypeTaggedPayload, PositionPayload,
    RadialGradientPayload, RadialSizePayload, RandomValueSharingPayload, RatioPayload, RayPayload, RectPayload,
    ScrollbarColorPayload, ShadowPayload, StyleValueBox, TransformationPayload, UrlPayload,
};
use crate::css::style_value_arc::StyleValueArc;
use std::cell::Cell;

#[cfg(test)]
mod grid_tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::css::css_tokenizer::{TokenizerInput, tokenize_for_parser};
    use crate::css::parser::component_value::consume_a_list_of_component_values;
    use crate::css::parser::value_parser::{ParseContext, ParseOutcome, parse_css_value};
    use crate::css::property_metadata::property_id;

    /// Absolutizes against a zeroed length context, handing back the value itself when it is
    /// unchanged.
    fn absolutize_for_test(value: &StyleValueData) -> StyleValueArc {
        // All fields are scalars or nullable pointers.
        let length = FfiLengthResolutionContext::default();
        let context = AbsolutizationContext {
            length: &length,
            scheme: None,
            resolved_viewport_relative_length: Cell::new(false),
            tree_counting: None,
            random_base_values: &[],
            document_base_url: &[],
            style_sheet_resource_context: None,
            current_color: None,
        };
        match absolutize(value, &context).unwrap() {
            Absolutized::Unchanged => unsafe {
                StyleValueArc::increment_strong_count(value);
                StyleValueArc::from_raw(value)
            },
            Absolutized::Changed(value) => value.into_arc(),
        }
    }

    fn parse(property: u16, source: &str) -> StyleValueArc {
        let units: Vec<_> = source.encode_utf16().collect();
        let values = consume_a_list_of_component_values(tokenize_for_parser(TokenizerInput::Utf16(&units))).unwrap();
        // All fields are scalars or nullable pointers.
        let context = ParseContext::default();
        let ParseOutcome::Parsed(value) = parse_css_value(&context, property, &values) else {
            panic!("invalid test value");
        };
        value
    }

    #[test]
    fn composite_resolution_preserves_shared_shapes_and_easing() {
        for (property, source) in [
            (property_id::CLIP_PATH, "inset(1px round 2px)"),
            (property_id::CLIP_PATH, "circle(2px at 25% 75%)"),
            (property_id::CLIP_PATH, "ellipse(2px 3px)"),
            (property_id::CLIP_PATH, "polygon(1px 2px, 3px 4px, 5px 6px)"),
            (property_id::D, "path(\"M0 0 L30 40\")"),
            (property_id::ANIMATION_TIMING_FUNCTION, "linear(0 0%, 1 50%)"),
            (property_id::ANIMATION_TIMING_FUNCTION, "cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"),
            (property_id::ANIMATION_TIMING_FUNCTION, "steps(4, jump-start)"),
        ] {
            let parsed = parse(property, source);
            let value = match &*parsed {
                StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. } => values.as_slice()[0].data(),
                value => value,
            };
            let same = absolutize_for_test(value);
            assert!(std::ptr::eq(value, &*same));
            let mut children = Vec::new();
            let mut retain_child = |child: &RetainedStyleValueData, _: &mut bool| {
                if child.optional_data().is_some() {
                    children.push((
                        child.clone(),
                        crate::css::serialize::serialize_style_value_to_utf16(child.data()),
                    ));
                }
                Some(child.clone())
            };
            match value {
                StyleValueData::BasicShape { .. } => {
                    absolutize_basic_shape(value, &mut retain_child).unwrap();
                }
                StyleValueData::Easing { .. } => {
                    absolutize_easing(value, &mut retain_child).unwrap();
                }
                _ => unreachable!(),
            }
            drop(same);
            drop(parsed);
            for (child, expected) in children {
                assert_eq!(
                    crate::css::serialize::serialize_style_value_to_utf16(child.data()),
                    expected
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn composite_resolution_resolves_contrast_color() {
        let parsed = parse(property_id::COLOR, "contrast-color(red)");
        let resolved = absolutize_for_test(&parsed);
        assert!(matches!(&*resolved, StyleValueData::ColorFunction { .. }));
        assert_eq!(
            to_color(&resolved, &EMPTY_INPUT),
            Some(crate::css::color_resolution::Rgba::BLACK)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn composite_resolution_canonicalizes_linear_easing_control_points() {
        let parsed = parse(property_id::ANIMATION_TIMING_FUNCTION, "linear(0, 0.25, 0.5 60%, 1)");
        let StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. } = &*parsed else {
            unreachable!();
        };
        let resolved = absolutize_for_test(values.as_slice()[0].data());
        let StyleValueData::Easing(easing_payload) = &*resolved else {
            unreachable!();
        };
        let EasingPayload { linear_stops, .. } = &**easing_payload;
        let inputs = linear_stops
            .as_slice()
            .iter()
            .map(|stop| {
                let StyleValueData::Percentage { value } = stop.input().data() else {
                    unreachable!();
                };
                *value
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        assert_eq!(inputs, [0.0, 30.0, 60.0, 100.0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn grid_leaf_resolution_preserves_identity_and_retained_children() {
        for (property, source) in [
            (property_id::GRID_ROW_START, "3"),
            (
                property_id::GRID_TEMPLATE_COLUMNS,
                "[雪] repeat(2, minmax(10px, 1fr)) [雨]",
            ),
        ] {
            let value = parse(property, source);
            let original = crate::css::serialize::serialize_style_value_to_utf16(&value);
            let same = absolutize_for_test(&value);
            assert!(StyleValueArc::ptr_eq(&value, &same));
            let mut retained = Vec::new();
            let mapped = map_grid_values(&value, &mut |child| {
                if child.optional_data().is_some() {
                    retained.push(child.clone());
                }
                Some(child.clone())
            })
            .unwrap();
            drop(value);
            drop(same);
            assert!(!retained.is_empty());
            assert_eq!(crate::css::serialize::serialize_style_value_to_utf16(&mapped), original);
            drop(mapped);
            for child in retained {
                crate::css::serialize::serialize_style_value_to_utf16(child.data());
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn grid_leaf_resolution_rebuilds_nested_tracks_without_changing_the_source() {
        let value = parse(
            property_id::GRID_TEMPLATE_COLUMNS,
            "[雪] repeat(2, minmax(10px, 1fr)) [雨]",
        );
        let resolved = StyleValueArc::new(
            map_grid_values(&value, &mut |child| {
                Some(match child.optional_data() {
                    Some(StyleValueData::Length { value, unit }) => retain_new(StyleValueData::Length {
                        value: value * 2.0,
                        unit: *unit,
                    }),
                    _ => child.clone(),
                })
            })
            .unwrap(),
        );
        assert!(!StyleValueArc::ptr_eq(&value, &resolved));
        for (value, expected) in [
            (&value, "[雪] repeat(2, minmax(10px, 1fr)) [雨]"),
            (&resolved, "[雪] repeat(2, minmax(20px, 1fr)) [雨]"),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(
                crate::css::serialize::serialize_style_value_to_utf16(value),
                expected.encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>()
            );
        }
    }
}

use crate::css::color_resolution::{
    ColorResolutionInput, EMPTY_INPUT, PREFERRED_COLOR_SCHEME_DARK, RECTANGULAR_COLOR_SPACE_OKLAB,
    calculate_a_color_mix, descriptor_for_color_type, percentage_from_style_value, resolve_alpha, resolve_hue,

pub(crate) struct AbsolutizationContext<'a> {
    pub(crate) length: &'a FfiLengthResolutionContext,
    /// The used color scheme, present exactly when the C++ computation context carries one:
    /// only the generic context kind sets it. PreferredColorScheme codes; Dark is 1.
    pub(crate) scheme: Option<u8>,
    /// Set when a viewport-relative length resolved, mirroring the C++ tracking flag.
    pub(crate) resolved_viewport_relative_length: Cell<bool>,
    /// Immutable sibling facts supplied only when a winning cascaded value uses a
    /// tree-counting function.
    pub(crate) tree_counting: Option<(u64, u64)>,
    /// Random base values captured before entering the longhand drive.
    pub(crate) random_base_values: &'a [crate::css::style_compute::FfiRandomBaseValue],
    /// The document base URL captured before entering the longhand drive.
    pub(crate) document_base_url: &'a [u8],
    /// The stylesheet resource context for the selected cascade source, if any.
    pub(crate) style_sheet_resource_context: Option<StyleSheetResourceContext<'a>>,
    /// The computed value `currentcolor` names while the value computes, which only the `color` property knows: its
    /// inherited value. Elsewhere `currentcolor` names the element's own color, which the computed value keeps
    /// unresolved until it is used.
    pub(crate) current_color: Option<&'a StyleValueData>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct StyleSheetResourceContext<'a> {
    pub(crate) base_url: &'a [u8],
    pub(crate) origin_clean: bool,
}

/// The outcome for one value: unchanged (preserve identity) or a new allocation.
pub(crate) enum Absolutized {
    Unchanged,
    Changed(RetainedStyleValueData),
}

fn retain_new(value: StyleValueData) -> RetainedStyleValueData {
    RetainedStyleValueData::from_arc(StyleValueArc::new(value))
}

/// Absolutizes one retained child slot. Returns the child for the rebuilt parent, whether any
/// change happened, or None when the child's absolutization declined. Null children stay null.
fn absolutize_child(
    child: &RetainedStyleValueData,
    context: &AbsolutizationContext,
    any_changed: &mut bool,
) -> Option<RetainedStyleValueData> {
    let Some(data) = child.optional_data() else {
        return Some(child.clone_retained());
    };
    match absolutize(data, context)? {
        Absolutized::Unchanged => Some(child.clone_retained()),
        Absolutized::Changed(new_child) => {
            *any_changed = true;
            Some(new_child)
        }
    }
}

fn absolutize_list(
    values: &RetainedStyleValueDataList,
    context: &AbsolutizationContext,
    any_changed: &mut bool,
) -> Option<Vec<RetainedStyleValueData>> {
    values
        .as_slice()
        .iter()
        .map(|child| absolutize_child(child, context, any_changed))
        .collect()
}

/// The absolutized children of a list, or none where every child is unchanged, allocating only once
/// one changes.
fn absolutize_list_if_changed(
    values: &RetainedStyleValueDataList,
    context: &AbsolutizationContext,
) -> Option<Option<Vec<RetainedStyleValueData>>> {
    let values = values.as_slice();
    let mut changed: Option<Vec<RetainedStyleValueData>> = None;
    for (index, child) in values.iter().enumerate() {
        let absolutized = match child.optional_data() {
            Some(data) => absolutize(data, context)?,
            None => Absolutized::Unchanged,
        };
        match (absolutized, &mut changed) {
            (Absolutized::Unchanged, None) => {}
            (Absolutized::Unchanged, Some(changed)) => changed.push(child.clone_retained()),
            (Absolutized::Changed(new_child), Some(changed)) => changed.push(new_child),
            (Absolutized::Changed(new_child), None) => {
                let mut list = Vec::with_capacity(values.len());
                list.extend(values[..index].iter().map(RetainedStyleValueData::clone_retained));
                list.push(new_child);
                changed = Some(list);
            }
        }
    }
    Some(changed)
}

fn zero_px_length() -> StyleValueData {
    StyleValueData::Length {
        value: 0.0,
        unit: crate::css::style_compute::px_length_unit(),
    }
}

fn currentcolor_keyword() -> StyleValueData {
    StyleValueData::Keyword {
        keyword: keyword::CURRENTCOLOR,
    }
}

// ColorStyleValue.h: ColorSyntax::Legacy = 0, Modern = 1.

fn retained_null() -> RetainedStyleValueData {
    RetainedStyleValueData::none()
}

fn absolutize_image(value: &StyleValueData, context: &AbsolutizationContext) -> Option<Absolutized> {
    let StyleValueData::Image(image_payload) = value else {
        return None;
    };
    let ImagePayload {
        url,
        url_type,
        url_modifiers,
        resource_context,
    } = &**image_payload;
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#local-urls
    // When serializing a url() with the local url flag set, it must serialize as just the fragment.
    if url.is_empty() || url.is_fragment() {
        return Some(Absolutized::Unchanged);
    }

    let base_url = context
        .style_sheet_resource_context
        .map(|resource_context| resource_context.base_url)
        .filter(|base_url| !base_url.is_empty())
        .or_else(|| {
            resource_context
                .has_base_url
                .then(|| resource_context.base_url.ascii_bytes())
        })
        .unwrap_or(context.document_base_url);
    if base_url.is_empty() {
        return Some(Absolutized::Unchanged);
    }

    let url_string = url.url_input();
    let should_absolutize_url_for_computed_value =
        context.style_sheet_resource_context.is_some() || resource_context.should_absolutize_url_for_computed_value;
    let absolutized_url = if should_absolutize_url_for_computed_value {
        if liburl_rust::basic_parse(url_string, liburl_rust::BasicParseOptions::new()).is_some() {
            url.clone()
        } else {
            let base_url = std::str::from_utf8(base_url).ok()?;
            let base_url = liburl_rust::basic_parse(base_url, liburl_rust::BasicParseOptions::new())?;
            let resolved_url =
                liburl_rust::basic_parse(url_string, liburl_rust::BasicParseOptions::new().base_url(&base_url));
            let Some(resolved_url) = resolved_url else {
                return Some(Absolutized::Unchanged);
            };
            crate::css::style_value::RetainedString::from_ascii(resolved_url.into())
        }
    } else {
        url.clone()
    };
    let base_url = std::str::from_utf8(base_url).ok()?;
    let base_url = crate::css::style_value::RetainedString::from_ascii(base_url.to_owned());

    let (has_parent_style_sheet_origin_clean, parent_style_sheet_origin_clean) = context
        .style_sheet_resource_context
        .map(|context| (true, context.origin_clean))
        .unwrap_or((
            resource_context.has_parent_style_sheet_origin_clean,
            resource_context.parent_style_sheet_origin_clean,
        ));

    Some(Absolutized::Changed(retain_new(StyleValueData::Image(
        StyleValueBox::new(ImagePayload {
            url: absolutized_url,
            url_type: *url_type,
            url_modifiers: url_modifiers.clone(),
            resource_context: crate::css::style_value::ImageResourceContext {
                base_url,
                has_base_url: true,
                has_parent_style_sheet_origin_clean,
                parent_style_sheet_origin_clean,
                should_absolutize_url_for_computed_value,
            },
        }),
    ))))
}

/// The color-resolution input the C++ absolutizers build from a computation context: the
/// context's color scheme and calculation inputs, the currentcolor it knows of, and no channels.
fn color_resolution_input<'a>(context: &'a AbsolutizationContext) -> ColorResolutionInput<'a> {
    let mut input = ColorResolutionInput {
        scheme: context.scheme,
        current_color: None,
        current_color_value: None,
        length: Some(context.length),
        channels: None,
    };
    if let Some(current_color) = context.current_color {
        input.current_color = to_color(current_color, &input);
        input.current_color_value = Some(current_color);
    }
    input
}

/// The rgb() function form ColorFunctionStyleValue::create builds for an already-resolved
/// color: number channels, a number alpha, no name and no origin.
fn rgb_color_function(r: f64, g: f64, b: f64, alpha: f64, color_syntax: u8) -> StyleValueData {
    StyleValueData::ColorFunction(StyleValueBox::new(ColorFunctionPayload {
        color_base: ColorBase {
            has_color_type: true,
            color_type: crate::css::color_conversion::RGB,
            color_syntax,
        },
        channel_0: RetainedStyleValueData::from_owned(StyleValueData::Number { value: r }),
        channel_1: RetainedStyleValueData::from_owned(StyleValueData::Number { value: g }),
        channel_2: RetainedStyleValueData::from_owned(StyleValueData::Number { value: b }),
        alpha: RetainedStyleValueData::from_owned(StyleValueData::Number { value: alpha }),
        has_name: false,
        name: CssString::none(),
        origin_color: retained_null(),
    }))
}

/// The canonical computed form of a fully-resolved legacy sRGB color.
fn canonical_legacy_rgb(value: &StyleValueData) -> Option<StyleValueData> {
    let rgba = crate::css::color_resolution::to_color(value, &EMPTY_INPUT)?;
    Some(rgb_color_function(
        f64::from(rgba.r),
        f64::from(rgba.g),
        f64::from(rgba.b),
        f64::from(rgba.a) / 255.0,
        COLOR_SYNTAX_LEGACY,
    ))
}

/// Whether `value` is the canonical computed form of a fully-resolved opaque legacy sRGB color, which
/// computes to itself.
pub(crate) fn color_function_is_canonical_legacy_rgb(value: &StyleValueData) -> bool {
    let StyleValueData::ColorFunction(color_function) = value else {
        return false;
    };
    let channel_is_a_byte = |channel: &RetainedStyleValueData| {
        matches!(channel.optional_data(), Some(StyleValueData::Number { value })
            if (0.0..=255.0).contains(value) && value.fract() == 0.0)
    };
    color_function.color_base.has_color_type
        && color_function.color_base.color_type == crate::css::color_conversion::RGB
        && color_function.color_base.color_syntax == COLOR_SYNTAX_LEGACY
        && !color_function.has_name
        && color_function.origin_color.optional_data().is_none()
        && channel_is_a_byte(&color_function.channel_0)
        && channel_is_a_byte(&color_function.channel_1)
        && channel_is_a_byte(&color_function.channel_2)
        && matches!(color_function.alpha.optional_data(), Some(StyleValueData::Number { value }) if *value == 1.0)
}

/// Port of hsl_to_absolutized_rgb() in ColorFunctionStyleValue.cpp.
// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/#hsl-to-rgb
fn hsl_to_absolutized_rgb(
    hue_degrees: f64,
    saturation_0_100: f64,
    lightness_0_100: f64,
    alpha_0_1: f64,
) -> StyleValueData {
    let mut hue = hue_degrees % 360.0;
    if hue < 0.0 {
        hue += 360.0;
    }
    let saturation = (saturation_0_100 / 100.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
    let lightness = (lightness_0_100 / 100.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0);

    let to_rgb = |offset: f64| {
        let k = (offset + hue / 30.0) % 12.0;
        let a = saturation * lightness.min(1.0 - lightness);
        lightness - a * (-1.0f64).max((k - 3.0).min(9.0 - k).min(1.0))
    };

    let r = to_rgb(0.0);
    let g = to_rgb(8.0);
    let b = to_rgb(4.0);

    rgb_color_function(
        (r * 255.0).clamp(0.0, 255.0),
        (g * 255.0).clamp(0.0, 255.0),
        (b * 255.0).clamp(0.0, 255.0),
        alpha_0_1.clamp(0.0, 1.0),
        COLOR_SYNTAX_LEGACY,
    )
}

/// Port of hwb_to_absolutized_rgb() in ColorFunctionStyleValue.cpp, including its
/// single-precision arithmetic.
// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/#hwb-to-rgb
fn hwb_to_absolutized_rgb(
    hue_degrees: f64,
    whiteness_0_100: f64,
    blackness_0_100: f64,
    alpha_0_1: f64,
) -> StyleValueData {
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/#the-hwb-notation
    // Values outside of these ranges are not invalid; hue angles outside the range [0,360) will be normalized to
    // that range and values of white and black which sum to 100% or greater will produce achromatic colors as
    // described below.
    // NB: The handling of negative white or black is unspecified, so they are clamped to 0%.
    let whiteness = (whiteness_0_100 / 100.0).max(0.0) as f32;
    let blackness = (blackness_0_100 / 100.0).max(0.0) as f32;

    if whiteness + blackness >= 1.0 {
        // The gray channel value is shared across the three slots, like the C++ code.
        let gray = retain_new(StyleValueData::Number {
            value: f64::from((whiteness / (whiteness + blackness) * 255.0).clamp(0.0, 255.0)),
        });
        return StyleValueData::ColorFunction(StyleValueBox::new(ColorFunctionPayload {
            color_base: ColorBase {
                has_color_type: true,
                color_type: crate::css::color_conversion::RGB,
                color_syntax: COLOR_SYNTAX_LEGACY,
            },
            channel_0: gray.clone_retained(),
            channel_1: gray.clone_retained(),
            channel_2: gray,
            alpha: retain_new(StyleValueData::Number {
                value: alpha_0_1.clamp(0.0, 1.0),
            }),
            has_name: false,
            name: CssString::none(),
            origin_color: retained_null(),
        }));
    }

    let mut hue = (hue_degrees as f32) % 360.0;
    if hue < 0.0 {
        hue += 360.0;
    }

    let hue_to_rgb = |offset: f32| {
        let k = (offset + hue / 30.0) % 12.0;
