/// A resolved color handed back to C++; `resolved` is false when the value names no color.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiResolvedColorValue {
    pub resolved: bool,
    pub rgba: [u8; 4],
}

/// Resolves a parsed style value to an sRGB color against a style record of `host`'s document, as the record
/// computes its own values: its used color-scheme and `color`, and its lengths. A null record names no style.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_style_value_to_color_against_style_record(
    host: &crate::render_state::DocumentHost,
    read: &crate::render_state::BegunRead,
    style_record: u64,
    value: &crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData,
) -> FfiResolvedColorValue {
    let color = crate::css::style::engine_calls::with_engine(read, host, |engine| {
        engine.color_against_style_record(style_record, value)
    });
    match color {
        Some(color) => FfiResolvedColorValue {
            resolved: true,
            rgba: [color.r, color.g, color.b, color.a],
        },
        None => FfiResolvedColorValue {
            resolved: false,
            rgba: [0; 4],
        },
    }
}

/// Resolves an absolutized style value to an sRGB color against a style, or declines.
///
/// # Safety
/// `style` must be null or point at a style whose group payloads outlive the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_style_value_to_color(
    value: &crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData,
    style: *const FfiColorResolutionStyle,
) -> FfiResolvedColorValue {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let resolution_input = unsafe { ColorResolutionInput::for_ffi_style(style) };
    match to_color(value, &resolution_input) {
        Some(color) => FfiResolvedColorValue {
            resolved: true,
            rgba: [color.r, color.g, color.b, color.a],
        },
        None => FfiResolvedColorValue {
            resolved: false,
            rgba: [0; 4],
        },
    }
}

#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiResolvedColorComponents {
    pub resolved: bool,
    pub components: [f32; 4],
}

/// Resolves a parsed style value to a used color against a style, converted to the color space of
/// `target_color_type` (a ColorStyleValue::ColorType), or declines. Unlike rust_style_value_to_color(), the
/// components keep their full precision and range, with missing components as 0.
///
/// # Safety
/// `style` must be null or point at a style whose group payloads outlive the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_style_value_to_color_components(
    value: &StyleValueData,
    style: *const FfiColorResolutionStyle,
    target_color_type: u8,
) -> FfiResolvedColorComponents {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let resolution_input = unsafe { ColorResolutionInput::for_ffi_style(style) };
    let components = resolve_color_for_interpolation(value, &resolution_input)
        .and_then(|resolved| color_conversion::convert(resolved.color_type, target_color_type, resolved.components));
    match components {
        Some(components) => FfiResolvedColorComponents {
            resolved: true,
            components,
        },
        None => FfiResolvedColorComponents {
            resolved: false,
            components: [0.0; 4],
        },
    }
}

//! What a style records beside its longhand values: whether each was important, inherited or
//! evaluated, the dependency flags, the metadata the host settles beside them, and the recorded
//! specified values helpers.

use std::ffi::c_void;

use crate::css::property_metadata::{FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID, LAST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID, property_is_inherited};
use crate::css::style_value::{RetainedStyleValueData, StyleValueData};

pub(crate) const LONGHAND_COUNT: usize = (LAST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID - FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID + 1) as usize;

pub(crate) fn is_current_color_keyword(value: &StyleValueData) -> bool {
    matches!(value, StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword } if *keyword == crate::css::style_compute::keyword::CURRENTCOLOR)
}

pub(crate) const LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES: usize = LONGHAND_COUNT.div_ceil(8);

/// The effective value of one longhand: the value data pointer together with
/// which source produced it, so the C++ side can preserve wrapper identity
/// for overlay values and stamp style sheet context only onto table mints.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiEffectiveLonghandValue {
    pub value: *const c_void,
    pub source: u8,
}

pub const EFFECTIVE_LONGHAND_SOURCE_TABLE: u8 = 0;
pub const EFFECTIVE_LONGHAND_SOURCE_OVERLAY: u8 = 1;
pub const EFFECTIVE_LONGHAND_SOURCE_SPECIFIED: u8 = 2;

/// The longhands that inherit by default, by slot.
const INHERITED_LONGHAND_BITS: [u8; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES] = {
    use crate::css::property_metadata::{FIRST_INHERITED_PROPERTY_ID, LAST_INHERITED_PROPERTY_ID};
    let mut bits = [0; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES];
    let mut property = FIRST_INHERITED_PROPERTY_ID;
    while property <= LAST_INHERITED_PROPERTY_ID {
        let index = (property - FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID) as usize;
        bits[index / 8] |= 1 << (index % 8);
        property += 1;
    }
    bits
};

/// The bit of `property_id` in a bitmap of longhands.
fn slot_index(property_id: u16) -> usize {
    assert!(
        (FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID..=LAST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID).contains(&property_id),
        "longhand bitmap indices are longhand property identifiers"
    );
    (property_id - FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID) as usize
}

fn bitmap_bit(bits: &[u8; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES], index: usize) -> bool {
    bits[index / 8] & (1 << (index % 8)) != 0
}

fn set_bitmap_bit(bits: &mut [u8; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES], index: usize, value: bool) {
    if value {
        bits[index / 8] |= 1 << (index % 8);
    } else {
        bits[index / 8] &= !(1 << (index % 8));
    }
}

/// What a longhand table publishes beside its values, its recorded specified values, its zoom,
/// box display, color scheme and dependency flags: whether each longhand's value was important,
/// inherited or evaluated by the computation, and what the box adjustments and monospace
/// recascades read.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct LonghandTableFlags {
    important_bits: [u8; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES],
    inherited_bits: [u8; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES],
    evaluated_bits: [u8; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES],
    overflow_before_adjustment: Option<[u16; 2]>,
    raw_cascaded_font_size: Option<RetainedStyleValueData>,
}

impl LonghandTableFlags {
    /// The flags of a copy of `initial` a drive starts from, before it computes anything.
    pub(crate) fn of_drive_copy(initial: &LonghandTableFlags) -> Self {
        Self {
            evaluated_bits: [0; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES],
            ..initial.clone()
        }
    }

    /// The flags of the table `initial` seeds for a child, before the child computes anything:
    /// every longhand that inherits by default is inherited, and none is evaluated.
    pub(crate) fn of_child_seed(initial: &LonghandTableFlags) -> Self {
        Self {
            important_bits: initial.important_bits,
            inherited_bits: INHERITED_LONGHAND_BITS,
            evaluated_bits: [0; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES],
            ..initial.clone()
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_important(&self, property_id: u16) -> bool {
        bitmap_bit(&self.important_bits, slot_index(property_id))
    }

    /// One bit per longhand: whether its value is important.
    pub(crate) fn importance_bits(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.important_bits
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_inherited(&self, property_id: u16) -> bool {
        bitmap_bit(&self.inherited_bits, slot_index(property_id))
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_evaluated(&self, property_id: u16) -> bool {
        bitmap_bit(&self.evaluated_bits, slot_index(property_id))
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_important(&mut self, property_id: u16, important: bool) {
        set_bitmap_bit(&mut self.important_bits, slot_index(property_id), important);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_inherited(&mut self, property_id: u16, inherited: bool) {
        set_bitmap_bit(&mut self.inherited_bits, slot_index(property_id), inherited);
    }

    /// The flags of a computation that starts from nothing: no longhand is important, inherited
    /// or evaluated.
    pub(crate) fn empty() -> Self {
        Self {
            important_bits: [0; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES],
            inherited_bits: [0; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES],
            evaluated_bits: [0; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES],
            overflow_before_adjustment: None,
            raw_cascaded_font_size: None,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn mark_evaluated(&mut self, property_id: u16) {
        set_bitmap_bit(&mut self.evaluated_bits, slot_index(property_id), true);
    }

    /// Takes the importance and inheritance a drive found for each longhand it evaluated, one bit
    /// per longhand index in each of the words.
    pub(crate) fn merge_driver_flags(
        &mut self,
        important_words: &[u64],
        inherited_words: &[u64],
        evaluated_words: &[u64],
    ) {
        assert!(important_words.len() * 64 >= LONGHAND_COUNT);
        assert_eq!(inherited_words.len(), important_words.len());
        assert_eq!(evaluated_words.len(), important_words.len());
        for (word_index, &evaluated_word) in evaluated_words.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut remaining = evaluated_word;
            while remaining != 0 {
                let bit = remaining.trailing_zeros() as usize;
                remaining &= remaining - 1;
                let index = word_index * 64 + bit;
                if index >= LONGHAND_COUNT {
                    break;
                }
                set_bitmap_bit(
                    &mut self.important_bits,
                    index,
                    important_words[word_index] & (1 << bit) != 0,
                );
                set_bitmap_bit(
                    &mut self.inherited_bits,
                    index,
                    inherited_words[word_index] & (1 << bit) != 0,
                );
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_overflow_before_adjustment(&mut self, overflow: [u16; 2]) {
        self.overflow_before_adjustment = Some(overflow);
    }

    /// The overflow keywords before the box adjustments, where they adjusted them.
    pub(crate) fn overflow_before_adjustment(&self) -> Option<[u16; 2]> {
        self.overflow_before_adjustment
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_raw_cascaded_font_size(&mut self, value: Option<RetainedStyleValueData>) {
        self.raw_cascaded_font_size = value;
    }

    /// The element's cascaded font size, where it declares one, which the monospace recascade of
    /// a descendant reads.
    pub(crate) fn raw_cascaded_font_size_value(&self) -> Option<&StyleValueData> {
        self.raw_cascaded_font_size
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(RetainedStyleValueData::optional_data)
    }

    /// Whether these are the very flags `other` are: the same bits, and the same cascaded font size
    /// value, not only an equal one.
    pub(crate) fn same_as(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.important_bits == other.important_bits
            && self.inherited_bits == other.inherited_bits
            && self.evaluated_bits == other.evaluated_bits
            && self.overflow_before_adjustment == other.overflow_before_adjustment
            && self
                .raw_cascaded_font_size
                .as_ref()
                .map(RetainedStyleValueData::pointer)
                == other
                    .raw_cascaded_font_size
                    .as_ref()
                    .map(RetainedStyleValueData::pointer)
    }

    /// Whether these are the flags `other` are, as a publication compares them.
    pub(crate) fn publication_equals(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        use crate::css::style_value::optional_style_values_equal;
        self.important_bits == other.important_bits
            && self.inherited_bits == other.inherited_bits
            && self.evaluated_bits == other.evaluated_bits
            && self.overflow_before_adjustment == other.overflow_before_adjustment
            && optional_style_values_equal(
                self.raw_cascaded_font_size
                    .as_ref()
                    .and_then(RetainedStyleValueData::optional_data),
                other
                    .raw_cascaded_font_size
                    .as_ref()
                    .and_then(RetainedStyleValueData::optional_data),
            )
    }

    /// What these flags hold differently from `other`, by name, for a diagnostic to show.
    pub(crate) fn publication_differences(&self, other: &Self) -> Vec<String> {
        let bits_differ = |name: &str, first: &[u8; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES], second: &[u8; LONGHAND_BITMAP_BYTES]| {
            let longhands: Vec<_> = (FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID..=LAST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID)
                .filter(|&property| {
                    let slot = slot_index(property);
                    bitmap_bit(first, slot) != bitmap_bit(second, slot)
                })
                .map(crate::css::property_metadata::property_name)
                .collect();
            (!longhands.is_empty()).then(|| format!("{name} of {}", longhands.join(", ")))
        };
        let mut differences: Vec<String> = [
            bits_differ("important bits", &self.important_bits, &other.important_bits),
            bits_differ("inherited bits", &self.inherited_bits, &other.inherited_bits),
            bits_differ("evaluated bits", &self.evaluated_bits, &other.evaluated_bits),
        ]
        .into_iter()
        .flatten()
        .collect();
        let mut note = |name: &str, first: String, second: String| {
            if first != second {
                differences.push(format!("{name} {first} != {second}"));
            }
        };
        note(
            "overflow before adjustment",
            format!("{:?}", self.overflow_before_adjustment),
            format!("{:?}", other.overflow_before_adjustment),
        );
        if !crate::css::style_value::optional_style_values_equal(
            self.raw_cascaded_font_size_value(),
            other.raw_cascaded_font_size_value(),
        ) {
            differences.push("cascaded font size".into());
        }
        differences
    }
}

/// The recorded specified value of `property` among `values`, where it has one.
fn inheritance_dependent_value_among<'a>(
    mut values: impl Iterator<Item = (u16, &'a RetainedStyleValueData)>,
    property: u16,
) -> Option<&'a RetainedStyleValueData> {
    values.find(|(held, _)| *held == property).map(|(_, value)| value)
}

/// Whether the recorded specified value of `property` moved from `old` to `new`, the recorded
/// specified values of two longhand tables or of the group values they are made from.
/// NB: Equal resolved colors can retain specified values that inherit differently.
fn inheritance_dependent_value_changed<'a, Values>(old: Values, new: Values, property: u16) -> bool
where
    Values: Iterator<Item = (u16, &'a RetainedStyleValueData)>,
{
    let old = inheritance_dependent_value_among(old, property);
    let new = inheritance_dependent_value_among(new, property);
    old.map(RetainedStyleValueData::pointer) != new.map(RetainedStyleValueData::pointer)
        && old.map(RetainedStyleValueData::data) != new.map(RetainedStyleValueData::data)
}

/// Whether a property that inherits by default retains another specified value among `new` than
/// among `old`, the recorded specified values of two longhand tables or of the group values they
/// are made from, which the children inheriting it resolve differently though the resolved colors
/// are equal.
pub(crate) fn inherited_inheritance_dependent_value_moved<'a, Values>(old: Values, new: Values) -> bool
where
    Values: Iterator<Item = (u16, &'a RetainedStyleValueData)> + Clone,
{
    old.clone().chain(new.clone()).any(|(property, _)| {
        property_is_inherited(property) && inheritance_dependent_value_changed(old.clone(), new.clone(), property)
    })
}

/// The non-inherited groups whose recorded specified values moved from `old` to `new`, the recorded
/// specified values of two longhand tables or of the group values they are made from.
/// NB: Report these source changes separately from resolved group payload changes.
pub(crate) fn non_inherited_inheritance_changes<'a, Values>(old: Values, new: Values) -> u32
where
    Values: Iterator<Item = (u16, &'a RetainedStyleValueData)> + Clone,
{
    // NB: A property both hold is visited once, through `old`.
    old.clone()
        .chain(
            new.clone()
                .filter(|(property, _)| inheritance_dependent_value_among(old.clone(), *property).is_none()),
        )
        .filter(|(property, _)| {
            !property_is_inherited(*property)
                && inheritance_dependent_value_changed(old.clone(), new.clone(), *property)
        })
        .fold(0, |groups, (property, _)| {
            groups
                | match crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroupMasks::get().dependencies(property) {
                    0 => u32::MAX,
                    mask => mask,
                }
        })
}

/// The dependency-flag bit of a record holding a value resolved against the viewport, as a `vw`
/// length is.
pub(crate) const DEPENDS_ON_VIEWPORT_METRICS: u8 = 1;
/// The dependency-flag bit of a record whose font metrics read the viewport, as a `vw` font size
/// does: what `em` and the other font-relative units resolve against moves with the viewport.
pub(crate) const FONT_METRICS_DEPEND_ON_VIEWPORT_METRICS: u8 = 1 << 1;
/// The dependency-flag bit of a record whose element is `display: none` or inherits from one that is.
pub(crate) const IN_DISPLAY_NONE_SUBTREE: u8 = 1 << 2;
/// The dependency-flag bit of a highlight pseudo-element record whose `color` or `background-color`
/// comes from the author origin, on itself or up its highlight chain, so the paired default colors
/// do not apply. Bits 0 to 4 are the viewport, font-metric, display-none, swap-eligibility and image
/// flags.
/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo-4/#paired-defaults
pub(crate) const HIGHLIGHT_COLORS_AUTHORED: u8 = 1 << 5;
/// The dependency-flag bit of a highlight pseudo-element record whose `color` is currentColor: the
/// computed value is the originating element's color, but painting draws the layer below instead.
/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo-4/#highlight-text
pub(crate) const HIGHLIGHT_COLOR_IS_CURRENT_COLOR: u8 = 1 << 6;
/// The dependency-flag bit of a record with a cascaded value from the author origin for any property that disables
/// native appearance for widgets.
/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#appearance-disabling-properties
pub(crate) const NATIVE_APPEARANCE_DISABLED: u8 = 1 << 7;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiComputedStyleMetadata {
    pub display_before_box_type_transformation: u32,
    pub effective_color_scheme: i16,
    pub dependency_flags: u8,
    pub in_display_none_subtree: bool,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use crate::css::style_value_arc::StyleValueArc;

    use super::*;
    use crate::css::property_metadata::property_id;
    use crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData;

    type Recorded = Vec<(u16, RetainedStyleValueData)>;

    fn entry((property, value): &(u16, RetainedStyleValueData)) -> (u16, &RetainedStyleValueData) {
        (*property, value)
    }

    fn table_inheritance_changes(old: &Recorded, new: &Recorded) -> u32 {
        non_inherited_inheritance_changes(old.iter().map(entry), new.iter().map(entry))
    }

    #[test]
    fn inheritance_source_changes_keep_their_exact_non_inherited_group() {
        let current_color: Recorded = vec![(
            property_id::TEXT_DECORATION_COLOR,
            RetainedStyleValueData::from_owned(StyleValueData::Keyword {
                keyword: crate::css::style_compute::keyword::CURRENTCOLOR,
            }),
        )];
        let equal: Recorded = vec![(
            property_id::TEXT_DECORATION_COLOR,
            RetainedStyleValueData::from_arc(StyleValueArc::new(StyleValueData::Keyword {
                keyword: crate::css::style_compute::keyword::CURRENTCOLOR,
            })),
        )];
        assert_eq!(table_inheritance_changes(&current_color, &equal), 0);
        let resolved = Recorded::new();
        let expected = 1 << crate::css::table_group_builder::group_index::TEXT_RESET;
        assert_eq!(table_inheritance_changes(&current_color, &resolved), expected);
        assert_eq!(table_inheritance_changes(&resolved, &current_color), expected);
        assert_eq!(table_inheritance_changes(&current_color, &current_color.clone()), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn inherited_source_changes_do_not_mark_non_inherited_groups() {
        let current_color: Recorded = vec![(
            property_id::COLOR,
            RetainedStyleValueData::from_owned(StyleValueData::Keyword {
                keyword: crate::css::style_compute::keyword::CURRENTCOLOR,
            }),
        )];
        assert_eq!(table_inheritance_changes(&current_color, &Recorded::new()), 0);
    }
}

/// The computed forms accepted by width and height sizing properties.
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ComputedSizeKind {
    Auto,
    Calculated,
    Length,
    Percentage,
    MinContent,
    MaxContent,
    FitContent,
    Stretch,
    None,
}

/// A computed sizing value. Scalar and calculated values retain their
/// immutable Rust style-value identity. Fit-content retains only its
/// argument, and keyword-only forms leave the handle empty.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ComputedStyleValueHandle {
    pub pointer: *const std::ffi::c_void,
}

// SAFETY: A non-null handle owns an Arc reference to immutable style value data and only exposes
// shared access to it, as `RetainedStyleValueData` does.
unsafe impl Send for ComputedStyleValueHandle where crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData: Send + Sync {}
unsafe impl Sync for ComputedStyleValueHandle where crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData: Send + Sync {}

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ComputedSize {
    pub kind: ComputedSizeKind,
    /// The plain length or percentage `value` holds, kept inline so that reading it needs no dereference: the form of
    /// `inline_value`, one of the forms `InlineLengthPercentage` decodes.
    pub inline_form: u8,
    pub inline_value: u32,
    pub value: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
}

/// Layout of the six computed sizing properties.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct SizingValues {
    pub width: ComputedSize,
    pub min_width: ComputedSize,
    pub max_width: ComputedSize,
    pub height: ComputedSize,
    pub min_height: ComputedSize,
    pub max_height: ComputedSize,
}

/// A computed flex-basis value. Content uses the flag; every other form
/// uses the same computed-size representation as width and height.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct ComputedFlexBasis {
    pub is_content: bool,
    pub size: ComputedSize,
}

/// A computed row-gap or column-gap value. Normal uses the flag; every
/// other form retains its immutable length-percentage identity.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct ComputedGap {
    pub is_normal: bool,
    pub value: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
}

/// Layout of the computed flexbox and box-alignment properties.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct AlignmentValues {
    pub webkit_box_orient: u8,
    pub webkit_box_align: u8,
    pub webkit_box_pack: u8,
    pub flex_direction: u8,
    pub flex_wrap: u8,
    pub flex_basis: ComputedFlexBasis,
    pub flex_grow: f64,
    pub flex_shrink: f64,
    pub webkit_box_flex: f64,
    pub order: i32,
    pub webkit_box_ordinal_group: i32,
    pub align_content: u8,
    pub align_items: u8,
    pub align_self: u8,
    pub align_items_is_last_baseline: bool,
    pub align_self_is_last_baseline: bool,
    pub align_content_is_last_baseline: bool,
    pub justify_content: u8,
    pub justify_items: u8,
    pub justify_self: u8,
    /// The explicit overflow alignment: one of the OVERFLOW_ALIGNMENT_* values.
    pub align_items_overflow: u8,
    pub justify_items_overflow: u8,
    pub align_self_overflow: u8,
    pub justify_self_overflow: u8,
    pub align_content_overflow: u8,
    pub justify_content_overflow: u8,
    pub column_gap: ComputedGap,
    pub row_gap: ComputedGap,
}

/// No explicit overflow alignment.
pub const OVERFLOW_ALIGNMENT_DEFAULT: u8 = 0;
/// The 'safe' overflow alignment.
pub const OVERFLOW_ALIGNMENT_SAFE: u8 = 1;
/// The 'unsafe' overflow alignment.
pub const OVERFLOW_ALIGNMENT_UNSAFE: u8 = 2;

/// A computed length-percentage-or-auto value.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto {
    pub is_auto: bool,
    /// The plain length or percentage `value` holds, as in [`ComputedSize`].
    pub inline_form: u8,
    pub inline_value: u32,
    pub value: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
}

/// Four physical computed length-percentage-or-auto sides.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct ComputedLengthBox {
    pub top: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto,
    pub right: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto,
    pub bottom: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto,
    pub left: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto,
}

/// Layout of the computed inset, margin, and padding properties, plus the
/// computed position-anchor value the anchor lookup beside the anchor insets
/// consults; an empty handle means position-anchor has no name. Each bare
/// anchor() inset also carries the calculated wrapper the layout pass
/// resolves, built with the payload so inset reads borrow it directly.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct SurroundValues {
    pub inset: ComputedLengthBox,
    pub top_anchor_inset: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
    pub right_anchor_inset: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
    pub bottom_anchor_inset: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
    pub left_anchor_inset: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
    pub top_anchor_inset_wrapper: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
    pub right_anchor_inset_wrapper: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
    pub bottom_anchor_inset_wrapper: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
    pub left_anchor_inset_wrapper: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
    pub position_anchor: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
    pub margin: ComputedLengthBox,
    pub padding: ComputedLengthBox,
}

/// A computed vertical-align value: an alignment keyword or a retained
/// length-percentage offset.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct ComputedVerticalAlign {
    pub is_keyword: bool,
    pub keyword: u8,
    pub value: ComputedStyleValueHandle,
}

/// The computed aspect-ratio value, carrying both the used form and the
/// as-computed form the serialization path reports. Absent ratios keep both
/// components at zero so payload equality stays field-wise.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct ComputedAspectRatio {
    pub use_natural_aspect_ratio_if_available: bool,
    pub has_preferred_ratio: bool,
    pub preferred_ratio_numerator: f64,
    pub preferred_ratio_denominator: f64,
    pub computed_use_natural_aspect_ratio_if_available: bool,
    pub has_computed_ratio: bool,
    pub computed_ratio_numerator: f64,
    pub computed_ratio_denominator: f64,
}

/// A computed contain-intrinsic-width or contain-intrinsic-height: auto? [ none | <length [0,∞]> ]. A false has_length
/// means none.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct ComputedContainIntrinsicSize {
    pub has_auto: bool,
    pub has_length: bool,
    pub length_px: f64,
}

impl ComputedContainIntrinsicSize {
    pub fn none() -> Self {
        Self {
            has_auto: false,
            has_length: false,
            length_px: 0.0,
        }
    }
}

/// The first group index of the rare group set a style shares; the inherited set's groups come
/// before it, from index zero.
pub const STYLE_GROUP_RARE_SET_START: usize = 5;
/// The first group index of the visual group set a style shares.
pub const STYLE_GROUP_VISUAL_SET_START: usize = 13;
/// The first group index of the groups a style keeps in its root, which run to the last group.
pub const STYLE_GROUP_ROOT_START: usize = 19;

/// The inherited longhands of few keywords a style holds as bits beside its inherited groups, in
/// place of a field of a group: each the code of its keyword in the CSS enum of the property, at
/// the field's shift.
#[repr(transparent)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub struct InheritedBits(pub u32);

pub const INHERITED_BITS_WRITING_MODE_SHIFT: u32 = 0;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_WRITING_MODE_WIDTH: u32 = 3;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_DIRECTION_SHIFT: u32 = 3;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_DIRECTION_WIDTH: u32 = 1;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_VISIBILITY_SHIFT: u32 = 4;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_VISIBILITY_WIDTH: u32 = 2;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_TEXT_ORIENTATION_SHIFT: u32 = 6;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_TEXT_ORIENTATION_WIDTH: u32 = 2;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_POINTER_EVENTS_SHIFT: u32 = 8;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_POINTER_EVENTS_WIDTH: u32 = 4;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_LIST_STYLE_POSITION_SHIFT: u32 = 12;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_LIST_STYLE_POSITION_WIDTH: u32 = 1;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_BORDER_COLLAPSE_SHIFT: u32 = 13;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_BORDER_COLLAPSE_WIDTH: u32 = 1;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_CAPTION_SIDE_SHIFT: u32 = 14;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_CAPTION_SIDE_WIDTH: u32 = 1;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_EMPTY_CELLS_SHIFT: u32 = 15;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_EMPTY_CELLS_WIDTH: u32 = 1;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_TEXT_ALIGN_SHIFT: u32 = 16;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_TEXT_ALIGN_WIDTH: u32 = 4;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_WHITE_SPACE_COLLAPSE_SHIFT: u32 = 20;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_WHITE_SPACE_COLLAPSE_WIDTH: u32 = 3;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_TEXT_WRAP_MODE_SHIFT: u32 = 23;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_TEXT_WRAP_MODE_WIDTH: u32 = 1;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_WORD_BREAK_SHIFT: u32 = 24;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_WORD_BREAK_WIDTH: u32 = 2;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_TEXT_ALIGN_LAST_SHIFT: u32 = 26;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_TEXT_ALIGN_LAST_WIDTH: u32 = 3;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_HYPHENS_SHIFT: u32 = 29;
pub const INHERITED_BITS_HYPHENS_WIDTH: u32 = 2;

/// The keywords of few values of properties that do not inherit a style holds as bits in its
/// root beside its own groups, in place of fields of its box group: each the code of its keyword
/// in the CSS enum of the property, at the field's shift.
#[repr(transparent)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub struct ResetBits(pub u32);

pub const RESET_BITS_POSITION_SHIFT: u32 = 0;
pub const RESET_BITS_POSITION_WIDTH: u32 = 3;
pub const RESET_BITS_FLOAT_SHIFT: u32 = 3;
pub const RESET_BITS_FLOAT_WIDTH: u32 = 3;
pub const RESET_BITS_CLEAR_SHIFT: u32 = 6;
pub const RESET_BITS_CLEAR_WIDTH: u32 = 3;
pub const RESET_BITS_OVERFLOW_X_SHIFT: u32 = 9;
pub const RESET_BITS_OVERFLOW_X_WIDTH: u32 = 3;
pub const RESET_BITS_OVERFLOW_Y_SHIFT: u32 = 12;
pub const RESET_BITS_OVERFLOW_Y_WIDTH: u32 = 3;
pub const RESET_BITS_BOX_SIZING_SHIFT: u32 = 15;
pub const RESET_BITS_BOX_SIZING_WIDTH: u32 = 1;
pub const RESET_BITS_UNICODE_BIDI_SHIFT: u32 = 16;
pub const RESET_BITS_UNICODE_BIDI_WIDTH: u32 = 3;
pub const RESET_BITS_TABLE_LAYOUT_SHIFT: u32 = 19;
pub const RESET_BITS_TABLE_LAYOUT_WIDTH: u32 = 1;

/// What a style's inherited set holds beside its groups for its readers to read directly: the
/// inherited longhands held as bits, and the effective zoom.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub struct InheritedSetValues {
    pub bits: InheritedBits,
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-viewport/#effective-zoom
    /// The bits of the effective zoom, as an `f32`.
    pub effective_zoom_bits: u32,
}

/// What a style holds as bits beside its groups: the inherited bits and zoom beside its inherited
/// set's groups, and the reset bits in its root.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub struct StyleBits {
    pub inherited: InheritedSetValues,
    pub reset: ResetBits,
}

/// A computed color as a group holds it: a color, or `currentcolor`, which its reader resolves
/// against the element's color, so that the group does not depend on the element's color.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct StyleColor {
    /// The color, in the C++ Color::value() bit layout; unused for `currentcolor`.
    pub rgba: u32,
    pub is_current_color: bool,
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<StyleColor>() == 8);

impl StyleColor {
    pub const CURRENT_COLOR: Self = Self {
        rgba: 0,
        is_current_color: true,
    };

    pub const fn rgba(rgba: u32) -> Self {
        Self {
            rgba,
            is_current_color: false,
        }
    }

    /// The color, with `currentcolor` resolved to `current_color`.
    #[inline]
    pub const fn resolve(self, current_color: u32) -> u32 {
        if self.is_current_color {
            current_color
        } else {
            self.rgba
        }
    }
}

/// The metrics of a style's first available font that lengths and line layout read.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct FirstAvailableFontMetrics {
    pub ascent: f32,
    pub descent: f32,
    pub x_height: f32,
    pub cap_height: f32,
    pub zero_advance: f32,
}

impl FontValues {
    /// The computed font size, which `font_size` holds rounded to the nearest pixel fraction, as
    /// the lengths relative to it read it: An em or rem length scales the size unrounded.
    pub fn font_size_for_lengths(&self) -> f64 {
        match self.font_size_value.style_value() {
            Some(crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData::Length { value, unit })
                if *unit == crate::css::style_compute::px_length_unit() =>
            {
                *value
            }
            _ => self.font_size.to_double(),
        }
    }

    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font
    /// The frozen cascade answers where the font computer published one: a load filling one of its
    /// faces in moves the answer without a new style. A cascade nobody published (a unit test's)
    /// answers what it was resolved with.
    pub fn first_available_font(&self) -> Option<&libgfx_rust::font::FontHandle> {
        Some(self.frozen_font_list.list()?.first_available_font())
    }

    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline-3/#line-height-property
    /// The used line height. A `normal` one is decided by the metrics of the first available font,
    /// read through the frozen cascade, so a load filling one of its faces in moves it without a
    /// new style.
    pub fn line_height_used(&self) -> crate::css::css_pixels::CssPixels {
        let is_normal = matches!(
            self.line_height.style_value(),
            Some(crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword })
                if *keyword == crate::css::style_compute::keyword::NORMAL
        );
        if is_normal && let Some(font) = self.first_available_font() {
            let facts = font.facts();
            return crate::css::css_pixels::CssPixels::from_integer(
                i64::from(facts.ascent.round_ties_even() as i32)
                    + i64::from(facts.descent.round_ties_even() as i32)
                    + i64::from(facts.line_gap.round_ties_even() as i32),
            );
        }
        self.resolved_line_height_used
    }

    /// The metrics of [`FontValues::first_available_font`].
    pub fn first_available_font_metrics(&self) -> FirstAvailableFontMetrics {
        match self.first_available_font() {
            Some(font) => {
                let facts = font.facts();
                FirstAvailableFontMetrics {
                    ascent: facts.ascent,
                    descent: facts.descent,
                    x_height: facts.x_height,
                    cap_height: facts.cap_height,
                    zero_advance: facts.zero_advance,
                }
            }
            None => FirstAvailableFontMetrics {
                ascent: self.resolved_font_ascent,
                descent: self.resolved_font_descent,
                x_height: self.resolved_font_x_height,
                cap_height: self.resolved_font_cap_height,
                zero_advance: self.resolved_font_zero_advance,
            },
        }
    }
}

//! Lazy readers over the computed style group payload types, mirroring the
//! C++ `CSS::Size` / `CSS::LengthPercentage` method surface: every query
//! resolves on demand from the stored computed representation, so readers
//! need no intermediate decoded value.

use crate::css::calc;
use crate::css::computed_value_types::{
    AlignmentValues, AnchorValues, BackgroundValues, BorderLayoutFacts, BorderValues, BoxValues, ComputedAspectRatio,
    ComputedGap, ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto, ComputedSize, ComputedSizeKind, ComputedStyleValueHandle,
    ContentValues, EffectsValues, FontValues, GridValues, InheritedListTableValues, InheritedSVGValues,
    InheritedTextLayoutFacts, InheritedTextValues, InheritedUIValues, MaskValues, MiscInteractionValues,
    MiscLayoutValues, SVGResetValues, SizingValues, SurroundValues, TextResetValues, TransformValues,
};
use crate::css::computed_values::StyleBitField;
use crate::css::css_enums::{direction, writing_mode};
use crate::css::css_pixels::CssPixels;
use crate::css::display::FfiDisplay;
use crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData;
use crate::css::style_value::{CalculatedPayload, ContentPayload, CounterDefinitionsPayload};
use crate::css::table_group_builder::group_index;
use std::ffi::c_void;

pub(crate) fn px_calc_resolution_context(percentage_basis: CssPixels) -> calc::FfiCalcResolutionContext {
    calc::FfiCalcResolutionContext {
        basis_kind: 3,
        basis_value: percentage_basis.to_double(),
        basis_unit: crate::css::style_compute::px_length_unit(),
        length_resolution_context: std::ptr::null(),
        element_facts: std::ptr::null(),
    }
}

pub(crate) fn resolve_calc_to_px_without_rounding(calculated: *const c_void, percentage_basis: CssPixels) -> f64 {
    assert!(!calculated.is_null());
    // SAFETY: The style value stays alive for the pass.
    let value = unsafe { &*calculated.cast::<StyleValueData>() };
    crate::css::calc::resolve_calculated_length_without_context(value, percentage_basis.to_double()).unwrap_or_else(|| {
        assert!(
            matches!(value, StyleValueData::Calculated(calculated) if calculated.rust_calculation.node().contains_anchor_function()),
            "computed length-percentage calc failed to resolve"
        );
        // NB: The abspos engine resolves the anchor functions it can itself, so these are unresolvable.
        crate::layout::style_values::resolve_calc_with_unresolvable_anchor_functions(calculated, percentage_basis)
    })
}

pub(crate) fn resolve_calc_to_px(calculated: *const c_void, percentage_basis: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
    CssPixels::truncated_value_for(resolve_calc_to_px_without_rounding(calculated, percentage_basis))
}

/// A borrowed computed `<length-percentage>`: a retained length, percentage
/// or calculated style value read in place, the Rust twin of the C++
/// `LengthPercentage::view` API.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct LengthPercentageRef<'a> {
    value: &'a StyleValueData,
}

impl<'a> LengthPercentageRef<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn over(value: &'a StyleValueData) -> Self {
        Self { value }
    }
}

impl LengthPercentageRef<'_> {
    pub(crate) fn is_calculated(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.value, StyleValueData::Calculated { .. })
    }

    pub(crate) fn absolute_length_to_px(self) -> CssPixels {
        let StyleValueData::Length { value, unit } = self.value else {
            unreachable!("computed length-percentage read as a length holds another style value");
        };
        let ratio = crate::css::style_compute::LENGTH_UNIT_CANONICAL_PX_RATIOS[*unit as usize];
        assert!(ratio.is_finite(), "computed length is not absolute");
        CssPixels::truncated_value_for(f64::from((value * ratio) as f32))
    }

    /// Matches Percentage::as_fraction(); the multiplication order is
    /// observable for some f64 inputs.
    pub(crate) fn as_fraction(self) -> f64 {
        let StyleValueData::Percentage { value } = self.value else {
            unreachable!("computed length-percentage read as a percentage holds another style value");
        };
        value * 0.01
    }

    /// The retained calculated style value, for handing to calc resolution.
    pub(crate) fn calculated_pointer(self) -> *const c_void {
        assert!(self.is_calculated());
        std::ptr::from_ref(self.value).cast()
    }

    pub(crate) fn contains_percentage(self) -> bool {
        match self.value {
            StyleValueData::Length { .. } => false,
            StyleValueData::Percentage { .. } => true,
            StyleValueData::Calculated(calculated_payload) => {
                let CalculatedPayload { rust_calculation, .. } = &**calculated_payload;
                rust_calculation.node().contains_percentage()
            }
            // A calc-size() whose basis is any or a calculation acts like a calculation.
            value @ StyleValueData::Function { .. } => {
                crate::css::calc_size::calc_size_arguments(value).is_some_and(|(basis, calculation)| {
                    [basis, calculation].into_iter().any(|argument| {
                        !matches!(argument, StyleValueData::Keyword { .. })
                            && LengthPercentageRef::over(argument).contains_percentage()
                    })
                })
            }
            _ => unreachable!("computed length-percentage holds a non-length-percentage style value"),
        }
    }

    /// The percentage the value is, as a fraction, when it is a percentage or a calculation that simplified to one,
    /// as `calc(10% + 15%)` does.
    pub(crate) fn percentage_fraction(self) -> Option<f64> {
        match self.value {
            StyleValueData::Percentage { .. } => Some(self.as_fraction()),
            StyleValueData::Calculated(calculated_payload) => {
                let CalculatedPayload { rust_calculation, .. } = &**calculated_payload;
                match rust_calculation.node() {
                    crate::css::calc::CalcNode::Numeric(crate::css::calc::CalcNumericValue::Percentage(value)) => {
                        Some(value * 0.01)
                    }
                    _ => None,
                }
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn contains_anchor_function(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.value, StyleValueData::Calculated(calculated) if calculated.rust_calculation.node().contains_anchor_function())
    }

    pub(crate) fn to_px(self, reference: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
        match self.value {
            StyleValueData::Length { .. } => self.absolute_length_to_px(),
            StyleValueData::Percentage { .. } => {
                CssPixels::truncated_value_for(reference.to_double() * self.as_fraction())
            }
            StyleValueData::Calculated { .. } => resolve_calc_to_px(self.calculated_pointer(), reference),
            // NB: A calc-size() that does not resolve is invalid at computed-value time, and resolves to zero.
            value @ StyleValueData::Function { .. } => CssPixels::nearest_value_for(
                crate::css::calc_size::resolve_calc_size(value, Some(reference.to_double()), &|_| 0.0).unwrap_or(0.0),
            ),
            _ => unreachable!("computed length-percentage holds a non-length-percentage style value"),
        }
    }
}

/// The plain length or percentage a computed size or length-percentage keeps inline beside its style value, as the
/// reads of the style value would resolve it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) enum InlineLengthPercentage {
    /// An absolute length, in CSS pixels.
    Length(CssPixels),
    /// A percentage, whose value as an f32 is exactly the f64 the style value holds.
    Percentage(f32),
}

impl InlineLengthPercentage {
    const NONE: u8 = 0;
    const LENGTH: u8 = 1;
    const PERCENTAGE: u8 = 2;

    /// What a computed value holding `value` keeps inline: nothing for a calculation, a relative length or a percentage
    /// an f32 does not hold.
    pub(crate) fn of(value: Option<&StyleValueData>) -> Option<Self> {
        match value? {
            StyleValueData::Length { value, unit } => {
                let ratio = crate::css::style_compute::LENGTH_UNIT_CANONICAL_PX_RATIOS[*unit as usize];
                ratio
                    .is_finite()
                    .then(|| Self::Length(CssPixels::truncated_value_for(f64::from((value * ratio) as f32))))
            }
            StyleValueData::Percentage { value } => {
                let narrowed = *value as f32;
                (f64::from(narrowed) == *value).then_some(Self::Percentage(narrowed))
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The form and value fields that hold `inline`.
    pub(crate) fn encode(inline: Option<Self>) -> (u8, u32) {
        match inline {
            None => (Self::NONE, 0),
            Some(Self::Length(pixels)) => (Self::LENGTH, pixels.raw_value() as u32),
            Some(Self::Percentage(value)) => (Self::PERCENTAGE, value.to_bits()),
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn decode(form: u8, value: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        match form {
            Self::LENGTH => Some(Self::Length(CssPixels::from_raw(value as i32))),
            Self::PERCENTAGE => Some(Self::Percentage(f32::from_bits(value))),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// As [`LengthPercentageRef::to_px`] resolves the style value.
    #[inline]
    fn to_px(self, reference: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
        match self {
            Self::Length(pixels) => pixels,
            Self::Percentage(value) => {
                CssPixels::truncated_value_for(reference.to_double() * (f64::from(value) * 0.01))
            }
        }
    }

    fn contains_percentage(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Percentage(_))
    }
}

impl ComputedStyleValueHandle {
    /// The lifetime is the caller's to choose: the referenced style value is
    /// retained by whatever owns the handle, not by the handle borrow itself.
    pub(crate) fn length_percentage<'a>(&self) -> Option<LengthPercentageRef<'a>> {
        if self.pointer.is_null() {
            return None;
        }
        // SAFETY: A non-null handle points at the retained style value owned
        // by the node's style group payload, which outlives every reader.
        Some(LengthPercentageRef {
            value: unsafe { &*self.pointer.cast::<StyleValueData>() },
        })
    }

    /// The retained style value itself, for the properties whose computed value is not a
    /// length-percentage.
    pub(crate) fn style_value<'a>(&self) -> Option<&'a StyleValueData> {
        // SAFETY: As above.
        unsafe { self.pointer.cast::<StyleValueData>().as_ref() }
    }
}

impl ComputedSize {
    pub(crate) fn is_auto(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind == ComputedSizeKind::Auto
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_length(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind == ComputedSizeKind::Length
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_percentage(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind == ComputedSizeKind::Percentage
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_min_content(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind == ComputedSizeKind::MinContent
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_max_content(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind == ComputedSizeKind::MaxContent
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_fit_content(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind == ComputedSizeKind::FitContent
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_stretch(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind == ComputedSizeKind::Stretch
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_none(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind == ComputedSizeKind::None
    }

    /// The calc-size() function this size was given as, if any. It acts as its basis for all purposes other
    /// than resolving the size.
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#calc-size
    pub(crate) fn calc_size(&self) -> Option<&StyleValueData> {
        self.value
            .style_value()
            .filter(|value| crate::css::calc_size::calc_size_arguments(value).is_some())
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_length_percentage(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.kind,
            ComputedSizeKind::Calculated | ComputedSizeKind::Length | ComputedSizeKind::Percentage
        )
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_intrinsic_sizing_constraint(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.kind,
            ComputedSizeKind::MinContent | ComputedSizeKind::MaxContent | ComputedSizeKind::FitContent
        )
    }

    /// The length-percentage term of a Length, Percentage or Calculated size.
    pub(crate) fn length_percentage(&self) -> LengthPercentageRef<'_> {
        debug_assert!(self.is_length_percentage());
        self.value
            .length_percentage()
            .expect("computed length-percentage size lost its style value")
    }

    /// The percentage the size is, as a fraction, when it is a percentage or a calculation that simplified to one.
    pub(crate) fn percentage_fraction(&self) -> Option<f64> {
        match self.kind {
            ComputedSizeKind::Percentage | ComputedSizeKind::Calculated => {
                self.length_percentage().percentage_fraction()
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The fit-content argument; None for the keyword-only form.
    pub(crate) fn fit_content_available_space(&self) -> Option<LengthPercentageRef<'_>> {
        debug_assert!(self.is_fit_content());
        if self.calc_size().is_some() {
            return None;
        }
        self.value.length_percentage()
    }

    /// The plain length or percentage the size keeps inline, if any.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn inline_length_percentage(&self) -> Option<InlineLengthPercentage> {
        InlineLengthPercentage::decode(self.inline_form, self.inline_value)
    }

    pub(crate) fn to_px(&self, reference: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
        match self.kind {
            ComputedSizeKind::Auto
            | ComputedSizeKind::MinContent
            | ComputedSizeKind::MaxContent
            | ComputedSizeKind::Stretch
            | ComputedSizeKind::None => CssPixels::default(),
            ComputedSizeKind::Calculated | ComputedSizeKind::Length | ComputedSizeKind::Percentage => {
                match self.inline_length_percentage() {
                    Some(inline) => inline.to_px(reference),
                    None => self.length_percentage().to_px(reference),
                }
            }
            ComputedSizeKind::FitContent => self
                .fit_content_available_space()
                .map_or(CssPixels::default(), |available_space| available_space.to_px(reference)),
        }
    }

    /// Whether the size is a calculation holding an anchor function. Only a calculation can hold one, so a plain length or
    /// percentage answers without reading its value.
    pub(crate) fn contains_anchor_function(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind == ComputedSizeKind::Calculated && self.length_percentage().contains_anchor_function()
    }

    pub(crate) fn contains_percentage(&self) -> bool {
        match self.kind {
            ComputedSizeKind::Auto
            | ComputedSizeKind::MinContent
            | ComputedSizeKind::MaxContent
            | ComputedSizeKind::None => false,
            // NB: A stretch size depends on the size of the containing block, and behaves as auto, zero or none
            //     wherever a percentage of it would not resolve.
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-3/#stretch-fit-sizing
            ComputedSizeKind::Stretch | ComputedSizeKind::Percentage => true,
            ComputedSizeKind::Length => false,
            ComputedSizeKind::Calculated => self.length_percentage().contains_percentage(),
            ComputedSizeKind::FitContent => self
                .fit_content_available_space()
                .is_some_and(|available_space| available_space.contains_percentage()),
        }
    }
}

impl ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto {
    pub(crate) fn is_auto(&self) -> bool {
        self.is_auto
    }

    pub(crate) fn length_percentage(&self) -> Option<LengthPercentageRef<'_>> {
        if self.is_auto {
            return None;
        }
        Some(
            self.value
                .length_percentage()
                .expect("non-auto computed length-percentage lost its style value"),
        )
    }

    /// The plain length or percentage the value keeps inline, if any.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn inline_length_percentage(&self) -> Option<InlineLengthPercentage> {
        InlineLengthPercentage::decode(self.inline_form, self.inline_value)
    }

    pub(crate) fn to_px(&self, reference: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
        if let Some(inline) = self.inline_length_percentage() {
            return inline.to_px(reference);
        }
        self.length_percentage()
            .map_or(CssPixels::default(), |value| value.to_px(reference))
    }

    pub(crate) fn contains_percentage(&self) -> bool {
        if let Some(inline) = self.inline_length_percentage() {
            return inline.contains_percentage();
        }
        self.length_percentage()
            .is_some_and(|value| value.contains_percentage())
    }
}

impl ComputedGap {
    pub(crate) fn is_normal(&self) -> bool {
        self.is_normal
    }

    pub(crate) fn length_percentage(&self) -> Option<LengthPercentageRef<'_>> {
        if self.is_normal {
            return None;
        }
        Some(
            self.value
                .length_percentage()
                .expect("non-normal computed gap lost its style value"),
        )
    }

    pub(crate) fn to_px(&self, reference: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
        self.length_percentage()
            .map_or(CssPixels::default(), |value| value.to_px(reference))
    }
}

struct SyncComputedSize(ComputedSize);

// SAFETY: The shared value's handle is null, so there is no pointee to race
// on.
unsafe impl Sync for SyncComputedSize {}

static AUTO_COMPUTED_SIZE: SyncComputedSize = SyncComputedSize(ComputedSize {
    kind: ComputedSizeKind::Auto,
    inline_form: InlineLengthPercentage::NONE,
    inline_value: 0,
    value: ComputedStyleValueHandle {
        pointer: std::ptr::null(),
    },
});

/// A shared computed `auto` size for readers that substitute auto for a
/// stored size.
pub(crate) fn auto_computed_size() -> &'static ComputedSize {
    &AUTO_COMPUTED_SIZE.0
}

static NONE_COMPUTED_SIZE: SyncComputedSize = SyncComputedSize(ComputedSize {
    kind: ComputedSizeKind::None,
    inline_form: InlineLengthPercentage::NONE,
    inline_value: 0,
    value: ComputedStyleValueHandle {
        pointer: std::ptr::null(),
    },
});

/// A shared computed `none` size for readers that substitute none for a
/// stored size.
pub(crate) fn none_computed_size() -> &'static ComputedSize {
    &NONE_COMPUTED_SIZE.0
}

fn counter_definitions(handle: &ComputedStyleValueHandle) -> &[crate::css::style_value::RetainedCounterDefinition] {
    match handle.data() {
        Some(StyleValueData::CounterDefinitions(counter_definitions_payload)) => {
            let CounterDefinitionsPayload { counter_definitions } = &**counter_definitions_payload;
            counter_definitions.as_slice()
        }
        _ => &[],
    }
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain-2/#containment-types
fn containment_applies_to_principal_box(display: FfiDisplay) -> bool {
    if display.is_internal_table() && !display.is_table_cell() {
        return false;
    }
    if display.is_inline_outside() && display.is_flow_inside() {
        return false;
    }
    true
}

/// The computed `aspect-ratio` <ratio> term as a CSSPixels fraction. A zero
/// denominator means no usable ratio (none specified, degenerate, or collapsed
/// to zero by the fixed-point conversion).
fn decode_css_preferred_aspect_ratio(ratio: &ComputedAspectRatio) -> (CssPixels, CssPixels) {
    let no_usable_ratio = (CssPixels::default(), CssPixels::default());
    if !ratio.has_preferred_ratio {
        return no_usable_ratio;
    }
    let numerator = ratio.preferred_ratio_numerator;
    let denominator = ratio.preferred_ratio_denominator;
    let is_degenerate = !numerator.is_finite() || numerator == 0.0 || !denominator.is_finite() || denominator == 0.0;
    if is_degenerate {
        return no_usable_ratio;
    }
    let (numerator, denominator) = CssPixels::fraction_nearest_values_for(numerator, denominator);
    if numerator.raw_value() == 0 {
        return no_usable_ratio;
    }
    (numerator, denominator)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct QuoteTransfer {
    outer_quotes_closed: u32,
    quotes_left_open: u32,
}

impl QuoteTransfer {
    pub(crate) const IDENTITY: Self = Self {
        outer_quotes_closed: 0,
        quotes_left_open: 0,
    };

    fn then_quote(self, opens: bool) -> Self {
        match (opens, self.quotes_left_open) {
            (true, quotes_left_open) => Self {
                quotes_left_open: quotes_left_open + 1,
                ..self
            },
            (false, 0) => Self {
                outer_quotes_closed: self.outer_quotes_closed + 1,
                ..self
            },
            (false, quotes_left_open) => Self {
                quotes_left_open: quotes_left_open - 1,
                ..self
            },
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn then(self, next: Self) -> Self {
        if self.quotes_left_open >= next.outer_quotes_closed {
            Self {
                outer_quotes_closed: self.outer_quotes_closed,
                quotes_left_open: self.quotes_left_open - next.outer_quotes_closed + next.quotes_left_open,
            }
        } else {
            Self {
                outer_quotes_closed: self.outer_quotes_closed + next.outer_quotes_closed - self.quotes_left_open,
                quotes_left_open: next.quotes_left_open,
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_identity(self) -> bool {
        self == Self::IDENTITY
    }

    pub(crate) fn apply(self, depth: u32) -> u32 {
        depth.saturating_sub(self.outer_quotes_closed) + self.quotes_left_open
    }
}

/// The groups of a computed style, at the front of what holds them: a style record, an anonymous
/// box's style or an animation overlay. Readers reach a group only through
/// [`ComputedValuesView`], whose `native_group` alone knows how one is found.
#[repr(transparent)]
pub(crate) struct StyleRecordGroups(pub(in crate::css) crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroups);

impl StyleRecordGroups {
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn of(groups: &crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroups) -> &Self {
        // SAFETY: The type is a transparent wrapper of the groups.
        unsafe { &*std::ptr::from_ref(groups).cast::<Self>() }
    }
}

/// A borrowed view over one node's computed style groups: the Rust twin of the C++
/// ComputedValues accessor surface, one thin pointer to the style. Every read hands out payload
/// references or lazy views; the groups must stay alive and unchanged while the view or anything
/// borrowed from it is in use.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct ComputedValuesView<'a>(&'a StyleRecordGroups);

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<ComputedValuesView<'static>>() == 8);

macro_rules! scalar_accessors {
    ($($group:ident: { $($name:ident: $ty:ty => $($field:ident).+,)+ })+) => {
        impl ComputedValuesView<'_> {
            $($(
                #[inline]
                pub(crate) fn $name(self) -> $ty {
                    self.$group().$($field).+
                }
            )+)+
        }
    };
}

        align_self: u8 => align_self,
        align_items_is_last_baseline: bool => align_items_is_last_baseline,
        align_self_is_last_baseline: bool => align_self_is_last_baseline,
        align_content_is_last_baseline: bool => align_content_is_last_baseline,
        align_content: u8 => align_content,
        justify_content: u8 => justify_content,
        justify_items: u8 => justify_items,
        justify_self: u8 => justify_self,
        align_items_overflow: u8 => align_items_overflow,
        justify_items_overflow: u8 => justify_items_overflow,
        align_self_overflow: u8 => align_self_overflow,
        justify_self_overflow: u8 => justify_self_overflow,
        align_content_overflow: u8 => align_content_overflow,
        justify_content_overflow: u8 => justify_content_overflow,
        flex_basis_is_content: bool => flex_basis.is_content,
    }
}

macro_rules! reference_accessors {
    ($($group:ident: { $($name:ident: $ty:ty => $($field:ident).+,)+ })+) => {
        impl<'a> ComputedValuesView<'a> {
            $($(
                #[inline]
                pub(crate) fn $name(self) -> &'a $ty {
                    &self.$group().$($field).+
                }
            )+)+
        }
    };
}

reference_accessors! {
    sizing: {
        width: ComputedSize => width,
        height: ComputedSize => height,
        min_width: ComputedSize => min_width,
        min_height: ComputedSize => min_height,
        max_width: ComputedSize => max_width,
        max_height: ComputedSize => max_height,
    }
    box_values: {
        column_width: ComputedSize => column_width,
    }
    surround: {
        margin_top: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto => margin.top,
        margin_right: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto => margin.right,
        margin_bottom: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto => margin.bottom,
        margin_left: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto => margin.left,
        padding_top: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto => padding.top,
        padding_right: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto => padding.right,
        padding_bottom: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto => padding.bottom,
        padding_left: ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto => padding.left,
    }
    alignment: {
        row_gap: ComputedGap => row_gap,
        column_gap: ComputedGap => column_gap,
    }
}

impl<'a> ComputedValuesView<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn block_ellipsis(self) -> &'a StyleValueData {
        self.inherited_text()
            .block_ellipsis
            .data()
            .expect("computed block-ellipsis has a style value")
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn of(groups: &'a crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroups) -> Self {
        Self(StyleRecordGroups::of(groups))
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn of_record_groups(groups: &'a StyleRecordGroups) -> Self {
        Self(groups)
    }

    /// The groups the view reads.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn record_groups(self) -> &'a StyleRecordGroups {
        self.0
    }

    #[inline]
    fn native_group<T>(self, group_index: usize) -> &'a T {
        let payload = self.0.0[group_index].as_ptr();
        // SAFETY: The payload is the Rust-defined group struct itself; C++
        // derives its mirror from the cbindgen twin of the same type, and the
        // node's ComputedValues keep it alive while readers exist.
        unsafe { &*payload.cast::<T>() }
    }

    /// The element's color, which `currentcolor` in its groups resolves to.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn current_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.inherited_text().color
    }

    pub(crate) fn border_top_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.border().border_top.color.resolve(self.current_color())
    }

    pub(crate) fn border_right_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.border().border_right.color.resolve(self.current_color())
    }

    pub(crate) fn border_bottom_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.border().border_bottom.color.resolve(self.current_color())
    }

    pub(crate) fn border_left_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.border().border_left.color.resolve(self.current_color())
    }

    pub(crate) fn text_decoration_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.text_reset().text_decoration_color.resolve(self.current_color())
    }

    pub(crate) fn outline_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.misc_layout().outline_color.resolve(self.current_color())
    }

    pub(crate) fn column_rule_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.misc_layout().column_rule_color.resolve(self.current_color())
    }

    pub(crate) fn background_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.background().background_color.resolve(self.current_color())
    }

    #[inline]
    fn content(self) -> &'a ContentValues {
        self.native_group(group_index::CONTENT)
    }

    /// Whether `counter-reset` names a counter counting down from its own last item, which the
    /// layout tree build cannot renumber without visiting every item again.
    pub(crate) fn counter_reset_has_reversed_counter(self) -> bool {
        match self.content().counter_reset.data() {
            Some(StyleValueData::CounterDefinitions(counter_definitions_payload)) => {
                let CounterDefinitionsPayload { counter_definitions } = &**counter_definitions_payload;
                counter_definitions
                    .as_slice()
                    .iter()
                    .any(crate::css::style_value::RetainedCounterDefinition::is_reversed)
            }
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    /// The computed `content` value.
    pub(crate) fn content_value(self) -> Option<&'a StyleValueData> {
        self.content().content.data()
    }

    /// The computed `quotes` value.
    pub(crate) fn quotes_value(self) -> Option<&'a StyleValueData> {
        self.inherited_list().quotes.data()
    }

    /// The `counter-reset` list, empty for `none`.
    pub(crate) fn counter_reset(self) -> &'a [crate::css::style_value::RetainedCounterDefinition] {
        counter_definitions(&self.content().counter_reset)
    }

    /// The `counter-increment` list, empty for `none`.
    pub(crate) fn counter_increment(self) -> &'a [crate::css::style_value::RetainedCounterDefinition] {
        counter_definitions(&self.content().counter_increment)
    }

    /// The `counter-set` list, empty for `none`.
    pub(crate) fn counter_set(self) -> &'a [crate::css::style_value::RetainedCounterDefinition] {
        counter_definitions(&self.content().counter_set)
    }

    /// Whether none of `counter-reset`, `counter-increment` and `counter-set` names a counter, so
    /// that regenerating the content cannot renumber anything around it.
    pub(crate) fn counter_properties_are_none(self) -> bool {
        let content = self.content();
        let is_none =
            |handle: &ComputedStyleValueHandle| matches!(handle.data(), None | Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { .. }));
        is_none(&content.counter_increment) && is_none(&content.counter_reset) && is_none(&content.counter_set)
    }

    /// Whether `content` is a bare keyword, which is what `normal` and `none` both spell.
    pub(crate) fn content_is_keyword(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.content().content.data(),
            None | Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { .. })
        )
    }

    /// Whether `content` is a list of nothing but strings: content a box can be regenerated with
    /// in place, because no counter, quote or `attr()` in it depends on where the box ends up.
    pub(crate) fn content_is_strings_only(self) -> bool {
        let Some(StyleValueData::Content(content_payload)) = self.content().content.data() else {
            return false;
        };
        let ContentPayload { content, .. } = &**content_payload;
        let Some(StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. }) = content.optional_data() else {
            return false;
        };
        values
            .as_slice()
            .iter()
            .all(|item| matches!(item.optional_data(), Some(StyleValueData::String { .. })))
    }

    /// Whether the style can move the generated-content state a later sibling reads: any counter
    /// it touches, or a quote its content opens or closes.
    pub(crate) fn affects_generated_content_state(self) -> bool {
        !self.counter_properties_are_none() || self.content_opens_or_closes_quotes()
    }

    /// Whether `content` opens or closes a quote, which moves the quote depth that every quote after it reads.
    pub(crate) fn content_opens_or_closes_quotes(self) -> bool {
        self.content_quote_keywords().next().is_some()
    }

    pub(crate) fn content_quote_transfer(self) -> QuoteTransfer {
        use crate::css::style_compute::keyword;
        self.content_quote_keywords()
            .fold(QuoteTransfer::IDENTITY, |transfer, quote_keyword| {
                transfer.then_quote(matches!(quote_keyword, keyword::OPEN_QUOTE | keyword::NO_OPEN_QUOTE))
            })
    }

    fn content_quote_keywords(self) -> impl Iterator<Item = u16> + 'a {
        use crate::css::style_compute::keyword;
        let values = match self.content().content.data() {
            Some(StyleValueData::Content(content_payload)) => {
                let ContentPayload { content, .. } = &**content_payload;
                match content.optional_data() {
                    Some(StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. }) => values.as_slice(),
                    _ => &[],
                }
            }
            _ => &[],
        };
        values.iter().filter_map(|item| match item.optional_data() {
            Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword })
                if matches!(
                    *keyword,
                    keyword::OPEN_QUOTE | keyword::CLOSE_QUOTE | keyword::NO_OPEN_QUOTE | keyword::NO_CLOSE_QUOTE
                ) =>
            {
                Some(*keyword)
            }
            _ => None,
        })
    }

    /// Whether `content` is a single image, which is what makes the element a replaced element
    /// whose box renders that image instead of its children.
    pub(crate) fn content_is_single_image(self) -> bool {
        let Some(StyleValueData::Content(content_payload)) = self.content().content.data() else {
            return false;
        };
        let ContentPayload { content, .. } = &**content_payload;
        let Some(StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. }) = content.optional_data() else {
            return false;
        };
        let values = values.as_slice();
        values.len() == 1
            && matches!(
                values[0].optional_data(),
                Some(
                    StyleValueData::Image { .. }
                        | StyleValueData::ImageSet { .. }
                        | StyleValueData::LinearGradient { .. }
                        | StyleValueData::ConicGradient { .. }
                        | StyleValueData::RadialGradient { .. }
                )
            )
    }

    #[inline]

    /// Whether `content` computes to the keyword `none`. The property takes exactly two keywords,
    /// so a keyword that is not `none` is `normal`.
    pub(crate) fn content_keyword_is_none(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.content().content.data(),
            Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) if *keyword == crate::css::css_enums::keyword::NONE
        )
    }

    /// Whether `line-height` computes to `normal`, which sizes an inline box by the metrics of every font its
    /// glyphs are set in rather than by its first available font alone.
    pub(crate) fn line_height_is_normal(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.font().line_height.data(),
            Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) if *keyword == crate::css::css_enums::keyword::NORMAL
        )
    }

    /// Whether `list-style-type` computes to `none`, the marker that renders nothing.
    pub(crate) fn list_style_type_is_none(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.inherited_list().list_style_type.data(),
            Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) if *keyword == crate::css::css_enums::keyword::NONE
        )
    }

    /// Whether `list-style-position` computes to `inside`, which puts the marker box inside the
    /// principal block box rather than outside it.
    pub(crate) fn list_style_position_is_inside(self) -> bool {
        self.bit(StyleBitField::ListStylePosition) == crate::css::css_enums::list_style_position::INSIDE
    }

    /// Whether the style names an image its box paints only once the host loads it: one in its background, mask, border
    /// image or list marker, but a gradient, which paints from the style alone.
    pub(crate) fn names_loaded_images(self) -> bool {
        fn names_loaded_image(value: Option<&StyleValueData>) -> bool {
            match value {
                None
                | Some(
                    StyleValueData::Keyword { .. }
                    | StyleValueData::LinearGradient { .. }
                    | StyleValueData::ConicGradient { .. }
                    | StyleValueData::RadialGradient { .. },
                ) => false,
                Some(StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. }) => values
                    .as_slice()
                    .iter()
                    .any(|value| names_loaded_image(value.optional_data())),
                Some(_) => true,
            }
        }
        [
            &self.background().background_image,
            &self.mask().mask_image,
            &self.border().border_image_source,
            &self.mask().mask_border_source,
            &self.inherited_list().list_style_image,
        ]
        .into_iter()
        .any(|image| names_loaded_image(image.data()))
    }

    /// Whether `list-style-image` names an image, which a list marker then shows instead of its
    /// marker string.
    pub(crate) fn list_style_image_is_set(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.inherited_list().list_style_image.data(),
            Some(
                StyleValueData::Image { .. }
                    | StyleValueData::ImageSet { .. }
                    | StyleValueData::LinearGradient { .. }
                    | StyleValueData::ConicGradient { .. }
                    | StyleValueData::RadialGradient { .. }
            )
        )
    }
