/// # Safety
/// The caller must not change the rule's values while it uses the returned view.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_font_feature_values_family_at(
    owner: &FontFeatureValuesRule,
    index: usize,
) -> FfiUtf16View<'_> {
    // SAFETY: The caller reads the family before it next changes the rule's values.
    let data = unsafe { owner.data.try_borrow_unguarded() }.expect("the values are not being changed");
    FfiUtf16View::from_utf16(data.families[index].units())
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) unsafe fn rust_font_feature_values_set_families(
    owner: &FontFeatureValuesRule,
    families: *const FfiUtf16View,
    count: usize,
) {
    let families = (0..count)
        .map(|index| CssString::from_utf16(&unsafe { (*families.add(index)).to_utf16() }.unwrap()))
        .collect();
    Arc::make_mut(&mut owner.data.borrow_mut()).families = families;
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_font_feature_values_count(
    owner: &FontFeatureValuesRule,
    kind: FontFeatureValuesRuleKind,
) -> usize {
    owner.data.borrow().maps[kind as usize].entries.len()
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_font_feature_values_find(
    owner: &FontFeatureValuesRule,
    kind: FontFeatureValuesRuleKind,
    name: FfiUtf16View,
) -> usize {
    let name = name.to_utf16().unwrap();
    owner.data.borrow().maps[kind as usize]
        .indices
        .get(name.as_slice())
        .copied()
        .unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
}

/// # Safety
/// The caller must not change the rule's values while it uses the returned entry.
#[cfg(test)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_font_feature_values_at(
    owner: &FontFeatureValuesRule,
    kind: FontFeatureValuesRuleKind,
    index: usize,
) -> FfiFeatureValueEntry<'_> {
    // SAFETY: The caller reads the entry before it next changes the rule's values.
    let data = unsafe { owner.data.try_borrow_unguarded() }.expect("the values are not being changed");
    let entry = &data.maps[kind as usize].entries[index];
    FfiFeatureValueEntry {
        name: FfiUtf16View::from_utf16(&entry.name),
        values: entry.values.as_ptr(),
        count: entry.values.len(),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_font_feature_values_set(
    owner: &FontFeatureValuesRule,
    kind: FontFeatureValuesRuleKind,
    name: FfiUtf16View,
    values: *const u32,
    count: usize,
) {
    let name = name.to_utf16().unwrap();
    // Copy borrowed inputs before COW can release or replace their storage.
    let values = (0..count)
        .map(|index| unsafe { *values.add(index) })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    owner.set_value(kind, &name, values);
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_font_feature_values_remove(
    owner: &FontFeatureValuesRule,
    kind: FontFeatureValuesRuleKind,
    name: FfiUtf16View,
) -> bool {
    owner.remove_value(kind, &name.to_utf16().unwrap())
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_font_feature_values_clear(owner: &FontFeatureValuesRule, kind: FontFeatureValuesRuleKind) {
    owner.clear_values(kind);
}

/// The OpenType features a style asks of a font, by tag, the later setting of a tag winning.
#[derive(Default)]
/// Each feature's tag, its value, and whether font-feature-settings set it.
struct ShapeFeatures(Vec<(u32, u32, bool)>);

impl ShapeFeatures {
    fn set(&mut self, tag: &[u8; 4], value: u32) {
        self.set_from(tag, value, false);
    }

    fn set_from(&mut self, tag: &[u8; 4], value: u32, set_by_feature_settings: bool) {
        let tag = u32::from_be_bytes(*tag);
        match self.0.iter_mut().find(|(existing, ..)| *existing == tag) {
            Some(feature) => (feature.1, feature.2) = (value, set_by_feature_settings),
            None => self.0.push((tag, value, set_by_feature_settings)),
        }
    }
}

/// The keywords a computed `font-variant-*` tuple holds, in its slot order: absent ones are `None`.
fn tuple_keywords(value: Option<&StyleValueData>) -> impl Iterator<Item = Option<u16>> + '_ {
    let slots = match value {
        Some(StyleValueData::Tuple { values }) => values.as_slice(),
        _ => &[],
    };
    slots.iter().map(|slot| match slot.optional_data() {
        Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) => Some(*keyword),
        _ => None,
    })
}

fn keyword_of(value: Option<&StyleValueData>) -> Option<u16> {
    match value {
        Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) => Some(*keyword),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn integer_of(value: &StyleValueData) -> Option<i32> {
    match value {
        StyleValueData::Integer { value } => Some(*value),
        calculated @ StyleValueData::Calculated { .. } => {
            crate::css::calc::resolve_calculated_integer_without_context(calculated)
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// The OpenType features the computed values of a font resolution request ask for, by
/// `FontResolutionFeatureInput` and null for a property with its initial value. The names in
/// `font-variant-alternates` are looked up in a family's `@font-feature-values` through `lookup`,
/// when `family_values` is not null. Each feature goes to `append` as a big-endian tag, a value,
/// and whether font-feature-settings set it.
/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts-4/#feature-variation-precedence
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `values` must address `FONT_RESOLUTION_FEATURE_INPUT_COUNT` null or live style values, and the
/// callbacks must accept `family_values` and `features`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_font_shape_features(
    values: *const *const c_void,
    family_values: *const c_void,
    lookup: unsafe extern "C" fn(*const c_void, FontFeatureValuesRuleKind, FfiUtf16View, &mut usize) -> *const u32,
    features: *mut c_void,
    append: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u32, u32, bool),
) {
    use crate::css::css_enums::keyword::*;
    use crate::css::style::bridge::{FONT_RESOLUTION_FEATURE_INPUT_COUNT, FontResolutionFeatureInput as Input};
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let values = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(values, FONT_RESOLUTION_FEATURE_INPUT_COUNT) };
    let value = |input: Input| unsafe { values[input as usize].cast::<StyleValueData>().as_ref() };
    let mut shape = ShapeFeatures::default();

    // 10. Font features implied by the value of the font-variant property, the related font-variant
    //     subproperties and any other CSS property that uses OpenType features (e.g. the
    //     font-kerning property) are applied.
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-variant-ligatures-prop
    let optimize_speed = keyword_of(value(Input::TextRendering)) == Some(OPTIMIZESPEED);
    let ligatures = value(Input::FontVariantLigatures).filter(|ligatures| keyword_of(Some(ligatures)) != Some(NORMAL));
    if keyword_of(ligatures) == Some(NONE) || (ligatures.is_none() && optimize_speed) {
        // AD-HOC: text-rendering: optimizeSpeed disables the ligatures normal enables.
        for tag in [b"liga", b"clig", b"dlig", b"hlig", b"calt"] {
            shape.set(tag, 0);
        }
    } else if ligatures.is_none() {
        // A value of normal specifies that common default features are enabled.
        shape.set(b"liga", 1);
        shape.set(b"clig", 1);
    }
    for keyword in tuple_keywords(ligatures).flatten() {
        let (tags, value): (&[&[u8; 4]], u32) = match keyword {
            COMMON_LIGATURES => (&[b"liga", b"clig"], 1),
            NO_COMMON_LIGATURES => (&[b"liga", b"clig"], 0),
            DISCRETIONARY_LIGATURES => (&[b"dlig"], 1),
            NO_DISCRETIONARY_LIGATURES => (&[b"dlig"], 0),
            HISTORICAL_LIGATURES => (&[b"hlig"], 1),
            NO_HISTORICAL_LIGATURES => (&[b"hlig"], 0),
            CONTEXTUAL => (&[b"calt"], 1),
            NO_CONTEXTUAL => (&[b"calt"], 0),
            _ => continue,
        };
        tags.iter().for_each(|tag| shape.set(tag, value));
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-variant-position-prop
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-variant-caps-prop
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-variant-numeric-prop
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-variant-east-asian-prop
    let keywords = [Input::FontVariantPosition, Input::FontVariantCaps]
        .into_iter()
        .map(|input| keyword_of(value(input)))
        .chain(tuple_keywords(value(Input::FontVariantNumeric)))
        .chain(tuple_keywords(value(Input::FontVariantEastAsian)));
    for keyword in keywords.flatten() {
        let tags: &[&[u8; 4]] = match keyword {
            SUB => &[b"subs"],
            SUPER => &[b"sups"],
            SMALL_CAPS => &[b"smcp"],
            ALL_SMALL_CAPS => &[b"c2sc", b"smcp"],
            PETITE_CAPS => &[b"pcap"],
            ALL_PETITE_CAPS => &[b"c2pc", b"pcap"],
            UNICASE => &[b"unic"],
            TITLING_CAPS => &[b"titl"],
            OLDSTYLE_NUMS => &[b"onum"],
            LINING_NUMS => &[b"lnum"],
            PROPORTIONAL_NUMS => &[b"pnum"],
            TABULAR_NUMS => &[b"tnum"],
            DIAGONAL_FRACTIONS => &[b"frac"],
            STACKED_FRACTIONS => &[b"afrc"],
            ORDINAL => &[b"ordn"],
            SLASHED_ZERO => &[b"zero"],
            JIS78 => &[b"jp78"],
            JIS83 => &[b"jp83"],
            JIS90 => &[b"jp90"],
            JIS04 => &[b"jp04"],
            SIMPLIFIED => &[b"smpl"],
            TRADITIONAL => &[b"trad"],
            FULL_WIDTH => &[b"fwid"],
            PROPORTIONAL_WIDTH => &[b"pwid"],
            RUBY => &[b"ruby"],
            _ => continue,
        };
        tags.iter().for_each(|tag| shape.set(tag, 1));
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-variant-alternates-prop
    // FIXME: These values never apply to generic font families
    let alternates = match value(Input::FontVariantAlternates) {
        Some(StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. }) => values.as_slice(),
        _ => &[],
    };
    for alternate in alternates.iter().map(|alternate| alternate.data()) {
        let StyleValueData::Function(function_payload) = alternate else {
            if keyword_of(Some(alternate)) == Some(HISTORICAL_FORMS) {
                shape.set(b"hist", 1);
            }
            continue;
        };
        let FunctionPayload { name, value } = &**function_payload;
        let Some(kind) = [
            ("stylistic", FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Stylistic),
            ("styleset", FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Styleset),
            ("character-variant", FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::CharacterVariant),
            ("swash", FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Swash),
            ("ornaments", FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Ornaments),
            ("annotation", FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Annotation),
        ]
        .into_iter()
        .find_map(|(function, kind)| equals_ascii_case_insensitive(name.units(), function.as_bytes()).then_some(kind)) else {
            continue;
        };
        let names = match value.data() {
            StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. } => values.as_slice(),
            _ => &[],
        };
        for feature_name in names {
            let feature_name = match feature_name.data() {
                StyleValueData::CustomIdent { custom_ident } => custom_ident.units(),
                StyleValueData::String { string, .. } => string.units(),
                _ => continue,
            };
            if family_values.is_null() {
                continue;
            }
            let mut count = 0;
            // SAFETY: The callback answers with `count` values that live through this call.
            let feature_values =
                unsafe { lookup(family_values, kind, FfiUtf16View::from_utf16(feature_name), &mut count) };
            if feature_values.is_null() || count == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let feature_values = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(feature_values, count) };
            let first = feature_values[0];
            match kind {
                // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#multi-value-features
                // Values between 1 and 99 enable OpenType features ss01 through ss99 and cv01
                // through cv99; greater ones and 0 enable none. A second character-variant value
                // is the value passed for the feature.
                FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Styleset => {
                    for &index in feature_values.iter().filter(|&&index| (1..=99).contains(&index)) {
                        shape.set(&numbered_tag(b"ss", index), 1);
                    }
                }
                FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::CharacterVariant if (1..=99).contains(&first) => {
                    shape.set(&numbered_tag(b"cv", first), feature_values.get(1).copied().unwrap_or(1));
                }
                FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::CharacterVariant => {}
                FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Swash => {
                    shape.set(b"swsh", first);
                    shape.set(b"cswh", first);
                }
                FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Stylistic => shape.set(b"salt", first),
                FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Ornaments => shape.set(b"ornm", first),
                _ => shape.set(b"nalt", first),
            }
        }
    }

    // FIXME: vkrn should be enabled for vertical text.
    // AD-HOC: Kerning is off with text-rendering: optimizeSpeed unless font-kerning asks for it.
    let kerning = match keyword_of(value(Input::FontKerning)) {
        Some(NONE) => 0,
        Some(NORMAL) => 1,
        _ => u32::from(!optimize_speed),
    };
    shape.set(b"kern", kerning);

    // 13. Font features implied by the value of font-feature-settings property are applied.
    if let Some(StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. }) = value(Input::FontFeatureSettings) {
        for setting in values.as_slice() {
            if let StyleValueData::OpenTypeTagged(open_type_tagged) = setting.data()
                && let Some(setting) = integer_of(open_type_tagged.value.data())
            {
                let packed_tag = open_type_tagged.packed_tag;
                // NB: A feature setting is kept as one byte.
                shape.set_from(&packed_tag.to_be_bytes(), u32::from(setting as u8), true);
            }
        }
    }

    for (tag, value, set_by_feature_settings) in shape.0 {
        // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
        unsafe { append(features, tag, value, set_by_feature_settings) };
    }
}

/// `ss01` through `ss99` and `cv01` through `cv99`.
fn numbered_tag(prefix: &[u8; 2], index: u32) -> [u8; 4] {
    [
        prefix[0],
        prefix[1],
        b'0' + (index / 10) as u8,
        b'0' + (index % 10) as u8,
    ]
}

/// The font variation axes a computed `font-variation-settings` value sets, in order, each handed
/// to `append` as a big-endian tag and a value.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `value` must be null or point to a live style value, and `append` must accept `axes`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_font_variation_axes(
    value: *const c_void,
    axes: *mut c_void,
    append: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u32, f64),
) {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let Some(StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. }) = (unsafe { value.cast::<StyleValueData>().as_ref() }) else {
        return;
    };
    for setting in values.as_slice() {
        let StyleValueData::OpenTypeTagged(open_type_tagged_payload) = setting.data() else {
            continue;
        };
        let OpenTypeTaggedPayload { packed_tag, value, .. } = &**open_type_tagged_payload;
        let value = match value.data() {
            StyleValueData::Number { value } => Some(*value),
            calculated => crate::css::calc::resolve_calculated_number_without_context(calculated),
        };
        if let Some(value) = value {
            // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
            unsafe { append(axes, *packed_tag, value) };
        }
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/css/font_matching.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

/// A face of the family being matched, as the font matching algorithm weighs it: its weight range,
/// its slope, and its width as one of the standard width buckets.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiFontMatchingCandidate {
    pub weight_min: i32,
    pub weight_max: i32,
    pub slope: i32,
    pub width: u32,
}

/// Writes the order in which to try a family's faces for the desired weight, width and slope to
/// `order`, by index, and returns how many it wrote: a partial implementation of
/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts-4/#font-matching-algorithm. The first face that renders is the
/// match.
fn font_matching_order(
    candidates: &[FfiFontMatchingCandidate],
    weight: i32,
    width: u32,
    slope: i32,
    order: &mut [usize],
) -> usize {
    let mut matching: Vec<usize> = (0..candidates.len()).collect();
    let mut narrow_to = |matches: &dyn Fn(&FfiFontMatchingCandidate) -> bool| {
        if matching.iter().any(|&index| matches(&candidates[index])) {
            matching.retain(|&index| matches(&candidates[index]));
        }
    };

    // 1. font-width is tried first.
    narrow_to(&|candidate| candidate.width == width);
    // 2. font-style is tried next.
    // We don't have complete support of italic and oblique fonts, so matching on font-style can be simplified to:
    // If a matching slope is found, all faces which don't have that matching slope are excluded from the matching set.
    narrow_to(&|candidate| candidate.slope == slope);
    matching.sort_by_key(|&index| candidates[index].weight_min);

    // The faces from the lightest one that matches on, and up to the heaviest one that does.
    let first = |matches: fn(&FfiFontMatchingCandidate, i32) -> bool| {
        matching
            .iter()
            .position(|&index| matches(&candidates[index], weight))
            .unwrap_or(matching.len())
    };
    let last = |matches: fn(&FfiFontMatchingCandidate, i32) -> bool| {
        matching
            .iter()
            .rposition(|&index| matches(&candidates[index], weight))
            .map_or(0, |last| last + 1)
    };
    let mut length = 0;
    let mut try_faces = |faces: &mut dyn Iterator<Item = &usize>| {
        for &index in faces {
            // A face that did not render the first time it was tried does not render later either.
            if !order[..length].contains(&index) {
                order[length] = index;
                length += 1;
            }
        }
    };

    // 3. font-weight is matched next.
    // If the matching set after performing the steps above includes faces with weight values containing the
    // font-weight desired value, faces with weight values which do not include the desired font-weight value are
    // removed from the matching set.
    // FIXME: This tries every face from the first one that contains the desired value instead.
    try_faces(&mut matching[first(|face, weight| (face.weight_min..=face.weight_max).contains(&weight))..].iter());

    // If there is no face which contains the desired value, a weight value is chosen using the rules below:
    if (400..=500).contains(&weight) {
        // - If the desired weight is inclusively between 400 and 500, weights greater than or equal to the target
        //   weight are checked in ascending order until 500 is hit and checked, followed by weights less than the
        //   target weight in descending order, followed by weights greater than 500, until a match is found.
        let heavier = first(|face, weight| face.weight_min >= weight);
        let above_500 = heavier.max(first(|face, _| face.weight_min > 500));
        try_faces(&mut matching[heavier..above_500].iter());
        try_faces(&mut matching[..last(|face, weight| face.weight_max < weight)].iter().rev());
        try_faces(&mut matching[above_500..].iter());
    } else if weight < 400 {
        // - If the desired weight is less than 400, weights less than or equal to the desired weight are checked in
        //   descending order followed by weights above the desired weight in ascending order until a match is found.
        try_faces(&mut matching[..last(|face, weight| face.weight_max <= weight)].iter().rev());
        try_faces(&mut matching[first(|face, weight| face.weight_min > weight)..].iter());
    } else {
        // - If the desired weight is greater than 500, weights greater than or equal to the desired weight are
        //   checked in ascending order followed by weights below the desired weight in descending order until a
        //   match is found.
        try_faces(&mut matching[first(|face, weight| face.weight_min >= weight)..].iter());
        try_faces(&mut matching[..last(|face, weight| face.weight_max < weight)].iter().rev());
    }
    length
}

/// Writes the order to try `candidates` in to `order`, which holds as many entries, and answers how many it wrote.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_font_matching_order(
    candidates: ak::Span<'_, FfiFontMatchingCandidate>,
    weight: i32,
    width: u32,
    slope: i32,
    order: ak::SpanMut<'_, usize>,
) -> usize {
    let order = order.into_slice();
    assert_eq!(candidates.as_slice().len(), order.len());
    font_matching_order(candidates.as_slice(), weight, width, slope, order)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn weights_are_tried_in_the_order_the_spec_gives() {
        let faces = [100, 300, 500, 700, 900].map(|weight| FfiFontMatchingCandidate {
            weight_min: weight,
            weight_max: weight,
            slope: 0,
            width: 5,
        });
        let order = |weight| {
            let mut order = [0; 5];
            assert_eq!(font_matching_order(&faces, weight, 5, 0, &mut order), 5);
            order
        };
        assert_eq!(order(400), [2, 1, 0, 3, 4]);
        assert_eq!(order(350), [1, 0, 2, 3, 4]);
        assert_eq!(order(600), [3, 4, 2, 1, 0]);
        assert_eq!(order(700), [3, 4, 2, 1, 0]);
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/css/host_shared.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! A pointer to a value the style update only borrows.
//!
//! The evaluation step reads computed style values, style-group payloads, longhand tables and
//! animated overlays that somebody else owns: the retained catalog, an earlier pass, or the host.
//! A raw pointer is neither `Send` nor `Sync`, so every struct holding one stops a walk's read
//! side or scratch from being shareable, even though the step never writes through it and never
//! touches its reference count. [`HostShared`] is that pointer with the contract written down.

use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};

/// A borrowed pointer to a value that is frozen for the length of a style update.
///
/// This is a plain `*const T` with one word of layout and no ownership: it retains nothing on
/// construction and releases nothing on drop. What it adds is the thread bound the raw pointer
/// refuses to give.
#[repr(transparent)]
pub(crate) struct HostShared<T: ?Sized>(*const T);

// SAFETY: The invariant, which every construction site upholds and the whole borrow-only
// computation contract rests on:
//
// 1. The pointee is immutable for the length of a style update. A style value, a style-group
//    payload, a frozen `ComputedLonghandTable` and an installed animated overlay are all written
//    once, before the walk that reads them begins, and are replaced rather than mutated.
// 2. No reference count on the pointee is touched through this handle. `HostShared` owns nothing:
//    the reference belongs to the catalog entry, the produced output or the host object that
//    minted it, and every retain and release happens in the serial installer or in a host round,
//    never inside an evaluation step.
//
// Together those make a `&HostShared<T>` - and the `HostShared<T>` itself, which is a copy of the
// same borrowed address - safe to hand to any number of workers at once, because reading an
// immutable value from several threads is not a race and no reference count moves.
// The invariant above covers who follows the pointer and when; it says nothing about what the
// pointee does with a shared reference, so a pointee that mutates through `&T` (a `Cell`) must not
// ride along. Requiring `T: Sync` keeps that the compiler's decision rather than the invariant's.
unsafe impl<T: Sync + ?Sized> Send for HostShared<T> {}
unsafe impl<T: Sync + ?Sized> Sync for HostShared<T> {}

impl<T: ?Sized> Clone for HostShared<T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        *self
    }
}

impl<T: ?Sized> Copy for HostShared<T> {}

impl<T: ?Sized> PartialEq for HostShared<T> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        std::ptr::eq(self.0, other.0)
    }
}

impl<T: ?Sized> Eq for HostShared<T> {}

impl<T> Hash for HostShared<T> {
    fn hash<H: Hasher>(&self, state: &mut H) {
        self.0.hash(state);
    }
}

impl<T: ?Sized> std::fmt::Debug for HostShared<T> {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(formatter, "HostShared({:p})", self.0)
    }
}

impl<T> Default for HostShared<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::null()
    }
}

impl<T> HostShared<T> {
    pub(crate) const fn null() -> Self {
        Self(std::ptr::null())
    }

    pub(crate) const fn new(pointer: *const T) -> Self {
        Self(pointer)
    }

    pub(crate) const fn as_ptr(self) -> *const T {
        self.0
    }

    pub(crate) fn cast<U>(self) -> HostShared<U> {
        HostShared(self.0.cast())
    }

    /// The pointee, for a caller that has already established it is live.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// The same requirements as dereferencing the raw pointer: it must be non-null, aligned and
    /// name a live value for `'a`.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn deref<'a>(self) -> &'a T {
        unsafe { &*self.0 }
    }

    /// The pointee, or `None` when the handle is null.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// A non-null handle must name a live value for `'a`.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn as_ref<'a>(self) -> Option<&'a T> {
        unsafe { self.0.as_ref() }
    }
}

#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiImportRuleView<'a> {
    pub url: *const c_void,
    pub has_layer: bool,
    pub layer: FfiUtf16View<'a>,
    pub supports: *const FfiQueryHandle,
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_import_rule_retain(rule: *const ImportRuleData) -> *const ImportRuleData {
    if !rule.is_null() {
        unsafe { Arc::increment_strong_count(rule) };
    }
    rule
}

pub extern "C" fn rust_import_rule_release(rule: OwnedArc<ImportRuleData>) {

        has_layer: rule.layer.is_some(),
        layer: FfiUtf16View::from_utf16(layer),
        supports: rule.supports.as_ref().map_or(std::ptr::null(), Arc::as_ptr),
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/css/inline_style_blocks.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The declaration blocks of a document's style attributes, by their text, so that elements that
//! write the same text hold one block.

use crate::css::css_tokenizer::TokenizerInput;
use crate::css::declaration_block::{DeclarationBlock, SharedDeclarationBlock};
use crate::css::ffi_support::{FfiUtf16View, OwnedBox, ascii_lowercase};
use crate::css::style_value::RetainedString;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::hash::{BuildHasher, Hasher};

struct InlineStyleEntry {
    /// One byte per unit when the text is ASCII, as most style attributes are.
    text: RetainedString,
    quirks: bool,
    block: SharedDeclarationBlock,
}

/// A document's style attribute blocks, by their text and the quirks mode they were parsed in.
pub struct InlineStyleBlocks {
    /// The entries by the hash of their text and quirks mode, one per hash.
    blocks: HashMap<u64, InlineStyleEntry>,
    /// The entries whose hash an entry of `blocks` already has, which a 64-bit hash makes rare.
    collisions: Vec<InlineStyleEntry>,
    /// How many entries the cache holds before it drops those only it still holds: twice as many
    /// as the last drop kept, so dropping costs a constant per entry inserted.
    sweep_threshold: usize,
    /// Keyed at random, so that a page cannot make many texts fall into one bucket.
    hasher: std::collections::hash_map::RandomState,
}

/// How many entries the cache holds before it first drops those only it still holds.
const MINIMUM_SWEEP_THRESHOLD: usize = 256;

fn units(text: TokenizerInput<'_>) -> impl Iterator<Item = u16> + '_ {
    let (ascii, utf16): (&[u8], &[u16]) = match text {
        TokenizerInput::Latin1(bytes) => (bytes, &[]),
        TokenizerInput::Utf16(units) => (&[], units),
    };
    ascii.iter().map(|&byte| u16::from(byte)).chain(utf16.iter().copied())
}

/// Whether a block parsed from `text` may be shared by every element of the document that writes
/// it. A value that resolves a URL, reads an attribute or is random per element is not, and an
/// escape could spell the name of such a function.
fn is_cacheable(text: TokenizerInput<'_>) -> bool {
    const FUNCTIONS: [&[u8]; 5] = [b"url(", b"image-set(", b"src(", b"attr(", b"random("];
    let lowered: Vec<u16> = units(text).map(ascii_lowercase).collect();
    if lowered.contains(&u16::from(b'\\')) {
        return false;
    }
    !FUNCTIONS.iter().any(|function| {
        lowered.windows(function.len()).any(|window| {
            window
                .iter()
                .zip(function.iter())
                .all(|(&unit, &byte)| unit == u16::from(byte))
        })
    })
}

impl InlineStyleBlocks {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            blocks: HashMap::new(),
            collisions: Vec::new(),
            sweep_threshold: MINIMUM_SWEEP_THRESHOLD,
            hasher: std::collections::hash_map::RandomState::new(),
        }
    }

    fn hash(&self, text: TokenizerInput<'_>, quirks: bool) -> u64 {
        let mut hasher = self.hasher.build_hasher();
        hasher.write_u8(u8::from(quirks));
        for unit in units(text) {
            hasher.write_u16(unit);
        }
        hasher.finish()
    }

    fn entry_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.blocks.len() + self.collisions.len()
    }

    pub(crate) fn find(&self, text: TokenizerInput<'_>, quirks: bool) -> Option<SharedDeclarationBlock> {
        let matches = |entry: &&InlineStyleEntry| entry.quirks == quirks && units(entry.text.units()).eq(units(text));
        let entry = self.blocks.get(&self.hash(text, quirks))?;
        if matches(&entry) {
            return Some(entry.block.clone());
        }
        self.collisions.iter().find(matches).map(|entry| entry.block.clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn insert(&mut self, text: TokenizerInput<'_>, quirks: bool, block: &SharedDeclarationBlock) {
        if !is_cacheable(text) || self.find(text, quirks).is_some() {
            return;
        }
        if self.entry_count() >= self.sweep_threshold {
            self.sweep();
        }
        let entry = InlineStyleEntry {
            text: RetainedString::from_text(text),
            quirks,
            block: block.clone(),
        };
        match self.blocks.entry(self.hash(text, quirks)) {
            std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Vacant(slot) => {
                slot.insert(entry);
            }
            std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Occupied(_) => self.collisions.push(entry),
        }
    }

    /// Drops the entries whose block no element holds any more.
    fn sweep(&mut self) {
        self.blocks.retain(|_, entry| !entry.block.is_unique());
        self.collisions.retain(|entry| !entry.block.is_unique());
        self.sweep_threshold = (2 * self.entry_count()).max(MINIMUM_SWEEP_THRESHOLD);
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_inline_style_blocks_create() -> *mut InlineStyleBlocks {
    Box::into_raw(Box::new(InlineStyleBlocks::new()))
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_inline_style_blocks_destroy(blocks: OwnedBox<InlineStyleBlocks>) {
    drop(blocks);
}

/// A new declaration block holding the block of `text`, or null when no element wrote it.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_inline_style_blocks_find(
    blocks: &InlineStyleBlocks,
    text: FfiUtf16View,
    quirks: bool,
) -> *mut DeclarationBlock {
    let Some(text) = text.units() else {
        return std::ptr::null_mut();
    };
    blocks.find(text, quirks).map_or(std::ptr::null_mut(), |block| {
        Box::into_raw(Box::new(DeclarationBlock::new(block)))
    })
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_inline_style_blocks_insert(
    blocks: &mut InlineStyleBlocks,
    text: FfiUtf16View,
    quirks: bool,
    block: &DeclarationBlock,
) {
    if let Some(text) = text.units() {
        blocks.insert(text, quirks, &block.data());
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::css::parser::syntax_parser::parse_shared_block;
    use crate::css::parser::value_parser::ParseContext;
    use crate::css::style::pipeline::allocation_count::count_live_bytes;

    fn parse(text: &str) -> SharedDeclarationBlock {
        let units: Vec<u16> = text.encode_utf16().collect();
        let context = ParseContext::default();
        let parse = parse_shared_block(
            TokenizerInput::Utf16(&units),
            vec![crate::css::parser::syntax_parser::RuleContext::Style],
            Some(&context),
            false,
        );
        let block = unsafe {
            Box::from_raw(crate::css::parser::syntax_parser::rust_css_syntax_parse_declaration_block(&parse))
        };
        block.data()
    }

    fn ascii(text: &str) -> TokenizerInput<'_> {
        TokenizerInput::Latin1(text.as_bytes())
    }

    #[test]
    fn equal_texts_share_one_block() {
        let mut blocks = InlineStyleBlocks::new();
        let text = "color: red; margin-left: 3.5px";
        let block = parse(text);
        blocks.insert(ascii(text), false, &block);
        let utf16: Vec<u16> = text.encode_utf16().collect();
        let hit = blocks.find(TokenizerInput::Utf16(&utf16), false).unwrap();
        assert!(SharedDeclarationBlock::ptr_eq(&hit, &block));
        assert!(blocks.find(ascii(text), true).is_none());
        assert!(blocks.find(ascii("color: red"), false).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn texts_whose_values_differ_per_element_are_not_kept() {
        let mut blocks = InlineStyleBlocks::new();
        for text in [
            "background: URL(a.png)",
            "background-image: image-set(\"a.png\" 1x)",
            "width: attr(data-w px)",
            "width: random(1px, 2px)",
            "c\\olor: red",
        ] {
            blocks.insert(ascii(text), false, &parse(text));
            assert!(blocks.find(ascii(text), false).is_none(), "{text}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_sweep_drops_the_blocks_only_the_cache_holds() {
        let mut blocks = InlineStyleBlocks::new();
        let held = parse("order: 0");
        blocks.insert(ascii("order: 0"), false, &held);
        for index in 1..=MINIMUM_SWEEP_THRESHOLD {
            let text = format!("order: {index}");
            blocks.insert(ascii(&text), false, &parse(&text));
        }
        assert_eq!(blocks.entry_count(), 2);
        assert!(blocks.find(ascii("order: 0"), false).is_some());
        assert_eq!(blocks.sweep_threshold, MINIMUM_SWEEP_THRESHOLD);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_hit_costs_the_element_its_declaration_block_handle() {
        const COUNT: usize = 500;
        let mut blocks = InlineStyleBlocks::new();
        let text = "color: red; margin-left: 3.5px";
        blocks.insert(ascii(text), false, &parse(text));
        let mut handles = Vec::with_capacity(COUNT);
        let ((), bytes) = count_live_bytes(|| {
            for _ in 0..COUNT {
                handles.push(Box::new(DeclarationBlock::new(
                    blocks.find(ascii(text), false).unwrap(),
                )));
            }
        });
        let per_element = bytes as f64 / COUNT as f64;
        eprintln!("inline style, text another element repeats {per_element:.1} B (ceiling 24; 8 B, cached)");
        assert!(per_element <= 24.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn own_text_costs_its_block_handle_and_entry() {
        const COUNT: usize = 500;
        // NB: Pooled values in pairs no other text repeats, so that each text parses a block of its own.
        let texts: Vec<String> = (0..COUNT)
            .map(|index| format!("z-index: {}; order: {}", index % 100, index / 100))
            .collect();
        let mut blocks = InlineStyleBlocks::new();
        for text in &texts {
            parse(text);
        }
        let mut handles = Vec::with_capacity(COUNT);
        let ((), bytes) = count_live_bytes(|| {
            for text in &texts {
                let block = parse(text);
                blocks.insert(ascii(text), false, &block);
                handles.push(Box::new(DeclarationBlock::new(block)));
            }
        });
        let per_element = bytes as f64 / COUNT as f64;
        eprintln!("inline style, own text, 2 declarations {per_element:.1} B (ceiling 176; 16 + 16 B per declaration)");
        assert!(per_element <= 176.0);
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/css/media_list.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

use ak::Utf16StringUnits;

use crate::css::css_tokenizer::TokenizerInput;
use crate::css::ffi_support::{FfiUtf16View, OwnedBox};
use crate::css::parser::query_parser::{
    FfiMediaEnvironment, FfiQueryHandle, MediaEnvironment, MediaQuery, VisitQuerySerialization, invalid_media_query,
    media_query_handle, parse_media_query_list, resolve_query_feature,
};
use crate::css::serialize::TextSink;
use crate::css::thin_slice::ThinSlice;
use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// A media list's queries, held by one pointer with their count before them.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct MediaListData {
    pub(crate) queries: ThinSlice<Arc<FfiQueryHandle>>,
}

const _: () = {
    const fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
    assert_send_sync::<MediaListData>();
};

impl MediaListData {
    pub(crate) fn from_queries(queries: Vec<MediaQuery>) -> Self {
        Self {
            queries: queries.into_iter().map(media_query_handle).collect(),
        }
    }
}

struct MediaListState {
    data: Arc<MediaListData>,
    matches: Vec<bool>,
}

pub enum MediaListDeleteResult {
    Invalid,
    Removed,
    NotFound,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct MediaList {
    owner: Rc<RefCell<MediaListState>>,
}

impl MediaList {
    pub(crate) fn data(&self) -> Arc<MediaListData> {
        self.owner.borrow().data.clone()
    }

    /// A list of its own with the media queries of this one, as they are now.
    pub fn share(&self) -> Self {
        Self::new(self.owner.borrow().data.clone())
    }

    /// The number of media queries in the collection of media queries.
    pub fn length(&self) -> usize {
        self.owner.borrow().data.queries.len()
    }

    /// The serialization of the collection of media queries.
    pub fn media_text(&self) -> ak::Utf16String {
        let state = self.owner.borrow();
        let mut text = TextSink::new();
        for (index, query) in state.data.queries.iter().enumerate() {
            if index != 0 {
                text.push_ascii(", ");
            }
            query
                .media_text()
                .into_iter()
                .for_each(|unit| text.push_code_unit(unit));
        }
        text.into_utf16_string()
    }

    /// The serialization of the media query at the index of the collection of media queries, if it has one there.
    pub fn item(&self, index: usize) -> Option<ak::Utf16String> {
        self.owner
            .borrow()
            .data
            .queries
            .get(index)
            .map(|query| ak::Utf16String::from_utf16(&query.media_text()))
    }

    /// Replaces the collection of media queries with the result of parsing the text.
    pub fn set_media_text(&self, text: Utf16StringUnits<'_>) {
        self.set_text(text.into());
    }

    /// Whether the medium was added.
    pub fn append_medium(&self, medium: Utf16StringUnits<'_>) -> bool {
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#dom-medialist-appendmedium
        // 1. Let m be the result of parsing the given value.
        // 2. If m is null, then return.
        let Some(query) = parse_medium(medium.into()) else {
            return false;
        };
        // 3. If comparing m with any of the media queries in the collection of media queries returns true, then return.
        let text = query.media_text();
        let mut state = self.owner.borrow_mut();
        if state.data.queries.iter().any(|existing| existing.media_text() == text) {
            return false;
        }
        // 4. Append m to the collection of media queries.
        Arc::make_mut(&mut state.data).queries.push(query);
        state.matches.push(false);
        true
    }

    pub fn delete_medium(&self, medium: Utf16StringUnits<'_>) -> MediaListDeleteResult {
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#dom-medialist-deletemedium
        // 1. Let m be the result of parsing the given value.
        // 2. If m is null, then return.
        let Some(query) = parse_medium(medium.into()) else {
            return MediaListDeleteResult::Invalid;
        };
        // 3. Remove any media query from the collection of media queries for which comparing the media query with m
        //    returns true. If nothing was removed, then throw a NotFoundError exception.
        let text = query.media_text();
        let mut state = self.owner.borrow_mut();
        let mut removed = false;
        for index in (0..state.data.queries.len()).rev() {
            if state.data.queries[index].media_text() == text {
                Arc::make_mut(&mut state.data).queries.remove(index);
                state.matches.remove(index);
                removed = true;
            }
        }
        if removed {
            MediaListDeleteResult::Removed
        } else {
            MediaListDeleteResult::NotFound
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_text(&self, source: TokenizerInput<'_>) {
        let data = Arc::new(parse(source));
        *self.owner.borrow_mut() = MediaListState {
            matches: vec![false; data.queries.len()],
            data,
        };
    }

    pub fn matches(&self) -> bool {
        let state = self.owner.borrow();
        state.matches.is_empty() || state.matches.iter().any(|matches| *matches)
    }

    pub(crate) fn evaluate(&self, environment: MediaEnvironment<'_>) -> bool {
        let mut state = self.owner.borrow_mut();
        for index in 0..state.data.queries.len() {
            state.matches[index] = state.data.queries[index].matches_media(environment);
        }
        state.matches.is_empty() || state.matches.iter().any(|matches| *matches)
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_matches(&self, matches: &[bool]) {
        self.owner.borrow_mut().matches.copy_from_slice(matches);
    }

    pub(crate) fn new(data: Arc<MediaListData>) -> Self {
        Self {
            owner: Rc::new(RefCell::new(MediaListState {
                matches: vec![false; data.queries.len()],
                data,
            })),
        }
    }
}

fn parse(source: TokenizerInput<'_>) -> MediaListData {
    MediaListData::from_queries(
        parse_media_query_list(source, &resolve_query_feature).unwrap_or_else(|| vec![invalid_media_query()]),
    )
}

fn parse_medium(source: TokenizerInput<'_>) -> Option<Arc<FfiQueryHandle>> {
    let mut data = parse(source);
    match data.queries.len() {
        0 => Some(media_query_handle(invalid_media_query())),
        1 => Some(data.queries.remove(0)),
        _ => None,
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_media_list_create() -> *mut MediaList {
    Box::into_raw(Box::new(MediaList::new(Arc::default())))
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_media_list_retain(list: &MediaList) -> *mut MediaList {
    Box::into_raw(Box::new(list.clone()))
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn rust_media_list_share(list: &MediaList) -> *mut MediaList {
    Box::into_raw(Box::new(list.share()))
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_media_list_free(list: OwnedBox<MediaList>) {
    drop(list);
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_media_list_length(list: &MediaList) -> usize {
    list.length()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_media_list_set_text(list: &MediaList, source: FfiUtf16View) {
    list.set_text(source.units().unwrap());
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_media_list_serialize(
    list: &MediaList,
    context: *mut c_void,
    visit: VisitQuerySerialization,
) {
    let text = list.media_text();
    let units = text.to_utf16();
    unsafe { visit(context, units.as_ptr(), units.len()) };
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_media_list_item(
    list: &MediaList,
    index: usize,
    context: *mut c_void,
    visit: VisitQuerySerialization,
) -> bool {
    let Some(text) = list.item(index) else {
        return false;
    };
    let units = text.to_utf16();
    unsafe { visit(context, units.as_ptr(), units.len()) };
    true
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_media_list_matches(list: &MediaList) -> bool {
    list.matches()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_media_list_item_matches(list: &MediaList, index: usize) -> bool {
    list.owner.borrow().matches[index]
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_media_list_evaluate(list: &MediaList, environment: FfiMediaEnvironment<'_>) -> bool {
    list.evaluate(environment.borrow())
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/css/parser/arbitrary_substitution.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

use crate::css::css_tokenizer::ParserTokenKind;
use crate::css::parser::component_value::{ComponentKind, ComponentValue};
use crate::css::parser::value_parser::equals_ascii_case_insensitive;
use std::collections::HashSet;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction {
    Attr,
    DashedFunction,
    Env,
    If,
    Inherit,
    Var,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct SubstitutionFunctionsPresence {
    pub attr: bool,
    pub dashed_function: bool,
    pub env: bool,
    pub if_: bool,
    pub inherit: bool,
    pub var: bool,
}

impl SubstitutionFunctionsPresence {
    pub(crate) fn has_any(self) -> bool {
        self.attr || self.dashed_function || self.env || self.if_ || self.inherit || self.var
    }
}

pub(crate) fn arbitrary_substitution_function(name: &[u16]) -> Option<ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction> {
    if equals_ascii_case_insensitive(name, b"attr") {
        return Some(ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Attr);
    }
    if name.starts_with(&[u16::from(b'-'), u16::from(b'-')]) {
        return Some(ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::DashedFunction);
    }
    if equals_ascii_case_insensitive(name, b"env") {
        return Some(ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Env);
    }
    if equals_ascii_case_insensitive(name, b"if") {
        return Some(ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::If);
    }
    if equals_ascii_case_insensitive(name, b"inherit") {
        return Some(ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Inherit);
    }
    if equals_ascii_case_insensitive(name, b"var") {
        return Some(ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Var);
    }
    None
}

/// Stops at the first arbitrary substitution function.
/// Does not validate argument syntax: a matching function with invalid arguments still returns true.
pub(crate) fn contains_arbitrary_substitution_function(values: &[ComponentValue]) -> bool {
    values.iter().any(|value| match &value.kind {
        ComponentKind::Function { name, values } => {
            arbitrary_substitution_function(name).is_some() || contains_arbitrary_substitution_function(values)
        }
        ComponentKind::SimpleBlock { values, .. } => contains_arbitrary_substitution_function(values),
        ComponentKind::Token(_) => false,
    })
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum EndToken {
    Colon,
    Comma,
}

fn is_end_token(value: &ComponentValue, end_token: EndToken) -> bool {
    match end_token {
        EndToken::Colon => value.is_colon(),
        EndToken::Comma => value.is_comma(),
    }
}

fn nested_declaration_value_is_valid(values: &[ComponentValue]) -> bool {
    let mut position = 0;
    consume_declaration_value(values, &mut position, None, true, false);
    position == values.len()
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#typedef-declaration-value
fn consume_declaration_value(
    values: &[ComponentValue],
    position: &mut usize,
    end_token: Option<EndToken>,
    nested: bool,
    disallow_top_level_curly_blocks: bool,
) {
    while let Some(value) = values.get(*position) {
        let valid = match &value.kind {
            ComponentKind::Function { values, .. } => nested_declaration_value_is_valid(values),
            ComponentKind::SimpleBlock { opening, values } => {
                if !nested && disallow_top_level_curly_blocks && matches!(opening, ParserTokenKind::OpenCurly) {
                    false
                } else {
                    nested_declaration_value_is_valid(values)
                }
            }
            ComponentKind::Token(token) => match token {
                ParserTokenKind::EndOfFile
                | ParserTokenKind::BadString
                | ParserTokenKind::BadUrl
                | ParserTokenKind::Function(_)
                | ParserTokenKind::OpenCurly
                | ParserTokenKind::OpenParen
                | ParserTokenKind::OpenSquare
                | ParserTokenKind::CloseCurly
                | ParserTokenKind::CloseParen
                | ParserTokenKind::CloseSquare => false,
                ParserTokenKind::Semicolon => nested,
                ParserTokenKind::Delim(value) if *value == u32::from(b'!') => nested,
                _ => nested || !end_token.is_some_and(|end_token| is_end_token(value, end_token)),
            },
        };
        if !valid {
            break;
        }
        *position += 1;
    }
}

fn consume_declaration_value_as_span(
    values: &[ComponentValue],
    position: &mut usize,
    end_token: Option<EndToken>,
    disallow_top_level_curly_blocks: bool,
) -> bool {
    let start = *position;
    consume_declaration_value(values, position, end_token, false, disallow_top_level_curly_blocks);
    *position != start
}

fn parse_declaration_value_then_optional_declaration_value(
    values: &[ComponentValue],
    position: &mut usize,
    separator: EndToken,
) -> bool {
    if !consume_declaration_value_as_span(values, position, Some(separator), false) {
        return false;
    }
    if *position == values.len() {
        return matches!(separator, EndToken::Comma);
    }
    if !is_end_token(&values[*position], separator) {
        return false;
    }
    *position += 1;
    consume_declaration_value_as_span(values, position, None, false);
    true
}

fn discard_whitespace(values: &[ComponentValue], position: &mut usize) {
    while values.get(*position).is_some_and(ComponentValue::is_whitespace) {
        *position += 1;
    }
}

fn parse_dashed_function_argument(values: &[ComponentValue], position: &mut usize) -> bool {
    let saved_position = *position;
    discard_whitespace(values, position);
    if let Some(ComponentValue {
        kind:
            ComponentKind::SimpleBlock {
                opening: ParserTokenKind::OpenCurly,
                values: block_values,
            },
        ..
    }) = values.get(*position)
    {
        let mut block_position = 0;
        discard_whitespace(block_values, &mut block_position);
        if consume_declaration_value_as_span(block_values, &mut block_position, None, false)
            && block_position == block_values.len()
        {
            *position += 1;
            return true;
        }
    }
    *position = saved_position;
    consume_declaration_value_as_span(values, position, Some(EndToken::Comma), true)
}

// This mirrors parse_according_to_argument_grammar() in
// CSS/Parser/ArbitrarySubstitutionFunctions.cpp.
/// The argument of a `var()` or `env()` before its first comma, without the whitespace around it.
fn first_argument(values: &[ComponentValue]) -> &[ComponentValue] {
    let comma = values.iter().position(ComponentValue::is_comma).unwrap_or(values.len());
    crate::css::parser::component_value::trim_whitespace(&values[..comma])
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-variables-1/#using-variables
// var() = var( <custom-property-name> , <declaration-value>? )
// AD-HOC: The argument grammar of var() takes any <declaration-value> as the name, which only the replacement algorithm
//         checks, at computed-value time. A name that isn't a <custom-property-name> makes the declaration invalid at
//         parse time instead, so that a var() with a typo in it doesn't override an earlier declaration.
// FIXME: Remove this check, and the one for env() below, once checking the name only at substitution time, as the
//        argument grammar does, is web-compatible.
fn names_a_custom_property(values: &[ComponentValue]) -> bool {
    let name = first_argument(values);
    name.len() == 1
        && name[0]
            .ident()
            .is_some_and(|ident| ident.len() > 2 && ident[0] == b'-' as u16 && ident[1] == b'-' as u16)
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-env-1/#env-function
// env() = env( <custom-ident> <integer [0,inf]>*, <declaration-value>? )
// AD-HOC: As for var(), a name that doesn't match this grammar makes the declaration invalid at parse time.
fn names_an_environment_variable(values: &[ComponentValue]) -> bool {
    let mut parts = first_argument(values).iter().filter(|value| !value.is_whitespace());
    let Some(name) = parts.next().and_then(ComponentValue::ident) else {
        return false;
    };
    crate::css::parser::value_parser::is_valid_custom_ident(name, &[])
        && parts.all(|value| {
            matches!(
                value.kind,
                ComponentKind::Token(ParserTokenKind::Number {
                    value,
                    number_type: crate::css::css_tokenizer::CssNumberType::Integer
                        | crate::css::css_tokenizer::CssNumberType::IntegerWithExplicitSign,
                }) if value >= 0.0
            )
        })
}

pub(crate) fn arguments_are_valid(function: ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction, values: &[ComponentValue]) -> bool {
    let mut position = 0;
    match function {
        ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Attr => {
            parse_declaration_value_then_optional_declaration_value(values, &mut position, EndToken::Comma)
                && position == values.len()
                && crate::css::custom_properties::literal_attr_arguments_are_valid(values)
        }
        ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Env => {
            parse_declaration_value_then_optional_declaration_value(values, &mut position, EndToken::Comma)
                && position == values.len()
                && names_an_environment_variable(values)
        }
        ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Inherit => {
            parse_declaration_value_then_optional_declaration_value(values, &mut position, EndToken::Comma)
                && position == values.len()
        }
        ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Var => {
            parse_declaration_value_then_optional_declaration_value(values, &mut position, EndToken::Comma)
                && position == values.len()
                && names_a_custom_property(values)
        }
        ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::DashedFunction => {
            discard_whitespace(values, &mut position);
            if position == values.len() {
                return true;
            }
            if !parse_dashed_function_argument(values, &mut position) {
                return false;
            }
            discard_whitespace(values, &mut position);
            while position < values.len() {
                if !values[position].is_comma() {
                    return false;
                }
                position += 1;
                discard_whitespace(values, &mut position);
                if !parse_dashed_function_argument(values, &mut position) {
                    return false;
                }
                discard_whitespace(values, &mut position);
            }
            true
        }
        ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::If => {
            discard_whitespace(values, &mut position);
            let mut branch_count = 0;
            while position < values.len() {
                if !parse_declaration_value_then_optional_declaration_value(values, &mut position, EndToken::Colon) {
                    return false;
                }
                branch_count += 1;
                if !values
                    .get(position)
                    .is_some_and(|value| matches!(value.kind, ComponentKind::Token(ParserTokenKind::Semicolon)))
                {
                    break;
                }
                position += 1;
                discard_whitespace(values, &mut position);
            }
            branch_count != 0 && position == values.len()
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn arguments_are_valid_for_ffi(function: u8, values: &[ComponentValue]) -> bool {
    let function = match function {
        0 => ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Attr,
        1 => ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::DashedFunction,
        2 => ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Env,
        3 => ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::If,
        4 => ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Inherit,
        5 => ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Var,
        _ => return false,
    };
    arguments_are_valid(function, values)
}

fn collect_presence_from_value(value: &ComponentValue, presence: &mut SubstitutionFunctionsPresence) -> Result<(), ()> {
    let nested_values = match &value.kind {
        ComponentKind::Function { name, values } => {
            if let Some(function) = arbitrary_substitution_function(name) {
                if !arguments_are_valid(function, values) {
                    return Err(());
                }
                match function {
                    ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Attr => presence.attr = true,
                    ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::DashedFunction => presence.dashed_function = true,
                    ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Env => presence.env = true,
                    ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::If => presence.if_ = true,
                    ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Inherit => presence.inherit = true,
                    ArbitrarySubstitutionFunction::Var => presence.var = true,
                }
            }
            values.as_ref()
        }
        ComponentKind::SimpleBlock { values, .. } => values.as_ref(),
        ComponentKind::Token(_) => return Ok(()),
    };
    collect_arbitrary_substitution_function_presence(nested_values, presence)
}

pub(crate) fn collect_arbitrary_substitution_function_presence(
    values: &[ComponentValue],
    presence: &mut SubstitutionFunctionsPresence,
) -> Result<(), ()> {
    for value in values {
        collect_presence_from_value(value, presence)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The attribute names the `attr()`s a document holds can read, ASCII-lowercased, or every name
/// once one computes its name. The document's host copies an attribute's value text only for names
/// a selector or this set can read, and backfills its elements when the set grows.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct AttrNamesRead {
    any_name: bool,
    names: HashSet<Box<[u16]>>,
    generation: u64,
}

impl AttrNamesRead {
    /// Grows with every name an `attr()` can newly read.
    pub(crate) fn generation(&self) -> u64 {
        self.generation
    }

    /// Whether an `attr()` may read an attribute with this local name.
    pub(crate) fn may_read(&self, local_name: &[u16]) -> bool {
        self.any_name || self.names.contains(ascii_lowercase(local_name).as_slice())
    }

    /// Record what the `attr()` functions of a declared value can read.
    pub(crate) fn note(&mut self, values: &[ComponentValue]) {
        let mut names = Vec::new();
        let mut any_name = false;
        collect_attr_names_read(values, &mut names, &mut any_name);
        let mut grew = any_name && !self.any_name;
        self.any_name |= any_name;
        for name in names {
            grew |= self.names.insert(name.into_boxed_slice());
        }
        if grew {
            self.generation += 1;
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn include(&mut self, other: &Self) {
        let count = self.names.len();
        self.names.extend(other.names.iter().cloned());
        if self.names.len() != count || (other.any_name && !self.any_name) {
            self.generation += 1;
        }
        self.any_name |= other.any_name;
    }

    /// The bytes the names hold on the heap.
    pub(crate) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        crate::heap_size::set_bytes(&self.names)
            + self.names.iter().map(|name| size_of_val::<[u16]>(name)).sum::<usize>()
    }
}

fn ascii_lowercase(text: &[u16]) -> Vec<u16> {
    text.iter()
        .map(|&unit| {
            if (u16::from(b'A')..=u16::from(b'Z')).contains(&unit) {
                unit + 32
            } else {
                unit
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#attr-notation
// attr( <attr-name> <attr-type>? , <declaration-value>?), where <attr-name> = [ <ident-token>? '|' ]? <ident-token>
fn collect_attr_names_read(values: &[ComponentValue], names: &mut Vec<Vec<u16>>, any_name: &mut bool) {
    for value in values {
        let nested = match &value.kind {
            ComponentKind::Function { name, values } => {
                if equals_ascii_case_insensitive(name, b"attr") {
                    let mut position = 0;
                    discard_whitespace(values, &mut position);
                    let first = values.get(position);
                    let mut local = first.and_then(ComponentValue::ident);
                    if first.is_some_and(|first| first.ident().is_some() || first.is_delim(b'*'))
                        && values.get(position + 1).is_some_and(|value| value.is_delim(b'|'))
                    {
                        local = values.get(position + 2).and_then(ComponentValue::ident);
                    } else if first.is_some_and(|first| first.is_delim(b'|')) {
                        local = values.get(position + 1).and_then(ComponentValue::ident);
                    }
                    match local {
                        Some(local) => names.push(ascii_lowercase(local)),
                        // A name that substitution computes can be any name.
                        None => *any_name = true,
                    }
                    // An attribute value read with a syntax is substituted in turn, so an attr() in
                    // it can name any attribute.
                    *any_name |= values.iter().take_while(|value| !value.is_comma()).any(|value| {
                        matches!(&value.kind, ComponentKind::Function { name, .. } if equals_ascii_case_insensitive(name, b"type"))
                    });
                }
                values.as_ref()
            }
            ComponentKind::SimpleBlock { values, .. } => values.as_ref(),
            ComponentKind::Token(_) => continue,
        };
        collect_attr_names_read(nested, names, any_name);
    }
}

pub(crate) fn declaration_value_is_valid(values: &[ComponentValue]) -> bool {
    let mut position = 0;
    consume_declaration_value_as_span(values, &mut position, None, false) && position == values.len()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        SubstitutionFunctionsPresence, collect_arbitrary_substitution_function_presence, collect_attr_names_read,
        declaration_value_is_valid,
    };
    use crate::css::css_tokenizer::tokenize_for_parser;
    use crate::css::parser::component_value::consume_a_list_of_component_values;

    fn attr_names_read(source: &str) -> (Vec<String>, bool) {
        let values = consume_a_list_of_component_values(tokenize_for_parser(source.as_bytes())).unwrap();
        let mut names = Vec::new();
        let mut any_name = false;
        collect_attr_names_read(&values, &mut names, &mut any_name);
        (
            names.iter().map(|name| String::from_utf16_lossy(name)).collect(),
            any_name,
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn attr_reads_the_names_it_names_and_any_name_through_a_syntax() {
        assert_eq!(
            attr_names_read("attr(Data-Size px)"),
            (vec!["data-size".to_string()], false)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            attr_names_read("attr(*|foo, attr(bar)) var(--x, attr(|baz))"),
            (vec!["foo".to_string(), "bar".to_string(), "baz".to_string()], false)
        );
        // The value read with a syntax is substituted in turn, so it can name any attribute.
        assert_eq!(
            attr_names_read("attr(data-foo type(*))"),
            (vec!["data-foo".to_string()], true)
        );
        // A name that substitution computes can be any name; a type() in the fallback is not a syntax.
        assert!(attr_names_read("attr(var(--name))").1);
        assert!(!attr_names_read("attr(data-foo, type(*))").1);
    }

    fn collect(source: &str) -> Result<SubstitutionFunctionsPresence, ()> {
        let values = consume_a_list_of_component_values(tokenize_for_parser(source.as_bytes())).unwrap();
        let mut presence = SubstitutionFunctionsPresence::default();
        collect_arbitrary_substitution_function_presence(&values, &mut presence)?;
        Ok(presence)
    }

    #[test]
    fn collects_nested_substitution_function_presence() {
        assert_eq!(
            collect("outer([ATTR(data-x, var(--fallback)) --mix({ value }, env(name))])"),
            Ok(SubstitutionFunctionsPresence {
                attr: true,
                dashed_function: true,
                env: true,
                var: true,
                ..Default::default()
            })
        );
        assert!(!collect("random-item(--choice, one, two)").unwrap().has_any());
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_declaration_value_argument_grammars() {
        for source in [
            "var(--name)",
            "var(--name,)",
            "var( --name ,fallback)",
            "env(name 0 1, fallback)",
            "attr(data-name type(<string>), fallback)",
            "env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)",
            "inherit(color, red)",
            "if(style(--flag): one; else: two;)",
            "--mix()",
            "--mix({ value }, fallback)",
        ] {
            assert!(collect(source).is_ok(), "expected valid arguments: {source}");
        }
        for source in [
            "var()",
            "var(,--fallback)",
            "var(--name 0px)",
            "var(name)",
            "var(--)",
            "var(var(--name))",
            "env(name 0px)",
            "env(name -1)",
            "env(name 1.5, fallback)",
            "env(\"name\", fallback)",
            "env(1px)",
            "attr(data-name ! invalid)",
            "env(name, fallback ! invalid)",
            "inherit(value; fallback)",
            "if()",
            "if(value)",
            "if(condition: value ! invalid)",
            "--mix(, value)",
            "--mix({})",
            "--mix(value ! invalid)",
        ] {
            assert!(collect(source).is_err(), "expected invalid arguments: {source}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_nested_substitution_functions() {
        assert!(collect("outer(var(--name, env(name)))").is_ok());
        assert!(collect("outer(var(--name, env()))").is_err());
        assert!(collect("var(--name, [attr()])").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_complete_declaration_values() {
        for source in ["value", "function(value; !important)", "{ value; !important }"] {
            let values = consume_a_list_of_component_values(tokenize_for_parser(source.as_bytes())).unwrap();
            assert!(
                declaration_value_is_valid(&values),
                "expected valid declaration value: {source}"
            );
        }
        for source in ["", "value; trailing", "value ! trailing", "url(bad\"url)"] {
            let values = consume_a_list_of_component_values(tokenize_for_parser(source.as_bytes())).unwrap();
            assert!(
                !declaration_value_is_valid(&values),
                "expected invalid declaration value: {source}"
            );
        }
    }
}

//! Input code units, and scans over blocks of them. Style sheet text is 8-bit ASCII or 16-bit UTF-16, and the lexer is
//! generic over the two.
//!
//! A scan works on a block of 16 code units narrowed to bytes, where anything above 0xFE saturates to 0xFF. ASCII stays
//! exact, so the classification is the same for both widths.

use crate::css::css_tokenizer::TokenizerInput;

/// How many code units a block holds.
pub(crate) const BLOCK: usize = 16;

pub(crate) trait Unit: Copy + Eq + std::hash::Hash + 'static {
    /// Whether a code point can take two units.
    const WIDE: bool;
    fn code(self) -> u32;
    /// Loads a block of units as bytes.
    fn load(units: &[Self; BLOCK]) -> Block;
    fn input(units: &[Self]) -> TokenizerInput<'_>;
}

impl Unit for u8 {
    const WIDE: bool = false;

    #[inline(always)]
    fn code(self) -> u32 {
        u32::from(self)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn load(units: &[u8; BLOCK]) -> Block {
        imp::load_narrow(units)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn input(units: &[u8]) -> TokenizerInput<'_> {
        TokenizerInput::Latin1(units)
    }
}

impl Unit for u16 {
    const WIDE: bool = true;

    #[inline(always)]
    fn code(self) -> u32 {
        u32::from(self)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn load(units: &[u16; BLOCK]) -> Block {
        imp::load_wide(units)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn input(units: &[u16]) -> TokenizerInput<'_> {
        TokenizerInput::Utf16(units)
    }
}

pub(crate) use imp::{Block, eq_mask, ident_mask};

#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
mod imp {
    use super::BLOCK;
    use core::arch::x86_64::*;

    pub(crate) type Block = __m128i;

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn load_narrow(units: &[u8; BLOCK]) -> Block {
        // SAFETY: The array is 16 readable bytes, and SSE2 is part of every x86-64 target.
        unsafe { _mm_loadu_si128(units.as_ptr().cast()) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn load_wide(units: &[u16; BLOCK]) -> Block {
        // SAFETY: The array is 32 readable bytes, and SSE2 is part of every x86-64 target.
        unsafe {
            let narrow = |half: __m128i| {
                // NB: Packing saturates as if the units were signed, so a unit with a high byte is made 0xFF first.
                let fits = _mm_cmpeq_epi16(_mm_srli_epi16::<8>(half), _mm_setzero_si128());
                _mm_or_si128(
                    _mm_and_si128(half, _mm_set1_epi16(0xFF)),
                    _mm_andnot_si128(fits, _mm_set1_epi16(0xFF)),
                )
            };
            let low = narrow(_mm_loadu_si128(units.as_ptr().cast()));
            let high = narrow(_mm_loadu_si128(units.as_ptr().add(8).cast()));
            _mm_packus_epi16(low, high)
        }
    }

    /// One bit per unit of the block: whether it is an ident code point, which every unit from 0x80 up is.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn ident_mask(block: Block) -> u32 {
        // SAFETY: SSE2 is part of every x86-64 target.
        unsafe {
            // NB: x <= k, unsigned, is min(x, k) == x.
            let at_most = |x: __m128i, k: i8| _mm_cmpeq_epi8(_mm_min_epu8(x, _mm_set1_epi8(k)), x);
            let letter = _mm_sub_epi8(_mm_or_si128(block, _mm_set1_epi8(0x20)), _mm_set1_epi8(b'a' as i8));
            let digit = _mm_sub_epi8(block, _mm_set1_epi8(b'0' as i8));
            let underscore = _mm_cmpeq_epi8(block, _mm_set1_epi8(b'_' as i8));
            let hyphen = _mm_cmpeq_epi8(block, _mm_set1_epi8(b'-' as i8));
            let ascii = _mm_or_si128(
                _mm_or_si128(at_most(letter, 25), at_most(digit, 9)),
                _mm_or_si128(underscore, hyphen),
            );
            // NB: The sign bit of a unit from 0x80 up is set already.
            _mm_movemask_epi8(_mm_or_si128(ascii, block)) as u32
        }
    }

    /// One bit per unit of the block: whether it is `byte`.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn eq_mask(block: Block, byte: u8) -> u32 {
        // SAFETY: SSE2 is part of every x86-64 target.
        unsafe { _mm_movemask_epi8(_mm_cmpeq_epi8(block, _mm_set1_epi8(byte as i8))) as u32 }
    }
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
mod imp {
    use super::BLOCK;
    use core::arch::aarch64::*;

    pub(crate) type Block = uint8x16_t;

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn load_narrow(units: &[u8; BLOCK]) -> Block {
        // SAFETY: The array is 16 readable bytes, and NEON is part of every AArch64 target.
        unsafe { vld1q_u8(units.as_ptr()) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn load_wide(units: &[u16; BLOCK]) -> Block {
        // SAFETY: The array is 32 readable bytes, and NEON is part of every AArch64 target.
        unsafe {
            vcombine_u8(
                vqmovn_u16(vld1q_u16(units.as_ptr())),
                vqmovn_u16(vld1q_u16(units.as_ptr().add(8))),
            )
        }
    }

    /// One bit per byte, from a vector whose bytes are all ones or all zeros.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn bits_of(block: Block) -> u32 {
        const BITS: [u8; 16] = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128];
        // SAFETY: NEON is part of every AArch64 target.
        unsafe {
            let masked = vandq_u8(block, vld1q_u8(BITS.as_ptr()));
            u32::from(vaddv_u8(vget_low_u8(masked))) | u32::from(vaddv_u8(vget_high_u8(masked))) << 8
        }
    }

    /// One bit per unit of the block: whether it is an ident code point, which every unit from 0x80 up is.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn ident_mask(block: Block) -> u32 {
        // SAFETY: NEON is part of every AArch64 target.
        unsafe {
            let letter = vcleq_u8(
                vsubq_u8(vorrq_u8(block, vdupq_n_u8(0x20)), vdupq_n_u8(b'a')),
                vdupq_n_u8(25),
            );
            let digit = vcleq_u8(vsubq_u8(block, vdupq_n_u8(b'0')), vdupq_n_u8(9));
            let underscore = vceqq_u8(block, vdupq_n_u8(b'_'));
            let hyphen = vceqq_u8(block, vdupq_n_u8(b'-'));
            let high = vcgeq_u8(block, vdupq_n_u8(0x80));
            bits_of(vorrq_u8(
                vorrq_u8(letter, digit),
                vorrq_u8(vorrq_u8(underscore, hyphen), high),
            ))
        }
    }

    /// One bit per unit of the block: whether it is `byte`.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn eq_mask(block: Block, byte: u8) -> u32 {
        // SAFETY: NEON is part of every AArch64 target.
        unsafe { bits_of(vceqq_u8(block, vdupq_n_u8(byte))) }
    }
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]
mod imp {
    use super::BLOCK;

    pub(crate) type Block = [u8; BLOCK];

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn load_narrow(units: &[u8; BLOCK]) -> Block {
        *units
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn load_wide(units: &[u16; BLOCK]) -> Block {
        units.map(|unit| unit.min(0xFF) as u8)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn bits_of(block: Block, test: impl Fn(u8) -> bool) -> u32 {
        block
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .fold(0, |bits, (index, &byte)| bits | u32::from(test(byte)) << index)
    }

    /// One bit per unit of the block: whether it is an ident code point, which every unit from 0x80 up is.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn ident_mask(block: Block) -> u32 {
        bits_of(block, |byte| {
            byte >= 0x80 || byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || byte == b'_' || byte == b'-'
        })
    }

    /// One bit per unit of the block: whether it is `byte`.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn eq_mask(block: Block, byte: u8) -> u32 {
        bits_of(block, |unit| unit == byte)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{BLOCK, Unit, eq_mask, ident_mask};

    #[test]
    fn masks_agree_with_the_scalar_classes() {
        for first in 0..=255u8 {
            let mut narrow = [b'a'; BLOCK];
            narrow[3] = first;
            narrow[15] = first;
            let expected = u32::from(first >= 0x80 || first.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || first == b'_' || first == b'-');
            let mask = ident_mask(u8::load(&narrow));
            assert_eq!(mask >> 3 & 1, expected, "{first:#x}");
            assert_eq!(mask >> 15 & 1, expected, "{first:#x}");
            assert_eq!(mask & 0x7ff7, 0x7ff7);
            assert_eq!(eq_mask(u8::load(&narrow), first) & (1 << 3 | 1 << 15), 1 << 3 | 1 << 15);
        }
        for unit in [0x80u16, 0xFF, 0x100, 0x2D00, 0x7FFF, 0x8000, 0xD800, 0xFFFF] {
            let mut wide = [u16::from(b'{'); BLOCK];
            wide[0] = unit;
            wide[9] = unit;
            assert_eq!(ident_mask(u16::load(&wide)), 1 | 1 << 9, "{unit:#x}");
            assert_eq!(eq_mask(u16::load(&wide), b'{'), 0xffff & !(1 | 1 << 9), "{unit:#x}");
        }
    }
}
