fn container_requirements(expression: &Expression) -> u8 {
    container_requirements_in(expression, QueryKind::Size)
}

fn container_requirements_in(expression: &Expression, kind: QueryKind) -> u8 {
    match expression {
        Expression::Not(child) | Expression::InParens(child) => container_requirements_in(child, kind),
        Expression::StyleFunction(child) => container_requirements_in(child, kind) | CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_STYLE,
        Expression::ScrollStateFunction(child) => {
            container_requirements_in(child, QueryKind::ScrollState) | CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_SCROLL_STATE
        }
        Expression::And(children) | Expression::Or(children) => children.iter().fold(0, |requirements, child| {
            requirements | container_requirements_in(child, kind)
        }),
        Expression::GeneralEnclosed { .. } | Expression::GeneralEnclosedValues { .. } => {
            CONTAINER_QUERY_HAS_UNKNOWN_FEATURE
        }
        Expression::QueryFeature(_) if kind == QueryKind::ScrollState => CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_SCROLL_STATE,
        Expression::QueryFeature(feature) => {
            let id = match feature {
                QueryFeature::Boolean { id } | QueryFeature::Plain { id, .. } | QueryFeature::Range { id, .. } => *id,
            };
            match id {
                0 | 4 => CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_WIDTH | CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_HEIGHT,
                1 => CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_BLOCK_SIZE,
                2 => CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_HEIGHT,
                3 => CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_INLINE_SIZE,
                5 => CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_WIDTH,
                _ => CONTAINER_QUERY_HAS_UNKNOWN_FEATURE,
            }
        }
        Expression::StyleFeature(_) => CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_STYLE,
        _ => CONTAINER_QUERY_HAS_UNKNOWN_FEATURE,
    }
}

fn container_size_value(id: u8, facts: &ContainerFacts) -> Option<ResolvedFeatureValue> {
    if !facts.size_available {
        return None;
    }
    Some(match id {
        0 => ResolvedFeatureValue::Ratio {
            numerator: facts.width,
            denominator: facts.height,
        },
        1 => ResolvedFeatureValue::Length(if facts.inline_axis_horizontal {
            facts.height
        } else {
            facts.width
        }),
        2 => ResolvedFeatureValue::Length(facts.height),
        3 => ResolvedFeatureValue::Length(if facts.inline_axis_horizontal {
            facts.width
        } else {
            facts.height
        }),
        4 => ResolvedFeatureValue::Ident(if facts.height >= facts.width {
            crate::css::css_enums::keyword::PORTRAIT
        } else {
            crate::css::css_enums::keyword::LANDSCAPE
        }),
        5 => ResolvedFeatureValue::Length(facts.width),
        _ => return None,
    })
}

fn evaluate_container_size_feature(
    feature: &QueryFeature,
    facts: &ContainerFacts,
    length_context: Option<&FfiLengthResolutionContext>,
) -> MatchResult {
    let id = match feature {
        QueryFeature::Boolean { id } | QueryFeature::Plain { id, .. } | QueryFeature::Range { id, .. } => *id,
    };
    let Some(queried_value) = container_size_value(id, facts) else {
        return MatchResult::Unknown;
    };
    match feature {
        QueryFeature::Boolean { .. } => match &queried_value {
            ResolvedFeatureValue::Length(value) => {
                if *value != 0.0 {
                    MatchResult::True
                } else {
                    MatchResult::False
                }
            }
            ResolvedFeatureValue::Ratio { numerator, denominator } => {
                if numerator.is_finite() && *numerator != 0.0 && denominator.is_finite() && *denominator != 0.0 {
                    MatchResult::True
                } else {
                    MatchResult::False
                }
            }
            ResolvedFeatureValue::Ident(_) => MatchResult::True,
            _ => MatchResult::False,
        },
        QueryFeature::Plain { name_type, value, .. } => {
            let value = parse_size_feature_value(id, value, length_context, facts.tree_counting);
            match name_type {
                FeatureNameType::Normal => compare_feature_values(&value, FeatureComparison::Equal, &queried_value),
                FeatureNameType::Min => {
                    compare_feature_values(&queried_value, FeatureComparison::GreaterThanOrEqual, &value)
                }
                FeatureNameType::Max => {
                    compare_feature_values(&queried_value, FeatureComparison::LessThanOrEqual, &value)
                }
            }
        }
        QueryFeature::Range { left, right, .. } => {
            if let Some((value, comparison)) = left.as_deref() {
                let value = parse_size_feature_value(id, value, length_context, facts.tree_counting);
                let result = compare_feature_values(&value, *comparison, &queried_value);
                if result != MatchResult::True {
                    return result;
                }
            }
            if let Some((comparison, value)) = right.as_deref() {
                let value = parse_size_feature_value(id, value, length_context, facts.tree_counting);
                let result = compare_feature_values(&queried_value, *comparison, &value);
                if result != MatchResult::True {
                    return result;
                }
            }
            MatchResult::True
        }
    }
}

fn scroll_state_side_edge(side: u8) -> u8 {
    1 << (side % 4)
}

fn scroll_state_axis_edges(side: u8) -> u8 {
    scroll_state_side_edge(side) | scroll_state_side_edge(side + 2)
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-conditional-5/#scroll-state-container
fn evaluate_container_scroll_state_feature(feature: &QueryFeature, facts: &ContainerFacts) -> MatchResult {
    use crate::css::css_enums::keyword;
    if !facts.scroll_state_available {
        return MatchResult::Unknown;
    }
    let (id, value) = match feature {
        QueryFeature::Boolean { id } => (*id, None),
        QueryFeature::Plain { id, value, .. } => (*id, Some(value)),
        QueryFeature::Range { .. } => return MatchResult::Unknown,
    };
    let state = match id {
        SCROLL_STATE_FEATURE_STUCK => facts.stuck,
        SCROLL_STATE_FEATURE_SCROLLABLE => facts.scrollable,
        SCROLL_STATE_FEATURE_SCROLLED => facts.scrolled,
        SCROLL_STATE_FEATURE_SNAPPED => facts.snapped,
        _ => return MatchResult::Unknown,
    };
    // In a boolean context, a feature matches when its value is anything but none.
    let Some(value) = value else {
        return if state != 0 {
            MatchResult::True
        } else {
            MatchResult::False
        };
    };
    let Some(value) = scroll_state_feature_value_keyword(id, value) else {
        return MatchResult::Unknown;
    };
    let matches = if id == SCROLL_STATE_FEATURE_SNAPPED {
        let axis_of_side = |side: u8| {
            if side.is_multiple_of(2) {
                SCROLL_STATE_SNAPPED_Y
            } else {
                SCROLL_STATE_SNAPPED_X
            }
        };
        match value {
            keyword::NONE => state == 0,
            keyword::X => state & SCROLL_STATE_SNAPPED_X != 0,
            keyword::Y => state & SCROLL_STATE_SNAPPED_Y != 0,
            keyword::BOTH => {
                state & (SCROLL_STATE_SNAPPED_X | SCROLL_STATE_SNAPPED_Y)
                    == SCROLL_STATE_SNAPPED_X | SCROLL_STATE_SNAPPED_Y
            }
            keyword::BLOCK => state & axis_of_side(facts.block_start_side) != 0,
            keyword::INLINE => state & axis_of_side(facts.inline_start_side) != 0,
            _ => return MatchResult::Unknown,
        }
    } else {
        let edges = match value {
            keyword::NONE => {
                return if state == 0 {
                    MatchResult::True
                } else {
                    MatchResult::False
                };
            }
            keyword::TOP => SCROLL_STATE_EDGE_TOP,
            keyword::RIGHT => SCROLL_STATE_EDGE_RIGHT,
            keyword::BOTTOM => SCROLL_STATE_EDGE_BOTTOM,
            keyword::LEFT => SCROLL_STATE_EDGE_LEFT,
            keyword::BLOCK_START => scroll_state_side_edge(facts.block_start_side),
            keyword::BLOCK_END => scroll_state_side_edge(facts.block_start_side + 2),
            keyword::INLINE_START => scroll_state_side_edge(facts.inline_start_side),
            keyword::INLINE_END => scroll_state_side_edge(facts.inline_start_side + 2),
            keyword::X => SCROLL_STATE_EDGE_LEFT | SCROLL_STATE_EDGE_RIGHT,
            keyword::Y => SCROLL_STATE_EDGE_TOP | SCROLL_STATE_EDGE_BOTTOM,
            keyword::BLOCK => scroll_state_axis_edges(facts.block_start_side),
            keyword::INLINE => scroll_state_axis_edges(facts.inline_start_side),
            _ => return MatchResult::Unknown,
        };
        state & edges != 0
    };
    if matches { MatchResult::True } else { MatchResult::False }
}

/// How a container condition answers a `style()` feature.
pub(crate) type EvaluateStyleFeature<'a> = dyn FnMut(&StyleFeature) -> MatchResult + 'a;

fn evaluate_container_expression(
    expression: &Expression,
    facts: &ContainerFacts,
    length_context: Option<&FfiLengthResolutionContext>,
    style: &mut EvaluateStyleFeature<'_>,
) -> MatchResult {
    evaluate_container_expression_in(expression, QueryKind::Size, facts, length_context, style)
}

fn evaluate_container_expression_in(
    expression: &Expression,
    kind: QueryKind,
    facts: &ContainerFacts,
    length_context: Option<&FfiLengthResolutionContext>,
    style: &mut EvaluateStyleFeature<'_>,
) -> MatchResult {
    match expression {
        Expression::Not(child) => match evaluate_container_expression_in(child, kind, facts, length_context, style) {
            MatchResult::False => MatchResult::True,
            MatchResult::True => MatchResult::False,
            MatchResult::Unknown => MatchResult::Unknown,
        },
        Expression::And(children) => {
            let mut result = MatchResult::True;
            for child in children {
                match evaluate_container_expression_in(child, kind, facts, length_context, style) {
                    MatchResult::False => return MatchResult::False,
                    MatchResult::Unknown => result = MatchResult::Unknown,
                    MatchResult::True => {}
                }
            }
            result
        }
        Expression::Or(children) => {
            let mut result = MatchResult::False;
            for child in children {
                match evaluate_container_expression_in(child, kind, facts, length_context, style) {
                    MatchResult::True => return MatchResult::True,
                    MatchResult::Unknown => result = MatchResult::Unknown,
                    MatchResult::False => {}
                }
            }
            result
        }
        Expression::InParens(child) | Expression::StyleFunction(child) => {
            evaluate_container_expression_in(child, kind, facts, length_context, style)
        }
        Expression::ScrollStateFunction(child) => {
            evaluate_container_expression_in(child, QueryKind::ScrollState, facts, length_context, style)
        }
        Expression::GeneralEnclosed { result, .. } | Expression::GeneralEnclosedValues { result, .. } => *result,
        Expression::QueryFeature(feature) if kind == QueryKind::ScrollState => {
            evaluate_container_scroll_state_feature(feature, facts)
        }
        Expression::QueryFeature(feature) => evaluate_container_size_feature(feature, facts, length_context),
        Expression::StyleFeature(feature) => style(feature),
        _ => MatchResult::Unknown,
    }
}

fn evaluate_media_query(
    query: &MediaQuery,
    environment: &[FfiMediaFeatureValue],
    length_context: Option<&FfiLengthResolutionContext>,
) -> MatchResult {
    let mut result = match query.media_type.as_ref().map(CssString::units) {
        None => MatchResult::True,
        Some(media_type) if equals_ascii_case_insensitive(media_type, b"all") => MatchResult::True,
        Some(media_type) if equals_ascii_case_insensitive(media_type, b"screen") => MatchResult::True,
        Some(media_type) if equals_ascii_case_insensitive(media_type, b"print") => MatchResult::False,
        Some(_) => MatchResult::False,
    };
    if result != MatchResult::False
        && let Some(condition) = &query.condition
    {
        result = match (
            result,
            evaluate_media_expression(condition, environment, length_context),
        ) {
            (MatchResult::False, _) | (_, MatchResult::False) => MatchResult::False,
            (MatchResult::True, MatchResult::True) => MatchResult::True,
            _ => MatchResult::Unknown,
        };
    }
    if query.negated {
        result = match result {
            MatchResult::False => MatchResult::True,
            MatchResult::True => MatchResult::False,
            MatchResult::Unknown => MatchResult::Unknown,
        };
    }
    result
}

pub(crate) type VisitQuerySerialization = unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const u16, usize);

enum SourceSizeValue {
    Auto,
    Length(StyleValueData),
}

fn parse_sizes_attribute_source_size_value(context: &ParseContext, value: &ComponentValue) -> Option<SourceSizeValue> {
    if is_ident(value, b"auto") {
        return Some(SourceSizeValue::Auto);
    }

    let mut stream = TokenStream::new(std::slice::from_ref(value));
    let value = parse_length_from_stream(
        context,
        crate::css::property_metadata::property_id::WIDTH,
        &mut stream,
        NumericRange::NON_NEGATIVE,
    )?;
    stream.discard_whitespace();
    if stream.has_next_token() {
        return None;
    }
    if matches!(&value, StyleValueData::Calculated { .. })
        && crate::css::calc::resolve_calculated_raw_length_without_context(&value)
            .is_some_and(|value| !value.is_finite())
    {
        return None;
    }
    Some(SourceSizeValue::Length(value))
}

fn default_source_size() -> StyleValueData {
    let unit = LENGTH_UNIT_NAMES.iter().position(|&unit| unit == "vw").unwrap();
    StyleValueData::Length {
        value: 100.0,
        unit: u8::try_from(unit).unwrap(),
    }
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html#parsing-a-sizes-attribute
fn parse_sizes_attribute(
    context: &ParseContext,
    source: TokenizerInput<'_>,
    media_environment: Option<(&[FfiMediaFeatureValue], Option<&FfiLengthResolutionContext>)>,
    img_auto_width: Option<f64>,
) -> StyleValueData {
    // 1. Let unparsed sizes list be the result of parsing a comma-separated list of component values
    //    from the value of element's sizes attribute (or the empty string, if the attribute is absent).
    let Some(values) = components_from_source(source) else {
        return default_source_size();
    };

    // 2. Let size be null.

    // 3. For each unparsed size in unparsed sizes list:
    for unparsed_size in values.split(ComponentValue::is_comma) {
        // 1. Remove all consecutive <whitespace-token>s from the end of unparsed size.
        //    If unparsed size is now empty, then that is a parse error; continue.
        let unparsed_size = trim_whitespace(unparsed_size);
        let Some((source_size_value, remaining)) = unparsed_size.split_last() else {
            continue;
        };

        // 2. If the last component value in unparsed size is a valid non-negative <source-size-value>,
        //    then set size to its value and remove the component value from unparsed size.
        //    Any CSS function other than the math functions is invalid.
        //    Otherwise, there is a parse error; continue.
        let Some(mut size) = parse_sizes_attribute_source_size_value(context, source_size_value) else {
            continue;
        };

        // 3. If size is auto, and img is not null, and img is being rendered, and img allows auto-sizes,
        //    then set size to the concrete object size width of img, in CSS pixels.
        if matches!(&size, SourceSizeValue::Auto)
            && let Some(width) = img_auto_width
        {
            size = SourceSizeValue::Length(StyleValueData::Length {
                value: width,
                unit: px_length_unit(),
            });
        }

        // 4. Remove all consecutive <whitespace-token>s from the end of unparsed size.
        //    If unparsed size is now empty:
        let remaining = trim_whitespace(remaining);
        if remaining.is_empty() {
            // 1. If this was not the last item in unparsed sizes list, that is a parse error.

            // 2. If size is not auto, then return size. Otherwise, continue.
            if let SourceSizeValue::Length(size) = size {
                return size;
            }
            continue;
        }

        // 5. Parse the remaining component values in unparsed size as a <media-condition>.
        //    If it does not parse correctly, or it does parse correctly but the <media-condition>
        //    evaluates to false, continue.
        let Some(condition) = parse_media_condition(remaining, &resolve_query_feature) else {
            continue;
        };
        let matches = media_environment.is_some_and(|(values, length_context)| {
            evaluate_media_expression(&condition, values, length_context) == MatchResult::True
        });
        if !matches {
            continue;
        }

        // 6. If size is not auto, then return size. Otherwise, continue.
        if let SourceSizeValue::Length(size) = size {
            return size;
        }
    }

    // 4. Return 100vw.
    default_source_size()
}

/// Parses a sizes attribute and returns its selected source-size value.
///
/// # Safety
/// The source, context, media environment, and optional auto width must remain readable for the
/// duration of the call. The media environment's nested pointers must be valid for their lengths.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_parse_sizes_attribute(
    source: FfiUtf16View,
    context: Option<&ParseContext>,
    media_environment: Option<&FfiMediaEnvironment<'_>>,
    img_auto_width: Option<&f64>,
) -> *const c_void {
    let Some(source) = source.units() else {
        return std::ptr::null();
    };
    let Some(context) = context else {
        return std::ptr::null();
    };
    let media_environment = media_environment.and_then(FfiMediaEnvironment::parts);
    let img_auto_width = img_auto_width.copied();
    crate::css::style_value_arc::StyleValueArc::into_raw(crate::css::style_value_arc::StyleValueArc::new(
        parse_sizes_attribute(context, source, media_environment, img_auto_width),
    ))
    .cast()
}

pub(crate) fn declared_namespaces_from_context<'a>(context: &ParseContext<'a>) -> Vec<TokenizerInput<'a>> {
    context
        .declared_namespaces
        .into_iter()
        .flat_map(|namespaces| namespaces.prefixes.iter())
        .map(|namespace| TokenizerInput::Utf16(namespace.units()))
        .collect()
}

fn create_expression_handle(expression: Expression, kind: QueryKind) -> *const FfiQueryHandle {
    Arc::into_raw(Arc::new(FfiQueryHandle {
        tree: QueryTree::Expression { expression, kind },
    }))
}

/// # Safety
/// The source pointers must identify readable storage for the duration of the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_parse_supports_condition(
    source: FfiUtf16View,
    context: Option<&ParseContext>,
) -> *const FfiQueryHandle {
    let Some(source) = source.units() else {
        return std::ptr::null();
    };
    let Some(context) = context else {
        return std::ptr::null();
    };
    let declared_namespaces = declared_namespaces_from_context(context);
    let Some(expression) = parse_supports_condition(source, &|kind, value| {
        supports_feature_matches(context, &declared_namespaces, kind, value)
    }) else {
        return std::ptr::null();
    };
    create_expression_handle(expression, QueryKind::Supports)
}

/// Adds one strong reference to a borrowed query handle.
///
/// # Safety
/// `handle` must be null or point to a live query handle.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn css_query_ref(handle: *const FfiQueryHandle) -> *const FfiQueryHandle {
    if !handle.is_null() {
        unsafe { Arc::increment_strong_count(handle) };
    }
    handle
}

/// Releases one strong reference to a query handle.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn css_query_unref(handle: OwnedArc<FfiQueryHandle>) {
    drop(handle);
}

/// Evaluates a retained supports condition whose feature results were captured while parsing.
/// Returns 3 when the handle does not contain a supports expression.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn css_query_evaluate_supports(handle: Option<&FfiQueryHandle>) -> u8 {
    handle
        .and_then(FfiQueryHandle::evaluate_supports)
        .map_or(3, |result| result as u8)
}

/// Evaluate a retained container condition against a container's facts, answering its `style()`
/// features with `style`.
///
/// # Safety
/// The length resolution context in `facts`, if any, must be readable for the call.
pub(crate) unsafe fn evaluate_container_query(
    handle: &FfiQueryHandle,
    facts: &ContainerFacts,
    style: &mut EvaluateStyleFeature<'_>,
) -> MatchResult {
    let QueryTree::Expression { expression, kind } = &handle.tree else {
        return MatchResult::Unknown;
    };
    if !matches!(kind, QueryKind::Size | QueryKind::Style) {
        return MatchResult::Unknown;
    }
    if !facts.container_available {
        return MatchResult::Unknown;
    }
    let length_context = unsafe {
        facts
            .length_resolution_context
            .cast::<FfiLengthResolutionContext>()
            .as_ref()
    };
    evaluate_container_expression(expression, facts, length_context, style)
}

/// The text of a retained query condition.
pub(crate) fn serialized_query_condition(handle: &FfiQueryHandle) -> ak::Utf16String {
    let QueryTree::Expression { expression, kind } = &handle.tree else {
        unreachable!("the condition of a rule is an expression")
    };
    let mut sink = TextSink::new();
    serialize_expression(&mut sink, expression, *kind);
    sink.into_utf16_string()
}

/// Whether a retained supports condition matches.
pub(crate) fn supports_query_matches(handle: &FfiQueryHandle) -> bool {
    css_query_evaluate_supports(Some(handle)) == 1
}

/// Serializes a retained query condition without changing its UTF-16 representation.
///
/// # Safety
/// `handle` must point to a live expression handle. The callback must be valid and may only
/// retain a copy of the borrowed UTF-16 slice.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn css_query_serialize_condition(
    handle: Option<&FfiQueryHandle>,
    context: *mut c_void,
    visit: VisitQuerySerialization,
) -> bool {
    let Some(handle) = handle else {
        return false;
    };
    let QueryTree::Expression { expression, kind } = &handle.tree else {
        return false;
    };
    let mut sink = TextSink::new();
    serialize_expression(&mut sink, expression, *kind);
    let serialized = sink.into_utf16();
    unsafe { visit(context, serialized.as_ptr(), serialized.len()) };
    true
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn parse_single_container_query(source: &[u8]) -> Option<Expression> {
        let mut conditions = parse_container_condition_list(source, &resolve_query_feature)?;
        if conditions.len() != 1 || conditions[0].name.is_some() {
            return None;
        }
        conditions.pop()?.query
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_media_and_size_feature_names() {
        for (id, metadata) in MEDIA_FEATURES.iter().enumerate() {
            let name = metadata.name.encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>();
            assert_eq!(
                media_feature_from_name(&name),
                Some((u8::try_from(id).unwrap(), metadata.allows_range))
            );
            let uppercase_name = metadata.name.to_ascii_uppercase().encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>();
            assert_eq!(
                media_feature_from_name(&uppercase_name),
                Some((u8::try_from(id).unwrap(), metadata.allows_range))
            );
        }
        assert_eq!(
            media_feature_from_name(&"unknown".encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>()),
            None
        );

        let expected_size_features = [
            ("aspect-ratio", true),
            ("block-size", true),
            ("height", true),
            ("inline-size", true),
            ("orientation", false),
            ("width", true),
        ];
        assert_eq!(
            SIZE_FEATURES
                .iter()
                .map(|metadata| (metadata.name, metadata.allows_range))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            expected_size_features
        );
        for (id, (name, allows_range)) in expected_size_features.into_iter().enumerate() {
            let name = name.to_ascii_uppercase().encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>();
            assert_eq!(
                feature_from_name(
                    SIZE_FEATURES.iter().map(|entry| (entry.name, entry.allows_range)),
                    &name
                ),
                Some((u8::try_from(id).unwrap(), allows_range))
            );
        }
        assert_eq!(
            feature_from_name(
                SIZE_FEATURES.iter().map(|entry| (entry.name, entry.allows_range)),
                &"unknown".encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>()
            ),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]

        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(queries.len(), 3);

    }

    }

    #[test]
    fn a_screen_with_high_dynamic_range_also_matches_standard() {
        let absent = FfiMediaFeatureValue {
            kind: FfiMediaFeatureValueKind::Absent,
            keyword: 0,
            value: 0.0,
            second_value: 0.0,
        };
        let id_of = |name: &str| MEDIA_FEATURES.iter().position(|feature| feature.name == name).unwrap();
        let environment_with_dynamic_range = |keyword| {
            let mut environment = vec![absent; MEDIA_FEATURES.len()];
            for name in ["dynamic-range", "video-dynamic-range"] {
                environment[id_of(name)] = FfiMediaFeatureValue {
                    kind: FfiMediaFeatureValueKind::Ident,
                    keyword,
                    ..absent
                };
            }
            environment
        };
        let matches = |environment: &[FfiMediaFeatureValue], source: &str| {
            let queries = parse_media_query_list(source.as_bytes(), &resolve_query_feature).unwrap();
            evaluate_media_query(&queries[0], environment, None) == MatchResult::True
        };

        let high = environment_with_dynamic_range(crate::css::css_enums::keyword::HIGH);
        for query in [
            "(dynamic-range: high)",
            "(dynamic-range: standard)",
            "(video-dynamic-range: high)",
            "(video-dynamic-range: standard)",
        ] {
            assert!(matches(&high, query), "{query}");
        }

        let standard = environment_with_dynamic_range(crate::css::css_enums::keyword::STANDARD);
        assert!(!matches(&standard, "(dynamic-range: high)"));
        assert!(matches(&standard, "(dynamic-range: standard)"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_sizes_attributes() {
        let value_context = FfiValueParsingContext {
            kind: FfiValueParsingContextKind::Property,
            value: crate::css::property_metadata::property_id::WIDTH,
            secondary_value: 0,
            name: Default::default(),
        };
        let context = media_value_parse_context(&value_context);
        let absent = FfiMediaFeatureValue {
            kind: FfiMediaFeatureValueKind::Absent,
            keyword: 0,
            value: 0.0,
            second_value: 0.0,
        };
        let mut environment = vec![absent; MEDIA_FEATURES.len()];
        let width_id = MEDIA_FEATURES
            .iter()
            .position(|feature| feature.name == "width")
            .unwrap();
        environment[width_id] = FfiMediaFeatureValue {
            kind: FfiMediaFeatureValueKind::Length,
            value: 800.0,
            ..absent
        };
        let parse = |source: &str, auto_width| {
            parse_sizes_attribute(
                &context,
                source.as_bytes().into(),
                Some((environment.as_slice(), None)),
                auto_width,
            )
        };
        let unit = |name| u8::try_from(LENGTH_UNIT_NAMES.iter().position(|&unit| unit == name).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let assert_length = |source, expected_value, expected_unit, auto_width| {
            let StyleValueData::Length { value, unit } = parse(source, auto_width) else {
                panic!("sizes attribute did not produce a length: {source}")
            };
            assert_eq!(value, expected_value, "{source}");
            assert_eq!(unit, expected_unit, "{source}");
        };

        assert_length("60px", 60.0, unit("px"), None);
        assert_length("(min-width: 0px) 40px, 60px", 40.0, unit("px"), None);
        assert_length("(width < 0px) 40px, 60px", 60.0, unit("px"), None);
        assert_length("10%, 60px", 60.0, unit("px"), None);
        assert_length("40px, 60px", 40.0, unit("px"), None);
        assert_length("calc(1px / 0), 60px", 60.0, unit("px"), None);
        assert_length("foo(40px), 60px", 60.0, unit("px"), None);
        assert_length("auto, 60px", 35.0, unit("px"), Some(35.0));
        assert_length("auto, 60px", 60.0, unit("px"), None);
        assert_length("", 100.0, unit("vw"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_supports_features() {
        let supported = |_, _: &[u16]| true;
        assert!(matches!(
            parse_supports_condition(b"(display: grid) and selector(:has(*))".as_slice(), &supported),
            Some(Expression::And(_))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            parse_supports_condition(b"font-tech(color-COLRv1)".as_slice(), &supported),
            Some(Expression::SupportsFeature(SupportsFeature::FontTech { .. }))
        ));
        assert!(
            parse_supports_condition(
                b"(display: grid) or (color: red) and (width: 1px)".as_slice(),
                &supported
            )
            .is_none()
        );
        assert!(parse_supports_condition(b"(--: a)".as_slice(), &supported).is_some());
        assert!(parse_supports_condition(b"(display : grid)".as_slice(), &supported).is_some());
        assert!(parse_supports_declaration_from_source(b"display : grid".as_slice(), &supported).is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn evaluates_supports_features_without_cpp() {
        let value_context = FfiValueParsingContext {
            kind: FfiValueParsingContextKind::Property,
            value: 0,
            secondary_value: 0,
            name: Default::default(),
        };
        let context = media_value_parse_context(&value_context);
        let utf16 = |value: &str| value.encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let evaluate = |kind, value: &[u16]| supports_feature_matches(&context, &[], kind, value);

        for (kind, name) in [
            (SupportsFeatureKind::FontFormat, "WOFF2"),
            (SupportsFeatureKind::FontTech, "COLOR-COLRV1"),
            (SupportsFeatureKind::AtRule, "-WEBKIT-KEYFRAMES"),
            (SupportsFeatureKind::Env, "PREFERRED-TEXT-SCALE"),
        ] {
            assert!(evaluate(kind, &utf16(name)), "{name}");
        }
        for (kind, name) in [
            (SupportsFeatureKind::FontFormat, "svg"),
            (SupportsFeatureKind::FontTech, "features-graphite"),
            (SupportsFeatureKind::AtRule, "charset"),
            (SupportsFeatureKind::Env, "unknown"),
        ] {
            assert!(!evaluate(kind, &utf16(name)), "{name}");
        }
        assert!(evaluate(SupportsFeatureKind::Declaration, &utf16("display: grid")));
        assert!(evaluate(SupportsFeatureKind::Selector, &utf16(":has(*)")));
        assert!(!evaluate(SupportsFeatureKind::Selector, &utf16("a, b")));
        assert!(!evaluate(SupportsFeatureKind::Selector, &utf16("::-webkit-unknown")));

        let namespace = utf16("known");
        assert!(supports_feature_matches(
            &context,
            &[TokenizerInput::Utf16(namespace.as_slice())],
            SupportsFeatureKind::Selector,
            &utf16("known|a")
        ));
        assert!(!supports_feature_matches(
            &context,
            &[TokenizerInput::Utf16(namespace.as_slice())],
            SupportsFeatureKind::Selector,
            &utf16("missing|a")
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn supports_rejects_contextual_pseudo_elements() {
        let value_context = FfiValueParsingContext {
            kind: FfiValueParsingContextKind::Property,
            value: 0,
            secondary_value: 0,
            name: Default::default(),
        };
        let context = media_value_parse_context(&value_context);
        let selectors = [
            ":is(::before)",
            ":where(.ok, ::after)",
            ":is(.ok, :unknown)",
            ":not(::before)",
            ":not(:is(::before))",
            ":has(::before)",
            ":has(:is(::before))",
            ":nth-child(2n of ::before)",
            ":nth-last-child(2n of :is(::before))",
            ":host(::before)",
            ":host(:is(::before))",
            "::slotted(::before)",
            "::slotted(:where(.ok, ::before))",
            ":is(::slotted(.ok))",
            "::-webkit-unknown",
        ];
        let wrongly_supported: Vec<_> = selectors
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|source| {
                let units: Vec<_> = source.encode_utf16().collect();
                supports_feature_matches(&context, &[], SupportsFeatureKind::Selector, &units)
            })
            .collect();
        assert!(
            wrongly_supported.is_empty(),
            "incorrectly supported: {wrongly_supported:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_and_serializes_scroll_state_queries() {
        let serialize = |source: &[u8]| {
            let expression = parse_single_container_query(source).unwrap();
            let mut sink = TextSink::new();
            serialize_expression(&mut sink, &expression, QueryKind::Size);
            String::from_utf16(&sink.into_utf16()).unwrap()
        };
        assert_eq!(
            serialize(b"scroll-state(        stuck:top)"),
            "scroll-state(stuck: top)"
        );
        assert_eq!(serialize(b"scroll-STate(stuck)"), "scroll-state(stuck)");
        assert_eq!(
            serialize(b"scroll-state(  ( stuck: BOTTOM) OR ( STUCK: inline-START  ) )"),
            "scroll-state((stuck: bottom) or (stuck: inline-start))"
        );
        assert_eq!(serialize(b"scroll-STate(stuck:    )"), "scroll-STate(stuck:    )");

        let requirements = |source: &[u8]| container_requirements(&parse_single_container_query(source).unwrap());
        for known in [
            b"scroll-state(snapped: both)".as_slice(),
            b"scroll-state(not ((scrollable: bottom) and (scrollable: right)))",
            b"(scroll-state(scrolled: inline-end))",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(requirements(known), CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_SCROLL_STATE);
        }
        for unknown in [
            b"scroll-state(stuck: x)".as_slice(),
            b"scroll-state(snapped: top)",
            b"scroll-state(stuck: auto)",
            b"scroll-state(stuck:)",
            b"scroll-state(--foo)",
            b"scroll-state(style(stuck: top))",
            b"style(scroll-state(stuck: top))",
        ] {
            assert_ne!(requirements(unknown) & CONTAINER_QUERY_HAS_UNKNOWN_FEATURE, 0);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn keeps_general_enclosed_forgiving() {
        assert!(matches!(
            parse_supports_condition(b"future(foo bar)".as_slice(), &|_, _| false),
            Some(Expression::GeneralEnclosed {
                result: MatchResult::False,
                ..
            })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            parse_single_container_query(b"future(foo bar)"),
            Some(Expression::GeneralEnclosed {
                result: MatchResult::Unknown,
                ..
            })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn serializes_media_feature_values_from_generated_metadata() {
        let serialize = |feature_name: &str, source: &[u8]| {
            let id = MEDIA_FEATURES
                .iter()
                .position(|metadata| metadata.name == feature_name)
                .and_then(|id| u8::try_from(id).ok())
                .unwrap();
            let value = QueryFeatureValue::new(components_from_source(source).unwrap());
            let mut sink = TextSink::new();
            serialize_query_feature_value(&mut sink, &value, id, QueryKind::Media);
            String::from_utf16(&sink.into_utf16()).unwrap()
        };

        assert_eq!(serialize("aspect-ratio", b"1/3"), "1 / 3");
        assert_eq!(serialize("device-aspect-ratio", b"4 / 3"), "4 / 3");
        assert_eq!(serialize("resolution", b"calc(1x + 2x)"), "calc(3dppx)");
    }

    #[test]
    fn container_requirement_bits_cover_every_ffi_capability() {
        let requirement_for_id = |id| container_requirements(&Expression::QueryFeature(QueryFeature::Boolean { id }));
        assert_eq!(
            requirement_for_id(0),
            CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_WIDTH | CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_HEIGHT
        );
        assert_eq!(requirement_for_id(1), CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_BLOCK_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(requirement_for_id(2), CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_HEIGHT);
        assert_eq!(requirement_for_id(3), CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_INLINE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(requirement_for_id(5), CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_WIDTH);
        assert_eq!(requirement_for_id(u8::MAX), CONTAINER_QUERY_HAS_UNKNOWN_FEATURE);
        assert_eq!(CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_SCROLL_STATE, 1 << 5);

        let style = Expression::StyleFunction(Box::new(Expression::And(Vec::new())));
        assert_eq!(container_requirements(&style), CONTAINER_QUERY_REQUIRES_STYLE);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_non_supports_handles_without_panicking() {
        let handle = FfiQueryHandle {
            tree: QueryTree::Expression {
                expression: Expression::And(Vec::new()),
                kind: QueryKind::Media,
            },
        };

        assert_eq!(css_query_evaluate_supports(None), 3);
        assert_eq!(css_query_evaluate_supports(Some(&handle)), 3);
    }
}

/*

 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! The tokens of a piece of source as rows of a buffer, and views of them as component values. A grammar reads the
//! views, and no component value is made: a function or a block is the rows from its first token to the token that
//! closes it, which the first token names.
//!
//! The buffer is scratch memory. Whoever parses many pieces of source fills the same buffer for each.

use super::block::Unit;
use super::component_value::MAXIMUM_COMPONENT_VALUE_NESTING_DEPTH;
use super::lexer::{Escapes, Kind, Lexer, Token, flag, number_of, string_range, unescape};
use crate::css::css_tokenizer::TokenizerInput;
use smallvec::SmallVec;
use std::ops::Range;

/// The text of a name or a string, as UTF-16.
pub(crate) type Name = SmallVec<[u16; 124]>;

/// The token that ends the block or function that a token of `kind` starts.
#[inline]
pub(crate) fn closer_of(kind: Kind) -> Option<Kind> {
    match kind {
        Kind::Function | Kind::OpenParen => Some(Kind::CloseParen),
        Kind::OpenSquare => Some(Kind::CloseSquare),
        Kind::OpenCurly => Some(Kind::CloseCurly),
        _ => None,
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Rows {
    /// The tokens, and after them one end-of-file token, which says whether whitespace or a comment ends the source.
    /// The `part` of a token that starts a function or a block is the row of the token that closes it, or the row of
    /// the end-of-file token if nothing closes it.
    tokens: Vec<Token>,
    open: Vec<u32>,
    /// Whether a token that was pushed is nested too deep, so that the rows are not a list of component values.
    is_too_deep: bool,
}

impl Rows {
    /// Removes all rows, to take the tokens of another source range.
    pub(crate) fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.tokens.clear();
        self.open.clear();
        self.is_too_deep = false;
    }

    /// Appends `token`, which follows the tokens that the rows have.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn push(&mut self, token: Token) {
        let row = self.tokens.len() as u32;
        if let Some(&open) = self.open.last()
            && closer_of(self.tokens[open as usize].kind) == Some(token.kind)
        {
            self.open.pop();
            self.tokens[open as usize].part = row;
        } else if closer_of(token.kind).is_some() {
            // NB: This is the depth at which a list of component values fails to parse.
            if self.open.len() >= MAXIMUM_COMPONENT_VALUE_NESTING_DEPTH {
                self.is_too_deep = true;
                return;
            }
            self.open.push(row);
        }
        self.tokens.push(token);
    }

    /// Ends the rows at `end`, where `next` is the token that follows them or the end of the source. Fails if the
    /// functions and blocks are nested too deep.
    pub(crate) fn finish(&mut self, next: Token, end: usize) -> Result<(), ()> {
        if self.is_too_deep {
            return Err(());
        }
        let row = self.tokens.len() as u32;
        // NB: Whitespace and comments before the end of the range are before the token that starts there. Those after
        //     the end of the range, which starts where the last row ends, are not in the rows.
        let end = (next.start as usize).min(end) as u32;
        let has_gap_in_range = self.tokens.last().is_none_or(|last| last.end < end);
        let flags = if has_gap_in_range {
            next.flags & (flag::SPACE_BEFORE | flag::COMMENT_BEFORE)
        } else {
            0
        };
        self.tokens.push(Token {
            start: end,
            end,
            part: 0,
            kind: Kind::EndOfFile,
            flags,
        });
        for &open in &self.open {
            self.tokens[open as usize].part = row;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Fills the rows with the tokens in `range` of `units`, which are preprocessed text. Fails if the functions and
    /// blocks are nested too deep.
    pub(crate) fn fill<U: Unit>(&mut self, units: &[U], range: Range<usize>) -> Result<(), ()> {
        self.clear();
        let mut lexer = Lexer::new(units);
        lexer.set_position(range.start);
        loop {
            let token = lexer.next();
            if token.kind == Kind::EndOfFile || token.start as usize >= range.end {
                return self.finish(token, range.end);
            }
            self.push(token);
            if self.is_too_deep {
                return Err(());
            }
        }
    }

    /// Fills the rows with the tokens of `input`, which is preprocessed text.
    pub(crate) fn fill_from(&mut self, input: TokenizerInput<'_>) -> Result<(), ()> {
        match input {
            TokenizerInput::Latin1(units) => self.fill(units, 0..units.len()),
            TokenizerInput::Utf16(units) => self.fill(units, 0..units.len()),
        }
    }

    /// The component values of the rows, which are tokens of `source`. With `skip_gap`, whitespace and comments before
    /// the first token are not part of them.
    pub(crate) fn values<'a>(&'a self, source: TokenizerInput<'a>, skip_gap: bool) -> Values<'a> {
        Values {
            tokens: &self.tokens,
            source,
            row: 0,
            end: self.tokens.len() as u32 - 1,
            gap_taken: skip_gap,
        }
    }
}

/// A list of component values, and a position in it.
///
/// Whitespace and comments are not rows. The list has one whitespace value wherever a row follows either, which is
/// what a grammar can tell about them.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct Values<'a> {
    tokens: &'a [Token],
    source: TokenizerInput<'a>,
    /// The row of the next value.
    row: u32,
    /// The row after the last value: the token that closes the list, or the end-of-file token.
    end: u32,
    /// Whether the whitespace before the next row is behind the position.
    gap_taken: bool,
}

impl<'a> Values<'a> {
    fn last_row(&self) -> u32 {
        self.tokens.len() as u32 - 1
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn peek(&self) -> Option<Cv<'a>> {
        let token = self.tokens[self.row as usize];
        let is_whitespace = !self.gap_taken && token.follows_a_gap();
        if self.row == self.end && !is_whitespace {
            return None;
        }
        Some(Cv {
            tokens: self.tokens,
            source: self.source,
            row: self.row,
            is_whitespace,
        })
    }

    /// The value after the next `offset` values.
    pub(crate) fn peek_n(&self, offset: usize) -> Option<Cv<'a>> {
        let mut values = *self;
        for _ in 0..offset {
            values.next()?;
        }
        values.peek()
    }

    #[inline]
    #[allow(clippy::should_implement_trait)]
    pub(crate) fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Cv<'a>> {
        let value = self.peek()?;
        if value.is_whitespace {
            self.gap_taken = true;
            return Some(value);
        }
        let token = self.tokens[self.row as usize];
        if closer_of(token.kind).is_none() {
            self.row += 1;
            self.gap_taken = false;
        } else if token.part == self.last_row() {
            // NB: Nothing closes the value, so what ends the source is in it, and not after it.
            self.row = token.part;
            self.gap_taken = true;
        } else {
            self.row = token.part + 1;
            self.gap_taken = false;
        }
        Some(value)
    }

    /// Goes past the next value.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn skip(&mut self) {
        self.next();
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.peek().is_none()
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn discard_whitespace(&mut self) {
        self.gap_taken = true;
    }

    /// The values from the position up to the next comma, and goes past them and the comma. `None` once the list is
    /// behind the position and no comma was the last value.
    pub(crate) fn split_at_comma(&mut self, is_first: bool) -> Option<Values<'a>> {
        if !is_first && self.row == self.end && self.gap_taken {
            return None;
        }
        let mut rest = *self;
        loop {
            match rest.peek() {
                Some(value) if value.is_comma() => {
                    let part = Values { end: rest.row, ..*self };
                    rest.skip();
                    *self = rest;
                    return Some(part);
                }
                Some(_) => rest.skip(),
                None => {
                    let part = *self;
                    // NB: The position is the end of the list with nothing before it, which says that no part is left.
                    self.row = self.end;
                    self.gap_taken = true;
                    return if is_first || part.row != part.end || !part.gap_taken {
                        Some(part)
                    } else {
                        None
                    };
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Where the values from the position on are in the source, without the whitespace before and after them.
    pub(crate) fn source_range(&self) -> Range<usize> {
        let mut values = *self;
        values.discard_whitespace();
        let start = self.tokens[values.row as usize].start as usize;
        let mut end = start;
        while let Some(value) = values.next() {
            if !value.is_whitespace {
                end = value.source_end();
            }
        }
        start..end
    }

    /// The text of the source in `range`.
    pub(crate) fn source_text(&self, range: Range<usize>) -> Vec<u16> {
        let mut text = Vec::new();
        self.source.slice(range).append_to(&mut text);
        text
    }
}

/// One component value of a list.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct Cv<'a> {
    tokens: &'a [Token],
    source: TokenizerInput<'a>,
    row: u32,
    is_whitespace: bool,
}

impl<'a> Cv<'a> {
    #[inline]
    fn token(&self) -> Token {
        self.tokens[self.row as usize]
    }

    #[inline]
    fn kind(&self) -> Option<Kind> {
        (!self.is_whitespace).then(|| self.token().kind)
    }

    #[inline]
    fn code_at(&self, index: usize) -> u32 {
        u32::from(self.source.code_unit_at(index))
    }

    fn text(&self, range: (usize, usize), escapes: Option<Escapes>) -> Name {
        let (start, end) = range;
        match (self.source, escapes) {
            (TokenizerInput::Latin1(units), None) => units[start..end].iter().map(|&unit| u16::from(unit)).collect(),
            (TokenizerInput::Utf16(units), None) => SmallVec::from_slice(&units[start..end]),
            (source, Some(escapes)) => {
                // NB: What the escapes mean is not longer than the escapes.
                let mut output = Name::new();
                match source {
                    TokenizerInput::Latin1(units) => unescape(&units[start..end], escapes, &mut output),
                    TokenizerInput::Utf16(units) => unescape(&units[start..end], escapes, &mut output),
                }
                output
            }
        }
    }

    fn name(&self) -> Name {
        let token = self.token();
        self.text(token.name_range(), token.has(flag::ESCAPED).then_some(Escapes::Name))
    }

    /// Where the value ends in the source.
    fn source_end(&self) -> usize {
        let token = self.token();
        if closer_of(token.kind).is_none() {
            return token.end as usize;
        }
        let closing = self.tokens[token.part as usize];
        closing.end as usize
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn is_whitespace(&self) -> bool {
        self.is_whitespace
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn is_comma(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind() == Some(Kind::Comma)
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn is_colon(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind() == Some(Kind::Colon)
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn is_delim(&self, expected: u8) -> bool {
        self.kind() == Some(Kind::Delim) && self.code_at(self.token().start as usize) == u32::from(expected)
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn is_ident(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind() == Some(Kind::Ident)
    }

    pub(crate) fn ident(&self) -> Option<Name> {
        self.is_ident().then(|| self.name())
    }

    /// The value of a hash token that is a valid identifier.
    pub(crate) fn id(&self) -> Option<Name> {
        (self.kind() == Some(Kind::Hash) && self.token().has(flag::ID)).then(|| self.name())
    }

    pub(crate) fn string(&self) -> Option<Name> {
        if self.kind() != Some(Kind::String) {
            return None;
        }
        let token = self.token();
        let (range, escapes) = match self.source {
            TokenizerInput::Latin1(units) => string_range(units, token),
            TokenizerInput::Utf16(units) => string_range(units, token),
        };
        Some(self.text((range.start, range.end), escapes))
    }

    /// The value of a number token, and whether it is written as an integer, and with a sign.
    pub(crate) fn number(&self) -> Option<(f64, bool, bool)> {
        (self.kind() == Some(Kind::Number)).then(|| self.numeric_value())
    }

    /// The value of a dimension token, whether it is written as an integer, and its unit.
    pub(crate) fn dimension(&self) -> Option<(f64, bool, Name)> {
        if self.kind() != Some(Kind::Dimension) {
            return None;
        }
        let (value, is_integer, _) = self.numeric_value();
        Some((value, is_integer, self.name()))
    }

    fn numeric_value(&self) -> (f64, bool, bool) {
        let token = self.token();
        let (start, end) = token.number_range();
        let value = match self.source {
            TokenizerInput::Latin1(units) => number_of(&units[start..end]),
            TokenizerInput::Utf16(units) => number_of(&units[start..end]),
        };
        (value, token.has(flag::INTEGER), token.has(flag::SIGNED))
    }

    fn contents(&self) -> Values<'a> {
        Values {
            tokens: self.tokens,
            source: self.source,
            row: self.row + 1,
            end: self.token().part,
            gap_taken: false,
        }
    }

    /// The name of a function, and its arguments.
    pub(crate) fn function(&self) -> Option<(Name, Values<'a>)> {
        (self.kind() == Some(Kind::Function)).then(|| (self.name(), self.contents()))
    }

    /// What is in a block in square brackets.
    pub(crate) fn square_block(&self) -> Option<Values<'a>> {
        (self.kind() == Some(Kind::OpenSquare)).then(|| self.contents())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{Rows, Values};
    use crate::css::css_tokenizer::{ParserTokenKind, TokenizerInput, tokenize_for_parser};
    use crate::css::parser::component_value::{ComponentKind, ComponentValue, consume_a_list_of_component_values};
    use std::fmt::Write;

    fn old_shape(values: &[ComponentValue], output: &mut String) {
        let mut was_whitespace = false;
        for value in values {
            // NB: A run of whitespace and comments is one whitespace value in the rows.
            if value.is_whitespace() {
                if !was_whitespace {
                    output.push('_');
                }
                was_whitespace = true;
                continue;
            }
            was_whitespace = false;
            match &value.kind {
                ComponentKind::Function { name, values } => {
                    write!(output, "f{}(", String::from_utf16_lossy(name.as_ref())).unwrap();
                    old_shape(values, output);
                    output.push(')');
                }
                ComponentKind::SimpleBlock { opening, values } => {
                    output.push(if matches!(opening, ParserTokenKind::OpenSquare) {
                        '['
                    } else {
                        '<'
                    });
                    old_shape(values, output);
                    output.push('>');
                }
                ComponentKind::Token(ParserTokenKind::Ident(name)) => {
                    write!(output, "i{} ", String::from_utf16_lossy(name.as_ref())).unwrap();
                }
                ComponentKind::Token(ParserTokenKind::String(text)) => {
                    write!(output, "s{} ", String::from_utf16_lossy(text.as_ref())).unwrap();
                }
                ComponentKind::Token(ParserTokenKind::Comma) => output.push(','),
                ComponentKind::Token(ParserTokenKind::Colon) => output.push(':'),
                ComponentKind::Token(ParserTokenKind::Hash { value, is_id: true }) => {
                    write!(output, "#{} ", String::from_utf16_lossy(value.as_ref())).unwrap();
                }
                ComponentKind::Token(ParserTokenKind::Number { value, .. }) => write!(output, "n{value} ").unwrap(),
                ComponentKind::Token(ParserTokenKind::Dimension { value, unit, .. }) => {
                    write!(output, "d{value}{} ", String::from_utf16_lossy(unit.as_ref())).unwrap();
                }
                _ => output.push('?'),
            }
        }
    }

    fn new_shape(mut values: Values<'_>, output: &mut String) {
        while let Some(value) = values.next() {
            if value.is_whitespace() {
                output.push('_');
            } else if let Some((name, arguments)) = value.function() {
                write!(output, "f{}(", String::from_utf16_lossy(&name)).unwrap();
                new_shape(arguments, output);
                output.push(')');
            } else if let Some(contents) = value.square_block() {
                output.push('[');
                new_shape(contents, output);
                output.push('>');
            } else if value.kind() == Some(super::Kind::OpenParen) || value.kind() == Some(super::Kind::OpenCurly) {
                output.push('<');
                new_shape(value.contents(), output);
                output.push('>');
            } else if let Some(name) = value.ident() {
                write!(output, "i{} ", String::from_utf16_lossy(&name)).unwrap();
            } else if let Some(text) = value.string() {
                write!(output, "s{} ", String::from_utf16_lossy(&text)).unwrap();
            } else if value.is_comma() {
                output.push(',');
            } else if value.is_colon() {
                output.push(':');
            } else if let Some(name) = value.id() {
                write!(output, "#{} ", String::from_utf16_lossy(&name)).unwrap();
            } else if let Some((number, _, _)) = value.number() {
                write!(output, "n{number} ").unwrap();
            } else if let Some((number, _, unit)) = value.dimension() {
                write!(output, "d{number}{} ", String::from_utf16_lossy(&unit)).unwrap();
            } else {
                output.push('?');
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn rows_have_no_whitespace_from_after_their_range() {
        let units: Vec<u16> = "a  {".encode_utf16().collect();
        let source = TokenizerInput::Utf16(&units);
        let mut rows = Rows::default();
        rows.fill(&units, 0..1).unwrap();
        let mut values = rows.values(source, false);
        assert!(values.next().is_some_and(|value| value.is_ident()));
        assert!(values.is_empty());
        rows.fill(&units, 0..3).unwrap();
        let mut values = rows.values(source, false);
        assert!(values.next().is_some_and(|value| value.is_ident()));
        assert!(values.next().is_some_and(|value| value.is_whitespace()));
        assert!(values.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn has_the_component_values_of_the_tokenizer() {
        for source in [
            "",
            " ",
            "a",
            " a ",
            "a b",
            "a/**/b",
            "a /* x */ /* y */ b",
            ".a > .b:not( .c , #d ) ~ e[f = \"g\" i]",
            "a:nth-child( 2n + 1 of .b ), c",
            "a(b[c)d]e)f",
            "a ( b ] c ) d } e",
            "a(b",
            "a(b ",
            "a(b[c ",
            "a( /* x */",
            "[a",
            "a\\62 c, #\\31 23, 'x\\'y' \"unclosed",
            "#1a .5em 10px -3 +4n",
            "a,",
            ",a,,b ,",
            "{a(b}c",
        ] {
            let tokens = tokenize_for_parser(source.as_bytes());
            let old = consume_a_list_of_component_values(tokens.as_slice()).unwrap();
            let mut expected = String::new();
            old_shape(&old, &mut expected);
            for wide in [false, true] {
                let utf16 = source.encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>();
                let input = if wide {
                    TokenizerInput::Utf16(&utf16)
                } else {
                    TokenizerInput::Latin1(source.as_bytes())
                };
                let mut rows = Rows::default();
                rows.fill_from(input).unwrap();
                let mut actual = String::new();
                new_shape(rows.values(input, false), &mut actual);
                assert_eq!(actual, expected, "{source:?}");
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn splits_at_commas_like_a_slice() {
        for (source, expected) in [
            ("", vec![""]),
            ("a", vec!["a"]),
            ("a,b", vec!["a", "b"]),
            ("a , b(c,d) ,", vec!["a", "b(c,d)", ""]),
            (",", vec!["", ""]),
            (" ", vec![""]),
            ("a, ", vec!["a", ""]),
        ] {
            let input = TokenizerInput::Latin1(source.as_bytes());
            let mut rows = Rows::default();
            rows.fill_from(input).unwrap();
            let mut values = rows.values(input, false);
            let mut parts = Vec::new();
            let mut is_first = true;
            while let Some(part) = values.split_at_comma(is_first) {
                is_first = false;
                parts.push(String::from_utf16(&part.source_text(part.source_range())).unwrap());
            }
            assert_eq!(parts, expected, "{source:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn fails_where_component_values_are_too_deep() {
        let source = "(".repeat(crate::css::parser::component_value::MAXIMUM_COMPONENT_VALUE_NESTING_DEPTH + 1);
        let tokens = tokenize_for_parser(source.as_bytes());
        assert!(consume_a_list_of_component_values(tokens.as_slice()).is_err());
        let mut rows = Rows::default();
        assert!(rows.fill_from(TokenizerInput::Latin1(source.as_bytes())).is_err());
        let source = &source[1..];
        let tokens = tokenize_for_parser(source.as_bytes());
        assert!(consume_a_list_of_component_values(tokens.as_slice()).is_ok());
        assert!(rows.fill_from(TokenizerInput::Latin1(source.as_bytes())).is_ok());
    }
}

/*

//! The text a style sheet was parsed from. Only DevTools reads it, so a text of some size is kept
//! compressed: a thread of its own compresses each text soon after the parse, and a reader gets a
//! decompressed copy.

use crate::css::css_tokenizer::TokenizerInput;
use crate::css::style_value::RetainedString;
use libcompress_rust::{Compressor, Decompressor, Format};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

/// The smallest text that is worth compressing, in bytes.
const SMALLEST_COMPRESSED_TEXT_SIZE: usize = 10 * 1024;

enum State {
    Plain(RetainedString),
    Compressed { deflated: Box<[u8]>, is_latin1: bool },
}

/// The text of a sheet. A text that is too small to compress costs the sheet no more than the text itself.
pub(crate) enum SheetSourceText {
    Plain(RetainedString),
    Compressible(Arc<CompressibleText>),
}

impl SheetSourceText {
    /// The text of a parse that is not of a whole sheet, which has none.
    pub(crate) fn empty() -> Self {
        Self::Plain(RetainedString::from_ascii(String::new()))
    }

    /// The text of a sheet, which is compressed soon if that is worth it.
    pub(crate) fn new(source: TokenizerInput<'_>) -> Self {
        let plain = RetainedString::from_text(source);
        let size = match plain.units() {
            TokenizerInput::Latin1(bytes) => bytes.len(),
            TokenizerInput::Utf16(units) => size_of_val(units),
        };
        if size < SMALLEST_COMPRESSED_TEXT_SIZE {
            return Self::Plain(plain);
        }
        let text = Arc::new(CompressibleText::plain(plain));
        // NB: The tests that count what a parse allocates must not count what the queue allocates now and then.
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        compress_soon(&text);
        Self::Compressible(text)
    }

    pub(crate) fn to_utf16_string(&self) -> ak::Utf16String {
        match self {
            Self::Plain(text) => utf16_string_of(text),
            Self::Compressible(text) => text.to_utf16_string(),
        }
    }
}

fn utf16_string_of(text: &RetainedString) -> ak::Utf16String {
    match text.units() {
        TokenizerInput::Latin1(bytes) => ak::Utf16String::from_latin1(bytes),
        TokenizerInput::Utf16(units) => ak::Utf16String::from_utf16(units),
    }
}

pub(crate) struct CompressibleText {
    state: Mutex<State>,
}

impl CompressibleText {
    fn plain(text: RetainedString) -> Self {
        Self {
            state: Mutex::new(State::Plain(text)),
        }
    }

    fn to_utf16_string(&self) -> ak::Utf16String {
        match &*self.state.lock().expect("no reader of a sheet's text panics") {
            State::Plain(text) => utf16_string_of(text),
            State::Compressed { deflated, is_latin1 } => {
                let bytes = Decompressor::new(Format::Deflate)
                    .decompress(deflated)
                    .expect("a compressed text is what the compressor made of it")
                    .output;
                if *is_latin1 {
                    return ak::Utf16String::from_latin1(&bytes);
                }
                let units: Vec<u16> = bytes
                    .as_chunks::<2>()
                    .0
                    .iter()
                    .map(|bytes| u16::from_ne_bytes(*bytes))
                    .collect();
                ak::Utf16String::from_utf16(&units)
            }
        }
    }

    fn compress(&self) {
        // NB: The lock is not held while the text is compressed, so a reader does not wait for that.
        let text = match &*self.state.lock().expect("no reader of a sheet's text panics") {
            State::Plain(text) => text.clone(),
            State::Compressed { .. } => return,
        };
        let mut compressor = Compressor::new(Format::Deflate);
        let mut deflated = Vec::new();
        let (is_latin1, size) = match text.units() {
            TokenizerInput::Latin1(bytes) => {
                let Ok(more) = compressor.compress(bytes) else {
                    return;
                };
                deflated = more;
                (true, bytes.len())
            }
            TokenizerInput::Utf16(units) => {
                let mut bytes = Vec::new();
                for chunk in units.chunks(1 << 16) {
                    bytes.clear();
                    bytes.extend(chunk.iter().flat_map(|unit| unit.to_ne_bytes()));
                    let Ok(more) = compressor.compress(&bytes) else {
                        return;
                    };
                    deflated.extend(more);
                }
                (false, size_of_val(units))
            }
        };
        let Ok(end) = compressor.finish() else {
            return;
        };
        deflated.extend(end);
        if deflated.len() >= size {
            return;
        }
        *self.state.lock().expect("no reader of a sheet's text panics") = State::Compressed {
            deflated: deflated.into_boxed_slice(),
            is_latin1,
        };
    }
}

/// Hands the text to the thread that compresses the texts, which starts when the first text comes.
#[cfg(not(test))]
fn compress_soon(text: &Arc<CompressibleText>) {
    use std::sync::mpsc::{Sender, channel};
    use std::sync::{OnceLock, Weak};

    static QUEUE: OnceLock<Option<Mutex<Sender<Weak<CompressibleText>>>>> = OnceLock::new();
    let queue = QUEUE.get_or_init(|| {
        let (sender, receiver) = channel::<Weak<CompressibleText>>();
        std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("CSS source text".into())
            .spawn(move || {
                let mut next = receiver.recv();
                while let Ok(text) = next {
                    if let Some(text) = text.upgrade() {
                        text.compress();
                    }
                    next = receiver.try_recv().or_else(|_| {
                        // NB: The allocator keeps what a thread freed until the thread allocates again, which this
                        //     thread does not do until the next text comes, and it frees each text it compresses.
                        //     Standalone Rust tests do not link the C++ allocator.
                        #[cfg(feature = "allocator")]
                        ak::release_unused_allocator_memory();
                        receiver.recv()
                    });
                }
            })
            .ok()
            .map(|_| Mutex::new(sender))
    });
    if let Some(queue) = queue {
        let _ = queue
            .lock()
            .expect("sending a text does not panic")
            .send(Arc::downgrade(text));
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn units_of(text: &CompressibleText) -> Vec<u16> {
        text.to_utf16_string().to_utf16().into_owned()
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_compressed_text_reads_as_the_text_it_was() {
        let ascii = "a { color: red; } /* a comment */\n".repeat(1000);
        let wide: Vec<u16> = "b::before { content: \"\u{2192} \u{1f600}\"; }\n"
            .repeat(1000)
            .encode_utf16()
            .collect();

        let text = CompressibleText::plain(RetainedString::from_text(TokenizerInput::Latin1(ascii.as_bytes())));
        text.compress();
        assert!(
            matches!(&*text.state.lock().unwrap(), State::Compressed { deflated, .. } if deflated.len() < ascii.len() / 4)
        );
        assert_eq!(units_of(&text), ascii.encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>());

        let text = CompressibleText::plain(RetainedString::from_text(TokenizerInput::Utf16(&wide)));
        text.compress();
        assert!(matches!(
            &*text.state.lock().unwrap(),
            State::Compressed { is_latin1: false, .. }
        ));
        assert_eq!(units_of(&text), wide);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_text_that_does_not_get_smaller_stays_as_it_is() {
        let text = CompressibleText::plain(RetainedString::from_text(TokenizerInput::Latin1(b"a{}")));
        text.compress();
        assert!(matches!(&*text.state.lock().unwrap(), State::Plain(_)));
        assert_eq!(units_of(&text), "a{}".encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>());
    }
}

use super::syntax_parser::ParsedStyleSheet;
use super::value_parser::{FfiValueParsingContext, ParseContext, RandomFunctionIndex};
use crate::css::css_tokenizer::TokenizerInput;
use crate::css::ffi_support::FfiUtf16View;
