use super::{CompilationContext, NativeRuleType, NativeStyleSheet};
use crate::css::rule::read::RuleRef;
use crate::css::selector::SelectorListRef;
use crate::css::selector_operations::scope_root_selector_list;
use crate::css::selector_parser::RustParsedSelectorList;
use crate::css::style::bridge::{BoundScopeChain, declares_transitions};
use crate::css::style::engine_calls::document_host;
use crate::css::style::pipeline::rule_store::RuleKind;
use crate::css::style::rule_writes::{BoundSelectors, CompiledRule, CompiledRuleKind, RuleWrite};
use crate::render_state::DocumentHost;
use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::sync::Arc;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct NativeCompilationResult {
    pub published: bool,
    pub declares_transitions: bool,
}

// All pointers are borrowed for main-thread compilation. Neither the parser nor the native
// stylesheet graph retains document hosts, interners, or host callbacks.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct NativeStylePublication {
    /// The host of the document whose style engine the rules are published to.
    pub host: *const DocumentHost,
    pub sheet: u32,
    /// The native identity of the published rule the rules go before, or 0 for the end of the sheet.
    pub before: u64,
}

/// What the rules a traversal reaches are directly inside, as their nested declarations see it.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
enum Enclosing {
    #[default]
    None,
    Scope,
    /// A style rule, with its selectors.
    Style(RustParsedSelectorList),
}

// Binding belongs to this document-thread traversal, not to the shared rule graph.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(super) struct SelectorInputs {
    enclosing: Enclosing,
    /// The scopes the rules are inside.
    scope: Arc<BoundScopeChain>,
}

impl SelectorInputs {
    /// The selectors the engine matches `rule` by, whose `&` names what the sheet's arena says.
    pub(super) fn matching_selectors(&self, rule: RuleRef<'_>) -> Option<RustParsedSelectorList> {
        match rule.rule_type() {
            NativeRuleType::Style => rule.selectors(),
            NativeRuleType::NestedDeclarations => match &self.enclosing {
                Enclosing::Style(selectors) => Some(selectors.clone()),
                Enclosing::Scope => Some(RustParsedSelectorList {
                    selectors: SelectorListRef::pack(&scope_root_selector_list()),
                }),
                Enclosing::None => unreachable!("nested declarations are inside a style rule or `@scope`"),
            },
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The scopes the rules are inside.
    pub(super) fn scope(&self) -> Arc<BoundScopeChain> {
        self.scope.clone()
    }

    pub(super) fn within(
        &self,
        rule: RuleRef<'_>,
        matching: Option<RustParsedSelectorList>,
        implicit_root: u32,
    ) -> Self {
        let mut nested = self.clone();
        if rule.rule_type() == NativeRuleType::Style
            && let Some(selectors) = matching.or_else(|| self.matching_selectors(rule))
        {
            nested.enclosing = Enclosing::Style(selectors);
        }
        if let Some(scope) = rule.scope() {
            Arc::make_mut(&mut nested.scope).push(scope.start.as_ref(), scope.end.as_ref(), implicit_root);
        }
        match rule.rule_type() {
            NativeRuleType::Scope => nested.enclosing = Enclosing::Scope,
            NativeRuleType::Import => nested.enclosing = Enclosing::None,
            _ => {}
        }
        nested
    }
}

/// The rules one compilation publishes to a sheet of a document's style engine, ahead of one rule, which it writes
/// as one write as it ends. The host notes each rule it publishes as it compiles it.
pub(super) struct Publisher<'a> {
    /// The document whose engine the rules go to, or none where the process keeps them.
    host: Option<&'a DocumentHost>,
    sheet: u32,
    before: u64,
    rules: RefCell<Vec<CompiledRule>>,
}

impl<'a> Publisher<'a> {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The publication's host must be a live document host, on its document's thread, which outlives the publisher.
    pub(super) unsafe fn new(publication: &NativeStylePublication) -> Self {
        Self {
            // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
            host: Some(unsafe { document_host(publication.host) }),
            sheet: publication.sheet,
            before: publication.before,
            rules: RefCell::default(),
        }
    }

    /// A publisher of a user agent sheet, whose rules the process keeps, once: no document notes them.
    pub(super) fn of_user_agent_sheet() -> Self {
        Self {
            host: None,
            sheet: 0,
            before: 0,
            rules: RefCell::default(),
        }
    }

    /// The rules the compilation published, of a publisher of a user agent sheet.
    pub(super) fn into_rules(self) -> Vec<CompiledRule> {
        debug_assert!(self.host.is_none());
        self.rules.into_inner()
    }

    pub(super) fn host(&self) -> &'a DocumentHost {
        self.host.expect("only the rules of a document's sheet are edited")
    }

    pub(super) fn sheet(&self) -> u32 {
        self.sheet
    }

    /// A publisher of the same sheet, whose rules go before the rule `before` names.
    pub(super) fn before(&self, before: u64) -> Self {
        Self {
            host: self.host,
            sheet: self.sheet,
            before,
            rules: RefCell::default(),
        }
    }

    /// Writes the rules the compilation published, as one write.
    pub(super) fn finish(self) {
        let host = self.host();
        let rules = self.rules.into_inner();
        if rules.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        host.write_rules(RuleWrite::PublishRules {
            sheet: self.sheet,
            before: self.before,
            rules,
        });
    }

    /// Writes the selectors `selectors` for the published style rule `rule`, which keeps its place and declarations.
    pub(super) fn replace_selectors(
        &self,
        rule: RuleRef<'_>,
        context: &CompilationContext,
        selectors: RustParsedSelectorList,
    ) {
        self.host().write_rules(RuleWrite::ReplaceSelectors {
            identity: rule.identity(),
            selectors: BoundSelectors {
                selectors,
                scope: context.selectors.scope(),
            },
        });
    }

    /// Compiles `rule`, of `source`, into the rules the compilation publishes, where it is a rule the engine has, and
    /// answers whether it is one and whether it declares transitions.
    pub(super) fn compile(
        &self,
        rule: RuleRef<'_>,
        source: &NativeStyleSheet,
        context: &CompilationContext,
        selectors: Option<&RustParsedSelectorList>,
    ) -> NativeCompilationResult {
        let kind = match rule.rule_type() {
            NativeRuleType::Style | NativeRuleType::NestedDeclarations => {
                let selectors = selectors.unwrap();
                if selectors.selectors.is_empty() {
                    return NativeCompilationResult::default();
                }
                CompiledRuleKind::Style {
                    selectors: BoundSelectors {
                        selectors: selectors.clone(),
                        scope: context.selectors.scope(),
                    },
                    gated_by_container_query: context.gated_by_container_query,
                }
            }
            NativeRuleType::FontFeatureValues => CompiledRuleKind::NonMatching(RuleKind::FontFeatureValues),
            NativeRuleType::CounterStyle => CompiledRuleKind::NonMatching(RuleKind::CounterStyle),
            NativeRuleType::Function => CompiledRuleKind::NonMatching(RuleKind::Function),
            NativeRuleType::Property => CompiledRuleKind::Named {
                kind: RuleKind::Property,
                name: rule.definition_name().unwrap().units().into(),
            },
            NativeRuleType::Keyframes => CompiledRuleKind::Named {
                kind: RuleKind::Keyframes,
                name: rule.definition_name().unwrap().units().into(),
            },
            _ => return NativeCompilationResult::default(),
        };
        let declarations = rule.cascade_declarations();
        let declares_transitions = matches!(kind, CompiledRuleKind::Style { .. })
            && declarations
                .as_ref()
                .is_some_and(|declarations| declares_transitions(declarations.properties()));
        let in_a_layer = context.in_a_layer
            && matches!(
                rule.rule_type(),
                NativeRuleType::Style | NativeRuleType::NestedDeclarations | NativeRuleType::CounterStyle
            );
        if let Some(host) = self.host {
            host.published_rules().insert(self.sheet, rule.identity());
            // NB: These rules hand over declarations the rule write does not hold.
            match rule.rule_type() {
                NativeRuleType::Function => super::super::function::note_attr_names_read_by_function(host, rule),
                NativeRuleType::Keyframes => {
                    let _ = rule.visit_children(&mut |keyframe| {
                        let (_, declarations) = keyframe.keyframe();
                        crate::css::style::host_atoms::note_attr_names_read_by_block(host, &declarations);
                        std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(())
                    });
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        self.rules.borrow_mut().push(CompiledRule {
            identity: rule.identity(),
            kind,
            declarations,
            source_identity: source.identity(),
            conditions_hold: context.conditions_hold,
            in_a_layer,
            layer_name: context.layer_name.clone(),
            containers: context
                .containers
                .iter()
                .rev()
                .map(|&container| {
                    // SAFETY: The rule the traversal borrows holds the container conditions, as an Arc.
                    unsafe {
                        Arc::increment_strong_count(container);
                        Arc::from_raw(container)
                    }
                })
                .collect(),
        });
        NativeCompilationResult {
            published: true,
            declares_transitions,
        }
    }
}

//! What the CSSOM reads and changes of a rule, for libweb_bindings_rust, whose interfaces are implemented in Rust.

use std::rc::Rc;
use std::sync::Arc;

use ak::Utf16String;

use super::{NativeRule, NativeRuleList, NativeRuleType, RuleInsertionResult, RulePayload, RuleRemovalResult};
use crate::css::css_string::CssString;
use crate::css::css_tokenizer::TokenizerInput;
use crate::css::descriptor_block::FfiDescriptorBlock;
use crate::css::descriptor_metadata::descriptor_metadata;
use crate::css::font_feature_values::FontFeatureValuesRuleKind;
use crate::css::parser::descriptor_parser::parse_descriptor_text;
use crate::css::parser::query_parser::{FfiQueryHandle, serialized_query_condition, supports_query_matches};
use crate::css::parser::syntax::SyntaxNode;
use crate::css::parser::syntax_parser::{
    PageSelectorList, parse_keyframe_selector_list, parse_page_selector_list, serialized_page_selectors,
};
use crate::css::serialize::{
    SerializationMode, StringUnits, TextSink, serialize_a_string, serialize_an_identifier, serialize_style_value,
};
use crate::css::style_value_arc::StyleValueArc;

/// The at-rule id of @counter-style, as the descriptors of the generated metadata know it.
const COUNTER_STYLE_AT_RULE: u8 = 3;

fn utf16(units: &[u16]) -> Utf16String {
    Utf16String::from_utf16(units)
}

fn css_utf16(string: &CssString) -> Utf16String {
    utf16(string.units())
}

fn string_units(string: &Utf16String) -> StringUnits<'_> {
    match string.as_units() {
        ak::Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(bytes) | ak::Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(bytes) => StringUnits::Ascii(bytes),
        ak::Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => StringUnits::Utf16(units),
    }
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#serialize-an-identifier
pub fn serialize_identifier(identifier: &Utf16String) -> Utf16String {
    let mut sink = TextSink::new();
    serialize_an_identifier(&mut sink, &string_units(identifier));
    sink.into_utf16_string()
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#serialize-a-string
pub fn serialize_string_value(string: &Utf16String) -> Utf16String {
    let mut sink = TextSink::new();
    serialize_a_string(&mut sink, &string_units(string));
    sink.into_utf16_string()
}

fn value_text(value: &StyleValueArc) -> Utf16String {
    let mut sink = TextSink::new();
    serialize_style_value(&mut sink, value, SerializationMode::Normal);
    sink.into_utf16_string()
}

fn syntax_text(syntax: &SyntaxNode) -> Utf16String {
    let mut sink = TextSink::new();
    syntax.serialize_to(&mut sink);
    sink.into_utf16_string()
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-mixins-1/#serialize-a-css-type
fn serialize_a_css_type(sink: &mut TextSink, syntax: &SyntaxNode) {
    // To serialize a CSS type, return the concatenation of the following:
    // If the <css-type> consists of a single <syntax-component>, return the corresponding syntax string.
    if syntax.is_single_component() {
        syntax.serialize_to(sink);
        return;
    }

    // Otherwise, return the concatenation of the following:
    // The string "type(", i.e. "type" followed by a single LEFT PARENTHESIS (U+0028).
    sink.push_ascii("type(");

    // The corresponding syntax string.
    syntax.serialize_to(sink);

    // The string ")", i.e. a single RIGHT PARENTHESIS (U+0029).
    sink.push_ascii(")");
}

/// The name, type and default value of a parameter of a custom function, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-mixins-1/#dictdef-functionparameter
pub struct FunctionParameter {
    pub name: Utf16String,
    pub parameter_type: Utf16String,
    pub default_value: Option<Utf16String>,
}

/// The name and the query of a <container-condition>, each empty when the condition does not have it.
pub struct ContainerCondition {
    pub name: Utf16String,
    pub query: Utf16String,
}

/// The kinds of feature values of a @font-feature-values rule, in the order of the rule's serialization.
pub const FONT_FEATURE_VALUES_KINDS: [(FontFeatureValuesRuleKind, &str); 7] = [
    (FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Annotation, "annotation"),
    (FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Ornaments, "ornaments"),
    (FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Stylistic, "stylistic"),
    (FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Swash, "swash"),
    (FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::CharacterVariant, "character-variant"),
    (FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::Styleset, "styleset"),
    (FontFeatureValuesRuleKind::HistoricalForms, "historical-forms"),
];

/// Whether the name of a @keyframes rule serializes as an identifier, and not as a string.
pub fn is_valid_animation_name(name: &Utf16String) -> bool {
    crate::css::parser::value_parser::is_valid_animation_name(name.as_units().into())
}

impl NativeRule {
    /// The rule that the pointer points to, which keeps its reference.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `rule` must point to a live rule that an `Rc` owns.
    pub unsafe fn retained_from_raw(rule: *const Self) -> Rc<Self> {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a pointer into a live Rc.
        unsafe {
            Rc::increment_strong_count(rule);
            Rc::from_raw(rule)
        }
    }

    pub fn cssom_identity(&self) -> u64 {
        self.identity
    }

    pub fn cssom_type(&self) -> NativeRuleType {
        self.rule_type
    }

    /// The list of child rules of a rule that has one, which a style rule makes when it is asked.
    pub fn cssom_children(&self) -> Option<Rc<NativeRuleList>> {
        self.child_rules().cloned()
    }

    /// The memory the rule owns outside the heap.
    pub fn cssom_external_memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        super::rule_external_memory_size(self)
    }

    pub fn cssom_set_selector_text(&self, text: &Utf16String, sheet_rules: Option<&NativeRuleList>) -> bool {
        self.set_selector_text(text.as_units().into(), sheet_rules)
    }

    /// Whether the rule has an empty block of declarations or descriptors.
    pub fn has_no_declarations(&self) -> bool {
        match &self.payload {
            RulePayload::FontFace(block)
            | RulePayload::FunctionDeclarations(block)
            | RulePayload::Page { descriptors: block, .. } => block.data().descriptors.is_empty(),
            _ => self.declaration_block().is_none_or(|block| block.data().is_empty()),
        }
    }

    fn descriptor_block(&self) -> &FfiDescriptorBlock {
        match &self.payload {
            RulePayload::FontFace(block)
            | RulePayload::FunctionDeclarations(block)
            | RulePayload::Page { descriptors: block, .. } => block,
            RulePayload::CounterStyle(rule) => rule.descriptor_block(),
            _ => unreachable!("expected a rule with descriptors"),
        }
    }

    /// The value of the descriptor with the name, serialized.
    pub fn descriptor_text(&self, at_rule: u8, name: &str) -> Option<Utf16String> {
        let name: Vec<u16> = name.encode_utf16().collect();
        let id = descriptor_metadata(at_rule, &name)?.id;
        let data = self.descriptor_block().data();
        let descriptor = data.descriptors.iter().find(|descriptor| descriptor.id == id)?;
        Some(value_text(&descriptor.value))
    }

    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-animations-1/#dom-csskeyframesrule-name
    pub fn keyframes_name(&self) -> Utf16String {
        let RulePayload::Keyframes(name) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @keyframes rule")
        };
        css_utf16(&name.borrow())
    }

    pub fn set_keyframes_name(&self, name: &Utf16String) {
        let RulePayload::Keyframes(current) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @keyframes rule")
        };
        *current.borrow_mut() = CssString::from_utf16(&name.to_utf16());
    }

    /// The index of the last keyframe with the selector.
    pub fn find_keyframe(&self, selector: &Utf16String) -> Option<usize> {
        let selectors = parse_keyframe_selector_list(selector.as_units().into())?;
        let matches = |frame: &Self| {
            let RulePayload::Keyframe(frame) = &frame.payload else {
                unreachable!("a @keyframes rule holds keyframes")
            };
            frame.keys() == selectors
        };
        let children = self.child_rules()?;
        if let Some(rules) = children.rules.borrow().as_ref() {
            return rules.iter().rposition(|frame| matches(frame));
        }
        // NB: Most keyframes are not exposed yet, and reading the parsed source leaves them that way.
        let parsed = children.parsed_source.borrow();
        let parsed = parsed.as_ref()?;
        let exposed = children.exposed_rules.borrow();
        (0..parsed.len()).rev().find(|index| match exposed.get(index) {
            Some(frame) => matches(frame),
            None => *parsed.rule_at(*index).keyframe().unwrap().keys == selectors,
        })
    }

    pub fn keyframe_keys(&self) -> Vec<f64> {
        let RulePayload::Keyframe(frame) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a keyframe rule")
        };
        frame.keys().to_vec()
    }

    pub fn page_selector_text(&self) -> Utf16String {
        let RulePayload::Page { selectors, .. } = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @page rule")
        };
        serialized_page_selectors(&selectors.borrow())
    }

    /// Replaces the selectors of a @page rule with what the text parses to, and returns whether it parsed.
    pub fn set_page_selector_text(&self, text: &Utf16String) -> bool {
        let RulePayload::Page { selectors, .. } = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @page rule")
        };
        let Some(parsed) = parse_page_selector_list(TokenizerInput::from(text.as_units())) else {
            return false;
        };
        *selectors.borrow_mut() = Arc::new(PageSelectorList::new(parsed));
        true
    }

    /// The name of a margin rule or of a @position-try rule.
    pub fn at_rule_name(&self) -> Utf16String {
        match &self.payload {
            RulePayload::Margin { name, .. } | RulePayload::PositionTry { name, .. } => css_utf16(name),
            _ => unreachable!("expected a margin or @position-try rule"),
        }
    }

    pub fn namespace_prefix(&self) -> Utf16String {
        let RulePayload::Namespace(data) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @namespace rule")
        };
        css_utf16(&data.prefix)
    }

    pub fn namespace_uri(&self) -> Utf16String {
        let RulePayload::Namespace(data) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @namespace rule")
        };
        css_utf16(&data.uri)
    }

    pub fn layer_names(&self) -> Vec<Utf16String> {
        let RulePayload::LayerNames(names) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @layer rule")
        };
        names.names.iter().map(css_utf16).collect()
    }

    fn property(&self) -> &crate::css::property_rule::PropertyRuleData {
        let RulePayload::Property(data) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @property rule")
        };
        data
    }

    pub fn property_name(&self) -> Utf16String {
        css_utf16(&self.property().name)
    }

    pub fn property_syntax(&self) -> Utf16String {
        css_utf16(&self.property().syntax_source)
    }

    pub fn property_inherits(&self) -> bool {
        self.property().inherits
    }

    pub fn property_initial_value(&self) -> Option<Utf16String> {
        self.property().initial_value.as_ref().map(value_text)
    }

    fn function(&self) -> &crate::css::function_signature::FunctionSignature {
        let RulePayload::Function(signature) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @function rule")
        };
        signature
    }

    pub fn function_name(&self) -> Utf16String {
        css_utf16(&self.function().name)
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-mixins-1/#dom-cssfunctionrule-getparameters
    pub fn function_parameters(&self) -> Vec<FunctionParameter> {
        self.function()
            .parameters
            .iter()
            .map(|parameter| FunctionParameter {
                // name
                // The name of the function parameter.
                name: Utf16String::from_utf16(&parameter.name.to_utf16()),

                // type
                // The type of the function parameter, represented as a syntax string, or "*" if the parameter has no
                // type.
                parameter_type: syntax_text(&parameter.syntax),

                // defaultValue
                // The default value of the function parameter, or `null` if the argument does not have a default.
                default_value: parameter.default_value.as_ref().map(value_text),
            })
            .collect()
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-mixins-1/#dom-cssfunctionrule-returntype
    pub fn function_return_type(&self) -> Utf16String {
        // The return type of the custom function, represented as a syntax string. If the custom function has no return
        // type, returns "*".
        // NB: We always store a return type (defaulting to "*")
        syntax_text(&self.function().return_type)
    }

    /// The text of the prelude of a @function rule, as the steps 1 to 5 of
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-mixins-1/#serialize-a-cssfunctionrule make it.
    pub fn function_prelude_text(&self) -> Utf16String {
        let signature = self.function();
        // To serialize a CSSFunctionRule, return the concatenation of the following:
        let mut sink = TextSink::new();

        // 1. The string "@function" followed by a single SPACE (U+0020).
        sink.push_ascii("@function ");

        // 2. The result of performing serialize an identifier on the name of the custom function, followed by a single
        //    LEFT PARENTHESIS (U+0028).
        serialize_an_identifier(&mut sink, &StringUnits::Utf16(signature.name.units()));
        sink.push_ascii("(");

        // 3. The result of serialize a function parameter on each of the custom function’s parameters, all joined by
        //    ", " (COMMA U+002C, followed by a single SPACE U+0020).
        for (index, parameter) in signature.parameters.iter().enumerate() {
            if index != 0 {
                sink.push_ascii(", ");
            }

            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-mixins-1/#serialize-a-function-parameter
            // To serialize a function parameter, return the concatenation of the following:

            // The result of performing serialize an identifier on the name of the function parameter.
            serialize_an_identifier(&mut sink, &StringUnits::Utf16(&parameter.name.to_utf16()));

            // If the function parameter has a type, and that type is not the universal syntax definition:
            if !parameter.syntax.is_universal() {
                // - A single SPACE (U+0020), followed by the result of performing serialize a CSS type on that type.
                sink.push_ascii(" ");
                serialize_a_css_type(&mut sink, &parameter.syntax);
            }

            // If the function parameter has a default value:
            if let Some(default_value) = &parameter.default_value {
                // - A single COLON (U+003A), followed by a single SPACE (U+0020), followed by the result of performing
                //   serialize a CSS value on that value.
                sink.push_ascii(": ");
                serialize_style_value(&mut sink, default_value, SerializationMode::Normal);
            }
        }

        // 4. A single RIGHT PARENTHESIS (U+0029).
        sink.push_ascii(")");

        // 5. If the custom function has return type, and that return type is not the universal syntax definition ("*"):
        if !signature.return_type.is_universal() {
            // - A single SPACE (U+0020), followed by the string "returns", followed by a single SPACE (U+0020).
            sink.push_ascii(" returns ");

            // - The result of performing serialize a CSS type on that type.
            serialize_a_css_type(&mut sink, &signature.return_type);
        }
        sink.into_utf16_string()
    }

    fn supports_handle(&self) -> &FfiQueryHandle {
        let RulePayload::Supports(handle) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @supports rule")
        };
        handle
    }

    pub fn supports_condition_text(&self) -> Utf16String {
        serialized_query_condition(self.supports_handle())
    }

    pub fn supports_condition_matches(&self) -> bool {
        supports_query_matches(self.supports_handle())
    }

    pub fn import_supports_text(&self) -> Option<Utf16String> {
        let RulePayload::Import { data, .. } = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected an @import rule")
        };
        data.supports
            .as_ref()
            .map(|supports| serialized_query_condition(supports))
    }

    pub fn import_layer(&self) -> Option<Utf16String> {
        let RulePayload::Import { data, .. } = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected an @import rule")
        };
        data.layer.as_ref().map(css_utf16)
    }

    /// The conditions of a @container rule, in the order of the rule.
    pub fn container_conditions(&self) -> Vec<ContainerCondition> {
        let RulePayload::Container(data) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @container rule")
        };
        data.conditions
            .iter()
            .map(|condition| ContainerCondition {
                name: condition
                    .name
                    .as_ref()
                    .map_or_else(|| utf16(&[]), |name| serialize_identifier(&css_utf16(name))),
                query: condition
                    .query
                    .as_ref()
                    .map_or_else(|| utf16(&[]), |query| serialized_query_condition(query)),
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// The media queries of a rule with a list of them, which the MediaList of the rule shares.
    pub fn media_list(&self) -> crate::NativeMediaList {
        match &self.payload {
            RulePayload::Media { list } | RulePayload::Import { media: list, .. } => list.clone(),
            _ => unreachable!("expected a @media or @import rule"),
        }
    }

    /// The selector list of a style rule, as a pointer that C++ turns into text.
    pub fn style_selector_list(&self) -> *const core::ffi::c_void {
        self.style_rule().selectors_pointer().cast()
    }

    /// The selector lists that a @scope or a scoped @import rule starts and ends with, as pointers that C++ turns into
    /// text. A list that the rule omits is null.
    pub fn scope_selector_lists(&self) -> Option<(*const core::ffi::c_void, *const core::ffi::c_void)> {
        let scope = match &self.payload {
            RulePayload::Scope(scope) => Arc::clone(&scope.borrow()),
            RulePayload::Import { scope: Some(scope), .. } => Arc::clone(scope),
            _ => return None,
        };
        let pointer = |list: &Option<crate::css::selector_parser::RustParsedSelectorList>| {
            list.as_ref()
                .map_or(core::ptr::null(), |list| std::ptr::from_ref(list).cast())
        };
        Some((pointer(&scope.start), pointer(&scope.end)))
    }

    fn counter_style(&self) -> &crate::css::counter_style::FfiCounterStyle {
        let RulePayload::CounterStyle(rule) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @counter-style rule")
        };
        rule
    }

    pub fn counter_style_name(&self) -> Utf16String {
        self.counter_style().name_text()
    }

    /// Sets the name of a @counter-style rule, and returns whether the name is valid.
    pub fn set_counter_style_name(&self, name: &Utf16String) -> bool {
        self.counter_style().set_name_text(&name.to_utf16())
    }

    /// The descriptor of a @counter-style rule, serialized, or the empty string if the rule does not have it.
    pub fn counter_style_descriptor(&self, name: &str) -> Utf16String {
        self.descriptor_text(COUNTER_STYLE_AT_RULE, name)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| utf16(&[]))
    }

    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-counter-styles-3/#the-csscounterstylerule-interface
    /// Sets the descriptor to the value that the text parses to, and returns whether it did.
    pub fn set_counter_style_descriptor(&self, name: &str, text: &Utf16String) -> bool {
        // 1. parse the given value as the descriptor associated with the attribute.
        let name_units: Vec<u16> = name.encode_utf16().collect();
        let Some(value) = parse_descriptor_text(COUNTER_STYLE_AT_RULE, &name_units, &text.to_utf16()) else {
            // 2. If the result is invalid according to the given descriptor’s grammar, or would cause the
            //    @counter-style rule to not define a counter style, do nothing and abort these steps. (For example,
            //    some systems require the symbols descriptor to contain two values.)
            return false;
        };
        let rule = self.counter_style();
        match name {
            "symbols" | "additive-symbols" => {
                if !rule.system_accepts_symbols(name == "additive-symbols", &value) {
                    return false;
                }
            }
            // 3. If the attribute being set is system, and the new value would change the algorithm used, do nothing
            //    and abort these steps.
            // Note: It’s okay to change an aspect of the algorithm, like the first symbol value of a fixed system.
            "system" if rule.system_change_alters_algorithm(&value) => return false,
            _ => {}
        }

        // 4. Set the descriptor to the value.
        rule.set_descriptor(&name_units, value);
        true
    }

    pub fn font_feature_values_families(&self) -> Vec<Utf16String> {
        self.font_feature_values().families_text()
    }

    pub fn set_font_feature_values_families(&self, families: Vec<Utf16String>) {
        self.font_feature_values().set_families_text(families);
    }

    fn font_feature_values(&self) -> &crate::css::font_feature_values::FontFeatureValuesRule {
        let RulePayload::FontFeatureValues(values) = &self.payload else {
            unreachable!("expected a @font-feature-values rule")
        };
        values
    }

    pub fn set_font_feature_value(&self, kind: FontFeatureValuesRuleKind, name: &Utf16String, values: Vec<u32>) {
        self.font_feature_values().set_value(kind, &name.to_utf16(), values);
    }

    pub fn remove_font_feature_value(&self, kind: FontFeatureValuesRuleKind, name: &Utf16String) -> bool {
        self.font_feature_values().remove_value(kind, &name.to_utf16())
    }

    pub fn clear_font_feature_values(&self, kind: FontFeatureValuesRuleKind) {
        self.font_feature_values().clear_values(kind);
    }

    /// The name and the values of each feature value of the kind, in the order of the map.
    pub fn font_feature_values_entries(&self, kind: FontFeatureValuesRuleKind) -> Vec<(Utf16String, Vec<u32>)> {
        self.font_feature_values().entries_of(kind)
    }
}

    }

        self.insert_css_rule(index, rule, nested)

        self.remove(index);
    }

        self.replace(source);
    }

    }

use super::NativeRuleType;
use super::read::{NativeRuleView, RuleRef};
use crate::css::container_conditions::ContainerConditionsData;
use crate::css::custom_properties::{
    SubstitutionFunctionDeclaration, prepare_function_declarations, prepare_function_parameter_defaults,
};
use crate::css::ffi_support::OwnedArc;
use crate::css::function_signature::FunctionSignature;
use crate::css::media_list::MediaListData;
use crate::css::parser::component_value::ComponentValueList;
use std::ops::ControlFlow;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// One block of a function's declarations, with the conditions that gate it.
pub(crate) struct FunctionDeclarationInput {
    pub(crate) declarations: Vec<SubstitutionFunctionDeclaration>,
    pub(crate) reads_attributes: bool,
    /// The container conditions around the block, nearest first, which hold for an element or not.
    pub(crate) containers: Vec<Arc<ContainerConditionsData>>,
    /// The `@media` lists around the block, which hold for the document or not.
    pub(crate) media: Vec<Arc<MediaListData>>,
}

// Immutable compilation output. Media and container conditions stay inputs, evaluated where the
// function is called. No live rule, sheet, or descriptor owner is retained.
pub struct CompiledFunction {
    pub(crate) identity: u64,
    pub(crate) signature: Arc<FunctionSignature>,
    pub(crate) parameter_defaults: Vec<Option<ComponentValueList>>,
    pub(crate) parameter_defaults_read_attributes: bool,
    pub(crate) inputs: Vec<FunctionDeclarationInput>,
}

impl CompiledFunction {
    fn compile(view: &NativeRuleView<'_>) -> Self {
        fn walk(
            rule: RuleRef<'_>,
            outer_containers: &[Arc<ContainerConditionsData>],
            containers: &mut Vec<Arc<ContainerConditionsData>>,
            media: &mut Vec<Arc<MediaListData>>,
            inputs: &mut Vec<FunctionDeclarationInput>,
        ) {
            match rule.rule_type() {
                NativeRuleType::FunctionDeclarations => {
                    // Preserve the declaration walk's nearest-container semantics: enclosing
                    // conditions join the chain when the body enters a container rule.
                    let conditions = if containers.is_empty() {
                        Vec::new()
                    } else {
                        containers
                            .iter()
                            .rev()
                            .chain(outer_containers.iter().rev())
                            .cloned()
                            .collect()
                    };
                    let (parsed_declarations, reads_attributes) =
                        prepare_function_declarations(&rule.descriptors().unwrap());
                    inputs.push(FunctionDeclarationInput {
                        declarations: parsed_declarations,
                        reads_attributes,
                        containers: conditions,
                        media: media.clone(),
                    });
                    return;
                }
                NativeRuleType::Container => containers.push(rule.container().unwrap().clone()),
                NativeRuleType::Media => media.push(rule.media_data()),
                NativeRuleType::Supports if rule.cached_condition_holds() => {}
                _ => return,
            }
            let _ = rule.visit_children(&mut |child| {
                walk(child, outer_containers, containers, media, inputs);
                ControlFlow::Continue(())
            });
            match rule.rule_type() {
                NativeRuleType::Container => {
                    containers.pop();
                }
                NativeRuleType::Media => {
                    media.pop();
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        let signature = view.rule.function_signature().unwrap();
        let (parameter_defaults, parameter_defaults_read_attributes) = prepare_function_parameter_defaults(&signature);
        let mut result = Self {
            identity: view.rule.identity(),
            signature,
            parameter_defaults,
            parameter_defaults_read_attributes,
            inputs: Vec::new(),
        };
        let _ = view.rule.visit_children(&mut |child| {
            walk(
                child,
                view.containers,
                &mut Vec::new(),
                &mut Vec::new(),
                &mut result.inputs,
            );
            ControlFlow::Continue(())
        });
        result
    }
}

/// Notes what the `attr()`s of the `@function` rule `rule`, which the host is handing the engine, can read.
pub(super) fn note_attr_names_read_by_function(host: &crate::render_state::DocumentHost, rule: RuleRef<'_>) {
    let function = CompiledFunction::compile(&NativeRuleView { rule, containers: &[] });
    let defaults = function
        .parameter_defaults
        .iter()
        .flatten()
        .filter(|_| function.parameter_defaults_read_attributes);
    let bodies = function
        .inputs
        .iter()
        .filter(|input| input.reads_attributes)
        .flat_map(|input| &input.declarations)
        .map(SubstitutionFunctionDeclaration::tokens);
    for tokens in defaults.map(|tokens| tokens.as_ref()).chain(bodies) {
        crate::css::style::host_atoms::note_attr_names_read_by_tokens(host, tokens);
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_view_compile_function(view: &NativeRuleView<'_>) -> *const CompiledFunction {
    Arc::into_raw(Arc::new(CompiledFunction::compile(view)))
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_compiled_function_release(function: OwnedArc<CompiledFunction>) {
    drop(function);
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_compiled_function_retain(
    function: crate::css::ffi_support::ArcRef<'_, CompiledFunction>,
) -> *const CompiledFunction {
    Arc::into_raw(function.to_arc())
}

/// The functions a style sheet's top-level `@function` rules compile to, in order, with no rule
/// owner left alive.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn compile_functions_for_testing(source: &str) -> Vec<CompiledFunction> {
    let units: Vec<_> = source.encode_utf16().collect();
    let context = crate::css::parser::value_parser::ParseContext::default();
    let parsed = crate::css::parser::syntax_parser::parse_shared_stylesheet(
        crate::css::css_tokenizer::TokenizerInput::Utf16(&units),
        Some(&context),
    );
    let rules = super::NativeRuleList::from_parsed(parsed);
    let mut compiled = Vec::new();
    let _ = rules.visit_rules(&mut |rule| {
        compiled.push(CompiledFunction::compile(&NativeRuleView { rule, containers: &[] }));
        ControlFlow::Continue(())
    });
    compiled
}

use super::read::RuleRef;
use super::{NativeRule, NativeRuleList, NativeRuleType, RulePayload};
use crate::css::style_sheet::NativeStyleSheet;
use std::ops::ControlFlow;
use std::rc::Rc;

// A false continuation skips descendants. Keyframe blocks belong to their definition and never
// occupy independent positions in the cascade program. Import conditions do not change ordering.
fn visit_rule(
    rule: &NativeRule,
    sheet: &NativeStyleSheet,
    detached_import: Option<&NativeStyleSheet>,
    visit: &mut impl FnMut(&NativeRule) -> ControlFlow<(), bool>,
) -> ControlFlow<()> {
    if !visit(rule)? {
        return ControlFlow::Continue(());
    }
    if rule.rule_type == NativeRuleType::Import {
        let imported = sheet.imported_sheet(rule.identity);
        if let Some(imported) = detached_import.or(imported.as_deref()) {
            visit_list(imported.rules(), imported, visit)?;
        }
    } else if rule.rule_type != NativeRuleType::Keyframes
        && let Some(children) = rule.children.get()
    {
        visit_list(children, sheet, visit)?;
    }
    ControlFlow::Continue(())
}

fn visit_list(
    list: &NativeRuleList,
    sheet: &NativeStyleSheet,
    visit: &mut impl FnMut(&NativeRule) -> ControlFlow<(), bool>,
) -> ControlFlow<()> {
    for rule in list.materialized_rules().iter() {
        visit_rule(rule, sheet, None, visit)?;
    }
    ControlFlow::Continue(())
}

/// The identity of the first rule after the subtree of the rule `identity` that is `published`, or 0 for none.
pub(crate) fn successor(sheet: &NativeStyleSheet, identity: u64, mut published: impl FnMut(u64) -> bool) -> u64 {
    fn walk(
        rule: RuleRef<'_>,
        sheet: &NativeStyleSheet,
        identity: u64,
        found: &mut bool,
        published: &mut impl FnMut(u64) -> bool,
    ) -> ControlFlow<u64> {
        if rule.identity() == identity {
            *found = true;
            return ControlFlow::Continue(());
        }
        if *found && published(rule.identity()) {
            return ControlFlow::Break(rule.identity());
        }
        let mut successor = ControlFlow::Continue(());
        let mut visit = |child: RuleRef<'_>, sheet: &NativeStyleSheet| {
            successor = walk(child, sheet, identity, found, published);
            successor.map_break(|_| ())
        };
        if rule.rule_type() == NativeRuleType::Import {
            if let Some(imported) = sheet.imported_sheet(rule.identity()) {
                let _ = imported.rules().visit_rules(&mut |child| visit(child, &imported));
            }
        } else if rule.rule_type() != NativeRuleType::Keyframes {
            let _ = rule.visit_children(&mut |child| visit(child, sheet));
        }
        successor
    }
    let mut found = false;
    let mut successor = 0;
    let _ = sheet.rules().visit_rules(&mut |rule| {
        walk(rule, sheet, identity, &mut found, &mut published).map_break(|identity| successor = identity)
    });
    successor
}

/// Snapshot native owners before any host notifications or engine mutation can reenter.
///
/// # Safety
/// The root and all descendants must belong to live Rc allocations.
pub(crate) unsafe fn removed_rules(
    rule: &NativeRule,
    sheet: &NativeStyleSheet,
    detached_import: Option<&NativeStyleSheet>,
) -> Vec<Rc<NativeRule>> {
    let mut rules = Vec::new();
    let _ = visit_rule(rule, sheet, detached_import, &mut |rule| {
        let pointer = std::ptr::from_ref(rule);
        unsafe { Rc::increment_strong_count(pointer) };
        rules.push(unsafe { Rc::from_raw(pointer) });
        ControlFlow::Continue(true)
    });
    rules
}

pub(crate) fn declares_layer(rule: &NativeRule) -> bool {
    matches!(
        rule.rule_type,
        NativeRuleType::LayerStatement | NativeRuleType::LayerBlock
    ) || matches!(&rule.payload, RulePayload::Import { data, .. } if data.layer.is_some())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::css::media_list::MediaList;
    use crate::css::parser::syntax_parser::parse_shared_stylesheet;
    use crate::css::parser::value_parser::ParseContext;
    use crate::css::rule::rust_rule_list_remove;

    fn sheet(source: &str) -> Rc<NativeStyleSheet> {
        let units: Vec<_> = source.encode_utf16().collect();
        let view = crate::css::css_tokenizer::TokenizerInput::Utf16(&units);
        // All context fields are booleans, integers, or nullable pointers.
        let context = ParseContext::default();
        let parsed = parse_shared_stylesheet(view, Some(&context));
        let rules = crate::css::rule::NativeRuleList::from_parsed(parsed);
        let media = MediaList::new(Default::default());
        NativeStyleSheet::new(rules, media)
    }

    #[test]
    fn successor_skips_the_inserted_subtree_and_uncompiled_rules() {
        let sheet = sheet("@media all { .一 {} .二 {} } @layer 空; @supports (display: grid) { .三 {} } .四 {}");
        let rules = sheet.rules().materialized_rules();
        let first = &rules[0];
        let inside = first.child_rules().unwrap().materialized_rules()[0].identity;
        let next = rules[2].child_rules().unwrap().materialized_rules()[0].identity;
        let last = rules[3].identity;
        let published = |identity| [inside, next, last].contains(&identity);
        assert_eq!(successor(&sheet, first.identity, published), next);
        assert_eq!(successor(&sheet, rules[2].identity, published), last);
        assert_eq!(successor(&sheet, last, published), 0);
        assert_eq!(successor(&sheet, 0, published), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn imports_participate_in_order_and_detached_subtree_retirement() {
        let root = sheet("@import '一.css' layer(外); .最後 {}");
        let imported = sheet("@import '二.css'; .途中 {}");
        let nested = sheet("@keyframes 動き { from { opacity: 0 } to { opacity: 1 } } .先頭 {}");
        let import = root.rules().materialized_rules()[0].clone();
        let nested_import = imported.rules().materialized_rules()[0].clone();
        root.set_import(import.identity, Some(imported.clone()));
        imported.set_import(nested_import.identity, Some(nested.clone()));
        let middle = imported.rules().materialized_rules()[1].identity;
        let last = root.rules().materialized_rules()[1].identity;
        let published = |identity| identity == middle || identity == last;
        assert_eq!(successor(&root, nested_import.identity, published), middle);
        assert_eq!(successor(&root, import.identity, published), last);
        assert!(declares_layer(&import));
        assert!(!declares_layer(&nested_import));

        rust_rule_list_remove(root.rules(), 0);
        root.set_import(import.identity, None);
        let removed = unsafe { removed_rules(&import, &root, Some(&imported)) };
        let kinds: Vec<_> = removed.iter().map(|rule| rule.rule_type).collect();
        assert!(
            kinds
                == [
                    NativeRuleType::Import,
                    NativeRuleType::Import,
                    NativeRuleType::Keyframes,
                    NativeRuleType::Style,
                    NativeRuleType::Style
                ]
        );
        assert!(!removed.iter().any(|rule| rule.identity == last));
        assert_eq!(removed.last().unwrap().identity, middle);
    }
}

use super::{NativeRule, NativeRuleList, NativeRuleType, RulePayload};
use crate::css::container_conditions::ContainerConditionsData;
use crate::css::css_string::CssString;
use crate::css::declaration_block::SharedDeclarationBlock;
use crate::css::descriptor_block::{DescriptorBlockData, FfiDescriptorBlock};
use crate::css::font_feature_values::FontFeatureValuesData;
use crate::css::function_signature::FunctionSignature;
use crate::css::import_rule::ImportRuleData;
use crate::css::layer_names::LayerNames;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum RuleRef<'a> {
    Materialized(&'a NativeRule),
    Shared(SharedRule<'a>, &'a NativeRuleList),
}

// Borrowed for one host callback. Retaining immutable payload data never retains this view
// or creates a live CSSOM rule. The host must not keep the view past the callback.
pub struct NativeRuleView<'a> {
    pub(crate) rule: RuleRef<'a>,
    pub(crate) containers: &'a [Arc<ContainerConditionsData>],
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_change_needs_style_environment_bump(rule: &NativeRule) -> bool {
    RuleRef::Materialized(rule).change_needs_style_environment_bump()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_view_identity(view: &NativeRuleView<'_>) -> u64 {
    view.rule.identity()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_view_type(view: &NativeRuleView<'_>) -> NativeRuleType {
    view.rule.rule_type()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_list_has_implicit_scope(list: &NativeRuleList) -> bool {
    list.visit_descendant_rules(&mut |rule| {
        if rule.scope().is_some_and(|scope| scope.start.is_none()) {
            ControlFlow::Break(())
        } else {
            ControlFlow::Continue(())
        }
    })
    .is_break()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_list_has_counter_style_rules(list: &NativeRuleList) -> bool {
    list.visit_descendant_rules(&mut |rule| {
        if rule.rule_type() == NativeRuleType::CounterStyle {
            ControlFlow::Break(())
        } else {
            ControlFlow::Continue(())
        }
    })
    .is_break()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_list_has_anonymous_layer(list: &NativeRuleList) -> bool {
    list.visit_descendant_rules(&mut |rule| {
        let anonymous = match rule {
            RuleRef::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::LayerNames(names) if rule.rule_type == NativeRuleType::LayerBlock => {
                    names.names[0].units().is_empty()
                }
                _ => false,
            },
            RuleRef::Shared(rule, _) => rule.layer_name().is_some_and(<[u16]>::is_empty),
        };
        if anonymous {
            ControlFlow::Break(())
        } else {
            ControlFlow::Continue(())
        }
    })
    .is_break()
}

// The caller must retain the source list or a snapshot for as long as it uses this identity.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_list_shared_contents_identity(list: &NativeRuleList) -> usize {
    list.shared_contents()
        .map_or(0, |contents| std::sync::Arc::as_ptr(&contents) as usize)
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_list_clone_shared_contents(list: &NativeRuleList) -> *const NativeRuleList {
    list.shared_contents().map_or(std::ptr::null(), |contents| {
        std::rc::Rc::into_raw(NativeRuleList::from_parsed(contents))
    })
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_view_property(view: &NativeRuleView<'_>) -> *const PropertyRuleData {
    match view.rule {
        RuleRef::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
            RulePayload::Property(property) => Arc::as_ptr(property),
            _ => std::ptr::null(),
        },
        RuleRef::Shared(rule, _) => rule.property().map_or(std::ptr::null(), std::ptr::from_ref),
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_view_container(view: &NativeRuleView<'_>) -> *const ContainerConditionsData {
    view.rule.container().map_or(std::ptr::null(), Arc::as_ptr)
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_view_descriptors(view: &NativeRuleView<'_>) -> *mut FfiDescriptorBlock {
    Box::into_raw(Box::new(FfiDescriptorBlock::new(view.rule.descriptors().unwrap())))
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_view_import(view: &NativeRuleView<'_>) -> *const ImportRuleData {
    match view.rule {
        RuleRef::Shared(rule, _) => Arc::as_ptr(rule.import().unwrap()),
        RuleRef::Materialized(rule) => {
            let RulePayload::Import { data, .. } = &rule.payload else {
                unreachable!()
            };
            Arc::as_ptr(data)
        }
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_view_import_media(view: &NativeRuleView<'_>) -> *mut MediaList {
    let media = match view.rule {
        RuleRef::Shared(rule, list) => list
            .import_media
            .borrow_mut()
            .entry(view.rule.identity())
            .or_insert_with(|| MediaList::new(rule.media_data()))
            .clone(),
        RuleRef::Materialized(rule) => {
            let RulePayload::Import { media, .. } = &rule.payload else {
                unreachable!()
            };
            media.clone()
        }
    };
    Box::into_raw(Box::new(media))
}

/// Materialize a facade's import rule, including one first exposed after detachment. `identity` must identify this
/// import, and `media` must be its loading state.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_materialize_import(
    identity: u64,
    data: crate::css::ffi_support::ArcRef<'_, ImportRuleData>,
    media: &MediaList,
) -> *const NativeRule {
    let data = data.to_arc();
    let scope = data.scope.clone();
    std::rc::Rc::into_raw(NativeRule::with_identity(
        identity,
        NativeRuleType::Import,
        RulePayload::Import {
            data,
            media: media.clone(),
            scope,
        },
        None,
        None,
    ))
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_view_font_feature_values(view: &NativeRuleView<'_>) -> *const FontFeatureValuesData {
    let data = match view.rule {
        RuleRef::Shared(rule, _) => rule.font_feature_values().unwrap(),
        RuleRef::Materialized(rule) => {
            let RulePayload::FontFeatureValues(values) = &rule.payload else {
                unreachable!()
            };
            values.snapshot()
        }
    };
    Arc::into_raw(data)
}

/// # Safety
/// The callback must not mutate the graph or retain borrowed name text.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_rule_view_name(
    view: &NativeRuleView<'_>,
    context: *mut std::ffi::c_void,
    visit: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut std::ffi::c_void, *const u16, usize),
) {
    let name = view.rule.definition_name().unwrap();
    unsafe {
        visit(context, name.units().as_ptr(), name.units().len());
    }
}

/// The declarations of a `@position-try` rule, retained for the caller.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_view_position_try_declarations(
    view: &NativeRuleView<'_>,
) -> *const crate::css::declaration_block::DeclarationBlockHeader {
    assert!(view.rule.rule_type() == NativeRuleType::PositionTry);
    view.rule.position_try_declarations().map_or(
        std::ptr::null(),
        crate::css::declaration_block::SharedDeclarationBlock::into_raw,
    )
}

impl NativeRuleView<'_> {
    /// Each keyframe block of the `@keyframes` rule this views: its keys and its declarations.
    pub(crate) fn for_each_keyframe(&self, mut visit: impl FnMut(&[f64], SharedDeclarationBlock)) {
        assert!(self.rule.rule_type() == NativeRuleType::Keyframes);
        let _ = self.rule.visit_children(&mut |frame| {
            let (keys, declarations) = frame.keyframe();
            visit(keys, declarations);
            ControlFlow::Continue(())
        });
    }
}

impl<'a> RuleRef<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn change_needs_style_environment_bump(self) -> bool {
        match self.rule_type() {
            NativeRuleType::Style
            | NativeRuleType::Media
            | NativeRuleType::Supports
            | NativeRuleType::Container
            | NativeRuleType::Scope
            | NativeRuleType::LayerBlock => self
                .visit_children(&mut |child| {
                    if child.change_needs_style_environment_bump() {
                        ControlFlow::Break(())
                    } else {
                        ControlFlow::Continue(())
                    }
                })
                .is_break(),
            NativeRuleType::NestedDeclarations
            | NativeRuleType::Property
            | NativeRuleType::LayerStatement
            | NativeRuleType::Keyframes
            | NativeRuleType::FontFace
            | NativeRuleType::Function
            | NativeRuleType::CounterStyle
            | NativeRuleType::FontFeatureValues => false,
            _ => true,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn function_signature(self) -> Option<Arc<FunctionSignature>> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::Function(signature) => Some(signature.clone()),
                _ => None,
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.function_signature(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn descriptors(self) -> Option<Arc<DescriptorBlockData>> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::FontFace(block)
                | RulePayload::FunctionDeclarations(block)
                | RulePayload::Page { descriptors: block, .. } => Some(block.data()),
                RulePayload::CounterStyle(rule) => Some(rule.descriptors()),
                _ => None,
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.descriptors(),
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn keyframe(self) -> (&'a [f64], SharedDeclarationBlock) {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => {
                let RulePayload::Keyframe(frame) = &rule.payload else {
                    unreachable!()
                };
                (frame.keys(), frame.declarations())
            }
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => {
                let frame = rule.keyframe().unwrap();
                (&frame.keys, frame.declarations.clone())
            }
        }
    }
    pub(crate) fn rule_type(self) -> NativeRuleType {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => rule.rule_type,
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.rule_type(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn identity(self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => rule.identity,
            Self::Shared(rule, list) => list.identity_for(rule.local_identity()),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn internal_layer_name(self) -> Option<Cow<'a, [u16]>> {
        let name = match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::LayerNames(names) if rule.rule_type == NativeRuleType::LayerBlock => {
                    names.names[0].units()
                }
                RulePayload::Import { data, .. } => data.layer.as_ref()?.units(),
                _ => return None,
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.layer_name()?,
        };
        if !name.is_empty() {
            return Some(Cow::Borrowed(name));
        }
        let mut buffer = [0_u16; 21];
        let mut start = buffer.len();
        let mut identity = self.identity();
        loop {
            start -= 1;
            buffer[start] = u16::from(b'0') + (identity % 10) as u16;
            identity /= 10;
            if identity == 0 {
                break;
            }
        }
        start -= 1;
        buffer[start] = u16::from(b'#');
        Some(Cow::Owned(buffer[start..].to_vec()))
    }

    pub(crate) fn definition_name(self) -> Option<CssString> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::Property(property) => Some(property.name.clone()),
                RulePayload::Keyframes(name) => Some(name.borrow().clone()),
                RulePayload::CounterStyle(rule) => Some(rule.name()),
                RulePayload::PositionTry { name, .. } => Some(name.clone()),
                _ => None,
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.definition_name(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn layer_names(self) -> Option<&'a LayerNames> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::LayerNames(names) => Some(names),
                _ => None,
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.layer_names(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn container(self) -> Option<&'a Arc<ContainerConditionsData>> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::Container(container) => Some(container),
                _ => None,
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.container(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn condition_holds(self, environment: MediaEnvironment<'_>) -> bool {
        if !self.supports_hold() {
            return false;
        }
        if self.rule_type() == NativeRuleType::Media {
            self.evaluate_media(environment)
        } else if self.rule_type() == NativeRuleType::Import {
            self.media_matches()
        } else {
            true
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn supports_hold(self) -> bool {
        let condition = match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::Supports(condition) => Some(condition),
                RulePayload::Import { data, .. } => data.supports.as_ref(),
                _ => None,
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.supports(),
        };
        condition.is_none_or(|condition| condition.evaluate_supports() == Some(super::MatchResult::True))
    }

    pub(crate) fn cached_condition_holds(self) -> bool {
        self.supports_hold()
            && (!matches!(self.rule_type(), NativeRuleType::Media | NativeRuleType::Import) || self.media_matches())
    }

    pub(crate) fn media_matches(self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::Media { list, .. } | RulePayload::Import { media: list, .. } => list.matches(),
                _ => unreachable!(),
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, list) => {
                if rule.rule_type() == NativeRuleType::Import
                    && let Some(media) = list.import_media.borrow().get(&self.identity())
                {
                    return media.matches();
                }
                let results = list.media_results.borrow();
                results.get(&self.identity()).map_or_else(
                    || rule.media().unwrap().queries.is_empty(),
                    |result| result.matches.is_empty() || result.matches.iter().any(|matches| *matches),
                )
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn media_data(self) -> Arc<crate::css::media_list::MediaListData> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::Media { list } => list.data(),
                _ => unreachable!(),
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.media_data(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn evaluate_media(self, environment: MediaEnvironment<'_>) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::Media { list, .. } | RulePayload::Import { media: list, .. } => list.evaluate(environment),
                _ => unreachable!(),
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, list) => {
                let mut results = list.media_results.borrow_mut();
                let result = results.entry(self.identity()).or_default();
                result.matches.clear();
                result.matches.extend(
                    rule.media()
                        .unwrap()
                        .queries
                        .iter()
                        .map(|query| query.matches_media(environment)),
                );
                result.matches.is_empty() || result.matches.iter().any(|matches| *matches)
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn namespace(self) -> Option<Arc<NamespaceRuleData>> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::Namespace(namespace) => Some(namespace.clone()),
                _ => None,
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.namespace().cloned(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn selectors(self) -> Option<RustParsedSelectorList> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::Style(style) => Some(style.selectors()),
                _ => None,
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.selectors(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn scope(self) -> Option<Arc<ScopeSelectors>> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::Scope(scope) => Some(scope.borrow().clone()),
                RulePayload::Import { scope: Some(scope), .. } => Some(scope.clone()),
                _ => None,
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.scope(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn cascade_declarations(self) -> Option<SharedDeclarationBlock> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => rule.cascade_declarations(),
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.cascade_declarations(),
        }
    }

    /// The declarations of a `@position-try` rule.
    pub(crate) fn position_try_declarations(self) -> Option<SharedDeclarationBlock> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match &rule.payload {
                RulePayload::PositionTry { declarations, .. } => Some(declarations.data()),
                _ => None,
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, _) => rule.position_try_declarations(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn visit_children(self, visit: &mut impl FnMut(RuleRef<'_>) -> ControlFlow<()>) -> ControlFlow<()> {
        match self {
            Self::Materialized(rule) => match rule.children.get() {
                Some(children) => children.visit_rules(visit),
                None => ControlFlow::Continue(()),
            },
            Self::Shared(rule, base) => rule.visit_children(&mut |child| visit(Self::Shared(child, base))),
        }
    }
}

impl NativeRuleList {
    pub(crate) fn visit_descendant_rules(
        &self,
        visit: &mut impl FnMut(RuleRef<'_>) -> ControlFlow<()>,
    ) -> ControlFlow<()> {
        fn walk(rule: RuleRef<'_>, visit: &mut impl FnMut(RuleRef<'_>) -> ControlFlow<()>) -> ControlFlow<()> {
            visit(rule)?;
            rule.visit_children(&mut |child| walk(child, visit))
        }
        self.visit_rules(&mut |rule| walk(rule, visit))
    }

    /// Visits the rules of [`Self::visit_rules`] a media evaluation reaches while the media of the list's sheet holds
    /// as it did: those that are, or hold, a `@media` or `@import` rule.
    pub(crate) fn visit_media_holding_rules(
        &self,
        visit: &mut impl FnMut(RuleRef<'_>) -> ControlFlow<()>,
    ) -> ControlFlow<()> {
        // A rule the CSSOM exposed or edited may hold a `@media` rule the parse did not.
        if self.rules.borrow().is_some() || !self.exposed_rules.borrow().is_empty() {
            return self.visit_rules(visit);
        }
        let parsed = self.parsed_source.borrow();
        let Some(parsed) = parsed.as_ref() else {
            return ControlFlow::Continue(());
        };
        parsed.visit_media_holding_rules(&mut |rule| visit(RuleRef::Shared(rule, self)))
    }

    pub(crate) fn visit_rules(&self, visit: &mut impl FnMut(RuleRef<'_>) -> ControlFlow<()>) -> ControlFlow<()> {
        if let Some(rules) = self.rules.borrow().as_ref() {
            for rule in rules {
                visit(RuleRef::Materialized(rule))?;
            }
            return ControlFlow::Continue(());
        }
        let parsed = self.parsed_source.borrow();
        let exposed = self.exposed_rules.borrow();
        let mut index = 0;
        parsed.as_ref().unwrap().visit_rules(&mut |rule| {
            let rule = match exposed.get(&index) {
                Some(rule) => RuleRef::Materialized(rule),
                None => RuleRef::Shared(rule, self),
            };
            index += 1;
            visit(rule)
        })
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_rule_list_descriptor_snapshot(list: &NativeRuleList, identity: u64) -> *mut FfiDescriptorBlock {
    let mut result = std::ptr::null_mut();
    let _ = list.visit_descendant_rules(&mut |rule| {
        if rule.identity() != identity {
            return ControlFlow::Continue(());
        }
        result = Box::into_raw(Box::new(FfiDescriptorBlock::new(rule.descriptors().unwrap())));
        ControlFlow::Break(())
    });
    result
}

/// # Safety
/// The callback must not mutate the list or retain the borrowed view.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_rule_list_visit_font_rules(
    list: &NativeRuleList,
    context: *const std::ffi::c_void,
    visit: unsafe extern "C" fn(*const std::ffi::c_void, &NativeRuleView<'_>),
) {
    let _ = list.visit_descendant_rules(&mut |rule| {
        if matches!(
            rule.rule_type(),
            NativeRuleType::FontFace | NativeRuleType::FontFeatureValues
        ) {
            unsafe {
                visit(context, &NativeRuleView { rule, containers: &[] });
            }
        }
        ControlFlow::Continue(())
    });
}

/// # Safety
/// The callback must not mutate the rule list or retain the borrowed view.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_rule_list_visit_rule_data(
    list: &NativeRuleList,
    context: *const std::ffi::c_void,
    visit: unsafe extern "C" fn(*const std::ffi::c_void, &NativeRuleView<'_>) -> bool,
) {
    let _ = list.visit_rules(&mut |rule| {
        if unsafe { visit(context, &NativeRuleView { rule, containers: &[] }) } {
            ControlFlow::Continue(())
        } else {
            ControlFlow::Break(())
        }
    });
}

//! Parsed selectors, as 8-byte components in one immutable arena per parsed list.
//!
//! Every selector of a list, nested argument lists included, is a run of [`Component`]s in
//! matching order: the subject compound first, and inside a compound the simple selectors in the
//! order they were written. The last component of each compound carries the [`Relation`] to the
//! compound left of it. A nested list is stored before the selector that names it, so runs never
//! interleave. Payloads that do not fit a component's 32-bit data go in typed side pools.
//!
//! Names are process style atoms, which the arena leases once each. The arena is `Send` and
//! `Sync`: it holds atoms, indices and text only.
//!
//! Readers see the components through borrowed views ([`Selector`], [`CompoundRef`],
//! [`SimpleSelector`]) that decode them on the fly.

use smallvec::SmallVec;
use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::css::selector::{
    AnPlusBPattern, AttributeCaseType, AttributeMatchType, Combinator, Direction, NameSelector, NamespaceType,
    PseudoClassParameterType, PseudoClassType, PseudoElementType, QualifiedName, SearchTextMatchFilter, Specificity,
    pseudo_class_from_ffi,
};
use crate::css::selector_tree as tree;
use crate::css::style::AtomLeases;
use crate::css::style::index::StyleAtomID;

/// The number a selector arena takes as it is frozen, which no other arena of the process ever
/// takes: what a cache keyed by a selector names its arena by, where an address could be reused
/// by the arena of a later parse.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub(crate) struct SelectorArenaSerial(u64);

impl SelectorArenaSerial {
    /// The next serial of the process, from `next`, the counter of its process style.
    pub(crate) fn next(next: &std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64) -> Self {
        Self(next.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed))
    }
}

/// Where a selector list starts in its arena.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub(crate) struct ListStart(u32);

/// A component's position in its arena.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub(crate) struct ComponentOffset(u32);

impl ComponentOffset {
    /// Where the page of `1 << page_bits` components the component is in starts, and where it is
    /// in that page.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn in_page(self, page_bits: u32) -> (Self, u32) {
        let mask = (1 << page_bits) - 1;
        (Self(self.0 & !mask), self.0 & mask)
    }

    /// The component `offset` components into the page starting at `self`.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn into_page(self, offset: u32) -> Self {
        Self(self.0 + offset)
    }
}

/// A style rule's place among the style rules whose selectors an arena holds: the rule a `&`
/// names, through the arena's rule lists.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub(crate) struct RuleOrdinal(u32);

/// What a `&` names.
///
/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-nesting/#nest-selector
/// The nesting selector represents the elements matched by the parent rule. When the parent rule
/// is a style rule, it represents the elements matched by that rule's selector list; inside a
/// scoped rule it represents the scoping root, and anywhere else the root of the tree.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Nesting<Rule> {
    /// The root of the tree, or the scoping root where a scope is bound.
    #[default]
    Root,
    /// The scoping root of the `@scope` the rule is directly in.
    Scope,
    /// The selectors of the style rule the rule is nested in, in the same arena.
    Rule(Rule),
    /// A style rule the parse did not see, as when the CSSOM parses a nested rule's selectors
    /// before it places the rule. Placing it binds the `&` to its parent.
    Unbound,
}

/// What a `&` names, as the parse that wrote it knew.
pub(crate) type NestingTarget = Nesting<RuleOrdinal>;

/// What a `&` in an arena names, decoded: the selectors of the parent style rule are `:is()` of them.
pub type NestingOfArena<'a> = Nesting<SelectorListView<'a>>;

const NESTING_ROOT: u8 = 0;
const NESTING_SCOPE: u8 = 1;
const NESTING_RULE: u8 = 2;
const NESTING_UNBOUND: u8 = 3;

impl NestingTarget {
    fn kind(self) -> u8 {
        match self {
            Self::Root => NESTING_ROOT,
            Self::Scope => NESTING_SCOPE,
            Self::Rule(_) => NESTING_RULE,
            Self::Unbound => NESTING_UNBOUND,
        }
    }
}

/// A run of entries in one of an arena's pools.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct PoolRange {
    start: u32,
    length: u32,
}

impl PoolRange {
    fn of<T>(pool: &[T], range: PoolRange) -> &[T] {
        &pool[range.start as usize..(range.start + range.length) as usize]
    }
}

fn index_u32(index: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::try_from(index).expect("a selector list holds fewer than 2^32 parts")
}

/// What a component is.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum ComponentKind {
    Universal,
    Tag,
    Id,
    Class,
    Attribute,
    PseudoClass,
    PseudoElement,
    Nesting,
    Invalid,
    /// The implicit leftmost compound of a selector that starts with a combinator.
    RelativeAnchor,
}

/// How the compound a component ends relates to the compound left of it, or `SubSelector` for a
/// component that does not end its compound.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub(crate) enum Relation {
    SubSelector,
    Descendant,
    Child,
    NextSibling,
    SubsequentSibling,
    Column,
    PseudoElement,
    /// The component ends the leftmost compound, and so the complex selector.
    Leftmost,
}

impl Relation {
    fn of(combinator: Combinator) -> Self {
        match combinator {
            Combinator::None => Self::Leftmost,
            Combinator::Descendant => Self::Descendant,
            Combinator::ImmediateChild => Self::Child,
            Combinator::NextSibling => Self::NextSibling,
            Combinator::SubsequentSibling => Self::SubsequentSibling,
            Combinator::Column => Self::Column,
            Combinator::PseudoElement => Self::PseudoElement,
        }
    }

    fn combinator(self) -> Combinator {
        match self {
            Self::Descendant => Combinator::Descendant,
            Self::Child => Combinator::ImmediateChild,
            Self::NextSibling => Combinator::NextSibling,
            Self::SubsequentSibling => Combinator::SubsequentSibling,
            Self::Column => Combinator::Column,
            Self::PseudoElement => Combinator::PseudoElement,
            Self::SubSelector | Self::Leftmost => Combinator::None,
        }
    }
}

const KIND_BITS: u32 = 0x0000_000f;
const RELATION_SHIFT: u32 = 4;
const RELATION_BITS: u32 = 0x0000_00f0;
const PSEUDO_SHIFT: u32 = 8;
const PSEUDO_BITS: u32 = 0x0000_ff00;
const LAST_IN_LIST: u32 = 1 << 16;
const IMPLICIT: u32 = 1 << 17;
const NAMESPACE_SHIFT: u32 = 18;
const NAMESPACE_BITS: u32 = 0b11 << NAMESPACE_SHIFT;
/// On a `:not()` component: its argument is `:current` alone, which picks the kind of search text match an entry
/// styles rather than constraining any element.
const SEARCH_TEXT_FILTER: u32 = 1 << 20;
/// On the first component of a selector: its subject compound holds no pseudo-element, `::part()` or `::slotted()`,
/// so that it describes the element it is matched against from its subject on.
const DESCRIBES_ITS_SUBJECT: u32 = 1 << 21;
const INLINE: u32 = 1 << 22;
const FORGIVING: u32 = 1 << 23;
/// The name of a type, id, class or attribute selector is its own ASCII-lowercase form.
const ASCII_LOWERCASE: u32 = 1 << 24;
/// An attribute selector names one of the attributes whose values HTML compares ASCII case-insensitively.
const LEGACY_CASE_INSENSITIVE: u32 = 1 << 25;
/// On the first component of a selector: the selector names the scoping root, with `:scope` or a `&` directly inside
/// `@scope`, anywhere in it.
const NAMES_THE_SCOPE: u32 = 1 << 26;
/// On the first component of a selector: the selector names an element in another tree, with `::slotted()` or
/// `::part()`, where the sheet's default namespace does not follow it.
const ESCAPES_ITS_NAMESPACE: u32 = 1 << 27;
/// On the first component of a compound: how many components the compound has, where it has fewer than 16, so that a
/// walk steps from a compound to the next one without reading the components between; zero for a longer compound,
/// which a walk reads to its end.
const COMPOUND_LENGTH_SHIFT: u32 = 28;
const COMPOUND_LENGTH_BITS: u32 = 0xf << COMPOUND_LENGTH_SHIFT;

/// The kind, relation and flags of a component, in 32 bits.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
#[repr(transparent)]
struct ComponentBits(u32);

impl ComponentBits {
    fn new(kind: ComponentKind) -> Self {
        Self(kind as u32)
    }

    fn kind(self) -> ComponentKind {
        const KINDS: [ComponentKind; 10] = [
            ComponentKind::Universal,
            ComponentKind::Tag,
            ComponentKind::Id,
            ComponentKind::Class,
            ComponentKind::Attribute,
            ComponentKind::PseudoClass,
            ComponentKind::PseudoElement,
            ComponentKind::Nesting,
            ComponentKind::Invalid,
            ComponentKind::RelativeAnchor,
        ];
        KINDS[(self.0 & KIND_BITS) as usize]
    }

    fn relation(self) -> Relation {
        const RELATIONS: [Relation; 8] = [
            Relation::SubSelector,
            Relation::Descendant,
            Relation::Child,
            Relation::NextSibling,
            Relation::SubsequentSibling,
            Relation::Column,
            Relation::PseudoElement,
            Relation::Leftmost,
        ];
        RELATIONS[((self.0 & RELATION_BITS) >> RELATION_SHIFT) as usize]
    }

    fn with_relation(self, relation: Relation) -> Self {
        Self((self.0 & !RELATION_BITS) | ((relation as u32) << RELATION_SHIFT))
    }

    fn pseudo(self) -> u8 {
        ((self.0 & PSEUDO_BITS) >> PSEUDO_SHIFT) as u8
    }
