use super::*;

/// Publish already bound immutable selector inputs, after all host interning has finished.
pub(crate) fn publish_style_rule(
    engine: &mut StyleEngine,
    sheet: u32,
    before_rule: u32,
    compiled: &SelectorListRef,
    bound_scope: &BoundScopeChain,
) -> u32 {
    if sheet == 0 || compiled.is_empty() {
        return 0;
    }
    let before = match before_rule {
        0 => None,
        id => Some(RuleID(id - 1)),
    };
    let rule = engine.add_style_rule_in_scope(SheetID(sheet - 1), before, compiled, Some(bound_scope));
    rule.0 + 1
}

/// Replace selectors using immutable compilation inputs, preserving rule identity.
pub(crate) fn publish_style_rule_selectors(
    engine: &mut StyleEngine,
    rule: u32,
    compiled: &SelectorListRef,
    bound_scope: &BoundScopeChain,
) {
    if rule == 0 || compiled.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    engine.replace_style_rule_selectors(RuleID(rule - 1), compiled, Some(bound_scope));
}
/// Whether a candidate animation overlay changes any effective value of the record `installed` views, in place of the
/// record's own overlay. The host reads it from the record it installed, as the engine would.
///
/// # Safety
/// `installed` must view a record the host holds live for this call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_animation_overlay_changed(
    installed: &FfiStyleRecordView,
    animated_overlay: Option<&AnimatedOverlay>,
) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let (longhands, old_overlay) = unsafe {
        (
            installed
                .longhands()
                .expect("the record of an element carries its longhands"),
            installed.animated_overlay(),
        )
    };
    crate::css::style::style_invalidation::animation_overlay_changed(longhands, old_overlay, animated_overlay)
}

/// What the host hands over to have an element's sampled animation overlay composed over the record it installed and
/// published.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiAnimationOverlayPublicationInput {
    pub style_node: u32,
    pub pseudo_kind: u8,
    /// The record the element installed, which the overlay was sampled on and composes over.
    pub style_record: u64,
    /// The style record whose longhands the overlay was sampled over.
    pub record: *const c_void,
    pub animated_overlay: *const c_void,
    /// The identity of the overlay, or 0 where it animates nothing, which releases the target's overlay record.
    pub animation_overlay_identity: u64,
    pub used_color_scheme: u8,
    pub display_before_box_type_transformation_raw: u32,
    pub is_document_element: bool,
    /// What a target the engine holds no overlay slot for is published again whole with, beside the installed record's
    /// base: the custom-property environment the target holds, with its store.
    pub custom_property_environment: u64,
    pub custom_property_store: *const c_void,
    pub callback_context: *mut c_void,
    /// Writes the animated style's platform font, a `ComputedValuesFFI::FfiFontGroupBuildInputs`;
    /// asked only where the font group is rebuilt.
    pub font_group_inputs: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void),
}

/// What publishing an element's sampled animation overlay answers: what replacing the installed record with it damages,
/// the record the target held and the one it holds now, with the view of the latter, which is missing where the engine
/// holds no record the overlay was sampled on.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiAnimationOverlayPublication {
    pub invalidation: FfiAnimationInvalidation,
    pub publication: FfiStyleRecordDelta,
    /// The record the host holds for the record the target holds now, with a reference the host takes over: a later
    /// publication of the same call can retire the record.
    pub record: *const crate::css::style::pipeline::Record,
    /// Whether the overlay named a value the groups could not be told from, or nothing at all.
    pub rebuilt_every_group: bool,
}

impl FfiAnimationOverlayPublication {
    fn missing() -> Self {
        Self {
            invalidation: FfiAnimationInvalidation::default(),
            publication: FfiStyleRecordDelta::default(),
            record: std::ptr::null(),
            rebuilt_every_group: false,
        }
    }
}

/// Whether the engine assigns a record to the pseudo-element `pseudo_kind` of `node`'s element, for its animations to
/// compose over. It assigns none to a pseudo-element that is not rendered, whose record a read of its style alone
/// holds.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_assigns_pseudo_element_record(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    read: &crate::render_state::BegunRead,
    node: u32,
    pseudo_kind: u8,
) -> bool {
    let Some(node) = StyleNodeID::from_raw(node) else {
        return false;
    };
    with_engine(read, host, |engine| {
        engine
            .computed_group_sets
            .holds_an_installed_record(crate::css::style::computed::ComputedStyleTarget::new(node, pseudo_kind))
    })
}

/// Composes each element's sampled animation overlay over the record it installed, rebuilding only the groups the
/// overlay writes (see `RetainedState::build_animation_overlay_payloads`), compares it with that record, and publishes
/// it as the target's record, writing what it answers to the same index of `out`: every element in one call of the
/// engine. An element whose overlay rebuilds the font group is published again in a call of its own: resolving the
/// animated font may read the engine, so the host resolves it between the two. The host keeps the view of each record
/// it answers, which it installs next.
///
/// # Safety
/// `host` must be a live document host, on its document's thread, `inputs` and `out` must point to `count` entries, and
/// everything an input points to must be live for the call, its table non-null.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_publish_sampled_animation_overlays(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    read: &crate::render_state::BegunRead,
    inputs: *const FfiAnimationOverlayPublicationInput,
    count: usize,
    out: *mut FfiAnimationOverlayPublication,
) {
    use crate::css::table_group_builder::FfiFontGroupBuildInputs;

    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let (inputs, out) = unsafe {
        (
            ak::slice_from_raw_parts(inputs, count),
            ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(out, count),
        )
    };
    with_engine(read, host, |engine| {
        for (input, out) in inputs.iter().zip(out.iter_mut()) {
            // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
            *out = unsafe { publish_sampled_animation_overlay(engine, input, None) }.unwrap_or_else(
                |crate::css::style::engine_sample::NeedsHostFont| FfiAnimationOverlayPublication::missing(),
            );
        }
    });
    for (input, out) in inputs.iter().zip(out.iter_mut()) {
        if out.record.is_null() {
            // A publication the first call could not make, for want of the font or of a record, is tried again with
            // the font.
            let mut font = std::mem::MaybeUninit::<FfiFontGroupBuildInputs>::uninit();
            // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller. The host writes the whole font.
            let font = unsafe {
                (input.font_group_inputs)(input.callback_context, font.as_mut_ptr().cast());
                font.assume_init()
            };
            // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
            *out = with_engine(read, host, |engine| unsafe {
                publish_sampled_animation_overlay(engine, input, Some(&font))
            })
            .unwrap_or_else(|crate::css::style::engine_sample::NeedsHostFont| {
                FfiAnimationOverlayPublication::missing()
            });
        }
        if !out.record.is_null() {
            host.engine_memo()
                .views
                .set(out.publication.new_style_record, out.record);
        }
    }
}

/// [`style_engine_publish_sampled_animation_overlays`]'s call of `engine` for one element, which answers `Err` where it
/// needs the animated font, `font`, it was not given.
///
/// # Safety
/// As for [`style_engine_publish_sampled_animation_overlays`], for one input.
pub(in crate::css::style) unsafe fn publish_sampled_animation_overlay(
    engine: &mut StyleEngine,
    input: &FfiAnimationOverlayPublicationInput,
    font: Option<&crate::css::table_group_builder::FfiFontGroupBuildInputs>,
) -> Result<FfiAnimationOverlayPublication, crate::css::style::engine_sample::NeedsHostFont> {
    use crate::css::table_group_builder::group_index;

    let Some(node) = StyleNodeID::from_raw(input.style_node) else {
        return Ok(FfiAnimationOverlayPublication::missing());
    };
    let Some(installed_style_record) = crate::css::style::computed::FinalStyleRecordID::from_raw(input.style_record)
    else {
        return Ok(FfiAnimationOverlayPublication::missing());
    };
    // NB: style styles an element-backed pseudo-element as the element of the shadow tree that
    //     backs it, so the animations of the pseudo-element compose over that element's record.
    let (node, pseudo_kind) = match input.pseudo_kind {
        kind @ FIRST_ELEMENT_REFERENCE_PSEUDO_ELEMENT_KIND..=LAST_ELEMENT_REFERENCE_PSEUDO_ELEMENT_KIND => {
            let element = crate::css::cascaded_properties::NO_PSEUDO_ELEMENT;
            let backing = engine
                .backing_elements(node, 1 << kind)
                .find(|&backing| {
                    engine.computed_group_sets.assigned_final_style_record(
                        crate::css::style::computed::ComputedStyleTarget::new(backing, element),
                    ) == Some(installed_style_record)
                })
                .expect(
                    "the engine assigns the record an element-backed pseudo-element installed to its backing element",
                );
            (backing, element)
        }
        kind => (node, kind),
    };
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let (longhands, overlay) = unsafe {
        (
            crate::css::style::ViewLonghands::of_raw_record(input.record),
            input.animated_overlay.cast::<AnimatedOverlay>().as_ref(),
        )
    };
    let mut payloads = [std::ptr::null(); group_index::COUNT];
    let Some(old_record) = engine.computed_group_sets.host_record(input.style_record).cloned() else {
        return Ok(FfiAnimationOverlayPublication::missing());
    };
    let old_view = crate::css::style::StyleRecordView::of_host_record(&old_record);
    let rebuilt = engine.build_animation_overlay_payloads(
        old_view,
        longhands,
        overlay,
        input.used_color_scheme,
        input.display_before_box_type_transformation_raw,
        font,
        &mut payloads,
    )?;
    // SAFETY: The rebuild wrote a live payload of each group.
    let groups = &unsafe { crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroups::retained(&payloads, rebuilt.bits) };
    // Compared before the publication, which may release the installed record: nothing else keeps a pseudo-element's.
    let invalidation = engine.compare_animation_overlay(
        old_view,
        input.animated_overlay.cast(),
        groups,
        input.is_document_element,
        engine.is_svg_graphics_element(node),
    );
    let (animated_overlay, overlay_payloads) = match input.animation_overlay_identity {
        0 => (std::ptr::null(), None),
        _ => (input.animated_overlay, Some(groups)),
    };
    let publication = match engine.publish_animation_overlay_impl(
        crate::css::style::computed::ComputedStyleTarget::new(node, pseudo_kind),
        input.animation_overlay_identity,
        HostShared::new(animated_overlay).cast(),
        overlay_payloads,
    ) {
        Some(publication) => FfiStyleRecordDelta {
            old_style_record: publication.previous_style_record.raw(),
            new_style_record: publication.style_record.raw(),
        },
        // NB: The engine assigns every pseudo-element it styles the record it installed, so a target it holds no
        //     assignment for has no style to compose over.
        None => {
            crate::css::style::engine_sample::release_rebuilt_overlay_payloads(&payloads, rebuilt.groups);
            return Ok(FfiAnimationOverlayPublication::missing());
        }
    };
    crate::css::style::engine_sample::release_rebuilt_overlay_payloads(&payloads, rebuilt.groups);
    engine
        .retained
        .live_counters
        .note_animated_sample(node, rebuilt.every_group);
    Ok(FfiAnimationOverlayPublication {
        invalidation,
        publication,
        record: engine
            .computed_group_sets
            .host_record(publication.new_style_record)
            .map_or(std::ptr::null(), |record| std::sync::Arc::into_raw(record.clone())),
        rebuilt_every_group: rebuilt.every_group,
    })
}

use super::*;

/// What a container condition the engine evaluated read of a container or its subject, which the
/// host records as it records its own evaluation's.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum FfiContainerEffectKind {
    /// The node is a container a size or scroll-state query asks about.
    SizeContainerUsage,
    /// The node is a container a style query asks about.
    StyleContainerUsage,
    /// The node is a scroll-state container a query asks about, whose state is snapshotted.
    ScrollStateContainerUsage,
    /// The node has no box yet, and the query is evaluated again after layout.
    NeedsEvaluationAfterLayout,
    /// The subject's style resolved a viewport-relative length in the query.
    SubjectViewportDependency,
    /// A container-relative length resolved against the node, which has no box yet, and is
    /// resolved again after layout, a partial relayout included.
    UnitsNeedEvaluationAfterLayout,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiContainerEffect {
    pub node: u32,
    pub kind: FfiContainerEffectKind,
}

/// What the container conditions of a row the engine answered read of its containers, besides the
/// effects: whether the row's style depends on a size or scroll-state query or a style query.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiContainerEffects {
    pub depends_on_size: bool,
    pub depends_on_style: bool,
}

/// Takes what the container conditions of the row the host is installing for `node` read of its
/// containers, for the host to record as it records its own evaluation's. Each effect is handed to
/// `record` with no engine borrow held, so recording may call the engine.
///
/// # Safety
/// `host` must be a live document host, on its document's thread.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_take_container_effects(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    read: &crate::render_state::BegunRead,
    node: u32,
    context: *mut c_void,
    record: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, FfiContainerEffect),
) -> FfiContainerEffects {
    let verdict = StyleNodeID::from_raw(node)
        .filter(|_| host.container_effects_may_be_held())
        .and_then(|node| with_engine(read, host, |engine| engine.take_container_effects_for_install(node)))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    for &(node, kind) in &verdict.effects {
        unsafe { record(context, FfiContainerEffect { node: node.raw(), kind }) };
    }
    FfiContainerEffects {
        depends_on_size: verdict.depends_on_size,
        depends_on_style: verdict.depends_on_style,
    }
}

use super::*;

#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiNativeRuleTarget {
    pub identity: u64,
    pub declaration_version: u32,
    pub source_identity: u64,
    pub declarations: *const c_void,
    pub layer_name: *const u16,
    pub layer_name_length: usize,
    pub has_container_conditions: bool,
    pub origin: FfiCascadeOrigin,
}

/// Issue a new identity for changed declaration contents, independently of CSSOM wrappers.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_next_declaration_block_version(host: &DocumentHost) -> u32 {
    host.next_declaration_block_version()
}

/// Queues a native declaration edit for the rule that owns the declarations, where the host published that rule to the
/// sheet `sheet`, and answers whether they declare transitions. The host is told first, with no engine borrowed.
///
/// # Safety
/// The callback must not mutate the native rule graph, and must remain valid for this call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_native_rule_declarations_changed(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    sheet: u32,
    rule: &crate::css::rule::NativeRule,
    context: *mut c_void,
    notify: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
) -> bool {
    let Some(identity) = rule
        .declaration_owner_identity()
        .filter(|&identity| host.published_rules().contains(sheet, identity))
    else {
        return false;
    };
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    unsafe { notify(context) };
    let declarations = rule.cascade_declarations();
    let transitions = declarations
        .as_ref()
        .is_some_and(|declarations| declares_transitions(declarations.properties()));
    host.write_rules(RuleWrite::RuleDeclarations { identity, declarations });
    transitions
}

/// The native identity of the first rule after an inserted native subtree that the host published to the sheet
/// `sheet`, or 0 for none, without creating CSSOM objects.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_native_rule_successor(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    sheet: u32,
    native: &crate::css::style_sheet::NativeStyleSheet,
    identity: u64,
) -> u64 {
    host.published_rules().successor(sheet, native, identity)
}

/// Retires a native subtree from the sheet `sheet`, with host callbacks only for document and cascade-cache
/// notifications, and queues the removal of the rules the host published there.
///
/// # Safety
/// `host` must be a live document host, on its document's thread, and the native sheet, rule, callbacks, and any
/// non-null detached import must be live. Native rules must belong to Rc allocations. No graph borrow spans a host
/// callback.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_remove_native_rule(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    native: *const c_void,
    rule: *const c_void,
    detached_import: *const c_void,
    sheet: u32,
    context: *mut c_void,
    begin: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, bool, bool),
    notify: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, bool),
) {
    use crate::css::rule::{NativeRule, NativeRuleType, mutation, read::RuleRef};
    use crate::css::style_sheet::NativeStyleSheet;
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let removed = unsafe {
        mutation::removed_rules(
            &*rule.cast::<NativeRule>(),
            &*native.cast::<NativeStyleSheet>(),
            detached_import.cast::<NativeStyleSheet>().as_ref(),
        )
    };
    let changes_environment =
        RuleRef::Materialized(unsafe { &*rule.cast::<NativeRule>() }).change_needs_style_environment_bump();
    let has_counter_style = removed
        .iter()
        .any(|rule| RuleRef::Materialized(rule).rule_type() == NativeRuleType::CounterStyle);
    unsafe { begin(context, changes_environment, has_counter_style) };
    let mut published = Vec::new();
    for rule in removed {
        unsafe { notify(context, mutation::declares_layer(&rule)) };
        let identity = RuleRef::Materialized(&rule).identity();
        if host.published_rules().remove(sheet, identity) {
            published.push(identity);
        }
    }
    if !published.is_empty() {
        host.write_rules(RuleWrite::RemoveRules(published.into()));
    }
}

/// Read a rule's native cascade data without a CSSOM facade.
///
/// On success the caller owns declarations and must release it with
/// rust_declaration_data_release. Layer text is borrowed until the next rule mutation; callers must
/// copy any text needed across such a mutation. Source identity never retains a native sheet.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_native_rule_target(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    read: &crate::render_state::BegunRead,
    rule: u32,
    result: &mut FfiNativeRuleTarget,
) -> bool {
    with_engine(read, host, |engine| native_rule_target(engine, rule, result))
}

/// [`style_engine_native_rule_target`] on `engine`.
pub fn native_rule_target(engine: &mut StyleEngine, rule: u32, result: &mut FfiNativeRuleTarget) -> bool {
    let Some(target) = rule
        .checked_sub(1)
        .and_then(|id| engine.rules.native_target(RuleID(id)))
    else {
        return false;
    };
    let Some(declarations) = engine.current_rule_block(RuleID(rule - 1)) else {
        return false;
    };
    let origin = engine.rules.sheet_origin(engine.rules.rule_sheet(RuleID(rule - 1)));
    *result = FfiNativeRuleTarget {
        identity: target.identity.get(),
        declaration_version: engine
            .current_rule_version(RuleID(rule - 1))
            .declaration_block
            .map_or(0, |version| version.raw()),
        source_identity: target.source_identity,
        declarations: crate::css::declaration_block::SharedDeclarationBlock::into_raw(declarations).cast(),
        layer_name: target.layer_name().as_ptr(),
        layer_name_length: target.layer_name().len(),
        has_container_conditions: !target.containers().is_empty(),
        origin: match origin {
            CascadeOrigin::Author => FfiCascadeOrigin::Author,
            CascadeOrigin::AuthorPresentationalHint => FfiCascadeOrigin::AuthorPresentationalHint,
            CascadeOrigin::User => FfiCascadeOrigin::User,
            CascadeOrigin::UserAgent => FfiCascadeOrigin::UserAgent,
        },
    };
    true
}

/*

use super::*;
use crate::css::ffi_support::{ArcRef, OwnedArc};
use crate::css::style::pipeline::Record;

/// The record the host holds for a base or live animation-overlay record, which the engine holds while it holds the
/// identity, or null for an identity it does not hold. The host counts a reference to it to hold it longer.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_host_record(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    read: &crate::render_state::BegunRead,
    style_record: u64,
) -> *const Record {
    if let Some(record) = crate::css::style::engine_calls::known_host_record(host, style_record) {
        return record;
    }
    let record = with_engine(read, host, |engine| host_record(engine, style_record));
    if !record.is_null() {
        host.engine_memo().views.set(style_record, record);
    }
    record
}

/// The record `engine` holds for the host for `style_record`, or null.
pub(in crate::css::style) fn host_record(engine: &StyleEngine, style_record: u64) -> *const Record {
    engine
        .computed_group_sets
        .host_record(style_record)
        .map_or(std::ptr::null(), std::sync::Arc::as_ptr)
}

/// The groups beneath the animation overlay of the record `view` views, which are its own groups
/// where it carries none, or null where the view is missing.
///
/// # Safety
/// `view` must be a view of a record the host holds live.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_view_base_groups(
    view: &FfiStyleRecordView,
) -> *const crate::css::computed_value_views::StyleRecordGroups {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    unsafe { view.base_groups() }.map_or(std::ptr::null(), |groups| {
        crate::css::computed_value_views::StyleRecordGroups::of(groups)
    })
}

/// Whether the element of the record `view` views would compute `display` to `none` when ignoring its animations:
/// those composed over the record, and the custom properties they sampled, which the record substitutes.
///
/// # Safety
/// `view` must be a view of a record the host holds live.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_view_display_is_none_ignoring_animations(view: &FfiStyleRecordView) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let Some(groups) = (unsafe { view.base_groups() }) else {
        return false;
    };
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let display_none_is_animated = unsafe { view.longhand_table_record.as_ref() }
        .is_some_and(|record| record.rare().reads.display_none_is_animated);
    crate::css::computed_value_views::ComputedValuesView::of(groups)
        .display()
        .is_none()
        && !display_none_is_animated
}

/// The view of `record`, a record the host holds, which reads nothing but the record.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_record_view(record: &Record) -> FfiStyleRecordView {
    FfiStyleRecordView::of_record(record)
}

/// The identity the engine names `record`, a record the host holds, by: that of the slot holding
/// it, or of the sample it is, or zero for a record no slot holds any longer.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_record_identity(record: &Record) -> u64 {
    host_record_identity(record)
}

/// The identity the engine names `record`, a record the host holds, by, as
/// [`style_engine_record_identity`] answers it.
pub(in crate::css::style) fn host_record_identity(record: &Record) -> u64 {
    match record.sample_of_animations() {
        Some(sample) => sample.identity.raw(),
        None => record.installed_record().map_or(0, |installed| {
            crate::css::style::computed::FinalStyleRecordID::installed(installed).raw()
        }),
    }
}

/// The identity of the custom-property environment `record`, a record the host holds, was
/// resolved in: that of the store it holds, or of the store of the record a sample samples over.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_record_custom_property_environment(record: &Record) -> u64 {
    record
        .sample_of_animations()
        .map_or(record, |sample| &sample.base)
        .custom_property_environment()
}

/// Takes one more reference to `record`, a style record a view named.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_record_retain(record: ArcRef<'_, Record>) {
    let _ = std::sync::Arc::into_raw(record.to_arc());
}

/// A reference of the engine's own to `record`, a record the host holds, or none for null.
///
/// # Safety
/// `record` must be null or a record the host holds a reference to.
pub(crate) unsafe fn retain_host_record(
    record: *const c_void,
) -> Option<std::sync::Arc<crate::css::style::pipeline::Record>> {
    let record = record.cast::<crate::css::style::pipeline::Record>();
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller: the record lives in an Arc.
    (!record.is_null()).then(|| unsafe {
        std::sync::Arc::increment_strong_count(record);
        std::sync::Arc::from_raw(record)
    })
}

/// Lets go of a reference taken with `style_engine_record_retain`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_record_release(record: OwnedArc<Record>) {
    drop(record);
}

/// Whether the `transition-*` values of the record `view` views give any longhand a matching
/// entry, as [`crate::css::transition::has_matching_transition_entries`] says.
///
/// # Safety
/// `view` must be a view of a live record.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_view_has_matching_transition_entries(
    view: &FfiStyleRecordView,
    has_existing_transitions: bool,
) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    unsafe { view.longhands() }.is_some_and(|longhands| {
        crate::css::transition::has_matching_transition_entries(longhands, has_existing_transitions)
    })
}

/// What a read of one element's style the host makes before the next style update asks of the
/// engine; see `StyleEngine::answer_record_demand`. A read-only demand leaves the engine as it
/// was: its record is only for the host to read. Any other is installed and acknowledged as a
/// style update's would be.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
#[expect(dead_code, reason = "C++ constructs the variants")]
#[expect(clippy::enum_variant_names, reason = "each is a read of the element")]
pub enum FfiRecordDemand {
    /// A read-only read of the element's record.
    ElementRead,
    /// A read-only read of what the element computes to as though it had no inline declaration,
    /// driven in full against the parent as it is now.
    ElementReadWithoutInlineStyle,
    /// A read-only read of the element's record, driven in full against the parent as it is now,
    /// which the reader assigned a record of its own.
    ElementReadAgainstParent,
}

/// What a read of one of an element's pseudo-elements the host makes before the next style update
/// asks of the engine, as `FfiRecordDemand` does of an element.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
#[expect(dead_code, reason = "C++ constructs the variants")]
pub enum FfiPseudoElementRecordDemand {
    /// A CSSOM read of the pseudo-element, settled against its element's installed record.
    CssomRead,
    /// A read-only read of what the pseudo-element computes to, whether or not it generates a box.
    ReadOnly,
}

/// A pseudo-element a record demand may read: a synthetic one, which the engine settles beside its
/// element, or, for a read-only read, one an element in the shadow tree backs or a named view
/// transition one, which it computes from the element's rules for it. Each is numbered as its kind.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
#[expect(dead_code, reason = "C++ constructs the variants")]
pub enum FfiDemandedPseudoElement {
    After = 0,
    Backdrop = 1,
    Before = 2,
    FirstLetter = 3,
    FirstLine = 4,
    Marker = 5,
    SearchText = 6,
    SearchTextCurrent = 7,
    Selection = 8,
    SpellingError = 9,
    ViewTransition = 10,
    WebkitColorSwatchWrapper = 11,
    WebkitSearchCancelButton = 12,
    ColorSwatch = 13,
    DetailsContent = 14,
    FileSelectorButton = 15,
    Placeholder = 16,
    SliderFill = 17,
    SliderThumb = 18,
    SliderTrack = 19,
    Highlight = 20,
    ViewTransitionGroup = 23,
    ViewTransitionImagePair = 24,
    ViewTransitionNew = 25,
    ViewTransitionOld = 26,
}

/// The answer to a record demand: the record, or that the pseudo-element read generates no box
/// with the custom-property environment its rules resolve to (zero where none styles it). A zero
/// `style_record` that is not absent leaves the read to C++.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiRecordDemandAnswer {
    pub record: FfiEngineComputedRecord,
    pub is_absent: bool,
    pub custom_property_environment: u64,
}

/// Answer a read of one element's style, or one of its pseudo-elements', the host makes before
/// the next style update.
pub(crate) fn answer_record_demand(
    engine: &mut StyleEngine,
    style_node: StyleNodeID,
    demand: crate::css::style::publication::RecordDemand,
) -> FfiRecordDemandAnswer {
    let answer = engine.answer_record_demand(style_node, demand);
    ffi_record_demand_answer(engine, answer)
}

/// The FFI form of `answer`, what a demand of an element's record answered, with the records
/// `engine` holds for the host for the records it names.
pub(in crate::css::style) fn ffi_record_demand_answer(
    engine: &StyleEngine,
    answer: crate::css::style::publication::RecordDemandAnswer,
) -> FfiRecordDemandAnswer {
    match answer {
        crate::css::style::publication::RecordDemandAnswer::Record { record } => FfiRecordDemandAnswer {
            record: FfiEngineComputedRecord {
                style_record: record.style_record,
                host_record: host_record(engine, record.style_record),
            },
            is_absent: false,
            custom_property_environment: 0,
        },
        crate::css::style::publication::RecordDemandAnswer::Absent {
            custom_property_environment,
        } => FfiRecordDemandAnswer {
            record: FfiEngineComputedRecord::default(),
            is_absent: true,
            custom_property_environment,
        },
    }
}

/// The record of an element no rule reaches, computed from its presentational hints and its
/// inline style alone over the initial values, its custom properties among them; see
/// `declared_only_record`. `subject` is the document's style node. Returns the record with a
/// reference the host takes over, or null where the engine computes none.
///
/// # Safety
/// `host` must be a live document host, on its document's thread. `hints` must borrow `hint_count`
/// `FfiDeclaredProperty` entries whose values point at live, Arc-backed `StyleValueData` roots. A
/// non-null `inline_block` must borrow a live `DeclarationBlock`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_declared_only_record(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    read: &crate::render_state::BegunRead,
    subject: u32,
    facts: u32,
    hint_kind: FfiElementDeclarationKind,
    hints: *const c_void,
    hint_count: usize,
    inline_block: *const c_void,
) -> *const Record {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let record = with_engine(read, host, |engine| {
        use crate::css::declaration_block::{DeclarationBlock, FfiDeclaredProperty, declaration_from_view};
        abort_on_panic(|| {
            let subject = StyleNodeID::from_raw(subject)?;
            let hints = if hint_count == 0 {
                &[]
            } else {
                unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(hints.cast::<FfiDeclaredProperty>(), hint_count) }
            };
            let hints = hints
                .iter()
                .map(|hint| unsafe { declaration_from_view(hint) })
                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
            let inline_data = unsafe { inline_block.cast::<DeclarationBlock>().as_ref() }.map(DeclarationBlock::data);
            let hint_kind = decode_element_declaration_kind(hint_kind);
            let mut by_kind: [Vec<_>; ElementDeclarationKind::COUNT] = Default::default();
            by_kind[hint_kind.index()] = crate::css::style::specified_value::element_declared_properties(
                hints
                    .iter()
                    .map(crate::css::declaration_block::DeclaredProperty::borrowed),
            );
            if let Some(data) = &inline_data {
                by_kind[ElementDeclarationKind::InlineStyle.index()] =
                    crate::css::style::specified_value::element_declared_properties(data.properties().iter());
            }
            let custom_declarations = collect_native_custom_declarations(
                engine,
                inline_data
                    .as_ref()
                    .map_or(Default::default(), |data| data.custom_properties()),
            );
            let declared = crate::css::style::pipeline::DeclaredOnly {
                declarations: crate::css::style::element_declarations::ElementDeclarationRow::new(
                    by_kind,
                    custom_declarations,
                ),
                // An element outside the document is no document element.
                facts: facts & !element_adjustment_fact::IS_DOCUMENT_ELEMENT,
            };
            // FIXME: A shape in a window whose document has no document element has a path and should measure, but an
            //        engine owns its document from its first style update with a document element, so no initial
            //        style exists yet to compute the record over.
            if !engine.has_live_style() {
                return None;
            }
            engine.declared_only_record(subject, declared)
        })
    });
    record.map_or(std::ptr::null(), std::sync::Arc::into_raw)
}

/// The store of an environment the engine resolved, with one strong reference transferred to the
/// caller, and the environment it was resolved over; null for an environment C++ published.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_borrow_engine_custom_property_environment(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    read: &crate::render_state::BegunRead,
    identity: u64,
    parent: &mut u64,
) -> *const c_void {
    with_engine(read, host, |engine| {
        let Some((store, parent_identity)) = engine.custom_property_environments.engine_environment(identity) else {
            return std::ptr::null();
        };
        *parent = parent_identity;
        std::sync::Arc::into_raw(std::sync::Arc::clone(store)).cast()
    })
}

//! Cascade priorities, and what a winning declaration is and where it comes from.
//!
//! The components of a priority, outermost first, follow the cascade sorting order:
//! origin and importance, encapsulation context, element-attached styles, layers, specificity,
//! scope proximity, and order of appearance. Importance reverses two of them - context and layers -
//! which is why importance is folded into the key when it is built rather than checked at every
//! comparison.

use std::hash::Hash;

use crate::css::cascaded_properties::CascadeOrigin;

use super::input_types::ElementDeclarationKind;
use super::pipeline::rule_store::RuleID;
use super::selector::Specificity;

/// Where an element-sourced declaration sits relative to the rules of its context.
///
/// Element-attached styles are a cascade component in their own right, above layers: a style
/// attribute beats every layered and unlayered rule in its context, whatever layer they are in.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Hash, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum ElementAttachment {
    /// A declaration from a stylesheet rule.
    Rule = 0,
    /// An HTML presentational hint or SVG presentation attribute mapped to declarations.
    PresentationalHint = 1,
    /// The `style` attribute.
    InlineStyle = 2,
}

/// The precedence ladder of origin and importance, lowest first.
///
/// Importance reverses the origin order, which is why this is one ladder rather than an origin plus
/// a flag: comparing an important user declaration against a normal author one is a comparison of
/// two rungs, not of two dimensions.
#[must_use]
pub fn origin_importance_rank(origin: CascadeOrigin, important: bool) -> u8 {
    match (origin, important) {
        (CascadeOrigin::UserAgent, false) => 0,
        (CascadeOrigin::User, false) => 1,
        (CascadeOrigin::AuthorPresentationalHint, false) => 2,
        (CascadeOrigin::Author, false) => 3,
        (CascadeOrigin::Author, true) => 5,
        (CascadeOrigin::AuthorPresentationalHint, true) => 6,
        (CascadeOrigin::User, true) => 7,
        (CascadeOrigin::UserAgent, true) => 8,
    }
}

/// The inputs a priority key is built from, before importance has been folded in.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct PriorityInputs {
    pub origin: CascadeOrigin,
    pub important: bool,
    /// Encapsulation depth: 0 for the document tree, increasing inwards.
    pub context_depth: u32,
    pub element_attachment: ElementAttachment,
    /// The layer's current rank, read from the layer order rather than copied into the rule.
    pub layer_rank: u64,
    pub specificity: Specificity,
    /// Distance from the `@scope` root; nearer wins. Zero when not scoped.
    pub scope_proximity: u32,
    /// The rule's position: its sheet's rank, then its own rank within that sheet.
    pub sheet_rank: u64,
    pub rule_rank: u64,
}

/// A total order over declarations. Greater wins.
///
/// The field order is the cascade sorting order, and `Ord` compares fields in declaration order, so
/// the comparison program is the struct layout.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Hash, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct CascadePriority {
    origin_importance: u8,
    /// Outer contexts win for normal declarations, inner contexts win for important ones.
    context: u32,
    element_attachment: ElementAttachment,
    /// Later layers win for normal declarations; the order is reversed for important ones.
    layer: u64,
    specificity: Specificity,
    /// Nearer scope roots win, so proximity is stored inverted.
    scope_proximity: u32,
    sheet_rank: u64,
    rule_rank: u64,
}

impl CascadePriority {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new(inputs: PriorityInputs) -> Self {
        Self {
            origin_importance: origin_importance_rank(inputs.origin, inputs.important),
            context: if inputs.important {
                inputs.context_depth
            } else {
                u32::MAX - inputs.context_depth
            },
            element_attachment: inputs.element_attachment,
            layer: if inputs.important {
                u64::MAX - inputs.layer_rank
            } else {
                inputs.layer_rank
            },
            specificity: inputs.specificity,
            scope_proximity: u32::MAX - inputs.scope_proximity,
            sheet_rank: inputs.sheet_rank,
            rule_rank: inputs.rule_rank,
        }
    }

    /// Whether a `revert` or `revert-layer` declared at this priority rolls back past a declaration
    /// at `other`, so that the declaration takes no part in what the property reverts to.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn reverts_past(&self, operator: CascadeOperator, other: &Self) -> bool {
        // UA, user, and author.
        let origin_group = |origin_importance: u8| match origin_importance {
            0 | 8 => 0,
            1 | 7 => 1,
            _ => 2,
        };
        match operator {
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-5/#valdef-all-revert
            CascadeOperator::Revert => origin_group(other.origin_importance) >= origin_group(self.origin_importance),
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-5/#valdef-all-revert-layer
            // The cascaded value rolls back to the earlier layers of the declaration's origin and
            // context, important or not.
            CascadeOperator::RevertLayer => {
                // NB: Inline styles occupy a separate cascade step, even though they share the implicit outer
                //     layer's rank with unlayered style rules, so a revert-layer in them only rolls back other
                //     inline styles.
                other.origin() == self.origin()
                    && other.context_depth() == self.context_depth()
                    && match self.element_attachment {
                        ElementAttachment::InlineStyle => other.element_attachment == ElementAttachment::InlineStyle,
                        _ => other.layer_rank() >= self.layer_rank(),
                    }
            }
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    /// The origin of the declaration this priority was built for.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn cascade_origin(&self) -> CascadeOrigin {
        match self.origin_importance {
            0 | 8 => CascadeOrigin::UserAgent,
            1 | 7 => CascadeOrigin::User,
            2 | 6 => CascadeOrigin::AuthorPresentationalHint,
            3 | 5 => CascadeOrigin::Author,
            rank => unreachable!("origin-importance rank {rank} names no origin"),
        }
    }

    /// The origin the priority was built from, as its rank among normal declarations.
    fn origin(&self) -> u8 {
        match self.is_important() {
            true => 8 - self.origin_importance,
            false => self.origin_importance,
        }
    }

    fn is_important(&self) -> bool {
        self.origin_importance > origin_importance_rank(CascadeOrigin::Author, false)
    }

    /// The encapsulation depth the priority was built from.
    fn context_depth(&self) -> u32 {
        match self.is_important() {
            true => self.context,
            false => u32::MAX - self.context,
        }
    }

    /// The rank of the layer the priority was built from.
    fn layer_rank(&self) -> u64 {
        match self.is_important() {
            true => u64::MAX - self.layer,
            false => self.layer,
        }
    }
}

// -- Winners and stopping keys -----------------------------------------------------------------

/// A CSS-wide keyword acts as a cascade operator rather than an eagerly flattened value, so its
/// dependency on parent style, origin, and layer topology stays explicit and repairable.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum CascadeOperator {
    /// An ordinary declared value.
    #[default]
    Declared,
    Inherit,
    Initial,
    Unset,
    /// Resumes below the current origin.
    Revert,
    /// Resumes below the current layer in the applicable origin and importance ordering.
    RevertLayer,
}

impl CascadeOperator {
    /// The operator of the largest number.
    pub(crate) const LAST: Self = Self::RevertLayer;

    /// The operator `bits` numbers, which is one.
    pub(crate) fn from_bits(bits: u8) -> Self {
        match bits {
            0 => Self::Declared,
            1 => Self::Inherit,
            2 => Self::Initial,
            3 => Self::Unset,
            4 => Self::Revert,
            5 => Self::RevertLayer,
            _ => unreachable!("not a cascade operator"),
        }
    }
}

/// The winning declaration for one property of one style node.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum WinnerSource {
    Rule(RuleID),
    Element(ElementDeclarationKind),
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn inputs(origin: CascadeOrigin, important: bool) -> PriorityInputs {
        PriorityInputs {
            origin,
            important,
            context_depth: 0,
            element_attachment: ElementAttachment::Rule,
            layer_rank: 100,
            specificity: Specificity::default(),
            scope_proximity: 0,
            sheet_rank: 10,
            rule_rank: 10,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_origin_ladder_puts_importance_where_the_cascade_does() {
        let normal_ua = CascadePriority::new(inputs(CascadeOrigin::UserAgent, false));
        let normal_user = CascadePriority::new(inputs(CascadeOrigin::User, false));
        let hint = CascadePriority::new(inputs(CascadeOrigin::AuthorPresentationalHint, false));
        let normal_author = CascadePriority::new(inputs(CascadeOrigin::Author, false));
        let important_author = CascadePriority::new(inputs(CascadeOrigin::Author, true));
        let important_user = CascadePriority::new(inputs(CascadeOrigin::User, true));
        let important_ua = CascadePriority::new(inputs(CascadeOrigin::UserAgent, true));

        let ladder = [
            normal_ua,
            normal_user,
            hint,
            normal_author,
            important_author,
            important_user,
            important_ua,
        ];
        assert!(ladder.windows(2).all(|pair| pair[0] < pair[1]));

        // A presentational hint loses to an author rule, however specific the hint's source.
        assert!(hint < normal_author);
    }

    #[test]
    fn importance_reverses_layer_order() {
        let mut early = inputs(CascadeOrigin::Author, false);
        early.layer_rank = 10;
        let mut late = inputs(CascadeOrigin::Author, false);
        late.layer_rank = 20;
        assert!(
            CascadePriority::new(early) < CascadePriority::new(late),
            "later layers win"
        );

        early.important = true;
        late.important = true;
        assert!(
            CascadePriority::new(late) < CascadePriority::new(early),
            "and the order reverses for important declarations"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn importance_reverses_encapsulation_context() {
        let mut outer = inputs(CascadeOrigin::Author, false);
        outer.context_depth = 0;
        let mut inner = inputs(CascadeOrigin::Author, false);
        inner.context_depth = 2;
        assert!(
            CascadePriority::new(inner) < CascadePriority::new(outer),
            "outer contexts win for normal declarations"
        );

        outer.important = true;
        inner.important = true;
        assert!(
            CascadePriority::new(outer) < CascadePriority::new(inner),
            "inner contexts win for important ones"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_element_attached_style_beats_every_rule_in_its_context() {
        let mut rule = inputs(CascadeOrigin::Author, false);
        rule.layer_rank = u64::MAX - 1;
        rule.specificity = Specificity {
            ids: 100,
            classes: 100,
            types: 100,
        };
        let mut inline = inputs(CascadeOrigin::Author, false);
        inline.element_attachment = ElementAttachment::InlineStyle;
        inline.layer_rank = 0;

        assert!(CascadePriority::new(rule) < CascadePriority::new(inline));
    }

    #[test]
    fn specificity_then_proximity_then_source_order_break_ties() {
        let base = inputs(CascadeOrigin::Author, false);
        let mut specific = base;
        specific.specificity = Specificity {
            classes: 1,
            ..Specificity::default()
        };
        assert!(CascadePriority::new(base) < CascadePriority::new(specific));

        let mut near = base;
        near.scope_proximity = 1;
        let mut far = base;
        far.scope_proximity = 5;
        assert!(
            CascadePriority::new(far) < CascadePriority::new(near),
            "nearer scopes win"
        );

        let mut early = base;
        early.rule_rank = 10;
        let mut late = base;
        late.rule_rank = 20;
        assert!(CascadePriority::new(early) < CascadePriority::new(late));

        let mut early_sheet = base;
        early_sheet.sheet_rank = 1;
        early_sheet.rule_rank = u64::MAX;
        let mut late_sheet = base;
        late_sheet.sheet_rank = 2;
        late_sheet.rule_rank = 0;
        assert!(
            CascadePriority::new(early_sheet) < CascadePriority::new(late_sheet),
            "sheet order outranks position within a sheet"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn importance_is_weighed_per_declaration_not_per_rule() {
        // Two author rules, the less specific one marking its declaration important. Ordering the
        // rules once by specificity would let the more specific normal declaration win; weighing
        // each declaration with its own importance puts the important one on a higher rung.
        let mut specific = inputs(CascadeOrigin::Author, false);
        specific.specificity = Specificity {
            ids: 1,
            ..Specificity::default()
        };
        specific.rule_rank = 20;

        let mut important = inputs(CascadeOrigin::Author, true);
        important.specificity = Specificity {
            classes: 1,
            ..Specificity::default()
        };
        important.rule_rank = 10;

        assert!(
            CascadePriority::new(specific) < CascadePriority::new(important),
            "an important author declaration outranks a more specific normal one"
        );

        // The same rule's other declaration, written without `!important`, does not.
        let mut normal = important;
        normal.important = false;
        assert!(
            CascadePriority::new(normal) < CascadePriority::new(specific),
            "and the same rule's normal declaration still loses to the more specific one"
        );
    }
}

/*

use std::ops::{Deref, DerefMut};

/// A directly indexed column whose missing rows all hold the default value.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(super) struct Column<T> {
    entries: Vec<T>,
}

impl<T: Default> Column<T> {
    /// Ensure that `index` is addressable and return newly allocated bytes.
    pub(super) fn ensure(&mut self, index: usize) -> u64 {
        if self.entries.len() > index {
            return 0;
        }
        let capacity_before = self.entries.capacity();
        let length = index.checked_add(1).expect("column identity space exhausted");
        self.entries.resize_with(length, T::default);
        ((self.entries.capacity() - capacity_before) * size_of::<T>()) as u64
    }

    /// Replace one row and return newly allocated bytes.
    pub(super) fn insert(&mut self, index: usize, value: T) -> u64 {
        let growth = self.ensure(index);
        self.entries[index] = value;
        growth
    }
}

impl<T> Column<T> {
    /// The bytes of the column's rows, which hold nothing on the heap.
    pub(super) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        crate::heap_size::vec_bytes(&self.entries)
    }
}

impl<P: PagedColumnPage> PagedColumn<P> {
    /// The bytes of the column's pages, which hold nothing on the heap.
    pub(super) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        crate::heap_size::vec_bytes(&self.pages) + self.pages.iter().flatten().count() * size_of::<P>()
    }
}

impl<T> Deref for Column<T> {
    type Target = Vec<T>;

    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
        &self.entries
    }
}

impl<T> DerefMut for Column<T> {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Target {
        &mut self.entries
    }
}

/// A directly indexed packed boolean column.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(super) struct BitColumn {
    words: crate::cow_column::CowVec<u64, 64>,
}

impl PartialEq for BitColumn {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        let (longer, shorter) = match self.words.len() >= other.words.len() {
            true => (&self.words, &other.words),
            false => (&other.words, &self.words),
        };
        longer
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .all(|(index, word)| shorter.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(0) == *word)
    }
}

impl Eq for BitColumn {}

impl BitColumn {
    pub(super) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.words.row_bytes()
    }

    /// Set one bit and return whether its value changed and newly allocated bytes.
    pub(super) fn set(&mut self, index: usize, value: bool) -> (bool, u64) {
        let word_index = index / u64::BITS as usize;
        let bytes_before = self.words.row_bytes();
        if self.words.len() <= word_index {
            if !value {
                return (false, 0);
            }
            self.words.resize_with_default(word_index + 1);
        }
        let growth = (self.words.row_bytes() - bytes_before) as u64;
        let mask = 1_u64 << (index % u64::BITS as usize);
        if (self.words[word_index] & mask != 0) == value {
            return (false, growth);
        }
        if value {
            self.words[word_index] |= mask;
        } else {
            self.words[word_index] &= !mask;
        }
        (true, growth)
    }

    pub(super) fn contains(&self, index: usize) -> bool {
        let word = index / u64::BITS as usize;
        let mask = 1_u64 << (index % u64::BITS as usize);
        self.words.get(word).is_some_and(|word| word & mask != 0)
    }
}

/// One specialized page stored by a [`PagedColumn`].
pub(super) trait PagedColumnPage: Default {
    type Value: Copy;

    const SHIFT: usize;

    fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<Self::Value>;
    fn insert(&mut self, index: usize, value: Self::Value);
}

pub(super) trait RemovablePagedColumnPage: PagedColumnPage {
    fn remove(&mut self, index: usize) -> Option<Self::Value>;
}

/// A sparse column whose directory and page accounting are shared across page layouts.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct PagedColumn<P: PagedColumnPage> {
    pages: Vec<Option<Box<P>>>,
    page_count: usize,
}

impl<P: PagedColumnPage> Default for PagedColumn<P> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            pages: Vec::new(),
            page_count: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl<P: PagedColumnPage> PagedColumn<P> {
    pub(super) fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<P::Value> {
        let page = self.pages.get(index >> P::SHIFT)?.as_ref()?;
        page.get(index & ((1 << P::SHIFT) - 1))
    }

    /// Publish one value and return the previous value and whether this allocated a page.
    #[inline]
    pub(super) fn insert(&mut self, index: usize, value: P::Value) -> (Option<P::Value>, bool) {
        let (page, page_was_absent) = self.page_mut_or_default(index);
        let index = index & ((1 << P::SHIFT) - 1);
        let previous = page.get(index);
        page.insert(index, value);
        (previous, page_was_absent)
    }

    pub(super) fn page_mut_or_default(&mut self, index: usize) -> (&mut P, bool) {
        let page_index = index >> P::SHIFT;
        if self.pages.len() <= page_index {
            self.pages.resize_with(page_index + 1, || None);
        }
        let page_was_absent = self.pages[page_index].is_none();
        let page = self.pages[page_index].get_or_insert_with(Box::default);
        self.page_count += usize::from(page_was_absent);
        (page, page_was_absent)
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(super) fn page_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.page_count
    }
}

impl<P: RemovablePagedColumnPage> PagedColumn<P> {
    pub(super) fn remove(&mut self, index: usize) -> Option<P::Value> {
        self.pages
            .get_mut(index >> P::SHIFT)?
            .as_mut()?
            .remove(index & ((1 << P::SHIFT) - 1))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::BitColumn;

    #[test]
    fn bit_column_equality_ignores_trailing_zero_words() {
        let mut left = BitColumn::default();
        left.set(1, true);
        left.set(70, true);
        left.set(70, false);

        let mut right = BitColumn::default();
        right.set(1, true);

        assert!(left == right);

        right.set(70, true);
        assert!(left != right);
    }
}

//! What the style engine models of selectors beside their components: which pseudo-classes are
//! boolean element state facts, and where an `@scope` with no `<scope-start>` roots.

use super::input_types::StateFact;
use super::tree::StyleNodeID;
use crate::css::selector::PseudoClassType;

/// Where an `@scope` with no `<scope-start>` roots.
///
/// The specification's answer is the parent element of the sheet's owner node, which is an element
/// rather than a selector, so the caller resolves it. When the sheet has no owner node - a
/// constructed sheet - the answer is the shadow host or the root of the containing node tree, and
/// which of those holds is a property of the scope the sheet is asked in rather than of the sheet,
/// so it is left to matching.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ImplicitScopeRoot {
    Node(StyleNodeID),
    ContainingTree,
}

// The pseudo-classes StyleEngine models as boolean element state facts.
//
// Returning `None` means the pseudo-class is an operator instead, not that it lacks a state fact.
include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/style_state_fact_compiler_generated.rs"));

/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! Matching selectors by walking their components: the evaluator the rule index, invalidation, the exact matcher and
//! the DOM queries match by.
//!
//! A selector matches compound by compound from its subject leftwards, reading each component where it is in its
//! sheet's arena. What the document decides (quirks folding, the HTML namespace) comes from the match context, and
//! the `@scope` levels of the rule from its bound scope chain.

use super::StyleAtomID;
use super::index::{DispatchKey, dispatch_bloom_bit};
use super::selector::attribute_value_matches;
use super::selector_evaluation::{ElementFeatures, SelectorEvaluator, SelectorSubject, SelectorTree, StructuralRead};
use crate::css::selector::{
    AttributeCaseType, AttributeMatchType, AttributeSelector, Combinator, CompoundRef, NamespaceType,
    PseudoClassSelector, PseudoClassType, Selector, SelectorListView, SimpleSelector,
};
use crate::css::selector_arena::{IdOrClass, Nesting};
use smallvec::SmallVec;

type Answer<S> = Result<bool, <S as SelectorSubject>::Incomplete>;

/// What matching a selector needs to know of the document it matches in.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct MatchContext<'a> {
    /// The HTML namespace in an HTML document, where tag and attribute names fold, and none elsewhere.
    pub(crate) html_namespace: StyleAtomID,
    /// Whether ids and classes compare ASCII case-insensitively, as in a quirks-mode document, whose elements
    /// publish their folded forms.
    pub(crate) fold_ids_and_classes: bool,
    /// The `@namespace` declarations of the sheet the selectors are in.
    pub(crate) namespaces: crate::css::selector_arena::SheetNamespaces<'a>,
    /// Whether the selector names an element in another tree, with `::slotted()` or `::part()`, where the sheet's
    /// default namespace does not follow it.
    pub(crate) escapes_its_namespace: bool,
    /// Whether the selector being matched is an argument of a logical pseudo-class, whose subject the default
    /// namespace does not constrain unless it writes a name of its own.
    pub(crate) logical_subject: bool,
}

/// How a walk along a selector's compounds ended: matched, or else which elements a walk further right has to try
/// again from.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Walk {
    Matched,
    /// No element of the walk left of a later sibling of the element tried can match either.
    RestartFromLaterSibling,
    /// Only an element further down, below a descendant combinator, can match.
    RestartFromDescendant,
    /// No element the walk can still reach matches.
    NotMatchedGlobally,
}

/// A positional pseudo-class, as the components say it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Position<'a> {
    step: i32,
    offset: i32,
    from_end: bool,
    of_type: bool,
    of: Option<SelectorListView<'a>>,
}

impl<S: SelectorSubject> SelectorEvaluator<S> {
    /// Whether `node` matches `selector`, walking its compounds from the subject leftwards.
    /// A selector targeting a pseudo-element matches the element it originates from: the compounds before it.
    pub(crate) fn matches_selector(
        &mut self,
        selector: Selector<'_>,
        node: S::Node,
        context: MatchContext<'_>,
    ) -> Answer<S> {
        // NB: The compounds are read from the subject leftwards where they lie in the arena: the compound a selector
        //     ends in, as `::part()`, `::slotted()` or a pseudo-element, is the first one read, which the arena notes
        //     most selectors end in none of.
        if selector.describes_its_subject() {
            return self.matches_from(selector, None, node, context);
        }
        let target = selector.first_compound();
        if targets_a_pseudo_element(&target) {
            let Some(left) = left_of(selector) else {
                return Ok(false);
            };
            // The pseudo-classes written after an element-backed pseudo-element describe the element backing it,
            // which stands in the originating element's shadow tree.
            match backed_pseudo_element_kind(&target) {
                Some(kind) => {
                    let Some(backing) = self.subject.tree().backing_element_of(node, kind) else {
                        return Ok(false);
                    };
                    for simple in target.simple_selectors.after_first().iter() {
                        if !self.matches_simple_component(&simple, backing, context)? {
                            return Ok(false);
                        }
                    }
                }
                // FIXME: The pseudo-classes written after a pseudo-element no element backs, which describe the
                //        pseudo-element itself, but for the search text filters, which pick the entry.
                None if target
                    .simple_selectors
                    .after_first()
                    .iter()
                    .any(|simple| crate::css::selector_arena::search_text_match_filter(&simple).is_none()) =>
                {
                    return Ok(false);
                }
                None => {}
            }
            return self.matches_chain_from(left, node, context);
        }
        self.matches_chain_from(selector, node, context)
    }

    /// As [`Self::matches_selector`], for the selector from `at` leftwards, once the compound of a pseudo-element it
    /// targets was matched.
    fn matches_chain_from(&mut self, at: Selector<'_>, node: S::Node, context: MatchContext<'_>) -> Answer<S> {
        let target = at.first_compound();
        let rest = left_of(at);
        if let Some(names) = part_names(&target) {
            return self.matches_part(rest, &target, names, node, context);
        }
        if let Some(argument) = slotted_argument(&target) {
            return self.matches_slotted(rest, argument, node, context);
        }
        self.matches_from(at, None, node, context)
    }

    /// Whether `node` is a part, named `names`, which a host the selector `rest` matches exposes, and matches the
    /// pseudo-classes written after `::part()`.
    ///
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-shadow-parts-1/#part
    fn matches_part(
        &mut self,
        rest: Option<Selector<'_>>,
        part: &CompoundRef<'_>,
        names: &[StyleAtomID],
        node: S::Node,
        context: MatchContext<'_>,
    ) -> Answer<S> {
        for simple in part.simple_selectors.after_first().iter() {
            if !self.matches_simple_component(&simple, node, context)? {
                return Ok(false);
            }
        }
        // `::part()` reaches one level down: into a tree hosted by an element of the tree the rule itself is in. A
        // compound naming `:host` reaches the rule's own tree as well, which is where a part forwarded out of it
        // stands.
        let tree = self.subject.tree();
        let scope_host = self.bindings.scope_shadow_root.and_then(|root| tree.host_of(root));
        let mentions_the_host = rest.is_some_and(|rest| {
            rest.first_compound().simple_selectors.iter().any(|simple| {
                matches!(simple, SimpleSelector::PseudoClass(pseudo_class) if pseudo_class.pseudo_class == PseudoClassType::Host)
            })
        });
        for level_host in self.subject.part_exposure_hosts(node) {
            let reaches_a_hosted_tree = tree.shadow_host_of(level_host) == scope_host;
            let reaches_its_own_tree = Some(level_host) == scope_host && mentions_the_host;
            if !reaches_a_hosted_tree && !reaches_its_own_tree {
                continue;
            }
            let mut exposed = true;
            for &name in names {
                if !self.subject.exposes_part_to(node, name, level_host)? {
                    exposed = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if !exposed {
                continue;
            }
            let host_matches = match rest {
                Some(rest) => self.matches_from(rest, None, level_host, context)?,
                None => true,
            };
            if host_matches {
                return Ok(true);
            }
        }
        Ok(false)
    }

    /// Whether `node`, slotted, matches `argument`, and a slot it is assigned to through the tree whose selectors are
    /// matched matches the selector `rest`.
    ///
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#slotted-pseudo
    fn matches_slotted(
        &mut self,
        rest: Option<Selector<'_>>,
        argument: Selector<'_>,
        node: S::Node,
        context: MatchContext<'_>,
    ) -> Answer<S> {
        let tree = self.subject.tree();
        if tree.assigned_slot_of(node).is_none() || !self.matches_selector(argument, node, context)? {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        // The chain can pass through several trees; the slot the compounds describe is the one in the tree whose
        // selectors are matched.
        const MAX_REASSIGNMENTS: usize = 32;
        let mut current = node;
        for _ in 0..MAX_REASSIGNMENTS {
            let Some(slot) = tree.assigned_slot_of(current) else {
                return Ok(false);
            };
            let in_this_tree = self.bindings.scope_shadow_root.is_none_or(|root| {
                std::iter::successors(Some(slot), |&node| tree.live_parent(node)).any(|node| node == root)
            });
            if in_this_tree {
                let slot_matches = match rest {
                    Some(rest) => self.matches_from(rest, None, slot, context)?,
                    None => true,
                };
                if slot_matches {
                    return Ok(true);
                }
            }
            current = slot;
        }
        Ok(false)
    }

    fn matches_scope_level(
        &mut self,
        scope: &super::bridge::BoundScopeChain,
        level: usize,
        selector: Selector<'_>,
        names_the_scope: bool,
        node: S::Node,
        context: MatchContext<'_>,
    ) -> Answer<S> {
        if level == scope.levels.len() {
            let matches = self.matches_selector(selector, node, context)?;
            if matches {
                self.bindings.matched_scope_root = self.bindings.scope_root_instance;
            }
            return Ok(matches);
        }
        let (roots, limits) = scope_level_ranges(scope, level);
        let innermost = level + 1 == scope.levels.len();
        // A scoped selector carries an implied `:scope ` prefix unless it names `:scope`, so the subject is a strict
        // descendant of the innermost root. An enclosing scope is satisfied by the subject being anywhere inside it.
        let inclusive = !innermost || names_the_scope;
        let enclosing_root = self.bindings.scope_root_instance;
        let scope_shadow_root = self.bindings.scope_shadow_root;
        let tree = self.subject.tree();
        let step = |candidate: Option<S::Node>| match candidate {
            Some(root) if Some(root) == scope_shadow_root => tree.host_of(root),
            candidate => candidate,
        };
        // A part stands inside a shadow tree, but an outer scope reaches it through the host exposing it, so scope
        // membership is measured from that host rather than from the part's parent chain.
        let part_hosts = match part_names(&selector.first_compound()) {
            Some(_) => self.subject.part_hosts_in_exposure_scope(node),
            None => None,
        };
        let starts: smallvec::SmallVec<[(Option<S::Node>, bool); 1]> = match &part_hosts {
            Some(hosts) => hosts
                .iter()
                .map(|&host| match inclusive {
                    true => (Some(host), false),
                    false => (tree.live_parent(host), false),
                })
                .collect(),
            None => smallvec::smallvec![(
                step(match inclusive {
                    true => Some(node),
                    false => tree.live_parent(node),
                }),
                true
            )],
        };
        for (start, steps_to_host) in starts {
            let mut candidate = start;
            while let Some(root) = candidate {
                if self.matches_scope_root(scope, level, roots.clone(), root, context)? {
                    let outer = self.bindings.scope_root_instance.replace(root);
                    let answer = (|| -> Answer<S> {
                        if self.is_beyond_scope_limit(scope, limits.clone(), node, root, context)? {
                            return Ok(false);
                        }
                        self.matches_scope_level(scope, level + 1, selector, names_the_scope, node, context)
                    })();
                    self.bindings.scope_root_instance = outer;
                    if answer? {
                        return Ok(true);
                    }
                }
                if Some(root) == enclosing_root {
                    break;
                }
                candidate = match steps_to_host {
                    true => step(tree.live_parent(root)),
                    false => tree.live_parent(root),
                };
            }
        }
        Ok(false)
    }

    /// Whether `candidate` roots a scope of `level`: its implicit root, or an element its `<scope-start>` matches,
    /// where `:scope` names the enclosing scope's root.
    fn matches_scope_root(
        &mut self,
        scope: &super::bridge::BoundScopeChain,
        level: usize,
        roots: std::ops::Range<usize>,
        candidate: S::Node,
        context: MatchContext<'_>,
    ) -> Answer<S> {
        if let Some(implicit) = scope.implicit_roots.get(level).copied().flatten() {
            let matches = match implicit {
                super::compiler::ImplicitScopeRoot::Node(named) => self.subject.is_node(candidate, named),
                super::compiler::ImplicitScopeRoot::ContainingTree => {
                    self.subject.is_root(candidate)
                        || self
                            .bindings
                            .scope_shadow_root
                            .is_some_and(|root| self.subject.tree().shadow_root_of(candidate) == Some(root))
                }
            };
            if matches {
                return Ok(true);
            }
        }
        let anchor = self.bindings.scope_root_instance;
        for root in &scope.roots[roots] {
            let root = root.view();
            let leading = root.leftmost_compound().combinator;
            // Directly inside another `@scope`, a start that begins with a combinator is relative to its root.
            let matches = match leading {
                Combinator::None => self.matches_selector(root, candidate, context)?,
                Combinator::Descendant => {
                    self.matches_with_leading(root, Combinator::None, None, candidate, context)?
                }
                _ => self.matches_with_leading(root, leading, anchor, candidate, context)?,
            };
            if matches {
                return Ok(true);
            }
        }
        Ok(false)
    }

    /// Whether `node`, or an element between it and the scoping root `root`, matches a `<scope-end>` of the level.
    fn is_beyond_scope_limit(
        &mut self,
        scope: &super::bridge::BoundScopeChain,
        limits: std::ops::Range<usize>,
        node: S::Node,
        root: S::Node,
        context: MatchContext<'_>,
    ) -> Answer<S> {
        if limits.is_empty() {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let tree = self.subject.tree();
        let mut walked = Some(node);
        while let Some(current) = walked {
            for (limit, &names_the_root) in scope.limits[limits.clone()]
                .iter()
                .zip(&scope.limits_name_the_root[limits.clone()])
            {
                let limit = limit.view();
                let leading = limit.leftmost_compound().combinator;
                // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-6/#scope-syntax
                // A `<scope-end>` is relative to the scoping root: one that starts with a combinator, or names
                // neither `&` nor `:scope`, is read as though `:where(:scope)` came first.
                let matches = match (leading, names_the_root) {
                    (Combinator::None, false) => {
                        self.matches_with_leading(limit, Combinator::Descendant, Some(root), current, context)?
                    }
                    (Combinator::None | Combinator::Descendant, true) => {
                        self.matches_with_leading(limit, Combinator::None, None, current, context)?
                    }
                    (leading, _) => self.matches_with_leading(limit, leading, Some(root), current, context)?,
                };
                if matches {
                    return Ok(true);
                }
            }
            if current == root {
                break;
            }
            walked = tree.live_parent(current);
        }
        Ok(false)
    }

    /// Whether `node` matches `selector` with its leftmost compound related to `anchor` by `leading`, or standing
    /// alone for no combinator.
    fn matches_with_leading(
        &mut self,
        selector: Selector<'_>,
        leading: Combinator,
        anchor: Option<S::Node>,
        node: S::Node,
        context: MatchContext<'_>,
    ) -> Answer<S> {
        let outer = std::mem::replace(&mut self.bindings.relative_anchor, anchor);
        let answer = self.matches_from(selector, Some(leading), node, context);
        self.bindings.relative_anchor = outer;
        answer
    }

    /// Whether `node` matches any selector of `list`.
    fn matches_any(&mut self, list: SelectorListView<'_>, node: S::Node, context: MatchContext<'_>) -> Answer<S> {
        let context = MatchContext {
            logical_subject: true,
            ..context
        };
        for selector in list {
            // A pseudo-element is not an element, which a logical pseudo-class's argument describes.
            if !targets_a_pseudo_element(&selector.first_compound())
                && self.matches_selector(selector, node, context)?
            {
                return Ok(true);
            }
        }
        Ok(false)
    }

    /// Whether `node` matches the selector from `at`, its subject compound, leftwards, with the leftmost compound
    /// related to the anchor by `leading` where one is given rather than by the combinator written.
    fn matches_from(
        &mut self,
        at: Selector<'_>,
        leading: Option<Combinator>,
        node: S::Node,
        context: MatchContext<'_>,
    ) -> Answer<S> {
        Ok(self.walk_compound(at, true, leading, node, context)? == Walk::Matched)
    }

    /// As [`Self::walk_compound`] for a compound left of the subject's, which an element whose dispatch keys lack an id
    /// or class it tests for cannot match: the bits the arena noted for the compound tell before its components are read.
    fn walk_rejecting_on_bloom(
        &mut self,
        at: Selector<'_>,
        leading: Option<Combinator>,
        node: S::Node,
        context: MatchContext<'_>,
    ) -> Result<Walk, S::Incomplete> {
        if S::FILTERS_BY_REQUIRED_DISPATCH_BLOOM {
            let required = required_dispatch_bloom(at, context);
            if required != 0 && !self.subject.may_match_required(required, node) {
                return Ok(Walk::RestartFromLaterSibling);
            }
        }
        self.walk_compound(at, false, leading, node, context)
    }

    /// Whether `node` matches the first compound of `at`, the subject compound where `is_subject`, and what is left
    /// of it, or else which elements no further one tried left of the combinator right of it can match from either.
    fn walk_compound(
        &mut self,
        at: Selector<'_>,
        is_subject: bool,
        leading: Option<Combinator>,
        node: S::Node,
        context: MatchContext<'_>,
    ) -> Result<Walk, S::Incomplete> {
        let compound = at.first_compound();
        if !self.matches_compound_components(&compound, node, context)?
            || self.is_outside_the_default_namespace(&compound, is_subject, node, context)?
        {
            return Ok(Walk::RestartFromLaterSibling);
        }
        self.walk_left_of(at, leading, node, context)
    }

    /// Whether `node` is outside the default namespace that constrains `compound`, the subject compound where
    /// `is_subject`.
    fn is_outside_the_default_namespace(
        &mut self,
        compound: &CompoundRef<'_>,
        is_subject: bool,
        node: S::Node,
        context: MatchContext<'_>,
    ) -> Answer<S> {
        // A compound with no type or universal selector written has one implied, which a default namespace
        // constrains as well, except where the compound names the host, the selector reaches into another tree, or
        // the compound is the subject of a logical pseudo-class's argument.
        // The universal selector the parse implies before a compound that starts with a pseudo-element is not
        // written.
        let written = match compound.is_implicit_universal_anchor {
            true => compound.simple_selectors.after_first(),
            false => compound.simple_selectors,
        };
        Ok(match context.namespaces.default {
            Some(default)
                if !context.escapes_its_namespace
                    && !(context.logical_subject && is_subject)
                    && !written.iter().any(|simple| {
                        matches!(simple, SimpleSelector::Universal(_) | SimpleSelector::TagName(_))
