    EffectsValues => EFFECTS,
    AnchorValues => ANCHOR,
    BorderValues => BORDER,
    InheritedTextValues => INHERITED_TEXT,
    TransformValues => TRANSFORM,
}

/// A style for layout's own use, which no record holds: a base style's groups, with those an edit
/// wrote replaced by copies. It is never interned or installed.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) struct LayoutScratchStyle(crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroups);

#[cfg(test)]
impl LayoutScratchStyle {
    /// `base`, with the groups `edit` writes replaced, the rest shared.
    pub(crate) fn over(
        base: crate::css::computed_value_views::ComputedValuesView<'_>,
        edit: impl FnOnce(&mut ScratchGroups),
    ) -> Self {
        let mut groups = ScratchGroups {
            groups: base.record_groups().0.clone(),
            written: [false; group_index::COUNT],
        };
        edit(&mut groups);
        Self(groups.groups)
    }

    /// The default groups, with the groups `edit` writes replaced.
    pub(crate) fn over_defaults(edit: impl FnOnce(&mut ScratchGroups)) -> Self {
        let defaults = crate::css::computed_values::DefaultGroups::default();
        Self::over(
            crate::css::computed_value_views::ComputedValuesView::of(defaults.groups()),
            edit,
        )
    }

    /// The style, for a row to read while this stays in place.
    pub(crate) fn style(&self) -> crate::layout::node_data::LayoutStyleRef {
        crate::layout::node_data::LayoutStyleRef::of_groups(&self.0)
    }
}

/// The groups of a [`LayoutScratchStyle`] being written: each group is copied the first time it is
/// written, and the copy is the scratch style's own.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) struct ScratchGroups {
    groups: crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroups,
    written: [bool; group_index::COUNT],
}

#[cfg(test)]
impl ScratchGroups {
    fn group_mut<T: LayoutStyleGroup>(&mut self) -> &mut T {
        if !self.written[T::INDEX] {
            // SAFETY: The private trait pairs each type with its registered group index.
            unsafe { self.groups.write_group::<T>(T::INDEX, |_| {}) };
            self.written[T::INDEX] = true;
        }
        // SAFETY: The group is a copy only these groups hold, written through `&mut self` alone, and
        //         the private trait pairs each type with its registered group index.
        unsafe { &mut *self.groups[T::INDEX].as_ptr().cast_mut().cast::<T>() }
    }

    pub(crate) fn box_mut(&mut self) -> &mut BoxValues {
        self.group_mut()
    }

    pub(crate) fn sizing_mut(&mut self) -> &mut SizingValues {
        self.group_mut()
    }

    pub(crate) fn surround_mut(&mut self) -> &mut SurroundValues {
        self.group_mut()
    }

    pub(crate) fn alignment_mut(&mut self) -> &mut AlignmentValues {
        self.group_mut()
    }

    pub(crate) fn border_mut(&mut self) -> &mut BorderValues {
        self.group_mut()
    }

    pub(crate) fn anchor_mut(&mut self) -> &mut AnchorValues {
        self.group_mut()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_position(&mut self, position: u8) {
        let reset = self
            .groups
            .reset_bits()
            .with(crate::css::computed_values::StyleBitField::Position, position);
        self.groups.set_reset_bits(reset);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_white_space_collapse(&mut self, collapse: u8) {
        let mut values = self.groups.inherited_values();
        values.bits = values
            .bits
            .with(crate::css::computed_values::StyleBitField::WhiteSpaceCollapse, collapse);
        self.groups.set_inherited_values(values);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_writing_mode(&mut self, writing_mode: u8) {
        let mut values = self.groups.inherited_values();
        values.bits = values
            .bits
            .with(crate::css::computed_values::StyleBitField::WritingMode, writing_mode);
        self.groups.set_inherited_values(values);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_overflow(&mut self, x: u8, y: u8) {
        use crate::css::computed_values::StyleBitField;
        let reset = self
            .groups
            .reset_bits()
            .with(StyleBitField::OverflowX, x)
            .with(StyleBitField::OverflowY, y);
        self.groups.set_reset_bits(reset);
    }
}

pub(crate) struct LayoutStyle {
    payloads: crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroups,
    /// The record whose longhands the style carries, which is read only once the style is interned.
    longhand_source: Option<u64>,
    changed: bool,
}

impl LayoutStyle {
    pub(crate) fn from_record(engine: &super::RetainedState, record: u64) -> Self {
        let view = engine
            .style_record_view(record)
            .expect("layout style record must be live");
        Self {
            payloads: view.payloads.clone(),
            longhand_source: Some(record),
            changed: false,
        }
    }

    fn inherited(engine: &StyleEngine, parent: u64) -> Self {
        let parent = engine
            .style_record_payloads(parent)
            .expect("anonymous box parent style must be live");
        let mut payloads = engine.default_groups().groups().clone();
        for index in
            crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroupIndex::all().take(super::computed::ENGINE_INHERITED_GROUP_COUNT)
        {
            payloads.share_group(parent, index);
        }
        payloads.set_inherited_values(parent.inherited_values());
        Self {
            payloads,
            longhand_source: None,
            changed: false,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn inherit_from(&mut self, engine: &StyleEngine, parent: u64) {
        let parent = engine
            .style_record_payloads(parent)
            .expect("anonymous box parent style must be live");
        for index in
            crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroupIndex::all().take(super::computed::ENGINE_INHERITED_GROUP_COUNT)
        {
            self.payloads.share_group(parent, index);
        }
        self.payloads.set_inherited_values(parent.inherited_values());
    }

    fn group<T: LayoutStyleGroup>(&self) -> &T {
        // SAFETY: The private trait pairs each type with its registered group index.
        unsafe { &*self.payloads[T::INDEX].as_ptr().cast::<T>() }
    }

    fn edit<T: LayoutStyleGroup>(&mut self, update: impl FnOnce(&mut T)) {
        let mut value = self.group::<T>().clone();
        update(&mut value);
        if value == *self.group::<T>() {
            return;
        }
        self.changed = true;
        // SAFETY: The private trait pairs each type with its registered group index.
        unsafe { self.payloads.write_group::<T>(T::INDEX, |payload| *payload = value) };
    }

    /// Draws text in its color at half its alpha, i.e. `color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 50%, transparent)`, which
    /// reads as a suggestion in light and dark color schemes alike.
    fn fade_text_color(&mut self) {
        let fade = |color: u32| (color >> 24).div_ceil(2) << 24 | (color & 0x00ff_ffff);
        let index = group_index::INHERITED_TEXT;
        // SAFETY: The group is the inherited text group.
        unsafe {
            self.payloads.write_group::<InheritedTextValues>(index, |values| {
                values.color = fade(values.color);
                values.webkit_text_fill_color = fade(values.webkit_text_fill_color);
                values.webkit_text_stroke_color.rgba = fade(values.webkit_text_stroke_color.rgba);
            });
        };
        self.changed = true;
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_unchanged(&self) -> bool {
        !self.changed
    }

    /// The group payloads of this style, for a row's style reads to see in place of its record's, as a record's
    /// payloads are named. They address the style where it is, so the caller keeps it in place while reads see them.
    pub(crate) fn payloads_for_style_reads(&self) -> crate::layout::node_data::LayoutStyleRef {
        crate::layout::node_data::LayoutStyleRef::of_groups(&self.payloads)
    }

    /// Builds the payloads of `groups` again from `table`, a longhand table holding the style's computed values with
    /// some of them replaced.
    /// The values `animated_overlay` samples over the table win over it where they do over the style's own table.
    pub(crate) fn replace_groups_from_values(
        &mut self,
        values: &crate::css::computed_values::GroupValues<'_>,
        groups: &[usize],
        defaults: &crate::css::computed_values::DefaultGroups,
    ) {
        let source = crate::css::table_group_builder::LonghandSource::Values { values, reads: None };
        for &group in groups {
            let current = self.payloads[group].as_ptr();
            // SAFETY: The style holds a reference to its payload of every group.
            let parent = unsafe { crate::css::computed_values::GroupPayloadRef::new(group, current) };
            let payload = crate::css::table_group_builder::rebuild_group_from_source(
                &source,
                group,
                crate::css::computed_values::GroupShares::new(defaults, group, parent),
                0,
                0,
                None,
            )
            .expect("a group of the accepted @position-try properties builds from its values");
            // SAFETY: The rebuild hands over a reference to a payload of the group.
            let payload = unsafe { crate::css::computed_values::HeldGroup::adopt(group, payload) };
            if payload.as_ptr() == current {
                continue;
            }
            self.changed = true;
            drop(self.payloads.replace(payload));
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn position_area(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.group::<AnchorValues>().position_area.as_slice().to_vec()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_position_area(&mut self, codes: Vec<u8>) {
        self.edit::<AnchorValues>(|values| values.position_area = RetainedPositionAreaList::from_vec(codes));
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_display(&mut self, display: FfiDisplay) {
        self.edit::<BoxValues>(|values| values.display = display);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_overflow(&mut self, x: u8, y: u8) {
        use crate::css::computed_values::StyleBitField;
        let reset = self
            .payloads
            .reset_bits()
            .with(StyleBitField::OverflowX, x)
            .with(StyleBitField::OverflowY, y);
        self.set_reset_bits(reset);
    }

    /// Puts `reset` in place of the style's reset bits.
    fn set_reset_bits(&mut self, reset: crate::css::computed_value_types::ResetBits) {
        if reset != self.payloads.reset_bits() {
            self.changed = true;
            self.payloads.set_reset_bits(reset);
        }
    }

    /// The style's reset bits, with the codes of `source`'s position, float and clear.
    fn with_position_float_clear_of(
        &self,
        source: crate::css::computed_value_types::ResetBits,
    ) -> crate::css::computed_value_types::ResetBits {
        use crate::css::computed_values::StyleBitField;
        [StyleBitField::Position, StyleBitField::Float, StyleBitField::Clear]
            .into_iter()
            .fold(self.payloads.reset_bits(), |bits, field| {
                bits.with(field, source.get(field))
            })
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_writing_mode_and_direction(&mut self, writing_mode: u8, direction: u8) {
        use crate::css::computed_values::StyleBitField;
        let mut values = self.payloads.inherited_values();
        values.bits = values
            .bits
            .with(StyleBitField::WritingMode, writing_mode)
            .with(StyleBitField::Direction, direction);
        if values != self.payloads.inherited_values() {
            self.changed = true;
            self.payloads.set_inherited_values(values);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_scrollbar_width(&mut self, width: u8) {
        self.edit::<MiscInteractionValues>(|values| values.scrollbar_width = width);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_overscroll_behavior(&mut self, x: u8, y: u8) {
        self.edit::<MiscInteractionValues>(|values| {
            values.overscroll_behavior_x = x;
            values.overscroll_behavior_y = y;
        });
    }

    // CSS table wrappers carry positioning and margins, and act as the table's flex or grid item.
    // z-index and vertical-align also follow the wrapper for interoperable painting and
    // inline alignment; clip only applies on the wrapper that receives position.
    fn transfer_table_properties(&mut self, source: &Self) {
        let box_values = source.group::<BoxValues>();
        self.edit::<BoxValues>(|target| {
            target.display = FfiDisplay::outside_and_inside(
                if box_values.display.is_inline_outside() {
                    display_outside::INLINE
                } else {
                    display_outside::BLOCK
                },
                display_inside::FLOW_ROOT,
                false,
            );
            // NB: The wrapper is the box that gets positioned, so it keeps the display the table was given, which
            //     decides where an absolutely positioned table's static position is.
            target.display_before_box_type_transformation = box_values.display_before_box_type_transformation;
            target.has_z_index = box_values.has_z_index;
            target.z_index = box_values.z_index;
            target.vertical_align = box_values.vertical_align.clone();
            target.baseline_source = box_values.baseline_source;
        });
        self.set_reset_bits(self.with_position_float_clear_of(source.payloads.reset_bits()));
        let misc_layout = source.group::<MiscLayoutValues>();
        self.edit::<MiscLayoutValues>(|target| {
            target.column_span = misc_layout.column_span;
            target.break_before = misc_layout.break_before;
            target.break_after = misc_layout.break_after;
            target.break_inside = misc_layout.break_inside;
        });
        self.copy_table_properties(source);
    }

    pub(crate) fn copy_column_properties(&mut self, source: &Self) {
        let box_values = source.group::<BoxValues>();
        self.edit::<BoxValues>(|target| {
            target.column_count = box_values.column_count;
            target.column_count_has_value = box_values.column_count_has_value;
            target.column_width = box_values.column_width.clone();
        });
        let misc_layout = source.group::<MiscLayoutValues>();
        self.edit::<MiscLayoutValues>(|target| {
            target.column_fill = misc_layout.column_fill;
            target.column_rule_style = misc_layout.column_rule_style;
            target.column_rule_width = misc_layout.column_rule_width;
            target.column_rule_color = misc_layout.column_rule_color;
        });
        let alignment = source.group::<AlignmentValues>();
        self.edit::<AlignmentValues>(|target| target.column_gap = alignment.column_gap.clone());
    }

    fn copy_table_properties(&mut self, source: &Self) {
        let surround = source.group::<SurroundValues>();
        self.edit::<SurroundValues>(|target| {
            target.inset = surround.inset.clone();
            target.position_anchor = surround.position_anchor.clone();
            target.margin = surround.margin.clone();
        });
        self.edit::<AnchorValues>(|target| {
            let source = source.group::<AnchorValues>();
            target.position_anchor_type = source.position_anchor_type;
            target.position_anchor_name = source.position_anchor_name.clone();
        });
        let alignment = source.group::<AlignmentValues>();
        self.edit::<AlignmentValues>(|target| {
            target.align_self = alignment.align_self;
            target.justify_self = alignment.justify_self;
            target.align_self_overflow = alignment.align_self_overflow;
            target.justify_self_overflow = alignment.justify_self_overflow;
            target.order = alignment.order;
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox-1/#flex-items
            // "In the case of flex items with display: table, the table wrapper box becomes the flex item"
            // NB: The flex longhands follow the wrapper, which the flex container sizes as the flex item.
            target.flex_basis = alignment.flex_basis.clone();
            target.flex_grow = alignment.flex_grow;
            target.flex_shrink = alignment.flex_shrink;
        });
        self.edit::<GridValues>(|target| {
            crate::css::computed_values::copy_grid_placements(source.group::<GridValues>(), target);
        });
        // INTEROP: Like other engines, transform the table wrapper box, so the captions move with the table and
        //          the transform origin is relative to the wrapper.
        let transform = source.group::<TransformValues>();
        self.edit::<TransformValues>(|target| *target = transform.clone());
        self.edit::<EffectsValues>(|target| {
            let source = source.group::<EffectsValues>();
            target.clip_is_rect = source.clip_is_rect;
            if source.clip_is_rect {
                target.clip_edges = source.clip_edges;
            }
        });
    }

    pub(crate) fn reset_table_properties(&mut self, defaults: &crate::css::computed_values::DefaultGroups) {
        let defaults = Self {
            payloads: defaults.groups().clone(),
            longhand_source: None,
            changed: false,
        };
        self.set_reset_bits(self.with_position_float_clear_of(crate::css::computed_value_types::ResetBits::INITIAL));
        let initial = defaults.group::<BoxValues>();
        self.edit::<BoxValues>(|target| {
            target.has_z_index = initial.has_z_index;
            target.z_index = initial.z_index;
            target.vertical_align = initial.vertical_align.clone();
            target.baseline_source = initial.baseline_source;
        });
        self.copy_table_properties(&defaults);
    }

    pub(crate) fn anonymous(
        engine: &StyleEngine,
        parent: u64,
        kind: AnonymousStyleKind,
        overrides: AnonymousStyleOverrides,
    ) -> Self {
        let mut style = if kind == AnonymousStyleKind::InlineStyleWrapper {
            Self::from_record(engine, parent)
        } else {
            Self::inherited(engine, parent)
        };
        let block_flow = FfiDisplay::outside_and_inside(display_outside::BLOCK, display_inside::FLOW, false);
        match kind {
            AnonymousStyleKind::Wrapper | AnonymousStyleKind::ButtonContentBox => style.set_display(block_flow),
            AnonymousStyleKind::TableRow => style.set_display(FfiDisplay::internal(display_internal::TABLE_ROW)),
            AnonymousStyleKind::TableCell | AnonymousStyleKind::MissingTableCell => {
                style.set_display(FfiDisplay::internal(display_internal::TABLE_CELL));
            }
            AnonymousStyleKind::Table => style.set_display(FfiDisplay::outside_and_inside(
                display_outside::BLOCK,
                display_inside::TABLE,
                false,
            )),
            AnonymousStyleKind::InlineTable => style.set_display(FfiDisplay::outside_and_inside(
                display_outside::INLINE,
                display_inside::TABLE,
                false,
            )),
            AnonymousStyleKind::TableWrapper => style.transfer_table_properties(&Self::from_record(engine, parent)),
            AnonymousStyleKind::ButtonFlexWrapper => {
                style.set_display(FfiDisplay::outside_and_inside(
                    display_outside::BLOCK,
                    display_inside::FLEX,
                    false,
                ));
                style.edit::<AlignmentValues>(|values| {
                    values.justify_content = justify_content::CENTER;
                    values.flex_direction = flex_direction::COLUMN;
                });
                style.edit::<SizingValues>(|values| {
                    values.height = ComputedSize::new(
                        ComputedSizeKind::Percentage,
                        ComputedStyleValueHandle::percentage(100.0),
                    );
                });
            }
            AnonymousStyleKind::FieldsetContentWrapper => {
                let source = Self::from_record(engine, parent);
                let content_display_inside = fieldset_content_display_inside(source.group::<BoxValues>().display);
                style.set_display(FfiDisplay::outside_and_inside(
                    display_outside::BLOCK,
                    content_display_inside,
                    false,
                ));
                style.edit::<AlignmentValues>(|target| {
                    crate::css::computed_values::copy_fieldset_content_alignment(
                        source.group::<AlignmentValues>(),
                        target,
                    );
                });
                if source.group::<BoxValues>().display.is_grid_inside() {
                    style.edit::<GridValues>(|target| {
                        crate::css::computed_values::copy_fieldset_content_grid_template(
                            source.group::<GridValues>(),
                            target,
                        );
                    });
                    style.edit::<BoxValues>(|target| {
                        let source = source.group::<BoxValues>();
                        target.grid_auto_flow_row = source.grid_auto_flow_row;
                        target.grid_auto_flow_dense = source.grid_auto_flow_dense;
                    });
                }
                style.set_overflow(overrides.overflow_x, overrides.overflow_y);
            }
            AnonymousStyleKind::InlineStyleWrapper | AnonymousStyleKind::WritingSuggestion => style.set_display(
                FfiDisplay::outside_and_inside(display_outside::INLINE, display_inside::FLOW, false),
            ),
        }
        if kind == AnonymousStyleKind::WritingSuggestion {
            style.fade_text_color();
        }
        if kind == AnonymousStyleKind::MissingTableCell {
            style.edit::<BoxValues>(|values| {
                values.vertical_align = ComputedVerticalAlign {
                    is_keyword: true,
                    keyword: vertical_align::MIDDLE,
                    value: ComputedStyleValueHandle::empty(),
                }
            });
        }
        if overrides.columns_from_parent {
            style.copy_column_properties(&Self::from_record(engine, parent));
        }
        if kind == AnonymousStyleKind::ButtonContentBox {
            style.edit::<SizingValues>(|values| {
                values.min_height = ComputedSize::new(ComputedSizeKind::Length, ComputedStyleValueHandle::length(0.0));
            });
        }
        style
    }

    pub(crate) fn intern(self, engine: &mut StyleEngine) -> DerivedStyleRecord {
        // A layout style holds the longhands of the record it was made from, or the initial ones
        // where it only inherits its parent's groups.
        let record = match self.longhand_source {
            Some(source) => engine
                .install_record_derived_from(
                    super::computed::FinalStyleRecordID::from_raw(source).expect("a layout style's source is a record"),
                    &self.payloads,
                )
                .expect("a layout style's source record is one the engine installed"),
            None => engine.install_initial_derived_record(&self.payloads, 0),
        };
        DerivedStyleRecord::pin(engine, record.raw())
    }
}

impl StyleEngine {
    /// Has the installation of a style update's rows in the boxes of their elements remember the record each
    /// anonymous box it styles again derives, until [`Self::end_reinheriting_for_install`]: the anonymous boxes under
    /// elements styled alike derive the same record, which is then found rather than built and interned again.
    pub(crate) fn begin_reinheriting_for_install(&mut self) {
        debug_assert!(self.host.reinherited_records.is_none());
        self.host.reinherited_records = Some(Default::default());
    }

    /// Ends what [`Self::begin_reinheriting_for_install`] began, letting go of the records it remembered.
    pub(crate) fn end_reinheriting_for_install(&mut self) {
        for (_, record) in self.host.reinherited_records.take().unwrap_or_default() {
            self.unpin_layout_style_record(record);
        }
    }

    /// The record an anonymous box holding `record` derives from `parent`, its parent's, taking the column properties
    /// of `column_source` where it has one, pinned for the box.
    pub(crate) fn reinherited_anonymous_style_record(
        &mut self,
        record: u64,
        parent: u64,
        column_source: Option<u64>,
    ) -> DerivedStyleRecord {
        let key = Reinheritance {
            record,
            parent,
            column_source,
        };
        if let Some(&derived) = self
            .host
            .reinherited_records
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|records| records.get(&key))
        {
            return DerivedStyleRecord::pin(self, derived);
        }
        let mut style = LayoutStyle::from_record(self, record);
        style.inherit_from(self, parent);
        if let Some(column_source) = column_source {
            style.copy_column_properties(&LayoutStyle::from_record(self, column_source));
        }
        let derived = style.intern(self);
        // NB: What is remembered stays pinned until the installation ends, as a box that took it may let go of it.
        if let Some(records) = self.host.reinherited_records.as_mut() {
            records.insert(key, derived.record);
            self.pin_layout_style_record(derived.record);
        }
        derived
    }

    pub(crate) fn pin_layout_style_record(&mut self, record: u64) {
        self.pin_style_record(record);
    }

    /// Pins `record` `times` times, as many calls of [`Self::pin_layout_style_record`] would.
    pub(crate) fn pin_layout_style_record_times(&mut self, record: u64, times: u32) {
        self.pin_style_record_times(record, times);
    }

    pub(crate) fn unpin_layout_style_record(&mut self, record: u64) {
        self.unpin_style_record(record);
    }
}

//! What a document's style engine holds on the heap, by owner.
//!
//! Each owner is a store of the engine, or one kind of thing several stores share: the records,
//! their group payloads and chunks, and the style values. A shared allocation is counted once, by
//! the first owner the report reaches it from, so the owners the report walks first are the ones
//! that hold the most of what others share: the initial style before the records sharing its
//! chunks, the records before the slots holding them. See [`crate::heap_size`] for what a count
//! is.

use crate::heap_size::{HeapSize, HeapSizer};
use std::sync::Arc;

macro_rules! memory_owners {
    ($($owner:ident => $name:literal,)*) => {
        /// An owner of style memory.
        #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
        #[repr(u8)]
        pub(crate) enum MemoryOwner {
            $($owner,)*
        }

        impl MemoryOwner {
            pub(crate) const ALL: &[MemoryOwner] = &[$(MemoryOwner::$owner,)*];
            pub(crate) const COUNT: usize = Self::ALL.len();

            pub(crate) fn name(self) -> &'static str {
                match self {
                    $(MemoryOwner::$owner => $name,)*
                }
            }
        }
    };
}

memory_owners! {
    Initial => "initial",
    RuleStore => "ruleStore",
    RuleIndex => "ruleIndex",
    UserAgentIndex => "userAgentIndex",
    SheetSegments => "sheetSegments",
    SharedDeclarations => "sharedDeclarations",
    Invalidation => "invalidation",
    Records => "records",
    Payloads => "payloads",
    GroupValueFacts => "groupValueFacts",
    CustomProperties => "customProperties",

/// A memory report under way, and then its result.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct MemoryReport {
    pub(crate) sizer: HeapSizer,
    bytes: [usize; MemoryOwner::COUNT],
    /// The elements the document holds.
    pub(crate) elements: usize,
    /// The elements that hold a style record.
    pub(crate) styled_elements: usize,
}

impl MemoryReport {
    /// A report of what `sizer` has not counted.
    pub(crate) fn past(sizer: HeapSizer) -> Self {
        Self {
            sizer,
            ..Self::default()
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn add(&mut self, owner: MemoryOwner, bytes: usize) {
        self.bytes[owner as usize] += bytes;
    }

    /// Counts `value`'s heap toward `owner`.
    pub(crate) fn count<T: HeapSize + ?Sized>(&mut self, owner: MemoryOwner, value: &T) {
        let bytes = value.heap_size(&mut self.sizer);
        self.add(owner, bytes);
    }

    pub(crate) fn bytes(&self, owner: MemoryOwner) -> usize {
        self.bytes[owner as usize]
    }

    /// Ends the report, moving the style values counted aside to their owner.
    pub(crate) fn finish(mut self) -> Self {
        let style_value_bytes = std::mem::take(&mut self.sizer.style_value_bytes);
        self.add(MemoryOwner::StyleValues, style_value_bytes);
        self
    }
}

impl super::StyleEngine {
    /// Lets go of what the engine's passes work in and keep for the next one, for a document that stopped styling.
    pub(crate) fn trim_scratch(&mut self) {
        if let Some(live) = self.retained.live_style.as_mut() {
            live.trim_scratch();
        }
    }

    /// What the engine holds on the heap, by owner, with the layout arena's style columns.
    pub(crate) fn memory_report(&self, arena: &crate::layout::LayoutNodeArena) -> MemoryReport {
        self.memory_report_into(MemoryReport::default(), arena)
    }

    /// [`Self::memory_report`], past what `report` has counted already.
    pub(crate) fn memory_report_into(
        &self,
        mut report: MemoryReport,
        arena: &crate::layout::LayoutNodeArena,
    ) -> MemoryReport {
        use crate::heap_size::{map_bytes, set_bytes, small_vec_bytes, vec_bytes};
        let state = &self.retained;
        let bytes = state.rules.heap_size(&mut report.sizer);
        report.add(MemoryOwner::RuleStore, bytes);
        // NB: The values the declarations were written with are the blocks' own, rather than
        //     counted aside.
        let style_value_bytes = report.sizer.style_value_bytes;
        let mut bytes = state.rules.declarations_heap_size(&mut report.sizer);
        if let Some(rules) = state.rules.user_agent_rules() {
            bytes += rules.declarations_heap_size(&mut report.sizer);
        }
        bytes += std::mem::replace(&mut report.sizer.style_value_bytes, style_value_bytes) - style_value_bytes;
        report.add(MemoryOwner::SharedDeclarations, bytes);
        if let Some(rules) = state.rules.user_agent_rules()
            && report.sizer.first_sight(Arc::as_ptr(rules))
        {
            let bytes = crate::heap_size::ARC_HEADER_BYTES + size_of_val(&**rules) + rules.heap_size(&mut report.sizer);
            report.add(MemoryOwner::UserAgentIndex, bytes);
        }
        if let Some(live) = &state.live_style {
            live.report_memory(&mut report);
        }
        state.computed_group_sets.report_memory(&mut report);
        let bytes = state.custom_property_environments.heap_size(&mut report.sizer);
        report.add(MemoryOwner::CustomProperties, bytes);
        report.add(
            MemoryOwner::CustomProperties,
            state.element_custom_property_data.heap_size()
                + state.pseudo_element_custom_property_data.heap_size()
                + state
                    .pseudo_element_custom_property_data
                    .values()
                    .map(vec_bytes)
                    .sum::<usize>(),
        );
        state.projection.report_memory(&mut report);
        let bytes = state.tree.heap_size(&mut report.sizer);
        report.add(MemoryOwner::HostTree, bytes);
        let bytes = state.element_declarations.heap_size(&mut report.sizer);
        report.add(MemoryOwner::ElementDeclarations, bytes);
        let held_style_records = state.held_style_records.heap_size(&mut report.sizer);
        report.add(
            MemoryOwner::HeldRecordMaps,
            held_style_records
                + state.held_pseudo_style_records.heap_size()
                + state
                    .held_pseudo_style_records
                    .values()
                    .map(small_vec_bytes)
                    .sum::<usize>(),
        );
        report.add(MemoryOwner::LayoutStyleColumns, arena.style_column_heap_size());
        if let Some(font_resolution) = &state.font_resolution {
            report.add(MemoryOwner::FontResolutions, font_resolution.heap_size());
        }
        let bytes = state.css_defined_animations.heap_size(&mut report.sizer);
        report.add(MemoryOwner::CssAnimations, bytes);
        let bytes = state.animation_effect_descriptions.heap_size(&mut report.sizer);
        report.add(MemoryOwner::AnimationEffects, bytes);
        report.add(
            MemoryOwner::OtherMaps,
            state.keyframes_reading_parent_reset_values.heap_size()
                + map_bytes(&state.layout_style_snapshots)
                + state.counter_style_environment_identities.heap_size()
                + state.backing_elements.heap_size()
                + state.replaced_content_inputs.heap_size()
                + state.demand_records.heap_size()
                + state.transition_baselines.heap_size()
                + state.scope_roots.heap_size()
                + state.scope_by_root.heap_size()
                + set_bytes(&state.unresolved_relational_arrival_keys),
        );
        report.finish()
    }
}

//! StyleEngine: selector evaluation, cascade, and computed-value construction modelled as a
//! memory-bounded incremental computation.
//!
//! DOM structure, element state, stylesheets, CSSOM mutations, cascade topology, and environment
//! values are versioned inputs. A style flush propagates exact changes through selectors, cascade
//! decisions, and computed values, and stops as soon as a semantic value is unchanged. Derived state
//! lives as long as the node or rule it describes.
//!
//! Everything between a style input and a computed value is authoritative here, on the Rust side.
//! C++ remains authoritative for DOM and CSSOM object identity, mutation semantics, document
//! lifecycle, loading order, style-observation barriers, layout, and paint - and holds no second
//! copy of the state this engine owns.

macro_rules! define_id {
    ($(#[$attribute:meta])* $visibility:vis struct $name:ident();) => {
        $(#[$attribute])*
        #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
        $visibility struct $name(u32);
    };
    ($(#[$attribute:meta])* $visibility:vis struct $name:ident($field_visibility:vis);) => {
        $(#[$attribute])*
        #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
        $visibility struct $name($field_visibility u32);
    };
    ($(#[$attribute:meta])* default $visibility:vis struct $name:ident();) => {
        $(#[$attribute])*
        #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
        $visibility struct $name(u32);
    };
    ($(#[$attribute:meta])* default $visibility:vis struct $name:ident($field_visibility:vis);) => {
        $(#[$attribute])*
        #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
        $visibility struct $name($field_visibility u32);
    };
}

/// Long-lived engine state: the document, its program, derived results and cross-flush
/// caches. This is the whole read side of an evaluation step; it holds no
/// host handle, no pending input intake and no borrowed FFI result storage.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct RetainedState {
    /// What the engine counts of its own decisions.
    counters: Counters,
    /// The elements the host shows each kind of highlight in.
    highlight_observers: pipeline::highlight_observers::HighlightObservers,
    tree: HostTree,
    /// The depth of the deepest element the tree ever held, which the document's host reads.
    deepest_element: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32>,
    /// Where the hover is.
    hover: hover_lane::Hover,
    rules: crate::fork::ForkShared<RuleStore>,
    /// The style data the engine shares with the other engines of the process.
    process_style: Arc<process_style::ProcessStyle>,
    /// The last declaration block version minted, by the engine or by its document's host, which mints without it.
    declaration_block_version: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32>,
    /// Latest document-wide scalar computation facts, copied at the transaction boundary. The host
    /// publishes them with every transaction, before it asks for any row.
    document_style_computation_inputs: bridge::FfiDocumentStyleComputationInputs,
    /// The base URLs a `url()` resolves against, copied at the transaction boundary with the inputs.
    document_resource_contexts: resource_contexts::DocumentResourceContexts,
    /// The document's media features, copied from each transaction's inputs.
    document_media: custom_property_cascade::DocumentMediaSnapshot,
    /// The `@function` definitions each scope sees, retained from each transaction's inputs.
    document_functions: custom_property_cascade::DocumentFunctionSnapshot,
    /// The custom-property registry the last transaction's inputs name, which the engine holds a
    /// reference to for as long as it reads the registry: the document makes its registry anew
    /// when the registrations change.
    custom_property_registry: Option<std::sync::Arc<crate::css::custom_properties::CustomPropertyRegistry>>,
    /// Every font resolution this document has been given. An evaluation step reads it; only a
    /// host round between passes adds to it.
    font_resolution: Option<font_resolution::FontResolutionCache>,
    /// The fonts the threads of the style pass under way resolve, where they do.
    pass_fonts: Option<std::sync::Arc<font_resolution::PassFonts>>,

    /// The shared computed-group payload tuple last published for each live element. This is the
    /// computed half of the eventual base style record; custom properties and metadata remain
    /// separate inputs until that record is complete.
    computed_group_sets: ComputedGroupSets,
    /// How many epochs of style record views the host has open. No computed record is reclaimed while one is.
    style_record_view_epoch_depth: u32,
    /// The stores behind the custom-property environments live records are published with.
    custom_property_environments: crate::fork::ForkShared<custom_property_environments::CustomPropertyEnvironments>,
    /// The custom-property environment each element holds, for the elements that hold one. This is
    /// the only copy: the element reads its environment from here.
    element_custom_property_data: crate::cow_map::CowMap<StyleNodeID, inputs::HeldCustomPropertyEnvironment>,
    /// The custom-property environments of each element's synthetic pseudo-elements, by
    /// pseudo-element kind, for the elements with a pseudo-element that holds one.
    pseudo_element_custom_property_data:
        crate::cow_map::CowMap<StyleNodeID, Vec<(u8, inputs::HeldCustomPropertyEnvironment)>>,
    /// The elements whose animations' keyframes say `inherit` for a property that does not
    /// inherit, as the host last sampled them: they read their parent's values of properties that
    /// do not inherit, whether or not their records do.
    keyframes_reading_parent_reset_values: crate::cow_map::CowSet<StyleNodeID>,
    /// What the container conditions of the rows the engine answered read of their containers,
    /// per element, taken when the host installs the element's record.
    container_effects_for_host: container_queries::ContainerEffectsForHost,
    /// What the last layout commit and scroll state say of each container's box, for the
    /// container queries that ask about it: a size container's, and a scroll-state container's.
    layout_style_snapshots: HashMap<StyleNodeID, crate::layout::style_snapshot::LayoutStyleSnapshotRow>,
    /// What the host learned about size container queries, which finds the elements a size
    /// query container's new box moves.
    size_container_queries: size_container_invalidation::SizeContainerQueryFacts,
    /// The counter-style registry each tree scope's style scope has, as one identity per scope:
    /// what a record whose `list-style-type` names a counter style the registry may define names,
    /// so that an edit to `@counter-style` moves it.
    counter_style_environment_identities: crate::cow_map::CowMap<TreeScopeID, u64>,
    /// The style record each element holds, for the elements that hold one, as the host reports
    /// every record it installs or clears.
    /// Copied on write in chunks of its own, which a fork shares.
    held_style_records: inputs::HeldStyleRecords,
    /// The style record each pseudo-element holds, for the elements whose pseudo-elements
    /// hold one, as the host reports every record it installs or clears.
    held_pseudo_style_records: HeldPseudoStyleRecords,
    /// The records a clock frame shows in place of the ones the host installed, which it lends the published reads
    /// for as long as it runs.
    tick_shown: engine_sample::TickShownRecords,
    /// Per shadow host, the elements of its shadow tree that stood for one of its element-backed
    /// pseudo-elements when the host published them; [`RetainedState::backing_elements`] reads the
    /// ones that still do.
    backing_elements: crate::cow_map::CowMap<StyleNodeID, SmallVec<[StyleNodeID; 2]>>,
    /// The names of the CSS animations the host holds for each element, which the computation of
    /// its animation definitions matches them against.
    css_defined_animations: crate::fork::ForkShared<animations::CssDefinedAnimations>,
    /// The `@keyframes` each of the document's style scopes defines, as the host's rule caches
    /// resolved them, which an animation definition's keyframes are resolved from.
    animation_keyframes: crate::fork::ForkShared<animations::AnimationKeyframes>,
    /// The `@position-try` rules each of the document's style scopes defines, as the host's rule caches resolved
    /// them, which the position options of an absolutely positioned box are made from.
    position_try_rules: crate::fork::ForkShared<position_try::PositionTryRules>,
    /// The animation effects the host holds for each element, described for sampling.
    animation_effect_descriptions: crate::fork::ForkShared<effect_descriptions::AnimationEffectDescriptions>,
    /// The font metrics of the record the host holds for the document element, which a `rem` the
    /// host resolves reads, once it holds one.
    held_root_font_inputs: Option<pipeline::compute::RootFontInputs>,
    /// The random base value each random caching key has been given, for the random functions the
    /// document's styles hold.
    random_base_values: random_bases::RandomBaseValues,
    /// What each element that has replaced content gives its natural size, which layout resolves
    /// against the style of the element's box.
    replaced_content_inputs: crate::cow_map::CowMap<StyleNodeID, inputs::ReplacedContentInput>,
    /// The before-change style each transition target's transitions are decided against for the
    /// rest of the style stabilization epoch, pinned until the epoch commits.
    transition_baselines: transition_baselines::TransitionBaselines,
    /// Whether the registrations used by this transaction differ from the preceding one. A
    /// previously substituted record must then be computed again, even when its cascade winners did
    /// not move.
    custom_property_registrations_changed: bool,
    /// The record a private demand last answered for each target it was asked about, pinned for
    /// the host to read: no node holds it.
    demand_records: crate::cow_map::CowMap<computed::ComputedStyleTarget, computed::FinalStyleRecordID>,

    /// The places of the children of parents with many of them, which sibling-counting functions
    /// read, kept while the tree's DOM order stands.
    sibling_positions: crate::fork::ForkReset<Mutex<publication::SiblingPositionCache>>,
    /// The elements a style() container query asked as containers with a value counting their place among their
    /// siblings. A fork shares them, as too many only walk more. An element's identity used again stays here too.
    containers_counted_by_style_queries: Arc<Mutex<HashSet<StyleNodeID>>>,
    /// What the engine keeps of the document it owns, which a fork goes on keeping.
    live_style: Option<Box<pipeline::Live>>,
    /// Whether this is the state the host writes, on which alone the engine starts.
    live_style_may_start: crate::fork::ForkReset<crate::fork::IsOriginal>,
    /// What the engine did on this state, for tests to read.
    live_counters: pipeline::counters::Counters,
    /// The threads style passes run on, which the process shares where a render state holds the
    /// engine.
    style_layout_pool: Option<std::sync::Arc<crate::style_layout_pool::StyleLayoutPool>>,
    /// The font longhand values the engine substituted, one value per property and content: the
    /// font resolver knows a family and its feature values by their values' identities.
    substituted_font_values: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<(u16, RetainedStyleValueData)>>>,
    /// The longhand properties each element declares itself, by the kind of declaration they came
    /// from. An element-attached declaration beats every rule in its context, so the cascade needs
    /// to know which properties one covers just as it does for a rule.
    element_declarations: element_declarations::ElementDeclarationStore,
    /// The document as the engine reads it: every element fact and link the host publishes.
    projection: pipeline::projection::Projection,
    /// The attribute names whose value text a selector reads, which the host holds a copy of between jobs.
    attribute_value_text_names: SelectorAttributeNames,
    /// The attribute names a selector tests in any way, which the host holds a copy of between jobs.
    tested_attribute_names: SelectorAttributeNames,
    attribute_value_text_requirements_version: u64,
    /// Whether a selector tests `:local-link`, which the host holds a copy of between jobs.
    selectors_test_local_link: bool,
    selectors_test_validity: bool,
    /// What an arrival has to carry to reach a `:has()` anchor, which the host holds a copy of between jobs.
    relational_arrival_keys: Arc<RelationalArrivalKeys>,
    /// The keys rules added since, which the host learns of once they are resolved.
    unresolved_relational_arrival_keys: HashSet<DispatchKey>,
    /// Moves whenever `relational_arrival_keys` does.
    relational_arrival_keys_version: u64,
    /// The node that owns each style scope, for the scopes that have one. The document's scope has
    /// no node, and a scope with no entry here is treated as the document's - which is the widest
    /// answer and therefore the safe one. Tree-scope identities are minted monotonically within one
    /// document, so the identity indexes the column directly.
    scope_roots: crate::fork::ForkShared<Column<Option<StyleNodeID>>>,
    /// The inverse of `scope_roots`. Departing ordinary elements vastly outnumber departing scope
    /// roots, so retirement must ask this index instead of scanning every historical tree scope.
    scope_by_root: crate::fork::ForkShared<SegmentedNodeColumn<TreeScopeID>>,
    /// Maps names and qualified names to process-global atoms. Selector names and DOM facts use
    /// the same owner, so a class in a stylesheet and a class on an element compare as one integer.
    ///
    /// An attribute in a namespace is published under this as well as under its local name, and a
    /// selector that names the namespace tests it. The owner retains one document reference to each
    /// global identity and releases it when this engine is destroyed.
    atoms: crate::fork::ForkShared<DocumentAtoms>,
    /// The HTML namespace when this is an HTML document, and none otherwise. Some attribute names
    /// compare their values ASCII case-insensitively on an HTML element in an HTML document.
    html_element_namespace: StyleAtomID,
    /// Whether the document matches id and class selectors ASCII case-insensitively, which a
    /// quirks-mode one does. Selectors are then compiled against the lowercase folding of the name,
    /// and the DOM side publishes the folding too, so `.item` and `ITEM` name one atom.
    fold_id_and_class_name_case: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct DeferredElementStyleInput {
    reaction: u8,
    inherited_style_groups: u8,
}

/// Host-facing engine state: C++ ownership and input intake.
/// Never reachable from an evaluation step.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct HostState {
    /// The host's synchronous font resolver. A step that misses the cache suspends its element;
    /// the round outside the step calls this and the element is retried.
    font_resolver: Option<font_resolution::FontResolverHost>,
    /// The element whose composition the host is settling, whose moves are told once it has.
    settling_composition: Option<pipeline::SettlingComposition>,
    /// The element inputs the next transaction takes beside the projection's changes.
    element_inputs: PendingElementInputs,
    /// Exact element reactions retained across rootless flushes until a style root can consume them.
    deferred_element_style_inputs: std::collections::BTreeMap<StyleNodeID, DeferredElementStyleInput>,
    /// Whether the deferred element style inputs moved since the document's host last took them.
    deferred_element_style_inputs_moved: bool,
    /// Whether the deferred element style inputs are owed to the next transaction, as opposed to
    /// held back by a flush without a document root.
    deferred_element_style_inputs_are_pending: bool,
    /// The rule edits this transaction staged, with their before and after values, until it is
    /// released.
    program_staging: ProgramStaging,
    sheet_occurrences: HashMap<TreeScopeID, pipeline::rule_store::ScopeSheetOccurrences>,
    /// The old dense rule sequence while one sheet is synchronously reparsed.
    sheet_rule_replacement: Option<SheetRuleReplacement>,
    /// Identities released at transaction settlement. The FFI keeps this batch borrowed until C++
    /// has removed its matching fly-string references and atom-keyed memo entries.
    reclaimed_style_atoms: Vec<ReclaimedStyleAtom>,
    /// Whether the transaction under way leaves its atom sweep to a later one: it runs beside the host, which may name
    /// an atom meanwhile that the sweep would reclaim before the host hears of it.
    defers_atom_sweep: bool,
    /// The records the anonymous boxes an installation styles again derive, by the record each held, its parent's and
    /// the one it takes its column properties from, while an installation runs.
    reinherited_records: Option<HashMap<layout_style::Reinheritance, u64>>,
    /// The style node identities the end of a transaction released since the job began, which the job's end pays the
    /// host to mint again.
    released_style_nodes: Vec<u32>,
    /// What the hover seal keeps between frames.
    hover_seal: pipeline::HoverSealMemo,
}

/// Mutable engine state; operations borrow their instrumentation from the boundary.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct StyleEngine {
    pub(super) retained: RetainedState,
    pub(super) host: HostState,
}

impl RetainedState {
    pub(crate) fn deepest_element_depth(&self) -> u32 {
        self.deepest_element.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    /// One past the greatest element slot the document holds a row for: about how many elements it has.
    pub(crate) fn element_slot_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.projection.element_slot_count()
    }

    pub(crate) fn started_style_layout_pool(&self) -> Option<std::sync::Arc<rayon::ThreadPool>> {
        self.style_layout_pool.as_ref()?.started()
    }

    /// The groups of default values every computation starting from nothing starts from.
    pub(crate) fn default_groups(&self) -> &crate::css::computed_values::DefaultGroups {
        &self.process_style.default_groups
    }
}

impl std::ops::Deref for StyleEngine {
    type Target = RetainedState;

    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
        &self.retained
    }
}

impl std::ops::DerefMut for StyleEngine {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Target {
        &mut self.retained
    }
}

//! Order-maintenance tokens for cascade source order.
//!
//! Source order is a comparison, never a stored rank. Tokens are stable handles into a flat label
//! table, while a second vector keeps the tokens in order. Insertion normally chooses the midpoint
//! of the neighbouring labels. When a gap is exhausted, all live labels are spread evenly again.
//!
//! Numeric relabeling changes no semantic version. Nothing downstream uses a label as identity; it
//! only reads the order labels imply. Relabeling is therefore invisible to selector truth, cascade
//! winners, and computed values.

define_id! {
    /// A stable handle on one position in an order. The numeric label behind it may be rewritten at
    /// any time; the handle does not change.
    pub struct OrderToken();
}

/// One totally ordered axis: stylesheet order within a tree context, nested rule order within a
/// sheet, or layer order within an origin.
#[derive(Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct OrderMaintenance {
    labels: Vec<u64>,
    free_entries: Vec<u32>,
    order: Vec<OrderToken>,
    /// How many times the labels were spread evenly again.
    relabels: u64,
}

impl OrderMaintenance {
    pub(super) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        use crate::heap_size::vec_bytes;
        vec_bytes(&self.labels) + vec_bytes(&self.free_entries) + vec_bytes(&self.order)
    }

    /// Give up the room the order holds beyond its entries.
    pub(super) fn shrink_to_fit(&mut self) {
        self.labels.shrink_to_fit();
        self.free_entries.shrink_to_fit();
        self.order.shrink_to_fit();
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    #[must_use]
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.order.len()
    }

    #[must_use]
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.order.is_empty()
    }

    /// The comparable rank of a position.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn rank(&self, token: OrderToken) -> u64 {
        self.labels[token.0 as usize]
    }

    /// How many times the order was relabeled, which moves the ranks of its positions without
    /// moving their order.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn relabels(&self) -> u64 {
        self.relabels
    }

    /// Insert at the end of the order.
    pub fn insert_last(&mut self) -> OrderToken {
        self.insert_at(self.order.len())
    }

    /// Insert at the start of the order.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn insert_first(&mut self) -> OrderToken {
        self.insert_at(0)
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn insert_after(&mut self, after: OrderToken) -> OrderToken {
        let position = self.locate(after);
        self.insert_at(position + 1)
    }

    pub fn insert_before(&mut self, before: OrderToken) -> OrderToken {
        let position = self.locate(before);
        self.insert_at(position)
    }

    pub fn remove(&mut self, token: OrderToken) {
        let position = self.locate(token);
        self.order.remove(position);
        self.free_entries.push(token.0);
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = OrderToken> + '_ {
        self.order.iter().copied()
    }

    fn insert_at(&mut self, position: usize) -> OrderToken {
        let (mut lower, mut upper) = self.bounds(position);
        if upper - lower < 2 {
            self.relabel();
            (lower, upper) = self.bounds(position);
        }
        assert!(
            upper - lower >= 2,
            "a relabeled order always leaves room for one insertion"
        );

        let token = self.allocate_entry(lower + (upper - lower) / 2);
        self.order.insert(position, token);
        token
    }

    fn bounds(&self, position: usize) -> (u64, u64) {
        let lower = position
            .checked_sub(1)
            .map_or(0, |index| self.labels[self.order[index].0 as usize]);
        let upper = self
            .order
            .get(position)
            .map_or(u64::MAX, |token| self.labels[token.0 as usize]);
        (lower, upper)
    }

    fn relabel(&mut self) {
        let length = u64::try_from(self.order.len()).expect("order length exceeds label space");
        let step = u64::MAX / (length + 1);
        assert!(step >= 2, "order label space exhausted");
        self.relabels += 1;
        for (index, token) in self.order.iter().enumerate() {
            self.labels[token.0 as usize] = step * (index as u64 + 1);
        }
    }

    fn allocate_entry(&mut self, label: u64) -> OrderToken {
        match self.free_entries.pop() {
            Some(index) => {
                self.labels[index as usize] = label;
                OrderToken(index)
            }
            None => {
                self.labels.push(label);
                OrderToken(u32::try_from(self.labels.len() - 1).expect("order token space exhausted"))
            }
        }
    }

    fn locate(&self, token: OrderToken) -> usize {
        self.order
            .iter()
            .position(|candidate| *candidate == token)
            .expect("an order token must be live")
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn is_sorted(order: &OrderMaintenance, tokens: &[OrderToken]) -> bool {
        tokens.windows(2).all(|pair| order.rank(pair[0]) < order.rank(pair[1]))
    }

    #[test]
    fn appending_keeps_positions_ordered() {
        let mut order = OrderMaintenance::new();
        let tokens: Vec<OrderToken> = (0..500).map(|_| order.insert_last()).collect();
        assert_eq!(order.len(), 500);
        assert!(is_sorted(&order, &tokens));
        assert_eq!(order.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(), tokens);
    }

    #[test]
    fn prepending_keeps_positions_ordered() {
        let mut order = OrderMaintenance::new();
        let mut tokens: Vec<OrderToken> = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..500 {
            tokens.insert(0, order.insert_first());
        }
        assert!(is_sorted(&order, &tokens));
        assert_eq!(order.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(), tokens);
    }

    #[test]
    fn repeatedly_inserting_at_the_same_point_keeps_positions_ordered() {
        let mut order = OrderMaintenance::new();
        let first = order.insert_last();
        let last = order.insert_last();

        let mut middles = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..2000 {
            middles.push(order.insert_after(first));
        }
        middles.reverse();

        let mut expected = vec![first];
        expected.extend(middles);
        expected.push(last);
        assert_eq!(order.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(), expected);
        assert!(is_sorted(&order, &expected));
    }

    #[test]
    fn interleaved_insertion_and_removal_keeps_the_order_consistent() {
        let mut order = OrderMaintenance::new();
        let mut tokens: Vec<OrderToken> = (0..200).map(|_| order.insert_last()).collect();

        for index in (0..tokens.len()).step_by(3).rev() {
            order.remove(tokens[index]);
            tokens.remove(index);
        }
        assert_eq!(order.len(), tokens.len());
        assert!(is_sorted(&order, &tokens));

        for index in (0..tokens.len()).step_by(2) {
            let inserted = order.insert_before(tokens[index]);
            assert!(order.rank(inserted) < order.rank(tokens[index]));
        }
        assert_eq!(order.iter().count(), order.len());
    }

    #[test]
    fn removing_every_position_reuses_the_entry_arena() {
        let mut order = OrderMaintenance::new();
        let tokens: Vec<OrderToken> = (0..300).map(|_| order.insert_last()).collect();
        for token in tokens {
            order.remove(token);
        }
        assert!(order.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(order.iter().count(), 0);

        let reinserted: Vec<OrderToken> = (0..300).map(|_| order.insert_last()).collect();
        assert!(is_sorted(&order, &reinserted));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_rank_orders_the_same_way_a_comparison_does() {
        let mut order = OrderMaintenance::new();
        let first = order.insert_last();
        let second = order.insert_last();
        for _ in 0..300 {
            order.insert_after(first);
        }
        assert!(order.rank(first) < order.rank(second));
        let all: Vec<OrderToken> = order.iter().collect();
        assert!(all.windows(2).all(|pair| order.rank(pair[0]) < order.rank(pair[1])));
    }
}

use super::pipeline::projection::NoteChanges;
use super::*;

impl RetainedState {
    /// Where the cascade of `node` weighs a match from `scope`. Each tree the element is in or slotted into stands at its depth, one deeper than the
    /// last, so only the element's own shadow tree, after all of those, stands elsewhere.
    pub(super) fn encapsulation_context(&self, node: StyleNodeID, scope: TreeScopeID) -> u32 {
        if self.own_shadow_tree(node) != Some(scope) {
            return self.tree_scope_depth(scope);
        }
        let slotted_into = self.scopes_slotted_into(node).count() as u32;
        self.tree_scope_depth(self.projection.tree_scope(node)) + slotted_into + 1
    }

    /// The tree the element's shadow root roots, where its `:host` rules decide from.
    fn own_shadow_tree(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> Option<TreeScopeID> {
        self.projection
            .shadow_root_of(node)
            .and_then(|shadow_root| self.scope_by_root.get(shadow_root))
    }

    /// Every tree whose `::slotted()` can name this element.
    ///
    /// A slot is itself a slottable, so an element can be assigned to a slot that is assigned to
    /// another: what stands in the flat tree at the end of that chain is the element, not the slots
    /// it passed through, and each tree along the way is one whose `::slotted()` names it.
    pub(super) fn scopes_slotted_into(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> impl Iterator<Item = TreeScopeID> {
        // A slot standing in a shadow tree is not a flattened slottable of the tree it is assigned
        // into: "find flattened slottables" recurses into its own slottables rather than appending
        // it. So no scope names it through `::slotted()`, even though its assignment is what carries
        // the chain onward for the nodes below it.
        let is_reslotted_slot = self.projection.written_facts(node).is_some_and(|facts| facts.is_slot())
            && self.projection.tree_scope(node) != TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT;
        // A chain is at most as deep as the trees are nested, and a cycle is impossible - a slot
        // cannot be assigned to itself - but a bound keeps a corrupted column from spinning.
        const MAX_REASSIGNMENTS: usize = 32;
        let mut current = node;
        let mut remaining = MAX_REASSIGNMENTS;
        std::iter::from_fn(move || {
            if remaining == 0 || is_reslotted_slot {
                return None;
            }
            remaining -= 1;
            let slot = self.projection.assigned_slot_of(current)?;
            current = slot;
            Some(self.projection.tree_scope(slot))
        })
    }

    /// How deeply a tree scope is encapsulated: the document is zero, a shadow tree inside it one,
    /// and one inside that two. It is where an element's cascade weighs a tree it is in or slotted
    /// into (`encapsulation_context`), outermost first for a normal declaration and innermost first
    /// for an important one.
    #[must_use]
    pub(super) fn tree_scope_depth(&self, tree_scope: TreeScopeID) -> u32 {
        let mut depth = 0;
        let mut scope = tree_scope;
        while scope != TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT {
            let Some(root) = self.scope_root(scope) else {
                break;
            };
            let Some(host) = self.projection.host_of(root) else {
                break;
            };
            depth += 1;
            let next = self.projection.tree_scope(host);
            if next == scope {
                break;
            }
            scope = next;
        }
        depth
    }

    pub(super) fn element_cascade_priority(
        &self,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        kind: ElementDeclarationKind,
        important: bool,
    ) -> CascadePriority {
        let tree_scope = self.projection.tree_scope(node);
        let (origin, element_attachment) = match kind {
            ElementDeclarationKind::InlineStyle => (CascadeOrigin::Author, ElementAttachment::InlineStyle),
            ElementDeclarationKind::PresentationalHint | ElementDeclarationKind::SvgPresentationAttribute => (
                CascadeOrigin::AuthorPresentationalHint,
                ElementAttachment::PresentationalHint,
            ),
        };
        CascadePriority::new(PriorityInputs {
            origin,
            important,
            context_depth: self.tree_scope_depth(tree_scope),
            element_attachment,
            layer_rank: self.rules.layer_rank(tree_scope, CascadeLayerID::UNLAYERED),
            specificity: Specificity::default(),
            scope_proximity: u32::MAX,
            sheet_rank: u64::MAX,
            rule_rank: u64::MAX,
        })
    }
}

impl StyleEngine {
    /// Normalize the pending inputs without advancing the committed snapshot.
    pub(super) fn drain_transaction(&mut self) -> StyleUpdate {
        // A transaction taken other than to flush a geometry read's seal takes everything written.
        self.retained.projection.drop_seal();
        self.finalize_staged_sheet_rule_replacements();
        let transaction = self.host.element_inputs.take_transaction();
        self.retained.counters.add(
            Counter::NormalizedUniqueKeys,
            (transaction.declarations.len() + transaction.style_inputs.len()) as u64,
        );
        transaction
    }

    /// Settle inputs which cannot be planned while the document has no style root. Exact element
    /// style reactions are edge-triggered, so preserve them for the first transaction with a root.
    pub(crate) fn flush_without_document_root(&mut self) {
        let transaction = self.take_transaction();
        for &(node, input) in &transaction.style_inputs {
            self.defer_element_style_input(node, input.reaction, input.inherited_style_groups);
        }
        // Held back rather than owed: without a root there is no transaction to take them.
        self.host.deferred_element_style_inputs_are_pending = false;
        self.release_transaction(transaction);
    }

    /// Merge one element style input into the deferred inputs, which are kept sorted by key.
    pub(crate) fn defer_element_style_input(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID, reaction: u8, inherited_style_groups: u8) {
        self.host.deferred_element_style_inputs_moved = true;
        let pending = self
            .host
            .deferred_element_style_inputs
            .entry(node)
            .or_insert(DeferredElementStyleInput {
                reaction: 0,
                inherited_style_groups: 0,
            });
        pending.reaction |= reaction;
        pending.inherited_style_groups |= inherited_style_groups;
    }

    /// Release a drained transaction's scratch charge.
    pub fn release_transaction(&mut self, transaction: StyleUpdate) {
        transaction.release();
        self.forget_departed_elements();
        // NB: Nothing is written between the barrier and here, so this commits only the
        //     departed elements' facts leaving.
        self.retained.projection.release();

        self.host.program_staging.clear();
        // NB: With nothing staged, the committed versions are every version naming a sheet's
        //     selectors. The store is asked first, as writing to it copies what a fork shares.
        if self.retained.rules.wants_letting_go_of_selectors() {
            self.retained.rules.let_go_of_unnamed_selectors();
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn collect_live_style_atoms(&self) -> (HashSet<StyleAtomID>, u64) {
        assert!(
            !self.retained.projection.has_written_links(),
            "style atom sweeping requires a settled tree"
        );
        let mut atoms = HashSet::default();
        let mut visited = self.retained.tree.collect_atoms(&mut atoms);
        visited += self.retained.projection.collect_atoms(&mut atoms);
        visited += self.retained.element_declarations.collect_atoms(&mut atoms);
        visited += self.retained.rules.collect_atoms(&mut atoms);
        if !self.retained.html_element_namespace.is_none() {
            atoms.insert(self.retained.html_element_namespace);
        }
        (atoms, visited)
    }

    pub(super) fn sweep_style_atoms(&mut self) {
        if !self.retained.atoms.should_sweep() || self.host.defers_atom_sweep {
            return;
        }
        let (mut live, visited) = self.collect_live_style_atoms();
        self.retained.atoms.mark_sweep_dependencies(&mut live);
        loop {
            let previous_live_count = live.len();
            self.retained.projection.extend_live_attribute_name_forms(&mut live);
            self.retained.atoms.mark_sweep_dependencies(&mut live);
            if live.len() == previous_live_count {
                break;
            }
        }
        let reclaimable = self.retained.atoms.reclaimable_for_sweep(&live);
        // NB: The host forgets what its catalogs spell of the reclaimed atoms as it learns of them.
        self.retained.custom_property_environments.forget_names(&reclaimable);
        let is_reclaimed = |atom: &StyleAtomID| reclaimable.binary_search(atom).is_ok();
        if self.retained.tested_attribute_names.iter().any(is_reclaimed) {
            Arc::make_mut(&mut self.retained.tested_attribute_names).retain(|atom| !is_reclaimed(atom));
        }
        let relational_arrival_key_is_reclaimed =
            |key: &DispatchKey| key.atom().is_some_and(|atom| is_reclaimed(&atom));
        if self
            .retained
            .relational_arrival_keys
            .keys
            .iter()
            .any(relational_arrival_key_is_reclaimed)
        {
            let mut keys = self.retained.relational_arrival_keys.keys.clone();
            keys.extend(self.retained.unresolved_relational_arrival_keys.drain());
            keys.retain(|key| !relational_arrival_key_is_reclaimed(key));
            self.retained.replace_relational_arrival_keys(keys);
        }
        if self.retained.attribute_value_text_names.iter().any(is_reclaimed) {
            Arc::make_mut(&mut self.retained.attribute_value_text_names).retain(|atom| !is_reclaimed(atom));
            self.retained.attribute_value_text_requirements_version += 1;
        }
        let reclaimed = self.retained.atoms.finish_sweep(&reclaimable);
        self.retained.counters.bump(Counter::AtomSweeps);
        self.retained.counters.add(Counter::AtomSweepRootSlotsVisited, visited);
        self.retained.counters.add(
            Counter::StyleAtomsReclaimed,
            u64::try_from(reclaimed.len()).expect("reclaimed atom count exceeds u64"),
        );
        self.host.reclaimed_style_atoms.extend(reclaimed);
    }

    /// Drop the fact rows of the elements that left, now that nothing can still route from them.
    ///
    /// A retired identity is not reused until the epoch that could name it has retired, so a row
    /// left behind here would be read as the next occupant's. Dropping it at the transaction
    /// boundary keeps the row alive for exactly as long as routing needs it.
    pub(super) fn forget_departed_elements(&mut self) {
        let projection = &self.retained.projection;
        let departed: Vec<StyleNodeID> = projection
            .relations_written()
            .filter(|&node| projection.written_relations(node).is_none())
            .collect();
        if departed.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        for node in departed {
            // NB: The host forgot the element's row as it published its departure.
            self.retained.element_declarations.forget(node);
            if let Some(tree_scope) = self.retained.scope_by_root.remove(node) {
                self.retained.scope_roots[tree_scope.0 as usize] = None;
            }
        }
    }
}

impl StyleEngine {
    /// Advance every staged input family to the transaction's final snapshot.
    pub(super) fn apply_staged_transaction(&mut self, transaction: &mut StyleUpdate, note_changes: NoteChanges) {
        transaction.rule_changes = self.commit_staged_program();
        self.settle_tree_at_barrier();
        self.retained.projection.commit_noting(note_changes);
    }

    /// Normalize and apply the staged inputs into one transaction. A required style observation
    /// drains here first, so normalization never combines changes across an observation boundary.
    pub fn take_transaction(&mut self) -> StyleUpdate {
        let mut transaction = self.drain_transaction();
        self.apply_staged_transaction(&mut transaction, NoteChanges::Yes);
        transaction
    }

    /// Release a transaction taken through the bridge and reclaim atoms before the bridge installs
    /// a new primary view. The returned reclamation batch lets C++ purge its atom memos before any
    /// reclaimed identity can be reused.
    pub(super) fn release_transaction_and_sweep_atoms(&mut self, transaction: StyleUpdate) {
        self.release_transaction(transaction);
        self.sweep_style_atoms();
    }
}

/*

//! The global allocator of this crate's unit test binary: the system allocator, counting what a
//! thread allocates while it runs `count_allocations`, and which of that the engine allocates itself,
//! inside a `StyleSection`. Only the test binary has it; the crate as the browser links it never
//! does.
//!
//! With LIBWEB_TEST_ALLOCATION_BACKTRACES set, each allocation counted prints a backtrace to
//! stderr, for a test that fails to name where its allocations come from.

use std::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout, System};
use std::cell::Cell;
use std::sync::OnceLock;

struct CountingAllocator;

#[global_allocator]
static COUNTING_ALLOCATOR: CountingAllocator = CountingAllocator;

thread_local! {
    static COUNTING: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) };
    static PRINTS_BACKTRACES: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) };
    static ALLOCATIONS: Cell<u64> = const { Cell::new(0) };
    static STYLE_ALLOCATIONS: Cell<u64> = const { Cell::new(0) };
    static STYLE_SECTION_DEPTH: Cell<u32> = const { Cell::new(0) };
    static LIVE_BYTES: Cell<i64> = const { Cell::new(0) };
}

/// How many times a thread allocated or reallocated.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Allocations {
    pub everywhere: u64,
    /// Those inside a `StyleSection`: invalidating, restyling and installing.
    pub in_style: u64,
}

/// Marks the allocations of the calling thread, until it drops, as the engine's own.
pub(super) struct StyleSection;

impl StyleSection {
    pub(super) fn enter() -> Self {
        STYLE_SECTION_DEPTH.with(|depth| depth.set(depth.get() + 1));
        Self
    }
}

impl Drop for StyleSection {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        STYLE_SECTION_DEPTH.with(|depth| depth.set(depth.get() - 1));
    }
}

/// Notes that the calling thread's live heap grew by `bytes`, or shrank where negative, while it counts.
fn note_live_bytes(bytes: i64) {
    let Ok(true) = COUNTING.try_with(Cell::get) else {
        return;
    };
    LIVE_BYTES.with(|live| live.set(live.get() + bytes));
}

fn note_allocation() {
    // NB: The thread-local keys have no destructors, so they stay readable while a thread exits.
    let Ok(true) = COUNTING.try_with(Cell::get) else {
        return;
    };
    ALLOCATIONS.with(|allocations| allocations.set(allocations.get() + 1));
    if STYLE_SECTION_DEPTH.with(Cell::get) != 0 {
        STYLE_ALLOCATIONS.with(|allocations| allocations.set(allocations.get() + 1));
    }
    if PRINTS_BACKTRACES.with(Cell::get) {
        // NB: Printing a backtrace allocates, so stop counting while it prints.
        COUNTING.with(|counting| counting.set(false));
        eprintln!("allocation:\n{}", std::backtrace::Backtrace::force_capture());
        COUNTING.with(|counting| counting.set(true));
    }
}

// SAFETY: Every call goes to the system allocator as it is.
unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for CountingAllocator {
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        note_allocation();
        note_live_bytes(layout.size() as i64);
        // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
        unsafe { System.alloc(layout) }
    }

    unsafe fn alloc_zeroed(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        note_allocation();
        note_live_bytes(layout.size() as i64);
        // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
        unsafe { System.alloc_zeroed(layout) }
    }

    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
        note_live_bytes(-(layout.size() as i64));
        // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
        unsafe { System.dealloc(pointer, layout) }
    }

    unsafe fn realloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout, new_size: usize) -> *mut u8 {
        note_allocation();
        note_live_bytes(new_size as i64 - layout.size() as i64);
        // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
        unsafe { System.realloc(pointer, layout, new_size) }
    }
}

/// Runs `body`, answering what it answers and how many times the calling thread allocated or
/// reallocated meanwhile. What other threads allocate is not counted.
pub(crate) fn count_allocations<T>(body: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> (T, Allocations) {
    static PRINTS_BACKTRACES_CACHE: OnceLock<bool> = OnceLock::new();
    let prints_backtraces =
        *PRINTS_BACKTRACES_CACHE.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("LIBWEB_TEST_ALLOCATION_BACKTRACES").is_some());
    assert!(!COUNTING.with(Cell::get), "allocations are counted once at a time");
    PRINTS_BACKTRACES.with(|prints| prints.set(prints_backtraces));
    ALLOCATIONS.with(|allocations| allocations.set(0));
    STYLE_ALLOCATIONS.with(|allocations| allocations.set(0));
    COUNTING.with(|counting| counting.set(true));
    let answer = body();
    COUNTING.with(|counting| counting.set(false));
    let allocations = Allocations {
        everywhere: ALLOCATIONS.with(Cell::get),
        in_style: STYLE_ALLOCATIONS.with(Cell::get),
    };
    (answer, allocations)
}

/// Runs `body`, answering what it answers and the bytes the calling thread allocated meanwhile
/// that are still allocated when it returns: what the answer holds, and what `body` left
/// elsewhere, as in a cache. What other threads allocate is not counted.
pub(crate) fn count_live_bytes<T>(body: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> (T, i64) {
    assert!(!COUNTING.with(Cell::get), "allocations are counted once at a time");
    PRINTS_BACKTRACES.with(|prints| prints.set(false));
    LIVE_BYTES.with(|live| live.set(0));
    COUNTING.with(|counting| counting.set(true));
    let answer = body();
    COUNTING.with(|counting| counting.set(false));
    (answer, LIVE_BYTES.with(Cell::get))
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
