//! How many times a style update allocates once the engine owns a document and has seen
//! the same transactions before. A transaction that changes no style should allocate nothing, in
//! the engine (invalidating, restyling and installing) or anywhere else.
//!
//! The engine runs on the calling thread here, where every allocation is counted. Run with
//! LIBWEB_TEST_ALLOCATION_BACKTRACES set to see where a test's allocations come from.

use super::super::bridge::element_adjustment_fact;
use super::super::*;
use super::allocation_count::{Allocations, count_allocations};
use super::test_support::*;

/// How many times each transaction a test measures is taken before, for every buffer it grows
/// to reach its size.
const WARMUP_ROUNDS: usize = 4;

/// How many times a test measures each transaction.
const MEASURED_ROUNDS: usize = 3;

/// How many times std's `Mutex` allocates in a transaction that restyles one element. On Apple
/// platforms it wraps a pthread mutex, which it boxes the first time it is locked: here the
/// scratch slot of the calling thread, made for each pass, and the longhand table recipe of the
/// element's new record. Elsewhere it is a futex, which allocates nothing.
const MUTEX_ALLOCATIONS_RESTYLING_ONE_ELEMENT: u64 = if cfg!(target_vendor = "apple") { 2 } else { 0 };

struct Document {
    engine: StyleEngine,
    root: StyleNodeID,
    leaf: StyleNodeID,
    /// A class one selector names.
    target: StyleAtomID,
    /// A class no selector names.
    unnamed: StyleAtomID,
}

impl Document {
    /// Builds `root -> [a, b, c]` with one rule for the class `target`, owned by the engine,
    /// and takes every transaction the tests measure `WARMUP_ROUNDS` times.
    fn warm() -> Self {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = linear_document();
        let sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
        add_rules(&mut engine, sheet, ".target { color: rgb(0, 128, 0); }");
        let target = atom(&mut engine, "target");
        let unnamed = atom(&mut engine, "unnamed");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        let mut document = Self {
            engine,
            root: nodes[0],
            leaf: nodes[3],
            target,
            unnamed,
        };
        for _ in 0..WARMUP_ROUNDS {
            document.toggle(target);
            document.toggle(unnamed);
            document.take_transaction();
        }
        document
    }

    fn take_transaction(&mut self) -> Allocations {
        let (engine, root) = (&mut self.engine, self.root);
        count_allocations(|| run_style_update(engine, root)).1
    }

    /// Adds `class` to the leaf in one transaction and removes it in another, and answers what
    /// each transaction allocated.
    fn toggle(&mut self, class: StyleAtomID) -> [Allocations; 2] {
        add_feature(&mut self.engine, self.leaf, LocalFeatureKey::Class(class));
        let added = self.take_transaction();
        remove_feature(&mut self.engine, self.leaf, LocalFeatureKey::Class(class));
        let removed = self.take_transaction();
        [added, removed]
    }

    /// What each of `MEASURED_ROUNDS` rounds of `transactions` allocated.
    fn measure(&mut self, mut transactions: impl FnMut(&mut Self) -> Vec<Allocations>) -> Vec<Allocations> {
        (0..MEASURED_ROUNDS).flat_map(|_| transactions(self)).collect()
    }

    fn empty_transactions(&mut self) -> Vec<Allocations> {
        self.measure(|document| vec![document.take_transaction()])
    }

    fn unnamed_class_toggles(&mut self) -> Vec<Allocations> {
        let unnamed = self.unnamed;
        self.measure(|document| document.toggle(unnamed).to_vec())
    }

    fn target_class_toggles(&mut self) -> Vec<Allocations> {
        let target = self.target;
        self.measure(|document| document.toggle(target).to_vec())
    }
}

fn in_style(allocations: &[Allocations]) -> Vec<u64> {
    allocations.iter().map(|allocations| allocations.in_style).collect()
}

fn everywhere(allocations: &[Allocations]) -> Vec<u64> {
    allocations.iter().map(|allocations| allocations.everywhere).collect()
}

fn assert_at_most(counts: Vec<u64>, bound: u64, what: &str) {
    assert!(
        counts.iter().all(|&count| count <= bound),
        "{what} allocate {counts:?} times, more than {bound}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_empty_transaction_allocates_nothing_in_style() {
    let allocations = Document::warm().empty_transactions();
    assert_at_most(in_style(&allocations), 0, "empty transactions");
}

#[test]
fn a_class_no_selector_names_allocates_nothing_in_style() {
    let allocations = Document::warm().unnamed_class_toggles();
    assert_at_most(in_style(&allocations), 0, "toggles of a class no selector names");
}

#[test]
fn a_class_one_selector_names_on_a_leaf_allocates_at_most_as_today() {
    let allocations = Document::warm().target_class_toggles();
    assert_at_most(
        in_style(&allocations),
        91 + MUTEX_ALLOCATIONS_RESTYLING_ONE_ELEMENT,
        "toggles of a class one selector names",
    );
    // FIXME: Lower this as the allocations an empty transaction makes outside
    //        the engine go away.
    assert_at_most(
        everywhere(&allocations),
        114 + MUTEX_ALLOCATIONS_RESTYLING_ONE_ELEMENT,
        "toggles of a class one selector names",
    );
}

/// What taking an element out of a list allocates in style, under `depth` ancestors, where the only
/// selector reading siblings tests nothing of the element or of the ancestors.
fn allocations_of_an_element_leaving_at_depth(depth: usize) -> Vec<u64> {
    let mut engine = hosted_engine();
    let nodes = allocate_nodes(&mut engine, depth + 2 + WARMUP_ROUNDS + MEASURED_ROUNDS);
    let (ancestors, others) = nodes.split_at(depth + 1);
    let (kept, leaving) = others.split_first().expect("the document holds the element kept");
    let (root, parent, kept) = (ancestors[0], ancestors[depth], *kept);
    engine.record_tree_delta(root, None, Some(relations(None, None, None)));
    for pair in ancestors.windows(2) {
        engine.record_tree_delta(pair[1], None, Some(relations(Some(pair[0]), None, None)));
    }
    engine.record_tree_delta(kept, None, Some(relations(Some(parent), None, None)));
    engine.set_element_adjustment_facts(root, element_adjustment_fact::IS_DOCUMENT_ELEMENT);
    for &node in ancestors.iter().chain([&kept]) {
        set_tag(&mut engine, node, "div");
    }
    for &node in ancestors {
        add_class(&mut engine, node, "ancestor");
        add_class(&mut engine, node, "other-ancestor");
    }
    add_class(&mut engine, kept, "y");
    let sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
    add_rules(&mut engine, sheet, ".x ~ .y { width: 10px; }");
    start_live(&mut engine, root);

    let in_the_list = relations(Some(parent), None, Some(kept));
    let allocations: Vec<u64> = leaving
        .iter()
        .map(|&node| {
            engine.record_tree_delta(node, None, Some(in_the_list));
            set_tag(&mut engine, node, "div");
            add_class(&mut engine, node, "leaving");
            run_style_update(&mut engine, root);
            engine.record_tree_delta(node, Some(in_the_list), None);
            count_allocations(|| run_style_update(&mut engine, root)).1.in_style
        })
        .collect();
    allocations[WARMUP_ROUNDS..].to_vec()
}

#[test]
fn an_element_leaving_reads_no_ancestors_where_no_selector_asks() {
    assert_eq!(
        allocations_of_an_element_leaving_at_depth(64),
        allocations_of_an_element_leaving_at_depth(2)
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_class_flip_of_a_rule_that_loses_computes_nothing() {
    let (mut engine, nodes) = linear_document();
    let sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
    add_rules(
        &mut engine,
        sheet,
        ".loser { color: rgb(2, 2, 2); } .winner { color: rgb(1, 1, 1); }",
    );
    add_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "winner");
    start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
    // The host holds the styles the engine installed as it took the document. A flip that leaves the element's record
    // as it was then installs nothing.
    let mut installation = engine.take_installation();
    installation.note_held_by_the_host(&mut engine.retained);
    for record in installation.pinned_records {
        engine.unpin_layout_style_record(record);
    }
    let (root, element) = (nodes[0], nodes[1]);
    let mut round = || {
        add_class(&mut engine, element, "loser");
        let (_, added) = count_allocations(|| run_style_update(&mut engine, root));
        remove_class(&mut engine, element, "loser");
        let (_, removed) = count_allocations(|| run_style_update(&mut engine, root));
        [added, removed]
    };
    for _ in 0..WARMUP_ROUNDS {
        round();
    }
    let allocations: Vec<Allocations> = (0..MEASURED_ROUNDS).flat_map(|_| round()).collect();
    // NB: Computing the record again allocates about twice this.
    assert_at_most(
        in_style(&allocations),
        20 + MUTEX_ALLOCATIONS_RESTYLING_ONE_ELEMENT,
        "flips of a rule that loses",
    );
}

/*

//! The ancestor Bloom filter: a counting filter over the ids, classes and tag names of the elements
//! above the one being matched, maintained as the traversal descends and climbs. A selector whose
//! combinator chain requires an ancestor key the filter lacks cannot match, so its ancestor walk is
//! never run.

use super::super::*;
use crate::css::selector_arena::IdOrClass;
use smallvec::SmallVec;

const KEY_BITS: u32 = 12;
const SLOT_COUNT: usize = 1 << KEY_BITS;
const KEY_MASK: u32 = (1 << KEY_BITS) - 1;

/// The most ancestor keys one selector checks against the filter. More would cost more probes than
/// the rejections they add.
const MAX_REQUIRED_HASHES: usize = 4;

/// The bits of a hash, all of which the filters read.
const HASH_BITS: u32 = 2 * KEY_BITS;
const HASH_MASK: u32 = (1 << HASH_BITS) - 1;

/// A filter hash of `HASH_BITS` bits, never zero, so that zero can stand for no hash.
fn hash_of(kind: u32, atom: StyleAtomID) -> u32 {
    let mixed = (u64::from(atom.0) | (u64::from(kind) << 32)).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
    ((mixed >> 32) as u32 & HASH_MASK).max(1)
}

pub(super) fn id_hash(atom: StyleAtomID) -> u32 {
    hash_of(1, atom)
}

pub(super) fn class_hash(atom: StyleAtomID) -> u32 {
    hash_of(2, atom)
}

pub(super) fn tag_hash(atom: StyleAtomID) -> u32 {
    hash_of(3, atom)
}

pub(super) fn attribute_hash(atom: StyleAtomID) -> u32 {
    hash_of(4, atom)
}

/// The ancestor keys a selector entry requires, as filter hashes, in a fixed number of slots so a
/// rule bucket holds them inline: three in the low bits of the words, and the fourth spread over
/// their high bytes. An unused slot is zero.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub(super) struct AncestorHashes {
    packed: [u32; 3],
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<AncestorHashes>() == 12);
const _: () = assert!(HASH_BITS == 24 && MAX_REQUIRED_HASHES == 4);

impl AncestorHashes {
    /// The keys every ancestor compound reached through `A B` and `A > B` from `compound`
    /// necessarily carries, past `A + B` and `A ~ B` too, since siblings share their ancestors.
    /// Only features standing directly in such a compound count, and those of the one selector of
    /// a `:is()`, `:where()` or `&` holding a single one: anything under a negation, a disjunction or
    /// a relative query may hold elsewhere or not at all. Only names written in ASCII lowercase
    /// count, which every document carries as written, and attribute names only where no namespace
    /// is named.
    pub(super) fn required_left_of(compound: crate::css::selector::Selector<'_>) -> Self {
        let mut hashes: SmallVec<[u32; MAX_REQUIRED_HASHES]> = SmallVec::new();
        collect_ancestor_hashes(compound, false, &mut hashes);
        let slot = |index: usize| hashes.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(0);
        let fourth = slot(3);
        Self {
            packed: std::array::from_fn(|index| slot(index) | ((fourth >> (8 * index)) & 0xFF) << HASH_BITS),
        }
    }

    /// Whether no key is required of the ancestors.
    pub(super) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.hashes().next().is_none()
    }

    /// The words the hashes are packed in, for a holder to keep those not zero.
    pub(super) fn packed_words(&self) -> [u32; 3] {
        self.packed
    }

    pub(super) fn from_packed_words(packed: [u32; 3]) -> Self {
        Self { packed }
    }

    /// The hashes, without the unused slots.
    fn hashes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = u32> {
        let [first, second, third] = self.packed;
        let fourth = (first >> HASH_BITS) | (second >> HASH_BITS) << 8 | (third >> HASH_BITS) << 16;
        [first & HASH_MASK, second & HASH_MASK, third & HASH_MASK, fourth]
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|&hash| hash != 0)
    }
}

/// Add the keys of the compounds of `selector` an ancestor of its subject matches to `hashes`, from
/// the compound left of the subject's, or from the subject's own where `from_subject`, as for the
/// one selector of a `:is()` standing in a compound an ancestor matches.
fn collect_ancestor_hashes(
    selector: crate::css::selector::Selector<'_>,
    from_subject: bool,
    hashes: &mut SmallVec<[u32; MAX_REQUIRED_HASHES]>,
) {
    use crate::css::selector::Combinator;
    let mut current = selector;
    let mut collects = from_subject;
    loop {
        if collects && !collect_compound_hashes(current, hashes) {
            return;
        }
        let Some((combinator, left)) = current.left() else {
            return;
        };
        current = left;
        collects = match combinator {
            Combinator::Descendant | Combinator::ImmediateChild => true,
            // A sibling's own keys say nothing of the subject's ancestors.
            Combinator::NextSibling | Combinator::SubsequentSibling => false,
            _ => return,
        };
    }
}

/// Add the keys of the first compound of `compound`, one an ancestor matches, to `hashes`, or
/// answer false where the walk goes no further: the compound names the host, which stands above a
/// shadow tree's elements in no tree the filter walks.
fn collect_compound_hashes(
    compound: crate::css::selector::Selector<'_>,
    hashes: &mut SmallVec<[u32; MAX_REQUIRED_HASHES]>,
) -> bool {
    use crate::css::selector::{NamespaceType, PseudoClassType, SimpleSelector};
    use crate::css::selector_arena::Nesting;
    let simple_selectors = compound.first_compound().simple_selectors;
    if simple_selectors.iter().any(|simple| {
        super::super::component_matching::mentions(&simple, &|simple| {
            matches!(simple, SimpleSelector::PseudoClass(pseudo_class) if pseudo_class.pseudo_class == PseudoClassType::Host)
        })
    }) {
        return false;
    }
    let push = |hash: u32, hashes: &mut SmallVec<[u32; MAX_REQUIRED_HASHES]>| {
        if hashes.len() < MAX_REQUIRED_HASHES && !hashes.contains(&hash) {
            hashes.push(hash);
        }
    };
    for simple in simple_selectors.iter() {
        let nested = match &simple {
            SimpleSelector::Id(name) if name.is_ascii_lowercase => {
                push(id_hash(name.name), hashes);
                None
            }
            SimpleSelector::Class(name) if name.is_ascii_lowercase => {
                push(class_hash(name.name), hashes);
                None
            }
            SimpleSelector::TagName(name) if name.name_is_ascii_lowercase => {
                push(tag_hash(name.name), hashes);
                None
            }
            SimpleSelector::Attribute(attribute)
                if attribute.qualified_name.name_is_ascii_lowercase
                    && !matches!(
                        attribute.qualified_name.namespace_type,
                        NamespaceType::Named | NamespaceType::Any
                    ) =>
            {
                push(attribute_hash(attribute.qualified_name.name), hashes);
                None
            }
            SimpleSelector::PseudoClass(pseudo_class)
                if matches!(pseudo_class.pseudo_class, PseudoClassType::Is | PseudoClassType::Where) =>
            {
                pseudo_class.argument_selector_list.single()
            }
            SimpleSelector::Nesting(Nesting::Rule(parent)) => parent.single(),
            _ => None,
        };
        // NB: The one selector of a `:is()` describes the element its compound does, from its own
        //     subject leftwards.
        if let Some(nested) = nested {
            collect_ancestor_hashes(nested, true, hashes);
        }
    }
    true
}

/// A counting Bloom filter of the keys of the current element's ancestors.
pub(super) struct AncestorFilter {
    counters: Box<[u8; SLOT_COUNT]>,
}

impl AncestorFilter {
    /// The bytes the filter holds on the heap.
    pub(super) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        size_of_val(&*self.counters)
    }

    pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            counters: Box::new([0; SLOT_COUNT]),
        }
    }

    fn slots(hash: u32) -> (usize, usize) {
        ((hash & KEY_MASK) as usize, ((hash >> KEY_BITS) & KEY_MASK) as usize)
    }

    /// Hold every key, rejecting nothing.
    pub(super) fn fill(&mut self) {
        self.counters.fill(u8::MAX);
    }

    pub(super) fn insert(&mut self, hash: u32) {
        let (first, second) = Self::slots(hash);
        self.counters[first] = self.counters[first].saturating_add(1);
        self.counters[second] = self.counters[second].saturating_add(1);
    }

    /// Removes a hash inserted before. A saturated counter stays saturated, which only costs the
    /// filter some rejections.
    pub(super) fn remove(&mut self, hash: u32) {
        let (first, second) = Self::slots(hash);
        for slot in [first, second] {
            if self.counters[slot] != u8::MAX {
                self.counters[slot] -= 1;
            }
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn might_contain_all(&self, hashes: &AncestorHashes) -> bool {
        hashes.hashes().all(|hash| {
            let (first, second) = Self::slots(hash);
            self.counters[first] != 0 && self.counters[second] != 0
        })
    }
}

/// A Bloom filter of the keys of the earlier siblings of the element being matched, which a
/// subsequent-sibling combinator rejects on as a descendant combinator does on the ancestor filter.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub(super) struct SiblingFilter {
    bits: [u64; 4],
}

impl SiblingFilter {
    fn bits_of(hash: u32) -> [(usize, u64); 2] {
        [hash & 0xff, (hash >> 8) & 0xff].map(|bit| ((bit / 64) as usize, 1_u64 << (bit % 64)))
    }

    /// Hold every key, rejecting nothing.
    pub(super) fn fill(&mut self) {
        self.bits = [u64::MAX; 4];
    }

    pub(super) fn insert(&mut self, hash: u32) {
        for (word, bit) in Self::bits_of(hash) {
            self.bits[word] |= bit;
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn might_contain(&self, hash: u32) -> bool {
        Self::bits_of(hash)
            .iter()
            .all(|&(word, bit)| self.bits[word] & bit != 0)
    }
}

/// The filter hash of a key every element the compound left of the subject of `selector` matches carries, where the
/// subject is right of `~`: what the filter of an element's earlier siblings rejects the selector on. Only names
/// written in ASCII lowercase count, which every document carries as written.
pub(super) fn earlier_sibling_key(selector: crate::css::selector::Selector<'_>) -> Option<u32> {
    let (combinator, left) = selector.left()?;
    if combinator != crate::css::selector::Combinator::SubsequentSibling || left.is_relative_anchor() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut id = None;
    for name in left.ids_and_classes() {
        match name {
            IdOrClass::Class(class) if class.is_ascii_lowercase => return Some(class_hash(class.name)),
            IdOrClass::Id(name) if name.is_ascii_lowercase => id = id.or(Some(id_hash(name.name))),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    id
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn required_hash_count(text: &str) -> usize {
        let parsed = crate::css::selector_parser::parse_selector_list(
            &text.encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<u16>>()[..],
            &[],
            crate::css::selector_parser::SelectorType::Standalone,
            crate::css::selector_parser::SelectorParsingMode::Standard,
        )
        .expect("a test writes valid selectors");
        let selectors = crate::css::selector::SelectorListRef::pack(&parsed.selectors);
        let selector = selectors.iter().next().expect("a test writes a selector");
        AncestorHashes::required_left_of(selector).hashes().count()
    }

    #[test]
    fn ancestors_are_required_to_carry_attribute_names_and_the_keys_of_a_lone_is() {
        for (selector, count) in [
            ("[data-x] .a", 1),
            ("[data-X] .a", 0),
            ("[*|data-x] .a", 0),
            (".p > [data-x=y] .a", 2),
            (":is(.p .q) .a", 2),
            (":where(.p) > .a", 1),
            (":is(.p, .q) .a", 0),
            (":not(.p) .a", 0),
            (".p :is(.q + .r) .a", 2),
            (".s + .a", 0),
            (":is(.p) .a:is(.q .r)", 1),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(required_hash_count(selector), count, "{selector}");
        }
    }
}

/*

//! The cascade of one element: its matched rules and its own declaration blocks, ordered by cascade
//! priority, with the first declaration of each longhand in that order winning.

use super::super::animations::DeclarationScope;
use super::super::*;
use super::matching::ElementMatch;
use super::rules::RuleIndex;
use crate::css::computed_longhand_table::LONGHAND_COUNT;
use crate::css::property_metadata::property_id::ANIMATION_NAME;
use crate::css::property_metadata::{FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID, LAST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID};
use crate::css::selector::Specificity;
use smallvec::SmallVec;

const LONGHAND_WORDS: usize = LONGHAND_COUNT.div_ceil(64);

/// The own declarations of an element no rule reaches and no style node holds the declarations
/// of, such as one outside the document, with the facts its style adjusts by. Its cascade and
/// computation take them in place of those of the node they are keyed by.
pub(in crate::css::style) struct DeclaredOnly {
    pub(in crate::css::style) declarations: super::super::element_declarations::ElementDeclarationRow,
    pub(in crate::css::style) facts: u32,
}

/// The declaration that won one longhand.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Eq, Hash, PartialEq)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct Winner {
    pub(super) property: u16,
    pub(super) important: bool,
    /// The block holding the declaration.
    pub(super) source: WinnerSource,
    /// The declaration's index in the block.
    pub(super) index: usize,
}

/// What the cascades of a pass decided.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct CascadeCounters {
    pub(super) winners: u64,
}

impl CascadeCounters {
    pub(super) fn add(&mut self, other: &Self) {
        self.winners += other.winners;
    }
}

/// How many blocks an element's cascade sorts into cascade order and walks, taking the first
/// declaration of each longhand. Beyond that many, it offers them in any order instead, keeping
/// the best declaration of each longhand, which saves sorting them all.
const ORDERED_BLOCKS: usize = 16;

/// The declarations of one block, with its custom property declarations and their written values.
type BlockDeclarations<'a> = (
    &'a [DeclarationEntry],
    Option<(&'a [CustomDeclaration], &'a [RetainedStyleValueData])>,
);

/// The best declaration of one longhand so far, in a cascade offered blocks in any order.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Candidate {
    priority: CascadePriority,
    important: bool,
    source: WinnerSource,
    index: usize,
    /// The rule index entry the declaration's block is of, or `u32::MAX` for an element's own.
    entry: u32,
    /// The tree scope the block's rule decides from, as its match says.
    scope: TreeScopeID,
}

/// A declaration of `revert` or `revert-layer`, by the priority of its block.
type Reverting = (CascadePriority, CascadeOperator);

/// Whether one of the declarations `reverted` rolls back past a declaration at `priority`.
fn rolled_back(reverted: &[Reverting], priority: &CascadePriority) -> bool {
    reverted
        .iter()
        .any(|(reverting, operator)| reverting.reverts_past(*operator, priority))
}

/// Whether a declaration of `operator` rolls the cascade back.
fn is_revert(operator: CascadeOperator) -> bool {
    matches!(operator, CascadeOperator::Revert | CascadeOperator::RevertLayer)
}

/// The best declaration of one custom property so far, in a cascade offered blocks in any order.
struct CustomCandidate {
    priority: CascadePriority,
    declaration: CustomDeclaration,
    written: RetainedStyleValueData,
}

/// Reusable scratch for cascading one element after another.
pub(super) struct Cascade {
    /// Each block with the rule index entry it is of, or `u32::MAX` for an element's own, and the
    /// tree scope its rule decides from.
    blocks: Vec<(CascadePriority, WinnerSource, bool, u32, TreeScopeID)>,
    decided: [u64; LONGHAND_WORDS],
    /// The best declaration of each longhand offered, by longhand, where `decided` says one was:
    /// the others are never written, so a cascade touches only the room of the longhands offered.
    best: Box<[std::mem::MaybeUninit<Candidate>]>,
    /// The longhands with a declaration offered, in the order they were first.
    offered: Vec<u16>,
    custom_candidates: Vec<CustomCandidate>,
    /// The declaration that won each decided longhand, highest priority first.
    pub(super) winners: Vec<Winner>,
    /// The custom property declaration that won each name, highest priority first, with the
    /// value it was written with.
    pub(super) custom_winners: Vec<(CustomDeclaration, RetainedStyleValueData)>,
    decided_names: Vec<StyleAtomID>,
    /// Each declaration of `revert` or `revert-layer` the ordered cascade met for a custom
    /// property it had not decided, with the name.
    reverting_names: Vec<(StyleAtomID, Reverting)>,
    /// The pseudo-element kind an element backing one of its shadow host's pseudo-elements stands
    /// for, which takes from the host's rules only the properties that pseudo-element supports, or
    /// `u8::MAX`.
    backed_kind: u8,
    /// The pseudo-element kind the last cascade was for, which takes from the rules only the
    /// properties that pseudo-element supports, or `u8::MAX` for the element itself.
    pseudo_kind: u8,
    /// The scope the winning `animation-name` was declared in, where the `@keyframes` it names
    /// are looked for first.
    pub(super) animation_name_scope: DeclarationScope,
    pub(super) statistics: CascadeCounters,
    /// The declarations a cascade of an element's own declarations alone takes in place of its
    /// node's.
    declared_only: Option<Box<DeclaredOnly>>,
}

impl Cascade {
    /// The best declaration of the longhand in `slot` offered so far, which `decided` says there is.
    fn best(&self, slot: usize) -> &Candidate {
        assert!(
            self.decided[slot / 64] & (1 << (slot % 64)) != 0,
            "a longhand's best declaration is read once one was offered"
        );
        // SAFETY: A longhand is decided once its best declaration is written, and a cascade clears
        //         every decided longhand before it starts.
        unsafe { self.best[slot].assume_init_ref() }
    }

    pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            blocks: Vec::new(),
            decided: [0; LONGHAND_WORDS],
            best: Box::new_uninit_slice(LONGHAND_COUNT),
            offered: Vec::new(),
            custom_candidates: Vec::new(),
            winners: Vec::new(),
            custom_winners: Vec::new(),
            decided_names: Vec::new(),
            reverting_names: Vec::new(),
            backed_kind: u8::MAX,
            pseudo_kind: u8::MAX,
            animation_name_scope: DeclarationScope::Unscoped,
            statistics: CascadeCounters::default(),
            declared_only: None,
        }
    }

    /// The cascade of `declared` alone, the own declarations of an element no rule reaches, keyed
    /// by `node`, which holds no declarations of its own.
    pub(super) fn of_declared_only(
        state: &RetainedState,
        index: &RuleIndex,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        declared: DeclaredOnly,
    ) -> Self {
        let mut cascade = Self::new();
        cascade.declared_only = Some(Box::new(declared));
        cascade.cascade(
            state,
            index,
            node,
            &[],
            super::PseudoElementTarget::of_kind(super::rules::ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND),
        );
        cascade
    }

    /// The declarations the cascade takes in place of its node's, where it is of an element's own
    /// declarations alone.
    pub(super) fn declared_only(&self) -> Option<&DeclaredOnly> {
        self.declared_only.as_deref()
    }

    /// Cascade the element's non-pseudo-element matches and element declarations into `winners`.
    pub(super) fn cascade_element(
        &mut self,
        state: &RetainedState,
        index: &RuleIndex,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        matches: &[ElementMatch],
    ) {
        self.backed_kind = u8::MAX;
        self.cascade(
            state,
            index,
            node,
            matches,
            super::PseudoElementTarget::of_kind(super::rules::ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND),
        );
    }

    /// Cascade an element standing for its shadow host's pseudo-element of `kind`, such as the
    /// element a `::placeholder` is: the host's matches for that pseudo-element, of which it takes
    /// only the properties the pseudo-element supports, with the element's own declarations.
    pub(super) fn cascade_backing_element(
        &mut self,
        state: &RetainedState,
        index: &RuleIndex,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        host_matches: &[ElementMatch],
        kind: u8,
    ) {
        self.backed_kind = kind;
        self.cascade(
            state,
            index,
            node,
            host_matches,
            super::PseudoElementTarget::of_kind(kind),
        );
    }

    /// Whether a declaration of `property` by `source` takes part in the cascade: a rule's for a
    /// pseudo-element where the pseudo-element supports the property.
    fn takes(&self, source: WinnerSource, property: u16) -> bool {
        self.pseudo_kind == u8::MAX
            || !matches!(source, WinnerSource::Rule(_))
            || crate::css::property_metadata::pseudo_element_supports_property(self.pseudo_kind, property)
    }

    /// Cascade the element's matches for its pseudo-element `target` into `winners`, as
    /// [`Self::cascade_element`] does for the element: the element's own declarations style the
    /// element alone.
    pub(super) fn cascade_pseudo_element(
        &mut self,
        state: &RetainedState,
        index: &RuleIndex,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        matches: &[ElementMatch],
        target: super::PseudoElementTarget,
    ) {
        self.backed_kind = u8::MAX;
        self.cascade(state, index, node, matches, target);
    }

    fn cascade(
        &mut self,
        state: &RetainedState,
        index: &RuleIndex,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        matches: &[ElementMatch],
        target: super::PseudoElementTarget,
    ) {
        let pseudo_kind = target.kind;
        self.pseudo_kind = pseudo_kind;
        self.decided = [0; LONGHAND_WORDS];
        self.winners.clear();
        self.custom_winners.clear();
        self.decided_names.clear();
        self.reverting_names.clear();
        self.blocks.clear();
        self.animation_name_scope = DeclarationScope::Unscoped;

        // Matches are in index order, so a rule's entries for one target are adjacent among the
        // target's; its greatest specificity decides for the rule.
        let mut targeted = matches
            .iter()
            .filter(|matched| matched.styles(index, target))
            .peekable();
        while let Some(first) = targeted.next() {
            let mut specificity: Specificity = first.specificity;
            let mut scope_proximity = first.scope_proximity;
            // A rule matched from several of the element's encapsulation contexts decides from each.
            while let Some(next) = targeted.next_if(|next| next.rule == first.rule && next.scope == first.scope) {
                specificity = specificity.max(next.specificity);
                scope_proximity = scope_proximity.min(next.scope_proximity);
            }
            // NB: The entry is read in place, from the segment holding it where it is a bound one.
            let entry = index.entries.view(first.entry as usize);
            let placement = index.entries.placement_of(entry);
            for important in [false, true] {
                if important && !entry.declares_important() {
                    continue;
                }
                let priority = CascadePriority::new(PriorityInputs {
                    origin: placement.origin,
                    important,
                    context_depth: first.context_depth,
                    element_attachment: ElementAttachment::Rule,
                    layer_rank: placement.layer_rank,
                    specificity,
                    scope_proximity,
                    sheet_rank: placement.sheet_rank,
                    rule_rank: entry.rule_rank(),
                });
                self.blocks.push((
                    priority,
                    WinnerSource::Rule(first.rule),
                    important,
                    first.entry,
                    first.scope,
                ));
            }
        }
        let own = self.declared_only.as_deref();
        let element_declares_custom_properties = custom_declarations_of(
            state,
            index,
            own,
            node,
            WinnerSource::Element(ElementDeclarationKind::InlineStyle),
            u32::MAX,
        )
        .is_some_and(|(declared, _)| !declared.is_empty());
        // An element's own declarations style the element alone, which is what an element backing
        // its host's pseudo-element is.
        for kind in ElementDeclarationKind::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|_| pseudo_kind == u8::MAX || self.backed_kind != u8::MAX)
        {
            let declares_custom_properties =
                kind == ElementDeclarationKind::InlineStyle && element_declares_custom_properties;
            if block_declarations(state, own, node, WinnerSource::Element(kind)).is_empty()
                && !declares_custom_properties
            {
                continue;
            }
            for important in [false, true] {
                let priority = state.element_cascade_priority(node, kind, important);
                self.blocks.push((
                    priority,
                    WinnerSource::Element(kind),
                    important,
                    u32::MAX,
                    TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT,
                ));
            }
        }
        if self.blocks.len() > ORDERED_BLOCKS {
            self.cascade_unordered(state, index, node);
            return;
        }
        self.blocks.sort_unstable_by_key(|block| std::cmp::Reverse(block.0));
        let entries = &index.entries;

        for &(priority, source, important, entry, scope) in &self.blocks {
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-variables-2/#defining-variables
            // A custom property cascades by its name, the way a longhand does.
            if let Some((declared, written)) =
                custom_declarations_of(state, index, self.declared_only.as_deref(), node, source, entry)
            {
                for (declaration, written) in declared.iter().zip(written) {
                    if declaration.important() != important
                        || self.decided_names.contains(&declaration.name)
                        || self.reverting_names.iter().any(|(name, (reverting, operator))| {
                            *name == declaration.name && reverting.reverts_past(*operator, &priority)
                        })
                    {
                        continue;
                    }
                    match declaration.operator() {
                        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-5/#default
                        // `revert` and `revert-layer` roll the cascaded value back to what lower
                        // declarations they do not roll back past cascade to.
                        operator @ (CascadeOperator::Revert | CascadeOperator::RevertLayer) => {
                            self.reverting_names.push((declaration.name, (priority, operator)));
                        }
                        CascadeOperator::Declared => {
                            self.decided_names.push(declaration.name);
                            self.custom_winners.push((*declaration, written.clone()));
                        }
                        // A registered name's CSS-wide keywords take its registration's initial value, or
                        // the parent's value of one that does not inherit, which the store resolves
                        // from the keyword written.
                        CascadeOperator::Inherit | CascadeOperator::Unset | CascadeOperator::Initial
                            if state.custom_property_name_is_registered(declaration.name) =>
                        {
                            self.decided_names.push(declaration.name);
                            self.custom_winners.push((*declaration, written.clone()));
                        }
                        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-variables-2/#defining-variables
                        // Custom properties are inherited, so these keep the inherited value.
                        CascadeOperator::Inherit | CascadeOperator::Unset => self.decided_names.push(declaration.name),
                        // The initial value of a custom property is the guaranteed-invalid value.
                        CascadeOperator::Initial => {
                            self.decided_names.push(declaration.name);
                            self.custom_winners.push((
                                *declaration,
                                RetainedStyleValueData::from_owned(
                                    crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData::GuaranteedInvalid,
                                ),
                            ));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            let declarations = block_declarations(state, self.declared_only.as_deref(), node, source);
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-5/#cascade-order
            // Within a block, the last declaration in document order wins. The winners keep that
            // order, which is how the computation pairs a logical longhand with its physical
            // counterpart: of the two, the one declared with higher priority decides both.
            for (index, declaration) in declarations.iter().enumerate().rev() {
                if declaration.important() != important {
                    continue;
                }
                // A shorthand declared whole waits on substitution, and its longhands are declared
                // beside it, each pending the shorthand's value.
                if !(FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID..=LAST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID).contains(&declaration.property()) {
                    continue;
                }
                if !self.takes(source, declaration.property()) {
                    continue;
                }
                let slot = usize::from(declaration.property() - FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID);
                let (word, bit) = (slot / 64, 1_u64 << (slot % 64));
                if self.decided[word] & bit != 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                self.decided[word] |= bit;
                if declaration.property() == ANIMATION_NAME {
                    self.animation_name_scope = declaration_scope(entries, entry, scope);
                }
                self.winners.push(Winner {
                    property: declaration.property(),
                    important: declaration.important(),
                    source,
                    index,
                });
            }
        }
        self.statistics.winners += self.winners.len() as u64;
    }

    /// Cascade the blocks gathered in any order, keeping the best declaration of each longhand and
    /// custom property name.
    #[inline(never)]
    fn cascade_unordered(&mut self, state: &RetainedState, index: &RuleIndex, node: StyleNodeID) {
        self.offered.clear();
        self.custom_candidates.clear();
        for block in 0..self.blocks.len() {
            let (priority, source, important, entry, scope) = self.blocks[block];
            let (declarations, custom): BlockDeclarations<'_> = (
                block_declarations(state, self.declared_only.as_deref(), node, source),
                custom_declarations_of(state, index, self.declared_only.as_deref(), node, source, entry),
            );
            for (index, declaration) in declarations.iter().enumerate() {
                if declaration.important() != important {
                    continue;
                }
                if !(FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID..=LAST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID).contains(&declaration.property())
                    || !self.takes(source, declaration.property())
                {
                    continue;
                }
                let slot = usize::from(declaration.property() - FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID);
                let (word, bit) = (slot / 64, 1_u64 << (slot % 64));
                let candidate = Candidate {
                    priority,
                    important,
                    source,
                    index,
                    entry,
                    scope,
                };
                if self.decided[word] & bit == 0 {
                    self.decided[word] |= bit;
                    self.best[slot].write(candidate);
                    self.offered.push(slot as u16);
                    continue;
                }
                let best = self.best(slot);
                if priority > best.priority
                    || (priority == best.priority && source == best.source && index > best.index)
                {
                    self.best[slot].write(candidate);
                }
            }
            let Some((declared, written)) = custom else {
                continue;
            };
            for (declaration, written) in declared.iter().zip(written) {
                if declaration.important() != important {
                    continue;
                }
                match self
                    .custom_candidates
                    .iter_mut()
                    .find(|candidate| candidate.declaration.name == declaration.name)
                {
                    Some(candidate) if priority > candidate.priority => {
                        candidate.priority = priority;
                        candidate.declaration = *declaration;
                        candidate.written = written.clone();
                    }
                    Some(_) => {}
                    None => self.custom_candidates.push(CustomCandidate {
                        priority,
                        declaration: *declaration,
                        written: written.clone(),
                    }),
                }
            }
        }

        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-variables-2/#defining-variables
        // A custom property cascades by its name, the way a longhand does.
        self.custom_candidates
            .sort_unstable_by_key(|candidate| std::cmp::Reverse(candidate.priority));
        for mut candidate in std::mem::take(&mut self.custom_candidates) {
            if is_revert(candidate.declaration.operator()) {
                let mut reverted: SmallVec<[Reverting; 2]> =
                    smallvec::smallvec![(candidate.priority, candidate.declaration.operator())];
                match self.custom_property_below(state, index, node, candidate.declaration.name, &mut reverted) {
                    Some(below) => candidate = below,
                    // Nothing below declares the name, which then inherits.
                    None => continue,
                }
            }
            let declaration = candidate.declaration;
            match declaration.operator() {
                CascadeOperator::Declared => self.custom_winners.push((declaration, candidate.written)),
                // A registered name's CSS-wide keywords take its registration's initial value, or
                // the parent's value of one that does not inherit, which the store resolves from
                // the keyword written.
                CascadeOperator::Inherit | CascadeOperator::Unset | CascadeOperator::Initial
                    if state.custom_property_name_is_registered(declaration.name) =>
                {
                    self.custom_winners.push((declaration, candidate.written));
                }
                // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-variables-2/#defining-variables
                // Custom properties are inherited, so these keep the inherited value.
                CascadeOperator::Inherit | CascadeOperator::Unset => {}
                // The initial value of a custom property is the guaranteed-invalid value.
                CascadeOperator::Initial => self.custom_winners.push((
                    declaration,
                    RetainedStyleValueData::from_owned(crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData::GuaranteedInvalid),
                )),
                CascadeOperator::Revert | CascadeOperator::RevertLayer => {
                    unreachable!("a reverting custom declaration rolls back above")
                }
            }
        }

        let animation_name_slot = usize::from(ANIMATION_NAME - FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID);
        if self.offered.contains(&(animation_name_slot as u16)) {
            let best = self.best(animation_name_slot);
            self.animation_name_scope = declaration_scope(&index.entries, best.entry, best.scope);
        }
        let mut winners: SmallVec<[Candidate; 16]> =
            self.offered.iter().map(|&slot| *self.best(usize::from(slot))).collect();
        // Highest priority first, and a block's later declarations before its earlier ones, as the
        // ordered cascade has them.
        winners.sort_unstable_by(|a, b| b.priority.cmp(&a.priority).then(b.index.cmp(&a.index)));
        self.winners.extend(winners.iter().map(|candidate| {
            let property = match candidate.source {
                WinnerSource::Rule(rule) => state.rules.declared_properties_of(rule)[candidate.index].property(),
                WinnerSource::Element(_) => {
                    block_declarations(state, self.declared_only.as_deref(), node, candidate.source)[candidate.index]
                        .property()
                }
            };
            Winner {
                property,
                important: candidate.important,
                source: candidate.source,
                index: candidate.index,
            }
        }));
        self.statistics.winners += self.winners.len() as u64;
    }

    /// The declaration of `property` or its counterpart the cascade rolls back to below the
    /// declarations of `revert` and `revert-layer` in `reverted`: the highest one they do not roll
    /// back past, where one that reverts in turn joins them. None where nothing below declares
    /// the longhand.
    fn longhand_below(
        &self,
        state: &RetainedState,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        property: u16,
        counterpart: Option<u16>,
        reverted: &mut SmallVec<[Reverting; 2]>,
    ) -> Option<(CascadePriority, Winner)> {
        loop {
            let mut best: Option<(CascadePriority, Winner, CascadeOperator)> = None;
            for &(priority, source, important, _, _) in &self.blocks {
                if best.is_some_and(|(best, ..)| best >= priority)
                    || rolled_back(reverted, &priority)
                    || (!self.takes(source, property) && counterpart.is_none_or(|other| !self.takes(source, other)))
                {
                    continue;
                }
                let declarations = block_declarations(state, self.declared_only.as_deref(), node, source);
                // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical-1/#box
                // "This shared value is determined by cascading the declarations of both properties together as one;"
                if let Some(at) = declarations.iter().rposition(|declaration| {
                    (declaration.property() == property || Some(declaration.property()) == counterpart)
                        && declaration.important() == important
                        && self.takes(source, declaration.property())
                }) {
                    best = Some((
                        priority,
                        Winner {
                            property: declarations[at].property(),
                            important,
                            source,
                            index: at,
                        },
                        declarations[at].operator(),
                    ));
                }
            }
            let (priority, winner, operator) = best?;
            if !is_revert(operator) {
                return Some((priority, winner));
            }
            reverted.push((priority, operator));
        }
    }

    /// What [`Self::longhand_below`] says for the custom property `name`.
    fn custom_property_below(
        &self,
        state: &RetainedState,
        index: &RuleIndex,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        name: StyleAtomID,
        reverted: &mut SmallVec<[Reverting; 2]>,
    ) -> Option<CustomCandidate> {
        loop {
            let mut best: Option<CustomCandidate> = None;
            for &(priority, source, important, entry, _) in &self.blocks {
                if best.as_ref().is_some_and(|best| best.priority >= priority) || rolled_back(reverted, &priority) {
                    continue;
                }
                let Some((declared, written)) =
                    custom_declarations_of(state, index, self.declared_only.as_deref(), node, source, entry)
                else {
                    continue;
                };
                if let Some(at) = declared
                    .iter()
                    .rposition(|declaration| declaration.name == name && declaration.important() == important)
                {
                    best = Some(CustomCandidate {
                        priority,
                        declaration: declared[at],
                        written: written[at].clone(),
                    });
                }
            }
            let best = best?;
            if !is_revert(best.declaration.operator()) {
                return Some(best);
            }
            reverted.push((best.priority, best.declaration.operator()));
        }
    }
}

/// The declarations of one of an element's cascade blocks.
fn block_declarations<'a>(
    state: &'a RetainedState,
    own: Option<&'a DeclaredOnly>,
    node: StyleNodeID,
    source: WinnerSource,
) -> &'a [DeclarationEntry] {
    match (source, own) {
        (WinnerSource::Rule(rule), _) => state.rules.declared_properties_of(rule),
        (WinnerSource::Element(kind), Some(own)) => own.declarations.declarations(kind).declared(),
        (WinnerSource::Element(kind), None) => state.element_declarations.declared_properties(node, kind),
    }
}

/// The custom property declarations of one of an element's cascade blocks, with the values they
/// were written with.
fn custom_declarations_of<'a>(
    state: &'a RetainedState,
    index: &'a RuleIndex,
    own: Option<&'a DeclaredOnly>,
    node: StyleNodeID,
    source: WinnerSource,
    entry: u32,
) -> Option<(&'a [CustomDeclaration], &'a [RetainedStyleValueData])> {
    match source {
        WinnerSource::Rule(_) if !index.entries.view(entry as usize).declares_custom_properties() => None,
        WinnerSource::Rule(rule) => Some((
            state.rules.custom_declarations_of(rule),
            state.rules.custom_written_values_of(rule),
        )),
        WinnerSource::Element(ElementDeclarationKind::InlineStyle) => match own {
            Some(own) => own.declarations.custom(),
            None => state.element_declarations.custom(node),
        }
        .map(|declarations| (declarations.declared(), declarations.written_values())),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// The scope a declaration of the block of the rule index entry `entry`, deciding from the tree
/// scope `scope`, was declared in, or of an element's own block where `entry` is `u32::MAX`: an
/// author rule's is the tree scope of the sheet attachment it decides from, and no other
/// declaration has a scope of its own.
pub(super) fn declaration_scope(
    entries: &super::rules::IndexEntries,
    entry: u32,
    scope: TreeScopeID,
) -> DeclarationScope {
    let Some(view) = entries.try_view(entry as usize) else {
        return DeclarationScope::Unscoped;
    };
    match (entries.placement_of(view).origin, scope) {
        (CascadeOrigin::Author, scope) if scope != TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT => DeclarationScope::Shadow(scope),
        _ => DeclarationScope::Unscoped,
    }
}

/// The last cascade of one element, which a winner of `revert` or `revert-layer`, declared or
/// substituted, rolls back through.
pub(super) struct CascadeBelow<'a> {
    pub(super) cascade: &'a Cascade,
    pub(super) state: &'a RetainedState,
    pub(super) node: StyleNodeID,
}

impl super::compute::CascadeBelow for CascadeBelow<'_> {
    fn priority_of(&self, source: WinnerSource, important: bool) -> CascadePriority {
        self.cascade
            .blocks
            .iter()
            .find(|block| block.1 == source && block.2 == important)
            .expect("a winner's block is in its cascade")
            .0
    }

    fn winner_below(
        &self,
        property: u16,
        counterpart: Option<u16>,
        reverted: &[(CascadePriority, CascadeOperator)],
    ) -> Option<(CascadePriority, Winner)> {
        let mut reverted: SmallVec<[Reverting; 2]> = reverted.into();
        self.cascade
            .longhand_below(self.state, self.node, property, counterpart, &mut reverted)
    }

    fn declared_only(&self) -> Option<&DeclaredOnly> {
        self.cascade.declared_only()
    }
}

//! The engine's computation of one element's style from the winners its cascade decided.

use super::super::process_style::{InitialGroupsInputs, SharedInitialGroups};
use super::super::publication::pseudo_kind;
use super::super::*;
use super::cascade::Winner;
use super::drive::{self, drive_font_metric};
use super::winner_store::{self, WinnerDeclaration, WinnerStore, WinnerValue, shorthand_longhand_data};
use crate::css::computed_longhand_table::FONT_METRICS_DEPEND_ON_VIEWPORT_METRICS;
use crate::css::computed_values::{GroupValueLayout, GroupValues, GroupValuesWriter, StyleGroupMasks};
use crate::css::style::input_types::StyleEnvironment;
use crate::css::style_compute::RootFontReads;
use crate::css::style_value::ShorthandPayload;
use crate::css::style_value::{RetainedStyleValueData, StyleValueData};

/// Root-relative computation reads these inputs independently of its inheritance parent.
/// Bitwise keys keep equality exact without using an invalidation generation as a substitute
/// for the values. The viewport-dependence bit matters even when today's metrics agree.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct RootFontInputs {
    metrics: [u64; 5],
    depends_on_viewport: bool,
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-viewport/#effective-zoom
    /// The bits of the effective zoom of the document element, which the metrics are zoomed by.
    effective_zoom: u64,
}

impl RootFontInputs {
    /// What of these inputs moved from `previous`, as the least a style must read of the root
    /// element's font to resolve its lengths again: a load of a face into the root element's font
    /// moves its metrics alone, which a `rem` does not read.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn moved_from(self, previous: Self) -> RootFontReads {
        if self.metrics[0] != previous.metrics[0]
            || self.depends_on_viewport != previous.depends_on_viewport
            || self.effective_zoom != previous.effective_zoom
        {
            return RootFontReads::FontSize;
        }
        match self == previous {
            true => RootFontReads::None,
            false => RootFontReads::Metrics,
        }
    }

    /// The metrics a `rem` resolves against, and whether they read the viewport.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn font_metrics(self) -> (crate::css::style_compute::FfiFontMetrics, bool) {
        let [font_size, x_height, cap_height, zero_advance, line_height] = self.metrics.map(f64::from_bits);
        (
            crate::css::style_compute::FfiFontMetrics {
                font_size,
                x_height,
                cap_height,
                zero_advance,
                line_height,
            },
            self.depends_on_viewport,
        )
    }

    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-viewport/#effective-zoom
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn effective_zoom(self) -> f64 {
        f64::from_bits(self.effective_zoom)
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn apply_to(self, inputs: &mut bridge::FfiDocumentStyleComputationInputs) {
        inputs.root_font_size = f64::from_bits(self.metrics[0]);
        inputs.root_font_x_height = f64::from_bits(self.metrics[1]);
        inputs.root_font_cap_height = f64::from_bits(self.metrics[2]);
        inputs.root_font_zero_advance = f64::from_bits(self.metrics[3]);
        inputs.root_line_height = f64::from_bits(self.metrics[4]);
        inputs.root_font_metrics_depend_on_viewport_metrics = self.depends_on_viewport;
        inputs.root_effective_zoom = f64::from_bits(self.effective_zoom);
    }

    /// The inputs a document element's computed groups and dependency flags give.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn from_payloads(
        payloads: &crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroups,
        dependency_flags: u8,
    ) -> Self {
        use crate::css::table_group_builder::group_index;
        // SAFETY: The payloads are a record's live font group.
        let font = unsafe {
            payloads[group_index::FONT]
                .cast::<crate::css::computed_value_types::FontValues>()
                .deref()
        };
        let first_available = font.first_available_font_metrics();
        Self {
            metrics: [
                font.font_size_for_lengths().to_bits(),
                drive_font_metric(first_available.x_height).to_bits(),
                drive_font_metric(first_available.cap_height).to_bits(),
                drive_font_metric(first_available.zero_advance).to_bits(),
                font.line_height_used().to_double().to_bits(),
            ],
            depends_on_viewport: dependency_flags & FONT_METRICS_DEPEND_ON_VIEWPORT_METRICS != 0,
            effective_zoom: f64::from(payloads.inherited_values().effective_zoom()).to_bits(),
        }
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn from_document(inputs: &bridge::FfiDocumentStyleComputationInputs) -> Self {
        Self {
            metrics: [
                inputs.root_font_size.to_bits(),
                inputs.root_font_x_height.to_bits(),
                inputs.root_font_cap_height.to_bits(),
                inputs.root_font_zero_advance.to_bits(),
                inputs.root_line_height.to_bits(),
            ],
            depends_on_viewport: inputs.root_font_metrics_depend_on_viewport_metrics,
            effective_zoom: inputs.root_effective_zoom.to_bits(),
        }
    }
}

/// What the drive of the initial values waits on, which can only be a font: they have no parent
/// and no declarations.
fn initial_drive_font_request(
    suspended_font: Option<font_resolution::FontRequest>,
) -> Box<font_resolution::FontRequest> {
    Box::new(suspended_font.expect("an unanswered initial drive waits on a font"))
}

fn is_quirk_inherit(property: u16, value: &RetainedStyleValueData) -> bool {
    property == crate::css::property_metadata::property_id::COLOR
        && matches!(
            value.data(),
            StyleValueData::Keyword {
                keyword: crate::css::style_compute::keyword::_LIBWEB_QUIRK_INHERIT
            }
        )
}

impl RetainedState {
    pub(super) fn is_quirks_table(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        self.document_style_computation_inputs.in_quirks_mode
            && self.projection.adjustment_facts(node) & bridge::element_adjustment_fact::IS_TABLE != 0
    }

    // https://quirks.spec.whatwg.org/#the-document%27s-body-element
    // The first HTML body child of the HTML document element supplies the color, wherever the table is.
    pub(super) fn quirks_table_body(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> Option<StyleNodeID> {
        use bridge::element_adjustment_fact as fact;
        let root = std::iter::successors(Some(node), |&node| self.projection.inheritance_parent(node))
            .find(|&node| self.projection.adjustment_facts(node) & fact::IS_DOCUMENT_ELEMENT != 0)?;
        if self.projection.adjustment_facts(root) & fact::IS_HTML_HTML_ELEMENT == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        std::iter::successors(self.projection.first_element_child(root), |&child| {
            self.projection.next_element_sibling(child)
        })
        .find(|&child| self.projection.adjustment_facts(child) & fact::IS_HTML_BODY_ELEMENT != 0)
    }

    /// The engine: the computed initial values, as an element with no declarations and no parent
    /// computes them, with the groups they assemble into, each holding one reference, and the
    /// color they resolve. Every table is seeded from this one, and an element whose
    /// declarations move none of a non-inherited group's longhands shares the initial group. A
    /// drive that waits on a font names the request to refill before trying again.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn initial_style(
        &self,
        root: StyleNodeID,
    ) -> Result<ComputedInitialStyle, Box<font_resolution::FontRequest>> {
        let inputs = InitialGroupsInputs::of(&self.document_style_computation_inputs);
        match self.process_style.initial_groups_of(&inputs) {
            Some(shared) => self.initial_style_over(root, &shared),
            None => self.initial_style_driven(root),
        }
    }

    /// The initial values computed from nothing: every longhand is driven and every group built.
    fn initial_style_driven(
        &self,
        root: StyleNodeID,
    ) -> Result<ComputedInitialStyle, Box<font_resolution::FontRequest>> {
        let subject = DriveSubject {
            target: computed::ComputedStyleTarget::new(root, u8::MAX),
            parent: None,
            facts: 0,
        };
        let store = WinnerStore::new(Vec::new());
        let inputs = self.document_style_computation_inputs;
        let mut suspended_font = None;
        // The initial values compute from nothing: from the default groups, which hold no values.
        crate::css::computed_values::with_default_seed(&self.process_style.default_groups, |seed| {
            let mut writer = GroupValuesWriter::seeded_for_child(
                seed,
                seed,
                std::iter::empty(),
                crate::css::computed_longhand_table::LonghandTableFlags::empty(),
                0,
            );
            match self.engine_drive_with(self, subject, &mut writer, None, &store, &inputs, &mut suspended_font) {
                Some(drive::DrivenValues { length, font }) => {
                    let (values, flags, dependency_flags) = writer.finish(&[]);
                    let source = crate::css::table_group_builder::LonghandSource::Values {
                        values: &values,
                        reads: None,
                    };
                    let color_inputs =
                        crate::css::table_group_builder::assembly_color_inputs_from_source(&source, &length);
                    let mut payloads = [std::ptr::null(); crate::css::table_group_builder::group_index::COUNT];
                    for (group, payload) in payloads.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                        // SAFETY: The values were driven for an element with no parent.
                        *payload = unsafe {
                            crate::css::table_group_builder::assemble_group_from_source(
                                &source,
                                group,
                                Some(&font),
                                crate::css::computed_values::GroupShares::new(
                                    &self.process_style.default_groups,
                                    group,
                                    None,
                                ),
                                color_inputs,
                                &length,
                            )
                        };
                    }
                    // The initial groups hold the initial values, each group in its own allocation.
                    // SAFETY: Each payload is a live payload of its group, whose reference the style takes.
                    unsafe { values.put_into(&mut payloads, 0) };
                    let initial_font = super::traversal::InitialFont {
                        first_available_font: font.first_available_font as usize,
                        font_cascade_list: font.font_cascade_list as usize,
                    };
                    let value_facts = values.facts().clone();
                    Ok(ComputedInitialStyle {
                        payloads,
                        value_groups: Some(values.into_groups()),
                        shared: None,
                        value_facts,
                        flags,
                        dependency_flags,
                        color: color_inputs.1,
                        font: initial_font,
                    })
                }
                None => Err(initial_drive_font_request(suspended_font)),
            }
        })
    }

    /// The initial values another document computed from what this one computes them from, which
    /// `shared` holds: only the font group holds anything of this document, its fonts.
    fn initial_style_over(
        &self,
        root: StyleNodeID,
        shared: &Arc<SharedInitialGroups>,
    ) -> Result<ComputedInitialStyle, Box<font_resolution::FontRequest>> {
        use crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroupIndex;
        use crate::css::table_group_builder::group_index;
        let subject = DriveSubject {
            target: computed::ComputedStyleTarget::new(root, u8::MAX),
            parent: None,
            facts: 0,
        };
        let store = WinnerStore::new(Vec::new());
        let inputs = self.document_style_computation_inputs;
        let mut suspended_font = None;
        let held = shared.values();
        let seed = crate::css::computed_values::GroupSeed::new(shared.seed_groups(), &held.value_facts);
        let mut writer = GroupValuesWriter::seeded_for_child(
            seed,
            seed,
            std::iter::empty(),
            held.flags.clone(),
            held.dependency_flags,
        );
        let selected = [0_u64; crate::css::property_metadata::LONGHAND_WORD_COUNT];
        let Some(drive::DrivenValues { length, font }) = self.engine_drive_with(
            self,
            subject,
            &mut writer,
            Some(&selected),
            &store,
            &inputs,
            &mut suspended_font,
        ) else {
            return Err(initial_drive_font_request(suspended_font));
        };
        let (values, _, _) = writer.finish(&[seed]);
        let source = crate::css::table_group_builder::LonghandSource::Values {
            values: &values,
            reads: None,
        };
        let color_inputs = crate::css::table_group_builder::assembly_color_inputs_from_source(&source, &length);
        let mut payloads = std::array::from_fn(|group| match group == group_index::FONT {
            // SAFETY: The values are those of an element with no parent.
            true => unsafe {
                crate::css::table_group_builder::assemble_group_from_source(
                    &source,
                    group_index::FONT,
                    Some(&font),
                    crate::css::computed_values::GroupShares::new(
                        &self.process_style.default_groups,
                        group_index::FONT,
                        None,
                    ),
                    color_inputs,
                    &length,
                )
            },
            false => shared
                .groups()
                .group(StyleGroupIndex::new(group))
                .held()
                .into_retained(),
        });
        // SAFETY: Each payload is a live payload of its group, whose reference the style takes, and the groups
        //         but the font group hold the values already.
        unsafe { values.put_into(&mut payloads, !(1 << group_index::FONT)) };
        let initial_font = super::traversal::InitialFont {
            first_available_font: font.first_available_font as usize,
            font_cascade_list: font.font_cascade_list as usize,
        };
        let computed = ComputedInitialStyle {
            payloads,
            value_groups: None,
            value_facts: held.value_facts.clone(),
            flags: held.flags.clone(),
            dependency_flags: held.dependency_flags,
            color: held.color,
            font: initial_font,
            shared: None,
        };
        if self.process_style.verifies_reads {
            self.verify_initial_style_over(root, shared, &computed, color_inputs.1);
        }
        Ok(ComputedInitialStyle {
            shared: Some(Arc::clone(shared)),
            ..computed
        })
    }

    /// Check that driving every longhand computes what the shared groups hold for this document.
    fn verify_initial_style_over(
        &self,
        root: StyleNodeID,
        shared: &SharedInitialGroups,
        computed: &ComputedInitialStyle,
        color: u32,
    ) {
        let Ok(driven) = self.initial_style_driven(root) else {
            return;
        };
        // SAFETY: The groups take over the references the drive made.
        let groups = unsafe {
            crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroups::adopt(
                driven.payloads,
                crate::css::computed_value_types::StyleBits::INITIAL,
            )
        };
        assert!(
            shared.hold_the_same_as(&groups)
                && driven.flags == computed.flags
                && driven.dependency_flags == computed.dependency_flags
                && driven.color == color
                && driven.color == computed.color
                && driven.value_facts.publication_equals(&computed.value_facts)
                && driven.font == computed.font,
            "a document's initial values are those of the documents it shares initial groups with"
        );
    }

    /// The engine: compute the record of `node` from the cascade winners it decided, against the
    /// records `records` holds for its ancestors, into a table seeded from `initial` and the
    /// inherited values of the parent's table. A winner the engine computes directly absolutizes
    /// against the element's context; the others go through the longhand drive, which then
    /// evaluates only them and the inputs every drive evaluates. An element whose winners all
    /// compute directly does not run the drive. Only the groups the winners move are assembled
    /// into `payloads`; the others share the parent's payload or the initial one. Each payload
    /// holds one reference the caller releases. A winner is the property it decides, whether it
    /// is important, and where it was declared: its source and its index in the source's block,
    /// highest priority first. Answers the frozen table, the element's resolved current color,
    /// and whether the element ran no drive.
    /// The engine: whether the `content` the pseudo-element of `kind` cascades to lets it generate a
    /// box: `none` generates nothing for every kind, and `normal`, the initial value, nothing for a
    /// `::before` or `::after`.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn pseudo_content_generates(&self, winners: &[Winner], kind: u8) -> bool {
        use crate::css::property_metadata::property_id as prop;
        use crate::css::style_compute::keyword;
        let generated = matches!(kind, pseudo_kind::BEFORE | pseudo_kind::AFTER);
        let Some(&Winner { source, index, .. }) = winners.iter().find(|winner| winner.property == prop::CONTENT) else {
            return !generated;
        };
        let WinnerSource::Rule(rule) = source else {
            return true;
        };
        match self
            .rules
            .written_values_of(rule)
            .get(index)
            .and_then(RetainedStyleValueData::optional_data)
        {
            Some(crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) => {
                *keyword != keyword::NONE && (*keyword != keyword::NORMAL || !generated)
            }
            _ => true,
        }
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, clippy::too_many_lines)]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn drive_element(
        &self,
        records: &impl drive::DriveRecords,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        parent: Option<(StyleNodeID, u32)>,
        initial: &super::traversal::InitialStyle,
        winners: &[Winner],
        cascade: &dyn CascadeBelow,
        suspended_font: &mut Option<font_resolution::FontRequest>,
        random_requests: &mut Vec<super::random_bases::RandomBaseRequest>,
        custom_properties: super::custom_properties::CustomPropertyStores<'_>,
        group_cache: &mut GroupCache,
        absolutized: &mut crate::css::style_compute::AbsolutizedValues,
        target_pseudo_element: super::PseudoElementTarget,
        root_font: Option<RootFontInputs>,
        group_seeds: GroupSeeds<'_>,
        quirks_color: Option<&RetainedStyleValueData>,
    ) -> Option<ComputedElement> {
        use crate::css::property_metadata::{FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID, LONGHAND_WORD_COUNT, property_id as prop};
        use crate::css::style_compute::{
            DIRECTION_COUNT, LOGICAL_ALIAS_BIT, PHYSICAL_TO_LOGICAL_BIT, WRITING_MODE_COUNT,
            map_logical_alias_to_physical, map_physical_to_logical_alias, table_row_bits,
        };
        use crate::css::table_group_builder::group_index;

        // Root-relative lengths resolve against the font of the document element's record as the
        // pass has it, where the pass knows one, rather than the inputs installed before.
        let mut inputs = self.document_style_computation_inputs;
        if let Some(root_font) = root_font {
            root_font.apply_to(&mut inputs);
        }
        let GroupSeeds {
            seeds,
            parent: seeded_parent,
        } = group_seeds;
        let parent_view = match parent {
            Some((parent, _)) => Some(records.assigned_record_view(parent)?),
            None => None,
        };
        let parent_longhands = parent_view.as_ref().map(computed::StyleRecordView::longhands);
        let parent_overlay = parent_view.as_ref().and_then(|view| view.animated_overlay);
        let target_pseudo_kind = target_pseudo_element.kind;
        // A pseudo-element's computation reads only the facts about its element's markup language.
        let is_pseudo_element = target_pseudo_kind != u8::MAX;
        let declared_only = cascade.declared_only();
        let facts = declared_only.map_or_else(|| self.projection.adjustment_facts(node), |own| own.facts);
        let facts = match is_pseudo_element {
            true => facts & PSEUDO_ELEMENT_ADJUSTMENT_FACTS,
            false => facts,
        };

        // Which winners compute directly, with their values, and which need the drive.
        let element_declarations = [
            ElementDeclarationKind::InlineStyle,
            ElementDeclarationKind::PresentationalHint,
            ElementDeclarationKind::SvgPresentationAttribute,
        ]
        .map(|kind| {
            match declared_only {
                Some(own) => Some(own.declarations.declarations(kind)),
                None => self.element_declarations.declarations(node, kind),
            }
            .map(|declarations| (kind, declarations))
        });
        let parent_values = ParentValues {
            longhands: parent_longhands,
            overlay: parent_overlay,
        };
        let parent_value = |property: u16| parent_values.value(property);
        let defaulting = WinnerDefaulting {
            parent: parent_values,
            winners,
            initial,
        };
        // The written values of the declarations live for the pass, so only substituted and
        // defaulted ones are held here.
        let mut easy = smallvec::SmallVec::new();
        let mut hard = smallvec::SmallVec::new();
        let mut native_font = smallvec::SmallVec::new();
        let mut direct_inheritance = smallvec::SmallVec::new();
        let mut substituted = smallvec::SmallVec::new();
        let mut deciding = smallvec::SmallVec::new();
        let mut keyword_aliases = smallvec::SmallVec::new();
        let mut reads = ElementWinnerReads::default();
        let mut decided = DecidedWinners {
            easy: &mut easy,
            hard: &mut hard,
            native_font: &mut native_font,
            direct_inheritance: &mut direct_inheritance,
            substituted: &mut substituted,
            deciding: &mut deciding,
            keyword_aliases: &mut keyword_aliases,
            reads: &mut reads,
        };
        // A winner that needs nothing but its value absolutized against the element's context, with
        // what it computes against known from how it was written, is applied as it is. An element
        // whose every winner is one takes no drive, whatever it declares.
        let takes_no_drive = parent_view.is_some()
            && !pseudo_kind::is_highlight(target_pseudo_kind)
            && parent_longhands.is_some_and(|longhands| longhands.effective_zoom() == 1.0);
        let mut plain_dependencies = takes_no_drive.then_some(0_u32);
        let mut plain_block = None;
        for &Winner {
            property,
            source,
            index,
            ..
        } in winners
        {
            let Some(dependencies) = plain_dependencies else {
                break;
            };
            // NB: A block's winners come one after another.
            if plain_block.is_none_or(|(held, _)| held != source) {
                plain_block = Some((
                    source,
                    match source {
                        WinnerSource::Rule(rule) => {
                            crate::css::style::element_declarations::ElementDeclarations::of_parts(
                                self.rules.declared_properties_of(rule),
                                self.rules.written_values_of(rule),
                                self.rules.written_value_checks_of(rule),
                            )
                        }
                        WinnerSource::Element(kind) => {
