//! Matching one element against the rule index: gather the bucket candidates its keys reach,
//! reject those whose required ancestor keys the filter lacks, and evaluate the rest.

use super::super::component_matching::EntrySelector;
use super::super::input_types::TransactionFactSide;
use super::super::selector_evaluation::StructuralRead;
use super::super::*;
use super::bloom::{AncestorFilter, SiblingFilter};
use super::extent_map::KeyHash;
use super::projection::{ElementFacts, Projection, ProjectionEvaluator};
use super::rules::{BucketSlots, BucketSource, Buckets, RuleIndex, ScopeGroupID, ScopeIndex};
use crate::css::selector::Specificity;
use smallvec::SmallVec;

/// One rule entry matching the element.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub(super) struct ElementMatch {
    /// The entry in the rule index.
    pub(super) entry: u32,
    pub(super) rule: RuleID,
    pub(super) specificity: Specificity,
    pub(super) scope_proximity: u32,
    /// The kind of pseudo-element the entry styles, or `ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND` for the element itself.
    pub(super) pseudo_kind: u8,
    /// Where the encapsulation context the entry's rule decides from stands among the element's,
    /// which its cascade weighs the match by.
    pub(super) context_depth: u32,
    /// The tree scope whose sheets the entry's rule decides from: the document for the document's
    /// sheets, and otherwise the shadow tree the entry reached the element from.
    pub(super) scope: TreeScopeID,
}

impl ElementMatch {
    pub(super) fn styles(&self, index: &RuleIndex, target: super::PseudoElementTarget) -> bool {
        self.pseudo_kind == target.kind
            && (target.kind != super::super::publication::pseudo_kind::HIGHLIGHT
                || index.entry_styles_custom_highlight(self.entry, target.highlight_name))
    }

    /// Whether the entry styles a pseudo-element.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(super) fn pseudo_element(&self) -> bool {
        self.pseudo_kind != super::rules::ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND
    }
}

/// Which of a scope's bucket families an element is matched against.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Family {
    Own,
    OwnRevalidation,
    Host,
    Slotted,
    Part,
}

impl ScopeIndex {
    fn family(&self, family: Family) -> &Buckets {
        match family {
            Family::Own => &self.own,
            Family::OwnRevalidation => &self.own_revalidation,
            Family::Host => &self.host,
            Family::Slotted => &self.slotted,
            Family::Part => &self.part,
        }
    }
}

/// How an element is reached by the entries of one bucket family of a scope.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Reach<'a> {
    scope: TreeScopeID,
    family: Family,
    /// Where the matches of the entries of the scope's own sheets stand among the element's
    /// encapsulation contexts; the document's stand outermost.
    scope_depth: u32,
    /// The filter of the element's ancestors, for the entries of its own tree, whose ancestors it
    /// holds.
    filter: Option<&'a AncestorFilter>,
    /// The tree scope the element is exposed to as a part, for the rules of a `::part()` reaching it.
    part_exposure: Option<TreeScopeID>,
}

/// What a bucket's candidates are rejected or proven on of the element they are offered to.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct ElementKeys {
    /// The dispatch bloom bits of the keys the element carries.
    bloom: u64,
    /// Whether the element's tag is its own ASCII-lowercase form.
    tag_is_lowercase: bool,
}

/// The dispatch bloom bits of the element being matched, or every bit where its ids and classes
/// compare to the selectors' folded, which the bits the selectors carry are not.
fn element_bloom_of(facts: &ElementFacts, is_document_root: bool, folds_ids_and_classes: bool) -> u64 {
    match folds_ids_and_classes {
        true => u64::MAX,
        false => facts.dispatch_bloom(is_document_root),
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct MatchCounters {
    pub(super) candidates: u64,
    pub(super) bloom_rejections: u64,
    pub(super) evaluations: u64,
    pub(super) matches: u64,
    /// The walks of the argument of a `:has()` that answered it for an anchor.
    pub(super) relative_walks: u64,
}

impl MatchCounters {
    pub(super) fn add(&mut self, other: &Self) {
        self.candidates += other.candidates;
        self.bloom_rejections += other.bloom_rejections;
        self.evaluations += other.evaluations;
        self.matches += other.matches;
        self.relative_walks += other.relative_walks;
    }
}

pub(super) struct Matcher<'a> {
    index: &'a RuleIndex,
    /// The buckets elements reach entries of `index` by: its own, or those of a part of it.
    buckets: &'a RuleIndex,
    state: &'a RetainedState,
    evaluator: ProjectionEvaluator<'a>,
    projection: &'a Projection,
    /// The node stamp each entry was last offered under, so an entry in several buckets an element
    /// reaches is evaluated once.
    offered: Vec<u32>,
    stamp: u32,
    /// The filter of the element asked for last, which its candidates ask for one after another.
    last_earlier_siblings: Option<(StyleNodeID, SiblingFilter)>,

    pub(super) statistics: MatchCounters,
}

impl<'a> Matcher<'a> {
    pub(super) fn new(index: &'a RuleIndex, state: &'a RetainedState) -> Self {
        Self::reaching(index, index, state)
    }

    /// A matcher of the entries of `index` that the buckets of `buckets` hold alone.
    pub(super) fn reaching(index: &'a RuleIndex, buckets: &'a RuleIndex, state: &'a RetainedState) -> Self {
        let projection = &state.projection;
        Self {
            index,
            buckets,
            state,
            // NB: A matcher lives for one pass, over which the projection holds still, so its
            //     evaluator keeps the sibling positions and positional answers it finds for the
            //     elements after: a long sibling list costs one walk, not one per element.
            evaluator: projection.evaluator().with_owned_match_workspace(),
            projection,
            offered: vec![0; index.entries.len()],
            stamp: 0,
            last_earlier_siblings: None,

            statistics: MatchCounters::default(),
        }
    }

    /// What the matcher measured, with the walks its evaluator took.
    pub(super) fn counters(&self) -> MatchCounters {
        MatchCounters {
            relative_walks: self.evaluator.relative_walks(),
            ..self.statistics
        }
    }

    /// Append the element's matches to `out`, in index order.
    pub(super) fn match_element(
        &mut self,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        facts: &ElementFacts,
        filter: &AncestorFilter,
        out: &mut Vec<ElementMatch>,
    ) -> Result<(), Incomplete> {
        self.match_in(Family::Own, node, facts, filter, out)
    }

    /// Append the element's matches among the entries that revalidate to `out`, in index order.
    pub(super) fn match_revalidation_entries(
        &mut self,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        facts: &ElementFacts,
        filter: &AncestorFilter,
        out: &mut Vec<ElementMatch>,
    ) -> Result<(), Incomplete> {
        self.match_in(Family::OwnRevalidation, node, facts, filter, out)
    }

    /// The filter of the keys of the earlier siblings of `node`. The traversal styles siblings one
    /// after another, so this mostly adds the keys of the sibling before to the filter of the element
    /// asked for last; an element that does not follow it has its earlier siblings gathered again, up
    /// to a bound past which the filter holds every key.
    fn earlier_siblings(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID) -> SiblingFilter {
        if let Some((last, filter)) = self.last_earlier_siblings
            && last == node
        {
            return filter;
        }
        let previous = self.projection.previous_element_sibling(node);
        let projection = self.projection;
        let add_keys = |filter: &mut SiblingFilter, sibling| {
            if let Some(row) = projection.row_of(sibling) {
                for key in super::ancestor_keys_of(row) {
                    filter.insert(key);
                }
            }
        };
        let filter = match self.last_earlier_siblings {
            Some((last, filter)) if previous == Some(last) => {
                let mut filter = filter;
                add_keys(&mut filter, last);
                filter
            }
            _ => {
                const MAX_GATHERED_SIBLINGS: usize = 32;
                let mut filter = SiblingFilter::default();
                let mut sibling = previous;
                for _ in 0..MAX_GATHERED_SIBLINGS {
                    let Some(current) = sibling else {
                        break;
                    };
                    add_keys(&mut filter, current);
                    sibling = self.projection.previous_element_sibling(current);
                }
                if sibling.is_some() {
                    filter.fill();
                }
                filter
            }
        };
        self.last_earlier_siblings = Some((node, filter));
        filter
    }

    /// Whether `node`, with `facts`, matches the entry, outside the buckets and the ancestor filter.
    /// An entry whose rule does not decide in the element's own tree matches nothing.
    pub(super) fn matches_entry(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID, entry: u32) -> Result<bool, Incomplete> {
        // NB: The invalidation map of a segment goes on naming the entries that died for this index.
        if !self.index.entries.view(entry as usize).live() {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let scope = self.projection.tree_scope(node);
        let placement = self.index.entries.placement(entry as usize);
        let applies = self.index.group_of(scope) == Some(placement.group)
            || (placement.group == ScopeGroupID::DOCUMENT
                && (self.state.rules.scope_uses_document_sheets(scope)
                    || matches!(placement.origin, CascadeOrigin::UserAgent | CascadeOrigin::User)));
        if !applies {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        // An element is rejected on the keys of its earlier siblings as a candidate of the buckets is.
        let selector = self.index.entry_selector(entry);
        if !self.index.entries.view(entry as usize).scoped()
            && let Some(key) = super::bloom::earlier_sibling_key(selector.selector)
            && !self.earlier_siblings(node).might_contain(key)
        {
            self.projection
                .note_structural_read(TransactionFactSide::After, node, StructuralRead::EarlierSiblings);
            return Ok(false);
        }
        self.enter_scope(scope, None);
        self.statistics.evaluations += 1;
        self.evaluator
            .matches_entry_selector(selector, node, self.state.document_matching())
    }

    /// The match of an unscoped entry of the own tree of `node`.
    pub(super) fn element_match(&self, node: StyleNodeID, entry: u32) -> ElementMatch {
        let indexed = self.index.entries.view(entry as usize);
        let scope = match self.index.entries.placement_of(indexed).group {
            ScopeGroupID::DOCUMENT => TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT,
            _ => self.projection.tree_scope(node),
        };
        ElementMatch {
            entry,
            rule: self.index.rule_of_view(indexed),
            specificity: indexed.specificity(),
            scope_proximity: u32::MAX,
            pseudo_kind: indexed.pseudo_kind(),
            context_depth: self.depth_of(scope),
            scope,
        }
    }

    /// How deeply `scope` is nested, which the matches of the rules of the trees an element is in
    /// stand at.
    fn depth_of(&self, scope: TreeScopeID) -> u32 {
        match scope {
            TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT => 0,
            _ => self.state.tree_scope_depth(scope),
        }
    }

    /// Evaluate the rules of `scope` from here on, for a part exposed to `part_exposure` if any.
    fn enter_scope(&mut self, scope: TreeScopeID, part_exposure: Option<TreeScopeID>) {
        let shadow_root = match scope {
            TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT => None,
            _ => self.state.scope_root(scope),
        };
        self.evaluator.set_scope_shadow_root(shadow_root);
        self.evaluator.set_part_exposure_scope(part_exposure);
    }

    /// Whether the rules of trees other than the element's own can match it: it hosts a shadow
    /// tree, is slotted, or is a part exposed outside its tree.
    pub(super) fn is_reached_from_other_trees(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        self.projection.is_reached_from_other_trees(node)
    }

    /// Append the element's matches among the entries of the trees other than its own that reach
    /// it to `out`: `:host` rules of its shadow tree, `::slotted()` rules of the trees it is slotted
    /// into, and `::part()` rules of the trees it is exposed to, or only the `::slotted()` rules
    /// for `revalidation`.
    ///
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping-1/#shadow-cascading
    fn match_other_trees(
        &mut self,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        facts: &ElementFacts,
        revalidation: bool,
        out: &mut Vec<ElementMatch>,
    ) -> Result<(), Incomplete> {
        if !self.is_reached_from_other_trees(node) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let state = self.state;
        let scope = self.projection.tree_scope(node);
        let inner_scope = self
            .projection
            .shadow_root_of(node)
            .and_then(|shadow_root| state.scope_by_root.get(shadow_root))
            .filter(|&inner| inner != scope);
        if let Some(inner_scope) = inner_scope
            && !revalidation
        {
            let reach = Reach {
                scope: inner_scope,
                family: Family::Host,
                scope_depth: state.encapsulation_context(node, inner_scope),
                filter: None,
                part_exposure: None,
            };
            self.match_family(reach, node, facts, out)?;
        }
        let slotted_scopes: SmallVec<[TreeScopeID; 2]> = state
            .scopes_slotted_into(node)
            .filter(|&slotted| slotted != scope && Some(slotted) != inner_scope)
            .collect();
        for &slotted_scope in &slotted_scopes {
            let reach = Reach {
                scope: slotted_scope,
                family: Family::Slotted,
                scope_depth: self.depth_of(slotted_scope),
                filter: None,
                part_exposure: None,
            };
            self.match_family(reach, node, facts, out)?;
        }
        if revalidation {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let part_scopes: SmallVec<[TreeScopeID; 2]> = state
            .part_exposure_scopes(node)
            .filter(|&exposed| exposed != scope && Some(exposed) != inner_scope && !slotted_scopes.contains(&exposed))
            .collect();
        for part_scope in part_scopes {
            let reach = Reach {
                scope: part_scope,
                family: Family::Part,
                scope_depth: self.depth_of(part_scope),
                filter: None,
                part_exposure: Some(part_scope),
            };
            self.match_family(reach, node, facts, out)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn match_in(
        &mut self,
        family: Family,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        facts: &ElementFacts,
        filter: &AncestorFilter,
        out: &mut Vec<ElementMatch>,
    ) -> Result<(), Incomplete> {
        let start = out.len();
        let scope = self.projection.tree_scope(node);
        let reach = Reach {
            scope,
            family,
            scope_depth: self.depth_of(scope),
            filter: Some(filter),
            part_exposure: None,
        };
        let result = self
            .match_family(reach, node, facts, out)
            .and_then(|()| self.match_other_trees(node, facts, family == Family::OwnRevalidation, out));
        if result.is_err() {
            out.truncate(start);
        }
        result?;
        out[start..].sort_unstable_by_key(|matched| (matched.entry, matched.scope));
        // An entry of the document's sheets can reach an element from more than one tree. One of a
        // group of shadow trees decides from each tree of the group that reaches the element.
        let mut kept = start;
        for index in start..out.len() {
            if kept == start || (out[kept - 1].entry, out[kept - 1].scope) != (out[index].entry, out[index].scope) {
                out[kept] = out[index];
                kept += 1;
            }
        }
        out.truncate(kept);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Append the element's matches among the entries of one bucket family of `scope` to `out`:
    /// those of the scope's own sheets, and of the document's sheets that decide in it.
    fn match_family(
        &mut self,
        reach: Reach<'_>,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        facts: &ElementFacts,
        out: &mut Vec<ElementMatch>,
    ) -> Result<(), Incomplete> {
        let (scope, family) = (reach.scope, reach.family);
        let index = self.buckets;
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping-1/#shadow-cascading
        // NB: A shadow tree decides with the document's user agent and user sheets, and with its
        //     author sheets as well where it is built from the document's styles.
        let mut sources: SmallVec<[BucketSource<'_>; 8]> = SmallVec::new();
        match scope {
            TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT => sources.extend(index.bucket_sources(ScopeGroupID::DOCUMENT, false)),
            _ => {
                if let Some(group) = index.group_of(scope) {
                    sources.extend(index.bucket_sources(group, false));
                }
                // NB: A tree built from the document's styles stands in for what they were written for, whose host they do
                //     not name.
                let non_author = family == Family::Host || !self.state.rules.scope_uses_document_sheets(scope);
                sources.extend(index.bucket_sources(ScopeGroupID::DOCUMENT, non_author));
            }
        }
        sources.extend(index.user_agent_buckets());
        if sources.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // NB: An entry is offered once for each tree that reaches the element: the shadow trees of
        //     one group share their entries.
        self.stamp = self.stamp.wrapping_add(1);
        if self.stamp == 0 {
            self.offered.fill(0);
            self.stamp = 1;
        }
        self.enter_scope(scope, reach.part_exposure);
        let projection = self.projection;
        let is_document_root = projection.parent(node).is_none();
        let keys = ElementKeys {
            bloom: element_bloom_of(
                facts,
                is_document_root,
                self.state.document_matching().fold_ids_and_classes,
            ),
            // NB: A tag that is its own ASCII-lowercase form has no folding of its own.
            tag_is_lowercase: facts.folded_tag().is_none(),
        };
        // NB: Each source is asked for the same keys, which are read from the element and hashed once.
        let mut probes: SmallVec<[(DispatchKey, KeyHash); 16]> = SmallVec::new();
        projection.for_each_dispatch_probe(facts, is_document_root, |key, _| {
            probes.push((key, Buckets::hash_of(&key)));
        });
        for source in sources {
            let buckets = source.buckets.family(family);
            if buckets.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            for (key, hash) in &probes {
                if let Some(bucket) = buckets.get_hashed(key, *hash) {
                    self.offer_all(bucket, source, node, reach, keys, out)?;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Offer the entries of `bucket` to the element, as `reach` reaches it.
    fn offer_all(
        &mut self,
        bucket: BucketSlots<'_>,
        source: BucketSource<'_>,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        reach: Reach<'_>,
        keys: ElementKeys,
        out: &mut Vec<ElementMatch>,
    ) -> Result<(), Incomplete> {
        let Reach {
            scope,
            family: _,
            scope_depth,
            filter,
            part_exposure: _,
        } = reach;
        let dead_in = source.binding_with_dead_entries();
        for bucket_entry in bucket {
            self.statistics.candidates += 1;
            // The subject compound's ids and classes, which the element's bits tell it lacks, first, as
            // they reject most candidates a bucket of one of its keys holds.
            if bucket_entry.subject_bloom() & !keys.bloom != 0 {
                self.statistics.bloom_rejections += 1;
                continue;
            }
            if filter.is_some_and(|filter| !filter.might_contain_all(&bucket_entry.ancestor_hashes())) {
                self.statistics.bloom_rejections += 1;
                continue;
            }
            let entry = source.first + bucket_entry.entry();
            if dead_in.is_some_and(|bound| bound.is_dead(entry)) {
                continue;
            }
            if bucket_entry.in_other_buckets() {
                let offered = &mut self.offered[entry as usize];
                if *offered == self.stamp {
                    continue;
                }
                *offered = self.stamp;
            }
            // An element of the entry's own tree is rejected on the keys of its earlier siblings as on those of its
            // ancestors.
            if filter.is_some()
                && let Some(key) = bucket_entry.sibling_key()
                && !self.earlier_siblings(node).might_contain(key)
            {
                // NB: What the element's earlier siblings carry rejected it, which an element arriving among them
                //     can move.
                self.projection
                    .note_structural_read(TransactionFactSide::After, node, StructuralRead::EarlierSiblings);
                self.statistics.bloom_rejections += 1;
                continue;
            }
            // NB: An entry its bucket's key proves matches without its selector being read, and
            //     matches unscoped.
            let scope_proximity = match bucket_entry.covered(keys.tag_is_lowercase) {
                true => u32::MAX,
                false => {
                    let selector = match bucket_entry.scoped() {
                        true => self.index.entry_selector(entry),
                        false => EntrySelector::unscoped(source.space.resolve(bucket_entry.selector())),
                    };
                    self.statistics.evaluations += 1;
                    let matches = match bucket_entry.subject_covered(keys.tag_is_lowercase) {
                        true => {
                            self.evaluator
                                .matches_left_of_subject(selector, node, self.state.document_matching())?
                        }
                        false => {
                            self.evaluator
                                .matches_entry_selector(selector, node, self.state.document_matching())?
                        }
                    };
                    if !matches {
                        continue;
                    }
                    self.evaluator.scope_proximity_of_match(node)
                }
            };
            // NB: The entry is read once, in place from the segment holding it where the buckets are one's.
            let matched = source.matched(self.index, entry);
            let (group, rule) = (matched.group, matched.rule);
            // A document sheet the scope holds too decides from the scope.
            if self.index.group_of(scope) != Some(group)
                && self
                    .state
                    .rules
                    .attachment_in_scope(self.state.rules.rule_sheet(rule), scope)
                    .is_some()
            {
                continue;
            }
            self.statistics.matches += 1;
            out.push(ElementMatch {
                entry,
                rule,
                specificity: matched.specificity,
                scope_proximity,
                pseudo_kind: matched.pseudo_kind,
                context_depth: match group {
                    ScopeGroupID::DOCUMENT => 0,
                    _ => scope_depth,
                },
                scope: match group {
                    ScopeGroupID::DOCUMENT => TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT,
                    _ => scope,
                },
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl crate::css::style::RetainedState {
    /// Every scope a `::part()` rule can address this element from, nearest host first.
    ///
    /// One per level of `exportparts` forwarding: the tree each forwarding host stands in holds
    /// rules that can name the element under the name that host exposed it by. Duplicates are
    /// dropped because two levels can stand in one tree.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn part_exposure_scopes(
        &self,
        node: StyleNodeID,
    ) -> impl Iterator<Item = TreeScopeID> + '_ {
        let mut seen: Vec<TreeScopeID> = Vec::new();
        self.projection
            .part_hosts_of(node)
            .iter()
            .map(|&(_, host)| self.projection.tree_scope(host))
            .filter(move |scope| match seen.contains(scope) {
                true => false,
                false => {
                    seen.push(*scope);
                    true
                }
            })
    }
}

/// The pseudo-elements a pass styles beside their element, in the order the host installs them.
pub(super) const PSEUDO_ELEMENT_KINDS: [u8; 9] = {

        AFTER, BACKDROP, BEFORE, FIRST_LETTER, MARKER, SEARCH_TEXT, SEARCH_TEXT_CURRENT, SELECTION, SPELLING_ERROR,

        MARKER,
    ]

/// ancestor that has one.

/// The keys an element contributes to its descendants' ancestor filter.
pub(super) fn ancestor_keys_of(facts: projection::ProjectionRow<'_>) -> SmallVec<[u32; 8]> {
    let mut keys = SmallVec::new();
    let id = facts.id();
    if !id.is_none() {
        keys.push(id_hash(id));
    }
    keys.extend(facts.classes().iter().map(|&class| class_hash(class)));
    for tag in [facts.tag(), facts.folded_tag()] {
        if !tag.is_none() {
            keys.push(tag_hash(tag));
        }
    }
    keys.extend(
        facts
            .attributes()
            .iter()
            .map(|attribute| attribute_hash(attribute.name)),
    );
    keys
}

/// What a computation waits on before it can answer.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct Waits {
    pub(super) fonts: Vec<font_resolution::FontRequest>,
    pub(super) random_bases: Vec<super::random_bases::RandomBaseRequest>,
}

/// How many rounds a computation may wait on fonts and random base values: a declined element hides
/// what its descendants wait on, so each round can find more.
const MAX_RESOLVE_ROUNDS: usize = 32;

/// How many more rounds a computation may wait for each element it inherits through, each of which it may compute with
/// a few fonts of its own and the random base values it draws in one round.
const MAX_RESOLVE_ROUNDS_PER_ANCESTOR: usize = 4;

impl StyleEngine {
    /// Runs `body` with the fonts of the document found by the content of their requests: a round
    /// computes the values its font requests name anew, so the fonts the round before asked for are
    /// found by the content of those values.
    fn matching_fonts_by_content<T>(&mut self, body: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> T) -> T {
        let set = |engine: &mut Self, matches_by_content| {
            let Some(cache) = &mut engine.retained.font_resolution else {
                return false;
            };
            let before = cache.matches_by_content();
            cache.set_matches_by_content(matches_by_content);
            before
        };
        let before = set(self, true);
        let answer = body(self);
        set(self, before);
        answer
    }

    /// The answer of `attempt`, run again until it no longer waits on anything, which this resolves
    /// for `node` between its runs, or none where it keeps waiting.
    pub(super) fn until_resolved<T>(
        &mut self,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        mut attempt: impl FnMut(&mut Self) -> Result<T, Waits>,
    ) -> Option<T> {
        self.matching_fonts_by_content(|engine| {
            let mut rounds = 0;
            let mut max_rounds = MAX_RESOLVE_ROUNDS;
            while rounds < max_rounds {
                match attempt(engine) {
                    Ok(answer) => return Some(answer),
                    Err(waits) => {
                        for request in waits.fonts {
                            engine.refill_font_request(node, request);
                        }
                        for request in waits.random_bases {
                            engine.retained.draw_random_base_value(request);
                        }
                    }
                }
                rounds += 1;
                if rounds == MAX_RESOLVE_ROUNDS {
                    let projection = &engine.retained.projection;
                    let ancestors = std::iter::successors(projection.inheritance_parent(node), |&parent| {
                        projection.inheritance_parent(parent)
                    });
                    max_rounds += MAX_RESOLVE_ROUNDS_PER_ANCESTOR * ancestors.count();
                }
            }
            None
        })
    }

    /// The computed initial values of the document under `root`.
    fn computed_initial(&mut self, root: StyleNodeID) -> Option<traversal::InitialStyle> {
        // The initial values compute against the document's initial font, which no element may
        // have asked the resolver for yet.
        self.until_resolved(root, |engine| {
            match engine.retained.initial_style(root) {
                Ok(mut computed) => {
                    // SAFETY: The initial style takes over the references the drive made.
                    let mut payloads = unsafe {
                        crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroups::adopt(
                            computed.payloads,
                            crate::css::computed_value_types::StyleBits {
                                inherited: crate::css::computed_value_types::InheritedSetValues {
                                    bits: crate::css::computed_value_types::InheritedBits::INITIAL,
                                    effective_zoom_bits: computed.value_facts.effective_zoom().to_bits(),
                                },
                                reset: crate::css::computed_value_types::ResetBits::INITIAL,
                            },
                        )
                    };
                    // The documents of the process share the initial groups but the font group.
                    let shared = computed.shared.take().unwrap_or_else(|| {
                        let value_groups = computed
                            .value_groups
                            .take()
                            .expect("a drive made the groups of its values");
                        let shared = engine.retained.process_style.share_initial_groups(
                            super::process_style::InitialGroupsInputs::of(
                                &engine.retained.document_style_computation_inputs,
                            ),
                            &payloads,
                            &value_groups,
                            super::process_style::InitialGroupsValues {
                                flags: computed.flags.clone(),
                                dependency_flags: computed.dependency_flags,
                                color: computed.color,
                                value_facts: computed.value_facts.clone(),
                            },
                        );
                        for index in crate::css::computed_values::StyleGroupIndex::all() {
                            if index.usize() != crate::css::table_group_builder::group_index::FONT {
                                payloads.share_group(shared.groups(), index);
                            }
                        }
                        shared
                    });
                    Ok(Some(traversal::InitialStyle::new(computed, payloads, shared)))
                }
                // NB: An engine no host published its fonts to yet, such as a test's bare engine, has no resolver
                //     to ask, and its initial style waits on fonts it cannot resolve yet.
                Err(_) if engine.host.font_resolver.is_none() => Ok(None),
                Err(request) => Err(Waits {
                    fonts: vec![*request],
                    random_bases: Vec::new(),
                }),
            }
        })
        .flatten()
    }

    /// Has style passes run on the threads of `pool`, which the process shares.
    pub(crate) fn share_style_layout_pool(&mut self, pool: std::sync::Arc<crate::style_layout_pool::StyleLayoutPool>) {
        self.retained.style_layout_pool = Some(pool);
    }

    /// The pool a pass on `threads` threads runs on besides the calling thread, or on the default
    /// number for the machine for none.
    fn style_layout_pool(&mut self, threads: u32) -> Option<std::sync::Arc<rayon::ThreadPool>> {
        // NB: An engine no render state holds, such as a test's, starts threads of its own.
        self.retained
            .style_layout_pool
            .get_or_insert_with(|| std::sync::Arc::new(crate::style_layout_pool::StyleLayoutPool::of_engine()))
            .for_threads(threads)
    }
}

impl RetainedState {
    /// What the audit of what passes reuse asks for: what the engine read as it started, or off
    /// without it.
    fn cache_audit_mode(&self) -> self_check::Mode {
        self.live_style
            .as_ref()
            .map_or(self_check::Mode::Off, |live| live.cache_audit)
    }
}

//! What the inputs the host has yet to settle may change, which the host asks to skip settling
//! them where nothing it reads can move: a geometry read reuses the committed layout where no
//! pending input may move geometry, and a hover reuses the read-only frame where no element can
//! match a compound testing `:hover`.
//!
//! The hover's question is asked of every frame and the host waits for its answer, so no element is read to answer it.
//! The compounds testing `:hover` are compiled once for the rules into the keys of the elements that may match them, and
//! a transaction notes the elements whose keys among those it moved.

use super::super::*;
use super::invalidation::{HoverCompounds, InvalidationMap, Trigger};
use super::live::Live;
use super::projection::{ElementChange, ProjectionGeneration};
use crate::fast_hash::FastSet;

/// What the hover seal keeps between frames.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct HoverSealMemo {
    carriers: Option<HoverCarriers>,
    cursor_facts: Option<HoverCursorFactsAnswer>,
}

// NB: A fork of the engine seals no frame, and has no use for what the host's seal kept.
impl Clone for HoverSealMemo {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }
}

/// The elements that may match a compound testing `:hover`, which the transactions keep up as they move the keys of the
/// compounds of `map`.
struct HoverCarriers {
    map: Arc<InvalidationMap>,
    compounds: HoverCompounds,
    elements: FastSet<StyleNodeID>,
}

/// The cursor facts published last, with the generations of what they read: the projection's, the tree's paint facts,
/// and the records the elements are assigned.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct HoverCursorFactsAnswer {
    projection: ProjectionGeneration,
    dom_paint_facts_version: u64,
    installed_column_version: u64,
    facts: Arc<super::super::hover_lane::HoverCursorFacts>,
    editable: Arc<FastSet<StyleNodeID>>,
}

impl StyleEngine {
    /// The cursor facts built last, where nothing they read moved since.
    pub(in super::super) fn memoized_hover_cursor_facts(
        &self,
    ) -> Option<Arc<super::super::hover_lane::HoverCursorFacts>> {
        let last = self.host.hover_seal.cursor_facts.as_ref()?;
        (last.dom_paint_facts_version == self.tree().dom_paint_facts_version()
            && last.installed_column_version == self.computed_group_sets.installed_column_version()
            && self.retained.projection.is_at_generation(&last.projection))
        .then(|| last.facts.clone())
    }

    /// The editable elements as they stand, shared with the cursor facts published last while the tree's paint facts
    /// did not move.
    pub(in super::super) fn hover_editable_nodes(&self) -> Arc<FastSet<StyleNodeID>> {
        match &self.host.hover_seal.cursor_facts {
            Some(last) if last.dom_paint_facts_version == self.tree().dom_paint_facts_version() => {
                last.editable.clone()
            }
            _ => Arc::new(self.tree().editable_nodes().collect()),
        }
    }

    /// Keep `facts`, the cursor facts as they stand, with what they read.
    pub(in super::super) fn memoize_hover_cursor_facts(
        &mut self,
        facts: Arc<super::super::hover_lane::HoverCursorFacts>,
    ) {
        self.host.hover_seal.cursor_facts = Some(HoverCursorFactsAnswer {
            projection: self.retained.projection.generation(),
            dom_paint_facts_version: self.tree().dom_paint_facts_version(),
            installed_column_version: self.computed_group_sets.installed_column_version(),
            editable: facts.editable(),
            facts,
        });
    }

    /// The engine of the document and its invalidation map, where the map describes the
    /// rules and elements as they stand.
    fn current_invalidation(&self) -> Option<(&Live, &InvalidationMap)> {
        let live = self.retained.live_style.as_deref()?;
        let map = live.current_invalidation()?;
        Some((live, map))
    }

    /// Whether settling the pending element inputs may move layout geometry: those the projection
    /// holds no row for always may, and so may a change made to
    /// the projection since the last barrier or geometry read seal that does by
    /// [`Self::change_may_affect_layout_geometry`].
    pub(in super::super) fn pending_inputs_may_affect_layout_geometry(&self) -> bool {
        if !self.host.element_inputs.is_empty() {
            return true;
        }
        let current = self.current_invalidation();
        self.retained.projection.any_change_since_seal(|node, change| {
            current.is_none_or(|(live, map)| self.change_may_affect_layout_geometry(live, map, node, change))
        })
    }

    /// Whether settling `change`, a pending change to one element's facts or relations, may move
    /// layout geometry: whether the elements it restyles may come to match, or stop matching, a
    /// rule that may move geometry, or substitute the element's attributes.
    fn change_may_affect_layout_geometry(
        &self,
        live: &Live,
        map: &InvalidationMap,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        change: ElementChange,
    ) -> bool {
        let program = &self.retained.rules;
        let rule_moves = |entry: u32| program.rule_may_affect_layout_geometry(live.index.rule_of(entry));
        let moves = |trigger: Trigger| {
            map.effects(&trigger).any(|effect| rule_moves(effect.entry))
                || map.lone_entries(&trigger).any(rule_moves)
                || map
                    .queries_testing(&trigger)
                    .any(|(query, _)| rule_moves(map.relative_entry(query)))
        };
        let feature = match change {
            ElementChange::State(fact) => return moves(Trigger::State(fact)),
            ElementChange::Id(old, new) => {
                return [old, new].into_iter().any(|id| !id.is_none() && moves(Trigger::Id(id)));
            }
            ElementChange::Feature(feature) => feature,
            ElementChange::Relations(..) | ElementChange::ArrivingFacts => return true,
        };
        match feature {
            LocalFeatureKey::Class(class) => moves(Trigger::Class(class)),
            LocalFeatureKey::Attribute(name) => {
                self.retained
                    .projection
                    .attribute_name_keys(name)
                    .into_iter()
                    .any(|name| !name.is_none() && moves(Trigger::Attribute(name)))
                    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#attr-notation
                    || std::iter::once(node)
                        .chain(self.retained.backing_elements(node, u64::MAX))
                        .any(|reader| {
                            live.records.get(reader).is_some_and(|record| record.rare().reads.reads_attributes)
                                || live
                                    .records
                                    .pseudo_element_records(reader)
                                    .iter()
                                    .any(|(_, record)| record.rare().reads.reads_attributes)
                        })
            }
            LocalFeatureKey::CustomState(state) => moves(Trigger::CustomState(state)),
            LocalFeatureKey::Emptiness => moves(Trigger::Emptiness),
            LocalFeatureKey::Language => moves(Trigger::Language),
            LocalFeatureKey::Directionality => moves(Trigger::Directionality),
            LocalFeatureKey::HeadingLevel => moves(Trigger::Heading),
            LocalFeatureKey::Part(part) => moves(Trigger::Part(part)),
            LocalFeatureKey::Id
            | LocalFeatureKey::PartExposure
            | LocalFeatureKey::TagName
            | LocalFeatureKey::FoldedTagName => true,
        }
    }

    /// Whether a hover under `root` needs the style engine: whether an element in its shadow-including subtree is a
    /// disabled control, or may come to match, or stop matching, a compound testing `:hover`. Reads only the elements
    /// a transaction moved the keys of those compounds of.
    pub(in super::super) fn hover_seal_needs_style_state(&mut self, root: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        let projection = &self.retained.projection;
        let tree = self.tree();
        let under_root =
            |node: &StyleNodeID| tree.is_live(*node) && projection.is_in_shadow_including_subtree_of(*node, root);
        if projection.written_disabled().iter().any(under_root) || !self.update_hover_carriers() {
            return true;
        }
        let projection = &self.retained.projection;
        let tree = self.tree();
        let under_root =
            |node: &StyleNodeID| tree.is_live(*node) && projection.is_in_shadow_including_subtree_of(*node, root);
        self.host
            .hover_seal
            .carriers
            .as_ref()
            .expect("the hover seal's carriers were just brought up")
            .elements
            .iter()
            .any(under_root)
    }

    /// Bring the elements that may match a compound testing `:hover` up to the rows and the rules as they stand,
    /// answering whether they say which elements may. They do not where no map describes the rules, or where any element
    /// may.
    fn update_hover_carriers(&mut self) -> bool {
        let Some(live) = self.retained.live_style.as_deref() else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(map) = live.current_invalidation_shared() else {
            return false;
        };
        let projection = &mut self.retained.projection;
        let known = self
            .host
            .hover_seal
            .carriers
            .take()
            .filter(|carriers| projection.watches_keys(carriers.compounds.keys()));
        let mut carriers = match known {
            Some(carriers) if Arc::ptr_eq(&carriers.map, map) => carriers,
            known => {
                let compounds = map.hover_compounds(&live.index);
                let elements = match known {
                    // NB: The rules moved around the same compounds: no key moved, and no element is read again.
                    Some(carriers) if carriers.compounds.are_the_same_as(&compounds) => carriers.elements,
                    _ => {
                        let writes = projection.take_watched_key_writes();
                        projection.reuse_watched_key_writes(writes);
                        projection
                            .committed_carriers_of(compounds.keys())
                            .filter(|&node| {
                                projection
                                    .row_of(node)
                                    .is_some_and(|row| compounds.may_match(map, &live.index, row))
                            })
                            .collect()
                    }
                };
                projection.watch_keys(compounds.keys().clone());
                HoverCarriers {
                    map: map.clone(),
                    compounds,
                    elements,
                }
            }
        };
        let writes = projection.take_watched_key_writes();
        for &node in &writes {
            let carries = projection
                .row_of(node)
                .is_some_and(|row| carriers.compounds.may_match(&carriers.map, &live.index, row));
            if carries {
                carriers.elements.insert(node);
            } else {
                carriers.elements.remove(&node);
            }
        }
        projection.reuse_watched_key_writes(writes);
        let says = !carriers.compounds.every_element();
        self.host.hover_seal.carriers = Some(carriers);
        says
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::super::test_support::{
        add_class, add_rules, add_sheet, linear_document, relations, remove_class, run_style_update, set_tag,
        start_live,
    };
    use super::*;

    fn document_with_rules(source: &str) -> (StyleEngine, Vec<StyleNodeID>) {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = linear_document();
        let sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
        add_rules(&mut engine, sheet, source);
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        (engine, nodes)
    }

    #[test]
    fn only_inputs_reaching_rules_that_move_geometry_may_affect_layout_geometry() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(
            ".paint { background-color: green; } .wide > * { width: 10px; } .moved { transform: scale(2); }",
        );
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "paint");
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "unstyled");
        assert!(engine.has_pending_transaction());
        assert!(!engine.pending_transaction_may_affect_layout_geometry());

        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[0], "wide");
        assert!(engine.pending_transaction_may_affect_layout_geometry());

        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(".moved { transform: scale(2); }");
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[3], "moved");
        assert!(engine.pending_transaction_may_affect_layout_geometry());
    }

    #[test]
    fn inputs_a_has_argument_reads_may_affect_layout_geometry_through_its_anchor() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(".anchor:has(.inner) { width: 1px; }");
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "inner");
        assert!(engine.pending_transaction_may_affect_layout_geometry());

        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(".anchor:has(.inner) { background-color: green; }");
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "inner");
        assert!(!engine.pending_transaction_may_affect_layout_geometry());
    }

    #[test]
    fn hover_restyles_only_where_an_element_may_match_a_hover_compound() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(".menu:hover .item { color: red; }");
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));

        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "menu");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));

        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(":is(button, .action):hover { color: red; }");
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        set_tag(&mut engine, nodes[2], "button");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn hover_restyles_through_a_type_selector_in_any_case() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules("A:hover { color: red; }");
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        set_tag(&mut engine, nodes[2], "a");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn hover_restyles_through_what_no_compound_of_its_own_tests() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(":nth-child(1 of :hover) { color: red; }");
        assert!(engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn hover_restyles_a_backed_pseudo_element_only_through_the_element_backing_it() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules("input::file-selector-button:hover { color: red; }");
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_hover_seal_follows_the_rows_written_since_it_answered() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(".menu:hover { color: red; }");
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "menu");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[3]));
        remove_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "menu");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[3], "menu");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[3]));
        assert!(engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn hover_compounds_select_what_reading_every_compound_selects() {
        for selector in [
            "A:hover",
            ".a.b:hover",
            ".a.c:hover",
            "#i:hover",
            "span.a:hover",
            "div.c:hover",
            ":is(.a, span):hover",
            ":is(.c, em):hover",
            ":where(:is(.b)):hover",
            ":is(.c):is(.a):hover",
        ] {
            let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(&format!("{selector} {{ color: red; }}"));
            add_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "a");
            add_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "b");
            set_tag(&mut engine, nodes[2], "span");
            add_class(&mut engine, nodes[3], "a");
            start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
            let (live, map) = engine.current_invalidation().expect("the map describes the rules");
            let compounds = map.hover_compounds(&live.index);
            assert!(!compounds.every_element(), "{selector}");
            let hover = Trigger::State(StateFact::Hover);
            for &node in &nodes {
                let row = engine.retained.projection.row_of(node).expect("the element has facts");
                assert_eq!(
                    compounds.may_match(map, &live.index, row),
                    map.effects(&hover)
                        .any(|effect| map.may_match_by_keys(&live.index, effect, row)),
                    "{selector}"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn hover_compounds_with_no_key_answer_for_every_element() {
        for selector in ["*:hover", ":hover", ":not(:hover)", "[data-x]:hover", ":not(.a):hover"] {
            let (engine, _) = document_with_rules(&format!("{selector} {{ color: red; }}"));
            let (live, map) = engine.current_invalidation().expect("the map describes the rules");
            assert!(map.hover_compounds(&live.index).every_element(), "{selector}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_hover_seal_follows_each_key_of_a_compound_as_transactions_move_them() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(".a.b:hover { color: red; }");
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "a");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "b");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        remove_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "a");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_hover_seal_hears_of_no_element_but_those_whose_watched_keys_moved() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(".menu:hover { color: red; }");
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "other");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(engine.retained.projection.take_watched_key_writes().is_empty());
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "menu");
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "other");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_eq!(engine.retained.projection.take_watched_key_writes(), [nodes[1]]);
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "another");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_eq!(engine.retained.projection.take_watched_key_writes(), [nodes[1]]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_hover_seal_reads_no_element_for_rules_that_leave_its_compounds_alone() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(".menu:hover { color: red; }");
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        // NB: Nothing carries the key of the compound: an element read again would be found not to carry it.
        let carriers = engine.host.hover_seal.carriers.as_mut().expect("the seal answered");
        carriers.elements.insert(nodes[3]);
        let sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
        add_rules(&mut engine, sheet, ".other { color: green; }");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_hover_seal_finds_the_elements_a_rule_added_later_may_match() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(".other { color: green; }");
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "menu");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        let sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
        add_rules(&mut engine, sheet, ".menu:hover { color: red; }");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_hover_seal_lets_go_of_an_element_that_leaves() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_rules(".menu:hover { color: red; }");
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[3], "menu");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
        engine.record_tree_delta(nodes[3], Some(relations(Some(nodes[0]), None, Some(nodes[2]))), None);
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!engine.hover_needs_style_state(nodes[0]));
    }
}

use std::sync::Mutex;

/// What each thread a pass runs on keeps between passes, by thread, the calling thread's last: a slot is made the first
/// time its thread asks for it, so a document, or a fork of its render state, holds only what its threads used.
pub(super) struct PerThread<T>([std::sync::OnceLock<Box<Mutex<T>>>; crate::style_layout_pool::MAX_THREAD_COUNT + 1]);

impl<T> Default for PerThread<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self(std::array::from_fn(|_| std::sync::OnceLock::new()))
    }
}

impl<T: Default> PerThread<T> {
    /// What thread `index` keeps, made where it is not yet, or none past the last thread.
    pub(super) fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&Mutex<T>> {
        self.0.get(index).map(|slot| &**slot.get_or_init(Box::default))
    }

    /// What the threads that asked keep.
    pub(super) fn made(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Mutex<T>> {
        self.0.iter().filter_map(|slot| slot.get().map(|made| &**made))
    }

    /// What the threads that asked keep, with the index of each thread.
    pub(super) fn made_with_index(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (usize, &Mutex<T>)> {
        self.0
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter_map(|(index, slot)| slot.get().map(|made| (index, &**made)))
    }

    /// How many threads may keep anything.
    pub(super) fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.0.len()
    }
}

//! The document as the engine reads it: each element's local facts and the links between elements,
//! projected from the writes the host makes, in the order it makes them.
//!
//! One row holds everything style reads of one element, addressed by its element slot, so reading
//! an element's facts and following a link out of it are one lookup each. Rows live in a
//! [`CowColumn`]: a fork shares every chunk of rows and copies one only when it writes there, and
//! the variable-length facts of a row are `Arc` slices, which a copied chunk shares in turn. The
//! catalogs keyed by atom (attribute name forms and the texts of values and languages) belong to
//! the document rather than to an element and are shared the same way.
//!
//! A row's facts and its links have lifetimes of their own. An element's links are reset when its
//! identity is minted and when it retires, as the tree changes; its facts exist from the first one
//! published until the element is forgotten at the end of the transaction it departed in, so that
//! invalidation can still read the facts of an element that left.
//!
//! Facts are written as their inputs arrive, ahead of the transaction they join, but style reads
//! them as the last transaction committed them: the projection publishes its rows at each
//! transaction barrier, and the facts readers see are those of that committed generation. An
//! element's links are read the same way; the shadow relations are read as written, as the host's
//! shadow tree changes between barriers are. While a transaction is
//! taken, the generation committed before it stays at hand too: the side of the transaction from
//! before it, which invalidation compares the elements' facts and relations against.

pub(in crate::css::style) use fact_lists::{FactListsIdentity, FactListsTable};
mod tree_reads;
mod writer;

/// How many rows a chunk of the projection holds, and so how many rows the first write after a fork
/// copies.
const ROWS_PER_CHUNK: usize = 64;

/// Empty a list of what one transaction wrote or changed. Keep small lists warm for the next transaction, but do not
/// retain what a batch of arriving elements grew one to for the lifetime of every document.
fn clear_transaction_list<T>(list: &mut Vec<T>) {
    list.clear();
    if list.capacity() * size_of::<T>() > 4096 {
        *list = Vec::new();
    }
}

/// A set of elements whose rows were written, each listed once, with a bit per element slot saying
/// which.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct WrittenRows {
    nodes: Vec<StyleNodeID>,
    bits: crate::cow_column::CowVec<u64, 64>,
}

impl WrittenRows {
    /// Add an element, saying whether it was not in the set yet.
    fn insert(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID, slot: usize) -> bool {
        let (word, bit) = (slot / 64, 1_u64 << (slot % 64));
        if word >= self.bits.len() {
            self.bits.resize_with_default(word + 1);
        }
        if self.bits[word] & bit != 0 {
            return false;
        }
        self.bits[word] |= bit;
        self.nodes.push(node);
        true
    }

    fn contains(&self, slot: usize) -> bool {
        self.bits
            .get(slot / 64)
            .is_some_and(|word| word & (1_u64 << (slot % 64)) != 0)
    }

    /// Take the elements out, leaving the set empty.
    fn take(&mut self) -> Vec<StyleNodeID> {
        let nodes = std::mem::take(&mut self.nodes);
        for node in &nodes {
            let slot = node.element_slot();
            self.bits[slot / 64] &= !(1_u64 << (slot % 64));
        }
        nodes
    }

    /// Empty the set, keeping `nodes`, taken from it, as its allocation.
    fn reuse(&mut self, mut nodes: Vec<StyleNodeID>) {
        debug_assert!(self.nodes.is_empty());
        clear_transaction_list(&mut nodes);
        self.nodes = nodes;
    }
}

/// The elements written since the last barrier, in the order of their writes, once per write, of which the first
/// `checked` were found to leave their rows as the committed generation has them, until written again.
#[derive(Default)]
struct PendingChangeScan {
    writes: Vec<StyleNodeID>,
    checked: std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize,
}

impl Clone for PendingChangeScan {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            writes: self.writes.clone(),
            checked: self.checked.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed).into(),
        }
    }
}

impl PendingChangeScan {
    fn clear(&mut self) {
        clear_transaction_list(&mut self.writes);
        *self.checked.get_mut() = 0;
    }

    fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        crate::heap_size::vec_bytes(&self.writes)
    }
}

/// A key of an element, which a compound can require of the elements it matches: a name its row holds, or the
/// element-backed pseudo-element of its shadow host it stands for.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub(in crate::css::style) enum CarriedKey {
    Tag(StyleAtomID),
    Class(StyleAtomID),
    Id(StyleAtomID),
    BackedPseudoElement(u8),
}

/// The keys a [`Projection`] notes the elements of: those that carried one, or carry one, and whose keys moved.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct WatchedKeys {
    keys: HashSet<CarriedKey>,
    /// A Bloom summary of the names among the keys, which rules out most elements without a lookup.
    names_bloom: u64,
    watches_pseudo_elements: bool,
}

impl WatchedKeys {
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn new(keys: impl IntoIterator<Item = CarriedKey>) -> Self {
        let keys: HashSet<CarriedKey> = keys.into_iter().collect();
        let mut watched = Self {
            names_bloom: 0,
            watches_pseudo_elements: false,
            keys: HashSet::default(),
        };
        for &key in &keys {
            match key {
                CarriedKey::Tag(tag) => watched.names_bloom |= dispatch_bloom_bit(DispatchKey::TagName(tag)),
                CarriedKey::Class(class) => watched.names_bloom |= dispatch_bloom_bit(DispatchKey::Class(class)),
                CarriedKey::Id(id) => watched.names_bloom |= dispatch_bloom_bit(DispatchKey::Id(id)),
                CarriedKey::BackedPseudoElement(_) => watched.watches_pseudo_elements = true,
            }
        }
        watched.keys = keys;
        watched
    }

    /// Whether an element with `facts` carries a key, without reading more of it than its names where its Bloom
    /// summary says it may.
    fn carried_by(&self, facts: &ElementFacts, host_fact_sets: &HostFactSets) -> bool {
        (facts.dispatch_bloom & self.names_bloom != 0 && facts.named_keys().any(|key| self.keys.contains(&key)))
            || (self.watches_pseudo_elements
                && backed_pseudo_element_key(facts, host_fact_sets).is_some_and(|key| self.keys.contains(&key)))
    }
}

fn backed_pseudo_element_key(facts: &ElementFacts, host_fact_sets: &HostFactSets) -> Option<CarriedKey> {
    host_fact_sets
        .get(facts.host_facts)
        .associated_pseudo_kind()
        .map(CarriedKey::BackedPseudoElement)
}

/// Whether the two say the same of the keys their elements carry.
fn carry_the_same_keys(was: &ElementFacts, is: &ElementFacts, host_fact_sets: &HostFactSets) -> bool {
    was.tag == is.tag
        && was.folded_tag() == is.folded_tag()
        && was.id() == is.id()
        && was.classes() == is.classes()
        && backed_pseudo_element_key(was, host_fact_sets) == backed_pseudo_element_key(is, host_fact_sets)
}

/// A list of atoms or pairs a row holds, shared by every copy of the row. An empty one holds no
/// allocation.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
struct SharedList<T>(Option<Arc<[T]>>);

impl<T> Default for SharedList<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self(None)
    }
}

impl<T: Clone> SharedList<T> {
    fn new(values: &[T]) -> Self {
        Self((!values.is_empty()).then(|| values.into()))
    }

    fn as_slice(&self) -> &[T] {
        self.0.as_deref().unwrap_or_default()
    }
}

/// What one element publishes of itself, which its selectors test.
#[derive(Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct ElementFacts {
    tag: StyleAtomID,
    /// The `ElementFacts::RESIDENT` and the other flags.
    flags: u8,
    /// The element's heading level, 1 to 9, or zero where it is not a heading.
    heading_level: u8,
    /// The identity of the set of facts the host publishes of the element beside the ones its selectors test, among
    /// the document's sets: what its box and its style adjustments read of it, and the element-backed pseudo-element
    /// of its shadow host it stands for.
    host_facts: HostFactSetID,
    states: StateSet,
    /// The element's id, namespace, language, directionality, tree scope and assigned slot, and its
    /// classes, attributes, parts and custom states, with its folded tag and part exposure, interned
    /// by content.
    lists: FactLists,
    /// A Bloom summary of the dispatch keys the element carries, document-root status aside: those
    /// its lists summarize, and its own. Kept beside the facts, as an ancestor walk reads it for
    /// every ancestor and the lists may be a cache miss away.
    dispatch_bloom: u64,
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<ElementFacts>() == 32);

impl ElementFacts {
    /// Whether anything was published about the element, or it is a shadow root standing in the
    /// tree. An element without facts is one the projection cannot answer for, which is not the same
    /// as an element that has none.
    const RESIDENT: u8 = 1 << 0;
    /// Whether a text or comment child keeps the element from being `:empty`.
    const HAS_TEXT_CONTENT: u8 = 1 << 1;
    /// Whether the element is a `<slot>`. A slot inside a shadow tree is not itself a flattened
    /// slottable, so `::slotted()` never names one even when its assignment carries a chain onward.
    const IS_SLOT: u8 = 1 << 2;
    /// Whether the row's identity is live, which belongs to its links rather than its facts and is
    /// kept here where the row has room for it.
    const LIVE: u8 = 1 << 3;
    /// Whether the element stands in a tree: it was inserted and has not left. An identity is
    /// minted as its node arrives, before its relations are published. Like `LIVE`, of its links.
    const CONNECTED: u8 = 1 << 4;

    fn flag(&self, flag: u8) -> bool {
        self.flags & flag != 0
    }

    fn set_flag(&mut self, flag: u8, value: bool) {
        match value {
            true => self.flags |= flag,
            false => self.flags &= !flag,
        }
    }

    fn resident(&self) -> bool {
        self.flag(Self::RESIDENT)
    }

    /// Whether the two say the same of their elements, leaving aside what they keep of their links: whether the
    /// identity is live and stands in a tree, its tree scope and its assigned slot.
    fn says_the_same_as(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        const LINK_FLAGS: u8 = ElementFacts::LIVE | ElementFacts::CONNECTED;
        self.tag == other.tag
            && self.flags & !LINK_FLAGS == other.flags & !LINK_FLAGS
            && self.heading_level == other.heading_level
            && self.host_facts == other.host_facts
            && self.states == other.states
            && self.lists.says_the_same_as(&other.lists)
    }

    /// Summarizes the dispatch keys the element carries again: those of its lists, which the lists summarize where they
    /// are made, and its own few.
    fn refresh_dispatch_bloom(&mut self) {
        let mut bloom = self.lists.bloom()
            | dispatch_bloom_bit(DispatchKey::Universal)
            | dispatch_bloom_bit(DispatchKey::TagName(self.tag));
        if self.heading_level() != 0 {
            bloom |= dispatch_bloom_bit(DispatchKey::Heading);
        }
        for fact in self.states.facts() {
            bloom |= dispatch_bloom_bit(DispatchKey::State(fact));
        }
        self.dispatch_bloom = bloom;
    }

    /// The facts the element is left with once they are forgotten: none, but what they keep of its links, and the host
    /// facts, which the element keeps until its identity is minted again, for what reads the departed element.
    fn forgotten(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            flags: self.flags & (Self::LIVE | Self::CONNECTED),
            host_facts: self.host_facts,
            ..Self::default()
        }
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn tag(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        self.tag
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn namespace(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        self.lists.namespace()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn id(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        self.lists.id()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn states(&self) -> StateSet {
        self.states
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn language(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        self.lists.language()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn directionality(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        self.lists.directionality()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn part_exposure(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        self.lists.part_exposure()
    }

    /// The ASCII-lowercase folding of the element's tag, where it differs from it.
    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn folded_tag(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        self.lists.folded_tag()
    }

    /// What is equal between two elements only if their lists are the same ones, and so everything
    /// they hold is: for as long as both stand in rows.
    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn lists_identity(&self) -> FactListsIdentity {
        self.lists.identity()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn heading_level(&self) -> u8 {
        self.heading_level
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn is_slot(&self) -> bool {
        self.flag(Self::IS_SLOT)
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn has_text_content(&self) -> bool {
        self.flag(Self::HAS_TEXT_CONTENT)
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn classes(&self) -> &[StyleAtomID] {
        self.lists.classes()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn attributes(&self) -> &[AttributeFact] {
        self.lists.attributes()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn parts(&self) -> &[StyleAtomID] {
        self.lists.parts()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn custom_states(&self) -> &[StyleAtomID] {
        self.lists.custom_states()
    }

    /// The keys of the element that name something of its own.
    fn named_keys(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = CarriedKey> + '_ {
        let (folded_tag, id) = (self.folded_tag(), self.id());
        [
            Some(CarriedKey::Tag(self.tag)),
            (!folded_tag.is_none()).then_some(CarriedKey::Tag(folded_tag)),
            (!id.is_none()).then_some(CarriedKey::Id(id)),
        ]
        .into_iter()
        .flatten()
        .chain(self.classes().iter().copied().map(CarriedKey::Class))
    }

    /// The Bloom summary of the dispatch keys the element carries.
    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn dispatch_bloom(&self, is_document_root: bool) -> u64 {
        self.dispatch_bloom
            | match is_document_root {
                true => dispatch_bloom_bit(DispatchKey::Root),
                false => 0,
            }
    }
}

/// How one element stands in the tree. Its tree scope and assigned slot are held in its fact lists,
/// and whether it is live and connected in its facts' flags, so that a row is 56 bytes.
#[derive(Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
struct Links {
    parent: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    first_element_child: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    previous_element_sibling: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    next_element_sibling: Option<StyleNodeID>,
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Links>() == 16);

/// The shadow relations of an element, which few elements have.
#[derive(Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
struct ShadowLinks {
    /// A shadow host's shadow root.
    shadow_root: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    /// A shadow root's host.
    host: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    /// A slot's assigned nodes, text nodes included, in the order the DOM assigned them.
    assigned_nodes: SharedList<StyleNodeID>,
    /// Every part name the element is addressable by, each with the host of the level that name
    /// reaches.
    part_hosts: SharedList<(StyleAtomID, StyleNodeID)>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
struct Row {
    facts: ElementFacts,
    links: Links,
    /// A Bloom summary of the classes and attribute names the element's descendants in its tree carry, by
    /// [`subtree_key_bits`]: a walk down the tree for a key the summary lacks finds no element below the element. The
    /// writer brings it up to date as it publishes the rows. A key that left the subtree stays until the identity is
    /// minted again.
    subtree_keys: u64,
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Row>() == 56);

/// The shadow relations of the elements by slot, in a column of their own that is made only as far as the last element
/// holding any: most documents have none, and most elements of those that do hold none either.
type ShadowColumn = CowColumn<Option<Arc<ShadowLinks>>, ROWS_PER_CHUNK>;
type ShadowSnapshot = ColumnSnapshot<Option<Arc<ShadowLinks>>, ROWS_PER_CHUNK>;

fn shadow_links_heap_size(shadow: Option<&Arc<ShadowLinks>>, sizer: &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer) -> usize {
    shadow.map_or(0, |shadow| {
        if !sizer.first_sight(Arc::as_ptr(shadow)) {
            return 0;
        }
        crate::heap_size::ARC_HEADER_BYTES
            + size_of::<ShadowLinks>()
            + shadow.assigned_nodes.heap_size(sizer)
            + shadow.part_hosts.heap_size(sizer)
    })
}

impl Row {
    /// Whether the row's element identity is live: minted and not retired.
    fn live(&self) -> bool {
        self.facts.flag(ElementFacts::LIVE)
    }

    /// Whether the row's element stands in a tree.
    fn connected(&self) -> bool {
        self.facts.flag(ElementFacts::CONNECTED)
    }
}

/// What a document's atoms spell, for the tests and substitutions that compare text.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct Catalogs {
    name_forms: Catalog<AttributeNameForms>,
    /// The local name an `attr()` reads an attribute in no namespace by.
    substitution_names: Catalog<Box<[u16]>>,
    /// What attribute-value atoms spell: the host's own string, which the document's attribute
    /// holds as well, shared by reference.
    value_texts: Catalog<RetainedUtf16FlyString>,
    language_texts: Catalog<Box<[u16]>>,
}

/// A catalog the writer adds to between publications, which every publication shares: a large base and the small part
/// added since the base was last folded, so that an addition after a publication copies only the small part. The part
/// is folded into the base once it grows past an eighth of it.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Catalog<T> {
    base: Arc<HashMap<StyleAtomID, T>>,
    recent: Arc<HashMap<StyleAtomID, T>>,
    /// How many entries additions copied, for a test.
    #[cfg(test)]
    copied: usize,
}

impl<T> Default for Catalog<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            base: Arc::default(),
            recent: Arc::default(),
            #[cfg(test)]
            copied: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl<T: Clone> Catalog<T> {
    fn get(&self, atom: &StyleAtomID) -> Option<&T> {
        self.recent.get(atom).or_else(|| self.base.get(atom))
    }

    fn contains_key(&self, atom: &StyleAtomID) -> bool {
        self.get(atom).is_some()
    }

    /// Every entry, once, the recent spelling of an atom standing for the one in the base.
    fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&StyleAtomID, &T)> {
        self.recent
            .iter()
            .chain(self.base.iter().filter(|(atom, _)| !self.recent.contains_key(atom)))
    }

    /// Notes, for a test, how many entries writing `map` now copies.
    #[cfg(test)]
    fn note_copy(copied: &mut usize, map: &Arc<HashMap<StyleAtomID, T>>) {
        if Arc::strong_count(map) > 1 {
            *copied += map.len();
        }
    }

    fn insert(&mut self, atom: StyleAtomID, value: T) {
        #[cfg(test)]
        Self::note_copy(&mut self.copied, &self.recent);
        Arc::make_mut(&mut self.recent).insert(atom, value);
        if self.recent.len() > self.base.len() / 8 + 64 {
            #[cfg(test)]
            Self::note_copy(&mut self.copied, &self.base);
            let recent = std::mem::take(&mut self.recent);
            let base = Arc::make_mut(&mut self.base);
            match Arc::try_unwrap(recent) {
                Ok(recent) => base.extend(recent),
                Err(recent) => base.extend(recent.iter().map(|(atom, value)| (*atom, value.clone()))),
            }
        }
    }

    /// Drops whatever the catalog holds of `atoms`.
    fn forget(&mut self, atoms: &[StyleAtomID]) {
        for map in [&mut self.base, &mut self.recent] {
            if atoms.iter().any(|atom| map.contains_key(atom)) {
                let map = Arc::make_mut(map);
                for atom in atoms {
                    map.remove(atom);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The bytes of the catalog's maps that `sizer` reaches for the first time.
    fn heap_size(&self, sizer: &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer) -> usize {
        [&self.base, &self.recent]
            .into_iter()
            .map(|map| sizer.arc_shallow(map) + crate::heap_size::map_bytes(map))
            .sum()
    }

    fn values(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &T> {
        self.iter().map(|(_, value)| value)
    }
}

/// The elements that match `:hover`, which the render owner places as the pointer moves rather than the host writes:
/// a small overlay over the rows, holding the hover chain as placed, and for each generation style reads the hovered
/// elements' facts with the hover fact set. A fork carries it whole, as it is the size of one chain.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct HoverOverlay {
    /// The chain as last placed, which the next transaction takes.
    placed: SmallVec<[StyleNodeID; 16]>,
    committed: HoveredFacts,
    before: HoveredFacts,
    /// The chain as the latest geometry read sealed it, beside the sealed rows.
    sealed: Option<SmallVec<[StyleNodeID; 16]>>,
}

/// The facts of the hovered elements of one generation, the hover fact set, which stand in for their rows' facts.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct HoveredFacts {
    facts: Vec<(StyleNodeID, ElementFacts)>,
    /// A bit per element slot modulo 64, which rules out most elements without a search.
    slots: u64,
}

impl HoveredFacts {
    /// The hovered elements of `chain` that `generation` holds facts of, with the hover fact set.
    fn of(chain: &[StyleNodeID], generation: &ColumnSnapshot<Row, ROWS_PER_CHUNK>) -> Self {
        let mut hovered = Self::default();
        for &node in chain {
            let Some(row) = generation.get(node.element_slot()).filter(|row| row.facts.resident()) else {
                continue;
            };
            let mut facts = row.facts.clone();
            facts.states.insert(StateFact::Hover);
