/// The projection's elements, as a selector is matched against them: their committed
/// facts, their links, and the workspace the evaluation keeps sibling positions in, if any.
pub(in crate::css::style) struct ProjectionSubject<'a> {
    projection: &'a Projection,
    /// Which side of the transaction being taken the elements' facts and relations are read on.
    side: TransactionFactSide,
    /// The outer tree scope asking about a part exposed from a shadow tree.
    part_exposure_scope: Option<TreeScopeID>,
    match_workspace: Option<&'a mut MatchScratch>,
    /// The workspace the evaluation keeps sibling positions in where none is lent to it.
    owned_match_workspace: Option<MatchScratch>,
    positional_index_policy: PositionalIndexPolicy,
    /// The structural read the evaluation noted last, which the candidates of one element note again
    /// one after another.
    last_structural_read: std::cell::Cell<Option<(StyleNodeID, StructuralRead)>>,
}

impl ProjectionSubject<'_> {
    fn workspace_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut MatchScratch> {
        match &mut self.match_workspace {
            Some(workspace) => Some(&mut **workspace),
            None => self.owned_match_workspace.as_mut(),
        }
    }

    /// The distinct hosts the element's part names reach, or the host of the tree it stands in,
    /// which is the only level it has where it exports no part.
    fn part_exposure_hosts_of(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> SmallVec<[StyleNodeID; 1]> {
        let pairs = self.projection.part_hosts_of(node);
        if pairs.is_empty() {
            return self.projection.shadow_host_of(node).into_iter().collect();
        }
        let mut hosts = SmallVec::new();
        for &(_, host) in pairs {
            if !hosts.contains(&host) {
                hosts.push(host);
            }
        }
        hosts
    }
}

impl<'a> SelectorSubject for ProjectionSubject<'a> {
    type Node = StyleNodeID;
    type Tree = ProjectionTree<'a>;
    type Row = ProjectionRow<'a>;
    type Attribute = AttributeFact;
    type Features<'s>
        = ProjectionRow<'a>
    where
        Self: 's;
    type Incomplete = Incomplete;

    #[inline]
    fn tree(&self) -> ProjectionTree<'a> {
        ProjectionTree {
            projection: self.projection,
            side: self.side,
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn row(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID) -> Result<ProjectionRow<'a>, Incomplete> {
        let facts = self
            .projection
            .facts_on(self.side, node)
            .ok_or(Incomplete::MissingFacts(node))?;
        Ok(ProjectionRow {
            facts,
            projection: self.projection,
        })
    }

    #[inline]
    fn features(&self, row: ProjectionRow<'a>) -> ProjectionRow<'a> {
        row
    }

    #[inline]
    fn same_type(&self, row: ProjectionRow<'a>, other: ProjectionRow<'a>) -> bool {
        row.facts.tag == other.facts.tag && row.facts.namespace() == other.facts.namespace()
    }

    #[inline]
    fn attribute_value_atom(&self, attribute: AttributeFact) -> StyleAtomID {
        attribute.value
    }

    #[inline]
    fn attribute_value_text(&self, attribute: AttributeFact) -> Option<TokenizerInput<'_>> {
        self.projection
            .attribute_value_text(attribute.value)
            .map(TokenizerInput::from)
    }

    #[inline]
    fn has_state(&self, row: ProjectionRow<'a>, fact: StateFact) -> bool {
        row.facts.states.contains(fact)
    }

    #[inline]
    fn language_tag(&self, row: ProjectionRow<'a>) -> TokenizerInput<'_> {
        let tag = self
            .projection
            .catalogs
            .language_texts
            .get(&row.facts.language())
            .map_or(&[][..], AsRef::as_ref);
        TokenizerInput::Utf16(tag)
    }

    #[inline]
    fn directionality_is(&self, row: ProjectionRow<'a>, direction: StyleAtomID) -> bool {
        row.facts.directionality() == direction
    }

    #[inline]
    fn has_custom_state(&self, row: ProjectionRow<'a>, state: StyleAtomID) -> bool {
        row.facts.custom_states().contains(&state)
    }

    #[inline]
    fn heading_level(&self, row: ProjectionRow<'a>) -> u8 {
        row.facts.heading_level()
    }

    /// Element children are rows and the links answer for them. A text or comment child is not,
    /// so the element publishes whether it holds one.
    #[inline]
    fn is_empty(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID) -> Result<bool, Incomplete> {
        let row = self.row(node)?;
        Ok(self.projection.first_element_child_on(self.side, node).is_none() && !row.facts.has_text_content())
    }

    #[inline]
    fn is_root(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        self.projection.parent_on(self.side, node).is_none()
    }

    #[inline]
    fn is_node(&self, node: StyleNodeID, named: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        node == named
    }

    #[inline]
    fn has_part(&self, row: ProjectionRow<'a>, part: StyleAtomID) -> bool {
        row.facts.parts().contains(&part)
    }

    fn part_exposure_hosts(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> SmallVec<[StyleNodeID; 1]> {
        self.part_exposure_hosts_of(node)
    }

    fn part_hosts_in_exposure_scope(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> Option<SmallVec<[StyleNodeID; 1]>> {
        let scope = self.part_exposure_scope?;
        let mut hosts = self.part_exposure_hosts_of(node);
        hosts.retain(|host| self.projection.tree_scope(*host) == scope);
        Some(hosts)
    }

    fn exposes_part_to(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID, part: StyleAtomID, host: StyleNodeID) -> Result<bool, Incomplete> {
        let row = self.row(node)?;
        let pairs = self.projection.part_hosts_of(node);
        Ok(match pairs.is_empty() {
            // With no pairing recorded the element is addressable only under the names it carries,
            // and all of them reach the host of the tree it stands in.
            true => row.facts.parts().contains(&part),
            false => pairs
                .iter()
                .any(|&(exposed, exposed_to)| exposed == part && exposed_to == host),
        })
    }

    #[inline]
    fn note_structural_read(&self, node: StyleNodeID, read: StructuralRead) {
        if self.last_structural_read.get() == Some((node, read)) {
            return;
        }
        self.last_structural_read.set(Some((node, read)));
        self.projection.note_structural_read(self.side, node, read);
    }

    const FILTERS_BY_REQUIRED_DISPATCH_BLOOM: bool = true;

    /// A row facts cannot answer for yet is never prejudged.
    #[inline]
    fn may_match_required(&self, required: u64, node: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        self.projection
            .facts_on(self.side, node)
            .is_none_or(|facts| facts.dispatch_bloom(false) & required == required)
    }

    /// NB: Only the workspace the evaluator owns keeps relative answers: an evaluator owning one
    ///     lives while the projection holds still, which is what an answer reads, as the sibling
    ///     positions it keeps do. A lent workspace may outlive a change of facts.
    fn relative_answer_of(
        &mut self,
        list: super::super::selector_evaluation::SelectorListKey,
        anchor: StyleNodeID,
        bindings: &SelectorBindings<StyleNodeID>,
    ) -> Option<bool> {
        let workspace = self.owned_match_workspace.as_ref()?;
        workspace.relative_answer(&RelativeAnswerKey::of_list(list, anchor, bindings))
    }

    fn record_relative_answer_of(
        &mut self,
        list: super::super::selector_evaluation::SelectorListKey,
        anchor: StyleNodeID,
        bindings: &SelectorBindings<StyleNodeID>,
        answer: bool,
    ) {
        if let Some(workspace) = self.owned_match_workspace.as_mut() {
            workspace.insert_relative_answer(RelativeAnswerKey::of_list(list, anchor, bindings), answer);
        }
    }

    const REMEMBERS_SIBLING_ANSWERS: bool = true;

    type WalkAnswers = SiblingAnswerTable;

    /// NB: Only the workspace the evaluator owns keeps sibling answers, as it keeps relative ones.
    fn walk_answers(
        &mut self,
        selector: super::super::selector_evaluation::SelectorKey,
        bindings: &SelectorBindings<StyleNodeID>,
    ) -> Option<SiblingAnswerTable> {
        let key = SiblingAnswerKey {
            selector,
            scope_shadow_root: bindings.scope_shadow_root,
            scope_root_instance: bindings.scope_root_instance,
            part_exposure_scope: self.part_exposure_scope,
        };
        let workspace = self.owned_match_workspace.as_mut()?;
        Some(workspace.sibling_table(key))
    }

    fn walk_answer(&self, table: SiblingAnswerTable, node: StyleNodeID) -> Option<bool> {
        let workspace = self.owned_match_workspace.as_ref()?;
        workspace.sibling_answer(table, node)
    }

    fn record_walk_answers(&mut self, table: SiblingAnswerTable, nodes: &[StyleNodeID], answer: bool) {
        if let Some(workspace) = self.owned_match_workspace.as_mut() {
            for &node in nodes {
                workspace.insert_sibling_answer(table, node, answer);
            }
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn sibling_index(&mut self, position: NthPosition, node: StyleNodeID) -> Result<Option<i64>, Incomplete> {
        if position.step == 0 && self.positional_index_policy != PositionalIndexPolicy::All {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let (projection, fact_side) = (self.projection, self.side);
        let Some(workspace) = self.workspace_mut() else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        workspace.indexed_sibling_position(
            position,
            node,
            SiblingSequenceSource {
                parent: projection.parent_on(fact_side, node),
                children: |parent| projection.children_on(fact_side, parent).collect(),
                type_of: |sibling| {
                    let facts = projection
                        .facts_on(fact_side, sibling)
                        .ok_or(Incomplete::MissingFacts(sibling))?;
                    Ok((facts.tag, facts.namespace()))
                },
            },
        )
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const DIV: StyleAtomID = StyleAtomID(1);
    const THEME: StyleAtomID = StyleAtomID(10);
    const ITEM: StyleAtomID = StyleAtomID(11);
    const HREF: StyleAtomID = StyleAtomID(20);
    const HREF_VALUE: StyleAtomID = StyleAtomID(21);

    fn element(index: u32) -> StyleNodeID {
        StyleNodeID::element(index)
    }

    /// `root > [first.item, second.item[href], third]`, root carrying `.theme`.
    fn document() -> Projection {
        let mut projection = Projection::default();
        for index in 1..=4 {
            projection.mint(element(index));
            projection.set_connected(element(index), true);
            projection.set_tag(element(index), DIV);
        }
        projection.set_class(element(1), THEME, true);
        projection.set_first_element_child(element(1), Some(element(2)));
        for index in 2..=4 {
            projection.set_parent(element(index), Some(element(1)));
            projection.set_previous_element_sibling(element(index), (index > 2).then(|| element(index - 1)));
            projection.set_next_element_sibling(element(index), (index < 4).then(|| element(index + 1)));
        }
        projection.set_class(element(2), ITEM, true);
        projection.set_class(element(3), ITEM, true);
        projection.set_attribute(element(3), HREF, HREF_VALUE, true);
        projection.commit();
        projection
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_catalog_copies_only_what_was_added_since_its_base_was_folded() {
        let mut catalog: Catalog<u32> = Catalog::default();
        let mut published = Vec::new();
        for index in 1..=10_000_u32 {
            catalog.insert(StyleAtomID(index), index);
            published.push(catalog.clone());
            if published.len() > 2 {
                published.remove(0);
            }
        }
        assert_eq!(catalog.get(&StyleAtomID(1)), Some(&1));
        assert_eq!(catalog.get(&StyleAtomID(10_000)), Some(&10_000));
        assert_eq!(catalog.iter().count(), 10_000);
        // NB: Copying the whole catalog for each addition would copy about 50 million entries.
        assert!(
            catalog.copied < 10_000 * 10_000 / 8,
            "additions copied {} entries",
            catalog.copied
        );
        catalog.forget(&[StyleAtomID(1), StyleAtomID(10_000)]);
        assert!(!catalog.contains_key(&StyleAtomID(1)) && !catalog.contains_key(&StyleAtomID(10_000)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn live_atoms_are_those_the_rows_hold_with_their_attribute_name_forms() {
        let mut projection = Projection::default();
        let node = element(1);
        projection.mint(node);
        projection.set_tag(node, StyleAtomID(1));
        projection.set_folded_tag(node, StyleAtomID(2));
        projection.set_id(node, StyleAtomID(3));
        projection.set_language(node, StyleAtomID(4));
        projection.set_namespace(node, StyleAtomID(5));
        projection.set_part_exposure(node, StyleAtomID(6));
        projection.set_directionality(node, StyleAtomID(7));
        projection.set_custom_states(node, &[StyleAtomID(8)]);
        projection.set_parts(node, &[StyleAtomID(9)]);
        projection.set_class(node, StyleAtomID(10), true);
        let forms = AttributeNameForms {
            local: StyleAtomID(13),
            folded_name: StyleAtomID(14),
            folded_local: StyleAtomID(15),
        };
        projection.note_attribute_name_forms(StyleAtomID(11), forms);
        projection.note_attribute_name_forms(StyleAtomID(16), forms);
        projection.set_attribute(node, StyleAtomID(11), StyleAtomID(12), true);
        projection.commit();
        projection.release();

        let mut atoms = HashSet::default();
        assert_eq!(projection.collect_atoms(&mut atoms), 2);
        assert_eq!(atoms, (1..=15).map(StyleAtomID).collect());

        // A name another root keeps live keeps its forms live with it.
        let mut live: HashSet<StyleAtomID> = [StyleAtomID(16)].into_iter().collect();
        projection.extend_live_attribute_name_forms(&mut live);
        assert_eq!(live, [16, 13, 14, 15].into_iter().map(StyleAtomID).collect());

        projection.retire(node);
        projection.forget(node);
        projection.release();
        let mut atoms = HashSet::default();
        projection.collect_atoms(&mut atoms);
        assert!(atoms.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_tree_reads_links() {
        let projection = document();
        assert_eq!(
            projection.children(element(1)).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            [element(2), element(3), element(4)]
        );
        assert_eq!(projection.preorder(element(1)).count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(projection.ancestors(element(4)).collect::<Vec<_>>(), [element(1)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_element_without_facts_is_incomplete_rather_than_featureless() {
        let mut projection = document();
        projection.mint(element(5));
        projection.commit();
        assert!(projection.facts(element(5)).is_none());
        let mut subject = projection.subject_on(TransactionFactSide::After);
        assert!(matches!(subject.row(element(5)), Err(Incomplete::MissingFacts(_))));
        projection.ensure_facts(element(5));
        assert!(
            projection
                .subject_on(TransactionFactSide::After)
                .row(element(5))
                .is_err(),
            "facts are read as the last transaction committed them"
        );
        projection.commit();
        assert!(
            projection
                .subject_on(TransactionFactSide::After)
                .row(element(5))
                .is_ok()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn facts_are_kept_sorted_and_edits_that_change_nothing_are_free() {
        let mut projection = document();
        projection.set_class(element(2), StyleAtomID(5), true);
        projection.set_class(element(2), StyleAtomID(50), true);
        projection.set_class(element(2), ITEM, false);
        projection.commit();
        let facts = projection.facts(element(2)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(facts.classes(), [StyleAtomID(5), StyleAtomID(50)]);
        projection.set_attribute(element(3), HREF, StyleAtomID(22), true);
        projection.set_attribute(element(3), StyleAtomID(15), StyleAtomID::NONE, true);
        projection.commit();
        let attributes = projection.facts(element(3)).unwrap().attributes();
        assert_eq!(
            attributes
                .iter()
                .map(|attribute| (attribute.name, attribute.value))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            [(StyleAtomID(15), StyleAtomID::NONE), (HREF, StyleAtomID(22))]
        );

        let mut fork = projection.clone();
        let version = fork.test_writer.rows_version();
        fork.set_class(element(2), StyleAtomID(5), true);
        fork.set_attribute(element(3), HREF, StyleAtomID(22), true);
        assert_eq!(
            fork.test_writer.rows_version(),
            version,
            "an edit that changes nothing copies no chunk"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_dispatch_bloom_follows_the_facts() {
        let mut projection = document();
        projection.note_attribute_name_forms(
            HREF,
            AttributeNameForms {
                local: StyleAtomID(22),
                folded_name: StyleAtomID::NONE,
                folded_local: StyleAtomID::NONE,
            },
        );
        projection.set_attribute(element(4), HREF, HREF_VALUE, true);
        projection.commit();
        let facts = projection.facts(element(4)).unwrap();
        let mut probes = Vec::new();
        projection.for_each_dispatch_probe(facts, true, |key, value| probes.push((key, value)));
        assert!(probes.contains(&(DispatchKey::Root, None)));
        assert!(probes.contains(&(DispatchKey::AttributeName(HREF), Some(HREF_VALUE))));
        assert!(probes.contains(&(DispatchKey::AttributeName(StyleAtomID(22)), Some(HREF_VALUE))));
        for (key, _) in probes {
            assert_ne!(facts.dispatch_bloom(true) & dispatch_bloom_bit(key), 0);
        }
        assert_eq!(facts.dispatch_bloom(false) & dispatch_bloom_bit(DispatchKey::Root), 0);

        projection.set_class(element(4), THEME, true);
        assert_eq!(
            projection.facts(element(4)).unwrap().dispatch_bloom(false) & dispatch_bloom_bit(DispatchKey::Class(THEME)),
            0,
            "an uncommitted write is not read"
        );
        projection.commit();
        assert_ne!(
            projection.facts(element(4)).unwrap().dispatch_bloom(false) & dispatch_bloom_bit(DispatchKey::Class(THEME)),
            0
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn written_links_are_noted_until_the_transaction_is_released() {
        let mut projection = document();
        projection.release();
        assert!(!projection.has_written_links());

        // Facts alone write no links.
        projection.set_class(element(4), ITEM, true);
        assert!(!projection.has_written_links());

        let relations = projection.written_relations(element(4)).unwrap();

        projection.write_relations(element(4), None);
        projection.write_relations(
            element(3),
            Some(TreeRelations {
                next_element_sibling: None,
                ..projection.written_relations(element(3)).unwrap()
            }),
        );
        assert!(projection.relations_were_written(element(4)));
        assert!(projection.relations_were_written(element(3)));
        assert!(!projection.relations_were_written(element(2)));
        projection.set_first_element_child(element(2), None);
        assert!(
            !projection.relations_were_written(element(2)),
            "a first element child is no relation"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            projection.links_written().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            [element(4), element(3), element(2)]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            projection.relations_written().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            [element(4), element(3)]
        );
        assert_eq!(projection.written_relations(element(4)), None);
        assert_eq!(projection.committed_relations(element(4)), Some(relations));

        projection.commit();
        assert!(projection.has_written_links(), "the barrier settles what was written");
        assert_eq!(projection.committed_relations(element(4)), None);
        projection.release();
        assert!(!projection.has_written_links());
        assert!(!projection.relations_were_written(element(4)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_fork_shares_rows_until_either_side_writes() {
        let projection = document();
        let mut fork = projection.clone();
        fork.set_class(element(4), ITEM, true);
        fork.set_folded_tag(element(4), StyleAtomID(2));
        fork.set_folded_tag(element(3), DIV);
        fork.commit();
        assert!(projection.facts(element(4)).unwrap().classes().is_empty());
        assert_eq!(fork.facts(element(4)).unwrap().classes(), [ITEM]);
        assert_eq!(fork.facts(element(4)).unwrap().folded_tag(), StyleAtomID(2));
        assert_eq!(fork.facts(element(3)).unwrap().folded_tag(), StyleAtomID::NONE);
        // The class list of an untouched element is the same allocation on both sides.
        let ours = projection.facts(element(2)).unwrap().classes();
        let theirs = fork.facts(element(2)).unwrap().classes();
        assert!(!ours.is_empty() && std::ptr::eq(ours.as_ptr(), theirs.as_ptr()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn shadow_trees_and_slots_shape_the_style_order() {
        // host(1) -> shadow root(2) -> slot(3); host's light child 4 is assigned to the slot, its
        // light child 5 is not; text 1 is assigned too.
        let mut projection = Projection::default();
        for index in 1..=5 {
            projection.mint(element(index));
        }
        projection.set_shadow_root(element(1), element(2));
        projection.set_first_element_child(element(2), Some(element(3)));
        projection.set_parent(element(3), Some(element(2)));
        projection.set_first_element_child(element(1), Some(element(4)));
        projection.set_parent(element(4), Some(element(1)));
        projection.set_next_element_sibling(element(4), Some(element(5)));
        projection.set_parent(element(5), Some(element(1)));
        projection.set_previous_element_sibling(element(5), Some(element(4)));
        projection.set_assigned_slot(element(4), Some(element(3)));
        let text = StyleNodeID::text(1);
        projection.set_assigned_nodes(element(3), &[element(4), text]);
        projection.commit();

        assert_eq!(projection.host_of(element(2)), Some(element(1)));
        assert_eq!(projection.inheritance_parent(element(3)), Some(element(1)));
        assert_eq!(projection.inheritance_parent(element(4)), Some(element(3)));
        assert_eq!(projection.shadow_host_of(element(3)), Some(element(1)));
        assert_eq!(projection.assigned_slot_of(text), Some(element(3)));
        assert_eq!(
            projection.style_preorder(element(1)).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            [element(1), element(3), element(4), element(5)]
        );

        projection.retire_texts([text]);
        assert_eq!(projection.assigned_nodes_of(element(3)), [element(4)]);
        projection.retire(element(4));
        assert!(projection.assigned_nodes_of(element(3)).is_empty());
        projection.retire(element(3));
        projection.retire(element(2));
        assert_eq!(projection.shadow_root_of(element(1)), None);

        // A new root for the host unpairs the old one.
        projection.mint(element(2));
        projection.mint(element(6));
        projection.set_shadow_root(element(1), element(2));
        projection.set_shadow_root(element(1), element(6));
        assert_eq!(projection.host_of(element(2)), None);
        assert_eq!(projection.host_of(element(6)), Some(element(1)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn forgotten_atoms_leave_the_catalogs() {
        let mut projection = document();
        let text: Vec<u16> = "https://example.com".encode_utf16().collect();
        projection.set_attribute_value_text(HREF_VALUE, RetainedUtf16FlyString::from_utf16(&text));
        projection.set_attribute_value_text(HREF_VALUE, RetainedUtf16FlyString::from_utf16(&[]));
        assert_eq!(
            projection
                .attribute_value_text(HREF_VALUE)
                .map(RetainedUtf16FlyString::to_utf16)
                .as_deref(),
            Some(&text[..])
        );
        projection.set_language(element(2), StyleAtomID(30));
        projection.set_language_text(StyleAtomID(30), &[u16::from(b'e'), u16::from(b'n')]);
        projection.commit();
        assert_eq!(projection.language_tag_of(element(2)).len(), 2);
        projection.forget_atoms(&[HREF_VALUE, StyleAtomID(30)]);
        assert_eq!(projection.attribute_value_text(HREF_VALUE), None);
        assert!(projection.language_tag_of(element(2)).is_empty());

        projection.forget(element(2));
        assert!(projection.facts(element(2)).is_some());
        projection.commit();
        assert!(projection.facts(element(2)).is_none());
        assert!(projection.is_live(element(2)));
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The facts of an element beside its tag and states: its id, namespace, language,
//! directionality, tree scope and assigned slot, and its lists of classes, attributes, parts and
//! custom states. They are packed into one allocation behind one pointer, which holds only what the
//! element has and which a row holding none of them leaves null. The process interns them by
//! content: siblings and cousins published alike point at one allocation, in every generation of
//! the rows.

use super::super::super::index::AttributeFact;
use super::super::super::index::StyleAtomID;
use crate::css::style::tree::{StyleNodeID, TreeScopeID};
use smallvec::SmallVec;
use std::alloc::Layout;
use std::ptr::NonNull;
use std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32;
use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;

/// Which optional atoms and lists an allocation holds.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Present(u16);

impl Present {
    // Atoms, in the order their words follow the header.
    const FOLDED_TAG: u16 = 1 << 0;
    const PART_EXPOSURE: u16 = 1 << 1;
    const NAMESPACE: u16 = 1 << 2;
    const ID: u16 = 1 << 3;
    const LANGUAGE: u16 = 1 << 4;
    const DIRECTIONALITY: u16 = 1 << 5;
    const TREE_SCOPE: u16 = 1 << 6;
    const ASSIGNED_SLOT: u16 = 1 << 7;
    const ATOMS: u16 = 0xff;
    // Lists, whose counts follow the atoms' words, in this order, and whose payloads follow the counts.
    const CLASSES: u16 = 1 << 8;
    const ATTRIBUTES: u16 = 1 << 9;
    const PARTS: u16 = 1 << 10;
    const CUSTOM_STATES: u16 = 1 << 11;
    const LISTS: [u16; 4] = [Self::CLASSES, Self::ATTRIBUTES, Self::PARTS, Self::CUSTOM_STATES];

    fn has(self, bit: u16) -> bool {
        self.0 & bit != 0
    }

    /// How many words of `bits` that come before `bit` the allocation holds.
    fn words_before(self, bits: u16, bit: u16) -> usize {
        (self.0 & bits & (bit - 1)).count_ones() as usize
    }

    fn atom_words(self) -> usize {
        (self.0 & Self::ATOMS).count_ones() as usize
    }

    fn count_words(self) -> usize {
        (self.0 & !Self::ATOMS).count_ones() as usize
    }
}

/// The start of a packed allocation: a word per atom the element has, then a count per list it has, then the lists'
/// entries, classes, attributes (two words each), parts and custom states.
#[repr(C)]
struct Header {
    references: AtomicU32,
    present: Present,
    // NB: Two bytes stay free here.
    _free: u16,
    /// The Bloom summary of the dispatch keys the lists carry, low half first.
    bloom: [u32; 2],
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Header>() == 16 && align_of::<Header>() == 4);
// NB: Every word that follows the header is a u32.
const _: () = assert!(align_of::<StyleAtomID>() == 4 && size_of::<StyleAtomID>() == 4);
const _: () = assert!(align_of::<AttributeFact>() == 4 && size_of::<AttributeFact>() == 8);

/// The rare facts of one element, shared by every copy of its row.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct FactLists(Option<NonNull<Header>>);

// SAFETY: The allocation is immutable once made, and its reference count is atomic.
unsafe impl Send for FactLists {}
// SAFETY: As above.
unsafe impl Sync for FactLists {}

/// The identity of one allocation of lists, which interning makes one per content.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct FactListsIdentity(Option<NonNull<Header>>);

/// The words of every list's entries, by `Present::LISTS` order.
fn entry_words(counts: [u32; 4]) -> [usize; 4] {
    [
        counts[0] as usize,
        2 * counts[1] as usize,
        counts[2] as usize,
        counts[3] as usize,
    ]
}

fn layout(present: Present, counts: [u32; 4]) -> Layout {
    let words = present.atom_words() + present.count_words() + entry_words(counts).iter().sum::<usize>();
    Layout::from_size_align(size_of::<Header>() + 4 * words, align_of::<Header>())
        .expect("an element's fact lists fit in memory")
}

impl FactLists {
    fn new(edit: &FactListsEdit) -> Self {
        if edit.is_empty() {
            return Self(None);
        }
        let count = |length: usize| u32::try_from(length).expect("an element's fact list fits in u32");
        let counts = [
            count(edit.classes.len()),
            count(edit.attributes.len()),
            count(edit.parts.len()),
            count(edit.custom_states.len()),
        ];
        let atoms: [(u16, u32); 8] = [
            (Present::FOLDED_TAG, edit.folded_tag.0),
            (Present::PART_EXPOSURE, edit.part_exposure.0),
            (Present::NAMESPACE, edit.namespace.0),
            (Present::ID, edit.id.0),
            (Present::LANGUAGE, edit.language.0),
            (Present::DIRECTIONALITY, edit.directionality.0),
            (Present::TREE_SCOPE, edit.tree_scope.0),
            (Present::ASSIGNED_SLOT, edit.assigned_slot.map_or(0, StyleNodeID::raw)),
        ];
        let mut present = Present::default();
        for &(bit, word) in &atoms {
            if word != 0 {
                present.0 |= bit;
            }
        }
        for (bit, &count) in Present::LISTS.iter().zip(&counts) {
            if count != 0 {
                present.0 |= bit;
            }
        }
        let layout = layout(present, counts);
        // SAFETY: The layout is never zero-sized, as it holds the header.
        let pointer = unsafe { std::alloc::alloc(layout) }.cast::<Header>();
        let Some(header) = NonNull::new(pointer) else {
            std::alloc::handle_alloc_error(layout);
        };
        // SAFETY: The allocation holds the header and the words after it, and every write stays within it.
        unsafe {
            header.write(Header {
                references: AtomicU32::new(1),
                present,
                _free: 0,
                bloom: [edit.bloom as u32, (edit.bloom >> 32) as u32],
            });
            let mut cursor = header.as_ptr().add(1).cast::<u32>();
            for &(_, word) in atoms.iter().filter(|&&(_, word)| word != 0) {
                cursor.write(word);
                cursor = cursor.add(1);
            }
            for &count in counts.iter().filter(|&&count| count != 0) {
                cursor.write(count);
                cursor = cursor.add(1);
            }
            let mut cursor = cursor.cast::<StyleAtomID>();
            cursor.copy_from_nonoverlapping(edit.classes.as_ptr(), edit.classes.len());
            cursor = cursor.add(edit.classes.len());
            cursor
                .cast::<AttributeFact>()
                .copy_from_nonoverlapping(edit.attributes.as_ptr(), edit.attributes.len());
            cursor = cursor.add(2 * edit.attributes.len());
            cursor.copy_from_nonoverlapping(edit.parts.as_ptr(), edit.parts.len());
            cursor = cursor.add(edit.parts.len());
            cursor.copy_from_nonoverlapping(edit.custom_states.as_ptr(), edit.custom_states.len());
        }
        Self(Some(header))
    }

    fn header(&self) -> Option<&Header> {
        // SAFETY: The allocation lives while this reference to it does.
        self.0.map(|header| unsafe { header.as_ref() })
    }

    /// The words that follow the header.
    fn words(header: &Header) -> *const u32 {
        // SAFETY: The words follow the header in its allocation.
        unsafe { std::ptr::from_ref(header).add(1).cast::<u32>() }
    }

    /// The word of the atom `bit`, where the allocation holds one.
    fn atom(&self, bit: u16) -> Option<u32> {
        let header = self.header()?;
        if !header.present.has(bit) {
            return None;
        }
        // SAFETY: A present atom's word is among the atom words that follow the header.
        Some(unsafe {
            Self::words(header)
                .add(header.present.words_before(Present::ATOMS, bit))
                .read()
        })
    }

    /// The counts of every list, by `Present::LISTS` order.
    fn counts(header: &Header) -> [u32; 4] {
        let present = header.present;
        let first_count = present.atom_words();
        Present::LISTS.map(|bit| match present.has(bit) {
            // SAFETY: A present list's count is among the count words that follow the atom words.
            true => unsafe {
                Self::words(header)
                    .add(first_count + present.words_before(!Present::ATOMS, bit))
                    .read()
            },
            false => 0,
        })
    }

    /// The first atom of list `list`, an index into `Present::LISTS`, and its length.
    fn list(&self, list: usize) -> Option<(*const StyleAtomID, usize)> {
        let header = self.header()?;
        if !header.present.has(Present::LISTS[list]) {
            return None;
        }
        let counts = Self::counts(header);
        let offset = header.present.atom_words()
            + header.present.count_words()
            + entry_words(counts).iter().take(list).sum::<usize>();
        // SAFETY: The offset stays within the allocation, which holds every list.
        let first = unsafe { Self::words(header).add(offset).cast::<StyleAtomID>() };
        Some((first, counts[list] as usize))
    }

    fn atoms(&self, list: usize) -> &[StyleAtomID] {
        match self.list(list) {
            // SAFETY: The list was written when the allocation was made, and lives with it.
            Some((first, length)) => unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(first, length) },
            None => &[],
        }
    }

    /// Sorted.
    pub(super) fn classes(&self) -> &[StyleAtomID] {
        self.atoms(0)
    }

    /// Sorted by name, each with the atom of its value.
    pub(super) fn attributes(&self) -> &[AttributeFact] {
        match self.list(1) {
            // SAFETY: The attributes were written as such when the allocation was made, and live
            //         with it.
            Some((first, length)) => unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(first.cast::<AttributeFact>(), length) },
            None => &[],
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn parts(&self) -> &[StyleAtomID] {
        self.atoms(2)
    }

    pub(super) fn custom_states(&self) -> &[StyleAtomID] {
        self.atoms(3)
    }

    pub(super) fn folded_tag(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        StyleAtomID(self.atom(Present::FOLDED_TAG).unwrap_or(0))
    }

    pub(super) fn part_exposure(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        StyleAtomID(self.atom(Present::PART_EXPOSURE).unwrap_or(0))
    }

    pub(super) fn namespace(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        StyleAtomID(self.atom(Present::NAMESPACE).unwrap_or(0))
    }

    pub(super) fn id(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        StyleAtomID(self.atom(Present::ID).unwrap_or(0))
    }

    pub(super) fn language(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        StyleAtomID(self.atom(Present::LANGUAGE).unwrap_or(0))
    }

    pub(super) fn directionality(&self) -> StyleAtomID {
        StyleAtomID(self.atom(Present::DIRECTIONALITY).unwrap_or(0))
    }

    pub(super) fn tree_scope(&self) -> TreeScopeID {
        self.atom(Present::TREE_SCOPE)
            .map_or(TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT, TreeScopeID)
    }

    pub(super) fn assigned_slot(&self) -> Option<StyleNodeID> {
        self.atom(Present::ASSIGNED_SLOT).and_then(StyleNodeID::from_raw)
    }

    /// The Bloom summary of the dispatch keys the lists carry.
    pub(super) fn identity(&self) -> FactListsIdentity {
        FactListsIdentity(self.0)
    }

    pub(super) fn bloom(&self) -> u64 {
        self.header().map_or(0, |header| {
            u64::from(header.bloom[0]) | (u64::from(header.bloom[1]) << 32)
        })
    }

    /// The facts to edit, whose lists stay borrowed until an edit changes them.
    pub(super) fn edit(&self) -> FactListsEdit<'_> {
        FactListsEdit {
            classes: EditedList::Held(self.classes()),
            attributes: EditedList::Held(self.attributes()),
            parts: EditedList::Held(self.parts()),
            custom_states: EditedList::Held(self.custom_states()),
            folded_tag: self.folded_tag(),
            part_exposure: self.part_exposure(),
            namespace: self.namespace(),
            id: self.id(),
            language: self.language(),
            directionality: self.directionality(),
            bloom: self.bloom(),
            tree_scope: self.tree_scope(),
            assigned_slot: self.assigned_slot(),
        }
    }

    fn holds_the_same_as(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.classes() == other.classes()
            && self.attributes() == other.attributes()
            && self.parts() == other.parts()
            && self.custom_states() == other.custom_states()
            && self.folded_tag() == other.folded_tag()
            && self.part_exposure() == other.part_exposure()
            && self.namespace() == other.namespace()
            && self.id() == other.id()
            && self.language() == other.language()
            && self.directionality() == other.directionality()
            && self.bloom() == other.bloom()
            && self.tree_scope() == other.tree_scope()
            && self.assigned_slot() == other.assigned_slot()
    }

    /// Whether the two hold the same facts of their elements, leaving aside their tree scopes and assigned slots, which
    /// are their elements' links.
    pub(super) fn says_the_same_as(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.0 == other.0
            || (self.classes() == other.classes()
                && self.attributes() == other.attributes()
                && self.parts() == other.parts()
                && self.custom_states() == other.custom_states()
                && self.folded_tag() == other.folded_tag()
                && self.part_exposure() == other.part_exposure()
                && self.namespace() == other.namespace()
                && self.id() == other.id()
                && self.language() == other.language()
                && self.directionality() == other.directionality())
    }

    /// Whether these are the facts `edit` holds.
    fn holds(&self, edit: &FactListsEdit) -> bool {
        self.classes() == &*edit.classes
            && self.attributes() == &*edit.attributes
            && self.parts() == &*edit.parts
            && self.custom_states() == &*edit.custom_states
            && self.folded_tag() == edit.folded_tag
            && self.part_exposure() == edit.part_exposure
            && self.namespace() == edit.namespace
            && self.id() == edit.id
            && self.language() == edit.language
            && self.directionality() == edit.directionality
            && self.bloom() == edit.bloom
            && self.tree_scope() == edit.tree_scope
            && self.assigned_slot() == edit.assigned_slot
    }

    /// The hash of what the lists hold, as [`FactListsEdit::content_hash`] gives it for an edit holding the same.
    fn content_hash(&self) -> u64 {
        self.edit().content_hash()
    }

    /// How many references to the allocation are live, the interning table's among them.
    fn references(&self) -> u32 {
        self.header()
            .map_or(0, |header| header.references.load(Ordering::Acquire))
    }

    pub(super) fn heap_size(&self, sizer: &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer) -> usize {
        match self.header() {
            // NB: The process's table holds an entry for every list, which the first document whose rows reach the
            //     list counts with it.
            Some(header) if sizer.first_sight(std::ptr::from_ref(header)) => {
                layout(header.present, Self::counts(header)).size()
                    + crate::heap_size::live_hash_table_bytes(1, size_of::<Self>())
            }
            _ => 0,
        }
    }
}

impl Clone for FactLists {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        if let Some(header) = self.header() {
            let references = header.references.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            assert!(references < u32::MAX / 2, "fact lists reference count overflow");
        }
        Self(self.0)
    }
}

impl Drop for FactLists {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let Some(header) = self.header() else {
            return;
        };
        if header.references.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Release) != 1 {
            return;
        }
        // NB: This load orders us after every earlier decrement, as a fence would. ThreadSanitizer does not model fences.
        let _ = header.references.load(Ordering::Acquire);
        let layout = layout(header.present, Self::counts(header));
        // SAFETY: This was the last reference, so nothing reads the allocation after this.
        unsafe { std::alloc::dealloc(self.0.expect("the header was read").as_ptr().cast(), layout) };
    }
}

impl PartialEq for FactLists {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.0 == other.0 || (self.0.is_some() && other.0.is_some() && self.holds_the_same_as(other))
    }
}

/// One list of an edit: the list as it stands until the edit changes it.
pub(super) enum EditedList<'a, T: Copy, const INLINE: usize> {
    Held(&'a [T]),
    Changed(SmallVec<[T; INLINE]>),
}

impl<T: Copy, const INLINE: usize> EditedList<'_, T, INLINE> {
    pub(super) fn to_mut(&mut self) -> &mut SmallVec<[T; INLINE]> {
        if let Self::Held(list) = *self {
            *self = Self::Changed(SmallVec::from_slice(list));
        }
        match self {
            Self::Changed(list) => list,
            Self::Held(_) => unreachable!("the list was just copied out"),
        }
    }
}

impl<T: Copy, const INLINE: usize> std::ops::Deref for EditedList<'_, T, INLINE> {
    type Target = [T];

    fn deref(&self) -> &[T] {
        match self {
            Self::Held(list) => list,
            Self::Changed(list) => list,
        }
    }
}

/// The rare facts of an element, to edit.
pub(super) struct FactListsEdit<'a> {
    pub(super) classes: EditedList<'a, StyleAtomID, 4>,
    pub(super) attributes: EditedList<'a, AttributeFact, 4>,
    pub(super) parts: EditedList<'a, StyleAtomID, 2>,
    pub(super) custom_states: EditedList<'a, StyleAtomID, 2>,
    pub(super) folded_tag: StyleAtomID,
    pub(super) part_exposure: StyleAtomID,
    pub(super) namespace: StyleAtomID,
    pub(super) id: StyleAtomID,
    pub(super) language: StyleAtomID,
    pub(super) directionality: StyleAtomID,
    /// The Bloom summary of the dispatch keys the lists carry, which the writer computes before it makes them.
    pub(super) bloom: u64,
    pub(super) tree_scope: TreeScopeID,
    pub(super) assigned_slot: Option<StyleNodeID>,
}

impl FactListsEdit<'_> {
    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.classes.is_empty()
            && self.attributes.is_empty()
            && self.parts.is_empty()
            && self.custom_states.is_empty()
            && self.folded_tag.is_none()
            && self.part_exposure.is_none()
            && self.namespace.is_none()
            && self.id.is_none()
            && self.language.is_none()
            && self.directionality.is_none()
            && self.tree_scope == TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT
            && self.assigned_slot.is_none()
    }

    fn content_hash(&self) -> u64 {
        use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
        let mut hasher = crate::fast_hash::fast_hasher();
        self.classes.hash(&mut hasher);
        for attribute in self.attributes.iter() {
            (attribute.name, attribute.value).hash(&mut hasher);
        }
        self.parts.hash(&mut hasher);
        self.custom_states.hash(&mut hasher);
        (
            self.folded_tag,
            self.part_exposure,
            self.namespace,
            self.id,
            self.language,
            self.directionality,
            self.bloom,
            self.tree_scope,
            self.assigned_slot,
        )
            .hash(&mut hasher);
        hasher.finish()
    }
}

/// The fact lists of the process, by content: one allocation per content while any row of any
/// document holds it, so that rows holding the same facts hold the same pointer. Each entry is
/// the lists' pointer alone, found by the hash of their content, which the table recomputes from
/// the lists themselves as it grows.
pub(crate) struct FactListsTable {
    lists: hashbrown::HashTable<FactLists>,
    /// How many lists the table holds before it drops those only it holds: twice as many as the
    /// last drop kept, so dropping costs a constant per list interned.
    drop_threshold: usize,
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<FactLists>() == 8);

/// How many lists the table holds before it first drops those only it holds.
const MINIMUM_DROP_THRESHOLD: usize = 1024;

impl Default for FactListsTable {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            lists: hashbrown::HashTable::new(),
            drop_threshold: MINIMUM_DROP_THRESHOLD,
        }
    }
}

impl FactListsTable {
    /// The fact lists holding what `edit` holds, whose content hashes to `hash`.
    fn intern(&mut self, edit: &FactListsEdit, hash: u64) -> FactLists {
        if let Some(lists) = self.lists.find(hash, |lists| lists.holds(edit)) {
            return lists.clone();
        }
        if self.lists.len() >= self.drop_threshold {
            self.drop_unheld();
        }
        let lists = FactLists::new(edit);
        self.lists.insert_unique(hash, lists.clone(), FactLists::content_hash);
        lists
    }

    /// Drops the lists no row holds any more.
    fn drop_unheld(&mut self) {
        self.lists.retain(|lists| lists.references() > 1);
        self.drop_threshold = (2 * self.lists.len()).max(MINIMUM_DROP_THRESHOLD);
    }
}

/// How many fact lists a writer keeps to share without asking the process's table, each in the slot its content
/// hashes to.
const RECENT_FACT_LISTS: usize = 64;

/// The fact lists a writer made last, by the hash of what they hold, which an element made the same facts again shares
/// without taking the process's table's lock, as siblings and cousins published alike do.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct RecentFactLists(Box<[FactLists; RECENT_FACT_LISTS]>);

impl Default for RecentFactLists {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self(Box::new(std::array::from_fn(|_| FactLists::default())))
    }
}

impl RecentFactLists {
    /// Fact lists holding what `edit` holds: one made recently where one holds it, or the ones the
    /// process's table interned.
    pub(super) fn make(&mut self, edit: &FactListsEdit, table: &std::sync::Mutex<FactListsTable>) -> FactLists {
        if edit.is_empty() {
            return FactLists(None);
        }
        let hash = edit.content_hash();
        let slot = &mut self.0[(hash % RECENT_FACT_LISTS as u64) as usize];
        if slot.0.is_some() && slot.holds(edit) {
            return slot.clone();
        }
        let lists = table
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)
            .intern(edit, hash);
        *slot = lists.clone();
        lists
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn lists_hash_as_the_edit_they_were_made_from() {
        let edit = FactListsEdit {
            classes: EditedList::Held(&[StyleAtomID(1), StyleAtomID(2)]),
            attributes: EditedList::Held(&[AttributeFact {
                name: StyleAtomID(3),
                value: StyleAtomID(4),
            }]),
            parts: EditedList::Held(&[StyleAtomID(5)]),
            custom_states: EditedList::Held(&[StyleAtomID(6)]),
            folded_tag: StyleAtomID(7),
            part_exposure: StyleAtomID(8),
            namespace: StyleAtomID(9),
            id: StyleAtomID(10),
            language: StyleAtomID(11),
            directionality: StyleAtomID(12),
            bloom: 0x1234_5678_9abc_def0,
            tree_scope: TreeScopeID(13),
            assigned_slot: StyleNodeID::from_raw(14),
        };
        let lists = FactLists::new(&edit);
        assert_eq!(lists.content_hash(), edit.content_hash());
        assert!(lists.holds(&edit));
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_combination_of_atoms_reads_back() {
        for mask in 0_u32..256 {
            let atom = |bit: u32, value: u32| if mask & (1 << bit) != 0 { value } else { 0 };
            let empty = FactLists::default();
            let mut edit = empty.edit();
            edit.folded_tag = StyleAtomID(atom(0, 11));
            edit.part_exposure = StyleAtomID(atom(1, 12));
            edit.namespace = StyleAtomID(atom(2, 13));
            edit.id = StyleAtomID(atom(3, 14));
            edit.language = StyleAtomID(atom(4, 15));
            edit.directionality = StyleAtomID(atom(5, 16));
            edit.tree_scope = TreeScopeID(atom(6, 17));
            edit.assigned_slot = StyleNodeID::from_raw(atom(7, 18));
            edit.classes = EditedList::Changed(SmallVec::from_slice(&[StyleAtomID(20 + mask)]));
            edit.parts = EditedList::Held(&[StyleAtomID(21), StyleAtomID(22)]);
            let lists = FactLists::new(&edit);
            assert!(lists.holds(&edit), "mask {mask:#x}");
            assert_eq!(lists.classes(), &*edit.classes);
            assert_eq!(lists.parts(), &*edit.parts);
            assert!(lists.attributes().is_empty() && lists.custom_states().is_empty());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn long_lists_read_back() {
        for length in [0_u32, 1, 70000] {
            let empty = FactLists::default();
            let mut edit = empty.edit();
            edit.classes = EditedList::Changed((0..length).map(StyleAtomID).collect());
            edit.attributes = EditedList::Changed(
                (0..length)
                    .map(|index| AttributeFact {
                        name: StyleAtomID(index),
                        value: StyleAtomID(index + 1),
                    })
                    .collect(),
            );
            edit.custom_states = EditedList::Held(&[StyleAtomID(9)]);
            let lists = FactLists::new(&edit);
            assert_eq!(lists.classes(), &*edit.classes);
            assert_eq!(lists.attributes(), &*edit.attributes);
            assert_eq!(lists.custom_states(), &*edit.custom_states);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_table_hands_out_one_lists_per_content() {
        let mut table = FactListsTable::default();
        let empty = FactLists::default();
        let mut edit = empty.edit();
        edit.id = StyleAtomID(1);
        let first = table.intern(&edit, edit.content_hash());
        let second = table.intern(&edit, edit.content_hash());
        assert_eq!(first.0, second.0);
        edit.id = StyleAtomID(2);
        assert_ne!(table.intern(&edit, edit.content_hash()).0, first.0);
    }
}

//! Walks over the projection's links that answer what the host tree answers of an element's place
//! in the shadow-including and flat trees.

use super::super::super::tree::StyleNodeID;
use super::Projection;

impl Projection {
    /// Every live element identity, including the roots of shadow trees, in element order.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn live_nodes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = StyleNodeID> + '_ {
        (1..self.slot_count).filter_map(|index| {
            let node = StyleNodeID::element(u32::try_from(index).expect("style node index space exhausted"));
            self.is_live(node).then_some(node)
        })
    }

    /// The element's parent in the tree it is in, or a shadow root's host. A text node has no row,
    /// so its parent is the host tree's to answer.
    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn parent_or_shadow_host(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> Option<StyleNodeID> {
        assert!(node.element_index().is_some(), "only an element has projection links");
        self.parent(node).or_else(|| self.host_of(node))
    }

    /// Whether the element `node` is `root` or lies below it in the shadow-including tree: the climb
    /// out of a shadow tree continues at the host rather than stopping there. A climb that runs out
    /// of parents has reached a child of the document, which no element contains.
    #[must_use]
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn is_in_shadow_including_subtree_of(
        &self,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        root: StyleNodeID,
    ) -> bool {
        assert!(node.element_index().is_some(), "only an element has projection links");
        if root.text_index().is_some() {
            return false;
        }
        let mut candidate = node;
        loop {
            if candidate == root {
                return true;
            }
            candidate = match self.host_of(candidate).or_else(|| self.parent(candidate)) {
                Some(next) => next,
                None => return false,
            };
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn element(index: u32) -> StyleNodeID {
        StyleNodeID::element(index)
    }

    /// document(1) -> host(2) -> [light 4, light 5]; host's shadow root(3) -> slot(6) -> fallback 7.
    /// Light 4 and text 1 are assigned to the slot. Element 8 is minted and never linked.
    fn shadow_document() -> Projection {
        let mut projection = Projection::default();
        for index in 1..=8 {
            projection.mint(element(index));
        }
        let link_children = |projection: &mut Projection, parent: u32, children: &[u32]| {
            projection.set_first_element_child(element(parent), children.first().map(|&child| element(child)));
            for (position, &child) in children.iter().enumerate() {
                projection.set_parent(element(child), Some(element(parent)));
                let previous = position.checked_sub(1).map(|previous| element(children[previous]));
                projection.set_previous_element_sibling(element(child), previous);
                projection
                    .set_next_element_sibling(element(child), children.get(position + 1).map(|&next| element(next)));
            }
        };
        link_children(&mut projection, 1, &[2]);
        link_children(&mut projection, 2, &[4, 5]);
        link_children(&mut projection, 3, &[6]);
        link_children(&mut projection, 6, &[7]);
        projection.set_shadow_root(element(2), element(3));
        projection.set_assigned_slot(element(4), Some(element(6)));
        projection.set_assigned_nodes(element(6), &[element(4), StyleNodeID::text(1)]);
        // Style reads an element's links as the last transaction committed them.
        projection.commit();
        projection
    }

    #[test]
    fn live_nodes_are_the_minted_elements_that_did_not_retire() {
        let mut projection = shadow_document();
        assert_eq!(
            projection.live_nodes().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            (1..=8).map(element).collect::<Vec<_>>()
        );
        projection.retire(element(5));
        projection.retire(element(8));
        assert_eq!(
            projection.live_nodes().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7].map(element)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn parent_or_shadow_host_climbs_from_a_shadow_root_to_its_host() {
        let projection = shadow_document();
        assert_eq!(projection.parent_or_shadow_host(element(6)), Some(element(3)));
        assert_eq!(projection.parent_or_shadow_host(element(3)), Some(element(2)));
        // A slotted element continues through its light-tree parent.
        assert_eq!(projection.parent_or_shadow_host(element(4)), Some(element(2)));
        assert_eq!(projection.parent_or_shadow_host(element(1)), None);
        assert_eq!(projection.parent_or_shadow_host(element(8)), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shadow_including_subtrees_cross_into_shadow_trees() {
        let projection = shadow_document();
        let is_in = |node, root| projection.is_in_shadow_including_subtree_of(element(node), element(root));
        assert!(is_in(7, 7));
        assert!(is_in(7, 3));
        assert!(is_in(7, 2));
        assert!(is_in(7, 1));
        assert!(is_in(4, 2));
        assert!(!is_in(4, 6));
        assert!(!is_in(2, 3));
        assert!(!is_in(5, 4));
        assert!(!is_in(8, 1));
        assert!(!projection.is_in_shadow_including_subtree_of(element(4), StyleNodeID::text(1)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn flat_tree_parents_follow_shadow_roots_and_slots() {
        let mut projection = shadow_document();
        // The host's flat children are its shadow root's, and the slot's are its assigned nodes,
        // which leave its fallback and the unassigned light child out.
        assert_eq!(projection.flat_tree_parent(element(4)), Some(element(6)));
        assert_eq!(projection.flat_tree_parent(element(5)), None);
        assert_eq!(projection.flat_tree_parent(element(7)), None);

        // With nothing assigned, the slot shows its fallback content.
        projection.set_assigned_slot(element(4), None);
        projection.set_assigned_nodes(element(6), &[]);
        assert_eq!(projection.flat_tree_parent(element(7)), Some(element(6)));
    }
}
