use super::super::super::*;

#[derive(Clone)]

struct SheetOccurrence {
    identity: u64,
    sheet: SheetID,
    conditions_hold: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct ScopeSheetOccurrences {
    occurrences: Vec<SheetOccurrence>,
    published: Vec<SheetID>,
}

impl StyleEngine {
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn attach_sheet_occurrence(
        &mut self,
        sheet: SheetID,
        scope: TreeScopeID,
        identity: u64,
        before: u64,
        conditions_hold: bool,
    ) {
        let entries = &mut self.host.sheet_occurrences.entry(scope).or_default().occurrences;
        entries.retain(|entry| entry.identity != identity);
        let position = entries
            .iter()
            .position(|entry| entry.identity == before)
            .unwrap_or(entries.len());
        entries.insert(
            position,
            SheetOccurrence {
                identity,
                sheet,
                conditions_hold,
            },
        );
        self.publish_sheet_occurrences(scope);
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn detach_sheet_occurrence(&mut self, scope: TreeScopeID, identity: u64) {
        let Some(state) = self.host.sheet_occurrences.get_mut(&scope) else {
            return;
        };
        state.occurrences.retain(|entry| entry.identity != identity);
        self.publish_sheet_occurrences(scope);
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn set_sheet_occurrence_conditions(
        &mut self,
        scope: TreeScopeID,
        identity: u64,
        conditions_hold: bool,
    ) {
        let Some(entry) = self
            .host
            .sheet_occurrences
            .get_mut(&scope)
            .and_then(|state| state.occurrences.iter_mut().find(|entry| entry.identity == identity))
        else {
            return;
        };
        if entry.conditions_hold == conditions_hold {
            return;
        }
        entry.conditions_hold = conditions_hold;
        self.publish_sheet_occurrences(scope);
    }

    fn publish_sheet_occurrences(&mut self, scope: TreeScopeID) {
        let state = self.host.sheet_occurrences.get_mut(&scope).unwrap();
        let mut seen = HashSet::default();
        let mut active: Vec<_> = state
            .occurrences
            .iter()
            .rev()
            .filter(|entry| entry.conditions_hold && seen.insert(entry.sheet))
            .map(|entry| entry.sheet)
            .collect();
        active.reverse();
        let old = std::mem::replace(&mut state.published, active);
        let active = state.published.clone();

        if state.occurrences.is_empty() {
            self.host.sheet_occurrences.remove(&scope);
            if self.host.sheet_occurrences.is_empty() {
                self.host.sheet_occurrences.shrink_to_fit();
            }
        }

        if old == active {
            return;
        }

        let old_set: HashSet<_> = old.iter().copied().collect();
        // Preserve legacy attachments, including the document's user and user-agent sheets.
        let mut sheets: Vec<_> = self
            .current_sheets_in_scope(scope)
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|sheet| !old_set.contains(sheet))
            .collect();
        sheets.extend_from_slice(&active);
        self.stage_sheets_in_scope(scope, sheets);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn duplicate_occurrences_preserve_positions_while_inactive() {
        let mut engine = StyleEngine::new();
        let shared = engine.add_sheet(CascadeOrigin::Author);
        let other = engine.add_sheet(CascadeOrigin::Author);
        let scope = TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT;
        engine.attach_sheet_occurrence(shared, scope, 1, 0, true);
        engine.attach_sheet_occurrence(other, scope, 2, 0, true);
        engine.attach_sheet_occurrence(shared, scope, 3, 0, true);
        assert_eq!(engine.current_sheets_in_scope(scope), &[other, shared]);

        engine.set_sheet_occurrence_conditions(scope, 3, false);
        assert_eq!(engine.current_sheets_in_scope(scope), &[shared, other]);
        engine.set_sheet_occurrence_conditions(scope, 1, false);
        assert_eq!(engine.current_sheets_in_scope(scope), &[other]);
        engine.set_sheet_occurrence_conditions(scope, 3, true);
        assert_eq!(engine.current_sheets_in_scope(scope), &[other, shared]);
        engine.set_sheet_occurrence_conditions(scope, 1, true);
        assert_eq!(engine.current_sheets_in_scope(scope), &[other, shared]);
        engine.detach_sheet_occurrence(scope, 3);
        assert_eq!(engine.current_sheets_in_scope(scope), &[shared, other]);
        engine.attach_sheet_occurrence(shared, scope, 1, 0, true);
        assert_eq!(engine.current_sheets_in_scope(scope), &[other, shared]);
        engine.attach_sheet_occurrence(shared, scope, 1, 2, true);
        assert_eq!(engine.current_sheets_in_scope(scope), &[shared, other]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn occurrence_conditions_are_local_to_their_scope_and_storage_is_released() {
        let mut engine = StyleEngine::new();
        let shared = engine.add_sheet(CascadeOrigin::Author);
        let first = TreeScopeID(1);
        let second = TreeScopeID(2);
        engine.attach_sheet_occurrence(shared, first, 1, 0, true);
        engine.attach_sheet_occurrence(shared, second, 2, 0, true);
        engine.set_sheet_occurrence_conditions(first, 1, false);
        assert!(engine.current_sheets_in_scope(first).is_empty());
        assert_eq!(engine.current_sheets_in_scope(second), &[shared]);
        assert!(engine.rules.sheet_conditions_hold(shared));
        engine.detach_sheet_occurrence(first, 1);
        engine.detach_sheet_occurrence(second, 2);
        assert!(engine.host.sheet_occurrences.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(engine.host.sheet_occurrences.capacity(), 0);
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/css/style/pipeline/rule_store/staging.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The rule edits a transaction stages, which the rule store takes at the transaction barrier.

use super::super::super::*;
use super::RuleDeclarations;
use crate::css::declaration_block::SharedDeclarationBlock;

#[derive(Clone)]
struct StagedFieldRow<V> {
    before: V,
    after: V,
    dirty: bool,
}

/// Sparse staging for one program field. The first write freezes `before`, later writes replace
/// `after`, and `take_dirty()` applies only the last write while retaining both sides for
/// `ProgramStaging::delta()`.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct StagedField<K, V> {
    rows: HashMap<K, StagedFieldRow<V>>,
    touched: Vec<K>,
    dirty_count: usize,
}

impl<K, V> Default for StagedField<K, V> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            rows: HashMap::default(),
            touched: Vec::new(),
            dirty_count: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl<K: Copy + Eq + Hash + Ord, V: Clone> StagedField<K, V> {
    fn current(&self, key: K, committed: impl FnOnce() -> V) -> V {
        self.side(key, TransactionFactSide::After, committed)
    }

    fn after(&self, key: K) -> Option<&V> {
        self.rows.get(&key).map(|row| &row.after)
    }

    fn side(&self, key: K, side: TransactionFactSide, resident: impl FnOnce() -> V) -> V {
        let row = self.rows.get(&key);
        match (side, row) {
            (TransactionFactSide::Before, Some(row)) => row.before.clone(),
            (TransactionFactSide::After, Some(row)) => row.after.clone(),
            _ => resident(),
        }
    }

    fn stage(&mut self, key: K, before: impl FnOnce() -> V, after: V) {
        match self.rows.entry(key) {
            std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Occupied(mut entry) => {
                let row = entry.get_mut();
                row.after = after;
                if !row.dirty {
                    row.dirty = true;
                    self.dirty_count += 1;
                }
            }
            std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) => {
                entry.insert(StagedFieldRow {
                    before: before(),
                    after,
                    dirty: true,
                });
                self.touched.push(key);
                self.dirty_count += 1;
            }
        }
    }

    fn take_dirty(&mut self) -> Vec<(K, V)> {
        if self.is_empty() {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let mut dirty = Vec::with_capacity(self.dirty_count);
        for &key in &self.touched {
            let row = self.rows.get_mut(&key).unwrap();
            if row.dirty {
                dirty.push((key, row.after.clone()));
                row.dirty = false;
            }
        }
        self.dirty_count = 0;
        dirty.sort_unstable_by_key(|(key, _)| *key);
        dirty
    }

    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.dirty_count == 0
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.rows.clear();
        self.touched.clear();
        // Keep small edit buffers warm, but do not retain stylesheet-loading capacity for the
        // lifetime of every document. These rows are only needed until transaction release.
        if self.rows.capacity() * size_of::<(K, StagedFieldRow<V>)>() > 4096 {
            self.rows = HashMap::default();
        }
        if self.touched.capacity() * size_of::<K>() > 4096 {
            self.touched = Vec::new();
        }
        self.dirty_count = 0;
    }

    fn pairs(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (K, &V, &V)> {
        self.touched.iter().map(|&key| {
            let row = self.rows.get(&key).unwrap();
            (key, &row.before, &row.after)
        })
    }
}

/// Program transaction staging. Every field preserves its first before value and last-writer
/// after value until release; `delta()` may read those pairs after the final values are applied.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct ProgramStaging {
    rule_conditions: StagedField<RuleID, bool>,
    sheet_conditions: StagedField<SheetID, bool>,
    rule_declarations: StagedField<RuleID, RuleDeclarations>,
    rule_versions: StagedField<RuleID, RuleVersion>,
    rule_gated_by_container_query: StagedField<RuleID, bool>,
    rule_liveness: StagedField<RuleID, bool>,
    layer_orders: StagedField<TreeScopeID, HashMap<CascadeLayerID, u32>>,
    scopes_using_document_sheets: StagedField<TreeScopeID, bool>,
    sheets_in_scope: StagedField<TreeScopeID, Vec<SheetID>>,
    sheet_rule_replacements: Column<Option<SheetRuleReplacement>>,
    /// Whether a registration made through `CSS.registerProperty()` waits for the next
    /// transaction, which says what moved of the registrations as it takes the registry in.
    registration_pending: bool,
    /// The names whose registration the registry the next transaction reads holds otherwise than
    /// the one the last transaction read.
    moved_registrations: Vec<ak::Utf16FlyString>,
}

impl ProgramStaging {
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn is_dirty(&self) -> bool {
        !self.rule_conditions.is_empty()
            || !self.sheet_conditions.is_empty()
            || !self.rule_declarations.is_empty()
            || !self.rule_versions.is_empty()
            || !self.rule_gated_by_container_query.is_empty()
            || !self.rule_liveness.is_empty()
            || !self.layer_orders.is_empty()
            || !self.scopes_using_document_sheets.is_empty()
            || !self.sheets_in_scope.is_empty()
            || self.sheet_rule_replacements.iter().any(Option::is_some)
            || self.registration_pending
            || !self.moved_registrations.is_empty()
    }

    /// Note a registration made through `CSS.registerProperty()`, which the registry the next
    /// transaction reads holds.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn note_registration_change(&mut self) {
        self.registration_pending = true;
    }

    /// Note what moved between the registry the last transaction read, `previous`, and the one
    /// the next reads, `registry`.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn note_registry_moved(
        &mut self,
        previous: &crate::css::custom_properties::CustomPropertyRegistry,
        registry: &crate::css::custom_properties::CustomPropertyRegistry,
    ) {
        for name in registry.names_registered_otherwise_than(previous) {
            if !self.moved_registrations.contains(&name) {
                self.moved_registrations.push(name);
            }
        }
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.rule_conditions.clear();
        self.sheet_conditions.clear();
        self.rule_declarations.clear();
        self.rule_versions.clear();
        self.rule_gated_by_container_query.clear();
        self.rule_liveness.clear();
        self.layer_orders.clear();
        self.scopes_using_document_sheets.clear();
        self.sheets_in_scope.clear();
        for index in 0..self.sheet_rule_replacements.len() {
            self.sheet_rule_replacements[index] = None;
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct ReplacedStyleRule {
    pub(in crate::css::style) rule: RuleID,
    pub(in crate::css::style) version: RuleVersion,
    pub(in crate::css::style) declared: Vec<DeclarationEntry>,
    pub(in crate::css::style) declarations_are_complete: bool,
    pub(in crate::css::style) gated_by_container_query: bool,
}

/// What a transaction changed of the rules, read off the program as it stood before the transaction
/// and as the transaction leaves it.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct RuleChanges {
    /// The rules whose contents, conditions, layering or existence moved. A rule of a sheet that was
    /// attached nowhere before the transaction is left out: what it decides arrives with the sheet.
    pub(crate) rules: Vec<RuleID>,
    /// Those of `rules` where more than their conditions moved, whose declarations and gates may
    /// not be the ones their entries were indexed with.
    pub(crate) rules_with_moved_contents: Vec<RuleID>,
    /// The sheets that were attached to or detached from a scope, or whose activation moved.
    pub(crate) sheets: Vec<SheetID>,
    /// The scopes whose sheet order or layer order moved, which reorders declarations that already
    /// matched without changing which elements they match.
    pub(crate) reordered_scopes: Vec<TreeScopeID>,
    /// The scopes whose layer order moved, which moves the layer ranks of their rules, whether or
    /// not it reorders any of them.
    pub(crate) layered_scopes: Vec<TreeScopeID>,
    /// The custom property names whose registration moved, through an `@property` rule or
    /// `CSS.registerProperty()`.
    pub(crate) registrations: Vec<ak::Utf16FlyString>,
}

impl RuleChanges {
    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.rules.is_empty()
            && self.sheets.is_empty()
            && self.reordered_scopes.is_empty()
            && self.layered_scopes.is_empty()
            && self.registrations.is_empty()
    }
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct SheetRuleReplacement {
    pub(in crate::css::style) sheet: SheetID,
    pub(in crate::css::style) rules: Vec<ReplacedStyleRule>,
    pub(in crate::css::style) reused: usize,
    pub(in crate::css::style) reuse_disabled: bool,
}

impl StyleEngine {
    /// Record that a tree scope decides with the document's author sheets as well as its own.
    pub fn set_tree_scope_uses_document_sheets(&mut self, tree_scope: TreeScopeID) {
        let previous = self
            .host
            .program_staging
            .scopes_using_document_sheets
            .current(tree_scope, || {
                self.retained.rules.scope_uses_document_sheets(tree_scope)
            });
        if previous {
            return;
        }
        self.host.program_staging.scopes_using_document_sheets.stage(
            tree_scope,
            || self.retained.rules.scope_uses_document_sheets(tree_scope),
            true,
        );
    }

    /// Put the qualified layer names in the order one tree scope declares them in.
    pub fn set_layer_order(&mut self, scope: TreeScopeID, layers: &[CascadeLayerID]) {
        let ranks = RuleStore::layer_ranks_in_order(layers);
        let pending_order = self.host.program_staging.layer_orders.after(scope);
        if pending_order.map_or_else(
            || self.retained.rules.layer_ranks_match(scope, &ranks),
            |pending| pending == &ranks,
        ) {
            return;
        }
        self.host
            .program_staging
            .layer_orders
            .stage(scope, || self.retained.rules.layer_ranks(scope), ranks);
    }

    /// The dense layer rank consumed by the C++ property cascade and non-style rule lookup.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn layer_index(&self, scope: TreeScopeID, layer: CascadeLayerID) -> u32 {
        self.host.program_staging.layer_orders.after(scope).map_or_else(
            || self.retained.rules.layer_index(scope, layer),
            |ranks| {
                ranks
                    .get(&layer)
                    .copied()
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| u32::try_from(ranks.len()).expect("cascade layer count exhausted"))
            },
        )
    }

    /// The declaration block `rule` holds, as this transaction staged it.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn current_rule_block(&self, rule: RuleID) -> Option<SharedDeclarationBlock> {
        match self.host.program_staging.rule_declarations.after(rule) {
            Some(staged) => staged.block.clone(),
            None => self.retained.rules.block_of(rule).cloned(),
        }
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn stage_rule_declarations(&mut self, rule: RuleID, declarations: RuleDeclarations) {
        // NB: As for its version, a rule this transaction reserved takes its declarations in place.
        if self.staged_rule_is_arriving(rule) && self.host.program_staging.rule_declarations.after(rule).is_none() {
            self.retained.rules.set_rule_declarations(rule, declarations);
            return;
        }
        self.host.program_staging.rule_declarations.stage(
            rule,
            || self.retained.rules.rule_declarations_of(rule),
            declarations,
        );
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn current_declared_properties_of(&self, rule: RuleID) -> &[DeclarationEntry] {
        self.host
            .program_staging
            .rule_declarations
            .after(rule)
            .map(|pending| pending.declared_properties())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.retained.rules.declared_properties_of(rule))
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn current_declarations_are_complete_for(&self, rule: RuleID) -> bool {
        self.host
            .program_staging
            .rule_declarations
            .after(rule)
            .map(|pending| pending.custom_declarations().is_empty())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.retained.rules.declarations_are_complete_for(rule))
    }

    pub fn set_rule_conditions_hold(&mut self, rule: RuleID, conditions_hold: bool) {
        let previous = self
            .host
            .program_staging
            .rule_conditions
            .current(rule, || self.retained.rules.rule_conditions_hold(rule));
        if previous == conditions_hold {
            return;
        }
        self.host.program_staging.rule_conditions.stage(
            rule,
            || self.retained.rules.rule_conditions_hold(rule),
            conditions_hold,
        );
    }

    /// Record whether a sheet's conditions hold, as evaluating its media queries decides.
    pub fn set_sheet_conditions_hold(&mut self, sheet: SheetID, conditions_hold: bool) {
        let previous = self
            .host
            .program_staging
            .sheet_conditions
            .current(sheet, || self.retained.rules.sheet_conditions_hold(sheet));
        if previous == conditions_hold {
            return;
        }
        self.host.program_staging.sheet_conditions.stage(
            sheet,
            || self.retained.rules.sheet_conditions_hold(sheet),
            conditions_hold,
        );
    }

    /// Begin rebuilding a sheet while retaining compatible style-rule identities by cascade
    /// position. The parsed CSSOM objects are new, but an unchanged semantic rule does not become a
    /// departure followed by an arrival merely because the whole sheet was reparsed.
    pub fn begin_sheet_rules_replacement(&mut self, sheet: SheetID) {
        assert!(
            self.host.sheet_rule_replacement.is_none(),
            "stylesheet replacements do not nest"
        );
        if let Some(slot) = self
            .host
            .program_staging
            .sheet_rule_replacements
            .get_mut(sheet.0 as usize)
            && let Some(mut replacement) = slot.take()
        {
            replacement.reused = 0;
            replacement.reuse_disabled = false;
            self.host.sheet_rule_replacement = Some(replacement);
            return;
        }
        let rules = self.current_rules_in_sheet(sheet);
        if rules
            .iter()
            .any(|&rule| self.current_rule_version(rule).kind != RuleKind::Style)
        {
            self.clear_sheet_rules(sheet);
            return;
        }
        let rules: Vec<ReplacedStyleRule> = rules
            .into_iter()
            .map(|rule| ReplacedStyleRule {
                rule,
                version: self.current_rule_version(rule),
                declared: self.current_declared_properties_of(rule).to_vec(),
                declarations_are_complete: self.current_declarations_are_complete_for(rule),
                gated_by_container_query: self.current_rule_is_gated_by_container_query(rule),
            })
            .collect();
        self.host.sheet_rule_replacement = Some(SheetRuleReplacement {
            sheet,
            rules,
            reused: 0,
            reuse_disabled: false,
        });
    }

    /// Finish a synchronous sheet rebuild, retiring unmatched old rules and publishing declaration
    /// changes on identities that were reused.
    pub fn finish_sheet_rules_replacement(&mut self, sheet: SheetID, declaration_block: u32) {
        let Some(replacement) = self.host.sheet_rule_replacement.take() else {
            return;
        };
        assert_eq!(replacement.sheet, sheet);
        for old in &replacement.rules[..replacement.reused] {
            let declarations_changed = !old.declarations_are_complete
                || !self.current_declarations_are_complete_for(old.rule)
                || self.current_declared_properties_of(old.rule) != old.declared
                || self.current_rule_is_gated_by_container_query(old.rule) != old.gated_by_container_query;
            if declarations_changed {
                let mut version = self.current_rule_version(old.rule);
                version.declaration_block = Some(DeclarationBlockID::new(declaration_block));
                self.replace_rule_version(old.rule, version);
            }
        }
        if replacement.reused < replacement.rules.len() {
            let index = sheet.0 as usize;
            self.host
                .program_staging
                .sheet_rule_replacements
                .insert(index, Some(replacement));
        }
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn finalize_staged_sheet_rule_replacements(&mut self) {
        for index in 0..self.host.program_staging.sheet_rule_replacements.len() {
            let Some(replacement) = self.host.program_staging.sheet_rule_replacements[index].take() else {
                continue;
            };
            for old in &replacement.rules[replacement.reused..] {
                self.remove_rule(old.rule);
            }
        }
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn reuse_replaced_style_rule(&mut self, sheet: SheetID) -> Option<RuleID> {
        let replacement = self.host.sheet_rule_replacement.as_mut()?;
        if replacement.sheet != sheet || replacement.reuse_disabled {
            return None;
        }
        let old = replacement.rules.get(replacement.reused)?;
        if old.version.kind != RuleKind::Style {
            replacement.reuse_disabled = true;
            return None;
        }
        let rule = old.rule;
        let declaration_block = old.version.declaration_block;
        replacement.reused += 1;

        self.set_rule_conditions_hold(rule, true);
        self.stage_rule_declarations(rule, RuleDeclarations::default());
        self.stage_rule_gated_by_container_query(rule, false);
        let mut version = RuleVersion::new(RuleKind::Style);
        version.declaration_block = declaration_block;
        self.replace_rule_version(rule, version);
        Some(rule)
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn current_rule_version(&self, rule: RuleID) -> RuleVersion {
        self.host
            .program_staging
            .rule_versions
            .current(rule, || self.retained.rules.rule_version(rule).clone())
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn stage_rule_version(&mut self, rule: RuleID, contents: RuleVersion) {
        // NB: A rule this transaction reserved has no committed version anything reads, and its
        //     arrival already names it a changed rule. Its version is written in place rather than
        //     staged with a before side nothing asks for, which for a sheet arriving whole would
        //     hold two versions of every one of its rules until the transaction is released.
        if self.staged_rule_is_arriving(rule) && self.host.program_staging.rule_versions.after(rule).is_none() {
            self.retained.rules.replace_reserved_rule_version(rule, contents);
            return;
        }
        // A staged version another one replaces is never committed, so the `@scope` levels only it
        // names are let go of here.
        if let Some(superseded) = self
            .host
            .program_staging
            .rule_versions
            .after(rule)
            .map(|version| version.scope)
            && superseded != contents.scope
            && superseded != self.retained.rules.rule_version(rule).scope
        {
            self.retained.rules.release_scope(superseded);
        }
        self.host.program_staging.rule_versions.stage(
            rule,
            || self.retained.rules.rule_version(rule).clone(),
            contents,
        );
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn current_rule_is_gated_by_container_query(&self, rule: RuleID) -> bool {
        self.host
            .program_staging
            .rule_gated_by_container_query
            .current(rule, || self.retained.rules.rule_is_gated_by_container_query(rule))
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn stage_rule_gated_by_container_query(&mut self, rule: RuleID, gated: bool) {
        self.host.program_staging.rule_gated_by_container_query.stage(
            rule,
            || self.retained.rules.rule_is_gated_by_container_query(rule),
            gated,
        );
    }

    /// What the staged program changes of the committed one, which has yet to take it.
    fn staged_rule_changes(&self) -> RuleChanges {
        fn moved<K: Copy, V: PartialEq>(pairs: impl Iterator<Item = (K, V, V)>) -> impl Iterator<Item = K> {
            pairs.filter_map(|(key, before, after)| (before != after).then_some(key))
        }
        let staging = &self.host.program_staging;
        let program = &self.retained.rules;
        let mut changes = RuleChanges::default();

        let attached = |rule: &RuleID| !program.sheet_scopes(program.rule_sheet(*rule)).is_empty();
        changes.rules_with_moved_contents = moved(staging.rule_declarations.pairs())
            .chain(moved(staging.rule_versions.pairs()))
            .chain(moved(staging.rule_gated_by_container_query.pairs()))
            .chain(moved(staging.rule_liveness.pairs()))
            .filter(attached)
            .collect();
        changes.rules_with_moved_contents.sort_unstable();
        changes.rules_with_moved_contents.dedup();
        let mut rules: Vec<RuleID> = moved(staging.rule_conditions.pairs())
            .filter(attached)
            .chain(changes.rules_with_moved_contents.iter().copied())
            .collect();
        rules.sort_unstable();
        rules.dedup();
        changes.rules = rules;

        changes.sheets = moved(staging.sheet_conditions.pairs()).collect();
        for (scope, before, after) in staging.sheets_in_scope.pairs() {
            let kept_before = before.iter().filter(|sheet| after.contains(sheet));
            let kept_after = after.iter().filter(|sheet| before.contains(sheet));
            if kept_before.ne(kept_after) {
                changes.reordered_scopes.push(scope);
            }
            changes.sheets.extend(
                before
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|sheet| !after.contains(sheet))
                    .chain(after.iter().filter(|sheet| !before.contains(sheet))),
            );
        }
        changes.sheets.sort_unstable();
        changes.sheets.dedup();

        changes.layered_scopes = moved(staging.layer_orders.pairs()).collect();
        // NB: A scope's first layer order places no layered rule that was there before it.
        changes
            .reordered_scopes
            .extend(moved(staging.layer_orders.pairs()).filter(|&scope| program.layer_order_is_initialized(scope)));
        changes.reordered_scopes.sort_unstable();
        changes.reordered_scopes.dedup();
        changes
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn commit_staged_program(&mut self) -> RuleChanges {
        let mut changes = self.staged_rule_changes();
        self.host.program_staging.registration_pending = false;
        changes.registrations = std::mem::take(&mut self.host.program_staging.moved_registrations);
        self.retained
            .counters
            .add(Counter::CascadeTopologyDeltas, changes.reordered_scopes.len() as u64);
        let rule_conditions = self.host.program_staging.rule_conditions.take_dirty();
        let sheet_conditions = self.host.program_staging.sheet_conditions.take_dirty();
        for (rule, conditions_hold) in rule_conditions {
            self.retained.rules.set_rule_conditions_hold(rule, conditions_hold);
        }
        for (sheet, conditions_hold) in sheet_conditions {
            self.retained.rules.set_sheet_conditions_hold(sheet, conditions_hold);
        }

        let declarations = self.host.program_staging.rule_declarations.take_dirty();
        for (rule, declarations) in declarations {
            self.retained.rules.set_rule_declarations(rule, declarations);
        }

        let mut versions = self.host.program_staging.rule_versions.take_dirty();
        if !versions.is_empty() {
            versions.sort_unstable_by_key(|(rule, _)| *rule);
            for (rule, version) in versions {
                if self.staged_rule_is_arriving(rule) {
                    self.retained.rules.replace_reserved_rule_version(rule, version);
                } else {
                    self.retained.rules.replace_rule_version(rule, version);
                }
            }
        }

        let gated_by_container_query = self.host.program_staging.rule_gated_by_container_query.take_dirty();
        for (rule, value) in gated_by_container_query {
            self.retained.rules.set_rule_gated_by_container_query(rule, value);
        }

        let mut liveness_changes = self.host.program_staging.rule_liveness.take_dirty();
        if !liveness_changes.is_empty() {
            liveness_changes.sort_unstable_by_key(|(rule, _)| *rule);
            self.retained.rules.set_rule_liveness(&liveness_changes);
        }

        let layer_orders = self.host.program_staging.layer_orders.take_dirty();
        let scopes = self.host.program_staging.scopes_using_document_sheets.take_dirty();
        if !layer_orders.is_empty() || !scopes.is_empty() {
            for (scope, ranks) in layer_orders {
                self.retained.rules.set_layer_ranks(scope, ranks);
            }
            for (scope, uses_document_sheets) in scopes {
                if uses_document_sheets {
                    self.retained.rules.set_scope_uses_document_sheets(scope);
                }
            }
        }

        let mut sheet_orders = self.host.program_staging.sheets_in_scope.take_dirty();
        if !sheet_orders.is_empty() {
            sheet_orders.sort_unstable_by_key(|(scope, _)| *scope);
            for (scope, sheets) in sheet_orders {
                self.retained.rules.set_sheets_in_scope(scope, sheets);
            }
        }
        changes
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn current_rule_is_live(&self, rule: RuleID) -> bool {
        self.host
            .program_staging
            .rule_liveness
            .current(rule, || self.retained.rules.rule_is_live(rule))
    }

    fn staged_rule_is_arriving(&self, rule: RuleID) -> bool {
        !self
            .host
            .program_staging
            .rule_liveness
            .side(rule, TransactionFactSide::Before, || {
                self.retained.rules.rule_is_live(rule)
            })
            && self.current_rule_is_live(rule)
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn stage_rule_liveness(&mut self, rule: RuleID, live: bool) {
        self.host
            .program_staging
            .rule_liveness
            .stage(rule, || self.retained.rules.rule_is_live(rule), live);
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn current_sheets_in_scope(&self, tree_scope: TreeScopeID) -> &[SheetID] {
        self.host
            .program_staging
            .sheets_in_scope
            .after(tree_scope)
            .map_or_else(|| self.retained.rules.sheets_in_scope(tree_scope), Vec::as_slice)
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn stage_sheets_in_scope(&mut self, tree_scope: TreeScopeID, sheets: Vec<SheetID>) {
        self.host.program_staging.sheets_in_scope.stage(
            tree_scope,
            || self.retained.rules.sheets_in_scope(tree_scope).to_vec(),
            sheets,
        );
    }
}

impl StyleEngine {
    pub fn set_rule_gated_by_container_query(&mut self, rule: RuleID) {
        self.stage_rule_gated_by_container_query(rule, true);
    }

    /// Record which cascade layer a rule sits in.
    ///
    /// Where a rule sits among the layers is part of what the rule is, and it is what the cascade
    /// compares; whether it is in one at all is what a layer topology change routes by.
    pub fn set_rule_layer(&mut self, rule: RuleID, layer: CascadeLayerID) {
        let mut version = self.current_rule_version(rule);
        if version.layer == layer {
            return;
        }
        version.layer = layer;
        self.replace_rule_version(rule, version);
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn append_rule(
        &mut self,
        sheet: SheetID,
        parent: Option<RuleID>,
        kind: RuleKind,
    ) -> RuleID {
        let rule = self.retained.rules.reserve_rule(sheet, parent, kind);
        self.stage_rule_liveness(rule, true);
        rule
    }

    /// Insert one rule between two neighbors. Existing rules are neither renumbered nor rematched.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn insert_rule_before(&mut self, before: RuleID, kind: RuleKind) -> RuleID {
        let rule = self.retained.rules.reserve_rule_before(before, kind);
        self.stage_rule_liveness(rule, true);
        rule
    }

    /// Delete a rule, taking its subtree with it. Every removed identity is a rule change, because a
    /// deleted winning declaration has to be repaired wherever it was winning.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn remove_rule(&mut self, rule: RuleID) -> Vec<RuleID> {
        if !self.current_rule_is_live(rule) {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let removed: Vec<RuleID> = self
            .rules
            .rule_subtree(rule)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|&rule| self.current_rule_is_live(rule))
            .collect();
        for &id in &removed {
            self.retained.rules.native.remove(id);
            self.stage_rule_liveness(id, false);
        }
        removed
    }

    /// Replace a rule's contents.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn replace_rule_version(&mut self, rule: RuleID, contents: RuleVersion) {
        self.stage_rule_version(rule, contents);
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn current_top_level_rules_in_sheet(&self, sheet: SheetID) -> Vec<RuleID> {
        self.retained
            .rules
            .all_top_level_rules_in_sheet(sheet)
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|&rule| self.current_rule_is_live(rule))
            .collect()
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn current_rules_in_sheet(&self, sheet: SheetID) -> Vec<RuleID> {
        self.retained
            .rules
            .all_rules_in_sheet(sheet)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|&rule| self.current_rule_is_live(rule))
            .collect()
    }

    /// Answers the identities the end of the transaction released, for the host to mint again.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn discard_style_update_outputs(&mut self) -> Vec<u32> {
        self.retained.tree.release_retired_identities()
    }

    /// Releases the identities the end of the transaction released, which the job pays the host to mint again.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn release_style_update_identities(&mut self) {
        let released = self.discard_style_update_outputs();
        self.host.released_style_nodes.extend(released);
    }

    pub(crate) fn take_released_style_nodes(&mut self) -> Vec<u32> {
        std::mem::take(&mut self.host.released_style_nodes)
    }
}

impl StyleEngine {
    /// Drop every rule of a sheet.
    ///
    /// This is for `replace()`, which really does swap the whole rule list. Every other edit to a
    /// sheet moves one rule and is patched one rule at a time, because retiring identities that did
    /// not change turns a one-rule edit into a program change over the whole sheet.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn clear_sheet_rules(&mut self, sheet: SheetID) {
        for rule in self.current_top_level_rules_in_sheet(sheet) {
            self.remove_rule(rule);
        }
    }

    /// Delete one rule and settle the program around it.
    pub fn remove_style_rule(&mut self, rule: RuleID) {
        self.remove_rule(rule);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn sparse_program_staging_freezes_before_until_release() {
        let rule = RuleID(7);
        let mut staged = StagedField::default();
        staged.stage(rule, || 10_u32, 20);
        staged.stage(rule, || panic!("the before value is already frozen"), 30);

        assert_eq!(staged.side(rule, TransactionFactSide::Before, || 0), 10);
        assert_eq!(staged.current(rule, || 0), 30);
        assert_eq!(staged.take_dirty(), [(rule, 30)]);
        assert!(staged.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(staged.side(rule, TransactionFactSide::Before, || 0), 10);
        assert_eq!(staged.current(rule, || 35), 30);

        staged.stage(rule, || panic!("the before value is already frozen"), 40);
        assert_eq!(staged.side(rule, TransactionFactSide::Before, || 0), 10);
        assert_eq!(staged.take_dirty(), [(rule, 40)]);
        assert_eq!(staged.current(rule, || 50), 40);

        staged.clear();
        assert_eq!(staged.current(rule, || 50), 50);
        assert!(staged.rows.is_empty());
        assert!(staged.touched.is_empty());
    }
}

//! The rules of the user agent's sheets, which the process keeps once and every document reads.
//!
//! A document records no user agent rule. Its user agent sheets stand for sheets of the process's
//! [`UserAgentRules`], whose rules it names by [`RuleID::of_user_agent`], and it keeps only which
//! of them its media leave out. Those sheets and left-out rules are the document's
//! [`UserAgentVariant`], the key of the user agent index it decides with.

use super::{RuleID, RuleStore, SheetID};
use crate::css::parser::arbitrary_substitution::AttrNamesRead;
use crate::css::style::atoms::DocumentAtoms;
use crate::css::style::selector_analysis::SelectorSummary;
use crate::fork::ForkShared;
use smallvec::SmallVec;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// The rules of the user agent's sheets the process published so far. Nothing edits a published
/// rule, and a sheet arriving makes a new table holding the old one's rules at their numbers, so
/// that a document holding an older table reads what it always read.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct UserAgentRules {
    store: RuleStore,
    sheets: SmallVec<[UserAgentSheet; 4]>,
}

impl Default for UserAgentRules {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            store: RuleStore::new(),
            sheets: SmallVec::new(),
        }
    }
}

/// A user agent sheet the process published.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct UserAgentSheet {
    /// The identity of the native sheet the rules were compiled from.
    source_identity: u64,
    sheet: SheetID,
    /// What a document learns of the selectors of the sheet's rules as it attaches the sheet.
    selectors: Arc<SelectorSummary>,
    attr_names: Arc<AttrNamesRead>,
    /// The references that keep the names the sheet's rules declare interned.
    _atoms: ForkShared<DocumentAtoms>,
}

impl UserAgentRules {
    /// The rules, numbered as [`RuleID::in_user_agent_rules`] answers.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn store(&self) -> &RuleStore {
        &self.store
    }

    /// The table holding what this one holds and `store`, the rule store that went on to hold the
    /// rules of the sheet `sheet`, published from the native sheet `source_identity`.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn with_sheet(
        &self,
        store: RuleStore,
        sheet: SheetID,
        source_identity: u64,
        selectors: SelectorSummary,
        atoms: ForkShared<DocumentAtoms>,
    ) -> Self {
        let mut attr_names = AttrNamesRead::default();
        for rule in store.all_rules_in_sheet(sheet) {
            for value in store
                .written_values_of(rule)
                .iter()
                .chain(store.custom_written_values_of(rule))
            {
                if let Some(unresolved) =
                    crate::css::style::custom_property_cascade::unresolved_reading_attributes(value.data())
                {
                    attr_names.note(unresolved.components().as_ref());
                }
            }
        }
        let mut sheets = self.sheets.clone();
        sheets.push(UserAgentSheet {
            source_identity,
            sheet,
            selectors: Arc::new(selectors),
            attr_names: Arc::new(attr_names),
            _atoms: atoms,
        });
        Self { store, sheets }
    }

    /// The sheet published from the native sheet `source_identity`.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn sheet_of_source(&self, source_identity: u64) -> Option<SheetID> {
        self.sheets
            .iter()
            .find(|sheet| sheet.source_identity == source_identity)
            .map(|sheet| sheet.sheet)
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn attr_names_read(&self, source_identity: u64) -> &AttrNamesRead {
        &self
            .sheets
            .iter()
            .find(|sheet| sheet.source_identity == source_identity)
            .expect("the process published the sheet")
            .attr_names
    }

    /// What the selectors of the rules of `sheet` say to a document attaching it.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn selector_summary(&self, sheet: SheetID) -> Arc<SelectorSummary> {
        let sheet = self.sheets.iter().find(|candidate| candidate.sheet == sheet);
        Arc::clone(&sheet.expect("the process published the sheet").selectors)
    }

    /// The bytes of the table, the first time `sizer` reaches each thing it holds.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn heap_size(&self, sizer: &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer) -> usize {
        let names = self
            .sheets
            .iter()
            .map(|sheet| {
                if sizer.first_sight(Arc::as_ptr(&sheet.attr_names)) {
                    size_of::<AttrNamesRead>() + sheet.attr_names.heap_size()
                } else {
                    0
                }
            })
            .sum::<usize>();
        self.store.heap_size(sizer) + self.sheets.len() * size_of::<UserAgentSheet>() + names
    }

    /// The bytes of the declarations of the rules, the first time `sizer` reaches each.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn declarations_heap_size(&self, sizer: &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer) -> usize {
        self.store.declarations_heap_size(sizer)
    }
}

/// Which of the process's user agent rules decide in a document: every rule of its contributing
/// user agent sheets, in cascade order, but those its media leave out. Documents alike in this
/// decide with one user agent index.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct UserAgentVariant {
    /// The contributing sheets, in cascade order, in the numbers of the process's rules.
    sheets: SmallVec<[SheetID; 4]>,
    /// The rules left out, in the numbers of the process's rules, in increasing order.
    left_out: SmallVec<[RuleID; 8]>,
}

impl UserAgentVariant {
    /// The rules of the sheet published from the native sheet `source_identity` alone, but those
    /// compiled from the native rules `failing`, whose conditions do not hold.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn of_published_sheet(
        rules: &UserAgentRules,
        source_identity: u64,
        failing: &[u64],
    ) -> Option<Self> {
        let sheet = rules.sheet_of_source(source_identity)?;
        let mut left_out: SmallVec<[RuleID; 8]> = failing
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|&identity| rules.store.native.identities.get(&identity))
            .collect();
        left_out.sort_unstable();
        let mut sheets = SmallVec::new();
        sheets.push(sheet);
        Some(Self { sheets, left_out })
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn sheets(&self) -> &[SheetID] {
        &self.sheets
    }

    /// Whether the media of the documents of the variant leave `rule` out.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn leaves_out(&self, rule: RuleID) -> bool {
        self.left_out.binary_search(&rule).is_ok()
    }

    pub(in crate::css::style) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        crate::heap_size::small_vec_bytes(&self.sheets) + crate::heap_size::small_vec_bytes(&self.left_out)
    }
}

/// What a document holds of the process's user agent rules.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct UserAgentBinding {
    rules: Arc<UserAgentRules>,
    /// The document's sheet each published sheet it attached is, by the published sheet's number.
    sheets: SmallVec<[(SheetID, SheetID); 4]>,
    /// The rules whose conditions do not hold in the document, in increasing order.
    left_out: SmallVec<[RuleID; 8]>,
}

impl UserAgentBinding {
    #[inline]
    pub(super) fn store(&self) -> &RuleStore {
        &self.rules.store
    }

    /// The document's sheet the rule `rule` of the process is in.
    pub(super) fn sheet_of(&self, rule: RuleID) -> SheetID {
        let published = self.store().rule_sheet(rule);
        let found = self.sheets.iter().find(|(sheet, _)| *sheet == published);
        found.expect("a document names the rules of the sheets it holds").1
    }

    /// Whether the conditions of `rule`, as the document names it, hold in the document.
    pub(super) fn rule_conditions_hold(&self, rule: RuleID) -> bool {
        let rule = rule.in_user_agent_rules().expect("a user agent rule");
        self.left_out.binary_search(&rule).is_err()
    }

    /// Note whether the conditions of `rule` hold in the document, answering whether that moved.
    pub(super) fn set_rule_conditions_hold(&mut self, rule: RuleID, conditions_hold: bool) -> bool {
        let rule = rule.in_user_agent_rules().expect("a user agent rule");
        match (self.left_out.binary_search(&rule), conditions_hold) {
            (Ok(place), true) => {
                self.left_out.remove(place);
                true
            }
            (Err(place), false) => {
                self.left_out.insert(place, rule);
                true
            }
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        crate::heap_size::small_vec_bytes(&self.sheets) + crate::heap_size::small_vec_bytes(&self.left_out)
    }
}

impl RuleStore {
    #[inline]
    pub(super) fn user_agent_binding(&self) -> &UserAgentBinding {
        self.user_agent
            .as_ref()
            .expect("a document names the rules of the sheets it holds")
    }

    pub(super) fn user_agent_binding_mut(&mut self) -> &mut UserAgentBinding {
        self.user_agent
            .as_mut()
            .expect("a document names the rules of the sheets it holds")
    }

    /// Have `sheet`, a sheet of the document that holds no rules, stand for `published`, a sheet of
    /// `rules`, the newest table of the process's user agent rules.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn bind_user_agent_sheet(
        &mut self,
        sheet: SheetID,
        rules: Arc<UserAgentRules>,
        published: SheetID,
    ) {
        self.sheets[sheet.0 as usize].user_agent = Some(published);
        match &mut self.user_agent {
            Some(binding) => {
                binding.rules = rules;
                binding.sheets.push((published, sheet));
            }
            None => {
                let mut sheets = SmallVec::new();
                sheets.push((published, sheet));
                self.user_agent = Some(UserAgentBinding {
                    rules,
                    sheets,
                    left_out: SmallVec::new(),
                });
            }
        }
    }

    /// The process's user agent rules the document holds.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn user_agent_rules(&self) -> Option<&Arc<UserAgentRules>> {
        self.user_agent.as_ref().map(|binding| &binding.rules)
    }

    /// Which of the process's user agent rules decide in the document, if any can.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn user_agent_variant(&self) -> Option<UserAgentVariant> {
        let binding = self.user_agent.as_ref()?;
        let sheets: SmallVec<[SheetID; 4]> = self
            .sheets_in_scope(super::TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT)
            .iter()
            .filter(|&&sheet| self.sheet_contributes(sheet))
            .filter_map(|&sheet| self.sheets[sheet.0 as usize].user_agent)
            .collect();
        (!sheets.is_empty()).then(|| UserAgentVariant {
            sheets,
            left_out: binding.left_out.clone(),
        })
    }

    /// The document's name of the user agent rule compiled from the native rule `identity`.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn user_agent_rule_of_identity(&self, identity: u64) -> Option<RuleID> {
        let binding = self.user_agent.as_ref()?;
        let rule = binding.store().native.identities.get(&identity)?;
        // NB: The process's table holds sheets the document may not have attached.
        let published = binding.store().rule_sheet(rule);
        binding
            .sheets
            .iter()
            .any(|(sheet, _)| *sheet == published)
            .then(|| RuleID::of_user_agent(rule))
    }

    /// The native rule `rule` was compiled from, as the document names it.
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn native_target(&self, rule: RuleID) -> Option<super::native::NativeRuleTargetRef<'_>> {
        match rule.in_user_agent_rules() {
            Some(rule) => self.user_agent.as_ref()?.store().native.targets.get(&rule),
            None => self.native.targets.get(&rule),
        }
    }
}

//! The rule index: every attached style rule entry of a tree scope, bucketed by the most selective
//! key its subject compound requires, with the ancestor keys its combinator chain requires.
//!
//! An entry keeps its number for as long as the index lives. A change to some rules indexes those
//! rules again alone: the entries of a rule that left or changed die, leaving every bucket, and the
//! entries of a rule that arrived or changed are appended. What the index indexed is kept by the
//! rule store's identities of the rules and sheets, so the rules a change does not name, such as
//! the user agent's, are never indexed again for it.
//!
//! Shadow trees whose ordered sheets and layers are the same decide with the same entries, which
//! they share as a group: a page with many instances of one component indexes its rules once.
//!
//! NB: An update works at the granularity of the rules a change names: an appended sheet's rules
//!     join the buckets the index has, and nothing else is indexed again.

use super::super::index::dispatch_bloom_bit;
use super::super::selector_analysis::{EntryFacts, collect_tested_ids, state_dispatch_key, subject_dispatch_keys};
use super::super::weak_pool::WeakPool;
use super::super::*;
use super::bloom::AncestorHashes;
use super::extent_map::{Extent, ExtentMap, FrozenExtentMap, KeyHash, PagedExtentMap};
use super::rule_changes::{Regrouped, RuleIndexChanges, StayedEntry};
use super::rule_store::UserAgentVariant;
use super::shared_pages::{PagePool, SharedPages};
use crate::css::container_conditions::ContainerConditionsData;
use crate::css::selector::Specificity;
use smallvec::SmallVec;
use std::hash::Hash;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// The container conditions a rule applies under, in the rule index's gates.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub(super) struct ContainerGateID(std::num::NonZeroU32);

/// The number of a document's first entry of its own. The numbers below it are those of the user
/// agent index the document shares, so a document's own entries keep their numbers whichever user
/// agent index it shares.
pub(super) const FIRST_DOCUMENT_ENTRY: u32 = 1024;

/// The tree scopes whose sheets an entry is of: the document, or a group of shadow trees deciding
/// with the same ordered sheets and layers, which share the entries of those sheets.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Hash, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub(super) struct ScopeGroupID(u32);

impl ScopeGroupID {
    /// The document's own sheets.
    pub(super) const DOCUMENT: Self = Self(0);
}

/// The entries a group of shadow trees shares, with what the trees have alike.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct ScopeGroup {
    pub(super) index: ScopeIndex,
    /// The trees of the group, in the order they joined it. The first ranks the layers of the
    /// entries, which are the same in every tree of the group.
    scopes: SmallVec<[TreeScopeID; 1]>,
    /// The sheets attached to each tree, in cascade order, the entries of which rank by their
    /// place here.
    sheets: Box<[SheetID]>,
    /// The ranks of the layers of each tree.
    layer_ranks: HashMap<CascadeLayerID, u32>,
}

/// The rule an entry is of: a rule of the document's rule store, or of the process's user agent
/// rules, as every document names those.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct EntryRule(u32);

impl EntryRule {
    fn document(rule: RuleID) -> Self {
        assert!(rule.in_user_agent_rules().is_none(), "rule identity space exhausted");
        Self(rule.0)
    }

    fn user_agent(rule: RuleID) -> Self {
        Self(RuleID::of_user_agent(rule).0)
    }
}

/// The number of an [`EntryPlacement`] among those of the entries it numbers.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub(super) struct PlacementID(u32);

/// Where the entries of the rules of one layer of one sheet deciding in one group of scopes
/// decide: every such entry shares the origin, group and ranks it holds, which move here alone
/// when the order of the sheets or layers does.
///
/// NB: An entry holds its rule's position alone, and leaves the sheet's origin, scope and layer
///     order to its placement, which every entry of the sheet and layer shares.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct EntryPlacement {
    pub(super) origin: CascadeOrigin,
    pub(super) group: ScopeGroupID,
    pub(super) layer_rank: u64,
    pub(super) sheet_rank: u64,
    layer: CascadeLayerID,
}

/// Where the selector of an entry is: the list of its rule, and where it starts in the list's arena.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct EntrySource {
    selectors: crate::css::selector::SelectorListRef,
    at: crate::css::selector_arena::ComponentOffset,
}

impl EntrySource {
    pub(in crate::css::style) fn selector(&self) -> crate::css::selector::Selector<'_> {
        self.selectors.selector_at(self.at)
    }

    /// What tells the selector from another for as long as the process lives.
    fn identity(&self) -> crate::css::selector_arena::SelectorKey {
        crate::css::selector_arena::SelectorKey {
            arena: self.selectors.serial(),
            at: self.at,
        }
    }
}

/// What an entry's pseudo-element kind is for an entry styling the element itself.
pub(super) const ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND: u8 = u8::MAX;

/// The entries the selector list `selectors` makes: one for each selector, and a second for a
/// selector styling every search text match, for the current one; with the specificity and the
/// kind of pseudo-element each styles, or `ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND` for the element itself.
pub(in crate::css::style) fn entries_of(
    selectors: &crate::css::selector::SelectorListRef,
) -> impl Iterator<Item = (crate::css::selector::Selector<'_>, Specificity, u8)> + '_ {
    use crate::css::selector::PseudoElementType;
    selectors.iter().flat_map(move |selector| {
        let specificity = selector.specificity();
        let kind = |pseudo_element: Option<PseudoElementType>| {
            pseudo_element.map_or(ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND, |kind| {
                u8::try_from(kind as u16).unwrap_or(ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND - 1)
            })
        };
        let current = selector
            .styles_every_search_text_match()
            .then(|| (selector, specificity, kind(Some(PseudoElementType::SearchTextCurrent))));
        std::iter::once((selector, specificity, kind(selector.target_pseudo_element()))).chain(current)
    })
}

/// One top-level complex selector of one attached style rule.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct IndexedEntry {
    rule: EntryRule,
    /// Where the entry decides, among the placements of the entries numbering it, below
    /// `PLACEMENT_BITS`, and the entry's [`EntryFlags`] above.
    placement_and_flags: u32,
    /// The entry's selector, in the space of the index holding the entry.
    selector: SelectorRef,
    /// The entry's [`PackedSpecificity`], which is three bytes, and the kind of pseudo-element the
    /// entry styles, or `ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND` for the element itself, in the byte above.
    specificity_and_kind: u32,
    pub(super) rule_rank: u64,
}

// NB: Every attached style rule's selector has one, in every document and group of scopes it decides
//     in, so what grows it grows every index. Its selector is a reference into the index's space,
//     and the container conditions of the few gated rules are the index's to say, by rule.
const _: () = assert!(size_of::<IndexedEntry>() == 24);

/// How many bits of [`IndexedEntry::placement_and_flags`] number the placement. Each placement has
/// an entry of its own, so a document has fewer placements than it could hold entries.
const PLACEMENT_BITS: u32 = 24;

/// The specificity of a selector packed into one word: its ids, classes and types counted in eight
/// bits each, from the most significant down, so that packed specificities compare as the
/// specificities do.
///
/// INTEROP: Other engines count each part of a specificity in eight bits too, saturating at 255.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
struct PackedSpecificity(u32);

impl PackedSpecificity {
    fn pack(specificity: Specificity) -> Self {
        Self(specificity.packed())
    }

    fn unpacked(self) -> Specificity {
        let part = |shift: u32| ((self.0 >> shift) & 0xff) as u16;
        Specificity {
            ids: part(16),
            classes: part(8),
            types: part(0),
        }
    }
}

/// The yes-or-no facts of an [`IndexedEntry`], one bit each.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
struct EntryFlags(u8);

impl EntryFlags {
    const SCOPED: u8 = 1 << 0;
    /// The number was of a segment the index let go of, which took the entry's selector with it.
    const SELECTOR_GONE: u8 = 1 << 7;
    /// The entry can match one of two elements and not the other where the style sharing key
    /// holds for both.
    const REVALIDATES: u8 = 1 << 1;
    /// The rule declares custom properties.
    const DECLARES_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES: u8 = 1 << 2;
    /// The rule declares something important.
    const DECLARES_IMPORTANT: u8 = 1 << 3;
    /// The entry is indexed: one whose rule left or changed is in no bucket, and keeps its number
    /// until the index is built again.
    const LIVE: u8 = 1 << 4;
    /// The rule applies under container conditions, which the index holds by rule.
    const GATED: u8 = 1 << 5;
    /// The entry stands for the number of an entry a segment the index binds holds, or for a
    /// number before or after such entries that no entry has.
    const BOUND: u8 = 1 << 6;

    fn has(self, flag: u8) -> bool {
        self.0 & flag != 0
    }
}

impl IndexedEntry {
    /// What tells the entry from another: its selector by its reference in the index's space, and
    /// the rest. Two indexes holding equal entries hold them alike for their own spaces.
    fn identity(&self) -> impl Eq + Hash + '_ {
        let Self {
            rule,
            placement_and_flags,
            selector,
            specificity_and_kind,
            rule_rank,
        } = self;
        (
            rule.0,
            *selector,
            (*specificity_and_kind, *placement_and_flags, *rule_rank),
        )
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    const fn new(
        rule: EntryRule,
        placement: PlacementID,
        selector: SelectorRef,
        specificity: PackedSpecificity,
        rule_rank: u64,
        pseudo_kind: u8,
        flags: EntryFlags,
    ) -> Self {
        assert!(placement.0 < 1 << PLACEMENT_BITS, "entry placement space exhausted");
        assert!(specificity.0 < 1 << 24, "a packed specificity is three bytes");
        Self {
            rule,
            placement_and_flags: placement.0 | (flags.0 as u32) << PLACEMENT_BITS,
            selector,
            specificity_and_kind: specificity.0 | (pseudo_kind as u32) << 24,
            rule_rank,
        }
    }

    /// What stands for the number of an entry of a segment the index let go of, which took the entry's selector with
    /// it, where the entry decided at `placement`.
    fn selector_gone(placement: PlacementID) -> Self {
        let mut entry = Self::BOUND_NUMBER;
        entry.placement_and_flags = placement.0 | (EntryFlags::SELECTOR_GONE as u32) << PLACEMENT_BITS;
        entry
    }

    /// Where the entry decides.
    fn placement(&self) -> PlacementID {
        PlacementID(self.placement_and_flags & ((1 << PLACEMENT_BITS) - 1))
    }

    fn flags(&self) -> EntryFlags {
        EntryFlags((self.placement_and_flags >> PLACEMENT_BITS) as u8)
    }

    fn specificity(&self) -> PackedSpecificity {
        PackedSpecificity(self.specificity_and_kind & 0x00ff_ffff)
    }

    /// The kind of pseudo-element the entry styles, or `ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND` for the element itself.
    pub(super) fn pseudo_kind(&self) -> u8 {
        (self.specificity_and_kind >> 24) as u8
    }

    /// What stands in the document's entries for the number of an entry a bound segment holds, alike
    /// in every document, so that the pages of a segment's numbers are one page of the process.
    const BOUND_NUMBER: Self = Self::new(
        EntryRule(0),
        PlacementID(0),
        SelectorRef(0),
        PackedSpecificity(0),
        0,
        ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND,
        EntryFlags(EntryFlags::BOUND),
    );

    pub(super) fn declares_important(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags().has(EntryFlags::DECLARES_IMPORTANT)
    }

    pub(super) fn live(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags().has(EntryFlags::LIVE)
    }

    fn kill(&mut self) {
        self.placement_and_flags &= !((EntryFlags::LIVE as u32) << PLACEMENT_BITS);
    }
}

/// An entry read in place where it is held: in the entries of the index numbering it or of the
/// user agent index, or in the segment the index binds, whose binding says the rest of it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) enum EntryView<'a> {
    /// An entry of the index's own entries, or of the user agent index's where `user_agent`.
    Held { entry: &'a IndexedEntry, user_agent: bool },
    /// An entry a bound segment holds.
    Bound {
        bound: &'a BoundSegment,
        entry: &'a SegmentEntry,
        /// Whether the entry died for the index binding the segment, which the segment knows nothing of.
        dead: bool,
    },
}

/// What `entry`, held by the document or by a segment, says alike in both of its shapes.
macro_rules! of_either_entry {
    ($view:expr, $entry:ident => $read:expr) => {
        match $view {
            EntryView::Held { entry: $entry, .. } => $read,
            EntryView::Bound { entry: $entry, .. } => $read,
        }
    };
}

impl EntryView<'_> {
    fn flags(&self) -> EntryFlags {
        match self {
            Self::Held { entry, .. } => entry.flags(),
            Self::Bound { entry, dead: false, .. } => entry.flags,
            Self::Bound { entry, dead: true, .. } => EntryFlags(entry.flags.0 & !EntryFlags::LIVE),
        }
    }

    /// The kind of pseudo-element the entry styles, or `ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND` for the element itself.
    pub(super) fn pseudo_kind(&self) -> u8 {
        match self {
            Self::Held { entry, .. } => entry.pseudo_kind(),
            Self::Bound { entry, .. } => entry.pseudo_kind,
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn rule_rank(&self) -> u64 {
        of_either_entry!(self, entry => entry.rule_rank)
    }

    /// The entry's selector, in the space of the index or segment holding the entry.
    pub(super) fn selector(&self) -> SelectorRef {
        of_either_entry!(self, entry => entry.selector)
    }

    fn rule(&self) -> EntryRule {
        match self {
            Self::Held { entry, .. } => entry.rule,
            Self::Bound { bound, entry, .. } => EntryRule::document(RuleID(bound.first_rule.0 + entry.rule)),
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn specificity(&self) -> Specificity {
        match self {
            Self::Held { entry, .. } => entry.specificity().unpacked(),
            Self::Bound { entry, .. } => entry.specificity.unpacked(),
        }
    }

    /// Whether the entry styles a pseudo-element.
    pub(super) fn pseudo_element(&self) -> bool {
        self.pseudo_kind() != ELEMENT_PSEUDO_KIND
    }

    pub(super) fn scoped(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags().has(EntryFlags::SCOPED)
    }

    pub(super) fn revalidates(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags().has(EntryFlags::REVALIDATES)
    }

    pub(super) fn declares_custom_properties(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags().has(EntryFlags::DECLARES_CUSTOM_PROPERTIES)
    }

    pub(super) fn declares_important(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags().has(EntryFlags::DECLARES_IMPORTANT)
    }

    pub(super) fn live(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags().has(EntryFlags::LIVE)
    }

    pub(super) fn gated(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags().has(EntryFlags::GATED)
    }

    /// The entry as the document has it, but for a bound entry's selector, which is in the
    /// segment's space.
    fn indexed(&self) -> IndexedEntry {
        match *self {
            Self::Held { entry, .. } => *entry,
            Self::Bound { bound, entry, .. } => IndexedEntry::new(
                self.rule(),
                bound.placements[usize::from(entry.placement)],
                entry.selector,
                entry.specificity,
                entry.rule_rank,
                entry.pseudo_kind,
                self.flags(),
            ),
        }
    }
}

impl PartialEq for IndexedEntry {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.identity() == other.identity()
    }
}

impl Hash for IndexedEntry {
    fn hash<H: std::hash::Hasher>(&self, state: &mut H) {
        self.identity().hash(state);
    }
}

/// One entry of a rule bucket, on its way into [`Buckets`], with the keys some ancestor of a matching
/// subject necessarily carries, and its selector.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct BucketEntry {
    ancestor_hashes: AncestorHashes,
    /// The entry's number, from the first of the segment where the buckets are a segment's, with
    /// [`Self::IN_OTHER_BUCKETS`], [`Self::SCOPED`], [`Self::COVERED`] and
    /// [`Self::HAS_SIBLING_KEY`].
    entry: u32,
    /// The entry's selector, in the space of the buckets' part.
    selector: SelectorRef,
    /// The key every earlier sibling of a subject right of `~` carries one of, where
    /// [`Self::HAS_SIBLING_KEY`] says the entry has one.
    sibling_key: u32,
    /// The dispatch bloom bits of the ids and classes the subject compound tests, which an element
    /// lacking any of cannot match.
    subject_bloom: u64,
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<BucketEntry>() == 32);

impl BucketEntry {
    /// The entry is in more buckets than this one, which an element can reach it by.
    const IN_OTHER_BUCKETS: u32 = 1 << 31;
    /// The entry's rule is inside `@scope`, whose levels matching reads from the entry.
    const SCOPED: u32 = 1 << 30;
    /// The bucket's key alone proves the selector: an element reaching the entry by its key matches.
    const COVERED: u32 = 1 << 29;
    /// The entry has a [`Self::sibling_key`].
    const HAS_SIBLING_KEY: u32 = 1 << 28;
    /// The bucket's key alone proves the subject compound of the selector, which an element reaching
    /// the entry by its key is matched left of, as it is the only thing the compound tests.
    const SUBJECT_COVERED: u32 = 1 << 26;
    /// [`Self::SUBJECT_COVERED`], where the element's tag is its own ASCII-lowercase form.
    const SUBJECT_COVERED_FOR_A_LOWERCASE_TAG: u32 = 1 << 25;
    /// The bucket's key proves the selector for an element whose tag is its own ASCII-lowercase
    /// form: the selector is a type selector alone, written in ASCII lowercase.
    const COVERED_FOR_A_LOWERCASE_TAG: u32 = 1 << 27;
    const FLAGS: u32 = Self::IN_OTHER_BUCKETS
        | Self::SCOPED
        | Self::COVERED
        | Self::HAS_SIBLING_KEY
        | Self::COVERED_FOR_A_LOWERCASE_TAG
        | Self::SUBJECT_COVERED
        | Self::SUBJECT_COVERED_FOR_A_LOWERCASE_TAG;

    /// The slot of the entry `entry` of `selector`, inside `@scope` where `scoped`.
    fn new(selector: crate::css::selector::Selector<'_>, entry: u32, selector_ref: SelectorRef, scoped: bool) -> Self {
        assert!(entry & Self::FLAGS == 0, "rule entry space exhausted");
        let sibling_key = super::bloom::earlier_sibling_key(selector);
        let mut flags = 0;
        if scoped {
            flags |= Self::SCOPED;
        }
        match is_covered_by_its_key(selector) {
            _ if scoped => {}
            Covered::No => {}
            Covered::Always => flags |= Self::COVERED,
            Covered::ForALowercaseTag => flags |= Self::COVERED_FOR_A_LOWERCASE_TAG,
        }
        match subject_is_covered_by_its_key(selector) {
            _ if scoped => {}
            Covered::No => {}
            Covered::Always => flags |= Self::SUBJECT_COVERED,
            Covered::ForALowercaseTag => flags |= Self::SUBJECT_COVERED_FOR_A_LOWERCASE_TAG,
        }
        if sibling_key.is_some() {
            flags |= Self::HAS_SIBLING_KEY;
        }
        Self {
            ancestor_hashes: AncestorHashes::required_left_of(super::super::selector_analysis::subject_compound(
                selector,
            )),
            entry: entry | flags,
            selector: selector_ref,
            sibling_key: sibling_key.unwrap_or(0),
            subject_bloom: selector.required_dispatch_bloom(),
        }
    }
}

/// The entries reached by each dispatch key.
///
/// A slot is one word for an entry its key proves, its number and flags, which no element reaching
/// it is rejected from. Any other is [`BUCKET_SLOT_WORDS`] words at fixed places, so a scan rejecting
/// candidates reads what it rejects on with nothing to decode.
///
/// NB: The buckets of a sheet segment never change once it is built, and take the smaller shape.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) enum Buckets {
    Growing(ExtentMap<DispatchKey, u32>),
    Frozen(FrozenExtentMap<DispatchKey, u32>),
}

impl Default for Buckets {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::Growing(ExtentMap::default())
    }
}

impl Buckets {
    /// The slots of `key`, where it has any.
    #[inline]
    pub(super) fn get(&self, key: &DispatchKey) -> Option<BucketSlots<'_>> {
        let words = match self {
            Self::Growing(map) => map.get(key),
            Self::Frozen(map) => map.get(key),
        };
        words.map(|words| BucketSlots { words })
    }

    /// The hash [`Self::get_hashed`] takes for `key`.
    #[inline]
    pub(super) fn hash_of(key: &DispatchKey) -> KeyHash {
        FrozenExtentMap::<DispatchKey, u32>::hash_of(key)
    }

    /// The slots of `key`, whose hash is `hash`, where it has any.
    #[inline]
    pub(super) fn get_hashed(&self, key: &DispatchKey, hash: KeyHash) -> Option<BucketSlots<'_>> {
        let words = match self {
            Self::Growing(map) => map.get(key),
            Self::Frozen(map) => map.get_hashed(key, hash),
        };
        words.map(|words| BucketSlots { words })
    }

    pub(super) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::Growing(map) => map.is_empty(),
            Self::Frozen(map) => map.is_empty(),
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn keys(&self) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = &DispatchKey> + '_> {
        match self {
            Self::Growing(map) => Box::new(map.keys()),
            Self::Frozen(map) => Box::new(map.keys()),
        }
    }

    fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::Growing(map) => map.heap_size(),
            Self::Frozen(map) => map.heap_size(),
        }
    }

    fn shrink_to_fit(&mut self) {
        if let Self::Growing(map) = self {
            map.shrink_to_fit();
        }
    }

    fn freeze(&mut self) {
        if let Self::Growing(map) = self {
            *self = Self::Frozen(FrozenExtentMap::of(std::mem::take(map)));
        }
    }

    fn has_slack(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Growing(map) if map.has_slack())
    }

    fn growing(&mut self) -> &mut ExtentMap<DispatchKey, u32> {
        match self {
            Self::Growing(map) => map,
            Self::Frozen(_) => unreachable!("the buckets of a segment do not change"),
        }
    }

    fn push(&mut self, key: DispatchKey, slot: &BucketEntry) {
        let words = self.growing();
        if slot.entry & BucketEntry::COVERED != 0 {
            words.push(key, slot.entry);
            return;
        }
        // NB: A key proving the subject leaves nothing an element reaching the slot could lack.
        let subject_bloom = match slot.entry & BucketEntry::SUBJECT_COVERED != 0 {
            true => 0,
            false => slot.subject_bloom,
        };
        let [first_hash, second_hash, third_hash] = slot.ancestor_hashes.packed_words();
        for word in [
            slot.entry,
            slot.selector.0,
            subject_bloom as u32,
            (subject_bloom >> 32) as u32,
            first_hash,
            second_hash,
            third_hash,
            slot.sibling_key,
        ] {
            words.push(key, word);
        }
    }

    /// Take the slots of the entry `entry` out of the list of `key`.
    fn remove(&mut self, key: &DispatchKey, entry: u32) {
        let Some(kept) = self.get(key).map(|slots| {
            slots
                .filter(|slot| slot.entry() != entry)
                .map(|slot| slot.entry_to_hold())
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        }) else {
            return;
        };
        self.growing().remove(key);
        for slot in &kept {
            self.push(*key, slot);
        }
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    fn count(&self) -> usize {
        let keys: Vec<DispatchKey> = self.keys().copied().collect();
        keys.iter().filter_map(|key| self.get(key)).map(Iterator::count).sum()
    }
}

/// How many words a slot of an entry its key does not prove takes, and where it holds what.
const BUCKET_SLOT_WORDS: usize = 8;
const BUCKET_SLOT_SELECTOR: usize = 1;
const BUCKET_SLOT_BLOOM_LOW: usize = 2;
const BUCKET_SLOT_BLOOM_HIGH: usize = 3;
const BUCKET_SLOT_HASHES: usize = 4;
const BUCKET_SLOT_SIBLING_KEY: usize = 7;

/// The slots of one bucket, as [`Buckets`] holds them.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct BucketSlots<'a> {
    words: &'a [u32],
}

impl<'a> Iterator for BucketSlots<'a> {
    type Item = BucketSlot<'a>;

    #[inline(always)]
    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<BucketSlot<'a>> {
        let &first = self.words.first()?;
        if first & BucketEntry::COVERED != 0 {
            self.words = &self.words[1..];
            // NB: Nothing rejects an element reaching a proven entry: it requires no bit of an element's, and no key
            //     of its ancestors or earlier siblings.
            return Some(BucketSlot {
                entry: first,
                words: &[0; BUCKET_SLOT_WORDS],
            });
        }
        let (words, rest) = self
            .words
            .split_first_chunk::<BUCKET_SLOT_WORDS>()
            .expect("a slot holds the words of a slot");
        self.words = rest;
        Some(BucketSlot { entry: first, words })
    }
}

/// One entry of a rule bucket, read where [`Buckets`] holds it, so that a candidate rejected on its
/// subject's bloom loads that and nothing more.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct BucketSlot<'a> {
    entry: u32,
    words: &'a [u32; BUCKET_SLOT_WORDS],
}

impl BucketSlot<'_> {
    /// The dispatch bloom bits of the ids and classes the subject compound tests, which an element
    /// lacking any of cannot match.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn subject_bloom(&self) -> u64 {
        u64::from(self.words[BUCKET_SLOT_BLOOM_LOW]) | u64::from(self.words[BUCKET_SLOT_BLOOM_HIGH]) << 32
    }

    /// The keys some ancestor of a matching subject necessarily carries.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn ancestor_hashes(&self) -> AncestorHashes {
        AncestorHashes::from_packed_words([
            self.words[BUCKET_SLOT_HASHES],
            self.words[BUCKET_SLOT_HASHES + 1],
            self.words[BUCKET_SLOT_HASHES + 2],
        ])
    }

    /// The entry's selector, in the space of the buckets' part, where the entry is not [`Self::covered`].
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn selector(&self) -> SelectorRef {
        SelectorRef(self.words[BUCKET_SLOT_SELECTOR])
    }

    /// The entry's number, from the first of the segment where the buckets are a segment's.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn entry(&self) -> u32 {
        self.entry & !BucketEntry::FLAGS
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn in_other_buckets(&self) -> bool {
        self.entry & BucketEntry::IN_OTHER_BUCKETS != 0
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn scoped(&self) -> bool {
        self.entry & BucketEntry::SCOPED != 0
    }

    /// Whether the bucket's key proves the selector for an element reaching the entry by it, whose
    /// tag is its own ASCII-lowercase form where `tag_is_lowercase`.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn covered(&self, tag_is_lowercase: bool) -> bool {
        self.entry & BucketEntry::COVERED != 0
            || (tag_is_lowercase && self.entry & BucketEntry::COVERED_FOR_A_LOWERCASE_TAG != 0)
    }

    /// Whether the bucket's key proves the subject compound for an element reaching the entry by it,
    /// whose tag is its own ASCII-lowercase form where `tag_is_lowercase`.
    #[inline(always)]
