//! The check of what the engine holds against a cold reference pass over the same document:
//! one thread, every cache off, on a fork of the engine, so that nothing the reference pass does
//! reaches the document's engine. With `LIBWEB_STYLE_SELFCHECK` set, the document is checked so
//! at the end of each style update that installed styles; `report` prints what differs, any other
//! value but `0` aborts on it. `threads` (or `threads-report`) also checks it against cold passes
//! with their caches on, on one thread and on several: each thread keeps caches and style sharing
//! candidates of its own, so what a pass reuses depends on how its elements spread over threads.
//! The unit tests check the engine with the same comparison.

use super::super::*;
use super::records::{Record, RecordCells, Records, RetainedRecords};
use super::rules::RuleIndex;
use super::traversal;
#[cfg(test)]
use super::write_once::WriteOnce;
use crate::css::custom_properties::CustomPropertyStore;
use crate::css::property_metadata::{FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID, LAST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID, property_name};
use crate::css::style_value::{RetainedStyleValueData, retained_style_values_equal};
use std::sync::Arc;

/// What `LIBWEB_STYLE_SELFCHECK` asks for.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum Mode {
    Off,
    /// Print what differs, and abort.
    Abort,
    /// Print what differs only.
    Report,
}

/// What `LIBWEB_STYLE_SELFCHECK` asks for, read once per document host.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(in super::super) struct SelfCheckSettings {
    mode: Mode,
    /// Whether it asks for the check against cold passes on one thread and on several.
    checks_thread_counts: bool,
}

impl SelfCheckSettings {
    pub(in super::super) fn from_environment() -> Self {
        let (mode, checks_thread_counts) = match std::env::var("LIBWEB_STYLE_SELFCHECK").as_deref() {
            Err(_) | Ok("" | "0") => (Mode::Off, false),
            Ok("report") => (Mode::Report, false),
            Ok("threads") => (Mode::Abort, true),
            Ok("threads-report") => (Mode::Report, true),
            Ok(_) => (Mode::Abort, false),
        };
        Self {
            mode,
            checks_thread_counts,
        }
    }

    pub(in super::super) fn is_enabled(self) -> bool {
        self.mode != Mode::Off
    }
}

/// How many threads the self-check's cold passes on several threads run on.
fn reference_thread_count() -> u32 {
    crate::style_layout_pool::default_thread_count().max(4) as u32
}

/// The names of the groups, by `group_index`.
const GROUP_NAMES: [&str; crate::css::table_group_builder::group_index::COUNT] = [
    "inherited list and table",
    "inherited UI",
    "inherited SVG",
    "inherited text",
    "font",
    "animation",
    "SVG reset",
    "grid",
    "anchor",
    "content",
    "alignment",
    "misc layout",
    "misc interaction",
    "effects",
    "mask",
    "text reset",
    "transform",
    "background",
    "border",
    "sizing",
    "surround",
    "box",
];

/// The element, as its tag, ID and classes, with `name_of` naming their atoms.
pub(super) fn describe(state: &RetainedState, node: StyleNodeID, name_of: &dyn Fn(StyleAtomID) -> String) -> String {
    let Some(facts) = state.projection.facts(node) else {
        return format!("node {}", node.raw());
    };
    let mut description = format!("<{}", name_of(facts.tag()));
    let id = facts.id();
    if !id.is_none() {
        description += &format!(" id={}", name_of(id));
    }
    let classes: Vec<_> = facts.classes().iter().map(|&class| name_of(class)).collect();
    if !classes.is_empty() {
        description += &format!(" class=\"{}\"", classes.join(" "));
    }
    description + &format!("> (node {})", node.raw())
}

pub(super) fn pseudo_element_name(kind: u8) -> String {
    use super::super::publication::pseudo_kind::{
        AFTER, BACKDROP, BEFORE, FIRST_LETTER, MARKER, SEARCH_TEXT, SEARCH_TEXT_CURRENT, SELECTION, SPELLING_ERROR,
    };
    match kind {
        BEFORE => "::before".to_owned(),
        AFTER => "::after".to_owned(),
        FIRST_LETTER => "::first-letter".to_owned(),
        SELECTION => "::selection".to_owned(),
        SEARCH_TEXT => "::search-text".to_owned(),
        SEARCH_TEXT_CURRENT => "::search-text:current".to_owned(),
        SPELLING_ERROR => "::spelling-error".to_owned(),
        BACKDROP => "::backdrop".to_owned(),
        MARKER => "::marker".to_owned(),
        kind => format!("pseudo-element {kind}"),
    }
}

pub(super) fn pseudo_element_target_name(target: super::PseudoElementTarget) -> String {
    match target.is_custom_highlight() {
        true => format!("::highlight() of atom {}", target.highlight_name.0),
        false => pseudo_element_name(target.kind),
    }
}

fn payloads_equal(
    group: usize,
    first: &crate::css::computed_values::GroupPointer,
    second: &crate::css::computed_values::GroupPointer,
) -> bool {
    let (first, second) = (first.as_ptr(), second.as_ptr());
    // SAFETY: Both are live payloads of the group.
    first == second || unsafe { crate::css::computed_values::style_group_payloads_equal(group, first, second) }
}

fn serialized(value: Option<&RetainedStyleValueData>) -> String {
    value.map_or_else(
        || "(none)".to_owned(),
        |value| String::from_utf16_lossy(&crate::css::serialize::serialize_style_value_to_utf16(value.data())),
    )
}

/// The values of the custom properties whose names resolve to different values in two stores,
/// whichever stores the values are in, as the first's and the second's.
fn custom_property_differences(
    first: Option<&Arc<CustomPropertyStore>>,
    second: Option<&Arc<CustomPropertyStore>>,
) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    fn append_names(store: &CustomPropertyStore, names: &mut Vec<usize>) {
        names.extend(store.own_values.keys());
        if let Some(parent) = store.parent() {
            append_names(parent, names);
        }
    }
    let (first, second) = (first.map(Arc::as_ref), second.map(Arc::as_ref));
    let mut all = Vec::new();
    for store in [first, second].into_iter().flatten() {
        append_names(store, &mut all);
    }
    all.sort_unstable();
    all.dedup();
    let describe = |entry: Option<&crate::css::custom_properties::CustomPropertyEntry>| {
        entry.map_or_else(
            || "(none)".to_owned(),
            |entry| match entry.important {
                true => format!("{} !important", serialized(Some(&entry.value))),
                false => serialized(Some(&entry.value)),
            },
        )
    };
    all.into_iter()
        .filter_map(|name| {
            let (first, second) = (
                first.and_then(|store| store.get(name)),
                second.and_then(|store| store.get(name)),
            );
            let equal = match (first, second) {
                (None, None) => true,
                (Some(first), Some(second)) => {
                    first.important == second.important && retained_style_values_equal(&first.value, &second.value)
                }
                _ => false,
            };
            (!equal).then(|| (describe(first), describe(second)))
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The parts `live` differs from `cold` in, compared by value: the payloads of the groups, the
/// longhands, what their groups are built from and their flags as published, the custom properties by the values their names resolve to, and
/// what the record notes of how it was computed, each with the values that differ where they
/// have a text.
pub(super) fn record_differences(live: &Record, cold: &Record) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut differences = Vec::new();
    let groups: Vec<_> = (0..crate::css::table_group_builder::group_index::COUNT)
        .filter(|&group| !payloads_equal(group, &live.payloads[group], &cold.payloads[group]))
        .map(|group| GROUP_NAMES[group])
        .collect();
    if !groups.is_empty() {
        differences.push(format!("the groups {}", groups.join(", ")));
    }
    let (live_longhands, cold_longhands) = (
        computed::ViewLonghands::of_record(live),
        computed::ViewLonghands::of_record(cold),
    );
    let longhands: Vec<_> = (FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID..=LAST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID)
        .filter_map(|property| {
            let (ours, theirs) = (live_longhands.handle(property), cold_longhands.handle(property));
            let equal = match (ours, theirs) {
                (None, None) => true,
                (Some(ours), Some(theirs)) => retained_style_values_equal(ours, theirs),
                _ => false,
            };
            (!equal).then(|| {
                format!(
                    "{}: live {}, cold {}",
                    property_name(property),
                    serialized(ours),
                    serialized(theirs)
                )
            })
        })
        .collect();
    if !longhands.is_empty() {
        differences.push(format!("the longhands {{{}}}", longhands.join("; ")));
    } else if !live.rare().value_facts.publication_equals(&cold.rare().value_facts) {
        differences.push(format!(
            "the groups, in {}",
            live.rare()
                .value_facts
                .difference(&cold.rare().value_facts)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "what they are built from beside their values".into())
        ));
    }
    let flags = live
        .rare()
        .table_flags
        .publication_differences(&cold.rare().table_flags);
    if !flags.is_empty() {
        differences.push(format!("the longhand table flags {{{}}}", flags.join("; ")));
    }
    if live.facts() != cold.facts() {
        differences.push("the record facts".into());
    }
    if live.payloads.current_color() != cold.payloads.current_color() {
        differences.push(format!(
            "current color {:#010x} != {:#010x}",
            live.payloads.current_color(),
            cold.payloads.current_color()
        ));
    }
    for (name, live, cold) in [
        ("custom properties", live.custom_properties(), cold.custom_properties()),
        (
            "inheritable custom properties",
            live.inheritable_custom_properties(),
            cold.inheritable_custom_properties(),
        ),
    ] {
        let values = custom_property_differences(live, cold);
        if !values.is_empty() {
            let values: Vec<_> = values
                .iter()
                .map(|(live, cold)| format!("live {live}, cold {cold}"))
                .collect();
            differences.push(format!("{name} {{{}}}", values.join("; ")));
        }
    }
    // NB: A cascade decides one declaration per name, so the order of the list says nothing.
    let custom_declarations_equal = match (&live.custom_declarations(), &cold.custom_declarations()) {
        (None, None) => true,
        (Some(first), Some(second)) => {
            let same_declaration =
                |first: &(CustomDeclaration, RetainedStyleValueData),
                 second: &(CustomDeclaration, RetainedStyleValueData)| {
                    first.0 == second.0 && retained_style_values_equal(&first.1, &second.1)
                };
            first.len() == second.len()
                && (first
                    .iter()
                    .zip(second.iter())
                    .all(|(first, second)| same_declaration(first, second))
                    || first
                        .iter()
                        .all(|declaration| second.iter().any(|other| same_declaration(declaration, other))))
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    if !custom_declarations_equal {
        differences.push("custom declarations".to_owned());
    }
    if live.rare().custom_property_reads != cold.rare().custom_property_reads {
        differences.push("the custom properties the longhands read".to_owned());
    }
    if live.rare().reads.parent_reset_groups != cold.rare().reads.parent_reset_groups {
        differences.push(format!(
            "parent_reset_groups {:#x} != {:#x}",
            live.rare().reads.parent_reset_groups,
            cold.rare().reads.parent_reset_groups
        ));
    }
    for (name, live, cold) in [
        (
            "reads_sibling_position",
            live.rare().reads.reads_sibling_position,
            cold.rare().reads.reads_sibling_position,
        ),
        (
            "reads_attributes",
            live.rare().reads.reads_attributes,
            cold.rare().reads.reads_attributes,
        ),
    ] {
        if live != cold {
            differences.push(format!("{name} {live} != {cold}"));
        }
    }
    if live.rare().reads.container_units != cold.rare().reads.container_units {
        differences.push(format!(
            "container units {:#x} != {:#x}",
            live.rare().reads.container_units,
            cold.rare().reads.container_units
        ));
    }
    if live.rare().counter_style_environment_identity != cold.rare().counter_style_environment_identity {
        differences.push("counter style environment".to_owned());
    }
    if live.rare().animation_name_scope != cold.rare().animation_name_scope {
        differences.push("animation name scope".to_owned());
    }
    differences
}

/// What the records `live` holds for the document under `root`, of each element and of its
/// pseudo-elements, differ in from those `cold` holds, one line per element or pseudo-element,
/// with `describe` naming the elements, and how many elements it compared.
pub(super) fn differences(
    state: &RetainedState,
    root: StyleNodeID,
    live: &RetainedRecords,
    cold: &RetainedRecords,
    describe: &dyn Fn(StyleNodeID) -> String,
) -> (Vec<String>, usize) {
    let (failures, compared) = differences_by_element(state, root, live, cold);
    let failures = failures
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(node, difference)| match difference.strip_prefix("::") {
            Some(of_pseudo_element) => {
                let (name, rest) = of_pseudo_element.split_once(": ").unwrap_or((of_pseudo_element, ""));
                format!("::{name} of {}: {rest}", describe(node))
            }
            None => format!("{}: {difference}", describe(node)),
        })
        .collect();
    (failures, compared)
}

/// What differs between `live` and `cold`, one line per element or pseudo-element beginning with
/// the name of the pseudo-element where it is one, with the element it is about.
pub(super) fn differences_by_element(
    state: &RetainedState,
    root: StyleNodeID,
    live: &RetainedRecords,
    cold: &RetainedRecords,
) -> (Vec<(StyleNodeID, String)>, usize) {
    let mut failures = Vec::new();
    let mut compared = 0;
    // NB: The engine keeps the records of the elements below one that stopped being displayed,
    //     which no pass keeps current and the host installs none of.
    let hidden_in_cold = |node| {
        std::iter::successors(state.projection.inheritance_parent(node), |&ancestor| {
            state.projection.inheritance_parent(ancestor)
        })
        .any(|ancestor| cold.get(ancestor).is_none_or(|record| !record.is_displayed()))
    };
    for node in state.projection.style_preorder(root) {
        match (live.get(node), cold.get(node)) {
            (None, None) => continue,
            (Some(_), None) if hidden_in_cold(node) => continue,
            (Some(_), None) => failures.push((node, "live holds a record, cold computed none".to_owned())),
            (None, Some(_)) => failures.push((node, "live holds no record, cold computed one".to_owned())),
            // NB: No pass samples the animations of an element that is not displayed. A cold pass reads what a read
            //     below it last sampled, which the record the passes keep does not, and a read samples them again.
            (Some(live), Some(_)) if !live.is_displayed() && state.element_samples_custom_properties(node) => continue,
            (Some(live), Some(cold)) => {
                let differences = record_differences(live, cold);
                if !differences.is_empty() {
                    failures.push((node, format!("live differs from cold in {}", differences.join(", "))));
                }
            }
        }
        compared += 1;
        let (live, cold) = (live.pseudo_element_records(node), cold.pseudo_element_records(node));
        let targets = |records: &[(super::PseudoElementTarget, Arc<Record>)]| {
            records.iter().map(|(target, _)| *target).collect::<Vec<_>>()
        };
        if targets(live) != targets(cold) {
            let names = |targets: Vec<super::PseudoElementTarget>| {
                targets.into_iter().map(pseudo_element_target_name).collect::<Vec<_>>()
            };
            failures.push((
                node,
                format!(
                    "live holds the pseudo-elements {:?}, cold computed {:?}",
                    names(targets(live)),
                    names(targets(cold))
                ),
            ));
            continue;
        }
        for ((target, live), (_, cold)) in live.iter().zip(cold) {
            let differences = record_differences(live, cold);
            if !differences.is_empty() {
                failures.push((
                    node,
                    format!(
                        "{}: live differs from cold in {}",
                        pseudo_element_target_name(*target),
                        differences.join(", ")
                    ),
                ));
            }
        }
    }
    (failures, compared)
}

/// What the records installed for the elements under `root` and their pseudo-elements, which the host renders, differ
/// in from those `live` holds for them, one line per element or pseudo-element, with `describe` naming the elements.
/// An element's animations compose over its installed record, which is what is compared.
pub(super) fn installed_differences(
    state: &RetainedState,
    root: StyleNodeID,
    live: &RetainedRecords,
    describe: &dyn Fn(StyleNodeID) -> String,
) -> Vec<String> {
    let installed = &state.computed_group_sets;
    let mut failures = Vec::new();
    for node in state.projection.style_preorder(root) {
        // NB: The engine keeps the records of the elements below one that stopped being displayed,
        //     which no pass keeps current and the host installs none of. What the host holds for an
        //     element that is itself not displayed is what a read below it last sampled, and a read
        //     of it demands its style again.
        let hidden = std::iter::successors(Some(node), |&ancestor| state.projection.inheritance_parent(ancestor))
            .any(|ancestor| live.get(ancestor).is_none_or(|record| !record.is_displayed()));
        if hidden {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(held) = live.get(node)
            && let Some(record) = installed
                .assigned_style_record(node)
                .and_then(|record| installed.installed_base_record(record))
        {
            let differences = record_differences(record, held);
            if !differences.is_empty() {
                failures.push(format!(
                    "{}: the installed record differs from live in {}",
                    describe(node),
                    differences.join(", ")
                ));
            }
        }
        for (target, held) in live.pseudo_element_records(node) {
            let Some(record) = state
                .installed_pseudo_style_record(node, *target)
                .and_then(|record| installed.installed_base_record(record))
            else {
                continue;
            };
            let differences = record_differences(record, held);
            if !differences.is_empty() {
                failures.push(format!(
                    "{} of {}: the installed record differs from live in {}",
                    pseudo_element_target_name(*target),
                    describe(node),
                    differences.join(", ")
                ));
            }
        }
    }
    failures
}

/// What a reference pass computed.
pub(super) struct ReferencePass {
    pub(super) records: RetainedRecords,
    /// What its last round produced for each element.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(super) outputs: Vec<WriteOnce<traversal::ElementOutput>>,
}

/// Style the document under `engine`'s `root` from scratch on `threads` threads, against a rule
/// index of its own, and with every cache off unless `uses_caches`, and keep what it computed, or
/// none where it computes no initial style or waits on fonts or random base values for good. It
/// resolves the fonts and draws the random base values it waits on in `engine`.
pub(super) fn reference_pass(
    engine: &mut StyleEngine,
    root: StyleNodeID,
    uses_caches: bool,
    threads: u32,
) -> Option<ReferencePass> {
    let initial = engine.computed_initial(root)?;
    // NB: A pass on one thread leaves the engine's pool as it is.
    let pool = (threads > 1).then(|| engine.style_layout_pool(threads)).flatten();
    let index = RuleIndex::build(&engine.retained.rules, engine.retained.process_rule_indexes());
    engine.retained.live_counters.note_cold_pass_index(&index);
    // A drive that waits on a font declines its element; the pass styles every element again once
    // the resolver answered.
    engine.until_resolved(root, |engine| {
        let state: &RetainedState = &engine.retained;
        let slot_count = state.projection.element_slot_count();
        let mut cells = RecordCells::default();
        cells.reserve(slot_count);
        #[cfg(test)]
        let outputs: Vec<WriteOnce<traversal::ElementOutput>> = (0..slot_count).map(|_| WriteOnce::default()).collect();
        let statistics = {
            let records = Records::new(state, &cells, None)
                .composing_over_equal_records(|first, second| record_differences(first, second).is_empty());
            let context = traversal::PassContext {
                #[cfg(test)]
                outputs: Some(&outputs),
                uses_caches,
                cache_audit: state.cache_audit_mode(),
                ..traversal::PassContext::new(state, &index, &initial, &records, None)
            };
            traversal::style_document(&context, pool.as_deref(), root)
        };
        if statistics.font_requests.is_empty() && statistics.random_requests.is_empty() {
            let styled: Vec<_> = state.projection.style_preorder(root).collect();
            let mut records = RetainedRecords::default();
            records.absorb(&mut cells, &styled, None, &mut Default::default());
            return Ok(ReferencePass {
                records,
                #[cfg(test)]
                outputs,
            });
        }
        Err(super::Waits {
            fonts: statistics.font_requests,
            random_bases: statistics.random_requests,
        })
    })
}

impl StyleEngine {
    /// What the records the engine holds for the document under `root` differ in from those of
    /// a reference pass over a fork of the engine, one line per element or pseudo-element, or none
    /// where the engine does not own the document or has restyling left to do. Where
    /// `other_threads` names a number of threads, they are also checked against cold passes with
    /// their caches on, on one thread and on that many, with their lines naming the pass.
    pub(super) fn self_check_failures(&self, root: StyleNodeID, other_threads: Option<u32>) -> Vec<String> {
        let Some(live) = self.retained.live_style.as_deref() else {
            return Vec::new();
        };
        // NB: A pass leaving children for the next one, to inherit the composition of their
        //     parents' animations, leaves their records as they were until then.
        if live.has_pending() {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let mut fork = self.clone();
        fork.detach_host_flags_for_fork();
        fork.detach_tree_depth_for_fork();
        let name_of = |atom: StyleAtomID| self.atoms.name_of(atom).unwrap_or_else(|| format!("atom{}", atom.0));
        let describe = |node| describe(&self.retained, node, &name_of);
        let mut references = vec![(None, false, 1)];
        if let Some(threads) = other_threads {
            references.push((Some("a cold pass on 1 thread with caches".to_owned()), true, 1));
            references.push((
                Some(format!("a cold pass on {threads} threads with caches")),
                true,
                threads,
            ));
        }
        let mut failures = Vec::new();
        for (name, uses_caches, threads) in references {
            let Some(ReferencePass { records: reference, .. }) = reference_pass(&mut fork, root, uses_caches, threads)
            else {
                failures.push(format!(
                    "the reference pass computes no style for the document{}",
                    name.as_ref().map_or_else(String::new, |name| format!(" on {name}"))
                ));
                continue;
            };
            let (differences, _) = differences(&self.retained, root, &live.records, &reference, &describe);
            failures.extend(differences.into_iter().map(|difference| match &name {
                Some(name) => format!("against {name}: {difference}"),
                None => difference,
            }));
        }
        failures.extend(installed_differences(&self.retained, root, &live.records, &describe));
        failures.extend(live.kept_hidden_differences(&self.retained, &describe));
        failures
    }

    /// What the engine holds for the document under `root` disagrees in with a reference pass over
    /// the same inputs and with the records the host installed, one line per element or
    /// pseudo-element, naming each element the engine holds no record of where the host installed one.
    pub(in super::super) fn self_check_report(&self, root: StyleNodeID) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut lines = self.self_check_failures(root, None);
        if let Some(live) = self.retained.live_style.as_deref() {
            let name_of = |atom: StyleAtomID| self.atoms.name_of(atom).unwrap_or_else(|| format!("atom{}", atom.0));
            for node in self.retained.projection.style_preorder(root) {
                if node.element_index().is_some()
                    && self.retained.computed_group_sets.assigned_style_record(node).is_some()
                    && live.records.get(node).is_none()
                {
                    lines.push(format!(
                        "{}: the host installed a record, live holds none",
                        describe(&self.retained, node, &name_of)
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
        lines
    }

    /// Check the records the engine holds for the document under `root` against a reference
    /// pass, as `settings` ask.
    pub(in super::super) fn run_self_check(&self, root: StyleNodeID, settings: SelfCheckSettings) {
        if !settings.is_enabled() {
            return;
        }
        let other_threads = settings.checks_thread_counts.then(reference_thread_count);
        conclude(&self.self_check_failures(root, other_threads), settings.mode);
    }
}

/// Print `failures` to stderr, and abort where `mode` asks to.
pub(super) fn conclude(failures: &[String], mode: Mode) {
    if failures.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    eprintln!(
        "Style self-check: the engine differs from a cold pass in {} places:",
        failures.len()
    );
    for failure in failures {
        eprintln!("    {failure}");
    }
    assert!(
        mode != Mode::Abort,
        "the engine differs from a cold pass; set LIBWEB_STYLE_SELFCHECK=report to only print the differences"
    );
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::super::test_support::*;
    use super::*;

    fn document_with_a_target() -> (StyleEngine, Vec<StyleNodeID>) {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = linear_document();
        let sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
        add_rules(
            &mut engine,
            sheet,
            ".target { color: rgb(0, 128, 0); width: 10px; } .target::before { content: \"x\"; }",
        );
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "target");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        (engine, nodes)
    }

    #[test]
    fn live_style_holds_what_a_reference_pass_computes() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_a_target();
        assert_eq!(engine.self_check_failures(nodes[0], None), Vec::<String>::new());

        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "target");
        remove_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "target");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_eq!(engine.self_check_failures(nodes[0], None), Vec::<String>::new());
    }

    #[test]
    fn live_style_holds_what_cold_passes_on_one_thread_and_on_four_compute() {
        let (engine, nodes) = document_with_a_target();
        assert_eq!(engine.self_check_failures(nodes[0], Some(4)), Vec::<String>::new());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_record_live_style_holds_wrongly_is_reported() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_a_target();
        // Seed a mismatch: the element no rule styles holds the record of the one the rule styles.
        let seeded = live_record(&engine, nodes[2]);
        let mut live = engine.retained.live_style.take().expect("the engine is live");
        let mut cells = RecordCells::default();
        cells.reserve(engine.retained.projection.element_slot_count());
        Records::new(&engine.retained, &cells, None).insert(nodes[1], seeded, nodes[1], None);
        live.records
            .absorb(&mut cells, &[nodes[1]], None, &mut Default::default());
        engine.retained.live_style = Some(live);

        let failures = engine.self_check_failures(nodes[0], Some(4));
        assert_eq!(failures.len(), 4, "{failures:?}");
        assert!(
            failures[1].starts_with("against a cold pass on 1 thread with caches: "),
            "{failures:?}"
        );
        assert!(
            failures[2].starts_with("against a cold pass on 4 threads with caches: "),
            "{failures:?}"
        );
        // NB: What it installed is what a pass computed before the seed, which the seeded record differs from too.
        assert!(
            failures[3].contains(&format!(
                "(node {}): the installed record differs from live in ",
                nodes[1].raw()
            )),
            "{failures:?}"
        );
        let failure = &failures[0];
        // NB: The atoms of a test's engine name no strings the self-check could show.
        assert!(
            failure.contains(&format!("(node {}): live differs from cold in ", nodes[1].raw())),
            "{failure}"
        );
        for part in [
            "the groups ",
            "inherited text",
            "color: live ",
            "width: live 10px, cold auto",
        ] {
            assert!(failure.contains(part), "{failure} names {part}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_record_installed_for_another_element_is_reported() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = document_with_a_target();
        // Seed a mismatch: the engine holds the right records, and the element no rule styles is
        // assigned the record installed for the one the rule styles.
        let sets = &mut engine.retained.computed_group_sets;
        let installed = sets.assigned_style_record(nodes[2]).expect("the element is installed");
        sets.assign_installed_record(nodes[1], installed);

        let failures = engine.self_check_failures(nodes[0], None);
        assert_eq!(failures.len(), 1, "{failures:?}");
        assert!(
            failures[0].contains(&format!(
                "(node {}): the installed record differs from live in ",
                nodes[1].raw()
            )),
            "{failures:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_report_only_prints_the_differences() {
        conclude(&["a difference".to_owned()], Mode::Report);
        conclude(&[], Mode::Abort);
    }

    #[test]
    #[should_panic(expected = "the engine differs from a cold pass")]
    fn a_difference_aborts() {
        conclude(&["a difference".to_owned()], Mode::Abort);
    }
}

/*

//! A vector held in pages that documents holding equal pages share through a pool of the
//! process's: frames of a site whose rules are numbered alike hold one copy of each page.
//!
//! A page is shared once it is published to the pool, and copied by the first edit after that, so
//! an edit never reaches another holder of the page.

use super::super::weak_pool::WeakPool;
use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

pub(super) const VALUES_PER_PAGE: usize = 128;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct Page<T> {
    values: Vec<T>,
    /// The hash the page is published to the pool under, or none while it is unpublished.
    shared_hash: Option<u64>,
}

/// The pool of a process's pages of one kind.
pub(super) type PagePool<T> = Mutex<WeakPool<Page<T>>>;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct SharedPages<T> {
    pages: Vec<Arc<Page<T>>>,
    len: usize,
}

impl<T> Default for SharedPages<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            pages: Vec::new(),
            len: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl<T: Clone + PartialEq + Hash> SharedPages<T> {
    pub(super) fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.len
    }

    pub(super) fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&T> {
        (index < self.len).then(|| &self.pages[index / VALUES_PER_PAGE].values[index % VALUES_PER_PAGE])
    }

    pub(super) fn get_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> &mut T {
        assert!(index < self.len);
        let page = Arc::make_mut(&mut self.pages[index / VALUES_PER_PAGE]);
        page.shared_hash = None;
        &mut page.values[index % VALUES_PER_PAGE]
    }

    pub(super) fn push(&mut self, value: T) {
        if self.len.is_multiple_of(VALUES_PER_PAGE) {
            self.pages.push(Arc::new(Page {
                values: Vec::with_capacity(VALUES_PER_PAGE),
                shared_hash: None,
            }));
        }
        let page = Arc::make_mut(self.pages.last_mut().expect("a page has room"));
        page.shared_hash = None;
        page.values.push(value);
        self.len += 1;
    }

    /// Keep the first `len` values alone.
    pub(super) fn truncate(&mut self, len: usize) {
        if len >= self.len {
            return;
        }
        self.pages.truncate(len.div_ceil(VALUES_PER_PAGE));
        if let Some(last) = self.pages.last_mut()
            && !len.is_multiple_of(VALUES_PER_PAGE)
        {
            let page = Arc::make_mut(last);
            page.shared_hash = None;
            page.values.truncate(len % VALUES_PER_PAGE);
        }
        self.len = len;
    }

    pub(super) fn shrink_to_fit(&mut self) {
        self.pages.shrink_to_fit();
        if let Some(last) = self.pages.last_mut()
            && last.values.len() != last.values.capacity()
        {
            Arc::make_mut(last).values.shrink_to_fit();
        }
    }

    /// Publish the pages to `pool`, taking an equal page another holder published instead of each.
    pub(super) fn share(&mut self, pool: &PagePool<T>) {
        let mut pool = pool.lock().unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
        for page in &mut self.pages {
            if page.shared_hash.is_some() {
                continue;
            }
            let mut hasher = super::super::fast_hash::fast_hasher();
            page.values.hash(&mut hasher);
            let hash = hasher.finish();
            if let Some(found) = pool.find(hash, |candidate| candidate.values == page.values) {
                *page = found;
                continue;
            }
            Arc::make_mut(page).shared_hash = Some(hash);
            pool.insert(hash, page);
        }
    }

    /// The bytes of the pages, each counted the first time `sizer` reaches it, with what
    /// `value_heap` says each value holds.
    pub(super) fn heap_size(
        &self,
        sizer: &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer,
        mut value_heap: impl FnMut(&T, &mut crate::heap_size::HeapSizer) -> usize,
    ) -> usize {
        let mut bytes = crate::heap_size::vec_bytes(&self.pages);
        for page in &self.pages {
            if sizer.first_sight(Arc::as_ptr(page)) {
                bytes += crate::heap_size::ARC_HEADER_BYTES
                    + size_of::<Page<T>>()
                    + crate::heap_size::vec_bytes(&page.values)
                    + page.values.iter().map(|value| value_heap(value, sizer)).sum::<usize>();
            }
        }
        bytes
    }
}

impl<T: Clone + PartialEq + Hash> std::ops::Index<usize> for SharedPages<T> {
    type Output = T;

    fn index(&self, index: usize) -> &T {
        self.get(index).expect("an index within the pages")
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn equal_pages_share_and_an_edit_copies_only_its_page() {
        let pool = PagePool::<u32>::default();
        let make = || {
            let mut pages = SharedPages::default();
            for value in 0..(VALUES_PER_PAGE * 2 + 1) as u32 {
                pages.push(value);
            }
            pages.share(&pool);
            pages
        };
        let first = make();
        let mut second = make();
        for (left, right) in first.pages.iter().zip(&second.pages) {
            assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(left, right));
        }
        *second.get_mut(VALUES_PER_PAGE + 3) = 7;
        assert_eq!(first[VALUES_PER_PAGE + 3], (VALUES_PER_PAGE + 3) as u32);
        assert_eq!(second[VALUES_PER_PAGE + 3], 7);
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&first.pages[0], &second.pages[0]));
        assert!(!Arc::ptr_eq(&first.pages[1], &second.pages[1]));
        second.push(9);
        assert_eq!(first.len(), VALUES_PER_PAGE * 2 + 1);
        assert_eq!(second.len(), first.len() + 1);
        assert_eq!(second[first.len()], 9);
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! A vector that starts with the elements of a frozen one it shares with others, and goes on with
//! its own: a structure built once for the process, such as the invalidation map of the user
//! agent's rules, is the shared start of every document's, which adds its own after it, and the
//! numbers of the shared elements are the same in every document.

use std::ops::{Index, IndexMut, Range};
use std::sync::Arc;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct SharedPrefixVec<T> {
    shared: Arc<[T]>,
    own: Vec<T>,
}

impl<T> Default for SharedPrefixVec<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            shared: Arc::from(Vec::new()),
            own: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}

impl<T: Clone> SharedPrefixVec<T> {
    pub(super) fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.shared.len() + self.own.len()
    }

    pub(super) fn push(&mut self, value: T) {
        self.own.push(value);
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(super) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &T> {
        self.shared.iter().chain(&self.own)
    }

    pub(super) fn shrink_to_fit(&mut self) {
        self.own.shrink_to_fit();
    }

    /// Make every element shared: clones of the vector then share all of them.
    pub(super) fn freeze(&mut self) {
        if self.own.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let mut all = Vec::with_capacity(self.len());
        all.extend_from_slice(&self.shared);
        all.append(&mut self.own);
        self.shared = Arc::from(all);
        self.own = Vec::new();
    }

    /// Whether the vector shares every element `base` holds, all of which it shares.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(super) fn shares_prefix_of(&self, base: &Self) -> bool {
        base.own.is_empty() && Arc::ptr_eq(&self.shared, &base.shared)
    }

    /// The bytes of the vector's own elements.
    pub(super) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        crate::heap_size::vec_bytes(&self.own)
    }

    /// The bytes of the elements the vector shares.
    pub(super) fn shared_heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        size_of_val::<[T]>(&self.shared)
    }
}

impl<T> Index<usize> for SharedPrefixVec<T> {
    type Output = T;

    fn index(&self, index: usize) -> &T {
        match index.checked_sub(self.shared.len()) {
            Some(own) => &self.own[own],
            None => &self.shared[index],
        }
    }
}

impl<T> IndexMut<usize> for SharedPrefixVec<T> {
    fn index_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> &mut T {
        let own = index
            .checked_sub(self.shared.len())
            .expect("a shared element is never written");
        &mut self.own[own]
    }
}

/// A range of elements all shared or all the vector's own, as the elements one thing added are.
impl<T> Index<Range<usize>> for SharedPrefixVec<T> {
    type Output = [T];

    fn index(&self, range: Range<usize>) -> &[T] {
        let shared = self.shared.len();
        if range.end <= shared {
            return &self.shared[range];
        }
        assert!(range.start >= shared, "a range is all shared or all own");
        &self.own[range.start - shared..range.end - shared]
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn a_clone_of_a_frozen_vector_shares_its_elements_and_adds_its_own() {
        let mut base = SharedPrefixVec::default();
        for value in [1, 2, 3] {
            base.push(value);
        }
        base.freeze();
        let mut document = base.clone();
        document.push(4);
        document.push(5);
        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&base.shared, &document.shared));
        assert_eq!(document.len(), 5);
        assert_eq!(document[1], 2);
        assert_eq!(document[4], 5);
        assert_eq!(&document[3..5], &[4, 5]);
        assert_eq!(&document[0..2], &[1, 2]);
        document[3] = 6;
        document[4] = 7;
        assert_eq!(document.iter().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [1, 2, 3, 6, 7]);
        assert_eq!(base.len(), 3);
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! The style sharing cache: an element that agrees with one styled shortly before it on everything
//! its style could depend on takes that element's record instead of matching, cascading and
//! computing its own.
//!
//! Two elements agree when their parents are the same element or shared a style through this cache, which by
//! induction makes their ancestor chains indistinguishable to selectors, and they themselves have
//! the same tag, namespace, classes and states, no id a selector tests for, and no declarations of
//! their own. Rule entries that read anything beyond that, such as attributes or siblings,
//! revalidate: they are evaluated for the element and must match exactly as they matched the
//! candidate.

use super::super::index::StateSet;
use super::super::*;
use super::matching::ElementMatch;
use super::projection::ElementFacts;
use super::records::Record;
use super::rules::RuleIndex;
use smallvec::SmallVec;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// How many recently styled elements each thread keeps to share with.
const CAPACITY: usize = 16;

/// What two elements must agree on, besides their classes, custom states and parts, to share.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) struct SharingKey {
    /// The sharing identity of the parent.
    parent: StyleNodeID,
    /// The sharing identity of the inheritance parent, or the inheritance parent itself where the
    /// host composes its animations over its record: elements sharing a record do not share a
    /// composition.
    inheritance_parent: StyleNodeID,
    inheritance_parent_composes: bool,
    tag: StyleAtomID,
    namespace: StyleAtomID,
    states: StateSet,
    directionality: StyleAtomID,
    language: StyleAtomID,
    heading_level: u8,
    part_exposure: StyleAtomID,
    adjustment_facts: u32,
    tree_scope: TreeScopeID,
    assigned_slot: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    /// The records of the highlight pseudo-elements of the inheritance parent, which those of the
    /// element inherit from.
    highlight_parents: [usize; 4],
    /// The highlights the host shows in the element, whose pseudo-elements a pass styles.
    highlight_observers: u8,
}

/// The matched entries that revalidate, with the scope proximity of each.
pub(super) type Revalidation = SmallVec<[(u32, u32); 4]>;

pub(super) fn revalidation_of(index: &RuleIndex, matches: &[ElementMatch]) -> Revalidation {
    matches
        .iter()
        .filter(|matched| index.entries.view(matched.entry as usize).revalidates())
        .map(|matched| (matched.entry, matched.scope_proximity))
        .collect()
}

/// The key `node` shares under, or none where it cannot share: it has an id a selector tests for,
/// declarations of its own, a shadow tree or parts, a composition of its animations over its
/// record, or a parent this pass did not style.
pub(super) fn key_of(
    state: &RetainedState,
    index: &RuleIndex,
    records: &super::records::Records<'_>,
    node: StyleNodeID,
    facts: &ElementFacts,
) -> Option<SharingKey> {
    let id = facts.id();
    if state.is_quirks_table(node)
        || (id != StyleAtomID::NONE && index.tests_id(id))
        || !state.element_declarations.custom_declarations(node).is_empty()
        || [
            ElementDeclarationKind::InlineStyle,
            ElementDeclarationKind::PresentationalHint,
            ElementDeclarationKind::SvgPresentationAttribute,
        ]
        .into_iter()
        .any(|kind| !state.element_declarations.declared_properties(node, kind).is_empty())
        || state.projection.shadow_root_of(node).is_some()
        || !state.projection.part_hosts_of(node).is_empty()
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo-4/#treelike
        // An element sharing a style takes the records of its pseudo-elements too, which inherit
        // the composition of the element's own animations, as no other element's style tells.
        || records.composition(node).is_some()
        // NB: A pseudo-element's record substitutes the custom properties its own animations sampled, which are not the
        //     same for two elements with the same rules: their animations can stand at different times.
        || state.pseudo_element_samples_custom_properties(node)
        || !state.highlight_observers.custom_highlights_of(node).is_empty()
    {
        return None;
    }
    let identity = |node: Option<StyleNodeID>| records.sharing_identity(node?);
    let inheritance_parent = state.projection.inheritance_parent(node);
    let inheritance_parent_composes = inheritance_parent.is_some_and(|parent| records.composition(parent).is_some());
    Some(SharingKey {
        parent: identity(state.projection.parent(node))?,
        inheritance_parent: match inheritance_parent_composes {
            true => inheritance_parent?,
            false => identity(inheritance_parent)?,
        },
        inheritance_parent_composes,
        tag: facts.tag(),
        namespace: facts.namespace(),
        states: facts.states(),
        directionality: facts.directionality(),
        language: facts.language(),
        heading_level: facts.heading_level(),
        part_exposure: facts.part_exposure(),
        adjustment_facts: state.projection.adjustment_facts(node),
        tree_scope: state.projection.tree_scope(node),
        assigned_slot: state.projection.assigned_slot_of(node),
        highlight_parents: {
            let parent_records = inheritance_parent.map_or(&[][..], |parent| records.pseudo_element_records(parent));
            super::HIGHLIGHT_KINDS.map(|kind| {
                parent_records
                    .iter()
                    .find(|(held, _)| *held == super::PseudoElementTarget::of_kind(kind))
                    .map_or(0, |(_, record)| Arc::as_ptr(record) as usize)
            })
        },
        highlight_observers: state.highlight_observers.kinds_of(node),
    })
}

struct Candidate {
    key: SharingKey,
    record: Arc<Record>,
    /// The element whose record the candidate holds, whose classes, custom states and parts the
    /// key leaves out.
    identity: StyleNodeID,
    revalidation: Revalidation,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct SharingCache {
    /// Most recently styled last.
    candidates: std::collections::VecDeque<Candidate>,
}

impl SharingCache {
    /// The record of a candidate an element with `facts` agrees with, asking `revalidate` for the
    /// element's matches among the entries that revalidate once some candidate agrees on
    /// everything else.
    pub(super) fn find(
        &mut self,
        projection: &super::projection::Projection,
        key: &SharingKey,
        facts: &ElementFacts,
        mut revalidate: impl FnMut() -> Option<Revalidation>,
    ) -> Option<(Arc<Record>, StyleNodeID)> {
        let mut revalidation = None;
        let position = self.candidates.iter().rposition(|candidate| {
            if candidate.key != *key {
                return false;
            }
            let Some(held) = projection.facts(candidate.identity) else {
                return false;
            };
            if held.classes() != facts.classes()
                || held.custom_states() != facts.custom_states()
                || held.parts() != facts.parts()
            {
                return false;
            }
            revalidation
                .get_or_insert_with(&mut revalidate)
                .as_ref()
                .is_some_and(|revalidation| *revalidation == candidate.revalidation)
        })?;
        let candidate = self.candidates.remove(position)?;
        let found = (candidate.record.clone(), candidate.identity);
        self.candidates.push_back(candidate);
        Some(found)
    }

    pub(super) fn insert(
        &mut self,
        key: SharingKey,
        record: Arc<Record>,
        identity: StyleNodeID,
        revalidation: Revalidation,
    ) {
        if self.candidates.len() == CAPACITY {
            self.candidates.pop_front();
        }
        self.candidates.push_back(Candidate {
            key,
            record,
            identity,
            revalidation,
        });
    }
}

//! What the unit tests of the engine build on: a host stand-in that lets an engine compute records,
//! documents and rules built through the inputs the host records, and a check of what live style
//! the engine holds against a cold pass over the same document, and of what that pass matched against the
//! reference matcher.

use super::super::bridge::{
    BoundScopeChain, FfiDocumentStyleComputationInputs, FfiFontResolutionRequest, FfiHostHandle, FfiResolvedFont,
    element_adjustment_fact, publish_style_rule,
};
use super::super::font_resolution::{FontResolverHost, PublishedFontFaces};
use super::super::*;
use super::records::Record;
use super::write_once::WriteOnce;
use super::{self_check, traversal};

/// Every request resolves to one font with these metrics, which nothing follows the handles of.
unsafe extern "C" fn resolve_font(
    _memo: *const std::ffi::c_void,
    _snapshot: *const std::ffi::c_void,
    _request: FfiFontResolutionRequest,
) -> FfiResolvedFont {
    FfiResolvedFont {
        first_available_font: FfiHostHandle::from_pointer(std::ptr::dangling()),
        font_cascade_list: FfiHostHandle::from_pointer(std::ptr::dangling()),
        ascent: 12.0,
        descent: 4.0,
        line_gap: 0.0,
        x_height: 8.0,
        cap_height: 11.0,
        zero_advance: 8.0,
        font_size_adjust_from_font: 0.0,
    }
}

/// An engine hosted as a document's is, as far as computing records goes: it has a font resolver
/// and a font resolution cache, and the document's computation inputs, those of an 800x600
/// viewport with a 16px font.
pub(super) fn hosted_engine() -> StyleEngine {
    let mut engine = StyleEngine::new();
    engine.share_the_process_style_for_test();
    // SAFETY: The test build's host object references and unreferences do nothing.
    let font_faces = unsafe { PublishedFontFaces::adopt(std::ptr::dangling(), std::ptr::dangling()) };
    engine.host.font_resolver = Some(FontResolverHost::with_callbacks(resolve_font, resolve_font, font_faces));
    engine.retained.font_resolution = Some(Default::default());
    // NB: CSS pixels count in 64ths of a pixel raw.
    engine.retained.document_style_computation_inputs = FfiDocumentStyleComputationInputs {
        viewport_width: 800.0,
        viewport_height: 600.0,
        root_font_size: 16.0,
        root_font_x_height: 8.0,
        root_font_cap_height: 11.0,
        root_font_zero_advance: 8.0,
        root_line_height: 18.0,
        root_effective_zoom: 1.0,
        initial_font_size: 16.0,
        initial_font_x_height: 8.0,
        initial_font_cap_height: 11.0,
        initial_font_zero_advance: 8.0,
        initial_font_size_raw: 16 << 6,
        default_font_size_raw: 16 << 6,
        device_pixels_per_css_pixel: 1.0,
        ..Default::default()
    };
    engine
}

/// The names `atom` interned: the strings, kept alive for their identities to stay theirs, and
/// the name of each atom, for a failure to name it by.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Names {
    strings: Vec<ak::Utf16FlyString>,
    by_atom: HashMap<StyleAtomID, String>,
}

thread_local! {
    static NAMES: RefCell<Names> = RefCell::new(Names::default());
}

/// The atom of `name`, as the host interns the names elements carry and selectors test.
pub(super) fn atom(engine: &mut StyleEngine, name: &str) -> StyleAtomID {
    let string = ak::Utf16FlyString::from_utf16(&name.encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>());
    let atom = engine.intern_atom(string.raw_identity());
    // NB: Each engine has atoms of its own, so the name of an atom is the one interned last.
    NAMES.with_borrow_mut(|names| {
        names.strings.push(string);
        names.by_atom.insert(atom, name.to_owned());
    });
    atom
}

fn name_of(atom: StyleAtomID) -> String {
    NAMES.with_borrow(|names| {
        names
            .by_atom
            .get(&atom)
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("atom{}", atom.0))
    })
}

pub(super) fn allocate_nodes(engine: &mut StyleEngine, count: usize) -> Vec<StyleNodeID> {
    let mut raw = vec![0_u32; count];
    engine.allocate_style_nodes(&mut raw);
    raw.iter().map(|&raw| StyleNodeID::from_raw(raw).unwrap()).collect()
}

pub(super) fn relations(
    parent: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    previous: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    next: Option<StyleNodeID>,
) -> TreeRelations {
    TreeRelations {
        parent,
        previous_element_sibling: previous,
        next_element_sibling: next,
        ..TreeRelations::detached(TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT)
    }
}

pub(super) fn add_feature(engine: &mut StyleEngine, node: StyleNodeID, feature: LocalFeatureKey) {
    engine.record_input(
        InputKey::LocalFeature(node, feature),
        InputValue::Feature(FeatureValue::Present),
    );
}

pub(super) fn remove_feature(engine: &mut StyleEngine, node: StyleNodeID, feature: LocalFeatureKey) {
    engine.record_input(
        InputKey::LocalFeature(node, feature),
        InputValue::Feature(FeatureValue::Absent),
    );
}

pub(super) fn set_atom_feature(
    engine: &mut StyleEngine,
    node: StyleNodeID,
    feature: LocalFeatureKey,
    atom: StyleAtomID,
) {
    engine.record_input(
        InputKey::LocalFeature(node, feature),
        InputValue::Feature(FeatureValue::Atom(atom)),
    );
}

pub(super) fn set_tag(engine: &mut StyleEngine, node: StyleNodeID, tag: &str) {
    let tag = atom(engine, tag);
    set_atom_feature(engine, node, LocalFeatureKey::TagName, tag);
}

pub(super) fn add_class(engine: &mut StyleEngine, node: StyleNodeID, class: &str) {
    let class = atom(engine, class);
    add_feature(engine, node, LocalFeatureKey::Class(class));
}

pub(super) fn remove_class(engine: &mut StyleEngine, node: StyleNodeID, class: &str) {
    let class = atom(engine, class);
    remove_feature(engine, node, LocalFeatureKey::Class(class));
}

/// Builds the document element `root`, a `div`, with `count - 1` `div` children, through the same
/// delta path C++ drives.
pub(super) fn document_with_children(count: usize) -> (StyleEngine, Vec<StyleNodeID>) {
    let mut engine = hosted_engine();
    let nodes = allocate_nodes(&mut engine, count);
    engine.record_tree_delta(nodes[0], None, Some(relations(None, None, None)));
    for index in 1..count {
        let previous = (index > 1).then(|| nodes[index - 1]);
        engine.record_tree_delta(nodes[index], None, Some(relations(Some(nodes[0]), previous, None)));
    }
    engine.set_element_adjustment_facts(nodes[0], element_adjustment_fact::IS_DOCUMENT_ELEMENT);
    for &node in &nodes {
        set_tag(&mut engine, node, "div");
    }
    (engine, nodes)
}

/// Builds `root -> [a, b, c]`.
pub(super) fn linear_document() -> (StyleEngine, Vec<StyleNodeID>) {
    document_with_children(4)
}

/// Builds `root -> a -> b -> c`.
pub(super) fn nested_document() -> (StyleEngine, Vec<StyleNodeID>) {
    let mut engine = hosted_engine();
    let nodes = allocate_nodes(&mut engine, 4);
    engine.record_tree_delta(nodes[0], None, Some(relations(None, None, None)));
    for pair in nodes.windows(2) {
        engine.record_tree_delta(pair[1], None, Some(relations(Some(pair[0]), None, None)));
    }
    engine.set_element_adjustment_facts(nodes[0], element_adjustment_fact::IS_DOCUMENT_ELEMENT);
    for &node in &nodes {
        set_tag(&mut engine, node, "div");
    }
    (engine, nodes)
}

/// Attaches the shadow tree `scope` to `host`: a shadow root and a chain of `depth` `div`
/// elements below it, root first.
pub(super) fn attach_shadow_tree(
    engine: &mut StyleEngine,
    host: StyleNodeID,
    scope: TreeScopeID,
    depth: usize,
) -> Vec<StyleNodeID> {
    let nodes = allocate_nodes(engine, depth + 1);
    engine.record_tree_delta(nodes[0], None, Some(TreeRelations::detached(scope)));
    for pair in nodes.windows(2) {
        engine.record_tree_delta(
            pair[1],
            None,
            Some(TreeRelations {
                parent: Some(pair[0]),
                tree_scope: scope,
                ..TreeRelations::detached(scope)
            }),
        );
        set_tag(engine, pair[1], "div");
    }
    engine.set_shadow_root(host, nodes[0]);
    engine.set_tree_scope_root(scope, nodes[0]);
    nodes
}

/// Builds `root -> [a, b, c]` with `.target:nth-of-type(2)`, where `a` and `c` are of one type and
/// `b`, with the same local name in another namespace, of another, and only `c` is a target.
pub(super) fn typed_nth_of_type_document() -> (StyleEngine, Vec<StyleNodeID>) {
    let (mut engine, nodes) = linear_document();
    let sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
    add_rules(&mut engine, sheet, ".target:nth-of-type(2) { color: rgb(0, 128, 0); }");
    let first_namespace = atom(&mut engine, "first-namespace");
    let other_namespace = atom(&mut engine, "other-namespace");
    for (node, namespace) in [
        (nodes[1], first_namespace),
        (nodes[2], other_namespace),
        (nodes[3], first_namespace),
    ] {
        engine.set_element_namespace(node, namespace);
    }
    add_class(&mut engine, nodes[3], "target");
    (engine, nodes)
}

/// Builds `root -> [a, b, c]` with `.target:nth-child(3n)`, where every child is a target.
pub(super) fn nth_target_document() -> (StyleEngine, Vec<StyleNodeID>) {
    let (mut engine, nodes) = linear_document();
    let sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
    add_rules(&mut engine, sheet, ".target:nth-child(3n) { color: rgb(0, 128, 0); }");
    for &node in &nodes[1..] {
        add_class(&mut engine, node, "target");
    }
    (engine, nodes)
}

/// An author sheet attached to `scope`.
pub(super) fn add_sheet(engine: &mut StyleEngine, scope: TreeScopeID) -> SheetID {
    add_sheet_with_origin(engine, scope, CascadeOrigin::Author)
}

pub(super) fn add_sheet_with_origin(engine: &mut StyleEngine, scope: TreeScopeID, origin: CascadeOrigin) -> SheetID {
    let sheet = engine.add_sheet(origin);
    engine.attach_sheet(sheet, scope);
    sheet
}

/// A style rule parsed as the host parses a sheet's: its selectors and its declarations.
pub(super) struct ParsedRule {
    selectors: crate::css::selector_parser::RustParsedSelectorList,
    pub(super) declarations: crate::css::declaration_block::SharedDeclarationBlock,
}

/// The style rules of `source`.
pub(super) fn parse_rules(source: &str) -> Vec<ParsedRule> {
    use crate::css::css_tokenizer::TokenizerInput;
    use crate::css::parser::syntax_parser::parse_shared_stylesheet;
    use crate::css::rule::{NativeRuleList, NativeRuleType, rust_rule_list_count, rust_rule_type};
    let units: Vec<_> = source.encode_utf16().collect();
    // NB: A random function parses only where its declaration is numbered, as the host numbers
    //     those of a sheet.
    let random_function_index = crate::css::parser::value_parser::RandomFunctionIndex::default();
    let context = crate::css::parser::value_parser::ParseContext {
        random_function_index: Some(&random_function_index),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    let rules = NativeRuleList::from_parsed(parse_shared_stylesheet(TokenizerInput::Utf16(&units), Some(&context)));
    let count = rust_rule_list_count(&rules);
    assert_ne!(count, 0, "no rule parses from {source:?}");
    (0..count)
        .map(|index| {
            let rule = rules.rule_at(index);
            assert!(
                matches!(rust_rule_type(&rule), NativeRuleType::Style),
                "only style rules are published: {source:?}"
            );
            ParsedRule {
                selectors: rule.style_rule().selectors(),
                declarations: rule.cascade_declarations().expect("a style rule declares"),
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Append `rule` to `sheet` with its selectors, answering the rule it is.
fn publish_parsed_rule(engine: &mut StyleEngine, sheet: SheetID, rule: &ParsedRule) -> RuleID {
    let published = publish_style_rule(
        engine,
        sheet.0 + 1,
        0,
        &rule.selectors.selectors,
        &BoundScopeChain::default(),
    );
    assert_ne!(published, 0, "the rule is published");
    RuleID(published - 1)
}

/// Append the style rules of `source` to `sheet`, as the host publishes a sheet's rules: their
/// selectors, then their declarations.
pub(super) fn add_rules(engine: &mut StyleEngine, sheet: SheetID, source: &str) -> Vec<RuleID> {
    parse_rules(source)
        .iter()
        .map(|parsed| {
            let rule = publish_parsed_rule(engine, sheet, parsed);
            engine.publish_block_declarations(rule, &parsed.declarations);
            rule
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Attach a user agent sheet of the style rules of `source` to the document, as the host does: the
/// process keeps its rules, which one published sheet holds for every document attaching `source`.
/// Answers the sheet and the rules, as the document names them.
pub(super) fn add_user_agent_sheet(engine: &mut StyleEngine, source: &str) -> (SheetID, Vec<RuleID>) {
    use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
    let mut hasher = crate::css::style::fast_hash::fast_hasher();
    source.hash(&mut hasher);
    let source_identity = hasher.finish();
    Arc::clone(&engine.process_style).publish_user_agent_sheet(source_identity, |engine, sheet| {
        add_rules(engine, sheet, source);
    });
    let sheet = engine.add_user_agent_sheet(source_identity);
    engine.attach_sheet(sheet, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
    let rules = engine.rules.rules_in_sheet(sheet);
    (sheet, rules)
}

/// Take a style update and every later wave of its pass, as the host does when it installs
/// each wave; nothing is installed here. The engine, where it owns the document, restyles what
/// the transaction changed as it does. The style trace holds the passes of this update only.
pub(super) fn run_style_update(engine: &mut StyleEngine, root: StyleNodeID) {
    engine.retained.live_counters.begin_trace();
    engine.run_style_update(root, |_| {});
}

/// Have the engine own the document under `root`, from a cold pass of it after the inputs
/// recorded so far, with its passes on one thread.
pub(super) fn start_live(engine: &mut StyleEngine, root: StyleNodeID) {
    start_live_on(engine, root, 1);
}

/// Have the engine own the document under `root` as `start_live` does, with its passes on
/// `threads` threads.
pub(super) fn start_live_on(engine: &mut StyleEngine, root: StyleNodeID, threads: u32) {
    run_style_update(engine, root);
    engine.restart_live_style(root, threads);
    // NB: The engine owned the document from its first transaction on, so the restart has the next
    //     transaction restyle everything. Take that one here, so the next a test takes restyles
    //     only what it changed.
    run_style_update(engine, root);
    assert!(engine.has_live_style(), "the engine owns the document");
}

/// What `node` matches by the reference matcher, one entry per rule and pseudo-element-ness.
type MatchedRule = (RuleID, bool, crate::css::selector::Specificity);

/// One entry per rule and pseudo-element-ness, with the greatest specificity among its matching
/// entries, as the cascade weighs a rule.
fn merged_by_rule(matches: impl Iterator<Item = MatchedRule>) -> Vec<MatchedRule> {
    let mut merged: Vec<MatchedRule> = Vec::new();
    for (rule, pseudo_element, specificity) in matches {
        match merged
            .iter_mut()
            .find(|(existing_rule, existing_pseudo, _)| *existing_rule == rule && *existing_pseudo == pseudo_element)
        {
            Some(existing) => existing.2 = existing.2.max(specificity),
            None => merged.push((rule, pseudo_element, specificity)),
        }
    }
    merged.sort_unstable();
    merged
}

pub(super) fn exact_matches(engine: &StyleEngine, node: StyleNodeID) -> Vec<MatchedRule> {
    let mut exact = Vec::new();
    assert!(
        engine
            .retained
            .append_exact_matches_in_every_scope(node, &mut exact)
            .is_ok(),
        "the reference matcher matches {}",
        describe(&engine.retained, node)
    );
    merged_by_rule(
        exact
            .iter()
            .map(|matched| (matched.rule, matched.pseudo_element.is_some(), matched.specificity)),
    )
}

/// The element, as its tag, ID and classes, for a failure to name.
pub(super) fn describe(state: &RetainedState, node: StyleNodeID) -> String {
    self_check::describe(state, node, &name_of)
}

/// The record the engine holds for `node`.
pub(super) fn live_record(engine: &StyleEngine, node: StyleNodeID) -> Arc<Record> {
    let records = engine
        .retained
        .live_style
        .as_ref()
        .expect("the engine is live")
        .records();
    records
        .get(node)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("the engine holds a record for {}", describe(&engine.retained, node)))
        .clone()
}

/// Whether two records hold equal values, as `assert_live_matches_cold` compares them.
pub(super) fn records_equal(first: &Record, second: &Record) -> bool {
    self_check::record_differences(first, second).is_empty()
}

/// Whether the records the engine holds for `first` and `second` hold equal values, for a test
/// to tell that a rule reached an element.
pub(super) fn live_records_equal(engine: &StyleEngine, first: StyleNodeID, second: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
    records_equal(&live_record(engine, first), &live_record(engine, second))
}

/// How many passes settling the engine may take, as levels of elements composing animations
/// below one another.
const MAX_SETTLING_PASSES: usize = 1024;

/// Settle the engine, then check every record it holds for the document under `root`, of an
/// element and of its pseudo-elements, against the record a cold pass over the document computes,
/// and what that pass matched for each element against the reference matcher. Answers how many
/// elements it checked.
///
/// The records are compared by value: the payloads of each group and the longhand tables as the
/// host is handed them, and the custom properties by what each name resolves to, since the live
/// records are not the cold pass's, and their custom property stores chain to other parents.
pub(super) fn assert_live_matches_cold(engine: &mut StyleEngine, root: StyleNodeID) -> usize {
    assert!(engine.has_live_style(), "the engine owns the document");
    for _ in 0..MAX_SETTLING_PASSES {
        if !engine
            .retained
            .live_style
            .as_ref()
            .is_some_and(|live| live.has_pending())
        {
            break;
        }
        engine.live_restyle(root);
    }
    assert!(engine.has_live_style(), "the engine kept the document as it settled");
    let self_check::ReferencePass {
        records: cold, outputs, ..
    } = self_check::reference_pass(engine, root, false, 1).expect("the cold pass styles the document");
    let state = &engine.retained;
    let live = state.live_style.as_ref().expect("the engine is live").records();
    let describe = |node| describe(state, node);
    let (mut failures, checked) = self_check::differences(state, root, live, &cold, &describe);
    for node in state.projection.style_preorder(root) {
        let Some(output) = outputs.get(node.element_slot()).and_then(WriteOnce::get) else {
            continue;
        };
        match output.outcome {
            traversal::Outcome::CascadeDeclined | traversal::Outcome::ComputeDeclined => {
                failures.push(format!("{}: the cold pass declined to style it", describe(node)));
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        if let Some(matches) = &output.matches {
            let ours = merged_by_rule(
                matches
                    .iter()
                    .map(|matched| (matched.rule, matched.pseudo_element(), matched.specificity)),
            );
            let reference = exact_matches(engine, node);
            if ours != reference {
                failures.push(format!(
                    "{}: the cold pass matched {ours:?}, the reference matcher {reference:?}",
                    describe(node)
                ));
            }
        }
    }
    assert!(
        failures.is_empty(),
        "the engine is not what a cold pass computes:\n{}",
        failures.join("\n")
    );
    checked
}

mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn an_element_holding_a_record_only_as_installed_hands_down_its_custom_properties() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = nested_document();
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        engine.install_test_record(computed::ComputedStyleTarget::new(nodes[1], u8::MAX), None, None, 0);
        let cells = crate::css::style::pipeline::records::RecordCells::default();
        let records = crate::css::style::pipeline::records::Records::new(&engine.retained, &cells, None);
        assert!(records.custom_stores_of(nodes[1]).is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_class_change_restyles_a_plain_document_as_a_cold_pass_does() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = linear_document();
        let sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
        add_rules(
            &mut engine,
            sheet,
            ".target { color: rgb(0, 128, 0); width: 10px; } .target::before { content: \"x\"; }",
        );
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "target");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_eq!(assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]), nodes.len());
        assert!(!live_records_equal(&engine, nodes[1], nodes[2]));

        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "target");
        remove_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "target");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(live_records_equal(&engine, nodes[2], nodes[3]));
        assert!(!live_records_equal(&engine, nodes[1], nodes[2]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_guard_change_restyles_a_nested_document_as_a_cold_pass_does() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = nested_document();
        let sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
        add_rules(
            &mut engine,
            sheet,
            ".guard { color: rgb(0, 0, 255); --size: 4px; } .guard .target { width: var(--size); }",
        );
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "guard");
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[3], "target");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);

        remove_class(&mut engine, nodes[1], "guard");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(live_records_equal(&engine, nodes[1], nodes[2]));

        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[2], "guard");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!live_records_equal(&engine, nodes[1], nodes[2]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_class_change_in_a_shadow_tree_restyles_it_as_a_cold_pass_does() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = linear_document();
        let scope = TreeScopeID(1);
        let shadow = attach_shadow_tree(&mut engine, nodes[1], scope, 3);
        let document_sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, TreeScopeID::DOCUMENT);
        add_rules(&mut engine, document_sheet, ".target { color: rgb(255, 0, 0); }");
        let shadow_sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, scope);
        add_rules(
            &mut engine,
            shadow_sheet,
            ":host { width: 20px; } .target { color: rgb(0, 128, 0); }",
        );
        add_class(&mut engine, shadow[2], "target");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        let checked = assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_eq!(checked, nodes.len() + shadow.len() - 1);

        remove_class(&mut engine, shadow[2], "target");
        add_class(&mut engine, shadow[3], "target");
        add_class(&mut engine, nodes[3], "target");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!live_records_equal(&engine, shadow[3], nodes[3]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_shadow_root_matches_no_compound_left_of_a_combinator() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = linear_document();
        let scope = TreeScopeID(1);
        let shadow = attach_shadow_tree(&mut engine, nodes[1], scope, 2);
        let shadow_sheet = add_sheet(&mut engine, scope);
        add_rules(
            &mut engine,
            shadow_sheet,
            "* > .child { color: rgb(0, 128, 0); } * .descendant { width: 20px; } \
             :not(.absent) > .child { height: 20px; }",
        );
        add_class(&mut engine, shadow[2], "child");
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!live_records_equal(&engine, shadow[2], nodes[2]));

        // The top-level element of the shadow tree has the shadow root for its parent and only
        // ancestor, which is not an element and matches nothing.
        remove_class(&mut engine, shadow[2], "child");
        add_class(&mut engine, shadow[1], "child");
        add_class(&mut engine, shadow[1], "descendant");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(exact_matches(&engine, shadow[1]).is_empty());
        assert!(live_records_equal(&engine, shadow[1], shadow[2]));

        remove_class(&mut engine, shadow[1], "child");
        add_class(&mut engine, shadow[2], "descendant");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!live_records_equal(&engine, shadow[1], shadow[2]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_departure_restyles_an_nth_of_type_document_as_a_cold_pass_does() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = typed_nth_of_type_document();
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!live_records_equal(&engine, nodes[2], nodes[3]));
        let untargeted = live_record(&engine, nodes[1]);

        // Another type leaving moves no position of the target's type.
        engine.record_tree_delta(
            nodes[2],
            Some(relations(Some(nodes[0]), Some(nodes[1]), Some(nodes[3]))),
            None,
        );
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!live_records_equal(&engine, nodes[1], nodes[3]));

        // The same type leaving makes the target the first of its type.
        engine.record_tree_delta(nodes[1], Some(relations(Some(nodes[0]), None, Some(nodes[3]))), None);
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(records_equal(&live_record(&engine, nodes[3]), &untargeted));
    }

    #[test]
    fn arrivals_and_departures_restyle_an_nth_child_document_as_a_cold_pass_does() {
        let (mut engine, nodes) = nth_target_document();
        start_live(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!live_records_equal(&engine, nodes[2], nodes[3]));

        // A departure makes the third child the second.
        engine.record_tree_delta(nodes[1], Some(relations(Some(nodes[0]), None, Some(nodes[2]))), None);
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(live_records_equal(&engine, nodes[2], nodes[3]));

        // An arrival before both makes the second child the third.
        let inserted = allocate_nodes(&mut engine, 1)[0];
        engine.record_tree_delta(inserted, None, Some(relations(Some(nodes[0]), None, Some(nodes[2]))));
        set_tag(&mut engine, inserted, "div");
        run_style_update(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert_live_matches_cold(&mut engine, nodes[0]);
        assert!(!live_records_equal(&engine, nodes[2], nodes[3]));
    }
}

/// A declaration block declaring each `(property, important, value)` of `declarations`.
pub(crate) fn declaration_block(
    declarations: &[(u16, bool, crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData)],
) -> crate::css::declaration_block::SharedDeclarationBlock {
    crate::css::declaration_block::DeclarationBlockBuilder {
        properties: declarations
            .iter()
            .map(
                |(property, important, value)| crate::css::declaration_block::DeclaredProperty {
                    property_id: *property,
                    important: *important,
                    value: crate::css::style_value_arc::StyleValueArc::new(value.clone()),
                },
            )
            .collect(),
        custom_properties: Vec::new(),
    }
    .finish()
}

//! The style traversal: every element of the flat tree, shadow trees included, is matched,
//! cascaded and computed once the parent it inherits from is, on a pool of threads.
//!
//! The calling thread styles the document breadth-first from its root. Once a level of the tree is
//! wide enough, it keeps a queue of elements for itself and hands the rest out in work units, which
//! the threads of the pool style the same way; a small or narrow document never leaves the calling
//! thread.
//! Every thread keeps its own matcher, cascade scratch and ancestor filter, which it reconciles with
//! the ancestor chain of each element's parent in its own tree as it moves between parents.

use super::super::container_queries::{ContainerRecords, ContainerVerdict};
use super::super::custom_property_cascade::{
    LonghandCustomPropertyReads, PreparedCustomFunctions, value_reads_substitution_subject,
};
use super::super::random_bases::RandomBaseRequest;
use super::super::*;
use super::bloom::AncestorFilter;
use super::cascade::{Cascade, CascadeCounters};
use super::compute::{GroupSeeds, RootFontInputs};
