//! https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#random-caching
//! The random base value each random caching key of the document has been given.

use super::RetainedState;
use super::tree::StyleNodeID;
use std::hash::BuildHasher;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

/// The random base values a document's random functions have drawn, by random caching key. The
/// key's document is the engine's own; its element is the node, or none for an `element-shared`
/// sharing.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(crate) struct RandomBaseValues {
    /// The keys whose element is null, by name, shared with a fork until either side writes it.
    document: crate::cow_map::CowMap<Box<[u16]>, f64>,
    /// The keys that name an element. Few elements draw, and those draw few names, so only they
    /// have a row and a row is searched in order. Shared with a fork until either side writes it.
    elements: crate::cow_map::CowMap<StyleNodeID, Vec<NamedBaseValue>>,
    /// Raised once any element has a row, and never lowered. The host watches it so that an element losing its
    /// identity asks for keys only once some element can have any.
    element_rows_exist: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    source: RandomSource,
}

/// A name's base value in an element's row.
pub(crate) type NamedBaseValue = (Box<[u16]>, f64);

/// The row of an element that has no style node, which the element holds: the engine moves the row in as the element
/// loses its node, and out to the node it gets next. Whichever of the element and the engine lets go of it last frees
/// it, so an element that never gets a node again takes its keys with it.
pub(crate) type ParkedBaseValues = Arc<Mutex<Vec<NamedBaseValue>>>;

/// A uniform pseudo-random source: a randomly keyed hash of a draw counter.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct RandomSource {
    state: std::collections::hash_map::RandomState,
    draws: u64,
}

impl RandomSource {
    /// A pseudo-random real number in `[0, 1)`, from a uniform distribution.
    fn draw(&mut self) -> f64 {
        self.draws += 1;
        // The top 53 bits fill the mantissa exactly, so the quotient is below one.
        (self.state.hash_one(self.draws) >> 11) as f64 / (1_u64 << 53) as f64
    }
}

impl RandomBaseValues {
    /// The base value of a key, drawn the first time the key is asked for. A key that names an
    /// element with no identity draws every time: nothing could find it again.
    pub(crate) fn ensure(&mut self, node: Option<StyleNodeID>, name: &[u16], element_shared: bool) -> f64 {
        if element_shared {
            if let Some(&value) = self.document.get(name) {
                return value;
            }
            let value = self.source.draw();
            self.document.insert(name.into(), value);
            return value;
        }
        let Some(node) = node else {
            return self.source.draw();
        };
        if let Some(value) = self.get(node, name, false) {
            return value;
        }
        let value = self.source.draw();
        self.row_mut(node).push((name.into(), value));
        value
    }

    /// The base value of a key, if it has been drawn.
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, node: StyleNodeID, name: &[u16], element_shared: bool) -> Option<f64> {
        if element_shared {
            return self.document.get(name).copied();
        }
        self.elements
            .get(&node)?
            .iter()
            .find(|(row_name, _)| **row_name == *name)
            .map(|(_, value)| *value)
    }

    /// An element's row, which may be new.
    fn row_mut(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID) -> &mut Vec<NamedBaseValue> {
        self.element_rows_exist.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.elements.entry(node).or_default()
    }

    /// Takes the keys that name an element, with their values, as the element loses its identity.
    pub(crate) fn take_element_values(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID) -> Vec<NamedBaseValue> {
        if !self.elements.contains_key(&node) {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        self.elements.remove(&node).unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// Give up the keys of an identity that retires. An identity can be minted again for another
    /// element, which must not see this one's values; the element itself took its own along when
    /// it lost the identity.
    pub(crate) fn retire(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID) {
        if self.elements.contains_key(&node) {
            self.elements.remove(&node);
        }
    }
}

/// A random caching key a style computation of `node` needs the base value of, which has not
/// been drawn. A pass draws none itself: the key is drawn between passes, as a font is resolved,
/// and the element is styled again.
pub(crate) struct RandomBaseRequest {
    pub(crate) node: StyleNodeID,
    pub(crate) name: Box<[u16]>,
    pub(crate) element_shared: bool,
}

impl RetainedState {
    /// Draw the base value of the random caching key `request` names.
    pub(crate) fn draw_random_base_value(&mut self, request: RandomBaseRequest) {
        self.random_base_values
            .ensure(Some(request.node), &request.name, request.element_shared);
    }

    /// The base value of a random caching key, if it has been drawn.
    pub(crate) fn drawn_random_base_value(&self, node: StyleNodeID, name: &[u16], element_shared: bool) -> Option<f64> {
        self.random_base_values.get(node, name, element_shared)
    }

    /// Give an element's new style node the keys the element kept while it had none.
    pub(crate) fn set_element_random_base_values(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID, row: Vec<NamedBaseValue>) {
        if !row.is_empty() {
            *self.random_base_values.row_mut(node) = row;
        }
    }

    /// Gives a fork of the engine flags of its own in place of those it shares with the host, holding what they hold
    /// now.
    pub(crate) fn detach_host_flags_for_fork(&mut self) {
        let exist = self.random_base_values.element_rows_exist.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.random_base_values.element_rows_exist = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(exist));
        self.detach_container_effects_held_for_fork();
        if let Some(font_resolution) = self.font_resolution.as_mut() {
            font_resolution.hold_cascades_for_fork();
        }
    }

    /// Raises `flag`, which the document's host reads, once any element has random base values, rather than a flag
    /// of the engine's own. The engine has none yet.
    pub(crate) fn share_element_random_base_values_exist(&mut self, flag: Arc<AtomicBool>) {
        debug_assert!(!self.random_base_values.element_rows_exist.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
        self.random_base_values.element_rows_exist = flag;
    }

    /// The random base value of the random caching key for a node's style and a sharing name.
    pub(crate) fn ensure_random_base_value(
        &mut self,
        node: Option<StyleNodeID>,
        name: &[u16],
        element_shared: bool,
    ) -> f64 {
        self.random_base_values.ensure(node, name, element_shared)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn a_key_keeps_its_value_and_an_element_key_retires_with_the_element() {
        let mut values = RandomBaseValues::default();
        let first = StyleNodeID::from_raw(1);
        let second = StyleNodeID::from_raw(2);
        let name = "--shared".encode_utf16().collect::<Vec<_>>();

        let document_value = values.ensure(first, &name, true);
        assert!((0.0..1.0).contains(&document_value));
        assert_eq!(document_value, values.ensure(second, &name, true));

        let element_value = values.ensure(first, &name, false);
        assert_eq!(element_value, values.ensure(first, &name, false));
        values.ensure(second, &name, false);
        assert_eq!(values.document.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(values.elements.len(), 2);

        values.retire(first.unwrap());
        assert_eq!(values.elements.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(document_value, values.ensure(second, &name, true));
    }
}

//! Applying the reactions of a style update to the elements they name.
//!
//! The engine decides what each reaction installs: the record it settled, or a record it demands now. The host installs a record on its element, runs the element's animations and transitions,
//! invalidates its layout, and reports what the installation did, from which the engine derives the reactions of the
//! element's children.

use super::StyleNodeID;
use super::engine_calls::{has_deferred_element_style_input, with_engine};
use super::pipeline::install::{StyleInstallation, StyleSwap};
use super::pipeline::main_effects::InstalledElementEffects;
use super::publication::PendingDemandInput;
use crate::render_state::{BegunRead, DocumentHost};

/// A `Web::DOM::Element`, which Rust names by pointer only.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct HostElement {
    _opaque: [u8; 0],
    _not_send_or_sync: std::marker::PhantomData<*const ()>,
}

/// The host's application of style reactions to its document's elements, which Rust names by pointer only.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct HostStyleReactionApplication {
    _opaque: [u8; 0],
    _not_send_or_sync: std::marker::PhantomData<*const ()>,
}

/// The host's element held in a struct, which C++ sees as an opaque pointer: the GC plugin rejects a raw cell pointer
/// field, and a `GC::Ptr` is no C type.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct HostElementPtr(pub *mut HostElement);

impl HostElementPtr {
    fn is_null(self) -> bool {
        self.0.is_null()
    }
}

/// The element a style node names, as the host holds it while it applies a reaction to it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiReactionElement {
    /// The host's element, or null where no element has the style node.
    pub element: HostElementPtr,
    pub style_node: u32,
    /// Whether the element is connected to the document whose reactions are applied.
    pub connected: bool,
    pub has_style: bool,
    pub style_record: u64,
    /// Whether the style the element holds has display:none.
    pub display_none: bool,
}

/// How a targeted style update of an element reads its style.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum FfiStyleUpdateMode {
    /// Every element the element inherits through computes the style it owes, under display:none ancestors too.
    Normal,
    /// Only an element without style, or one that owes a style input, computes its style.
    #[expect(
        dead_code,
        reason = "only the host asks for this mode, which the engine reads by elimination"
    )]
    OnlyIfNeeded,
    /// As `OnlyIfNeeded`, but a display:none ancestor stops the update: the element has no style to read.
    StopAtDisplayNone,
}

/// What a targeted style update answers a read of an element's style.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum FfiTargetedStyleAnswer {
    /// The element has no style to read.
    Unstyled,
    /// The element has the style it reads.
    Styled,
    /// The element has the style it holds, if any.
    HeldStyle,
    /// The style the element reads needs a style update of its document first.
    NeedsStyleUpdate,
}

/// What the reaction passes of a style update did, for the host's counters.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiStyleReactionCounts {
    /// Whether the update had reactions to apply at all.
    pub had_reactions: bool,
    pub batch_runs: u32,
    pub reaction_elements: u32,
    pub published_reactions: u32,
    pub pass_guard_hits: u32,
    pub apply_microseconds: u64,
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_css_style_inheritance_parent(
        application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication,
        element: *mut HostElement,
    ) -> FfiReactionElement;
    fn web_css_run_style_update(application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication, flown: bool);
    fn web_css_has_pending_style_update(application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication) -> bool;
    fn web_css_note_style_update_has_reactions(application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication);
    fn web_css_sample_animations_for_style_update(application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication);
    fn web_css_begin_style_update_pass(application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication, first: bool);
    fn web_css_sample_undisplayed_animations_for_read(
        application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication,
        element: *mut HostElement,
    );
    fn web_css_style_reaction_element(application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication, node: u32) -> FfiReactionElement;
    #[expect(improper_ctypes, reason = "C++ holds the record a swap installs opaque, by pointer")]
    fn web_css_install_styles(
        application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication,
        swaps: *const StyleSwap,
        swap_count: usize,
        effects: *const InstalledElementEffects,
        effect_count: usize,
        cleared_descendants: *const u32,
        cleared_descendant_count: usize,
        document_damage: u32,
    );
}

/// The host's application of a batch of reactions to its document's elements, which the host names by pointer.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Application<'a> {
    host: &'a DocumentHost,
    read: &'a BegunRead,
    host_application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication,
}

impl Application<'_> {
    fn element(self, node: u32) -> FfiReactionElement {
        // SAFETY: The host lends its application for the call that applies the batch.
        unsafe { web_css_style_reaction_element(self.host_application, node) }
    }

    /// A targeted update of `node`: the engine computes the record it demands for the element now, and the host takes
    /// the installation of that record as it takes a style update's. Answers whether the engine could: where it could
    /// not, the element keeps what it holds until the next style update. Where the record would read an input the
    /// next transaction has yet to take, it answers that input, and the host runs a style update first.
    fn demand(self, node: StyleNodeID) -> Result<bool, PendingDemandInput> {
        let Some(installation) = with_engine(self.read, self.host, |engine| engine.demand_installation(node))? else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        self.install_styles(&installation);
        with_engine(self.read, self.host, |engine| {
            for &record in &installation.pinned_records {
                engine.unpin_layout_style_record(record);
            }
        });
        Ok(true)
    }
}

/// A style update applies at most this many passes of reactions that publish new style, beyond which it stops: a
/// style change that keeps feeding back into itself would never settle.
const MAX_STYLE_UPDATE_PASSES: u32 = 8;

impl Application<'_> {
    /// Takes the next style update of the host's update_style(), the one computed beside the event loop first where it
    /// drains it, and answers the style installation the render side made of it for the host to swap in.
    fn take_transaction(self, flown: bool) -> StyleInstallation {
        // SAFETY: The host lends its application for the call that updates the style.
        unsafe { web_css_run_style_update(self.host_application, flown) };
        self.host.take_transaction_installation().unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// Has the host swap in the styles of `installation`, a style installation, and perform their side effects.
    fn install_styles(self, installation: &StyleInstallation) {
        // SAFETY: The host lends its application for the call that updates the style, and the slices live for it.
        unsafe {
            web_css_install_styles(
                self.host_application,
                installation.swaps.as_ptr(),
                installation.swaps.len(),
                installation.effects.as_ptr(),
                installation.effects.len(),
                installation.cleared_descendants.as_ptr(),
                installation.cleared_descendants.len(),
                installation.document_damage,
            );
        }
    }

    fn has_pending_transaction(self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: As above.
        unsafe { web_css_has_pending_style_update(self.host_application) }
    }
}

/// Applies the reactions of the style updates of one update_style(), from the first, computed beside the event
/// loop where it drains one, until the reactions they feed back settle. Each pass applies one transaction's
/// reactions, closed over the elements they inherit through, and the consequences produced while applying them become
/// the next transaction.
fn update_style(application: Application<'_>, drains_flown_transaction: bool) -> FfiStyleReactionCounts {
    let mut counts = FfiStyleReactionCounts::default();
    let mut taken = application.take_transaction(drains_flown_transaction);
    let is_empty = |installation: &StyleInstallation| installation.swaps.is_empty() && installation.effects.is_empty();
    // SAFETY: The host lends its application for the call that updates the style.
    unsafe {
        if !is_empty(&taken) {
            web_css_note_style_update_has_reactions(application.host_application);
        }
        web_css_sample_animations_for_style_update(application.host_application);
    }
    if is_empty(&taken) && application.has_pending_transaction() {
        taken = application.take_transaction(false);
    }
    // SAFETY: As above.
    unsafe { web_css_begin_style_update_pass(application.host_application, true) };
    if is_empty(&taken) {
        return counts;
    }
    counts.had_reactions = true;

    let mut style_update_passes = 0;
    let mut first_pass = true;
    while !is_empty(&taken) {
        let apply_started_at = std::time::Instant::now();
        if !std::mem::take(&mut first_pass) {
            // SAFETY: As above.
            unsafe { web_css_begin_style_update_pass(application.host_application, false) };
        }
        let published_reactions = taken.swaps.len() as u32;
        if published_reactions > 0 {
            style_update_passes += 1;
            if style_update_passes > MAX_STYLE_UPDATE_PASSES {
                counts.pass_guard_hits += 1;
                // NB: The render side noted the records the installation swaps in as the host's, so the host takes it
                //     before it stops.
                application.install_styles(&taken);
                counts.apply_microseconds += apply_started_at.elapsed().as_micros() as u64;
                break;
            }
        }
        counts.batch_runs += 1;
        counts.reaction_elements += published_reactions;
        application.install_styles(&taken);
        counts.apply_microseconds += apply_started_at.elapsed().as_micros() as u64;

        // The consequences produced while installing become the next transaction in this stabilization epoch.
        taken = match application.has_pending_transaction() {
            true => application.take_transaction(false),
            false => StyleInstallation::default(),
        };
    }
    counts
}

/// Whether `LIBWEB_STYLE_SELFCHECK` asks for what `style_engine_self_check` does.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_self_check_is_enabled(host: &DocumentHost) -> bool {
    host.engine_memo().style_self_check.is_enabled()
}

/// Whether a style update that flew is yet to be checked, which an update finding nothing to do has to do.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_flown_update_awaits_self_check(host: &DocumentHost) -> bool {
    host.engine_memo().flown_update_awaits_self_check.get()
}

/// Checks what the engine holds for the host's document under `root`, its document element's style node or zero,
/// against a cold pass, as `LIBWEB_STYLE_SELFCHECK` asks, once a style update has settled.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_self_check(host: &DocumentHost, read: &BegunRead, root: u32) {
    let settings = host.engine_memo().style_self_check;
    host.engine_memo().flown_update_awaits_self_check.set(false);
    if let Some(root) = StyleNodeID::from_raw(root)
        && settings.is_enabled()
    {
        with_engine(read, host, |engine| engine.run_self_check(root, settings));
    }
}

/// Hands `consume` each line of what the engine holds for the host's document under `root`, its document element's style
/// node or zero, disagrees in with a cold pass over the same inputs and with the records the host installed.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `consume` must copy the bytes it is handed before it returns.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_self_check_report(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    read: &BegunRead,
    root: u32,
    context: *mut std::ffi::c_void,
    consume: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut std::ffi::c_void, *const u8, usize),
) {
    let Some(root) = StyleNodeID::from_raw(root) else {
        return;
    };
    for line in with_engine(read, host, |engine| engine.self_check_report(root)) {
        // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
        unsafe { consume(context, line.as_ptr(), line.len()) };
    }
}

/// Applies the reactions of the style updates of one update_style() of the host's document, from the one computed
/// beside the event loop
/// where `drains_flown_transaction`, through `host_application`, the host's state for applying them, and answers what
/// they did for its counters.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `host` must be a live document host, on its document's thread, and `host_application` must be live for the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_update_style(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    read: &BegunRead,
    host_application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication,
    drains_flown_transaction: bool,
) -> FfiStyleReactionCounts {
    let application = Application {
        host,
        read,
        host_application,
    };
    update_style(application, drains_flown_transaction)
}

/// What an inheritance chain holds, by depth from its first element.
#[derive(Default)]
struct InheritanceChainScan {
    /// The topmost element that has to compute its style: it has none, or it owes a style input.
    topmost_requiring_style: Option<usize>,
    topmost_display_none: Option<usize>,
    nearest_display_none: Option<usize>,
}

impl InheritanceChainScan {
    fn display_none_above_every_element_requiring_style(&self) -> bool {
        self.topmost_display_none.is_some_and(|display_none| {
            self.topmost_requiring_style
                .is_none_or(|requiring| display_none > requiring)
        })
    }
}

impl Application<'_> {
    /// The elements an element inherits its style through, from `first` up to the root.
    fn inheritance_chain(self, first: FfiReactionElement) -> impl Iterator<Item = FfiReactionElement> {
        let present = |element: FfiReactionElement| (!element.element.is_null()).then_some(element);
        std::iter::successors(present(first), move |element| {
            // SAFETY: The host lends its application for the call, and the element is live while it is read.
            present(unsafe { web_css_style_inheritance_parent(self.host_application, element.element.0) })
        })
    }

    /// Scans the chain an element inherits its style through, from `first`, where every element may owe a style
    /// input unless `may_owe_style_inputs` is false.
    fn scan_inheritance_chain(self, first: FfiReactionElement, may_owe_style_inputs: bool) -> InheritanceChainScan {
        let mut scan = InheritanceChainScan::default();
        for (depth, element) in self.inheritance_chain(first).enumerate() {
            if !element.has_style
                || (may_owe_style_inputs
                    && StyleNodeID::from_raw(element.style_node)
                        .is_some_and(|node| has_deferred_element_style_input(self.host, self.read, node)))
            {
                scan.topmost_requiring_style = Some(depth);
            }
            if element.display_none {
                scan.topmost_display_none = Some(depth);
                scan.nearest_display_none.get_or_insert(depth);
            }
        }
        scan
    }

    /// Answers a read of an element's style, whose chain of elements it inherits through starts at `first`, from the
    /// styles they hold, where neither its document nor an embedding one has style work pending.
    fn read_settled_inheritance_chain(
        self,
        first: FfiReactionElement,
        mode: FfiStyleUpdateMode,
    ) -> FfiTargetedStyleAnswer {
        let scan = self.scan_inheritance_chain(first, false);
        if mode == FfiStyleUpdateMode::StopAtDisplayNone && scan.display_none_above_every_element_requiring_style() {
            FfiTargetedStyleAnswer::Unstyled
        } else if scan.topmost_requiring_style.is_none() {
            FfiTargetedStyleAnswer::Styled
        } else {
            FfiTargetedStyleAnswer::NeedsStyleUpdate
        }
    }

    /// Updates the style of the chain of elements an element inherits through, from `first`: re-cascades from the
    /// rootmost element on the chain that has to compute its style back down to the element.
    fn update_style_for_inheritance_chain(
        self,
        first: FfiReactionElement,
        mode: FfiStyleUpdateMode,
        embedding_document_layout_was_stale: bool,
    ) -> FfiTargetedStyleAnswer {
        let scan = self.scan_inheritance_chain(first, true);
        if mode == FfiStyleUpdateMode::StopAtDisplayNone && scan.display_none_above_every_element_requiring_style() {
            return FfiTargetedStyleAnswer::Unstyled;
        }
        // NB: The records the engine installs for a document it owns are current once the style update ran, but
        //     for those below an element that is not displayed, which no style update styles: a read in normal mode
        //     demands them again, as their inputs may have moved since they were demanded last.
        if scan.topmost_requiring_style.is_none()
            && (mode != FfiStyleUpdateMode::Normal || scan.nearest_display_none.is_none())
        {
            return FfiTargetedStyleAnswer::HeldStyle;
        }
        // NB: No style update samples the animations of an element that is not displayed. What a read below one sees of
        //     them is sampled here, from the top down, for the demands below to compute from.
        if mode == FfiStyleUpdateMode::Normal && scan.nearest_display_none.is_some() {
            let elements: smallvec::SmallVec<[_; 32]> =
                self.inheritance_chain(first).map(|element| element.element).collect();
            for element in elements.into_iter().rev() {
                // SAFETY: The host lends its application for the call, and the element is live while it is read.
                unsafe { web_css_sample_undisplayed_animations_for_read(self.host_application, element.0) };
            }
        }
        // Normal mode also re-cascades the target path under its display:none ancestors.
        let mut topmost_element_to_recompute = scan.topmost_requiring_style;
        if mode == FfiStyleUpdateMode::Normal && topmost_element_to_recompute.is_none() {
            topmost_element_to_recompute = scan.nearest_display_none.and_then(|depth| depth.checked_sub(1));
        }
        let topmost_element_to_recompute = match topmost_element_to_recompute {
            Some(depth) => depth,
            None if mode != FfiStyleUpdateMode::Normal && !embedding_document_layout_was_stale => {
                return FfiTargetedStyleAnswer::HeldStyle;
            }
            None => 0,
        };

        // The chain is named by style node: an element it names is looked up again as the walk reaches it.
        let chain: smallvec::SmallVec<[u32; 32]> = self
            .inheritance_chain(first)
            .take(topmost_element_to_recompute + 1)
            .map(|element| element.style_node)
            .collect();
        for &style_node in chain.iter().rev() {
            let element = self.element(style_node);
            let Some(node) = StyleNodeID::from_raw(style_node).filter(|_| !element.element.is_null()) else {
                return FfiTargetedStyleAnswer::HeldStyle;
            };
            match self.demand(node) {
                Ok(true) => {}
                Ok(false) => return FfiTargetedStyleAnswer::HeldStyle,
                // NB: The host records inputs as it installs a record, as where it composes the element's animations,
                //     and beside its last style update. The elements below read them once a style update took them.
                Err(_) => return FfiTargetedStyleAnswer::NeedsStyleUpdate,
            }

            let element = self.element(style_node);
            if element.display_none && mode == FfiStyleUpdateMode::StopAtDisplayNone {
                return FfiTargetedStyleAnswer::Unstyled;
            }
        }
        FfiTargetedStyleAnswer::HeldStyle
    }
}

/// Answers a read of an element's style from the styles held by the chain of elements it inherits through, from
/// `first`, where neither its document nor an embedding one has style work pending, or that it needs a style update.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `host` must be a live document host, on its document's thread, and `host_application` and the element `first`
/// names must be live for the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_read_settled_inheritance_chain(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    read: &BegunRead,
    host_application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication,
    first: FfiReactionElement,
    mode: FfiStyleUpdateMode,
) -> FfiTargetedStyleAnswer {
    let application = Application {
        host,
        read,
        host_application,
    };
    application.read_settled_inheritance_chain(first, mode)
}

/// Updates the style of the chain of elements an element inherits through, from `first`, for a read of the element's
/// style, and answers the read, or that it needs a style update first: an element of the chain would read an input
/// the next transaction has yet to take.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `host` must be a live document host, on its document's thread, and `host_application` and the element `first`
/// names must be live for the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn style_engine_update_style_for_inheritance_chain(
    host: &DocumentHost,
    read: &BegunRead,
    host_application: *mut HostStyleReactionApplication,
    first: FfiReactionElement,
    mode: FfiStyleUpdateMode,
    embedding_document_layout_was_stale: bool,
) -> FfiTargetedStyleAnswer {
    let application = Application {
        host,
        read,
        host_application,
    };
    application.update_style_for_inheritance_chain(first, mode, embedding_document_layout_was_stale)
}

//! What a `url()` resolves against: the document's base URL, and the resource context of the style
//! sheet a rule came from, keyed by the native sheet's identity (an imported sheet's own, not its
//! importer's). The host lends them at each style update boundary; the engine keeps a copy.

use super::fast_hash::FastMap as HashMap;

use super::bridge::{FfiDocumentStyleComputationInputs, FfiHostHandle, FfiStyleSheetResourceContextEntry};
use crate::css::style_compute::FfiStyleSheetResourceContext;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct StyleSheetResourceContext {
    pub(crate) base_url: Box<[u8]>,
    pub(crate) has_base_url: bool,
    pub(crate) origin_clean: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct DocumentResourceContexts {
    pub(crate) document_base_url: Box<[u8]>,
    by_source: HashMap<u64, StyleSheetResourceContext>,
    /// Which collection of the contexts the host last lent, which `by_source` holds.
    version: u64,
}

impl DocumentResourceContexts {
    /// Take in what the host lent with the inputs, and clear the borrowed fields so the inputs
    /// compare by value from here on. No record the engine keeps across transactions read the
    /// contexts held before, so nothing is forgotten when they move. Most transactions lend
    /// exactly the contexts already held, which are then kept as they are.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// The borrowed fields must name live buffers of their stated lengths for this call.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn take_in(&mut self, inputs: &mut FfiDocumentStyleComputationInputs) {
        fn lent<'a>(address: *const u8, length: usize) -> &'a [u8] {
            if address.is_null() || length == 0 {
                &[]
            } else {
                unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(address, length) }
            }
        }
        let document_base_url = lent(
            inputs.document_base_url.as_pointer().cast(),
            inputs.document_base_url_length,
        );
        let entries =
            if inputs.style_sheet_resource_contexts.is_none() || inputs.style_sheet_resource_context_count == 0 {
                &[][..]
            } else {
                unsafe {
                    ak::slice_from_raw_parts(
                        inputs
                            .style_sheet_resource_contexts
                            .as_pointer()
                            .cast::<FfiStyleSheetResourceContextEntry>(),
                        inputs.style_sheet_resource_context_count,
                    )
                }
            };
        inputs.document_base_url = FfiHostHandle::default();
        inputs.document_base_url_length = 0;
        inputs.style_sheet_resource_contexts = FfiHostHandle::default();
        inputs.style_sheet_resource_context_count = 0;

        if *self.document_base_url != *document_base_url {
            self.document_base_url = document_base_url.into();
        }
        if std::mem::replace(&mut self.version, inputs.style_sheet_resource_contexts_version)
            == inputs.style_sheet_resource_contexts_version
        {
            return;
        }
        let held = |entry: &FfiStyleSheetResourceContextEntry| {
            self.by_source.get(&entry.source_identity).is_some_and(|context| {
                *context.base_url == *lent(entry.base_url, entry.base_url_length)
                    && context.has_base_url == entry.has_base_url
                    && context.origin_clean == entry.origin_clean
            })
        };
        if entries.len() == self.by_source.len() && entries.iter().all(held) {
            return;
        }
        self.by_source = entries
            .iter()
            .map(|entry| {
                let context = StyleSheetResourceContext {
                    base_url: lent(entry.base_url, entry.base_url_length).into(),
                    has_base_url: entry.has_base_url,
                    origin_clean: entry.origin_clean,
                };
                (entry.source_identity, context)
            })
            .collect();
    }

    pub(crate) fn for_source(&self, source_identity: u64) -> Option<&StyleSheetResourceContext> {
        self.by_source.get(&source_identity)
    }
}

impl StyleSheetResourceContext {
    /// The context as the drive reads it, borrowing this one's base URL.
    pub(crate) fn as_drive_context(&self) -> FfiStyleSheetResourceContext {
        FfiStyleSheetResourceContext {
            base_url: if self.has_base_url {
                self.base_url.as_ptr()
            } else {
                std::ptr::null()
            },
            base_url_length: if self.has_base_url { self.base_url.len() } else { 0 },
            has_value: true,
            origin_clean: self.origin_clean,
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn lend(
        contexts: &mut DocumentResourceContexts,
        document_base_url: &str,
        sheets: &[(u64, &str)],
    ) -> FfiDocumentStyleComputationInputs {
        let entries: Vec<_> = sheets
            .iter()
            .map(|&(source_identity, base_url)| FfiStyleSheetResourceContextEntry {
                source_identity,
                base_url: base_url.as_ptr(),
                base_url_length: base_url.len(),
                has_base_url: true,
                origin_clean: true,
            })
            .collect();
        let mut inputs = FfiDocumentStyleComputationInputs {
            document_base_url: FfiHostHandle::from_pointer(document_base_url.as_ptr().cast()),
            document_base_url_length: document_base_url.len(),
            style_sheet_resource_contexts: FfiHostHandle::from_pointer(entries.as_ptr().cast()),
            style_sheet_resource_context_count: entries.len(),
            style_sheet_resource_contexts_version: contexts.version + 1,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        unsafe { contexts.take_in(&mut inputs) };
        inputs
    }

    #[test]
    fn contexts_follow_what_the_host_lends() {
        let mut contexts = DocumentResourceContexts::default();
        let inputs = lend(&mut contexts, "https://a/", &[(1, "https://a/one.css")]);
        assert!(inputs.document_base_url.is_none() && inputs.style_sheet_resource_contexts.is_none());
        assert_eq!(inputs.style_sheet_resource_context_count, 0);
        assert_eq!(&*contexts.document_base_url, b"https://a/");

        // A sheet that joins, or leaves.
        lend(
            &mut contexts,
            "https://a/",
            &[(1, "https://a/one.css"), (2, "https://b/")],
        );
        assert_eq!(
            contexts.for_source(2).map(|context| &*context.base_url),
            Some(&b"https://b/"[..])
        );
        lend(&mut contexts, "https://a/", &[(1, "https://a/one.css")]);
        assert!(contexts.for_source(2).is_none());

        // A held sheet whose base URL moved, and the document's.
        lend(&mut contexts, "https://a/", &[(1, "https://c/one.css")]);
        assert_eq!(
            contexts.for_source(1).map(|context| &*context.base_url),
            Some(&b"https://c/one.css"[..])
        );
        lend(&mut contexts, "https://d/", &[(1, "https://c/one.css")]);
        assert_eq!(&*contexts.document_base_url, b"https://d/");
    }
}

//! The writes the host makes of its document's style sheets to the style engine. The host compiles a sheet's rules
//! itself and writes them, named by their native identities, which the engine resolves to rules of its own as it
//! applies the writes: where the frame is here, as the host makes them, and beside a frame in flight, once it is taken
//! in. The host numbers the sheets and keeps which rules it published to each, so a write to a sheet never asks the
//! engine anything.

use super::StyleEngine;
use super::bridge::{
    BoundScopeChain, FfiCascadeOrigin, intern_native_text, publish_style_rule, publish_style_rule_selectors,
};
use super::pipeline::rule_store::{CascadeLayerID, RuleDeclarations, RuleID, RuleKind, SheetID};
use super::tree::TreeScopeID;
use crate::css::container_conditions::ContainerConditionsData;
use crate::css::declaration_block::SharedDeclarationBlock;
use crate::css::selector_parser::RustParsedSelectorList;
use crate::css::style_sheet::NativeStyleSheet;
use crate::fast_hash::FastMap;
use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// How many native identities share one word of a sheet's table: a parsed sheet numbers its rules in one range.
const IDENTITIES_PER_WORD: u64 = u128::BITS as u64;

/// The rules the host published to each sheet of its document's style engine, by native identity, which the host
/// reads where it would otherwise ask the engine which of a sheet's rules it has. The engine numbers its sheets in the
/// order they are added and never reuses a number, so the host numbers them as it adds them.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct PublishedRules {
    /// The identities each sheet holds, by the sheet's number less one, as one bit per identity.
    sheets: RefCell<Vec<FastMap<u64, u128>>>,
}

impl PublishedRules {
    /// Numbers the next sheet the host adds, as the boundary does: one more than the engine's own number.
    pub(crate) fn mint_sheet(&self) -> u32 {
        let mut sheets = self.sheets.borrow_mut();
        sheets.push(FastMap::default());
        u32::try_from(sheets.len()).expect("sheet identity space exhausted")
    }

    /// Whether the host published the rule `identity` to the sheet `sheet`.
    pub(crate) fn contains(&self, sheet: u32, identity: u64) -> bool {
        let sheets = self.sheets.borrow();
        sheet
            .checked_sub(1)
            .and_then(|index| sheets.get(index as usize))
            .and_then(|words| words.get(&(identity / IDENTITIES_PER_WORD)))
            .is_some_and(|word| word & bit(identity) != 0)
    }

    /// Notes that the host published the rule `identity` to the sheet `sheet`.
    pub(crate) fn insert(&self, sheet: u32, identity: u64) {
        let mut sheets = self.sheets.borrow_mut();
        *sheets[sheet as usize - 1]
            .entry(identity / IDENTITIES_PER_WORD)
            .or_default() |= bit(identity);
    }

    /// Takes the rule `identity` out of the sheet `sheet`, answering whether the host had published it there.
    pub(crate) fn remove(&self, sheet: u32, identity: u64) -> bool {
        let mut sheets = self.sheets.borrow_mut();
        let Some(words) = sheet.checked_sub(1).and_then(|index| sheets.get_mut(index as usize)) else {
            return false;
        };
        let key = identity / IDENTITIES_PER_WORD;
        let Some(word) = words.get_mut(&key) else {
            return false;
        };
        let held = *word & bit(identity) != 0;
        *word &= !bit(identity);
        if *word == 0 {
            words.remove(&key);
        }
        held
    }

    /// Forgets every rule of the sheet `sheet`, whose rules the engine is to replace.
    pub(crate) fn forget(&self, sheet: u32) {
        let mut sheets = self.sheets.borrow_mut();
        if let Some(words) = sheet.checked_sub(1).and_then(|index| sheets.get_mut(index as usize)) {
            *words = FastMap::default();
        }
    }

    /// The identity of the first rule after the subtree of the rule `identity` in `native`, the native sheet whose
    /// rules the host publishes to the sheet `sheet`, that the host published there, or 0 for none.
    pub(crate) fn successor(&self, sheet: u32, native: &NativeStyleSheet, identity: u64) -> u64 {
        crate::css::rule::mutation::successor(native, identity, |identity| self.contains(sheet, identity))
    }
}

fn bit(identity: u64) -> u128 {
    1 << (identity % IDENTITIES_PER_WORD)
}

/// A style rule's bound selectors and the scopes it is inside.
pub(crate) struct BoundSelectors {
    pub(crate) selectors: RustParsedSelectorList,
    pub(crate) scope: Arc<BoundScopeChain>,
}

/// What a compiled rule is to the engine.
pub(crate) enum CompiledRuleKind {
    /// A style rule, or nested declarations, which matches elements.
    Style {
        selectors: BoundSelectors,
        gated_by_container_query: bool,
    },
    /// A rule found by the name it declares: `@property` or `@keyframes`.
    Named { kind: RuleKind, name: Box<[u16]> },
    /// A rule that neither matches nor is found by name: `@font-feature-values`, `@counter-style` or `@function`.
    NonMatching(RuleKind),
}

/// One rule the host compiled, as owned data the engine publishes.
pub(crate) struct CompiledRule {
    pub(crate) identity: u64,
    pub(crate) kind: CompiledRuleKind,
    pub(crate) declarations: Option<SharedDeclarationBlock>,
    /// The native sheet the rule comes from, which may be a sheet the rule's sheet imports.
    pub(crate) source_identity: u64,
    pub(crate) conditions_hold: bool,
    /// Whether the rule cascades in the named layer `layer_name`.
    pub(crate) in_a_layer: bool,
    pub(crate) layer_name: Arc<[u16]>,
    /// The container conditions the rule is inside, innermost first.
    pub(crate) containers: Box<[Arc<ContainerConditionsData>]>,
}

impl CompiledRule {
    fn publish(self, engine: &mut StyleEngine, sheet: u32, before: u32) {
        let place = sheet
            .checked_sub(1)
            .map(|sheet| (SheetID(sheet), before.checked_sub(1).map(RuleID)));
        let rule = match &self.kind {
            CompiledRuleKind::Style { selectors, .. } => {
                let id = publish_style_rule(engine, sheet, before, &selectors.selectors.selectors, &selectors.scope);
                let rule = id.checked_sub(1).map(RuleID);
                if let (Some(rule), Some(declarations)) = (rule, &self.declarations) {
                    engine.publish_block_declarations(rule, declarations);
                }
                rule
            }
            CompiledRuleKind::Named { kind, name } => {
                let name = intern_native_text(engine, name);
                place.map(|(sheet, before)| match kind {
                    RuleKind::Property => engine.add_property_rule(sheet, before, name),
                    RuleKind::Keyframes => engine.add_keyframes_rule(sheet, before, name),
                    _ => unreachable!("only @property and @keyframes rules are found by name"),
                })
            }
            CompiledRuleKind::NonMatching(kind) => {
                assert!(
                    matches!(
                        kind,
                        RuleKind::FontFeatureValues | RuleKind::CounterStyle | RuleKind::Function
                    ),
                    "only rules of a non-matching kind are published without a name"
                );
                place.map(|(sheet, before)| engine.add_non_matching_rule(sheet, before, *kind))
            }
        };
        let Some(rule) = rule else {
            return;
        };
        if matches!(
            self.kind,
            CompiledRuleKind::Style {
                gated_by_container_query: true,
                ..
            }
        ) {
            engine.set_rule_gated_by_container_query(rule);
        }
        if !self.conditions_hold {
            engine.set_rule_conditions_hold(rule, false);
        }
        if self.in_a_layer {
            let layer = intern_native_text(engine, &self.layer_name).0;
            engine.set_rule_layer(rule, CascadeLayerID(layer));
        }
        engine.register_native_rule(
            rule,
            self.identity,
            self.source_identity,
            self.layer_name,
            self.containers,
        );
    }
}

/// A write to a document's style sheets, which the engine applies in the order the host made it.
pub(crate) enum RuleWrite {
    /// The engine adds the sheet the host numbered `sheet`, which cascades in `origin`.
    AddSheet { sheet: u32, origin: FfiCascadeOrigin },
    /// The engine adds the sheet the host numbered `sheet`, which stands for the user agent sheet the process published
    /// from the native sheet `source_identity`.
    AddUserAgentSheet { sheet: u32, source_identity: u64 },
    /// The engine begins to replace the rules of `sheet`, keeping the identities of those the replacement keeps.
    BeginSheetRulesReplacement(u32),
    /// Rules the host compiled into `sheet`, in order, ahead of the rule `before` names, or at the sheet's end.
    PublishRules {
        sheet: u32,
        before: u64,
        rules: Vec<CompiledRule>,
    },
    /// A style rule keeps its place and its declarations, and selects what `selectors` select.
    ReplaceSelectors { identity: u64, selectors: BoundSelectors },
    /// Rules leave the engine, in the order the host removed them.
    RemoveRules(Box<[u64]>),
    /// The rule `identity` declares `declarations`.
    RuleDeclarations {
        identity: u64,
        declarations: Option<SharedDeclarationBlock>,
    },
    /// Whether the conditions of each rule hold.
    RuleConditions(Box<[(u64, bool)]>),
    /// The order of the cascade layers of a tree scope, by qualified name, the unnamed outer layer as an empty one.
    LayerOrder { tree_scope: u32, names: Vec<Vec<u16>> },
}

impl RuleWrite {
    pub(crate) fn apply(self, engine: &mut StyleEngine) {
        match self {
            Self::AddSheet { sheet, origin } => {
                let added = engine.add_sheet(origin.decode());
                assert_eq!(added.0 + 1, sheet, "the engine numbers a sheet as its host did");
            }
            Self::AddUserAgentSheet { sheet, source_identity } => {
                let added = engine.add_user_agent_sheet(source_identity);
                assert_eq!(added.0 + 1, sheet, "the engine numbers a sheet as its host did");
            }
            Self::BeginSheetRulesReplacement(sheet) => {
                if let Some(sheet) = sheet.checked_sub(1) {
                    engine.begin_sheet_rules_replacement(SheetID(sheet));
                }
            }
            Self::PublishRules { sheet, before, rules } => {
                let before = rule_number(engine, before);
                for rule in rules {
                    rule.publish(engine, sheet, before);
                }
            }
            Self::ReplaceSelectors { identity, selectors } => {
                let rule = rule_number(engine, identity);
                publish_style_rule_selectors(engine, rule, &selectors.selectors.selectors, &selectors.scope);
            }
            Self::RemoveRules(identities) => {
                for identity in identities {
                    if let Some(rule) = engine.native_rule_id(identity) {
                        engine.remove_style_rule(rule);
                    }
                }
            }
            Self::RuleDeclarations { identity, declarations } => {
                if let Some(rule) = engine.native_rule_id(identity) {
                    publish_native_rule_declarations(engine, declarations, rule);
                }
            }
            Self::RuleConditions(conditions) => {
                for (identity, holds) in conditions {
                    if let Some(rule) = engine.native_rule_id(identity) {
                        engine.set_rule_conditions_hold(rule, holds);
                    }
                }
            }
            Self::LayerOrder { tree_scope, names } => {
                let layers: Vec<_> = names
                    .iter()
                    .map(|name| {
                        CascadeLayerID(if name.is_empty() {
                            0
                        } else {
                            intern_native_text(engine, name).0
                        })
                    })
                    .collect();
                engine.set_layer_order(TreeScopeID(tree_scope), &layers);
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The engine's number of the rule the native identity `identity` names, as the boundary numbers it, or 0 for none.
fn rule_number(engine: &StyleEngine, identity: u64) -> u32 {
    engine.native_rule_id(identity).map_or(0, |rule| rule.0 + 1)
}

/// Publishes `declarations` as what the engine's rule `rule` declares.
pub(crate) fn publish_native_rule_declarations(
    engine: &mut StyleEngine,
    declarations: Option<SharedDeclarationBlock>,
    rule: RuleID,
) {
    let version = engine.next_declaration_block_version();
    engine.record_rule_declarations_changed(rule, version);
    match &declarations {
        Some(declarations) => {
            engine.publish_block_declarations(rule, declarations);
        }
        None => engine.stage_rule_declarations(rule, RuleDeclarations::default()),
    }
}

/// Adds a sheet to the document's style engine, which cascades in `origin`, and answers the number the host gave it.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_add_sheet(host: &crate::render_state::DocumentHost, origin: FfiCascadeOrigin) -> u32 {
    let sheet = host.published_rules().mint_sheet();
    host.write_rules(RuleWrite::AddSheet { sheet, origin });
    sheet
}

/// Publishes `rules`, compiled from the native user agent sheet `source_identity`, as the process's. Each rule's
/// conditions are its document's, which the document notes where they do not hold.
pub(crate) fn publish_user_agent_sheet(source_identity: u64, rules: Vec<CompiledRule>) {
    crate::render_state::process_style().publish_user_agent_sheet(source_identity, |engine, sheet| {
        for mut rule in rules {
            assert!(!rule.in_a_layer, "no user agent rule cascades in a layer");
            rule.conditions_hold = true;
            rule.publish(engine, sheet.0 + 1, 0);
        }
    });
}

/// Adds a sheet to the document's style engine standing for the user agent sheet the process published from the native
/// sheet `source_identity`, and answers the number the host gave it.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_add_user_agent_sheet(
    host: &crate::render_state::DocumentHost,
    source_identity: u64,
) -> u32 {
    let sheet = host.published_rules().mint_sheet();
    host.write_rules(RuleWrite::AddUserAgentSheet { sheet, source_identity });
    sheet
}

/// Has the render owner apply the rule writes the host queued now, beside the host's task rather than in its next job.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_stream_rule_writes(host: &crate::render_state::DocumentHost) {
    host.stream_writes_now();
}

/// Begins to replace the rules of the sheet `sheet`, whose rules the host compiles again, or none.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn style_engine_begin_sheet_rules_replacement(host: &crate::render_state::DocumentHost, sheet: u32) {
    host.published_rules().forget(sheet);
    host.write_rules(RuleWrite::BeginSheetRulesReplacement(sheet));
}

/*

//! What the rule index reads of an entry's selector, from its components: which families of
//! buckets it is in, whether it revalidates, the ids it tests for, and the key a compound reached
//! by no name is bucketed by.

use super::StyleAtomID;
use super::component_matching::{CompoundTarget, EntrySelector, compound_target, mentions};
use super::index::DispatchKey;
use crate::css::selector::{
    Combinator, CompoundRef, PseudoClassType, PseudoElementType, PseudoElementValue, Selector, SelectorListView,
    SimpleSelector,
};
use crate::css::selector_arena::{Nesting, SheetNamespaces};
use smallvec::SmallVec;

/// What the rule index reads of one entry.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct EntryFacts {
    pub(super) never_matches: bool,
    pub(super) scoped: bool,
    pub(super) revalidates: bool,
    pub(super) host: bool,
    pub(super) slotted: bool,
    pub(super) part: bool,
}

impl EntryFacts {
    pub(super) fn of(entry: EntrySelector<'_>) -> Self {
        let scoped = entry.scope().is_some();
        let subject = subject_compound(entry.selector);
        let first = subject.first_compound();
        let pseudo_element = match first.simple_selectors.first() {
            Some(SimpleSelector::PseudoElement(pseudo_element)) => Some(pseudo_element.pseudo_element),
            _ => None,
        };
        Self {
            never_matches: never_matches(&first),
            scoped,
            revalidates: scoped || revalidates(entry.selector),
            // NB: Asking the host is the wider of the two answers where the subject may be the
            //     scoping root, which can be the host.
            host: scoped || names_the_host(&first),
            slotted: pseudo_element == Some(PseudoElementType::Slotted),
            part: pseudo_element == Some(PseudoElementType::Part),
        }
    }
}

/// The compound of `selector` an element matching it is the subject of: its first, or the one
/// left of a pseudo-element no element stands for.
pub(super) fn subject_compound(selector: Selector<'_>) -> Selector<'_> {
    let first = selector.first_compound();
    let transparent = matches!(compound_target(&first), CompoundTarget::Transparent);
    match (transparent, selector.left()) {
        (true, Some((Combinator::PseudoElement, left))) => left,
        _ => selector,
    }
}

/// Whether the compound tests something no element satisfies, as a `:has()`, `:is()` or
/// `:where()` all of whose arguments were invalid does.
pub(crate) fn never_matches(compound: &CompoundRef<'_>) -> bool {
    compound.simple_selectors.iter().any(|simple| match simple {
        SimpleSelector::PseudoClass(pseudo_class) => match pseudo_class.pseudo_class {
            PseudoClassType::Has | PseudoClassType::Is | PseudoClassType::Where => {
                pseudo_class.argument_selector_list.is_empty()
            }
            PseudoClassType::State => pseudo_class.identifier_identity.is_none(),
            _ => false,
        },
        SimpleSelector::Invalid(_) => true,
        _ => false,
    })
}

/// Whether a compound can match the featureless host of the tree its rule is in: one of its
/// simple selectors names the host or the scoping root, and every other one may match the host.
fn names_the_host(compound: &CompoundRef<'_>) -> bool {
    let names = |simple: &SimpleSelector<'_>| {
        mentions(simple, &|simple| match simple {
            SimpleSelector::PseudoClass(pseudo_class) => {
                matches!(
                    pseudo_class.pseudo_class,
                    PseudoClassType::Host | PseudoClassType::Scope
                )
            }
            SimpleSelector::Nesting(Nesting::Root | Nesting::Scope) => true,
            _ => false,
        })
    };
    compound.simple_selectors.iter().any(|simple| names(&simple))
}

/// Whether a selector can tell apart two elements that agree on the style sharing key: their tag,
/// namespace, classes and states, the absence of an id a selector tests for, and parents that are
/// the same element or themselves shared a style, all the way up. What it reads of the elements
/// and their ancestors beyond that key, such as attributes, siblings and tree position, it has to
/// be evaluated for.
fn revalidates(selector: Selector<'_>) -> bool {
    let mut compound = Some(subject_compound(selector));
    while let Some(current) = compound {
        if current.is_relative_anchor() {
            return true;
        }
        if current
            .first_compound()
            .simple_selectors
            .iter()
            .any(|simple| simple_revalidates(&simple))
        {
            return true;
        }
        compound = match current.left() {
            None => None,
            Some((Combinator::ImmediateChild | Combinator::Descendant, left)) => Some(left),
            Some(_) => return true,
        };
    }
    false
}

fn simple_revalidates(simple: &SimpleSelector<'_>) -> bool {
    let any = |list: SelectorListView<'_>| list.iter().any(revalidates);
    match simple {
        SimpleSelector::Universal(_)
        | SimpleSelector::TagName(_)
        | SimpleSelector::Id(_)
        | SimpleSelector::Class(_) => false,
        SimpleSelector::PseudoClass(pseudo_class) => match pseudo_class.pseudo_class {
            PseudoClassType::Root => false,
            PseudoClassType::Is | PseudoClassType::Where | PseudoClassType::Not => {
                any(pseudo_class.argument_selector_list)
            }
            kind => super::compiler::state_fact_for(kind).is_none(),
        },
        SimpleSelector::Nesting(Nesting::Rule(parent)) => any(*parent),
        _ => true,
    }
}

/// Collect the ids `selector`, which does not revalidate, tests for, in each form an element
/// carries them.
pub(super) fn collect_tested_ids(selector: Selector<'_>, ids: &mut Vec<StyleAtomID>) {
    let atoms = super::process_atoms();
    for current in subject_compound(selector).compounds() {
        for simple in current.simple_selectors.iter() {
            let simple = &simple;
            match simple {
                SimpleSelector::Id(name) => {
                    ids.push(name.name);
                    if !name.is_ascii_lowercase {
                        ids.push(atoms.ascii_lowercase(name.name));
                    }
                }
                SimpleSelector::PseudoClass(pseudo_class)
                    if matches!(
                        pseudo_class.pseudo_class,
                        PseudoClassType::Is | PseudoClassType::Where | PseudoClassType::Not
                    ) =>
                {
                    for selector in pseudo_class.argument_selector_list {
                        collect_tested_ids(selector, ids);
                    }
                }
                SimpleSelector::Nesting(Nesting::Rule(parent)) => {
                    for selector in *parent {
                        collect_tested_ids(selector, ids);
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A key only elements the subject compound of `selector` can match carry, for a compound reached
/// by no name: a state, being a heading, or being the document element.
pub(super) fn state_dispatch_key(selector: Selector<'_>) -> Option<DispatchKey> {
    let compound = subject_compound(selector).first_compound();
    compound.simple_selectors.iter().find_map(|simple| match simple {
        SimpleSelector::PseudoClass(pseudo_class) => match pseudo_class.pseudo_class {
            PseudoClassType::Heading => Some(DispatchKey::Heading),
            PseudoClassType::Root => Some(DispatchKey::Root),
            kind => super::compiler::state_fact_for(kind).map(DispatchKey::State),
        },
        _ => None,
    })
}

/// How many keys a compound may carry before checking them all costs more than the rejections save.
const MAX_DISPATCH_KEYS: usize = 8;

/// The keys an element matching the subject compound of `selector` carries one of, which its entry
/// is bucketed by, or none where it carries none in particular: the universal bucket's.
///
/// A name not written in ASCII lowercase is bucketed under its lowercase form too, which a
/// quirks-mode document, an HTML element's tag name and an HTML attribute name are carried in.
pub(super) fn subject_dispatch_keys(selector: Selector<'_>) -> SmallVec<[DispatchKey; 4]> {
    let mut keys = compound_dispatch_keys(&subject_compound(selector).first_compound()).unwrap_or_default();
    keys.sort_unstable();
    keys.dedup();
    keys
}

/// The cheapest set of keys one of which every element matching `compound` carries.
fn compound_dispatch_keys(compound: &CompoundRef<'_>) -> Option<SmallVec<[DispatchKey; 4]>> {
    compound
        .simple_selectors
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|simple| simple_dispatch_keys(&simple))
        .min_by_key(|keys| {
            keys.iter()
                .map(|&key| u32::from(dispatch_selectivity(key)) + 1)
                .sum::<u32>()
        })
}

fn simple_dispatch_keys(simple: &SimpleSelector<'_>) -> Option<SmallVec<[DispatchKey; 4]>> {
    let atoms = super::process_atoms();
    let both = |make: fn(StyleAtomID) -> DispatchKey, name: StyleAtomID, lowercase: bool| {
        let mut keys: SmallVec<[DispatchKey; 4]> = smallvec::smallvec![make(name)];
        if !lowercase {
            keys.push(make(atoms.ascii_lowercase(name)));
        }
        Some(keys)
    };
    let alternatives = |list: SelectorListView<'_>| {
        let mut keys: SmallVec<[DispatchKey; 4]> = SmallVec::new();
        for selector in list {
            keys.extend(compound_dispatch_keys(&selector.first_compound())?);
            if keys.len() > MAX_DISPATCH_KEYS {
                return None;
            }
        }
        (!keys.is_empty()).then_some(keys)
    };
    match simple {
        SimpleSelector::Id(name) => both(DispatchKey::Id, name.name, name.is_ascii_lowercase),
        SimpleSelector::Class(name) => both(DispatchKey::Class, name.name, name.is_ascii_lowercase),
        SimpleSelector::TagName(name) => both(DispatchKey::TagName, name.name, name.name_is_ascii_lowercase),
        SimpleSelector::Attribute(attribute) => both(
            DispatchKey::AttributeName,
            attribute.qualified_name.name,
            attribute.qualified_name.name_is_ascii_lowercase,
        )
        // NB: A name qualified by a namespace is carried qualified, which the components do not hold.
        .filter(|_| {
            matches!(
                attribute.qualified_name.namespace_type,
                crate::css::selector::NamespaceType::Default | crate::css::selector::NamespaceType::None
            )
        }),
        SimpleSelector::PseudoClass(pseudo_class) => match pseudo_class.pseudo_class {
            PseudoClassType::Is | PseudoClassType::Where => alternatives(pseudo_class.argument_selector_list),
            PseudoClassType::Host => pseudo_class
                .argument_selector_list
                .single()
                .and_then(|argument| compound_dispatch_keys(&argument.first_compound())),
            PseudoClassType::State if !pseudo_class.identifier_identity.is_none() => {
                Some(smallvec::smallvec![DispatchKey::CustomState(
                    pseudo_class.identifier_identity
                )])
            }
            // NB: A state without a posting names nothing to find its elements by, and admitting it
            //     would take the compound away from names that do.
            kind => super::compiler::state_fact_for(kind)
                .filter(|fact| fact.has_selector_posting())
                .map(|fact| smallvec::smallvec![DispatchKey::State(fact)]),
        },
        SimpleSelector::PseudoElement(pseudo_element) => match pseudo_element.value {
            PseudoElementValue::CompoundSelector(argument)
                if pseudo_element.pseudo_element == PseudoElementType::Slotted =>
            {
                compound_dispatch_keys(&argument.first_compound())
            }
            _ if pseudo_element.pseudo_element == PseudoElementType::Part => pseudo_element
                .identifier_identities
                .first()
                .map(|&part| smallvec::smallvec![DispatchKey::Part(part)]),
            _ => None,
        },
        SimpleSelector::Nesting(Nesting::Rule(parent)) => alternatives(*parent),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// How selective a dispatch key is expected to be, lowest first.
pub(super) fn dispatch_selectivity(key: DispatchKey) -> u8 {
    match key {
        DispatchKey::Part(_) | DispatchKey::CustomState(_) | DispatchKey::Id(_) => 0,
        DispatchKey::Class(_) => 1,
        DispatchKey::AttributeName(_) => 2,
        DispatchKey::TagName(_) => 3,
        DispatchKey::Directionality(_) => 4,
        _ => 5,
    }
}

/// What the host and the arrival routing ask of a document's selectors: the attribute names they
/// test, those whose values they read as text, whether they test `:local-link` or a control's validity, and what an
/// element arriving has to carry to reach the anchor of one of their `:has()`.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(in crate::css::style) struct SelectorSummary {
    pub(super) tested_attribute_names: Vec<StyleAtomID>,
    pub(super) attribute_value_text_names: Vec<StyleAtomID>,
    pub(super) tests_local_link: bool,
    pub(super) tests_validity: bool,
    pub(super) relational_arrival_keys: Vec<DispatchKey>,
}

impl SelectorSummary {
    /// The summary of the selectors of `list`, inside the `@scope` levels `scope`.
    pub(super) fn of(list: SelectorListView<'_>, scope: Option<&super::bridge::BoundScopeChain>) -> Self {
        let mut summary = Self::default();
        for selector in list {
            summary.add_selector(selector, false);
        }
        for bound in scope
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|scope| scope.roots.iter().chain(&scope.limits))
        {
            let selector = bound.view();
            summary.add_selector(selector, false);
        }
        summary
    }

    fn add_selector(&mut self, selector: Selector<'_>, in_argument: bool) {
        for current in selector.compounds() {
            for simple in current.simple_selectors.iter() {
                self.add_simple(&simple, selector.namespaces(), in_argument);
            }
        }
    }

    fn add_list(&mut self, list: SelectorListView<'_>, in_argument: bool) {
        for selector in list {
            self.add_selector(selector, in_argument);
        }
    }

    fn arrival_key(&mut self, in_argument: bool, key: DispatchKey) {
        if in_argument && !self.relational_arrival_keys.contains(&key) {
            self.relational_arrival_keys.push(key);
        }
    }

    fn add_simple(&mut self, simple: &SimpleSelector<'_>, namespaces: SheetNamespaces<'_>, in_argument: bool) {
        let atoms = super::process_atoms();
        let forms = |name: StyleAtomID, lowercase: bool| -> SmallVec<[StyleAtomID; 2]> {
            match lowercase {
                true => smallvec::smallvec![name],
                false => smallvec::smallvec![name, atoms.ascii_lowercase(name)],
            }
        };
        match simple {
            SimpleSelector::Universal(_) => self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::Structural),
            SimpleSelector::TagName(name) => {
                for form in forms(name.name, name.name_is_ascii_lowercase) {
                    self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::TagName(form));
                }
            }
            SimpleSelector::Id(name) => {
                for form in forms(name.name, name.is_ascii_lowercase) {
                    self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::Id(form));
                }
            }
            SimpleSelector::Class(name) => {
                for form in forms(name.name, name.is_ascii_lowercase) {
                    self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::Class(form));
                }
            }
            SimpleSelector::Attribute(attribute) => {
                // `[*|x]` tests the name qualified by no namespace, `[ns|x]` the one qualified by the
                // namespace the prefix names, and `[x]` the bare local name.
                let qualifier = match attribute.qualified_name.namespace_type {
                    crate::css::selector::NamespaceType::Any => Some(StyleAtomID::NONE),
                    crate::css::selector::NamespaceType::Named => {
                        match namespaces.namespace_of(attribute.qualified_name.namespace) {
                            Some(namespace) => Some(namespace),
                            None => return,
                        }
                    }
                    _ => None,
                };
                // NB: The selector's arena leases the qualified names too, which keeps them live
                //     while the rule is.
                let names: SmallVec<[StyleAtomID; 2]> = forms(
                    attribute.qualified_name.name,
                    attribute.qualified_name.name_is_ascii_lowercase,
                )
                .into_iter()
                .map(|name| match qualifier {
                    Some(namespace) => super::AtomLease::acquire_qualified(atoms, namespace, name).atom(),
                    None => name,
                })
                .collect();
                let reads_text = attribute.match_type != crate::css::selector::AttributeMatchType::HasAttribute
                    && (attribute.match_type != crate::css::selector::AttributeMatchType::ExactValue
                        || attribute.case_type == crate::css::selector::AttributeCaseType::Insensitive
                        || attribute.names_a_legacy_case_insensitive_attribute);
                for &name in &names {
                    if !self.tested_attribute_names.contains(&name) {
                        self.tested_attribute_names.push(name);
                    }
                    if reads_text && !self.attribute_value_text_names.contains(&name) {
                        self.attribute_value_text_names.push(name);
                    }
                    self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::AttributeName(name));
                }
            }
            SimpleSelector::PseudoClass(pseudo_class) => {
                let list = pseudo_class.argument_selector_list;
                match pseudo_class.pseudo_class {
                    PseudoClassType::Has => self.add_list(list, true),
                    PseudoClassType::State if !pseudo_class.identifier_identity.is_none() => {
                        self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::CustomState(pseudo_class.identifier_identity));
                    }
                    PseudoClassType::Lang => self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::Language),
                    // NB: Which direction `:dir()` names is a fact of the tree's shape as an arrival
                    //     sees it.
                    PseudoClassType::Root
                    | PseudoClassType::Empty
                    | PseudoClassType::Scope
                    | PseudoClassType::Heading
                    | PseudoClassType::Dir => self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::Structural),
                    kind => {
                        if let Some(fact) = super::compiler::state_fact_for(kind) {
                            self.tests_local_link |= fact == super::input_types::StateFact::LocalLink;
                            self.tests_validity |= matches!(
                                fact,
                                super::input_types::StateFact::Valid
                                    | super::input_types::StateFact::Invalid
                                    | super::input_types::StateFact::UserValid
                                    | super::input_types::StateFact::UserInvalid
                            );
                            self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::State(fact));
                        }
                        if reads_position(pseudo_class) {
                            self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::Structural);
                        }
                        self.add_list(list, in_argument);
                    }
                }
            }
            SimpleSelector::PseudoElement(pseudo_element) => match pseudo_element.value {
                PseudoElementValue::CompoundSelector(argument) => self.add_selector(argument, in_argument),
                _ if pseudo_element.pseudo_element == PseudoElementType::Part => {
                    for &part in pseudo_element.identifier_identities {
                        self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::Part(part));
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            },
            SimpleSelector::Nesting(Nesting::Rule(parent)) => self.add_list(*parent, in_argument),
            SimpleSelector::Nesting(_) => self.arrival_key(in_argument, DispatchKey::Structural),
            SimpleSelector::Invalid(_) => {}
        }
    }
}

/// Whether a pseudo-class reads where the element stands among its siblings.
fn reads_position(pseudo_class: &crate::css::selector::PseudoClassSelector<'_>) -> bool {
    matches!(
        pseudo_class.pseudo_class,
        PseudoClassType::FirstChild
            | PseudoClassType::LastChild
            | PseudoClassType::OnlyChild
            | PseudoClassType::FirstOfType
            | PseudoClassType::LastOfType
            | PseudoClassType::OnlyOfType
            | PseudoClassType::NthChild
            | PseudoClassType::NthLastChild
            | PseudoClassType::NthOfType
            | PseudoClassType::NthLastOfType
    )
}
