//! What selectors are matched against: a subject holding the elements and the facts a selector
//! tests, and the evaluator walking selector components over it.
//!
//! The style engine's subject reads its own storage, and the DOM query subject reads the live DOM.
//! Every matching rule lives in the evaluator, so two subjects can differ in what their storage
//! holds and never in what a selector means.
//!
//! A subject brings its accelerations along as hooks. A hook can only skip work: each default is
//! the answer the evaluation reaches without the shortcut.

use smallvec::SmallVec;

use super::index::StyleAtomID;
use super::input_types::StateFact;
use super::selector::NthPosition;
use super::selector::RelativeAxis;
use super::tree::StyleNodeID;
use crate::css::css_tokenizer::TokenizerInput;

/// Visit the candidate witnesses of a relative selector along `axis` from `anchor` in `tree`, in tree
/// order, until `visit` returns false. A walk of a subtree goes below the elements `holds_below` says
/// can hold a witness below them, and past the descendants of the others.
pub(crate) fn walk_relative_axis<T: SelectorTree>(
    tree: T,
    axis: RelativeAxis,
    below_the_axis: bool,
    anchor: T::Node,
    holds_below: impl Fn(T::Node) -> bool,
    mut visit: impl FnMut(T::Node) -> bool,
) {
    // Visit the subtree of `root`, `root` itself included when `inclusive`, until `visit` returns false.
    fn visit_subtree<T: SelectorTree>(
        tree: T,
        root: T::Node,
        inclusive: bool,
        holds_below: &impl Fn(T::Node) -> bool,
        visit: &mut impl FnMut(T::Node) -> bool,
    ) -> bool {
        if inclusive && !visit(root) {
            return false;
        }
        let mut current = root;
        loop {
            let next = match holds_below(current) {
                true => tree.next_in_subtree(current, root),
                false => tree.next_after_subtree(current, root),
            };
            let Some(candidate) = next else {
                return true;
            };
            if !visit(candidate) {
                return false;
            }
            current = candidate;
        }
    }

    let (first, every_sibling, subtree) = match axis {
        RelativeAxis::Descendant => {
            visit_subtree(tree, anchor, false, &holds_below, &mut visit);
            return;
        }
        RelativeAxis::Child => (tree.first_child(anchor), true, false),
        RelativeAxis::NextSibling => (tree.next_sibling(anchor), false, false),
        RelativeAxis::FollowingSibling => (tree.next_sibling(anchor), true, false),
        // The witness lies under the sibling rather than being it, so the sibling's whole subtree is the
        // candidate range.
        RelativeAxis::NextSiblingSubtree => (tree.next_sibling(anchor), false, true),
        RelativeAxis::FollowingSiblingSubtree => (tree.next_sibling(anchor), true, true),
    };
    let mut sibling = first;
    while let Some(candidate) = sibling {
        let proceed = match subtree {
            true => visit_subtree(tree, candidate, !below_the_axis, &holds_below, &mut visit),
            false => visit(candidate),
        };
        if !proceed || !every_sibling {
            return;
        }
        sibling = tree.next_sibling(candidate);
    }
}

/// How a subject's nodes relate.
///
/// A copyable handle, so a walk can hold it while it evaluates candidates. The nodes are elements,
/// plus the shadow root of the tree whose selectors are evaluated: that is where a combinator walking
/// up out of a shadow tree arrives, and the evaluator never asks a shadow root for a fact.
pub(crate) trait SelectorTree: Copy {
    type Node: Copy + Eq;

    fn parent(self, node: Self::Node) -> Option<Self::Node>;
    fn previous_sibling(self, node: Self::Node) -> Option<Self::Node>;
    fn next_sibling(self, node: Self::Node) -> Option<Self::Node>;
    fn first_child(self, parent: Self::Node) -> Option<Self::Node>;
    /// The parent in the tree as it stands now. Scope, slot and relational walks read it even where
    /// the combinators read an earlier state of the tree.
    fn live_parent(self, node: Self::Node) -> Option<Self::Node> {
        self.parent(node)
    }

    fn shadow_root_of(self, host: Self::Node) -> Option<Self::Node>;
    fn host_of(self, shadow_root: Self::Node) -> Option<Self::Node>;

    /// Whether the element stands for its shadow host's element-backed pseudo-element of `kind`.
    fn backs_pseudo_element(self, _node: Self::Node, _kind: u16) -> bool {
        false
    }

    /// The element of `host`'s shadow tree that stands for its element-backed pseudo-element of `kind`.
    fn backing_element_of(self, host: Self::Node, kind: u16) -> Option<Self::Node> {
        let shadow_root = self.shadow_root_of(host)?;
        let mut node = self.next_in_subtree(shadow_root, shadow_root);
        while let Some(current) = node {
            if self.backs_pseudo_element(current, kind) {
                return Some(current);
            }
            node = self.next_in_subtree(current, shadow_root);
        }
        None
    }

    /// The element after `node` in tree order that is a descendant of `root`, where `node` is `root` itself to start.
    fn next_in_subtree(self, node: Self::Node, root: Self::Node) -> Option<Self::Node> {
        if let Some(child) = self.first_child(node) {
            return Some(child);
        }
        self.next_after_subtree(node, root)
    }

    /// The element after `node` and its descendants in tree order that is a descendant of `root`.
    fn next_after_subtree(self, node: Self::Node, root: Self::Node) -> Option<Self::Node> {
        let mut current = node;
        while current != root {
            if let Some(sibling) = self.next_sibling(current) {
                return Some(sibling);
            }
            current = self.parent(current)?;
        }
        None
    }

    /// Whether [`Self::subtree_may_carry`] rejects elements, so that a walk for the witnesses of a relative selector
    /// has what they carry looked up at all.
    const SUMMARIZES_SUBTREE_KEYS: bool = false;

    /// Whether the descendants of `node` can possibly carry, between them, every class and attribute name whose
    /// bits in the Bloom summary of the keys a subtree carries `keys` holds. A shortcut that can only skip work:
    /// the default is the answer a walk of the descendants reaches without it.
    fn subtree_may_carry(self, _node: Self::Node, _keys: u64) -> bool {
        true
    }

    /// The slot an element is assigned to.
    fn assigned_slot_of(self, _node: Self::Node) -> Option<Self::Node> {
        None
    }

    /// The host of the shadow tree a node is in.
    fn shadow_host_of(self, _node: Self::Node) -> Option<Self::Node> {
        None
    }
}

/// What a feature test reads of one element. Names are process atoms.
pub(crate) trait ElementFeatures {
    type Attribute: Copy;

    fn local_name_is(&self, name: StyleAtomID) -> bool;
    /// `NONE` names the null namespace.
    fn namespace_is(&self, namespace: StyleAtomID) -> bool;
    fn has_id(&self, id: StyleAtomID) -> bool;
    fn has_class(&self, class: StyleAtomID) -> bool;
    /// The attributes with the qualified name `name`, or with the local name `name` in any namespace.
    fn attributes_named(&self, name: StyleAtomID, any_namespace: bool) -> impl Iterator<Item = Self::Attribute> + '_;
}

/// What a selector read of how an element stands among its siblings, or of whether it is empty: what a change to
/// its siblings or children can move the answer of.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub(crate) enum StructuralRead {
    /// The element's previous sibling, across a `+`.
    PreviousSibling,
    /// The element's earlier siblings, across a `~`.
    EarlierSiblings,
    /// Where the element stands among its siblings: counted from the end, among those of its type, and in a way that
    /// tells more than whether it stands first where `beyond_edge`.
    Position {
        from_end: bool,
        of_type: bool,
        beyond_edge: bool,
    },
    /// Whether the element is `:empty`.
    Emptiness,
    /// Where the element stands among its siblings, for a value of its style or of a pseudo-element's.
    SiblingPositionValue,
}

/// The elements a selector is matched against, and their facts.
///
/// Facts are read through a row, which a subject fetches once per element and the evaluator then
/// asks every test of. Names are process atoms. A subject answers what its
/// storage holds, and nothing else: which name, case or namespace a test compares is decided here.
pub(crate) trait SelectorSubject {
    type Node: Copy + Eq;
    type Tree: SelectorTree<Node = Self::Node>;
    type Row: Copy;
    type Attribute: Copy;
    type Features<'s>: ElementFeatures<Attribute = Self::Attribute>
    where
        Self: 's;
    type Incomplete: Copy;
    fn tree(&self) -> Self::Tree;

    fn row(&mut self, node: Self::Node) -> Result<Self::Row, Self::Incomplete>;
    /// Have the features of `row` answer for its attributes, which a test asks before it reads them.
    fn read_attributes(&mut self, _row: Self::Row) {}
    fn features(&self, row: Self::Row) -> Self::Features<'_>;
    /// Whether two elements have the same local name and namespace.
    fn same_type(&self, row: Self::Row, other: Self::Row) -> bool;
    /// An attribute's value as an atom, or `NONE` where the subject interned none.
    fn attribute_value_atom(&self, attribute: Self::Attribute) -> StyleAtomID;
    fn attribute_value_text(&self, attribute: Self::Attribute) -> Option<TokenizerInput<'_>>;
    fn has_state(&self, row: Self::Row, fact: StateFact) -> bool;
    /// The element's resolved language tag, empty when it has none.
    fn language_tag(&self, row: Self::Row) -> TokenizerInput<'_>;
    fn directionality_is(&self, row: Self::Row, direction: StyleAtomID) -> bool;
    fn has_custom_state(&self, row: Self::Row, state: StyleAtomID) -> bool;
    /// The element's heading level, or zero when it is not a heading.
    fn heading_level(&self, row: Self::Row) -> u8;
    /// Whether no child of the element keeps it from being `:empty`.
    fn is_empty(&mut self, node: Self::Node) -> Result<bool, Self::Incomplete>;
    /// Whether the element is the root of its document.
    fn is_root(&self, node: Self::Node) -> bool;

    /// Whether the element is the one named by identity.
    fn is_node(&self, _node: Self::Node, _named: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        false
    }

    /// Whether the element carries the part name `part` in its own tree.
    fn has_part(&self, _row: Self::Row, _part: StyleAtomID) -> bool {
        false
    }

    /// The distinct hosts a `::part()` rule can address the element from, nearest first.
    fn part_exposure_hosts(&self, _node: Self::Node) -> SmallVec<[Self::Node; 1]> {
        SmallVec::new()
    }

    /// When a part is evaluated through the tree scope it is exposed to, the hosts through which the
    /// element is exposed there.
    fn part_hosts_in_exposure_scope(&self, _node: Self::Node) -> Option<SmallVec<[Self::Node; 1]>> {
        None
    }

    /// Whether the element is exposed to `host` under the part name.
    fn exposes_part_to(
        &mut self,
        _node: Self::Node,
        _part: StyleAtomID,
        _host: Self::Node,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Incomplete> {
        Ok(false)
    }

    // Accelerations. Each default is what the evaluation does without one.

    /// Whether [`Self::may_match_required`] rejects elements, so that a walk up has the bits a compound requires
    /// worked out at all.
    const FILTERS_BY_REQUIRED_DISPATCH_BLOOM: bool = false;

    /// Whether `node` can possibly carry every dispatch key whose bloom bits `required` holds.
    fn may_match_required(&self, _required: u64, _node: Self::Node) -> bool {
        true
    }

    /// The element's 1-based index in the sequence a positional test with no `of S` counts.
    fn sibling_index(&mut self, _position: NthPosition, _node: Self::Node) -> Result<Option<i64>, Self::Incomplete> {
        Ok(None)
    }

    /// A remembered answer of whether an element relative to `anchor` matches the selector list `list`, the
    /// argument of a `:has()`, evaluated under `bindings`.
    fn relative_answer_of(
        &mut self,
        _list: SelectorListKey,
        _anchor: Self::Node,
        _bindings: &SelectorBindings<Self::Node>,
    ) -> Option<bool> {
        None
    }

    /// Whether the subject remembers what a walk up across a descendant combinator found.
    const REMEMBERS_ANCESTOR_ANSWERS: bool = false;

    /// Whether the subject remembers what a walk back across a subsequent-sibling combinator found.
    const REMEMBERS_SIBLING_ANSWERS: bool = false;

    /// What a walk remembers its answers in, found once per walk.
    type WalkAnswers: Copy;

    /// Where what walks from the compound `selector` names, under `bindings`, found is remembered, for a subject that
    /// remembers it.
    fn walk_answers(
        &mut self,
        _selector: SelectorKey,
        _bindings: &SelectorBindings<Self::Node>,
    ) -> Option<Self::WalkAnswers> {
        None
    }

    /// Whether `node`, or an element a walk goes on to from it, matches what `answers` are of, as a walk remembered it.
    fn walk_answer(&self, _answers: Self::WalkAnswers, _node: Self::Node) -> Option<bool> {
        None
    }

    /// Record in `answers` that each of `nodes`, or an element a walk goes on to from it, does or does not match.
    fn record_walk_answers(&mut self, _answers: Self::WalkAnswers, _nodes: &[Self::Node], _answer: bool) {}

    /// Note that a selector read `read` of `node`, for a subject that keeps what selectors read of the structure of
    /// its tree, whether or not the selector matched.
    fn note_structural_read(&self, _node: Self::Node, _read: StructuralRead) {}

    /// Whether the subject remembers the indices of elements among the siblings an `of S` list matches, which
    /// [`Self::of_index_of`] answers.
    fn remembers_of_indices(&self) -> bool {
        false
    }

    /// The 1-based index of `node`, which matches the selector list `list`, among its inclusive siblings that match
    /// it, counted from the end when `from_end`, as an earlier count remembered it.
    fn of_index_of(&self, _list: SelectorListKey, _from_end: bool, _node: Self::Node) -> Option<i64> {
        None
    }

    /// Record the index of `node` among its inclusive siblings that match `list`, as [`Self::of_index_of`] answers it.
    fn record_of_index(&mut self, _list: SelectorListKey, _from_end: bool, _node: Self::Node, _index: i64) {}

    /// Record the completed answer of a `:has()` argument list for `anchor`, evaluated under `bindings`.
    fn record_relative_answer_of(
        &mut self,
        _list: SelectorListKey,
        _anchor: Self::Node,
        _bindings: &SelectorBindings<Self::Node>,
        _answer: bool,
    ) {
    }
}

/// What a selector's context names while it is evaluated.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct SelectorBindings<N> {
    /// The shadow root of the tree whose selectors are evaluated, when it is one. `:host` names the
    /// host of the tree its selector is in, so a selector from a document names no host at all.
    pub(crate) scope_shadow_root: Option<N>,
    /// The scoping root `:scope` names: the root of the scope a `<scope-end>` is checked against, or
    /// the element a query is scoped to.
    pub(crate) scope_root_instance: Option<N>,
    /// Whether evaluation is inside the argument of `:host()`. A nested `:host` does not describe a
    /// feature of the host and must not match there.
    pub(crate) matching_host_argument: bool,
    /// The anchor of the relational query being evaluated. Bound only while the witness walk runs,
    /// so that a nested `:has()` names its own anchor.
    pub(crate) relative_anchor: Option<N>,
    /// The scoping root of the innermost `@scope` level the last entry asked for matched in.
    pub(crate) matched_scope_root: Option<N>,
    /// Whether evaluation is inside the argument of a `:has()`.
    pub(crate) matching_relative_argument: bool,
}

pub(crate) use crate::css::selector_arena::SelectorKey;

pub(crate) type SelectorListKey = (
    crate::css::selector_arena::SelectorArenaSerial,
    crate::css::selector_arena::ListStart,
);

impl<N> Default for SelectorBindings<N> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            scope_shadow_root: None,
            scope_root_instance: None,
            matching_host_argument: false,
            relative_anchor: None,
            matched_scope_root: None,
            matching_relative_argument: false,
        }
    }
}

/// Matches selectors against one subject.
pub(crate) struct SelectorEvaluator<S: SelectorSubject> {
    pub(crate) subject: S,
    pub(crate) bindings: SelectorBindings<S::Node>,
}

//! What a match keeps as it runs: where elements stand among their siblings, the answers of the
//! tests that read them, and what walks back across `~` found, with the attribute value tests.

use super::column::PagedColumn;
use super::column::PagedColumnPage;
use super::fast_hash::FastMap as HashMap;
use super::index::StyleAtomID;
use smallvec::SmallVec;
use std::hash::Hash;

use super::selector_evaluation::SelectorEvaluator;
use super::selector_evaluation::SelectorSubject;
use super::tree::StyleNodeID;
pub use crate::css::selector::Specificity;

/// An `an+b` positional test, optionally restricted to siblings sharing a type.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct NthPosition {
    pub step: i32,
    pub offset: i32,
    /// `:nth-last-child()` and `:nth-last-of-type()` count from the end.
    pub from_end: bool,
    /// `:nth-of-type()` family: only siblings sharing the subject's type contribute.
    pub of_type: bool,
}

/// The single axis a simple relative selector traverses from its anchor.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum RelativeAxis {
    /// `:has(.error)`
    Descendant,
    /// `:has(> .item)`
    Child,
    /// `:has(+ .selected)`
    NextSibling,
    /// `:has(~ .selected)`
    FollowingSibling,
    /// `:has(+ .row .cell)`: the witness is somewhere under the anchor's next sibling.
    NextSiblingSubtree,
    /// `:has(~ .row .cell)`: the witness is somewhere under one of the following siblings.
    FollowingSiblingSubtree,
}

/// Why a match evaluation could not produce an exact answer.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Incomplete {
    /// The fact batch does not cover a style node the evaluation had to read. This is never a
    /// negative answer: the caller widens the batch or asks a different question.
    MissingFacts(StyleNodeID),
}

/// Which positional tests an evaluator answers from its workspace's shared sibling index.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum PositionalIndexPolicy {
    /// Every test, and every answer is memoized. A traversal that styles whole sequences asks
    /// many programs about the same children, which amortizes building each index.
    All,
    /// Only tests with a step, which have to count the whole sequence anyway, and no memo. A
    /// bounded test such as `:first-child` stops at its near end, so a narrow exact ask over
    /// scattered candidates answers it more cheaply than materializing every sequence it walks
    /// through - and asks the same test about the same node too rarely for a memo to pay for
    /// its insertion.
    SteppedOnly,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub(super) struct SiblingPositions {
    pub(super) from_start: u32,
    pub(super) from_end: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct SiblingSequenceMembership {
    sequence: u32,
    ordinal: u32,
}

const VALUE_PAGE_SHIFT: usize = 6;
const VALUE_PAGE_SIZE: usize = 1 << VALUE_PAGE_SHIFT;

#[derive(Clone)]
struct ValuePage<T: Copy + Default> {
    known: u64,
    values: [T; VALUE_PAGE_SIZE],
}

impl<T: Copy + Default> Default for ValuePage<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            known: 0,
            values: [T::default(); VALUE_PAGE_SIZE],
        }
    }
}

impl<T: Copy + Default> PagedColumnPage for ValuePage<T> {
    type Value = T;

    const SHIFT: usize = VALUE_PAGE_SHIFT;

    fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<T> {
        (self.known & (1 << index) != 0).then_some(self.values[index])
    }

    fn insert(&mut self, index: usize, value: T) {
        self.known |= 1 << index;
        self.values[index] = value;
    }
}

type SiblingPositionColumn = PagedColumn<ValuePage<SiblingPositions>>;
type SiblingSequenceMembershipColumn = PagedColumn<ValuePage<SiblingSequenceMembership>>;

#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(super) struct SiblingSequenceGeometry {
    sequences: Vec<Box<[StyleNodeID]>>,
    memberships: SiblingSequenceMembershipColumn,
}

impl SiblingSequenceGeometry {
    fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        crate::heap_size::vec_bytes(&self.sequences)
            + self
                .sequences
                .iter()
                .map(|sequence| size_of_val(&**sequence))
                .sum::<usize>()
            + self.memberships.heap_size()
    }

    fn insert_sequence(&mut self, children: Vec<StyleNodeID>) {
        u32::try_from(children.len()).expect("sibling sequence space exhausted");
        let sequence = u32::try_from(self.sequences.len()).expect("sibling sequence index space exhausted");
        for (ordinal, &child) in children.iter().enumerate() {
            self.memberships.insert(
                child
                    .element_index()
                    .expect("only elements belong to sibling sequences") as usize,
                SiblingSequenceMembership {
                    sequence,
                    ordinal: u32::try_from(ordinal).expect("sibling sequence space exhausted"),
                },
            );
        }
        self.sequences.push(children.into_boxed_slice());
    }

    fn sequence_and_ordinal(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> Option<(&[StyleNodeID], u32)> {
        let membership = self.memberships.get(node.element_index()? as usize)?;
        Some((&*self.sequences[membership.sequence as usize], membership.ordinal))
    }

    fn sibling_sequence(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> Option<&[StyleNodeID]> {
        self.sequence_and_ordinal(node).map(|(sequence, _)| sequence)
    }

    pub(super) fn sibling_positions(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> Option<SiblingPositions> {
        let (sequence, ordinal) = self.sequence_and_ordinal(node)?;
        let count = u32::try_from(sequence.len()).expect("sibling sequence space exhausted");
        Some(SiblingPositions {
            from_start: ordinal + 1,
            from_end: count - ordinal,
        })
    }
}

/// Caller-owned scratch lent exclusively to one evaluator at a time, which reads one tree: the
/// positions and answers it keeps are of that tree.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct MatchScratch {
    sibling_geometry: SiblingSequenceGeometry,
    type_positions: SiblingPositionColumn,
    /// The answers of relative queries, by the anchor each was asked for.
    relative_answers: HashMap<RelativeAnswerKey, bool>,
    /// How many of those answers took a walk: each one here did, as an evaluation that finds one takes no walk.
    relative_walks: u64,
    /// The number of the table of what walks back across a subsequent-sibling combinator found, by
    /// what the walks start from.
    sibling_tables: HashMap<SiblingAnswerKey, u32>,
    /// The pages of each table, by the page of the element slots they hold, or `NO_SIBLING_PAGE`:
    /// a table holds pages for the elements its walks passed alone, which a pass styling a few
    /// elements of a large document keeps small.
    sibling_answers: Vec<Vec<u32>>,
    /// What the tables' walks found for each sibling they passed, by its element slot in its
    /// table's page: none yet, false or true.
    sibling_answer_pages: Vec<[u8; SIBLING_ANSWER_PAGE]>,
}

/// How many element slots a page of a sibling answer table holds.
const SIBLING_ANSWER_PAGE: usize = 128;
const NO_SIBLING_PAGE: u32 = u32::MAX;

/// The table of what walks back across one `~` found, among a workspace's.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub(super) struct SiblingAnswerTable(u32);

/// What a walk back across `~` found depends on besides the facts of the tree: the compound left of
/// the `~`, and the bindings and part exposure it was evaluated under.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub(super) struct SiblingAnswerKey {
    pub(super) selector: super::selector_evaluation::SelectorKey,
    pub(super) scope_shadow_root: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    pub(super) scope_root_instance: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    pub(super) part_exposure_scope: Option<super::tree::TreeScopeID>,
}

/// What a `:has()` argument list's answer for one anchor depends on besides the facts of the tree:
/// the list, and the bindings it was evaluated under, but for the anchor of an enclosing query,
/// which the query binds to its own.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub(super) struct RelativeAnswerKey {
    list: super::selector_evaluation::SelectorListKey,
    anchor: StyleNodeID,
    scope_shadow_root: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    scope_root_instance: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    matching_host_argument: bool,
}

impl RelativeAnswerKey {
    /// The key of the `:has()` argument list `list`, asked for `anchor` under `bindings`.
    pub(super) fn of_list(
        list: super::selector_evaluation::SelectorListKey,
        anchor: StyleNodeID,
        bindings: &super::selector_evaluation::SelectorBindings<StyleNodeID>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            list,
            anchor,
            scope_shadow_root: bindings.scope_shadow_root,
            scope_root_instance: bindings.scope_root_instance,
            matching_host_argument: bindings.matching_host_argument,
        }
    }
}

/// Where a subject's sibling sequences come from, for [`MatchScratch::indexed_sibling_position`]:
/// the parent of the element asked about and the children of a parent in the tree it reads, and
/// the type of a sibling as its facts tell it.
pub(super) struct SiblingSequenceSource<Children, TypeOf> {
    pub(super) parent: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    pub(super) children: Children,
    pub(super) type_of: TypeOf,
}

impl MatchScratch {
    /// The bytes the scratch keeps on the heap: the sibling sequences, positions and answers it
    /// measured.
    pub(super) fn heap_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.sibling_geometry.heap_size()
            + self.type_positions.heap_size()
            + crate::heap_size::map_bytes(&self.relative_answers)
            + crate::heap_size::map_bytes(&self.sibling_tables)
            + crate::heap_size::vec_bytes(&self.sibling_answers)
            + self
                .sibling_answers
                .iter()
                .map(crate::heap_size::vec_bytes)
                .sum::<usize>()
            + crate::heap_size::vec_bytes(&self.sibling_answer_pages)
    }

    /// Return a sibling position from this scratch, building that sequence on its first ask.
    ///
    /// A broad matching batch asks many positional selectors about the same children. Counting from
    /// an end for every `(selector, child)` pair is quadratic in the sequence length and repeated
    /// across rules.
    pub(super) fn indexed_sibling_position<Children, TypeOf>(
        &mut self,
        position: NthPosition,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        source: SiblingSequenceSource<Children, TypeOf>,
    ) -> Result<Option<i64>, Incomplete>
    where
        Children: FnOnce(StyleNodeID) -> Vec<StyleNodeID>,
        TypeOf: FnMut(StyleNodeID) -> Result<(StyleAtomID, StyleAtomID), Incomplete>,
    {
        let SiblingSequenceSource {
            parent,
            children,
            mut type_of,
        } = source;
        let answer = |cached: SiblingPositions| {
            Ok(Some(i64::from(match position.from_end {
                true => cached.from_end,
                false => cached.from_start,
            })))
        };
        if let Some(cached) = self.sibling_position(node, position.of_type) {
            return answer(cached);
        }

        let Some(parent) = parent else {
            if position.of_type {
                type_of(node)?;
            }
            return Ok(Some(1));
        };
        if self.sibling_geometry.sibling_sequence(node).is_none() {
            self.sibling_geometry.insert_sequence(children(parent));
        }
        let siblings = self.sibling_geometry.sibling_sequence(node).unwrap();
        if siblings.is_empty() {
            return Ok(None);
        }

        if position.of_type {
            let mut type_ids = HashMap::default();
            let mut sibling_types = Vec::with_capacity(siblings.len());
            let mut type_positions: SmallVec<[SiblingPositions; 1]> = SmallVec::new();
            for &sibling in siblings {
                let sibling_type = type_of(sibling)?;
                let next_type_id = u32::try_from(type_positions.len()).expect("sibling type space exhausted");
                let type_id = *type_ids.entry(sibling_type).or_insert_with(|| {
                    type_positions.push(SiblingPositions {
                        from_start: 0,
                        from_end: 0,
                    });
                    next_type_id
                });
                sibling_types.push(type_id);
                type_positions[type_id as usize].from_end += 1;
            }
            let siblings = self.sibling_geometry.sibling_sequence(node).unwrap();
            let positions = &mut self.type_positions;
            for (&sibling, type_id) in siblings.iter().zip(sibling_types) {
                let position = &mut type_positions[type_id as usize];
                position.from_start += 1;
                positions.insert(
                    sibling.element_index().expect("only elements have sibling positions") as usize,
                    *position,
                );
                position.from_end -= 1;
            }
        }

        match self.sibling_position(node, position.of_type) {
            Some(cached) => answer(cached),
            None => Ok(None),
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn sibling_position(&self, node: StyleNodeID, of_type: bool) -> Option<SiblingPositions> {
        match of_type {
            true => self.type_positions.get(node.element_index()? as usize),
            false => self.sibling_geometry.sibling_positions(node),
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn relative_walks(&self) -> u64 {
        self.relative_walks
    }

    pub(super) fn relative_answer(&self, key: &RelativeAnswerKey) -> Option<bool> {
        self.relative_answers.get(key).copied()
    }

    pub(super) fn insert_relative_answer(&mut self, key: RelativeAnswerKey, answer: bool) {
        self.relative_walks += 1;
        self.relative_answers.insert(key, answer);
    }

    /// The table of the walks `key` says.
    pub(super) fn sibling_table(&mut self, key: SiblingAnswerKey) -> SiblingAnswerTable {
        let next = u32::try_from(self.sibling_answers.len()).expect("sibling answer tables exhausted");
        let table = *self.sibling_tables.entry(key).or_insert(next);
        if table == next {
            self.sibling_answers.push(Vec::new());
        }
        SiblingAnswerTable(table)
    }

    pub(super) fn sibling_answer(&self, table: SiblingAnswerTable, node: StyleNodeID) -> Option<bool> {
        let slot = node.element_slot();
        let page = *self.sibling_answers[table.0 as usize].get(slot / SIBLING_ANSWER_PAGE)?;
        if page == NO_SIBLING_PAGE {
            return None;
        }
        match self.sibling_answer_pages[page as usize][slot % SIBLING_ANSWER_PAGE] {
            1 => Some(false),
            2 => Some(true),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn insert_sibling_answer(&mut self, table: SiblingAnswerTable, node: StyleNodeID, answer: bool) {
        let slot = node.element_slot();
        let pages = &mut self.sibling_answers[table.0 as usize];
        if pages.len() <= slot / SIBLING_ANSWER_PAGE {
            pages.resize(slot / SIBLING_ANSWER_PAGE + 1, NO_SIBLING_PAGE);
        }
        let page = &mut pages[slot / SIBLING_ANSWER_PAGE];
        if *page == NO_SIBLING_PAGE {
            *page = u32::try_from(self.sibling_answer_pages.len()).expect("sibling answer pages exhausted");
            self.sibling_answer_pages.push([0; SIBLING_ANSWER_PAGE]);
        }
        self.sibling_answer_pages[*page as usize][slot % SIBLING_ANSWER_PAGE] = 1 + u8::from(answer);
    }
}

/// What matching the entries of the rule index asks of an evaluator, against whichever elements it
/// is matched against.
impl<S> SelectorEvaluator<S>
where
    S: SelectorSubject<Node = StyleNodeID, Incomplete = Incomplete>,
{
    /// Evaluate the rules attached to the shadow tree of `shadow_root` from here on, or the
    /// document's for none.
    pub(super) fn set_scope_shadow_root(&mut self, shadow_root: Option<StyleNodeID>) {
        self.bindings.scope_shadow_root = shadow_root;
    }
}

/// `index` is a 1-based position; the test is whether it equals `step * n + offset` for some
/// non-negative integer `n`.
pub(super) fn matches_an_plus_b(step: i32, offset: i32, index: i64) -> bool {
    let step = i64::from(step);
    let offset = i64::from(offset);
    if step == 0 {
        return index == offset;
    }
    let difference = index - offset;
    difference % step == 0 && difference / step >= 0
}

fn fold(unit: u16) -> u16 {
    if (u16::from(b'A')..=u16::from(b'Z')).contains(&unit) {
        return unit + u16::from(b'a' - b'A');
    }
    unit
}

pub(crate) fn attribute_value_matches<T: Copy + Into<u16>>(
    operator: crate::css::selector::AttributeMatchType,
    value: &[T],
    literal: &[u16],
    insensitive: bool,
) -> bool {
    use crate::css::selector::AttributeMatchType;
    match operator {
        AttributeMatchType::HasAttribute => true,
        AttributeMatchType::ExactValue => equals(value, literal, insensitive),
        AttributeMatchType::ContainsWord => {
            !literal.is_empty()
                && value
                    .split(|unit| matches!((*unit).into(), 0x20 | 0x09 | 0x0A | 0x0C | 0x0D))
                    .any(|token| equals(token, literal, insensitive))
        }
        AttributeMatchType::StartsWithSegment => {
            equals(value, literal, insensitive)
                || (value.len() > literal.len()
                    && value[literal.len()].into() == u16::from(b'-')
                    && starts_with(value, literal, insensitive))
        }
        AttributeMatchType::StartsWithString => !literal.is_empty() && starts_with(value, literal, insensitive),
        AttributeMatchType::EndsWithString => {
            !literal.is_empty()
                && value.len() >= literal.len()
                && equals(&value[value.len() - literal.len()..], literal, insensitive)
        }
        AttributeMatchType::ContainsString => {
            !literal.is_empty()
                && value.len() >= literal.len()
                && (0..=value.len() - literal.len())
                    .any(|start| equals(&value[start..start + literal.len()], literal, insensitive))
        }
    }
}

fn equals<T: Copy + Into<u16>>(value: &[T], literal: &[u16], insensitive: bool) -> bool {
    if !insensitive {
        return value.len() == literal.len() && value.iter().zip(literal).all(|(&left, &right)| left.into() == right);
    }
    value.len() == literal.len()
        && value
            .iter()
            .zip(literal)
            .all(|(&left, &right)| fold(left.into()) == fold(right))
}

fn starts_with<T: Copy + Into<u16>>(value: &[T], literal: &[u16], insensitive: bool) -> bool {
    value.len() >= literal.len() && equals(&value[..literal.len()], literal, insensitive)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn an_plus_b_handles_the_boundary_forms() {
        assert!(matches_an_plus_b(0, 1, 1));
        assert!(!matches_an_plus_b(0, 1, 2));
        assert!(matches_an_plus_b(2, 0, 2));
        assert!(!matches_an_plus_b(2, 0, 3));
        assert!(matches_an_plus_b(2, 1, 1));
        assert!(matches_an_plus_b(-1, 3, 3));
        assert!(matches_an_plus_b(-1, 3, 1));
        assert!(!matches_an_plus_b(-1, 3, 4));
        assert!(matches_an_plus_b(1, 0, 5));
    }
}

//! Recording the elements whose style a size query container's new box moves.

use super::bridge::FfiContainerEffectKind;
use super::container_queries::ContainerVerdict;
use super::fast_hash::{FastMap as HashMap, FastSet as HashSet};
use super::pipeline::Record;
use super::{RetainedState, StyleEngine, StyleNodeID};
use std::collections::hash_map::Entry;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// What the host learned about size container queries while it computed styles: which elements
/// were asked about, which elements asked, and which containers had no box to answer with yet.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(super) struct SizeContainerQueryFacts {
    /// Elements some size query or container-relative unit resolved against. `container-type` is
    /// set far more widely than it is asked about, so a container outside this set has no
    /// dependent below it to find.
    queried_containers: HashSet<StyleNodeID>,
    /// Elements whose style some size query or container-relative unit decided.
    dependents: HashSet<StyleNodeID>,
    /// Containers a style computation asked about before they had a committed box. The layout
    /// that gives them one is where their dependents move.
    needing_evaluation_after_layout: HashSet<StyleNodeID>,
    /// Containers asked about without a box that a full layout left without one, as one under an element that is not
    /// rendered stays. Their dependents read nothing new until a commit gives them a box.
    awaiting_box: HashSet<StyleNodeID>,
    /// Queried containers whose font moved since their dependents were last recorded, each with the record it held
    /// before the move. An animated container passes through its base record within every update, on its way to the
    /// record with its animated values, so only a font that differs from the one before it counts.
    font_moves: HashMap<StyleNodeID, Arc<Record>>,
    /// A container's eligibility changed, so units can newly select it even when it was not queried before.
    availability_changed: HashSet<StyleNodeID>,
    /// The size containers whose records say they answer size queries, as the records they were last published
    /// with say.
    available: HashSet<StyleNodeID>,
    /// Elements the dependent walks have visited, for the style invalidation counters.
    scan_visits: u64,
}

impl SizeContainerQueryFacts {
    pub(super) fn is_queried_container(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        self.queried_containers.contains(&node)
    }

    /// Whether a layout left `node` without the box a style computation asked it about.
    pub(super) fn is_awaiting_box(&self, node: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        self.awaiting_box.contains(&node)
    }

    /// Font-relative size queries can change even when the container's box keeps the same dimensions.
    pub(super) fn note_held_record_change(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID, previous: Arc<Record>, current: &Record) {
        if !self.is_queried_container(node) {
            return;
        }
        match self.font_moves.entry(node) {
            Entry::Occupied(entry) => {
                if same_font(entry.get(), current) {
                    entry.remove();
                }
            }
            Entry::Vacant(entry) => {
                if !same_font(&previous, current) {
                    entry.insert(previous);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Follows whether `node` answers size queries, noting where that changed.
    pub(super) fn set_availability(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID, available: bool) {
        if self.available.contains(&node) != available {
            set_contains(&mut self.available, node, available);
            self.availability_changed.insert(node);
        }
    }

    /// Forgets that `node` answers size queries, without noting a change.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(super) fn forget_availability(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID) {
        self.available.remove(&node);
    }

    pub(super) fn retire(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID) {
        self.queried_containers.remove(&node);
        self.dependents.remove(&node);
        self.needing_evaluation_after_layout.remove(&node);
        self.awaiting_box.remove(&node);
        self.font_moves.remove(&node);
        self.availability_changed.remove(&node);
        self.available.remove(&node);
    }
}

fn same_font(first: &Record, second: &Record) -> bool {
    let font_group = crate::css::table_group_builder::group_index::FONT;
    let (first, second) = (
        first.payloads[font_group].as_ptr(),
        second.payloads[font_group].as_ptr(),
    );
    // SAFETY: Both records hold a reference to their font payloads.
    first == second || unsafe { crate::css::computed_values::style_group_payloads_equal(font_group, first, second) }
}

fn set_contains(set: &mut HashSet<StyleNodeID>, node: StyleNodeID, contains: bool) {
    if contains {
        set.insert(node);
    } else {
        set.remove(&node);
    }
}

impl StyleEngine {
    /// The host's two facts about an element: whether a size query or container-relative unit
    /// resolved against it, and whether one decided its style.
    pub fn set_element_size_container_query_facts(
        &mut self,
        node: StyleNodeID,
        is_queried_container: bool,
        depends_on_size_container_query: bool,
    ) {
        let facts = &mut self.retained.size_container_queries;
        set_contains(&mut facts.queried_containers, node, is_queried_container);
        set_contains(&mut facts.dependents, node, depends_on_size_container_query);
    }

    pub fn note_size_container_needs_evaluation_after_layout(&mut self, node: StyleNodeID) {
        self.retained
            .size_container_queries
            .needing_evaluation_after_layout
            .insert(node);
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn has_size_containers_needing_evaluation_after_layout(&self) -> bool {
        !self
            .retained
            .size_container_queries
            .needing_evaluation_after_layout
            .is_empty()
            || !self.retained.size_container_queries.font_moves.is_empty()
            || !self.retained.size_container_queries.availability_changed.is_empty()
    }

    /// What the record the host installs for `node` read of its containers. A container the record
    /// found without a box may have been handed the box it holds since, as an earlier record of
    /// the same installation made it a size container (see
    /// `LayoutNodeArena::publish_new_size_container_geometry`). The element is computed again
    /// against that box before the update settles, as every later computation of it reads it.
    pub(crate) fn take_container_effects_for_install(
        &mut self,
        node: StyleNodeID,
    ) -> Option<std::sync::Arc<ContainerVerdict>> {
        let verdict = self.retained.take_container_effects_for_host(node)?;
        let read_a_box_given_since = verdict.effects.iter().any(|&(container, kind)| {
            matches!(
                kind,
                FfiContainerEffectKind::NeedsEvaluationAfterLayout
                    | FfiContainerEffectKind::UnitsNeedEvaluationAfterLayout
            ) && self
                .retained
                .layout_style_snapshot(container)
                .is_some_and(|row| row.has_committed_box)
        });
        if read_a_box_given_since {
            self.record_container_query_input(node);
        }
        Some(verdict)
    }

    /// Take the box geometry a completed layout commit gathered, keeping each row's scroll state.
    pub(crate) fn apply_layout_style_snapshot_commit(
        &mut self,
        rows: &[crate::layout::style_snapshot::CommittedGeometry],
    ) {
        let mut resized = self.retained.take_layout_style_snapshot_rows(rows);
        // A container its dependents read without a box answers them once a commit gives it one.
        let awaiting_box = &mut self.retained.size_container_queries.awaiting_box;
        if !awaiting_box.is_empty() {
            let mut recorded: HashSet<StyleNodeID> = resized.iter().copied().collect();
            for geometry in rows {
                if geometry.has_committed_box && awaiting_box.remove(&geometry.node) && recorded.insert(geometry.node) {
                    resized.push(geometry.node);
                }
            }
        }
        for container in resized {
            self.record_size_container_query_dependents(container);
        }
    }

    /// Take the box of an element whose new style makes it a size container, which no commit has gathered a row for.
    /// The container-relative units below it that were computed while it had no box resolved past it, to a container
    /// further out or the viewport, so they are computed again against its box before any layout runs again. Their
    /// records can come out the same as before the element became a container, so nothing else would ask for that.
    pub(crate) fn apply_new_size_container_geometry(&mut self, row: crate::layout::style_snapshot::CommittedGeometry) {
        let container = row.node;
        self.apply_layout_style_snapshot_commit(&[row]);
        self.record_size_container_query_dependents_after_input_change(container, true);
    }

    /// The elements the dependent walks have visited, optionally starting the count again.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn size_query_container_scan_visits(&mut self, reset: bool) -> u64 {
        let visits = &mut self.retained.size_container_queries.scan_visits;
        if reset { std::mem::take(visits) } else { *visits }
    }

    /// A layout gave the containers that had no box when they were asked about one; their
    /// dependents are computed again against it. A container the layout left without a box is
    /// computed against once more, as no longer eligible, and its dependents then wait for the
    /// commit that gives it one; computing them again after every layout would only ask for this
    /// evaluation again.
    pub fn evaluate_size_containers_needing_evaluation_after_layout(&mut self) {
        let mut containers = std::mem::take(&mut self.retained.size_container_queries.needing_evaluation_after_layout);
        containers.retain(|&container| {
            let has_box = self
                .retained
                .layout_style_snapshot(container)
                .is_some_and(|row| row.has_committed_box);
            // The units below a container the layout left without a box started out against no box at all. They are
            // computed again once, now resolving past it, and then wait for a commit that gives it a box.
            has_box || self.retained.size_container_queries.awaiting_box.insert(container)
        });
        let availability_changed = std::mem::take(&mut self.retained.size_container_queries.availability_changed);
        containers.extend(availability_changed.iter().copied());
        containers.extend(std::mem::take(&mut self.retained.size_container_queries.font_moves).into_keys());
        for container in containers {
            // A container that has left the document has no dependents left to move.
            if self.retained.projection.is_live(container) {
                self.record_size_container_query_dependents_after_input_change(
                    container,
                    availability_changed.contains(&container),
                );
            }
        }
    }

    /// What `container` answers to the queries below it changed: its content box moved along an
    /// axis its container type queries, or its scroll state moved. Every element whose style a
    /// size query or container-relative unit decided below it, and the container itself for its
    /// own pseudo-elements, is recorded to compute again.
    pub fn record_size_container_query_dependents(&mut self, container: StyleNodeID) {
        self.record_size_container_query_dependents_after_input_change(container, false);
    }

    fn record_size_container_query_dependents_after_input_change(
        &mut self,
        container: StyleNodeID,
        availability_changed: bool,
    ) {
        let (changed, visits) = if availability_changed {
            self.retained.size_container_query_dependents_in_subtree(container)
        } else {
            self.retained.size_container_query_dependents(container)
        };
        self.retained.size_container_queries.scan_visits += visits;
        for node in changed {
            self.record_container_query_input(node);
        }
    }
}

impl RetainedState {
    /// The elements whose style a size query or container-relative unit decided below `container`, and the container
    /// itself for its own pseudo-elements, with the number of elements the walk for them visited. None where nothing
    /// resolved against the container.
    pub(super) fn size_container_query_dependents(&self, container: StyleNodeID) -> (Vec<StyleNodeID>, u64) {
        if !self.size_container_queries.queried_containers.contains(&container) {
            return (Vec::new(), 0);
        }
        self.size_container_query_dependents_in_subtree(container)
    }

    fn size_container_query_dependents_in_subtree(&self, container: StyleNodeID) -> (Vec<StyleNodeID>, u64) {
        let facts = &self.size_container_queries;
        if facts.dependents.is_empty() {
            return (Vec::new(), 0);
        }
        let mut changed = Vec::new();
        // The container's own pseudo-elements select it as their query container too, and their
        // styles are computed again with the element's.
        if facts.dependents.contains(&container) {
            changed.push(container);
        }

        // The flat tree below the container is the inverse of the walk that selects a query
        // container, which is what makes it the right one for finding that container's dependents.
        let mut visits = 0;
        let mut stack: Vec<StyleNodeID> = self.projection.flat_tree_children(container).collect();
        while let Some(node) = stack.pop() {
            // A text node holds a place among a slot's assigned nodes, but has no style of its own.
            if node.text_index().is_some() {
                continue;
            }
            visits += 1;
            if facts.dependents.contains(&node) {
                changed.push(node);
            }
            stack.extend(self.projection.flat_tree_children(node));
        }
        (changed, visits)
    }
}

//! The entries elements' own declarations take.

use crate::css::declaration_block;
use crate::css::declaration_block::DeclarationEntry;
use crate::css::style_value::RetainedStyleValueData;
use crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData;

/// The entries of the longhands `declarations` declare, each with the value an element declaring
/// it is written with, a shorthand's longhands taking its value.
pub(crate) fn element_declared_properties<'a>(
    declarations: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = declaration_block::DeclarationRef<'a>>,
) -> Vec<(DeclarationEntry, RetainedStyleValueData)> {
    fn append(
        property: u16,
        declaration: declaration_block::DeclarationRef<'_>,
        declarations: &mut Vec<(DeclarationEntry, RetainedStyleValueData)>,
    ) {
        use crate::css::property_metadata::{longhands_for_shorthand, property_is_shorthand};
        // Element declarations decide longhands. Presentation attributes can name shorthands
        // whose children are themselves shorthands, so expand the complete property inventory.
        // The longhands of a shorthand awaiting substitution have declarations of their own, which
        // a later change to the block may have replaced or removed.
        if property_is_shorthand(property)
            && !matches!(
                &**declaration.value,
                StyleValueData::Unresolved { .. } | StyleValueData::PendingSubstitution { .. }
            )
        {
            for &longhand in longhands_for_shorthand(property) {
                append(longhand, declaration, declarations);
            }
        } else {
            declarations.push((
                DeclarationEntry::new(property, declaration.important, declaration.operator),
                RetainedStyleValueData::from_arc(declaration.value.clone()),
            ));
        }
    }
    let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(declarations.len());
    for declaration in declarations {
        append(declaration.property_id, declaration, &mut entries);
    }
    entries
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::css::declaration_block::DeclarationBlockBuilder;
    use crate::css::declaration_block::DeclaredProperty;
    use crate::css::property_metadata::property_id;
    use crate::css::style_value::shared_style_value;

    #[test]
    fn a_shorthand_hint_declares_each_longhand_with_one_value() {
        let mut hints = DeclarationBlockBuilder::default();
        hints.append_in_specified_order(DeclaredProperty {
            property_id: property_id::BORDER,
            important: false,
            value: shared_style_value(StyleValueData::Keyword {
                keyword: crate::css::style_compute::keyword::INHERIT,
            }),
        });
        let declared = element_declared_properties(hints.properties.iter().map(DeclaredProperty::borrowed));
        // The longhands comprise four widths, four styles, four colors, and five border-image properties.
        assert_eq!(declared.len(), 17);
        assert!(
            declared
                .iter()
                .all(|(_, written)| written.pointer() == declared[0].1.pointer())
        );
    }
}

use super::bridge::{ElementBoxKind, FfiAnimationInvalidation, FfiStyleInvalidationField, element_adjustment_fact};
use super::computed::{StyleRecordView, ViewLonghands};

    self, FIRST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID, LAST_LONGHAND_PROPERTY_ID, NUMBER_OF_LONGHAND_PROPERTIES, property_id,
