        // The margin after the block counts toward the block size of its block container only where the block ends it,
        // where a quirks-mode body or table cell leaves out the quirky margins.
        let block_end_margin = self
            .margin_state()
            .collapsed_margin_at_block_end_of(&self.facts(containing_block.node));
        line_builder.append_block_level_box(
            node,
            line_index,
            block_bottom,
            block_end_margin,
            line_box::BlockLevelBoxOnLine {
                content_offset: outcome.content_offset,
                cells: outcome.cells,
                baselines: formatting_context::baselines_of_block_level_box_on_line(
                    &self.run.pass,
                    node,
                    &outcome.cells,
                    outcome.content_baselines,
                    outcome.content_offset.y,
                ),
            },
        );
        outcome.collapses_through
    }

    /// Resolves the block size of a float that has no run of its own, sized at the inline size its block formatting
    /// context gave it, where that follows without laying out its contents.
    pub(crate) fn resolve_float_root_block_size_in_parent(&self, sized_float: ChildSizedHere<'_>, input: &LayoutInput) {
        let node = sized_float.node;
        let available_space = input.available_space;
        self.resolve_used_block_size_if_not_treated_as_auto(
            sized_float,
            available_space,
            input.containing_block_constraints,
        );
        let block_size_is_definite_from_aspect_ratio = self.metrics_of(sized_float).has_definite_inline_size()
            && self.facts(node).has_preferred_aspect_ratio()
            && self.sizing().box_is_sized_as_replaced_element(
                sizing_context::SizedBox::new(node, &self.metrics_of(sized_float)),
                available_space,
                input.containing_block_constraints,
            );
        if self.facts(node).has_auto_content_box_size()
            || block_size_is_definite_from_aspect_ratio
            || self.style(node).display().is_flex_inside()
        {
            self.resolve_used_block_size_if_treated_as_auto(
                sized_float,
                available_space,
                input.containing_block_constraints,
                None,
                None,
            );
        }
    }

    /// Resolves the vertical box model and the inline size of a float, which depends on the floats placed beside the
    /// content box of its containing block, at `containing_block_position_in_root`, before.
    pub(crate) fn dimension_float_root_inline_size(
        &self,
        sized_float: ChildSizedHere<'_>,
        block_container: BlockContainer,
        input: &LayoutInput,
        containing_block_position_in_root: FfiCssPixelPoint,
    ) {
        let available_space = input.available_space;
        let block_container_inline_size = block_container.cells.content_inline_size;
        self.resolve_vertical_box_model_metrics(
            sized_float,
            block_container_inline_size,
            input.containing_block_constraints,
        );
        let containing_block_rect = self.containing_block_rect(block_container, containing_block_position_in_root);
        let containing_block_rect_now = containing_block_rect.translated(
            CssPixels::default(),
            self.block_offset_adjustment_from_pending_ancestor_block_start_margins(block_container.node),
        );
        self.compute_inline_size(
            sized_float,
            available_space,
            input.containing_block_constraints,
            FfiCssPixelPoint {
                x: containing_block_rect_now.x,
                y: containing_block_rect_now.y,
            },
        );
    }

    /// Lays out and places `node`, a float, and returns what its insets resolved to, which is nothing for a float it
    /// leaves unplaced, the box a run of its own handed back where one laid it out, and the offset of its content box
    /// in its containing block where it placed the float.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn layout_floating_box(
        &self,
        run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>,
        sized_float: ChildSizedHere<'_>,
        block_container: BlockContainer,
        input: LayoutInput,
        containing_block_position_in_root: FfiCssPixelPoint,
        block_offset: CssPixels,
        line_builder: Option<&mut line_builder::LineBuilder<'_, '_>>,
        fragment_facts: run_state::FragmentFactsDecidedByParent,
    ) -> (
        abspos_engine::InFlowBoxInsets,
        Option<LaidOutBox>,
        Option<FfiCssPixelPoint>,
    ) {
        let laid_out_float = self.lay_out_float_ahead_of_its_position(
            run,
            sized_float,
            block_container,
            input.clone(),
            containing_block_position_in_root,
        );
        self.position_laid_out_float(
            run,
            laid_out_float,
            block_container,
            input,
            containing_block_position_in_root,
            block_offset,
            line_builder,
            fragment_facts,
        )
    }

    /// Sizes a float in the cells of `sized_float`, and returns the input of its run.
    fn size_float_for_its_run(
        &self,
        sized_float: ChildSizedHere<'_>,
        block_container: BlockContainer,
        input: &LayoutInput,
        containing_block_position_in_root: FfiCssPixelPoint,
    ) -> LayoutInput {
        let node = sized_float.node;
        let available_space = input.available_space;
        assert!(self.facts(node).is_floating());
        // NB: This is found ahead of the float's inline size, which can make its block size transfer through its aspect
        //     ratio.
        let flex_container_resolves_its_own_automatic_block_size =
            formatting_context::flex_self_block_size_resolution_space(
                &self.sizing(),
                sizing_context::SizedBox::new(node, &self.metrics_of(sized_float)),
                available_space,
                input.containing_block_constraints,
            )
            .is_some();
        let float_input = LayoutInput {
            available_space,
            containing_block_constraints: input.containing_block_constraints,
            sizing: RootSizingDirectives::default(),
            participation: ParticipationInParentFormattingContext::Float {
                flex_container_resolves_its_own_automatic_block_size,
            },
        };
        self.dimension_float_root_inline_size(
            sized_float,
            block_container,
            &float_input,
            containing_block_position_in_root,
        );
        float_input
    }

    /// Lays out the contents of a float, which does not depend on where the float goes.
    pub(crate) fn lay_out_float_ahead_of_its_position(
        &self,
        run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>,
        sized_float: ChildSizedHere<'_>,
        block_container: BlockContainer,
        mut input: LayoutInput,
        containing_block_position_in_root: FfiCssPixelPoint,
    ) -> FloatLaidOutAheadOfItsPosition {
        let node = sized_float.node;
        self.adjust_table_cell_child_input(node, &block_container, &mut input);
        let float_input =
            self.size_float_for_its_run(sized_float, block_container, &input, containing_block_position_in_root);
        let layout = self.layout_inside(run, sized_float, block_container, float_input, false);
        FloatLaidOutAheadOfItsPosition {
            node,
            placed_float: layout.placed_child(),
            cells: layout.cells(),
            laid_out_float_handed_back_by_its_run: layout.result().is_some().then(|| LaidOutBox::of_layout(&layout)),
            fragment_arrival: layout.into_fragment_arrival(run),
        }
    }

    /// Positions and places a float laid out ahead of its position.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn position_laid_out_float(
        &self,
        run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>,
        laid_out_float: FloatLaidOutAheadOfItsPosition,
        block_container: BlockContainer,
        input: LayoutInput,
        containing_block_position_in_root: FfiCssPixelPoint,
        block_offset: CssPixels,
        mut line_builder: Option<&mut line_builder::LineBuilder<'_, '_>>,
        fragment_facts: run_state::FragmentFactsDecidedByParent,
    ) -> (
        abspos_engine::InFlowBoxInsets,
        Option<LaidOutBox>,
        Option<FfiCssPixelPoint>,
    ) {
        let node = laid_out_float.node;
        let Some(side) = Self::float_side(self.style(node)) else {
            formatting_context::leave_child_unplaced(
                run,
                laid_out_float.placed_float.with_fragment_facts(fragment_facts),
                laid_out_float.fragment_arrival,
            );
            return (
                abspos_engine::InFlowBoxInsets::default(),
                laid_out_float.laid_out_float_handed_back_by_its_run,
                None,
            );
        };
        let (floating_box, content_block_offset) = self.add_float_beside_lines(
            node,
            side,
            &laid_out_float.cells,
            block_container,
            input,
            containing_block_position_in_root,
            block_offset,
            line_builder.as_deref_mut(),
        );
        if line_builder.is_none()
            && self.run.fragmentainer.is_some()
            && self.allows_unforced_breaks()
            && self.defer_float_past_column(floating_box, true)
        {
            if let Some(fragments) = run.fragments {
                fragments.discard_unplaced_subtree(node, laid_out_float.fragment_arrival);
            }
            return (
                abspos_engine::InFlowBoxInsets::default(),
                laid_out_float.laid_out_float_handed_back_by_its_run,
                None,
            );
        }
        if let Some(line_builder) = line_builder {
            line_builder.recalculate_available_space();
        }
        self.place_positioned_float(
            run,
            PositionedFloat {
                laid_out_float,
                floating_box,
                content_block_offset,
            },
            block_container,
            fragment_facts,
        )
    }

    pub(crate) fn place_positioned_float(
        &self,
        run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>,
        positioned: PositionedFloat,
        block_container: BlockContainer,
        fragment_facts: run_state::FragmentFactsDecidedByParent,
    ) -> (
        abspos_engine::InFlowBoxInsets,
        Option<LaidOutBox>,
        Option<FfiCssPixelPoint>,
    ) {
        let PositionedFloat {
            laid_out_float,
            floating_box,
            content_block_offset,
        } = positioned;
        let FloatLaidOutAheadOfItsPosition {
            node,
            placed_float,
            laid_out_float_handed_back_by_its_run,
            fragment_arrival,
            ..
        } = laid_out_float;
        let margin_box_rect = floating_box.margin_box_rect_in_root_coordinate_space;

        let bottom_margin_edge = margin_box_rect.bottom();
        if self.keeps_column_box_layouts() {
            self.note_column_content_block_end(
                bottom_margin_edge + self.block_offset_adjustment_from_pending_ancestor_block_start_margins(node),
            );
        }
        if let Some(fragmentainer) = self.run.fragmentainer.as_ref()
            && self.allows_unforced_breaks()
        {
            let bottom_margin_edge_in_column =
                bottom_margin_edge + self.block_offset_adjustment_from_pending_ancestor_block_start_margins(node);
            fragmentainer.note_unbreakable_block_size(margin_box_rect.height);
            if fragmentainer.exceeds(bottom_margin_edge_in_column) {
                fragmentainer.note_space_shortage(bottom_margin_edge_in_column);
                fragmentainer.outcome_mut().overflows = true;
            }
        }
        self.lowest_floating_descendant_bottom_margin_edge.set(Some(
            self.lowest_floating_descendant_bottom_margin_edge
                .get()
                .map_or(bottom_margin_edge, |lowest| lowest.max(bottom_margin_edge)),
        ));
        let insets = self.compute_inset(run, node, block_container);

        let inline_offset = if floating_box.side == FloatSide::Left {
            floating_box.offset_from_edge
        } else {
            floating_box.percentage_basis_inline_size.unwrap_or_default() - floating_box.offset_from_edge
        };
        let content_offset = FfiCssPixelPoint {
            x: inline_offset,
            y: content_block_offset,
        };
        formatting_context::place_child(
            &self.run,
            node,
            placed_float
                .with_in_flow_box_insets(insets)
                .with_fragment_facts(fragment_facts),
            content_offset,
            None,
            fragment_arrival,
        );
        (insets, laid_out_float_handed_back_by_its_run, Some(content_offset))
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn position_inline_float_in_column(
        &self,
        laid_out_float: FloatLaidOutAheadOfItsPosition,
        block_container: BlockContainer,
        input: LayoutInput,
        containing_block_position_in_root: FfiCssPixelPoint,
        line_builder: &mut line_builder::LineBuilder<'_, '_>,
    ) -> (PositionedFloat, bool) {
        let node = laid_out_float.node;
        let side = Self::float_side(self.style(node)).expect("an inline float has a floating side");
        let (floating_box, content_block_offset) = self.add_float_beside_lines(
            node,
            side,
            &laid_out_float.cells,
            block_container,
            input,
            containing_block_position_in_root,
            CssPixels::default(),
            Some(&mut *line_builder),
        );
        let deferred = self.defer_float_past_column(floating_box, true);
        line_builder.recalculate_available_space();
        (
            PositionedFloat {
                laid_out_float,
                floating_box,
                content_block_offset,
            },
            deferred,
        )
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-break-3/#parallel-flows
    // The contents of a float vs. the content wrapping outside the float.
    // AD-HOC: These flows can fragment independently, but a float's contents are laid out as an unbroken box here.
    //         Move the whole float when it doesn't fit, until its layout can return a continuation of its contents.
    fn defer_float_past_column(&self, floating_box: FloatingBox, records_measurement: bool) -> bool {
        let Some(fragmentainer) = self.run.fragmentainer.as_ref() else {
            return false;
        };
        let rect = floating_box.margin_box_rect_in_root_coordinate_space.translated(
            CssPixels::default(),
            self.block_offset_adjustment_from_pending_ancestor_block_start_margins(floating_box.box_),
        );
        if records_measurement {
            fragmentainer.note_unbreakable_block_size(rect.height);
        }
        let deferred = self.deferred_float_sides.get() != 0
            || (rect.y > CssPixels::default() && fragmentainer.exceeds(rect.bottom()));
        if !deferred {
            return false;
        }
        if records_measurement {
            fragmentainer.note_space_shortage(rect.bottom());
        }
        self.deferred_float_sides
            .set(self.deferred_float_sides.get() | if floating_box.side == FloatSide::Left { 1 } else { 2 });
        self.floats.borrow_mut().pop();
        self.rebuild_float_bands();
        true
    }

    pub(crate) fn retain_inline_floats(&self, first: usize, kept: &HashSet<Node>) {
        let mut floats = self.take_floating_boxes_from(first);
        floats.retain(|float| kept.contains(&float.box_));
        self.append_floating_boxes(floats);
    }

    /// Adds a float laid out in `float_box` beside the lines `line_builder` builds, only to find where they break.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn add_float_for_finding_line_breaks(
        &self,
        node: Node,
        float_box: &used_values::RootInputCells,
        block_container: BlockContainer,
        input: LayoutInput,
        containing_block_position_in_root: FfiCssPixelPoint,
        line_builder: &mut line_builder::LineBuilder<'_, '_>,
        fragments_lines: bool,
    ) {
        let Some(side) = Self::float_side(self.style(node)) else {
            return;
        };
        let (floating_box, _) = self.add_float_beside_lines(
            node,
            side,
            float_box,
            block_container,
            input,
            containing_block_position_in_root,
            CssPixels::default(),
            Some(&mut *line_builder),
        );
        if fragments_lines {
            self.defer_float_past_column(floating_box, false);
        }
        line_builder.recalculate_available_space();
    }

    /// The floats and margins of this context before finding where lines break changes them.
    pub(crate) fn state_before_finding_line_breaks(&self) -> StateBeforeFindingLineBreaks {
        StateBeforeFindingLineBreaks {
            float_count: self.floating_box_count(),
            deferred_float_sides: self.deferred_float_sides.get(),
            bands: self.bands.borrow().clone(),
            lowest_left_margin_edge: self.lowest_left_margin_edge.get(),
            lowest_right_margin_edge: self.lowest_right_margin_edge.get(),
            margin_state: self.margin_state().clone(),
        }
    }

    /// Takes out the floats added and restores the margins committed to find where lines break since `state` was the
    /// state of this context.
    pub(crate) fn restore_state_after_finding_line_breaks(&self, state: StateBeforeFindingLineBreaks) {
        *self.margin_state_mut() = state.margin_state;
        self.deferred_float_sides.set(state.deferred_float_sides);
        if self.floating_box_count() == state.float_count {
            return;
        }
        self.floats.borrow_mut().truncate(state.float_count);
        *self.bands.borrow_mut() = state.bands;
        self.lowest_left_margin_edge.set(state.lowest_left_margin_edge);
        self.lowest_right_margin_edge.set(state.lowest_right_margin_edge);
    }

    fn float_side(style: StyleValues<'_>) -> Option<FloatSide> {
        // FIXME: Honor writing-mode, direction and text-orientation.
        if matches!(style.float_(), float::LEFT | float::INLINE_START) {
            Some(FloatSide::Left)
        } else if matches!(style.float_(), float::RIGHT | float::INLINE_END) {
            Some(FloatSide::Right)
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    /// Floats the box laid out in `float_box` to `side`, below the content `line_builder` already put on its line
    /// where the float does not fit beside it, and adds it to the floats of this context.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    fn add_float_beside_lines(
        &self,
        node: Node,
        side: FloatSide,
        float_box: &used_values::RootInputCells,
        block_container: BlockContainer,
        input: LayoutInput,
        containing_block_position_in_root: FfiCssPixelPoint,
        block_offset: CssPixels,
        line_builder: Option<&mut line_builder::LineBuilder<'_, '_>>,
    ) -> (FloatingBox, CssPixels) {
        let style = self.style(node);
        let containing_block_rect = self.containing_block_rect(block_container, containing_block_position_in_root);
        let containing_block_rect_now = containing_block_rect.translated(
            CssPixels::default(),
            self.block_offset_adjustment_from_pending_ancestor_block_start_margins(block_container.node),
        );
        let mut margin_box_ceiling = if let Some(line_builder) = line_builder {
            line_builder.ceiling_for_float_to_be_inserted_here(float_box.margin_box_inline_size(false))
        } else {
            block_offset
        };
        // NB: A float that ends above this position cannot reach the float being placed, whichever edge of it the steps
        //     below compare with.
        self.note_float_read_from(containing_block_rect_now.y + margin_box_ceiling);
        // https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS2/visuren.html#flow-control
        // A float clears the floats of the sides its 'clear' names, whichever side it floats to itself.
        if matches!(style.clear(), clear::LEFT | clear::BOTH | clear::INLINE_START)
            && let Some(lowest_left_margin_edge) = self.lowest_left_margin_edge.get()
        {
            margin_box_ceiling = margin_box_ceiling.max(lowest_left_margin_edge - containing_block_rect_now.y);
        }
        if matches!(style.clear(), clear::RIGHT | clear::BOTH | clear::INLINE_END)
            && let Some(lowest_right_margin_edge) = self.lowest_right_margin_edge.get()
        {
            margin_box_ceiling = margin_box_ceiling.max(lowest_right_margin_edge - containing_block_rect_now.y);
        }
        let mut ceiling_in_root = containing_block_rect_now.y + margin_box_ceiling;
        if let Some(last) = self.floats.borrow().last().copied() {
            ceiling_in_root = ceiling_in_root.max(
                last.margin_box_rect_in_root_coordinate_space.y
                    + self.block_offset_adjustment_from_pending_ancestor_block_start_margins(last.box_),
            );
        }
        let placement = self.place_float(
            side,
            float_box,
            input.available_space,
            containing_block_rect_now,
            ceiling_in_root,
        );
        let content_block_offset = placement.block_start - containing_block_rect_now.y
            + float_box.margin_top()
            + float_box.border_box_top(false);
        let mut margin_box_rect = Self::margin_box_rect(float_box)
            .translated(CssPixels::default(), content_block_offset)
            .translated(containing_block_rect.x, containing_block_rect.y);
        let mut floating_box = FloatingBox {
            box_: node,
            side,
            offset_from_edge: placement.offset_from_edge,
            left_margin_edge_to_content_edge: float_box.margin_left() + float_box.border_box_left(false),
            left_content_edge_to_right_margin_edge: float_box.content_inline_size()
                + float_box.margin_right()
                + float_box.border_box_right(false),
            bottom_margin_edge: content_block_offset
                + float_box.content_block_size()
                + float_box.margin_box_bottom(false),
            margin_box_rect_in_root_coordinate_space: margin_box_rect,
            containing_block_rect_in_root_coordinate_space: containing_block_rect,
            percentage_basis_inline_size: input.containing_block_constraints.percentage_basis_inline_size,
        };
        margin_box_rect.x = floating_box.margin_box_left_in_root_coordinate_space();
        floating_box.margin_box_rect_in_root_coordinate_space = margin_box_rect;
        self.floats.borrow_mut().push(floating_box);
        self.add_float_to_bands(floating_box);
        (floating_box, content_block_offset)
    }

    fn layout_inline_children(
        &self,
        run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>,
        block_container: BlockContainer,
        input: LayoutInput,
        containing_block_position_in_root: FfiCssPixelPoint,
        available_space_for_children: AvailableSpace,
    ) -> ChildrenSummary {
        assert!(self.facts(block_container.node).children_are_inline());
        debug_assert!(
            block_container.cells.has_definite_inline_size,
            "lines are laid out in a block container of definite inline size"
        );
        let inline_input = self.child_layout_input(block_container, input, available_space_for_children);
        let mut context = inline_formatting_context::InlineFormattingContext::new_with_rust_parent(
            run,
            block_container,
            inline_input,
            containing_block_position_in_root,
            self.run.pass,
            self,
        );
        let summary = context.run();
        if summary.baselines.first.is_some() {
            self.outside_marker_line.set(None);
        }
        summary
    }

    fn compute_automatic_block_size_for_block_level_element(
        &self,
        sized_child: ChildSizedHere<'_>,
        available_space: AvailableSpace,
        constraints: ContainingBlockConstraints,
        automatic_content_block_size_of_completed_run: Option<CssPixels>,
        children: Option<&ChildrenSummary>,
    ) -> CssPixels {
        let node = sized_child.node;
        let automatic_content_block_size = self.automatic_block_size_for_block_level_element_disregarding_marker(
            sized_child,
            available_space,
            constraints,
            automatic_content_block_size_of_completed_run,
            true,
            children,
        );
        floor_list_item_automatic_block_size_by_marker_line_height(self.run.pass, node, automatic_content_block_size)
            .max(
                children
                    .and_then(|children| children.outside_marker_line_box_block_size)
                    .unwrap_or_default(),
            )
    }

    fn automatic_block_size_for_block_level_element_disregarding_marker(
        &self,
        sized_child: ChildSizedHere<'_>,
        available_space: AvailableSpace,
        constraints: ContainingBlockConstraints,
        automatic_content_block_size_of_completed_run: Option<CssPixels>,
        applies_editing_host_floor: bool,
        children: Option<&ChildrenSummary>,
    ) -> CssPixels {
        let node = sized_child.node;
        let facts = self.facts(node);
        let style = self.style(node);
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain-2/#containment-size
        // Giving an element size containment makes its principal box a size containment box and has the following
        // effects:
        // 1. The intrinsic sizes of the size containment box are determined as if the element had no content, following
        //    the same logic as when sizing as if empty.
        if facts.node_has_size_containment() {
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-4/#intrinsic-size-override
            // If an element has an explicit intrinsic inner size in an axis, then after laying out the element as
            // normal for size containment, the size of the contents in that axis are instead treated as being the
            // explicit intrinsic inner size instead of what was calculated in layout, and layout is performed again if
            // necessary.
            // FIXME: Nothing re-runs layout here. The substituted size replaces the block size the contents produced,
            //        and size containment keeps those contents from depending on it, so a second pass has nothing to
            //        change today.
            if style.contain_intrinsic_height_has_length() {
                return CssPixels::nearest_value_for(style.contain_intrinsic_height_px());
            }
            return CssPixels::default();
        }
        if facts.creates_block_formatting_context()
            || style.display().is_flex_inside()
            || style.display().is_grid_inside()
            || style.display().is_table_inside()
        {
            return formatting_context::independent_root_automatic_block_size(
                &self.sizing(),
                sizing_context::SizedBox::new(node, &self.metrics_of(sized_child)),
                available_space,
                constraints,
                automatic_content_block_size_of_completed_run,
            );
        }

        if let Some(automatic_content_block_size) = automatic_content_block_size_of_completed_run {
            return automatic_content_block_size;
        }

        // https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/visudet.html#normal-block
        // 10.6.3 Block-level non-replaced elements in normal flow when 'overflow' computes to 'visible'

        // The element's block size is the distance from its block-start content edge to the first applicable edge below.
        // 1. the bottom edge of the last line box, if the box establishes a inline formatting context with one or more lines
        if facts.children_are_inline()
            && let Some(last_line) = children.and_then(|children| children.last_line)
        {
            let mut block_size = last_line.physical_vertical_end();
            if last_line.has_block_level_box {
                let mut margin_state = self.margin_state_mut();
                let mut margin_bottom =
                    if children.is_some_and(|children| children.pending_margins_collapse_through_block_start) {
                        CssPixels::default()
                    } else {
                        margin_state.collapsed_margin_at_block_end_of(&facts)
                    };
                let metrics = self.metrics_of(sized_child);
                if metrics.padding_bottom() == CssPixels::default() && metrics.border_bottom() == CssPixels::default() {
                    margin_state.box_last_in_flow_child_margin_bottom_collapsed = true;
                    margin_bottom = CssPixels::default();
                }
                block_size = (block_size + margin_bottom).max(CssPixels::default());
            }
            return block_size;
        }

        // 2. the bottom edge of the bottom (possibly collapsed) margin of its last in-flow child, if the child's bottom margin does not collapse with the element's bottom margin
        // 3. the bottom border edge of the last in-flow child whose top margin doesn't collapse with the element's bottom margin
        if !facts.children_are_inline()
            && let Some(last_in_flow_child) = children.and_then(|children| children.last_in_flow_child)
        {
            let mut margin_state = self.margin_state_mut();
            let mut margin_bottom = if self.line_clamp_reached() {
                last_in_flow_child.margin_bottom
            } else {
                margin_state.collapsed_margin_at_block_end_of(&facts)
            };
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#collapsing-margins
            // If the top and bottom margins of an element with clearance are adjoining, its margins collapse with the
            // adjoining margins of following siblings but that resulting margin does not collapse with the bottom
            // margin of the parent block.
            // NB: So the collapsed margin stays inside this box, and starts where the margins of that child began.
            if let Some(margins_after_clearance) = last_in_flow_child.collapsed_margin_after_clearance
                && !self.line_clamp_reached()
            {
                return (last_in_flow_child.border_box_block_end - margins_after_clearance + margin_bottom)
                    .max(CssPixels::default());
            }
            let used = self.cells_laid_out_here(sized_child);
            if used.padding_bottom() == CssPixels::default() && used.border_bottom() == CssPixels::default() {
                margin_state.box_last_in_flow_child_margin_bottom_collapsed = true;
                margin_bottom = CssPixels::default();
            }
            return (last_in_flow_child.border_box_block_end + margin_bottom).max(CssPixels::default());
        }
        // NB: Where margins collapse through every in-flow child, and that collapsed margin can't collapse with this
        //     box's top margin either, it's the margin of the last of those children: Unless it collapses with this
        //     box's bottom margin as well, the box runs to its bottom edge, from the block-start content edge.
        if !facts.children_are_inline()
            && children.is_some_and(|children| !children.pending_margins_collapse_through_block_start)
        {
            let margin_bottom = self.margin_state_mut().collapsed_margin_at_block_end_of(&facts);
            let used = self.cells_laid_out_here(sized_child);
            if margin_bottom != CssPixels::default()
                && (used.padding_bottom() != CssPixels::default() || used.border_bottom() != CssPixels::default())
            {
                return margin_bottom.max(CssPixels::default());
            }
        }

        // AD-HOC: Contenteditable elements must have a minimum block size (line-height) when empty, to remain clickable
        //         and usable for text input, even though this is not specified.
        //         See: https://github.com/w3c/editing/issues/70.
        if facts.is_editing_host() && applies_editing_host_floor {
            return style.line_height();
        }
        // 4. zero, otherwise
        CssPixels::default()
    }

    fn resolve_automatic_line_clamp_block_size(&self, input: LayoutInput) -> Option<CssPixels> {
        if self.root_cells.has_definite_block_size {
            return Some(self.root_cells.content_block_size);
        }

        let style = self.style(self.run.box_);
        let sizing = self.sizing();
        if style.max_height().is_auto()
            || sizing.should_treat_max_block_size_as_none(
                self.run.box_,
                input.available_space.block_size,
                input.containing_block_constraints,
            )
        {
            return None;
        }
        let mut block_size = sizing.calculate_inner_block_size(
            sizing_context::SizedBox::of_own_metrics(self.run.box_, &self.root_cells, self.run.pass.frame),
            input.available_space,
            style.max_height(),
            input.containing_block_constraints,
        );
        if !crate::layout::sizing_context::is_plain_auto(style.min_height()) {
            block_size = block_size.max(sizing.calculate_inner_block_size(
                sizing_context::SizedBox::of_own_metrics(self.run.box_, &self.root_cells, self.run.pass.frame),
                input.available_space,
                style.min_height(),
                input.containing_block_constraints,
            ));
        }
        Some(block_size)
    }

    fn automatic_line_clamp_max_lines(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-4/#line-clamp-containers
        // The auto clamp point will be set to the last possible clamp point such that, for it and all previous
        // possible clamp points, the line-clamp container's automatic block size is not greater than the block size
        // the box would have if its automatic block size were infinite.
        let automatic_block_size = self.automatic_line_clamp_block_size.get()?;
        if self.automatic_content_block_size() <= automatic_block_size {
            return None;
        }
        self.automatic_line_clamp_max_lines
            .get()
            .or_else(|| (self.line_clamp_line_count.get() == 0).then_some(0))
    }

    fn automatic_content_block_size(&self) -> CssPixels {
        self.block_size_of_contents(self.run.fragmentainer.is_none())
    }

    fn block_size_of_contents(&self, honors_size_containment: bool) -> CssPixels {
        if let Some(block_size) = self.multicol_automatic_content_block_size.get() {
            return block_size;
        }
        let line_clamp_reached = self.line_clamp_reached();
        let block_size = automatic_block_size_for_bfc_root(
            self.root_lines.borrow().last_line(),
            self.run.pass,
            self.run.box_,
            &self.root_flow_children.borrow(),
            honors_size_containment,
            (!line_clamp_reached)
                .then_some(self.lowest_floating_descendant_bottom_margin_edge.get())
                .flatten(),
            (!line_clamp_reached)
                .then_some(self.trailing_collapsed_margin.get())
                .flatten(),
        );
        if self.run.fragmentainer.is_some() {
            return block_size;
        }
        floor_list_item_automatic_block_size_by_marker_line_height(self.run.pass, self.run.box_, block_size).max(
            self.outside_marker_line_box_block_size_of_root
                .get()
                .unwrap_or_default(),
        )
    }

    fn line_clamp_subtree_contains_line(&self, node: Node) -> bool {
        let facts = self.facts(node);
        if facts.is_text_node() {
            return !self.run.pass.text_content(node).untransformed_text_is_ascii_whitespace;
        }
        if facts.is_atomic_inline() || (facts.is_anonymous() && facts.children_are_inline()) {
            return true;
        }
        if facts.has_dom_node()
            && (facts.is_floating()
                || facts.is_absolutely_positioned()
                || facts.uses_button_layout()
                || self.style(node).own_style_establishes_block_formatting_context()
                || !self.style(node).display().is_flow_inside())
        {
            return false;
        }
        self.children(node)
            .any(|child| self.line_clamp_subtree_contains_line(child))
    }

    fn line_clamp_has_future_content(&self, anchor: Node) -> Option<bool> {
        let mut node = anchor;
        let mut has_intervening_in_flow_box = false;
        while node != self.run.box_ {
            let mut sibling = self.next_sibling(node);
            while !sibling.is_invalid() {
                let facts = self.facts(sibling);
                if !facts.is_absolutely_positioned() && self.floats.borrow().iter().all(|float| float.box_ != sibling) {
                    if self.line_clamp_subtree_contains_line(sibling) {
                        return Some(!has_intervening_in_flow_box);
                    }
                    if facts.is_flow_layout_participant() {
                        has_intervening_in_flow_box = true;
                    }
                }
                sibling = self.next_sibling(sibling);
            }
            node = self.run.pass.parent(node);
        }
        has_intervening_in_flow_box.then_some(true)
    }
}

pub(crate) fn is_line_clamp_container(pass: &LayoutPass<'_>, node: Node) -> bool {
    let style = StyleValues::for_node(pass, node);
    let computed_continue = style.continue_();
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-4/#continue
    // If the box is a block container, then it must establish an independent formatting context that also becomes
    // a line-clamp container.
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-4/#webkit-line-clamp
    // The -webkit-legacy value behaves identically to collapse, except that it only takes effect if the specified
    // value of the display property is -webkit-box or -webkit-inline-box and the value of the -webkit-box-orient
    // property is vertical.
    (computed_continue == continue_value::COLLAPSE
        || (computed_continue == continue_value::_WEBKIT_LEGACY
            && style.display_before_box_type_transformation().is_webkit_box_inside()
            && style.webkit_box_orient() == webkit_box_orient::VERTICAL))
        && !NodeFacts::new(pass, node).lays_out_in_columns()
}

pub(crate) fn is_column_spanner(pass: &LayoutPass<'_>, node: Node) -> bool {
    let facts = NodeFacts::new(pass, node);
    facts.is_flow_layout_participant()
        && !facts.is_floating()
        && facts.display().is_block_outside()
        && StyleValues::for_node(pass, node).column_span() == column_span::ALL
}

pub(crate) fn box_avoids_floats_because_it_establishes_formatting_context(pass: &LayoutPass<'_>, node: Node) -> bool {
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#floats
    // The border box of a table, a block-level replaced element, or an element in the normal flow that establishes
    // a new block formatting context (such as an element with 'overflow' other than 'visible') must not overlap the
    // margin box of any floats in the same block formatting context as the element itself. If necessary,
    // implementations should clear the said element by placing it below any preceding floats, but may place it
    // adjacent to such floats if there is sufficient space. They may even make the border box of said element
    // narrower than defined by section 10.3.3. CSS2 does not define when a UA may put said element next to the
    // float or by how much said element may become narrower.

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox/#flex-containers
    // A flex container establishes a new flex formatting context for its contents. This is the same as establishing
    // a block formatting context, except that flex layout is used instead of block layout. For example, floats do
    // not intrude into the flex container, and the flex container’s margins do not collapse with the margins of its
    // contents.

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid/#grid-containers
    // A grid container that is not a subgrid establishes an independent grid formatting context for its contents.
    // This is the same as establishing an independent block formatting context, except that grid layout is used
    // instead of block layout: floats do not intrude into the grid container, and the grid container’s margins do
    // not collapse with the margins of its contents.
    let facts = NodeFacts::new(pass, node);
    facts.is_replaced_box()
        || matches!(
            formatting_context::formatting_context_type_created_by_box(facts),
            Some(
                formatting_context::FormattingContextType::Block
                    | formatting_context::FormattingContextType::Flex
                    | formatting_context::FormattingContextType::Grid
                    | formatting_context::FormattingContextType::Math
            )
        )
}

fn table_box_of_wrapper(pass: LayoutPass<'_>, wrapper: Node) -> Node {
    for child in pass.children(wrapper) {
        if NodeFacts::new(&pass, child).is_box() && StyleValues::for_node(&pass, child).display().is_table_inside() {
            return child;
        }
    }
    unreachable!("a table wrapper contains its table box")
}

// Flow-ordered children of a table wrapper's block formatting context: top captions in document
// order, then the table box, then bottom captions in document order. Captions are tree children
// of the table box; absolutely positioned captions are out of flow and are registered by
// register_table_abspos_descendants instead.
pub(crate) fn table_wrapper_flow_children(pass: LayoutPass<'_>, wrapper: Node) -> Vec<Node> {
    let table_box = table_box_of_wrapper(pass, wrapper);
    let mut flow_children = Vec::new();
    let mut bottom_captions = Vec::new();
    for child in pass.children(table_box) {
        let facts = NodeFacts::new(&pass, child);
        if facts.is_box() && facts.is_table_caption() && !facts.is_absolutely_positioned() {
            if StyleValues::for_node(&pass, child).caption_side() == caption_side::TOP {
                flow_children.push(child);
            } else {
                bottom_captions.push(child);
            }
        }
    }
    flow_children.push(table_box);
    flow_children.extend(bottom_captions);
    flow_children
}

/// Whether margins can collapse through `node` as far as the box itself goes, before its children are considered, where
/// `introduced_clearance` says if placing it introduced clearance. The block size of its border box is read only where
/// nothing else keeps margins from collapsing through it.
pub(crate) fn margins_can_collapse_through_box_itself(
    facts: NodeFacts<'_>,
    introduced_clearance: bool,
    border_box_block_size: impl FnOnce() -> CssPixels,
) -> bool {
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#adjoining-margins
    // Two margins are adjoining if and only if:
    // - both belong to in-flow block-level boxes that participate in the same block formatting context
    //   NB: Yes, we're dealing with one and the same box here.

    // - no line boxes, no clearance, no padding and no border separate them (Note that certain zero-height line boxes
    //   (see 9.4.2) are ignored for this purpose.)
    // NB: Border and padding are handled further down. A box with clear introduces clearance only where there's a float
    //     for it to clear; otherwise clear has no effect, and margins collapse through it like through any other box.
    if introduced_clearance {
        return false;
    }
    // - both belong to vertically-adjacent box edges, i.e. form one of the following pairs:
    //   - top and bottom margins of a box that does not establish a new block formatting context and that has zero
    //     computed 'min-height', zero or 'auto' computed 'height', and no in-flow children
    if facts.creates_block_formatting_context() {
        return false;
    }
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display-3/#independent-formatting-context
    // NOTE: [..] margins do not collapse across formatting context boundaries.
    if formatting_context::formatting_context_type_created_by_box(facts).is_some() {
        return false;
    }
    // NB: This should take care of the height and min-height constraints.
    //     ( also see https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/pull/13699#issuecomment-4103045370 for spec ambiguity )
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-4/#aspect-ratio-margin-collapse
    // FIXME: For the purpose of margin collapsing (CSS 2 §8.3.1 Collapsing margins), if the block axis is the
    //        ratio-dependent axis, it is not considered to have a computed block-size of auto.
    border_box_block_size() == CssPixels::default()
}

// https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/visudet.html#root-height
pub(crate) fn automatic_block_size_for_bfc_root(
    root_last_line: Option<inline_content::LineRecord>,
    pass: LayoutPass<'_>,
    root: Node,
    flow_children: &[RootFlowChild],
    honors_size_containment: bool,
    lowest_floating_descendant_bottom_margin_edge: Option<CssPixels>,
    trailing_collapsed_margin: Option<(Option<usize>, CssPixels)>,
) -> CssPixels {
    let facts = NodeFacts::new(&pass, root);
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain-2/#containment-size
    // A size-contained box is sized as if it had no contents.
    if honors_size_containment && facts.node_has_size_containment() {
        return CssPixels::default();
    }
    let mut bottom = None;
    if facts.children_are_inline() {
        // If it only has inline-level children, the block size is the distance between
        // the top content edge and the bottom of the bottommost line box.
        if let Some(last_line) = root_last_line {
            bottom = Some(last_line.physical_vertical_end());
            // A trailing interrupting block's bottom margin cannot collapse out of a BFC root,
            // so it contributes to the root's automatic block size. The line box bottom excludes it.
            if last_line.has_block_level_box {
                bottom = Some((bottom.unwrap() + last_line.block_level_box_block_end_margin).max(CssPixels::default()));
            }
        }
    } else {
        // If it has block-level children, the block size is the distance between
        // the top margin-edge of the topmost block-level child box
        // and the bottom margin-edge of the bottommost block-level child box.
        // NOTE: The top margin edge of the topmost block-level child box is the same as the top content edge of the root box.
        // NB: Captions flow in a table wrapper's formatting context while remaining tree children of the table box, so
        //     the flow children of a wrapper are its captions and its table box.
        let participates = |child: &RootFlowChild| {
            let child_facts = NodeFacts::new(&pass, child.node);
            child_facts.is_flow_layout_participant() && !child_facts.is_floating()
        };
        // AD-HOC: The spec ends the root at "the bottom margin-edge of the bottommost block-level child box". The
        //         root ends at the bottom margin edge of its last in-flow child instead, which is where its flow
        //         ends — and what pages are written to: A negative margin that pulls the last child up, over the
        //         child before it, pulls the end of the root up with it, and the child before it overflows the root.
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#collapsing-margins
        // NB: The margins of a box that margins collapse through collapse with those of the boxes around it, so the
        //     box reaches no further than the collapsed margin they all end with, which the box before it accounts
        //     for, or the run's start where there's no such box.
        let last_child =
            flow_children.iter().enumerate().rev().find(|(_, child)| {
                participates(child) && !child.is_invisible_for_line_clamp && !child.collapses_through
            });
        if let Some((index, child)) = last_child {
            // Margins cannot collapse out of a BFC root: below the last real in-flow
            // child, the run's trailing collapsed margin (which folds in any trailing
            // collapse-through siblings) replaces that child's own bottom margin.
            let margin_bottom = match trailing_collapsed_margin {
                Some((Some(index_of_last_real_child), aggregate)) if index_of_last_real_child == index => aggregate,
                _ => child.margin_bottom,
            };
            // NB: The margins that collapse through a box with clearance start before the box, past the clearance.
            bottom = Some(
                child.border_box_block_end - child.collapsed_margin_after_clearance.unwrap_or_default() + margin_bottom,
            );
        }
        // Where margins collapse through every in-flow child, their collapsed margin starts at the top content edge.
        if let Some((None, aggregate)) = trailing_collapsed_margin {
            bottom = Some(bottom.map_or(aggregate, |value| value.max(aggregate)));
        }
    }
    // In addition, if the element has any floating descendants
    // whose bottom margin edge is below the element's bottom content edge,
    // then the block size is increased to include those edges.
    if let Some(lowest) = lowest_floating_descendant_bottom_margin_edge {
        bottom = Some(bottom.map_or(lowest, |value| value.max(lowest)));
    }
    bottom.unwrap_or_default().max(CssPixels::default())
}

/// The automatic block size a block formatting context gives a box with a formatting context of its own ahead of the
/// box's run, while none of the box's contents are laid out.
pub(crate) fn automatic_block_size_of_independent_root_ahead_of_its_contents(
    sizing: &sizing_context::SizingContext<'_, '_>,
    sized: sizing_context::SizedBox<'_>,
    available_space: AvailableSpace,
    constraints: ContainingBlockConstraints,
) -> CssPixels {
    let node = sized.node;
    let pass = *sizing.pass();
    let facts = NodeFacts::new(&pass, node);
    let style = StyleValues::for_node(&pass, node);
    let display = style.display();
    let automatic_content_block_size = if facts.node_has_size_containment() {
        if style.contain_intrinsic_height_has_length() {
            CssPixels::nearest_value_for(style.contain_intrinsic_height_px())
        } else {
            CssPixels::default()
        }
    } else if facts.creates_block_formatting_context()
        || display.is_flex_inside()
        || display.is_grid_inside()
        || display.is_table_inside()
    {
        formatting_context::independent_root_automatic_block_size(sizing, sized, available_space, constraints, None)
    } else if facts.is_editing_host() {
        style.line_height()
    } else {
        CssPixels::default()
    };
    floor_list_item_automatic_block_size_by_marker_line_height(pass, node, automatic_content_block_size)
}

pub(crate) fn floor_list_item_automatic_block_size_by_marker_line_height(
    pass: LayoutPass<'_>,
    node: Node,
    automatic_content_block_size: CssPixels,
) -> CssPixels {
    let facts = NodeFacts::new(&pass, node);
    if !facts.is_list_item_box() {
        return automatic_content_block_size;
    }
    let marker = facts.list_item_marker();
    if marker.is_invalid() {
        return automatic_content_block_size;
    }
    automatic_content_block_size.max(StyleValues::for_node(&pass, marker).line_height())
}

/// The inline layout of the table box inside `child` that `kept` holds for the run of `child`, which stays kept for
/// another child.
pub(crate) fn take_table_inline_layout_kept_for(
    kept: &Cell<Option<(Node, std::sync::Arc<table_formatting_context::TableInlineLayout>)>>,
    child: Node,
) -> Option<std::sync::Arc<table_formatting_context::TableInlineLayout>> {
    let (kept_for, layout) = kept.take()?;
    if kept_for != child {
        kept.set(Some((kept_for, layout)));
        return None;
    }
    Some(layout)
}

//! https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align-3/
//! The keywords of the self-alignment and content-distribution properties, resolved to the side of an axis that they
//! align to. Each layout mode sizes and places its boxes from the resolved alignment.

use super::*;

/// The low side of an axis, its center, or its high side. The low side is the left or top side in the frame the caller
/// measures offsets in, once the writing mode, the direction and any reversal of the axis are resolved.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum AxisEdge {
    Start,
    Center,
    End,
}

impl AxisEdge {
    pub(crate) fn low_side_if(is_low: bool) -> Self {
        if is_low { Self::Start } else { Self::End }
    }

    pub(crate) fn reversed(self) -> Self {
        match self {
            Self::Start => Self::End,
            Self::Center => Self::Center,
            Self::End => Self::Start,
        }
    }

    /// The offset from the low side of an alignment container of a subject aligned to this edge, where the container
    /// leaves `free_space` beside the subject.
    pub(crate) fn offset(self, free_space: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
        match self {
            Self::Start => CssPixels::default(),
            Self::Center => free_space / 2,
            Self::End => free_space,
        }
    }
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align-3/#overflow-values
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum OverflowSafety {
    /// Neither safe nor unsafe is specified, so the layout mode decides.
    Default,
    Safe,
    Unsafe,
}

impl OverflowSafety {
    fn of(computed: u8) -> Self {
        match computed {
            OVERFLOW_ALIGNMENT_SAFE => Self::Safe,
            OVERFLOW_ALIGNMENT_UNSAFE => Self::Unsafe,
            _ => Self::Default,
        }
    }

    fn is_safe(self, layout_mode_default: Self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::Default => layout_mode_default == Self::Safe,
            safety => safety == Self::Safe,
        }
    }
}

/// The directions of an axis that the alignment keywords name its sides by, as whether each start side is its low side.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct AxisDirections {
    pub(crate) container_start_is_low: bool,
    /// The main-start or cross-start side of a flex container. Elsewhere, flex-start is the container's start side.
    pub(crate) flex_start_is_low: bool,
    /// The start side of the alignment subject, which self-start and self-end name.
    pub(crate) self_start_is_low: bool,
    /// The line-left or physical left side, or None where left and right behave as start.
    pub(crate) line_left_is_low: Option<bool>,
}

impl AxisDirections {
    pub(crate) fn of(container_start_is_low: bool, line_left_is_low: Option<bool>) -> Self {
        Self {
            container_start_is_low,
            flex_start_is_low: container_start_is_low,
            self_start_is_low: container_start_is_low,
            line_left_is_low,
        }
    }

    fn left_is_low(self) -> bool {
        self.line_left_is_low.unwrap_or(self.container_start_is_low)
    }

    fn right_is_low(self) -> bool {
        self.line_left_is_low
            .map_or(self.container_start_is_low, |left_is_low| !left_is_low)
    }
}

/// A keyword of justify-self, justify-items, align-self or align-items.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum SelfKeyword {
    Normal,
    Stretch,
    Baseline,
    Center,
    Start,
    End,
    SelfStart,
    SelfEnd,
    FlexStart,
    FlexEnd,
    Left,
    Right,
    AnchorCenter,
}

impl SelfKeyword {
    /// The justify-self keyword of a box styled `style` and its safety, where auto takes the justify-items value of
    /// the container styled `container_style`, or behaves as normal for an absolutely positioned box, which passes
    /// none.
    pub(crate) fn justify_self_of(
        style: ComputedValuesView<'_>,
        container_style: Option<ComputedValuesView<'_>>,
    ) -> (Self, OverflowSafety) {
        let keyword = match style.justify_self() {
            justify_self::AUTO => {
                let Some(container_style) = container_style else {
                    return (Self::Normal, OverflowSafety::Default);
                };
                let keyword = match container_style.justify_items() {
                    justify_items::NORMAL | justify_items::LEGACY => Self::Normal,
                    justify_items::STRETCH => Self::Stretch,
                    justify_items::BASELINE => Self::Baseline,
                    justify_items::CENTER => Self::Center,
                    justify_items::START => Self::Start,
                    justify_items::END => Self::End,
                    justify_items::SELF_START => Self::SelfStart,
                    justify_items::SELF_END => Self::SelfEnd,
                    justify_items::FLEX_START => Self::FlexStart,
                    justify_items::FLEX_END => Self::FlexEnd,
                    justify_items::LEFT => Self::Left,
                    justify_items::RIGHT => Self::Right,
                    _ => unreachable!("invalid justify-items value"),
                };
                return (keyword, OverflowSafety::of(container_style.justify_items_overflow()));
            }
            justify_self::NORMAL => Self::Normal,
            justify_self::STRETCH => Self::Stretch,
            justify_self::BASELINE => Self::Baseline,
            justify_self::CENTER => Self::Center,
            justify_self::START => Self::Start,
            justify_self::END => Self::End,
            justify_self::SELF_START => Self::SelfStart,
            justify_self::SELF_END => Self::SelfEnd,
            justify_self::FLEX_START => Self::FlexStart,
            justify_self::FLEX_END => Self::FlexEnd,
            justify_self::LEFT => Self::Left,
            justify_self::RIGHT => Self::Right,
            justify_self::ANCHOR_CENTER => Self::AnchorCenter,
            _ => unreachable!("invalid justify-self value"),
        };
        (keyword, OverflowSafety::of(style.justify_self_overflow()))
    }

    /// The align-self keyword of a box styled `style` and its safety, where auto takes the align-items value of the
    /// container styled `container_style`, or behaves as normal for an absolutely positioned box, which passes none.
    pub(crate) fn align_self_of(
        style: ComputedValuesView<'_>,
        container_style: Option<ComputedValuesView<'_>>,
    ) -> (Self, OverflowSafety) {
        let keyword = match style.align_self() {
            align_self::AUTO => {
                return container_style.map_or((Self::Normal, OverflowSafety::Default), Self::align_items_of);
            }
            align_self::NORMAL => Self::Normal,
            align_self::STRETCH => Self::Stretch,
            align_self::BASELINE => Self::Baseline,
            align_self::CENTER => Self::Center,
            align_self::START => Self::Start,
            align_self::END => Self::End,
            align_self::SELF_START => Self::SelfStart,
            align_self::SELF_END => Self::SelfEnd,
            align_self::FLEX_START => Self::FlexStart,
            align_self::FLEX_END => Self::FlexEnd,
            align_self::ANCHOR_CENTER => Self::AnchorCenter,
            _ => unreachable!("invalid align-self value"),
        };
        (keyword, OverflowSafety::of(style.align_self_overflow()))
    }

    /// The alignment that the -webkit-box-align of a legacy webkit box styled `style` gives its items.
    pub(crate) fn webkit_box_align_of(style: ComputedValuesView<'_>) -> Self {
        match style.webkit_box_align() {
            webkit_box_align::STRETCH => Self::Stretch,
            webkit_box_align::START => Self::FlexStart,
            webkit_box_align::END => Self::FlexEnd,
            webkit_box_align::CENTER => Self::Center,
            webkit_box_align::BASELINE => Self::Baseline,
            _ => unreachable!("invalid -webkit-box-align value"),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn align_items_of(style: ComputedValuesView<'_>) -> (Self, OverflowSafety) {
        let keyword = match style.align_items() {
            align_items::NORMAL => Self::Normal,
            align_items::STRETCH => Self::Stretch,
            align_items::BASELINE => Self::Baseline,
            align_items::CENTER => Self::Center,
            align_items::START => Self::Start,
            align_items::END => Self::End,
            align_items::SELF_START => Self::SelfStart,
            align_items::SELF_END => Self::SelfEnd,
            align_items::FLEX_START => Self::FlexStart,
            align_items::FLEX_END => Self::FlexEnd,
            _ => unreachable!("invalid align-items value"),
        };
        (keyword, OverflowSafety::of(style.align_items_overflow()))
    }

    /// The alignment of a subject along an axis with the directions `directions`.
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/#valdef-justify-self-anchor-center
    /// If the box is not absolutely positioned, or does not have a default anchor box, this value behaves as center
    /// and has no additional effect on how inset properties resolve.
    pub(crate) fn resolve(self, safety: OverflowSafety, directions: AxisDirections) -> SelfAlignment {
        let edge = |side_is_low| SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::low_side_if(side_is_low));
        let position = match self {
            Self::Normal => SelfPosition::Normal,
            Self::Stretch => SelfPosition::Stretch,
            Self::Baseline => SelfPosition::Baseline,
            Self::Center | Self::AnchorCenter => SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::Center),
            Self::Start => edge(directions.container_start_is_low),
            Self::End => edge(!directions.container_start_is_low),
            Self::SelfStart => edge(directions.self_start_is_low),
            Self::SelfEnd => edge(!directions.self_start_is_low),
            Self::FlexStart => edge(directions.flex_start_is_low),
            Self::FlexEnd => edge(!directions.flex_start_is_low),
            Self::Left => edge(directions.left_is_low()),
            Self::Right => edge(directions.right_is_low()),
        };
        SelfAlignment {
            position,
            safety,
            container_start: AxisEdge::low_side_if(directions.container_start_is_low),
        }
    }
}

/// Where a box aligns itself along an axis. The layout mode decides what normal alignment does.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum SelfPosition {
    Normal,
    Stretch,
    Baseline,
    Edge(AxisEdge),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct SelfAlignment {
    pub(crate) position: SelfPosition,
    pub(crate) safety: OverflowSafety,
    /// The edge of the alignment container's start side.
    pub(crate) container_start: AxisEdge,
}

impl SelfAlignment {
    /// The position of a subject whose alignment container leaves `free_space` beside it, in a layout mode whose
    /// overflow alignment is `layout_mode_default` where the style specifies neither safe nor unsafe.
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align-3/#overflow-values
    /// safe: If the size of the alignment subject overflows the alignment container, the alignment subject is instead
    ///       aligned as if the alignment mode were start.
    pub(crate) fn position_for(self, free_space: CssPixels, layout_mode_default: OverflowSafety) -> SelfPosition {
        if free_space < CssPixels::default() && self.safety.is_safe(layout_mode_default) {
            return SelfPosition::Edge(self.container_start);
        }
        self.position
    }
}

/// A keyword of justify-content or align-content.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum ContentKeyword {
    Normal,
    Stretch,
    SpaceBetween,
    SpaceAround,
    SpaceEvenly,
    Center,
    Start,
    End,
    FlexStart,
    FlexEnd,
    Left,
    Right,
}

impl ContentKeyword {
    /// The distribution that the -webkit-box-pack of a legacy webkit box styled `style` gives its items.
    pub(crate) fn webkit_box_pack_of(style: ComputedValuesView<'_>) -> Self {
        match style.webkit_box_pack() {
            webkit_box_pack::START => Self::FlexStart,
            webkit_box_pack::END => Self::FlexEnd,
            webkit_box_pack::CENTER => Self::Center,
            webkit_box_pack::JUSTIFY => Self::SpaceBetween,
            _ => unreachable!("invalid -webkit-box-pack value"),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn justify_content_of(style: ComputedValuesView<'_>) -> (Self, OverflowSafety) {
        let keyword = match style.justify_content() {
            justify_content::NORMAL => Self::Normal,
            justify_content::STRETCH => Self::Stretch,
            justify_content::SPACE_BETWEEN => Self::SpaceBetween,
            justify_content::SPACE_AROUND => Self::SpaceAround,
            justify_content::SPACE_EVENLY => Self::SpaceEvenly,
            justify_content::CENTER => Self::Center,
            justify_content::START => Self::Start,
            justify_content::END => Self::End,
            justify_content::FLEX_START => Self::FlexStart,
            justify_content::FLEX_END => Self::FlexEnd,
            justify_content::LEFT => Self::Left,
            justify_content::RIGHT => Self::Right,
            _ => unreachable!("invalid justify-content value"),
        };
        (keyword, OverflowSafety::of(style.justify_content_overflow()))
    }

    /// The align-content keyword of a container styled `style` and its safety.
    /// AD-HOC: Baseline values align as flex-start rather than with their fallback alignment, matching other engines.
    pub(crate) fn align_content_of(style: ComputedValuesView<'_>) -> (Self, OverflowSafety) {
        let keyword = match style.align_content() {
            align_content::NORMAL => Self::Normal,
            align_content::STRETCH => Self::Stretch,
            align_content::SPACE_BETWEEN => Self::SpaceBetween,
            align_content::SPACE_AROUND => Self::SpaceAround,
            align_content::SPACE_EVENLY => Self::SpaceEvenly,
            align_content::CENTER => Self::Center,
            align_content::START => Self::Start,
            align_content::END => Self::End,
            align_content::FLEX_START | align_content::BASELINE => Self::FlexStart,
            align_content::FLEX_END => Self::FlexEnd,
            _ => unreachable!("invalid align-content value"),
        };
        (keyword, OverflowSafety::of(style.align_content_overflow()))
    }

    /// The alignment of the content of a container along an axis with the directions `directions`.
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align-3/#distribution-values
    pub(crate) fn resolve(self, safety: OverflowSafety, directions: AxisDirections) -> ContentAlignment {
        let edge = AxisEdge::low_side_if;
        let flex_start = edge(directions.flex_start_is_low);
        let (distribution, packed_against) = match self {
            // normal: [...] behaves as stretch.
            // stretch: The default fallback alignment for this value is flex-start.
            Self::Normal | Self::Stretch => (Some(ContentDistribution::Stretch), flex_start),
            // space-between: The default fallback alignment for this value is flex-start.
            Self::SpaceBetween => (Some(ContentDistribution::SpaceBetween), flex_start),
            // space-around: The default fallback alignment for this value is safe center.
            Self::SpaceAround => (Some(ContentDistribution::SpaceAround), AxisEdge::Center),
            // space-evenly: The default fallback alignment for this value is safe center.
            Self::SpaceEvenly => (Some(ContentDistribution::SpaceEvenly), AxisEdge::Center),
            Self::Center => (None, AxisEdge::Center),
            Self::Start => (None, edge(directions.container_start_is_low)),
            Self::End => (None, edge(!directions.container_start_is_low)),
            Self::FlexStart => (None, flex_start),
            Self::FlexEnd => (None, flex_start.reversed()),
            Self::Left => (None, edge(directions.left_is_low())),
            Self::Right => (None, edge(directions.right_is_low())),
        };
        ContentAlignment {
            distribution,
            edge: packed_against,
            safety,
            container_start: edge(directions.container_start_is_low),
        }
    }
}

/// The alignment of the contents of a block container styled `style` along its block axis.
pub(crate) fn block_container_content_alignment(style: ComputedValuesView<'_>) -> ContentAlignment {
    let (keyword, safety) = ContentKeyword::align_content_of(style);
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align-3/#baseline-values
    // The fallback alignment for last baseline is safe end.
    let keyword = if style.align_content_is_last_baseline() {
        ContentKeyword::End
    } else {
        keyword
    };
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align-3/#distribution-block
    // If a <content-distribution> is specified its fallback alignment is used instead.
    keyword.resolve(safety, AxisDirections::of(true, None))
}

/// How a table cell aligns its contents along the block axis.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum CellAlignment {
    /// The first baseline of the cell lines up with the baseline of the first row it spans.
    Baseline,
    Content(ContentAlignment),
}

/// The alignment of the contents of a table cell styled `style`. align-content applies to table cells, where a value
/// other than normal overrides vertical-align: https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align-3/#distribution-block
/// Of the vertical-align values, "the following values apply to cells: baseline, top, middle, bottom", while the others
/// "do not apply to cells; the cell is aligned at the baseline instead": https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#height-layout
pub(crate) fn cell_alignment(style: StyleValues<'_>) -> CellAlignment {
    match style.align_content() {
        align_content::NORMAL => {}
        align_content::BASELINE if !style.align_content_is_last_baseline() => return CellAlignment::Baseline,
        _ => return CellAlignment::Content(block_container_content_alignment(*style)),
    }
    if !style.vertical_align_is_keyword() {
        return CellAlignment::Baseline;
    }
    let keyword = match style.vertical_align_keyword() {
        vertical_align::TOP => ContentKeyword::Start,
        vertical_align::MIDDLE => ContentKeyword::Center,
        vertical_align::BOTTOM => ContentKeyword::End,
        _ => return CellAlignment::Baseline,
    };
    CellAlignment::Content(keyword.resolve(OverflowSafety::Unsafe, AxisDirections::of(true, None)))
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align-3/#distribution-values
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum ContentDistribution {
    Stretch,
    SpaceBetween,
    SpaceAround,
    SpaceEvenly,
}

/// How a container aligns its content along an axis.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct ContentAlignment {
    /// How free space is distributed between the alignment subjects, if it is.
    pub(crate) distribution: Option<ContentDistribution>,
    /// The edge the alignment subjects are packed against: their position, or the fallback alignment of their
    /// distribution.
    pub(crate) edge: AxisEdge,
    pub(crate) safety: OverflowSafety,
    /// The edge of the alignment container's start side.
    pub(crate) container_start: AxisEdge,
}

impl ContentAlignment {
    /// The offset from the low side of the alignment container of its content, as one subject that leaves
    /// `free_space` in the container, in a layout mode whose overflow alignment is `layout_mode_default` where the
    /// style specifies neither safe nor unsafe. The fallback alignments of space-around and space-evenly are safe.
    pub(crate) fn offset(self, free_space: CssPixels, layout_mode_default: OverflowSafety) -> CssPixels {
        let falls_back_safely = matches!(
            self.distribution,
            Some(ContentDistribution::SpaceAround | ContentDistribution::SpaceEvenly)
        ) || self.safety.is_safe(layout_mode_default);
        if free_space < CssPixels::default() && falls_back_safely {
            return self.container_start.offset(free_space);
        }
        self.edge.offset(free_space)
    }

    /// This alignment where the container leaves `free_space` beside its alignment subjects, in a layout mode whose
    /// overflow alignment is `layout_mode_default` where the style specifies neither safe nor unsafe. A safe alignment
    /// packs overflowing subjects against the container's start.
    pub(crate) fn for_free_space(self, free_space: CssPixels, layout_mode_default: OverflowSafety) -> Self {
        if free_space < CssPixels::default() && self.safety.is_safe(layout_mode_default) {
            return Self {
                distribution: None,
                edge: self.container_start,
                ..self
            };
        }
        self
    }

    /// The free space the distribution places before and between `count` alignment subjects, where the container
    /// leaves `free_space` beside them. It distributes no negative free space.
    pub(crate) fn distributed_space(self, free_space: CssPixels, count: usize) -> SpaceDistribution {
        let space = free_space.max(CssPixels::default());
        match self.distribution {
            Some(ContentDistribution::SpaceBetween) => SpaceDistribution::new(space, count.saturating_sub(1), 0, 1),
            Some(ContentDistribution::SpaceAround) => SpaceDistribution::new(space, count * 2, 1, 2),
            Some(ContentDistribution::SpaceEvenly) => SpaceDistribution::new(space, count + 1, 1, 1),
            Some(ContentDistribution::Stretch) | None => SpaceDistribution::default(),
        }
    }
}

/// Free space split into equal shares, placed before a run of boxes and between them. Each share is rounded such that
/// the shares add up to the whole space, instead of losing the rounding remainder of every share.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub(crate) struct SpaceDistribution {
    space: CssPixels,
    shares: usize,
    shares_before_first_box: usize,
    shares_between_boxes: usize,
}

impl SpaceDistribution {
    pub(crate) fn new(
        space: CssPixels,
        shares: usize,
        shares_before_first_box: usize,
        shares_between_boxes: usize,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            space,
            shares,
            shares_before_first_box,
            shares_between_boxes,
        }
    }

    /// The space placed before the box at the given position in the run.
    pub(crate) fn space_before(self, position: usize) -> CssPixels {
        if self.shares == 0 {
            return CssPixels::default();
        }
        let count = (self.shares_before_first_box + position * self.shares_between_boxes).min(self.shares);
        let raw = i64::from(self.space.raw_value()) * count as i64 / self.shares as i64;
        CssPixels::from_raw(raw as i32)
    }

    /// The space placed between the box at the given position and the next one.
    pub(crate) fn space_after(self, position: usize) -> CssPixels {
        self.space_before(position + 1) - self.space_before(position)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn px(value: i64) -> CssPixels {
        CssPixels::from_integer(value)
    }

    fn reversed_axis_with_left_low() -> AxisDirections {
        AxisDirections {
            flex_start_is_low: true,
            self_start_is_low: true,
            ..AxisDirections::of(false, Some(true))
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn self_keywords_name_the_sides_of_their_directions() {
        let directions = reversed_axis_with_left_low();
        let edge_of = |keyword: SelfKeyword| keyword.resolve(OverflowSafety::Default, directions).position;
        assert_eq!(edge_of(SelfKeyword::Start), SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::End));
        assert_eq!(edge_of(SelfKeyword::End), SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::Start));
        assert_eq!(edge_of(SelfKeyword::FlexStart), SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::Start));
        assert_eq!(edge_of(SelfKeyword::SelfEnd), SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::End));
        assert_eq!(edge_of(SelfKeyword::Left), SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::Start));
        assert_eq!(edge_of(SelfKeyword::Right), SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::End));
        assert_eq!(edge_of(SelfKeyword::AnchorCenter), SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::Center));
        assert_eq!(edge_of(SelfKeyword::Normal), SelfPosition::Normal);
    }

    #[test]
    fn left_and_right_behave_as_start_off_the_line_axis() {
        let directions = AxisDirections::of(false, None);
        for keyword in [SelfKeyword::Left, SelfKeyword::Right] {
            assert_eq!(
                keyword.resolve(OverflowSafety::Default, directions).position,
                SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::End)
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn safe_self_alignment_falls_back_to_the_container_start_on_overflow() {
        let directions = reversed_axis_with_left_low();
        let safe = SelfKeyword::FlexStart.resolve(OverflowSafety::Safe, directions);
        assert_eq!(
            safe.position_for(px(10), OverflowSafety::Unsafe),
            SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::Start)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            safe.position_for(px(-10), OverflowSafety::Unsafe),
            SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::End)
        );
        let default = SelfKeyword::FlexStart.resolve(OverflowSafety::Default, directions);
        assert_eq!(
            default.position_for(px(-10), OverflowSafety::Unsafe),
            SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::Start)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            default.position_for(px(-10), OverflowSafety::Safe),
            SelfPosition::Edge(AxisEdge::End)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn content_offsets_follow_the_edge_and_the_distribution_fallbacks() {
        let directions = AxisDirections::of(true, None);
        let offset = |keyword: ContentKeyword, free_space: i64| {
            keyword
                .resolve(OverflowSafety::Default, directions)
                .offset(px(free_space), OverflowSafety::Unsafe)
        };
        assert_eq!(offset(ContentKeyword::Center, -20), px(-10));
        assert_eq!(offset(ContentKeyword::End, 20), px(20));
        assert_eq!(offset(ContentKeyword::SpaceAround, 20), px(10));
        assert_eq!(offset(ContentKeyword::SpaceEvenly, -20), px(0));
        assert_eq!(offset(ContentKeyword::SpaceBetween, 20), px(0));
        assert_eq!(offset(ContentKeyword::Normal, 20), px(0));
    }
}

use super::*;
use crate::css::style::tree::StyleNodeID;
use crate::layout::node_data::DomPaintFact;
use crate::painting::node_painting;
use crate::painting::paint_read::PaintRead;

use crate::painting::record::change_ticks::RowPaintChange;
