                .get_mut(&entry.coordinate_space_box.slot_index())
            {
                Some(pending_fragment) => {
                    pending_fragment.pending_abspos.push(entry);
                    inner.holds_pending_abspos_below_root = true;
                }
                None => inner.pending_abspos_at_root.push(entry),
            }
        }
        let own_candidate = own_anchor_candidate_border_box_rect.map(|border_box_rect| AnchorCandidate {
            node,
            border_box_rect,
            coordinate_space_box: containing_block.unwrap_or(node),
        });
        for mut candidate in anchor_candidates_from_placed_box.into_iter().chain(own_candidate) {
            propagate_payload_into_containing_block_space(
                &mut candidate,
                node,
                containing_block,
                content_offset,
                frames,
            );
            match inner
                .pending_fragments
                .get_mut(&candidate.coordinate_space_box.slot_index())
            {
                Some(pending_fragment) => pending_fragment.anchor_candidates.push(candidate),
                None => inner.anchor_candidates_at_root.push(candidate),
            }
        }
        for mut payload in inline_containing_block_rects_from_placed_box {
            propagate_payload_into_containing_block_space(&mut payload, node, containing_block, content_offset, frames);
            match inner
                .pending_fragments
                .get_mut(&payload.coordinate_space_box.slot_index())
            {
                Some(pending_fragment) => pending_fragment.inline_containing_block_rects.push(payload),
                None => inner.inline_containing_block_rects_at_root.push(payload),
            }
        }
        PlacedFragment {
            fragment,
            exports_payloads,
            abspos_boxes_placed_with_it: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// How many abspos containing block contributions the run has collected so far.
    /// How many abspos containing block info contributions the run has received so far, which only grows.
    pub(crate) fn abspos_containing_block_info_contributions_received(&self) -> u64 {
        self.inner.borrow().abspos_containing_block_info_contributions_received
    }

    fn attach(
        &self,
        pass: &LayoutPass<'_>,
        inner: &mut RunFragmentBuilderInner,
        link: PendingLink,
        containing_block: Option<crate::layout::node_data::NodeSlotId>,
    ) {
        let Some(containing_block) = containing_block else {
            self.push_to_top_scope(pass, inner, link);
            return;
        };
        if containing_block == self.root_node || Some(containing_block.slot_index()) == self.root_containing_block_slot
        {
            self.push_to_top_scope(pass, inner, link);
            return;
        }
        if let Some(pending_fragment) = inner.pending_fragments.get_mut(&containing_block.slot_index()) {
            pending_fragment.children.push(link);
            return;
        }
        // NB: A containing block the run placed already is sealed, so the box goes to the top of the run's fragments.
        if self.is_entry_accumulator || self.with_placements(pass, |placements| placements.is_placed(containing_block))
        {
            inner.holds_links_beside_their_sealed_containing_blocks |= !self.is_entry_accumulator;
            self.push_to_top_scope(pass, inner, link);
            return;
        }
        let mut pending_fragment = PendingFragment::new(containing_block);
        pending_fragment.children.push(link);
        inner
            .pending_fragments
            .insert(containing_block.slot_index(), pending_fragment);
    }

    /// Puts `link` at the top of the run's fragments, with the physical content size of its containing block where the
    /// run placed that block already.
    fn push_to_top_scope(&self, pass: &LayoutPass<'_>, inner: &mut RunFragmentBuilderInner, mut link: PendingLink) {
        if link.containing_block_size.is_none() {
            let containing_block = effective_containing_block(pass, &link);
            link.containing_block_size =
                self.with_placements(pass, |placements| placements.physical_content_size_of(containing_block));
        }
        inner.top_scope_links.push(link);
    }

    pub(crate) fn take_run_contents(&self, pass: &LayoutPass<'_>) -> RunContents {
        debug_assert!(
            !self.is_entry_accumulator,
            "an entry accumulator closes as a pass, not a run"
        );
        self.close(pass)
    }

    pub(crate) fn take_completed_pass(&self, pass: &LayoutPass<'_>) -> CompletedPassFragments {
        debug_assert!(
            self.is_entry_accumulator,
            "an ordinary run closes into the contents of its root"
        );
        let root = self.close(pass);
        // NB: A link at the top of a pass whose containing block the pass did not place, such as the containing block of
        //     a partial relayout's root, keeps the containing block it committed.
        CompletedPassFragments {
            roots: root
                .scoped_descendants
                .into_iter()
                .map(|link| {
                    let containing_block_size = link
                        .containing_block_size
                        .unwrap_or_else(|| committed_content_size_of(pass, effective_containing_block(pass, &link)));
                    link.into_link(containing_block_size)
                })
                .collect(),
        }
    }

    fn close(&self, pass: &LayoutPass<'_>) -> RunContents {
        let mut inner = self.inner.take();
        let mut payloads_past_run = PayloadsPastRun {
            pending_abspos: std::mem::take(&mut inner.pending_abspos_at_root),
            anchor_candidates: std::mem::take(&mut inner.anchor_candidates_at_root),
            inline_containing_block_rects: std::mem::take(&mut inner.inline_containing_block_rects_at_root),
            abspos_containing_block_info: std::mem::take(&mut inner.abspos_containing_block_info_contributions),
        };
        let mut pending_fragments = std::mem::take(&mut inner.pending_fragments);
        for (_, pending_fragment) in pending_fragments.drain() {
            payloads_past_run.pending_abspos.extend(pending_fragment.pending_abspos);
            payloads_past_run
                .anchor_candidates
                .extend(pending_fragment.anchor_candidates);
            payloads_past_run
                .inline_containing_block_rects
                .extend(pending_fragment.inline_containing_block_rects);
            // NB: Every formatting context places the containing blocks of the children it places, or leaves them
            //     unplaced with the children they contain.
            assert!(
                pending_fragment.children.is_empty(),
                "{:?} contains placed children but was never placed",
                pending_fragment.node
            );
        }
        // NB: A child run's root that the run never placed keeps its fragment at the top of the run's fragments, as its
        //     subtree goes with it.
        for ChildLeftUnplaced { root, unplaced_child } in std::mem::take(&mut inner.children_left_unplaced) {
            let node = root.fragment.node;
            let facts = unplaced_child.facts_decided_by_parent;
            let placement = LinkPlacement::of_box(&facts, &unplaced_child.geometry.cells, None, None, pass.frame);
            let link = PendingLink {
                fragment: fragment_of_placed_box(
                    pass,
                    node,
                    Some(root.fragment),
                    Vec::new(),
                    unplaced_child.geometry,
                    facts.fragment_facts.breaks,
                    PendingPayload::default(),
                    FfiCssPixelPoint::default(),
                ),
                offset_in_frame: FfiCssPixelPoint::default(),
                frame: pass.frame,
                placement,
                containing_block_size: None,
            };
            self.push_to_top_scope(pass, &mut inner, link);
        }
        self.with_placements(pass, |placements| {
            for entry in &mut payloads_past_run.pending_abspos {
                debug_assert!(
                    {
                        let containing_block = entry.containing_block();
                        containing_block.is_invalid()
                            || containing_block == self.root_node
                            || !placements.is_placed(containing_block)
                    },
                    "a drainable abspos registration survived its containing block's run (slot {})",
                    entry.child_box.slot_index()
                );
                propagate_payload_toward_run_root_space(entry, self.root_node, placements, pass);
            }
            for candidate in &mut payloads_past_run.anchor_candidates {
                propagate_payload_toward_run_root_space(candidate, self.root_node, placements, pass);
            }
            for payload in &mut payloads_past_run.inline_containing_block_rects {
                propagate_payload_toward_run_root_space(payload, self.root_node, placements, pass);
            }
        });
        let mut placed_boxes = std::mem::take(&mut inner.placed_boxes);
        placed_boxes.placed_slots.clear();
        placed_boxes.cells_of_abspos_containing_blocks.clear();
        return_spare_fragment_builder_buffers(
            pass.worker_scratch(),
            FragmentBuilderBuffers {
                pending_fragments,
                placed_boxes,
            },
        );
        RunContents {
            node: self.root_node,
            scoped_descendants: inner.top_scope_links,
            holds_links_beside_their_sealed_containing_blocks: inner.holds_links_beside_their_sealed_containing_blocks,
            payloads_past_run,
        }
    }
}

// A pass's fragments are an immutable publication that later passes and paintable rows share.
const _: () = {
    const fn assert_send_and_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
    assert_send_and_sync::<CompletedPassFragments>();
};

/*

use super::*;
use std::cell::{RefCell, RefMut};
use std::rc::Rc;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct ColumnGeometry {
    pub(crate) count: usize,
    pub(crate) inline_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) gap: CssPixels,
}

impl ColumnGeometry {
    pub(crate) fn pitch(&self) -> CssPixels {
        self.inline_size + self.gap
    }

    pub(crate) fn column_inline_offset(
        &self,
        index: usize,
        content_inline_size: CssPixels,
        is_right_to_left: bool,
    ) -> CssPixels {
        let offset = self.pitch() * index;
        if is_right_to_left {
            content_inline_size - self.inline_size - offset
        } else {
            offset
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn gap_center(
        &self,
        gap_index: usize,
        content_inline_size: CssPixels,
        is_right_to_left: bool,
    ) -> CssPixels {
        self.column_inline_offset(gap_index, content_inline_size, is_right_to_left)
            .min(self.column_inline_offset(gap_index + 1, content_inline_size, is_right_to_left))
            + self.inline_size
            + self.gap / 2usize
    }
}

pub(crate) fn used_column_gap(style: StyleValues<'_>, percentage_basis: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
    let gap = style.column_gap();
    if gap.is_normal() {
        return style.font_size();
    }
    gap.to_px(percentage_basis).max(CssPixels::default())
}

pub(crate) const MAXIMUM_COLUMN_COUNT: usize = 1000;

pub(crate) fn effects_need_unbroken_box(style: ComputedValuesView<'_>) -> bool {
    crate::painting::style_queries::clip_path_has_value(style.mask())
        || crate::painting::style_queries::has_css_mask_image(style.mask())
        || style.effects().backdrop_filter.operations.length != 0
}

pub(crate) fn resolved_column_count(style: StyleValues<'_>) -> usize {
    (style.column_count().max(1) as usize).min(MAXIMUM_COLUMN_COUNT)
}

pub(crate) fn resolved_column_width(style: StyleValues<'_>, percentage_basis: CssPixels) -> Option<CssPixels> {
    let column_width = style.column_width();
    (!column_width.is_auto()).then(|| column_width.to_px(percentage_basis).max(CssPixels::from_integer(1)))
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-multicol-1/#pseudo-algorithm
pub(crate) fn resolve_column_geometry(style: StyleValues<'_>, available_inline_size: CssPixels) -> ColumnGeometry {
    let available_inline_size = available_inline_size.max(CssPixels::default());
    let gap = used_column_gap(style, available_inline_size);
    let count = match resolved_column_width(style, available_inline_size) {
        // (04) N := column-count
        None => resolved_column_count(style),
        Some(column_width) => {
            // (06) N := max(1, floor((U + column-gap)/(column-width + column-gap)))
            let fitting_count = ((i64::from(available_inline_size.raw_value()) + i64::from(gap.raw_value()))
                / (i64::from(column_width.raw_value()) + i64::from(gap.raw_value())))
            .clamp(1, MAXIMUM_COLUMN_COUNT as i64) as usize;
            if style.has_column_count() {
                // (08) N := min(column-count, max(1, floor((U + column-gap)/(column-width + column-gap))))
                fitting_count.min(resolved_column_count(style))
            } else {
                fitting_count
            }
        }
    };
    // (09) W := max(0, ((U + column-gap)/N - column-gap))
    let inline_size = CssPixels::from_raw(
        ((i64::from(available_inline_size.raw_value()) + i64::from(gap.raw_value())) / count as i64
            - i64::from(gap.raw_value()))
        .max(0) as i32,
    );
    ColumnGeometry {
        count,
        inline_size,
        gap,
    }
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-multicol-1/#intrinsic-sizes
pub(crate) fn multicol_intrinsic_inline_size(
    style: StyleValues<'_>,
    content_inline_size: CssPixels,
    is_min_content: bool,
) -> CssPixels {
    let column_count = if style.has_column_count() {
        resolved_column_count(style)
    } else {
        1
    };
    let gaps = used_column_gap(style, CssPixels::default()) * (column_count - 1);
    let column_width = resolved_column_width(style, CssPixels::default());
    if is_min_content {
        // The min-content inline size of a multi-column container with a computed column-width not auto is the
        // smaller of its column-width and the largest min-content contribution of its contents.
        if let Some(column_width) = column_width {
            return column_width.min(content_inline_size);
        }
        // The min-content inline size of a multi-column container with a computed column-width of auto is the
        // largest min-content contribution of its contents multiplied by its column-count (treating auto as 1),
        // plus its column-gap multiplied by column-count minus 1.
        return content_inline_size * column_count + gaps;
    }
    // The max-content inline size of a multi-column container is the product of its column-count (treating auto
    // as 1) and the larger of its column-width (treating auto as zero) and the largest max-content contribution of
    // its contents, plus its column-gap multiplied by one less than its column-count.
    content_inline_size.max(column_width.unwrap_or_default()) * column_count + gaps
}

pub(crate) fn ceil_divide(value: CssPixels, divisor: usize) -> CssPixels {
    let divisor = divisor.max(1) as i64;
    CssPixels::from_raw(((value.raw_value() as i64 + divisor - 1).div_euclid(divisor)) as i32)
}

pub(crate) fn is_forced_column_break(value: u8) -> bool {
    value == break_between::COLUMN
}

pub(crate) fn avoids_column_break_between(value: u8) -> bool {
    matches!(value, break_between::AVOID | break_between::AVOID_COLUMN)
}

pub(crate) fn avoids_column_break_inside(value: u8) -> bool {
    matches!(value, break_inside::AVOID | break_inside::AVOID_COLUMN)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct ColumnRow {
    pub(crate) block_offset: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) block_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) column_count: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct MulticolLayoutData {
    pub(crate) geometry: ColumnGeometry,
    pub(crate) rows: Vec<ColumnRow>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum BlockResume {
    BeforeChild { child: Node, after_forced_break: bool },
    InsideChild(Rc<BlockBreakToken>),
    AfterChildren,
    AtLine(LinePosition),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct LinePosition {
    pub(crate) item_index: usize,
    pub(crate) offset_in_node: usize,
}

impl LinePosition {
    pub(crate) const AFTER_LAST_LINE: Self = Self {
        item_index: usize::MAX,
        offset_in_node: 0,
    };
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct BlockBreakToken {
    pub(crate) node: Node,
    pub(crate) consumed_block_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) resume: BlockResume,
    pub(crate) deferred_floats: Vec<Node>,
}

impl BlockResume {
    pub(crate) fn resume_child(&self) -> Option<Node> {
        match self {
            BlockResume::BeforeChild { child, .. } => Some(*child),
            BlockResume::InsideChild(token) => Some(token.node),
            BlockResume::AfterChildren | BlockResume::AtLine(_) => None,
        }
    }
}

impl BlockBreakToken {
    pub(crate) fn follows_forced_break(&self) -> bool {
        match &self.resume {
            BlockResume::BeforeChild { after_forced_break, .. } => *after_forced_break,
            BlockResume::InsideChild(token) => token.follows_forced_break(),
            BlockResume::AfterChildren | BlockResume::AtLine(_) => false,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct LineRootFragmentation {
    pub(crate) block_size: Option<CssPixels>,
    pub(crate) resume: Option<LinePosition>,
    pub(crate) deferred_floats: Vec<Node>,
    pub(crate) fragmentainer_had_content: bool,
    pub(crate) break_before_is_avoided: bool,
}

/// The layout of a box in the pass that measures the contents of a multicol container, which later passes over the
/// columns place wherever the box stays unbroken.
pub(super) struct ColumnBoxLayout {
    pub(super) entry: std::sync::Arc<in_flow_block_cache::InFlowBlockEntry>,
    pub(super) fragment: std::sync::Arc<fragment_tree::Fragment>,
    /// How far a column has to reach below the start of the box's border box for nothing in the box to break.
    pub(super) block_size_that_stays_unbroken: CssPixels,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct ColumnBoxLayouts {
    layouts_by_slot: RefCell<HashMap<u32, Rc<ColumnBoxLayout>>>,
}

impl ColumnBoxLayouts {
    pub(super) fn keep(&self, node: Node, layout: ColumnBoxLayout) {
        self.layouts_by_slot
            .borrow_mut()
            .insert(node.slot_index(), Rc::new(layout));
    }

    pub(super) fn layout_of(&self, node: Node) -> Option<Rc<ColumnBoxLayout>> {
        self.layouts_by_slot.borrow().get(&node.slot_index()).cloned()
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct FragmentainerOutcome {
    pub(crate) outgoing: Option<Rc<BlockBreakToken>>,
    pub(crate) needs_early_break_before: Option<Node>,
    pub(crate) minimal_space_shortage: Option<CssPixels>,
    pub(crate) tallest_unbreakable_block_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) violates_break_avoidance: bool,
    pub(crate) overflows: bool,
    /// How far the in-flow content laid out in the fragmentainer reaches: the furthest block end of its boxes and lines,
    /// which a negative margin after them doesn't take back.
    pub(crate) content_block_end: CssPixels,
    /// The furthest block end of the unbreakable lines of a line root inside the box being laid out, which counts toward
    /// `content_block_end` only once that box stays in the fragmentainer.
    pub(crate) pending_nested_lines_block_end: Option<CssPixels>,
}

/// The space a fragmentainer run lays out in: the fragmentainer's size, the break the run continues from, how it
/// breaks, and the memos the columns of a multi-column box share.
pub(crate) struct FragmentainerSpace {
    pub(crate) block_size: Option<CssPixels>,
    pub(crate) honors_forced_breaks: bool,
    pub(crate) incoming: Option<Rc<BlockBreakToken>>,
    pub(crate) inline_items: Rc<inline_level_iterator::InlineItemCache>,
    pub(crate) box_layouts: Rc<ColumnBoxLayouts>,
    /// Whether this run keeps the layouts of its boxes for the passes after it, which place them instead.
    pub(crate) keeps_box_layouts: bool,
    pub(crate) early_break_before: Option<Node>,
    pub(crate) allows_early_break_requests: bool,
}

impl FragmentainerSpace {
    pub(crate) fn exceeds(&self, block_end: CssPixels) -> bool {
        self.block_size.is_some_and(|block_size| block_end > block_size)
    }
}

/// The fragmentainer a run lays out in, as the run sees it: its space, and what the run found out so far about
/// breaking in it, which the run's state keeps.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct Fragmentainer<'run> {
    space: &'run FragmentainerSpace,
    outcome: &'run RefCell<FragmentainerOutcome>,
}

impl std::ops::Deref for Fragmentainer<'_> {
    type Target = FragmentainerSpace;

    fn deref(&self) -> &FragmentainerSpace {
        self.space
    }
}

impl<'run> Fragmentainer<'run> {
    pub(crate) fn new(space: &'run FragmentainerSpace, outcome: &'run RefCell<FragmentainerOutcome>) -> Self {
        Self { space, outcome }
    }

    pub(crate) fn outcome_mut(&self) -> RefMut<'run, FragmentainerOutcome> {
        self.outcome.borrow_mut()
    }

    pub(crate) fn request_early_break_before(&self, node: Node) -> bool {
        if !self.allows_early_break_requests {
            return false;
        }
        let mut outcome = self.outcome.borrow_mut();
        if outcome.needs_early_break_before.is_none() {
            outcome.needs_early_break_before = Some(node);
        }
        true
    }

    pub(crate) fn note_space_shortage(&self, block_end: CssPixels) {
        let Some(block_size) = self.block_size else {
            return;
        };
        let shortage = block_end - block_size;
        if shortage <= CssPixels::default() {
            return;
        }
        let mut outcome = self.outcome.borrow_mut();
        outcome.minimal_space_shortage = Some(
            outcome
                .minimal_space_shortage
                .map_or(shortage, |minimal| minimal.min(shortage)),
        );
    }

    pub(crate) fn note_unbreakable_block_size(&self, block_size: CssPixels) {
        let mut outcome = self.outcome.borrow_mut();
        outcome.tallest_unbreakable_block_size = outcome.tallest_unbreakable_block_size.max(block_size);
    }

    pub(crate) fn note_content_block_end(&self, block_end: CssPixels) {
        let mut outcome = self.outcome.borrow_mut();
        outcome.content_block_end = outcome.content_block_end.max(block_end);
    }

    pub(crate) fn note_pending_nested_lines_block_end(&self, block_end: CssPixels) {
        let mut outcome = self.outcome.borrow_mut();
        outcome.pending_nested_lines_block_end = Some(
            outcome
                .pending_nested_lines_block_end
                .map_or(block_end, |end| end.max(block_end)),
        );
    }

    pub(crate) fn take_pending_nested_lines_block_end(&self) -> Option<CssPixels> {
        self.outcome.borrow_mut().pending_nested_lines_block_end.take()
    }
}

/// What the run of a fragmentainer hands the run of the box the fragmentainer belongs to.
pub(crate) struct FragmentainerRunResult {
    pub(crate) layout: super::formatting_context::LayoutResult,
    pub(crate) outcome: FragmentainerOutcome,
    /// What the run laid out in the fragmentainer, where it builds fragments, as the fragmentainer has no fragment of
    /// its own.
    pub(crate) contents: Option<super::fragment_tree::RunContents>,
    /// The lines the run laid out in the fragmentainer.
    pub(crate) root_line_data: Option<std::sync::Arc<super::inline_content::InlineContent>>,
}

use super::*;
use crate::css::css_pixels::CssPixels;
use crate::css::style::bridge::{FfiFrameSetDimension, FfiFrameSetDimensionUnit};

// NB: Pixel values are integers, as in other browsers. This bound keeps the products below in range of an i64.
const MAXIMUM_PIXEL_VALUE: i64 = i32::MAX as i64;

fn integer_pixels(value: f64) -> i64 {
    value.floor().clamp(0.0, MAXIMUM_PIXEL_VALUE as f64) as i64
}

fn indices_with_unit(input_list: &[FfiFrameSetDimension], unit: FfiFrameSetDimensionUnit) -> Vec<usize> {
    (0..input_list.len())
        .filter(|&index| input_list[index].unit == unit)
        .collect()
}

/// Sets the entries to their share of `space`, in proportion to their values, and answers how much of it they took.
fn scale_entries_to_space(output_list: &mut [i64], indices: &[usize], total: i64, space: i64) -> i64 {
    let mut taken = 0;
    for &index in indices {
        output_list[index] = output_list[index] * space / total;
        taken += output_list[index];
    }
    taken
}

/// Grows the entries by their share of `space`, in proportion to their values, and answers how much of it they took.
fn grow_entries_by_share_of_space(output_list: &mut [i64], indices: &[usize], total: i64, space: i64) -> i64 {
    let mut taken = 0;
    for &index in indices {
        let growth = output_list[index] * space / total;
        output_list[index] += growth;
        taken += growth;
    }
    taken
}

/// Grows each entry by the same amount, and answers how much of `space` they took.
fn grow_entries_equally(output_list: &mut [i64], indices: &[usize], space: i64) -> i64 {
    let growth = space / indices.len() as i64;
    for &index in indices {
        output_list[index] += growth;
    }
    growth * indices.len() as i64
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#convert-a-list-of-dimensions-to-a-list-of-pixel-values
fn convert_a_list_of_dimensions_to_a_list_of_pixel_values(
    input_list: &[FfiFrameSetDimension],
    input_dimension: i64,
) -> Vec<i64> {
    // 1. Let input list be the list of numbers and units passed to the algorithm.
    //    Let output list be a list of numbers the same length as input list, all zero.
    //    Entries in output list correspond to the entries in input list that have the same position.
    let mut output_list = vec![0i64; input_list.len()];

    // 2. Let input dimension be the size passed to the algorithm.
    let absolute_indices = indices_with_unit(input_list, FfiFrameSetDimensionUnit::Absolute);
    let percentage_indices = indices_with_unit(input_list, FfiFrameSetDimensionUnit::Percentage);
    let relative_indices = indices_with_unit(input_list, FfiFrameSetDimensionUnit::Relative);

    // 3. Let total percentage be the sum of all the numbers in input list whose unit is percentage.
    //    Let total relative be the sum of all the numbers in input list whose unit is relative.
    //    Let total absolute be the sum of all the numbers in input list whose unit is absolute.
    //    Let remaining space be the value of input dimension.
    // INTEROP: The totals of absolute and percentage entries are totals of their sizes in integer pixels, and each
    //          relative entry weighs at least one.
    for &index in &absolute_indices {
        output_list[index] = integer_pixels(input_list[index].value);
    }
    for &index in &percentage_indices {
        output_list[index] = integer_pixels(input_list[index].value * input_dimension as f64 / 100.0);
    }
    let relative_weight = |index: usize| integer_pixels(input_list[index].value.max(1.0));
    let total_absolute: i64 = absolute_indices.iter().map(|&index| output_list[index]).sum();
    let total_percentage: i64 = percentage_indices.iter().map(|&index| output_list[index]).sum();
    let total_relative: i64 = relative_indices.iter().map(|&index| relative_weight(index)).sum();
    let mut remaining_space = input_dimension;

    // 4. If total absolute is greater than remaining space, then for each entry in input list whose unit is absolute,
    //    set the corresponding value in output list to the number of the entry in input list multiplied by remaining
    //    space and divided by total absolute. Then, set remaining space to zero.
    //    Otherwise, for each entry in input list whose unit is absolute, set the corresponding value in output list to
    //    the number of the entry in input list. Then, decrement remaining space by total absolute.
    if total_absolute > remaining_space {
        remaining_space -= scale_entries_to_space(&mut output_list, &absolute_indices, total_absolute, remaining_space);
    } else {
        remaining_space -= total_absolute;
    }

    // 5. If total percentage multiplied by the input dimension and divided by 100 is greater than remaining space, then
    //    for each entry in input list whose unit is percentage, set the corresponding value in output list to the
    //    number of the entry in input list multiplied by remaining space and divided by total percentage. Then, set
    //    remaining space to zero.
    //    Otherwise, for each entry in input list whose unit is percentage, set the corresponding value in output list
    //    to the number of the entry in input list multiplied by the input dimension and divided by 100. Then, decrement
    //    remaining space by total percentage multiplied by the input dimension and divided by 100.
    if total_percentage > remaining_space {
        remaining_space -=
            scale_entries_to_space(&mut output_list, &percentage_indices, total_percentage, remaining_space);
    } else {
        remaining_space -= total_percentage;
    }

    // 6. For each entry in input list whose unit is relative, set the corresponding value in output list to the number
    //    of the entry in input list multiplied by remaining space and divided by total relative.
    if let Some(&last_relative_index) = relative_indices.last() {
        let space_for_relative_entries = remaining_space;
        for &index in &relative_indices {
            output_list[index] = relative_weight(index) * space_for_relative_entries / total_relative;
            remaining_space -= output_list[index];
        }
        // User agents working with integer values for frame widths (as opposed to user agents that can lay frames out
        // with subpixel accuracy) are expected to distribute the remainder first to the last entry whose unit is
        // relative, then equally (not proportionally) to each entry whose unit is percentage, then equally (not
        // proportionally) to each entry whose unit is absolute, and finally, failing all else, to the last entry.
        output_list[last_relative_index] += remaining_space;
        remaining_space = 0;
    }

    // INTEROP: Space that no relative entry takes goes to the percentage entries in proportion to their sizes, or
    //          failing that, to the absolute entries in proportion to theirs. Only what rounding leaves over is
    //          distributed equally.
    if remaining_space > 0 && total_percentage > 0 {
        let space = remaining_space;
        remaining_space -=
            grow_entries_by_share_of_space(&mut output_list, &percentage_indices, total_percentage, space);
    } else if remaining_space > 0 && total_absolute > 0 {
        let space = remaining_space;
        remaining_space -= grow_entries_by_share_of_space(&mut output_list, &absolute_indices, total_absolute, space);
    }
    if remaining_space > 0 && !percentage_indices.is_empty() {
        remaining_space -= grow_entries_equally(&mut output_list, &percentage_indices, remaining_space);
    } else if remaining_space > 0 && !absolute_indices.is_empty() {
        remaining_space -= grow_entries_equally(&mut output_list, &absolute_indices, remaining_space);
    }
    if remaining_space > 0
        && let Some(last) = output_list.last_mut()
    {
        *last += remaining_space;
    }

    // 7. Return output list.
    output_list
}

/// The sizes of a frameset's tracks along an axis of its surface.
// INTEROP: The specification draws borders on the rectangles. In other browsers, the borders between tracks take their
//          space from the tracks.
pub(crate) fn frameset_track_sizes(
    dimensions: &[FfiFrameSetDimension],
    surface_size: CssPixels,
    border_thickness: u32,
) -> Vec<CssPixels> {
    let borders = (dimensions.len() as i64 - 1).max(0) * i64::from(border_thickness);
    let input_dimension = (i64::from(surface_size.to_int()) - borders).max(0);
    convert_a_list_of_dimensions_to_a_list_of_pixel_values(dimensions, input_dimension)
        .into_iter()
        .map(CssPixels::from_integer)
        .collect()
}

fn layout_frameset_child(
    run: &formatting_context::FormattingContextRun,
    child: Node,
    size: (CssPixels, CssPixels),
    offset: used_values::FfiCssPixelPoint,
) {
    let (inline_size, block_size) = size;
    let constraints = geometry::ContainingBlockConstraints {
        percentage_basis_inline_size: Some(inline_size),
        percentage_basis_block_size: Some(block_size),
        quirks_mode_percentage_basis_block_size: None,
    };
    let mut cells = used_values::cells_before_sizing(&run.pass, child, constraints);
    let style = StyleValues::for_node(&run.pass, child);
    cells.border_left = style.border_left_width();
    cells.border_right = style.border_right_width();
    cells.border_top = style.border_top_width();
    cells.border_bottom = style.border_bottom_width();
    cells.padding_left = style.padding_left().to_px(inline_size);
    cells.padding_right = style.padding_right().to_px(inline_size);
    cells.padding_top = style.padding_top().to_px(inline_size);
    cells.padding_bottom = style.padding_bottom().to_px(inline_size);
    cells.set_content_inline_size(
        (inline_size - cells.border_left - cells.padding_left - cells.padding_right - cells.border_right)
            .max(CssPixels::default()),
    );
    cells.set_content_block_size(
        (block_size - cells.border_top - cells.padding_top - cells.padding_bottom - cells.border_bottom)
            .max(CssPixels::default()),
    );
    let offset = used_values::FfiCssPixelPoint {
        x: offset.x + cells.border_left + cells.padding_left,
        y: offset.y + cells.border_top + cells.padding_top,
    };
    let plan = formatting_context::ChildRunPlan {
        fc_type: formatting_context::independent_formatting_context_type(child, &run.pass),
        root_containing_block: run.pass.in_flow_containing_block(child),
        input: geometry::LayoutInput {
            available_space: geometry::AvailableSpace {
                inline_size: geometry::AvailableSize::definite(inline_size),
                block_size: geometry::AvailableSize::definite(block_size),
            },
            containing_block_constraints: constraints,
            sizing: geometry::RootSizingDirectives::default(),
            participation: geometry::ParticipationInParentFormattingContext::Item,
        },
    };
    let outcome = formatting_context::run_formatting_context(
        run.pass,
        formatting_context::RunRequest::of_child(run, child, plan, cells),
        formatting_context::RunSideInputs::default(),
    );
    formatting_context::place_child(
        run,
        child,
        outcome.placed_child(),
        offset,
        None,
        outcome.into_fragment_arrival(run),
    );
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#frames-and-framesets
/// The formatting context of a frameset, which lays its frames out in the grid of its rows and columns.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct FrameSetFormattingContext;

impl<'pass> formatting_context::FormattingContextAlgorithm<'pass> for FrameSetFormattingContext {
    fn lay_out(
        &mut self,
        run: &formatting_context::FormattingContextRun<'pass>,
        input: formatting_context::AlgorithmInput<'_>,
    ) -> formatting_context::AlgorithmOutput {
        let mut root = input.root_cells;
        let result = layout_frameset(run, &mut root);
        formatting_context::AlgorithmOutput::of_root(result, root)
    }
}

fn layout_frameset(
    run: &formatting_context::FormattingContextRun,
    root: &mut used_values::RootInputCells,
) -> formatting_context::ChildLayoutResult {
    // NB: The UA style sheet gives a frameset the size of the viewport, and a nested frameset has both sizes from its
    //     rectangle.
    let (surface_inline_size, surface_block_size) = (root.content_inline_size, root.content_block_size);
    root.has_definite_inline_size = true;
    root.has_definite_block_size = true;
    let result = formatting_context::ChildLayoutResult {
        automatic_content_block_size: surface_block_size,
        ..formatting_context::ChildLayoutResult::default()
    };

    let layout = run
        .pass
        .arena()
        .replaced_paint_facts(run.box_)
        .and_then(|facts| facts.frameset());
    let mut children = run.pass.children(run.box_);

    if let Some(layout) = layout {
        // 4. Invoke the algorithm defined below to convert a list of dimensions to a list of pixel values using cols as
        //    the input list, and the width of the surface that the frameset is being rendered into, in CSS pixels, as
        //    the input dimension. Let sized cols be the resulting list.
        //    Invoke the algorithm defined below to convert a list of dimensions to a list of pixel values using rows as
        //    the input list, and the height of the surface that the frameset is being rendered into, in CSS pixels, as
        //    the input dimension. Let sized rows be the resulting list.
        let sized_cols = frameset_track_sizes(&layout.columns, surface_inline_size, layout.border_thickness);
        let sized_rows = frameset_track_sizes(&layout.rows, surface_block_size, layout.border_thickness);
        let border_thickness = CssPixels::from_integer(i64::from(layout.border_thickness));

        // 5. Split the surface into a grid of w×h rectangles, where w is the number of entries in sized cols and h is
        //    the number of entries in sized rows.
        //    Size the columns so that each column in the grid is as many CSS pixels wide as the corresponding entry in
        //    the sized cols list.
        //    Size the rows so that each row in the grid is as many CSS pixels high as the corresponding entry in the
        //    sized rows list.
        // 6. Let children be the list of frame and frameset elements that are children of the frameset element for which
        //    the algorithm was invoked.
        // 7. For each row of the grid of rectangles created in the previous step, from top to bottom, run these substeps:
        let mut y = CssPixels::default();
        'rows: for &row_size in &sized_rows {
            // 1. For each rectangle in the row, from left to right, run these substeps:
            let mut x = CssPixels::default();
            for &column_size in &sized_cols {
                // 1. If there are any elements left in children, take the first element in the list, and assign it to
                //    the rectangle.
                //    If this is a frameset element, then recurse the entire frameset layout algorithm for that frameset
                //    element, with the rectangle as the surface.
                //    Otherwise, it is a frame element; render its content navigable, positioned and sized to fit the
                //    rectangle.
                // 2. If there are any elements left in children, remove the first element from children.
                let Some(child) = children.next() else {
                    break 'rows;
                };
                layout_frameset_child(
                    run,
                    child,
                    (column_size, row_size),
                    used_values::FfiCssPixelPoint { x, y },
                );
                x += column_size + border_thickness;
            }
            y += row_size + border_thickness;
        }
    }

    // NB: Children that the grid has no rectangle for are not rendered. They still get a box, of no size.
    for child in children {
        layout_frameset_child(
            run,
            child,
            (CssPixels::default(), CssPixels::default()),
            used_values::FfiCssPixelPoint::default(),
        );
    }
    result
}

//! What the layout tree build puts inside a pseudo-element's box: its `content` resolved against the
//! counters sets and the quote depth, or the marker string of a list marker whose `content` is
//! `normal`.

use super::counters::{CounterName, CounterOwner, CountersSets, LIST_ITEM_COUNTER_NAME};
use super::layout_node_arena::LayoutNodeArena;
use crate::css::computed_value_views::ComputedValuesView;
use crate::css::counter_representation::{
    CounterStyle, decimal, generate_a_counter_representation, resolve_counter_style_value,
};
use crate::css::css_enums::keyword;
use crate::css::style::tree::StyleNodeID;
use crate::css::style_value::{COUNTER_FUNCTION_COUNTER, StyleValueData};
use crate::css::style_value::{ContentPayload, CounterPayload};
use std::sync::Arc;

/// What a list marker whose `content` is `normal` shows, resolved from the published records of the
/// marker box and of the list item box it belongs to.
pub(crate) enum MarkerContent<'a> {
    Image,
    String(&'a [u16]),
    /// A counter style, or `None` for a name that resolves to none.
    CounterStyle(Option<Arc<CounterStyle>>),
}

/// What the tree build recorded for the generated content of each pseudo-element it built a box for.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(crate) struct GeneratedContent {
    /// The text each pseudo-element's content resolved to, the way accessibility reads it.
    accessible_texts: crate::cow_map::CowMap<CounterOwner, Vec<u16>>,
    /// The counter styles the box built for a pseudo-element was rendered from, one per
    /// `counter()` or `counters()` the content names and one for the counter style a normal
    /// marker shows. A later style change compares what the pseudo-element's record names now
    /// against this to decide whether the box has to be rebuilt.
    content_counter_styles_in_use: crate::cow_map::CowMap<CounterOwner, Vec<Option<Arc<CounterStyle>>>>,
}

impl GeneratedContent {
    /// The text the content of `owner` last resolved to, the way accessibility reads it: the alt text
    /// when there is one, otherwise every string in order.
    pub(crate) fn accessible_text(&self, owner: CounterOwner) -> &[u16] {
        self.accessible_texts.get(&owner).map_or(&[], Vec::as_slice)
    }

    /// Whether the content `owner` last resolved to shows the value of a counter, which a counter changing before it
    /// changes: a `counter()` or `counters()` of its content, or the counter style its marker shows, that represents
    /// some values differently.
    pub(crate) fn shows_counter_value(&self, owner: CounterOwner) -> bool {
        self.content_counter_styles_in_use.get(&owner).is_some_and(|styles| {
            styles
                .iter()
                .any(|style| style.as_deref().is_none_or(|style| !style.representation_is_constant()))
        })
    }

    /// Records what the content of `owner`, which a build just made the box of, resolved to: the counter styles its box
    /// renders from, and its accessible text.
    pub(crate) fn note_content(&mut self, owner: CounterOwner, record: ContentRecord) {
        let ContentRecord {
            counter_styles,
            accessible_text,
        } = record;
        match accessible_text {
            AccessibleText::Unchanged => {}
            AccessibleText::Remove => {
                self.accessible_texts.remove(&owner);
            }
            AccessibleText::Set(text) => {
                self.accessible_texts.insert(owner, text);
            }
            AccessibleText::Pending => unreachable!("a content is recorded once its accessible text is known"),
        }
        self.content_counter_styles_in_use.insert(owner, counter_styles);
    }

    /// Drops everything kept for an element's pseudo-elements, once its identity is retired.
    pub(crate) fn forget(&mut self, element: StyleNodeID) {
        // NB: One lookup per owner, not a walk over every pseudo-element of the document: a removed
        //     subtree retires its identities one at a time.
        for owner in CounterOwner::every_owner_of(element) {
            self.accessible_texts.remove(&owner);
            self.content_counter_styles_in_use.remove(&owner);
        }
    }
}

/// What the generated content of a pseudo-element records for later builds and for accessibility, see
/// [`GeneratedContent`].
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct ContentRecord {
    pub(crate) counter_styles: Vec<Option<Arc<CounterStyle>>>,
    pub(crate) accessible_text: AccessibleText,
}

/// The text of a pseudo-element's content the way accessibility reads it.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) enum AccessibleText {
    /// A list marker whose `content` is `normal` leaves what is recorded as it was.
    Unchanged,
    /// A content that is no list has none.
    Remove,
    Set(Vec<u16>),
    /// The text shows counter values or quotes not known yet.
    Pending,
}

/// One thing to put in a pseudo-element's box, in order.
pub(crate) enum ContentItem {
    /// A text, `None` until the counter values or the quote depth it shows are known. A text of `close-quote`s alone
    /// that closes no quote is not `made`: it puts nothing in the box.
    Text { text: Option<Vec<u16>>, made: bool },
    /// The `<image>` at this index of the `content` list.
    Image(usize),
}

/// What a pseudo-element's `content` resolved to, see [`resolve_content`].
pub(crate) struct ResolvedContent {
    pub(crate) items: Vec<ContentItem>,
    /// Whether the content is a list of items, as opposed to `normal` or `none`.
    pub(crate) is_list: bool,
    pub(crate) counter_styles: Vec<Option<Arc<CounterStyle>>>,
    pub(crate) accessible_text: AccessibleText,
    /// Whether the content shows the value of the `list-item` counter, which the document tracks to
    /// know when renumbering a list changed what is rendered.
    pub(crate) renders_list_item_counter_value: bool,
}

/// Where the values of the counters a pseudo-element's content shows come from: the counters set of the
/// pseudo-element.
pub(crate) trait CounterValues {
    /// The value of the innermost counter named `name` in the set, which instantiates one at 0 where the set holds
    /// none.
    fn innermost(&mut self, name: &[u16]) -> i32;
    /// The values of every counter named `name` in the set, outermost first, which instantiates one at 0 where the set
    /// holds none.
    fn every(&mut self, name: &[u16]) -> Vec<i32>;
}

/// The counters sets the arena stores, which a pseudo-element whose counters a build resolves after its commit reads.
pub(crate) struct StoredCounterValues<'a> {
    pub(crate) arena: &'a LayoutNodeArena,
    pub(crate) sets: &'a mut CountersSets,
    pub(crate) owner: CounterOwner,
}

impl CounterValues for StoredCounterValues<'_> {
    fn innermost(&mut self, name: &[u16]) -> i32 {
        self.sets
            .counter_value_for_use(self.arena, self.owner, &CounterName::Units(name))
    }

    fn every(&mut self, name: &[u16]) -> Vec<i32> {
        self.sets
            .counter_values_for_use(self.arena, self.owner, &CounterName::Units(name))
    }
}

fn representation(
    arena: &LayoutNodeArena,
    tree_scope: u32,
    counter_style: Option<&CounterStyle>,
    value: i32,
) -> Vec<u16> {
    arena.with_counter_style_registry(|registry| {
        generate_a_counter_representation(registry, tree_scope, counter_style, value)
    })
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#text-markers
/// What a list marker whose `content` is `normal` shows, resolved from the marker's own
/// `list-style-image` and the list item's `list-style-type`. The build and the comparison after a
/// style change both answer through this, so they cannot disagree about what the marker shows.
pub(crate) fn marker_content<'a>(
    arena: &LayoutNodeArena,
    tree_scope: u32,
    marker_style: ComputedValuesView<'a>,
    list_item_style: ComputedValuesView<'a>,
) -> MarkerContent<'a> {
    if marker_style.list_style_image_is_set() {
        return MarkerContent::Image;
    }
    let list_style_type = list_item_style.inherited_list().list_style_type.data();
    if let Some(StyleValueData::String { string, .. }) = list_style_type {
        return MarkerContent::String(string.units());
    }
    MarkerContent::CounterStyle(
        arena
            .with_counter_style_registry(|registry| resolve_counter_style_value(registry, tree_scope, list_style_type)),
    )
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#text-markers
// "<counter-style>: Specifies the element's marker string as the value of the list-item counter
// represented using the specified <counter-style>. Specifically, the marker string is the result of
// generating a counter representation of the list-item counter value using the specified
// <counter-style>, prefixed by the prefix of the <counter-style>, and followed by the suffix of the
// <counter-style>. If the specified <counter-style> does not exist, decimal is assumed.
// <string>: The element's marker string is the specified <string>."
/// The marker string of a list marker whose `content` is `normal` and which shows the value `value` of the `list-item`
/// counter in `counter_style`, or in decimal for none.
pub(crate) fn marker_counter_text(
    arena: &LayoutNodeArena,
    tree_scope: u32,
    counter_style: Option<&CounterStyle>,
    value: i32,
) -> Vec<u16> {
    let counter_style = counter_style.unwrap_or(decimal());
    let counter_representation = representation(arena, tree_scope, Some(counter_style), value);
    [&*counter_style.prefix, &counter_representation, &*counter_style.suffix].concat()
}

/// The counter style a normal marker renders from, as the list its box records for a later style
/// change to compare against. A marker showing an image or a string renders from none.
pub(crate) fn marker_counter_styles_in_use(content: &MarkerContent<'_>) -> Vec<Option<Arc<CounterStyle>>> {
    match content {
        MarkerContent::CounterStyle(counter_style) => vec![counter_style.clone()],
        MarkerContent::Image | MarkerContent::String(_) => Vec::new(),
    }
}

enum QuotesData<'a> {
    None,
    Auto,
    Specified(&'a [crate::css::style_value::RetainedStyleValueData]),
}

fn quotes_data(value: Option<&StyleValueData>) -> QuotesData<'_> {
    match value {
        Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) if *keyword == keyword::NONE => QuotesData::None,
        Some(StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. }) => {
            let values = values.as_slice();
            assert!(values.len().is_multiple_of(2));
            QuotesData::Specified(values)
        }
        _ => QuotesData::Auto,
    }
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn unicode_quotation_mark(
        language: *const u16,
        length: usize,
        open: bool,
        alternate: bool,
        result: *mut *const u16,
    ) -> usize;
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[unsafe(export_name = "unicode_quotation_mark")]
extern "C" fn quotation_mark_test_stub(_: *const u16, _: usize, _: bool, _: bool, _: *mut *const u16) -> usize {
    0
}

fn append_quote(text: &mut Vec<u16>, quotes: &QuotesData<'_>, open: bool, depth: u32, language: &[u16]) {
    let mark: &[u16] = match quotes {
        QuotesData::None => &[],
        QuotesData::Auto => {
            if !language.is_empty() {
                let mut mark = std::ptr::null();
                // SAFETY: The language is readable during the call. The thread's locale cache owns the returned mark.
                let length = unsafe {
                    unicode_quotation_mark(language.as_ptr(), language.len(), open, depth != 0, &raw mut mark)
                };
                if length != 0 {
                    text.extend_from_slice(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(mark, length) });
                    return;
                }
            }
            match (open, depth) {
                (true, 0) => &[0x201C],
                (true, _) => &[0x2018],
                (false, 0) => &[0x201D],
                (false, _) => &[0x2019],
            }
        }
        QuotesData::Specified(values) => {
            // If the depth is greater than the number of pairs, the last pair is repeated.
            let Some(last_pair) = (values.len() / 2).checked_sub(1) else {
                return;
            };
            let level = (depth as usize).min(last_pair);
            let quote = &values[level * 2 + usize::from(!open)];
            match quote.optional_data() {
                Some(StyleValueData::String { string, .. }) => string.units(),
                _ => panic!("a quote is a string"),
            }
        }
    };
    text.extend_from_slice(mark);
}

// counter( <counter-name>, <counter-style>? )
// counters( <counter-name>, <string>, <counter-style>? )
fn counter_text(
    arena: &LayoutNodeArena,
    tree_scope: u32,
    values: &mut dyn CounterValues,
    counter_style: Option<&CounterStyle>,
    counter_payload: &CounterPayload,
) -> Vec<u16> {
    let CounterPayload {
        function,
        counter_name,
        join_string,
        ..
    } = counter_payload;
    // "If no counter named <counter-name> exists on an element where counter() or counters() is used,
    // one is first instantiated with a starting value of 0."
    // "Represents the value of the innermost counter in the element’s CSS counters set named <counter-name>
    // using the counter style named <counter-style>."
    if *function == COUNTER_FUNCTION_COUNTER {
        let value = values.innermost(counter_name.units());
        return representation(arena, tree_scope, counter_style, value);
    }

    // "Represents the values of all the counters in the element’s CSS counters set named <counter-name>
    // using the counter style named <counter-style>, sorted in outermost-first to innermost-last order
    // and joined by the specified <string>."
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    for value in values.every(counter_name.units()) {
        let counter_string = representation(arena, tree_scope, counter_style, value);
        if !result.is_empty() {
            result.extend_from_slice(join_string.units());
        }
        result.extend_from_slice(&counter_string);
    }
    result
}

/// The counter styles a `content` value names, in the order they appear in the content list and
/// then in its alt text; `None` for a name no scope in the chain registers, which reads as
/// `decimal`.
fn content_counter_styles(
    arena: &LayoutNodeArena,
    content: Option<&StyleValueData>,
    tree_scope: u32,
) -> Vec<Option<Arc<CounterStyle>>> {
    let Some(StyleValueData::Content(content_payload)) = content else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let ContentPayload {
        content: content_list,
        alt_text,
    } = &**content_payload;
    let mut styles = Vec::new();
    arena.with_counter_style_registry(|registry| {
        for list in [content_list.optional_data(), alt_text.optional_data()] {
            for item in value_list(list) {
                if let Some(StyleValueData::Counter(counter_payload)) = item.optional_data() {
                    let CounterPayload { counter_style, .. } = &**counter_payload;
                    styles.push(resolve_counter_style_value(
                        registry,
                        tree_scope,
                        counter_style.optional_data(),
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
    });
    styles
}

/// Calls `visit` with the name of every counter a `counter()` or `counters()` of the content `style` gives a
/// pseudo-element uses, in its content list and then in its alt text, as resolving the content uses them. A list marker
/// whose content is `normal` uses the `list-item` counter instead, unless it shows an image.
pub(crate) fn for_each_counter_name_content_uses(
    style: ComputedValuesView<'_>,
    is_list_item_marker: bool,
    mut visit: impl FnMut(&[u16]),
) {
    let content = style.content_value();
    if is_list_item_marker && content_is_normal(content) {
        if !style.list_style_image_is_set() {
            visit(&LIST_ITEM_COUNTER_NAME);
        }
        return;
    }
    let Some(StyleValueData::Content(content_payload)) = content else {
        return;
    };
    let ContentPayload {
        content: content_list,
        alt_text,
    } = &**content_payload;
    for list in [content_list.optional_data(), alt_text.optional_data()] {
        for item in value_list(list) {
            if let Some(StyleValueData::Counter(counter_payload)) = item.optional_data() {
                visit(counter_payload.counter_name.units());
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Whether the content of a pseudo-element whose style is `style` makes no text but white space, as far as can be told
/// before counters and quotes are resolved: its items are strings of white space, and keywords and items that make no
/// text. A counter, a quote and an image make content that is not white space.
pub(crate) fn content_is_white_space(style: ComputedValuesView<'_>) -> bool {
    let Some(StyleValueData::Content(content_payload)) = style.content_value() else {
        return false;
    };
    value_list(content_payload.content.optional_data())
        .iter()
        .all(|item| match item.optional_data() {
            Some(StyleValueData::String { string, .. }) => {
                string.units().iter().all(|unit| matches!(unit, 0x09..=0x0d | 0x20))
            }
            Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) => {
                !matches!(*keyword, keyword::OPEN_QUOTE | keyword::CLOSE_QUOTE)
            }
            Some(StyleValueData::Counter(_) | StyleValueData::Image { .. } | StyleValueData::ImageSet { .. }) => false,
            _ => true,
        })
}

fn value_list(value: Option<&StyleValueData>) -> &[crate::css::style_value::RetainedStyleValueData] {
    match value {
        Some(StyleValueData::ValueList { values, .. }) => values.as_slice(),
        _ => &[],
    }
}

pub(crate) fn content_is_normal(content: Option<&StyleValueData>) -> bool {
    matches!(content, Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) if *keyword == keyword::NORMAL)
}

/// The text of a run of strings and quotes of a `content` list, one item of the content, as far as the walk over the list
/// got: the quotes need the depth to be spelled.
struct TextRun {
    text: Vec<u16>,
    made: bool,
    shows_quote_depth: bool,
}

/// Resolves the `content` of a pseudo-element of `element`, whose style is `style`: the items it puts in the
/// pseudo-element's box, and what is recorded of it. With the quote depth before the content and the values of the
/// counters of the pseudo-element, every text is known; without them, the items are those it makes either way, but the
/// texts that show the depth or a value, which are `None`. A list marker whose `content` is `normal` shows its marker
/// string instead, which the caller resolves (see [`marker_content`]).
pub(crate) fn resolve_content(
    arena: &LayoutNodeArena,
    tree_scope: u32,
    style: ComputedValuesView<'_>,
    quote_depth: Option<u32>,
    quote_language: &[u16],
    mut values: Option<&mut dyn CounterValues>,
) -> ResolvedContent {
    let content = style.content_value();
    let counter_styles = content_counter_styles(arena, content, tree_scope);
    let Some(StyleValueData::Content(content_payload)) = content else {
        return ResolvedContent {
            items: Vec::new(),
            is_list: false,
            counter_styles,
            accessible_text: AccessibleText::Remove,
            renders_list_item_counter_value: false,
        };
    };
    let ContentPayload {
        content: content_list,
        alt_text,
    } = &**content_payload;
    let quotes = quotes_data(style.quotes_value());
    let mut quote_nesting_level = quote_depth;
    let mut next_counter_style = 0;
    let mut renders_list_item_counter_value = false;

    let mut items = Vec::new();
    let mut pending_text: Option<TextRun> = None;
    let flush_pending_text = |items: &mut Vec<ContentItem>, pending_text: &mut Option<TextRun>| {
        if let Some(run) = pending_text.take() {
            items.push(ContentItem::Text {
                made: run.made || run.shows_quote_depth && quote_depth.is_none(),
                text: (!run.shows_quote_depth || quote_depth.is_some()).then_some(run.text),
            });
        }
    };
    let new_run = || TextRun {
        text: Vec::new(),
        made: false,
        shows_quote_depth: false,
    };
    let mut resolve_counter = |counter_payload: &CounterPayload, values: &mut Option<&mut dyn CounterValues>| {
        if counter_payload.counter_name.units() == LIST_ITEM_COUNTER_NAME {
            renders_list_item_counter_value = true;
        }
        let counter_style = counter_styles[next_counter_style].as_deref();
        next_counter_style += 1;
        values
            .as_deref_mut()
            .map(|values| counter_text(arena, tree_scope, values, counter_style, counter_payload))
    };

    for (index, item) in value_list(content_list.optional_data()).iter().enumerate() {
        match item.optional_data() {
            Some(StyleValueData::String { string, .. }) => {
                let run = pending_text.get_or_insert_with(new_run);
                run.made = true;
                run.text.extend_from_slice(string.units());
            }
            Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) => match *keyword {
                keyword::OPEN_QUOTE => {
                    let run = pending_text.get_or_insert_with(new_run);
                    run.made = true;
                    run.shows_quote_depth = true;
                    if let Some(level) = &mut quote_nesting_level {
                        append_quote(&mut run.text, &quotes, true, *level, quote_language);
                        *level += 1;
                    }
                }
                keyword::CLOSE_QUOTE => {
                    // A 'close-quote' or 'no-close-quote' that would make the depth negative is in error and is ignored
                    // (at rendering time): the depth stays at 0 and no quote mark is rendered (although the rest of the
                    // 'content' property's value is still inserted).
                    // - https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS21/generate.html#quotes-insert
                    // (This is missing from the CONTENT-3 spec.)
                    // NB: Until the depth is known, the close-quote may make the item.
                    match &mut quote_nesting_level {
                        Some(level) if *level > 0 => {
                            *level -= 1;
                            let run = pending_text.get_or_insert_with(new_run);
                            run.made = true;
                            run.shows_quote_depth = true;
                            append_quote(&mut run.text, &quotes, false, *level, quote_language);
                        }
                        // NB: A text of such close-quotes alone makes no item, but is one whatever the depth.
                        Some(_) | None => pending_text.get_or_insert_with(new_run).shows_quote_depth = true,
                    }
                }
                keyword::NO_OPEN_QUOTE => {
                    if let Some(level) = &mut quote_nesting_level {
                        *level += 1;
                    }
                }
                keyword::NO_CLOSE_QUOTE => {
                    // NOTE: See CloseQuote
                    if let Some(level) = &mut quote_nesting_level {
                        *level = level.saturating_sub(1);
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            },
            Some(StyleValueData::Counter(counter_payload)) => {
                flush_pending_text(&mut items, &mut pending_text);
                let text = resolve_counter(counter_payload, &mut values);
                items.push(ContentItem::Text { text, made: true });
            }
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-content-3/#typedef-content-list
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-4/#typedef-image
            // <content-list> accepts <image>, and image-set() is an <image>.
            Some(StyleValueData::Image { .. } | StyleValueData::ImageSet { .. }) => {
                flush_pending_text(&mut items, &mut pending_text);
                items.push(ContentItem::Image(index));
            }
            // TODO: Implement images, and other things.
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    flush_pending_text(&mut items, &mut pending_text);

    let mut accessible_text = Vec::new();
    let mut accessible_text_is_known = true;
    if let Some(alt_text) = alt_text.optional_data() {
        for item in value_list(Some(alt_text)) {
            match item.optional_data() {
                Some(StyleValueData::String { string, .. }) => accessible_text.extend_from_slice(string.units()),
                Some(StyleValueData::Counter(counter_payload)) => match resolve_counter(counter_payload, &mut values) {
                    Some(text) => accessible_text.extend(text),
                    None => accessible_text_is_known = false,
                },
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    } else {
        for item in &items {
            match item {
                ContentItem::Text {
                    text: Some(text),
                    made: true,
                } => accessible_text.extend_from_slice(text),
                ContentItem::Text { text: None, .. } => accessible_text_is_known = false,
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }

    ResolvedContent {
        items,
        is_list: true,
        counter_styles,
        accessible_text: if accessible_text_is_known {
            AccessibleText::Set(accessible_text)
        } else {
            AccessibleText::Pending
        },
        renders_list_item_counter_value,
    }
}

/*

use super::*;

// NB: Layout computes every box in the "frame" of the writing mode of the formatting context that lays it out: the
//     frame is that writing mode's flow-relative view of the plane, turned so that its line-left side is the frame's
//     left side and its block-start side is the frame's top side. Within a frame, the inline axis is the horizontal
//     one and blocks stack downwards, so every layout algorithm can work as if in horizontal-tb. The left and right
//     sides of a frame are line-relative rather than inline-start and inline-end, which keeps 'direction' working the
//     same in every writing mode. Painting maps the frame back onto the physical plane.
//     https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes-4/#logical-to-physical

/// A side of a box, in a frame or in the physical plane.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub(crate) enum Side {
    Top = 0,
    Right = 1,
    Bottom = 2,
    Left = 3,
}

impl Side {
    const ALL: [Side; 4] = [Side::Top, Side::Right, Side::Bottom, Side::Left];

    fn from_index(index: u8) -> Side {
        Self::ALL[index as usize & 3]
    }
}

/// The physical side each side of the frame of a writing mode lies on, indexed by the frame side.
const FRAME_SIDES_IN_PHYSICAL_PLANE: [[u8; 4]; 5] = [
    // horizontal-tb
    [0, 1, 2, 3],
    // vertical-rl: block-start is right, line-left is top.
    [1, 2, 3, 0],
    // vertical-lr: block-start is left, line-left is top.
    [3, 2, 1, 0],
    // sideways-rl: block-start is right, line-left is top.
    [1, 2, 3, 0],
    // sideways-lr: block-start is left, line-left is bottom.
    [3, 0, 1, 2],
];

/// The frame side that each physical side lies on, indexed by the physical side.
const PHYSICAL_SIDES_IN_FRAME: [[u8; 4]; 5] = [[0, 1, 2, 3], [3, 0, 1, 2], [3, 2, 1, 0], [3, 0, 1, 2], [1, 2, 3, 0]];

/// The widths of the sides of a box, such as its borders or paddings, in a frame or in the physical plane.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct Sides {
    pub(crate) top: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) right: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) bottom: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) left: CssPixels,
}

impl Sides {
    /// The sides, which frame `from` holds, as frame `to` holds them.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn in_frame(self, from: Frame, to: Frame) -> Self {
        let [top, right, bottom, left] = from.sides_in([self.top, self.right, self.bottom, self.left], to);
        Self {
            top,
            right,
            bottom,
            left,
        }
    }
}

/// The frame of a writing mode.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct Frame(u8);

impl Default for Frame {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::PHYSICAL
    }
}

impl Frame {
    pub(crate) const PHYSICAL: Frame = Frame(writing_mode::HORIZONTAL_TB);

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn of(writing_mode: u8) -> Frame {
        Frame(if writing_mode <= writing_mode::SIDEWAYS_LR {
            writing_mode
        } else {
            writing_mode::HORIZONTAL_TB
        })
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn writing_mode(self) -> u8 {
        self.0
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn is_physical(self) -> bool {
        self.0 == writing_mode::HORIZONTAL_TB
    }

    /// Whether the frame's horizontal axis runs along the physical vertical axis.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn is_transposed(self) -> bool {
        self.0 != writing_mode::HORIZONTAL_TB
    }

    /// Whether the frames run their inline axes along perpendicular physical axes.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn is_orthogonal_to(self, other: Frame) -> bool {
        self.is_transposed() != other.is_transposed()
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn physical_side(self, side: Side) -> Side {
        Side::from_index(FRAME_SIDES_IN_PHYSICAL_PLANE[self.0 as usize][side as usize])
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn frame_side(self, physical_side: Side) -> Side {
        Side::from_index(PHYSICAL_SIDES_IN_FRAME[self.0 as usize][physical_side as usize])
    }

    /// The side of `other` that lies on the same physical side as the given side of this frame.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn side_in(self, side: Side, other: Frame) -> Side {
        other.frame_side(self.physical_side(side))
    }

    /// Maps per-side values, indexed top, right, bottom, left, from this frame to `other`.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn sides_in<T: Copy>(self, values: [T; 4], other: Frame) -> [T; 4] {
        if self == other {
            return values;
        }
        Side::ALL.map(|side| values[other.side_in(side, self) as usize])
    }

    /// Whether the frame's horizontal axis runs opposite to the physical axis it lies on.
    pub(crate) fn horizontal_axis_is_reversed(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.physical_side(Side::Left), Side::Right | Side::Bottom)
    }

    /// Whether the frame's vertical axis runs opposite to the physical axis it lies on.
    pub(crate) fn vertical_axis_is_reversed(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.physical_side(Side::Top), Side::Right | Side::Bottom)
    }

    /// Maps a rect in this frame to the physical plane, within a box whose physical size is `container_size`, both
    /// relative to that box's top-left corner and its frame origin respectively.
    pub(crate) fn rect_to_physical(self, rect: CssPixelRect, container_size: FfiCssPixelSize) -> CssPixelRect {
        if self.is_physical() {
            return rect;
        }
        // NB: In a transposed frame, the horizontal frame axis runs along the physical vertical axis.
        let (mut x, mut y, width, height) = (rect.y, rect.x, rect.height, rect.width);
        if self.vertical_axis_is_reversed() {
            x = container_size.width - x - width;
        }
        if self.horizontal_axis_is_reversed() {
            y = container_size.height - y - height;
        }
        CssPixelRect { x, y, width, height }
    }

    /// Maps a physical rect within a box of physical size `container_size` to this frame.
    pub(crate) fn rect_from_physical(self, rect: CssPixelRect, container_size: FfiCssPixelSize) -> CssPixelRect {
        if self.is_physical() {
            return rect;
        }
        let (mut x, mut y) = (rect.x, rect.y);
        if self.vertical_axis_is_reversed() {
            x = container_size.width - x - rect.width;
        }
        if self.horizontal_axis_is_reversed() {
            y = container_size.height - y - rect.height;
        }
        CssPixelRect {
            x: y,
            y: x,
            width: rect.height,
            height: rect.width,
        }
    }

    /// Maps a rect within a box from this frame to `other`, where the box has the physical size `container_size`.
    pub(crate) fn rect_in(self, rect: CssPixelRect, other: Frame, container_size: FfiCssPixelSize) -> CssPixelRect {
        if self == other {
            return rect;
        }
        other.rect_from_physical(self.rect_to_physical(rect, container_size), container_size)
    }

    /// Maps an offset in this frame to the physical plane, as the corner of an empty rect at the origin of an empty box
    /// maps.
    pub(crate) fn offset_to_physical(self, offset: FfiCssPixelPoint) -> FfiCssPixelPoint {
        let corner = self.rect_to_physical(
            CssPixelRect::new(offset.x, offset.y, CssPixels::default(), CssPixels::default()),
            FfiCssPixelSize::default(),
        );
        FfiCssPixelPoint {
            x: corner.x,
            y: corner.y,
        }
    }

    /// Maps a physical offset to this frame.
    pub(crate) fn offset_from_physical(self, offset: FfiCssPixelPoint) -> FfiCssPixelPoint {
        let corner = self.rect_from_physical(
            CssPixelRect::new(offset.x, offset.y, CssPixels::default(), CssPixels::default()),
            FfiCssPixelSize::default(),
        );
        FfiCssPixelPoint {
            x: corner.x,
            y: corner.y,
        }
    }

    /// The physical half-plane before the block-end edge of a content box whose contents use this frame and whose
    /// physical size is `content_size`, relative to that content box.
    pub(crate) fn half_plane_before_block_end(self, content_size: FfiCssPixelSize) -> CssPixelRect {
        let extent = CssPixels::from_integer((crate::css::css_pixels::MAX_INTEGER_VALUE / 4) as i64);
        let block_size = if self.is_transposed() {
            content_size.width
        } else {
            content_size.height
        };
        self.rect_to_physical(
            CssPixelRect::new(-extent, -extent, extent * 2, extent + block_size),
            content_size,
        )
    }

    /// Maps a physical size to this frame.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn size_from_physical(self, size: FfiCssPixelSize) -> FfiCssPixelSize {
        self.size_to_physical(size.width, size.height)
    }

    /// Maps a size in this frame to the physical plane.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn size_to_physical(self, width: CssPixels, height: CssPixels) -> FfiCssPixelSize {
        if self.is_transposed() {
            FfiCssPixelSize {
                width: height,
                height: width,
            }
        } else {
            FfiCssPixelSize { width, height }
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn to_physical<T>(writing_mode: u8, inline: T, block: T) -> (T, T) {
    if writing_mode == writing_mode::HORIZONTAL_TB {
        (inline, block)
    } else {
        (block, inline)
    }
}

/// Whether the start side, in the given writing mode and direction, of the axis that runs along the given physical
/// axis is its left (horizontal) or top (vertical) side.
pub(crate) fn start_is_left_or_top(writing_mode: u8, direction: u8, horizontal: bool) -> bool {
    let is_ltr = direction == direction::LTR;
    match (writing_mode, horizontal) {
        (writing_mode::HORIZONTAL_TB, true) => is_ltr,
        (writing_mode::HORIZONTAL_TB, false) => true,
        (writing_mode::VERTICAL_RL | writing_mode::SIDEWAYS_RL, true) => false,
        (writing_mode::VERTICAL_LR | writing_mode::SIDEWAYS_LR, true) => true,
        (writing_mode::SIDEWAYS_LR, false) => !is_ltr,
        (_, false) => is_ltr,
        _ => true,
    }
}

/// Whether the start side, in the given writing mode and direction, of the axis that runs along the given axis of
/// `frame` is that axis's left (horizontal) or top (vertical) side in the frame.
pub(crate) fn start_is_low_side_in_frame(
    frame: Frame,
    writing_mode: u8,
    direction: u8,
    frame_horizontal: bool,
) -> bool {
    let physical_horizontal = frame_horizontal != frame.is_transposed();
    let start_is_physical_low_side = start_is_left_or_top(writing_mode, direction, physical_horizontal);
    let physical_low_side = if physical_horizontal { Side::Left } else { Side::Top };
    matches!(frame.frame_side(physical_low_side), Side::Left | Side::Top) == start_is_physical_low_side
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AvailableSize {
    Definite(CssPixels),
    #[default]
    Indefinite,
    MinContent,
    MaxContent,
}

impl AvailableSize {
    pub fn definite(value: CssPixels) -> Self {
        assert!(!matches!(value.raw_value(), i32::MIN | i32::MAX));
        Self::Definite(value)
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_intrinsic_sizing_constraint(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::MinContent | Self::MaxContent)
    }

    pub(crate) fn to_px_or_zero(self) -> CssPixels {
        match self {
            Self::Definite(value) => value,
            _ => CssPixels::default(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn pixels_greater_than(self, pixels: CssPixels) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::MaxContent | Self::Indefinite => false,
            Self::MinContent => true,
            Self::Definite(value) => pixels > value,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn pixels_less_than(self, pixels: CssPixels) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::MaxContent | Self::Indefinite => true,
            Self::MinContent => false,
            Self::Definite(value) => pixels < value,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct AvailableSpace {
    pub inline_size: AvailableSize,
    pub block_size: AvailableSize,
}

impl Default for AvailableSpace {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            inline_size: AvailableSize::Indefinite,
            block_size: AvailableSize::Indefinite,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct PackedOptionalCssPixels(i32);

impl PackedOptionalCssPixels {
    const NONE_RAW_VALUE: i32 = i32::MIN;

    pub(crate) fn get(self) -> Option<CssPixels> {
        (self.0 != Self::NONE_RAW_VALUE).then(|| CssPixels::from_raw(self.0))
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_none(self) -> bool {
        self.0 == Self::NONE_RAW_VALUE
    }
}

impl Default for PackedOptionalCssPixels {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self(Self::NONE_RAW_VALUE)
    }
}

impl From<Option<CssPixels>> for PackedOptionalCssPixels {
    fn from(value: Option<CssPixels>) -> Self {
        match value {
            Some(pixels) => Self(pixels.raw_value().max(Self::NONE_RAW_VALUE + 1)),
            None => Self::default(),
        }
    }
}

use super::*;
