            if track.base_size >= limit {
                continue;
            }
            track.base_size = limit.min(track.base_size + per_track);
            if track.base_size >= limit {
                growable -= 1;
            }
        }
        free_space = match available {
            AvailableSize::Definite(available_size) => {
                let sum = tracks.iter().fold(gap_size, |sum, track| sum + track.base_size);
                CssPixels::default().max(available_size - sum)
            }
            AvailableSize::MinContent => CssPixels::default(),
            _ => CssPixels::from_raw(i32::MAX),
        };
        if free_space == old_free_space {
            break;
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn expand_flexible_tracks_indefinite(tracks: &mut [Track<'_>], items: &[ItemContribution]) {
    // First, find the grid’s used flex fraction:
    // Otherwise, if the free space is an indefinite length:
    // The used flex fraction is the maximum of:
    let mut flex_fraction = formatting_context::PixelFraction::zero();
    // For each flexible track, if the flexible track’s flex factor is greater than one, the result of dividing
    // the track’s base size by its flex factor; otherwise, the track’s base size.
    for track in tracks.iter() {
        if let Some(factor) = track.max_sizing.flex_factor() {
            flex_fraction = flex_fraction.max(fr_size_fraction(track.base_size, factor.max(1.0)));
        }
    }
    // For each grid item that crosses a flexible track, the result of finding the size of an fr using all the
    // grid tracks that the item crosses and a space to fill of the item’s max-content contribution.
    for item in items {
        if !item
            .spanned_tracks
            .clone()
            .any(|index| tracks[index].max_sizing.flex_factor().is_some())
        {
            continue;
        }
        flex_fraction = flex_fraction.max(find_fr_size(&tracks[item.spanned_tracks.clone()], item.max_content));
    }
    for track in tracks {
        if let Some(factor) = track.max_sizing.flex_factor() {
            track.base_size = track.base_size.max(size_of_flex_factor(flex_fraction, factor));
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn stretch_auto_tracks(
    tracks: &mut [Track<'_>],
    gap_size: CssPixels,
    available: AvailableSize,
    content_distribution_is_normal_or_stretch: bool,
) {
    // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/#algo-stretch
    // 12.8. Stretch auto Tracks
    // This step expands tracks that have an auto max track sizing function by dividing any remaining positive,
    // definite free space equally amongst them. If the free space is indefinite, but the grid container has a
    // definite min-width/height, use that size to calculate the free space for this step instead.
    if !content_distribution_is_normal_or_stretch {
        return;
    }
    let auto_count = tracks
        .iter()
        .filter(|track| track.max_sizing.is_auto(available))
        .count();
    if auto_count == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let remaining = if let AvailableSize::Definite(available_size) = available {
        let sum = tracks.iter().fold(gap_size, |sum, track| sum + track.base_size);
        CssPixels::default().max(available_size - sum)
    } else {
        CssPixels::default()
    };
    let per_track = remaining / auto_count;
    for track in tracks {
        if track.max_sizing.is_auto(available) {
            track.base_size += per_track;
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn run_track_sizing<MaximumSize>(
    tracks: &mut [Track<'_>],
    gap_size: CssPixels,
    items: &mut [ItemContribution],
    available: AvailableSize,
    grid_container_maximum_size: MaximumSize,
    content_distribution_is_normal_or_stretch: bool,
) where
    MaximumSize: FnOnce() -> Option<CssPixels>,
{
    // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/#algo-track-sizing
    // 12.3. Track Sizing Algorithm
    //
    // 1. Initialize Track Sizes
    let has_flexible = initialize_track_sizes(tracks, available);
    // 2. Resolve Intrinsic Track Sizes
    resolve_intrinsic_track_sizes(tracks, items, available);
    // 3. Maximize Tracks
    let saved_base_sizes = tracks
        .iter()
        .filter(|track| !track.is_gap)
        .map(|track| track.base_size)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    maximize_tracks(tracks, gap_size, available);
    // If this would cause the grid to be larger than the grid container’s inner size as limited by its
    // max-width/height, then redo this step, treating the available grid space as equal to the grid
    // container’s inner size when it’s sized to its max-width/height.
    let grid_container_inner_size = tracks
        .iter()
        .filter(|track| !track.is_gap)
        .fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, track| sum + track.base_size);
    if let Some(maximum_size) = grid_container_maximum_size()
        && grid_container_inner_size > maximum_size
    {
        for (track, saved_base_size) in tracks.iter_mut().filter(|track| !track.is_gap).zip(saved_base_sizes) {
            track.base_size = saved_base_size;
        }
        maximize_tracks(tracks, gap_size, AvailableSize::definite(maximum_size));
    }
    // 4. Expand Flexible Tracks
    if has_flexible {
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid/#algo-flex-tracks
        // 12.7. Expand Flexible Tracks
        // This step sizes flexible tracks using the largest value it can assign to an fr without exceeding
        // the available space.
        if let AvailableSize::Definite(available_size) = available {
            // First, find the grid’s used flex fraction:
            // Otherwise, if the free space is a definite length:
            // The used flex fraction is the result of finding the size of an fr using all of the grid tracks and a space
            // to fill of the available grid space.
            expand_flexible_tracks(tracks, available_size - gap_size);
        // If the free space is zero or if sizing the grid container under a min-content constraint:
        // The used flex fraction is zero.
        } else if available != AvailableSize::MinContent {
            expand_flexible_tracks_indefinite(tracks, items);
        }
    }
    // 5. Expand Stretched auto Tracks
    stretch_auto_tracks(tracks, gap_size, available, content_distribution_is_normal_or_stretch);
    // If calculating the layout of a grid item in this step depends on the available space in the block
    // axis, assume the available space that it would have if any row with a definite max track sizing
    // function had that size and all other rows were infinite. If both the grid container and all
    // tracks have definite sizes, also apply align-content to find the final effective size of any gaps
    // spanned by such items; otherwise ignore the effects of track alignment in this estimation.
}

pub(crate) const REPEAT_AUTO_FIT: u8 = 0;
const REPEAT_AUTO_FILL: u8 = 1;
pub(crate) const REPEAT_FIXED: u8 = 2;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct LineName {
    pub(crate) name_index: u32,
    pub(crate) raw: usize,
    pub(crate) implicit: bool,
    pub(crate) adopted_from_parent: bool,
    pub(crate) area_name_raw: usize,
    pub(crate) area_is_start: bool,
}

impl LineName {
    pub(crate) fn explicit(name_index: u32, raw: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            name_index,
            raw,
            implicit: false,
            adopted_from_parent: false,
            area_name_raw: 0,
            area_is_start: false,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn implicit(name_index: u32, raw: usize, area_name_raw: usize, area_is_start: bool) -> Self {
        Self {
            name_index,
            raw,
            implicit: true,
            adopted_from_parent: false,
            area_name_raw,
            area_is_start,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct TrackDefinition<'pass> {
    pub(crate) min: GridTrackBreadth<'pass>,
    pub(crate) max: GridTrackBreadth<'pass>,
    pub(crate) is_auto_fit: bool,
    pub(crate) is_auto_repeat: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct ExpandedTrackList<'pass> {
    pub(crate) lines: Vec<Vec<LineName>>,
    pub(crate) tracks: Vec<TrackDefinition<'pass>>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct TrackListSource<'pass> {
    pub(crate) names: &'pass [usize],
    pub(crate) entries: &'pass [ComputedGridTrackEntry],
    pub(crate) name_indices: &'pass [u32],
}

impl<'pass> TrackListSource<'pass> {
    fn from_grid_style(grid_style: &'pass GridValues) -> Self {
        Self {
            names: grid_style.names.raws(),
            entries: grid_style.entries.as_slice(),
            name_indices: grid_style.name_indices.as_slice(),
        }
    }

    fn entry(&self, index: u32) -> &'pass ComputedGridTrackEntry {
        assert_ne!(index, GRID_NO_INDEX);
        &self.entries[index as usize]
    }

    fn names(&self, entry: &ComputedGridTrackEntry) -> impl Iterator<Item = LineName> + 'pass {
        let end = entry
            .name_index_start
            .checked_add(entry.name_index_count)
            .expect("grid line-name range overflow");
        let name_raws = self.names;
        self.name_indices[entry.name_index_start..end]
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .map(move |name_index| LineName::explicit(name_index, name_raws[name_index as usize]))
    }

    fn for_each_entry(
        &self,
        list: ComputedGridTrackList,
        mut callback: impl FnMut(u32, &'pass ComputedGridTrackEntry),
    ) {
        let mut index = list.first_entry;
        let mut visited = 0usize;
        while index != GRID_NO_INDEX {
            assert!(visited < self.entries.len(), "cyclic grid track-list snapshot");
            let entry = self.entry(index);
            callback(index, entry);
            index = entry.next_sibling;
            visited += 1;
        }
    }
}

fn definition_for(entry: &ComputedGridTrackEntry, auto_fit: bool, auto_repeat: bool) -> TrackDefinition<'_> {
    match entry.kind {
        kind if kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::TrackSize as u8 => {
            let size = grid_track_breadth_view(&entry.size);
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-2/#algo-terms
            // min track sizing function:
            // If the track was sized with a minmax() function, this is the first argument to that function.
            // If the track was sized with a <flex> value or fit-content() function, auto. Otherwise, the track’s sizing function.
            let min = if matches!(size, GridTrackBreadth::Flex(_) | GridTrackBreadth::FitContent(_)) {
                GridTrackBreadth::Auto
            } else {
                size
            };
            TrackDefinition {
                min,
                max: size,
                is_auto_fit: auto_fit,
                is_auto_repeat: auto_repeat,
            }
        }
        kind if kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::MinMax as u8 => TrackDefinition {
            min: grid_track_breadth_view(&entry.min_size),
            max: grid_track_breadth_view(&entry.max_size),
            is_auto_fit: auto_fit,
            is_auto_repeat: auto_repeat,
        },
        _ => unreachable!("only track-size entries form tracks"),
    }
}

// NB: A repeat() copies its line names into every repetition, so a long name list repeated many times would expand into
//     a huge number of names. Names past this limit are dropped, as lines past MAX_GRID_LINE_NUMBER are.
const MAX_EXPANDED_LINE_NAMES: usize = 100_000;

/// Appends `names` to `line`, dropping those past the `names_left` an expansion still may make.
fn extend_line_names(line: &mut Vec<LineName>, names: impl Iterator<Item = LineName>, names_left: &mut usize) {
    let length_before = line.len();
    line.extend(names.take(*names_left));
    *names_left -= line.len() - length_before;
}

#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn expand_standalone_list<'pass>(
    source: TrackListSource<'pass>,
    list: ComputedGridTrackList,
    lines: &mut Vec<Vec<LineName>>,
    tracks: &mut Vec<TrackDefinition<'pass>>,
    pending_names: &mut Vec<LineName>,
    names_left: &mut usize,
    auto_repeat_count: &mut impl FnMut(u32, &ComputedGridTrackEntry) -> usize,
    inherited_auto_fit: bool,
    inherited_auto_repeat: bool,
) {
    source.for_each_entry(list, |entry_index, entry| match entry.kind {
        kind if kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::LineNames as u8 => {
            extend_line_names(pending_names, source.names(entry), names_left);
        }
        kind if kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::TrackSize as u8
            || kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::MinMax as u8 =>
        {
            // NB: Lines past the limit are dropped (see MAX_GRID_LINE_NUMBER), so a repeat() with a huge count does not
            //     expand into more tracks than can be placed into.
            if tracks.len() >= MAX_GRID_LINE_NUMBER as usize {
                return;
            }
            lines.push(std::mem::take(pending_names));
            tracks.push(definition_for(entry, inherited_auto_fit, inherited_auto_repeat));
        }
        kind if kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::Repeat as u8 => {
            let is_auto_fit = entry.repeat_type == REPEAT_AUTO_FIT;
            let is_auto_repeat = is_auto_fit || entry.repeat_type == REPEAT_AUTO_FILL;
            let repeat_count = match entry.repeat_type {
                REPEAT_FIXED => entry.repeat_count,
                REPEAT_AUTO_FIT | REPEAT_AUTO_FILL => auto_repeat_count(entry_index, entry),
                _ => unreachable!("invalid grid repeat type"),
            };
            for _ in 0..repeat_count {
                if tracks.len() >= MAX_GRID_LINE_NUMBER as usize {
                    break;
                }
                expand_standalone_list(
                    source,
                    entry.repeat_list,
                    lines,
                    tracks,
                    pending_names,
                    names_left,
                    auto_repeat_count,
                    inherited_auto_fit || is_auto_fit,
                    inherited_auto_repeat || is_auto_repeat,
                );
            }
        }
        _ => unreachable!("invalid grid track-list entry kind"),
    });
}

/// Expands the recursive FFI encoding into the exact line/track order consumed
/// by placement. `auto_repeat_count` performs the container-size-dependent
/// auto-fill/auto-fit calculation.
pub(crate) fn expand_standalone(
    source: TrackListSource<'_>,
    list: ComputedGridTrackList,
    mut auto_repeat_count: impl FnMut(u32, &ComputedGridTrackEntry) -> usize,
) -> ExpandedTrackList<'_> {
    if list.is_subgrid {
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-2/#subgrid-listing
        // If there is no parent grid, or if the grid container is otherwise
        // forced to establish an independent formatting context, the used value
        // is the initial value, grid-template-rows/none, and the grid container
        // is not a subgrid.
        return ExpandedTrackList {
            lines: vec![Vec::new()],
            tracks: Vec::new(),
        };
    }

    let mut result = ExpandedTrackList::default();
    let mut pending_names = Vec::new();
    let mut names_left = MAX_EXPANDED_LINE_NAMES;
    expand_standalone_list(
        source,
        list,
        &mut result.lines,
        &mut result.tracks,
        &mut pending_names,
        &mut names_left,
        &mut auto_repeat_count,
        false,
        false,
    );
    result.lines.push(pending_names);
    result
}

pub(crate) fn count_subgrid_line_name_lists(source: TrackListSource<'_>, list: ComputedGridTrackList) -> usize {
    let mut count = 0usize;
    source.for_each_entry(list, |_index, entry| match entry.kind {
        kind if kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::LineNames as u8 => count += 1,
        kind if kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::Repeat as u8 => {
            let nested = count_subgrid_line_name_lists(source, entry.repeat_list);
            count += if entry.repeat_type == REPEAT_FIXED {
                nested.saturating_mul(entry.repeat_count)
            } else {
                nested
            };
        }
        _ => {}
    });
    count
}

pub(crate) fn automatic_subgrid_span(source: TrackListSource<'_>, list: ComputedGridTrackList) -> usize {
    count_subgrid_line_name_lists(source, list).saturating_sub(1).max(1)
}

fn expand_subgrid_names(
    source: TrackListSource<'_>,
    list: ComputedGridTrackList,
    lines: &mut [Vec<LineName>],
    line_index: &mut usize,
    names_left: &mut usize,
) {
    let entries = {
        let mut entries: Vec<(u32, &ComputedGridTrackEntry)> = Vec::new();
        source.for_each_entry(list, |index, entry| entries.push((index, entry)));
        entries
    };

    for (position, (_entry_index, entry)) in entries.iter().enumerate() {
        match entry.kind {
            kind if kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::LineNames as u8 => {
                if let Some(line) = lines.get_mut(*line_index) {
                    extend_line_names(line, source.names(entry), names_left);
                }
                *line_index += 1;
            }
            kind if kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::Repeat as u8 => {
                let repeat_count = match entry.repeat_type {
                    REPEAT_FIXED => entry.repeat_count,
                    REPEAT_AUTO_FILL => {
                        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-2/#auto-repeat
                        // On a subgridded axis, the auto-fill keyword is only valid once per
                        // <line-name-list>, and repeats enough times for the name list to match the
                        // subgrid's specified grid span, falling back to 0 if the span is already
                        // fulfilled.
                        let per_repeat = count_subgrid_line_name_lists(source, entry.repeat_list);
                        let remaining = entries[position + 1..]
                            .iter()
                            .map(|(_, entry)| match entry.kind {
                                kind if kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::LineNames as u8 => 1,
                                kind if kind == ComputedGridTrackEntryKind::Repeat as u8 => {
                                    count_subgrid_line_name_lists(source, entry.repeat_list)
                                        * if entry.repeat_type == REPEAT_FIXED {
                                            entry.repeat_count
                                        } else {
                                            1
                                        }
                                }
                                _ => 0,
                            })
                            .sum::<usize>();
                        if per_repeat > 0 && *line_index < lines.len() && lines.len() - *line_index > remaining {
                            (lines.len() - *line_index - remaining) / per_repeat
                        } else {
                            0
                        }
                    }
                    REPEAT_AUTO_FIT => 0,
                    _ => unreachable!("invalid grid repeat type"),
                };
                for _ in 0..repeat_count {
                    if *line_index >= lines.len() {
                        break;
                    }
                    expand_subgrid_names(source, entry.repeat_list, lines, line_index, names_left);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn expand_subgrid<'pass>(
    source: TrackListSource<'pass>,
    list: ComputedGridTrackList,
    track_count: usize,
    inherited_lines: &[Vec<LineName>],
) -> ExpandedTrackList<'pass> {
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-2/#subgrid-span
    // The number of explicit tracks in the subgrid in a subgridded dimension always corresponds
    // to the number of grid tracks that it spans in its parent grid.
    let mut lines = vec![Vec::new(); track_count.saturating_add(1)];
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-2/#subgrid-line-name-inheritance
    // Since subgrids can be placed before their contents are placed, the subgridded lines
    // automatically receive the explicitly-assigned line names specified on the corresponding
    // lines of the parent grid. These names are in addition to any line names specified locally
    // on the subgrid.
    for (line, inherited) in lines.iter_mut().zip(inherited_lines) {
        line.extend(inherited.iter().filter(|name| !name.implicit).map(|name| LineName {
            name_index: name.name_index,
            raw: name.raw,
            implicit: false,
            adopted_from_parent: true,
            area_name_raw: 0,
            area_is_start: false,
        }));
    }
    let mut line_index = 0;
    let mut names_left = MAX_EXPANDED_LINE_NAMES;
    expand_subgrid_names(source, list, &mut lines, &mut line_index, &mut names_left);
    ExpandedTrackList {
        lines,
        tracks: Vec::new(),
    }
}

pub(crate) fn add_template_area_lines(
    columns: &mut Vec<Vec<LineName>>,
    rows: &mut Vec<Vec<LineName>>,
    column_lines_are_fixed: bool,
    row_lines_are_fixed: bool,
    areas: &[ComputedGridArea],
    names: &[usize],
) {
    // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/#implicitly-assigned-line-name
    // 7.3.2. Implicitly-Assigned Line Names
    // The grid-template-areas property generates implicitly-assigned line names from the named grid areas in the
    // template. For each named grid area foo, four implicitly-assigned line names are created: two named foo-start,
    // naming the row-start and column-start lines of the named grid area, and two named foo-end, naming the row-end
    // and column-end lines of the named grid area.
    //
    // NB: The lines of a subgridded axis are those of the subgrid's explicit grid, which its areas cannot extend. An
    //     area that reaches past them names the last line instead, as a partially overlapped area of the parent grid
    //     does.
    let max_column = areas.iter().map(|area| area.column_end).max().unwrap_or_default();
    let max_row = areas.iter().map(|area| area.row_end).max().unwrap_or_default();
    if !column_lines_are_fixed {
        columns.resize_with(columns.len().max(max_column.saturating_add(1)), Vec::new);
    }
    if !row_lines_are_fixed {
        rows.resize_with(rows.len().max(max_row.saturating_add(1)), Vec::new);
    }
    let last_column = columns.len().saturating_sub(1);
    let last_row = rows.len().saturating_sub(1);

    for area in areas {
        let column_start = area.column_start.min(last_column);
        let column_end = area.column_end.min(last_column);
        let row_start = area.row_start.min(last_row);
        let row_end = area.row_end.min(last_row);
        if columns.is_empty() || rows.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        columns[column_start].push(LineName::implicit(
            area.implicit_start_name_index,
            names[area.implicit_start_name_index as usize],
            names[area.name_index as usize],
            true,
        ));
        columns[column_end].push(LineName::implicit(
            area.implicit_end_name_index,
            names[area.implicit_end_name_index as usize],
            names[area.name_index as usize],
            false,
        ));
        rows[row_start].push(LineName::implicit(
            area.implicit_start_name_index,
            names[area.implicit_start_name_index as usize],
            names[area.name_index as usize],
            true,
        ));
        rows[row_end].push(LineName::implicit(
            area.implicit_end_name_index,
            names[area.implicit_end_name_index as usize],
            names[area.name_index as usize],
            false,
        ));
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) enum TrackSizingFunction<'pass> {
    Auto,
    Fixed(&'pass ComputedSize),
    /// A synthesized fixed track with no backing style value: collapsed
    /// tracks, gap tracks, and fixed subgrid tracks carry a resolved px size.
    FixedPx(CssPixels),
    Flex(f64),
    MinContent,
    MaxContent,
    FitContent(&'pass ComputedSize),
}

impl<'pass> TrackSizingFunction<'pass> {
    pub(crate) fn from_breadth(value: GridTrackBreadth<'pass>) -> Self {
        match value {
            GridTrackBreadth::Auto => Self::Auto,
            GridTrackBreadth::LengthPercentage(size) => Self::Fixed(size),
            GridTrackBreadth::Flex(factor) => Self::Flex(factor),
            GridTrackBreadth::MinContent => Self::MinContent,
            GridTrackBreadth::MaxContent => Self::MaxContent,
            GridTrackBreadth::FitContent(size) => Self::FitContent(size),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_auto(self, available: AvailableSize) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::Auto => true,
            Self::Fixed(value) => value.contains_percentage() && !matches!(available, AvailableSize::Definite(_)),
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_fixed(self, available: AvailableSize) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::Fixed(value) => !value.contains_percentage() || matches!(available, AvailableSize::Definite(_)),
            Self::FixedPx(_) => true,
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_intrinsic(self, available: AvailableSize) -> bool {
        self.is_auto(available) || matches!(self, Self::MinContent | Self::MaxContent | Self::FitContent(_))
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_min_content(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::MinContent)
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_max_content(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::MaxContent)
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_fit_content(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::FitContent(_))
    }

    pub(crate) fn flex_factor(self) -> Option<f64> {
        match self {
            Self::Flex(factor) => Some(factor),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn resolve(self, available: AvailableSize) -> CssPixels {
        match self {
            Self::Fixed(value) | Self::FitContent(value) => value.to_px(available.to_px_or_zero()),
            Self::FixedPx(px) => px,
            _ => CssPixels::default(),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Track<'pass> {
    pub(crate) min_sizing: TrackSizingFunction<'pass>,
    pub(crate) max_sizing: TrackSizingFunction<'pass>,
    pub(crate) base_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) growth_limit: Option<CssPixels>,
    sizing: TrackSizingState,
    pub(crate) max_is_intrinsic: bool,
    pub(crate) max_is_max_content: bool,
    pub(crate) infinitely_growable: bool,
    pub(crate) is_gap: bool,
    pub(crate) is_auto_fit: bool,
    pub(crate) is_auto_repeat: bool,
    pub(crate) is_collapsed: bool,
}

impl<'pass> Track<'pass> {
    pub(crate) fn fixed(base_size: CssPixels) -> Self {
        Self {
            min_sizing: TrackSizingFunction::FixedPx(base_size),
            max_sizing: TrackSizingFunction::FixedPx(base_size),
            base_size,
            growth_limit: Some(base_size),
            sizing: TrackSizingState::default(),
            max_is_intrinsic: false,
            max_is_max_content: false,
            infinitely_growable: false,
            is_gap: false,
            is_auto_fit: false,
            is_auto_repeat: false,
            is_collapsed: false,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn auto() -> Self {
        Self {
            min_sizing: TrackSizingFunction::Auto,
            max_sizing: TrackSizingFunction::Auto,
            base_size: CssPixels::default(),
            growth_limit: Some(CssPixels::default()),
            sizing: TrackSizingState::default(),
            max_is_intrinsic: true,
            max_is_max_content: false,
            infinitely_growable: false,
            is_gap: false,
            is_auto_fit: false,
            is_auto_repeat: false,
            is_collapsed: false,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_definition(definition: TrackDefinition<'pass>) -> Self {
        // NOTE: repeat() is expected to be expanded beforehand.
        let min_sizing = TrackSizingFunction::from_breadth(definition.min);
        let max_sizing = TrackSizingFunction::from_breadth(definition.max);
        Self {
            min_sizing,
            max_sizing,
            base_size: CssPixels::default(),
            growth_limit: Some(CssPixels::default()),
            sizing: TrackSizingState::default(),
            max_is_intrinsic: false,
            max_is_max_content: max_sizing.is_max_content(),
            infinitely_growable: false,
            is_gap: false,
            is_auto_fit: definition.is_auto_fit,
            is_auto_repeat: definition.is_auto_repeat,
            is_collapsed: false,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn gap(size: CssPixels) -> Self {
        // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/#gutters
        // For the purpose of track sizing, each gutter is treated as an extra, empty, fixed-size
        // track of the specified size, so its growth limit must equal its base size or spanning
        // items' growth-limit distributions would treat the gap itself as distributable space.
        let mut track = Self::fixed(size);
        track.is_gap = true;
        track
    }

    pub(crate) fn collapse(&mut self) {
        self.min_sizing = TrackSizingFunction::FixedPx(CssPixels::default());
        self.max_sizing = TrackSizingFunction::FixedPx(CssPixels::default());
        self.is_collapsed = true;
    }
}

pub(crate) fn initialize_track_sizes(tracks: &mut [Track<'_>], available: AvailableSize) -> bool {
    // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/#algo-init
    // 12.4. Initialize Track Sizes
    // Initialize each track’s base size and growth limit.
    let mut has_flexible_tracks = false;
    for track in tracks {
        track.infinitely_growable = false;
        if track.is_gap {
            continue;
        }

        if !matches!(available, AvailableSize::Definite(_))
            && matches!(track.max_sizing, TrackSizingFunction::FitContent(value) if value.contains_percentage())
        {
            // Normalize fit-content tracks with unresolvable percentage arguments to max-content,
            // since the percentage cannot be resolved against an indefinite available size.
            track.max_sizing = TrackSizingFunction::MaxContent;
        }

        if track.min_sizing.is_fixed(available) {
            track.base_size = track.min_sizing.resolve(available);
        } else if track.min_sizing.is_intrinsic(available) {
            track.base_size = CssPixels::default();
        } else {
            unreachable!("flexible values cannot be minimum track sizing functions");
        }

        if track.max_sizing.is_fixed(available) {
            track.growth_limit = Some(track.max_sizing.resolve(available));
        } else if track.max_sizing.flex_factor().is_some() {
            has_flexible_tracks = true;
            track.growth_limit = None;
        } else if track.max_sizing.is_intrinsic(available) {
            track.growth_limit = None;
        } else {
            unreachable!("invalid maximum track sizing function");
        }
        track.max_is_intrinsic = track.max_sizing.is_intrinsic(available);
        track.max_is_max_content = track.max_sizing.is_max_content();
        if track.growth_limit.is_some_and(|limit| limit < track.base_size) {
            // In all cases, if the growth limit is less than the base size, increase the growth limit to match
            // the base size.
            track.growth_limit = Some(track.base_size);
        }
    }
    has_flexible_tracks
}

/// The size of an fr as `space` divided by a sum of flex factors, keeping the precision of fractional flex factors.
fn fr_size_fraction(space: CssPixels, flex_factor_sum: f64) -> formatting_context::PixelFraction {
    let (numerator, denominator) = CssPixels::fraction_nearest_values_for(space.to_double(), flex_factor_sum);
    if denominator == CssPixels::default() {
        return formatting_context::PixelFraction::zero();
    }
    formatting_context::PixelFraction::new(numerator, denominator)
}

/// The product of the size of an fr and a flex factor.
fn size_of_flex_factor(fr_size: formatting_context::PixelFraction, flex_factor: f64) -> CssPixels {
    CssPixels::nearest_value_for(fr_size.numerator.to_double() / fr_size.denominator.to_double() * flex_factor)
}

pub(crate) fn find_fr_size(tracks: &[Track<'_>], space_to_fill: CssPixels) -> formatting_context::PixelFraction {
    // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/#algo-find-fr-size
    let mut inflexible = vec![false; tracks.len()];
    loop {
        // 1. Let leftover space be the space to fill minus the base sizes of the non-flexible grid tracks.
        let mut leftover_space = space_to_fill;
        for (index, track) in tracks.iter().enumerate() {
            if inflexible[index] || track.max_sizing.flex_factor().is_none() {
                leftover_space -= track.base_size;
            }
        }

        // 2. Let flex factor sum be the sum of the flex factors of the flexible tracks.
        //    If this value is less than 1, set it to 1 instead.
        let mut flex_factor_sum = 0.0;
        for (index, track) in tracks.iter().enumerate() {
            if inflexible[index] {
                continue;
            }
            if let Some(factor) = track.max_sizing.flex_factor() {
                flex_factor_sum += factor;
            }
        }
        if flex_factor_sum < 1.0 {
            flex_factor_sum = 1.0;
        }
        // 3. Let the hypothetical fr size be the leftover space divided by the flex factor sum.
        let hypothetical_fr_size = fr_size_fraction(leftover_space, flex_factor_sum);

        // 4. If the product of the hypothetical fr size and a flexible track’s flex factor is less than the track’s
        //    base size, restart this algorithm treating all such tracks as inflexible.
        let mut restart = false;
        for (index, track) in tracks.iter().enumerate() {
            if inflexible[index] {
                continue;
            }
            let Some(factor) = track.max_sizing.flex_factor() else {
                continue;
            };
            let scaled = size_of_flex_factor(hypothetical_fr_size, factor);
            if scaled < track.base_size {
                inflexible[index] = true;
                restart = true;
            }
        }
        if !restart {
            // 5. Return the hypothetical fr size.
            return hypothetical_fr_size;
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn expand_flexible_tracks(tracks: &mut [Track<'_>], space_to_fill: CssPixels) {
    let flex_fraction = find_fr_size(tracks, space_to_fill);
    // For each flexible track, if the product of the used flex fraction and the track’s flex factor is greater than
    // the track’s base size, set its base size to that product.
    for track in tracks {
        let Some(factor) = track.max_sizing.flex_factor() else {
            continue;
        };
        let scaled = size_of_flex_factor(flex_fraction, factor);
        if scaled > track.base_size {
            track.base_size = scaled;
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn contribution(spanned_tracks: Range<usize>, size: i64) -> ItemContribution {
        let size = CssPixels::from_integer(size);
        ItemContribution {
            span: spanned_tracks.len(),
            spanned_tracks,
            minimum: size,
            min_content: size,
            limited_min_content: size,
            max_content: size,
            limited_max_content: size,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn intrinsic_distribution_keeps_span_groups_independent() {
        let mut tracks = [Track::auto(); 3];
        let mut items = [contribution(0..1, 10), contribution(1..3, 40), contribution(0..3, 80)];
        initialize_track_sizes(&mut tracks, AvailableSize::MaxContent);
        resolve_intrinsic_track_sizes(&mut tracks, &mut items, AvailableSize::MaxContent);
        assert_eq!(tracks.map(|track| track.base_size.to_int()), [20, 30, 30]);
        for track in &tracks {
            assert_eq!(track.growth_limit, Some(track.base_size));
            assert!(!track.infinitely_growable);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn growth_distribution_distinguishes_zero_increase_from_unaffected_tracks() {
        let mut tracks = [Track::auto(); 2];
        initialize_track_sizes(&mut tracks, AvailableSize::MaxContent);
        let item = contribution(0..1, 0);
        distribute_growth_limits_for_span_group(
            &mut tracks,
            &[item],
            AvailableSize::MaxContent,
            |_| true,
            |item| item.min_content,
            true,
            false,
        );
        assert_eq!(tracks[0].growth_limit, Some(CssPixels::default()));
        assert!(tracks[0].infinitely_growable);
        assert_eq!(tracks[1].growth_limit, None);
        assert!(!tracks[1].infinitely_growable);

        // The next phase must not carry the first track's planned increase into this phase.
        tracks[0].growth_limit = None;
        tracks[0].infinitely_growable = false;
        let item = contribution(1..2, 0);
        distribute_growth_limits_for_span_group(
            &mut tracks,
            &[item],
            AvailableSize::MaxContent,
            |_| true,
            |item| item.min_content,
            true,
            false,
        );
        assert_eq!(tracks[0].growth_limit, None);
        assert!(!tracks[0].infinitely_growable);
        assert_eq!(tracks[1].growth_limit, Some(CssPixels::default()));
        assert!(tracks[1].infinitely_growable);
    }

    #[test]
    fn intrinsic_distribution_is_independent_of_item_order() {
        let mut overlapping = contribution(1..4, 30);
        overlapping.min_content = CssPixels::from_integer(80);
        overlapping.limited_min_content = CssPixels::from_integer(60);
        overlapping.max_content = CssPixels::from_integer(110);
        overlapping.limited_max_content = CssPixels::from_integer(90);
        let items = [
            contribution(0..1, 10),
            contribution(2..3, 20),
            contribution(0..3, 80),
            overlapping,
            contribution(2..5, 70),
            contribution(0..5, 120),
        ];
        for available in [
            AvailableSize::MinContent,
            AvailableSize::MaxContent,
            AvailableSize::Indefinite,
        ] {
            let mut expected = None;
            for offset in 0..items.len() {
                let mut items = items.clone();
                items.rotate_left(offset);
                let mut tracks = [
                    Track::auto(),
                    Track::gap(CssPixels::from_integer(2)),
                    Track::auto(),
                    Track::auto(),
                    Track::auto(),
                ];
                tracks[2].min_sizing = TrackSizingFunction::MinContent;
                tracks[4].max_sizing = TrackSizingFunction::Flex(0.5);
                initialize_track_sizes(&mut tracks, available);
                resolve_intrinsic_track_sizes(&mut tracks, &mut items, available);
                let sizes = tracks.map(|track| (track.base_size, track.growth_limit));
                if let Some(expected) = expected {
                    assert_eq!(sizes, expected);
                } else {
                    expected = Some(sizes);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/*

//! Grid lanes layout, which lays out items into tracks in one axis and stacks them freely in the other.
//! https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/

use super::*;

/// The grid lanes layout of a grid lanes container.
// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#grid-lanes-model
// Grid lanes layout lays out items into pre-defined tracks similar to grid layout in one axis (called the grid axis),
// but flows them freely similar to flex layout in the other (called the stacking axis).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(super) struct GridLanes {
    /// The physical axis of this formatting context that is the grid axis of the grid lanes container.
    pub(super) grid_axis: Axis,
}

impl GridLanes {
    pub(super) fn stacking_axis(self) -> Axis {
        self.grid_axis.opposite()
    }
}

/// Where a grid lanes item is placed in the stacking axis: the offset of its margin box from the start of the stacking
/// range, and the size of its alignment container, which is its margin box unless it is adjacent to a gap.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub(super) struct StackingAxisArea {
    pub(super) offset: CssPixels,
    pub(super) size: CssPixels,
    pub(super) is_adjacent_to_gap: bool,
}

/// The intrinsic size contributions of the hypothetical copies of the auto-placed items that share a span size.
// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#track-sizing-performance
struct ItemGroup {
    span: usize,
    is_scroll_container: bool,
    /// One virtual grid item per start position the items could be placed at.
    virtual_items: Vec<ItemContribution>,
}

impl GridFormattingContext<'_> {
    pub(super) fn grid_lanes_for_container(&self) -> Option<GridLanes> {
        if !self.facts(self.run.box_).display().is_grid_lanes_inside() {
            return None;
        }
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#grid-lanes-orientation
        // The initial value of this property is normal, which determines the orientation from the grid-template-*
        // properties:
        // * If grid-template-columns is none and grid-template-rows is not none, the grid container’s block axis is
        //   the grid axis (establishing rows).
        // * Otherwise (thus by default), the grid container’s inline axis is the grid axis (establishing columns).
        let grid_style = self.grid_style(self.run.box_);
        let is_none = |list: ComputedGridTrackList| !list.is_subgrid && list.first_entry == GRID_NO_INDEX;
        let establishes_rows = is_none(grid_style.template_columns) && !is_none(grid_style.template_rows);
        // NB: This formatting context's Column axis is the grid container's inline axis, unless the grid's axes are
        //     transposed in it.
        let grid_axis = if establishes_rows != self.grid_axes_are_transposed {
            Axis::Row
        } else {
            Axis::Column
        };
        Some(GridLanes { grid_axis })
    }

    pub(super) fn is_grid_lanes_stacking_axis(&self, axis: Axis) -> bool {
        self.lanes.is_some_and(|lanes| lanes.stacking_axis() == axis)
    }

    /// The size of the grid lanes container's content box in the stacking axis, which forms the containing block of
    /// its items in that axis.
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#containing-block
    // The containing block for a grid item participating in grid lanes layout is formed by its grid area in the grid
    // axis and the grid container's content box in the stacking axis.
    pub(super) fn grid_lanes_stacking_containing_block_size(&self, axis: Axis) -> Option<CssPixels> {
        match self.axis_available(axis) {
            AvailableSize::Definite(size) => Some(size),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The available space an item is sized against in the stacking axis, where it is sized as for fit-content.
    pub(super) fn grid_lanes_stacking_available_size(&self, axis: Axis) -> CssPixels {
        match self.axis_available(axis) {
            AvailableSize::Definite(size) => size,
            AvailableSize::MinContent => CssPixels::default(),
            AvailableSize::MaxContent | AvailableSize::Indefinite => {
                clamp_to_max_dimension_value(CssPixels::from_raw(i32::MAX))
            }
        }
    }

    /// The tie threshold, or None if it is infinite.
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#placement-tolerance
    fn tie_threshold(&self, grid_axis: Axis) -> Option<CssPixels> {
        use crate::css::css_enums::keyword;
        use crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData;

        let value = &self.grid_style(self.run.box_).fit_tolerance_style_value;
        match value.style_value() {
            // normal: Resolves to a used value of 1em in grid lanes layout and a used value of 0 in all other layout
            //         modes.
            None => Some(self.container_style.font_size()),
            Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) if *keyword == keyword::NORMAL => {
                Some(self.container_style.font_size())
            }
            // infinite: Specifies an infinite tie threshold.
            Some(StyleValueData::Keyword { keyword }) if *keyword == keyword::INFINITE => None,
            // <length-percentage>: Specifies the tie threshold for the grid lanes container.
            // Percentages: relative to the grid-axis content box size of the grid lanes container
            Some(_) => {
                let reference = match self.axis_available(grid_axis) {
                    AvailableSize::Definite(size) => size,
                    _ => self.track_sum(grid_axis),
                };
                Some(
                    value
                        .length_percentage()
                        .map_or(CssPixels::default(), |value| value.to_px(reference)),
                )
            }
        }
    }

    /// Places the items in the grid axis as far as that is possible before layout: items with a definite grid position
    /// in the grid axis are placed there, and every item is placed in the single track of the stacking axis.
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#grid-lanes-track-placement
    // In the grid axis, items can be explicitly placed into tracks and span them using the familiar grid-placement
    // properties’ syntax. Auto-placement, however, uses the Grid Lanes Layout and Placement Algorithm, placing each
    // item with an automatic grid position into the “shortest” track available.
    pub(super) fn place_grid_lanes_items(&mut self, lanes: GridLanes) {
        let inputs = self.collect_grid_items();
        let grid_axis = lanes.grid_axis;
        let resolved = |input: &PlacementInput| grid_axis.select(input.column, input.row);
        let subgridded = self.container_is_subgridded(grid_axis);
        let lines = grid_axis.select(&self.column_lines, &self.row_lines);
        let explicit_track_count = lines.len().saturating_sub(1) as i32;

        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#grid-lanes-track-templates
        // The explicit grid and implicit grid are formed in the same way as for a regular grid container.
        let mut first_line = 0i32;
        let mut last_line = explicit_track_count;
        for input in &inputs {
            let placement = resolved(input);
            match placement.start {
                Some(start) => {
                    first_line = first_line.min(start);
                    last_line = last_line.max(start.saturating_add(placement.span as i32));
                }
                None => last_line = last_line.max(placement.span as i32),
            }
        }
        if subgridded {
            first_line = 0;
            last_line = explicit_track_count;
        }
        let explicit_start = first_line.unsigned_abs() as usize;
        let track_count = (last_line - first_line).max(0) as usize;

        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#grid-lanes-layout-algorithm
        // For each item in order-modified document order:
        let mut ordered_indices = (0..inputs.len()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        ordered_indices.sort_by_key(|&index| (inputs[index].order, index));
        for index in ordered_indices {
            let input = inputs[index];
            let placement = resolved(&input);
            let mut span = placement.span;
            let mut start = placement.start.map_or(0, |start| start - first_line);
            if subgridded {
                Self::clamp_area_to_subgrid(&mut start, &mut span, track_count);
            }
            let mut item = self.new_grid_item(input.id);
            item.set_position(grid_axis, start, span);
            item.set_position(lanes.stacking_axis(), 0, 1);
            item.is_auto_placed_in_grid_lanes = placement.start.is_none();
            self.items.push(item);
        }

        let (explicit_start_field, lines) = grid_axis.select(
            (&mut self.explicit_column_start, &mut self.column_lines),
            (&mut self.explicit_row_start, &mut self.row_lines),
        );
        *explicit_start_field = explicit_start;
        if explicit_start > 0 {
            let mut prepended = Vec::with_capacity(lines.len() + explicit_start);
            prepended.resize_with(explicit_start, Vec::new);
            prepended.append(lines);
            *lines = prepended;
        }
        lines.resize_with(track_count.saturating_add(1), Vec::new);
    }

    /// The tracks considered occupied for collapsing the empty tracks of a repeat(auto-fit) in the grid axis.
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#repeat-auto-fit
    // However, because placement occurs after track sizing, grid lanes containers use a heuristic to determine if a
    // track will be occupied:
    pub(super) fn grid_lanes_occupied_tracks(&self, axis: Axis) -> Vec<bool> {
        let track_count = self.axis_tracks(axis).len();
        let mut occupied = vec![false; track_count];
        let mut auto_placed_span_sum = 0usize;
        for item in &self.items {
            if item.is_auto_placed_in_grid_lanes {
                auto_placed_span_sum = auto_placed_span_sum.saturating_add(item.span(axis));
                continue;
            }
            // * All tracks occupied by explicitly placed items are considered occupied.
            let start = item.position(axis).max(0) as usize;
            let end = start.saturating_add(item.span(axis)).min(track_count);
            for track in occupied.iter_mut().take(end).skip(start) {
                *track = true;
            }
        }
        // * With the sum of the spans of all auto-placed items as N, all unoccupied tracks up to the Nth such track
        //   are considered occupied.
        for track in occupied
            .iter_mut()
            .filter(|occupied| !**occupied)
            .take(auto_placed_span_sum)
        {
            *track = true;
        }
        occupied
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#track-sizing
    // Track sizing works the same as in CSS Grid, except that when considering which items contribute to intrinsic
    // sizes:
    // * All items explicitly placed in that track contribute, and
    // * All items with an automatic grid position contribute (regardless of whether they are ultimately placed in that
    //   track).
    //
    // In the case of spanning items with an automatic grid position, they are assumed to be placed at every possible
    // start position, and contribute accordingly.
    pub(super) fn grid_lanes_item_contributions_to_track_sizing(&self, axis: Axis) -> Vec<ItemContribution> {
        let track_count = self.axis_tracks(axis).len();
        let mut result = Vec::new();
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#track-sizing-performance
        // Track sizing can be optimized by aggregating items that have the same span size and placement into a single
        // virtual item as follows:
        // 1. Separate all the grid items into item groups, according to the following properties:
        //    * the span of the item
        //    * the placement of the item, i.e. which tracks it is allowed to be placed in
        //    * the item's baseline-sharing group
        // 2. For each item group, synthesize a virtual grid item that has the maximum of every intrinsic size
        //    contribution among the items in that group.
        // 3. Place hypothetical copies of each virtual grid item into the grid axis tracks in every position that the
        //    item could potentially occupy, and run the track sizing algorithm with those items.
        // NB: Explicitly placed items keep their own contributions, since each is placed in only one position. The
        //     contributions of an auto-placed item can depend on the tracks it spans, so each copy of a virtual item
        //     takes the maximum of the contributions of its items placed at that position. Scroll containers form
        //     their own groups, since track sizing treats their contributions differently.
        let mut groups: Vec<ItemGroup> = Vec::new();
        for item in self.items.iter().copied() {
            if !item.is_auto_placed_in_grid_lanes {
                if self.grid_item_is_subgridded(item, axis) {
                    result.extend(self.subgrid_item_contributions_to_track_sizing(item, axis));
                } else {
                    result.push(self.item_contribution(item, axis, track_count));
                }
                continue;
            }
            let span = item.span(axis);
            let start_count = track_count.saturating_sub(span).saturating_add(1);
            if self.grid_item_is_subgridded(item, axis) {
                // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#track-sizing-subgrid
                // When sizing the tracks of a grid lanes container, a subgrid with an automatic grid position (whether
                // a regular grid subgrid or grid lanes subgrid) also has special handling of its items:
                // * Every item is placed into every possible parent grid track that could be spanned by the subgrid,
                //   (ignoring any explicit placement of the item).
                // FIXME: Ignore the explicit placement of the subgrid's items.
                for start in 0..start_count {
                    let mut placed = item;
                    placed.set_position(axis, start as i32, span);
                    result.extend(self.subgrid_item_contributions_to_track_sizing(placed, axis));
                }
                continue;
            }
            let is_scroll_container = self.item_facts(item).is_scroll_container();
            let group_index = match groups
                .iter()
                .position(|group| group.span == span && group.is_scroll_container == is_scroll_container)
            {
                Some(index) => index,
                None => {
                    groups.push(ItemGroup {
                        span,
                        is_scroll_container,
                        virtual_items: Vec::with_capacity(start_count),
                    });
                    groups.len() - 1
                }
            };
            for start in 0..start_count {
                let mut placed = item;
                placed.set_position(axis, start as i32, span);
                let contribution = self.item_contribution(placed, axis, track_count);
                let virtual_items = &mut groups[group_index].virtual_items;
                match virtual_items.get_mut(start) {
                    Some(virtual_item) => {
                        virtual_item.minimum = virtual_item.minimum.max(contribution.minimum);
                        virtual_item.min_content = virtual_item.min_content.max(contribution.min_content);
                        virtual_item.limited_min_content =
                            virtual_item.limited_min_content.max(contribution.limited_min_content);
                        virtual_item.max_content = virtual_item.max_content.max(contribution.max_content);
                        virtual_item.limited_max_content =
                            virtual_item.limited_max_content.max(contribution.limited_max_content);
                    }
                    None => virtual_items.push(contribution),
                }
            }
        }
        for group in groups {
            result.extend(group.virtual_items);
        }
        result
    }

    /// Sizes the tracks of the grid axis and places and sizes every item.
    pub(super) fn run_grid_lanes_track_sizing_and_placement(&mut self, lanes: GridLanes) {
        let stacking_axis = lanes.stacking_axis();
        // NB: The single track of the stacking axis stands for the content box of the grid lanes container while the
        //     items are sized, since that forms their containing block in that axis.
        let containing_block_size = self
            .grid_lanes_stacking_containing_block_size(stacking_axis)
            .unwrap_or_default();
        *axis_tracks_mut(self, stacking_axis) = vec![Track::fixed(containing_block_size)];

        if lanes.grid_axis.is_column() {
            self.resolve_item_metrics(Axis::Column);
            self.run_track_sizing(Axis::Column);
        } else {
            // NB: An item's inline size in the stacking axis does not depend on where it is placed, but its block size
            //     contributions to the rows depend on it.
            self.resolve_item_metrics(Axis::Column);
            self.resolve_item_sizes(Axis::Column);
            self.resolve_item_metrics(Axis::Row);
            self.run_track_sizing(Axis::Row);
        }
        self.run_grid_lanes_layout_and_placement_algorithm(lanes);
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#grid-lanes-layout-algorithm
    fn run_grid_lanes_layout_and_placement_algorithm(&mut self, lanes: GridLanes) {
        let grid_axis = lanes.grid_axis;
        let stacking_axis = lanes.stacking_axis();
        let track_count = self.axis_tracks(grid_axis).len();
        let tie_threshold = self.tie_threshold(grid_axis);
        let gap = self.resolved_gap(stacking_axis, self.axis_available(stacking_axis));
        let collapsed = self
            .axis_tracks(grid_axis)
            .iter()
            .map(|track| track.is_collapsed)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let dense = self.container_style.grid_auto_flow_dense();
        let mut skipped_spaces = vec![Vec::<SkippedSpace>::new(); track_count];

        // For each of the tracks in the grid axis, keep a running position initialized to zero. Maintain also a
        // auto-placement cursor, initially pointing to the first line.
        let mut running_positions = vec![CssPixels::default(); track_count];
        let mut items_in_tracks = vec![Vec::new(); track_count];
        let mut auto_placement_cursor = 0usize;

        let max_running_position = |running_positions: &[CssPixels], start: usize, span: usize| {
            running_positions[start..start + span]
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .max()
                .unwrap_or_default()
        };

        // For each item in order-modified document order:
        for item_index in 0..self.items.len() {
            let mut item = self.items[item_index];
            let span = item.span(grid_axis).min(track_count);
            if track_count == 0 || span == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let auto_placement_cursor_before_placement = auto_placement_cursor;
            // 1. If the item has a definite grid position in the grid axis, use that placement.
            //    Otherwise, resolve its grid axis placement using these substeps:
            if item.is_auto_placed_in_grid_lanes {
                // 1. Starting at the first grid axis line in the implicit grid, find the largest running position of
                //    the grid axis tracks that the item would span if it were placed at this line, and call this
                //    position max_pos.
                // 2. Repeat the previous step for each successive line number until the item would no longer fit
                //    inside the grid.
                // NB: A collapsed grid track cannot accept placement of auto-placed items.
                let candidates = (0..=track_count - span)
                    .filter(|&line| !collapsed[line..line + span].iter().any(|&collapsed| collapsed))
                    .map(|line| (line, max_running_position(&running_positions, line, span)))
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
                // 3. Let possible lines be the line that resulted in the smallest max_pos, and all lines that result
                //    in a max_pos within the tie threshold of this max_pos.
                let smallest_max_pos = candidates.iter().map(|&(_, max_pos)| max_pos).min();
                let is_possible = |max_pos: CssPixels| {
                    tie_threshold.is_none_or(|threshold| {
                        smallest_max_pos.is_some_and(|smallest| max_pos - smallest <= threshold)
                    })
                };
                let possible_lines = candidates
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|&&(_, max_pos)| is_possible(max_pos))
                    .map(|&(line, _)| line);
                // 4. Choose the first line in possible lines greater than or equal to the auto-placement cursor as the
                //    item's position in the grid axis; or if there are none such, choose the first one.
                let line = possible_lines
                    .clone()
                    .find(|&line| line >= auto_placement_cursor)
                    .or_else(|| possible_lines.clone().next())
                    .unwrap_or(0);
                // 5. Update the auto-placement cursor to point to item's last line.
                auto_placement_cursor = line + span;
                item.set_position(grid_axis, line as i32, span);
            }
            let start = (item.position(grid_axis).max(0) as usize).min(track_count - span);

            // 2. Place the item in its grid axis tracks at the maximum of the running positions of the tracks it spans.
            let max_pos = max_running_position(&running_positions, start, span);
            self.items[item_index] = item;

            // 3. Calculate the size of the item's containing block and then layout the item. Set the running position
            //    of the spanned grid axis tracks to max_pos + outer size + grid-gap.
            if grid_axis.is_column() {
                self.resolve_metrics_of_item(item_index, Axis::Column);
                self.resolve_size_of_item(item_index, Axis::Column);
            }
            self.resolve_metrics_of_item(item_index, Axis::Row);
            self.resolve_size_of_item(item_index, Axis::Row);
            let item = self.items[item_index];
            let content_size = axis_content_size(&self.cells_of(item), stacking_axis);
            // For this purpose, the outer sizes of the box are floored at zero.
            let outer_size = self
                .add_outer_size(item, stacking_axis, content_size)
                .max(CssPixels::default());

            // 4. If the grid lanes container uses dense packing, and there exists skipped spaces in the layout (e.g.
            //    due to spanning items) into which the item, as it is sized now, could have fit if it were placed
            //    earlier, and where the spanned tracks have the same total used size as the tracks into which it is
            //    currently placed, then instead place it into the highest such space. If there are multiple valid
            //    spaces within the tie threshold of the highest space, place it in the start-most of them. Rewind the
            //    auto-placement cursor and the running position to their values before this item’s placement.
            let dense_placement = dense
                .then(|| {
                    let span_size = |line: usize| self.grid_lanes_span_size(grid_axis, line, span);
                    let current_size = span_size(start);
                    let lines = if item.is_auto_placed_in_grid_lanes {
                        0..track_count - span + 1
                    } else {
                        start..start + 1
                    };
                    let lines = lines.filter(|&line| {
                        !collapsed[line..line + span].iter().any(|&collapsed| collapsed)
                            && span_size(line) == current_size
                    });
                    find_dense_placement(&skipped_spaces, lines, span, outer_size, gap, tie_threshold)
                        .filter(|&(_, position)| position < max_pos)
                })
                .flatten();
            let (line, position) = match dense_placement {
                Some((line, position)) => {
                    auto_placement_cursor = auto_placement_cursor_before_placement;
                    for spaces in &mut skipped_spaces[line..line + span] {
                        fill_skipped_space(spaces, position, position + outer_size + gap);
                    }
                    self.items[item_index].set_position(grid_axis, line as i32, span);
                    (line, position)
                }
                None => {
                    for track in start..start + span {
                        if dense && running_positions[track] < max_pos {
                            skipped_spaces[track].push(SkippedSpace {
                                start: running_positions[track],
                                end: max_pos,
                            });
                        }
                        running_positions[track] = max_pos + outer_size + gap;
                    }
                    (start, max_pos)
                }
            };
            for items in &mut items_in_tracks[line..line + span] {
                items.push(item_index);
            }
            self.items[item_index].grid_lanes_stacking_area = Some(StackingAxisArea {
                offset: position,
                size: outer_size,
                is_adjacent_to_gap: false,
            });
        }
        // NB: Dense packing places items before the items placed earlier in their tracks.
        if dense {
            for items in &mut items_in_tracks {
                items.sort_by_key(|&index| {
                    self.items[index]
                        .grid_lanes_stacking_area
                        .map_or(CssPixels::default(), |area| area.offset)
                });
            }
        }

        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#stacking-range
        // The stacking range is the range between the startmost outer edge among the first items of each track and the
        // endmost outer edge among the last items of each track.
        let stacking_range = running_positions
            .iter()
            .zip(&items_in_tracks)
            .filter(|&(_, items)| !items.is_empty())
            .map(|(&position, _)| position - gap)
            .max()
            .unwrap_or_default()
            .max(CssPixels::default());
        *axis_tracks_mut(self, stacking_axis) = vec![Track::fixed(stacking_range)];
        self.align_grid_lanes_items_in_gaps(stacking_axis, &items_in_tracks, stacking_range, gap);
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#stacking-self-alignment
    // In the stacking axis, the self-alignment properties only apply to items that are adjacent to a “gap” in the
    // layout, i.e. placed in their grid track(s) either immediately before a spanning item or as the last item. The
    // alignment subject is the item's margin box, and the alignment container is that box plus the adjacent “gap”. For
    // the last item in a track, the alignment container extends to the lowest bottom outer edge among all the last
    // items in all tracks.
    fn align_grid_lanes_items_in_gaps(
        &mut self,
        stacking_axis: Axis,
        items_in_tracks: &[Vec<usize>],
        stacking_range: CssPixels,
        gap: CssPixels,
    ) {
        let mut alignment_container_ends = vec![stacking_range; self.items.len()];
        for items in items_in_tracks {
            for pair in items.windows(2) {
                let next_offset = self.items[pair[1]]
                    .grid_lanes_stacking_area
                    .map_or(CssPixels::default(), |area| area.offset);
                let end = &mut alignment_container_ends[pair[0]];
                *end = (*end).min(next_offset - gap);
            }
        }
        for (item_index, end) in alignment_container_ends.into_iter().enumerate() {
            let Some(mut area) = self.items[item_index].grid_lanes_stacking_area else {
                continue;
            };
            if end - area.offset <= area.size {
                continue;
            }
            area.size = end - area.offset;
            area.is_adjacent_to_gap = true;
            self.items[item_index].grid_lanes_stacking_area = Some(area);
            // NB: Alignment of an item does not affect the size or position of other items' alignment containers.
            self.resolve_size_of_item(item_index, stacking_axis);
        }
    }

    /// The alignment of an item in the stacking axis, where Start and End are the left/top and right/bottom sides of
    /// its alignment container.
    pub(super) fn grid_lanes_stacking_axis_item_alignment(&self, item: GridItem, axis: Axis) -> SelfAlignment {
        let alignment = self.item_physical_alignment(item, axis);
        let start = SelfAlignment {
            position: SelfPosition::Edge(alignment.container_start),
            ..alignment
        };
        if !item
            .grid_lanes_stacking_area
            .is_some_and(|area| area.is_adjacent_to_gap)
        {
            return start;
        }
        match alignment.position {
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#grid-lanes-baseline-alignment
            // Baseline alignment is not supported in the stacking axis. The baseline alignment values of the
            // self-alignment properties on grid items are treated as their fallback alignment in this axis.
            // NB: Normal alignment does not stretch an item in the stacking axis.
            SelfPosition::Normal | SelfPosition::Baseline => start,
            _ => alignment,
        }
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#grid-lanes-baseline-alignment
    // The first baseline set of the grid container in this axis is generated from the highest alignment baseline among
    // the grid items placed first in each track, and the last baseline set from the lowest alignment baseline among the
    // grid items placed last in each track.
    pub(super) fn grid_lanes_baseline_of_items(
        &self,
        lanes: GridLanes,
        baseline_set: formatting_context::BaselineSet,
    ) -> Option<CssPixels> {
        let grid_axis = lanes.grid_axis;
        let track_count = self.axis_tracks(grid_axis).len();
        // NB: Whether an item is first or last in its tracks depends only on placement, including dense packing
        //     adjustments, so the item that is placed highest (lowest) in a track is its first (last) item.
        let mut items_by_track: Vec<Option<(CssPixels, GridItem)>> = vec![None; track_count];
        for item in &self.items {
            let Some(area) = item.grid_lanes_stacking_area else {
                continue;
            };
            let start = (item.position(grid_axis).max(0) as usize).min(track_count);
            let end = start.saturating_add(item.span(grid_axis)).min(track_count);
            for slot in &mut items_by_track[start..end] {
                let replaces = slot.is_none_or(|(offset, _)| match baseline_set {
                    formatting_context::BaselineSet::First => area.offset < offset,
                    formatting_context::BaselineSet::Last => area.offset >= offset,
                });
                if replaces {
                    *slot = Some((area.offset, *item));
                }
            }
        }
        let container_writing_mode = self.container_style.writing_mode();
        let baselines = items_by_track.into_iter().flatten().filter_map(|(_, item)| {
            // NB: An item in another writing mode has no baseline in the grid's inline axis.
            let source = if self.item_style(item).writing_mode() != container_writing_mode {
                formatting_context::ChildBaselineSource::Synthesized
            } else {
                formatting_context::ChildBaselineSource::OwnOrSynthesized
            };
            self.baseline_of_placed_item(item, baseline_set, source)
        });
        match baseline_set {
            formatting_context::BaselineSet::First => baselines.min(),
            formatting_context::BaselineSet::Last => baselines.max(),
        }
    }

    /// The size of the tracks from the given line spanning the given number of tracks in the grid axis, with the
    /// gutters between them.
    fn grid_lanes_span_size(&self, axis: Axis, line: usize, span: usize) -> CssPixels {
        let tracks = self.axis_tracks(axis);
        let gaps = self.axis_gaps(axis);
        let mut size = CssPixels::default();
        for (index, track) in tracks[line..line + span].iter().enumerate() {
            size += track.base_size;
            if index + 1 < span {
                size += gaps.get(line + index).map_or(CssPixels::default(), |gap| gap.base_size);
            }
        }
        size
    }

    /// The offset and size of an item's alignment container in the stacking axis, from the content edge the tracks
    /// start at.
    pub(super) fn grid_lanes_stacking_axis_area(&self, area: StackingAxisArea, axis: Axis) -> (CssPixels, CssPixels) {
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#stacking-content-alignment
        // In the stacking axis, content-distribution is applied to the content as a whole, similarly to how it behaves
        // in block containers. More specifically, the alignment subject is the stacking range.
        let start = self.content_start_offset(axis, self.grid_container_alignment_size(axis));
        (start + area.offset, area.size)
    }
}

/// A space in a track that placement skipped over, which an item placed at an offset in it fits in if the item and the
/// gutter after it end by its end.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
struct SkippedSpace {
    start: CssPixels,
    end: CssPixels,
}

/// The highest line and offset at which an item fits in the skipped spaces of the tracks it would span, or the
/// start-most of those within the tie threshold of the highest.
fn find_dense_placement(
    skipped_spaces: &[Vec<SkippedSpace>],
    lines: impl Iterator<Item = usize>,
    span: usize,
    outer_size: CssPixels,
    gap: CssPixels,
    tie_threshold: Option<CssPixels>,
) -> Option<(usize, CssPixels)> {
    let mut placements = Vec::new();
    for line in lines {
        let tracks = &skipped_spaces[line..line + span];
        let mut offsets = tracks.iter().flatten().map(|space| space.start).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        offsets.sort();
        let fits = |offset: CssPixels| {
            tracks.iter().all(|spaces| {
                spaces
                    .iter()
                    .any(|space| space.start <= offset && offset + outer_size + gap <= space.end)
            })
        };
        if let Some(offset) = offsets.into_iter().find(|&offset| fits(offset)) {
            placements.push((line, offset));
        }
    }
    let highest = placements.iter().map(|&(_, offset)| offset).min()?;
    placements
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|&(_, offset)| tie_threshold.is_none_or(|threshold| offset - highest <= threshold))
        .min_by_key(|&(line, _)| line)
}

/// Removes the range an item fills, with the gutter after it, from the skipped space that holds it.
fn fill_skipped_space(spaces: &mut Vec<SkippedSpace>, start: CssPixels, end: CssPixels) {
    let Some(index) = spaces.iter().position(|space| space.start <= start && end <= space.end) else {
        return;
    };
    let space = spaces.remove(index);
    if space.start < start {
        spaces.push(SkippedSpace {
            start: space.start,
            end: start,
        });
    }
    if end < space.end {
        spaces.push(SkippedSpace {
            start: end,
            end: space.end,
        });
    }
}

fn axis_tracks_mut<'context, 'pass>(
    context: &'context mut GridFormattingContext<'pass>,
    axis: Axis,
) -> &'context mut Vec<Track<'pass>> {
    axis.select(&mut context.columns, &mut context.rows)
}

fn axis_content_size(cells: &used_values::RootInputCells, axis: Axis) -> CssPixels {
    axis.select(cells.content_inline_size, cells.content_block_size)
}
