//! Layout outputs retained for the next style stage: what a container query asks of a container's
//! box. A layout commit gathers its rows in the arena and hands them to the style engine together
//! once it completes, so no style evaluation reads a partly committed set.

use crate::css::style::tree::StyleNodeID;
use crate::layout::LayoutNodeArena;
use crate::layout::node_data::NodeSlotId;
use crate::layout::used_values::FfiCssPixelSize;

/// What the last layout commit and scroll state say of one element's box, for the container
/// queries that ask about it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct LayoutStyleSnapshotRow {
    pub(crate) content_width_raw: i32,
    pub(crate) content_height_raw: i32,
    /// Whether the element has a box at all; a size query on one without is unknown.
    pub(crate) has_committed_box: bool,
    pub(crate) stuck: u8,
    pub(crate) snapped: u8,
    pub(crate) scrollable: u8,
    pub(crate) scrolled: u8,
}

/// The box geometry one commit gathers for one element.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct CommittedGeometry {
    pub(crate) node: StyleNodeID,
    pub(crate) content_width_raw: i32,
    pub(crate) content_height_raw: i32,
    pub(crate) has_committed_box: bool,
}

impl LayoutNodeArena {
    /// The style node a node's row is for; `None` for a node whose box the style engine takes no row of.
    fn snapshot_target(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> Option<StyleNodeID> {
        let style_node = self
            .node_style_node(node)
            .filter(|style_node| style_node.element_index().is_some())?;
        if !self.has_style_engine() || self.bound_row(style_node) != node {
            return None;
        }
        Some(style_node)
    }

    fn committed_geometry(&self, node: NodeSlotId, style_node: StyleNodeID) -> CommittedGeometry {
        let rows = self.paintable_rows();
        let has_committed_box = rows.paintable_row_is_populated(node);
        let size = if has_committed_box {
            crate::painting::paintable_geometry::committed_content_size(&rows, node)
        } else {
            FfiCssPixelSize::default()
        };
        CommittedGeometry {
            node: style_node,
            content_width_raw: size.width.raw_value(),
            content_height_raw: size.height.raw_value(),
            has_committed_box,
        }
    }

    /// What a size container's new box moved from, for a commit that has no earlier fragment of it to compare. The
    /// layout tree can rebuild the box in the update that resizes it, with no commit between to say it lost the old one,
    /// so the row still holds the size of the box it replaced.
    pub(crate) fn content_size_change_of_rebuilt_box(
        &self,
        node: NodeSlotId,
    ) -> Option<(FfiCssPixelSize, FfiCssPixelSize)> {
        if !node_is_size_container(self, node) {
            return None;
        }
        let style_node = self.snapshot_target(node)?;
        let row = self.with_style_store(|engine| engine.layout_style_snapshot(style_node))?;
        if !row.has_committed_box {
            return None;
        }
        let geometry = self.committed_geometry(node, style_node);
        let size = |width_raw, height_raw| FfiCssPixelSize {
            width: crate::css::css_pixels::CssPixels::from_raw(width_raw),
            height: crate::css::css_pixels::CssPixels::from_raw(height_raw),
        };
        let (old_size, new_size) = (
            size(row.content_width_raw, row.content_height_raw),
            size(geometry.content_width_raw, geometry.content_height_raw),
        );
        (old_size != new_size).then_some((old_size, new_size))
    }

    /// Gathers the node's row for the style engine. Style asks layout only about size containers,
    /// and about scroll-state containers, whose rows the scroll state makes; an element that
    /// stops being one keeps its row up to date until it goes.
    pub(crate) fn gather_layout_style_snapshot_geometry(&mut self, node: NodeSlotId) {
        let is_size_container = node_is_size_container(self, node);
        // OPTIMIZATION: Most committed boxes are no size container, and while no container is held, none is gathered.
        if !is_size_container
            && self.has_style_engine()
            && !self.with_style_store(|engine| engine.has_layout_style_snapshots())
        {
            return;
        }
        let Some(style_node) = self.snapshot_target(node) else {
            return;
        };
        if !is_size_container && !self.with_style_store(|engine| engine.layout_style_snapshot(style_node).is_some()) {
            return;
        }
        let row = self.committed_geometry(node, style_node);
        self.layout_style_snapshot_commit.push(row);
    }

    /// Hands the style engine the committed box of a node whose new style makes it a size
    /// container, which the last commit gathered no row for. Until the next commit, a size query
    /// on it reads that box, as the host's evaluation reads the box it holds.
    pub(crate) fn publish_new_size_container_geometry(&mut self, node: NodeSlotId) {
        if !node_is_size_container(self, node) {
            return;
        }
        let Some(style_node) = self.snapshot_target(node) else {
            return;
        };
        if self.with_style_store(|engine| engine.layout_style_snapshot(style_node).is_some()) {
            return;
        }
        let row = self.committed_geometry(node, style_node);
        if row.has_committed_box {
            self.with_style_engine(|engine| engine.apply_new_size_container_geometry(row));
        }
    }

    /// Gathers a row without a box for a node that holds a row and lost its bound box: no commit
    /// reaches a node without one, and a size query on it is unknown.
    pub(crate) fn gather_layout_style_snapshot_box_loss(&mut self, style_node: StyleNodeID) {
        if !self.has_style_engine()
            || !self.bound_row(style_node).is_invalid()
            || !self.with_style_store(|engine| engine.layout_style_snapshot(style_node).is_some())
        {
            return;
        }
        self.layout_style_snapshot_commit.push(CommittedGeometry {
            node: style_node,
            content_width_raw: 0,
            content_height_raw: 0,
            has_committed_box: false,
        });
    }

    /// Hands the rows a completed commit gathered to the style engine.
    pub(crate) fn publish_layout_style_snapshot_commit(&mut self) {
        let rows = std::mem::take(&mut self.layout_style_snapshot_commit);
        if rows.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        self.with_style_engine(|engine| engine.apply_layout_style_snapshot_commit(&rows));
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::css::style::StyleEngine;

    #[test]
    fn a_commit_keeps_the_scroll_state_and_the_scroll_state_keeps_the_geometry() {
        let mut engine = StyleEngine::new();
        let node = StyleNodeID::element(1);
        engine.set_element_scroll_state(node, 1, 2, 4, 8);
        engine.apply_layout_style_snapshot_commit(&[CommittedGeometry {
            node,
            content_width_raw: 11,
            content_height_raw: 13,
            has_committed_box: true,
        }]);
        assert_eq!(
            engine.layout_style_snapshot(node),
            Some(LayoutStyleSnapshotRow {
                content_width_raw: 11,
                content_height_raw: 13,
                has_committed_box: true,
                stuck: 1,
                snapped: 2,
                scrollable: 4,
                scrolled: 8,
            })
        );
        engine.set_element_scroll_state(node, 0, 0, 0, 0);
        let row = engine.layout_style_snapshot(node).unwrap();
        assert!(row.has_committed_box);
        assert_eq!((row.content_width_raw, row.stuck), (11, 0));
    }
}

fn node_is_size_container(arena: &LayoutNodeArena, node: NodeSlotId) -> bool {
    crate::layout::node_facts::node_style_view(arena.data(node)).is_some_and(|style| {
        let box_values = style.box_values();
        box_values.is_size_container || box_values.is_inline_size_container
    })
}

use super::*;

/// A resolved px-or-auto inset produced by anchor resolution. It takes
/// precedence over every style read and reports
/// contains_anchor_function() == false.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum ResolvedInsetOverride {
    Auto,
    Pixels(CssPixels),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum InsetValue<'a> {
    FromStyle(&'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto),
    BareAnchor(&'a crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData),
    Resolved(ResolvedInsetOverride),
}

impl InsetValue<'_> {
    pub(crate) fn auto_value() -> Self {
        Self::Resolved(ResolvedInsetOverride::Auto)
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_auto(self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::FromStyle(value) => value.is_auto(),
            Self::BareAnchor(_) => false,
            Self::Resolved(resolved) => matches!(resolved, ResolvedInsetOverride::Auto),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn to_px(self, reference: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
        match self {
            Self::FromStyle(value) => value.to_px(reference),
            Self::BareAnchor(wrapper) => resolve_calc_to_px(std::ptr::from_ref(wrapper).cast(), reference),
            Self::Resolved(ResolvedInsetOverride::Auto) => CssPixels::default(),
            Self::Resolved(ResolvedInsetOverride::Pixels(px)) => px,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn contains_percentage(self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::FromStyle(value) => value.contains_percentage(),
            Self::BareAnchor(_) | Self::Resolved(_) => false,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn contains_anchor_function(self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::FromStyle(value) => value
                .length_percentage()
                .is_some_and(|length_percentage| length_percentage.contains_anchor_function()),
            Self::BareAnchor(_) => true,
            Self::Resolved(_) => false,
        }
    }

    /// The calculated style value carrying the anchor() function, for the
    /// abspos engine's anchor-aware resolution.
    pub(crate) fn anchor_bearing_calculated(self) -> *const c_void {
        match self {
            Self::FromStyle(value) => value
                .length_percentage()
                .expect("anchor-bearing inset must hold a style value")
                .calculated_pointer(),
            Self::BareAnchor(wrapper) => std::ptr::from_ref(wrapper).cast(),
            Self::Resolved(_) => unreachable!("resolved inset overrides never carry anchor functions"),
        }
    }
}

/// A sizing property whose computed value holds anchor-size() functions, as the abspos engine resolved it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum ResolvedSizeOverride {
    Length(CssPixels),
    Keyword(ComputedSizeKind),
}

/// The sizing and margin properties of one positioned box whose computed values hold anchor-size() functions, with
/// those functions resolved by the abspos engine. A property without one stays None and reads from style, as does a
/// sizing property whose anchor-size() functions all resolve to their fallback values. Margins also carry the zero that
/// auto resolves to in the axes a position area or anchor-center aligns the box in.
/// NB: The properties are those of the frame the box is laid out in, as style reads see them there.
/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/#anchor-size-fn
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct ResolvedAnchorSizes {
    pub(crate) width: Option<ResolvedSizeOverride>,
    pub(crate) min_width: Option<ResolvedSizeOverride>,
    pub(crate) max_width: Option<ResolvedSizeOverride>,
    pub(crate) height: Option<ResolvedSizeOverride>,
    pub(crate) min_height: Option<ResolvedSizeOverride>,
    pub(crate) max_height: Option<ResolvedSizeOverride>,
    pub(crate) margin_top: Option<CssPixels>,
    pub(crate) margin_right: Option<CssPixels>,
    pub(crate) margin_bottom: Option<CssPixels>,
    pub(crate) margin_left: Option<CssPixels>,
}

impl ResolvedAnchorSizes {
    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        *self == Self::default()
    }
}

/// The computed values `ResolvedAnchorSizes` stands for, which style reads borrow.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct AnchorResolvedValues {
    width: Option<ComputedSize>,
    min_width: Option<ComputedSize>,
    max_width: Option<ComputedSize>,
    height: Option<ComputedSize>,
    min_height: Option<ComputedSize>,
    max_height: Option<ComputedSize>,
    margin_top: Option<ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto>,
    margin_right: Option<ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto>,
    margin_bottom: Option<ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto>,
    margin_left: Option<ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto>,
    /// The frame the box is laid out in, whose sides and axes the values are those of.
    frame: geometry::Frame,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for AnchorResolvedValues {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter.debug_struct("AnchorResolvedValues").finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl AnchorResolvedValues {
    pub(crate) fn new(resolved: &ResolvedAnchorSizes, frame: geometry::Frame) -> Self {
        let size = |value: Option<ResolvedSizeOverride>| {
            value.map(|value| match value {
                ResolvedSizeOverride::Length(px) => ComputedSize::new(
                    ComputedSizeKind::Length,
                    ComputedStyleValueHandle::length(px.to_double()),
                ),
                ResolvedSizeOverride::Keyword(kind) => ComputedSize::keyword(kind),
            })
        };
        let margin = |value: Option<CssPixels>| {
            value.map(|px| ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto::new(false, ComputedStyleValueHandle::length(px.to_double())))
        };
        Self {
            width: size(resolved.width),
            min_width: size(resolved.min_width),
            max_width: size(resolved.max_width),
            height: size(resolved.height),
            min_height: size(resolved.min_height),
            max_height: size(resolved.max_height),
            margin_top: margin(resolved.margin_top),
            margin_right: margin(resolved.margin_right),
            margin_bottom: margin(resolved.margin_bottom),
            margin_left: margin(resolved.margin_left),
            frame,
        }
    }
}

/// A padding read: the style's, or zero for a non-devolvable widget.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum PaddingValue<'a> {
    FromStyle(&'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto),
    Zero,
}

impl PaddingValue<'_> {
    pub(crate) fn to_px(self, reference: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
        match self {
            Self::FromStyle(value) => value.to_px(reference),
            Self::Zero => CssPixels::default(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn contains_percentage(self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::FromStyle(value) => value.contains_percentage(),
            Self::Zero => false,
        }
    }
}

/// The layout pass view of a node's computed style: the pure payload view
/// plus the resolved anchor insets the abspos engine threads to the four
/// inset reads of the box it is placing, the line builder's vertical-align
/// keyword substitution, and the padding and border widths a non-devolvable
/// widget drops. Every other read derefs to ComputedValuesView.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct StyleValues<'a> {
    style: ComputedValuesView<'a>,
    resolved_anchor_insets: Option<&'a formatting_context::ResolvedAnchorInsets>,
    anchor_resolved_values: Option<&'a AnchorResolvedValues>,
    vertical_align_override: Option<u8>,
    is_non_devolvable_widget: bool,
    frame: geometry::Frame,
}

impl<'a> std::ops::Deref for StyleValues<'a> {
    type Target = ComputedValuesView<'a>;

    fn deref(&self) -> &ComputedValuesView<'a> {
        &self.style
    }
}

impl<'a> StyleValues<'a> {
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn new(payloads: ComputedValuesView<'a>) -> Self {
        Self {
            style: payloads,
            resolved_anchor_insets: None,
            anchor_resolved_values: None,
            vertical_align_override: None,
            is_non_devolvable_widget: false,
            frame: geometry::Frame::PHYSICAL,
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn for_node(pass: &LayoutPass<'a>, node: Node) -> Self {
        let (data, style) = pass.row_and_style(node);
        StyleValues::new(style.expect("styled node must publish its style container before layout"))
            .for_kind(data.kind.get())
            .in_frame(pass.frame)
    }

    /// The view as seen from `frame`, whose sides and axes the box's sizes and box model properties are read in.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn in_frame(mut self, frame: geometry::Frame) -> Self {
        self.frame = frame;
        self
    }

    #[inline]
    fn physical(self, side: geometry::Side) -> geometry::Side {
        if self.frame.is_physical() {
            return side;
        }
        self.frame.physical_side(side)
    }

    /// `physical`, unless the frame is transposed and so reads the value of the other physical axis, `transposed`.
    #[inline]
    fn physical_or_transposed<T>(self, physical: T, transposed: T) -> T {
        if self.frame.is_transposed() {
            transposed
        } else {
            physical
        }
    }

    /// Whether the inline-start side is the frame's right side rather than its left side.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn inline_axis_is_reverse(self) -> bool {
        if self.frame.is_physical() {
            return self.style.inline_axis_is_reverse();
        }
        // NB: The left side of a frame is the line-left side, which is inline-start in ltr text.
        self.style.direction() == direction::RTL
    }

    /// Whether the block-start side is the frame's bottom side rather than its top side.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn block_axis_is_reverse(self) -> bool {
        if self.frame.is_physical() {
            return self.style.block_axis_is_reverse();
        }
        false
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn unresolved_width(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        self.physical_or_transposed(self.style.width(), self.style.height())
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn unresolved_height(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        self.physical_or_transposed(self.style.height(), self.style.width())
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn unresolved_min_width(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        self.physical_or_transposed(self.style.min_width(), self.style.min_height())
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn unresolved_min_height(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        self.physical_or_transposed(self.style.min_height(), self.style.min_width())
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn unresolved_max_width(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        self.physical_or_transposed(self.style.max_width(), self.style.max_height())
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn unresolved_max_height(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        self.physical_or_transposed(self.style.max_height(), self.style.max_width())
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn contain_intrinsic_width_has_length(self) -> bool {
        self.physical_or_transposed(
            self.style.contain_intrinsic_width_has_length(),
            self.style.contain_intrinsic_height_has_length(),
        )
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn contain_intrinsic_width_px(self) -> f64 {
        self.physical_or_transposed(
            self.style.contain_intrinsic_width_px(),
            self.style.contain_intrinsic_height_px(),
        )
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn contain_intrinsic_height_has_length(self) -> bool {
        self.physical_or_transposed(
            self.style.contain_intrinsic_height_has_length(),
            self.style.contain_intrinsic_width_has_length(),
        )
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn contain_intrinsic_height_px(self) -> f64 {
        self.physical_or_transposed(
            self.style.contain_intrinsic_height_px(),
            self.style.contain_intrinsic_width_px(),
        )
    }

    /// The preferred aspect ratio as a width to height fraction in the frame.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn css_preferred_aspect_ratio(self) -> (CssPixels, CssPixels) {
        let (numerator, denominator) = self.style.css_preferred_aspect_ratio();
        if self.frame.is_transposed() {
            (denominator, numerator)
        } else {
            (numerator, denominator)
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_spacing_horizontal(self) -> CssPixels {
        self.physical_or_transposed(
            self.style.border_spacing_horizontal(),
            self.style.border_spacing_vertical(),
        )
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_spacing_vertical(self) -> CssPixels {
        self.physical_or_transposed(
            self.style.border_spacing_vertical(),
            self.style.border_spacing_horizontal(),
        )
    }

    #[inline]
    fn physical_margin(self, side: geometry::Side) -> &'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto {
        match side {
            geometry::Side::Top => self.style.margin_top(),
            geometry::Side::Right => self.style.margin_right(),
            geometry::Side::Bottom => self.style.margin_bottom(),
            geometry::Side::Left => self.style.margin_left(),
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn unresolved_margin_top(self) -> &'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto {
        self.physical_margin(self.physical(geometry::Side::Top))
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn unresolved_margin_right(self) -> &'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto {
        self.physical_margin(self.physical(geometry::Side::Right))
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn unresolved_margin_bottom(self) -> &'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto {
        self.physical_margin(self.physical(geometry::Side::Bottom))
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn unresolved_margin_left(self) -> &'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto {
        self.physical_margin(self.physical(geometry::Side::Left))
    }

    #[inline]
    fn physical_border(self, side: geometry::Side) -> (CssPixels, u8, u32) {
        match side {
            geometry::Side::Top => (
                self.style.border_top_width(),
                self.style.border_top_style(),
                self.style.border_top_color(),
            ),
            geometry::Side::Right => (
                self.style.border_right_width(),
                self.style.border_right_style(),
                self.style.border_right_color(),
            ),
            geometry::Side::Bottom => (
                self.style.border_bottom_width(),
                self.style.border_bottom_style(),
                self.style.border_bottom_color(),
            ),
            geometry::Side::Left => (
                self.style.border_left_width(),
                self.style.border_left_style(),
                self.style.border_left_color(),
            ),
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_top_style(self) -> u8 {
        self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Top)).1
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_right_style(self) -> u8 {
        self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Right)).1
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_bottom_style(self) -> u8 {
        self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Bottom)).1
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_left_style(self) -> u8 {
        self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Left)).1
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_top_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Top)).2
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_right_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Right)).2
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_bottom_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Bottom)).2
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_left_color(self) -> u32 {
        self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Left)).2
    }

    /// The view for a box of `kind`. A non-devolvable widget is drawn natively to fill its box, so author padding and
    /// borders don't apply to it.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn for_kind(mut self, kind: NodeKind) -> Self {
        self.is_non_devolvable_widget = node_facts::kind_is_non_devolvable_widget(kind);
        self
    }

    pub(crate) fn with_resolved_insets(
        mut self,
        resolved: Option<&'a formatting_context::ResolvedAnchorInsets>,
    ) -> Self {
        self.resolved_anchor_insets = resolved;
        self
    }

    pub(crate) fn with_anchor_resolved_values(mut self, resolved: Option<&'a AnchorResolvedValues>) -> Self {
        // FIXME: Map the resolved values into the frame of a box that lays out its contents in another writing mode
        //        than its containing block, rather than reading its computed values there.
        self.anchor_resolved_values = resolved.filter(|resolved| resolved.frame == self.frame);
        self
    }

    pub(crate) fn width(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        self.anchor_resolved_values
            .and_then(|resolved| resolved.width.as_ref())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| unresolvable_anchor_size_or(self.unresolved_width(), auto_computed_size()))
    }

    pub(crate) fn min_width(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        self.anchor_resolved_values
            .and_then(|resolved| resolved.min_width.as_ref())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| unresolvable_anchor_size_or(self.unresolved_min_width(), auto_computed_size()))
    }

    pub(crate) fn max_width(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        self.anchor_resolved_values
            .and_then(|resolved| resolved.max_width.as_ref())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| unresolvable_anchor_size_or(self.unresolved_max_width(), none_computed_size()))
    }

    pub(crate) fn height(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        self.anchor_resolved_values
            .and_then(|resolved| resolved.height.as_ref())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| unresolvable_anchor_size_or(self.unresolved_height(), auto_computed_size()))
    }

    /// Whether the box is a table row, row group or cell, whose 'min-height' and 'max-height' are ignored.
    // NB: "In CSS 2.1, the effect of 'min-height' and 'max-height' on tables, inline tables, table cells, table rows,
    //     and row groups is undefined." https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/visudet.html#min-max-heights
    // INTEROP: Other engines ignore them on table cells, rows and row groups.
    fn ignores_min_and_max_height(self) -> bool {
        let display = self.display();
        display.is_table_cell() || display.is_table_row() || display.is_table_row_group_kind()
    }

    pub(crate) fn min_height(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        if self.ignores_min_and_max_height() {
            return auto_computed_size();
        }
        self.anchor_resolved_values
            .and_then(|resolved| resolved.min_height.as_ref())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| unresolvable_anchor_size_or(self.unresolved_min_height(), auto_computed_size()))
    }

    pub(crate) fn max_height(self) -> &'a ComputedSize {
        if self.ignores_min_and_max_height() {
            return none_computed_size();
        }
        self.anchor_resolved_values
            .and_then(|resolved| resolved.max_height.as_ref())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| unresolvable_anchor_size_or(self.unresolved_max_height(), none_computed_size()))
    }

    pub(crate) fn margin_top(self) -> &'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto {
        self.anchor_resolved_values
            .and_then(|resolved| resolved.margin_top.as_ref())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.unresolved_margin_top())
    }

    pub(crate) fn margin_right(self) -> &'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto {
        self.anchor_resolved_values
            .and_then(|resolved| resolved.margin_right.as_ref())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.unresolved_margin_right())
    }

    pub(crate) fn margin_bottom(self) -> &'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto {
        self.anchor_resolved_values
            .and_then(|resolved| resolved.margin_bottom.as_ref())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.unresolved_margin_bottom())
    }

    pub(crate) fn margin_left(self) -> &'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto {
        self.anchor_resolved_values
            .and_then(|resolved| resolved.margin_left.as_ref())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.unresolved_margin_left())
    }

    fn bare_anchor_wrapper(self, physical_side: geometry::Side) -> Option<&'a crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData> {
        let values = self.style.surround();
        let handle = match physical_side {
            geometry::Side::Top => &values.top_anchor_inset_wrapper,
            geometry::Side::Right => &values.right_anchor_inset_wrapper,
            geometry::Side::Bottom => &values.bottom_anchor_inset_wrapper,
            geometry::Side::Left => &values.left_anchor_inset_wrapper,
        };
        // SAFETY: The node's style group payload retains the wrapper for the
        // view's lifetime.
        unsafe {
            handle
                .pointer
                .cast::<crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData>()
                .as_ref()
        }
    }

    fn inset_value(self, side: geometry::Side) -> InsetValue<'a> {
        // NB: The abspos engine resolves anchor functions per side of the frame it lays the box out in.
        if let Some(resolved) = self.resolved_anchor_insets.and_then(|insets| insets.override_for(side)) {
            return InsetValue::Resolved(resolved);
        }
        let physical_side = self.physical(side);
        if let Some(wrapper) = self.bare_anchor_wrapper(physical_side) {
            return InsetValue::BareAnchor(wrapper);
        }
        let values = self.style.surround();
        InsetValue::FromStyle(match physical_side {
            geometry::Side::Top => &values.inset.top,
            geometry::Side::Right => &values.inset.right,
            geometry::Side::Bottom => &values.inset.bottom,
            geometry::Side::Left => &values.inset.left,
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn inset_top(self) -> InsetValue<'a> {
        self.inset_value(geometry::Side::Top)
    }

    pub(crate) fn inset_right(self) -> InsetValue<'a> {
        self.inset_value(geometry::Side::Right)
    }

    pub(crate) fn inset_bottom(self) -> InsetValue<'a> {
        self.inset_value(geometry::Side::Bottom)
    }

    pub(crate) fn inset_left(self) -> InsetValue<'a> {
        self.inset_value(geometry::Side::Left)
    }

    // AD-HOC: CSS UI only says a non-devolvable widget keeps its native appearance whatever its border; it doesn't say
    //         the border takes no room, nor anything about padding. A native control fills its box, so its border
    //         widths and its padding read as zero.
    fn padding_unless_non_devolvable(self, padding: &'a ComputedLengthPercentageOrAuto) -> PaddingValue<'a> {
        if self.is_non_devolvable_widget {
            PaddingValue::Zero
        } else {
            PaddingValue::FromStyle(padding)
        }
    }

    fn border_width_unless_non_devolvable(self, width: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
        if self.is_non_devolvable_widget {
            CssPixels::default()
        } else {
            width
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn physical_padding(self, side: geometry::Side) -> PaddingValue<'a> {
        self.padding_unless_non_devolvable(match side {
            geometry::Side::Top => self.style.padding_top(),
            geometry::Side::Right => self.style.padding_right(),
            geometry::Side::Bottom => self.style.padding_bottom(),
            geometry::Side::Left => self.style.padding_left(),
        })
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn padding_top(self) -> PaddingValue<'a> {
        self.physical_padding(self.physical(geometry::Side::Top))
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn padding_right(self) -> PaddingValue<'a> {
        self.physical_padding(self.physical(geometry::Side::Right))
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn padding_bottom(self) -> PaddingValue<'a> {
        self.physical_padding(self.physical(geometry::Side::Bottom))
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn padding_left(self) -> PaddingValue<'a> {
        self.physical_padding(self.physical(geometry::Side::Left))
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_top_width(self) -> CssPixels {
        self.border_width_unless_non_devolvable(self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Top)).0)
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_right_width(self) -> CssPixels {
        self.border_width_unless_non_devolvable(self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Right)).0)
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_bottom_width(self) -> CssPixels {
        self.border_width_unless_non_devolvable(self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Bottom)).0)
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn border_left_width(self) -> CssPixels {
        self.border_width_unless_non_devolvable(self.physical_border(self.physical(geometry::Side::Left)).0)
    }

    pub(crate) fn with_vertical_align_keyword(mut self, keyword: u8) -> Self {
        self.vertical_align_override = Some(keyword);
        self
    }

    pub(crate) fn vertical_align_is_keyword(self) -> bool {
        self.vertical_align_override.is_some() || self.style.box_values().vertical_align.is_keyword
    }

    pub(crate) fn vertical_align_keyword(self) -> u8 {
        self.vertical_align_override
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.style.box_values().vertical_align.keyword)
    }
}

/// `size`, or `initial` when `size` holds an anchor function that is unresolvable and has no fallback value.
/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/#anchor-size-resolution
/// If no fallback value is specified, it makes the declaration referencing it invalid at computed-value time.
/// NB: Outside of the resolutions the abspos engine installs, an anchor function is unresolvable.
fn unresolvable_anchor_size_or<'a>(size: &'a ComputedSize, initial: &'static ComputedSize) -> &'a ComputedSize {
    if !size.contains_anchor_function() {
        return size;
    }
    let mut percentage_basis = CssPixels::default();
    // SAFETY: The callback context is the percentage basis, live for this synchronous resolution.
    let resolved = unsafe {
        resolve_calc_with_external_resolutions(
            size.length_percentage().calculated_pointer(),
            percentage_basis,
            (&raw mut percentage_basis).cast(),
            Some(resolve_unresolvable_anchor_function),
        )
    };
    if resolved.resolved { size } else { initial }
}

/// A px calc node, holding one reference for the external-resolution snapshot that releases it.
pub(crate) fn calc_node_create_px_dimension(value: f64) -> *const c_void {
    crate::css::calc::calc_node_create_numeric_dimension(
        formatting_context::CALC_NUMERIC_KIND_LENGTH,
        value,
        crate::css::style_compute::px_length_unit(),
    )
    .cast()
}

/// The calc node the fallback value of an unresolvable anchor() or anchor-size() function resolves to, or null when
/// it has none. Nested anchor functions resolve through `resolve_non_math_function`.
/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/#anchor-resolution
///
/// # Safety
/// `callback_context` must be what `resolve_non_math_function` expects, and stay live for the resolution.
pub(crate) unsafe fn anchor_function_fallback_node(
    fallback_value: &crate::css::style_value::RetainedStyleValueData,
    percentage_basis: CssPixels,
    callback_context: *mut c_void,
    resolve_non_math_function: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const c_void) -> *const c_void,
) -> *const c_void {
    use crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData;
    match fallback_value.optional_data() {
        None => std::ptr::null(),
        Some(StyleValueData::Length { value, unit }) => {
            // Computed anchor() fallbacks hold absolute lengths only; relative
            // units carry NaN canonical ratios.
            let ratio = crate::css::style_compute::LENGTH_UNIT_CANONICAL_PX_RATIOS[*unit as usize];
            assert!(ratio.is_finite());
            calc_node_create_px_dimension(CssPixels::nearest_value_for(*value * ratio).to_double())
        }
        Some(StyleValueData::Percentage { value }) => {
            calc_node_create_px_dimension(percentage_basis.to_double() * (value / 100.0))
        }
        Some(StyleValueData::Calculated { .. }) => {
            // SAFETY: The anchor function shell retains the fallback calculation for
            // this synchronous resolution.
            let resolved = unsafe {
                resolve_calc_with_external_resolutions(
                    fallback_value.pointer().cast(),
                    percentage_basis,
                    callback_context,
                    Some(resolve_non_math_function),
                )
            };
            if !resolved.resolved {
                return std::ptr::null();
            }
            calc_node_create_px_dimension(resolved.value)
        }
        // SAFETY: The outer anchor function shell retains the nested one for this synchronous resolution.
        Some(StyleValueData::Anchor { .. } | StyleValueData::AnchorSize { .. }) => unsafe {
            resolve_non_math_function(callback_context, fallback_value.pointer().cast())
        },
        Some(_) => {
            unreachable!("anchor function fallback must be a length, percentage, calculation or anchor function")
        }
    }
}

/// Resolves an anchor() or anchor-size() function outside the abspos engine, where it is unresolvable and resolves
/// to its fallback value. The callback context is the percentage basis.
unsafe extern "C" fn resolve_unresolvable_anchor_function(context: *mut c_void, shell: *const c_void) -> *const c_void {
    use crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData;
    // SAFETY: The context is the percentage basis resolve_calc_with_unresolvable_anchor_functions passes.
    let percentage_basis = unsafe { *context.cast::<CssPixels>() };
    // SAFETY: `shell` is the live style value the calc core's non-math-function node retains.
    match unsafe { &*shell.cast::<StyleValueData>() }.anchor_name_and_fallback() {
        Some((_, _, fallback_value)) => unsafe {
            anchor_function_fallback_node(
                fallback_value,
                percentage_basis,
                context,
                resolve_unresolvable_anchor_function,
            )
        },
        None => std::ptr::null(),
    }
}

/// Resolves `calculated`, whose anchor functions are unresolvable, to px. A function without a fallback value makes
/// the declaration invalid at computed-value time, which this approximates as zero.
pub(crate) fn resolve_calc_with_unresolvable_anchor_functions(
    calculated: *const c_void,
    mut percentage_basis: CssPixels,
) -> f64 {
    // SAFETY: The callback context is the percentage basis, live for this synchronous resolution.
    let resolved = unsafe {
        resolve_calc_with_external_resolutions(
            calculated,
            percentage_basis,
            (&raw mut percentage_basis).cast(),
            Some(resolve_unresolvable_anchor_function),
        )
    };
    if resolved.resolved { resolved.value } else { 0.0 }
}

pub(crate) unsafe fn resolve_calc_with_external_resolutions(
    calculated: *const c_void,
    percentage_basis: CssPixels,
    callback_context: *mut c_void,
    resolve_non_math_function: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const c_void) -> *const c_void>,
) -> crate::css::calc::FfiResolvedCalc {
    use crate::css::calc::{
        CalcExternalResolutionKind, CalcNode, calc_root_from_calculated, collect_external_resolutions,
        resolve_calculated,
    };

    let context = px_calc_resolution_context(percentage_basis);
    let root = unsafe { &*calc_root_from_calculated(calculated) };
    let mut externals = Vec::new();
    collect_external_resolutions(root, &mut externals);
    if let Some(resolve_non_math_function) = resolve_non_math_function {
        for resolution in &mut externals {
            if resolution.kind == CalcExternalResolutionKind::NonMathFunction {
                let node = unsafe { resolve_non_math_function(callback_context, resolution.source.pointer().cast()) }
                    .cast::<CalcNode>();
                // SAFETY: The resolver hands back one reference to each node it resolves.
                resolution.resolved_node = (!node.is_null()).then(|| unsafe { std::sync::Arc::from_raw(node) });
            }
        }
    }
    resolve_calculated(
        unsafe { &*calculated.cast::<crate::css::style_value::StyleValueData>() },
        &context,
        &externals,
        true,
    )
}

use super::*;
use crate::layout::used_transform;
use libgfx_rust::{FloatPoint, FloatRect, FloatSize};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiFloatPoint {
    pub x: f32,
    pub y: f32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiFloatRect {
    pub x: f32,
    pub y: f32,
    pub width: f32,
    pub height: f32,
}

/// The glyph cell one code unit of an SVG text content element's character data occupies, in the
/// element's coordinate system. The SVG DOM text methods read these back from the committed box.
/// https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/coords.html#BoundingBoxes
/// The full glyph cell must have width equal to the horizontal advance and height equal to the EM
/// box for horizontal text.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiSvgTextCharacterCell {
    pub x: f32,
    pub y: f32,
    pub width: f32,
    pub height: f32,
    /// Where the alignment point of the typographic character is along the block axis: The current text position the
    /// character was placed at, which the dominant baseline of its font is aligned to.
    pub alignment_point_y: f32,
    /// Whether this code unit is the first, in document order, of the typographic character whose
    /// cell this is. A later code unit of the same character carries the same cell, unmarked.
    pub starts_typographic_character: bool,
}

/// Appends the cell of each character the edits map the given cells back to: Where an edit turned characters into
/// others, the characters it took share the cell of those it made.
fn append_svg_text_cells_through_edits<'a>(
    cells: &[FfiSvgTextCharacterCell],
    edits: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a super::rendered_text::RenderedTextEdit>,
    out: &mut Vec<FfiSvgTextCharacterCell>,
) {
    let mut cursor = 0;
    for edit in edits {
        let start = edit.rendered_start_offset;
        let end = start + edit.rendered_length_in_code_units;
        out.extend_from_slice(&cells[cursor..start]);
        cursor = end;
        if edit.dom_length_in_code_units == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        let mut cell = svg_text_cell_for_source_span(cells, start, end);
        out.push(cell);
        cell.starts_typographic_character = false;
        out.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(cell, edit.dom_length_in_code_units - 1));
    }
    out.extend_from_slice(&cells[cursor..]);
}

fn svg_text_cell_for_source_span(
    cells: &[FfiSvgTextCharacterCell],
    start: usize,
    end: usize,
) -> FfiSvgTextCharacterCell {
    if let Some((&first, others)) = cells[start..end].split_first() {
        let mut bounds = FloatRect::new(first.x, first.y, first.width, first.height);
        for other in others {
            bounds = united_even_if_empty(
                Some(bounds),
                FloatRect::new(other.x, other.y, other.width, other.height),
            );
        }
        return FfiSvgTextCharacterCell {
            x: bounds.x,
            y: bounds.y,
            width: bounds.width,
            height: bounds.height,
            ..first
        };
    }
    // A source character removed by casing has an empty cell at its position between the surrounding glyphs.
    let mut cell = cells.get(start).copied().unwrap_or_else(|| {
        let mut last = cells.last().copied().unwrap_or_default();
        last.x += last.width;
        last
    });
    cell.width = 0.0;
    cell.starts_typographic_character = false;
    cell
}

/// What shaping one SVG text run yields: its glyphs, its total advance, the union of its glyph
/// cells, and the glyph cell of every one of its code units.
struct ShapedSvgText {
    runs: Vec<libgfx_rust::path::GlyphRun>,
    advance: f32,
    glyph_cells: SvgCssPixelRect,
    character_cells: Vec<FfiSvgTextCharacterCell>,
}

impl ShapedSvgText {
    fn shift_glyphs(&mut self, shifts: &[FfiFloatPoint]) {
        let mut run_offset = 0;
        for run in &mut self.runs {
            let mut run_length = 0;
            let offsets: Vec<_> = run
                .glyphs
                .placed()
                .map(|glyph| {
                    run_length += glyph.glyph.length_in_code_units();
                    shifts[run_offset + glyph.cluster_start as usize]
                })
                .collect();
            if offsets.iter().all(|offset| offset.x == 0.0 && offset.y == 0.0) {
                run_offset += run_length;
                continue;
            }
            let mut offsets = offsets.into_iter();
            run.glyphs.update_positions(|_, x, y| {
                let offset = offsets.next().expect("one offset per glyph");
                *x += offset.x;
                *y += offset.y;
            });
            run_offset += run_length;
        }
    }
}

/// A path with a closed subpath around each of the given rects.
fn path_of_rects(rects: &[FloatRect]) -> libgfx_rust::path::Path {
    let mut path = libgfx_rust::path::Path::new();
    for rect in rects {
        path.move_to(FloatPoint { x: rect.x, y: rect.y });
        path.line_to(FloatPoint {
            x: rect.right(),
            y: rect.y,
        });
        path.line_to(FloatPoint {
            x: rect.right(),
            y: rect.bottom(),
        });
        path.line_to(FloatPoint {
            x: rect.x,
            y: rect.bottom(),
        });
        path.close();
    }
    path
}

/// Appends the glyph cell of each code unit of one shaped run, in code unit order. A typographic
/// character's cell spans its advance, less the `spacing_after_each_character` the run was shaped
/// with; every code unit of it carries that cell, and the first one is marked as the one that starts
/// it.
/// https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/text.html#TermTypographicCharacterUnit
/// A unit of a writing system - such as a Latin alphabetic letter (including its diacritics),
/// Hangul syllable, Chinese ideographic character, Myanmar syllable cluster - that is indivisible
/// with respect to a particular typographic operation [...]
/// FIXME: The glyphs are taken to be in code unit order, which holds for the left-to-right text
///        this layout shapes.
fn append_svg_text_character_cells(
    cells: &mut Vec<FfiSvgTextCharacterCell>,
    glyphs: &libgfx_rust::text_layout::GlyphBuffer,
    length_in_code_units: usize,
    run_end_x: f32,
    top: f32,
    height: f32,
    spacing_after_each_character: f32,
) {
    let placed: Vec<_> = glyphs.placed().collect();
    let mut covered = 0usize;
    let mut index = 0usize;
    while index < placed.len() && covered < length_in_code_units {
        let first = placed[index];
        // A glyph that maps to no code unit of its own (a combining mark's, e.g.) belongs to the
        // typographic character before it, so it extends that character's cell. One at the start
        // of the run has no character before it, so it joins the character after it instead.
        let mut next = index + 1;
        let mut code_units = first.glyph.length_in_code_units();
        while next < placed.len() && (placed[next].glyph.length_in_code_units() == 0 || code_units == 0) {
            code_units += placed[next].glyph.length_in_code_units();
            next += 1;
        }
        let end_x = placed.get(next).map_or(run_end_x, |glyph| glyph.x);
        let code_units = code_units.max(1).min(length_in_code_units - covered);
        let cell = FfiSvgTextCharacterCell {
            x: first.x,
            y: top,
            width: end_x - first.x - spacing_after_each_character,
            height,
            alignment_point_y: 0.0,
            starts_typographic_character: true,
        };
        cells.push(cell);
        cells.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(
            FfiSvgTextCharacterCell {
                starts_typographic_character: false,
                ..cell
            },
            code_units - 1,
        ));
        covered += code_units;
        index = next;
    }
    // A code unit no glyph accounts for gets an empty cell at the run's end, so that indices keep
    // lining up with the characters.
    cells.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(
        FfiSvgTextCharacterCell {
            x: run_end_x,
            y: top,
            width: 0.0,
            height,
            alignment_point_y: 0.0,
            starts_typographic_character: false,
        },
        length_in_code_units - covered,
    ));
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiAffineTransform {
    pub a: f32,
    pub b: f32,
    pub c: f32,
    pub d: f32,
    pub e: f32,
    pub f: f32,
}

impl Default for FfiAffineTransform {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            a: 1.0,
            b: 0.0,
            c: 0.0,
            d: 1.0,
            e: 0.0,
            f: 0.0,
        }
    }
}

#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiSvgViewBox {
    pub min_x: f64,
    pub min_y: f64,
    pub width: f64,
    pub height: f64,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiSvgNumberPercentage {
    pub value: f32,

/// A `<number> | <length> | <percentage>` attribute value, exactly as the element parsed it. A
/// relative length follows the element's font rather than its attributes, so the pass - not the
/// publication - is what turns one into pixels.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiSvgLengthValue {
    pub value: f64,
    pub kind: u8,
    /// The `CSS::LengthUnit` a length was written in; meaningless for the other kinds.
    pub unit: u8,
}

/// One addressable character's entries in the four positioning lists; an exhausted list has an absent value.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiSvgTextPosition {
    pub x: FfiSvgLengthValue,
    pub y: FfiSvgLengthValue,
    pub dx: FfiSvgLengthValue,
    pub dy: FfiSvgLengthValue,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
struct SvgTextPosition {
    x: Option<f32>,
    y: Option<f32>,
    dx: Option<f32>,
    dy: Option<f32>,
}

impl SvgTextPosition {
    fn starts_chunk(self) -> bool {
        self.x.is_some() || self.y.is_some()
    }

    fn is_specified(self) -> bool {
        self.starts_chunk() || self.dx.is_some() || self.dy.is_some()
    }
}

pub const SVG_LENGTH_KIND_NONE: u8 = 0;
pub const SVG_LENGTH_KIND_NUMBER: u8 = 1;
pub const SVG_LENGTH_KIND_LENGTH: u8 = 2;

/// The values an SVG box resolves from its own computed style and the viewport it sits in. They
/// are not element data - an ancestor's viewBox feeds a descendant's percentage basis - so the
/// pass computes them rather than reading them from a publication.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
struct SvgElementFacts {
    is_document_element: bool,
    document_is_decoded_svg: bool,
    additional_element_transform: FfiAffineTransform,
    visible_stroke_width: f32,
}

/// The SVG attributes one element parses, as the document last published them under
/// its style node. They are element data, not layout output: the document writes them when the
/// style tree names the element and whenever an attribute changes, so a running pass reads the
/// published copy instead of asking.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiSvgAttributeFacts {
    /// The element class tests the pass cannot make from a row's NodeKind: `SVGGraphicsBox` also
    /// stands for `<g>`, `<symbol>` and `<pattern>`, and `<rect>` carries the same computed `x`/`y`
    /// properties that give `<use>` its additional transform.
    pub is_graphics_element: bool,
    pub is_use_element: bool,
    pub is_text_element: bool,
    pub is_fit_to_view_box: bool,
    pub has_active_view_box: bool,
    pub active_view_box: FfiSvgViewBox,
    pub preserve_aspect_ratio_align: u8,
    pub preserve_aspect_ratio_meet_or_slice: u8,
    pub content_units: u8,
    pub pattern_units: u8,
    pub pattern_width: FfiSvgNumberPercentage,
    pub pattern_height: FfiSvgNumberPercentage,
    pub mask_units: u8,
    pub mask_x: FfiSvgNumberPercentage,
    pub mask_y: FfiSvgNumberPercentage,
    pub mask_width: FfiSvgNumberPercentage,
    pub mask_height: FfiSvgNumberPercentage,
    /// Which shape a geometry element draws, and the endpoints a <line> parses. Every other
    /// shape's geometry is computed style, which the row already carries.
    pub geometry_kind: u8,
    pub line_x1: FfiSvgNumberPercentage,
    pub line_y1: FfiSvgNumberPercentage,
    pub line_x2: FfiSvgNumberPercentage,
    pub line_y2: FfiSvgNumberPercentage,
    /// The `pathLength` a geometry element parses, where it parses one: the length its stroke's dashes measure the
    /// path in.
    pub has_path_length: bool,
    pub path_length: f32,
    /// The `textLength` of a `<text>`, where it gives a valid one, and whether its `lengthAdjust` is
    /// `spacingAndGlyphs`.
    pub text_length: FfiSvgLengthValue,
    pub text_length_adjusts_glyphs: bool,
    /// The element this one's `href` names, as the style mirror's id index answers for it: the
    /// URL's decoded fragment, interned as the atom an element's id is indexed under. Zero when
    /// the element names nothing, or names a URL with no fragment.
    pub reference_fragment_atom: u32,
    /// The resources this element's style names, in the same form. These come from `mask`,
    /// `clip-path`, `fill` and `stroke`, so they are republished whenever the element's style
    /// record is replaced rather than when an attribute changes.
    pub mask_reference_atom: u32,
    pub clip_path_reference_atom: u32,
    pub fill_reference_atom: u32,
    pub stroke_reference_atom: u32,
    /// The `startOffset` of a `<textPath>`, against the length of the path it follows.
    pub text_path_start_offset: FfiSvgNumberPercentage,
    /// An `<svg>`'s `width` and `height` where they are a `<length>`, which its natural size is
    /// negotiated from.
    pub natural_width: FfiSvgLengthValue,
    pub natural_height: FfiSvgLengthValue,
    /// The natural aspect ratio an `<svg>`'s active SVG view or viewBox gives it, which the
    /// negotiation falls back to where its width and height do not both give it one.
    pub has_view_box_aspect_ratio: bool,
    pub view_box_aspect_ratio_numerator: CssPixels,
    pub view_box_aspect_ratio_denominator: CssPixels,
}

pub const SVG_GEOMETRY_KIND_NONE: u8 = 0;
pub const SVG_GEOMETRY_KIND_PATH: u8 = 1;
pub const SVG_GEOMETRY_KIND_RECT: u8 = 2;
pub const SVG_GEOMETRY_KIND_CIRCLE: u8 = 3;
pub const SVG_GEOMETRY_KIND_ELLIPSE: u8 = 4;
pub const SVG_GEOMETRY_KIND_LINE: u8 = 5;
pub const SVG_GEOMETRY_KIND_POLYLINE: u8 = 6;
pub const SVG_GEOMETRY_KIND_POLYGON: u8 = 7;

impl FfiSvgNumberPercentage {
    pub(crate) fn resolve_relative_to(self, length: f32) -> f32 {
        if self.is_percentage {
            self.value * length
        } else {
            self.value
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) const PRESERVE_ASPECT_RATIO_NONE: u8 = 0;
pub(crate) const PRESERVE_ASPECT_RATIO_X_MIN_Y_MIN: u8 = 1;
pub(crate) const PRESERVE_ASPECT_RATIO_X_MID_Y_MID: u8 = 5;
pub(crate) const PRESERVE_ASPECT_RATIO_X_MAX_Y_MAX: u8 = 9;
pub(crate) const MEET_OR_SLICE_MEET: u8 = 0;
pub(crate) const MEET_OR_SLICE_SLICE: u8 = 1;
const SVG_UNITS_OBJECT_BOUNDING_BOX: u8 = 0;
const SVG_UNITS_USER_SPACE_ON_USE: u8 = 1;

pub(crate) fn kind_is_svg_graphics_box(kind: NodeKind) -> bool {
    matches!(
        kind,
        NodeKind::SVGGraphicsBox
            | NodeKind::SVGGeometryBox
            | NodeKind::SVGImageBox
            | NodeKind::SVGMaskBox
            | NodeKind::SVGTextBox
            | NodeKind::SVGTextPathBox
    )
}

fn kind_is_svg_container_element(kind: NodeKind) -> bool {
    // SVGGraphicsBox is the concrete kind used for <a>, <g>, <switch>,
    // <symbol>, and <use>.
    // FIXME: Include clipPath, defs, marker, and pattern once they are
    // treated as container elements by SVG layout.
    matches!(
        kind,
        NodeKind::SVGGraphicsBox | NodeKind::SVGMaskBox | NodeKind::SVGSVGBox
    )
}

/// The geometry layout found for an SVG element, in the user units of the SVG viewport the element is laid out in.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct SvgGeometry {
    /// The bounding box of the element's fill: its path or glyph cells, or the union of its children's object bounding
    /// boxes, each mapped through the child's local transform.
    pub object_bounding_box: FloatRect,
    /// The bounding box that covers the element's stroke too, which is the element's box.
    pub stroke_bounding_box: FloatRect,
    /// The element's transform about its transform origin, with a <use> element's translation.
    pub local_transform: FfiAffineTransform,
    /// The SVG viewport that the element's own lengths resolve against.
    pub viewport_user_rect: FloatRect,
    /// The SVG viewport that the element lays its contents out in, where it lays out contents of its own.
    pub establishes_viewport: bool,
    pub established_viewport_user_rect: FloatRect,
}

impl SvgGeometry {
    /// What the element's stroke percentages resolve against.
    pub(crate) fn percentage_basis(&self) -> CssPixels {
        crate::svg::stroke_style::percentage_basis(FfiCssPixelSize {
            width: CssPixels::nearest_value_for_f32(self.viewport_user_rect.width),
            height: CssPixels::nearest_value_for_f32(self.viewport_user_rect.height),
        })
    }

    /// The transform reference box that a used `transform-box` value names.
    pub(crate) fn transform_reference_box(&self, transform_box: u8) -> CssPixelRect {
        css_pixel_rect_of(match transform_box {
            transform_box::FILL_BOX => self.object_bounding_box,
            transform_box::VIEW_BOX => {
                FloatRect::new(0.0, 0.0, self.viewport_user_rect.width, self.viewport_user_rect.height)
            }
            _ => self.stroke_bounding_box,
        })
    }
}

pub(crate) fn css_pixel_rect_of(rect: FloatRect) -> CssPixelRect {
    CssPixelRect::new(
        CssPixels::nearest_value_for_f32(rect.x),
        CssPixels::nearest_value_for_f32(rect.y),
        CssPixels::nearest_value_for_f32(rect.width),
        CssPixels::nearest_value_for_f32(rect.height),
    )
}

/// The union of `rect` and `other`, which keeps the extent of an empty rect too.
fn united_even_if_empty(rect: Option<FloatRect>, other: FloatRect) -> FloatRect {
    let Some(rect) = rect else {
        return other;
    };
    let (left, top) = (rect.x.min(other.x), rect.y.min(other.y));
    let (right, bottom) = (rect.right().max(other.right()), rect.bottom().max(other.bottom()));
    FloatRect::new(left, top, right - left, bottom - top)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct SvgCssPixelRect {
    x: CssPixels,
    y: CssPixels,
    width: CssPixels,
    height: CssPixels,
}

impl SvgCssPixelRect {
    fn inflate(&mut self, width: CssPixels, height: CssPixels) {
        self.x -= width / 2;
        self.width += width;
        self.y -= height / 2;
        self.height += height;
    }

    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.width <= CssPixels::default() || self.height <= CssPixels::default()
    }

    fn to_float_rect(self) -> FloatRect {
        FloatRect::new(
            self.x.to_float(),
            self.y.to_float(),
            self.width.to_float(),
            self.height.to_float(),
        )
    }

    /// Grows this rect to cover `other` too. An empty rect covers nothing, so it doesn't take part.
    fn unite(&mut self, other: SvgCssPixelRect) {
        if other.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        if self.is_empty() {
            *self = other;
            return;
        }
        let right = (self.x + self.width).max(other.x + other.width);
        let bottom = (self.y + self.height).max(other.y + other.height);
        self.x = self.x.min(other.x);
        self.y = self.y.min(other.y);
        self.width = right - self.x;
        self.height = bottom - self.y;
    }
}

impl From<FfiAffineTransform> for libgfx_rust::AffineTransform {
    fn from(transform: FfiAffineTransform) -> Self {
        let FfiAffineTransform { a, b, c, d, e, f } = transform;
        Self::new(a, b, c, d, e, f)
    }
}

impl From<libgfx_rust::AffineTransform> for FfiAffineTransform {
    fn from(transform: libgfx_rust::AffineTransform) -> Self {
        let [a, b, c, d, e, f] = transform.values;
        Self { a, b, c, d, e, f }
    }
}

impl FfiAffineTransform {
    fn is_identity(self) -> bool {
        libgfx_rust::AffineTransform::from(self).is_identity()
    }

    pub(crate) fn translated(self, x: f32, y: f32) -> Self {
        libgfx_rust::AffineTransform::from(self).translated(x, y).into()
    }

    pub(crate) fn scaled(self, x: f32, y: f32) -> Self {
        libgfx_rust::AffineTransform::from(self).scaled(x, y).into()
    }
}

fn float_rect_to_css_pixels(rect: FloatRect) -> SvgCssPixelRect {
    SvgCssPixelRect {
        x: CssPixels::nearest_value_for_f32(rect.x),
        y: CssPixels::nearest_value_for_f32(rect.y),
        width: CssPixels::nearest_value_for_f32(rect.width),
        height: CssPixels::nearest_value_for_f32(rect.height),
    }
}

// https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/coords.html#PreserveAspectRatioAttribute
fn view_box_transform(
    align: u8,
    meet_or_slice: u8,
    view_box: FfiSvgViewBox,
    viewport_size: (CssPixels, CssPixels),
) -> FfiAffineTransform {
    // NB: The scales pass through f32, as the transform stores them.
    let scale_x = f64::from((viewport_size.0.to_double() / view_box.width) as f32);
    let scale_y = f64::from((viewport_size.1.to_double() / view_box.height) as f32);
    let (scale_x, scale_y, offset) = if align == PRESERVE_ASPECT_RATIO_NONE {
        // Do not force uniform scaling. Scale the graphic content of the given element non-uniformly
        // if necessary such that the element's bounding box exactly matches the SVG viewport rectangle.
        (scale_x, scale_y, (CssPixels::default(), CssPixels::default()))
    } else {
        let scale = match meet_or_slice {
            // meet (the default) - Scale the graphic such that:
            // - aspect ratio is preserved
            // - the entire ‘viewBox’ is visible within the SVG viewport
            // - the ‘viewBox’ is scaled up as much as possible, while still meeting the other criteria
            MEET_OR_SLICE_MEET => scale_x.min(scale_y),
            // slice - Scale the graphic such that:
            // aspect ratio is preserved
            // the entire SVG viewport is covered by the ‘viewBox’
            // the ‘viewBox’ is scaled down as much as possible, while still meeting the other criteria
            MEET_OR_SLICE_SLICE => scale_x.max(scale_y),
            _ => panic!("invalid preserveAspectRatio meet-or-slice value"),
        };
        assert!(
            (PRESERVE_ASPECT_RATIO_X_MIN_Y_MIN..=PRESERVE_ASPECT_RATIO_X_MAX_Y_MAX).contains(&align),
            "invalid preserveAspectRatio alignment value"
        );
        // NB: The alignments count up from xMinYMin through min, mid and max along x, then through min, mid and max
        //     along y. Each aligns the min, the midpoint or the max of the ‘viewBox’ with that of the SVG viewport, so
        //     it offsets the content by none, half or all of the space the scaled ‘viewBox’ leaves.
        let alignment = align - PRESERVE_ASPECT_RATIO_X_MIN_Y_MIN;
        let offset = |alignment_in_axis: u8, viewport_size: CssPixels, view_box_size: f64| {
            let free_space = viewport_size - CssPixels::nearest_value_for(view_box_size * scale);
            match alignment_in_axis {
                0 => CssPixels::default(),
                1 => free_space / 2,
                _ => free_space,
            }
        };
        (
            scale,
            scale,
            (
                offset(alignment % 3, viewport_size.0, view_box.width),
                offset(alignment / 3, viewport_size.1, view_box.height),
            ),
        )
    };
    FfiAffineTransform::default()
        .translated(offset.0.to_float(), offset.1.to_float())
        .scaled(scale_x as f32, scale_y as f32)
        .translated(-view_box.min_x as f32, -view_box.min_y as f32)
}

/// What laying out a <text>, a <tspan>, or an <a> inside one yields.
#[derive(Default)]
struct SvgTextBoxContents {
    /// The glyph outlines of the element's own text nodes.
    path: libgfx_rust::path::Path,
    /// Those outlines split by the child elements between them, where text follows a child element.
    segments: Option<Vec<fragment_tree::SvgTextSegment>>,
    /// The cells the glyphs of the element's own text nodes occupy.
    glyph_cells: SvgCssPixelRect,
    /// The glyph cell of each character in the element's subtree, in document order.
    character_cells: Vec<FfiSvgTextCharacterCell>,
    /// The glyph cell of each character of the element's own text nodes, in document order.
    own_character_cells: Vec<FfiSvgTextCharacterCell>,
    /// The union of the boxes of the element's text content child elements.
    children_bounding_box: SvgCssPixelRect,
}

/// A stretch of text that one text node of a text content element renders, which a text decoration line runs along.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
struct SvgTextRunSpan {
    x: f32,
    advance: f32,
    baseline: f32,
    /// The ascent of the first available font of the element the text is in, and that element's font size.
    ascent: f32,
    font_size: f32,
}

/// The text decoration lines a text content element draws along the text in its subtree.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
struct SvgTextDecorationLines {
    underline: bool,
    overline: bool,
    line_through: bool,
    /// The thickness the element's 'text-decoration-thickness' gives the lines, where it gives one.
    thickness: Option<f32>,
    /// The element's 'text-decoration-style'.
    style: u8,
}

/// Which way a decoration line that's drawn wider than its thickness (a double or a wavy one) grows: away from the
/// text for an underline or an overline, and about its center for a line through the text.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
enum SvgDecorationLineGrowth {
    Down,
    Up,
    AboutCenter,
}

impl SvgTextDecorationLines {
    fn thickness_for(&self, span: &SvgTextRunSpan) -> f32 {
        self.thickness.unwrap_or(span.font_size / 10.0).max(1.0)
    }

    /// The underline and the overline along `span`, which paint before the text.
    fn add_lines_under_text(&self, span: &SvgTextRunSpan, path: &mut libgfx_rust::path::Path) {
        let thickness = self.thickness_for(span);
        if self.underline {
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-decor-4/#text-underline-position-property
            // The user agent may use any algorithm to determine the underline's position; however it must be placed
            // at or under the alphabetic baseline.
            let gap = (thickness / 2.0).ceil().max(1.0);
            self.add_line(
                span,
                span.baseline + gap,
                thickness,
                SvgDecorationLineGrowth::Down,
                path,
            );
        }
        if self.overline {
            let top = span.baseline - span.ascent - thickness;
            self.add_line(span, top, thickness, SvgDecorationLineGrowth::Up, path);
        }
    }

    /// The line through `span`, which paints after the text.
    fn add_lines_over_text(&self, span: &SvgTextRunSpan, path: &mut libgfx_rust::path::Path) {
        if self.line_through {
            let thickness = self.thickness_for(span);
            let top = span.baseline - span.ascent / 3.0 - thickness / 2.0;
            self.add_line(span, top, thickness, SvgDecorationLineGrowth::AboutCenter, path);
        }
    }

    /// Adds the outline of one decoration line along `span`, in the element's 'text-decoration-style', whose solid
    /// form would cover the rows from `top` down to `top + thickness`. The outline is filled and stroked as the
    /// text's glyphs are.
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-decor-4/#text-decoration-style-property
    fn add_line(
        &self,
        span: &SvgTextRunSpan,
        top: f32,
        thickness: f32,
        growth: SvgDecorationLineGrowth,
        path: &mut libgfx_rust::path::Path,
    ) {
        let (x, length) = (span.x, span.advance);
        // NB: A dashed, dotted, or wavy line takes a few segments per thickness of its length, so a line too long for
        //     a pattern of reasonable size is drawn solid.
        const MAX_PATTERN_LENGTH_IN_THICKNESSES: f32 = 40_000.0;
        let style =
            if length / thickness > MAX_PATTERN_LENGTH_IN_THICKNESSES && self.style != text_decoration_style::DOUBLE {
                text_decoration_style::SOLID
            } else {
                self.style
            };
        match style {
            text_decoration_style::DOUBLE => {
                // NB: Two lines of the thickness, a thickness apart.
                let (first_top, second_top) = match growth {
                    SvgDecorationLineGrowth::Down => (top, top + 2.0 * thickness),
                    SvgDecorationLineGrowth::Up => (top - 2.0 * thickness, top),
                    SvgDecorationLineGrowth::AboutCenter => (top - thickness, top + thickness),
                };
                path.append_path(&path_of_rects(&[
                    FloatRect::new(x, first_top, length, thickness),
                    FloatRect::new(x, second_top, length, thickness),
                ]));
            }
            text_decoration_style::DASHED => {
                // NB: An odd number of dashes and gaps of equal length, a little over twice the thickness each, so
                //     that the line starts and ends with a dash. Each end reaches half the thickness past the text.
                let total = length + thickness;
                let count = (total / thickness / 4.0).floor() * 2.0 + 1.0;
                let dash = total / count;
                let start = x - thickness / 2.0;
                let rects: Vec<FloatRect> = (0..count as usize)
                    .step_by(2)
                    .map(|index| FloatRect::new(start + index as f32 * dash, top, dash, thickness))
                    .collect();
                path.append_path(&path_of_rects(&rects));
            }
            text_decoration_style::DOTTED => {
                // NB: Round dots as wide as the line is thick, about twice that apart, with one at each end.
                let radius = thickness / 2.0;
                let center_y = top + radius;
                let count = ((length - thickness) / (2.0 * thickness)).floor().max(0.0) as usize + 1;
                let step = if count > 1 {
                    (length - thickness) / (count - 1) as f32
                } else {
                    0.0
                };
                for index in 0..count {
                    let center_x = x + radius + index as f32 * step;
                    path.move_to(FloatPoint {
                        x: center_x - radius,
                        y: center_y,
                    });
                    path.arc_to(
                        FloatPoint {
                            x: center_x + radius,
                            y: center_y,
                        },
                        radius,
                        false,
                        true,
                    );
                    path.arc_to(
                        FloatPoint {
                            x: center_x - radius,
                            y: center_y,
                        },
                        radius,
                        false,
                        true,
                    );
                    path.close();
                }
            }
            text_decoration_style::WAVY => {
                // NB: A zigzag whose crests and troughs are one and a half times the thickness off its center line,
                //     at 45 degrees, stroked at the thickness. It grows away from the text as a double line does.
                let peak = 1.5 * thickness;
                let center_y = top
                    + thickness / 2.0
                    + match growth {
                        SvgDecorationLineGrowth::Down => peak,
                        SvgDecorationLineGrowth::Up => -peak,
                        SvgDecorationLineGrowth::AboutCenter => 0.0,
                    };
                // NB: The zigzag is built from the span's start and moved there afterward, so that each vertex
                //     advances by its full step even where the span starts at a coordinate too large to add it to.
                let mut wave = libgfx_rust::path::Path::new();
                let mut previous = FloatPoint { x: 0.0, y: center_y };
                wave.move_to(previous);
                let mut vertex = FloatPoint {
                    x: peak,
                    y: center_y - peak,
                };
                while vertex.x < length {
                    wave.line_to(vertex);
                    previous = vertex;
                    vertex = FloatPoint {
                        x: vertex.x + 2.0 * peak,
                        y: 2.0 * center_y - vertex.y,
                    };
                }
                let fraction = (length - previous.x) / (vertex.x - previous.x);
                wave.line_to(FloatPoint {
                    x: length,
                    y: previous.y + (vertex.y - previous.y) * fraction,
                });
                let wave = wave.copy_transformed([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, x, 0.0]);
                path.append_path(&wave.stroke_to_fill(&libgfx_rust::path::StrokeStyle {
                    thickness,
                    cap_style: libgfx_rust::CapStyle::Butt,
                    join_style: libgfx_rust::JoinStyle::Miter,
                    miter_limit: 4.0,
                    dash_array: Vec::new(),
                    dash_offset: 0.0,
                }));
            }
            _ => path.append_path(&path_of_rects(&[FloatRect::new(x, top, length, thickness)])),
        }
    }
}

/// What a text content element paints in one go: glyph outlines, or the rects of text decoration lines.
enum SvgTextPaintPart {
    Glyphs(Vec<libgfx_rust::path::GlyphRun>),
    /// Glyphs of a color font, which have no outlines.
    ColorGlyphs(Vec<fragment_tree::SvgColorGlyphRun>),
    DecorationLines(libgfx_rust::path::Path),
}

/// The parts a text content element paints, each with the child element it paints after, in paint order.
#[derive(Default)]
struct SvgTextPaintParts {
    parts: Vec<(Node, SvgTextPaintPart)>,
}

impl SvgTextPaintParts {
    fn add_glyphs(&mut self, after_child: Node, runs: Vec<libgfx_rust::path::GlyphRun>) {
        if runs.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        if let Some((last_after_child, SvgTextPaintPart::Glyphs(last_runs))) = self.parts.last_mut()
            && *last_after_child == after_child
        {
            last_runs.extend(runs);
            return;
        }
        self.parts.push((after_child, SvgTextPaintPart::Glyphs(runs)));
    }

    fn add_color_glyphs(&mut self, after_child: Node, run: fragment_tree::SvgColorGlyphRun) {
        if run.glyphs.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        if let Some((last_after_child, SvgTextPaintPart::ColorGlyphs(last_runs))) = self.parts.last_mut()
            && *last_after_child == after_child
        {
            last_runs.push(run);
            return;
        }
        self.parts.push((after_child, SvgTextPaintPart::ColorGlyphs(vec![run])));
    }

    fn add_decoration_lines(&mut self, after_child: Node, lines: libgfx_rust::path::Path) {
        if lines.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        if let Some((last_after_child, SvgTextPaintPart::DecorationLines(last_lines))) = self.parts.last_mut()
            && *last_after_child == after_child
        {
            last_lines.append_path(&lines);
            return;
        }
        self.parts.push((after_child, SvgTextPaintPart::DecorationLines(lines)));
    }

    /// Whether the parts are just the glyphs of text that comes before every child element, which the element's
    /// path paints as it is.
    fn are_one_path(&self) -> bool {
        match self.parts.as_slice() {
            [] => true,
            [(after_child, SvgTextPaintPart::Glyphs(_))] => after_child.is_invalid(),
            _ => false,
        }
    }
}

/// How a text content element adjusts its text to its 'textLength'.
/// https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/text.html#TextElementLengthAdjustAttribute
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
enum SvgTextLengthAdjustment {
    #[default]
    None,
    /// spacing: Indicates that only the advance values are adjusted. The glyphs themselves are not stretched or
    /// compressed.
    /// NB: Holds the space to add after each typographic character.
    Spacing(f32),
    /// spacingAndGlyphs: Indicates that the advance values are adjusted and the glyphs themselves stretched or
    /// compressed in one axis (i.e., a direction parallel to the inline-base direction).
    /// NB: Holds the factor to scale by along that axis.
    SpacingAndGlyphs(f32),
}

impl SvgTextLengthAdjustment {
    fn spacing(self) -> f32 {
        match self {
            Self::Spacing(spacing) => spacing,
            _ => 0.0,
        }
    }

    fn glyph_scale(self) -> f32 {
        match self {
            Self::SpacingAndGlyphs(scale) => scale,
            _ => 1.0,
        }
    }
}

/// The extent excludes trailing 'textLength' spacing; the advance includes it for text that follows the subtree.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
struct SvgTextLengthMeasurement {
    start: f32,
    end: f32,
    advance: f32,
    characters: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct SvgResolvedTextLength {
    adjustment: SvgTextLengthAdjustment,
    measurement: SvgTextLengthMeasurement,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
struct SvgTextChunkMeasurement {
    /// The least and the greatest position along the x axis that the characters of the chunk cover, counted from where
    /// the chunk starts.
    start: f32,
    end: f32,
    anchor: u8,
}

impl Default for SvgTextChunkMeasurement {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            start: 0.0,
            end: 0.0,
            anchor: text_anchor::START,
        }
    }
}

/// Processes the white space in the character data of a text content block element: `sources` holds the text of each
/// of its text nodes, in document order, with the 'white-space-collapse' value of the element the text node is in.
/// Returns the characters each text node renders.
/// https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/text.html#WhiteSpace
/// Rendering of white space in SVG 2 is controlled by the white-space property. [...] Values and
/// their meanings are defined in CSS Text Module Level 3.
/// NB: SVG text is laid out as one line, so both phases of CSS Text's white space processing
///     happen here, on the characters themselves, before they are shaped.
fn process_svg_text_white_space(sources: &[(&[u16], u8)]) -> Vec<Vec<u16>> {
    const SPACE: u16 = b' ' as u16;
    const TAB: u16 = b'\t' as u16;
