// Horizontal border lines run between (and around) rows: there are row_count + 1 of them, each with
// one segment per column. Vertical border lines run between (and around) columns: column_count + 1
// of them, each with one segment per row.
//
// Table parts must be applied in order of decreasing precedence — cells, rows, row groups, columns,
// column groups, and lastly the table — with parts of equal precedence applied leftmost/topmost
// first. A candidate border only replaces the current winner of a segment when it is strictly more
// specific (steps 1-3 of the border conflict resolution algorithm), so ties resolve towards the
// earlier-applied part, which implements step 4 without tracking element kinds or coordinates.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct BorderWidths {
    pub(crate) top: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) right: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) bottom: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) left: CssPixels,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CollapsedBorderEdge {
    pub border_data: formatting_context::BorderData,
    pub source_order: u32,
}

#[derive(PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct OwnedCollapsedTableBorders {
    pub(crate) row_offsets: Vec<CssPixels>,
    pub(crate) column_offsets: Vec<CssPixels>,
    pub(crate) horizontal_edges: Vec<CollapsedBorderEdge>,
    pub(crate) vertical_edges: Vec<CollapsedBorderEdge>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum TableParticipantPreparation {
    CellsOfEveryParticipant,
    CellsOfTableCellsOnly,
}

fn grid_line_offsets(sizes: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = CssPixels>) -> Vec<CssPixels> {
    let mut offsets = Vec::with_capacity(sizes.len() + 1);
    let mut offset = CssPixels::default();
    offsets.push(offset);
    for size in sizes {
        offset += size;
        offsets.push(offset);
    }
    offsets
}

pub(crate) struct CollapsedBorderGrid {
    horizontal_lines: Vec<Vec<CollapsedBorderEdge>>,
    vertical_lines: Vec<Vec<CollapsedBorderEdge>>,
}

impl CollapsedBorderGrid {
    pub(crate) fn new(row_count: usize, column_count: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            horizontal_lines: vec![vec![CollapsedBorderEdge::default(); column_count]; row_count + 1],
            vertical_lines: vec![vec![CollapsedBorderEdge::default(); row_count]; column_count + 1],
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn apply_borders(
        &mut self,
        borders: ElementBorders,
        row_start: usize,
        row_end: usize,
        column_start: usize,
        column_end: usize,
        source_order: u32,
    ) {
        Self::apply_to_segments(
            &mut self.horizontal_lines[row_start],
            column_start,
            column_end,
            borders.top,
            source_order,
        );
        Self::apply_to_segments(
            &mut self.horizontal_lines[row_end],
            column_start,
            column_end,
            borders.bottom,
            source_order,
        );
        Self::apply_to_segments(
            &mut self.vertical_lines[column_start],
            row_start,
            row_end,
            borders.left,
            source_order,
        );
        Self::apply_to_segments(
            &mut self.vertical_lines[column_end],
            row_start,
            row_end,
            borders.right,
            source_order,
        );
    }

    pub(crate) fn hide_segments_inside_span(
        &mut self,
        row_start: usize,
        row_end: usize,
        column_start: usize,
        column_end: usize,
        source_order: u32,
    ) {
        // Segments strictly inside a spanning cell are not borders of any element; mark them as hidden
        // so that borders of rows and columns crossing the span cannot win there.
        let hidden = CollapsedBorderEdge {
            border_data: formatting_context::BorderData {
                color: 0,
                line_style: LINE_STYLE_HIDDEN,
                width: CssPixels::default(),
            },
            source_order,
        };
        for row in row_start + 1..row_end {
            for column in column_start..column_end {
                self.horizontal_lines[row][column] = hidden;
            }
        }
        for column in column_start + 1..column_end {
            for row in row_start..row_end {
                self.vertical_lines[column][row] = hidden;
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn resolve_used_widths_for_cell(
        &self,
        row_start: usize,
        row_end: usize,
        column_start: usize,
        column_end: usize,
    ) -> BorderWidths {
        BorderWidths {
            top: Self::most_specific(&self.horizontal_lines[row_start], column_start, column_end)
                .border_data
                .width,
            right: Self::most_specific(&self.vertical_lines[column_end], row_start, row_end)
                .border_data
                .width,
            bottom: Self::most_specific(&self.horizontal_lines[row_end], column_start, column_end)
                .border_data
                .width,
            left: Self::most_specific(&self.vertical_lines[column_start], row_start, row_end)
                .border_data
                .width,
        }
    }

    fn apply_to_segments(
        line: &mut [CollapsedBorderEdge],
        start: usize,
        end: usize,
        data: formatting_context::BorderData,
        source_order: u32,
    ) {
        if data.line_style == LINE_STYLE_NONE {
            return;
        }
        for segment in &mut line[start..end] {
            if candidate_wins(data, segment.border_data) {
                *segment = CollapsedBorderEdge {
                    border_data: data,
                    source_order,
                };
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn outer_edge_widths(&self) -> BorderWidths {
        let max_width = |segments: &[CollapsedBorderEdge]| {
            segments
                .iter()
                .fold(CssPixels::default(), |max, segment| max.max(segment.border_data.width))
        };
        BorderWidths {
            top: max_width(&self.horizontal_lines[0]),
            right: max_width(self.vertical_lines.last().expect("grid has vertical lines")),
            bottom: max_width(self.horizontal_lines.last().expect("grid has horizontal lines")),
            left: max_width(&self.vertical_lines[0]),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn has_paintable_edges(&self) -> bool {
        let paints = |segment: &CollapsedBorderEdge| {
            segment.border_data.width > CssPixels::default()
                && segment.border_data.line_style != LINE_STYLE_NONE
                && segment.border_data.line_style != LINE_STYLE_HIDDEN
        };
        self.horizontal_lines.iter().flatten().any(paints) || self.vertical_lines.iter().flatten().any(paints)
    }

    pub(crate) fn take_edges(self) -> (Vec<CollapsedBorderEdge>, Vec<CollapsedBorderEdge>) {
        (
            self.horizontal_lines.iter().flatten().copied().collect(),
            self.vertical_lines.iter().flatten().copied().collect(),
        )
    }

    fn most_specific(line: &[CollapsedBorderEdge], start: usize, end: usize) -> CollapsedBorderEdge {
        let mut winner = line[start];
        for segment in &line[start + 1..end] {
            if candidate_wins(segment.border_data, winner.border_data) {
                winner = *segment;
            }
        }
        winner
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct Column {
    pub(crate) min_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) max_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) used_inline_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) has_intrinsic_percentage: bool,
    pub(crate) intrinsic_percentage: f64,
    // In fixed mode, the cell intrinsic offsets of the cell whose percentage width the column uses; they are added
    // to the resolved percentage (see compute_cell_measures).
    pub(crate) percentage_offsets: CssPixels,
    // Store whether the column is constrained: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#constrainedness
    pub(crate) is_constrained: bool,
    // Store whether the column has originating cells, defined in https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#terminology.
    pub(crate) has_originating_cells: bool,
    // Whether the column, or its column group, has 'visibility: collapse' (see remove_collapsed_columns).
    pub(crate) is_collapsed: bool,
}

fn total_used(columns: &[Column]) -> CssPixels {
    columns
        .iter()
        .fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, column| sum + column.used_inline_size)
}

fn total_candidates(candidates: &[CssPixels]) -> CssPixels {
    candidates
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .fold(CssPixels::default(), std::ops::Add::add)
}

fn commit_candidates(columns: &mut [Column], candidates: &[CssPixels]) {
    assert_eq!(columns.len(), candidates.len());
    for (column, candidate) in columns.iter_mut().zip(candidates) {
        column.used_inline_size = *candidate;
    }
}

fn assign_linear_combination(columns: &mut [Column], candidates: &[CssPixels], available: CssPixels) {
    let candidate_total = total_candidates(candidates);
    let used_total = total_used(columns);
    if candidate_total == used_total {
        return;
    }
    let weight = (available - used_total).to_double() / (candidate_total - used_total).to_double();
    for (column, candidate) in columns.iter_mut().zip(candidates) {
        column.used_inline_size = CssPixels::nearest_value_for(
            weight * candidate.to_double() + (1.0 - weight) * column.used_inline_size.to_double(),
        );
    }
}

fn distribute_proportionally(
    columns: &mut [Column],
    excess: CssPixels,
    filter: impl Fn(&Column) -> bool,
    base: impl Fn(&Column) -> CssPixels,
) -> bool {
    let mut found = false;
    let mut total = CssPixels::default();
    for column in columns.iter() {
        if filter(column) {
            total += base(column);
            found = true;
        }
    }
    if !found {
        return false;
    }
    assert!(total > CssPixels::default());
    for column in columns.iter_mut() {
        if filter(column) {
            column.used_inline_size +=
                CssPixels::nearest_value_for(excess.to_double() * base(column).to_double() / total.to_double());
        }
    }
    true
}

fn distribute_equally(columns: &mut [Column], excess: CssPixels, filter: impl Fn(&Column) -> bool) -> bool {
    let count = columns.iter().filter(|column| filter(column)).count();
    if count == 0 {
        return false;
    }
    for column in columns.iter_mut() {
        if filter(column) {
            column.used_inline_size += excess / count;
        }
    }
    true
}

fn distribute_by_percentage(columns: &mut [Column], excess: CssPixels, filter: impl Fn(&Column) -> bool) -> bool {
    let mut found = false;
    let mut total = 0.0;
    for column in columns.iter() {
        if filter(column) {
            found = true;
            total += column.intrinsic_percentage;
        }
    }
    if !found {
        return false;
    }
    for column in columns.iter_mut() {
        if filter(column) {
            column.used_inline_size +=
                CssPixels::nearest_value_for(excess.to_double() * column.intrinsic_percentage / total);
        }
    }
    true
}

fn distribute_excess_fixed(columns: &mut [Column], excess: CssPixels) {
    // Implements the fixed mode for https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#distributing-width-to-columns.

    // If any columns have no specified inline size, distribute the excess inline size equally to them.
    if distribute_equally(columns, excess, |column| {
        !column.is_constrained && !column.has_intrinsic_percentage
    }) {
        return;
    }
    // Otherwise, distribute proportionally among columns with non-zero length sizes from the base assignment.
    if distribute_proportionally(
        columns,
        excess,
        |column| column.used_inline_size > CssPixels::default(),
        |column| column.used_inline_size,
    ) {
        return;
    }
    // Otherwise, distribute proportionally among columns with non-zero percentage sizes from the base assignment.
    if distribute_by_percentage(columns, excess, |column| column.intrinsic_percentage > 0.0) {
        return;
    }
    // Otherwise, distribute the excess inline size equally to the zero-sized columns.
    distribute_equally(columns, excess, |column| {
        column.used_inline_size == CssPixels::default()
    });
}

fn distribute_excess(columns: &mut [Column], available: CssPixels, fixed: bool) {
    // Implements https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#distributing-width-to-columns
    let used = total_used(columns);
    if used >= available {
        return;
    }
    let mut excess = available - used;
    if excess == CssPixels::default() {
        return;
    }
    if fixed {
        distribute_excess_fixed(columns, excess);
        return;
    }

    // 1. If there are non-constrained columns that have originating cells with intrinsic percentage width of 0% and with nonzero
    //    max-content width (aka the columns allowed to grow by this rule), the distributed widths of the columns allowed to grow
    //    by this rule are increased in proportion to max-content width so the total increase adds to the excess width.
    if distribute_proportionally(
        columns,
        excess,
        |column| {
            !column.is_constrained
                && column.has_originating_cells
                && column.intrinsic_percentage == 0.0
                && column.max_size > CssPixels::default()
        },
        |column| column.max_size,
    ) {
        excess = available - total_used(columns);
    }
    if excess == CssPixels::default() {
        return;
    }
    // 2. Otherwise, if there are non-constrained columns that have originating cells with intrinsic percentage width of 0% (aka the columns
    //    allowed to grow by this rule, which thanks to the previous rule must have zero max-content width), the distributed widths of the
    //    columns allowed to grow by this rule are increased by equal amounts so the total increase adds to the excess width.
    if distribute_equally(columns, excess, |column| {
        !column.is_constrained && column.has_originating_cells && column.intrinsic_percentage == 0.0
    }) {
        excess = available - total_used(columns);
    }
    if excess == CssPixels::default() {
        return;
    }
    // 3. Otherwise, if there are constrained columns with intrinsic percentage width of 0% and with nonzero max-content width
    //    (aka the columns allowed to grow by this rule, which, due to other rules, must have originating cells), the distributed widths of the
    //    columns allowed to grow by this rule are increased in proportion to max-content width so the total increase adds to the excess width.
    if distribute_proportionally(
        columns,
        excess,
        |column| column.is_constrained && column.intrinsic_percentage == 0.0 && column.max_size > CssPixels::default(),
        |column| column.max_size,
    ) {
        excess = available - total_used(columns);
    }
    if excess == CssPixels::default() {
        return;
    }
    // 4. Otherwise, if there are columns with intrinsic percentage width greater than 0% (aka the columns allowed to grow by this rule,
    //    which, due to other rules, must have originating cells), the distributed widths of the columns allowed to grow by this rule are
    //    increased in proportion to intrinsic percentage width so the total increase adds to the excess width.
    if distribute_by_percentage(columns, excess, |column| column.intrinsic_percentage > 0.0) {
        excess = available - total_used(columns);
    }
    if excess == CssPixels::default() {
        return;
    }
    // 5. Otherwise, if there is any such column, the distributed widths of all columns that have originating cells are increased by equal amounts
    //    so the total increase adds to the excess width.
    if distribute_equally(columns, excess, |column| column.has_originating_cells) {
        excess = available - total_used(columns);
    }
    if excess == CssPixels::default() {
        return;
    }
    // 6. Otherwise, the distributed widths of all columns are increased by equal amounts so the total increase adds to the excess width.
    distribute_equally(columns, excess, |_| true);
}

pub(crate) fn distribute_inline_size(columns: &mut [Column], available: CssPixels, fixed: bool) {
    // Implements https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#width-distribution-algorithm

    let mut candidates = vec![CssPixels::default(); columns.len()];
    // 1. The min-content sizing guess assigns every column its min-content inline size.
    for (index, column) in columns.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        // In fixed mode, the min-content width of percent-columns and auto-columns is considered to be zero:
        // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#width-distribution-in-fixed-mode
        if fixed && !column.is_constrained {
            continue;
        }
        column.used_inline_size = column.min_size;
        candidates[index] = column.min_size;
    }
    // 2. The min-content-percentage sizing-guess is the set of column width assignments where:
    //    - each percent-column is assigned the larger of:
    //      - its intrinsic percentage width times the assignable width and
    //      - its min-content width.
    //    - all other columns are assigned their min-content width.
    for (candidate, column) in candidates.iter_mut().zip(columns.iter()) {
        if column.has_intrinsic_percentage {
            *candidate = column.min_size.max(
                CssPixels::nearest_value_for(column.intrinsic_percentage / 100.0 * available.to_double())
                    + column.percentage_offsets,
            );
        }
    }
    // If the assignable inline size is no larger than the max-content sizing guess, use the linear combination
    // of the consecutive sizing guesses whose sums bound the available inline size.
    if available < total_candidates(&candidates) {
        assign_linear_combination(columns, &candidates, available);
        return;
    }
    commit_candidates(columns, &candidates);

    // 3. The min-content-specified sizing-guess is the set of column width assignments where:
    //    - each percent-column is assigned the larger of:
    //      - its intrinsic percentage width times the assignable width and
    //      - its min-content width
    //    - any other column that is constrained is assigned its max-content width
    //    - all other columns are assigned their min-content width.
    for (candidate, column) in candidates.iter_mut().zip(columns.iter()) {
        if column.is_constrained {
            *candidate = column.max_size;
        }
    }
    if available < total_candidates(&candidates) {
        assign_linear_combination(columns, &candidates, available);
        return;
    }
    commit_candidates(columns, &candidates);

    // 4. The max-content sizing-guess is the set of column width assignments where:
    //    - each percent-column is assigned the larger of:
    //      - its intrinsic percentage width times the assignable width and
    //      - its min-content width
    //    - all other columns are assigned their max-content width.
    for (candidate, column) in candidates.iter_mut().zip(columns.iter()) {
        if !column.has_intrinsic_percentage {
            *candidate = column.max_size;
        }
    }
    if available < total_candidates(&candidates) {
        assign_linear_combination(columns, &candidates, available);
        return;
    }
    commit_candidates(columns, &candidates);
    // Otherwise, start from the max-content sizing guess and distribute the excess inline size to the columns.
    distribute_excess(columns, available, fixed);
}

/// What a table keeps of a cell while it lays the cell out.
#[derive(Default)]
struct CellLayoutState {
    /// The input cells of the cell's box as this table sizes it, from the box's starting cells through the borders
    /// and padding of the table's border model and the sizes of its columns and rows to what the cell's run hands back.
    box_cells: used_values::RootInputCells,
    /// What the cell's fragment shows of the table's layout.
    fragment_facts: run_state::FragmentFactsDecidedByParent,
    inside_layout_input: AvailableSpace,
    /// The content block size the table hands the cell's run, which the cell's contents resolve percentages against.
    pre_layout_content_block_size: CssPixels,
    /// What the layout of the cell hands its placement, which places every cell once the rows are positioned.
    fragment_arrival: Option<fragment_tree::RunRootFragment>,
    /// What placing the cell takes of the box its layout handed back.
    placed: Option<formatting_context::PlacedChild>,
    content_baselines: DerivedBaselines,
    /// Whether the cell's run laid out the absolutely positioned boxes the cell contains against its final size.
    run_laid_out_abspos_contained_by_cell: bool,
    /// Whether the cell's contents resolve percentages against the block size of the cell.
    contents_depend_on_percentage_block_size: bool,
    /// How far the table moves the contents of the cell along the block axis to align them in the rows it spans.
    contents_block_offset: CssPixels,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct TableCell {
    pub(crate) box_: Node,
    pub(crate) column_index: usize,
    pub(crate) row_index: usize,
    pub(crate) column_span: usize,
    pub(crate) row_span: usize,
    pub(crate) baseline: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) outer_min_inline_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) outer_max_inline_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) outer_min_block_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) outer_max_block_size: CssPixels,
    // The max-content inline size of the cell's content box, if its column measures read it (see compute_cell_measures).
    pub(crate) max_content_inline_size: Option<CssPixels>,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct Row {
    pub(crate) box_: Node,
    pub(crate) base_block_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) reference_block_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) final_block_size: CssPixels,
    /// The baseline established by the row's baseline-aligned cells, if it has any (see row_baseline).
    pub(crate) baseline: Option<CssPixels>,
    /// How far below their baseline the row's baseline-aligned cells reach at most (see grow_rows_to_aligned_cells).
    pub(crate) max_cell_descent: CssPixels,
    /// The smallest bottom padding and border among the row's cells, which puts the bottom content edge of the lowest
    /// cell (see row_baseline).
    pub(crate) smallest_cell_block_end_offset: Option<CssPixels>,
    pub(crate) min_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) max_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) is_collapsed: bool,
    pub(crate) has_intrinsic_percentage: bool,
    pub(crate) intrinsic_percentage: f64,
}

impl Row {
    fn new(box_: Node, is_collapsed: bool) -> Self {
        Self {
            box_,
            base_block_size: CssPixels::default(),
            reference_block_size: CssPixels::default(),
            final_block_size: CssPixels::default(),
            baseline: None,
            max_cell_descent: CssPixels::default(),
            smallest_cell_block_end_offset: None,
            min_size: CssPixels::default(),
            max_size: CssPixels::default(),
            is_collapsed,
            has_intrinsic_percentage: false,
            intrinsic_percentage: 0.0,
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) struct TableGrid {
    pub(crate) column_count: usize,
    pub(crate) cells: Vec<TableCell>,
    pub(crate) rows: Vec<Row>,
    pub(crate) occupancy: TableGridOccupancy,
}

/// A table cell whose row span covers rows after the row it starts in.
struct CellSpanningRows {
    columns: Range<usize>,
    row_end: usize,
}

/// The slots of a table grid that its cells cover, each cell with its whole row and column span.
pub(crate) struct TableGridOccupancy {
    /// The covered columns of every row, as sorted half-open ranges that neither overlap nor touch. The ranges of row
    /// `r` are `covered_columns[first_range_of_row[r]..first_range_of_row[r + 1]]`; those of the row being built are
    /// the ranges past the last entry of `first_range_of_row`.
    covered_columns: Vec<Range<usize>>,
    first_range_of_row: Vec<usize>,
    /// The cells whose row span covers rows after the row being built, or after the last row once all rows are built.
    cells_spanning_later_rows: Vec<CellSpanningRows>,
}

impl TableGridOccupancy {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            covered_columns: Vec::new(),
            first_range_of_row: vec![0],
            cells_spanning_later_rows: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Whether a cell covers the slot at `(column, row)`.
    pub(crate) fn contains(&self, &(column, row): &(usize, usize)) -> bool {
        let built_row_count = self.first_range_of_row.len() - 1;
        if row < built_row_count {
            let ranges = &self.covered_columns[self.first_range_of_row[row]..self.first_range_of_row[row + 1]];
            return Self::range_covering(ranges, column).is_some();
        }
        self.cells_spanning_later_rows
            .iter()
            .any(|cell| row < cell.row_end && cell.columns.contains(&column))
    }

    fn range_covering(ranges: &[Range<usize>], column: usize) -> Option<&Range<usize>> {
        ranges
            .get(ranges.partition_point(|range| range.end <= column))
            .filter(|range| range.start <= column)
    }

    fn ranges_of_row_being_built(&self) -> &[Range<usize>] {
        &self.covered_columns[*self.first_range_of_row.last().unwrap()..]
    }

    fn cover_columns_of_row_being_built(&mut self, columns: Range<usize>) {
        if columns.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let first_range_of_row = *self.first_range_of_row.last().unwrap();
        let ranges = &self.covered_columns[first_range_of_row..];
        let first_touching = first_range_of_row + ranges.partition_point(|range| range.end < columns.start);
        let end_touching = first_range_of_row + ranges.partition_point(|range| range.start <= columns.end);
        if first_touching == end_touching {
            self.covered_columns.insert(first_touching, columns);
            return;
        }
        let merged = self.covered_columns[first_touching].start.min(columns.start)
            ..self.covered_columns[end_touching - 1].end.max(columns.end);
        self.covered_columns[first_touching] = merged;
        self.covered_columns.drain(first_touching + 1..end_touching);
    }

    /// Starts building row `row`, which the cells of earlier rows that span it cover.
    fn start_row(&mut self, row: usize) {
        debug_assert_eq!(self.first_range_of_row.len(), row + 1);
        let mut cells = std::mem::take(&mut self.cells_spanning_later_rows);
        cells.retain(|cell| {
            self.cover_columns_of_row_being_built(cell.columns.clone());
            cell.row_end > row + 1
        });
        self.cells_spanning_later_rows = cells;
    }

    /// The first column from `column` on that no cell covers in the row being built, or `column_count` if every one up
    /// to it is covered.
    fn first_uncovered_column_of_row_being_built(&self, column: usize, column_count: usize) -> usize {
        if column >= column_count {
            return column;
        }
        Self::range_covering(self.ranges_of_row_being_built(), column)
            .map_or(column, |range| range.end.min(column_count))
    }

    /// Covers the slots of a cell that starts in the row being built, `row`.
    fn cover_cell(&mut self, columns: Range<usize>, row: usize, row_span: usize) {
        if row_span > 1 && !columns.is_empty() {
            self.cells_spanning_later_rows.push(CellSpanningRows {
                columns: columns.clone(),
                row_end: row + row_span,
            });
        }
        self.cover_columns_of_row_being_built(columns);
    }

    fn finish_row(&mut self) {
        self.first_range_of_row.push(self.covered_columns.len());
    }

    /// Ends a row group, whose cells cover no row after it.
    fn finish_row_group(&mut self) {
        self.cells_spanning_later_rows.clear();
    }
}

/// Ends the row group whose cells start at `first_cell_of_group` in `cells`, now that every one of its rows is built:
/// No cell spans a row past the last row of its group.
fn finish_row_group(
    cells: &mut [TableCell],
    first_cell_of_group: usize,
    row_count: usize,
    occupancy: &mut TableGridOccupancy,
) {
    for cell in &mut cells[first_cell_of_group..] {
        cell.row_span = cell.row_span.min(row_count - cell.row_index);
    }
    occupancy.finish_row_group();
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct TableInlineLayout {
    table_box: Node,
    table_constraints: ContainingBlockConstraints,
    cells: Vec<TableCell>,
    columns: Vec<Column>,
    rows: Vec<Row>,
}

impl TableInlineLayout {
    pub(crate) fn table_box(&self) -> Node {
        self.table_box
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct TableInlineSizeMeasures {
    spacing: CssPixels,
    grid_min: CssPixels,
    grid_max: CssPixels,
    capmin: CssPixels,
}

fn matching_children<T: TableTree>(tree: &T, parent: Node, predicate: impl Fn(FfiDisplay) -> bool) -> Vec<Node> {
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    let mut child = tree.first_child(parent);
    while !child.is_invalid() {
        if node_facts::kind_is_box(tree.node_data(child).kind.get()) && predicate(tree.display(child)) {
            result.push(child);
        }
        child = tree.next_sibling(child);
    }
    result
}

fn count_columns_in_subtree<T: TableTree>(tree: &T, root: Node) -> usize {
    let mut count = 0usize;
    let mut stack = vec![root];
    while let Some(node) = stack.pop() {
        let mut child = tree.first_child(node);
        while !child.is_invalid() {
            if node_facts::kind_is_box(tree.node_data(child).kind.get()) && tree.display(child).is_table_column() {
                count = count.saturating_add(tree.table_column_span(child));
            }
            stack.push(child);
            child = tree.next_sibling(child);
        }
    }
    count
}

/// The table-row and table-row-group boxes among the children of a table root, in the order their rows are laid out.
fn row_containers_in_layout_order<T: TableTree>(tree: &T, table: Node) -> Vec<Node> {
    // https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#table-display
    // table-header-group: Like 'table-row-group', but for visual formatting, the row group is always displayed before
    // all other rows and row groups and after any top captions. [...] If a table contains multiple elements with
    // 'display: table-header-group', only the first is rendered as a header; the others are treated as if they had
    // 'display: table-row-group'.
    // table-footer-group: Like 'table-row-group', but for visual formatting, the row group is always displayed after
    // all other rows and row groups and before any bottom captions. [...] If a table contains multiple elements with
    // 'display: table-footer-group', only the first is rendered as a footer; the others are treated as if they had
    // 'display: table-row-group'.
    let children = matching_children(tree, table, |display| {
        display.is_table_row_group_kind() || display.is_table_row()
    });
    let header = children
        .iter()
        .position(|&child| tree.display(child).is_table_header_group());
    let footer = children
        .iter()
        .position(|&child| tree.display(child).is_table_footer_group());
    let mut ordered = Vec::with_capacity(children.len());
    ordered.extend(header.map(|index| children[index]));
    ordered.extend(
        children
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|&(index, _)| Some(index) != header && Some(index) != footer)
            .map(|(_, &child)| child),
    );
    ordered.extend(footer.map(|index| children[index]));
    ordered
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum MissingTableCells {
    Include,
    Exclude,
}

pub(crate) fn calculate_table_grid<T: TableTree>(tree: &T, table: Node, missing_cells: MissingTableCells) -> TableGrid {
    let mut cells = Vec::new();
    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    let mut occupancy = TableGridOccupancy::new();
    let mut column_count = 0usize;

    for child in matching_children(tree, table, |display| {
        display.is_table_column_group() || display.is_table_column()
    }) {
        // A table-column box is a child of a table-column-group, or a direct child of the table root: the fixup
        // algorithm leaves the latter in place, as "A table-column box is misparented if its parent is neither a
        // table-column-group box nor a table-root box": https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#fixup-algorithm
        // A table-column-group box without table-column children stands for the columns it spans itself, as
        // the HTML table forming algorithm forms them: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#forming-a-table
        let columns_in_child = if tree.display(child).is_table_column() {
            tree.table_column_span(child)
        } else {
            match count_columns_in_subtree(tree, child) {
                0 => tree.table_column_span(child),
                count => count,
            }
        };
        column_count = column_count.saturating_add(columns_in_child);
    }

    let process_row = |tree: &T,
                       row: Node,
                       row_group: Option<Node>,
                       cells: &mut Vec<TableCell>,
                       rows: &mut Vec<Row>,
                       occupancy: &mut TableGridOccupancy,
                       column_count: &mut usize| {
        let current_row = rows.len();
        let mut current_column = 0usize;
        occupancy.start_row(current_row);
        for cell_box in matching_children(tree, row, |display| display.is_table_cell()) {
            if missing_cells == MissingTableCells::Exclude
                && node_facts::has_flag(tree.node_data(cell_box), NodeFlag::IsMissingTableCell)
            {
                continue;
            }
            current_column = occupancy.first_uncovered_column_of_row_being_built(current_column, *column_count);
            if current_column == *column_count {
                *column_count += 1;
            }

            let column_span = tree.table_column_span(cell_box);
            let mut row_span = tree.table_row_span(cell_box);
            if row_span == 0 {
                // Downward-growing cells remain deliberately unimplemented.
                row_span = 1;
            }
            *column_count = (*column_count).max(current_column + column_span);
            occupancy.cover_cell(current_column..current_column + column_span, current_row, row_span);
            cells.push(TableCell {
                box_: cell_box,
                column_index: current_column,
                row_index: current_row,
                column_span,
                row_span,
                baseline: CssPixels::default(),
                outer_min_inline_size: CssPixels::default(),
                outer_max_inline_size: CssPixels::default(),
                outer_min_block_size: CssPixels::default(),
                outer_max_block_size: CssPixels::default(),
                max_content_inline_size: None,
            });
            current_column += column_span;
        }

        occupancy.finish_row();
        rows.push(Row::new(row, tree.row_is_collapsed(row, row_group)));
    };

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#forming-a-table
    // Each row group (and each run of rows that are children of the table itself) forms its own block of rows, which
    // the "algorithm for ending a row group" closes off. So, a cell's row span ends at the last row of its group.
    let mut first_cell_of_group = 0usize;
    let mut in_run_of_rows = false;
    for child in row_containers_in_layout_order(tree, table) {
        let is_row = tree.display(child).is_table_row();
        if !(is_row && in_run_of_rows) {
            finish_row_group(&mut cells, first_cell_of_group, rows.len(), &mut occupancy);
            first_cell_of_group = cells.len();
        }
        in_run_of_rows = is_row;
        if is_row {
            process_row(
                tree,
                child,
                None,
                &mut cells,
                &mut rows,
                &mut occupancy,
                &mut column_count,
            );
        } else {
            for row in matching_children(tree, child, |display| display.is_table_row()) {
                process_row(
                    tree,
                    row,
                    Some(child),
                    &mut cells,
                    &mut rows,
                    &mut occupancy,
                    &mut column_count,
                );
            }
        }
    }

    finish_row_group(&mut cells, first_cell_of_group, rows.len(), &mut occupancy);

    for cell in &mut cells {
        cell.column_span = cell.column_span.min(column_count - cell.column_index);
    }

    TableGrid {
        column_count,
        cells,
        rows,
        occupancy,
    }
}

pub(super) const BORDER_COLLAPSE_SEPARATE: u8 = 0;
const TABLE_LAYOUT_FIXED: u8 = 1;

/// The grid columns that a table-column box, or a table-column-group box without table-column children, corresponds
/// to (see collect_column_track_ranges()).
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct ColumnTrackRange {
    /// The table-column box, or the table-column-group box that stands for the columns it spans itself.
    box_: Node,
    /// The table-column-group box of the columns, if any.
    group: Option<Node>,
    start: usize,
    end: usize,
}

impl ColumnTrackRange {
    fn is_group_without_columns(&self) -> bool {
        self.group == Some(self.box_)
    }
}

pub(crate) trait TableTree {
    fn first_child(&self, node: Node) -> Node;
    fn next_sibling(&self, node: Node) -> Node;
    fn node_data(&self, node: Node) -> &NodeData;
    fn display(&self, node: Node) -> FfiDisplay;

    fn table_column_span(&self, node: Node) -> usize {
        self.node_data(node).table_column_span as usize
    }

    fn table_row_span(&self, node: Node) -> usize {
        self.node_data(node).table_row_span as usize
    }

    fn row_is_collapsed(&self, _row: Node, _row_group: Option<Node>) -> bool {
        false
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum TrackAxis {
    Row,
    Column,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum AutoTableInlineSize {
    FillsAvailableInlineSize,
    ShrinksToFitAvailableInlineSize,
}

pub(super) struct TableFormattingContext<'pass> {
    run: FormattingContextRun<'pass>,
    /// The cells in which this table sizes its own box.
    table_box_cells: Cell<used_values::RootInputCells>,
    auto_table_inline_size: AutoTableInlineSize,
    table_constraints: ContainingBlockConstraints,
    participant_constraints: ContainingBlockConstraints,
    available_space: AvailableSpace,
    table_block_size: CssPixels,
    /// The block size that percentage block sizes of rows and cells resolve against (see compute_table_block_size).
    table_percentage_basis: CssPixels,
    /// The border box inline size a flex container sizes the table box to, if it does.
    forced_border_box_inline_size: Option<CssPixels>,
    pub(super) automatic_content_block_size: CssPixels,
    /// The collapsed borders the table box's fragment paints, once they are materialized.
    collapsed_table_borders: Option<std::sync::Arc<OwnedCollapsedTableBorders>>,
    table_box_content_block_offset_in_wrapper: CssPixels,
    min_border_box_block_size_from_flex_item: Option<CssPixels>,
    needs_row_measurement: bool,
    cells: Vec<TableCell>,
    /// What the table keeps of each cell while it lays the cell out, by the cell's index in `cells`, once the table
    /// prepared its participants.
    cell_layouts: Vec<CellLayoutState>,
    columns: Vec<Column>,
    column_track_ranges: Vec<ColumnTrackRange>,
    /// The inline offset of each column from the first, and past the last, each followed by the border spacing after
    /// it, once the columns are sized.
    column_offsets: Vec<CssPixels>,
    rows: Vec<Row>,
    /// The box of each row as this table lays it out, by row index, once the table prepared its participants.
    row_boxes: Vec<TableParticipantBox>,
    /// The box of each row group as this table lays it out, in the order the rows are laid out (see
    /// row_groups_in_layout_order()), once the table prepared its participants.
    row_group_boxes: Vec<(Node, TableParticipantBox)>,
    /// The box of each column group and column as this table lays it out, in tree order (see column_boxes()), once
    /// the table prepared its participants.
    column_group_and_column_boxes: Vec<(Node, TableParticipantBox)>,
    collapsed_border_grid: Option<CollapsedBorderGrid>,
    derived_baselines_of_root_box: Cell<DerivedBaselines>,
}

/// A row, row group, column group or column, which its table lays out in cells it keeps itself.
struct TableParticipantBox {
    cells: Cell<used_values::RootInputCells>,
    /// The offset of the box's content box in its containing block, once the table placed the box.
    content_offset: Cell<FfiCssPixelPoint>,
}

impl TableTree for TableFormattingContext<'_> {
    fn first_child(&self, node: Node) -> Node {
        self.run.pass.first_child(node)
    }

    fn next_sibling(&self, node: Node) -> Node {
        self.run.pass.next_sibling(node)
    }

    fn node_data(&self, node: Node) -> &NodeData {
        self.run.pass.node_data(node)
    }

    fn display(&self, node: Node) -> FfiDisplay {
        self.run
            .pass
            .computed_values_view_if_styled(node)
            .map_or_else(FfiDisplay::block, |style| style.display())
    }

    fn row_is_collapsed(&self, row: Node, row_group: Option<Node>) -> bool {
        // CSS::Visibility::Collapse is pinned to zero in
        // LayoutRustBridge.cpp.
        self.style(row).visibility() == 0 || row_group.is_some_and(|group| self.style(group).visibility() == 0)
    }
}

impl TableFormattingContext<'_> {
    fn column_is_collapsed(&self, column: Node) -> bool {
        // CSS::Visibility::Collapse is pinned to zero in LayoutRustBridge.cpp.
        if self.style(column).visibility() == 0 {
            return true;
        }
        let parent = self.parent(column);
        !parent.is_invalid() && self.node_facts(parent).is_table_column_group() && self.style(parent).visibility() == 0
    }

    /// The number of columns a cell spans that are not collapsed; the border spacing inside the cell's span is the
    /// spacing between those.
    fn visible_spanned_columns(&self, cell: TableCell) -> usize {
        (cell.column_index..cell.column_index + cell.column_span)
            .filter(|&index| !self.columns[index].is_collapsed)
            .count()
    }

    fn visible_column_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.columns.iter().filter(|column| !column.is_collapsed).count()
    }

    /// Removes the columns with 'visibility: collapse' once the table is sized and its inline size distributed as
    /// if they were visible: "This value causes the entire row or column to be removed from the display, and the
    /// space normally taken up by the row or column to be made available for other content. [...] The suppression
    /// of the row or column, however, does not otherwise affect the layout of the table."
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#dynamic-effects
    /// A collapsed column keeps no inline size and no border spacing, and the table box shrinks by what the column
    /// took, as in other engines. Its table wrapper keeps the inline size it was given for the table.
    fn remove_collapsed_columns(&mut self) {
        let spacing = self.border_spacing_inline();
        let mut removed = CssPixels::default();
        for column in &mut self.columns {
            if column.is_collapsed {
                removed += column.used_inline_size + spacing;
                column.used_inline_size = CssPixels::default();
            }
        }
        if removed > CssPixels::default() {
            let table_used = &self.table_box_cells;
            table_used.set_content_inline_size(table_used.content_inline_size() - removed);
        }
    }
}

impl<'pass> formatting_context::FormattingContextAlgorithm<'pass> for TableFormattingContext<'pass> {
    fn lay_out(
        &mut self,
        run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>,
        input: formatting_context::AlgorithmInput<'_>,
    ) -> formatting_context::AlgorithmOutput {
        self.run(run, input.body_input, input.table_inline_layout);
        let mut root_payload = fragment_tree::PendingPayload::default();
        if let Some(collapsed_table_borders) = self.collapsed_table_borders.take() {
            root_payload.set(fragment_tree::FcPayload::Table(collapsed_table_borders));
        }
        formatting_context::AlgorithmOutput::of_root(
            formatting_context::ChildLayoutResult {
                automatic_content_block_size: self.automatic_content_block_size,
                baselines: self.derived_baselines_of_root_box(),
                ..formatting_context::ChildLayoutResult::default()
            },
            self.table_box_cells(),
        )
        .with_root_payload(root_payload)
    }

    fn after_root_is_dimensioned(
        &self,
        run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>,
        _root_cells_in_own_frame: used_values::RootInputCells,
    ) -> formatting_context::AfterDimensioning {
        formatting_context::register_table_abspos_descendants(run, run.box_);
        formatting_context::AfterDimensioning::LaysOutAbsposContainedByRoot
    }
}

impl<'pass> TableFormattingContext<'pass> {
    fn node_facts(&self, node: Node) -> NodeFacts<'_> {
        NodeFacts::new(&self.run.pass, node)
    }

    #[inline]
    fn style(&self, node: Node) -> StyleValues<'pass> {
        StyleValues::for_node(&self.run.pass, node)
    }

    pub(super) fn new(
        run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>,
        table_box_cells: used_values::RootInputCells,
        auto_table_inline_size: AutoTableInlineSize,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            run: run.clone(),
            table_box_cells: Cell::new(table_box_cells),
            auto_table_inline_size,
            table_constraints: ContainingBlockConstraints::default(),
            participant_constraints: ContainingBlockConstraints::default(),
            available_space: AvailableSpace::default(),
            table_block_size: CssPixels::default(),
            table_percentage_basis: CssPixels::default(),
            forced_border_box_inline_size: None,
            automatic_content_block_size: CssPixels::default(),
            collapsed_table_borders: None,
            table_box_content_block_offset_in_wrapper: CssPixels::default(),
            min_border_box_block_size_from_flex_item: None,
            needs_row_measurement: false,
            cells: Vec::new(),
            cell_layouts: Vec::new(),
            columns: Vec::new(),
            column_track_ranges: Vec::new(),
            column_offsets: Vec::new(),
            rows: Vec::new(),
            row_boxes: Vec::new(),
            row_group_boxes: Vec::new(),
            column_group_and_column_boxes: Vec::new(),
            collapsed_border_grid: None,
            derived_baselines_of_root_box: Cell::new(DerivedBaselines::default()),
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn take_inline_layout(&mut self) -> TableInlineLayout {
        TableInlineLayout {
            table_box: self.run.box_,
            table_constraints: self.table_constraints,
            cells: std::mem::take(&mut self.cells),
            columns: std::mem::take(&mut self.columns),
            rows: std::mem::take(&mut self.rows),
        }
    }

    fn reuse_inline_layout(&mut self, input: LayoutInput, layout: TableInlineLayout) -> bool {
        if layout.table_box != self.run.box_ || layout.table_constraints != input.containing_block_constraints {
            return false;
        }

        self.available_space = input.available_space;
        self.table_constraints = input.containing_block_constraints;
        self.participant_constraints = ContainingBlockConstraints {
            percentage_basis_inline_size: self.table_constraints.percentage_basis_inline_size,
            percentage_basis_block_size: if self.style(self.run.box_).height().is_auto() {
                None
            } else {
                self.table_constraints.percentage_basis_block_size
            },
            quirks_mode_percentage_basis_block_size: self.table_constraints.quirks_mode_percentage_basis_block_size,
        };
        self.cells = layout.cells;
        self.columns = layout.columns;
        self.rows = layout.rows;

        // The wrapper sizing pass deliberately omits intrinsic row measurement. Reusing its
        // inline result is only sufficient when the committing pass would omit it as well.
        if !self.can_skip_row_intrinsic_measurement() {
            return false;
        }

        self.column_track_ranges = self.collect_column_track_ranges();
        self.needs_row_measurement = false;
        self.prepare_table_participants(TableParticipantPreparation::CellsOfEveryParticipant);
        self.border_conflict_resolution();
        self.compute_table_inline_size();
        true
    }

    #[inline]
    fn sizing(&self) -> sizing_context::SizingContext<'pass, 'static> {
        sizing_context::SizingContext::new(self.run.state, self.run.pass)
    }

    fn parent(&self, node: Node) -> Node {
        self.run.pass.parent(node)
    }

    fn matching_children(&mut self, parent: Node, predicate: impl Fn(NodeFacts<'_>) -> bool) -> Vec<Node> {
        self.run
            .pass
            .children(parent)
            .filter(|&child| {
                let facts = self.node_facts(child);
                facts.is_box() && predicate(facts)
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// The grid columns of the table-column boxes in tree order, each spanning the columns that its span attribute
    /// gives it. A table-column-group box without table-column children stands for the columns it spans itself, as
    /// the HTML table forming algorithm forms them: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#forming-a-table
    /// A table-column box is a child of a table-column-group, or a direct child of the table root: the fixup
    /// algorithm leaves the latter in place, as "A table-column box is misparented if its parent is neither a
    /// table-column-group box nor a table-root box": https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#fixup-algorithm
    fn collect_column_track_ranges(&mut self) -> Vec<ColumnTrackRange> {
        let column_count = self.columns.len();
        let mut ranges = Vec::new();
        let mut column_index = 0usize;
        for child in self.matching_children(self.run.box_, |facts| {
            facts.is_table_column_group() || facts.is_table_column()
        }) {
            let (group, columns) = if self.node_facts(child).is_table_column() {
                (None, vec![child])
            } else {
                let columns = self.matching_children(child, |facts| facts.is_table_column());
                (Some(child), if columns.is_empty() { vec![child] } else { columns })
            };
            for column in columns {
                let end = (column_index + self.table_column_span(column)).min(column_count);
                ranges.push(ColumnTrackRange {
                    box_: column,
                    group,
                    start: column_index,
                    end,
                });
                column_index = end;
            }
        }
        ranges
    }

    /// Whether the columns of the table run from right to left: "Column boxes are placed next to each other in the
    /// order they occur. The first column box may be either on the left or on the right, depending on the value of
    /// the 'direction' property of the table."
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#table-layout
    /// The columns are counted in the table's column order, from its first column, so only where they are placed
    /// do they count from the left (see `physical_columns`).
    fn is_right_to_left(&self) -> bool {
        self.style(self.run.box_).direction() == direction::RTL
    }

    /// The columns `columns` of the table's column order, as physical columns counted from the left.
    fn physical_columns(&self, columns: Range<usize>) -> Range<usize> {
        if !self.is_right_to_left() {
            return columns;
        }
        let column_count = self.columns.len();
        column_count - columns.end..column_count - columns.start
    }

    /// The box whose style gives the width specified for the columns of a range, which is also the one that makes
    /// them constrained and gives them a percentage contribution.
    fn column_sizing_box(&self, range: ColumnTrackRange) -> Node {
        // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#min-content-width-of-a-column-based-on-cells-of-span-up-to-1
        // the width specified for the column:
        // - the outer min-content width of its corresponding table-column, if any (and not auto)
        // - the outer min-content width of its corresponding table-column-group, if any
        // - or 0, if there is none
        // NB: The first of these that applies is the width specified for the column, for its outer max-content
        //     width, its constrainedness and its percentage contribution as well.
        match range.group {
            Some(group) if range.is_group_without_columns() || self.style(range.box_).width().is_auto() => group,
            _ => range.box_,
        }
    }

    /// The table-column-group boxes and table-column boxes of the table in tree order (see collect_column_track_ranges()).
    fn column_boxes(&mut self) -> Vec<Node> {
        let mut boxes = Vec::new();
        for child in self.matching_children(self.run.box_, |facts| {
            facts.is_table_column_group() || facts.is_table_column()
        }) {
            boxes.push(child);
            if self.node_facts(child).is_table_column_group() {
                boxes.extend(self.matching_children(child, |facts| facts.is_table_column()));
            }
        }
        boxes
    }

    /// The table-row-group boxes of the table, header and footer groups included, in the order their rows are laid
    /// out: see row_containers_in_layout_order().
    fn row_groups_in_layout_order(&self) -> Vec<Node> {
        row_containers_in_layout_order(self, self.run.box_)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|&child| self.node_facts(child).is_table_row_group_kind())
            .collect()
    }

    pub(super) fn table_box_cells(&self) -> used_values::RootInputCells {
        self.table_box_cells.get()
    }

    /// The box of each row as this table lays it out, in the order of the rows.
    fn row_boxes_by_row_index(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &TableParticipantBox> {
        (0..self.rows.len()).map(|row_index| &self.row_boxes[row_index])
    }

    /// The row groups that contain rows, in layout order, each with the range of the indices of its rows. The rows
    /// of a row group are contiguous in layout order.
    fn row_ranges_of_row_groups(&self) -> Vec<(Node, Range<usize>)> {
        let mut row_ranges: Vec<(Node, Range<usize>)> = Vec::new();
        for row_index in 0..self.rows.len().min(self.row_boxes.len()) {
            let parent = self.parent(self.rows[row_index].box_);
            if parent == self.run.box_ {
                continue;
            }
            match row_ranges.last_mut() {
                Some((group, rows)) if *group == parent && rows.end == row_index => rows.end += 1,
                _ => row_ranges.push((parent, row_index..row_index + 1)),
            }
        }
        row_ranges
    }

    /// Places `node`, a participant this table lays out as `participant_box`, with what its fragment shows of the
    /// table's layout `fragment_facts`. The box's metrics are final once it is placed.
    fn place_participant(
        &self,
        node: Node,
        participant_box: &TableParticipantBox,
        fragment_facts: run_state::FragmentFactsDecidedByParent,
        x: CssPixels,
        y: CssPixels,
    ) {
        let content_offset = FfiCssPixelPoint { x, y };
        formatting_context::place_child(
            &self.run,
            node,
            formatting_context::PlacedChild::laid_out_here(participant_box.cells.get(), None, &self.run)
                .with_fragment_facts(fragment_facts),
            content_offset,
            None,
            None,
        );
        participant_box.content_offset.set(content_offset);
    }

    fn border_spacing_inline(&self) -> CssPixels {
        let style = self.style(self.run.box_);
        // When a table is laid out in collapsed-borders mode, the border-spacing of the table-root is ignored (as if it was set to 0px):
        // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#collapsed-style-overrides
        if style.border_collapse() != BORDER_COLLAPSE_SEPARATE {
            CssPixels::default()
        } else {
            style.border_spacing_horizontal()
        }
    }

    fn border_spacing_block(&self) -> CssPixels {
        let style = self.style(self.run.box_);
        // When a table is laid out in collapsed-borders mode, the border-spacing of the table-root is ignored (as if it was set to 0px):
        // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#collapsed-style-overrides
        if style.border_collapse() != BORDER_COLLAPSE_SEPARATE {
            CssPixels::default()
        } else {
            style.border_spacing_vertical()
        }
    }

    fn element_borders(&self, node: Node) -> ElementBorders {
        let style = self.style(node);
        ElementBorders {
            top: formatting_context::BorderData {
                color: style.border_top_color(),
                line_style: style.border_top_style(),
                width: style.border_top_width(),
            },
            right: formatting_context::BorderData {
                color: style.border_right_color(),
                line_style: style.border_right_style(),
                width: style.border_right_width(),
            },
            bottom: formatting_context::BorderData {
                color: style.border_bottom_color(),
                line_style: style.border_bottom_style(),
                width: style.border_bottom_width(),
            },
            left: formatting_context::BorderData {
                color: style.border_left_color(),
                line_style: style.border_left_style(),
                width: style.border_left_width(),
            },
        }
    }

    fn border_conflict_resolution(&mut self) {
        if self.style(self.run.box_).border_collapse() == BORDER_COLLAPSE_SEPARATE {
            return;
        }

        let row_count = self.rows.len();
        let column_count = self.columns.len();
        let mut grid = CollapsedBorderGrid::new(row_count, column_count);
        let mut next_source_order = 0u32;
        let mut take_source_order = move || {
            let source_order = next_source_order;
            next_source_order += 1;
            source_order
        };
        // Cells, column by column in the table's column order, so that on ties the cell further to the left (to the
        // right, in a right-to-left table), then further to the top, wins. TableCell spans are already clipped to the
        // table end by TableGrid. The border grid counts its columns from the left.
        let mut cells = self.cells.clone();
        cells.sort_by_key(|cell| (cell.column_index, cell.row_index));
        for cell in cells {
            let source_order = take_source_order();
            let columns = self.physical_columns(cell.column_index..cell.column_index + cell.column_span);
            if cell.row_span > 1 || cell.column_span > 1 {
                grid.hide_segments_inside_span(
                    cell.row_index,
                    cell.row_index + cell.row_span,
                    columns.start,
                    columns.end,
                    source_order,
                );
            }
            let borders = self.element_borders(cell.box_);
            grid.apply_borders(
                borders,
                cell.row_index,
                cell.row_index + cell.row_span,
                columns.start,
                columns.end,
                source_order,
            );
        }
        for row_index in 0..row_count {
            let row_box = self.rows[row_index].box_;
            let borders = self.element_borders(row_box);
            grid.apply_borders(borders, row_index, row_index + 1, 0, column_count, take_source_order());
        }
        // Row groups, in the order their rows appear in the grid. Rows of a group are contiguous in
        // m_rows, since TableGrid collects them in tree order.
        let mut row_index = 0;
        while row_index < row_count {
            let group = self.parent(self.rows[row_index].box_);
            if group.is_invalid() {
                row_index += 1;
                continue;
            }
            let facts = self.node_facts(group);
            if !(facts.is_table_row_group() || facts.is_table_header_group() || facts.is_table_footer_group()) {
                row_index += 1;
                continue;
            }
            let start = row_index;
            while row_index < row_count && self.parent(self.rows[row_index].box_) == group {
                row_index += 1;
            }
            let borders = self.element_borders(group);
            grid.apply_borders(borders, start, row_index, 0, column_count, take_source_order());
        }

        // Column (<col>) elements, inside a column group or directly under the table root (see
        // collect_column_track_ranges()).
        let mut column_group_ranges: Vec<(Node, usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
        for &range in &self.column_track_ranges {
            if let Some(group) = range.group {
                match column_group_ranges.last_mut() {
                    Some((last_group, _, group_end)) if *last_group == group => *group_end = range.end,
                    _ => column_group_ranges.push((group, range.start, range.end)),
                }
            }
            if range.is_group_without_columns() {
                continue;
            }
            let borders = self.element_borders(range.box_);
            let source_order = take_source_order();
            // A column spanning several columns applies its borders to them in the table's column order, so that where two
            // of them tie, the one further to the left (to the right, in a right-to-left table) wins.
            for column_index in range.start..range.end {
                let column = self.physical_columns(column_index..column_index + 1).start;
                grid.apply_borders(borders, 0, row_count, column, column + 1, source_order);
            }
        }
        for (column_group, group_start, group_end) in column_group_ranges {
            if group_start < group_end {
                let borders = self.element_borders(column_group);
                let columns = self.physical_columns(group_start..group_end);
                grid.apply_borders(borders, 0, row_count, columns.start, columns.end, take_source_order());
            }
        }
        let table_borders = self.element_borders(self.run.box_);
        grid.apply_borders(table_borders, 0, row_count, 0, column_count, take_source_order());

        let outer = grid.outer_edge_widths();
        let table_used = &self.table_box_cells;
        let old_border_box_top = table_used.border_box_top(false);
        let old_inline_borders = table_used.border_box_left(false) + table_used.border_box_right(false);
        table_used.update_cells(|cells| {
            cells.border_top = outer.top;
            cells.border_right = outer.right;
            cells.border_bottom = outer.bottom;
            cells.border_left = outer.left;
            // https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#collapsing-borders
            // "In this model, a table does not have padding (but does have margins)."
            cells.padding_top = CssPixels::default();
            cells.padding_right = CssPixels::default();
            cells.padding_bottom = CssPixels::default();
            cells.padding_left = CssPixels::default();
            cells.uses_collapsing_borders_model = true;
            cells.is_collapsed_borders_table_box = true;
        });
        self.table_box_content_block_offset_in_wrapper += table_used.border_box_top(true) - old_border_box_top;
        let freed_inline = old_inline_borders - (table_used.border_box_left(true) + table_used.border_box_right(true));
        if let AvailableSize::Definite(available) = self.available_space.inline_size {
            self.available_space.inline_size = AvailableSize::definite(available + freed_inline);
        }

        for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
            let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
            self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells.uses_collapsing_borders_model = true;
            // A missing cell (https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#missing-cells-fixup) is an anonymous box without an
            // element, so no border belongs to it: the borders at its edges are those of its neighbours, and it takes
            // no share of them. That keeps a row made of missing cells at its specified block size, with the borders
            // of the rows around it overlapping on the same grid line.
            if node_facts::has_flag(self.node_data(cell.box_), NodeFlag::IsMissingTableCell) {
                continue;
            }
            let row_end = cell.row_index + cell.row_span;
            let columns = self.physical_columns(cell.column_index..cell.column_index + cell.column_span);
            let widths = grid.resolve_used_widths_for_cell(cell.row_index, row_end, columns.start, columns.end);
            let cell_box = &mut self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells;
            cell_box.border_top = widths.top;
            cell_box.border_right = widths.right;
            cell_box.border_bottom = widths.bottom;
            cell_box.border_left = widths.left;
        }
        self.collapsed_border_grid = Some(grid);
    }

    fn materialize_collapsed_table_borders(&mut self) {
        let Some(grid) = self.collapsed_border_grid.take() else {
            return;
        };
        if self.run.fragments.is_none() {
            return;
        }
        if !grid.has_paintable_edges() {
            return;
        }
        // NB: The collapsing border model has no border spacing, so the columns are next to each other.
        let column_offsets = std::mem::take(&mut self.column_offsets);
        let row_offsets = grid_line_offsets(self.rows.iter().map(|row| {
            if row.is_collapsed {
                CssPixels::default()
            } else {
                row.final_block_size
            }
        }));
        let (horizontal_edges, vertical_edges) = grid.take_edges();
        self.collapsed_table_borders = Some(std::sync::Arc::new(OwnedCollapsedTableBorders {
            row_offsets,
            column_offsets,
            horizontal_edges,
            vertical_edges,
        }));
    }

    // Participants resolve percentages against the table's input basis inside this context, so
    // their dependency is charged here rather than through child runs.
    fn prepare_table_participants(&mut self, preparation: TableParticipantPreparation) {
        let row_groups = self.row_groups_in_layout_order();
        // Column groups and columns have no content to lay out, but they are painted: their backgrounds cover the
        // cells of their columns (CSS 2.2 §17.5.1), so they get boxes, positioned by position_column_boxes().
        let column_boxes = self.column_boxes();
        let prepares_cells_of_rows_row_groups_and_columns =
            preparation == TableParticipantPreparation::CellsOfEveryParticipant;
        let sizing = self.sizing();
        let note_percentage_block_size_dependency_of = |participant| {
            if sizing.own_style_depends_on_percentage_block_size(participant) {
                self.run
                    .state
                    .note_descendant_depends_on_percentage_block_size(self.run.box_);
            }
        };
        let participant_box = |participant| TableParticipantBox {
            cells: Cell::new(used_values::cells_before_sizing(
                &self.run.pass,
                participant,
                self.participant_constraints,
            )),
            content_offset: Cell::new(FfiCssPixelPoint::default()),
        };
        let mut row_group_boxes = Vec::new();
        for participant in row_groups {
            if prepares_cells_of_rows_row_groups_and_columns {
                row_group_boxes.push((participant, participant_box(participant)));
            }
            note_percentage_block_size_dependency_of(participant);
        }
        let mut column_group_and_column_boxes = Vec::new();
        for participant in column_boxes {
            if prepares_cells_of_rows_row_groups_and_columns {
                column_group_and_column_boxes.push((participant, participant_box(participant)));
            }
            note_percentage_block_size_dependency_of(participant);
        }
        let mut row_boxes = Vec::new();
        for row in &self.rows {
            if prepares_cells_of_rows_row_groups_and_columns {
                row_boxes.push(participant_box(row.box_));
            }
            note_percentage_block_size_dependency_of(row.box_);
        }
        self.row_group_boxes = row_group_boxes;
        self.column_group_and_column_boxes = column_group_and_column_boxes;
        self.row_boxes = row_boxes;
        let cell_layouts = self
            .cells
            .iter()
            .map(|cell| {
                note_percentage_block_size_dependency_of(cell.box_);
                CellLayoutState {
                    box_cells: used_values::cells_before_sizing(
                        &self.run.pass,
                        cell.box_,
                        self.participant_constraints,
                    ),
                    fragment_facts: run_state::FragmentFactsDecidedByParent {
                        show: fragment_tree::ParentShowFacts {
                            table_column_index: cell.column_index as u32,
                            table_column_span: cell.column_span as u32,
                            ..fragment_tree::ParentShowFacts::default()
                        },
                        ..run_state::FragmentFactsDecidedByParent::default()
                    },
                    ..CellLayoutState::default()
                }
            })
            .collect();
        self.cell_layouts = cell_layouts;
    }

    /// Whether a length or percentage `height` on a cell sizes its border box rather than its content box. CSS 2
    /// §17.5.3 sizes rows by "the computed 'height' of each cell", which is a content box size unless
    /// `box-sizing: border-box`; the table cell height box sizing quirk makes it a border box size in quirks mode:
    /// https://quirks.spec.whatwg.org/#the-table-cell-height-box-sizing-quirk
    fn cell_specified_block_size_is_border_box(&self, cell_box: Node, style: &StyleValues<'_>) -> bool {
        style.box_sizing() == box_sizing::BORDER_BOX || self.node_facts(cell_box).document_in_quirks_mode()
    }

    /// The outer (border box) block size that a `height` resolved to `specified` gives a cell whose padding and
    /// borders take up `block_offsets`.
    fn cell_specified_outer_block_size(
        &self,
        cell_box: Node,
        style: &StyleValues<'_>,
        specified: CssPixels,
        block_offsets: CssPixels,
    ) -> CssPixels {
        if self.cell_specified_block_size_is_border_box(cell_box, style) {
            specified
        } else {
            specified + block_offsets
        }
    }

    /// A cell's percentage block size resolves against the table's block size only when the table's own block size
    /// isn't auto, just like the percentage block sizes of its participants; otherwise the cell is sized as if its
    /// block size were auto. (CSS 2.1 leaves percentage cell heights undefined: "CSS 2.1 does not define how the height
    /// of table cells and table rows is calculated when their height is specified using percentage values.")
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS21/tables.html#height-layout
    fn cell_has_resolvable_percentage_block_size(&self, cell_box: Node) -> bool {
        self.style(cell_box).height().percentage_fraction().is_some() && !self.table_block_size_is_auto()
    }

    /// Whether the table's block size is auto, or a percentage that has nothing to resolve against, which acts as
    /// auto (see compute_table_block_size).
    fn table_block_size_is_auto(&self) -> bool {
        let height = self.style(self.run.box_).height();
        height.is_auto()
            || (height.contains_percentage()
                && self.table_constraints.percentage_basis_block_size.is_none()
                && !(self.node_facts(self.run.box_).document_in_quirks_mode()
                    && self.table_constraints.quirks_mode_percentage_basis_block_size.is_some()))
    }

    fn use_fixed_mode_layout(&self) -> bool {
        // Implements https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#in-fixed-mode.
        // A table-root is said to be laid out in fixed mode whenever the computed value of the table-layout property is equal to fixed, and the
        // specified width of the table root is either a <length-percentage>, min-content or fit-content. When the specified width is not one of
        // those values, or if the computed value of the table-layout property is auto, then the table-root is said to be laid out in auto mode.
        let style = self.style(self.run.box_);
        let width = style.width();
        // NB: A calc-size() width counts as well, whatever its basis.
        //     https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#calc-size
        // NB: So does a stretch width, as resolved in https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/10937.
        style.table_layout() == TABLE_LAYOUT_FIXED
            && (width.is_length_percentage()
                || width.is_min_content()
                || width.is_fit_content()
                || width.is_stretch()
                || width.calc_size().is_some())
    }

    /// Whether a cell takes part in measuring the tracks of an axis. https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#computing-column-measures:
    /// "For the purpose of measuring a column when laid out in fixed mode, only cells which originate in the first row
    /// of the table (after reordering the header and footer) will be considered, if any."
    fn cell_is_measured(&self, cell: TableCell, axis: TrackAxis) -> bool {
        axis == TrackAxis::Row || cell.row_index == 0 || !self.use_fixed_mode_layout()
    }

    fn compute_constrainedness(&mut self) {
        // Definition of constrainedness: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#constrainedness
        let fixed = self.use_fixed_mode_layout();
        // NB: The definition uses https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS21/visudet.html#propdef-width for width, which doesn't include
        //     keyword values. The remaining checks can be simplified to checking whether the size is a length.
        for &range in &self.column_track_ranges {
            if self.style(self.column_sizing_box(range)).width().is_length() {
                for index in range.start..range.end {
                    self.columns[index].is_constrained = true;
                }
            }
        }
        for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
            let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
            // In fixed mode, only the cells of the first row measure the columns (see cell_is_measured), so a length
            // width on a cell in a later row doesn't constrain its column either.
            if !self.cell_is_measured(cell, TrackAxis::Column) {
                continue;
            }
            let style = self.style(cell.box_);
            // "any of the cells spanning only that column"
            if cell.column_span == 1 && style.width().is_length() {
                self.columns[cell.column_index].is_constrained = true;
            }
            // INTEROP: In fixed mode, a cell of the first row with a length inline size constrains every column it
            //          spans, which share that inline size, as in other engines: "the width of the cell is divided
            //          over the columns" (CSS 2.1 §17.5.2.1).
            if fixed && cell.row_index == 0 && cell.column_span > 1 && style.width().is_length() {
                for index in cell.column_index..cell.column_index + cell.column_span {
                    self.columns[index].is_constrained = true;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn calculate_min_content_inline_size_of_caption(&self, caption: Node) -> CssPixels {
        self.sizing()
            .calculate_min_content_inline_size(sizing_context::SizedBox::unheld(caption), self.participant_constraints)
    }

    fn calculate_max_content_inline_size_of_caption(&self, caption: Node) -> CssPixels {
        self.sizing()
            .calculate_max_content_inline_size(sizing_context::SizedBox::unheld(caption), self.participant_constraints)
    }

    /// The box of the cell at `cell_index`, sized in the cells this table keeps of it.
    fn sized_cell(&self, cell_index: usize) -> sizing_context::SizedBox<'_> {
        sizing_context::SizedBox::new(self.cells[cell_index].box_, &self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells)
    }

    /// What the padding percentages of the cells resolve against once the table is sized: its content inline size
    /// without the border spacing before the first column and after the last. While the columns are measured, they
    /// resolve against zero.
    fn cell_padding_percentage_basis(&self) -> CssPixels {
        self.table_box_cells.content_inline_size() - self.border_spacing_inline() * 2usize
    }

    /// The cells of the box of the cell at `cell_index` with its paddings, whose percentages resolve against
    /// `inline_basis` in both axes, and in the separated borders model its borders.
    fn cell_box_with_resolved_sides(
        &self,
        cell_index: usize,
        collapsed: bool,
        inline_basis: CssPixels,
    ) -> used_values::RootInputCells {
        let style = self.style(self.cells[cell_index].box_);
        let mut cell_box = self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells;
        cell_box.padding_top = style.padding_top().to_px(inline_basis);
        cell_box.padding_bottom = style.padding_bottom().to_px(inline_basis);
        cell_box.padding_left = style.padding_left().to_px(inline_basis);
        cell_box.padding_right = style.padding_right().to_px(inline_basis);
        // The collapsing border model resolves the borders of cells in border_conflict_resolution().
        if !collapsed {
            cell_box.border_top = style.border_top_width();
            cell_box.border_bottom = style.border_bottom_width();
            cell_box.border_left = style.border_left_width();
            cell_box.border_right = style.border_right_width();
        }
        cell_box
    }

    fn compute_cell_measures(&mut self) {
        // Implements https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#computing-cell-measures.
        let inline_basis = self.table_constraints.inline_basis();
        self.compute_constrainedness();
        let fixed = self.use_fixed_mode_layout();
