        let collapsed = self.style(self.run.box_).border_collapse() != BORDER_COLLAPSE_SEPARATE;

        for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
            let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
            let style = self.style(cell.box_);
            let cell_box = self.cell_box_with_resolved_sides(cell_index, collapsed, CssPixels::default());
            let inline_offsets = cell_box.border_box_left(collapsed) + cell_box.border_box_right(collapsed);
            let width = style.width();
            let max_width = style.max_width();
            // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#percentage-contribution
            // "Please note that 'min-width' is not included in this computation. As a result, a percentage 'min-width'
            // is ignored."
            let min_width = style.min_width();
            let mut min_inline = if min_width.is_length() {
                min_width.to_px(inline_basis)
            } else {
                CssPixels::default()
            };
            let mut inline_size = if width.is_length() {
                width.to_px(inline_basis)
            } else {
                CssPixels::default()
            };
            let mut max_inline = if max_width.is_length() {
                max_width.to_px(inline_basis)
            } else {
                CssPixels::from_raw(i32::MAX)
            };
            if style.box_sizing() == box_sizing::BORDER_BOX {
                // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-sizing-3/#box-sizing: the content box cannot be smaller than zero, so a
                // border-box size below the padding and borders leaves an empty content box.
                min_inline = (min_inline - inline_offsets).max(CssPixels::default());
                inline_size = (inline_size - inline_offsets).max(CssPixels::default());
                max_inline = (max_inline - inline_offsets).max(CssPixels::default());
            }

            if fixed && !width.is_length() {
                // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#width-distribution-in-fixed-mode
                // "The min-content width of percent-columns and auto-columns is considered to be zero": a cell without a
                // length width contributes nothing to its column in fixed mode, not even its padding and borders, so
                // that "any remaining columns equally divide the remaining horizontal table space" (CSS 2 §17.5.2.1)
                // and the table keeps its specified width.
                // AD-HOC: The same section says percentage cells ignore their border and padding, but Blink and Gecko
                //         add the cell intrinsic offsets of a content-box percentage cell to its resolved percentage
                //         (CSS 2.1's fixed-table-layout-025..031 expect that). The offsets are kept as the outer sizes
                //         of such a cell and become the column's percentage_offsets in initialize_intrinsic_percentages.
                let outer = if width.percentage_fraction().is_some() && style.box_sizing() != box_sizing::BORDER_BOX {
                    inline_offsets
                } else {
                    CssPixels::default()
                };
                self.cells[cell_index].outer_min_inline_size = outer;
                self.cells[cell_index].outer_max_inline_size = outer;
                continue;
            }

            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#computing-column-measures
            // For the purpose of measuring a column when laid out in fixed mode [...] the min-content and max-content width
            // of cells is considered zero unless they are directly specified as a length-percentage, in which case they are
            // resolved based on the table width (if it is definite, otherwise use 0).
            let (min_content_inline, max_content_inline) = if fixed {
                (inline_size, inline_size)
            } else {
                let content_sizes = self
                    .sizing()
                    .content_inline_sizes(self.sized_cell(cell_index), self.participant_constraints, None)
                    .sizes;
                (content_sizes.min, content_sizes.max)
            };
            // The outer min-content inline size of a table cell is its minimum inline size adjusted by the cell intrinsic offsets.
            // AD-HOC: The spec's max(min-width, min-content width) lets the min-content width override a definite max-width,
            //         so a cell whose content can't wrap widens its column past its max-width, where pages expect the cell
            //         to cut that content off. So cap the min-content width at the max-width; min-width still wins over both.
            let capped_min_content_inline = min_content_inline.min(max_inline);
            self.cells[cell_index].outer_min_inline_size = min_inline.max(capped_min_content_inline) + inline_offsets;
            self.cells[cell_index].max_content_inline_size = (!fixed).then_some(max_content_inline);

            // See the explanation for block_size and max_block_size above.
            self.cells[cell_index].outer_max_inline_size = if self.columns[cell.column_index].is_constrained {
                // The outer max-content width of a table-cell in a constrained column is
                // max(min-width, width, min-content width, min(max-width, width)) adjusted by the cell intrinsic offsets.

                // AD-HOC: The formula defined by the spec doesn't respect max-width. We use a different formula that
                //         matches the behavior that is expected by WPT and is implemented by other browsers.
                // FIXME: Open a spec issue about this.
                css_clamp(inline_size.max(min_content_inline), min_inline, max_inline) + inline_offsets
            } else {
                // The outer max-content width of a table-cell in a non-constrained column is
                // max(min-width, width, min-content width, min(max-width, max-content width)) adjusted by the cell intrinsic offsets.
                // AD-HOC: With the min-content width capped at a definite max-width, as for the outer min-content width.
                min_inline.max(inline_size.max(capped_min_content_inline.max(max_inline.min(max_content_inline))))
                    + inline_offsets
            };
        }
    }

    fn initialize_row_content_sizes(&mut self) {
        // NB: A row's percentage block sizes resolve against the table's block size, which an auto-height table doesn't
        //     have yet, so they count as 0px there: "the computed height (if definite, percentages being considered 0px)"
        //     https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#computing-the-table-height
        let basis = if self.table_block_size_is_auto() {
            CssPixels::default()
        } else {
            self.table_constraints.block_basis()
        };
        for row_index in 0..self.rows.len() {
            let style = self.style(self.rows[row_index].box_);
            let min_size = style.min_height().to_px(basis);
            let max_size = if style.max_height().is_length() {
                style.max_height().to_px(basis)
            } else {
                CssPixels::from_raw(i32::MAX)
            };
            // NB: A percentage block size counts as 0px here, as the specification says above, and is applied when
            //     the table block size is distributed to the rows (see distribute_block_size_to_rows).
            let size = if style.height().contains_percentage() {
                CssPixels::default()
            } else {
                style.height().to_px(basis)
            };
            // The outer min-content block size of a table row or row group is max(min-block-size, block-size).
            self.rows[row_index].min_size = min_size.max(size);
            // The outer max-content block size is max(min-block-size, min(max-block-size, block-size)).
            self.rows[row_index].max_size = min_size.max(max_size.min(size));
        }
    }

    fn compute_outer_content_sizes(&mut self) {
        let basis = self.table_constraints.inline_basis();
        // Only lengths take part in the outer sizes of a column. A percentage width or max-width is the column's
        // percentage contribution (https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#percentage-contribution) and is resolved
        // against the assignable table inline size during distribution, not against the containing block.
        let outer_sizes = |style: StyleValues<'_>| {
            let length_or_zero = |size: &ComputedSize| {
                if size.is_length() {
                    size.to_px(basis)
                } else {
                    CssPixels::default()
                }
            };
            let min_size = length_or_zero(style.min_width());
            let max_size = if style.max_width().is_length() {
                style.max_width().to_px(basis)
            } else {
                CssPixels::from_raw(i32::MAX)
            };
            let size = length_or_zero(style.width());
            // The outer min-content width of a table-column or table-column-group is max('min-width', 'width').
            // The outer max-content width of a table-column or table-column-group is
            // max('min-width', min('max-width', 'width')).
            (min_size.max(size), min_size.max(max_size.min(size)))
        };
        for &range in &self.column_track_ranges {
            let (min_size, max_size) = outer_sizes(self.style(self.column_sizing_box(range)));
            for index in range.start..range.end {
                self.columns[index].min_size = min_size;
                self.columns[index].max_size = max_size;
            }
        }
        self.initialize_row_content_sizes();
    }

    // Accessors to enable direction-agnostic table measurement.

    fn track_count(&self, axis: TrackAxis) -> usize {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => self.rows.len(),
            TrackAxis::Column => self.columns.len(),
        }
    }

    fn track_min(&self, axis: TrackAxis, index: usize) -> CssPixels {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => self.rows[index].min_size,
            TrackAxis::Column => self.columns[index].min_size,
        }
    }

    fn set_track_min(&mut self, axis: TrackAxis, index: usize, value: CssPixels) {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => self.rows[index].min_size = value,
            TrackAxis::Column => self.columns[index].min_size = value,
        }
    }

    fn track_max(&self, axis: TrackAxis, index: usize) -> CssPixels {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => self.rows[index].max_size,
            TrackAxis::Column => self.columns[index].max_size,
        }
    }

    fn set_track_max(&mut self, axis: TrackAxis, index: usize, value: CssPixels) {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => self.rows[index].max_size = value,
            TrackAxis::Column => self.columns[index].max_size = value,
        }
    }

    fn track_percentage(&self, axis: TrackAxis, index: usize) -> f64 {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => self.rows[index].intrinsic_percentage,
            TrackAxis::Column => self.columns[index].intrinsic_percentage,
        }
    }

    fn set_track_percentage(&mut self, axis: TrackAxis, index: usize, value: f64) {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => self.rows[index].intrinsic_percentage = value,
            TrackAxis::Column => self.columns[index].intrinsic_percentage = value,
        }
    }

    fn set_track_has_percentage(&mut self, axis: TrackAxis, index: usize, value: bool) {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => self.rows[index].has_intrinsic_percentage = value,
            TrackAxis::Column => self.columns[index].has_intrinsic_percentage = value,
        }
    }

    fn cell_span(cell: TableCell, axis: TrackAxis) -> usize {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => cell.row_span,
            TrackAxis::Column => cell.column_span,
        }
    }

    fn cell_index(cell: TableCell, axis: TrackAxis) -> usize {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => cell.row_index,
            TrackAxis::Column => cell.column_index,
        }
    }

    fn cell_min(cell: TableCell, axis: TrackAxis) -> CssPixels {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => cell.outer_min_block_size,
            TrackAxis::Column => cell.outer_min_inline_size,
        }
    }

    fn cell_max(cell: TableCell, axis: TrackAxis) -> CssPixels {
        match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => cell.outer_max_block_size,
            TrackAxis::Column => cell.outer_max_inline_size,
        }
    }

    fn cell_percentage(style: StyleValues, axis: TrackAxis) -> f64 {
        // Definition of percentage contribution: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#percentage-contribution
        let (size, max_size) = match axis {
            TrackAxis::Row => (style.height(), style.max_height()),
            TrackAxis::Column => (style.width(), style.max_width()),
        };
        // NB: A calculation that simplified to a percentage, like calc(10% + 15%), is that percentage.
        let maximum = max_size
            .percentage_fraction()
            .map_or(f64::INFINITY, |fraction| fraction * 100.0);
        let preferred = size.percentage_fraction().map_or(0.0, |fraction| fraction * 100.0);
        preferred.min(maximum)
    }

    fn initialize_intrinsic_percentages(&mut self, axis: TrackAxis) {
        if axis == TrackAxis::Row {
            for index in 0..self.rows.len() {
                let style = self.style(self.rows[index].box_);
                // Definition of percentage contribution: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#percentage-contribution
                self.rows[index].has_intrinsic_percentage = style.max_height().percentage_fraction().is_some()
                    || style.height().percentage_fraction().is_some();
                self.rows[index].intrinsic_percentage = Self::cell_percentage(style, axis);
            }
        } else {
            for &range in &self.column_track_ranges {
                let style = self.style(self.column_sizing_box(range));
                // Definition of percentage contribution: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#percentage-contribution
                let has_intrinsic_percentage =
                    style.max_width().percentage_fraction().is_some() || style.width().percentage_fraction().is_some();
                let intrinsic_percentage = Self::cell_percentage(style, axis);
                for index in range.start..range.end {
                    self.columns[index].has_intrinsic_percentage = has_intrinsic_percentage;
                    self.columns[index].intrinsic_percentage = intrinsic_percentage;
                }
            }
        }

        let fixed = self.use_fixed_mode_layout();
        for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
            let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
            if !self.cell_is_measured(cell, axis) {
                continue;
            }
            let style = self.style(cell.box_);
            let size = match axis {
                TrackAxis::Row => style.height(),
                TrackAxis::Column => style.width(),
            };
            if size.percentage_fraction().is_none() {
                continue;
            }
            let start = Self::cell_index(cell, axis);
            let span = Self::cell_span(cell, axis);
            for index in start..start + span {
                self.set_track_has_percentage(axis, index, true);
            }
            if span == 1 {
                let percentage = Self::cell_percentage(style, axis);
                if percentage >= self.track_percentage(axis, start) {
                    self.set_track_percentage(axis, start, percentage);
                    if axis == TrackAxis::Column && fixed {
                        // The outer sizes of a percentage cell in fixed mode are its offsets (see compute_cell_measures).
                        self.columns[start].percentage_offsets = cell.outer_min_inline_size;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn compute_intrinsic_percentage(&mut self, axis: TrackAxis, max_span: usize) {
        // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#intrinsic-percentage-width-of-a-column-based-on-cells-of-span-up-to-1
        self.initialize_intrinsic_percentages(axis);
        let count = self.track_count(axis);
        // Stores intermediate values for intrinsic percentage based on cells of span up to N for the iterative algorithm, to store them back at the end of the step.
        let mut contributions = (0..count)
            .map(|index| self.track_percentage(axis, index))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        for current_span in 2..=max_span {
            // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#intrinsic-percentage-width-of-a-column-based-on-cells-of-span-up-to-n-n--1
            for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
                let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
                if Self::cell_span(cell, axis) != current_span || !self.cell_is_measured(cell, axis) {
                    continue;
                }
                let style = self.style(cell.box_);
                let start = Self::cell_index(cell, axis);
                let end = start + current_span;
                // 1. Start with the percentage contribution of the cell.
                let mut contribution = CssPixels::nearest_value_for(Self::cell_percentage(style, axis));
                // 2. Subtract the intrinsic percentage width of the column based on cells of span up to N-1 of all columns
                //    that the cell spans. If this gives a negative result, change it to 0%.
                for index in start..end {
                    contribution -= CssPixels::nearest_value_for(self.track_percentage(axis, index));
                    contribution = contribution.max(CssPixels::default());
                }
                // Compute the sum of the non-spanning max-content sizes of all rows / columns spanned by the cell that have an intrinsic percentage
                // size of the row / column based on cells of span up to N-1 equal to 0%, to be used in step 3 of the cell contribution algorithm.
                let mut zero_sum = CssPixels::default();
                let mut zero_count = 0usize;
                for index in start..end {
                    if self.track_percentage(axis, index) == 0.0 {
                        zero_sum += self.track_max(axis, index);
                        zero_count += 1;
                    }
                }
                for (index, saved) in contributions.iter_mut().enumerate().take(end).skip(start) {
                    // If the intrinsic percentage width of a column based on cells of span up to N-1 is greater than 0%, then the intrinsic percentage width of
                    // the column based on cells of span up to N is the same as the intrinsic percentage width of the column based on cells of span up to N-1.
                    if self.track_percentage(axis, index) > 0.0 {
                        continue;
                    }
                    // Otherwise, it is the largest of the contributions of the cells in the column whose colSpan is N,
                    // where the contribution of a cell is the result of taking the following steps:
                    // 1. Start with the percentage contribution of the cell.
                    // 2. Subtract the intrinsic percentage width of the column based on cells of span up to N-1 of all columns
                    //    that the cell spans. If this gives a negative result, change it to 0%.
                    // 3. Multiply by the ratio of the column’s non-spanning max-content width to the sum of the non-spanning max-content widths of all
                    //    columns spanned by the cell that have an intrinsic percentage width of the column based on cells of span up to N-1 equal to 0%.
                    let adjusted = if zero_sum != CssPixels::default() {
                        contribution.scaled(self.track_max(axis, index).to_double() / zero_sum.to_double())
                    } else {
                        // However, if this ratio is undefined because the denominator is zero, instead use the 1 divided by the number of columns
                        // spanned by the cell that have an intrinsic percentage width of the column based on cells of span up to N-1 equal to zero.
                        contribution / zero_count
                    };
                    *saved = saved.max(adjusted.to_double());
                }
            }
            for (index, value) in contributions.iter().copied().enumerate() {
                self.set_track_percentage(axis, index, value);
            }
        }
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#width-distribution-in-fixed-mode
        // If, when percentages are resolved based on the assignable table width, the sum of columns widths based on this
        // resolution would exceed the assignable table width, they are instead to be resolved relative to their
        // percentage value such that the sum of columns width meets the assignable table width exactly.
        if axis == TrackAxis::Column && self.use_fixed_mode_layout() {
            let sum: f64 = (0..count).map(|index| self.track_percentage(axis, index)).sum();
            if sum > 100.0 {
                for index in 0..count {
                    let value = self.track_percentage(axis, index) * 100.0 / sum;
                    self.set_track_percentage(axis, index, value);
                }
            }
            return;
        }
        // Clamp total intrinsic percentage to 100%: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#intrinsic-percentage-width-of-a-column
        let mut total = 0.0;
        for index in 0..count {
            let value = self.track_percentage(axis, index).min(100.0 - total).max(0.0);
            self.set_track_percentage(axis, index, value);
            total += value;
        }
    }

    fn initialize_table_measures(&mut self, axis: TrackAxis) {
        if axis == TrackAxis::Row {
            for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
                let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
                if cell.row_span == 1 {
                    // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#row-layout makes specified cell height part of the initialization formula for row table measures:
                    // This is done by running the same algorithm as the column measurement, with the span=1 value being initialized (for min-content) with
                    // the largest of the resulting height of the previous row layout, the height specified on the corresponding table-row (if any), and
                    // the largest height specified on cells that span this row only (the algorithm starts by considering cells of span 2 on top of that assignment).
                    // The row measures are outer sizes, so the specified height counts with the cell's padding and
                    // borders (the cell's outer minimum has it, see compute_table_block_size).
                    let row = &mut self.rows[cell.row_index];
                    row.min_size = row.min_size.max(cell.outer_min_block_size);
                    row.max_size = row.max_size.max(cell.outer_max_block_size);
                }
            }
        } else {
            // Implement the following parts of the specification, accounting for fixed layout mode:
            // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#min-content-width-of-a-column-based-on-cells-of-span-up-to-1
            // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#max-content-width-of-a-column-based-on-cells-of-span-up-to-1
            for &cell in &self.cells {
                if cell.column_span == 1 && self.cell_is_measured(cell, axis) {
                    let column = &mut self.columns[cell.column_index];
                    column.min_size = column.min_size.max(cell.outer_min_inline_size);
                    column.max_size = column.max_size.max(cell.outer_max_inline_size);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn compute_table_measures(&mut self, axis: TrackAxis) {
        self.initialize_table_measures(axis);
        let max_span = self
            .cells
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .map(|cell| Self::cell_span(cell, axis))
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(1)
            .max(1);
        // Since the intrinsic percentage specification uses non-spanning max-content size for the iterative algorithm,
        // run it before we compute the spanning max-content size with its own iterative algorithm for span up to N.
        self.compute_intrinsic_percentage(axis, max_span);
        let track_count = self.track_count(axis);
        for current_span in 2..=max_span {
            // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#min-content-width-of-a-column-based-on-cells-of-span-up-to-n-n--1
            let mut min_contributions = (0..track_count)
                .map(|index| self.track_min(axis, index))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
            // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#max-content-width-of-a-column-based-on-cells-of-span-up-to-n-n--1
            let mut max_contributions = (0..track_count)
                .map(|index| self.track_max(axis, index))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
            let track_spacing = match axis {
                TrackAxis::Row => self.border_spacing_block(),
                TrackAxis::Column => self.border_spacing_inline(),
            };
            for &cell in &self.cells {
                if Self::cell_span(cell, axis) != current_span || !self.cell_is_measured(cell, axis) {
                    continue;
                }
                let start = Self::cell_index(cell, axis);
                let end = start + current_span;
                // Define the baseline max-content size as the sum of the max-content sizes based on cells of span up to N-1 of all columns that the cell spans.
                let baseline_max =
                    (start..end).fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, index| sum + self.track_max(axis, index));
                let baseline_min =
                    (start..end).fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, index| sum + self.track_min(axis, index));
                // Define the baseline border spacing as the sum of the horizontal border-spacing for any columns spanned by the cell, other than the one in which the cell originates.
                let spacing = track_spacing * (current_span - 1);
                // AD-HOC: The spec gives what the cell needs beyond the baseline max-content size to all the columns it
                //         spans, in proportion to their max-content sizes. Other browsers give it to the spanned columns
                //         that aren't constrained, and give a constrained column only what it needs itself, unless all
                //         the spanned columns are constrained.
                let unconstrained_tracks = (start..end)
                    .filter(|&index| axis == TrackAxis::Column && !self.columns[index].is_constrained)
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
                let growing_tracks = if unconstrained_tracks.is_empty() {
                    (start..end).collect::<Vec<_>>()
                } else {
                    unconstrained_tracks
                };
                let growing_max = growing_tracks
                    .iter()
                    .fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, &index| sum + self.track_max(axis, index));
                // Each growing track takes its share of what the cell needs beyond the baseline max-content size, in
                // proportion to its max-content size. The shares are the differences between the rounded running totals
                // of those proportions, so that they always add up to all of it, however many tracks share it.
                // AD-HOC: The spec does not define behavior when baseline is zero. We distribute equally.
                //         This matches how undefined ratios are handled elsewhere.
                let mut growing_fractions_before = Vec::with_capacity(growing_tracks.len() + 1);
                growing_fractions_before.push(0.0);
                let mut fraction_so_far = 0.0;
                for &index in &growing_tracks {
                    fraction_so_far += if growing_max != CssPixels::default() {
                        self.track_max(axis, index).to_double() / growing_max.to_double()
                    } else {
                        1.0 / growing_tracks.len() as f64
                    };
                    growing_fractions_before.push(fraction_so_far);
                }
                let share_beyond_max = |index: usize, beyond_max: CssPixels| {
                    let Ok(position) = growing_tracks.binary_search(&index) else {
                        return CssPixels::default();
                    };
                    let running_total = |fraction: f64| CssPixels::nearest_value_for(fraction * beyond_max.to_double());
                    running_total(growing_fractions_before[position + 1])
                        - running_total(growing_fractions_before[position])
                };
                // Add contribution from all rows / columns, since we've weighted the gap to the desired spanned size by the the
                // ratio of the max-content size based on cells of span up to N-1 of the row / column to the baseline max-content width.
                for index in start..end {
                    // The contribution of the cell is the sum of:
                    // the min-content size of the column based on cells of span up to N-1
                    let mut min_contribution = self.track_min(axis, index);
                    // the product of:
                    // - the ratio of:
                    //   - the max-content size of the row / column based on cells of span up to N-1 of the row / column minus the
                    //     min-content size of the row / column based on cells of span up to N-1 of the row / column, to
                    //   - the baseline max-content size minus the baseline min-content size
                    //   or zero if this ratio is undefined, and
                    // - the outer min-content size of the cell minus the baseline min-content size and the baseline border spacing, clamped
                    //   to be at least 0 and at most the difference between the baseline max-content size and the baseline min-content size
                    let normalized = if baseline_max != baseline_min {
                        (self.track_max(axis, index) - self.track_min(axis, index)).to_double()
                            / (baseline_max - baseline_min).to_double()
                    } else {
                        0.0
                    };
                    let clamped = (Self::cell_min(cell, axis) - baseline_min - spacing)
                        .max(CssPixels::default())
                        .min(baseline_max - baseline_min);
                    min_contribution += CssPixels::nearest_value_for(normalized * clamped.to_double());
                    // the product of:
                    // - the ratio of the max-content size based on cells of span up to N-1 of the column to the baseline max-content size
                    // - the outer min-content size of the cell minus the baseline max-content size and baseline border spacing, or 0 if this is negative
                    min_contribution += share_beyond_max(
                        index,
                        (Self::cell_min(cell, axis) - baseline_max - spacing).max(CssPixels::default()),
                    );

                    // The contribution of the cell is the sum of:
                    // the max-content size of the column based on cells of span up to N-1
                    let mut max_contribution = self.track_max(axis, index);
                    // and the product of:
                    // - the ratio of the max-content size based on cells of span up to N-1 of the column to the baseline max-content size
                    // - the outer max-content size of the cell minus the baseline max-content size and the baseline border spacing, or 0 if this is negative
                    max_contribution += share_beyond_max(
                        index,
                        (Self::cell_max(cell, axis) - baseline_max - spacing).max(CssPixels::default()),
                    );
                    min_contributions[index] = min_contributions[index].max(min_contribution);
                    max_contributions[index] = max_contributions[index].max(max_contribution);
                }
            }
            for index in 0..track_count {
                // min-content size of a row / column based on cells of span up to N (N > 1) is
                // the largest of the min-content size of the row / column based on cells of span up to N-1 and
                // the contributions of the cells in the row / column whose rowSpan / colSpan is N
                self.set_track_min(axis, index, min_contributions[index]);
                // max-content size of a row / column based on cells of span up to N (N > 1) is
                // the largest of the max-content size based on cells of span up to N-1 and the contributions of
                // the cells in the row / column whose rowSpan / colSpan is N
                self.set_track_max(axis, index, max_contributions[index]);
            }
        }
    }

    fn compute_capmin(&mut self) -> CssPixels {
        // The caption width minimum (CAPMIN) is the largest of the table captions min-content contribution:
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#computing-the-table-width
        let basis = self.table_constraints.inline_basis();
        let mut capmin = CssPixels::default();
        for caption in self.matching_children(self.run.box_, |facts| facts.is_table_caption()) {
            let style = self.style(caption);
            let outer = |inner: CssPixels| {
                inner
                    + style.margin_left().to_px(basis)
                    + style.border_left_width()
                    + style.padding_left().to_px(basis)
                    + style.padding_right().to_px(basis)
                    + style.border_right_width()
                    + style.margin_right().to_px(basis)
            };
            let mut contribution = outer(self.calculate_min_content_inline_size_of_caption(caption));
            let width = style.width();
            if width.is_length_percentage() && !width.contains_percentage() {
                let mut preferred = width.to_px(basis);
                if style.box_sizing() == box_sizing::BORDER_BOX {
                    preferred = formatting_context::subtract_border_box_adjustment(
                        preferred,
                        style.border_left_width(),
                        style.padding_left().to_px(basis),
                        style.border_right_width(),
                        style.padding_right().to_px(basis),
                    );
                }
                contribution = contribution.max(outer(preferred));
            } else if width.is_max_content() {
                contribution = contribution.max(outer(self.calculate_max_content_inline_size_of_caption(caption)));
            }
            capmin = capmin.max(contribution);
        }
        capmin
    }

    /// The content inline size a calc-size() with a sizing keyword basis resolves to, given the content size of that
    /// keyword, or that size for a plain keyword. As for other boxes, the size is that of the box the box-sizing
    /// property names.
    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#resolving-calc-size
    fn resolve_calc_size_of_keyword(
        &self,
        size: &ComputedSize,
        keyword_size: CssPixels,
        basis: CssPixels,
    ) -> CssPixels {
        let Some(calc_size) = size.calc_size() else {
            return keyword_size;
        };
        let edges = if self.style(self.run.box_).box_sizing() == box_sizing::BORDER_BOX {
            let used = &self.table_box_cells;
            let collapsed = used.uses_collapsing_borders_model();
            used.border_box_left(collapsed) + used.border_box_right(collapsed)
        } else {
            CssPixels::default()
        };
        let resolved = crate::css::calc_size::resolve_calc_size(calc_size, Some(basis.to_double()), &|_| {
            (keyword_size + edges).to_double()
        });
        resolved.map_or(keyword_size, |resolved| {
            (CssPixels::nearest_value_for(resolved) - edges).max(CssPixels::default())
        })
    }

    fn resolve_inline_constraint(
        &mut self,
        constraint: &ComputedSize,
        grid_min: CssPixels,
        grid_max: CssPixels,
        basis: CssPixels,
    ) -> CssPixels {
        if constraint.is_min_content() {
            return self.resolve_calc_size_of_keyword(constraint, grid_min, basis);
        }
        if constraint.is_max_content() {
            return self.resolve_calc_size_of_keyword(constraint, grid_max, basis);
        }
        if constraint.is_fit_content() {
            let limit = if constraint.fit_content_available_space().is_some() {
                constraint.to_px(basis)
            } else {
                basis
            };
            return self.resolve_calc_size_of_keyword(constraint, grid_max.min(grid_min.max(limit)), basis);
        }
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-3/#stretch-fit-sizing
        // NB: The table wrapper box carries the margins, so a stretch size fills the basis with the table's border box.
        if constraint.is_stretch() {
            let used = &self.table_box_cells;
            let collapsed = used.uses_collapsing_borders_model();
            let stretch_fit_size =
                (basis - used.border_box_left(collapsed) - used.border_box_right(collapsed)).max(CssPixels::default());
            return self.resolve_calc_size_of_keyword(constraint, stretch_fit_size, basis);
        }
        // CSS Sizing says box-sizing:border-box applies length/percentage width/min-width/max-width constraints to
        // the border box. The table inline-size algorithm compares content inline sizes, so convert them before comparing.
        let mut resolved = constraint.to_px(basis);
        if self.style(self.run.box_).box_sizing() == box_sizing::BORDER_BOX {
            let used = &self.table_box_cells;
            let collapsed = used.uses_collapsing_borders_model();
            resolved -= used.border_box_left(collapsed) + used.border_box_right(collapsed);
        }
        resolved.max(CssPixels::default())
    }

    fn should_treat_max_inline_size_as_none(&self, available: AvailableSize) -> bool {
        self.sizing()
            .should_treat_max_inline_size_as_none(self.run.box_, available, self.table_constraints)
    }

    fn table_inline_size_measures(&mut self) -> TableInlineSizeMeasures {
        // Compute undistributable space due to border spacing: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#computing-undistributable-space.
        let spacing = (self.columns.len() + 1) * self.border_spacing_inline();
        // The row/column-grid inline-size minimum (GRIDMIN) is the sum of the min-content inline size
        // of all the columns plus cell spacing or borders.
        let grid_min = self
            .columns
            .iter()
            .fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, column| sum + column.min_size)
            + spacing;
        // The row/column-grid inline-size maximum (GRIDMAX) is the sum of the max-content inline size
        // of all the columns plus cell spacing or borders.
        let grid_max = self
            .columns
            .iter()
            .fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, column| sum + column.max_size)
            + spacing;
        let capmin = self.compute_capmin();
        TableInlineSizeMeasures {
            spacing,
            grid_min,
            grid_max,
            capmin,
        }
    }

    fn used_table_inline_size(
        &mut self,
        available_inline: AvailableSize,
        measures: TableInlineSizeMeasures,
    ) -> CssPixels {
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#computing-the-table-width

        let TableInlineSizeMeasures {
            spacing,
            grid_min,
            grid_max,
            capmin,
        } = measures;
        let table_style = self.style(self.run.box_);
        // INTEROP: A table laid out in fixed mode with a percentage width fills whatever inline size its container
        //          offers, so it has an infinite max-content inline size, capped at a large value.
        const TABLE_MAX_INLINE_SIZE: i64 = 1_000_000;
        let max_content_inline_size = if self.use_fixed_mode_layout()
            && table_style.width().is_length_percentage()
            && table_style.width().contains_percentage()
        {
            CssPixels::from_integer(TABLE_MAX_INLINE_SIZE)
        } else {
            grid_max
        };
        // Percentages on 'width' and 'height' on the table are relative to the table wrapper box's containing block,
        // not the table wrapper box itself.
        let basis = self.table_constraints.inline_basis();
        // The used minimum inline size of a table is the greater of the resolved min-width, CAPMIN, and GRIDMIN.
        let mut used_min = grid_min.max(capmin);
        if !crate::layout::sizing_context::is_plain_auto(table_style.min_width()) {
            used_min = used_min.max(self.resolve_inline_constraint(table_style.min_width(), grid_min, grid_max, basis));
        }
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox-1/#flex-items
        // "[...] like width and height, the flex longhands apply to the table box as follows: the flex item's final
        // size is calculated by performing layout as if the distance between the table wrapper box's edges and the
        // table box's content edges were all part of the table box's border+padding area, and the table box were the
        // flex item."
        // NB: So once the flex container sizes the wrapper along the table's inline axis, the table fills that size,
        //     and its specified inline size only takes part in the flex base size, through the max-content inline size.
        //     The min-content inline size, which the automatic minimum size of the item comes from, ignores it.
        let width_is_flexed = self.forced_border_box_inline_size.is_some()
            || (available_inline == AvailableSize::MinContent && self.wrapper_is_flex_item_along_inline_axis());
        let width_is_auto_or_indefinite_percentage = width_is_flexed
            || table_style.width().is_auto()
            || (table_style.width().contains_percentage()
                && self.table_constraints.percentage_basis_inline_size.is_none());
        let mut used = if width_is_auto_or_indefinite_percentage {
            // If the table-root has 'width: auto', the used inline size is the greater of
            // min(GRIDMAX, the table’s containing block inline size), the used minimum inline size of the table.
            // NOTE: In normal layout the available inline size already is the wrapper's used inline size, which the
            //       parent context resolved with shrink-to-fit; filling it keeps the table and its
            //       wrapper consistent without reading the wrapper's state from here.
            let mut value = match available_inline {
                AvailableSize::MinContent => grid_min,
                AvailableSize::MaxContent => max_content_inline_size,
                AvailableSize::Definite(available)
                    if self.auto_table_inline_size == AutoTableInlineSize::FillsAvailableInlineSize =>
                {
                    available.max(used_min)
                }
                AvailableSize::Definite(available) => max_content_inline_size.min(available).max(used_min),
                AvailableSize::Indefinite => grid_max.max(used_min),
            };
            if !matches!(available_inline, AvailableSize::MinContent | AvailableSize::MaxContent) {
                // https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#auto-table-layout
                // A percentage value for a column inline size is relative to the table inline size. If the table has
                // 'width: auto', a percentage represents a constraint on the column's inline size, which a UA should try to satisfy.
                for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
                    let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
                    let cell_width = self.style(cell.box_).width();
                    if let Some(fraction) = cell_width.percentage_fraction() {
                        let mut adjusted = spacing;
                        let percentage = fraction * 100.0;
                        if percentage != 0.0 {
                            adjusted += CssPixels::nearest_value_for(
                                (100.0 / percentage * cell.outer_max_inline_size.to_double()).ceil(),
                            );
                        }
                        value = if let AvailableSize::Definite(available) = available_inline {
                            value.max(adjusted).min(available)
                        } else {
                            value.max(adjusted)
                        };
                    }
                }
                // AD-HOC: Whatever the percentage columns take of the table, the other columns have the rest for their
                //         max-content sizes, so the table grows until they fit in it. Once the percentages reach 100%,
                //         nothing is left for them, so the table fills its container. Other browsers do the same.
                let percentage_sum = self
                    .columns
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|column| column.has_intrinsic_percentage)
                    .map(|column| column.intrinsic_percentage)
                    .sum::<f64>()
                    .min(100.0);
                let non_percentage_max = self
                    .columns
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|column| !column.has_intrinsic_percentage)
                    .fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, column| sum + column.max_size);
                if percentage_sum > 0.0 && non_percentage_max > CssPixels::default() {
                    if percentage_sum < 100.0 {
                        let needed = spacing
                            + CssPixels::nearest_value_for(
                                non_percentage_max.to_double() * 100.0 / (100.0 - percentage_sum),
                            );
                        value = match available_inline {
                            AvailableSize::Definite(available) => value.max(needed).min(available),
                            _ => value.max(needed),
                        };
                    } else if let AvailableSize::Definite(available) = available_inline {
                        value = value.max(available);
                    }
                }
            }
            value
        } else if table_style.width().is_max_content() {
            self.resolve_calc_size_of_keyword(table_style.width(), grid_max, basis)
        } else {
            // If the table-root’s width property has a computed value (resolving to the table inline size) other than auto,
            // the used inline size is the greater of the resolved table inline size and the used minimum inline size.
            let mut value = self
                .resolve_inline_constraint(table_style.width(), grid_min, grid_max, basis)
                .max(used_min);
            if !self.should_treat_max_inline_size_as_none(available_inline) {
                value = value.min(self.resolve_inline_constraint(table_style.max_width(), grid_min, grid_max, basis));
            }
            value
        };
        if !self.should_treat_max_inline_size_as_none(available_inline) {
            used = used.min(self.resolve_inline_constraint(table_style.max_width(), grid_min, grid_max, basis));
        }
        used.max(used_min)
    }

    /// Whether the table wrapper is a flex item whose main axis is the inline axis of the table.
    fn wrapper_is_flex_item_along_inline_axis(&self) -> bool {
        let wrapper = self.parent(self.run.box_);
        if wrapper.is_invalid()
            || !self.node_facts(wrapper).is_table_wrapper()
            || self.node_facts(wrapper).is_absolutely_positioned()
        {
            return false;
        }
        let container = self.parent(wrapper);
        if container.is_invalid() {
            return false;
        }
        let container_style = self.style(container);
        if !container_style.display().is_flex_inside()
            && container_style.display().inside != display_inside::_WEBKIT_BOX
        {
            return false;
        }
        let is_row_layout = matches!(
            container_style.effective_flex_direction(),
            flex_direction::ROW | flex_direction::ROW_REVERSE
        );
        let table_is_orthogonal = geometry::Frame::of(self.style(self.run.box_).writing_mode())
            .is_orthogonal_to(geometry::Frame::of(container_style.writing_mode()));
        is_row_layout != table_is_orthogonal
    }

    fn compute_table_inline_size(&mut self) {
        let measures = self.table_inline_size_measures();
        let available = if let Some(forced) = self.forced_border_box_inline_size {
            let used = &self.table_box_cells;
            let collapsed = used.uses_collapsing_borders_model();
            AvailableSize::definite(
                (forced - used.border_box_left(collapsed) - used.border_box_right(collapsed)).max(CssPixels::default()),
            )
        } else {
            self.available_space.inline_size
        };
        let used = self.used_table_inline_size(available, measures);
        self.table_box_cells.set_content_inline_size(used);
    }

    fn can_skip_row_intrinsic_measurement(&mut self) -> bool {
        for row_index in 0..self.rows.len() {
            if self.rows[row_index].is_collapsed {
                return false;
            }
            let style = self.style(self.rows[row_index].box_);
            if !style.height().is_auto()
                || !crate::layout::sizing_context::is_plain_auto(style.min_height())
                || !style.max_height().is_none()
            {
                return false;
            }
        }
        for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
            let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
            if cell.row_span != 1 {
                return false;
            }
            let style = self.style(cell.box_);
            if !style.height().is_auto()
                || !crate::layout::sizing_context::is_plain_auto(style.min_height())
                || !style.max_height().is_none()
            {
                return false;
            }
        }
        true
    }

    pub(super) fn run_until_inline_size_calculation(&mut self, input: LayoutInput, skip_row_measurement: bool) {
        self.measure_tracks(input, skip_row_measurement);
        // Compute the inline size of the table.
        self.compute_table_inline_size();
    }

    fn measures_for_intrinsic_inline_sizes(&mut self, input: LayoutInput) -> TableInlineSizeMeasures {
        self.measure_tracks(
            LayoutInput {
                available_space: AvailableSpace {
                    inline_size: AvailableSize::MaxContent,
                    ..input.available_space
                },
                ..input
            },
            true,
        );
        self.table_inline_size_measures()
    }

    pub(super) fn content_inline_sizes(&mut self, input: LayoutInput) -> sizing_context::ContentSizes {
        let measures = self.measures_for_intrinsic_inline_sizes(input);
        sizing_context::ContentSizes {
            min: self.used_table_inline_size(AvailableSize::MinContent, measures),
            max: self.used_table_inline_size(AvailableSize::MaxContent, measures),
        }
    }

    fn max_inline_size_fits_content_to_unknown_containing_block_inline_size(&self) -> bool {
        let max_inline_size = self.style(self.run.box_).max_width();
        self.table_constraints.percentage_basis_inline_size.is_none()
            && max_inline_size.is_fit_content()
            && max_inline_size.fit_content_available_space().is_none()
    }

    fn used_table_inline_size_when_laid_out_at_intrinsic_inline_size(
        &mut self,
        intrinsic_sizing_constraint: AvailableSize,
        measures: TableInlineSizeMeasures,
    ) -> CssPixels {
        let intrinsic_inline_size = self.used_table_inline_size(intrinsic_sizing_constraint, measures);
        // NB: The specified inline size of a flexed table takes no part in its min-content inline size (see
        //     used_table_inline_size).
        let min_content_ignores_specified_inline_size =
            intrinsic_sizing_constraint == AvailableSize::MinContent && self.wrapper_is_flex_item_along_inline_axis();
        if min_content_ignores_specified_inline_size
            || self.max_inline_size_fits_content_to_unknown_containing_block_inline_size()
        {
            return intrinsic_inline_size;
        }
        self.used_table_inline_size(AvailableSize::Definite(intrinsic_inline_size), measures)
    }

    pub(super) fn border_box_inline_sizes(&mut self, input: LayoutInput) -> sizing_context::ContentSizes {
        let measures = self.measures_for_intrinsic_inline_sizes(input);
        let content_box_inline_sizes = sizing_context::ContentSizes {
            min: self
                .used_table_inline_size_when_laid_out_at_intrinsic_inline_size(AvailableSize::MinContent, measures),
            max: self
                .used_table_inline_size_when_laid_out_at_intrinsic_inline_size(AvailableSize::MaxContent, measures),
        };
        let table_used = &self.table_box_cells;
        let collapsed = table_used.uses_collapsing_borders_model();
        let border_box_inline_size = |content_inline_size: CssPixels| {
            table_used.border_box_left(collapsed) + content_inline_size + table_used.border_box_right(collapsed)
        };
        sizing_context::ContentSizes {
            min: border_box_inline_size(content_box_inline_sizes.min),
            max: border_box_inline_size(content_box_inline_sizes.max),
        }
    }

    fn measure_tracks(&mut self, input: LayoutInput, skip_row_measurement: bool) {
        self.available_space = input.available_space;
        // Determine the number of rows/columns the table requires.
        let table_grid = calculate_table_grid(self, self.run.box_, MissingTableCells::Include);
        self.cells = table_grid.cells;
        self.rows = table_grid.rows;
        self.columns = vec![Column::default(); table_grid.column_count];
        for cell in &self.cells {
            self.columns[cell.column_index].has_originating_cells = true;
        }
        self.column_track_ranges = self.collect_column_track_ranges();
        for &range in &self.column_track_ranges {
            if self.column_is_collapsed(range.box_) {
                for index in range.start..range.end {
                    self.columns[index].is_collapsed = true;
                }
            }
        }

        // The containing block of every internal table box and caption is the table wrapper;
        // the table's own input carries the wrapper's constraints, and participant percentages
        // resolve against those. Percentage block sizes of participants only resolve once the table
        // itself has a non-auto block size.
        self.table_constraints = input.containing_block_constraints;
        let table_height_auto = self.style(self.run.box_).height().is_auto();
        self.participant_constraints = ContainingBlockConstraints {
            percentage_basis_inline_size: self.table_constraints.percentage_basis_inline_size,
            percentage_basis_block_size: if table_height_auto {
                None
            } else {
                self.table_constraints.percentage_basis_block_size
            },
            quirks_mode_percentage_basis_block_size: self.table_constraints.quirks_mode_percentage_basis_block_size,
        };
        let participant_preparation =
            if skip_row_measurement && self.style(self.run.box_).border_collapse() == BORDER_COLLAPSE_SEPARATE {
                // OPTIMIZATION: Wrapper inline sizing measures cell contents in isolated measurement runs and does not
                //               read the cells of rows or row groups in the separated-borders model.
                TableParticipantPreparation::CellsOfTableCellsOnly
            } else {
                TableParticipantPreparation::CellsOfEveryParticipant
            };
        self.prepare_table_participants(participant_preparation);
        self.border_conflict_resolution();

        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#ROWMIN
        // ROWMIN is defined as the sum of the minimum block sizes of the rows after a first row layout pass.
        // NB: So the rows are measured once the columns have their used inline sizes (see compute_table_block_size),
        //     where each cell is laid out at the inline size it will have.
        // OPTIMIZATION: Row measurements are only needed when row block-size constraints or row spans can affect the
        //               later row distribution. Simple tables get their actual row block sizes from cell layout.
        self.needs_row_measurement = !skip_row_measurement && !self.can_skip_row_intrinsic_measurement();
        // Compute the minimum width of each column.
        self.compute_cell_measures();
        self.compute_outer_content_sizes();
        self.compute_table_measures(TrackAxis::Column);
    }

    /// Lays out the contents of the cell at `cell_index` with `sizing`, in the cells and with the input this table
    /// keeps of it, and keeps what its layout hands back.
    fn layout_inside_cell(
        &mut self,
        run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>,
        cell_index: usize,
        sizing: RootSizingDirectives,
    ) {
        let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
        let layout = &self.cell_layouts[cell_index];
        let laid_out = formatting_context::layout_inside_child_with_input_cells(
            run,
            None,
            None,
            cell.box_,
            LayoutInput {
                available_space: layout.inside_layout_input,
                containing_block_constraints: ContainingBlockConstraints::default(),
                sizing,
                participation: ParticipationInParentFormattingContext::Item,
            },
            layout.box_cells,
            None,
            false,
            // NB: A table cell is a containing block of its own to the percentage block insets of its descendants.
            run.percentage_block_insets_of_root_children_have_definite_basis(&self.table_box_cells),
        );
        laid_out.report_percentage_block_size_dependency_of(run, cell.box_);
        let layout = &mut self.cell_layouts[cell_index];
        layout.box_cells = laid_out.cells();
        layout.content_baselines = laid_out.baselines();
        layout.run_laid_out_abspos_contained_by_cell = laid_out.laid_out_abspos_contained_by_root();
        layout.contents_depend_on_percentage_block_size = laid_out.contents_depend_on_percentage_block_size();
        layout.placed = Some(laid_out.placed_child());
        layout.fragment_arrival = laid_out.into_fragment_arrival(run);
    }

    /// The baseline of a cell, from the top of its border box: "The baseline of a cell is the baseline of the first
    /// in-flow line box in the cell, or the first in-flow table-row in the cell, whichever comes first. If there is no
    /// such line box or table-row, the baseline is the bottom of content edge of the cell."
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#height-layout
    /// The cell's own 'vertical-align' says where the cell goes in its row, not where its baseline is.
    fn cell_baseline(&self, cell_index: usize) -> CssPixels {
        let layout = &self.cell_layouts[cell_index];
        let cell_box = &layout.box_cells;
        let collapsed = cell_box.uses_collapsing_borders_model;
        cell_box.border_box_top(collapsed) + layout.content_baselines.first.unwrap_or(cell_box.content_block_size)
    }

    /// Notes what a cell contributes to the baseline of its row (see row_baseline) and to the row's height (see
    /// grow_rows_to_aligned_cells).
    fn note_cell_in_row_baseline(&mut self, cell_index: usize, style: &StyleValues<'_>) {
        let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
        let cell_box = self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells;
        let collapsed = cell_box.uses_collapsing_borders_model;
        let block_end_offset = cell_box.border_box_bottom(collapsed);
        let block_size = cell_box.border_box_block_size(collapsed);
        let row = &mut self.rows[cell.row_index];
        if box_alignment::cell_alignment(*style) == box_alignment::CellAlignment::Baseline {
            row.baseline = Some(
                row.baseline
                    .map_or(cell.baseline, |baseline| baseline.max(cell.baseline)),
            );
            // A cell spanning several rows reaches into the rows below, not below the bottom of this one.
            if cell.row_span == 1 {
                row.max_cell_descent = row.max_cell_descent.max(block_size - cell.baseline);
            }
        }
        row.smallest_cell_block_end_offset = Some(
            row.smallest_cell_block_end_offset
                .map_or(block_end_offset, |offset| offset.min(block_end_offset)),
        );
    }

    fn compute_table_block_size(&mut self, run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>) {
        // First pass of row block-size calculation:
        for row_index in 0..self.rows.len() {
            if self.rows[row_index].is_collapsed {
                self.rows[row_index].base_block_size = CssPixels::default();
                continue;
            }
            let height = self.style(self.rows[row_index].box_).height();
            if height.is_length() {
                // NOTE: A <length> block size resolves without a percentage basis.
                self.rows[row_index].base_block_size = self.rows[row_index]
                    .base_block_size
                    .max(height.to_px(CssPixels::default()));
            }
        }
        let cell_padding_basis = self.cell_padding_percentage_basis();
        let fixed = self.use_fixed_mode_layout();
        let participant_block_basis = self.participant_constraints.block_basis();
        let collapsed = self.style(self.run.box_).border_collapse() != BORDER_COLLAPSE_SEPARATE;
        let inline_spacing = self.border_spacing_inline();
        // First pass of cells layout:
        for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
            let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
            let style = self.style(cell.box_);
            let span_inline = (0..cell.column_span).fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, index| {
                sum + self.columns[cell.column_index + index].used_inline_size
            });
            let mut cell_box = self.cell_box_with_resolved_sides(cell_index, collapsed, cell_padding_basis);
            // The row measures the cell's contents without a definite percentage block-size basis. The specified
            // cell height still contributes to the row minimum, and stretch_cells_to_their_rows resolves the contents
            // against the final height. Quirks mode keeps its percentage-height calculation.
            // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#row-layout
            if !self.node_facts(cell.box_).document_in_quirks_mode() || style.height().contains_percentage() {
                cell_box.has_definite_block_size = false;
            }
            // A cell whose columns all have 'visibility: collapse' is removed from the display along with them, as in
            // other engines: "This value causes the entire row or column to be removed from the display". It is laid
            // out like any other cell (with no inline size, see remove_collapsed_columns), and painting skips it.
            // https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#dynamic-effects
            let hidden_by_collapsed_columns = self.visible_spanned_columns(cell) == 0;
            self.cell_layouts[cell_index]
                .fragment_facts
                .show
                .hidden_by_collapsed_columns = hidden_by_collapsed_columns;
            let height = style.height();
            let mut specified_outer_block_size = None;
            if !self.rows[cell.row_index].is_collapsed && height.is_length() {
                let offsets = cell_box.border_box_top(collapsed) + cell_box.border_box_bottom(collapsed);
                let cell_size = self.cell_specified_outer_block_size(
                    cell.box_,
                    &style,
                    height.to_px(participant_block_basis),
                    offsets,
                );
                cell_box.set_content_block_size(cell_size - offsets);
                specified_outer_block_size = Some(cell_size);
                // Only a cell that spans its row exclusively gives the row its specified block size (see below). A
                // cell spanning several rows reaches them through the row measures instead, as its minimum.
                if cell.row_span == 1 {
                    self.rows[cell.row_index].base_block_size =
                        self.rows[cell.row_index].base_block_size.max(cell_size);
                }
            }
            // Compute cell inline size as specified by https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#bounding-box-assignment:
            // The position of any table cell, track, or track group is defined by the sums of its spanned columns and rows:
            // - the inline/block sizes of all spanned visible columns/rows
            // - the inline/block border spacing times the amount of spanned visible columns/rows minus one
            // (collapsed columns have no inline size, see remove_collapsed_columns).
            let cell_inline_size = span_inline + inline_spacing * self.visible_spanned_columns(cell).saturating_sub(1);
            // In fixed mode, columns are sized without regard to the padding and borders of cells that have no
            // specified inline size (https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#width-distribution-in-fixed-mode), so a
            // column can be narrower than those. The cell still occupies exactly its columns, with an empty content
            // box, as in other engines: shrink its used padding and borders to fit, so that the box painted for the
            // cell stays within its columns. In auto mode, only percentage paddings, which resolve against zero while
            // the columns are measured, can be wider than the columns: the end padding shrinks to fit, and the start
            // padding keeps its used value.
            Self::shrink_cell_offsets_to_fit(&mut cell_box, collapsed, cell_inline_size, fixed);
            cell_box.set_content_inline_size(
                cell_inline_size - cell_box.border_box_left(collapsed) - cell_box.border_box_right(collapsed),
            );

            let inner = cell_box.available_inner_space_or_constraints_from(self.available_space);
            let layout = &mut self.cell_layouts[cell_index];
            layout.inside_layout_input = inner;
            layout.pre_layout_content_block_size = cell_box.content_block_size;
            layout.box_cells = cell_box;
            self.layout_inside_cell(
                run,
                cell_index,
                RootSizingDirectives {
                    content_block_size_after_run: geometry::ContentBlockSizeAfterRun::Automatic,
                    ..RootSizingDirectives::default()
                },
            );
            let cell_box = self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells;
            if self.needs_row_measurement {
                // The outer min-content block size of a cell is the larger of its laid-out block size and its
                // specified one.
                let measured = cell_box
                    .border_box_block_size(collapsed)
                    .max(specified_outer_block_size.unwrap_or_default());
                self.cells[cell_index].outer_min_block_size = measured;
                self.cells[cell_index].outer_max_block_size = measured;
            }
            self.cells[cell_index].baseline = self.cell_baseline(cell_index);
            // Implements https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#computing-the-table-height

            // The minimum block size of a row is the maximum of:
            // - the computed block size (if definite, percentages being considered 0px) of its corresponding table row,
            // - the computed block size of each cell spanning the current row exclusively (if definite, percentages being treated as 0px), and
            // - the minimum block size (ROWMIN) required by the cells spanning the row.
            // Note that we've already applied the first rule at the top of the method.
            if !self.rows[cell.row_index].is_collapsed {
                if cell.row_span == 1 {
                    let size = cell_box.border_box_block_size(collapsed);
                    self.rows[cell.row_index].base_block_size = self.rows[cell.row_index].base_block_size.max(size);
                }
                if !self.needs_row_measurement {
                    self.rows[cell.row_index].base_block_size = self.rows[cell.row_index]
                        .base_block_size
                        .max(self.rows[cell.row_index].min_size);
                }
                self.note_cell_in_row_baseline(cell_index, &style);
            }
        }
        self.grow_rows_to_aligned_cells(|row| &mut row.base_block_size);

        if self.needs_row_measurement {
            self.initialize_row_content_sizes();
            self.compute_table_measures(TrackAxis::Row);
            for row in &mut self.rows {
                if !row.is_collapsed {
                    row.base_block_size = row.base_block_size.max(row.min_size);
                }
            }
        }
        self.table_block_size = self
            .rows
            .iter()
            .fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, row| sum + row.base_block_size);
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#computing-the-table-height
        // The height of a table is the sum of the row heights plus any cell spacing or borders.
        let visible_rows = self.rows.iter().filter(|row| !row.is_collapsed).count();
        let row_spacing = if visible_rows == 0 {
            CssPixels::default()
        } else {
            self.border_spacing_block() * (visible_rows + 1)
        };
        if let Some(minimum) = self.min_border_box_block_size_from_flex_item {
            let used = &self.table_box_cells;
            let collapsed = used.uses_collapsing_borders_model();
            let content_min =
                minimum - used.border_box_top(collapsed) - used.border_box_bottom(collapsed) - row_spacing;
            self.table_block_size = self.table_block_size.max(content_min);
        }
        let table_style = self.style(self.run.box_);
        // https://quirks.spec.whatwg.org/#the-percentage-height-calculation-quirk
        // NB: In quirks mode, a percentage block size of the table resolves against the nearest ancestor with a
        //     block size when its containing block has none.
        let block_basis = self.table_constraints.percentage_basis_block_size.unwrap_or_else(|| {
            if self.node_facts(self.run.box_).document_in_quirks_mode() {
                self.table_constraints
                    .quirks_mode_percentage_basis_block_size
                    .unwrap_or_default()
            } else {
                CssPixels::default()
            }
        });
        let border_box_offsets = if table_style.box_sizing() == box_sizing::BORDER_BOX {
            let used = &self.table_box_cells;
            let collapsed = used.uses_collapsing_borders_model();
            used.border_box_top(collapsed) + used.border_box_bottom(collapsed)
        } else {
            CssPixels::default()
        };
        // If the table has a `height` property other than auto, it is treated as a minimum block size for the
        // table grid, and will eventually be distributed to the rows if their collective minimum block size is smaller.
        // The table's `max-height` lowers that size, and its `min-height` raises it, as for the block size of any box.
        let mut specified =
            (!table_style.height().is_auto()).then(|| table_style.height().to_px(block_basis) - border_box_offsets);
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-4/#aspect-ratio
        // NB: An auto block size follows from the inline size through the preferred aspect ratio. Like a specified
        //     block size, it only gives the table grid a minimum block size.
        if specified.is_none()
            && let Some(ratio) = self.node_facts(self.run.box_).preferred_aspect_ratio()
        {
            let used = &self.table_box_cells;
            let collapsed = used.uses_collapsing_borders_model();
            let inline_size = if table_style.box_sizing() == box_sizing::BORDER_BOX {
                used.border_box_inline_size(collapsed)
            } else {
                used.content_inline_size()
            };
            specified = Some(ratio.divide(inline_size) - border_box_offsets);
        }
        if let Some(size) = specified.as_mut()
            && table_style.max_height().is_length()
        {
            *size = (*size).min(table_style.max_height().to_px(block_basis) - border_box_offsets);
        }
        if !crate::layout::sizing_context::is_plain_auto(table_style.min_height()) {
            let minimum = table_style.min_height().to_px(block_basis) - border_box_offsets;
            specified = Some(specified.map_or(minimum, |size| size.max(minimum)));
        }
        if let Some(specified) = specified {
            self.table_block_size = self.table_block_size.max(specified - row_spacing);
        }
        let table_percentage_basis = self.table_block_size + row_spacing;
        for row in &mut self.rows {
            // Reference size is the largest of
            // - its initial base block size and
            // - its new base block size (the one evaluated during the second layout pass, where percentages used in
            //   row groups, rows, and cells were resolved according to the table block size, instead of
            //   being ignored as 0px).

            // Assign reference size to base size. Later, the reference size might change to a larger value during
            // the second pass of rows layout.
            row.reference_block_size = row.base_block_size;
        }
        // NB: Percentage block sizes of rows and cells don't raise the reference sizes here. They are applied when the
        //     table block size is distributed to the rows (see distribute_block_size_to_rows), where a row grows to its
        //     percentage block size only as far as the table block size allows.
        for row in &mut self.rows {
            if row.is_collapsed {
                row.reference_block_size = CssPixels::default();
            }
        }
        self.table_percentage_basis = table_percentage_basis;
        // Second pass cells layout:
        // At this point, percentage cell block sizes can be resolved because the final table block size is calculated.
        for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
            let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
            if !self.cell_has_resolvable_percentage_block_size(cell.box_) {
                continue;
            }
            let style = self.style(cell.box_);
            let mut cell_box = self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells;
            let offsets = cell_box.border_box_top(collapsed) + cell_box.border_box_bottom(collapsed);
            let cell_size = self.cell_specified_outer_block_size(
                cell.box_,
                &style,
                style.height().to_px(table_percentage_basis),
                offsets,
            );
            cell_box.set_content_block_size(cell_size - offsets);
            self.cell_layouts[cell_index].pre_layout_content_block_size = cell_box.content_block_size;
            let span_inline = (0..cell.column_span).fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, index| {
                sum + self.columns[cell.column_index + index].used_inline_size
            });
            cell_box.set_content_inline_size(
                span_inline - cell_box.border_box_left(collapsed) - cell_box.border_box_right(collapsed)
                    + inline_spacing * self.visible_spanned_columns(cell).saturating_sub(1),
            );
            let inner = cell_box.available_inner_space_or_constraints_from(self.available_space);
            self.cell_layouts[cell_index].inside_layout_input = inner;
            self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells = cell_box;
            // The resolved size supplies the percentage basis for descendants. Keep the content's automatic size
            // for alignment within the rows, as in the first pass.
            self.layout_inside_cell(
                run,
                cell_index,
                RootSizingDirectives {
                    content_block_size_after_run: geometry::ContentBlockSizeAfterRun::Automatic,
                    ..RootSizingDirectives::default()
                },
            );
            self.cells[cell_index].baseline = self.cell_baseline(cell_index);
            if !self.rows[cell.row_index].is_collapsed {
                let border_size = self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells.border_box_block_size(collapsed);
                self.rows[cell.row_index].reference_block_size =
                    self.rows[cell.row_index].reference_block_size.max(border_size);
                self.note_cell_in_row_baseline(cell_index, &style);
            }
        }
        self.grow_rows_to_aligned_cells(|row| &mut row.reference_block_size);
    }

    /// Makes each row at least as tall as its baseline-aligned cells reach once they are aligned. A cell whose
    /// baseline lies above the row's baseline is moved down to it (see cell_contents_block_offset), so the row must
    /// hold the row's baseline plus the largest descent below it: "First the cells that are aligned on their baseline
    /// are positioned. This will establish the baseline of the row. [...] The row now has a top, possibly a baseline,
    /// and a provisional height, which is the distance from the top to the lowest bottom of the cells positioned so
    /// far." https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#height-layout
    fn grow_rows_to_aligned_cells(&mut self, block_size: impl Fn(&mut Row) -> &mut CssPixels) {
        for row in &mut self.rows {
            if row.is_collapsed {
                continue;
            }
            if let Some(baseline) = row.baseline {
                let reach = baseline + row.max_cell_descent;
                let size = block_size(row);
                *size = (*size).max(reach);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Shrinks the used padding, then the used borders, of a cell so that they fit within `inline_size`, the inline
    /// size of the columns the cell spans, or only its end padding unless `shrinks_start_padding_and_borders`. The end
    /// side goes first so that the content keeps its position relative to the start of the cell for as long as
    /// possible.
    fn shrink_cell_offsets_to_fit(
        cell_box: &mut used_values::RootInputCells,
        collapsed: bool,
