        inline_size: CssPixels,
        shrinks_start_padding_and_borders: bool,
    ) {
        let excess = |cell_box: &used_values::RootInputCells| {
            cell_box.border_box_left(collapsed) + cell_box.border_box_right(collapsed) - inline_size
        };
        let shrinking_sides: &[bool] = if shrinks_start_padding_and_borders {
            &[false, true]
        } else {
            &[false]
        };
        for &is_start_side in shrinking_sides {
            let reduction = excess(cell_box)
                .min(if is_start_side {
                    cell_box.padding_left
                } else {
                    cell_box.padding_right
                })
                .max(CssPixels::default());
            let padding = if is_start_side {
                &mut cell_box.padding_left
            } else {
                &mut cell_box.padding_right
            };
            *padding -= reduction;
        }
        if !shrinks_start_padding_and_borders {
            return;
        }
        for is_start_side in [false, true] {
            let remaining = excess(cell_box);
            if remaining <= CssPixels::default() {
                return;
            }
            // In the collapsing border model the cell's share of a border is the part of it on its side of the grid
            // line (see BoxMetricCells::border_left_collapsed).
            let share = |cell_box: &used_values::RootInputCells| {
                if is_start_side {
                    cell_box.border_left_collapsed(collapsed)
                } else {
                    cell_box.border_right_collapsed(collapsed)
                }
            };
            let set_border = |cell_box: &mut used_values::RootInputCells, width: CssPixels| {
                if is_start_side {
                    cell_box.border_left = width;
                } else {
                    cell_box.border_right = width;
                }
            };
            let allowed = (share(cell_box) - remaining).max(CssPixels::default());
            let mut width = if collapsed { allowed * 2usize } else { allowed };
            set_border(cell_box, width);
            // The whole-pixel split can leave the share above the allowed size by up to a pixel.
            while share(cell_box) > allowed && width > CssPixels::default() {
                width = (width - CssPixels::from_integer(1)).max(CssPixels::default());
                set_border(cell_box, width);
            }
        }
    }

    /// The block size a row takes from its own percentage block size and those of the cells that span only that
    /// row, resolved against `basis`, if any of them has one. `cells_of_row` holds the indices of the cells that
    /// originate in the row.
    fn row_percentage_block_size(
        &self,
        row_index: usize,
        cells_of_row: &[usize],
        basis: CssPixels,
    ) -> Option<CssPixels> {
        let row_height = self.style(self.rows[row_index].box_).height();
        let mut size = row_height
            .percentage_fraction()
            .is_some()
            .then(|| row_height.to_px(basis));
        let collapsed = self.style(self.run.box_).border_collapse() != BORDER_COLLAPSE_SEPARATE;
        for &cell_index in cells_of_row {
            let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
            if cell.row_span != 1 {
                continue;
            }
            let style = self.style(cell.box_);
            if style.height().percentage_fraction().is_none() {
                continue;
            }
            let cell_box = &self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells;
            let offsets = cell_box.border_box_top(collapsed) + cell_box.border_box_bottom(collapsed);
            let cell_size =
                self.cell_specified_outer_block_size(cell.box_, &style, style.height().to_px(basis), offsets);
            size = Some(size.map_or(cell_size, |size: CssPixels| size.max(cell_size)));
        }
        size
    }

    /// Whether neither a row nor any of its cells has a specified block size, so that its block size depends only on
    /// its contents. `cells_of_row` holds the indices of the cells that originate in the row.
    fn row_is_auto(&self, row_index: usize, cells_of_row: &[usize]) -> bool {
        // INTEROP: A calculation that mixes a percentage with a length, like calc(25% + 10px), counts as auto here, as
        //          in other engines.
        let acts_as_auto = |size: &ComputedSize| {
            size.is_auto() || (size.contains_percentage() && size.percentage_fraction().is_none())
        };
        acts_as_auto(self.style(self.rows[row_index].box_).height())
            && cells_of_row
                .iter()
                .all(|&cell_index| acts_as_auto(self.style(self.cells[cell_index].box_).height()))
    }

    /// Adds `amount` to the final block sizes of `rows`, in proportion to their current final block sizes, or in
    /// equal shares if they are all empty.
    fn grow_rows_proportionally(&mut self, rows: &[usize], amount: CssPixels) {
        let total = rows.iter().fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, &index| {
            sum + self.rows[index].final_block_size
        });
        let weights = rows
            .iter()
            .map(|&index| {
                if total > CssPixels::default() {
                    self.rows[index].final_block_size.to_double()
                } else {
                    1.0
                }
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let total_weight: f64 = weights.iter().sum();
        // Hand out cumulative shares so that the rounded increments add up to exactly `amount`.
        let mut accumulated_weight = 0.0;
        let mut distributed = CssPixels::default();
        for (&index, weight) in rows.iter().zip(weights) {
            accumulated_weight += weight;
            let target = CssPixels::nearest_value_for(amount.to_double() * accumulated_weight / total_weight);
            self.rows[index].final_block_size += target - distributed;
            distributed = target;
        }
    }

    // NB: The specification's distribution of the table block size to the rows
    //     (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#distributing-height-to-rows) is not what browsers do, and is
    //     unresolved (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/4418).
    // INTEROP: Rows keep their reference sizes, and the rest of the table block size goes first to rows with a
    //          percentage block size, in row order, each growing to at most that size. What remains then goes to the
    //          rows whose block size depends only on their contents, in proportion to their block sizes, or else to
    //          all rows in proportion to their block sizes. When the table has rows outside of header and footer
    //          groups, only those rows grow, and their percentages resolve against their share of the table.
    fn distribute_block_size_to_rows(&mut self) {
        let visible = self.rows.iter().filter(|row| !row.is_collapsed).count();
        if visible == 0 {
            return;
        }
        for row in &mut self.rows {
            row.final_block_size = if row.is_collapsed {
                CssPixels::default()
            } else {
                row.reference_block_size
            };
        }
        let sum = self
            .rows
            .iter()
            .fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, row| sum + row.final_block_size);
        if self.table_block_size <= sum {
            self.table_block_size = sum;
        } else {
            let mut excess = self.table_block_size - sum;
            let mut cells_by_row = vec![Vec::new(); self.rows.len()];
            for (cell_index, cell) in self.cells.iter().enumerate() {
                cells_by_row[cell.row_index].push(cell_index);
            }
            // NB: Only the first header group and the first footer group are rendered as such, and the rows are in
            //     layout order, which puts them first and last (see row_containers_in_layout_order). Any other header
            //     or footer group acts as an ordinary row group.
            let row_group_if = |row: Option<&Row>, is_group: fn(&NodeFacts) -> bool| {
                row.map(|row| self.parent(row.box_))
                    .filter(|&parent| is_group(&self.node_facts(parent)))
            };
            let header_group = row_group_if(self.rows.first(), |facts| facts.is_table_header_group());
            let footer_group = row_group_if(self.rows.last(), |facts| facts.is_table_footer_group());
            let body_rows = (0..self.rows.len())
                .filter(|&index| {
                    if self.rows[index].is_collapsed {
                        return false;
                    }
                    let parent = Some(self.parent(self.rows[index].box_));
                    parent != header_group && parent != footer_group
                })
                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
            let (growing_rows, percentage_basis) = if body_rows.is_empty() || body_rows.len() == visible {
                let rows = (0..self.rows.len())
                    .filter(|&index| !self.rows[index].is_collapsed)
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
                (rows, self.table_percentage_basis)
            } else {
                let body_sum = body_rows.iter().fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, &index| {
                    sum + self.rows[index].final_block_size
                });
                (body_rows, body_sum + excess)
            };
            for &index in &growing_rows {
                if excess <= CssPixels::default() {
                    break;
                }
                if let Some(size) = self.row_percentage_block_size(index, &cells_by_row[index], percentage_basis) {
                    let growth = (size - self.rows[index].final_block_size)
                        .max(CssPixels::default())
                        .min(excess);
                    self.rows[index].final_block_size += growth;
                    excess -= growth;
                }
            }
            if excess > CssPixels::default() {
                let auto_rows = growing_rows
                    .iter()
                    .copied()
                    .filter(|&index| self.row_is_auto(index, &cells_by_row[index]))
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
                if auto_rows.is_empty() {
                    self.grow_rows_proportionally(&growing_rows, excess);
                } else {
                    self.grow_rows_proportionally(&auto_rows, excess);
                }
            }
        }
        // Add undistributable space due to border spacing: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#computing-undistributable-space.
        let spacing = self.border_spacing_block();
        self.table_block_size += (visible + 1) * spacing;
    }

    fn position_row_boxes(&mut self) {
        let block_spacing = self.border_spacing_block();
        let inline_spacing = self.border_spacing_inline();
        let table_used = &self.table_box_cells;
        let inline_offset = table_used.border_box_left(table_used.uses_collapsing_borders_model()) + inline_spacing;
        let mut row_block_offset = self.table_box_content_block_offset_in_wrapper + block_spacing;
        let row_inline_size = self
            .columns
            .iter()
            .fold(CssPixels::default(), |sum, column| sum + column.used_inline_size)
            + inline_spacing * self.visible_column_count().saturating_sub(1);
        for (row, row_box) in self.rows.iter().zip(self.row_boxes_by_row_index()) {
            let used = &row_box.cells;
            used.set_content_block_size(row.final_block_size);
            used.set_content_inline_size(row_inline_size);
            self.place_participant(
                row.box_,
                row_box,
                run_state::FragmentFactsDecidedByParent::default(),
                inline_offset,
                row_block_offset,
            );
            if !row.is_collapsed {
                row_block_offset += row.final_block_size + block_spacing;
            }
        }

        // A row group spans the rows it contains, which were positioned above in layout order together with the rows
        // that are direct children of the table box. Rows outside any group can lie between two groups, so a group
        // starts at its first row rather than where the previous group ended; a group without rows is empty at the
        // position that the rows placed so far reached.
        let mut group_block_offset = self.table_box_content_block_offset_in_wrapper + block_spacing;
        let mut row_ranges_of_row_groups = self.row_ranges_of_row_groups().into_iter().peekable();
        for (group, group_box) in &self.row_group_boxes {
            let group = *group;
            let mut block_start = group_block_offset;
            let mut block_end = group_block_offset;
            let mut inline_size = CssPixels::default();
            let mut has_rows = false;
            let rows_of_group = row_ranges_of_row_groups
                .next_if(|(group_of_rows, _)| *group_of_rows == group)
                .map_or(0..0, |(_, rows)| rows);
            for row_box in &self.row_boxes[rows_of_group] {
                let used = &row_box.cells;
                let row_block_offset = row_box.content_offset.get().y;
                if !has_rows {
                    block_start = row_block_offset;
                    has_rows = true;
                }
                block_end = row_block_offset + used.border_box_block_size(false);
                inline_size = inline_size.max(used.border_box_inline_size(false));
            }
            let used = &group_box.cells;
            used.set_content_block_size(block_end - block_start);
            used.set_content_inline_size(inline_size);
            self.place_participant(
                group,
                group_box,
                run_state::FragmentFactsDecidedByParent::default(),
                inline_offset,
                block_start,
            );
            group_block_offset = block_end + if has_rows { block_spacing } else { CssPixels::default() };
        }
        debug_assert!(
            row_ranges_of_row_groups.next().is_none(),
            "the row groups lay out their rows in the order of the groups"
        );
        let padding_top = table_used.padding_top();
        let total =
            row_block_offset.max(group_block_offset) - self.table_box_content_block_offset_in_wrapper - padding_top;
        self.table_block_size = self.table_block_size.max(total);
    }

    /// Whether the block size of a cell is definite once the rows are sized, so that its contents resolve percentage
    /// block sizes against it.
    // INTEROP: CSS 2.1 leaves this undefined. Like other engines, the cell's block size is definite when the cell has a
    //          length block size, or when the table has a computed block size other than auto (even a percentage
    //          that acts as auto) and the rows gave the cell a block size other than the one its contents gave it. A
    //          block size the row specifies alone doesn't make it definite.
    fn cell_block_size_is_definite_after_row_sizing(&self, cell_index: usize, collapsed: bool) -> bool {
        let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
        if self.style(cell.box_).height().is_length() {
            return true;
        }
        !self.style(self.run.box_).height().is_auto()
            && self.compute_row_content_block_size(cell)
                != self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells.border_box_block_size(collapsed)
    }

    /// Stretches each cell to the rows it spans and aligns its contents in them: the table moves the contents as it
    /// places the cell, or, where the cell's run laid out the absolutely positioned boxes the cell contains, lays the
    /// cell out again at its stretched size with its contents moved, for those boxes to be laid out against it.
    fn stretch_cells_to_their_rows(&mut self, run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>) {
        let collapsed = self.style(self.run.box_).border_collapse() != BORDER_COLLAPSE_SEPARATE;
        let mut relaid_out_any_cell = false;
        for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
            let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
            if self.cell_layouts[cell_index].contents_depend_on_percentage_block_size
                && self.cell_block_size_is_definite_after_row_sizing(cell_index, collapsed)
            {
                // Lay the contents out again with the final block size of the cell as their percentage basis.
                let mut cell_box = self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells;
                let offsets = cell_box.border_box_top(collapsed) + cell_box.border_box_bottom(collapsed);
                cell_box.set_content_block_size(self.compute_row_content_block_size(cell) - offsets);
                cell_box.has_definite_block_size = true;
                let layout = &mut self.cell_layouts[cell_index];
                layout.inside_layout_input = cell_box.available_inner_space_or_constraints_from(self.available_space);
                layout.pre_layout_content_block_size = cell_box.content_block_size;
                layout.box_cells = cell_box;
                self.layout_inside_cell(
                    run,
                    cell_index,
                    RootSizingDirectives {
                        content_block_size_after_run: geometry::ContentBlockSizeAfterRun::Automatic,
                        ..RootSizingDirectives::default()
                    },
                );
                self.cells[cell_index].baseline = self.cell_baseline(cell_index);
                relaid_out_any_cell = true;
            }
        }
        // The contents laid out again can put a cell's baseline elsewhere, so the rows take their baselines from the
        // cells as they are now, before any cell is aligned on one.
        if relaid_out_any_cell {
            for row in &mut self.rows {
                row.baseline = None;
                row.max_cell_descent = CssPixels::default();
                row.smallest_cell_block_end_offset = None;
            }
            for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
                let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
                if !self.rows[cell.row_index].is_collapsed {
                    let style = self.style(cell.box_);
                    self.note_cell_in_row_baseline(cell_index, &style);
                }
            }
        }
        for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
            let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
            let laid_out = self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells;
            let free_space = self.compute_row_content_block_size(cell) - laid_out.border_box_block_size(collapsed);
            let contents_block_offset = self.cell_contents_block_offset(cell_index, free_space);
            let stretched_content_block_size = laid_out.content_block_size + free_space;
            let layout = &mut self.cell_layouts[cell_index];
            if !layout.run_laid_out_abspos_contained_by_cell
                || (free_space == CssPixels::default() && contents_block_offset == CssPixels::default())
            {
                layout.box_cells.set_content_block_size(stretched_content_block_size);
                layout.contents_block_offset = contents_block_offset;
                continue;
            }
            layout
                .box_cells
                .set_content_block_size(layout.pre_layout_content_block_size);
            self.layout_inside_cell(
                run,
                cell_index,
                RootSizingDirectives {
                    content_block_size_after_run: geometry::ContentBlockSizeAfterRun::Given(
                        stretched_content_block_size,
                    ),
                    table_cell_contents_block_offset: contents_block_offset,
                    ..RootSizingDirectives::default()
                },
            );
        }
    }

    /// How far the contents of the cell at `cell_index` move down to align them in the rows it spans, which leave
    /// `free_space` beside its border box.
    fn cell_contents_block_offset(&self, cell_index: usize, free_space: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
        let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
        // An anonymous cell around a flex or grid container (such as a <td> with display: flex, which CSS Tables 3
        // wraps in one) aligns the container at its top, so that the container aligns its children itself.
        if self.anonymous_cell_wraps_flex_or_grid(cell) {
            return CssPixels::default();
        }
        match box_alignment::cell_alignment(self.style(cell.box_)) {
            // The baseline of the cell is put at the same height as the baseline of the first of the rows it spans.
            box_alignment::CellAlignment::Baseline => {
                self.rows[cell.row_index].baseline.unwrap_or(cell.baseline) - cell.baseline
            }
            box_alignment::CellAlignment::Content(alignment) => {
                alignment.offset(free_space, box_alignment::OverflowSafety::Safe)
            }
        }
    }

    fn compute_row_content_block_size(&self, cell: TableCell) -> CssPixels {
        // The block size of a cell is the sum of all spanned rows, as described in
        // https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#bounding-box-assignment
        let first = &self.row_boxes[cell.row_index].cells;
        if cell.row_span == 1 {
            return first.content_block_size();
        }
        // When the row span is greater than 1, the borders of inner rows within the span have to be
        // included in the content block size of the spanning cell. First top and final bottom borders are
        // excluded to be consistent with the handling of row span 1 case above, which uses the content
        // block size (no top and bottom borders) of the row.
        let mut span = CssPixels::default();
        for index in 0..cell.row_span {
            let used = &self.row_boxes[cell.row_index + index].cells;
            if index == 0 {
                span += used.content_block_size() + used.border_box_bottom(false);
            } else if index == cell.row_span - 1 {
                span += used.border_box_top(false) + used.content_block_size();
            } else {
                span += used.border_box_block_size(false);
            }
        }
        // Compute cell block size as specified by https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#bounding-box-assignment:
        // The logical size is the sum of:
        // - the inline/block sizes of all spanned visible columns/rows
        // - the inline/block border spacing times the amount of spanned visible columns/rows minus one
        // FIXME: Account for visibility.
        span + self.border_spacing_block() * (cell.row_span - 1)
    }

    fn anonymous_cell_wraps_flex_or_grid(&self, cell: TableCell) -> bool {
        if !self.node_facts(cell.box_).is_anonymous() {
            return false;
        }
        let child = self.first_child(cell.box_);
        if child.is_invalid() || !self.next_sibling(child).is_invalid() {
            return false;
        }
        let facts = self.node_facts(child);
        facts.is_box() && (facts.display().is_flex_inside() || facts.display().is_grid_inside())
    }

    fn position_cell_boxes(&mut self) {
        let collapsed = self.style(self.run.box_).border_collapse() != BORDER_COLLAPSE_SEPARATE;
        let table_box = self.table_box_cells();
        let inset_percentage_basis = geometry::LogicalSize {
            inline_size: table_box.content_inline_size(),
            block_size: table_box.content_block_size(),
        };
        let percentage_block_insets_have_definite_basis = self
            .run
            .percentage_block_insets_of_root_children_have_definite_basis(&table_box);
        for cell_index in 0..self.cells.len() {
            let cell = self.cells[cell_index];
            let cell_box = self.cell_layouts[cell_index].box_cells;
            let row_content_offset = self.row_boxes[cell.row_index].content_offset.get();
            // Compute cell position as specified by https://www.w3.org/TR/css-tables-3/#bounding-box-assignment:
            // left/top location is the sum of:
            // - for top: the height reserved for top captions (including margins), if any
            // - the padding-left/padding-top and border-left-width/border-top-width of the table
            // - the border spacing after each visible column before the cell (in its column's offset)
            let x = row_content_offset.x
                + cell_box.border_box_left(collapsed)
                + self.column_offsets[self
                    .physical_columns(cell.column_index..cell.column_index + cell.column_span)
                    .start];
            let y = row_content_offset.y + cell_box.border_box_top(collapsed);
            // A relatively positioned cell is offset from where the table places it, as any in-flow box is.
            let insets = abspos_engine::compute_inset_native(
                &self.run,
                cell.box_,
                &table_box,
                inset_percentage_basis,
                percentage_block_insets_have_definite_basis,
            );
            let layout = &mut self.cell_layouts[cell_index];
            let mut placed_cell = layout.placed.take().expect("a cell is laid out before it is placed");
            placed_cell.geometry.cells = cell_box;
            let placed_cell = placed_cell
                .with_fragment_facts(layout.fragment_facts)
                .with_in_flow_box_insets(insets)
                .with_contents_shift(FfiCssPixelPoint {
                    x: CssPixels::default(),
                    y: layout.contents_block_offset,
                });
            formatting_context::place_child(
                &self.run,
                cell.box_,
                placed_cell,
                FfiCssPixelPoint { x, y },
                None,
                layout.fragment_arrival.take(),
            );
        }
    }

    /// Positions the table-column-group and table-column boxes over the cells of their columns. Their backgrounds
    /// are painted in the area of those cells but positioned relative to the column or column group box:
    /// "Each column group extends from the top of the cells in the top row to the bottom of the cells on the bottom
    /// row and from the left edge of its leftmost column to the right edge of its rightmost column. [...] Each
    /// column is as tall as the column groups and as wide as a normal (single-column-spanning) cell in the column."
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#table-layers
    fn position_column_boxes(&mut self) {
        let inline_spacing = self.border_spacing_inline();
        let block_spacing = self.border_spacing_block();
        let table_used = &self.table_box_cells;
        let inline_offset = table_used.border_box_left(table_used.uses_collapsing_borders_model()) + inline_spacing;

        // The rows were positioned by position_row_boxes(): the columns extend from the first row to the end of
        // the last one.
        let block_start = self.row_boxes_by_row_index().next().map_or(
            self.table_box_content_block_offset_in_wrapper + block_spacing,
            |row_box| row_box.content_offset.get().y,
        );
        let mut block_end = block_start;
        for (row, row_box) in self.rows.iter().zip(self.row_boxes_by_row_index()) {
            if row.is_collapsed {
                continue;
            }
            let used = &row_box.cells;
            block_end = block_end.max(row_box.content_offset.get().y + used.border_box_block_size(false));
        }
        let block_size = block_end - block_start;

        // A range of columns spans the border spacing between them but not the spacing around them.
        let column_offsets = &self.column_offsets;
        // Columns are assigned to grid columns in tree order, like the cells they contain (see
        // collect_column_track_ranges()). A column group is placed before its columns: a table-column-group box is the
        // containing block of its columns, so they are positioned relative to it. So the placements come in the
        // order of column_boxes(), and each column refers to the placement of its group by its index.
        let mut placements: Vec<(Node, Option<usize>, usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
        let mut group_placement: Option<usize> = None;
        for &range in &self.column_track_ranges {
            match range.group {
                Some(group) => match group_placement {
                    Some(index) if placements[index].0 == group => placements[index].3 = range.end,
                    _ => {
                        group_placement = Some(placements.len());
                        placements.push((group, None, range.start, range.end));
                    }
                },
                None => group_placement = None,
            }
            if !range.is_group_without_columns() {
                placements.push((range.box_, group_placement, range.start, range.end));
            }
        }
        debug_assert_eq!(placements.len(), self.column_group_and_column_boxes.len());
        for (placement_index, (node, group_placement, start, end)) in placements.into_iter().enumerate() {
            let inline_size = if (start..end).any(|index| !self.columns[index].is_collapsed) {
                let columns = self.physical_columns(start..end);
                column_offsets[columns.end] - column_offsets[columns.start] - inline_spacing
            } else {
                CssPixels::default()
            };
            let fragment_facts = run_state::FragmentFactsDecidedByParent {
                show: fragment_tree::ParentShowFacts {
                    table_column_index: start as u32,
                    table_column_span: (end - start) as u32,
                    ..fragment_tree::ParentShowFacts::default()
                },
                ..run_state::FragmentFactsDecidedByParent::default()
            };
            let (column_node, column_box) = &self.column_group_and_column_boxes[placement_index];
            debug_assert!(
                *column_node == node,
                "a column is placed in the order of column_boxes()"
            );
            let used = &column_box.cells;
            used.set_content_inline_size(inline_size);
            used.set_content_block_size(block_size);
            let mut x = inline_offset + column_offsets[self.physical_columns(start..end).start];
            let mut y = block_start;
            if let Some((group, group_box)) =
                group_placement.map(|group_placement| &self.column_group_and_column_boxes[group_placement])
                && self.run.pass.in_flow_containing_block(node) == *group
            {
                let group_offset = group_box.content_offset.get();
                x -= group_offset.x;
                y -= group_offset.y;
            }
            self.place_participant(node, column_box, fragment_facts, x, y);
        }
    }

    /// The baseline of a row, from its top. The baseline-aligned cells "are positioned so their baselines align. This
    /// will establish the baseline of the row." and "If a row has no cell box aligned to its baseline, the baseline
    /// of that row is the bottom content edge of the lowest cell in the row."
    /// https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#height-layout
    fn row_baseline(&self, row_index: usize) -> CssPixels {
        let row = &self.rows[row_index];
        if let Some(baseline) = row.baseline {
            return baseline;
        }
        // Every cell is as tall as its row, so the lowest content edge lies above the row's bottom by the smallest
        // bottom padding and border among its cells. A row without cells has its baseline at its top, as in Blink.
        row.smallest_cell_block_end_offset
            .map_or(CssPixels::default(), |offset| {
                (row.final_block_size - offset).max(CssPixels::default())
            })
    }

    /// Derives the baselines of the table box, which are what the table exports to outside consumers (e.g. an
    /// inline-table participating in a line box): "The baseline of an 'inline-table' is the baseline of the first row of
    /// the table." (https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#height-layout) and its last baseline is that of its last row.
    /// Rows are positioned in the coordinate space of the table wrapper (see position_row_boxes), so the baselines are
    /// made relative to the content box of the table box here.
    fn derive_table_box_baselines(&self) {
        let arena = self.run.pass.arena();
        if arena.element_adjustment_facts(arena.dom_node_style_node(self.run.box_))
            & element_adjustment_fact::IS_MATHML_MTABLE
            != 0
        {
            let baseline = math_formatting_context::table_baseline(&self.style(self.run.box_), self.table_box_cells());
            self.derived_baselines_of_root_box.set(DerivedBaselines {
                first: Some(baseline),
                last: Some(baseline),
                inline_alignment: Some(baseline),
            });
            return;
        }

        let baseline_in_wrapper =
            |row_index: usize| self.row_boxes[row_index].content_offset.get().y + self.row_baseline(row_index);
        // Collapsed rows are removed from the display (https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#dynamic-effects).
        let visible_rows = (0..self.rows.len())
            .filter(|&row_index| !self.rows[row_index].is_collapsed)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let content_block_offset = self.table_box_content_block_offset_in_wrapper;
        self.derived_baselines_of_root_box.set(DerivedBaselines {
            inline_alignment: None,
            first: visible_rows
                .first()
                .map(|&row_index| baseline_in_wrapper(row_index) - content_block_offset),
            last: visible_rows
                .last()
                .map(|&row_index| baseline_in_wrapper(row_index) - content_block_offset),
        });
    }

    fn run(&mut self, run: &FormattingContextRun<'pass>, input: LayoutInput, inline_layout: Option<TableInlineLayout>) {
        self.available_space = input.available_space;
        self.min_border_box_block_size_from_flex_item = input.sizing.forced_min_border_box_block_size.get();
        self.forced_border_box_inline_size = input.sizing.forced_table_box_border_box_inline_size.get();
        self.table_box_content_block_offset_in_wrapper = input
            .sizing
            .table_box_content_block_offset_in_wrapper
            .get()
            .unwrap_or_default();
        if inline_layout.is_none_or(|layout| !self.reuse_inline_layout(input.clone(), layout)) {
            self.run_until_inline_size_calculation(input, false);
        }
        if matches!(
            self.available_space.inline_size,
            AvailableSize::MinContent | AvailableSize::MaxContent
        ) && !matches!(
            self.available_space.block_size,
            AvailableSize::MinContent | AvailableSize::MaxContent
        ) {
            return;
        }

        // The total inline-axis border spacing is defined for each table:
        // - For tables laid out in separated-borders mode containing at least one column, the inline-axis component of the computed value of the border-spacing property times one plus the number of columns in the table
        // - Otherwise, 0
        let total_spacing = if self.columns.is_empty() {
            CssPixels::default()
        } else {
            (self.columns.len() + 1) * self.border_spacing_inline()
        };
        // The assignable table inline size is its used inline size minus the inline-axis border spacing.
        let assignable = self.table_box_cells.content_inline_size() - total_spacing;
        let fixed = self.use_fixed_mode_layout();
        // Distribute the inline size of the table among columns.
        distribute_inline_size(&mut self.columns, assignable, fixed);
        self.remove_collapsed_columns();
        let inline_spacing = self.border_spacing_inline();
        // The offsets of the columns are physical ones, from the left, as those of the collapsed borders are.
        let column_inline_size = |column: &Column| {
            if column.is_collapsed {
                CssPixels::default()
            } else {
                column.used_inline_size + inline_spacing
            }
        };
        self.column_offsets = if self.is_right_to_left() {
            grid_line_offsets(self.columns.iter().rev().map(column_inline_size))
        } else {
            grid_line_offsets(self.columns.iter().map(column_inline_size))
        };
        self.compute_table_block_size(run);
        self.distribute_block_size_to_rows();
        self.position_row_boxes();
        self.stretch_cells_to_their_rows(run);
        self.position_cell_boxes();
        self.position_column_boxes();
        self.materialize_collapsed_table_borders();
        self.table_box_cells.set_content_block_size(self.table_block_size);
        self.derive_table_box_baselines();
        self.automatic_content_block_size = self.table_block_size;
    }

    fn derived_baselines_of_root_box(&self) -> DerivedBaselines {
        self.derived_baselines_of_root_box.get()
    }
}

use super::*;

use std::borrow::Cow;

use libgfx_rust::font::{EmojiPresentation, FontHandle, FrozenFontList, emoji_presentation_for_code_point};

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum LineBreakMode {
    Strict,
    Normal,
    Loose,
    LooseJapanese,
    LooseChinese,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum LineBreakLanguage {
    Other,
    Japanese,
    Chinese,
}

impl LineBreakLanguage {
    pub(crate) fn from_tag(tag: &[u16]) -> Self {
        let is_alpha = |subtag: &[u16]| {
            subtag
                .iter()
                .all(|&unit| u8::try_from(unit).is_ok_and(|unit| unit.is_ascii_alphabetic()))
        };
        let matches = |subtag: &[u16], expected: &[u8]| {
            subtag.len() == expected.len()
                && subtag
                    .iter()
                    .zip(expected)
                    .all(|(&unit, &expected)| (unit | 0x20) == u16::from(expected))
        };
        let mut subtags = tag.split(|&unit| unit == u16::from(b'-'));
        let primary = subtags.next().unwrap_or_default();
        if !(2..=8).contains(&primary.len()) || !is_alpha(primary) {
            return Self::Other;
        }
        let mut candidate = subtags.next();
        // BCP47 permits up to three extlang subtags, only after a two- or three-letter primary language.
        if primary.len() <= 3 {
            for _ in 0..3 {
                if !candidate.is_some_and(|subtag| subtag.len() == 3 && is_alpha(subtag)) {
                    break;
                }
                candidate = subtags.next();
            }
        }
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#script-tagging
        // Only this position can name a script. Region, variant, extension and private-use subtags cannot override it.
        if let Some(script) = candidate.filter(|subtag| subtag.len() == 4 && is_alpha(subtag)) {
            if [b"hant", b"hans", b"hani", b"hanb", b"bopo"]
                .iter()
                .any(|name| matches(script, *name))
            {
                return Self::Chinese;
            }
            if [b"jpan", b"hrkt", b"hira", b"kana"]
                .iter()
                .any(|name| matches(script, *name))
            {
                return Self::Japanese;
            }
            return Self::Other;
        }
        if matches(primary, b"ja") {
            Self::Japanese
        } else if matches(primary, b"zh") {
            Self::Chinese
        } else {
            Self::Other
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod language_tests {
    use super::LineBreakLanguage::{self, Chinese, Japanese, Other};

    #[test]
    fn explicit_script_overrides_line_break_language() {
        for (tag, expected) in [
            ("ko-Hani", Chinese),
            ("ja-Latn", Other),
            ("zh-Latn", Other),
            ("ja-Hans", Chinese),
            ("zh-Hira", Japanese),
            ("en-Jpan", Japanese),
            ("en-Hant", Chinese),
            ("en-Hans", Chinese),
            ("en-Hani", Chinese),
            ("en-Hanb", Chinese),
            ("en-Bopo", Chinese),
            ("en-Hrkt", Japanese),
            ("en-Hira", Japanese),
            ("en-Kana", Japanese),
            ("ja-Hang", Other),
            ("ja-Kore", Other),
            ("zh-Jamo", Other),
            ("zh-Zzzz", Other),
            ("JA-hAnS", Chinese),
            ("zh-cmn-Jpan", Japanese),
            ("ja-abc-def-ghi-Hans", Chinese),
            ("yue-Hant", Chinese),
        ] {
            let units: Vec<_> = tag.encode_utf16().collect();
            assert!(LineBreakLanguage::from_tag(&units) == expected, "{tag}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn only_the_script_position_changes_line_break_language() {
        for (tag, expected) in [
            ("ja", Japanese),
            ("ja-JP", Japanese),
            ("JA-jp", Japanese),
            ("zh", Chinese),
            ("zh-Hant-TW", Chinese),
            ("ja-x-Latn", Japanese),
            ("ja-u-ca-hans", Japanese),
            ("ja-JP-Latn", Japanese),
            ("ja-1996-Latn", Japanese),
            ("ja-fonipa-Latn", Japanese),
            ("en-x-Jpan", Other),
            ("en-u-ca-jpan", Other),
            ("abcd-xyz-Jpan", Other),
            ("x-Jpan", Other),
            ("jあ-Jpan", Other),
            ("japanesee-Jpan", Other),
            ("", Other),
        ] {
            let units: Vec<_> = tag.encode_utf16().collect();
            assert!(LineBreakLanguage::from_tag(&units) == expected, "{tag}");
        }
    }
}

// LibUnicode's CJKScriptClass, in declaration order.
mod cjk_script_class {
    pub(super) const OTHER: u8 = 0;
    pub(super) const CJK: u8 = 1;
    pub(super) const NEUTRAL: u8 = 2;
}

/// Which code units of `text` are in a run of CJK script.
pub(crate) fn cjk_script_runs(text: &[u16]) -> Vec<bool> {
    let mut characters = Vec::with_capacity(text.len());
    let mut lengths = Vec::with_capacity(text.len());
    for character in char::decode_utf16(text.iter().copied()) {
        let (class, bracket, length) = match character {
            Ok(character) => {
                let class = unicode_layout_cjk_script_class(u32::from(character));
                let bracket = if class == cjk_script_class::NEUTRAL {
                    unicode_layout_paired_bracket_key(u32::from(character))
                } else {
                    0
                };
                (class, bracket, character.len_utf16())
            }
            Err(_) => (cjk_script_class::OTHER, 0, 1),
        };
        characters.push((class, bracket));
        lengths.push(length);
    }
    let runs = resolve_cjk_script_runs(&characters);
    runs.iter()
        .zip(lengths)
        .flat_map(|(&in_run, length)| std::iter::repeat_n(in_run, length))
        .collect()
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-decor-4/#text-decoration-skip-ink-property
// [...] the UA should resolve the text into script runs as described in the "Implementation Notes" of [UAX24]
// "Unicode Script Property", in particular subsections 5.1 and 5.2.
// NB: A character of the Common or Inherited script takes the script of the character before it, or, at the start of
//     the text, of the first character after it that has a script of its own. But a closing bracket takes the script of
//     the opening bracket it pairs with, as does the text after it. Each character is a class and its paired-bracket key.
fn resolve_cjk_script_runs(characters: &[(u8, i32)]) -> Vec<bool> {
    // https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr24/#Common
    // [...] a stack depth of 63 is sufficient for most purposes.
    const OPEN_BRACKET_LIMIT: usize = 63;
    let mut runs = Vec::with_capacity(characters.len());
    let mut current = characters
        .iter()
        .find(|(class, _)| *class != cjk_script_class::NEUTRAL)
        .is_some_and(|(class, _)| *class == cjk_script_class::CJK);
    let mut open_brackets: Vec<(i32, bool)> = Vec::new();
    for &(class, bracket) in characters {
        if class != cjk_script_class::NEUTRAL {
            current = class == cjk_script_class::CJK;
        } else if bracket > 0 {
            if open_brackets.len() == OPEN_BRACKET_LIMIT {
                open_brackets.remove(0);
            }
            open_brackets.push((bracket, current));
        } else if bracket < 0
            && let Some(index) = open_brackets.iter().rposition(|(opening, _)| *opening == -bracket)
        {
            current = open_brackets[index].1;
            open_brackets.truncate(index);
        }
        runs.push(current);
    }
    runs
}

fn line_break_class(code_point: u32) -> u8 {
    unicode_layout_line_break_class(code_point)

pub(crate) const SOFT_HYPHEN: u16 = 0xad;

/// Whether a line that breaks right after `text[..end]` breaks at a soft hyphen there, and so ends in a hyphen: The
/// text has to end in a soft hyphen that no whitespace follows, since the line breaks at that whitespace instead.
pub(crate) fn breaks_at_soft_hyphen(text: &[u16], end: usize) -> bool {
    end > 0
        && text[end - 1] == SOFT_HYPHEN
        && text
            .get(end)
            .is_none_or(|&code_unit| !(code_unit < 0x80 && code_point_is_ascii_space(u32::from(code_unit))))
}

// LibUnicode's JoiningType, in declaration order.
mod joining_type {
    pub(super) const NON_JOINING: u8 = 0;
    pub(super) const TRANSPARENT: u8 = 1;
    pub(super) const DUAL_JOINING: u8 = 2;
    pub(super) const JOIN_CAUSING: u8 = 3;
    pub(super) const LEFT_JOINING: u8 = 4;
    pub(super) const RIGHT_JOINING: u8 = 5;
}

fn joining_type(code_point: u32) -> u8 {
    // OPTIMIZATION: Below U+0300, only U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN takes part in joining, as a transparent character.
    if code_point < 0x300 && code_point != 0xad {
        return joining_type::NON_JOINING;
    }
    unicode_layout_joining_type(code_point)
}

/// The joining type of the first character in `text[start..end]` that is not transparent to joining, such as most marks
/// are, which shaping looks past for the letter that a letter joins.
fn first_joining_type_in(text: &[u16], start: usize, end: usize) -> u8 {
    let mut index = start;
    while index < end {
        let code_point = code_point_at(text, index);
        let joining_type = joining_type(code_point);
        if joining_type != joining_type::TRANSPARENT {
            return joining_type;
        }
        index += code_unit_length_for_code_point(code_point);
    }
    joining_type::NON_JOINING
}

/// Like `first_joining_type_in()`, for the last such character.
fn last_joining_type_in(text: &[u16], start: usize, end: usize) -> u8 {
    let mut index = end;
    while index > start {
        let joining_type = joining_type(previous_code_point_at(text, &mut index));
        if joining_type != joining_type::TRANSPARENT {
            return joining_type;
        }
    }
    joining_type::NON_JOINING
}

/// Whether the letters at the edges of `range` join the letters of `text` around it, so that shaping the range on its
/// own gives them the forms they take in the whole text.
pub(crate) fn joining_context(text: &[u16], range: std::ops::Range<usize>) -> libgfx_rust::text_layout::JoiningContext {
    use joining_type::*;
    if range.is_empty() {
        return Default::default();
    }
    let joins_following = |joining_type| matches!(joining_type, DUAL_JOINING | JOIN_CAUSING | LEFT_JOINING);
    let joins_preceding = |joining_type| matches!(joining_type, DUAL_JOINING | JOIN_CAUSING | RIGHT_JOINING);
    libgfx_rust::text_layout::JoiningContext {
        joins_before: joins_preceding(first_joining_type_in(text, range.start, range.end))
            && joins_following(last_joining_type_in(text, 0, range.start)),
        joins_after: joins_following(last_joining_type_in(text, range.start, range.end))
            && joins_preceding(first_joining_type_in(text, range.end, text.len())),
    }
}

// Classifies a code point for direction-run splitting: strong LTR/RTL, direction-neutral Common, or ContextDependent
// (resolved from surrounding runs).
fn text_type_for_code_point(code_point: u32) -> u8 {
    use line_box_fragment::{
        GLYPH_TEXT_TYPE_COMMON as C, GLYPH_TEXT_TYPE_CONTEXT_DEPENDENT as X, GLYPH_TEXT_TYPE_LTR as L,
        GLYPH_TEXT_TYPE_RTL as R,
    };

    // Each ASCII character has a statically known bidi class.
    #[rustfmt::skip]
    const ASCII_TEXT_TYPES: [u8; 128] = [
        // 0x00-0x0F: Control characters (BN=Common, S/B/WS=ContextDependent)
        C, C, C, C, C, C, C, C, C, X, X, X, X, X, C, C,
        // 0x10-0x1F: Control characters
        C, C, C, C, C, C, C, C, C, C, C, C, X, X, X, X,
        // 0x20-0x2F: Space and punctuation
        X, C, C, X, X, X, C, C, C, C, C, X, X, X, X, X,
        // 0x30-0x3F: Digits and punctuation
        X, X, X, X, X, X, X, X, X, X, X, C, C, C, C, C,
        // 0x40-0x4F: @ and uppercase letters
        C, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L,
        // 0x50-0x5F: Uppercase letters and punctuation
        L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, C, C, C, C, C,
        // 0x60-0x6F: ` and lowercase letters
        C, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L,
        // 0x70-0x7F: Lowercase letters and punctuation
        L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, L, C, C, C, C, C,
    ];
    if let Some(&text_type) = ASCII_TEXT_TYPES.get(code_point as usize) {
        return text_type;
    }

    match unicode_layout_bidirectional_class(code_point) {
        // LibUnicode's BidiClass, in declaration order: AN, B, CS, NSM, EN, ES, ET, S, WS.
        0 | 1 | 3..=7 | 21 | 22 => X,
        // BN, FSI, ON, PDF, PDI.
        2 | 8 | 13..=15 => C,
        // L, LRE, LRI, LRO.
        9..=12 => L,
        // R, AL, RLE, RLI, RLO.
        16..=20 => R,
        _ => unreachable!("invalid bidi class"),
    }
}
