        let row = self.tree.push(image_node);
        self.commit_one_by_one(
            row,
            OneByOneRowSource::GeneratedImage {
                generator: element,
                generated_for,
                style_box,
                image,
            },
        );
        row
    }

    /// Makes the row of an image of generated content and places it in `node`, a pseudo-element's box.
    fn place_generated_image(
        &mut self,
        element: StyleNodeID,
        generated_for: u8,
        node: NodeSlotId,
        style_box: NodeSlotId,
        image: super::GeneratedImage,
    ) -> NodeSlotId {
        let row = self.push_generated_image_row(element, generated_for, style_box, image);
        self.place(node, row, true, ChildPosition::Append);
        row
    }

    /// Tells the document that the generated content of a pseudo-element of `element` shows the value of a `list-item`
    /// counter.
    fn report_list_item_counter_rendering(&mut self, element: StyleNodeID) {
        self.reports.push(FfiCommitMessage::new(
            element.raw(),
            FfiCommitMessageKind::ListItemCounterValueRendered,
        ));
    }

    /// The box a fresh build makes for the pseudo-element of kind `generated_for` of `element`, placed below `parent`,
    /// if it makes one.
    fn pseudo_element_box_shape(
        &self,
        element: StyleNodeID,
        generated_for: u8,
        parent: NodeSlotId,
    ) -> Option<PseudoElementBoxShape> {
        let engine = self.engine;
        if engine.element_box_kind(element) == ElementBoxKind::FrameSet {
            return None;
        }
        let view = engine.pseudo_published_style_view(element, pseudo_kind_of(generated_for))?;
        let pseudo_element = match generated_for {
            GENERATED_FOR_BEFORE => FfiPseudoElement::Before,
            GENERATED_FOR_AFTER => FfiPseudoElement::After,
            GENERATED_FOR_BACKDROP => FfiPseudoElement::Backdrop,
            _ => FfiPseudoElement::Marker,
        };
        let display = view.display();
        // NB: See plan_element_box_descendants(): a table-column-group keeps only its table-column children.
        if self.in_column_group_list && !display.is_table_column() {
            return None;
        }
        let mut facts = PseudoElementFacts {
            has_style: true,
            pseudo_element,
            content_type: if !view.content_is_keyword() {
                ComputedContentType::List
            } else if view.content_keyword_is_none() {
                ComputedContentType::None
            } else {
                ComputedContentType::Normal
            },
            display_is_none: display.is_none(),
            display_is_contents: display.is_contents(),
            display_is_list_item: display.is_list_item(),
            has_content_replacement: view.content_is_single_image(),
            normal_marker_has_content: false,
            marker_position_is_inside: false,
        };
        // A ::marker belongs to the list item box its element was built as, and takes its position and its default
        // content from that box's style.
        let is_marker_of_list_item =
            pseudo_element == FfiPseudoElement::Marker && self.tree.node(parent).kind() == NodeKind::ListItemBox;
        if is_marker_of_list_item && let Some(list_style) = self.tree.style_of(parent) {
            facts.normal_marker_has_content =
                !list_style.list_style_type_is_none() || list_style.list_style_image_is_set();
            facts.marker_position_is_inside = list_style.list_style_position_is_inside();
        }
        let decision = pseudo_element_decision(facts, is_marker_of_list_item);
        let is_list_item_marker = decision == PseudoElementDecision::Box && is_marker_of_list_item;
        let kind = match decision {
            PseudoElementDecision::None => return None,
            // The image box owns the image it replaces the pseudo-element's contents with.
            PseudoElementDecision::ContentReplacement => NodeKind::ImageBox,
            PseudoElementDecision::Contents => NodeKind::InlineNode,
            PseudoElementDecision::Box if is_list_item_marker => NodeKind::ListItemMarkerBox,
            PseudoElementDecision::Box => node_kind_for_display(display)?,
        };
        let mut flags = node_facts::construction_flags(kind, true, 0) | NodeFlag::IsPseudoElementPrincipalBox as u32;
        if is_list_item_marker && facts.marker_position_is_inside {
            flags |= NodeFlag::ListMarkerIsInside as u32;
        }
        let display = used_display_of_box(kind, flags, display);
        let box_facts = if decision == PseudoElementDecision::Contents {
            box_facts_of_display(display) | box_fact::HAS_STYLE
        } else {
            (box_facts_of_style(view) & !box_fact::OF_DISPLAY)
                | box_facts_of_display(display)
                | item_context_facts(kind, flags, display)
        };
        Some(PseudoElementBoxShape {
            kind,
            flags,
            box_facts,
            display,
            is_list_item_marker,
            marker_position_is_inside: facts.marker_position_is_inside,
            decision,
        })
    }

    /// Places the box `node` of a pseudo-element among the descendants of `parent`.
    fn place_pseudo_element_box(
        &mut self,
        parent: NodeSlotId,
        node: NodeSlotId,
        is_outside_list_item_marker: bool,
        position: ChildPosition,
    ) {
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#list-style-position-outside
        // "the marker box is a block container and is placed outside the principal block box"
        if is_outside_list_item_marker {
            let first_child = self.tree.node(parent).first_child();
            self.tree.attach(parent, node, first_child);
        } else {
            let is_inline_outside = self.tree.node(node).has_fact(box_fact::INLINE_OUTSIDE);
            self.place(parent, node, is_inline_outside, position);
        }
    }

    /// The box of the `::before`, `::after` or `::marker` of the element whose child list the walk plans again that the
    /// walk can keep: no mark asked for it again, a fresh build makes a box of the same kind for it, and it is attached
    /// in the list. A `::marker` goes first among the boxes whatever comes before it in the walk.
    fn keepable_pseudo_element_row(
        &self,
        element: StyleNodeID,
        generated_for: u8,
        kind: NodeKind,
        flags: u32,
    ) -> Option<NodeSlotId> {
        let unit = self.unit?;
        if !unit.keeps_pseudo_element_boxes || self.unit_entry >= unit.fresh_from_entry {
            return None;
        }
        // NB: A replaced box lays out the children of its shadow root in its first anonymous child, which is a list of
        //     the list, and may be its ::before box.
        if node_facts::kind_is_replaced_box(self.tree.node(self.root_row).kind()) {
            return None;
        }
        let arena = self.arena;
        let row = arena.bound_pseudo_element_row(element, generated_for);
        if row.is_invalid() {
            return None;
        }
        let data = arena.data(row);
        const PLACEMENT_FLAGS: u32 = NodeFlag::IsPseudoElementPrincipalBox as u32 | NodeFlag::ListMarkerIsInside as u32;
        if data.kind.get() != kind || (data.flags.get() ^ flags) & PLACEMENT_FLAGS != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let entry_top = arena.list_entry_top_row(row);
        if !arena.is_in_child_list_of(entry_top, self.root_row) {
            return None;
        }
        if generated_for != GENERATED_FOR_MARKER && arena.node_pre_order_label(entry_top) <= self.last_kept_label {
            return None;
        }
        Some(row)
    }

    fn plan_text(&mut self, text: StyleNodeID) {
        let engine = self.engine;
        let parent = self.current_parent();
        // NB: See plan_element_box_descendants(): a table-column-group keeps only its table-column children.
        if self.tree.node(parent).kind() == NodeKind::FrameSetBox || self.in_column_group_list {
            self.note_text_without_box(text);
            self.note_stale_text(text);
            return;
        }
        let text_is_ascii_whitespace = engine.text_is_ascii_whitespace(text);
        if text_is_ascii_whitespace && !self.whitespace_text_needs_box(parent, text) {
            self.note_text_without_box(text);
            self.note_stale_text(text);
            return;
        }
        let facts = engine.text_style_parent_facts(text);
        let needs_style_wrapper = crate::layout::tree_builder::display_contents_text_needs_style_wrapper(
            facts.has_style_parent,
            facts.parent_display_is_contents,
            text_is_ascii_whitespace,
            facts.parent_collapses_whitespace,
        );
        if self.in_unit_list && self.plan_kept_text(text, needs_style_wrapper) {
            return;
        }
        let construction_facts = engine.element_construction_facts(text);
        let mut flags = node_facts::construction_flags(NodeKind::TextNode, false, construction_facts);
        let is_in_user_agent_shadow_tree =
            construction_facts & element_construction_fact::IS_IN_USER_AGENT_SHADOW_TREE != 0;
        if crate::layout::tree_builder::text_produces_line_box_fragment_when_empty(
            engine,
            text,
            is_in_user_agent_shadow_tree,
        ) {
            flags |= NodeFlag::ProducesLineBoxFragmentWhenEmpty as u32;
        }
        if self.arena.style_node_has_scroll_offset(text) {
            flags |= NodeFlag::HasScrollOffset as u32;
        }
        let mut text_facts = box_fact::INLINE_OUTSIDE;
        if let Some(parent) = engine
            .text_parent(text)
            .filter(|parent| parent.element_index().is_some())
            && !engine.publishes_no_pseudo_element_records(parent)
            && self.holds_highlight_style(parent)
        {
            text_facts |= box_fact::PARENT_HOLDS_HIGHLIGHT_STYLE;
        }
        self.places_boxes_of_unbound_nodes |= self.arena.bound_row(text).is_invalid();
        let text_node = self.tree.push(PlanNode::new(NodeKind::TextNode, flags, text_facts));
        *self.tree.row_mut(text_node).dom_paint_facts.get_mut() = engine.node_dom_paint_facts(text);
        self.tree.set_columns(
            text_node,
            super::RowColumns {
                style_record: 0,
                style_node: Some(text),
                unique_node_id: 0,
                ..Default::default()
            },
        );
        if needs_style_wrapper {
            // NB: The children of the wrapper are derived as the commit attaches them, as the wrapper's style is.
            let wrapper = self.tree.push(PlanNode::new(
                NodeKind::InlineNode,
                node_facts::construction_flags(NodeKind::InlineNode, true, 0) | NodeFlag::ChildrenAreInline as u32,
                box_facts_of_display(FfiDisplay::outside_and_inside(
                    crate::css::css_enums::display_outside::INLINE,
                    crate::css::css_enums::display_inside::FLOW,
                    false,
                )) | box_fact::HAS_STYLE
                    | box_fact::OWN_CHILDREN_DERIVED_ON_COMMIT,
            ));
            self.place(parent, wrapper, true, ChildPosition::Append);
            self.commit_one_by_one(
                wrapper,
                OneByOneRowSource::DisplayContentsTextWrapper {
                    text,
                    record: facts.style_record,
                },
            );
            self.tree.attach(wrapper, text_node, NodeSlotId::INVALID);
        } else {
            self.place(parent, text_node, true, ChildPosition::Append);
        }
        self.list_text_row(text_node, text);
        self.note_text_with_box(text);
    }

    /// Plans `text`, an entry of the child list the walk plans again that renders, as the box it has, if the walk can keep
    /// it (see [`Self::keepable_row`]), and answers whether it did. A text whose box a `::first-letter` or a writing
    /// suggestion split is built again, which splits it again.
    fn plan_kept_text(&mut self, text: StyleNodeID, needs_style_wrapper: bool) -> bool {
        let Some((row, entry_top)) = self.keepable_row(text) else {
            return false;
        };
        let arena = self.arena;
        if arena.text_has_source_range(row) || arena.data(row).kind.get() != NodeKind::TextNode {
            return false;
        }
        let has_style_wrapper = entry_top != row;
        if has_style_wrapper != needs_style_wrapper {
            assert!(
                !self.unit.is_some_and(|unit| unit.verifies_kept_boxes),
                "the kept layout box of {text:?} is not in the style wrapper a fresh build makes"
            );
            return false;
        }
        let top = arena.data(entry_top);
        let facts = if has_style_wrapper {
            box_facts_of_display(FfiDisplay::outside_and_inside(
                crate::css::css_enums::display_outside::INLINE,
                crate::css::css_enums::display_inside::FLOW,
                false,
            )) | box_fact::HAS_STYLE
                | box_fact::OWN_CHILDREN_DERIVED_ON_COMMIT
        } else {
            box_fact::INLINE_OUTSIDE
        };
        let node = PlanNode {
            style: top.style.get(),
            ..PlanNode::new(top.kind.get(), top.flags.get(), facts)
        };
        self.place_kept_row(entry_top, node, false);
        self.note_text_with_box(text);
        true
    }

    /// Places a box in the child list of `parent`, by the insertion rules of [`super::child_list`].
    fn place(&mut self, parent: NodeSlotId, node: NodeSlotId, is_inline_outside: bool, position: ChildPosition) {
        self.tree
            .insert_node_into_inline_or_block_ancestor(parent, node, is_inline_outside, position);
    }

    /// Whether a flat-tree ancestor of the element keeps it out of the rendered tree. Only an element ever hides a
    /// subtree, and no record at all means the style update pass skipped a display:none subtree.
    fn has_unrendered_flat_tree_ancestor(&self, element: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        let mut ancestor = self.arena.flat_tree_parent(element);
        while let Some(current) = ancestor {
            if !self
                .engine
                .element_published_box_facts(current)
                .is_some_and(|facts| !facts.display.is_none())
            {
                return true;
            }
            ancestor = self.arena.flat_tree_parent(current);
        }
        false
    }

    /// Whether the element published a record for a highlight pseudo-element.
    fn holds_highlight_style(&self, element: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        element_holds_highlight_style(self.engine, element)
    }

    /// A text's contribution to what comes before later white space texts among its layout parent's boxes.
    fn text_preceding_content(&self, text: StyleNodeID, has_box: bool) -> Option<PrecedingContent> {
        let engine = self.engine;
        let (is_empty, ends_in_white_space) = engine.text_data_ends(text);
        let is_collapsing_whitespace =
            engine.text_is_ascii_whitespace(text) && !is_empty && engine.text_collapses_white_space(text) == Some(true);
        if is_collapsing_whitespace {
            return Some(PrecedingContent::Text {
                ends_in_collapsible_white_space: true,
            });
        }
        if !has_box {
            return None;
        }
        Some(PrecedingContent::Text {
            ends_in_collapsible_white_space: ends_in_white_space
                && engine.text_collapses_white_space(text) == Some(true),
        })
    }

    /// Notes that the text node `text` gets no box, which clears what it held. A text that holds no box and no layout
    /// tree update mark holds nothing to clear.
    fn note_stale_text(&mut self, text: StyleNodeID) {
        if !self.arena.bound_row(text).is_invalid() || self.arena.layout_tree_update_marks().holds_any(text) {
            self.stale_subtrees.push((text, StaleSubtreeScope::Inclusive));
        }
    }

    fn note_text_with_box(&mut self, text: StyleNodeID) {
        if let Some(content) = self.text_preceding_content(text, true) {
            self.preceding_content.push(content);
        }
    }

    fn note_text_without_box(&mut self, text: StyleNodeID) {
        if let Some(content) = self.text_preceding_content(text, false) {
            self.preceding_content.push(content);
        }
    }

    /// The nearest box before a text among the boxes of `layout_parent`.
    fn preceding_box(&self, layout_parent: NodeSlotId) -> PrecedingBox {
        for content in self.preceding_content[self.preceding_content_start..].iter().rev() {
            match *content {
                PrecedingContent::Text {
                    ends_in_collapsible_white_space,
                } => {
                    return PrecedingBox::Text {
                        ends_in_collapsible_white_space,
                    };
                }
                PrecedingContent::Box(node) => {
                    let data = self.tree.node(node);
                    if crate::layout::tree_builder::node_kind_is_node_with_style(data.kind())
                        && self.tree.is_out_of_flow_child_of(layout_parent, node)
                    {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if data.kind() == NodeKind::BreakNode {
                        return PrecedingBox::LineStart;
                    }
                    if data.is_table_non_root_for_table_fixup() {
                        return PrecedingBox::TableInternal;
                    }
                    if data.has_fact(box_fact::INLINE_OUTSIDE) {
                        return PrecedingBox::InlineLevel;
                    }
                    return PrecedingBox::LineStart;
                }
            }
        }
        PrecedingBox::Nothing
    }

    /// Whether the text node `text`, which holds nothing but white space, gets a box among the children of
    /// `layout_parent`.
    fn whitespace_text_needs_box(&self, layout_parent: NodeSlotId, text: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
        let engine = self.engine;
        let parent = self.tree.node(layout_parent);
        if parent.is_svg_content() {
            // SVG renders text only inside a text content element.
            let mut ancestor = layout_parent;
            loop {
                let node = self.tree.node(ancestor);
                match node.kind() {
                    NodeKind::SVGTextBox | NodeKind::SVGTextPathBox => return true,
                    NodeKind::SVGSVGBox => return false,
                    _ => {}
                }
                if node.parent().is_invalid() {
                    break;
                }
                ancestor = node.parent();
            }
            // Above the plan's root, the ancestors are rows of the tree.
            let mut row = self.arena.data(self.root_row).parent.get();
            while !row.is_invalid() {
                match self.arena.data(row).kind.get() {
                    NodeKind::SVGTextBox | NodeKind::SVGTextPathBox => return true,
                    NodeKind::SVGSVGBox => return false,
                    _ => row = self.arena.data(row).parent.get(),
                }
            }
            return false;
        }
        if engine.text_collapses_white_space(text) != Some(true)
            || crate::layout::tree_builder::text_produces_line_box_fragment_when_empty(
                engine,
                text,
                engine.text_is_in_user_agent_shadow_tree(text),
            )
        {
            return true;
        }
        let preceding = self.preceding_box(layout_parent);
        if parent.has_fact(box_fact::FLEX_OR_GRID_INSIDE | box_fact::MATH_INSIDE) {
            // Only white space that continues a run of text joins an item; a run of nothing but white space is none.
            return preceding
                == PrecedingBox::Text {
                    ends_in_collapsible_white_space: false,
                };
        }
        match preceding {
            // An inline box keeps the white space that starts it, and an inside marker comes before it once it is
            // built, after the children.
            PrecedingBox::Nothing => {
                parent.kind() == NodeKind::InlineNode
                    || (parent.kind() == NodeKind::ListItemBox && parent.has_fact(box_fact::LIST_STYLE_POSITION_INSIDE))
            }
            PrecedingBox::Text {
                ends_in_collapsible_white_space,
            } => !ends_in_collapsible_white_space,
            PrecedingBox::InlineLevel => true,
            PrecedingBox::TableInternal => !parent.has_fact(box_fact::TABULAR_CONTAINER),
            PrecedingBox::LineStart => false,
        }
    }
}

/// Whether the element published a record for a highlight pseudo-element.
/// The box a fresh build makes for a pseudo-element, see [`Planner::pseudo_element_box_shape`].
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct PseudoElementBoxShape {
    kind: NodeKind,
    flags: u32,
    box_facts: u32,
    /// The display of the box, which the commit gives it.
    display: FfiDisplay,
    is_list_item_marker: bool,
    marker_position_is_inside: bool,
    decision: PseudoElementDecision,
}

pub(crate) fn element_holds_highlight_style(engine: &RetainedState, element: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
    crate::painting::selection::HighlightPseudoElement::ALL
        .iter()
        .any(|highlight| {
            engine
                .pseudo_published_style_record(element, highlight.pseudo_kind())
                .is_some()
        })
        || !engine.pseudo_published_custom_highlight_records(element).is_empty()
}

/// What the walk reads of an element to plan its box, before it places anything: what the style mirror published for
/// it, and what its row is stamped with. It depends on nothing the walk decided but whether the walk plans the
/// content of an SVG mask, clip path or pattern, so the walk reads it for the children of a long child list ahead of
/// placing them, on as many threads as it has.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct PreparedElement {
    type_facts: u32,
    /// What its published style says, or `None` where nothing published a style for the element.
    style: Option<PreparedStyle>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct PreparedStyle {
    record: u64,
    /// The computed `display`.
    display: FfiDisplay,
    content_visibility: u8,
    may_change_counters: bool,
    box_kind: ElementBoxKind,
    layout_kind: ElementLayoutKind,
    /// The element's principal box, where its display makes one.
    principal_box: Option<PreparedBox>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct PreparedBox {
    kind: NodeKind,
    construction_facts: u32,
    publishes_no_pseudo_element_records: bool,
    has_style_containment: bool,
    flags: u32,
    /// See [`box_fact`].
    box_facts: u32,
    payloads: crate::layout::node_data::LayoutStyleRef,
    /// See `planned_style_facts_for_kind`.
    style_facts: u32,
    /// Whether the element has no box bound to it.
    is_unbound: bool,
    /// What the walk stamps the box's row with, unless the builder's own steps stamp it.
    stamped_row: Option<StampedRow>,
}

/// What an element's row is stamped with besides what its plan node holds.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct StampedRow {
    /// The flags the row's style and scroll offset add.
    flags: u32,
    dom_paint_facts: u8,
    spans: crate::css::style::tree::TableSpans,
    unique_node_id: i64,
}

/// What decides whether the walk keeps an element's box: it keeps a box whose shape is the one a fresh build gives.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
struct BoxShape {
    kind: NodeKind,
    /// See [`NodeFlag::CONSTRUCTION`].
    flags: u32,
    /// See [`used_display_of_box`].
    display: FfiDisplay,
}

/// The shape of the principal box a fresh build makes from `style`, if any.
fn fresh_box_shape(style: &PreparedStyle) -> Option<BoxShape> {
    let principal_box = style.principal_box.as_ref()?;
    Some(BoxShape {
        kind: principal_box.kind,
        flags: principal_box.flags,
        display: used_display_of_box(principal_box.kind, principal_box.flags, style.display),
    })
}

/// The shape of the box `row` as the style it shows makes it.
fn row_box_shape(arena: &LayoutNodeArena, row: NodeSlotId) -> Option<BoxShape> {
    let data = arena.data(row);
    let (kind, flags) = (data.kind.get(), data.flags.get() & NodeFlag::CONSTRUCTION);
    let display = arena.style_view(row)?.display();
    Some(BoxShape {
        kind,
        flags,
        display: used_display_of_box(kind, flags, display),
    })
}

/// Reads what the walk needs of `element` to plan its box, for a walk that plans the content of an SVG mask or clip
/// path, or of an SVG pattern, as `layout_svg_mask_or_clip_path` and `layout_svg_pattern` say.
fn prepare_element(
    engine: &RetainedState,
    arena: &LayoutNodeArena,
    element: StyleNodeID,
    layout_svg_mask_or_clip_path: bool,
    layout_svg_pattern: bool,
) -> PreparedElement {
    let inputs = engine.element_layout_inputs(element);
    let type_facts = inputs.adjustment_facts;
    let Some(published) = inputs.record else {
        return PreparedElement {
            type_facts,
            style: None,
        };
    };
    let summary = published.summary();
    let record = published.raw;
    let box_kind = inputs.box_kind;
    let published_display = summary.display;
    let mut prepared_style = PreparedStyle {
        record,
        display: published_display,
        content_visibility: summary.content_visibility,
        may_change_counters: summary.may_change_counters,
        box_kind,
        layout_kind: ElementLayoutKind::Normal,
        principal_box: None,
    };
    if published_display.is_none() || published_display.is_contents() {
        return PreparedElement {
            type_facts,
            style: Some(prepared_style),
        };
    }
    let has_content_replacement = summary.content_is_single_image;
    let construction_facts = inputs.construction_facts;
    let uses_button_layout = construction_facts & element_construction_fact::USES_BUTTON_LAYOUT != 0;
    let layout_kind = crate::layout::tree_builder::element_layout_kind(
        has_content_replacement,
        type_facts,
        layout_svg_mask_or_clip_path,
        layout_svg_pattern,
    );
    prepared_style.layout_kind = layout_kind;
    // NB: A replaced element whose kind of box follows from its display gets the kind for the display it uses, so a
    //     table display never makes it a table part. And as an atomic inline, an inline one gets a block container.
    let kind_display = if node_facts::construction_facts_name_replaced_element(construction_facts) {
        let display = crate::layout::tree_builder::used_display_of_replaced_element(published_display);
        if display.is_inline_outside() && display.is_flow_inside() {
            FfiDisplay::outside_and_inside(display.outside, crate::css::css_enums::display_inside::FLOW_ROOT, false)
        } else {
            display
        }
    } else {
        published_display
    };
    let kind = match layout_kind {
        ElementLayoutKind::ContentReplacement => Some(NodeKind::ImageBox),
        ElementLayoutKind::SvgMask => Some(NodeKind::SVGMaskBox),
        ElementLayoutKind::SvgClipPath => Some(NodeKind::SVGClipBox),
        ElementLayoutKind::SvgPattern => Some(NodeKind::SVGPatternBox),
        ElementLayoutKind::Normal => match node_kind_for_element_box_kind(box_kind, kind_display, summary.appearance) {
            Some(NodeKind::ListItemBox) if uses_button_layout => Some(NodeKind::BlockContainer),
            kind => kind,
        },
    };
    let Some(kind) = kind else {
        return PreparedElement {
            type_facts,
            style: Some(prepared_style),
        };
    };
    let publishes_no_pseudo_element_records = engine.publishes_no_pseudo_element_records(element);
    let holds_highlight_style = !publishes_no_pseudo_element_records && element_holds_highlight_style(engine, element);
    let groups = published.payloads;
    let mut flags = node_facts::construction_flags(kind, false, construction_facts);
    // A media element renders the children of its shadow root, such as its controls.
    if matches!(kind, NodeKind::AudioBox | NodeKind::VideoBox) && engine.shadow_root_of(element).is_some() {
        flags |= NodeFlag::ReplacedBoxCanHaveChildren as u32;
    }
    let mut box_facts = summary.box_facts;
    let display = used_display_of_box(kind, flags, published_display);
    box_facts = (box_facts & !box_fact::OF_DISPLAY) | box_facts_of_display(display);
    box_facts |= item_context_facts(kind, flags, display);
    // NB: A row of a kind its element asks for itself, or whose display the build adjusts, is made by the builder's
    //     own steps, which the planned row's facts do not cover.
    if box_kind != ElementBoxKind::FromDisplay
        || layout_kind != ElementLayoutKind::Normal
        || display != published_display
        || flags & NodeFlag::IsReplacedElement as u32 != 0
    {
        box_facts |= box_fact::STAMPED_BY_BUILDER;
    }
    // NB: The builder's own steps adjust a replaced element's display, which its children are derived from.
    if box_facts & box_fact::STAMPED_BY_BUILDER != 0 && flags & NodeFlag::IsReplacedElement as u32 != 0 {
        box_facts |= box_fact::OWN_CHILDREN_DERIVED_ON_COMMIT;
    }
    if has_content_replacement {
        box_facts |= box_fact::OWNS_CONTENT_REPLACEMENT_IMAGE;
    }
    if holds_highlight_style {
        box_facts |= box_fact::HOLDS_HIGHLIGHT_STYLE;
    }
    let style_facts = summary.style_facts(kind);
    let stamped_row = (box_facts & box_fact::STAMPED_BY_BUILDER == 0).then(|| {
        let mut flags = crate::layout::layout_node_arena::planned_style_flags(style_facts);
        if arena.style_node_has_scroll_offset(element) {
            flags |= NodeFlag::HasScrollOffset as u32;
        }
        StampedRow {
            flags,
            dom_paint_facts: engine.node_dom_paint_facts(element),
            spans: engine.element_table_spans(element),
            unique_node_id: engine.element_unique_node_id(element),
        }
    });
    prepared_style.principal_box = Some(PreparedBox {
        kind,
        construction_facts,
        publishes_no_pseudo_element_records,
        has_style_containment: summary.has_style_containment,
        flags,
        box_facts,
        payloads: crate::layout::node_data::LayoutStyleRef::of_groups(groups),
        style_facts,
        is_unbound: arena.bound_row(element).is_invalid(),
        stamped_row,
    });
    PreparedElement {
        type_facts,
        style: Some(prepared_style),
    }
}

/// Whether a box of `kind`, with `flags`, holds the boxes of its children. See `node_facts::node_can_have_children`.
fn kind_can_have_children(kind: NodeKind, flags: u32) -> bool {
    match kind {
        NodeKind::BreakNode | NodeKind::WordBreakOpportunityNode => false,
        NodeKind::AudioBox | NodeKind::VideoBox => flags & NodeFlag::ReplacedBoxCanHaveChildren as u32 != 0,
        NodeKind::SVGSVGBox => true,
        kind if node_facts::kind_is_replaced_box(kind) => false,
        _ => true,
    }
}

/// Whether the box of an element can hold the boxes of its ::before and ::after pseudo-elements. A form control whose
/// content the user agent supplies holds none: a text control, a range input, an input element shown as a button, or a
/// select.
fn box_can_have_generated_children(kind: NodeKind, flags: u32, construction_facts: u32) -> bool {
    if matches!(
        kind,
        NodeKind::TextInputBox | NodeKind::TextAreaBox | NodeKind::RangeInputBox
    ) {
        return false;
    }
    if flags & NodeFlag::IsHtmlInputElement as u32 != 0 && flags & NodeFlag::UsesButtonLayout as u32 != 0 {
        return false;
    }
    construction_facts & element_construction_fact::IS_HTML_SELECT_ELEMENT == 0
}

/// Whether the children of a box of `kind` are its flex or grid items, as `formatting_context_type_created_by_node_data`
/// decides it for a box whose display is flex or grid.
fn item_context_facts(kind: NodeKind, flags: u32, display: FfiDisplay) -> u32 {
    if !(display.is_flex_inside() || display.is_grid_inside())
        || matches!(
            kind,
            NodeKind::SVGSVGBox | NodeKind::FrameSetBox | NodeKind::FieldSetBox
        )
        || node_facts::kind_is_replaced_box(kind)
        || !kind_can_have_children(kind, flags)
    {
        return 0;
    }
    if display.is_flex_inside() {
        box_fact::ESTABLISHES_FLEX_ITEMS
    } else {
        box_fact::ESTABLISHES_GRID_ITEMS
    }
}

/// The boxes of a job.
struct JobSpec {
    roots: Vec<JobRoot>,
}

/// A box of a job: where it goes in the deferring walk's plan, its slot, what its stand-in row is, the ancestor facts
/// and MathML layout of the box, which the job derives its children's facts from, and how many of its children count
/// as inline-level or in flow, and as block-level and in flow.
struct JobRoot {
    root: DeferredRoot,
    stand_in: PlanNode,
    ancestor_facts: u8,
    math_layout_kind: MathLayoutKind,
}

/// What the jobs of one build take from the walk that made them.
struct JobShared<'a> {
    claims: super::ChunkClaims,
    fork_budget: Option<ForkBudget>,
    writing_suggestion_parent: Option<StyleNodeID>,
    enclosing_ancestor_rows: &'a [NodeSlotId],
    root_row: NodeSlotId,
    /// The style of the box the build plans the descendants of, which the row standing in for it in a job shows.
    root_style: Option<ComputedValuesView<'a>>,
    /// The jobs of the build handed to the style layout threads, which the thread that started the build runs too
    /// once its own are done (see [`Planner::run_jobs_left`]).
    handed_on: std::sync::Mutex<std::collections::VecDeque<std::sync::Arc<JobSlot>>>,
    progress: JobProgress,
    /// Where the walks of the build name the counters they find, see `counter_walk.rs`.
    counter_ids: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32>,
    /// Whether the walks list the owners that a build before stored a counters set for which they no longer need: none
    /// where the build resolves every owner of the document, or where no owner has a set.
    removes_stale_counters_sets: bool,
    /// See `CounterWalk::resolves_counters`.
    resolves_counters: bool,
}

/// How many children a child list has at least for the walk to plan it in runs, how many children a run has at least,
/// and how far the walk looks for a child a run may start with.
const MINIMUM_CHILDREN_TO_PLAN_IN_RUNS: usize = 512;
const MINIMUM_CHILDREN_PER_RUN: usize = 128;
const RUN_START_SEARCH_LENGTH: usize = 32;

/// How many children of a long child list one task reads ahead, and how many the walk reads ahead before it places them.
const PREPARED_CHILDREN_PER_TASK: usize = 128;
const PREPARED_CHILDREN_PER_WINDOW: usize = 4096;

/// How the walk of a build that makes jobs splits child lists: how many children a list has at least for each way of
/// splitting it, and how big the pieces are.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct ListSplits {
    /// See [`ForkBudget::MINIMUM_CHILDREN_TO_SPLIT`] and [`ForkBudget::MINIMUM_ROOTS_PER_JOB`].
    children_to_split: usize,
    minimum_roots_per_job: usize,
    /// See [`MINIMUM_CHILDREN_TO_PLAN_IN_RUNS`] and [`MINIMUM_CHILDREN_PER_RUN`].
    children_to_plan_in_runs: usize,
    children_per_run: usize,
    /// See [`PREPARED_CHILDREN_PER_TASK`] and [`PREPARED_CHILDREN_PER_WINDOW`].
    prepared_children_per_task: usize,
    prepared_children_per_window: usize,
}

impl ListSplits {
    const DEFAULT: Self = Self {
        children_to_split: ForkBudget::MINIMUM_CHILDREN_TO_SPLIT,
        minimum_roots_per_job: ForkBudget::MINIMUM_ROOTS_PER_JOB,
        children_to_plan_in_runs: MINIMUM_CHILDREN_TO_PLAN_IN_RUNS,
        children_per_run: MINIMUM_CHILDREN_PER_RUN,
        prepared_children_per_task: PREPARED_CHILDREN_PER_TASK,
        prepared_children_per_window: PREPARED_CHILDREN_PER_WINDOW,
    };

    /// NB: Where the document forces parallel layout (see [`LayoutNodeArena::forces_parallel_layout`]), each way of
    ///     splitting a list takes the fewest children it can split, so that tests of a few dozen elements reach it.
    const FORCED: Self = Self {
        children_to_split: 2,
        minimum_roots_per_job: 1,
        children_to_plan_in_runs: 8,
        children_per_run: 2,
        prepared_children_per_task: 2,
        prepared_children_per_window: 8,
    };

    /// How many children a child list has at least for the walk to plan it from a list of them: read ahead in windows,
    /// or in runs.
    fn children_of_a_long_list(&self) -> usize {
        self.prepared_children_per_task * 2
    }
}

//! What a tree build reads of an element's style record, read from its groups in one go.

use crate::css::computed_value_views::ComputedValuesView;

/// See the module documentation.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct StyleBoxSummary {
    /// The computed `display`.
    pub(crate) display: FfiDisplay,
    /// The computed `content-visibility`.
    pub(crate) content_visibility: u8,
    /// The computed `appearance`.
    pub(crate) appearance: u8,
    /// See [`super::box_facts_of_style`].
    pub(crate) box_facts: u32,
    /// See [`crate::layout::layout_node_arena::planned_record_style_facts`].
    record_style_facts: u32,
    /// Whether the style names a counter in `counter-reset`, `counter-increment` or `counter-set`, or is a list
    /// item's, which increments `list-item`.
    pub(crate) may_change_counters: bool,
    /// Whether the style replaces the element's contents with a single image.
    pub(crate) content_is_single_image: bool,
    /// See [`crate::painting::style_queries::has_style_containment`].
    pub(crate) has_style_containment: bool,
}

impl StyleBoxSummary {
    /// The summary of the style `style` views.
    pub(crate) fn of(style: ComputedValuesView<'_>) -> Self {
        let display = style.display();
        Self {
            display,
            content_visibility: style.content_visibility(),
            appearance: style.appearance(),

        crate::layout::layout_node_arena::planned_style_facts_for_kind(self.record_style_facts, kind)
    }
}

//! Table fixup of child lists, steps 1 to 3 of the fixup algorithm, written once for the two trees it goes over: the
//! plan of a walk, which fixes up each list it planned all of as the list closes, and the arena, where the commit fixes
//! up the lists the walk left to it. The steps that read and change the child list of a box read and change only that
//! list and those of the anonymous boxes in it, so fixing up each list on its own makes the tree passes over the whole
//! tree make.
//! https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#fixup-algorithm

use super::{OneByOneRowSource, PlanNode, PlanTree, RowCommittedOneByOne, box_fact};
use crate::css::style::tree::StyleNodeID;
use crate::layout::FfiDisplay;
use crate::layout::node_data::{NodeFlag, NodeKind};
use crate::layout::node_facts;
use libcompositing_rust::node_slot_id::NodeSlotId;

/// The kind of anonymous box table fixup generates around a sequence of children.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum AnonymousTableBoxKind {
    TableRow,
    TableCell,
    Table,
    InlineTable,
}

impl AnonymousTableBoxKind {
    /// The style the box takes from the box it is generated in, and the kind of box it is.
    pub(crate) fn style_and_node_kind(self) -> (crate::css::style::layout_style::AnonymousStyleKind, NodeKind) {
        use crate::css::style::layout_style::AnonymousStyleKind;
        match self {
            Self::TableRow => (AnonymousStyleKind::TableRow, NodeKind::Box),
            Self::TableCell => (AnonymousStyleKind::TableCell, NodeKind::BlockContainer),
            Self::Table => (AnonymousStyleKind::Table, NodeKind::Box),
            Self::InlineTable => (AnonymousStyleKind::InlineTable, NodeKind::Box),
        }
    }
}

/// A tree table fixup goes over.
pub(crate) trait TableFixupTree {
    fn parent(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> NodeSlotId;
    fn first_child(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> NodeSlotId;
    fn next_sibling(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> NodeSlotId;
    fn previous_sibling(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> NodeSlotId;
    fn kind(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> NodeKind;
    fn has_flag(&self, node: NodeSlotId, flag: NodeFlag) -> bool;
    fn is_out_of_flow(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> bool;
    fn is_inline_outside(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> bool;
    /// The display of the box `node`, the one its box uses; that of its parent for a text, whose style it carries.
    fn display(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> FfiDisplay;
    /// Whether `text`, a text, holds nothing but white space.
    fn text_is_white_space(&mut self, text: NodeSlotId) -> bool;
    /// Takes `nodes` out of the tree, as if they were `display: none`.
    fn remove(&mut self, nodes: &[NodeSlotId]);
    /// Makes an anonymous box of `kind` below `parent`, before `before`, and moves `nodes`, consecutive children of
    /// `parent`, into it. Answers the box.
    fn wrap_in_anonymous_table_box(
        &mut self,
        parent: NodeSlotId,
        nodes: &[NodeSlotId],
        before: NodeSlotId,
        kind: AnonymousTableBoxKind,
    ) -> NodeSlotId;
    fn set_children_are_inline(&mut self, node: NodeSlotId, children_are_inline: bool);
    /// Wraps `table_root` in a new anonymous table wrapper box, which takes the table's outer properties.
    fn wrap_table_root(&mut self, table_root: NodeSlotId);
}

/// Whether a walk over a child list goes into the children of the box it visits.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Visit {
    Children,
    SkipChildren,
}

/// Fixes up the parts of tables in the child lists of `owners`, each with those of the anonymous boxes in it: steps 1
/// to 3 of the fixup algorithm, each over every list before the next. Answers the table roots the steps reached.
pub(crate) fn fix_up_tables_in_child_lists(tree: &mut impl TableFixupTree, owners: &[NodeSlotId]) -> Vec<NodeSlotId> {
    for &owner in owners {
        remove_irrelevant_boxes(tree, owner);
    }
    for &owner in owners {
        generate_missing_child_wrappers(tree, owner);
    }
    let mut table_roots = Vec::new();
    for &owner in owners {
        generate_missing_parents(tree, owner, &mut table_roots);
    }
    table_roots
}

fn is_table_track(display: FfiDisplay) -> bool {
    display.is_table_row() || display.is_table_column()
}

fn is_table_track_group(display: FfiDisplay) -> bool {
    // Unless explicitly mentioned otherwise, mentions of table-row-groups in this spec also encompass the specialized
    // table-header-groups and table-footer-groups.
    display.is_table_row_group()
        || display.is_table_header_group()
        || display.is_table_footer_group()
        || display.is_table_column_group()
}

/// The display of `node` the steps read.
pub(crate) fn display_for_table_fixup(tree: &impl TableFixupTree, node: NodeSlotId) -> FfiDisplay {
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#fixup-algorithm
    // For the purposes of these rules, out-of-flow elements are represented as inline elements of zero width and
    // height. Their containing blocks are chosen accordingly.
    // NB: So an absolutely positioned or floated table-internal box, which is blockified, is wrapped like any other
    //     block: in an anonymous row and cell, where it gets its static position from where it is among the rows.
    tree.display(node)
}

fn is_proper_table_child(tree: &impl TableFixupTree, node: NodeSlotId) -> bool {
    let display = display_for_table_fixup(tree, node);
    is_table_track_group(display) || is_table_track(display) || display.is_table_caption()
}

fn is_table_non_root_box(tree: &impl TableFixupTree, node: NodeSlotId) -> bool {
    let display = tree.display(node);
    display.is_internal_table() || display.is_table_caption()
}

fn is_table_non_root_box_sibling(tree: &impl TableFixupTree, sibling: NodeSlotId) -> bool {
    // Text nodes carry their parent's style, so only boxes can be table-non-root boxes.
    !sibling.is_invalid() && node_facts::kind_is_box(tree.kind(sibling)) && is_table_non_root_box(tree, sibling)
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#tabular-container
pub(crate) fn is_tabular_container(tree: &impl TableFixupTree, node: NodeSlotId) -> bool {
    let display = tree.display(node);
    display.is_table_inside()
        || display.is_table_row()
        || display.is_table_row_group()
        || display.is_table_header_group()
        || display.is_table_footer_group()
}

fn is_ignorable_whitespace(tree: &mut impl TableFixupTree, node: NodeSlotId) -> bool {
    if node_facts::kind_is_text(tree.kind(node)) {
        return tree.text_is_white_space(node);
    }
    if !tree.has_flag(node, NodeFlag::Anonymous)
        || !node_facts::kind_is_block_container(tree.kind(node))
        || !tree.has_flag(node, NodeFlag::ChildrenAreInline)
    {
        return false;
    }
    let mut contains_only_whitespace = true;
    for_each_in_subtree(tree, node, &mut |tree, descendant| {
        let holds_only_whitespace = if node_facts::kind_is_text(tree.kind(descendant)) {
            tree.text_is_white_space(descendant)
        } else {
            !tree.is_out_of_flow(descendant) && tree.has_flag(descendant, NodeFlag::Anonymous)
        };
        contains_only_whitespace &= holds_only_whitespace;
        holds_only_whitespace.then_some(Visit::Children)
    });
    contains_only_whitespace
}

/// Visits `root` and the boxes of its subtree in pre-order, reading where to go next once each visit returns; a visit
/// answering none ends the walk. A visit may change the tree below the box it visits.
fn for_each_in_subtree<T: TableFixupTree>(
    tree: &mut T,
    root: NodeSlotId,
    visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut T, NodeSlotId) -> Option<Visit>,
) {
    let mut current = root;
    loop {
        let Some(decision) = visit(tree, current) else {
            return;
        };
        if decision == Visit::Children {
            let first_child = tree.first_child(current);
            if !first_child.is_invalid() {
                current = first_child;
                continue;
            }
        }
        while current != root && tree.next_sibling(current).is_invalid() {
            current = tree.parent(current);
        }
        if current == root {
            return;
        }
        current = tree.next_sibling(current);
    }
}

/// Visits `owner` and the boxes of its child list in pre-order, telling `visit` whether the child list of the box it
/// visits is part of what table fixup goes over: the child list of `owner`, and those of the anonymous boxes in it that
/// are no pseudo-element's. The steps that act on the children of a box act only on these lists.
fn for_each_in_table_fixup_child_list<T: TableFixupTree>(
    tree: &mut T,
    owner: NodeSlotId,
    visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut T, NodeSlotId, bool) -> Visit,
) {
    for_each_in_subtree(tree, owner, &mut |tree, node| {
        let child_list_is_in_scope = node == owner
            || (!node_facts::kind_is_text(tree.kind(node))
                && tree.has_flag(node, NodeFlag::Anonymous)
                && !tree.has_flag(node, NodeFlag::IsPseudoElementPrincipalBox));
        match visit(tree, node, child_list_is_in_scope) {
            Visit::Children if child_list_is_in_scope => Some(Visit::Children),
            _ => Some(Visit::SkipChildren),
        }
    });
}

/// Wraps each sequence of consecutive children of `parent` that `matcher` matches, with the white space between them,
/// in an anonymous box of `kind`.
fn for_each_sequence_of_consecutive_children_matching<T: TableFixupTree>(
    tree: &mut T,
    parent: NodeSlotId,
    matcher: &dyn Fn(&T, NodeSlotId) -> bool,
    kind: AnonymousTableBoxKind,
) {
    let mut sequences = Vec::new();
    let mut sequence: Vec<NodeSlotId> = Vec::new();
    let mut end_sequence = |tree: &mut T, sequence: &mut Vec<NodeSlotId>, mut nearest_sibling: NodeSlotId| {
        // Whitespace that follows the last matching child is not part of the sequence. The fixup algorithm only
        // discards whitespace-only boxes that lie between two table-non-root boxes (step 1), so whitespace after the
        // last box of the sequence stays outside the anonymous wrapper: in "a <cell>b</cell><cell>c</cell> d" the
        // space before "d" is ordinary inline content next to the generated inline-table.
        while sequence.last().is_some_and(|&last| !matcher(tree, last)) {
            nearest_sibling = sequence.pop().expect("a trailing whitespace node");
        }
        if !sequence.iter().all(|&node| is_ignorable_whitespace(tree, node)) {
            sequences.push((std::mem::take(sequence), nearest_sibling));
        }
        sequence.clear();
    };
    let mut child = tree.first_child(parent);
    while !child.is_invalid() {
        if matcher(tree, child) || (!sequence.is_empty() && is_ignorable_whitespace(tree, child)) {
            sequence.push(child);
        } else if !sequence.is_empty() {
            end_sequence(tree, &mut sequence, child);
        }
        child = tree.next_sibling(child);
    }
    if !sequence.is_empty() {
        end_sequence(tree, &mut sequence, NodeSlotId::INVALID);
    }
    for (sequence, nearest_sibling) in sequences {
        wrap_in_anonymous_table_box(tree, parent, &sequence, nearest_sibling, kind);
    }
}

fn wrap_in_anonymous_table_box(
    tree: &mut impl TableFixupTree,
    parent: NodeSlotId,
    nodes: &[NodeSlotId],
    before: NodeSlotId,
    kind: AnonymousTableBoxKind,
) {
    let wrapper = tree.wrap_in_anonymous_table_box(parent, nodes, before, kind);
    // An anonymous table-cell takes over the run of content it is generated around, so it has inline children
    // exactly when that run is inline-level. Anonymous table-row, table and inline-table boxes only ever own
    // table-internal boxes (their wrapped children are, or become through the remaining fixup steps, table-internal
    // boxes), so they never have inline children, not even when they are generated inside an inline box. An
    // inline-table with inline children would also not derive its baseline from its first row.
    let children_are_inline =
        kind == AnonymousTableBoxKind::TableCell && nodes.iter().any(|&node| tree.is_inline_outside(node));
    tree.set_children_are_inline(wrapper, children_are_inline);
    // The wrapper takes the place of the run in its parent. A table-row, table-cell or table box is block-level,
    // so a parent whose inline content it replaced entirely (a table-row-group or table around text, a table-row
    // around text or inline boxes) no longer has inline children. A stale flag would make baseline derivation look
    // for line boxes the parent does not have, leaving it and every box that derives its baseline from it (a cell
    // around a nested table, an inline-table in a line) without a baseline. A parent that keeps inline-level
    // children next to the wrapper (text around an anonymous table generated for out-of-flow row groups, which
    // the fixup treats as inline-level boxes of zero size) still lays its children out in a line, and inline
    // boxes keep their inline children: the table-row generated around their cells is wrapped in an inline-level
    // inline-table next.
    if kind != AnonymousTableBoxKind::InlineTable && node_facts::kind_is_box(tree.kind(parent)) {
        let mut child = tree.first_child(parent);
        while !child.is_invalid() {
            if child != wrapper && tree.is_inline_outside(child) {
                return;
            }
            child = tree.next_sibling(child);
        }
        tree.set_children_are_inline(parent, false);
    }
}

fn remove_irrelevant_boxes(tree: &mut impl TableFixupTree, owner: NodeSlotId) {
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#fixup-algorithm
    // 1. Remove irrelevant boxes:
    // The following boxes are discarded as if they were display:none:
    // NB: Steps 1 and 2, the children of a table-column and those of a table-column-group which are not a
    //     table-column, are never planned.
    let mut to_remove = Vec::new();
    for_each_in_table_fixup_child_list(tree, owner, &mut |tree, node, _| {
        if node == owner {
            return Visit::Children;
        }
        let (parent, previous, next) = (tree.parent(node), tree.previous_sibling(node), tree.next_sibling(node));

        // 3. Anonymous inline boxes which contain only white space and are between two immediate siblings each of
        //    which is a table-non-root box.
        // This is what keeps "<cell>b</cell> <cell>c</cell>" a single table with adjacent cells, regardless of whether
        // the siblings live in a table, in a block (where the whitespace sits in an anonymous block wrapper) or in an
        // inline box. The whitespace before the first and after the last table-non-root box of such a run is not
        // discarded and remains ordinary inline content.
        if is_table_non_root_box_sibling(tree, previous)
            && is_table_non_root_box_sibling(tree, next)
            && is_ignorable_whitespace(tree, node)
        {
            to_remove.push(node);
            return Visit::SkipChildren;
        }

        // 4. Anonymous inline boxes which meet all of the following criteria:
        //    - they contain only white space
        //    - they are the first and/or last child of a tabular container
        //    - whose immediate sibling, if any, is a table-non-root box
        if node_facts::kind_is_box(tree.kind(node))
            && is_tabular_container(tree, parent)
            && !tree.has_flag(parent, NodeFlag::Anonymous)
            && (previous.is_invalid() || next.is_invalid())
            && (previous.is_invalid() || is_table_non_root_box(tree, previous))
            && (next.is_invalid() || is_table_non_root_box(tree, next))
            && is_ignorable_whitespace(tree, node)
        {
            to_remove.push(node);
            return Visit::SkipChildren;
        }
        Visit::Children
    });
    tree.remove(&to_remove);
}

fn generate_missing_child_wrappers<T: TableFixupTree>(tree: &mut T, owner: NodeSlotId) {
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#fixup-algorithm
    // 2. Generate missing child wrappers:
    for_each_in_table_fixup_child_list(tree, owner, &mut |tree, parent, child_list_is_in_scope| {
        let kind = tree.kind(parent);
        // AD-HOC: SVG layout derives box types from the element, so display values must not introduce anonymous boxes
        //         inside SVG content.
        if !child_list_is_in_scope || !node_facts::kind_is_box(kind) || node_facts::kind_is_svg_content(kind) {
            return Visit::Children;
        }
        let has_style = |tree: &T, child: NodeSlotId| tree.has_flag(child, NodeFlag::HasStyle);
        let display = tree.display(parent);
        if display.is_table_inside() {
            // 1. An anonymous table-row box must be generated around each sequence of consecutive children of a
            //    table-root box which are not proper table child boxes.
            for_each_sequence_of_consecutive_children_matching(
                tree,
                parent,
                &|tree, child| !has_style(tree, child) || !is_proper_table_child(tree, child),
                AnonymousTableBoxKind::TableRow,
            );
        } else if display.is_table_row_group() || display.is_table_header_group() || display.is_table_footer_group() {
            // 2. An anonymous table-row box must be generated around each sequence of consecutive children of a
            //    table-row-group box which are not table-row boxes.
            for_each_sequence_of_consecutive_children_matching(
                tree,
                parent,
                &|tree, child| !has_style(tree, child) || !tree.display(child).is_table_row(),
                AnonymousTableBoxKind::TableRow,
            );
        } else if display.is_table_row() {
            // 3. An anonymous table-cell box must be generated around each sequence of consecutive children of a
            //    table-row box which are not table-cell boxes.
            for_each_sequence_of_consecutive_children_matching(
                tree,
                parent,
                &|tree, child| !has_style(tree, child) || !tree.display(child).is_table_cell(),
                AnonymousTableBoxKind::TableCell,
            );
        }
        Visit::Children
    });
}

fn generate_missing_parents<T: TableFixupTree>(tree: &mut T, owner: NodeSlotId, table_roots: &mut Vec<NodeSlotId>) {
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables-3/#fixup-algorithm
    // 3. Generate missing parents:
    let mut table_roots_to_wrap = Vec::new();
    for_each_in_table_fixup_child_list(tree, owner, &mut |tree, parent, child_list_is_in_scope| {
        if !tree.has_flag(parent, NodeFlag::HasStyle) {
            return Visit::Children;
        }
        let current_display = tree.display(parent);
        // NB: The steps below wrap children of the box, but for the last, which wraps the box itself.
        let wraps_children = child_list_is_in_scope && !node_facts::kind_is_svg_content(tree.kind(parent));

        // 1. An anonymous table-row box must be generated around each sequence of consecutive table-cell boxes whose
        //    parent is not a table-row.
        if wraps_children && !current_display.is_table_row() {
            for_each_sequence_of_consecutive_children_matching(
                tree,
                parent,
                &|tree, child| tree.has_flag(child, NodeFlag::HasStyle) && tree.display(child).is_table_cell(),
                AnonymousTableBoxKind::TableRow,
            );
        }

        // 2. An anonymous table or inline-table box must be generated around each sequence of consecutive proper table
        //    child boxes which are misparented.
        // If the box’s parent is an inline, run-in, or ruby box (or any box that would perform inlinification of its
        // children), then an inline-table box must be generated; otherwise it must be a table box.
        // NB: An inline box is a non-atomic inline: an inline-block or other inline-level block container is not one, so
        //     a table generated inside it is block-level.
        // FIXME: run-in and ruby boxes
        let anonymous_table_kind = if tree.is_inline_outside(parent) && tree.display(parent).is_flow_inside() {
            AnonymousTableBoxKind::InlineTable
        } else {
            AnonymousTableBoxKind::Table
        };

        // A table-row is misparented if its parent is neither a table-row-group nor a table-root box.
        // A table-column box is misparented if its parent is neither a table-column-group box nor a table-root box.
        // A table-row-group, table-column-group, or table-caption box is misparented if its parent is not a table-root
        // box.
        // NB: The sequence spans misparented proper table children of every kind: the anonymous table-row generated
        //     around loose cells by step 1 and the table-row-group next to it belong to the same anonymous table.
        if wraps_children && !current_display.is_table_inside() {
            let is_table_row_group = current_display.is_table_row_group_kind();
            let is_table_column_group = current_display.is_table_column_group();
            for_each_sequence_of_consecutive_children_matching(
                tree,
                parent,
                &|tree, child| {
                    if !tree.has_flag(child, NodeFlag::HasStyle) {
                        return false;
                    }
                    let display = tree.display(child);
                    if display.is_table_row() {
                        return !is_table_row_group;
                    }
                    if display.is_table_column() {
                        return !is_table_column_group;
                    }
                    let display = display_for_table_fixup(tree, child);
                    is_table_track_group(display) || display.is_table_caption()
                },
                anonymous_table_kind,
            );
        }

        // 3. An anonymous table-wrapper box must be generated around each table-root.
        if node_facts::kind_is_box(tree.kind(parent)) && current_display.is_table_inside() {
            let wrap_parent = tree.parent(parent);
            if !wrap_parent.is_invalid() && !node_facts::kind_is_svg_content(tree.kind(wrap_parent)) {
                table_roots.push(parent);
                if tree.kind(wrap_parent) != NodeKind::TableWrapper {
                    table_roots_to_wrap.push(parent);
                }
            }
        }
        Visit::Children
    });
    for table_root in table_roots_to_wrap {
        tree.wrap_table_root(table_root);
    }
}

/// The plan of a walk as table fixup goes over it, where `text_is_whitespace` tells whether a text holds only white
/// space.
struct PlanTableFixup<'t> {
    tree: &'t mut PlanTree,
    text_is_whitespace: &'t dyn Fn(StyleNodeID) -> bool,
}

impl TableFixupTree for PlanTableFixup<'_> {
    fn parent(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> NodeSlotId {
        self.tree.node(node).parent()
    }

    fn first_child(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> NodeSlotId {
        self.tree.node(node).first_child()
    }

    fn next_sibling(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> NodeSlotId {
        self.tree.node(node).next_sibling()
    }

    fn previous_sibling(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> NodeSlotId {
        self.tree.node(node).previous_sibling()
    }

    fn kind(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> NodeKind {
        self.tree.node(node).kind()
    }

    fn has_flag(&self, node: NodeSlotId, flag: NodeFlag) -> bool {
        self.tree.node(node).has_flag(flag)
    }

    fn is_out_of_flow(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> bool {
        self.tree.node(node).is_out_of_flow()
    }

    fn is_inline_outside(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> bool {
        self.tree.node(node).has_fact(box_fact::INLINE_OUTSIDE)
    }

    fn display(&self, node: NodeSlotId) -> FfiDisplay {
        let planned = self.tree.node(node);
        if node_facts::kind_is_text(planned.kind()) {
            return self.display(planned.parent());
        }
        if let Some(&display) = self.tree.table_part_displays.get(&node) {
            return display;
        }
        match self.tree.style_of(node) {
            Some(style) => {
                crate::layout::tree_builder::used_display_of_box(planned.kind(), planned.flags(), style.display())
            }
            // NB: Every other box without a style of its own the walk made is an anonymous box that is no part of a
            //     table.
            None if planned.has_fact(box_fact::INLINE_OUTSIDE) => FfiDisplay::inline(),
            None => FfiDisplay::block(),
        }
    }

    fn text_is_white_space(&mut self, text: NodeSlotId) -> bool {
        if let Some(text) = self.tree.style_node(text) {
            return (self.text_is_whitespace)(text);
        }
        // NB: The commit spells a generated text, which holds only white space where the content of the pseudo-element
        //     it is generated for does.
        let mut ancestor = self.tree.node(text).parent();
        while !ancestor.is_invalid() && !self.tree.node(ancestor).has_flag(NodeFlag::IsPseudoElementPrincipalBox) {
            ancestor = self.tree.node(ancestor).parent();
        }
        self.tree.white_space_pseudo_element_boxes.contains(&ancestor)
    }

    fn remove(&mut self, nodes: &[NodeSlotId]) {
        // NB: The commit frees the rows of the boxes removed, once it committed every row of the plan.
        for &node in nodes {
            self.tree.detach(node);
            self.tree.dropped_rows.push(node);
        }
    }

    fn wrap_in_anonymous_table_box(
        &mut self,
        parent: NodeSlotId,
        nodes: &[NodeSlotId],
        _: NodeSlotId,
        kind: AnonymousTableBoxKind,
    ) -> NodeSlotId {
        let tree = &mut *self.tree;
        let display = match kind {
            AnonymousTableBoxKind::TableRow => FfiDisplay::internal(crate::css::css_enums::display_internal::TABLE_ROW),
            AnonymousTableBoxKind::TableCell => {
                FfiDisplay::internal(crate::css::css_enums::display_internal::TABLE_CELL)
            }
            AnonymousTableBoxKind::Table => FfiDisplay::table(),
            AnonymousTableBoxKind::InlineTable => FfiDisplay::inline_table(),
        };
        let node_kind = kind.style_and_node_kind().1;
        let wrapper = tree.push(PlanNode::new(
            node_kind,
            node_facts::construction_flags(node_kind, true, 0),
            super::box_facts_of_display(display) | box_fact::HAS_STYLE,
        ));
        tree.table_part_displays.insert(wrapper, display);
        // NB: The wrapper goes before the children it takes, so the pre-order positions of all of them stay in order.
        tree.attach(parent, wrapper, nodes[0]);
        for &node in nodes {
            tree.move_child(node, wrapper);
        }
        let facts = tree.node(wrapper).facts();
        tree.rows_committed_one_by_one.push(RowCommittedOneByOne {
            slot: wrapper,
            facts,
            source: OneByOneRowSource::AnonymousTableBox {
                style_parent: parent,
                kind,
            },
        });
        wrapper
    }

    fn set_children_are_inline(&mut self, node: NodeSlotId, children_are_inline: bool) {
        self.tree
            .set_flag(node, NodeFlag::ChildrenAreInline, children_are_inline);
    }

    fn wrap_table_root(&mut self, table_root: NodeSlotId) {
        let parent = self.tree.node(table_root).parent();
        let wrapper = self.tree.push_table_wrapper(table_root);
        self.tree.attach(parent, wrapper, table_root);
        self.tree.move_child(table_root, wrapper);
        self.tree.note_table_wrapper(wrapper, table_root);
    }
}

impl PlanTree {
    /// Fixes up the parts of tables in the child list of `owner`, a box whose children the walk planned all of, see
    /// [`fix_up_tables_in_child_lists`]. `text_is_whitespace` tells whether a text holds only white space.
    pub(crate) fn fix_up_tables_in_child_list(
        &mut self,
        owner: NodeSlotId,
        text_is_whitespace: &dyn Fn(StyleNodeID) -> bool,
    ) {
        if !self
            .node(owner)
            .has_fact(box_fact::HAS_TABLE_PART_CHILD | box_fact::TABULAR_CONTAINER)
        {
            return;
        }
        fix_up_tables_in_child_lists(
            &mut PlanTableFixup {
                tree: self,
                text_is_whitespace,
            },
            &[owner],
        );
    }

    /// Makes the anonymous table wrapper box of `table`, a table root the walk planned below `parent`, which is to go
    /// where the table is, or is placed by `place` where the walk places the table: the box that takes the table's
    /// outer properties, see [`OneByOneRowSource::TableWrapper`]. Answers the wrapper.
    pub(crate) fn push_table_wrapper(&mut self, table: NodeSlotId) -> NodeSlotId {
        let table_box = self.node(table);
        // NB: The facts of the wrapper, as those of a kept table's wrapper, are those of the table but for its inside
        //     display: its own is flow-root.
        let facts = table_box.facts()
            & !(box_fact::TABLE_INSIDE
                | box_fact::TABULAR_CONTAINER
                | box_fact::STAMPED_BY_BUILDER
                | box_fact::OWNS_CONTENT_REPLACEMENT_IMAGE
                | box_fact::HOLDS_HIGHLIGHT_STYLE
                | box_fact::OF_CHILDREN
                | box_fact::OPEN_PARENT
                | box_fact::HAS_TABLE_PART_CHILD
                | box_fact::DERIVED_ON_COMMIT
                | box_fact::CHILDREN_DERIVED_ON_COMMIT
                | box_fact::SUBTREE_DERIVED_ON_COMMIT
                | box_fact::OWN_CHILDREN_DERIVED_ON_COMMIT
                | box_fact::ESTABLISHES_FLEX_ITEMS
                | box_fact::ESTABLISHES_GRID_ITEMS);
        self.push(PlanNode::new(
            NodeKind::TableWrapper,
            node_facts::construction_flags(NodeKind::TableWrapper, true, 0),
            facts | box_fact::HAS_STYLE,
        ))
    }

    /// Lists what the commit does for `wrapper`, the table wrapper of `table`, once the walk linked both.
    pub(crate) fn note_table_wrapper(&mut self, wrapper: NodeSlotId, table: NodeSlotId) {
        let facts = self.node(wrapper).facts();
        self.rows_committed_one_by_one.push(RowCommittedOneByOne {
            slot: wrapper,
            facts,
            source: OneByOneRowSource::TableWrapper { table },
        });
        self.table_roots.push(table);
    }
}
