/// The sizes, size constraints and box sides of a box.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct RootInputCells {
    pub(crate) content_inline_size: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) content_block_size: CssPixels,

    pub(crate) margin_left: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) margin_right: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) margin_top: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) margin_bottom: CssPixels,

    pub(crate) border_left: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) border_right: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) border_top: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) border_bottom: CssPixels,

    pub(crate) padding_left: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) padding_right: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) padding_top: CssPixels,
    pub(crate) padding_bottom: CssPixels,

    pub(crate) has_definite_inline_size: bool,
    pub(crate) has_definite_block_size: bool,
    /// A button, or the anonymous wrapper of its content, whose automatic block size was made definite only so the
    /// content can be centered within a larger min-height. Percentages inside the button still treat it as indefinite.
    pub(crate) has_definite_block_size_only_for_button_content_alignment: bool,
    pub(crate) uses_collapsing_borders_model: bool,
    /// In the collapsing borders model, whether this is the table box rather than a cell. Both store the full widths
    /// of the collapsed borders at their edges, of which only a part lies inside the box (see border_left_collapsed()
    /// and friends): the table's border area lies outside the grid, so it owns the part of an outer border on the far
    /// side of the first or last grid line, while a cell owns the part on the inner side of its grid lines.
    pub(crate) is_collapsed_borders_table_box: bool,
}

impl RootInputCells {
    /// Resolves the left and right margins, borders and padding of `style`, with percentages against `basis`.
    pub(crate) fn resolve_horizontal_box_model(&mut self, style: &StyleValues<'_>, basis: CssPixels) {
        self.margin_left = style.margin_left().to_px(basis);
        self.margin_right = style.margin_right().to_px(basis);
        self.border_left = style.border_left_width();
        self.border_right = style.border_right_width();
        self.padding_left = style.padding_left().to_px(basis);
        self.padding_right = style.padding_right().to_px(basis);
    }

    /// Resolves the top and bottom margins, borders and padding of `style`, with percentages against `basis`.
    pub(crate) fn resolve_vertical_box_model(&mut self, style: &StyleValues<'_>, basis: CssPixels) {
        self.margin_top = style.margin_top().to_px(basis);
        self.margin_bottom = style.margin_bottom().to_px(basis);
        self.border_top = style.border_top_width();
        self.border_bottom = style.border_bottom_width();
        self.padding_top = style.padding_top().to_px(basis);
        self.padding_bottom = style.padding_bottom().to_px(basis);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_content_inline_size(&mut self, value: CssPixels) {
        // Negative inline sizes are not allowed in CSS. We have a bug somewhere! Clamp to 0 to avoid doing too much damage.
        self.content_inline_size = clamp_to_max_dimension_value(value.max(CssPixels::default()));
        self.has_definite_inline_size = true;
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_content_block_size(&mut self, value: CssPixels) {
        // Negative block sizes are not allowed in CSS. We have a bug somewhere! Clamp to 0 to avoid doing too much damage.
        self.content_block_size = clamp_to_max_dimension_value(value.max(CssPixels::default()));
    }

    /// Resolves every margin, border and padding of `style`, with percentages against `basis`.
    pub(crate) fn resolve_box_model(&mut self, style: &StyleValues<'_>, basis: CssPixels) {
        self.resolve_horizontal_box_model(style, basis);
        self.resolve_vertical_box_model(style, basis);
    }

    /// The content size, borders and paddings the fragment of the box shows.
    pub(crate) fn box_sides(&self) -> fragment_tree::BoxSides {
        fragment_tree::BoxSides {
            content_size: FfiCssPixelSize {
                width: self.content_inline_size,
                height: self.content_block_size,
            },
            border: geometry::Sides {
                top: self.border_top,
                right: self.border_right,
                bottom: self.border_bottom,
                left: self.border_left,
            },
            padding: geometry::Sides {
                top: self.padding_top,
                right: self.padding_right,
                bottom: self.padding_bottom,
                left: self.padding_left,
            },
            collapsing: fragment_tree::CollapsingBorders::of(
                self.uses_collapsing_borders_model,
                self.is_collapsed_borders_table_box,
            ),
        }
    }

    /// The used margins of the box.
    pub(crate) fn margins(&self) -> geometry::Sides {
        geometry::Sides {
            top: self.margin_top,
            right: self.margin_right,
            bottom: self.margin_bottom,
            left: self.margin_left,
        }
    }

    /// The sizes and box sides `link` and its fragment show, read in `frame`, with both sizes definite.
    pub(crate) fn of_committed_fragment_link(link: &fragment_tree::FragmentLink, frame: geometry::Frame) -> Self {
        let mut cells = Self {
            has_definite_block_size: true,
            ..Self::default()
        };
        cells.take_box_metrics_of_committed_link(link, frame);
        cells
    }

    /// Takes the sizes and box sides `link` and its fragment show, read in `frame`.
    pub(crate) fn take_box_metrics_of_committed_link(
        &mut self,
        link: &fragment_tree::FragmentLink,
        frame: geometry::Frame,
    ) {
        let sides = link.fragment.sides.in_frame(geometry::Frame::PHYSICAL, frame);
        let margins = link
            .placement
            .shown_as
            .margins
            .in_frame(geometry::Frame::PHYSICAL, frame);
        self.set_content_inline_size(sides.content_size.width);
        self.set_content_block_size(sides.content_size.height);
        self.margin_left = margins.left;
        self.margin_right = margins.right;
        self.margin_top = margins.top;
        self.margin_bottom = margins.bottom;
        self.border_left = sides.border.left;
        self.border_right = sides.border.right;
        self.border_top = sides.border.top;
        self.border_bottom = sides.border.bottom;
        self.padding_left = sides.padding.left;
        self.padding_right = sides.padding.right;
        self.padding_top = sides.padding.top;
        self.padding_bottom = sides.padding.bottom;
    }

    /// The cells, with the sizes, size constraints and box sides they hold in frame `from` read in frame `to` instead.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn in_frame(mut self, from: geometry::Frame, to: geometry::Frame) -> Self {
        if from == to {
            return self;
        }
        [self.margin_top, self.margin_right, self.margin_bottom, self.margin_left] = from.sides_in(
            [self.margin_top, self.margin_right, self.margin_bottom, self.margin_left],
            to,
        );
        [self.border_top, self.border_right, self.border_bottom, self.border_left] = from.sides_in(
            [self.border_top, self.border_right, self.border_bottom, self.border_left],
            to,
        );
        [
            self.padding_top,
            self.padding_right,
            self.padding_bottom,
            self.padding_left,
        ] = from.sides_in(
            [
                self.padding_top,
                self.padding_right,
                self.padding_bottom,
                self.padding_left,
            ],
            to,
        );
        if from.is_orthogonal_to(to) {
            std::mem::swap(&mut self.content_inline_size, &mut self.content_block_size);
            std::mem::swap(&mut self.has_definite_inline_size, &mut self.has_definite_block_size);
        }
        self
    }
}

macro_rules! box_metric_getters {
    ($($name:ident: $value:ty,)+) => {
        $(
            #[inline]
            fn $name(&self) -> $value {
                self.cells().$name
            }
        )+
    };
}

/// The sizes, size constraints and box sides of a box, with what derives from them, whether a cell holds them or they
/// are read as a value.
pub(crate) trait BoxMetricCells {
    /// The sizes, size constraints and box sides these metrics hold.
    fn cells(&self) -> RootInputCells;

    box_metric_getters! {
        content_inline_size: CssPixels,
        content_block_size: CssPixels,
        margin_left: CssPixels,
        margin_right: CssPixels,
        margin_top: CssPixels,
        margin_bottom: CssPixels,
        border_left: CssPixels,
        border_right: CssPixels,
        border_top: CssPixels,
        border_bottom: CssPixels,
        padding_left: CssPixels,
        padding_right: CssPixels,
        padding_top: CssPixels,
        padding_bottom: CssPixels,
        has_definite_inline_size: bool,
        has_definite_block_size: bool,
        has_definite_block_size_only_for_button_content_alignment: bool,
        uses_collapsing_borders_model: bool,
        is_collapsed_borders_table_box: bool,
    }

    fn border_left_collapsed(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        if collapsed {
            collapsed_border_share(self.border_left(), true, self.is_collapsed_borders_table_box())
        } else {
            self.border_left()
        }
    }

    fn border_right_collapsed(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        if collapsed {
            collapsed_border_share(self.border_right(), false, self.is_collapsed_borders_table_box())
        } else {
            self.border_right()
        }
    }

    fn border_top_collapsed(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        if collapsed {
            collapsed_border_share(self.border_top(), true, self.is_collapsed_borders_table_box())
        } else {
            self.border_top()
        }
    }

    fn border_bottom_collapsed(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        if collapsed {
            collapsed_border_share(self.border_bottom(), false, self.is_collapsed_borders_table_box())
        } else {
            self.border_bottom()
        }
    }

    fn border_box_left(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        self.border_left_collapsed(collapsed) + self.padding_left()
    }

    fn border_box_right(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        self.border_right_collapsed(collapsed) + self.padding_right()
    }

    fn border_box_top(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        self.border_top_collapsed(collapsed) + self.padding_top()
    }

    fn border_box_bottom(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        self.border_bottom_collapsed(collapsed) + self.padding_bottom()
    }

    fn horizontal_margin_border_padding(&self) -> CssPixels {
        self.margin_left()
            + self.border_left()
            + self.padding_left()
            + self.padding_right()
            + self.border_right()
            + self.margin_right()
    }

    fn border_box_inline_size(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        self.border_box_left(collapsed) + self.content_inline_size() + self.border_box_right(collapsed)
    }

    fn border_box_block_size(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        self.border_box_top(collapsed) + self.content_block_size() + self.border_box_bottom(collapsed)
    }

    fn margin_box_bottom(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        self.margin_bottom() + self.border_box_bottom(collapsed)
    }

    fn margin_box_top(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        self.margin_top() + self.border_box_top(collapsed)
    }

    fn margin_box_inline_size(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        self.margin_left()
            + self.border_box_left(collapsed)
            + self.content_inline_size()
            + self.border_box_right(collapsed)
            + self.margin_right()
    }

    fn margin_box_block_size(&self, collapsed: bool) -> CssPixels {
        self.margin_top()
            + self.border_box_top(collapsed)
            + self.content_block_size()
            + self.margin_box_bottom(collapsed)
    }

    fn available_inner_space_or_constraints_from(&self, outer: AvailableSpace) -> AvailableSpace {
        let mut inline_size = if self.has_definite_inline_size() {
            AvailableSize::definite(self.content_inline_size())
        } else {
            AvailableSize::Indefinite
        };
        let block_size = if self.has_definite_block_size() {
            AvailableSize::definite(self.content_block_size())
        } else {
            AvailableSize::Indefinite
        };
        if inline_size == AvailableSize::Indefinite
            && matches!(outer.inline_size, AvailableSize::MinContent | AvailableSize::MaxContent)
        {
            inline_size = outer.inline_size;
        }
        AvailableSpace {
            inline_size,
            block_size,
        }
    }
}

impl BoxMetricCells for RootInputCells {
    #[inline]
    fn cells(&self) -> RootInputCells {
        *self
    }
}

impl BoxMetricCells for Cell<RootInputCells> {
    #[inline]
    fn cells(&self) -> RootInputCells {
        self.get()
    }
}

/// Writes the metrics a cell holds. Not `update`: the inherent `Cell::update` would shadow it.
pub(crate) trait BoxMetricCellsMut {
    /// Writes the metrics, which `write` sees and changes as the cell holds them.
    fn update_cells(&self, write: impl FnOnce(&mut RootInputCells));

    fn set_content_inline_size(&self, value: CssPixels) {
        self.update_cells(|cells| cells.set_content_inline_size(value));
    }

    fn set_content_block_size(&self, value: CssPixels) {
        self.update_cells(|cells| cells.set_content_block_size(value));
    }
}

impl BoxMetricCellsMut for Cell<RootInputCells> {
    fn update_cells(&self, write: impl FnOnce(&mut RootInputCells)) {
        let mut cells = self.get();
        write(&mut cells);
        self.set(cells);
    }
}

/// The part of a collapsed border that lies after its grid line (below or right of it), the rest lying before it.
/// A collapsed border "is centered on the grid line" (CSS 2.2 §17.6.2), but layout keeps box edges on whole CSS
/// pixels, so the border is split on whole pixels, an odd width giving its extra pixel to the part before the line.
/// Every box on a grid line splits the border the same way, so the shares of the boxes on both sides of the line add
/// up to the border width: a 1px border takes 1px of layout space, not a rounded-up half on each side.
/// https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS22/tables.html#collapsing-borders
pub(crate) fn collapsed_border_part_after_line(width: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
    if width <= CssPixels::default() {
        return CssPixels::default();
    }
    (width / 2usize).floor()
}

/// The part of a collapsed border that lies before its grid line, see collapsed_border_part_after_line().
pub(crate) fn collapsed_border_part_before_line(width: CssPixels) -> CssPixels {
    if width <= CssPixels::default() {
        return CssPixels::default();
    }
    width - collapsed_border_part_after_line(width)
}

/// The part of a collapsed border of the given width that lies inside a box on the border's grid line; `start_edge`
/// says whether the line is at the box's top or left edge rather than its bottom or right one. A cell lies inside its
/// grid lines, so it owns the part after the line at its start edges and the part before the line at its end edges;
/// the table box lies around the grid and owns the opposite parts of its outer borders.
pub(crate) fn collapsed_border_share(width: CssPixels, start_edge: bool, is_table_box: bool) -> CssPixels {
    if start_edge != is_table_box {
        collapsed_border_part_after_line(width)
    } else {
        collapsed_border_part_before_line(width)
    }
}

/// The input cells of `node` before anything sizes the box: the sizes its style makes definite without layout.
pub(crate) fn cells_before_sizing(
    pass: &LayoutPass<'_>,
    node: Node,
    constraints: ContainingBlockConstraints,
) -> RootInputCells {
    assert!(!node.is_invalid());
    let facts = NodeFacts::new(pass, node);

    let style = StyleValues::for_node(pass, node);
    let percentage_basis_inline_size = constraints.percentage_basis_inline_size;
    let percentage_basis_block_size = constraints.percentage_basis_block_size;

    // NOTE: In the code below, we decide if `node` has definite inline
    // and/or block size. This attempts to cover all the *general* cases
    // where CSS considers sizes to be definite. If `node` has definite
    // values for min/max-width or min/max-height and a definite preferred
    // size in the same axis, we clamp the preferred size here as well.
    //
    // There are additional cases where CSS considers values to be
    // definite. We model all of those by considering sizes definite once
    // they are assigned through set_content_inline_size() or
    // set_content_block_size().
    let mut cells = RootInputCells::default();

    #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
    enum Axis {
        Inline,
        Block,
    }

    let containing_block_size_for_axis = |axis: Axis| match axis {
        Axis::Inline => percentage_basis_inline_size.unwrap_or_default(),
        Axis::Block => percentage_basis_block_size.unwrap_or_default(),
    };
    let containing_block_has_definite_size = |axis: Axis| match axis {
        Axis::Inline => percentage_basis_inline_size.is_some(),
        Axis::Block => percentage_basis_block_size.is_some(),
    };

    let adjust_for_box_sizing = |unadjusted: crate::layout::CssPixels, computed_size: &ComputedSize, axis: Axis| {
        // box-sizing: content-box and automatic sizes need no
        // adjustment.
        if style.box_sizing() == box_sizing::CONTENT_BOX || computed_size.is_auto() {
            return unadjusted;
        }

        // box-sizing: border-box subtracts the relevant border and
        // padding. Block-axis padding percentages also resolve against
        // the containing block's inline size.
        let inline_basis = percentage_basis_inline_size.unwrap_or_default();
        let border_and_padding = match axis {
            Axis::Inline => {
                style.border_left_width()
                    + style.padding_left().to_px(inline_basis)
                    + style.border_right_width()
                    + style.padding_right().to_px(inline_basis)
            }
            Axis::Block => {
                style.border_top_width()
                    + style.padding_top().to_px(inline_basis)
                    + style.border_bottom_width()
                    + style.padding_bottom().to_px(inline_basis)
            }
        };
        unadjusted - border_and_padding
    };

    let is_definite_size = |size: &ComputedSize, axis: Axis| -> Option<crate::layout::CssPixels> {
        // A definite size can be determined without performing
        // layout: a length, an initial-containing-block size, or a
        // percentage/formula resolved solely against definite sizes.
        if size.is_auto() {
            // The inline size of a non-flex-item block is definite when
            // it is auto and its containing block has a definite inline
            // size. This is the stretch-fit case from css-sizing-3.
            // Replaced boxes and auto-width buttons are sized from their content during layout.
            if matches!(axis, Axis::Inline)
                && !facts.is_replaced_box()
                && !facts.uses_button_layout()
                && !facts.is_floating()
                && !facts.is_absolutely_positioned()
                && facts.display().is_block_outside()
                && facts.parent_is_unfloated_flow_container()
                && containing_block_has_definite_size(Axis::Inline)
                && !formatting_context::frame_established_by(pass, node).is_orthogonal_to(pass.frame)
            {
                let available = containing_block_size_for_axis(Axis::Inline);
                return Some(clamp_to_max_dimension_value(
                    available - cells.horizontal_margin_border_padding(),
                ));
            }
            return None;
        }

        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-3/#stretch-fit-sizing
        // NB: A stretch size is definite where percentages resolve to a definite value, and sizes the margin box to
        //     fill the containing block exactly, treating auto margins as zero.
        if size.is_stretch() && size.calc_size().is_none() {
            if !containing_block_has_definite_size(axis) {
                return None;
            }
            let inline_basis = percentage_basis_inline_size.unwrap_or_default();
            let margins_borders_and_padding = match axis {
                Axis::Inline => {
                    style.margin_left().to_px(inline_basis)
                        + style.border_left_width()
                        + style.padding_left().to_px(inline_basis)
                        + style.padding_right().to_px(inline_basis)
                        + style.border_right_width()
                        + style.margin_right().to_px(inline_basis)
                }
                Axis::Block => {
                    let (margin_top, margin_bottom) =
                        crate::layout::sizing_context::stretch_fit_block_margins(pass, node, inline_basis);
                    margin_top
                        + style.border_top_width()
                        + style.padding_top().to_px(inline_basis)
                        + style.padding_bottom().to_px(inline_basis)
                        + style.border_bottom_width()
                        + margin_bottom
                }
            };
            return Some(clamp_to_max_dimension_value(
                (containing_block_size_for_axis(axis) - margins_borders_and_padding)
                    .max(crate::layout::CssPixels::default()),
            ));
        }
        if !size.is_length_percentage() {
            return None;
        }
        if size.contains_percentage() && !containing_block_has_definite_size(axis) {
            return None;
        }
        let basis = if size.contains_percentage() {
            containing_block_size_for_axis(axis)
        } else {
            crate::layout::CssPixels::default()
        };
        Some(clamp_to_max_dimension_value(adjust_for_box_sizing(
            size.to_px(basis),
            size,
            axis,
        )))
    };

    let min_inline_size = is_definite_size(style.min_width(), Axis::Inline);
    let max_inline_size = is_definite_size(style.max_width(), Axis::Inline);
    let min_block_size = is_definite_size(style.min_height(), Axis::Block);
    let max_block_size = is_definite_size(style.max_height(), Axis::Block);
    let mut content_inline_size = is_definite_size(style.width(), Axis::Inline);
    let mut content_block_size = is_definite_size(style.height(), Axis::Block);

    cells.has_definite_inline_size = content_inline_size.is_some();
    cells.has_definite_block_size = content_block_size.is_some();
    if let Some(size) = content_inline_size.as_mut() {
        if let Some(minimum) = min_inline_size {
            *size = clamp_to_max_dimension_value((*size).max(minimum));
        }
        if let Some(maximum) = max_inline_size {
            *size = clamp_to_max_dimension_value((*size).min(maximum));
        }
    }
    if let Some(size) = content_block_size.as_mut() {
        if let Some(minimum) = min_block_size {
            *size = clamp_to_max_dimension_value((*size).max(minimum));
        }
        if let Some(maximum) = max_block_size {
            *size = clamp_to_max_dimension_value((*size).min(maximum));
        }
    }
    cells.content_inline_size = content_inline_size.unwrap_or_default();
    cells.content_block_size = content_block_size.unwrap_or_default();

    cells
}

//! Propagation of the root element's and its body's style to the viewport: the principal
//! writing mode, the viewport's overflow and its overscroll behavior. The inputs are the
//! elements' own published style records rather than their boxes, since the previous pass
//! rewrote the boxes' values and a `display: none` body has style but no box. The boxes' final
//! styles are derived before the layout pass borrows their payloads.

use crate::css::computed_value_views::ComputedValuesView;
use crate::css::css_enums::{overflow, overscroll_behavior};
use crate::css::style::RetainedState;
use crate::css::style::bridge::{element_adjustment_fact, element_construction_fact};
use crate::css::style::tree::StyleNodeID;
use crate::layout::LayoutNodeArena;
use crate::layout::node_data::NodeSlotId;
use crate::painting::record::change_ticks::RowPaintChange;

/// What the propagation reads of the document element and its first HTML body child element.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct ViewportPropagationFacts {
    /// Invalid when there is no document element or it has no box.
    pub root_layout_node: NodeSlotId,
    pub root_is_html_html_element: bool,
    pub root_overflow_x: u8,
    pub root_overflow_y: u8,
    pub root_overscroll_behavior_x: u8,
    pub root_overscroll_behavior_y: u8,
    pub root_writing_mode: u8,
    pub root_direction: u8,
    /// Any of size, inline-size, layout, style or paint containment.
    pub root_has_containment: bool,
    /// The root element has an HTML body child element with computed style.
    pub has_styled_body: bool,
    /// Invalid when the body has no box.
    pub body_layout_node: NodeSlotId,
    pub body_display_is_none: bool,
    pub body_overflow_x: u8,
    pub body_overflow_y: u8,
    pub body_writing_mode: u8,
    pub body_direction: u8,
    pub body_has_containment: bool,
}

/// The published style record the style engine holds for an element.
fn published_style(engine: &RetainedState, node: StyleNodeID) -> Option<ComputedValuesView<'_>> {
    engine.element_published_style(node)
}

fn has_any_containment(style: ComputedValuesView<'_>) -> bool {
    let values = style.box_values();
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-conditional-5/#valdef-container-type-size
    // Applies style containment and size containment to the principal box, and establishes an independent formatting
    // context.
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-conditional-5/#valdef-container-type-inline-size
    // Applies style containment and inline-size containment to the principal box, and establishes an independent
    // formatting context.
    values.size_containment
        || values.inline_size_containment
        || values.layout_containment
        || values.style_containment
        || values.paint_containment
        || values.is_size_container
        || values.is_inline_size_container
}

/// The document element, which is the first DOM child of the style node the viewport box was
/// built for.
fn document_element(arena: &LayoutNodeArena) -> Option<StyleNodeID> {
    arena.first_dom_child(arena.document_style_node()?)
}

/// The first child of the document element that is an HTML body element.
fn first_html_body_child(engine: &RetainedState, root_element: StyleNodeID) -> Option<StyleNodeID> {
    engine
        .dom_children(root_element)
        .find(|&child| engine.element_adjustment_facts(child) & element_adjustment_fact::IS_HTML_BODY_ELEMENT != 0)
}

pub(crate) fn element_is_viewport_propagation_source(arena: &LayoutNodeArena, element: StyleNodeID) -> bool {
    let Some(root_element) = document_element(arena) else {
        return false;
    };
    root_element == element
        || arena.with_style_store(|engine| {
            engine.element_adjustment_facts(element) & element_adjustment_fact::IS_HTML_BODY_ELEMENT != 0
                && engine.element_construction_facts(root_element) & element_construction_fact::IS_HTML_HTML_ELEMENT
                    != 0
                && first_html_body_child(engine, root_element) == Some(element)
        })
}

/// The inputs of the propagation: the document element and its first HTML body child element, as
/// their own published style records have them.
pub(crate) fn viewport_propagation_facts(arena: &LayoutNodeArena) -> ViewportPropagationFacts {
    let mut facts = ViewportPropagationFacts {
        root_layout_node: NodeSlotId::INVALID,
        root_is_html_html_element: false,
        root_overflow_x: 0,
        root_overflow_y: 0,
        root_overscroll_behavior_x: overscroll_behavior::AUTO,
        root_overscroll_behavior_y: overscroll_behavior::AUTO,
        root_writing_mode: 0,
        root_direction: 0,
        root_has_containment: false,
        has_styled_body: false,
        body_layout_node: NodeSlotId::INVALID,
        body_display_is_none: false,
        body_overflow_x: 0,
        body_overflow_y: 0,
        body_writing_mode: 0,
        body_direction: 0,
        body_has_containment: false,
    };
    let Some(root_element) = document_element(arena) else {
        return facts;
    };
    let root_row = arena.bound_row(root_element);
    if root_row.is_invalid() {
        return facts;
    }
    arena.with_style_store(|engine| {
        let root_style = published_style(engine, root_element)
            .expect("the document element's box was built from its published style");
        facts.root_layout_node = root_row;
        facts.root_is_html_html_element =
            engine.element_construction_facts(root_element) & element_construction_fact::IS_HTML_HTML_ELEMENT != 0;
        facts.root_overflow_x = root_style.overflow_x();
        facts.root_overflow_y = root_style.overflow_y();
        facts.root_overscroll_behavior_x = root_style.misc_interaction().overscroll_behavior_x;
        facts.root_overscroll_behavior_y = root_style.misc_interaction().overscroll_behavior_y;
        facts.root_writing_mode = root_style.writing_mode();
        facts.root_direction = root_style.direction();
        facts.root_has_containment = has_any_containment(root_style);

        let Some(body_element) = first_html_body_child(engine, root_element) else {
            return;
        };
        let Some(body_style) = published_style(engine, body_element) else {
            return;
        };
        facts.has_styled_body = true;
        facts.body_layout_node = arena.bound_row(body_element);
        facts.body_display_is_none = body_style.display().is_none();
        facts.body_overflow_x = body_style.overflow_x();
        facts.body_overflow_y = body_style.overflow_y();
        facts.body_writing_mode = body_style.writing_mode();
        facts.body_direction = body_style.direction();
        facts.body_has_containment = has_any_containment(body_style);
    });
    facts
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds-3/#body-background
/// The boxes the canvas background is painted from: the document element's and the document's
/// body's, whose background the canvas takes over when the root's is transparent and has no image.
pub(crate) fn root_background_source(arena: &LayoutNodeArena) -> crate::painting::host::RootBackgroundSource {
    let mut source = crate::painting::host::RootBackgroundSource::default();
    let Some(root_element) = document_element(arena) else {
        return source;
    };
    source.root_layout_node = arena.bound_row(root_element);
    arena.with_style_store(|engine| {
        // The document's body is the first child of its <html> document element that is a <body>
        // or a <frameset>.
        let root_is_html_html_element =
            engine.element_construction_facts(root_element) & element_construction_fact::IS_HTML_HTML_ELEMENT != 0;
        let body_or_frameset =
            element_adjustment_fact::IS_HTML_BODY_ELEMENT | element_adjustment_fact::IS_HTML_FRAMESET_ELEMENT;
        if root_is_html_html_element
            && let Some(body) = engine
                .dom_children(root_element)
                .find(|&child| engine.element_adjustment_facts(child) & body_or_frameset != 0)
        {
            source.body_layout_node = arena.bound_row(body);
        }

        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain-2/#contain-property
        // Additionally, when any containments are active on either the HTML <html> or <body> elements, propagation of
        // properties from the <body> element to the initial containing block, the viewport, or the canvas background,
        // is disabled.
        if source.root_layout_node.is_invalid() || !root_is_html_html_element {
            return;
        }
        let Some(root_style) = published_style(engine, root_element) else {
            return;
        };
        if has_any_containment(root_style) {
            return;
        }
        let Some(body_element) = first_html_body_child(engine, root_element) else {
            return;
        };
        if arena.bound_row(body_element).is_invalid()
            || published_style(engine, body_element).is_none_or(has_any_containment)
        {
            return;
        }
        source.use_body_background_properties =
            !crate::painting::style_queries::background_layers_have_image(root_style)
                && root_style.background_color() == 0;
    });
    source
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct PropagatedViewportStyles {
    pub(crate) writing_mode: u8,
    pub(crate) direction: u8,
    pub(crate) viewport_overflow: (u8, u8),
    pub(crate) viewport_overscroll_behavior: (u8, u8),
    pub(crate) root_overflow: (u8, u8),
    /// Present when the body has a box that takes part in overflow propagation.
    pub(crate) body_overflow: Option<(u8, u8)>,
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-3/#overflow-propagation
// If 'visible' is applied to the viewport, it must be interpreted as 'auto'. If 'clip' is applied
// to the viewport, it must be interpreted as 'hidden'.
fn overflow_as_applied_to_viewport(value: u8) -> u8 {
    match value {
        overflow::VISIBLE => overflow::AUTO,
        overflow::CLIP => overflow::HIDDEN,
        other => other,
    }
}

/// `None` when the document element has no box; the viewport then only gets `overflow: auto`.
pub(crate) fn decide_viewport_propagation(facts: &ViewportPropagationFacts) -> Option<PropagatedViewportStyles> {
    if facts.root_layout_node.is_invalid() {
        return None;
    }
    let body_is_styled = facts.has_styled_body;
    let body_is_rendered = body_is_styled && !facts.body_display_is_none;

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes-4/#principal-flow
    // The principal writing mode of the document is determined by the used writing-mode,
    // direction, and text-orientation values of the root element. As a special case for handling
    // HTML documents, if the root element has a body child element whose display value is not
    // none, the used value of the writing-mode and direction properties on the root element are
    // taken from the computed writing-mode and direction of the first such child element instead
    // of from the root element's own values.
    // NOTE: Using containment disables this special handling of the HTML body element.
    let mut writing_mode = facts.root_writing_mode;
    let mut direction = facts.root_direction;
    let propagation_is_disabled_by_containment =
        facts.root_has_containment || (body_is_styled && facts.body_has_containment);
    if facts.root_is_html_html_element && !propagation_is_disabled_by_containment && body_is_rendered {
        writing_mode = facts.body_writing_mode;
        direction = facts.body_direction;
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain-2/#contain-property
    // Additionally, when any containments are active on either the HTML <html> or <body>
    // elements, propagation of properties from the <body> element to the initial containing
    // block, the viewport, or the canvas background, is disabled. Notably, this affects:
    // - 'overflow' and its longhands (see CSS Overflow 3 § 3.3 Overflow Viewport Propagation)
    let body_can_propagate_overflow = body_is_rendered && !facts.body_layout_node.is_invalid();
    let body_propagation_is_disabled_by_containment = (facts.root_is_html_html_element && facts.root_has_containment)
        || (body_is_styled && facts.body_has_containment);

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-3/#overflow-propagation
    // UAs must apply the overflow-* values set on the root element to the viewport when the
    // root element's display value is not none. However, when the root element is an [HTML]
    // html element (including XML syntax for HTML) whose overflow value is visible (in both
    // axes), and that element has as a child a body element whose display value is also not
    // none, user agents must instead apply the overflow-* values of the first such child element
    // to the viewport.
    let root_overflow = (facts.root_overflow_x, facts.root_overflow_y);
    let body_overflow = (facts.body_overflow_x, facts.body_overflow_y);
    let body_is_overflow_origin = facts.root_is_html_html_element
        && !body_propagation_is_disabled_by_containment
        && root_overflow == (overflow::VISIBLE, overflow::VISIBLE)
        && body_can_propagate_overflow;
    let origin_overflow = if body_is_overflow_origin {
        body_overflow
    } else {
        root_overflow
    };

    // The element from which the value is propagated must then have a used overflow value of
    // visible.
    // FIXME: Apply this to the used values, not the computed ones.
    let visible = (overflow::VISIBLE, overflow::VISIBLE);
    Some(PropagatedViewportStyles {
        writing_mode,
        direction,
        viewport_overflow: (
            overflow_as_applied_to_viewport(origin_overflow.0),
            overflow_as_applied_to_viewport(origin_overflow.1),
        ),
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overscroll-1/#scroll-chaining-and-boundary-default-actions
        // The viewport participates in scroll chaining as the document's scrollingElement, both
        // regarding placement in the scroll chain as well as adhering to the chaining rules
        // applied to it.
        // NOTE: The rules are those of the root element. Unlike overflow, the body never supplies them.
        viewport_overscroll_behavior: (facts.root_overscroll_behavior_x, facts.root_overscroll_behavior_y),
        root_overflow: if body_is_overflow_origin {
            root_overflow
        } else {
            visible
        },
        body_overflow: body_can_propagate_overflow.then_some(if body_is_overflow_origin {
            visible
        } else {
            body_overflow
        }),
    })
}

/// Applies the propagation in the order the boxes were always rewritten in: the root's writing
/// mode and direction, the viewport's, then the viewport's overflow and overscroll behavior, and
/// the root's and the body's overflow.
/// Every box receives its final values exactly once, so a steady-state pass leaves every style
/// record untouched instead of oscillating values within the pass.
///
/// `viewport` and the boxes named by the facts must be live, and the call must precede the
/// layout pass's style borrows.
pub(crate) fn propagate_root_styles_to_viewport(
    host_calls: crate::layout::tree_mutation::HostCalls<'_>,
    arena: &mut LayoutNodeArena,
    viewport: NodeSlotId,
    facts: &ViewportPropagationFacts,
) {
    assert!(!viewport.is_invalid());
    let apply_overflow = |arena: &mut LayoutNodeArena, node: NodeSlotId, (x, y): (u8, u8)| {
        let (x, y) = if node == viewport && arena.suppresses_viewport_scrolling {
            (overflow::HIDDEN, overflow::HIDDEN)
        } else {
            (x, y)
        };
        arena.update_layout_style(host_calls, node, |style, _| style.set_overflow(x, y));
    };
    let apply_writing_mode_and_direction =
        |arena: &mut LayoutNodeArena, node: NodeSlotId, writing_mode: u8, direction: u8| {
            arena.update_layout_style(host_calls, node, |style, _| {
                style.set_writing_mode_and_direction(writing_mode, direction);
            });
        };
    let apply_viewport_overscroll_behavior = |arena: &mut LayoutNodeArena, (x, y): (u8, u8)| {
        let mut changed = false;
        arena.update_layout_style(host_calls, viewport, |style, _| {
            style.set_overscroll_behavior(x, y);
            changed = !style.is_unchanged();
        });
        // The viewport's scroll node records what the viewport does at its boundary, and a new style for the
        // viewport box does not get it recorded again by itself.
        if changed {
            arena.note_paint_change(viewport, RowPaintChange::SCROLL_METADATA);
        }
    };

    let Some(styles) = decide_viewport_propagation(facts) else {
        apply_overflow(arena, viewport, (overflow::AUTO, overflow::AUTO));
        apply_viewport_overscroll_behavior(arena, (overscroll_behavior::AUTO, overscroll_behavior::AUTO));
        return;
    };
    let root = facts.root_layout_node;
    apply_writing_mode_and_direction(arena, root, styles.writing_mode, styles.direction);
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes-4/#icb
    // The principal writing mode is propagated to the initial containing block and to the
    // viewport, thereby affecting the layout of the root element and the scrolling direction of
    // the viewport.
    apply_writing_mode_and_direction(arena, viewport, styles.writing_mode, styles.direction);
    apply_overflow(arena, viewport, styles.viewport_overflow);
    apply_viewport_overscroll_behavior(arena, styles.viewport_overscroll_behavior);
    apply_overflow(arena, root, styles.root_overflow);
    if let Some(body_overflow) = styles.body_overflow {
        apply_overflow(arena, facts.body_layout_node, body_overflow);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::css::css_enums::{direction, writing_mode};

    fn html_document_facts() -> ViewportPropagationFacts {
        ViewportPropagationFacts {
            root_layout_node: NodeSlotId::new(1, 1),
            root_is_html_html_element: true,
            root_overflow_x: overflow::VISIBLE,
            root_overflow_y: overflow::VISIBLE,
            root_overscroll_behavior_x: overscroll_behavior::AUTO,
            root_overscroll_behavior_y: overscroll_behavior::AUTO,
            root_writing_mode: writing_mode::HORIZONTAL_TB,
            root_direction: direction::LTR,
            root_has_containment: false,
            has_styled_body: true,
            body_layout_node: NodeSlotId::new(2, 1),
            body_display_is_none: false,
            body_overflow_x: overflow::SCROLL,
            body_overflow_y: overflow::HIDDEN,
            body_writing_mode: writing_mode::VERTICAL_RL,
            body_direction: direction::RTL,
            body_has_containment: false,
        }
    }

    const VISIBLE: (u8, u8) = (overflow::VISIBLE, overflow::VISIBLE);

    #[test]
    fn a_visible_html_root_hands_propagation_to_its_body() {
        let styles = decide_viewport_propagation(&html_document_facts()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(styles.writing_mode, writing_mode::VERTICAL_RL);
        assert_eq!(styles.direction, direction::RTL);
        assert_eq!(styles.viewport_overflow, (overflow::SCROLL, overflow::HIDDEN));
        assert_eq!(styles.root_overflow, VISIBLE);
        assert_eq!(styles.body_overflow, Some(VISIBLE));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_root_with_its_own_overflow_stays_the_origin_and_maps_the_viewport_keywords() {
        let mut facts = html_document_facts();
        facts.root_overflow_x = overflow::CLIP;
        let styles = decide_viewport_propagation(&facts).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(styles.viewport_overflow, (overflow::HIDDEN, overflow::AUTO));
        assert_eq!(styles.root_overflow, VISIBLE);
        assert_eq!(styles.body_overflow, Some((overflow::SCROLL, overflow::HIDDEN)));
        assert_eq!(styles.writing_mode, writing_mode::VERTICAL_RL);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_body_without_a_box_still_supplies_the_writing_mode_but_no_overflow() {
        let mut facts = html_document_facts();
        facts.body_layout_node = NodeSlotId::INVALID;
        let styles = decide_viewport_propagation(&facts).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(styles.writing_mode, writing_mode::VERTICAL_RL);
        assert_eq!(styles.viewport_overflow, (overflow::AUTO, overflow::AUTO));
        assert_eq!(styles.root_overflow, VISIBLE);
        assert_eq!(styles.body_overflow, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_display_none_body_takes_no_part_in_either_propagation() {
        let mut facts = html_document_facts();
        facts.body_layout_node = NodeSlotId::INVALID;
        facts.body_display_is_none = true;
        let styles = decide_viewport_propagation(&facts).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(styles.writing_mode, writing_mode::HORIZONTAL_TB);
        assert_eq!(styles.direction, direction::LTR);
        assert_eq!(styles.viewport_overflow, (overflow::AUTO, overflow::AUTO));
        assert_eq!(styles.body_overflow, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn containment_on_either_element_disables_both_body_special_cases() {
        for containment_is_on_root in [true, false] {
            let mut facts = html_document_facts();
            facts.root_has_containment = containment_is_on_root;
            facts.body_has_containment = !containment_is_on_root;
            let styles = decide_viewport_propagation(&facts).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(styles.writing_mode, writing_mode::HORIZONTAL_TB);
            assert_eq!(styles.viewport_overflow, (overflow::AUTO, overflow::AUTO));
            assert_eq!(styles.root_overflow, VISIBLE);
            assert_eq!(styles.body_overflow, Some((overflow::SCROLL, overflow::HIDDEN)));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_root_that_is_not_an_html_element_ignores_its_body_child() {
        let mut facts = html_document_facts();
        facts.root_is_html_html_element = false;
        let styles = decide_viewport_propagation(&facts).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(styles.writing_mode, writing_mode::HORIZONTAL_TB);
        assert_eq!(styles.viewport_overflow, (overflow::AUTO, overflow::AUTO));
        assert_eq!(styles.root_overflow, VISIBLE);
        assert_eq!(styles.body_overflow, Some((overflow::SCROLL, overflow::HIDDEN)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_viewport_takes_the_overscroll_behavior_of_the_root_whichever_element_supplies_its_overflow() {
        let mut facts = html_document_facts();
        facts.root_overscroll_behavior_x = overscroll_behavior::CONTAIN;
        facts.root_overscroll_behavior_y = overscroll_behavior::NONE;
        let the_roots = (overscroll_behavior::CONTAIN, overscroll_behavior::NONE);

        let styles_with_overflow_from_the_body = decide_viewport_propagation(&facts).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(styles_with_overflow_from_the_body.body_overflow, Some(VISIBLE));
        assert_eq!(
            styles_with_overflow_from_the_body.viewport_overscroll_behavior,
            the_roots
        );

        facts.root_overflow_y = overflow::SCROLL;
        let styles_with_overflow_from_the_root = decide_viewport_propagation(&facts).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            styles_with_overflow_from_the_root.body_overflow,
            Some((overflow::SCROLL, overflow::HIDDEN))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            styles_with_overflow_from_the_root.viewport_overscroll_behavior,
            the_roots
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_root_box_leaves_only_the_viewport_default() {
        let mut facts = html_document_facts();
        facts.root_layout_node = NodeSlotId::INVALID;
        assert_eq!(decide_viewport_propagation(&facts), None);
    }
}

/// The red, green, blue and alpha of a CSS <color> in ASCII that needs nothing to be resolved against, or None for any
/// other value, as the color cache of the 2D canvas contexts parses it.
pub fn parse_simple_color_ascii(source: &[u8]) -> Option<[u8; 4]> {
    css::parser::color_parser::parse_simple_color(source.into())
}

/// The red, green, blue and alpha of a CSS <color> in UTF-16 that needs nothing to be resolved against, or None for any
/// other value, as the color cache of the 2D canvas contexts parses it.
pub fn parse_simple_color_utf16(source: &[u16]) -> Option<[u8; 4]> {
    css::parser::color_parser::parse_simple_color(source.into())
}

/// The red, green, blue and alpha of an 8-bit sRGB color converted to the predefined color space of a 2D canvas (the
/// underlying value of a Web::Bindings::PredefinedColorSpace), and clipped to its gamut, as the 'relative-colorimetric'
/// rendering intent does. https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#predefinedcolorspace
pub fn srgb_color_in_predefined_color_space(color: [u8; 4], predefined_color_space: u8) -> [u8; 4] {
    css::color_resolution::srgb_color_in_predefined_color_space(color, predefined_color_space)
}

// NB: Only C++ calls into the HTML tokenizer and parser, so nothing in this crate names them. Linking the crate keeps
//     their extern "C" functions in the static library.

use crate::rust_panic::abort_on_panic;

unsafe fn bytes_from_raw<'a>(bytes: *const u8, len: usize) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
    unsafe {
        if len == 0 {
            return Some(&[]);
        }
        if bytes.is_null() {
            eprintln!("bytes_from_raw: null pointer with non-zero length {len}");
            return None;
        }
        Some(ak::slice_from_raw_parts(bytes, len))
    }
}

//! The Paint thread, and the stage it presents frames on: the poster frames reach the compositor through.
//!
//! Presenting a frame takes a [`Presenting`], which only the jobs this module hands the Paint thread are lent, there,
//! and which alone reaches the poster. The Paint thread runs its jobs one at a time and in the order they were handed to
//! it, so frames reach the compositor in the order their jobs were handed out, and code that runs anywhere else cannot
//! present a frame: it has no [`Presenting`] to present with.

use crate::painting::display_list::chunks::{Chunk, ChunkId};
use crate::painting::display_list::commands::CompositorContextId;
use crate::painting::display_list::storage::{PackedChunkSize, packed_size_of_chunks, write_packed_chunks};
use crate::painting::presentation::SentDisplayListChunks;
use crate::render_state::SampledFrame;
use crate::stage_thread::{InFlight, Relay, Riding, StageThread};
use libcompositing_rust::ipc_types::{
    Compositing_AsyncScrollingMetadata, Compositing_DisplayListProperties, Core_AnonymousBuffer, SharedDisplayList,
};
use libgfx_rust::font::FontHandle;
use libgfx_rust::image_frame::ImageFrameHandle;
use libipc_rust::cpp_connection::{FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster, ThreadSafeMessagePoster};
use libipc_rust::wire::{EndpointMessage, File};
use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::marker::PhantomData;
use std::ptr::NonNull;
use std::sync::OnceLock;

/// Shared memory C++ made for a message, which the caller writes and then releases: `Web::Compositor::FfiSharedBuffer`.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiSharedBuffer {
    data: *mut u8,
    size: usize,
    /// A descriptor of the memory of its own, which the caller takes over.
    descriptor: i32,
    owner: *mut c_void,
}

/// Posts messages to the compositor from the thread that holds it: Rust encodes what it can, and C++ the fonts, image
/// frames and screenshot targets, which are C++ objects.
pub(crate) struct CompositorPoster(ThreadSafeMessagePoster);

impl CompositorPoster {
    /// Takes over the reference `ffi` holds.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `ffi` must hold one reference to a live poster on the transport of the connection to the compositor.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn adopt(ffi: FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
        Self(unsafe { ThreadSafeMessagePoster::adopt(ffi) })
    }

    /// Posts `message`, and answers whether the compositor could still be reached.
    pub(crate) fn post<M: EndpointMessage>(&self, message: M) -> bool {
        self.0.try_post(message).expect("a message to the compositor encodes")
    }

    /// Describes `fonts` to the compositor context `context_id` names and registers `image_frames` with the
    /// compositor, ahead of the display list or the visual context tree that draws them, and answers whether the
    /// compositor could still be reached. The caller holds `image_frames` until it has posted what draws them.
    pub(crate) fn post_fonts_and_image_frames(
        &self,
        context_id: CompositorContextId,
        fonts: &[FontHandle],
        image_frames: &[ImageFrameHandle],
    ) -> bool {
        if fonts.is_empty() && image_frames.is_empty() {
            return true;
        }
        let fonts: Vec<*const c_void> = fonts.iter().map(FontHandle::as_raw).collect();
        let image_frames: Vec<*const c_void> = image_frames.iter().map(ImageFrameHandle::as_raw).collect();
        // SAFETY: This holds a reference to the poster, and the handles keep the fonts and frames live for the call, in
        // which C++ takes references of its own.
        unsafe {
            web_compositor_post_fonts_and_image_frames(
                self.0.as_cpp_poster(),
                context_id.0,
                fonts.as_ptr(),
                fonts.len(),
                image_frames.as_ptr(),
                image_frames.len(),
            )
        }
    }

    /// The display list that names `chunks_in_paint_order` and carries `new_chunks`, the ones the compositor does not
    /// keep, with `properties` and `async_scrolling_metadata`, as a message carries it, or none where the chunks cannot
    /// be placed in shared memory.
    pub(crate) fn share_display_list(
        &self,
        chunks_in_paint_order: Vec<ChunkId>,
        new_chunks: &[&Chunk],
        properties: Compositing_DisplayListProperties,
        async_scrolling_metadata: Option<Compositing_AsyncScrollingMetadata>,
    ) -> Option<SharedDisplayList> {
        let packed_chunks = self.shared_buffer_with(packed_size_of_chunks(new_chunks), |destination| {
            write_packed_chunks(new_chunks, destination);
        })?;
        Some(SharedDisplayList {
            chunks_in_paint_order,
            packed_chunks,
            packed_chunk_sizes: new_chunks.iter().map(|chunk| PackedChunkSize::of(chunk)).collect(),
            properties,
            async_scrolling_metadata,
        })
    }

    /// Shared memory of `size` bytes that `write` fills, as a message carries it, or none where it cannot be made. The
    /// memory is sealed where the platform supports it, so the receiver cannot be faulted by the file shrinking.
    fn shared_buffer_with(&self, size: usize, write: impl FnOnce(&mut [u8])) -> Option<Core_AnonymousBuffer> {
        if size == 0 {
            return Some(Core_AnonymousBuffer { shared_memory: None });
        }
        let mut buffer = FfiSharedBuffer {
            data: std::ptr::null_mut(),
            size: 0,
            descriptor: -1,
            owner: std::ptr::null_mut(),
        };
        // SAFETY: C++ fills `buffer` where it answers true.
        if !unsafe { web_compositor_create_shared_buffer(size, &mut buffer) } {
            return None;
        }
        assert_eq!(buffer.size, size);
        // SAFETY: C++ mapped `size` writable bytes at `data`, which stay mapped until the owner is released.
        write(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(buffer.data, size) });
        // SAFETY: The owner is released once, after the last write.
        unsafe { web_compositor_shared_buffer_release(buffer.owner) };
        #[cfg(unix)]
        // SAFETY: C++ hands over a descriptor of its own.
        let descriptor = unsafe { <std::os::fd::OwnedFd as std::os::fd::FromRawFd>::from_raw_fd(buffer.descriptor) };
        #[cfg(windows)]
        // SAFETY: C++ hands over a descriptor of its own.
        let descriptor = unsafe { libipc_rust::transport_windows::OwnedDescriptor::from_raw(buffer.descriptor) };
        Some(Core_AnonymousBuffer {
            shared_memory: Some((size as u64, File(descriptor))),
        })
    }

    /// Stages `fonts` and `image_frames` for the rasterization `token` names into `target_bitmap`, a shareable
    /// `Gfx::Bitmap`, and answers whether the compositor could still be reached.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `target_bitmap` must be live for the call.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn stage_rasterization(
        &self,
        token: u64,
        fonts: &[FontHandle],
        image_frames: &[ImageFrameHandle],
        target_bitmap: *const c_void,
    ) -> bool {
        let fonts: Vec<*const c_void> = fonts.iter().map(FontHandle::as_raw).collect();
        let image_frames: Vec<*const c_void> = image_frames.iter().map(ImageFrameHandle::as_raw).collect();
        // SAFETY: This holds a reference to the poster, the handles keep the fonts and frames live for the call, in
        // which C++ takes references of its own, and the caller keeps the bitmap live for it.
        unsafe {
            web_compositor_stage_rasterization(
                self.0.as_cpp_poster(),
                token,
                fonts.as_ptr(),
                fonts.len(),
                image_frames.as_ptr(),
                image_frames.len(),
                target_bitmap,
            )
        }
    }

    /// The `IPC::ThreadSafeMessagePoster` this posts through, for C++ to post what it encodes.
    pub(crate) fn as_cpp_poster(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.as_cpp_poster()
    }
}

/// The Paint thread, which records display lists from the frames the render states publish, and presents frames.
struct PaintThread {
    thread: StageThread,
    stage: StageCell,
}

/// The stage, which only the jobs that are lent a [`Presenting`] reach, on the Paint thread.
struct StageCell(RefCell<PaintStage>);

// SAFETY: The stage is made empty on whichever thread first reaches the Paint thread, and from then on only the Paint
// thread reaches it, in the jobs it runs one at a time.
unsafe impl Send for StageCell {}
unsafe impl Sync for StageCell {}

/// What the Paint thread presents with.
#[derive(Default)]
struct PaintStage {
    /// The poster of the connection to the compositor, while it can be reached.
    poster: Option<CompositorPoster>,
    /// What the compositor at the other end of the poster keeps of the display lists sent for each context, which a
    /// new connection starts without.
    sent_display_list_chunks: std::collections::HashMap<CompositorContextId, SentDisplayListChunks>,
    /// A clock tick that runs as a context is destroyed can still hand the Paint thread a frame of it after it was
    /// forgotten. No context takes the id of a destroyed one, so its frames are dropped.
    destroyed_context_ids: std::collections::HashSet<CompositorContextId>,
}

impl PaintStage {
    fn present_through(&mut self, poster: Option<CompositorPoster>) {
        self.poster = poster;
        self.sent_display_list_chunks.clear();
    }
}

static PAINT_THREAD: OnceLock<PaintThread> = OnceLock::new();

fn the_paint_thread() -> &'static PaintThread {
    PAINT_THREAD.get_or_init(|| PaintThread {
        thread: StageThread::spawn(
            "Paint",
            crate::render_state::release_unused_memory_of_style_layout_threads,
        ),
        stage: StageCell(RefCell::default()),
    })
}

/// The Paint thread, for jobs that present nothing.
pub(crate) fn paint_thread() -> &'static StageThread {
    &the_paint_thread().thread
}

/// What a job on the Paint thread presents with. Only this module makes one, on the Paint thread, for one job at a time.
/// The raw pointer marker makes it neither [`Send`] nor [`Sync`], so it cannot leave the job it is lent to.
pub(crate) struct Presenting<'stage> {
    stage: &'stage mut PaintStage,
    not_send_or_sync: PhantomData<*const ()>,
}

impl Presenting<'_> {
    /// Lends `job` what it presents with. Only a job running on the Paint thread may call this.
    fn lend<R>(job: impl FnOnce(&mut Presenting) -> R) -> R {
        let paint_thread = the_paint_thread();
        debug_assert!(paint_thread.thread.is_current(), "only the Paint thread presents");
        let mut stage = paint_thread.stage.0.borrow_mut();
        job(&mut Presenting {
            stage: &mut stage,
            not_send_or_sync: PhantomData,
        })
    }

    /// The poster frames are presented through, or none while the compositor cannot be reached.
    pub(crate) fn poster(&self) -> Option<&CompositorPoster> {
        self.stage.poster.as_ref()
    }

    /// The poster frames are presented through, with what the compositor keeps of the display lists sent for each
    /// context, or none while the compositor cannot be reached.
    pub(crate) fn poster_and_sent_display_list_chunks(
        &mut self,
    ) -> Option<(
        &CompositorPoster,
        &mut std::collections::HashMap<CompositorContextId, SentDisplayListChunks>,
    )> {
        let stage = &mut *self.stage;
        Some((stage.poster.as_ref()?, &mut stage.sent_display_list_chunks))
    }

    pub(crate) fn context_was_destroyed(&self, context_id: CompositorContextId) -> bool {
        self.stage.destroyed_context_ids.contains(&context_id)
    }

    /// Drops the poster of a compositor that can no longer be reached: the connection learns of that on its own thread,
    /// and hands over the poster of the next one.
    pub(crate) fn lose_compositor(&mut self) {
        self.stage.present_through(None);
    }
}

/// Hands `job` to the Paint thread with `frame`, which the render owner sampled: the Paint thread runs it after the jobs
/// handed to it before, beside whoever holds the ride, and lends it what it presents with. A job that presents is only
/// ever handed a sampled frame, so the Paint thread presents frames in the order the render owner sampled them.
pub(crate) fn ride_presenting<T: Send + 'static, R: Send + 'static>(
    frame: SampledFrame<T>,
    job: impl FnOnce(SampledFrame<T>, &mut Presenting) -> R + Send + 'static,
) -> Riding<R> {
    paint_thread().ride(move || Presenting::lend(|presenting| job(frame, presenting)))
}

/// Hands `job` on to the Paint thread with `frame`, which the render owner sampled, and `relay`, the relay of the job
/// submitted to the render owner that sampled it, which lands what `job` answers (see [`ride_presenting`]).
pub(crate) fn relay_presenting<T: Send + 'static, R: Send + 'static>(
    relay: Relay<R>,
    frame: SampledFrame<T>,
    job: impl FnOnce(SampledFrame<T>, &mut Presenting) -> R + Send + 'static,
) {
    relay.hand_on(paint_thread(), move |_| {
        Presenting::lend(|presenting| job(frame, presenting))
    });
}

/// Submits `job` to the Paint thread with `frame`, which the render owner sampled (see [`ride_presenting`]), and answers
/// the flight of what it answers.
pub(crate) fn submit_presenting<T: Send + 'static, R: Send + 'static>(
    frame: SampledFrame<T>,
    job: impl FnOnce(SampledFrame<T>, &mut Presenting) -> R + Send + 'static,
) -> InFlight<R> {
    paint_thread().submit(move |_| Presenting::lend(|presenting| job(frame, presenting)))
}

/// A poster on the way to the Paint stage.
struct IncomingPoster(CompositorPoster);

// SAFETY: A poster posts from any thread, and nothing reaches it on the way.
unsafe impl Send for IncomingPoster {}

/// Has the Paint stage present frames through `poster`, a poster on the transport of a new connection to the compositor,
/// from the frames handed to the Paint thread after this on. Only the connection calls this, which declares it.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `poster` must hold one reference to a live poster, which the caller gives up.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn paint_stage_adopt_compositor_poster(poster: FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster) {
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    let incoming = IncomingPoster(unsafe { CompositorPoster::adopt(poster) });
    paint_thread().post(move || {
        let IncomingPoster(poster) = incoming;
        Presenting::lend(|presenting| presenting.stage.present_through(Some(poster)));
    });
}

/// Forgets what the compositor kept of the display lists sent for the context `context_id` names, after the frames
/// handed to the Paint thread before, and drops the frames of the context handed to it after. Only the compositor host
/// calls this, as it destroys the context, which declares it. The compositor never gives a destroyed context's id to
/// another context.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn paint_stage_forget_destroyed_compositor_context(context_id: u64) {
    let Some(paint_thread) = PAINT_THREAD.get() else {
        return;
    };
    paint_thread.thread.post(move || {
        Presenting::lend(|presenting| {
            let context_id = CompositorContextId(context_id);
            presenting.stage.sent_display_list_chunks.remove(&context_id);
            presenting.stage.destroyed_context_ids.insert(context_id);
        });
    });
}

/// A screenshot of what the compositor composes for a context (a `Web::Compositor::ScreenshotRequestForPaintThread`), on
/// its way to the Paint thread, which asks the compositor for it after the frames handed to it before.
struct ScreenshotRequest(NonNull<c_void>);

// SAFETY: A request owns everything it carries, and nothing else reaches it on the way.
unsafe impl Send for ScreenshotRequest {}

impl Drop for ScreenshotRequest {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: The box owns the request.
        unsafe { web_screenshot_request_destroy(self.0.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

/// Asks the compositor for the screenshot `request` names after the frames handed to the Paint thread before it. Only
/// the connection calls this, which declares it.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `request` must be a `Web::Compositor::ScreenshotRequestForPaintThread`, which the caller gives up.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn paint_stage_request_screenshot(request: NonNull<c_void>) {
    let request = ScreenshotRequest(request);
    paint_thread().post(move || {
        Presenting::lend(|presenting| {
            let Some(poster) = presenting.poster() else {
                return;
            };
            let request = std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(request);
            // SAFETY: The stage holds the poster, and C++ takes the request over.
            if !unsafe { web_compositor_post_screenshot_request(poster.as_cpp_poster(), request.0.as_ptr()) } {
                presenting.lose_compositor();
            }
        });
    });
}

use crate::css::computed_value_views::LengthPercentageRef;
use crate::css::css_pixels::{CssPixelFraction, CssPixels};
use crate::css::css_pixels::{CssPixelPoint, CssPixelRect};
use crate::layout::node_data::NodeSlotId;
use crate::painting::display_list::device_pixels::DevicePixelConverter;
use crate::painting::paint_read::PaintRead;
use crate::painting::paintable_geometry;
use libgfx_rust::{CornerRadii, CornerRadius};

pub(crate) fn normalize_border_radii_data(
    border_rect: CssPixelRect,
    reference_rect: CssPixelRect,
    corner_radius_pairs: [(LengthPercentageRef<'_>, LengthPercentageRef<'_>); 4],
) -> BorderRadii {
    scale_radii_to_fit(border_rect, resolve_corner_radii(reference_rect, corner_radius_pairs))
}

pub(crate) fn resolve_corner_radii(
    reference_rect: CssPixelRect,
    corner_radius_pairs: [(LengthPercentageRef<'_>, LengthPercentageRef<'_>); 4],
) -> BorderRadii {
    let mut radii = BorderRadii::default();
    for (corner, (horizontal, vertical)) in corner_radius_pairs.into_iter().enumerate() {
        radii.values[corner * 2] = horizontal.to_px(reference_rect.width);
        radii.values[corner * 2 + 1] = vertical.to_px(reference_rect.height);
    }
    radii
}

pub(crate) fn scale_radii_to_fit(border_rect: CssPixelRect, mut radii: BorderRadii) -> BorderRadii {
    let zero = CssPixels::from_raw(0);
    let border_width = border_rect.width.max(zero);
    let border_height = border_rect.height.max(zero);
    for _iteration in 0..2 {
        let [tl_h, tl_v, tr_h, tr_v, br_h, br_v, bl_h, bl_v] = radii.values;
        let s_top = tl_h + tr_h;
        let s_right = tr_v + br_v;
        let s_bottom = br_h + bl_h;
        let s_left = bl_v + tl_v;

        let mut f = CssPixelFraction::one();
        if s_top > zero && s_top > border_width {
            f = f.min(CssPixelFraction::ratio_of(border_width, s_top));
        }
        if s_right > zero && s_right > border_height {
            f = f.min(CssPixelFraction::ratio_of(border_height, s_right));
        }
        if s_bottom > zero && s_bottom > border_width {
            f = f.min(CssPixelFraction::ratio_of(border_width, s_bottom));
        }
        if s_left > zero && s_left > border_height {
            f = f.min(CssPixelFraction::ratio_of(border_height, s_left));
        }

        if f.is_at_least_one() {
            break;
        }
        for value in &mut radii.values {
            *value = value.mul_by_fraction(f);
        }
    }
    radii
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct BorderRadii {
    pub values: [CssPixels; 8],
}

impl BorderRadii {
    fn corner_present(horizontal: CssPixels, vertical: CssPixels) -> bool {
        horizontal > CssPixels::from_raw(0) && vertical > CssPixels::from_raw(0)
    }

    pub fn shrink(&mut self, top: CssPixels, right: CssPixels, bottom: CssPixels, left: CssPixels) {
        let zero = CssPixels::from_raw(0);
        let shrink_one = |radius: &mut CssPixels, by: CssPixels| {
            if *radius != zero {
                *radius = (*radius - by).max(zero);
            }
        };
        shrink_one(&mut self.values[0], left);
        shrink_one(&mut self.values[1], top);
        shrink_one(&mut self.values[2], right);
        shrink_one(&mut self.values[3], top);
        shrink_one(&mut self.values[4], right);
        shrink_one(&mut self.values[5], bottom);
        shrink_one(&mut self.values[6], left);
        shrink_one(&mut self.values[7], bottom);
    }

    pub fn shrunken(mut self, top: CssPixels, right: CssPixels, bottom: CssPixels, left: CssPixels) -> Self {
        self.shrink(top, right, bottom, left);
        self
    }

    pub fn inflate(&mut self, top: CssPixels, right: CssPixels, bottom: CssPixels, left: CssPixels) {
        self.shrink(-top, -right, -bottom, -left);
    }

    fn corner(&self, index: usize, converter: &DevicePixelConverter) -> CornerRadius {
        CornerRadius {
            horizontal_radius: converter.floored_device_pixels(self.values[index]),
            vertical_radius: converter.floored_device_pixels(self.values[index + 1]),
        }
    }

    pub fn as_corners(&self, converter: &DevicePixelConverter) -> CornerRadii {
        if !self.has_any_radius() {
            return CornerRadii::default();
        }
        self.corners_unconditionally(converter)
    }

    pub fn corners_unconditionally(&self, converter: &DevicePixelConverter) -> CornerRadii {
        CornerRadii {
            top_left: self.corner(0, converter),
            top_right: self.corner(2, converter),
            bottom_right: self.corner(4, converter),
            bottom_left: self.corner(6, converter),
        }
    }

    pub fn has_any_radius(&self) -> bool {
        let [tl_h, tl_v, tr_h, tr_v, br_h, br_v, bl_h, bl_v] = self.values;
        Self::corner_present(tl_h, tl_v)
            || Self::corner_present(tr_h, tr_v)
            || Self::corner_present(br_h, br_v)
            || Self::corner_present(bl_h, bl_v)
    }

    pub fn contains(&self, point: CssPixelPoint, rect: CssPixelRect) -> bool {
        if !rect.contains_point(point) {
            return false;
        }
        if !self.has_any_radius() {
            return true;
        }
        let outside_ellipse =
            |horizontal: CssPixels, vertical: CssPixels, center_x: CssPixels, center_y: CssPixels| -> bool {
                let dx = (point.x - center_x).to_double() / horizontal.to_double();
                let dy = (point.y - center_y).to_double() / vertical.to_double();
                dx * dx + dy * dy > 1.0
            };
        let [tl_h, tl_v, tr_h, tr_v, br_h, br_v, bl_h, bl_v] = self.values;
        if Self::corner_present(tl_h, tl_v) {
            let center_x = rect.left() + tl_h;
            let center_y = rect.top() + tl_v;
            if point.x < center_x && point.y < center_y && outside_ellipse(tl_h, tl_v, center_x, center_y) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        if Self::corner_present(tr_h, tr_v) {
            let center_x = rect.right() - tr_h;
            let center_y = rect.top() + tr_v;
            if point.x > center_x && point.y < center_y && outside_ellipse(tr_h, tr_v, center_x, center_y) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        if Self::corner_present(br_h, br_v) {
            let center_x = rect.right() - br_h;
            let center_y = rect.bottom() - br_v;
            if point.x > center_x && point.y > center_y && outside_ellipse(br_h, br_v, center_x, center_y) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        if Self::corner_present(bl_h, bl_v) {
            let center_x = rect.left() + bl_h;
            let center_y = rect.bottom() - bl_v;
            if point.x < center_x && point.y > center_y && outside_ellipse(bl_h, bl_v, center_x, center_y) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        true
    }
}

pub(crate) fn border_radii(arena: &impl PaintRead, paintable: NodeSlotId) -> BorderRadii {
    let Some(style) = arena.node_style_if_live(paintable) else {
        return BorderRadii::default();
    };
    crate::painting::visual_context::node_values::border_radii_data(style, arena, paintable)
}

pub(crate) fn piece_border_radii(
    arena: &impl PaintRead,
    paintable: NodeSlotId,
    piece: &crate::painting::paintable_data::InlineBoxPieceRecord,
) -> BorderRadii {
    let Some(style) = arena.node_style_if_live(paintable) else {
        return BorderRadii::default();
    };
    crate::painting::visual_context::node_values::piece_border_radii_data(
        style,
        piece.border_box_rect.width,
        piece.border_box_rect.height,
        piece.present_edges,
    )
}

pub(crate) fn fragment_border_box_and_radii(
    arena: &impl PaintRead,
    paintable: NodeSlotId,
    index: usize,
) -> (CssPixelRect, BorderRadii) {
    let rect = paintable_geometry::absolute_fragment_border_box_rect(arena, paintable, index);
    let Some(style) = arena.node_style_if_live(paintable) else {
        return (rect, BorderRadii::default());
    };
    let radii = crate::painting::visual_context::node_values::piece_border_radii_data(
        style,
        rect.width,
        rect.height,
        paintable_geometry::committed_fragment_present_edges(arena, paintable, index),
    );
    (rect, radii)
}

pub(crate) fn border_boxes_and_radii_of_fragments(
    arena: &impl PaintRead,
    paintable: NodeSlotId,
) -> smallvec::SmallVec<[(CssPixelRect, BorderRadii); 1]> {
    let fragment_count = paintable_geometry::fragment_count(arena, paintable);
    if fragment_count > 1 && !crate::painting::node_painting::is_fragmented_inline(arena, paintable) {
        return (0..fragment_count)
            .map(|index| fragment_border_box_and_radii(arena, paintable, index))
            .collect();
    }
    smallvec::smallvec![(
        paintable_geometry::absolute_border_box_rect(arena, paintable),
        border_radii(arena, paintable)
    )]
}
