//! Contours of boxes whose corners are shaped by `corner-shape`.
//!
//! https://drafts.csswg.org/css-borders-4/#corner-shape-rendering

use crate::css::computed_value_views::ComputedValuesView;
use ak::math;
use libgfx_rust::path::Path;
use libgfx_rust::{CornerRadii, CornerRadius, FloatPoint, FloatRect};

/// The superellipse parameter of each corner, in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-right,
/// bottom-left.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct CornerShapes(pub [f64; 4]);

// How many line segments approximate each curved corner.
const SEGMENTS_PER_CURVED_CORNER: u32 = 32;

impl CornerShapes {
    pub(crate) fn of(style: ComputedValuesView<'_>) -> Self {
        let border = style.border();
        Self([
            border.corner_top_left_shape,
            border.corner_top_right_shape,
            border.corner_bottom_right_shape,
            border.corner_bottom_left_shape,
        ])
    }

    /// Whether the corners with a radius need a contour other than the elliptical arcs that rounded
    /// rectangles are drawn with.
    pub(crate) fn needs_contour(&self, radii: CornerRadii) -> bool {
        [radii.top_left, radii.top_right, radii.bottom_right, radii.bottom_left]
            .into_iter()
            .zip(self.0)
            .any(|(radius, shape)| radius.is_present() && shape != 1.0)
    }
}

/// Insets from the border box to the edge a contour traces, positive inward.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct Insets {
    pub top: f64,
    pub right: f64,
    pub bottom: f64,
    pub left: f64,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
struct Point {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
struct Vector {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

impl Point {
    fn extended_by(self, vector: Vector) -> Point {
        Point {
            x: self.x + vector.x,
            y: self.y + vector.y,
        }
    }

    fn vector_to(self, other: Point) -> Vector {
        Vector {
            x: other.x - self.x,
            y: other.y - self.y,
        }
    }
}

impl Vector {
    fn scaled(self, factor: f64) -> Vector {
        Vector {
            x: self.x * factor,
            y: self.y * factor,
        }
    }

    fn plus(self, other: Vector) -> Vector {
        Vector {
            x: self.x + other.x,
            y: self.y + other.y,
        }
    }

    fn normalized(self) -> Vector {
        let length = math::hypot(self.x, self.y);
        if length == 0.0 {
            return self;
        }
        self.scaled(1.0 / length)
    }

    fn perpendicular(self) -> Vector {
        Vector { x: -self.y, y: self.x }
    }

    fn dot(self, other: Vector) -> f64 {
        self.x * other.x + self.y * other.y
    }
}

/// The intersection between the lines through `a1` and `a2` and through `b1` and `b2`, if they are
/// not parallel.
fn line_intersection(a1: Point, a2: Point, b1: Point, b2: Point) -> Option<Point> {
    let a = a1.vector_to(a2);
    let b = b1.vector_to(b2);
    let denominator = a.x * b.y - a.y * b.x;
    if denominator.abs() < 1e-12 {
        return None;
    }
    let t = ((b1.x - a1.x) * b.y - (b1.y - a1.y) * b.x) / denominator;
    Some(a1.extended_by(a.scaled(t)))
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-borders-4/#normalized-superellipse-half-corner
fn normalized_superellipse_half_corner(k: f64) -> f64 {
    if k == f64::NEG_INFINITY {
        return 0.0;
    }
    if k == f64::INFINITY {
        return 1.0;
    }
    let n = math::pow(2f64, k.abs());
    let convex_half_corner = math::pow(0.5f64, 1.0 / n);
    if k < 0.0 {
        1.0 - convex_half_corner
    } else {
        convex_half_corner
    }
}

struct CornerInputs {
    start_radius: f64,
    end_radius: f64,
    start_inset: f64,
    end_inset: f64,
    target_corner_outer: Point,
    normalized_v3: Vector,
    normalized_v2: Vector,
    k: f64,
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-borders-4/#border-aligned-corner-clip-out-path
// NB: The clip-out path runs from the corner's start edge to its end edge, clockwise around the box, so
//     the points it extends to replace the corner of the contour. `None` clips nothing out, which leaves
//     the corner square.
fn border_aligned_corner_clip_out_path(inputs: CornerInputs) -> Option<Vec<Point>> {
    let CornerInputs {
        start_radius,
        end_radius,
        start_inset,
        end_inset,
        target_corner_outer,
        normalized_v3,
        normalized_v2,
        k,
    } = inputs;

    // 1. If startRadius or endRadius is zero, then return an empty path.
    if start_radius == 0.0 || end_radius == 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    // 2. If K is ∞, then return an empty path.
    if k == f64::INFINITY {
        return None;
    }

    // 3. Let vectorToOriginalCornerOuterV3 be normalizedV3, scaled by -endInset.
    let vector_to_original_corner_outer_v3 = normalized_v3.scaled(-end_inset);
    // 4. Let vectorToOriginalCornerOuterV2 be normalizedV2, scaled by -startInset.
    let vector_to_original_corner_outer_v2 = normalized_v2.scaled(-start_inset);
    // 5. Let originalCornerOuter be targetCornerOuter, extended by « vectorToOriginalCornerOuterV3,
    //    vectorToOriginalCornerOuterV2 ».
    let original_corner_outer = target_corner_outer
        .extended_by(vector_to_original_corner_outer_v3)
        .extended_by(vector_to_original_corner_outer_v2);

    // 6. Let originalCornerStart be originalCornerOuter, extended by « normalizedV3 scaled by endRadius ».
    let original_corner_start = original_corner_outer.extended_by(normalized_v3.scaled(end_radius));
    // 7. Let originalCornerEnd be originalCornerOuter, extended by « normalizedV2 scaled by startRadius ».
    let original_corner_end = original_corner_outer.extended_by(normalized_v2.scaled(start_radius));

    // 8. Let halfCornerX be the normalized superellipse half corner given K.
    let half_corner_x = normalized_superellipse_half_corner(k);
    // 9. Let controlPointX be clamp(0, 1/(sqrt(2) - 1) ⋅ halfCornerX - 1/sqrt(2), 1).
    let control_point_x =
        (1.0 / (std::f64::consts::SQRT_2 - 1.0) * half_corner_x - 1.0 / std::f64::consts::SQRT_2).clamp(0.0, 1.0);

    // 10. Let insetDiff be clamp(-startRadius, endInset - startInset, endRadius).
    let inset_diff = (end_inset - start_inset).clamp(-start_radius, end_radius);
    // 11. If K is smaller than or equal to zero, and insetDiff is equal to -startRadius or endRadius, then return
    //     an empty path.
    if k <= 0.0 && (inset_diff == -start_radius || inset_diff == end_radius) {
        return None;
    }

    // 12. Let startControlPointX be controlPointX.
    let mut start_control_point_x = control_point_x;
    // 13. Let endControlPointX be controlPointX.
    let mut end_control_point_x = control_point_x;
    // 14. If insetDiff is not zero:
    if inset_diff != 0.0 {
        let root = (start_radius * start_radius + end_radius * end_radius - inset_diff * inset_diff).sqrt();
        // 1. Let bevelNormalVectorX be endRadius ⋅ insetDiff + startRadius ⋅ sqrt(startRadius² + endRadius² -
        //    insetDiff²).
        let bevel_normal_vector_x = end_radius * inset_diff + start_radius * root;
        // 2. Let bevelNormalVectorY be -startRadius ⋅ insetDiff + endRadius ⋅ sqrt(startRadius² + endRadius² -
        //    insetDiff²).
        let bevel_normal_vector_y = -start_radius * inset_diff + end_radius * root;
        // 3. Let bevelControlPointX be (startRadius ⋅ bevelNormalVectorY)/(startRadius ⋅ bevelNormalVectorY +
        //    endRadius ⋅ bevelNormalVectorX).
        let bevel_control_point_x = (start_radius * bevel_normal_vector_y)
            / (start_radius * bevel_normal_vector_y + end_radius * bevel_normal_vector_x);
        // 4. Set startControlPointX to bevelControlPointX · (2 · controlPointX) if K is less than zero,
        //    1 - (1 - bevelControlPointX) · (2 · (1 - controlPointX)) otherwise.
        start_control_point_x = if k < 0.0 {
            bevel_control_point_x * (2.0 * control_point_x)
        } else {
            1.0 - (1.0 - bevel_control_point_x) * (2.0 * (1.0 - control_point_x))
        };
        // 5. Set endControlPointX to 2 ⋅ controlPointX - startControlPointX.
        end_control_point_x = 2.0 * control_point_x - start_control_point_x;
    }

    // 15. Let unmappedStartNormalVector be the two-dimensional vector ((1 - startControlPointX) ⋅ startRadius,
    //     startControlPointX ⋅ endRadius), normalized.
    let unmapped_start_normal_vector = Vector {
        x: (1.0 - start_control_point_x) * start_radius,
        y: start_control_point_x * end_radius,
    }
    .normalized();
    // 16. Let unmappedEndNormalVector be the two-dimensional vector (endControlPointX ⋅ startRadius,
    //     (1 - endControlPointX) ⋅ endRadius), normalized.
    let unmapped_end_normal_vector = Vector {
        x: end_control_point_x * start_radius,
        y: (1.0 - end_control_point_x) * end_radius,
    }
    .normalized();

    // 17. Let startNormalVector be the sum of « normalizedV3 scaled by unmappedStartNormalVector[0], normalizedV2
    //     scaled by unmappedStartNormalVector[1] ».
    let start_normal_vector = normalized_v3
        .scaled(unmapped_start_normal_vector.x)
        .plus(normalized_v2.scaled(unmapped_start_normal_vector.y));
    // 18. Let endNormalVector be the sum of « normalizedV3 scaled by unmappedEndNormalVector[0], normalizedV2
    //     scaled by unmappedEndNormalVector[1] ».
    let end_normal_vector = normalized_v3
        .scaled(unmapped_end_normal_vector.x)
        .plus(normalized_v2.scaled(unmapped_end_normal_vector.y));

    // 19. Let adjustedCornerStart be originalCornerStart, extended by « startNormalVector scaled by startInset ».
    let mut adjusted_corner_start = original_corner_start.extended_by(start_normal_vector.scaled(start_inset));
    // 20. Let adjustedCornerEnd be originalCornerEnd, extended by « endNormalVector scaled by endInset ».
    let mut adjusted_corner_end = original_corner_end.extended_by(end_normal_vector.scaled(end_inset));

    // 21. Let startTangentVector be the perpendicular of startNormalVector, scaled by -1.
    let start_tangent_vector = start_normal_vector.perpendicular().scaled(-1.0);
    // 22. Let endTangentVector be the perpendicular of endNormalVector.
    let end_tangent_vector = end_normal_vector.perpendicular();

    // 23. Let miterStart be adjustedCornerStart.
    let mut miter_start = adjusted_corner_start;
    // 24. Let miterEnd be adjustedCornerEnd.
    let mut miter_end = adjusted_corner_end;

    // 25. If startInset is less than zero:
    if start_inset < 0.0 {
        // 1. Let clipStart be targetCornerOuter, extended by « normalizedV3 ».
        let clip_start = target_corner_outer.extended_by(normalized_v3);
        // 2. Set miterStart to the intersection between the lines (adjustedCornerStart, adjustedCornerStart
        //    extended by « startTangentVector ») and (clipStart, targetCornerOuter). If the lines are parallel,
        //    let it be adjustedCornerStart.
        miter_start = line_intersection(
            adjusted_corner_start,
            adjusted_corner_start.extended_by(start_tangent_vector),
            clip_start,
            target_corner_outer,
        )
        .unwrap_or(adjusted_corner_start);
        // 3. If K is greater than or equal to zero, set adjustedCornerStart to miterStart.
        if k >= 0.0 {
            adjusted_corner_start = miter_start;
        }
    }

    // 26. If endInset is less than zero:
    if end_inset < 0.0 {
        // 1. Let clipEnd be targetCornerOuter, extended by « normalizedV2 ».
        let clip_end = target_corner_outer.extended_by(normalized_v2);
        // 2. Set miterEnd to the intersection between the lines (adjustedCornerEnd, adjustedCornerEnd extended by
        //    « endTangentVector ») and (clipEnd, targetCornerOuter). If the lines are parallel, let it be
        //    adjustedCornerEnd.
        miter_end = line_intersection(
            adjusted_corner_end,
            adjusted_corner_end.extended_by(end_tangent_vector),
            clip_end,
            target_corner_outer,
        )
        .unwrap_or(adjusted_corner_end);
        // 3. If K is greater than or equal to zero, set adjustedCornerEnd to miterEnd.
        if k >= 0.0 {
            adjusted_corner_end = miter_end;
        }
    }

    // 27. Let adjustedCornerDiagonalVector be the vector between adjustedCornerStart and adjustedCornerEnd.
    let adjusted_corner_diagonal_vector = adjusted_corner_start.vector_to(adjusted_corner_end);
    // 28. Let adjustedCornerHeight be the dot product of adjustedCornerDiagonalVector and normalizedV2.
    let adjusted_corner_height = adjusted_corner_diagonal_vector.dot(normalized_v2);

    // 29. Let adjustedCornerOuter be adjustedCornerEnd, extended by « normalizedV2 scaled by
    //     -adjustedCornerHeight ».
    let adjusted_corner_outer = adjusted_corner_end.extended_by(normalized_v2.scaled(-adjusted_corner_height));
    // 30. Let adjustedCornerCenter be adjustedCornerStart, extended by « normalizedV2 scaled by
    //     adjustedCornerHeight ».
    let adjusted_corner_center = adjusted_corner_start.extended_by(normalized_v2.scaled(adjusted_corner_height));

    // 31. Let mapPointToCorner be the following steps, given numbers x and y, DOMPointReadOnly start, end, and
    //     center:
    let map_point_to_corner = |x: f64, y: f64, start: Point, end: Point, center: Point| {
        // 1. Let v1 be the vector between center and end, scaled by x.
        let v1 = center.vector_to(end).scaled(x);
        // 2. Let v4 be the vector between center and start, scaled by y.
        let v4 = center.vector_to(start).scaled(y);
        // 3. Return center, extended by « v1, v4 ».
        center.extended_by(v1).extended_by(v4)
    };

    // 32. Let selfIntersection be undefined.
    let mut self_intersection = None;
    // 33. If K, startInset, and endInset are less than zero:
    if k < 0.0 && start_inset < 0.0 && end_inset < 0.0 {
        // 1. If -endInset is greater than or equal to startRadius:
        if -end_inset >= start_radius {
            // 1. Set selfIntersection to the intersection between the segment (miterStart, adjustedCornerStart) and
            //    the line (miterEnd, adjustedCornerEnd).
            self_intersection = line_intersection(miter_start, adjusted_corner_start, miter_end, adjusted_corner_end);
        }
        // 2. If -startInset is greater than or equal to endRadius, and selfIntersection is undefined:
        if -start_inset >= end_radius && self_intersection.is_none() {
            // 1. Set selfIntersection to the intersection between the segment (miterEnd, adjustedCornerEnd) and
            //    the line (miterStart, adjustedCornerStart).
            self_intersection = line_intersection(miter_end, adjusted_corner_end, miter_start, adjusted_corner_start);
        }
    }

    // 34. Let path be a path, starting at miterStart.
    let mut path = vec![miter_start];

    // 35. If selfIntersection is a defined point:
    if let Some(self_intersection) = self_intersection {
        // 1. Extend path to selfIntersection.
        path.push(self_intersection);
    }
    // 36. Otherwise, if K is -∞:
    else if k == f64::NEG_INFINITY {
        // 1. Extend path to adjustedCornerCenter.
        path.push(adjusted_corner_center);
    }
    // 37. Otherwise, if K is greater than zero or less than or equal to -1:
    else if k > 0.0 || k <= -1.0 {
        // 1. Let n be 2^abs(K).
        let n = math::pow(2f64, k.abs());
        // 2. Let curveCenter be adjustedCornerOuter if K is less than zero, adjustedCornerCenter otherwise.
        let curve_center = if k < 0.0 {
            adjusted_corner_outer
        } else {
            adjusted_corner_center
        };
        // 3. For every T between 0 and 1, in an implementation-approximated manner, extend path to the result of
        //    calling mapPointToCorner given T^(1/n) and (1 - T)^(1/n), adjustedCornerStart, adjustedCornerEnd,
        //    and curveCenter.
        for step in 0..=SEGMENTS_PER_CURVED_CORNER {
            let t = f64::from(step) / f64::from(SEGMENTS_PER_CURVED_CORNER);
            path.push(map_point_to_corner(
                math::pow(t, 1.0 / n),
                math::pow(1.0 - t, 1.0 / n),
                adjusted_corner_start,
                adjusted_corner_end,
                curve_center,
            ));
        }
    }
    // 38. Otherwise, if K is greater than -1 and less than zero:
    else if k > -1.0 && k < 0.0 {
        // 1. Let tangentIntersection be the intersection between the lines (adjustedCornerStart,
        //    adjustedCornerStart extended by « startTangentVector ») and (adjustedCornerEnd, adjustedCornerEnd
        //    extended by « endTangentVector »). If the lines are parallel, let it be adjustedCornerStart.
        let tangent_intersection = line_intersection(
            adjusted_corner_start,
            adjusted_corner_start.extended_by(start_tangent_vector),
            adjusted_corner_end,
            adjusted_corner_end.extended_by(end_tangent_vector),
        )
        .unwrap_or(adjusted_corner_start);
        // 2. For every T between 0 and 1, in an implementation-approximated manner, extend path to the result of
        //    calling mapPointToCorner given 1 - (1 - T)^(1/2) and 1 - T^(1/2), adjustedCornerStart,
        //    adjustedCornerEnd, and tangentIntersection.
        for step in 0..=SEGMENTS_PER_CURVED_CORNER {
            let t = f64::from(step) / f64::from(SEGMENTS_PER_CURVED_CORNER);
            path.push(map_point_to_corner(
                1.0 - (1.0 - t).sqrt(),
                1.0 - t.sqrt(),
                adjusted_corner_start,
                adjusted_corner_end,
                tangent_intersection,
            ));
        }
    }

    // 39. Extend path to miterEnd.
    path.push(miter_end);
    // 40. Return path.
    Some(path)
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-borders-4/#border-contour-path
/// `border_rect` and `radii` are the border box and its used radii, in the device space the path is built in.
pub(crate) fn border_contour_path(
    border_rect: FloatRect,
    radii: CornerRadii,
    shapes: CornerShapes,
    insets: Insets,
) -> Path {
    let mut builder = Path::new();
    append_border_contour_path(&mut builder, border_rect, radii, shapes, insets);
    builder
}

/// Appends the border contour path to `builder` as a closed subpath of its own.
pub(crate) fn append_border_contour_path(
    builder: &mut Path,
    border_rect: FloatRect,
    radii: CornerRadii,
    shapes: CornerShapes,
    insets: Insets,
) {
    // 1. Let borderRect be element's border box.
    // 2. Let targetRect be borderRect, inset by topInset, rightInset, bottomInset, leftInset.
    let left = f64::from(border_rect.x) + insets.left;
    let top = f64::from(border_rect.y) + insets.top;
    let right = f64::from(border_rect.x + border_rect.width) - insets.right;
    let bottom = f64::from(border_rect.y + border_rect.height) - insets.bottom;

    // 3. Let path be a path that traces targetRect.
    // 4-7. Let topRightRadius, bottomRightRadius, bottomLeftRadius, and topLeftRadius be element's used values of
    //      the border radii.
    let width = |radius: CornerRadius| f64::from(radius.horizontal_radius);
    let height = |radius: CornerRadius| f64::from(radius.vertical_radius);

    // 8. Let adjustedInset be the following steps, given a radius radius, and numbers insetX and insetY:
    //    1. Let adjustedRadius be the outset-adjusted border radius given borderRect's size, radius, and the
    //       outset (-insetX, -insetY).
    //    2. Return the inset (radius's width - adjustedRadius's width, radius's height - adjustedRadius's height).
    // NB: An inward outset reduces a radius by the outset, down to zero, so the inset a corner is adjusted by is
    //     at most its radius. Outward insets keep their size.
    let adjusted_inset = |radius: f64, inset: f64| if inset > 0.0 { inset.min(radius) } else { inset };

    // 9-12. Clip out from path the border-aligned corner clip-out path of each corner.
    // NB: Each clip-out path runs clockwise from the edge before its corner to the one after it, so the contour
    //     is those paths in clockwise order, with a corner that clips nothing out left square.
    let corners = [
        // Top-left.
        CornerInputs {
            start_radius: width(radii.top_left),
            end_radius: height(radii.top_left),
            start_inset: adjusted_inset(width(radii.top_left), insets.left),
            end_inset: adjusted_inset(height(radii.top_left), insets.top),
            target_corner_outer: Point { x: left, y: top },
            normalized_v3: Vector { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 },
            normalized_v2: Vector { x: 1.0, y: 0.0 },
            k: shapes.0[0],
        },
        // Top-right.
        CornerInputs {
            start_radius: height(radii.top_right),
            end_radius: width(radii.top_right),
            start_inset: adjusted_inset(height(radii.top_right), insets.top),
            end_inset: adjusted_inset(width(radii.top_right), insets.right),
            target_corner_outer: Point { x: right, y: top },
            normalized_v3: Vector { x: -1.0, y: 0.0 },
            normalized_v2: Vector { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 },
            k: shapes.0[1],
        },
        // Bottom-right.
        CornerInputs {
            start_radius: width(radii.bottom_right),
            end_radius: height(radii.bottom_right),
            start_inset: adjusted_inset(width(radii.bottom_right), insets.right),
            end_inset: adjusted_inset(height(radii.bottom_right), insets.bottom),
            target_corner_outer: Point { x: right, y: bottom },
            normalized_v3: Vector { x: 0.0, y: -1.0 },
            normalized_v2: Vector { x: -1.0, y: 0.0 },
            k: shapes.0[2],
        },
        // Bottom-left.
        CornerInputs {
            start_radius: height(radii.bottom_left),
            end_radius: width(radii.bottom_left),
            start_inset: adjusted_inset(height(radii.bottom_left), insets.bottom),
            end_inset: adjusted_inset(width(radii.bottom_left), insets.left),
            target_corner_outer: Point { x: left, y: bottom },
            normalized_v3: Vector { x: 1.0, y: 0.0 },
            normalized_v2: Vector { x: 0.0, y: -1.0 },
            k: shapes.0[3],
        },
    ];

    let mut first = true;
    let mut extend = |point: Point| {
        if first {
            builder.move_to(FloatPoint {
                x: point.x as f32,
                y: point.y as f32,
            });
            first = false;
        } else {
            builder.line_to(FloatPoint {
                x: point.x as f32,
                y: point.y as f32,
            });
        }
    };
    let target_rect = (left, top, right, bottom);
    for corner in corners {
        let corner_outer = corner.target_corner_outer;
        // NB: Clipping the corner out of targetRect leaves the part of the clip-out path inside targetRect as the
        //     contour, which also holds when an inset moves the clip-out path partly outside targetRect.
        let inside = border_aligned_corner_clip_out_path(corner)
            .map(|points| polyline_inside_rect(&points, target_rect))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        if inside.is_empty() {
            extend(corner_outer);
        } else {
            inside.into_iter().for_each(&mut extend);
        }
    }
    builder.close();
    // 13. Return path.
}

/// The parts of `polyline` inside the rectangle `(left, top, right, bottom)`, in order.
fn polyline_inside_rect(polyline: &[Point], (left, top, right, bottom): (f64, f64, f64, f64)) -> Vec<Point> {
    const EPSILON: f64 = 1e-6;
    let mut inside: Vec<Point> = Vec::new();
    for segment in polyline.windows(2) {
        let (from, to) = (segment[0], segment[1]);
        let delta = from.vector_to(to);
        // Liang-Barsky: narrow the segment's parameter range to each side of the rectangle in turn.
        let (mut entry, mut exit) = (0.0f64, 1.0f64);
        let mut visible = true;
        for (step, room) in [
            (-delta.x, from.x - left + EPSILON),
            (delta.x, right - from.x + EPSILON),
            (-delta.y, from.y - top + EPSILON),
            (delta.y, bottom - from.y + EPSILON),
        ] {
            if step == 0.0 {
                if room < 0.0 {
                    visible = false;
                }
                continue;
            }
            let t = room / step;
            if step < 0.0 {
                entry = entry.max(t);
            } else {
                exit = exit.min(t);
            }
        }
        if !visible || entry > exit {
            continue;
        }
        for t in [entry, exit] {
            let point = from.extended_by(delta.scaled(t));
            if inside
                .last()
                .is_none_or(|last| (last.x - point.x).abs() > EPSILON || (last.y - point.y).abs() > EPSILON)
            {
                inside.push(point);
            }
        }
    }
    inside
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn corner(k: f64, start_inset: f64, end_inset: f64) -> Vec<Point> {
        border_aligned_corner_clip_out_path(CornerInputs {
            start_radius: 10.0,
            end_radius: 10.0,
            start_inset,
            end_inset,
            target_corner_outer: Point { x: 100.0, y: 0.0 },
            normalized_v3: Vector { x: -1.0, y: 0.0 },
            normalized_v2: Vector { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 },
            k,
        })
        .unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_bevel_cuts_the_corner_with_a_straight_line() {
        assert_eq!(
            corner(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            [Point { x: 90.0, y: 0.0 }, Point { x: 100.0, y: 10.0 }]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_notch_steps_in_to_the_corner_center() {
        assert_eq!(
            corner(f64::NEG_INFINITY, 0.0, 0.0),
            [
                Point { x: 90.0, y: 0.0 },
                Point { x: 90.0, y: 10.0 },
                Point { x: 100.0, y: 10.0 }
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_round_corner_passes_through_the_arc_midpoint() {
        let points = corner(1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
        let middle = points[points.len() / 2];
        let expected = 90.0 + 10.0 * std::f64::consts::FRAC_1_SQRT_2;
        assert!(
            (middle.x - expected).abs() < 1e-9
                && (middle.y - (10.0 - 10.0 * std::f64::consts::FRAC_1_SQRT_2)).abs() < 1e-9
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_inset_bevel_is_the_outer_bevel_moved_inward_along_its_normal() {
        // The border box corner is at (100, 0), and the target corner is 2px inside it.
        let points = border_aligned_corner_clip_out_path(CornerInputs {
            start_radius: 10.0,
            end_radius: 10.0,
            start_inset: 2.0,
            end_inset: 2.0,
            target_corner_outer: Point { x: 98.0, y: 2.0 },
            normalized_v3: Vector { x: -1.0, y: 0.0 },
            normalized_v2: Vector { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 },
            k: 0.0,
        })
        .unwrap();
        let offset = std::f64::consts::SQRT_2;
        let (start, end) = (points[0], points[points.len() - 1]);
        assert!((start.x - (90.0 - offset)).abs() < 1e-9 && (start.y - offset).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert!((end.x - (100.0 - offset)).abs() < 1e-9 && (end.y - (10.0 + offset)).abs() < 1e-9);
    }

    #[test]
    fn only_the_part_of_a_polyline_inside_the_rect_is_kept() {
        let inside = polyline_inside_rect(
            &[
                Point { x: -5.0, y: 5.0 },
                Point { x: 5.0, y: 5.0 },
                Point { x: 5.0, y: 15.0 },
            ],
            (0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 10.0),
        );
        assert_eq!(inside.len(), 3);
        assert!((inside[0].x - 0.0).abs() < 1e-5 && (inside[0].y - 5.0).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert_eq!(inside[1], Point { x: 5.0, y: 5.0 });
        assert!((inside[2].x - 5.0).abs() < 1e-9 && (inside[2].y - 10.0).abs() < 1e-5);
    }
}

//! Lowers CSS filter functions to the filter graphs painting hands over as bytes.

use libgfx_rust::filter::{Filter, MAXIMUM_FILTER_DEPTH};
use libgfx_rust::{Color, ColorFilterType};

use crate::css::computed_value_types::{ComputedFilter, ComputedFilterOperation};
use crate::css::css_pixels::CssPixels;
use crate::painting::filter_bytes::filter_functions_graph;
use crate::painting::host::visual_context::ResolvedSvgFilter;

const FILTER_KIND_BLUR: u8 = 0;
const FILTER_KIND_DROP_SHADOW: u8 = 1;
const FILTER_KIND_HUE_ROTATE: u8 = 2;
const FILTER_KIND_COLOR: u8 = 3;
pub(crate) const FILTER_KIND_URL: u8 = 4;

pub(crate) fn can_spread(filter: &ComputedFilter) -> bool {
    filter
        .operations
        .as_slice()
        .iter()
        .any(|operation| !matches!(operation.kind, FILTER_KIND_HUE_ROTATE | FILTER_KIND_COLOR))
}

pub(crate) fn contains_url(filter: &ComputedFilter) -> bool {
    filter
        .operations
        .as_slice()
        .iter()
        .any(|operation| operation.kind == FILTER_KIND_URL)
}

/// The serialized graph for a filter list's functions; `None` when the list has none, or more than a graph can hold.
pub(crate) fn serialize_non_url_filter(filter: &ComputedFilter, device_pixels_per_css_pixel: f64) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    css_filter(filter.operations.as_slice(), device_pixels_per_css_pixel)?.serialize_within_maximum_depth()
}

/// Resolves the `url()` references of a filter list through the host, one reference at a time.
/// The last reference's graph and region are the ones that apply; a reference the host cannot
/// resolve fails the list as a whole.
/// The serialized graph for a filter list whose `url()` references the host has resolved.
pub(crate) fn serialize_filter_with_resolved_svg(
    filter: &ComputedFilter,
    resolved_svg_filter: ResolvedSvgFilter,
    device_pixels_per_css_pixel: f64,
) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    if resolved_svg_filter.failed {
        return None;
    }
    css_filter_with_svg(
        filter.operations.as_slice(),
        resolved_svg_filter.filter,
        device_pixels_per_css_pixel,
    )?
    .serialize_within_maximum_depth()
}

/// Combines the functions of a filter list with the SVG filter its `url()` references resolved
/// to, which is applied last, after every function. A list with more functions than a graph can
/// hold has no graph, so its SVG filter does not apply alone.
fn css_filter_with_svg(
    operations: &[ComputedFilterOperation],
    svg_filter: Option<Filter>,
    device_pixels_per_css_pixel: f64,
) -> Option<Filter> {
    let function_count = operations
        .iter()
        .filter(|operation| operation.kind != FILTER_KIND_URL)
        .count();
    if function_count > MAXIMUM_FILTER_DEPTH {
        return None;
    }
    match (svg_filter, css_filter(operations, device_pixels_per_css_pixel)) {
        (Some(svg_filter), Some(css_filter)) => Some(Filter::compose(svg_filter, css_filter)),
        (Some(filter), None) | (None, Some(filter)) => Some(filter),
        (None, None) => None,
    }
}

/// The graph of a computed filter list's functions, skipping the `url()` references the host
/// resolves.
pub(crate) fn css_filter(operations: &[ComputedFilterOperation], device_pixels_per_css_pixel: f64) -> Option<Filter> {
    filter_functions_graph(
        operations
            .iter()
            .filter(|operation| operation.kind != FILTER_KIND_URL)
            .map(|operation| filter_function(operation, device_pixels_per_css_pixel)),
    )
}

fn filter_function(operation: &ComputedFilterOperation, device_pixels_per_css_pixel: f64) -> Filter {
    match operation.kind {
        FILTER_KIND_BLUR => {
            let radius =
                (CssPixels::nearest_value_for_f32(operation.amount).to_double() * device_pixels_per_css_pixel) as f32;
            Filter::blur(radius, radius, None)
        }
        FILTER_KIND_DROP_SHADOW => {
            let scale = |raw| (CssPixels::from_raw(raw).to_double() * device_pixels_per_css_pixel) as f32;
            Filter::drop_shadow(
                scale(operation.shadow_offset_x),
                scale(operation.shadow_offset_y),
                scale(operation.shadow_radius),
                Color(operation.shadow_color),
                None,
            )
        }
        FILTER_KIND_COLOR => {
            let kind = ColorFilterType::from_i32(i32::from(operation.color_operation))
                .expect("computed filter holds an unknown color operation");
            Filter::color(kind, operation.amount, None)
        }
        FILTER_KIND_HUE_ROTATE => Filter::hue_rotate(operation.amount, None),
        _ => unreachable!("computed filter holds an unknown operation kind"),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::css::computed_value_types::ComputedStyleValueHandle;

    fn operation(kind: u8) -> ComputedFilterOperation {
        ComputedFilterOperation {
            kind,
            color_operation: 0,
            amount: 0.0,
            shadow_offset_x: 0,
            shadow_offset_y: 0,
            shadow_radius: 0,
            shadow_color: 0,
            url_value: ComputedStyleValueHandle {
                pointer: std::ptr::null(),
            },
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn blur_rounds_to_css_pixels_before_scaling_to_device_pixels() {
        let mut blur = operation(FILTER_KIND_BLUR);
        blur.amount = 1.257;
        assert_eq!(css_filter(&[blur], 2.0), Some(Filter::blur(2.5, 2.5, None)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn later_operations_wrap_earlier_ones() {
        let mut color = operation(FILTER_KIND_COLOR);
        color.color_operation = ColorFilterType::Saturate as u8;
        color.amount = 0.75;
        let mut hue_rotate = operation(FILTER_KIND_HUE_ROTATE);
        hue_rotate.amount = 90.0;
        assert_eq!(
            css_filter(&[color, hue_rotate], 1.0),
            Some(Filter::compose(
                Filter::hue_rotate(90.0, None),
                Filter::color(ColorFilterType::Saturate, 0.75, None)
            ))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_empty_list_lowers_to_no_filter() {
        assert_eq!(css_filter(&[], 1.0), None);
        assert_eq!(css_filter(&[operation(FILTER_KIND_URL)], 1.0), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_resolved_svg_filter_wraps_the_filter_functions() {
        let hue_rotate = || {
            let mut hue_rotate = operation(FILTER_KIND_HUE_ROTATE);
            hue_rotate.amount = 90.0;
            hue_rotate
        };
        let svg_filter = Filter::blur(3.0, 3.0, None);
        assert_eq!(
            css_filter_with_svg(&[hue_rotate()], Some(svg_filter.clone()), 1.0),
            Some(Filter::compose(svg_filter.clone(), Filter::hue_rotate(90.0, None)))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            css_filter_with_svg(&[], Some(svg_filter.clone()), 1.0),
            Some(svg_filter.clone())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            css_filter_with_svg(&[hue_rotate()], None, 1.0),
            Some(Filter::hue_rotate(90.0, None))
        );
        assert_eq!(css_filter_with_svg(&[], None, 1.0), None);

        let too_many_functions = vec![hue_rotate(); MAXIMUM_FILTER_DEPTH + 1];
        assert_eq!(css_filter_with_svg(&too_many_functions, Some(svg_filter), 1.0), None);
    }
}

use crate::css::style::tree::StyleNodeID;
use crate::layout::{formatting_context, grid_formatting_context};

use serde_json::{Value, json};

fn grid_track_type_name(type_: grid_formatting_context::GridTrackType) -> &'static str {
    match type_ {
        grid_formatting_context::GridTrackType::Explicit => "explicit",
        grid_formatting_context::GridTrackType::Implicit => "implicit",
    }
}

fn grid_track_state_name(state: grid_formatting_context::GridTrackState) -> &'static str {
    match state {
        grid_formatting_context::GridTrackState::Static => "static",
        grid_formatting_context::GridTrackState::Repeat => "repeat",
        grid_formatting_context::GridTrackState::Removed => "removed",
    }
}

fn serialize_grid_line(line: &grid_formatting_context::GridLayoutLine) -> Value {
    json!({
        "breadth": line.breadth.to_double(),
        "names": line.names,
        "negativeNumber": line.negative_number,
        "number": line.number,
        "start": line.start.to_double(),
        "type": grid_track_type_name(line.type_),
    })
}

fn serialize_grid_track(track: &grid_formatting_context::GridLayoutTrack) -> Value {
    json!({
        "breadth": track.breadth.to_double(),
        "start": track.start.to_double(),
        "state": grid_track_state_name(track.state),
        "type": grid_track_type_name(track.type_),
    })
}

fn serialize_grid_area(area: &grid_formatting_context::GridLayoutArea) -> Value {
    json!({
        "columnEnd": area.column_end,
        "columnStart": area.column_start,
        "name": area.name,
        "rowEnd": area.row_end,
        "rowStart": area.row_start,
        "type": grid_track_type_name(area.type_),
    })
}

fn serialize_grid_dimension(dimension: &grid_formatting_context::GridLayoutDimension) -> Value {
    json!({
        "lines": dimension.lines.iter().map(serialize_grid_line).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        "tracks": dimension.tracks.iter().map(serialize_grid_track).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    })
}

fn serialize_grid_fragment(fragment: &grid_formatting_context::GridLayoutFragment) -> Value {
    json!({
        "areas": fragment.areas.iter().map(serialize_grid_area).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        "cols": serialize_grid_dimension(&fragment.columns),
        "rows": serialize_grid_dimension(&fragment.rows),
    })
}

pub(crate) fn serialize_grid_layout(data: &grid_formatting_context::GridLayoutData, container_node_id: i64) -> Vec<u8> {
    serde_json::to_vec(&json!({
        "containerNodeId": container_node_id,
        "direction": crate::css::css_enums::direction::NAMES[data.direction as usize],
        "gridFragments": data.fragments.iter().map(serialize_grid_fragment).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        "isSubgrid": data.is_subgrid,
        "writingMode": crate::css::css_enums::writing_mode::NAMES[data.writing_mode as usize],
    }))
    .expect("grid layout data serializes to JSON")
}

fn flex_layout_growth_state_name(state: formatting_context::FlexLayoutGrowthState) -> &'static str {
    match state {
        formatting_context::FlexLayoutGrowthState::Growing => "growing",
        formatting_context::FlexLayoutGrowthState::Shrinking => "shrinking",
    }
}

fn flex_layout_clamp_state_name(state: formatting_context::FlexLayoutClampState) -> &'static str {
    match state {
        formatting_context::FlexLayoutClampState::Unclamped => "unclamped",
        formatting_context::FlexLayoutClampState::ClampedToMin => "clamped_to_min",
        formatting_context::FlexLayoutClampState::ClampedToMax => "clamped_to_max",
    }
}

fn axis_direction_name(direction: u8) -> &'static str {
    match direction {
        0 => "horizontal-lr",
        1 => "horizontal-rl",
        2 => "vertical-tb",
        3 => "vertical-bt",
        _ => unreachable!("invalid flex axis direction"),
    }
}

pub(crate) fn serialize_flex_layout(
    data: &formatting_context::FlexLayoutData,
    container_node_id: i64,
    resolve_node_id: impl Fn(StyleNodeID) -> Option<i64>,
) -> Vec<u8> {
    let main_axis_direction = axis_direction_name(data.main_axis_direction);
    let cross_axis_direction = axis_direction_name(data.cross_axis_direction);
    let main_size_property_name = if data.main_axis_direction <= 1 {
        "width"
    } else {
        "height"
    };
    let items = data
        .lines
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|line| {
            line.items.iter().filter_map(|item| {
                let node_id = resolve_node_id(item.style_node?)?;
                let sizing = json!({
                    "clampState": flex_layout_clamp_state_name(item.clamp_state),
                    "crossAxisDirection": cross_axis_direction,
                    "crossMaxSize": item.cross_max_size.to_double(),
                    "crossMinSize": item.cross_min_size.to_double(),
                    "lineGrowthState": flex_layout_growth_state_name(line.growth_state),
                    "mainAxisDirection": main_axis_direction,
                    "mainBaseSize": item.main_base_size.to_double(),
                    "mainDeltaSize": item.main_delta_size.to_double(),
                    "mainMaxSize": item.main_max_size.to_double(),
                    "mainMinSize": item.main_min_size.to_double(),
                });
                let mut properties = serde_json::Map::new();
                properties.insert("flex-basis".into(), item.flex_basis.clone().into());
                properties.insert("flex-grow".into(), item.flex_grow.into());
                properties.insert("flex-shrink".into(), item.flex_shrink.into());
                properties.insert(main_size_property_name.into(), item.main_size_property.clone().into());
                properties.insert(
                    format!("min-{main_size_property_name}"),
                    item.main_min_size_property.clone().into(),
                );
                properties.insert(
                    format!("max-{main_size_property_name}"),
                    item.main_max_size_property.clone().into(),
                );
                Some(json!({
                    "nodeId": node_id,
                    "flexItemSizing": sizing,
                    "properties": properties,
                    "computedStyle": {
                        "flexGrow": item.flex_grow,
                        "flexShrink": item.flex_shrink,
                    },
                }))
            })
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();

    serde_json::to_vec(&json!({
        "containerNodeId": container_node_id,
        "properties": {
            "align-content": crate::css::css_enums::align_content::NAMES[data.align_content as usize],
            "align-items": crate::css::css_enums::align_items::NAMES[data.align_items as usize],
            "flex-direction": crate::css::css_enums::flex_direction::NAMES[data.flex_direction as usize],
            "flex-wrap": crate::css::css_enums::flex_wrap::NAMES[data.flex_wrap as usize],
            "justify-content": crate::css::css_enums::justify_content::NAMES[data.justify_content as usize],
        },
        "items": items,
    }))
    .expect("flex layout data serializes to JSON")
}

/*

//! What a display list draws besides its tape: fonts, image frames and the SVG images its commands name, which the list
//! holds for as long as anything holds the list. The compositor is sent a description of the fonts ahead of the list,
//! has the image frames registered with it for as long as anything holds them, and gets the records of the SVG images
//! in the list's tape.

use crate::painting::display_list::builder::RecordedDisplayList;
use crate::painting::display_list::summary::{DisplayListSummary, summarize};
use crate::painting::vector_image_records::VectorImageRecords;
use libgfx_rust::font::FontHandle;
use libgfx_rust::image_frame::ImageFrameHandle;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// The resources a display list draws, each under the id its commands name it by.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(crate) struct DisplayListResources {
    pub(crate) fonts: HashMap<u64, FontHandle>,
    pub(crate) image_frames: HashMap<u64, ImageFrameHandle>,
    pub(crate) vector_images: HashMap<u64, Arc<VectorImageRecords>>,
}

impl DisplayListResources {
    /// Takes the fonts and the image frames `other` holds that this does not.
    pub(crate) fn include_fonts_and_image_frames(&mut self, other: &Self) {
        for (id, font) in &other.fonts {
            self.fonts.entry(*id).or_insert_with(|| font.clone());
        }
        for (id, frame) in &other.image_frames {
            self.image_frames.entry(*id).or_insert_with(|| frame.clone());
        }
    }

    /// These and what the records of their SVG images draw: everything the compositor needs to replay a list that
    /// draws these.
    pub(crate) fn with_vector_image_resources(&self) -> Self {
        let mut closure = self.clone();
        for vector_image in self.vector_images.values() {
            closure.include_fonts_and_image_frames(&vector_image.resources);
        }
        closure
    }

    /// Takes what `source` holds of what `summary` names and this lacks: what a recording copied from the one it read
    /// paint commands from draws.
    pub(crate) fn complete_from(&mut self, summary: &DisplayListSummary, source: &Self) {
        for id in &summary.font_ids {
            if let Some(font) = source.fonts.get(id) {
                self.fonts.entry(*id).or_insert_with(|| font.clone());
            }
        }
        for id in &summary.image_frame_ids {
            if let Some(frame) = source.image_frames.get(id) {
                self.image_frames.entry(*id).or_insert_with(|| frame.clone());
            }
        }
        for id in &summary.vector_image_ids {
            if let Some(vector_image) = source.vector_images.get(id) {
                self.vector_images.entry(*id).or_insert_with(|| vector_image.clone());
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The ids of the resources the commands of `display_list` name.
pub(crate) fn summary_of(display_list: &RecordedDisplayList) -> DisplayListSummary {
    summarize(&display_list.bytes, &display_list.command_runs)
}

/*

//! What changed between two JSON Lines dumps of the display list of one document. Each dump builds the visual context
//! tree anew and names nodes and chunks by what the tape holds, so nodes are matched by their owner and role, records
//! by their owner, phase and command, and neither by an index.

use serde_json::{Map, Value};
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::fmt::Write;

struct DumpedEntry {
    // The owner and role of a node, or the owner, phase and command of a record, with how many came before it.
    key: String,
    // What is compared, with the indices and the names that depend on them left out.
    content: String,
    // What the report prints of it.
    line: String,
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct ParsedDump {
    nodes: Vec<DumpedEntry>,
    records: Vec<DumpedEntry>,
    chunk_ids: Vec<String>,
}

// A node or resource name, such as s12, c3 or font2, as a placeholder, since names count up in print order.
fn without_numbered_names(text: &str) -> String {
    let mut result = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    let characters: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    let mut index = 0;
    while index < characters.len() {
        let character = characters[index];
        let starts_word = index == 0 || !characters[index - 1].is_ascii_alphanumeric();
        if starts_word && character.is_ascii_alphabetic() {
            let word_end = (index..characters.len())
                .find(|&end| !characters[end].is_ascii_alphanumeric() && characters[end] != '_')
                .unwrap_or(characters.len());
            let word: String = characters[index..word_end].iter().collect();
            let letters_end = word.find(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(word.len());
            let (letters, digits) = word.split_at(letters_end);
            if !digits.is_empty() && digits.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
                result.push_str(letters);
                result.push('#');
            } else {
                result.push_str(&word);
            }
            index = word_end;
            continue;
        }
        result.push(character);
        index += 1;
    }
    result
}

// The raw indices and ids of the names in a value, which differ from one dump to the next.
fn without_raw_indices(value: &Value) -> Value {
    match value {
        Value::Object(object) => Value::Object(
            object
                .iter()
                .filter(|(key, _)| key.as_str() != "raw")
                .map(|(key, value)| (key.clone(), without_raw_indices(value)))
                .collect::<Map<_, _>>(),
        ),
        Value::Array(values) => Value::Array(values.iter().map(without_raw_indices).collect()),
        value => value.clone(),
    }
}

fn string_of(object: &Map<String, Value>, key: &str) -> String {
    object.get(key).and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string()
}

fn node_role(description: &str) -> &str {
    let end = description.find(['=', ' ', '(', '[']).unwrap_or(description.len());
    &description[..end]
}

fn parse_dump(jsonl: &str) -> ParsedDump {
    let mut dump = ParsedDump::default();
    let mut key_counts: HashMap<String, usize> = HashMap::new();
    let mut numbered_key = |key: String| {
        let count = key_counts.entry(key.clone()).or_default();
        *count += 1;
        format!("{key}|{count}")
    };
    for line in jsonl.lines() {
        let Ok(Value::Object(object)) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line) else {
            continue;
        };
        match object.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) {
            Some("node") => {
                let (kind, owner, description) = (
                    string_of(&object, "kind"),
                    string_of(&object, "owner"),
                    string_of(&object, "description"),
                );
                let mut line = format!("[{}] {description}", string_of(&object, "name"));
                if !owner.is_empty() {
                    write!(line, " ({owner})").unwrap();
                }
                dump.nodes.push(DumpedEntry {
                    key: numbered_key(format!("node|{kind}|{owner}|{}", node_role(&description))),
                    content: without_numbered_names(&description),
                    line,
                });
            }
            Some("record") => {
                let (op, owner, phase) = (
                    string_of(&object, "op"),
                    string_of(&object, "owner"),
                    string_of(&object, "phase"),
                );
                let compared: Map<String, Value> = ["context", "fields", "inline_clips", "inline_transform", "text"]
                    .into_iter()
                    .filter_map(|key| Some((key.to_string(), without_raw_indices(object.get(key)?))))
                    .collect();
                let fields = object.get("fields").map(without_raw_indices).unwrap_or_default();
                let mut line = format!("{op} {fields}");
                if let Some(text) = object.get("text").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                    write!(line, " text={text:?}").unwrap();
                }
                write!(line, " owner={owner} phase={phase}").unwrap();
                dump.records.push(DumpedEntry {
                    key: numbered_key(format!("record|{op}|{owner}|{phase}")),
                    content: without_numbered_names(&Value::Object(compared).to_string()),
                    line,
                });
            }
            Some("chunk") => dump.chunk_ids.push(string_of(&object, "id")),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    dump
}

fn report_entries(report: &mut String, label: &str, previous: &[DumpedEntry], current: &[DumpedEntry]) {
    let previous_by_key: HashMap<&str, &DumpedEntry> =
        previous.iter().map(|entry| (entry.key.as_str(), entry)).collect();
    let current_keys: HashSet<&str> = current.iter().map(|entry| entry.key.as_str()).collect();
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    let (mut added, mut changed, mut unchanged) = (0, 0, 0);
    for entry in current {
        match previous_by_key.get(entry.key.as_str()) {
            None => {
                added += 1;
                lines.push(format!("  + {}", entry.line));
            }
            Some(previous_entry) if previous_entry.content != entry.content => {
                changed += 1;
                lines.push(format!("  ~ {}\n    was {}", entry.line, previous_entry.line));
            }
            Some(_) => unchanged += 1,
        }
    }
    let mut removed = 0;
    for entry in previous {
        if !current_keys.contains(entry.key.as_str()) {
            removed += 1;
            lines.push(format!("  - {}", entry.line));
        }
    }
    writeln!(
        report,
        "{label}: {added} added, {removed} removed, {changed} changed, {unchanged} unchanged"
    )
    .unwrap();
    for line in lines {
        writeln!(report, "{line}").unwrap();
    }
}

/// What changed from the dump `previous` to the dump `current`, both JSON Lines dumps of the display list of one
/// document, or a summary of `current` where there is no previous one.
pub(crate) fn display_list_dump_changes(previous: Option<&str>, current: &str) -> String {
    let current = parse_dump(current);
    let mut report = String::new();
    let Some(previous) = previous.map(parse_dump) else {
        writeln!(
            report,
            "No previous dump of this document. This one, of {} nodes, {} records and {} chunks, is what the next one is compared with.",
            current.nodes.len(),
            current.records.len(),
            current.chunk_ids.len()
        )
        .unwrap();
        return report;
    };
    report_entries(&mut report, "Nodes", &previous.nodes, &current.nodes);
    report_entries(&mut report, "Records", &previous.records, &current.records);
    let previous_chunk_ids: HashSet<&String> = previous.chunk_ids.iter().collect();
    let kept_chunk_count = current
        .chunk_ids
        .iter()
        .filter(|id| previous_chunk_ids.contains(id))
        .count();
    writeln!(
        report,
        "Chunks: {kept_chunk_count} of {} kept their id",
        current.chunk_ids.len()
    )
    .unwrap();
    report
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const BEFORE: &str = concat!(
        r#"{"type":"node","kind":"spatial","name":"s0","raw":0,"depth":0,"description":"transform=[1,0,0,1,0,0] origin=(0,0)","owner":"Viewport<#document>"}"#,
        "\n",
        r#"{"type":"node","kind":"spatial","name":"s1","raw":4,"depth":1,"description":"transform=[1,0,0,1,5,0] origin=(0,0)","owner":"BlockContainer<DIV>#moved"}"#,
        "\n",
        r#"{"type":"chunk","name":"k1","id":"aa"}"#,
        "\n",
        r#"{"type":"record","id":1,"op":"FillRect","context":{"spatial":{"name":"s1","raw":4}},"fields":{"rect":[0,0,10,10]},"owner":"BlockContainer<DIV>#moved","phase":"background"}"#,
        "\n",
        r#"{"type":"record","id":2,"op":"FillRect","context":{"spatial":{"name":"s0","raw":0}},"fields":{"rect":[0,0,5,5]},"owner":"BlockContainer<DIV>#gone","phase":"background"}"#,
        "\n",
    );

    const AFTER: &str = concat!(
        r#"{"type":"node","kind":"spatial","name":"s0","raw":0,"depth":0,"description":"transform=[1,0,0,1,0,0] origin=(0,0)","owner":"Viewport<#document>"}"#,
        "\n",
        r#"{"type":"node","kind":"spatial","name":"s1","raw":2,"depth":1,"description":"transform=[1,0,0,1,9,0] origin=(0,0)","owner":"BlockContainer<DIV>#moved"}"#,
        "\n",
        r#"{"type":"chunk","name":"k1","id":"bb"}"#,
        "\n",
        r#"{"type":"record","id":1,"op":"FillRect","context":{"spatial":{"name":"s1","raw":2}},"fields":{"rect":[0,0,10,10]},"owner":"BlockContainer<DIV>#moved","phase":"background"}"#,
        "\n",
        r#"{"type":"record","id":2,"op":"DrawGlyphRun","context":{"spatial":{"name":"s0","raw":0}},"fields":{"glyphs":2},"text":"hi","owner":"BlockContainer<DIV>#new","phase":"foreground"}"#,
        "\n",
    );

    #[test]
    fn nodes_and_records_are_matched_by_owner_not_by_index() {
        assert_eq!(
            display_list_dump_changes(Some(BEFORE), AFTER),
            concat!(
                "Nodes: 0 added, 0 removed, 1 changed, 1 unchanged\n",
                "  ~ [s1] transform=[1,0,0,1,9,0] origin=(0,0) (BlockContainer<DIV>#moved)\n",
                "    was [s1] transform=[1,0,0,1,5,0] origin=(0,0) (BlockContainer<DIV>#moved)\n",
                "Records: 1 added, 1 removed, 0 changed, 1 unchanged\n",
                "  + DrawGlyphRun {\"glyphs\":2} text=\"hi\" owner=BlockContainer<DIV>#new phase=foreground\n",
                "  - FillRect {\"rect\":[0,0,5,5]} owner=BlockContainer<DIV>#gone phase=background\n",
                "Chunks: 0 of 1 kept their id\n",
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_first_dump_is_summarized() {
        assert_eq!(
            display_list_dump_changes(None, BEFORE),
            "No previous dump of this document. This one, of 2 nodes, 2 records and 1 chunks, is what the next one is compared with.\n"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn numbered_names_are_compared_without_their_numbers() {
        assert_eq!(
            without_numbered_names("sticky scroller=s12 parent_sticky=s3 in c40 font2 x1y"),
            "sticky scroller=s# parent_sticky=s# in c# font# x1y"
        );
    }
}
