use std::cell::UnsafeCell;
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU8, AtomicU64, AtomicUsize, Ordering};

use crate::web_audio::control_thread::{ControlThread, ControlThreadCell};

pub trait AudioWorkletPipeClient {
    fn pump(&self);
}

pub struct Config {
    pub quantum_size: usize,
    pub input_count: usize,
    pub output_count: usize,

    // Per input: the largest channel count a slot can carry.
    pub input_channel_capacity: Vec<u32>,

    // Per output: the largest channel count a slot can carry.
    pub output_channel_capacity: Vec<u32>,
    pub output_channel_count_matches_input: bool,
    pub param_count: usize,

    // Per parameter: a-rate blocks carry quantum_size samples, k-rate blocks one.
    pub param_is_a_rate: Vec<bool>,

    // Slots per ring; must be a power of two.
    pub ring_capacity: usize,

    // Silent output quanta pushed before rendering starts; at most ring_capacity.
    pub prime_level: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum WorkletPipeState {
    Running,
    Failed,
    ShutDown,
}

#[repr(align(64))]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Counter(AtomicUsize);

#[derive(Default)]
struct Ring {
    // Producer-owned: the next slot to write.
    tail: Counter,

    // Consumer-owned: the next slot to read.
    head: Counter,
}

// A lock-free bridge between the realtime render node and the main-thread processor. Two SPSC rings share a
// preallocated arena; underruns render silence and a full input ring drops quanta. Each ring uses acquire/release
// head-tail discipline, and the slot stride is configured at run time.
//
// Per-slot layout; strides are rounded up to 64 bytes so slots start cache-line-aligned relative to the arena:
//
//   Input slot                                            Output slot
//     u64 start_frame                                       u64 start_frame
//     u32 flags (bit 0: gap before this quantum)            u32 flags (bit 0: processor active; bit 1: reserved
//     u32 actual_channel_count[input_count]                     for a per-quantum processing-error signal)
//     f32 samples[input_channel_capacity[0]][quantum_size]  u32 actual_channel_count[output_count]
//       ... one sample block per input ...                  f32 samples[output_channel_capacity[0]][quantum_size]
//     f32 param_block[param_count]: quantum_size samples      ... one sample block per output ...
//         each for a-rate parameters, 1 for k-rate
//
// Slots are accessed in place through the writer/reader views below, which are only valid inside the callback they
// are passed to. A slot's unwritten regions keep stale data from the previous trip around the ring, so a writer
// must set the channel counts it wants a reader to trust; the flags are cleared on every push.
pub struct AudioWorkletPipe {
    pub config: Config,
    ring_index_mask: usize,
    input_slot_stride: usize,
    output_slot_stride: usize,
    output_region_offset: usize,
    input_samples_offset: Vec<usize>,
    output_samples_offset: Vec<usize>,
    param_block_offset: Vec<usize>,
    param_block_length: Vec<usize>,
    arena: Box<[UnsafeCell<u64>]>,
    input_ring: Ring,
    output_ring: Ring,
    control_thread: ControlThread,
    client: ControlThreadCell<Option<Rc<dyn AudioWorkletPipeClient>>>,
    pump_scheduled: AtomicBool,
    state: AtomicU8,
    underrun_count: AtomicU64,
    dropped_input_count: AtomicU64,
}

// SAFETY: Each ring transfers its disjoint arena slots between one producer and one consumer with acquire/release counters.
unsafe impl Send for AudioWorkletPipe {}
unsafe impl Sync for AudioWorkletPipe {}
const SLOT_FLAGS_OFFSET: usize = 8;
const SLOT_CHANNEL_COUNTS_OFFSET: usize = 12;
const SLOT_ALIGNMENT: usize = 64;

impl AudioWorkletPipe {
    pub fn new(config: Config) -> Arc<Self> {
        assert!(config.quantum_size > 0);
        assert_eq!(config.input_channel_capacity.len(), config.input_count);
        assert_eq!(config.output_channel_capacity.len(), config.output_count);
        assert_eq!(config.param_is_a_rate.len(), config.param_count);
        assert!(config.ring_capacity.is_power_of_two());
        assert!(config.prime_level <= config.ring_capacity);
        let channel_bytes = config.quantum_size * size_of::<f32>();
        let mut offset = SLOT_CHANNEL_COUNTS_OFFSET + config.input_count * size_of::<u32>();
        let mut input_samples_offset = Vec::with_capacity(config.input_count);
        for input in 0..config.input_count {
            input_samples_offset.push(offset);
            offset += config.input_channel_capacity[input] as usize * channel_bytes;
        }
        let mut param_block_offset = Vec::with_capacity(config.param_count);
        let mut param_block_length = Vec::with_capacity(config.param_count);
        for param in 0..config.param_count {
            param_block_offset.push(offset);
            let block_length = if config.param_is_a_rate[param] {
                config.quantum_size
            } else {
                1
            };
            param_block_length.push(block_length);
            offset += block_length * size_of::<f32>();
        }
        let input_slot_stride = (offset + SLOT_ALIGNMENT - 1) & !(SLOT_ALIGNMENT - 1);
        offset = SLOT_CHANNEL_COUNTS_OFFSET + config.output_count * size_of::<u32>();
        let mut output_samples_offset = Vec::with_capacity(config.output_count);
        for output in 0..config.output_count {
            output_samples_offset.push(offset);
            offset += config.output_channel_capacity[output] as usize * channel_bytes;
        }
        let output_slot_stride = (offset + SLOT_ALIGNMENT - 1) & !(SLOT_ALIGNMENT - 1);
        let output_region_offset = config.ring_capacity * input_slot_stride;
        let arena_size = output_region_offset + config.ring_capacity * output_slot_stride;
        Arc::new(Self {
            ring_index_mask: config.ring_capacity - 1,
            config,
            input_slot_stride,
            output_slot_stride,
            output_region_offset,
            input_samples_offset,
            output_samples_offset,
            param_block_offset,
            param_block_length,
            arena: (0..arena_size / size_of::<u64>()).map(|_| UnsafeCell::new(0)).collect(),
            input_ring: Ring::default(),
            output_ring: Ring::default(),
            control_thread: ControlThread::current(),
            client: ControlThreadCell::new(None),
            pump_scheduled: AtomicBool::new(false),
            state: AtomicU8::new(WorkletPipeState::Running as u8),
            underrun_count: AtomicU64::new(0),
            dropped_input_count: AtomicU64::new(0),
        })
    }

    // Accessed only on the control thread, including by deferred wakeups.
    pub fn set_client(&self, client: Option<Rc<dyn AudioWorkletPipeClient>>) {
        self.client.replace(client);
    }

    fn input_slot(&self, counter: usize) -> *mut u8 {
        unsafe {
            self.arena
                .as_ptr()
                .cast::<u8>()
                .cast_mut()
                .add((counter & self.ring_index_mask) * self.input_slot_stride)
        }
    }

    fn output_slot(&self, counter: usize) -> *mut u8 {
        unsafe {
            self.arena
                .as_ptr()
                .cast::<u8>()
                .cast_mut()
                .add(self.output_region_offset + (counter & self.ring_index_mask) * self.output_slot_stride)
        }
    }

    // Fills the next input slot in place. Returns false, and counts a dropped quantum, when the ring is full; the
    // caller should then mark the next successful push with set_had_gap() so the processor can tell that quanta
    // went missing.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn try_push_input(&self, fill: impl FnOnce(*mut u8)) -> bool {
        let tail = self.input_ring.tail.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        if tail.wrapping_sub(self.input_ring.head.0.load(Ordering::Acquire)) == self.config.ring_capacity {
            self.dropped_input_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            return false;
        }
        let slot = self.input_slot(tail);
        unsafe {
            *slot.add(SLOT_FLAGS_OFFSET).cast::<u32>() = 0;
        }
        fill(slot);
        self.input_ring.tail.0.store(tail.wrapping_add(1), Ordering::Release);
        true
    }

    pub(crate) unsafe fn try_pop_input(&self, read: impl FnOnce(*mut u8)) -> bool {
        let head = self.input_ring.head.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        if head == self.input_ring.tail.0.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
            return false;
        }
        read(self.input_slot(head));
        self.input_ring.head.0.store(head.wrapping_add(1), Ordering::Release);
        true
    }

    pub(crate) unsafe fn try_push_output(&self, fill: impl FnOnce(*mut u8)) -> bool {
        let tail = self.output_ring.tail.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        if tail.wrapping_sub(self.output_ring.head.0.load(Ordering::Acquire)) == self.config.ring_capacity {
            return false;
        }
        let slot = self.output_slot(tail);
        unsafe {
            *slot.add(SLOT_FLAGS_OFFSET).cast::<u32>() = 0;
        }
        fill(slot);
        self.output_ring.tail.0.store(tail.wrapping_add(1), Ordering::Release);
        true
    }

    // Reads the oldest processed quantum. Returns false, and counts an underrun, when none is ready; the caller
    // then outputs silence, never blocking the audio callback.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn try_pop_output(&self, read: impl FnOnce(*mut u8)) -> bool {
        let head = self.output_ring.head.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        if head == self.output_ring.tail.0.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
            self.underrun_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            return false;
        }
        read(self.output_slot(head));
        self.output_ring.head.0.store(head.wrapping_add(1), Ordering::Release);
        true
    }

    pub fn output_occupancy(&self) -> usize {
        self.output_ring
            .tail
            .0
            .load(Ordering::Acquire)
            .wrapping_sub(self.output_ring.head.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
    }

    // Drops the oldest processed quanta until at most target_occupancy remain. After a main-thread stall the pump
    // catches up and refills the output ring past the prime level; clamping back down keeps the pipe's added
    // latency from ratcheting up permanently.
    pub fn discard_outputs_down_to(&self, target_occupancy: usize) {
        // A consumer-side pop-without-read: advancing the head releases the discarded slots back to the producer. New
        // pushes can only move the tail further along, so the snapshot below never overshoots.
        let head = self.output_ring.head.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        let tail = self.output_ring.tail.0.load(Ordering::Acquire);
        if tail.wrapping_sub(head) <= target_occupancy {
            return;
        }
        self.output_ring
            .head
            .0
            .store(tail.wrapping_sub(target_occupancy), Ordering::Release);
    }

    /// Pushes `count` silent, processor-active output quanta. Called on the control thread before the pipe is handed
    /// to the render node, so the audio thread has a burst worth of lookahead before the first processed quantum.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// The caller must be the sole producer of the output ring.
    pub unsafe fn prime_outputs_with_silence(&self, count: usize) {
        for _i in 0..count {
            let pushed = unsafe {
                self.try_push_output(|slot| {
                    Self::set_start_frame(slot, 0);
                    Self::set_flag(slot, true);
                    for output in 0..self.config.output_count {
                        let channel_count = if self.config.output_channel_count_matches_input {
                            1
                        } else {
                            self.config.output_channel_capacity[output]
                        };
                        *self.channel_count(slot, true, output) = channel_count;
                        for channel in 0..channel_count {
                            let (samples, length) = self.channel(slot, true, output, channel as usize);
                            ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(samples, length).fill(0.);
                        }
                    }
                })
            };
            assert!(pushed);
        }
    }

    // Schedules the pump on the main thread's event loop. Coalesced: only the first request after
    // clear_wakeup_flag() posts an event, so a device burst of several dozen quanta causes one pump run.
    pub fn request_wakeup(self: &Arc<Self>) {
        // Coalesce a device burst into one main-thread pump instead of posting once per quantum.
        if self.pump_scheduled.swap(true, Ordering::AcqRel) {
            return;
        }
        let pipe = Arc::clone(self);
        self.control_thread.post(move || {
            if pipe.state() == WorkletPipeState::ShutDown {
                return;
            }
            if let Some(client) = pipe.client.get() {
                client.pump();
            }
        });
    }

    // The pump calls this before draining the input ring, so a burst that lands while the pump is running schedules
    // another run instead of being lost.
    pub fn clear_wakeup_flag(&self) {
        // A read-modify-write rather than a plain store: it synchronizes with the audio thread's exchange in
        // request_wakeup(), so whenever that exchange elides a wakeup (returns true), everything the audio thread
        // pushed beforehand is visible to this pump run's drain.
        self.pump_scheduled.swap(false, Ordering::AcqRel);
    }

    pub fn state(&self) -> WorkletPipeState {
        match self.state.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
            0 => WorkletPipeState::Running,
            1 => WorkletPipeState::Failed,
            2 => WorkletPipeState::ShutDown,
            _ => unreachable!(),
        }
    }

    pub fn set_state(&self, state: WorkletPipeState) {
        self.state.store(state as u8, Ordering::Release);
    }

    pub fn underrun_count(&self) -> u64 {
        self.underrun_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    pub fn dropped_input_count(&self) -> u64 {
        self.dropped_input_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    /// # Safety
    /// The caller must be the only consumer of the input ring.
    pub unsafe fn try_read_input(&self, read: impl FnOnce(&InputSlotReader<'_>)) -> bool {
        unsafe { self.try_pop_input(|slot| read(&InputSlotReader { pipe: self, slot })) }
    }

    /// # Safety
    /// The caller must be the only producer of the output ring.
    pub unsafe fn try_write_output(&self, fill: impl FnOnce(&mut OutputSlotWriter<'_>)) -> bool {
        unsafe { self.try_push_output(|slot| fill(&mut OutputSlotWriter { pipe: self, slot })) }
    }

    pub(crate) unsafe fn start_frame(slot: *const u8) -> u64 {
        unsafe { *slot.cast::<u64>() }
    }

    pub(crate) unsafe fn set_start_frame(slot: *mut u8, frame: u64) {
        unsafe {
            *slot.cast::<u64>() = frame;
        }
    }

    pub(crate) unsafe fn set_flag(slot: *mut u8, enabled: bool) {
        let flags = unsafe { &mut *slot.add(SLOT_FLAGS_OFFSET).cast::<u32>() };
        if enabled {
            *flags |= 1;
        } else {
            *flags &= !1;
        }
    }

    pub(crate) unsafe fn flag(slot: *const u8) -> bool {
        unsafe { *slot.add(SLOT_FLAGS_OFFSET).cast::<u32>() & 1 != 0 }
    }

    pub(crate) unsafe fn channel_count(&self, slot: *mut u8, output: bool, index: usize) -> *mut u32 {
        assert!(
            index
                < if output {
                    self.config.output_count
                } else {
                    self.config.input_count
                }
        );
        unsafe { slot.add(SLOT_CHANNEL_COUNTS_OFFSET + index * size_of::<u32>()).cast() }
    }

    pub(crate) unsafe fn channel(
        &self,
        slot: *mut u8,
        output: bool,
        index: usize,
        channel: usize,
    ) -> (*mut f32, usize) {
        let (capacity, offsets) = if output {
            (&self.config.output_channel_capacity, &self.output_samples_offset)
        } else {
            (&self.config.input_channel_capacity, &self.input_samples_offset)
        };
        assert!(index < capacity.len());
        assert!(channel < capacity[index] as usize);
        (
            unsafe {
                slot.add(offsets[index])
                    .cast::<f32>()
                    .add(channel * self.config.quantum_size)
            },
            self.config.quantum_size,
        )
    }

    pub(crate) unsafe fn param_block(&self, slot: *mut u8, param: usize) -> (*mut f32, usize) {
        assert!(param < self.config.param_count);
        (
            unsafe { slot.add(self.param_block_offset[param]).cast() },
            self.param_block_length[param],
        )
    }
}

pub struct RingSizing {
    pub ring_capacity: usize,
    pub prime_level: usize,
}

// The renderer produces a device buffer's worth of quanta in one burst, so lookahead must cover a full burst plus
// scheduling margin. At the 100 ms, 48 kHz defaults this is 38 quanta, a prime level of 48, and capacity 64.
pub fn ring_sizing_for_device_latency(device_latency_ms: u32, sample_rate: f32, quantum_size: usize) -> RingSizing {
    assert!(sample_rate > 0.);
    assert!(quantum_size > 0);
    let burst_quanta =
        (f64::from(device_latency_ms) / 1000. * f64::from(sample_rate) / quantum_size as f64).ceil() as usize;
    let prime = (burst_quanta * 5).div_ceil(4);
    let mut capacity = 1;
    while capacity < prime + (burst_quanta / 4).max(1) {
        capacity *= 2;
    }
    RingSizing {
        ring_capacity: capacity,
        prime_level: prime,
    }
}

pub struct InputSlotReader<'a> {
    pipe: &'a AudioWorkletPipe,
    slot: *mut u8,
}

impl InputSlotReader<'_> {
    pub fn start_frame(&self) -> u64 {
        unsafe { AudioWorkletPipe::start_frame(self.slot) }
    }

    pub fn had_gap(&self) -> bool {
        unsafe { AudioWorkletPipe::flag(self.slot) }
    }

    pub fn actual_channel_count(&self, input: usize) -> u32 {
        unsafe { *self.pipe.channel_count(self.slot, false, input) }
    }

    pub fn input_channel(&self, input: usize, channel: usize) -> &[f32] {
        let (samples, length) = unsafe { self.pipe.channel(self.slot, false, input, channel) };
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(samples, length) }
    }

    pub fn param_block(&self, param: usize) -> &[f32] {
        let (samples, length) = unsafe { self.pipe.param_block(self.slot, param) };
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(samples, length) }
    }
}

pub struct OutputSlotWriter<'a> {
    pipe: &'a AudioWorkletPipe,
    slot: *mut u8,
}

impl OutputSlotWriter<'_> {
    pub fn set_start_frame(&mut self, frame: u64) {
        unsafe { AudioWorkletPipe::set_start_frame(self.slot, frame) };
    }

    pub fn set_processor_active(&mut self, active: bool) {
        unsafe { AudioWorkletPipe::set_flag(self.slot, active) };
    }

    pub fn set_actual_channel_count(&mut self, output: usize, channel_count: u32) {
        unsafe { *self.pipe.channel_count(self.slot, true, output) = channel_count };
    }

    pub fn output_channel(&mut self, output: usize, channel: usize) -> &mut [f32] {
        let (samples, length) = unsafe { self.pipe.channel(self.slot, true, output, channel) };
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(samples, length) }
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/web_audio/rendering/audio_worklet_render_node.rs
/*

#![allow(clippy::needless_range_loop)]
use std::sync::Arc;

use super::audio_worklet_pipe::{AudioWorkletPipe, WorkletPipeState};
use super::render_graph::RenderGraph;
use super::render_node::*;
use super::render_nodes::{BusRef, NodeProcessor, node_handle};

// Script runs on the main-thread pump, `prime_level` quanta behind this render node; this side
// only exchanges preallocated pipe slots and renders silence on underrun.
struct AudioWorkletRenderNode {
    pipe: Arc<AudioWorkletPipe>,
    params: Vec<Arc<RenderAudioParam>>,
    param_scratch: Vec<f32>,
    output_channel_capacities: Vec<u32>,
}

impl NodeProcessor for AudioWorkletRenderNode {
    fn for_each_param(&self, callback: &mut dyn FnMut(&RenderAudioParam)) {
        for param in &self.params {
            callback(param);
        }
    }

    unsafe fn process(&mut self, data: &RenderNodeData, graph: &RenderGraph, context: &RenderContext) {
        unsafe {
            // A failed (processor threw) or shut-down (node finalized / context closed) worklet renders
            // silence forever; the pump side owns the state transitions.
            if self.pipe.state() != WorkletPipeState::Running {
                for output in 0..data.output_count() {
                    BusRef(data.output(output)).zero();
                }
                return;
            }
            self.pipe.try_push_input(|slot| {
                AudioWorkletPipe::set_start_frame(slot, context.quantum_start_frame);
                for input in 0..data.input_count() {
                    // Unlike the render graph's silent mono bus, an unconnected worklet input
                    // is represented by an empty channel array in process().
                    if (&*data.input_connections.get())[input].is_empty() {
                        *self.pipe.channel_count(slot, false, input) = 0;
                        continue;
                    }
                    let input_bus = BusRef(data.pull_input(graph, context, input).cast_mut());
                    let capacity_channels = self.pipe.config.input_channel_capacity[input];
                    let channels_to_copy = input_bus.channel_count().min(capacity_channels as usize);
                    *self.pipe.channel_count(slot, false, input) = channels_to_copy as u32;
                    for channel in 0..channels_to_copy {
                        let (pointer, length) = self.pipe.channel(slot, false, input, channel);
                        let destination = ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(pointer, length);
                        let source = input_bus.channel(channel);
                        assert_eq!(destination.len(), source.len());
                        destination.copy_from_slice(source);
                    }
                }
                for param_index in 0..self.params.len() {
                    let (pointer, length) = self.pipe.param_block(slot, param_index);
                    let block = ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(pointer, length);

                    // a-rate params fill the whole block; k-rate blocks are a single value. compute() handles
                    // both through the shared timeline + any audio-rate param connections.
                    self.param_scratch.resize(block.len(), 0.);
                    self.params[param_index].compute(graph, context, &mut self.param_scratch[..block.len()]);
                    block.copy_from_slice(&self.param_scratch[..block.len()]);
                }
            });
            self.pipe.request_wakeup();
            let popped = self.pipe.try_pop_output(|slot| {
                for output in 0..data.output_count() {
                    let output_bus = BusRef(data.output(output));
                    let channel_count = (*self.pipe.channel_count(slot, true, output) as usize)
                        .min(self.output_channel_capacities[output] as usize);
                    output_bus.set_channel_count(channel_count.max(1));
                    output_bus.zero();
                    for channel in 0..channel_count {
                        let (pointer, length) = self.pipe.channel(slot, true, output, channel);
                        let source = ak::slice_from_raw_parts(pointer, length);
                        let destination = output_bus.channel_mut(channel);
                        let frames = source.len().min(destination.len());
                        destination[..frames].copy_from_slice(&source[..frames]);
                    }
                }
            });
            if !popped {
                for output in 0..data.output_count() {
                    BusRef(data.output(output)).zero();
                }
                return;
            }

            // Latency clamp: after a main-thread stall, the pump refills the output ring past the configured
            // lookahead (the audio side emitted silence meanwhile). Discard the excess so the stall does not
            // permanently ratchet up this node's latency.
            if self.pipe.output_occupancy() > self.pipe.config.prime_level {
                self.pipe.discard_outputs_down_to(self.pipe.config.prime_level);
            }
        }
    }
}

#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "mirror the C++ render node constructor")]
pub fn create_audio_worklet_render_node(
    node_id: u64,
    input_count: usize,
    output_count: usize,
    quantum_size: usize,
    output_channel_capacities: &[u32],
    channel_count: usize,
    channel_count_mode: ChannelCountMode,
    channel_interpretation: ChannelInterpretation,
    pipe: Arc<AudioWorkletPipe>,
    params: Vec<Arc<RenderAudioParam>>,
) -> Box<NodeHandle> {
    let mut data = RenderNodeData::new(node_id, input_count, output_count, quantum_size, 1);
    for (output, &channel_capacity) in output_channel_capacities.iter().enumerate() {
        data.reserve_output_channels(output, channel_capacity as usize);
    }

    // Channel configuration must be set here: the SetChannelConfig messages queued during node
    // construction arrive before our AddNode and are dropped by the graph.
    data.channel_count.set(channel_count);
    data.channel_count_mode.set(channel_count_mode);
    data.channel_interpretation.set(channel_interpretation);
    node_handle(
        data,
        AudioWorkletRenderNode {
            pipe,
            params,
            param_scratch: vec![0.; quantum_size],
            output_channel_capacities: output_channel_capacities.to_vec(),
        },
    )
}

use ak::math;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum BiquadFilterType {
    Lowpass,
    Highpass,
    Bandpass,
    Lowshelf,
    Highshelf,
    Peaking,
    Notch,
    Allpass,
}

// Normalized biquad transfer function coefficients, with a0 divided out.
// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#filters-characteristics
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct BiquadCoefficients {
    pub b0: f64,
    pub b1: f64,
    pub b2: f64,
    pub a1: f64,
    pub a2: f64,
}

// Computes filter coefficients from the BiquadFilterNode's computed parameter values. frequency is expected to already
// include the detune factor and be given as a fraction of the Nyquist frequency, in the range [0, 1].
// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#filters-characteristics
#[allow(unused_assignments)]
pub fn compute_biquad_coefficients(
    filter_type: BiquadFilterType,
    normalized_frequency: f64,
    q: f64,
    gain_db: f64,
) -> BiquadCoefficients {
    let omega = std::f64::consts::PI * normalized_frequency;
    let sin_omega = math::sin(omega);
    let cos_omega = math::cos(omega);
    let a = math::pow(10., gain_db / 40.);

    let mut b0 = 1.0;
    let mut b1 = 0.0;
    let mut b2 = 0.0;
    let mut a0 = 1.0;
    let mut a1 = 0.0;
    let mut a2 = 0.0;

    match filter_type {
        BiquadFilterType::Lowpass => {
            // NB: For lowpass and highpass filters, Q is interpreted as being in dB.
            let alpha_q_db = sin_omega / (2. * math::pow(10., q / 20.));
            b0 = (1. - cos_omega) / 2.;
            b1 = 1. - cos_omega;
            b2 = b0;
            a0 = 1. + alpha_q_db;
            a1 = -2. * cos_omega;
            a2 = 1. - alpha_q_db;
        }
        BiquadFilterType::Highpass => {
            let alpha_q_db = sin_omega / (2. * math::pow(10., q / 20.));
            b0 = (1. + cos_omega) / 2.;
            b1 = -(1. + cos_omega);
            b2 = b0;
            a0 = 1. + alpha_q_db;
            a1 = -2. * cos_omega;
            a2 = 1. - alpha_q_db;
        }
        BiquadFilterType::Bandpass => {
            let alpha_q = if q > 0. { sin_omega / (2. * q) } else { 1. };
            b0 = alpha_q;
            b1 = 0.;
            b2 = -alpha_q;
            a0 = 1. + alpha_q;
            a1 = -2. * cos_omega;
            a2 = 1. - alpha_q;
        }
        BiquadFilterType::Notch => {
            let alpha_q = if q > 0. { sin_omega / (2. * q) } else { 1. };
            b0 = 1.;
            b1 = -2. * cos_omega;
            b2 = 1.;
            a0 = 1. + alpha_q;
            a1 = b1;
            a2 = 1. - alpha_q;
        }
        BiquadFilterType::Allpass => {
            let alpha_q = if q > 0. { sin_omega / (2. * q) } else { 1. };
            b0 = 1. - alpha_q;
            b1 = -2. * cos_omega;
            b2 = 1. + alpha_q;
            a0 = 1. + alpha_q;
            a1 = b1;
            a2 = 1. - alpha_q;
        }
        BiquadFilterType::Peaking => {
            let alpha_q = if q > 0. { sin_omega / (2. * q) } else { 1. };
            b0 = 1. + alpha_q * a;
            b1 = -2. * cos_omega;
            b2 = 1. - alpha_q * a;
            a0 = 1. + alpha_q / a;
            a1 = b1;
            a2 = 1. - alpha_q / a;
        }
        BiquadFilterType::Lowshelf => {
            // NB: For the shelf filters, α_S uses a shelf slope S of 1.
            let alpha_s = sin_omega / 2. * 2.0_f64.sqrt();
            let two_sqrt_a_alpha_s = 2. * a.sqrt() * alpha_s;
            b0 = a * ((a + 1.) - (a - 1.) * cos_omega + two_sqrt_a_alpha_s);
            b1 = 2. * a * ((a - 1.) - (a + 1.) * cos_omega);
            b2 = a * ((a + 1.) - (a - 1.) * cos_omega - two_sqrt_a_alpha_s);
            a0 = (a + 1.) + (a - 1.) * cos_omega + two_sqrt_a_alpha_s;
            a1 = -2. * ((a - 1.) + (a + 1.) * cos_omega);
            a2 = (a + 1.) + (a - 1.) * cos_omega - two_sqrt_a_alpha_s;
        }
        BiquadFilterType::Highshelf => {
            let alpha_s = sin_omega / 2. * 2.0_f64.sqrt();
            let two_sqrt_a_alpha_s = 2. * a.sqrt() * alpha_s;
            b0 = a * ((a + 1.) + (a - 1.) * cos_omega + two_sqrt_a_alpha_s);
            b1 = -2. * a * ((a - 1.) + (a + 1.) * cos_omega);
            b2 = a * ((a + 1.) + (a - 1.) * cos_omega - two_sqrt_a_alpha_s);
            a0 = (a + 1.) - (a - 1.) * cos_omega + two_sqrt_a_alpha_s;
            a1 = 2. * ((a - 1.) - (a + 1.) * cos_omega);
            a2 = (a + 1.) - (a - 1.) * cos_omega - two_sqrt_a_alpha_s;
        }
    }

    BiquadCoefficients {
        b0: b0 / a0,
        b1: b1 / a0,
        b2: b2 / a0,
        a1: a1 / a0,
        a2: a2 / a0,
    }
}

// Evaluates the transfer function's magnitude and phase at the given frequency, given as a fraction of the Nyquist
// frequency in the range [0, 1].
// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-biquadfilternode-getfrequencyresponse
pub fn biquad_frequency_response(coefficients: &BiquadCoefficients, normalized_frequency: f64) -> (f32, f32) {
    // NB: The response is evaluated at z = e^(jω) with ω = π * normalized_frequency:
    //         H(z) = (b0 + b1 z^-1 + b2 z^-2) / (1 + a1 z^-1 + a2 z^-2)
    let omega = std::f64::consts::PI * normalized_frequency;
    let cos_omega = math::cos(omega);
    let sin_omega = math::sin(omega);
    let cos_2_omega = math::cos(2. * omega);
    let sin_2_omega = math::sin(2. * omega);
    let numerator_real = coefficients.b0 + coefficients.b1 * cos_omega + coefficients.b2 * cos_2_omega;
    let numerator_imaginary = -(coefficients.b1 * sin_omega + coefficients.b2 * sin_2_omega);
    let denominator_real = 1. + coefficients.a1 * cos_omega + coefficients.a2 * cos_2_omega;
    let denominator_imaginary = -(coefficients.a1 * sin_omega + coefficients.a2 * sin_2_omega);
    let denominator_magnitude_squared =
        denominator_real * denominator_real + denominator_imaginary * denominator_imaginary;
    let response_real = (numerator_real * denominator_real + numerator_imaginary * denominator_imaginary)
        / denominator_magnitude_squared;
    let response_imaginary = (numerator_imaginary * denominator_real - numerator_real * denominator_imaginary)
        / denominator_magnitude_squared;
    let magnitude = (response_real * response_real + response_imaginary * response_imaginary).sqrt() as f32;
    let phase = math::atan2(response_imaginary, response_real) as f32;
    (magnitude, phase)
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/web_audio/rendering/convolver_kernel.rs
/*

 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

#![allow(clippy::needless_range_loop)]

use std::cell::UnsafeCell;
use std::sync::Arc;

use ak::Span;

use super::fft::{FFT, FFTDirection};

pub struct AudioBufferContents<'a> {
    pub channels: &'a [Span<'a, f32>],
    pub sample_rate: f32,
}

impl AudioBufferContents<'_> {
    pub fn length(&self) -> usize {
        self.channels.first().map_or(0, |channel| channel.as_slice().len())
    }
}

struct Channel {
    head: Vec<f32>,
    real: Vec<f32>,
    imag: Vec<f32>,
}

// An impulse response prepared for convolution on the rendering thread, built on the control thread when a
// ConvolverNode's buffer is set so the rendering thread never has to transform a whole impulse response in a single
// quantum.
//
// The first partition is kept in the time domain: it is the one that carries the quietest part of the output, where the
// round-off of a transform round trip is most audible. Everything after it is cut into equally sized partitions and
// transformed. Only the first half of each partition's spectrum plus the Nyquist bin is stored; the remaining bins
// follow from the Hermitian symmetry of the transform of a real signal.
// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#ConvolverNode
pub struct ConvolverKernel {
    channels: Vec<Channel>,
    partition_count: usize,
    bin_count: usize,
}

// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-convolvernode-normalize
fn calculate_normalization_scale(contents: &AudioBufferContents<'_>) -> f32 {
    const GAIN_CALIBRATION: f64 = 0.00125;
    const GAIN_CALIBRATION_SAMPLE_RATE: f64 = 44100.;
    const MIN_POWER: f64 = 0.000125;

    // Normalize by RMS power.
    let mut power = 0.;
    for samples in contents.channels {
        for &sample in samples.as_slice() {
            power += f64::from(sample) * f64::from(sample);
        }
    }
    power = (power / (contents.channels.len() * contents.length()) as f64).sqrt();

    // Protect against accidental overload.
    if !power.is_finite() || power < MIN_POWER {
        power = MIN_POWER;
    }

    let mut scale = 1. / power;

    // Calibrate to make perceived volume same as unprocessed.
    scale *= GAIN_CALIBRATION;

    // Scale depends on sample-rate.
    if contents.sample_rate != 0. {
        scale *= GAIN_CALIBRATION_SAMPLE_RATE / f64::from(contents.sample_rate);
    }

    // True-stereo compensation.
    if contents.channels.len() == 4 {
        scale *= 0.5;
    }

    scale as f32
}

impl ConvolverKernel {
    pub fn create(contents: &AudioBufferContents<'_>, partition_size: usize, normalize: bool) -> Option<Arc<Self>> {
        let length = contents.length();
        if length == 0 {
            return None;
        }

        let scale = if normalize {
            calculate_normalization_scale(contents)
        } else {
            1.
        };

        // Each partition is zero-padded to twice its length so that the cyclic convolution of the transform produces the
        // linear convolution the rendering thread is after.
        let transform_size = 2 * partition_size;
        let bin_count = partition_size + 1;
        let partition_count = if length > partition_size {
            (length - partition_size).div_ceil(partition_size)
        } else {
            0
        };

        let fft = FFT::new(transform_size);
        let mut real = vec![0.; transform_size];
        let mut imag = vec![0.; transform_size];

        let mut channels = Vec::with_capacity(contents.channels.len());
        for samples in contents.channels {
            let samples = samples.as_slice();
            let mut channel = Channel {
                head: vec![0.; partition_size],
                real: vec![0.; partition_count * bin_count],
                imag: vec![0.; partition_count * bin_count],
            };

            for frame in 0..partition_size.min(length) {
                channel.head[frame] = samples[frame] * scale;
            }

            for partition in 0..partition_count {
                let offset = (partition + 1) * partition_size;
                let frames_in_partition = partition_size.min(length - offset);
                for frame in 0..frames_in_partition {
                    real[frame] = samples[offset + frame] * scale;
                }
                for frame in frames_in_partition..transform_size {
                    real[frame] = 0.;
                }
                for frame in 0..transform_size {
                    imag[frame] = 0.;
                }

                fft.transform(&mut real, &mut imag, FFTDirection::Forward);

                for bin in 0..bin_count {
                    channel.real[partition * bin_count + bin] = real[bin];
                    channel.imag[partition * bin_count + bin] = imag[bin];
                }
            }

            channels.push(channel);
        }

        Some(Arc::new(Self {
            channels,
            partition_count,
            bin_count,
        }))
    }

    pub fn channel_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.channels.len()
    }

    // The number of partitions that are held in the frequency domain, which excludes the time-domain head.
    pub fn partition_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.partition_count
    }

    pub fn bin_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.bin_count
    }

    pub fn head(&self, channel: usize) -> &[f32] {
        &self.channels[channel].head
    }

    pub fn partition_real(&self, channel: usize, partition: usize) -> &[f32] {
        &self.channels[channel].real[partition * self.bin_count..(partition + 1) * self.bin_count]
    }

    pub fn partition_imag(&self, channel: usize, partition: usize) -> &[f32] {
        &self.channels[channel].imag[partition * self.bin_count..(partition + 1) * self.bin_count]
    }
}

// The ring of input spectra a ConvolverRenderNode multiplies with the kernel's partitions, one slot per partition plus
// one for the window written in the current quantum. It is sized after the kernel, so it is allocated here on the
// control thread and handed over together with the kernel, keeping allocation off the rendering thread.
pub struct ConvolverDelayLine {
    length: usize,
    real: [UnsafeCell<Vec<f32>>; Self::MAX_CHANNEL_COUNT],
    imag: [UnsafeCell<Vec<f32>>; Self::MAX_CHANNEL_COUNT],
}

// SAFETY: Delay-line samples are only accessed by the rendering thread after transfer.
unsafe impl Send for ConvolverDelayLine {}
unsafe impl Sync for ConvolverDelayLine {}
impl ConvolverDelayLine {
    // The input to a ConvolverNode is mono or stereo and cannot be increased.
    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#ConvolverNode
    pub const MAX_CHANNEL_COUNT: usize = 2;

    pub fn create(kernel: &ConvolverKernel) -> Self {
        let length = kernel.partition_count() + 1;
        let real = std::array::from_fn(|_| UnsafeCell::new(vec![0.; length * kernel.bin_count()]));
        let imag = std::array::from_fn(|_| UnsafeCell::new(vec![0.; length * kernel.bin_count()]));
        Self { length, real, imag }
    }

    #[allow(clippy::mut_from_ref)]
    pub(crate) unsafe fn real_shared(&self, channel: usize) -> &mut [f32] {
        unsafe { &mut *self.real[channel].get() }
    }

    #[allow(clippy::mut_from_ref)]
    pub(crate) unsafe fn imag_shared(&self, channel: usize) -> &mut [f32] {
        unsafe { &mut *self.imag[channel].get() }
    }

    pub fn length(&self) -> usize {
        self.length
    }

    pub fn real(&mut self, channel: usize) -> &mut [f32] {
        self.real[channel].get_mut()
    }

    pub fn imag(&mut self, channel: usize) -> &mut [f32] {
        self.imag[channel].get_mut()
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/web_audio/rendering/fft.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

use ak::math;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum FFTDirection {
    Forward,
    Inverse,
}

pub struct FFT {
    size: usize,
    twiddle_real: Vec<f32>,
    twiddle_imag: Vec<f32>,
}

impl FFT {
    // Radix-2 Cooley-Tukey FFT of a fixed power-of-two size. The twiddle factors depend only on that size, so they are
    // computed once here and shared by every transform.
    pub fn new(size: usize) -> Self {
        assert!(size != 0 && (size & (size - 1)) == 0);

        let mut twiddle_real = vec![0.; size / 2];
        let mut twiddle_imag = vec![0.; size / 2];
        for index in 0..size / 2 {
            let angle = -2. * std::f64::consts::PI * index as f64 / size as f64;
            twiddle_real[index] = math::cos(angle) as f32;
            twiddle_imag[index] = math::sin(angle) as f32;
        }
        Self {
            size,
            twiddle_real,
            twiddle_imag,
        }
    }

    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
        self.size
    }

    // Both spans must hold exactly `size()` samples. The inverse transform includes the 1/N scaling.
    pub fn transform(&self, re: &mut [f32], im: &mut [f32], direction: FFTDirection) {
        assert!(re.len() == self.size && im.len() == self.size);

        let mut j = 0;
        for i in 1..self.size {
            let mut bit = self.size >> 1;
            while j & bit != 0 {
                j ^= bit;
                bit >>= 1;
            }
            j ^= bit;
            if i < j {
                re.swap(i, j);
                im.swap(i, j);
            }
        }

        let twiddle_sign = if direction == FFTDirection::Forward { 1. } else { -1. };
        let mut len = 2;
        while len <= self.size {
            let half = len >> 1;
            let twiddle_stride = self.size / len;
            for i in (0..self.size).step_by(len) {
                for k in 0..half {
                    let w_re = self.twiddle_real[k * twiddle_stride];
                    let w_im = self.twiddle_imag[k * twiddle_stride] * twiddle_sign;
                    let u_re = re[i + k];
                    let u_im = im[i + k];
                    let v_re = re[i + k + half] * w_re - im[i + k + half] * w_im;
                    let v_im = re[i + k + half] * w_im + im[i + k + half] * w_re;
                    re[i + k] = u_re + v_re;
                    im[i + k] = u_im + v_im;
                    re[i + k + half] = u_re - v_re;
                    im[i + k + half] = u_im - v_im;
                }
            }
            len <<= 1;
        }

        if direction == FFTDirection::Inverse {
            let inverse_size = 1. / self.size as f32;
            for i in 0..self.size {
                re[i] *= inverse_size;
                im[i] *= inverse_size;
            }
        }
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#![allow(clippy::needless_range_loop)]
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

use super::audio_bus::AudioBus;
use super::audio_frame_ring::{AudioFrameRing, AudioFrameRingCallbacks};
use super::pipe_callbacks::{CallbackService, PipeCallbacks};
use super::render_graph::RenderGraph;
use super::render_node::*;
use super::render_nodes::{NodeProcessor, node_handle};
use crate::web_audio::control_message::FfiSharedCppObject;

// The render thread only touches the ring and pending flag; the control thread owns the drain
// callback so its captured GC roots never cross threads.
struct SharedState {
    ring: AudioFrameRing,

    // Set by the rendering thread when it schedules a drain on the control thread and cleared
    // by the control thread when the drain runs, coalescing the notifications down to one
    // wakeup per rendered burst.
    drain_pending: AtomicBool,
    callbacks: CallbackService,
}

// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode
struct MediaStreamDestinationRenderNode {
    shared_state: Arc<SharedState>,
    mix_bus: AudioBus,
    interleaved_scratch: Vec<f32>,
}

impl NodeProcessor for MediaStreamDestinationRenderNode {
    unsafe fn process(&mut self, data: &RenderNodeData, graph: &RenderGraph, context: &RenderContext) {
        unsafe {
            let input = &*data.pull_input(graph, context, 0);

            // Mix the input to the track's channel count and interleave it into the shared ring. If
            // the control thread has stalled and the ring is full, the newest frames are dropped; the
            // consumer resynchronizes when it drains.
            self.mix_bus.zero();
            self.mix_bus.sum_from(
                input,
                data.channel_interpretation.get() == ChannelInterpretation::Speakers,
            );
            let channel_count = self.mix_bus.channel_count();
            for frame in 0..context.quantum_size {
                for channel_index in 0..channel_count {
                    self.interleaved_scratch[frame * channel_count + channel_index] =
                        self.mix_bus.channel(channel_index)[frame];
                }
            }
            self.shared_state.ring.try_push(&self.interleaved_scratch);

            // Coalesced render→control notification, following the renderer's ended-sources pattern:
            // at most one queued drain per rendered burst, so the control thread wakes up ~10 times
            // per second rather than once per quantum.
            if !self.shared_state.drain_pending.swap(true, Ordering::AcqRel) {
                unsafe extern "C" fn invoke(task: *mut c_void) {
                    let shared_state = unsafe { Arc::from_raw(task.cast::<SharedState>()) };
                    shared_state.drain_pending.store(false, Ordering::Release);
                    unsafe {
                        (shared_state.callbacks.callbacks.on_wakeup)(shared_state.callbacks.owner.pointer);
                    }
                }
                let task = Arc::into_raw(Arc::clone(&self.shared_state));
                self.shared_state.callbacks.post(task.cast_mut().cast(), invoke);
            }
        }
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn web_audio_node_create_media_stream_destination(
    node_id: u64,
    quantum_size: usize,
    channel_count: usize,
    ring: FfiSharedCppObject,
    ring_callbacks: AudioFrameRingCallbacks,
    callbacks: PipeCallbacks,
) -> *mut NodeHandle {
    let data = RenderNodeData::new(node_id, 1, 0, quantum_size, channel_count);

    // NB: The control thread queues SetChannelConfig before AddNode and messages addressed to
    //     unknown nodes are dropped, so the constructor must establish the node's channel
    //     configuration itself.
    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode
    data.channel_count.set(channel_count);
    data.channel_count_mode.set(ChannelCountMode::Explicit);
    data.channel_interpretation.set(ChannelInterpretation::Speakers);
    Box::into_raw(node_handle(
        data,
        MediaStreamDestinationRenderNode {
            shared_state: Arc::new(SharedState {
                ring: AudioFrameRing {
                    owner: unsafe { ring.acquire() }.unwrap(),
                    callbacks: ring_callbacks,
                },
                drain_pending: AtomicBool::new(false),
                callbacks: unsafe { CallbackService::new(callbacks) },
            }),
            mix_bus: AudioBus::new(channel_count, quantum_size),
            interleaved_scratch: vec![0.; quantum_size * channel_count],
        },
    ))
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#![allow(clippy::needless_range_loop)]
use super::audio_frame_ring::{AudioFrameRing, AudioFrameRingCallbacks};
use super::node_message::NodeMessage;
use super::render_graph::RenderGraph;
use super::render_node::*;
use super::render_nodes::{BusRef, NodeProcessor, node_handle};
use crate::web_audio::MAX_NUMBER_OF_CHANNELS;

// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#MediaStreamAudioSourceNode
struct MediaStreamSourceRenderNode {
    ring: Option<AudioFrameRing>,
    ring_callbacks: AudioFrameRingCallbacks,
    channel_count: u32,
    interleaved_scratch: Vec<f32>,
}

impl NodeProcessor for MediaStreamSourceRenderNode {
    fn handle_message(&mut self, message: &NodeMessage) {
        if let NodeMessage::SetMediaStreamSourceRing(set_ring) = message {
            self.ring = set_ring.ring.as_ref().map(|ring| AudioFrameRing {
                owner: ring.clone(),
                callbacks: self.ring_callbacks,
            });

            // NB: The ring's own channel count wins over the message field so the interleaved
            //     stride below can never disagree with the ring's layout.
            self.channel_count = if let Some(ring) = &self.ring {
                ring.channel_count()
            } else {
                set_ring.channel_count.max(1)
            };
        }
    }

    unsafe fn process(&mut self, data: &RenderNodeData, _graph: &RenderGraph, context: &RenderContext) {
        unsafe {
            let source_output = BusRef(data.output(0));

            // The number of channels of the output corresponds to the number of channels of the track.
            source_output.set_channel_count(self.channel_count as usize);
            source_output.zero();
            let Some(ring) = &self.ring else {
                return;
            };

            // Drain the ring sequentially, up to one render quantum. When the producer has not
            // delivered enough frames yet (startup, scheduling jitter), the tail of the quantum stays
            // silent; skipping ahead to "the most recent frames" instead would drift against the
            // producer's cadence and repeat or drop content.
            let frames_to_pop = context.quantum_size.min(ring.frames_available());
            if frames_to_pop == 0 {
                return;
            }
            self.interleaved_scratch
                .resize(frames_to_pop * self.channel_count as usize, 0.);
            let frames_popped = ring.try_pop(&mut self.interleaved_scratch);
            for channel_index in 0..self.channel_count as usize {
                let output_samples = source_output.channel_mut(channel_index);
                for frame in 0..frames_popped {
                    output_samples[frame] =
                        self.interleaved_scratch[frame * self.channel_count as usize + channel_index];
                }
            }

            // The producer converts track samples to the context's sample rate before filling the ring.
        }
    }
}

/// # Safety
/// The callbacks must accept the ring handles supplied in later node messages.
pub unsafe fn create_media_stream_source_render_node(
    node_id: u64,
    quantum_size: usize,
    callbacks: AudioFrameRingCallbacks,
) -> Box<NodeHandle> {
    let mut data = RenderNodeData::new(node_id, 0, 1, quantum_size, 2);
    data.reserve_output_channels(0, MAX_NUMBER_OF_CHANNELS);

    // NB: The control thread queues SetChannelConfig before AddNode and messages addressed to
    //     unknown nodes are dropped, so the constructor must establish the node's channel
    //     configuration itself.
    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#MediaStreamAudioSourceNode
    data.channel_count.set(2);
    data.channel_count_mode.set(ChannelCountMode::Max);
    data.channel_interpretation.set(ChannelInterpretation::Speakers);
    node_handle(
        data,
        MediaStreamSourceRenderNode {
            ring: None,
            ring_callbacks: callbacks,
            channel_count: 1,
            interleaved_scratch: Vec::with_capacity(quantum_size * MAX_NUMBER_OF_CHANNELS),
        },
    )
}

pub struct SharedCppObject {
    pub pointer: *mut c_void,
    pub retain: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
    pub release: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
}

// SAFETY: These handles own references to C++ objects whose reference counts are atomic.
unsafe impl Send for SharedCppObject {}
unsafe impl Sync for SharedCppObject {}
impl Clone for SharedCppObject {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        unsafe {
            (self.retain)(self.pointer);
        }
        Self {
            pointer: self.pointer,
            retain: self.retain,
            release: self.release,
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for SharedCppObject {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        unsafe {
            (self.release)(self.pointer);
        }
    }
}

// A control message that updates the state of a single render node.
pub enum NodeMessage {
    SetBiquadFilterType(SetBiquadFilterType),
    SetBufferSourceParameters(SetBufferSourceParameters),
    SetConvolverKernel(SetConvolverKernel),
    SetMediaStreamSourceRing(SetMediaStreamSourceRing),
    SetOscillatorWaveform(SetOscillatorWaveform),
    SetPannerParameters(SetPannerParameters),
    SetWaveShaperParameters(SetWaveShaperParameters),
    StartBufferSource(StartBufferSource),
    StartSource(StartSource),
    StopSource(StopSource),
}

pub fn node_message_target(message: &NodeMessage) -> u64 {
    match message {
        NodeMessage::SetBiquadFilterType(value) => value.node_id,
        NodeMessage::SetBufferSourceParameters(value) => value.node_id,
        NodeMessage::SetConvolverKernel(value) => value.node_id,
        NodeMessage::SetMediaStreamSourceRing(value) => value.node_id,
        NodeMessage::SetOscillatorWaveform(value) => value.node_id,
        NodeMessage::SetPannerParameters(value) => value.node_id,
        NodeMessage::SetWaveShaperParameters(value) => value.node_id,
        NodeMessage::StartBufferSource(value) => value.node_id,
        NodeMessage::StartSource(value) => value.node_id,
        NodeMessage::StopSource(value) => value.node_id,
    }
}

/*

#![allow(clippy::needless_range_loop, clippy::manual_memcpy)]

use std::cell::UnsafeCell;
use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Condvar, Mutex};

use super::render_graph::RenderGraph;
use super::render_node::RenderContext;
use crate::web_audio::control_message_queue::ControlMessageQueue;
use crate::web_audio::control_thread::{ControlThread, ControlThreadCell};

pub trait OfflineAudioRendererClient {
    fn rendering_suspended(&self, suspend_time: f64);
    fn rendering_completed(&self, rendered_channels: &[Vec<f32>]);
    fn sources_ended(&self, nodes: &[u64]);
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct SuspensionState {
    suspend_frames: HashSet<u64>,

    // The next render quantum boundary at which the rendering thread will look for a scheduled suspension. It is
    // published under the same lock that guards the suspension set, so a suspension can never be registered for a
    // boundary the rendering thread has already checked.
    next_suspend_check_frame: u64,
    suspended: bool,
    shutting_down: bool,
}

// Renders an OfflineAudioContext's graph on a dedicated rendering thread, which is created when rendering starts and
// exits once the last render quantum has been processed. Progress is reported back to the control thread by posting
// events to the main thread's event loop.
// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#OfflineAudioContext
pub struct OfflineAudioRenderer {
    control_message_queue: Arc<ControlMessageQueue>,
    destination_node_id: u64,
    number_of_channels: usize,
    length: usize,
    sample_rate: f32,
    quantum_size: usize,
    control_thread: ControlThread,
    client: ControlThreadCell<Option<Rc<dyn OfflineAudioRendererClient>>>,
    thread: UnsafeCell<Option<std::thread::Thread>>,
    graph: UnsafeCell<RenderGraph>,
    rendered_channels: UnsafeCell<Vec<Vec<f32>>>,
    frames_rendered: AtomicU64,
    suspend_mutex: Mutex<SuspensionState>,
    resume_signal: Condvar,
}

// SAFETY: One render thread owns graph/sample mutations, and suspension/progress use the original synchronization.
unsafe impl Send for OfflineAudioRenderer {}
unsafe impl Sync for OfflineAudioRenderer {}
enum Notification {
    Complete,
    Suspended(f64),
    SourcesEnded(Vec<u64>),
}

impl OfflineAudioRenderer {
    pub fn new(
        control_message_queue: Arc<ControlMessageQueue>,
        destination_node_id: u64,
        number_of_channels: usize,
        length: usize,
        sample_rate: f32,
        quantum_size: usize,
    ) -> Arc<Self> {
        let mut rendered_channels = Vec::new();
        rendered_channels.resize_with(number_of_channels, Vec::new);
        for channel in &mut rendered_channels {
            channel.resize(length, 0.);
        }
        Arc::new(Self {
            control_message_queue,
            destination_node_id,
            number_of_channels,
            length,
            sample_rate,
            quantum_size,
            control_thread: ControlThread::current(),
            client: ControlThreadCell::new(None),
            thread: UnsafeCell::new(None),
            graph: UnsafeCell::new(RenderGraph::default()),
            rendered_channels: UnsafeCell::new(rendered_channels),
            frames_rendered: AtomicU64::new(0),
            suspend_mutex: Mutex::new(SuspensionState::default()),
            resume_signal: Condvar::new(),
        })
    }

    /// The callbacks below are set on the control thread before rendering starts and are always invoked on the control
    /// thread. They are cleared once rendering completes to break the reference cycle with the context.
    pub fn set_client(&self, client: Option<Rc<dyn OfflineAudioRendererClient>>) {
        self.client.replace(client);
    }

    pub fn start_rendering(self: &Arc<Self>) {
        assert!(unsafe { &*self.thread.get() }.is_none());
        unsafe { &mut *self.graph.get() }.set_destination(self.destination_node_id);
        let renderer = Arc::clone(self);
        let thread = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("OfflineAudioRenderer".into())
            .spawn(move || {
                renderer.render_thread_main();
            })
            .unwrap();
        unsafe {
            *self.thread.get() = Some(thread.thread().clone());
        }
        drop(thread);
    }

    /// Ends rendering without completing it, unblocking the rendering thread if it is waiting in a suspension.
    pub fn stop(&self) {
        let mut state = self.suspend_mutex.lock().unwrap();
        state.shutting_down = true;
        self.resume_signal.notify_all();
    }

    /// Registers a suspension at the given render quantum boundary. Returns false if the rendering thread already
    /// looked for suspensions at that boundary.
    pub fn request_suspend(&self, frame: u64) -> bool {
        let mut state = self.suspend_mutex.lock().unwrap();
        if frame < state.next_suspend_check_frame {
            return false;
        }
        state.suspend_frames.insert(frame);
        true
    }

    pub fn resume(&self) {
        let mut state = self.suspend_mutex.lock().unwrap();
        state.suspended = false;
        self.resume_signal.notify_all();
    }

    pub fn frames_rendered(&self) -> u64 {
        self.frames_rendered.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
    }

    fn post_to_control_thread(self: &Arc<Self>, notification: Notification) {
        let renderer = Arc::clone(self);
        self.control_thread.post(move || {
            let Some(client) = renderer.client.get() else {
                return;
            };
            match notification {
                Notification::Complete => {
                    // SAFETY: The rendering thread posts the completion after its last write.
                    client.rendering_completed(unsafe { &*renderer.rendered_channels.get() });
                }
                Notification::Suspended(time) => client.rendering_suspended(time),
                Notification::SourcesEnded(nodes) => client.sources_ended(&nodes),
            }
        });
    }

    fn render_thread_main(self: &Arc<Self>) {
        let mut current_frame = 0_u64;
        while current_frame < self.length as u64 {
            // Suspend rendering if a suspension was scheduled at this render quantum boundary.
            {
                let mut state = self.suspend_mutex.lock().unwrap();
                if state.shutting_down {
                    return;
                }
                state.next_suspend_check_frame = current_frame + self.quantum_size as u64;
                if state.suspend_frames.remove(&current_frame) {
                    state.suspended = true;
                    let suspend_time = current_frame as f64 / f64::from(self.sample_rate);
                    self.post_to_control_thread(Notification::Suspended(suspend_time));
                    while state.suspended && !state.shutting_down {
                        state = self.resume_signal.wait(state).unwrap();
                    }
                    if state.shutting_down {
                        return;
                    }
                }
            }
            let graph = unsafe { &mut *self.graph.get() };
            graph.apply_control_messages(self.control_message_queue.drain());
            let context = RenderContext {
                sample_rate: f64::from(self.sample_rate),
                quantum_size: self.quantum_size,
                quantum_start_frame: current_frame,
            };
            graph.render_quantum(&context);

            // Copy the destination's captured output into the rendered buffer.
            if let Some(destination_node) = graph.destination() {
                let destination_output = unsafe { &*destination_node.data().output(0) };
                let frames_to_copy = self.quantum_size.min(self.length - current_frame as usize);
                let rendered_channels = unsafe { &mut *self.rendered_channels.get() };
                for channel_index in 0..self.number_of_channels {
                    if channel_index >= destination_output.channel_count() {
                        break;
                    }
                    let samples = destination_output.channel(channel_index);
                    for frame in 0..frames_to_copy {
                        rendered_channels[channel_index][current_frame as usize + frame] = samples[frame];
                    }
                }
            }
            current_frame += self.quantum_size as u64;
            self.frames_rendered.store(current_frame, Ordering::SeqCst);
            let ended_nodes = graph.take_ended_nodes();
            if !ended_nodes.is_empty() {
                self.post_to_control_thread(Notification::SourcesEnded(ended_nodes));
            }
        }
        self.post_to_control_thread(Notification::Complete);
    }
}

use std::ffi::c_void;

use super::node_message::SharedCppObject;
use crate::web_audio::control_message::FfiSharedCppObject;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct PipeCallbacks {
    pub service: FfiSharedCppObject,
    pub post_task: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void, unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void)),
    pub on_wakeup: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
}

pub(crate) struct CallbackService {
    pub owner: SharedCppObject,
    pub callbacks: PipeCallbacks,
}

// SAFETY: Callback services are atomically reference-counted and invoked on their control-thread event loop.
unsafe impl Send for CallbackService {}
unsafe impl Sync for CallbackService {}
impl CallbackService {
    pub(crate) unsafe fn new(callbacks: PipeCallbacks) -> Self {
        Self {
            owner: unsafe { callbacks.service.acquire() }.unwrap(),
            callbacks,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) unsafe fn post(&self, task: *mut c_void, invoke: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void)) {
        unsafe {
            (self.callbacks.post_task)(self.owner.pointer, task, invoke);
        }
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/web_audio/rendering/realtime_audio_renderer.rs
/*

 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

#![allow(clippy::needless_range_loop, clippy::manual_memcpy)]
use std::cell::UnsafeCell;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicI64, AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering, fence};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use super::audio_bus::AudioBus;
use super::node_message::SharedCppObject;
use super::render_graph::RenderGraph;
use super::render_node::RenderContext;
use crate::web_audio::control_message::{FfiSharedCppObject, clone_arc};
use crate::web_audio::control_message_queue::ControlMessageQueue;
use crate::web_audio::control_thread::{ControlThread, ControlThreadCell};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_audio_output_open(factory: *mut c_void, renderer: *const c_void);
    fn web_audio_output_resume(stream: *mut c_void);
    fn web_audio_output_drain_and_suspend(stream: *mut c_void);
    fn web_audio_output_discard_and_suspend(stream: *mut c_void);
    fn web_audio_monotonic_now_nanoseconds() -> i64;
}

pub trait RealtimeAudioRendererClient {
    fn sources_ended(&self, nodes: &[u64]);
}

// The output buffer most recently handed to the stream, and when its first frame plays.
#[derive(Default)]
struct OutputAnchor {
    version: AtomicU64,
    first_frame_index: AtomicU64,
    end_frame_index: AtomicU64,
    plays_at_nanoseconds: AtomicI64,
}

impl OutputAnchor {
    fn store(&self, first_frame_index: u64, end_frame_index: u64, plays_at_nanoseconds: i64) {
        let version = self.version.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.version.store(version.wrapping_add(1), Ordering::Relaxed);
        fence(Ordering::SeqCst);
        self.first_frame_index.store(first_frame_index, Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.end_frame_index.store(end_frame_index, Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.plays_at_nanoseconds.store(plays_at_nanoseconds, Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.version.store(version.wrapping_add(2), Ordering::Release);
    }

    fn read(&self) -> Option<(u64, u64, i64)> {
        for _retry in 0..32 {
            let version_before = self.version.load(Ordering::Acquire);
            if !version_before.is_multiple_of(2) {
                continue;
            }
            let copy = (
                self.first_frame_index.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
                self.end_frame_index.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
                self.plays_at_nanoseconds.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            );
            fence(Ordering::Acquire);
            let version_after = self.version.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
            if version_before == version_after {
                return Some(copy);
            }
        }
        None
    }
}

// State below is only used on the audio thread, except that the device configuration is recorded on the control
// thread after stream creation, before the first data request callback can run.
struct RenderState {
    graph: RenderGraph,
    device_bus: Option<Box<AudioBus>>,
    device_channel_count: usize,
    frames_output: u64,
    playhead_step: f64,
    playhead: f64,
    pending_samples: Vec<f32>,
}

// Renders an AudioContext's graph in real time, pulled by the audio output device: the playback stream's data request
// callback runs on the platform's audio thread and renders just enough render quanta to fill the device's buffer.
// Progress is reported back to the control thread by posting events to the main thread's event loop.
// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#AudioContext
pub struct RealtimeAudioRenderer {
    control_message_queue: Arc<ControlMessageQueue>,
    destination_node_id: u64,
    sample_rate: f32,
    quantum_size: usize,
    audio_output_factory: SharedCppObject,
    playback_stream: Mutex<Option<SharedCppObject>>,
    control_thread: ControlThread,
    client: ControlThreadCell<Option<Rc<dyn RealtimeAudioRendererClient>>>,
    frames_rendered: AtomicU64,
    suspended: AtomicBool,
    shutting_down: AtomicBool,
    output_anchor: OutputAnchor,
    device_sample_rate: AtomicU32,
    state: UnsafeCell<RenderState>,
}

// SAFETY: Only the audio thread mutates render state after the suspended stream's device configuration is recorded.
unsafe impl Send for RealtimeAudioRenderer {}
unsafe impl Sync for RealtimeAudioRenderer {}
impl RealtimeAudioRenderer {
    pub fn new(
        queue: Arc<ControlMessageQueue>,
        destination_node_id: u64,
        sample_rate: f32,
        quantum_size: usize,
        audio_output_factory: SharedCppObject,
    ) -> Arc<Self> {
        Arc::new(Self {
            control_message_queue: queue,
            destination_node_id,
            sample_rate,
            quantum_size,
            audio_output_factory,
            playback_stream: Mutex::new(None),
            control_thread: ControlThread::current(),
            client: ControlThreadCell::new(None),
            frames_rendered: AtomicU64::new(0),
            suspended: AtomicBool::new(false),
            shutting_down: AtomicBool::new(false),
            output_anchor: OutputAnchor::default(),
            device_sample_rate: AtomicU32::new(0),
            state: UnsafeCell::new(RenderState {
                graph: RenderGraph::default(),
                device_bus: None,
                device_channel_count: 0,
                frames_output: 0,
                playhead_step: 1.,
                playhead: 0.,
                pending_samples: Vec::new(),
            }),
        })
    }

    /// The callback is set on the control thread before rendering starts and is always invoked on the control thread. It
    /// is cleared when the context is suspended, closes, or its document becomes inactive.
    pub fn set_client(&self, client: Option<Rc<dyn RealtimeAudioRendererClient>>) {
        self.client.replace(client);
    }

    pub fn start_rendering(self: &Arc<Self>) {
        assert!(self.playback_stream.lock().unwrap().is_none());
        unsafe { &mut *self.state.get() }
            .graph
            .set_destination(self.destination_node_id);

        // The stream is created in a suspended state so the device configuration can be recorded before the first data
        // request callback runs on the audio thread.
        unsafe { web_audio_output_open(self.audio_output_factory.pointer, Arc::as_ptr(self).cast()) };
    }

    fn set_playback_stream(self: &Arc<Self>, stream: SharedCppObject, channel_count: usize, sample_rate: u32) {
        if self.shutting_down.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            unsafe { web_audio_output_discard_and_suspend(stream.pointer) };
            return;
        }
        let state = unsafe { &mut *self.state.get() };
        if state.device_channel_count != channel_count {
            state.pending_samples.clear();
            state.playhead = 0.;
        }
        state.device_channel_count = channel_count;
        self.device_sample_rate.store(sample_rate, Ordering::Relaxed);
        state.device_bus = Some(Box::new(AudioBus::new(channel_count, self.quantum_size)));

        // When the device sample rate differs from the context's, the rendered audio is resampled by advancing
        // through the rendered frames at this rate.
        state.playhead_step = f64::from(self.sample_rate) / f64::from(sample_rate);
        *self.playback_stream.lock().unwrap() = Some(stream.clone());
        if !self.suspended.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            unsafe { web_audio_output_resume(stream.pointer) };
        }
    }

    fn playback_stream(&self) -> Option<SharedCppObject> {
        self.playback_stream.lock().unwrap().clone()
    }

    // The device went away with the process behind it: a new stream picks the graph up where it stands.
    fn output_lost(self: &Arc<Self>) {
        if self.shutting_down.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            return;
        }
        *self.playback_stream.lock().unwrap() = None;
        self.start_rendering();
    }

    pub fn resume(&self) {
        self.suspended.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
        if let Some(stream) = self.playback_stream() {
            unsafe { web_audio_output_resume(stream.pointer) };
        }
    }

    pub fn suspend(&self) {
        self.suspended.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        if let Some(stream) = self.playback_stream() {
            unsafe { web_audio_output_drain_and_suspend(stream.pointer) };
        }
    }

    pub fn stop(&self) {
        self.shutting_down.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        let stream = self.playback_stream.lock().unwrap().take();
        if let Some(stream) = stream {
            unsafe { web_audio_output_discard_and_suspend(stream.pointer) };
        }
    }

    pub fn frames_rendered(&self) -> u64 {
        self.frames_rendered.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
    }

    /// The amount of audio the output device has played so far, in seconds.
    pub fn output_time_played(&self) -> f64 {
        let now_nanoseconds = unsafe { web_audio_monotonic_now_nanoseconds() };
        let maybe_anchor = self.output_anchor.read();
        let device_sample_rate = self.device_sample_rate.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        if maybe_anchor.is_none() || device_sample_rate == 0 {
            return 0.;
        }
        let (first_frame_index, end_frame_index, plays_at_nanoseconds) = maybe_anchor.unwrap();
        let seconds_since_buffer_started = (now_nanoseconds - plays_at_nanoseconds).max(0) as f64 / 1e9;
        let buffer_start_seconds = first_frame_index as f64 / f64::from(device_sample_rate);
        let buffer_end_seconds = end_frame_index as f64 / f64::from(device_sample_rate);
        if buffer_end_seconds < buffer_start_seconds + seconds_since_buffer_started {
            buffer_end_seconds
        } else {
            buffer_start_seconds + seconds_since_buffer_started
        }
    }

    unsafe fn fill_output_buffer(self: &Arc<Self>, buffer: &mut [f32], buffer_starts_playing_at: i64) -> usize {
        let state = unsafe { &mut *self.state.get() };
        if self.shutting_down.load(Ordering::SeqCst) || state.device_channel_count == 0 {
            return 0;
        }
        let channel_count = state.device_channel_count;
        let frames_requested = buffer.len() / channel_count;
        self.output_anchor.store(
            state.frames_output,
            state.frames_output + frames_requested as u64,
            buffer_starts_playing_at,
        );
        state.frames_output += frames_requested as u64;
        for frame in 0..frames_requested {
            let first_frame = state.playhead as usize;
            let fraction = (state.playhead - first_frame as f64) as f32;

            // Interpolation between adjacent rendered frames requires one frame of lookahead.
            while state.pending_samples.len() / channel_count < first_frame + 2 {
                self.render_quantum_into_pending_samples(state);
            }
            for channel in 0..channel_count {
                let mut sample = state.pending_samples[first_frame * channel_count + channel];
                if fraction != 0. {
                    let next_sample = state.pending_samples[(first_frame + 1) * channel_count + channel];
                    sample += fraction * (next_sample - sample);
                }
                buffer[frame * channel_count + channel] = sample;
            }
            state.playhead += state.playhead_step;
        }

        // Trim rendered frames preceding the playhead. If resampling advances the playhead beyond the rendered frames,
        // carry the remaining offset into the next callback.
        let rendered_frames = state.pending_samples.len() / channel_count;
        let consumed_frames = (state.playhead as usize).min(rendered_frames);
        if consumed_frames > 0 {
            state.pending_samples.drain(..consumed_frames * channel_count);
            state.playhead -= consumed_frames as f64;
        }
        buffer.len()
    }

    fn render_quantum_into_pending_samples(self: &Arc<Self>, state: &mut RenderState) {
        state.graph.apply_control_messages(self.control_message_queue.drain());
        let context = RenderContext {
            sample_rate: f64::from(self.sample_rate),
            quantum_size: self.quantum_size,
            quantum_start_frame: self.frames_rendered.load(Ordering::SeqCst),
        };
        state.graph.render_quantum(&context);

        // Mix the destination's output to the stream's channel layout and append it as interleaved samples.
        if let Some(device_bus) = &mut state.device_bus {
            device_bus.zero();
            if let Some(destination_node) = state.graph.destination() {
                device_bus.sum_from(unsafe { &*destination_node.data().output(0) }, true);
            }
            let sample_offset = state.pending_samples.len();
            state
                .pending_samples
                .resize(sample_offset + self.quantum_size * state.device_channel_count, 0.);
            for frame in 0..self.quantum_size {
                for channel in 0..state.device_channel_count {
                    state.pending_samples[sample_offset + frame * state.device_channel_count + channel] =
                        device_bus.channel(channel)[frame];
                }
            }
        }
        self.frames_rendered
            .fetch_add(self.quantum_size as u64, Ordering::SeqCst);
        let ended_nodes = state.graph.take_ended_nodes();
        if !ended_nodes.is_empty() {
            let renderer = Arc::clone(self);
            self.control_thread.post(move || {
                if let Some(client) = renderer.client.get() {
                    client.sources_ended(&ended_nodes);
                }
            });
        }
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn web_audio_realtime_renderer_retain(renderer: *const RealtimeAudioRenderer) {
    unsafe { Arc::increment_strong_count(renderer) };
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn web_audio_realtime_renderer_release(renderer: *const RealtimeAudioRenderer) {
    unsafe { Arc::decrement_strong_count(renderer) };
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn web_audio_realtime_renderer_fill(
    renderer: *const RealtimeAudioRenderer,
    output: ak::SpanMut<'_, f32>,
    plays_at_nanoseconds: i64,
) -> usize {
    let renderer = unsafe { clone_arc(renderer) };
    unsafe { renderer.fill_output_buffer(output.into_slice(), plays_at_nanoseconds) }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn web_audio_realtime_renderer_output_opened(
    renderer: *const RealtimeAudioRenderer,
    stream: FfiSharedCppObject,
    channel_count: usize,
    sample_rate: u32,
) {
    let renderer = unsafe { clone_arc(renderer) };
    let stream = unsafe { stream.acquire() }.expect("an opened output has a stream");
    renderer.set_playback_stream(stream, channel_count, sample_rate);
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn web_audio_realtime_renderer_output_lost(renderer: *const RealtimeAudioRenderer) {
    unsafe { clone_arc(renderer) }.output_lost();
}
