class CSSPixelFraction;

/// CSSPixels: A position or length in CSS "reference pixels", independent of zoom or screen DPI.
/// See https://www.w3.org/TR/css-values-3/#reference-pixel
class WEBCOMMON_API CSSPixels {
    enum class ValueRounding : u8 {
        Nearest,
        Floor,
        Truncate,
    };

public:
    static constexpr i32 fractional_bits = 6;
    static constexpr i32 fixed_point_denominator = 1 << fractional_bits;

    static constexpr i32 radix_mask = fixed_point_denominator - 1;

    static constexpr i32 max_integer_value = NumericLimits<int>::max() >> fractional_bits;
    static constexpr i32 min_integer_value = NumericLimits<int>::min() >> fractional_bits;

    // NOTE: This is apparently the largest value allowed by Firefox. Probably enough for us as well.
    static constexpr float max_dimension_value = 17895700;

    constexpr CSSPixels() = default;
    template<Signed I>
    constexpr CSSPixels(I value)
    {
        if (value > max_integer_value) [[unlikely]]
            m_value = NumericLimits<int>::max();
        else if (value < min_integer_value) [[unlikely]]
            m_value = NumericLimits<int>::min();
        else
            m_value = static_cast<int>(value) << fractional_bits;
    }

    template<FloatingPoint F>
    explicit CSSPixels(F value)
    {
        *this = nearest_value_for(value);
    }

    template<FloatingPoint F>
    static CSSPixels nearest_value_for(F value)
    {
        return value_for<ValueRounding::Nearest>(value);
    }

    template<FloatingPoint F>
    static CSSPixels floored_value_for(F value)
    {
        return value_for<ValueRounding::Floor>(value);
    }

    template<FloatingPoint F>
    static CSSPixels truncated_value_for(F value)
    {
        return value_for<ValueRounding::Truncate>(value);
    }

    template<Unsigned U>
    constexpr CSSPixels(U value)
    {
        if (value > max_integer_value) [[unlikely]]
            m_value = NumericLimits<int>::max();
        else
            m_value = static_cast<int>(value) << fractional_bits;
    }

    static constexpr CSSPixels from_raw(int value)
    {
        CSSPixels res;
        res.set_raw_value(value);
        return res;
    }

    static constexpr CSSPixels min()
    {
        return from_raw(NumericLimits<int>::min());
    }

    static constexpr CSSPixels max()
    {
        return from_raw(NumericLimits<int>::max());
    }

    static constexpr CSSPixels smallest_positive_value()
    {
        return from_raw(1);
    }

    constexpr float to_float() const { return static_cast<float>(m_value) / fixed_point_denominator; }
    constexpr double to_double() const { return static_cast<double>(m_value) / fixed_point_denominator; }
    constexpr int to_int() const { return m_value / fixed_point_denominator; }

    constexpr int raw_value() const { return m_value; }
    constexpr void set_raw_value(int value) { m_value = value; }

    constexpr bool might_be_saturated() const { return raw_value() == NumericLimits<i32>::max() || raw_value() == NumericLimits<i32>::min(); }

    constexpr bool operator==(CSSPixels const& other) const = default;

    explicit operator double() const { return to_double(); }
    explicit operator float() const { return to_float(); }
    explicit operator int() const { return to_int(); }

    constexpr CSSPixels& operator++()
    {
        m_value = saturating_add(m_value, fixed_point_denominator);
        return *this;
    }
    constexpr CSSPixels& operator--()
    {
        m_value = saturating_sub(m_value, fixed_point_denominator);
        return *this;
    }

    constexpr int operator<=>(CSSPixels const& other) const
    {
        return raw_value() > other.raw_value()
            ? 1
            : raw_value() < other.raw_value()
            ? -1
            : 0;
    }

    constexpr CSSPixels operator+() const { return from_raw(+raw_value()); }
    constexpr CSSPixels operator-() const { return from_raw(saturating_sub(0, raw_value())); }

    constexpr CSSPixels operator+(CSSPixels const& other) const
    {
        return from_raw(saturating_add(raw_value(), other.raw_value()));
    }

    constexpr CSSPixels operator-(CSSPixels const& other) const
    {
        return from_raw(saturating_sub(raw_value(), other.raw_value()));
    }

    constexpr CSSPixels operator*(CSSPixels const& other) const
    {
        i64 value = raw_value();
        value *= other.raw_value();

        int int_value = AK::clamp_to<int>(value >> fractional_bits);

        // Rounding:
        // If last bit cut off was 1:
        if (value & (1u << (fractional_bits - 1))) {
            // If any bit after was 1 as well
            if (value & (radix_mask >> 1u)) {
                // We need to round away from 0
                int_value = saturating_add(int_value, 1);
            } else {
                // Otherwise we round to the next even value
                // Which means we add the least significant bit of the raw integer value
                int_value = saturating_add(int_value, int_value & 1);
            }
        }

        return from_raw(int_value);
    }
    constexpr CSSPixels operator*(CSSPixelFraction const& other) const;

    constexpr CSSPixelFraction operator/(CSSPixels const& other) const;
    constexpr CSSPixels operator/(CSSPixelFraction const& other) const;

    constexpr CSSPixels& operator+=(CSSPixels const& other)
    {
        *this = *this + other;
        return *this;
    }
    constexpr CSSPixels& operator-=(CSSPixels const& other)
    {
        *this = *this - other;
        return *this;
    }
    constexpr CSSPixels& operator*=(CSSPixels const& other)
    {
        *this = *this * other;
        return *this;
    }
    constexpr CSSPixels& operator*=(CSSPixelFraction const& other)
    {
        *this = *this * other;
        return *this;
    }

    constexpr CSSPixels abs() const { return raw_value() < 0 ? from_raw(saturating_sub(0, raw_value())) : *this; }

    CSSPixels& scale_by(float value)
    {
        *this = CSSPixels(to_float() * value);
        return *this;
    }

    CSSPixels& scale_by(double value)
    {
        *this = CSSPixels(to_double() * value);
        return *this;
    }

    CSSPixels scaled(float value) const
    {
        auto result = *this;
        result.scale_by(value);
        return result;
    }

    CSSPixels scaled(double value) const
    {
        auto result = *this;
        result.scale_by(value);
        return result;
    }

private:
    template<ValueRounding rounding, FloatingPoint F>
    static CSSPixels value_for(F value)
    {
        if (isnan(value))
            return {};

        auto scaled_value = value * fixed_point_denominator;
        if constexpr (rounding == ValueRounding::Floor)
            scaled_value = floor(scaled_value);
        else if constexpr (rounding == ValueRounding::Truncate)
            scaled_value = trunc(scaled_value);
        auto raw_value = AK::clamp_to<int>(scaled_value);

        if constexpr (LIBWEB_CSS_DEBUG) {
            // Note: The resolution of CSSPixels is 0.015625, so care must be taken when converting floats/doubles to
            // CSSPixels as small values (such as scale factors) can underflow to zero, or otherwise produce inaccurate
            // results (when scaled back up).
            if (raw_value == 0 && value != 0)
                dbgln("CSSPixels: Conversion from float or double underflowed to zero");
        }

        return from_raw(raw_value);
    }

    i32 m_value { 0 };
};

template<Integral T>
constexpr bool operator==(CSSPixels left, T right) { return left == CSSPixels(right); }
inline bool operator==(CSSPixels left, float right) { return left.to_float() == right; }
inline bool operator==(CSSPixels left, double right) { return left.to_double() == right; }

template<Integral T>
constexpr bool operator>(CSSPixels left, T right) { return left > CSSPixels(right); }
inline bool operator>(CSSPixels left, float right) { return left.to_float() > right; }
inline bool operator>(CSSPixels left, double right) { return left.to_double() > right; }

template<Integral T>
constexpr bool operator<(CSSPixels left, T right) { return left < CSSPixels(right); }
inline bool operator<(CSSPixels left, float right) { return left.to_float() < right; }
inline bool operator<(CSSPixels left, double right) { return left.to_double() < right; }

template<Integral T>
constexpr CSSPixels operator*(CSSPixels left, T right) { return left * CSSPixels(right); }
inline float operator*(CSSPixels left, float right) { return left.to_float() * right; }
inline double operator*(CSSPixels left, double right) { return left.to_double() * right; }

template<Integral T>
constexpr CSSPixels operator*(T left, CSSPixels right) { return CSSPixels(left) * right; }
inline float operator*(float left, CSSPixels right) { return right.to_float() * left; }
inline double operator*(double left, CSSPixels right) { return right.to_double() * left; }

class CSSPixelFraction {
public:
    constexpr CSSPixelFraction(CSSPixels numerator, CSSPixels denominator)
        : m_numerator(numerator)
        , m_denominator(denominator)
    {
        VERIFY(denominator != 0);
    }

    explicit constexpr CSSPixelFraction(CSSPixels value)
        : m_numerator(value)
        , m_denominator(1)
    {
    }

    template<Signed I>
    constexpr CSSPixelFraction(I numerator, I denominator = 1)
        : m_numerator(numerator)
        , m_denominator(denominator)
    {
        VERIFY(denominator != 0);
    }

    template<FloatingPoint F>
    constexpr CSSPixelFraction(F numerator, F denominator = 1)
    {
        if (CSSPixels::nearest_value_for(denominator) == 0) {
            numerator = numerator / denominator;
            denominator = 1;
        }

        m_numerator = CSSPixels(numerator);
        m_denominator = CSSPixels(denominator);

        VERIFY(denominator != 0);
    }

    constexpr operator CSSPixels() const
    {
        i64 wide_value = m_numerator.raw_value();
        wide_value <<= CSSPixels::fractional_bits;
        wide_value /= m_denominator.raw_value();
        return CSSPixels::from_raw(AK::clamp_to<int>(wide_value));
    }

    constexpr CSSPixels operator-(CSSPixels const& other) const
    {
        return CSSPixels(*this) - other;
    }
    constexpr CSSPixels operator+(CSSPixels const& other) const
    {
        return CSSPixels(*this) + other;
    }

    constexpr CSSPixelFraction operator-() const
    {
        return CSSPixelFraction(-numerator(), denominator());
    }

    constexpr int operator<=>(CSSPixelFraction const& other) const
    {
        auto left = static_cast<i64>(m_numerator.raw_value()) * other.m_denominator.raw_value();
        auto right = static_cast<i64>(other.m_numerator.raw_value()) * m_denominator.raw_value();
        if (left > right)
            return 1;
        if (left < right)
            return -1;
        return 0;
    }

    template<Signed I>
    constexpr int operator<=>(I const& other) const
    {
        return *this <=> CSSPixelFraction(other);
    }

    constexpr CSSPixels numerator() const { return m_numerator; }
    constexpr CSSPixels denominator() const { return m_denominator; }

    float to_float() const { return m_numerator.to_float() / m_denominator.to_float(); }
    double to_double() const { return m_numerator.to_double() / m_denominator.to_double(); }
    int to_int() const { return CSSPixels(*this).to_int(); }
    bool might_be_saturated() const { return CSSPixels(*this).might_be_saturated(); }

private:
    CSSPixels m_numerator;
    CSSPixels m_denominator;
};

constexpr CSSPixels CSSPixels::operator*(CSSPixelFraction const& other) const
{
    i64 wide_value = raw_value();
    wide_value *= other.numerator().raw_value();
    wide_value /= other.denominator().raw_value();
    return CSSPixels::from_raw(AK::clamp_to<int>(wide_value));
}

constexpr CSSPixelFraction CSSPixels::operator/(CSSPixels const& other) const
{
    return CSSPixelFraction(*this, other);
}
constexpr CSSPixels CSSPixels::operator/(CSSPixelFraction const& other) const
{
    i64 wide_value = raw_value();
    wide_value *= other.denominator().raw_value();
    wide_value /= other.numerator().raw_value();
    return CSSPixels::from_raw(AK::clamp_to<int>(wide_value));
}

template<Integral T>
constexpr CSSPixelFraction operator/(CSSPixels left, T right) { return left / CSSPixels(right); }
inline float operator/(CSSPixels left, float right) { return left.to_float() / right; }
inline double operator/(CSSPixels left, double right) { return left.to_double() / right; }

using CSSPixelRect = Gfx::Rect<CSSPixels>;
using CSSPixelSize = Gfx::Size<CSSPixels>;

using DevicePixelPoint = Gfx::Point<DevicePixels>;
using DevicePixelRect = Gfx::Rect<DevicePixels>;
using DevicePixelSize = Gfx::Size<DevicePixels>;

constexpr Web::CSSPixels abs(Web::CSSPixels const& value)
{
    return value.abs();
}

constexpr Web::CSSPixels floor(Web::CSSPixels const& value)
{
    return Web::CSSPixels::from_raw(value.raw_value() & ~Web::CSSPixels::radix_mask);
}

constexpr Web::CSSPixels ceil(Web::CSSPixels const& value)
{
    auto floor_value = value.raw_value() & ~Web::CSSPixels::radix_mask;
    auto ceil_value = floor_value + (value.raw_value() & Web::CSSPixels::radix_mask ? Web::CSSPixels::fixed_point_denominator : 0);
    return Web::CSSPixels::from_raw(ceil_value);
}

constexpr Web::CSSPixels round(Web::CSSPixels const& value)
{
    // FIXME: Maybe do this with bit-fiddling instead
    if (value > 0)
        return floor(value + Web::CSSPixels::from_raw(Web::CSSPixels::fixed_point_denominator >> 1 /* 0.5 */));
    return ceil(value - Web::CSSPixels::from_raw(Web::CSSPixels::fixed_point_denominator >> 1 /* 0.5 */));
}

inline Web::CSSPixels sqrt(Web::CSSPixels const& value)
{
    return Web::CSSPixels::nearest_value_for(AK::sqrt(value.to_float()));
}

constexpr Web::DevicePixels abs(Web::DevicePixels const& value)
{
    return AK::abs(value.value());
}

constexpr Web::CSSPixels square_distance_between(Web::CSSPixelPoint const& a, Web::CSSPixelPoint const& b)
{
    auto delta_x = abs(a.x() - b.x());
    auto delta_y = abs(a.y() - b.y());
    return delta_x * delta_x + delta_y * delta_y;
}

constexpr Web::CSSPixelPoint constrained(Web::CSSPixelPoint const& point, Web::CSSPixelRect const& rect)
{
    return {
        clamp(point.x(), rect.left(), rect.right() - 1),
        clamp(point.y(), rect.top(), rect.bottom() - 1),
    };
}

template<>
template<>
[[nodiscard]] ALWAYS_INLINE Web::CSSPixelRect Web::CSSPixelRect::to_rounded<Web::CSSPixels>() const
{
    return {
        round(x()),
        round(y()),
        round(width()),
        round(height()),
    };
}

#include <AK/CharacterTypes.h>
#include <LibWebCommon/ReferrerPolicy/ReferrerPolicy.h>

namespace Web::ReferrerPolicy {

static bool equals_ignoring_ascii_case(Utf16View string, StringView ascii_string)
{
    if (string.length_in_code_units() != ascii_string.length())
        return false;

    for (size_t i = 0; i < string.length_in_code_units(); ++i) {
        if (AK::to_ascii_lowercase(string.code_unit_at(i)) != AK::to_ascii_lowercase(ascii_string[i]))
            return false;
    }

    return true;
}

StringView to_string(ReferrerPolicy referrer_policy)
{
    switch (referrer_policy) {
    case ReferrerPolicy::EmptyString:
        return ""sv;
    case ReferrerPolicy::NoReferrer:
        return "no-referrer"sv;
    case ReferrerPolicy::NoReferrerWhenDowngrade:
        return "no-referrer-when-downgrade"sv;
    case ReferrerPolicy::SameOrigin:
        return "same-origin"sv;
    case ReferrerPolicy::Origin:
        return "origin"sv;
    case ReferrerPolicy::StrictOrigin:
        return "strict-origin"sv;
    case ReferrerPolicy::OriginWhenCrossOrigin:
        return "origin-when-cross-origin"sv;
    case ReferrerPolicy::StrictOriginWhenCrossOrigin:
        return "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"sv;
    case ReferrerPolicy::UnsafeURL:
        return "unsafe-url"sv;
    }
    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

Optional<ReferrerPolicy> from_string(StringView string)
{
    if (string.is_empty())
        return ReferrerPolicy::EmptyString;
    if (string.equals_ignoring_ascii_case("no-referrer"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::NoReferrer;
    if (string.equals_ignoring_ascii_case("no-referrer-when-downgrade"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::NoReferrerWhenDowngrade;
    if (string.equals_ignoring_ascii_case("same-origin"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::SameOrigin;
    if (string.equals_ignoring_ascii_case("origin"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::Origin;
    if (string.equals_ignoring_ascii_case("strict-origin"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::StrictOrigin;
    if (string.equals_ignoring_ascii_case("origin-when-cross-origin"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::OriginWhenCrossOrigin;
    if (string.equals_ignoring_ascii_case("strict-origin-when-cross-origin"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::StrictOriginWhenCrossOrigin;
    if (string.equals_ignoring_ascii_case("unsafe-url"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::UnsafeURL;
    return {};
}

Optional<ReferrerPolicy> from_string(Utf16String const& string)
{
    return from_string(string.utf16_view());
}

Optional<ReferrerPolicy> from_string(Utf16View string)
{
    if (string.is_empty())
        return ReferrerPolicy::EmptyString;
    if (equals_ignoring_ascii_case(string, "no-referrer"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::NoReferrer;
    if (equals_ignoring_ascii_case(string, "no-referrer-when-downgrade"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::NoReferrerWhenDowngrade;
    if (equals_ignoring_ascii_case(string, "same-origin"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::SameOrigin;
    if (equals_ignoring_ascii_case(string, "origin"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::Origin;
    if (equals_ignoring_ascii_case(string, "strict-origin"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::StrictOrigin;
    if (equals_ignoring_ascii_case(string, "origin-when-cross-origin"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::OriginWhenCrossOrigin;
    if (equals_ignoring_ascii_case(string, "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::StrictOriginWhenCrossOrigin;
    if (equals_ignoring_ascii_case(string, "unsafe-url"sv))
        return ReferrerPolicy::UnsafeURL;
    return {};
}

}

use std::env;
use std::error::Error;
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    let manifest_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")?);
    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("OUT_DIR")?);

    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=cbindgen.toml");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=src");

    cbindgen::generate(manifest_dir).map_or_else(
        |error| match error {
            cbindgen::Error::ParseSyntaxError { .. } => {}
            e => panic!("{e:?}"),
        },
        |bindings| {
            let header_path = out_dir.join("RustFFI.h");
            bindings.write_to_file(&header_path);
        },
    );

    Ok(())
}

/*

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::{Base64Alphabet, LastChunkHandling, Span, Utf16StringUnits, decode_base64};
use liburl_rust::url::percent_decode_bytes;

use crate::mime_sniff::ffi::{OnMimeType, lend_mime_type};
use crate::mime_sniff::mime_type::MimeType;
use crate::rust_panic::abort_on_panic;

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#data-url-struct
pub struct DataUrl {
    pub mime_type: MimeType,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
}

// https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#forgiving-base64-decode
fn forgiving_base64_decode(string: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    // NB: A code point outside ASCII is never part of base64 data, nor ASCII whitespace.
    if !string.is_ascii() {
        return None;
    }
    let result = decode_base64(
        Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(string),
        Base64Alphabet::Base64,
        LastChunkHandling::Loose,
        None,
    );
    result.error.is_none().then_some(result.bytes)
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#data-url-processor
// NB: C++ runs steps 1 and 2, and passes the serialization of the URL as input.
pub fn process_data_url(input: &str) -> Option<DataUrl> {
    // 3. Remove the leading "data:" from input.
    let input = input.strip_prefix("data:").expect("the URL's scheme is data");

    // 4. Let position point at the start of input.
    // 5. Let mimeType be the result of collecting a sequence of code points that are not equal to U+002C (,), given
    //    position.
    let position = input.find(',');
    let mime_type = &input[..position.unwrap_or(input.len())];

    // 6. Strip leading and trailing ASCII whitespace from mimeType.
    let mut mime_type = mime_type.trim_ascii();

    // 7. If position is past the end of input, then return failure.
    let position = position?;

    // 8. Advance position by 1.
    // 9. Let encodedBody be the remainder of input.
    let encoded_body = &input[position + 1..];

    // 10. Let body be the percent-decoding of encodedBody.
    let mut body = percent_decode_bytes(encoded_body.as_bytes());

    // 11. If mimeType ends with U+003B (;), followed by zero or more U+0020 SPACE, followed by an ASCII
    //     case-insensitive match for "base64", then:
    let base64_suffix_start = mime_type.len().checked_sub("base64".len());
    if let Some(start) = base64_suffix_start
        && mime_type[start..].eq_ignore_ascii_case("base64")
        && mime_type[..start].trim_end_matches(' ').ends_with(';')
    {
        // 1. Let stringBody be the isomorphic decode of body.
        // 2. Set body to the forgiving-base64 decode of stringBody.
        // 3. If body is failure, then return failure.
        body = forgiving_base64_decode(&body)?;

        // 4. Remove the last 6 code points from mimeType.
        // 5. Remove trailing U+0020 SPACE code points from mimeType, if any.
        // 6. Remove the last U+003B (;) from mimeType.
        let without_base64 = mime_type[..start].trim_end_matches(' ');
        mime_type = &without_base64[..without_base64.len() - 1];
    }

    // 12. If mimeType starts with ";", then prepend "text/plain" to mimeType.
    let mime_type: Vec<char> = if mime_type.starts_with(';') {
        "text/plain".chars().chain(mime_type.chars()).collect()
    } else {
        mime_type.chars().collect()
    };

    // 13. Let mimeTypeRecord be the result of parsing mimeType.
    // 14. If mimeTypeRecord is failure, then set mimeTypeRecord to text/plain;charset=US-ASCII.
    let mime_type_record = MimeType::parse(&mime_type).unwrap_or_else(|| {
        let mut mime_type_record = MimeType::new("text".to_owned(), "plain".to_owned());
        mime_type_record.set_parameter("charset".to_owned(), "US-ASCII".to_owned());
        mime_type_record
    });

    // 15. Return a new data: URL struct whose MIME type is mimeTypeRecord and body is body.
    Some(DataUrl {
        mime_type: mime_type_record,
        body,
    })
}

type OnBytes = unsafe extern "C" fn(ctx: *mut c_void, bytes: Span<'_, u8>);

/// Processes the serialization of a data: URL, without its fragment. Calls `on_body` with the body of the data: URL
/// struct and `on_mime_type` with its MIME type, and returns whether it succeeded.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `input` must be ASCII, and `on_body` and `on_mime_type` must be safe to call with `ctx`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn fetch_process_data_url(
    input: Span<'_, u8>,
    ctx: *mut c_void,
    on_body: OnBytes,
    on_mime_type: OnMimeType,
) -> bool {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        let input = core::str::from_utf8(input.as_slice()).expect("C++ passes a URL serialization");
        let Some(data_url) = process_data_url(input) else {
            return false;
        };
        // SAFETY: The caller passes callbacks for `ctx`.
        unsafe {
            on_body(ctx, Span::new(&data_url.body));
            lend_mime_type(&data_url.mime_type, ctx, on_mime_type);
        }
        true
    })
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWebCommon/Rust/src/html/serialization_records.rs
/*

 * Copyright (c) 2022, Andrew Kaster <akaster@serenityos.org>
 * Copyright (c) 2023-2024, Kenneth Myhra <kennethmyhra@serenityos.org>

 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

//! The formats of the records of structured serialization, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html
//!
//! A record, an HTML::IPCSerializationRecord or an HTML::StorageSerializationRecord of
//! LibWebCommon/HTML/SerializationRecords.h, holds the values that a serialization writes in one of two formats. The
//! IPC format is read only by the build that writes it, and holds integers at their full width in the byte order of
//! the host. The storage format is stable on disk, for IndexedDB: a storage record starts with the prologue of the
//! format, and holds integers as LEB128 varints and everything else in little-endian byte order.

use core::cell::Cell;

use ak::Utf16StringUnits;

/// HTML::storage_format_magic, which every storage record starts with.
const STORAGE_FORMAT_MAGIC: [u8; 4] = *b"LBSC";

/// HTML::storage_format_version, the on-disk version of the storage format. Bumping it is a deliberate format change.
const STORAGE_FORMAT_VERSION: u64 = 1;

/// HTML::storage_format_flags, for optional features of the envelope. A change to the encoding of values bumps the
/// version instead.
const STORAGE_FORMAT_FLAGS: u64 = 0;

/// HTML::SerializationType, the format of a record.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SerializationType {
    Ipc,
    Storage,
}

fn append_unsigned_leb128(data: &mut Vec<u8>, mut value: u64) {
    loop {
        let byte = (value & 0x7f) as u8;
        value >>= 7;
        if value == 0 {
            data.push(byte);
            return;
        }
        data.push(byte | 0x80);
    }
}

fn append_signed_leb128(data: &mut Vec<u8>, mut value: i64) {
    loop {
        let byte = (value & 0x7f) as u8;
        // NB: An arithmetic shift, which keeps the sign.
        value >>= 7;
        let sign_bit_set = byte & 0x40 != 0;
        if (value == 0 && !sign_bit_set) || (value == -1 && sign_bit_set) {
            data.push(byte);
            return;
        }
        data.push(byte | 0x80);
    }
}

/// The bytes of a record, to which the encode functions append values in the format of the record.
pub struct RecordEncoder {
    serialization_type: SerializationType,
    data: Vec<u8>,
}

impl RecordEncoder {
    pub fn new(serialization_type: SerializationType) -> Self {
        let mut data = Vec::new();
        if serialization_type == SerializationType::Storage {
            data.extend_from_slice(&STORAGE_FORMAT_MAGIC);
            append_unsigned_leb128(&mut data, STORAGE_FORMAT_VERSION);
            append_unsigned_leb128(&mut data, STORAGE_FORMAT_FLAGS);
        }
        Self {
            serialization_type,
            data,
        }
    }

    pub fn serialization_type(&self) -> SerializationType {
        self.serialization_type
    }

    pub fn bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.data
    }

    pub fn into_bytes(self) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.data
    }

    pub fn encode_u8(&mut self, value: u8) {
        self.data.push(value);
    }

    pub fn encode_bool(&mut self, value: bool) {
        self.encode_u8(u8::from(value));
    }

    pub fn encode_u16(&mut self, value: u16) {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => self.data.extend_from_slice(&value.to_ne_bytes()),
            SerializationType::Storage => append_unsigned_leb128(&mut self.data, u64::from(value)),
        }
    }

    pub fn encode_i32(&mut self, value: i32) {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => self.data.extend_from_slice(&value.to_ne_bytes()),
            SerializationType::Storage => append_signed_leb128(&mut self.data, i64::from(value)),
        }
    }

    pub fn encode_u32(&mut self, value: u32) {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => self.data.extend_from_slice(&value.to_ne_bytes()),
            SerializationType::Storage => append_unsigned_leb128(&mut self.data, u64::from(value)),
        }
    }

    pub fn encode_u64(&mut self, value: u64) {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => self.data.extend_from_slice(&value.to_ne_bytes()),
            SerializationType::Storage => append_unsigned_leb128(&mut self.data, value),
        }
    }

    pub fn encode_i64(&mut self, value: i64) {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => self.data.extend_from_slice(&value.to_ne_bytes()),
            SerializationType::Storage => append_signed_leb128(&mut self.data, value),
        }
    }

    pub fn encode_f64(&mut self, value: f64) {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => self.data.extend_from_slice(&value.to_bits().to_ne_bytes()),
            SerializationType::Storage => self.data.extend_from_slice(&value.to_bits().to_le_bytes()),
        }
    }

    /// The length of a string or of bytes in an IPC record, which LibIPC holds as a u32.
    fn encode_ipc_size(&mut self, size: usize) {
        let size = u32::try_from(size).expect("an IPC record holds fewer than 2^32 elements of a value");
        self.data.extend_from_slice(&size.to_ne_bytes());
    }

    /// A string, whose Latin-1 storage the record keeps: an IPC record holds whether the string has it and the length of
    /// the string, and a storage record holds both in one varint, the length shifted left by one.
    pub fn encode_utf16_string(&mut self, string: Utf16StringUnits<'_>) {
        let (has_latin1_storage, length) = match string {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(characters) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(characters) => (true, characters.len()),
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(code_units) => (false, code_units.len()),
        };
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => {
                self.encode_bool(has_latin1_storage);
                self.encode_ipc_size(length);
            }
            SerializationType::Storage => {
                append_unsigned_leb128(&mut self.data, ((length as u64) << 1) | u64::from(has_latin1_storage));
            }
        }
        match string {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(characters) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(characters) => {
                self.data.extend_from_slice(characters);
            }
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(code_units) => {
                for &code_unit in code_units {
                    match self.serialization_type {
                        SerializationType::Ipc => self.data.extend_from_slice(&code_unit.to_ne_bytes()),
                        SerializationType::Storage => self.data.extend_from_slice(&code_unit.to_le_bytes()),
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn encode_bytes(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => self.encode_ipc_size(bytes.len()),
            SerializationType::Storage => append_unsigned_leb128(&mut self.data, bytes.len() as u64),
        }
        self.data.extend_from_slice(bytes);
    }

    /// A BigInt, as the bytes that LibCrypto's SignedBigInteger::export_data() writes: 1 if the value is negative and 0
    /// otherwise, then its magnitude, big-endian, without leading zeros, which is empty for zero.
    pub fn encode_big_int(&mut self, is_negative: bool, magnitude: &[u8]) {
        let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(1 + magnitude.len());
        bytes.push(u8::from(is_negative));
        bytes.extend_from_slice(magnitude);
        self.encode_bytes(&bytes);
    }
}

fn storage_size(size: u64) -> Result<usize, DecodeError> {
    usize::try_from(size).map_err(|_| DecodeError("Structured serialize storage size does not fit on this platform"))
}

/// Why a record cannot be read: it does not hold what reading it expects.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DecodeError(pub &'static str);

/// A string that a record holds: the characters of a string with Latin-1 storage, or the code units of any other.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DecodedString<'a> {
    Latin1(&'a [u8]),
    Utf16(Vec<u16>),
}

/// The bytes of a record, from which the decode functions read what the encode functions of RecordEncoder wrote. They
/// reject what AK's decoding of the formats rejected, as a truncated record or a varint too long for its type, and
/// accept the varints it accepted, as one with redundant bytes.
pub struct RecordDecoder<'a> {
    serialization_type: SerializationType,
    data: &'a [u8],
    position: Cell<usize>,
}

impl<'a> RecordDecoder<'a> {
    /// A decoder of the bytes of a record, which reads the prologue of a storage record.
    pub fn new(serialization_type: SerializationType, data: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        let decoder = Self {
            serialization_type,
            data,
            position: Cell::new(0),
        };
        if serialization_type == SerializationType::Storage {
            if decoder.read_bytes(STORAGE_FORMAT_MAGIC.len())? != STORAGE_FORMAT_MAGIC {
                return Err(DecodeError("Invalid structured serialize storage magic"));
            }
            if decoder.decode_u64()? != STORAGE_FORMAT_VERSION {
                return Err(DecodeError("Unsupported structured serialize storage version"));
            }
            if decoder.decode_u64()? != STORAGE_FORMAT_FLAGS {
                return Err(DecodeError("Unsupported structured serialize storage flags"));
            }
        }
        Ok(decoder)
    }

    pub fn serialization_type(&self) -> SerializationType {
        self.serialization_type
    }

    /// Whether the decoder has read every byte of the record.
    pub fn is_at_end(&self) -> bool {
        self.position.get() == self.data.len()
    }

    fn remaining(&self) -> usize {
        self.data.len() - self.position.get()
    }

    fn read_bytes(&self, count: usize) -> Result<&'a [u8], DecodeError> {
        if count > self.remaining() {
            return Err(DecodeError("Truncated structured serialization record"));
        }
        let start = self.position.get();
        self.position.set(start + count);
        Ok(&self.data[start..start + count])
    }

    fn read_array<const N: usize>(&self) -> Result<[u8; N], DecodeError> {
        Ok(self.read_bytes(N)?.try_into().expect("read_bytes() reads N bytes"))
    }

    /// An unsigned LEB128 varint of a value of `bits` bits, as AK::LEB128 reads one: the last byte that can hold bits
    /// of the value ends the varint, and holds no bits that the value does not have.
    fn read_unsigned_leb128(&self, bits: u32) -> Result<u64, DecodeError> {
        let mut value = 0;
        let mut shift = 0;
        loop {
            let byte = self.decode_u8()?;
            value |= u64::from(byte & 0x7f) << shift;
            if shift + 7 >= bits {
                if u32::from(byte) >> (bits - shift) != 0 {
                    return Err(DecodeError("LEB128 varint does not fit its type"));
                }
                return Ok(value);
            }
            if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
                return Ok(value);
            }
            shift += 7;
        }
    }

    /// A signed LEB128 varint of a value of `bits` bits, as AK::LEB128 reads one: the last byte that can hold bits of
    /// the value ends the varint, and its bits that the value does not have are copies of the sign bit.
    fn read_signed_leb128(&self, bits: u32) -> Result<i64, DecodeError> {
        let mut value: u64 = 0;
        let mut shift = 0;
        loop {
            let byte = self.decode_u8()?;
            value |= u64::from(byte & 0x7f) << shift;
            if shift + 7 >= bits {
                let sign_and_unused = ((byte << 1) as i8) >> (bits - shift);
                if byte & 0x80 != 0 || (sign_and_unused != 0 && sign_and_unused != -1) {
                    return Err(DecodeError("LEB128 varint does not fit its type"));
                }
                let unused = 64 - bits;
                return Ok(((value << unused) as i64) >> unused);
            }
            shift += 7;
            if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
                let mut value = value as i64;
                if byte & 0x40 != 0 {
                    value |= -1 << shift;
                }
                return Ok(value);
            }
        }
    }

    /// The length of a string or of bytes: in an IPC record a u32, which is no more than the bytes of the record that
    /// follow it, as LibIPC reads one, and in a storage record a varint.
    fn decode_size(&self) -> Result<usize, DecodeError> {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => {
                let size = u32::from_ne_bytes(self.read_array()?) as usize;
                if size > self.remaining() {
                    return Err(DecodeError("IPC decode: Size exceeds the rest of the message"));
                }
                Ok(size)
            }
            SerializationType::Storage => storage_size(self.decode_u64()?),
        }
    }

    pub fn decode_u8(&self) -> Result<u8, DecodeError> {
        Ok(self.read_array::<1>()?[0])
    }

    pub fn decode_bool(&self) -> Result<bool, DecodeError> {
        match self.decode_u8()? {
            0 => Ok(false),
            1 => Ok(true),
            _ => Err(DecodeError("Invalid structured serialization bool")),
        }
    }

    pub fn decode_u16(&self) -> Result<u16, DecodeError> {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => Ok(u16::from_ne_bytes(self.read_array()?)),
            SerializationType::Storage => Ok(self.read_unsigned_leb128(16)? as u16),
        }
    }

    pub fn decode_i32(&self) -> Result<i32, DecodeError> {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => Ok(i32::from_ne_bytes(self.read_array()?)),
            SerializationType::Storage => Ok(self.read_signed_leb128(32)? as i32),
        }
    }

    pub fn decode_u32(&self) -> Result<u32, DecodeError> {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => Ok(u32::from_ne_bytes(self.read_array()?)),
            SerializationType::Storage => Ok(self.read_unsigned_leb128(32)? as u32),
        }
    }

    pub fn decode_u64(&self) -> Result<u64, DecodeError> {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => Ok(u64::from_ne_bytes(self.read_array()?)),
            SerializationType::Storage => self.read_unsigned_leb128(64),
        }
    }

    pub fn decode_i64(&self) -> Result<i64, DecodeError> {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => Ok(i64::from_ne_bytes(self.read_array()?)),
            SerializationType::Storage => self.read_signed_leb128(64),
        }
    }

    pub fn decode_f64(&self) -> Result<f64, DecodeError> {
        match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => Ok(f64::from_bits(u64::from_ne_bytes(self.read_array()?))),
            SerializationType::Storage => Ok(f64::from_bits(u64::from_le_bytes(self.read_array()?))),
        }
    }

    pub fn decode_utf16_string(&self) -> Result<DecodedString<'a>, DecodeError> {
        let (has_latin1_storage, length) = match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => (self.decode_bool()?, self.decode_size()?),
            SerializationType::Storage => {
                let header = self.decode_u64()?;
                (header & 1 != 0, storage_size(header >> 1)?)
            }
        };
        if has_latin1_storage {
            return Ok(DecodedString::Latin1(self.read_bytes(length)?));
        }
        let byte_count = length
            .checked_mul(2)
            .ok_or(DecodeError("Truncated structured serialization record"))?;
        let bytes = self.read_bytes(byte_count)?;
        let code_unit_from_bytes = match self.serialization_type {
            SerializationType::Ipc => u16::from_ne_bytes,
            SerializationType::Storage => u16::from_le_bytes,
        };
        Ok(DecodedString::Utf16(
            bytes
                .as_chunks::<2>()
                .0
                .iter()
                .map(|&bytes| code_unit_from_bytes(bytes))
                .collect(),
        ))
    }

    pub fn decode_bytes(&self) -> Result<&'a [u8], DecodeError> {
        let length = self.decode_size()?;
        self.read_bytes(length)
    }

    /// What encode_big_int() writes: whether the value is negative, which any sign but 0 says, and its magnitude.
    pub fn decode_big_int(&self) -> Result<(bool, &'a [u8]), DecodeError> {
        let Some((&sign, magnitude)) = self.decode_bytes()?.split_first() else {
            return Err(DecodeError("Invalid BigInt"));
        };
        Ok((sign != 0, magnitude))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const PROLOGUE: [u8; 6] = [b'L', b'B', b'S', b'C', 0x01, 0x00];

    fn storage(encode: impl FnOnce(&mut RecordEncoder)) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut encoder = RecordEncoder::new(SerializationType::Storage);
        encode(&mut encoder);
        assert_eq!(encoder.bytes()[..PROLOGUE.len()], PROLOGUE);
        encoder.bytes()[PROLOGUE.len()..].to_vec()
    }

    fn ipc(encode: impl FnOnce(&mut RecordEncoder)) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut encoder = RecordEncoder::new(SerializationType::Ipc);
        encode(&mut encoder);
        encoder.bytes().to_vec()
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_storage_record_starts_with_the_prologue() {
        assert_eq!(RecordEncoder::new(SerializationType::Storage).bytes(), PROLOGUE);
        assert!(RecordEncoder::new(SerializationType::Ipc).bytes().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_storage_record_holds_integers_as_leb128_varints() {
        assert_eq!(storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_bool(true)), [0x01]);
        assert_eq!(storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_u8(0xff)), [0xff]);
        assert_eq!(storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_u16(300)), [0xac, 0x02]);
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_u32(0x0102_0304)),
            [0x84, 0x86, 0x88, 0x08]
        );
        assert_eq!(storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_u64(0)), [0x00]);
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_u64(u64::MAX)),
            [0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x01]
        );
        assert_eq!(storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_i64(-2)), [0x7e]);
        assert_eq!(storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_i64(63)), [0x3f]);
        assert_eq!(storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_i64(64)), [0xc0, 0x00]);
        assert_eq!(storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_i64(-65)), [0xbf, 0x7f]);
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_i32(i32::MAX)),
            [0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x07]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_i32(i32::MIN)),
            [0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x78]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_storage_record_holds_a_double_as_its_little_endian_bits() {
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_f64(1.0)),
            [0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xf0, 0x3f]
        );
        assert_eq!(storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_f64(-0.0))[7], 0x80);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_ipc_record_holds_integers_at_their_full_width() {
        assert_eq!(ipc(|encoder| encoder.encode_bool(false)), [0x00]);
        assert_eq!(ipc(|encoder| encoder.encode_u16(0x0102)), 0x0102_u16.to_ne_bytes());
        assert_eq!(ipc(|encoder| encoder.encode_i32(-2)), (-2_i32).to_ne_bytes());
        assert_eq!(
            ipc(|encoder| encoder.encode_u32(0x0102_0304)),
            0x0102_0304_u32.to_ne_bytes()
        );
        assert_eq!(ipc(|encoder| encoder.encode_u64(1)), 1_u64.to_ne_bytes());
        assert_eq!(ipc(|encoder| encoder.encode_i64(-1)), (-1_i64).to_ne_bytes());
        assert_eq!(
            ipc(|encoder| encoder.encode_f64(13.5)),
            13.5_f64.to_bits().to_ne_bytes()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_storage_record_holds_a_latin1_string_as_one_byte_per_code_unit() {
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"AB"))),
            [0x05, b'A', b'B']
        );
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(&[b'A', 0xe9]))),
            [0x05, b'A', 0xe9]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b""))),
            [0x01]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_storage_record_holds_a_utf16_string_as_little_endian_code_units() {
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(&[0x41, 0xd800, 0x42]))),
            [0x06, 0x41, 0x00, 0x00, 0xd8, 0x42, 0x00]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_storage_record_holds_the_length_of_a_string_as_a_varint() {
        let characters = [b'a'; 64];
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(&characters[..63])))[..1],
            [0x7f]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(&characters)))[..2],
            [0x81, 0x01]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_ipc_record_holds_the_storage_and_the_length_of_a_string_before_it() {
        let mut expected = vec![0x01];
        expected.extend_from_slice(&2_u32.to_ne_bytes());
        expected.extend_from_slice(b"AB");
        assert_eq!(
            ipc(|encoder| encoder.encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"AB"))),
            expected
        );

        let mut expected = vec![0x00];
        expected.extend_from_slice(&1_u32.to_ne_bytes());
        expected.extend_from_slice(&0xd800_u16.to_ne_bytes());
        assert_eq!(
            ipc(|encoder| encoder.encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(&[0xd800]))),
            expected
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_record_holds_the_length_of_bytes_before_them() {
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_bytes(&[0xde, 0xad])),
            [0x02, 0xde, 0xad]
        );
        assert_eq!(storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_bytes(&[])), [0x00]);

        let mut expected = 2_u32.to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
        expected.extend_from_slice(&[0xde, 0xad]);
        assert_eq!(ipc(|encoder| encoder.encode_bytes(&[0xde, 0xad])), expected);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_record_holds_a_big_int_as_its_sign_then_its_magnitude() {
        assert_eq!(storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_big_int(false, &[])), [0x01, 0x00]);
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_big_int(false, &[0x01, 0x00])),
            [0x03, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            storage(|encoder| encoder.encode_big_int(true, &[0x05])),
            [0x02, 0x01, 0x05]
        );
    }

    fn storage_record(value: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut bytes = PROLOGUE.to_vec();
        bytes.extend_from_slice(value);
        bytes
    }

    fn storage_decoder(bytes: &[u8]) -> RecordDecoder<'_> {
        RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Storage, bytes).expect("the record has a prologue")
    }

    fn round_trip(
        serialization_type: SerializationType,
        encode: impl FnOnce(&mut RecordEncoder),
        decode: impl FnOnce(&RecordDecoder),
    ) {
        let mut encoder = RecordEncoder::new(serialization_type);
        encode(&mut encoder);
        let decoder = RecordDecoder::new(serialization_type, encoder.bytes()).expect("the record has a prologue");
        decode(&decoder);
        assert!(decoder.is_at_end());
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_value_round_trips_through_both_formats() {
        for serialization_type in [SerializationType::Ipc, SerializationType::Storage] {
            round_trip(
                serialization_type,
                |encoder| {
                    encoder.encode_bool(false);
                    encoder.encode_bool(true);
                    encoder.encode_u8(0xab);
                    encoder.encode_u16(0xfedc);
                    encoder.encode_i32(-12345);
                    encoder.encode_i32(i32::MIN);
                    encoder.encode_u32(0xfedc_ba98);
                    encoder.encode_u64(0x0102_0304_0506_0708);
                    encoder.encode_u64(u64::MAX);
                    encoder.encode_i64(-0x0102_0304_0506_0708);
                    encoder.encode_i64(i64::MIN);
                    encoder.encode_f64(13.5);
                    encoder.encode_f64(-0.0);
                    encoder.encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"stored string"));
                    encoder.encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(&[0x68, 0xe9, 0xd83e, 0xdeac]));
                    encoder.encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b""));
                    encoder.encode_bytes(&[0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef]);
                    encoder.encode_big_int(true, &[0x01, 0x00]);
                },
                |decoder| {
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_bool(), Ok(false));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_bool(), Ok(true));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_u8(), Ok(0xab));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_u16(), Ok(0xfedc));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_i32(), Ok(-12345));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_i32(), Ok(i32::MIN));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_u32(), Ok(0xfedc_ba98));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_u64(), Ok(0x0102_0304_0506_0708));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_u64(), Ok(u64::MAX));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_i64(), Ok(-0x0102_0304_0506_0708));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_i64(), Ok(i64::MIN));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_f64(), Ok(13.5));
                    assert!(
                        decoder
                            .decode_f64()
                            .is_ok_and(|value| value == 0.0 && value.is_sign_negative())
                    );
                    assert_eq!(
                        decoder.decode_utf16_string(),
                        Ok(DecodedString::Latin1(b"stored string"))
                    );
                    assert_eq!(
                        decoder.decode_utf16_string(),
                        Ok(DecodedString::Utf16(vec![0x68, 0xe9, 0xd83e, 0xdeac]))
                    );
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_utf16_string(), Ok(DecodedString::Latin1(b"")));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_bytes(), Ok(&[0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef][..]));
                    assert_eq!(decoder.decode_big_int(), Ok((true, &[0x01, 0x00][..])));
                },
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_storage_record_needs_the_prologue() {
        assert!(RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Storage, &PROLOGUE).is_ok());
        assert!(RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Storage, b"LBS").is_err());
        assert!(RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Storage, &[b'L', b'B', b'S', b'D', 0x01, 0x00]).is_err());
        assert!(RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Storage, &[b'L', b'B', b'S', b'C', 0x02, 0x00]).is_err());
        assert!(RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Storage, &[b'L', b'B', b'S', b'C', 0x01, 0x01]).is_err());
        assert!(RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Ipc, &[]).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_record_holds_a_bool_as_0_or_1() {
        let record = storage_record(&[0x02]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_bool().is_err());
        assert!(
            RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Ipc, &[0x02]).is_ok_and(|decoder| decoder.decode_bool().is_err())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_varint_ends_at_the_last_byte_its_type_can_hold() {
        // A non-canonical varint that its type can hold reads as its value.
        let record = storage_record(&[0x81, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x00]);
        assert_eq!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_u32(), Ok(1));

        let record = storage_record(&[0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x0f]);
        assert_eq!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_u32(), Ok(u32::MAX));
        let record = storage_record(&[0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x1f]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_u32().is_err());
        let record = storage_record(&[0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x00]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_u32().is_err());

        let record = storage_record(&[0xff, 0xff, 0x03]);
        assert_eq!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_u16(), Ok(u16::MAX));
        let record = storage_record(&[0xff, 0xff, 0x07]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_u16().is_err());

        let record = storage_record(&[0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x02]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_u64().is_err());

        let record = storage_record(&[0x80]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_u64().is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_signed_varint_sign_extends_its_last_byte() {
        let record = storage_record(&[0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x07]);
        assert_eq!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_i32(), Ok(i32::MAX));
        let record = storage_record(&[0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x78]);
        assert_eq!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_i32(), Ok(i32::MIN));
        // The unused bits of the last byte differ from the sign bit.
        let record = storage_record(&[0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x0f]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_i32().is_err());
        let record = storage_record(&[0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x00]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_i32().is_err());
        let record = storage_record(&[0xff]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_i32().is_err());

        let record = storage_record(&[0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x7f]);
        assert_eq!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_i64(), Ok(i64::MIN));
        let record = storage_record(&[0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x01]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_i64().is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_string_holds_the_characters_its_header_claims() {
        // Latin-1 storage that holds a byte that is not ASCII.
        let record = storage_record(&[0x03, 0xe9]);
        assert_eq!(
            storage_decoder(&record).decode_utf16_string(),
            Ok(DecodedString::Latin1(&[0xe9]))
        );

        // Fewer bytes than the length claims.
        let record = storage_record(&[0x07, b'a', b'b']);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_utf16_string().is_err());
        let record = storage_record(&[0x04, 0x41, 0x00, 0x42]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_utf16_string().is_err());
        let record = storage_record(&[0xfe, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x01]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_utf16_string().is_err());

        // A non-canonical length.
        let record = storage_record(&[0x85, 0x00, b'a', b'b']);
        assert_eq!(
            storage_decoder(&record).decode_utf16_string(),
            Ok(DecodedString::Latin1(b"ab"))
        );

        // A string ends at its length, not at the end of the record.
        let record = storage_record(&[0x03, b'a', b'b']);
        let decoder = storage_decoder(&record);
        assert_eq!(decoder.decode_utf16_string(), Ok(DecodedString::Latin1(b"a")));
        assert!(!decoder.is_at_end());
    }

    #[test]
    fn bytes_need_their_whole_length() {
        let record = storage_record(&[0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x01]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_bytes().is_err());

        let mut record = 3_u32.to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
        record.extend_from_slice(&[0x01, 0x02]);
        assert!(
            RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Ipc, &record).is_ok_and(|decoder| decoder.decode_bytes().is_err())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_big_int_has_a_sign() {
        let record = storage_record(&[0x00]);
        assert!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_big_int().is_err());
        let record = storage_record(&[0x01, 0x00]);
        assert_eq!(storage_decoder(&record).decode_big_int(), Ok((false, &[][..])));
    }
}

// https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace
pub const fn is_ascii_whitespace(code_point: u32) -> bool {
    // ASCII whitespace is U+0009 TAB, U+000A LF, U+000C FF, U+000D CR, or U+0020 SPACE.
    matches!(code_point, 0x09 | 0x0A | 0x0C | 0x0D | 0x20)
}

//! The C ABI through which LibWebCommon's MimeSniff::MimeType and MimeSniff::Resource reach the crate. C++ lends its
//! MIME types to the crate as a [`FfiMimeType`] of spans into its strings, and the crate lends its own back to a
//! callback the same way.

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Span;

use super::mime_type::{Essence, MimeType, is_javascript_mime_type_essence_match};
use super::resource::{SniffingContext, sniff};
use crate::rust_panic::abort_on_panic;

/// A string that C++ lends as UTF-8 or as UTF-16, of `length` code units.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FfiStringInput {
    pub utf8: *const u8,
    pub latin1: *const u8,
    pub utf16: *const u16,
    pub length: usize,
}

impl FfiStringInput {
    /// The code points of the string, with each unpaired surrogate replaced by U+FFFD, or `None` for bytes that are
    /// not UTF-8.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The pointer that is not null must lend `length` code units.
    unsafe fn code_points(self) -> Option<Vec<char>> {
        if self.length == 0 {
            return Some(Vec::new());
        }
        if !self.utf16.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: The caller lends `length` UTF-16 code units.
            let units = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.utf16, self.length) };
            return Some(
                char::decode_utf16(units.iter().copied())
                    .map(|code_point| code_point.unwrap_or(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER))
                    .collect(),
            );
        }
        if !self.latin1.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: The caller lends `length` Latin-1 code units.
            let units = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.latin1, self.length) };
            return Some(units.iter().map(|&unit| char::from(unit)).collect());
        }
        // SAFETY: The caller lends `length` bytes.
        let bytes = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.utf8, self.length) };
        Some(std::str::from_utf8(bytes).ok()?.chars().collect())
    }
}

#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiMimeTypeParameter<'a> {
    pub name: Span<'a, u8>,
    pub value: Span<'a, u8>,
}

/// A MIME type whose strings, which are UTF-8, its lender keeps alive.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiMimeType<'a> {
    pub type_: Span<'a, u8>,
    pub subtype: Span<'a, u8>,
    pub parameters: Span<'a, FfiMimeTypeParameter<'a>>,
}

pub(crate) type OnMimeType = unsafe extern "C" fn(ctx: *mut c_void, mime_type: *const FfiMimeType<'_>);
type OnString = unsafe extern "C" fn(ctx: *mut c_void, string: Span<'_, u8>);

#[repr(u8)]
pub enum MimeTypeGroup {
    Image,
    AudioOrVideo,
    Font,
    Xml,
    Html,
    JavaScript,
    Json,
}

fn str_from_span(span: Span<'_, u8>) -> &str {
    std::str::from_utf8(span.as_slice()).expect("C++ lends UTF-8 strings")
}

fn essence<'a>(type_: Span<'a, u8>, subtype: Span<'a, u8>) -> Essence<'a> {
    Essence {
        type_: str_from_span(type_),
        subtype: str_from_span(subtype),
    }
}

impl FfiMimeType<'_> {
    fn to_mime_type(&self) -> MimeType {
        let mut mime_type = MimeType::new(
            str_from_span(self.type_).to_owned(),
            str_from_span(self.subtype).to_owned(),
        );
        for parameter in self.parameters.as_slice() {
            mime_type.set_parameter(
                str_from_span(parameter.name).to_owned(),
                str_from_span(parameter.value).to_owned(),
            );
        }
        mime_type
    }
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `on_mime_type` must be safe to call with `ctx`.
pub(crate) unsafe fn lend_mime_type(mime_type: &MimeType, ctx: *mut c_void, on_mime_type: OnMimeType) {
    let parameters: Vec<_> = mime_type
        .parameters()
        .map(|(name, value)| FfiMimeTypeParameter {
            name: Span::new(name.as_bytes()),
            value: Span::new(value.as_bytes()),
        })
        .collect();
    let ffi_mime_type = FfiMimeType {
        type_: Span::new(mime_type.type_().as_bytes()),
        subtype: Span::new(mime_type.subtype().as_bytes()),
        parameters: Span::new(&parameters),
    };
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a callback for `ctx`, and the MIME type outlives the call.
    unsafe { on_mime_type(ctx, &raw const ffi_mime_type) };
}

/// Parses the input as a MIME type, and calls `on_mime_type` with the MIME type if that succeeds. Returns whether it
/// succeeded.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `input` must lend its code units for the call, and `on_mime_type` must be safe to call with `ctx`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn mime_sniff_parse_mime_type(
    input: FfiStringInput,
    ctx: *mut c_void,
    on_mime_type: OnMimeType,
) -> bool {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        // SAFETY: The caller lends the code units of the input.
        let Some(mime_type) = unsafe { input.code_points() }.as_deref().and_then(MimeType::parse) else {
            return false;
        };
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a callback for `ctx`.
        unsafe { lend_mime_type(&mime_type, ctx, on_mime_type) };
        true
    })
}

/// Calls `on_serialization` with the serialization of the MIME type.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `mime_type` must be a valid MIME type for the call, and `on_serialization` must be safe to call with `ctx`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn mime_sniff_serialize_mime_type(
    mime_type: *const FfiMimeType<'_>,
    ctx: *mut c_void,
    on_serialization: OnString,
) {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        // SAFETY: The caller lends a MIME type for the call.
        let serialization = unsafe { &*mime_type }.to_mime_type().serialize();
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a callback for `ctx`.
        unsafe { on_serialization(ctx, Span::new(serialization.as_bytes())) };
    });
}

/// Whether the MIME type with the type and subtype belongs to the group.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn mime_sniff_mime_type_is_in_group(
    group: MimeTypeGroup,
    type_: Span<'_, u8>,
    subtype: Span<'_, u8>,
) -> bool {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        let essence = essence(type_, subtype);
        match group {
            MimeTypeGroup::Image => essence.is_image(),
            MimeTypeGroup::AudioOrVideo => essence.is_audio_or_video(),
            MimeTypeGroup::Font => essence.is_font(),
            MimeTypeGroup::Xml => essence.is_xml(),
            MimeTypeGroup::Html => essence.is_html(),
            MimeTypeGroup::JavaScript => essence.is_javascript(),
            MimeTypeGroup::Json => essence.is_json(),
        }
    })
}

/// Calls `on_minimized` with the minimized MIME type of the MIME type with the type and subtype.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `on_minimized` must be safe to call with `ctx`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn mime_sniff_minimize_a_supported_mime_type(
    type_: Span<'_, u8>,
    subtype: Span<'_, u8>,
    is_supported_by_the_user_agent: bool,
    ctx: *mut c_void,
    on_minimized: OnString,
) {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        let minimized = essence(type_, subtype).minimize_a_supported_mime_type(is_supported_by_the_user_agent);
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a callback for `ctx`.
        unsafe { on_minimized(ctx, Span::new(minimized.as_bytes())) };
    });
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `string` must lend its code units for the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn mime_sniff_is_javascript_mime_type_essence_match(string: FfiStringInput) -> bool {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        // SAFETY: The caller lends the code units of the string.
        unsafe { string.code_points() }.is_some_and(|code_points| is_javascript_mime_type_essence_match(&code_points))
    })
}

/// Calls `on_mime_type` with the computed MIME type of the resource whose data is `data`. `supplied_type` is null if
/// there is no supplied MIME type.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `supplied_type` must be null or a valid MIME type for the call, `scheme` must be UTF-8, and `on_mime_type` must be
/// safe to call with `ctx`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn mime_sniff_sniff(
    data: Span<'_, u8>,
    sniffing_context: SniffingContext,
    scheme: Span<'_, u8>,
    supplied_type: *const FfiMimeType<'_>,
    no_sniff: bool,
    ctx: *mut c_void,
    on_mime_type: OnMimeType,
) {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        // SAFETY: The caller lends a MIME type for the call, if any.
        let supplied_type = unsafe { supplied_type.as_ref() }.map(FfiMimeType::to_mime_type);
        let computed_mime_type = sniff(
            data.as_slice(),
            sniffing_context,
            str_from_span(scheme),
            supplied_type,
            no_sniff,
        );
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a callback for `ctx`.
        unsafe { lend_mime_type(&computed_mime_type, ctx, on_mime_type) };
    });
}
